target.recipe_text:
skillet bow tie lasagna

this quick recipe from my best of country cooking cookbook collection tastes like lasagna, but you make it on the
stove. it's very tasty and is always a hit with my family.

1. in a large skillet , cook beef , onion and garlic until meat is no longer pink
2. drain
3. add the tomatoes , water , tomato paste , parsley , oregano and salt
4. mix well
5. stir in pasta
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer for 20-25 minutes or until pasta is tender , stirring once
9. combine cheeses
10. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto pasta mixture
11. cover and cook for 5 minutes
12. yield: 4 servings
target.review:
It suprised me... this was REALLY good.  I used quinoa instead of regular pasta (I'm gluten-free), so if you do, too, take the simmer time down to about 10 minutes, or until the noodles are almost done, but still a little hard.

Thanks for sharing this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: I think this is a really great recipe, I've made it several times.  However, it doesn't double well (rice doesn't always), so don't do what Kristi Don't does. ;)  Did I mention this was really good? :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
latin black bean soup

i have enjoyed this recipe for years.  i think it is the red wine vinegar that makes it interesting and unique.  what i like best to do with it is to leave out some of the water to make it thick enough to fill a pita with sprouts and a sweet dressing.

1. sort and wash black beans
2. boil in water for 2 minutes
3. let rest 45 minutes
4. add onion , garlic , green pepper , oregano , and cumin
5. cover and cook on low for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
6. add tomato pate , vinegar and tamari
7. cook 30 minutes
8. add chillis , rice , tabasco , and cilantro
9. cook 10 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I can't believe how good this was.  I made a few modifications to reflect those things I actually had on hand, but I have to say that this was probably the best bean dish I've had all year.  These are the modifications I made:  used only 4 cups of water and added 4 tsp. of vegetable base, used two med jalapenos instead of chiles, replaced oregano with summer savory and used white rice instead of brown.  I also soaked my beans overnight, but I don't think that really would have made a huge difference either way.  We LOVED this dish.  We will definately be having this again and taking it to potlucks!!!  Thank you for sharing it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry comfort

this is a combination of recipes for chicken curry/massamun. i love the comfort of creamy coconut milk and spicy red curry. the aroma of the rice with the sweet yet spicy sauce just warms me up. my husband loves it and it's one of those delicious dishes that doesn't take much time.

1. cook rice according to package
2. heat coconut milk on medium , whisk in curry paste when milk is warm
3. add chicken broth
4. cook for 2 minutes until bubbly
5. add the brown sugar and salt to taste
6. add the vegetable and cook on medium for 4 minutes
7. add the chicken and reduce to low heat
8. simmer for 20 minutes to absorb best flavor
9. remove from heat and serve over rice
demonstrations.review: I'm wondering if you meant 1-4 tsp. of red curry paste... ours was unbelievably hot with 2 tblsp.  We generally eat hot things, so hot is HOT, baby! :)  Flavor was good, though, heat was just a lot much.  I'll be making this again, but with adjustments. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato cheese soup

requested recipe from my sister and i made  slight changes, it's so soothing and great winter food!

1. barely cover potatoes with water add the salts and cook till tender
2. this water is part of soup do not pour off
3. while potatoes are boiling saut onions and parsley in oil just till onion wilted
4. add the evaporated milk once potatoes are tender
5. ladle some of the potatoes with liquid in food processor or blender and puree
6. add back to pot
7. on the next 2 rounds of puree potatoes and liquid add 1 / 2 of the onions and parsley mix
8. use slotted spoon to find the rest of the potatoes to put in food processor
9. soup should still be hot enough add the cheese and stir
10. if not , heat only on low do not boil so cheese can melt
11. season with the black pepper and garlic powder
12. guessed on the amount of water to cover potatoes make take more or less !
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I felt compelled to doctor this recipie as I put it together.  I doubled the cheese, but I still don't think it has enough.  Also, I pureed about 8 cups of the whole mixture at one time.  I wanted some whole bits of potato left.

My husband really liked it, he loves potatoes, but I think I will work with this some more.  What about adding some bacon or ham?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean rice in a rice cooker

this side or a vegetarian main is loaded with flavor and texture. i made this in a rice cooker if you add more water will increase the cooking time and produce softer rice; reducing the amount of water will produce firmer rice. but once you've found the ratio that's right for you, it'll be very easy to have perfect rice your way. yes you can make stove top as well. be sure not to remove the lid till done cooking.

1. put aside 1 tablespoon scallions and 1 teaspoon coconut for garnish
2. place all the rest ingredients in rice cooker
3. pour broth 3 / 4 inch above the level of the rice
4. press the cook button
5. when done fluff with fork place in a serving dish and top with reserved coconut and scallions place lime along side for garnish and use as wanted
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.  It did have a little bit of a blandness, but that might just be a personal thing.  We will make it again, but next time, maybe use some pineapple juice and buillion instead of chicken broth.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
apple bundt cake

i have to make this cake at least once a month for my family . i sometimes leave the walnuts out and even without the nuts this cake is a hit. i use fiji apples for this cake.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. mix apples , cinnamon and sugar , set aside
3. mix all the rest of the ingredients , mix well
4. grease bundt pan
5. add 1 / 3 of batter mixture to the pan
6. sprinkle half of the apple mixture over the batter then follow with 1 / 3 batter , and then add rest of apples and top with rest of batter
7. bake for 55- 60 minutes
target.review: I have been making this cake for several years, and we LOVE LOVE LOVE it!!!  I've started using a little less sugar, and I've even used 1/2 whole wheat flour once with good results.  A real favorite, jam packed full of good things!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell taco seasoning clone copycat

this copycat recipe is on many websites, but wasn't on zaar, so i posted it. better than those storebought packages.

1. combine and store in an air-tight container
2. add seasoning mix and 3 / 4 cup of water
3. bring to a boil then reduce heat
4. simmer uncovered , 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: Very good!  We don't usually eat tacos much- but that will change now that we've tried this.  I've already made up a canister full to keep handy.  Looks like I'll need 5 tablespoons of the mix per pound of ground beef (I use half ground beef and half ground turkey).  Thanks for the great mix!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy butterfinger dessert

this dessert makes a really yummy treat

1. crumble up angel food cake
2. freeze candybars ahead of time- leave wrappers on
3. crush bars- with wrappers on
4. cream butter , egg yolks , sugar and vanilla
5. gently add cool whip
6. in a 9 x 13 inch pan , spread out 1 / 2 angel food cake
7. next layer 1 / 2 creamed mixture
8. next sprinkle 1 / 2 butterfingers
9. repeat and serve
demonstrations.review: I was just about to post a very similar recipe when I saw this one.  The only difference with mine is that I whip up my own unsweetened whipped cream instead of Cool Whip.  Even with the unsweetened whipped cream it is still a very rich dessert, and a little too sweet for my personal taste.  But it is always well received and eaten right up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barb s gumbo

this is my recipe for gumbo. i have made it with shrimp or chicken. we like it either way. you can make it as spicy as you like . we do not care for it to spicy or hot.

1. add oil to skillet , heat over medium heat add the flour , to make a roux
2. this may take about 15 minutes
3. stir in onion , celery , bell pepper , garlic , and black pepper
4. cook over medium heat about 3 minutes or till vegetables are crisp tender
5. gradually stir in chicken broth , tomatoes , salt , worcestershire sauce , pepper sauce , corn , okra , basil , thyme , cumin and bay leaf
6. bring to boiling point
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes
9. add shrimp during the last 5 minutes
10. serve over rice
11. this can also be made with chicken , if using chicken
12. use chicken breast cut in chunks add during the last 20 to 30 minute cooking time
13. smoked sausage is also good added with the chicken
14. i have added a can of crabmeat to the shrimp version
demonstrations.review: We LOVE this!  I don't put in quite as much Worchestershire sauce as it calls for, but I love what it adds to the recipe.  I have never used it in gumbo before.  Thanks for taking the time to write out a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s buttermilk scones

i adopted this recipe after the original poster, mean chef (ihhdro), departed the site. he posted the recipe on aug 19, 2002.

1. put dry ingredients in food processor , pulse to mix
2. add butter , pulse until butter is in pieces about the size of a hazelnut
3. dump into bowl
4. pour in buttermilk and mix with a fork until a shaggy mass forms
5. form into a disk about 1 1 / 2 inches high , cut disk in half and in half again
6. cut each of the 4 pieces either into thirds to get 12 or in half again to get 8
7. place on parchment lined sheet pan and freeze for 20 minutes remove from freezer , brush tops with egg yolk / cream mixture sprinkle with sugar
8. bake for about 12 minutes at 400
demonstrations.review:
Holy cow!  These are soooo good!  I made 2 batches of these yesterday, and they were gone in a flash.  I made one batch plain.  In the other batch I reduced the sugar to 1/4 cup, added some chopped dried cherries, topped with chopped almonds, and served with an almond butter.
The plain ones were excellent, but I think I'll be adding fun stuff every time I make them.  What a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza snack cups

i make these all the time. they are good for quick suppers or kids birthday parties. my husband loves them.

1. pre heat oven to 375
2. in 12 cup muffin pan , evenly press each biscuit in bottom and up the side of each cup
3. chill until ready to fill
4. in skillet brown beef , drain and add pizza sauce
5. evenly spoon mixture into each one of the cups
6. bake for 15 minutes
7. sprinkle with cheese and bake an additional 5 minutes until cheese is melted and biscuits are golden
8. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Everyone enjoyed this recipe.  It was a little bit tedious for the results, so I will probably not make it often.  Instead of just hamburger for the filling I used hamburger, Italian sausage and chopped pepperoni.  5 minutes was not enough time for the cheese, so I bake the second pan for 10 mintes, added the cheese and baked another 10 minutes (instead of 15 and 5).  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
strawberry twinkie delight

taste of home; needs to refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving.

1. in a bowl , mix together the strawberries and glaze
2. set aside
3. slice the twinkies in half lengthwise
4. place in an ungreased 13x9 inch baking dish with cream side up
5. in a bowl , beat cream cheese and sweetened condensed milk with an electric mixer , until smooth
6. fold in the whipped topping
7. spread over the twinkies
8. spoon strawberry mixture on top
9. cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes , then serve
target.review: Oh WOW!! How could something this sinfully delicious be so easy to make? It was so easy that my daughter did most of the work. Get the insulin because your going to need it. Very sweet and rich. A little bit goes a long way. Reminds me of strawberry shortcake only much richer. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kidney beans and rice

easy, hearty, stick-to-your ribs dinner.

1. in a skillet , cook beef , onion , and garlic until meat is browned
2. drain
3. stir in the beans , tomatoes , and seasonings
4. cover and simmer for 5 minutes
5. add rice
6. cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated
7. discard bay leaf
8. serve
demonstrations.review: Oooh yeah!! My family loved this dish. Tasted like a milder version of red beans and rice, with beef instead of sausage. Very good and an easy to make recipe. Made a hearty meal and the left-overs were taken care of the next day with no problem. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tennessee hot chocolate

my favorite 'help me get to sleep' drink.

1. combine milk and half-and-half in a medium saucepan
2. cook over medium heat until thoroughly heated
3. add sugar and cocoa , whisking until blended
4. remove from heat
5. whisk in vanilla and bourbon
6. pour into mugs
7. top with marshmallows , if desired
demonstrations.review: Nurse Di, you have done it again. My husband and I love your recipes. This hot chocolate drink is to "Di" for (he-he)! Creamy, sweet, and laced with bourbon. We enjoyed as we watched the snow falling outside and were glad to be inside and warm. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and hash browns bake

easy and yummy.

1. thaw hash browns overnight in refrigerator
2. layer in an ungreased 13x9 inch baking dish
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. place chicken and mushrooms over hash browns
5. stir together sour cream , broth , soup , bouillon , onion , and garlic
6. pour over chicken and mushrooms
7. sprinkle with paprika
8. bake , uncovered at 350 degrees for 50-60 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and so delicious. Everyone at the table asked for seconds. This casserole was so easy to make and  the creamy chicken filling and hash browned potatoes went well together. A good comfort food casserole. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey apple salad

taste of home

1. in a large bowl , toss apples with lemon juice
2. add grapes , celery and dates
3. in a small bowl , combine mayonnaise , honey , sour cream , and salt
4. mix well
5. pour over apple mixture and toss to coat
6. stir in the walnuts
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yum, Yum!! I made this salad tonight to go with our dinner. We thought it was very delicious and different from our usual. Interesting combination of ingredients and the honey in the dressing is the secret and special ingredient. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s best brisket

my dad knows how much i love this. thanks for the recipe.

1. center brisket on a large heavy piece of foil in a roaster
2. sprinkle with liquid smoke
3. sprinkle brisket with celery salt , garlic salt , onion salt , and pepper
4. fold sides of foil over to seal
5. refrigerate overnight
6. 6 1 / 2 hour before serving , open foil and season with salt , pepper , and worcestershire sauce
7. reseal and cook in a slow oven at 300 degrees for 5 hours
8. uncover and pour barbecue sauce over brisket
9. cook 1 additional hour , uncovered
10. let sit 20 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Yipee Skipee, this brisket was very delish. Your directions were  easy to follow. The meat was tender enough to cut with a fork. The sauce was some of the best I have ever had. It had a smoked tangy sweet flavor that made us drool. I think you have outdone yourself with this one, Nurse Di. Thanks. Worth at least 10 stars.

target.recipe_text:
cranberry nut loaf

nan

1. sift flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and baking soda in a large bowl
2. cut in butter until mixture is crumbly
3. add egg , orange peel and orange juice all at once
4. stir just until mixture is evenly moist
5. fold in cranberries and walnuts
6. spoon into a 9 x 5 x 3 inch loaf pan
7. bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean
8. remove from pan and cool on wire rack
target.review: i searched through all the similar cranberry cake recipes on this site, and this one is definitely the winner.  simple, straightforward and DELICIOUS!  the light flavor of orange is perfect, as well as the amount of cranberries - any more and it would have been falling apart.  thanks so much Theresa/Thunderbird for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan cupcakes

a simple cupcake

1. preheat the oven to 350f and line muffin pan with cupcake liners
2. whisk the soy milk and vinegar a measuring cup and set aside a few minutes to get good and curdled
3. in a large bowl , sift the flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda and salt
4. stir to combine
5. in a separate large bowl , beat together the soy milk mixture , oil , sugar and vanilla
6. stir the dry ingredients and mix until no large lumps remain
7. fill cupcake liners two-thirds full and bake for 20-22 minutes till done
8. transfer to a cooling rack and let cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: this is a fantastic recipe.  i don't have a muffin tin, so i made this as a 9 inch cake.  the only change i made was using 1 tablespoon of vinegar instead of 1 teaspoon, as i have used the larger amount with 1 cup of milk in other recipes... and the teaspoon didn't seem to curdle the soymilk enough.  the cake is moist and rich.  i put vegan chocolate frosting and coconut flakes on top - everyone loved it!  what a simple, great recipe.  i will definitely be using it again.  thanks swirlycinnacakes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
triple berry pie   delicious

this is from www.kraftfoods.com. a delicious, easy recipe to enjoy those fresh summer berries. enjoy!

1. mix berries , sugar and tapioca in large bowl
2. let stand 15 minutes
3. preheat oven to 400 degrees
4. prepare pie crust as directed on package for 2-crust pie , using 9-inch pie plate
5. fill with fruit mixture and dot with butter
6. cover with second pie crust
7. seal and flute edge
8. cut several slits in top crust to vent steam
9. bake 45-50 minutes or until juices form bubbles that burst slowly
10. cool
demonstrations.review: you can't really get a better pie recipe.  i searched the entire site and elsewhere... i think 4 cups of fruit is the perfect amount to make a berry pie.  i also forgot the butter and it didn't make a difference.  will use this recipe as a base from now on... maybe next time add a tablespoon of grand marnier?  thanks for a great recipe Amy020!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip cake  no eggs no milk

nan

1. mix first five ingredients in a bowl
2. make a well in the middle of the dry ingredients and pour next three ingredients
3. blend well with the dry ingredients
4. pour batter in an 8-inch greased and floured pan and bake at 375c for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: i have made this cake about 5 times now.  the first time as written, the next time, i substituted the 1 cup of chocolate chips with a mixed cup of nuts, chocolate chips and dried cranberries.  the few times after that, i used a cup of several kinds of nuts (pecans, sliced almonds, walnuts) and just a dash of chocolate chips.  each time it was received with rave reviews!  this is such a simple and wonderful recipe.  i love the club soda action on the batter - like a successful science project.  thanks so much jas kaur for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frosted chocolate cake and cupcakes  gluten  dairy   egg fre

really yummy chocolate cake recipe that also makes delicious cupcakes!  you don't even know that it's allergen free!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray an 8" square or 9" round cake pan with nonstick spray or line a dozen muffin cups with cupcake liners
3. in a medium size bowl , stir together the brown rice flour , xanthan gum , cocoa , brown sugar , chocolate chips , nuts , baking soda , and salt
4. in a two cup glass measuring cup , measure the 1 / 2 cup oil , add the 1 cup of liquid , then add the vinegar and vanilla extract
5. stir to combine
6. stir the liquid ingredients into the dry ingredients until just moistened
7. pour the batter into the prepared pan and bake for 30-35 minutes for cake or 25 minutes for cupcakes , or until the cake tests done
8. set aside to cool
9. for frosting , combine the chocolate chips and milk / water in a small saucepan
10. heat over medium , stirring constantly until the chips are melted and the glaze is smooth
11. spoon over the cooled cake and refrigerate until set
demonstrations.review: yummy, yummy, yummy!  i have tried several gluten-free recipes from this site but they called for gluten-free flour blends - my results were mixed.  this recipe has taught me that brown rice flour is the way to go!  the cupcakes rose perfectly and had a very desirable texture - surprising for gluten-free. also, they were delectable!  i brought them to my knitting group and each person had 2 - they were gone in 10 minutes.  thank you so much for a great recipe and for opening my eyes to the magic of brown rice flour!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla eggless and dairy free vegan cake

this is a simple yellow cake that is easy to make and very tasty. it can also be cut into slices and served with fruit.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. prepare cake pan: line 8-inch round or square cake pan with parchment paper and grease bottom and sides of the pan
3. then flour the pan
4. whisk together flour , sugar , baking soda , and salt
5. add vegetable oil , soy milk , and vanilla extract
6. whisk until no lumps appear and batter is smooth
7. add vinegar , stir about seven times , and quickly pour into pan
8. bake around 30 minutes , until cake begins to pull away from sides and / or toothpick inserted in the center pulls out clean
9. let sit for ten to fifteen minutes , invert , and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: amazing. this may be my new favorite cake! i added 1/2 cup chopped sliced almonds. such a simple recipe with great instructions. i will definitely use this again, as it lends itself so easily to variation! thanks very much MeowMeow00!!!

target.recipe_text:
french onion salisbury steak

this is a dish you can get on the table in about a half hour flat, and as my teenagers say--hella bomb!  from cuisine at home.  serve over recipe #139580 or frozen cheese toasts.

1. combine chuck , parsley , scallion , salt , and pepper
2. divide evenly into 4 portions and shape into 3 / 4 to 1-inch thick oval patties
3. place 2 tablespoons of flour in a shallow dish
4. dredge each patty in flour
5. reserve 1 teaspoon flour
6. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a saut pan over medium-high heat
7. add patties and saut 3 minutes on each side , or until browned
8. remove from pan
9. add onions and sugar to pan
10. saut 5 minutes
11. stir in garlic and tomato paste
12. saut 1 minute , or until paste begins to brown
13. sprinkle onions with reserved flour
14. cook 1 minute
15. stir in broth and wine , and then add the salt and thyme
16. return meat to pan and bring soup to a boil
17. reduce heat to medium-low , cover and simmer 10 minutes
18. serve steaks on cheese toasts with onion soup ladled over
19. garnish with parsley and parmesan
target.review: Outstanding!  One of the best things I've made in a while.  I didn't have a problem with the patties since the soup and bread are both incredibly flavorful.  If you live near a Trader Joe's, use their Parmesean Garlic Baguette for this recipe.  Out of this world!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: WOW - all that flavor with so little work! I am definitely impressed. I let the sauce simmer on very low heat for about 3 hours, then we ate the spaghetti. I'm making the lasagna tomorrow for company, and I expect the same raves I got out of DH tonight! This goes into the keeper file for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot stuffing

nan

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , melt the butter
2. saute the celery , onion , parsley and mushrooms until onions are soft
3. in a large bowl , combine the bread cubes and vegetables
4. add the poultry seasoning , thyme , sage , pepper , salt and marjoram
5. toss together well
6. add egg and enough broth to moisten
7. lightly pack into slow cooker
8. cover and cook on high for 45 minutes
9. reduce to low and cook for 4 to 8 hours
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!  I made this at Thanksgiving, and my Mom, who had come over to "help" me cook, had eaten half of it out of the crockpot before we sat down to dinner!  (OK, I will admit I picked at it too!)  Definitely use only about half the liquid called for, but I kept an eye on it and added broth as needed.  Garlic marinated mushrooms gave this a little extra kick.  Will make every Thanksgiving!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled vietnamese chicken

this chicken is just full of flavor.  scoring the breast or thigh before marinating allows the marinade to penetrate the meat better and faster.  i found this recipe in cooking pleasures magazine and we just loved it.  another plus is a short marinading time that does not compromise the flavor at all.  longer would only make it better.

1. heat grill
2. place all the ingredients except the chicken in a shallow glass baking dish and stir them together
3. make shallow slits across the chicken breast , going a little deeper in the thick end
4. make shallow slits long ways , resulting in a slight diamond pattern in the meat
5. put the chicken in the marinade and make sure some gets in the slits
6. this only needs to marinade for 10 or 15 minutes to pick up the flavor , i believe this is because of the slits
7. place on grill and cook for 8 to 10 minutes , until no longer pink
8. turn once during cooking
demonstrations.review: This is a staple in our house in the summer. I never have molasses around, so I just use honey. I will substitute lime juice most of the time as well since I have a weird citrus thing - lemon= Mediterranean; lime=Asian in my weird little brain. Oh well. Excellent and tremendously easy chicken!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review:
This was, without question, the best chicken I have ever had.  I forgot to rub the spice mixture on until about five hours before I made the chicken, but I can't imagine it being any better that how it turned out.  I actually made this in my Ronco rotisserie, and it turned out so moist and flavorful that DH was fighting me for the white meat, which he usually won't touch because it's "too dry."

I also only had spring onions, so I chopped those up and put them into the cavity.  YUM!!  I will make this over and over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf  hey virginia  mine is better

ha-ha, i do love the "meatloaf: yes virginia, there is a great meatloaf" recipe, however i believe mine is just a hint better.  you be the judge.  i made this for my husband’s birthday- party of 15, and everyone raved over it- so, hey everyone- give it a shot, i would love some feedback.  i use dried onion as opposed to fresh because i didn't like the bite of fresh onion, it's much more subtle yet still flavorful to use dried... you be the judge though- use 1 small fresh yellow onion chopped if you like. by the way- some of you may be wondering- this is not a 'sweet meat'... it may be confusing with all the brown sugar and sweetened condensed milk- but i assure you- this is not sweet- if you want to- just omit the savory sauce and make it on the side to use as a dipping sauce the first time around... i'm highly confident in this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. mix all ingredients thoroughly in mixing bowl and pat into a 9" round pie plate and pat flat
3. mix the "savory sauce" in a separate bowl and spoon over the meatloaf
4. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This recipe convinced me that I need to start making good old fashioned comfort food more often.  I thought my husband was going to cry from happiness.  Not only that, this recipe is a bit healthier than your average meatloaf due to the oats.  (Plus I used 2% milk, and decreased the sugar and it still turned out perfectly.)  Thank you for a new staple!

target.recipe_text:
real irish soda bread

i have never found an irish soda bread recipe (or commericially available loaf) that can hold a candle to this recipe. it is simple to make and you can also mix the dry ingredients, add a hang-tag listing the wet ingredients and baking instructions and you have an outrageously good gift.  

this is an absolutely authentic irish recipe, and if you have never had a soda bread with fruit or caraway, it is probably due to the baker's preference to omit it, cost cutting measures or the way in which this recipe is prepared in a few regions of the country.

note:  if you don't like caraway seeds, currants or raisins, don't add them.  and don't overmix this dough.  i blend wet and dry ingredients with a large spooon only until incorporated.

also, if like pretty111, you provide a low-star review because you think the recipe isn't traditional, don't bother.  this recipe is not listed as "traditional", just delicious.  i think that if you do not try a recipe, you have some nerve giving it a low-star review.  it is just unfair.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees farenheit
2. butter and flour a pie plate or round cake pan
3. sprinkle uncooked oats on the bottom of the pan
4. combine dry ingredients and currants
5. mix melted butter , eggs and then buttermilk and sour cream
6. stir in dry ingredients only until incorporated
7. put dough into a prepared pie pan , in a mound with a rounded top
8. cut an x in the top of the loaf
9. bake for 50 minutes
target.review: After looking for days all over the internet, I chose this recipe. It is wonderful. I even found some recipes that were supposed to be "traditional". Well, they can keep them as they would not be eaten by us. We attended a St. Patrick>s Day dinner last night and I supplied this bread. It was a hit! We liked it so well, I am making it again tomorrow for the weekend. Why wait for St. Patrick's day? That is too far away. Thank you so much for posting. BTW, the only change I made was to add some salt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot hamburger cabbage casserole revised

last year i posted this recipe from another weight watchers member at a meeting.  with the helpful comments from other 'zaar' members, i made some adjustments.  if you like cabbage rolls but not the work of making them, this is a perfect recipe for you.  there is a similar recipe posted on the 'zaar', but this one has a few differences and is worth the try.

1. place 3 cups or 1 / 2 bag of cabbage in bottom of crock pot
2. brown beef with onions , garlic salt , and italian mixed spices in non-stick skillet and drain
3. put beef on top of cabbage , and then do the same with the rice
4. top with remaining cabbage , and sprinkle with salt and pepper
5. combine spaghetti sauce , water , tomatoes , basil , and seasoned salt in a bowl
6. pour sauce mixture over top of cabbage
7. cover and cook on high for 4 to 5 hours
8. makes 6 servings with each serving size being 1 1 / 4 heaping cups
9. for all weight watchers folks , this is 4 points per serving and is very filling
demonstrations.review: We love stuffed cabbage leaves, but I no longer make them. I made this yesterday and we loved it. I followed the recipe the best that I could, but, made it with homemade frozen spaghetti sauce, tomatoes and herbs. I ended up with 4 quarts (4 meals) for the two of us. This is definitely something I will make again and again. I am freezing 2 quarts and will let you know how they do. Thank you so much for posting! Edited to add that it freezes well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne with smoked salmon and peas

make sure you get good smoked salmon.

1. cook pasta in salted boiling water
2. cook , stirring until the pasta is"al dente"
3. drain the pasta and return it to the warm pot
4. add the peas , smoked salmon , lemon zest , lemon juice , butter , olive oil , scallions , and stock
5. simmer till heated through
6. stir
7. add salt and pepper to taste
8. garnish with fresh dill
demonstrations.review: This is an outstanding dish. As there are only two of us, I halved the recipe and we still have enough for another meal. I add some dill when I added the salmon, peas, etc. and I will continue to do so. This is so easy and could not possible be better. This is a must try for a light, easy wonder dish. Thank you so much for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
club wraps

another great recipe from southern living. we have these for a quick, easy lunch when we are on the go. omit any ingredient that is not to your liking. add what you like. very flexible.

1. spread mustard-mayo blend evenly over 1 side of each tortilla , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border
2. layer turkey and next 6 ingredients evenly over tortillas
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. roll up tortilla
5. cut in half diagonally , and secure with wooden picks
demonstrations.review:
I served these to friends out on the deck with cocktails - what a hit! Everyone loved them and wanted the recipe. The only thing I did different was use plain mayonnaise. These will be made again and again. 
Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortured chicken   beer can

i first saw these "tortured" chickens served at a bar-b-q. lined up on a serving platter, beer cans still in place! talk about a conversation starter!the dry rub sounds bizarre, but i guarantee the proportions blend into a delicious combination.

1. mix 4 dry ingredients together
2. use this rub inside and out of the cleaned , dry chicken
3. be generous
4. place 1 / 2 can of beer in center of roasting pan
5. position"bottom" of chicken over beer and slide chicken over the can of beer until the chicken is"sitting" upright in the pan
6. the fit will be snug and chicken will be secure
7. roast uncovered at 350 degrees for 1 hour
8. do not baste , do not turn pan
9. the beer will steam the chicken deliciously
10. when done , carefully remove can of beer from chicken and serve
11. chicken can also be carved while"sitting" on the beer can
12. i have"tortured" 2 or 3 chickens in the same roaster and did not have to adjust cooking time
13. this melt-in-your-mouth chicken will get rave reviews
demonstrations.review: This is an an excellent way to cook chicken and keep it moist. I have cooked chicken this way for years and vary the seasonings a lot. I now use a Tipsy Chicken cooker for my chicken instead of a beer can. It will not tip over. Go to the Tipsy Chicken or Char Broil web site to order one. One more thing, in Texas these are Beer in the Rear Chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I thought I had written a review a few years ago - sorry to be so slow. This is a wonderful recipe. I add potatoes and carrots. My only other change is to cut the Italian dressing in half and add a couple shakes of dried Italian herbs. All who have eaten this go home with the recipe. Thank you for posting.

target.recipe_text:
cheese filled hamburgers

this is my adaptation of a recipie that came from a barbeque book many years ago. i can't remember the book, but i make these for nearly every barbeque we have (and we have a lot)

1. mix the top five ingredients together in one bowl
2. mix the last two ingredients together in another bowl
3. form them into four balls
4. put a deep well into each of the four balls of meat , and place a ball of grated cheese and chopped onion into that well
5. carefully cover the cheese and onion with the meat ,
6. then carefully flatten the burgers , until they are about 1 / 2" thick
7. then put them in the freezer for approximately 1 hour before you cook them
8. then cook them on the barbeque or in the frying pan
target.review: For some reason we didn't find these to have a lot of flavor. I followed the recipe exactly and used the cheddar and onion filling. I think the burger itself may have needed a little extra spice or maybe some BBQ sauce...sorry...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous macaroni and cheese

this is the most awesome macaroni & cheese that we have ever eaten. it is a family favorite and we have it once a week. all four of my kids request it often, and my husband thinks it's incredible. hope you enjoy this comfort food.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. cook macaroni according to package instructions
3. drain , rinse and set aside
4. in same pot over low heat , melt the butter
5. add flour , salt and pepper and whisk into melted butter until smooth
6. simmer and stir until mixture thickens into a paste and is golden
7. slowly add milk and whisk into butter mixture until smooth
8. bring to boil and then simmer until thickened
9. there is no way to tell you how thick , except to say it should be thicker than gravy but not as thick as pudding
10. if you have made basic white sauce , you will know when it is thick enough
11. remove pot from heat
12. add cheddar cheese and stir until cheese starts to melt
13. add macaroni and stir until coated
14. pour into a 9 x 12 baking dish or 2 quart casserole
15. as an extra indulgence , you can sprinkle 4 oz more cheese on top
16. i only do this if i happen to buy a 12 oz bag or block instead of 8 oz
17. bake about 20- 30 minutes , when you see top getting a bit crispy and brown
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much Karen! This was delicious. My kids (and husband) ate it like they hadn't eaten in days! As always, I made some minor changes: used rice milk instead of milk, added   parmesan to the cheddar cheese blend. Will definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
haddock supreme

a quick and easy fish recipe

1. lightly salt and pepper fillets
2. dust fillets in flour
3. dip in mixture of egg , milk and ketchup
4. dip in the bread crumb mixture
5. sprinkle with seasoning salt
6. let stand for 15 minutes
7. saute garlic in the oil for 1 minute
8. add fish and fry on both sides
9. place fish on warm platter
10. add wine and butter to the pan , scrape and bring to a boil
11. drizzle over fish
demonstrations.review: What a delicious way to prepare haddock!! We all loved it and I will definitely make this one again. I must admit I was a little skeptical about the addition of ketchup to the egg mixture but it added a really subtle taste and color to the mixture. Thanks for sharing Allyoop!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portabella and gouda burger with garlic mayo

i prefer a good portabella mushroom sandwich to a typical veggie burger anyday, and this one is excellent. it's juicy, garlicky and cheesy, and really quick. try it on the grill in the summer, on grilled french bread with garden-fresh tomato ... mmmmmmm! prep time includes marinating mushrooms.

1. combine 2 tablespoons olive oil , sliced garlic clove and thyme in a zipper-lock bag
2. add portabella mushroom caps , zip up and marinate for at least 30 to 45 minutes
3. in the meantime , combine the garlic mayo ingredients and allow to blend in the refrigerator
4. when mushroom caps are ready , heat a little olive oil in a skillet and saute for about 5 minutes , stem side down
5. try to include as much of the sliced garlic and thyme as possible in the skillet
6. turn mushroom caps over and top with cheese
7. cover skillet and cook for about another 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
8. alternatively , these are delicious on the grill as well !
9. serve with tomato on toasted rolls or french bread spread with garlic mayo
10. really nice with some avocado on the side
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! These were tasty. The texture and the flavor were a great combination.My husband initially snubbed his nose at it, but before long he was asking for a few bites of mine. Another keeper!! Thanks EGA!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice  baked

brown rice is so much better for you than white rice. it has more nutrients and about 3 times more fiber than white rice does. 
i never really cared for brown rice until i tasted this one. you can do as many variations as you like with it. add your favorite herbs, spices or veggies to it. make it vegetarian by using veggie cubes instead of chicken. the rice turns out perfectly fluffy and delicious. the aroma that fills your house while it's baking is wonderful and it's hard to wait until it's done to sneak a taste. as it bakes the bay leaves will rise to the top so they can be easily 'fished' out of the casserole before serving. i like to top the finished rice with freshly chopped cilantro and a twist of black pepper. for a nice crunch you can add chopped water chestnuts.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. heat heavy skillet until hot
3. add oil and then add uncooked brown rice
4. stir rice in oil until golden brown , stirring constantly
5. in the meantime heat water and add bay leaves , bouillon cubes , poultry seasoning , black pepper , minced onion flakes , parsley , oregano , basil and pepper flakes
6. bring to a boil
7. when rice is golden and ready , pour rice into a covered 2 quart casserole dish
8. add the boiling liquid on top of the rice
9. careful ! it will sputter
10. cover casserole with aluminum foil and the cover for the casserole dish
11. bake for 1 hour
12. remove from oven and let sit covered for 15 minutes
13. fluff with fork before serving
demonstrations.review: After reading some of the other comments, I added more water but still the grains were very undercooked even after being in the oven for about 1 1/2 hours. We didn't find the combination of seasonings all that exciting either...sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh cream of mushroom soup

this quick and easy recipe is so much better than the canned stuff. great as a first course, or with salad or sandwiches. of course, you can use it in your favorite recipes, too.  to make it thicker, use less stock and/or use heavy cream instead of the half-and-half cream or milk.

1. lighly saute mushrooms in butter
2. add flour and stir constantly for about 5 minutes
3. slowly add stock , stirring until all is incorporated
4. simmer about 10 minutes
5. add cream , stir and serve
demonstrations.review: I must admit I had my doubts with such a simple recipe but decided to give it a try after reading many of the raving reviews. I agree with one reviewer that this is a great starter mushroom soup, but it definitely needs something. I added salt, pepper and garlic powder and it all came together beautifully. Also, I used brown cremini mushrooms and this had a really authentic 'canned' taste. I used whipping cream instead of half and half b/c that's all I had. This soup converted some of the pickiest "I hate mushrooms" eaters in my house!! Will be making this again!!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
target.review: Bellisimo! Loved..loved..loved this recipe! I used a mix of minced beef and pork. Family devoured them...going to make again tomorrow night and they're already oohhh and ahhhing. Thanks so much Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate blood

this is a craft recipe for fake blood. got a halloween costume, school play, haunted house, or you feel like leaving work early and you need some fake blood that looks realistic and doesn't taste half-bad? here it is...

1. mix cocoa powder into the water before adding the other ingredients
2. after adding the rest , blend well , then wait for it to settle a bit
3. either skim the bubbles and chocolate scum off the top with the edge of a facial tissue , or pour the mixture into another container
4. the longer it sits , the more the cocoa tends to settle to the bottom , which oddly mimicks the effect of real blood separating
5. if you splatter this mixture onto cloth , it makes neat two-part marks which dry into pretty convincing bloodstains
6. if you let it run from a victim's mouth and then let it dry , the blood darkens and cakes to the skin in much the same way real blood does
demonstrations.review: I had so much fun with this on the weekend with three 12 y.o boys and a 10 y.o boy. It's so realistic I told them to stay away from the road as people may think I'd done some damage to them LOL. Excellent recipe and will be definately used again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drew s marinade and tenderizer

this is especially good for marinating meats for stir-frying, as well as chicken breasts, roasts, pork chops, or cubed venison. double recipe if using a large cut of meat, such as roasts.

1. add all ingredients , except baking soda , and mix
2. add baking soda and mix
3. it will begin to froth , and that's normal
4. place meat in resealable plastic bag and refrigerate for 20 minutes up to several hours
5. grill or stir-fry meats
demonstrations.review: This was great!! Exactly what I was looking for. I used this marinade on rib eye steak and it was so tender and flavoursome I couldn't get enough of it. My search has ended...TY so much for this post.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered southwestern dip

this is my best friend's stevie's recipe. she gave it to me years' ago at easter and it has been my job to make it for thanksgiving each year since. it is the kind of dip that has people just pull up their chairs to the dish and leave only when the pan is scraped clean. simple and delicious.

1. mash avocado with 1 tablespoon lemon juice
2. spread into the bottom of a 9" pie plate
3. spread sour cream evenly on top
4. sprinkle with sliced green onions
5. spoon 8 ounce taco sauce over the top and cover with cheese
6. serve with nacho dorito chips
demonstrations.review: Mmmmm...Mmmmmm..Mmmmmm! This was everything I hoped it to be and more. Next time I will make it with a hotter taco sauce coz we like hot stuff but it was great the original way too. Just what I felt like for the day after Christmas when I was in a food picking mood. TY so much for posting this recipe, it's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean guy s general tso s chicken

this is an adoptee.  i have made it many many times and want to be able to help people out when they make it!  one of the best i've ever had.  takes some time, but oh so worth it.   good eats ;-)

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly blend the 1 / 2 cup of cornstarch and the eggs
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. if the mixture is too thick , add some vegetable oil to separate the pieces
4. in a small bowl , prepare the sauce mixture by combining the 2 tsp cornstarch with the wine , vinegar , sugar and soy sauce
5. first-stage frying: heat 1-2 inches of peanut oil in a wok to medium-high heat
6. fry the chicken in small batches , just long enough to cook the chicken through
7. remove the chicken to absorbent paper and allow to stand
8. second-stage frying: leave a tablespoon or two of the oil in the wok
9. add the pepper pods to the oil and stir-fry briefly , awakening the aroma but not burning them
10. return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the pieces are crispy brown
11. the general's favorite sauce: add the sauce-mixture to the wok , tossing over the heat until the sauce caramelizes into a glaze
12. serve immediately
13. serves 4 , along with steamed broccoli and rice
demonstrations.review: Now this was really nice! We dont have General Tso's here in Oz so I dont have anything to compare it with, but I loved the blended flavours. I took Puckheads advise and used chicken breast and it was devine! Definately a recipe that sticks in your head if your looking to do something with chicken. Well done Mean chef!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat mc donald s hamburgers cheeseburgers

my friend found this for me(when i was having a mcdonalds burger obsession) in one of her cookbooks and it's delicious.

1. mix the dried onion with the boiling water and let sit until re hydrated and no longer dry & crunchy
2. roll ground beef into a ball and press flat on waxed paper until about 1 / 8 inch thick
3. brown faces of bun in a dry frying pan over medium heat
4. remove bun and cook burger in the same pan for 2 min per side , salting each side lightly during cooking
5. on the top bun-half spread the ketchup , mustard , and onion , in the order , and top with the pickle slice
6. put the beef patty on the bottom bun and quickly slap the top and bottom together
7. microwave the burger on high for 10-15 seconds
8. for cheeseburgers: follow the above recipe , but add a slice of american cheese on top of the beef patty in the final assembly
9. microwave for 15 seconds on high to help steam the bun and simulate being wrapped in paper
demonstrations.review: This was pretty close to the real deal. A great snack and so very easy to make. My kids loved them and we will definately make them again one weekend. If you REALLY need the cheeseburger fix this one should keep you happy! Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
panera broccoli cheese soup

a very good broccoli cheese soup. served with crusty bread.

1. saut onion in butter
2. set aside
3. cook melted butter and flour using a whisk over medium heat for 3-5 minutes or until you see a noticeable golden brown color in your pan
4. slowly add in the chicken stock and whisk again to combine
5. simmer contents covered for 20 minutes on medium heat
6. add the broccoli , carrots and the sauteed onions , into the pot
7. stir , add the milk and half & half
8. cook covered over low heat 20-25 minutes but do not bring to a boil
9. this may cause the milk to curdle
10. add salt , pepper & nutmeg
11. continue to cook the soup on low heat and slowly add the grated cheese a handful at a time and stir to avoid clumps
12. once all the cheese has been added is melted , remove from heat , and serve immediately
13. suggestion: serve with crusty bread or in a breadbowl
14. refrigerate leftovers after they have cooled and store in a airtight container up to 5 days in the refrigerator
target.review: It's been a long time since I had Panera's soup and I missed it since it's the only broccoli cheddar soup I've ever really liked. This recipe was quite a find. I used vegetable broth instead of chicken stock but otherwise didn't change a thing. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice and lentil casserole

this is a great meal that we eat here often in the winter time. with some dark bread and maybe a salad it is a really hearty meal, though we have been known to eat just this for dinner. the recipe is adapted from amy dacyczyn's "the complete tightwad gazette"

1. preheat the oven to 300 degrees
2. mix all ingredients except the cheese in a baking dish
3. cover with foil and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes
4. then remove the foil , add the cheese , and bake for an additional 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty, simple, inexpensive and healthy. I served it with a salad but next time may add veggies right in the dish. DH felt it needed a little more flavor so I'll adjust that next time I make it. DD even liked it--I didn't tell her until after she was done that there were onions in it! I wasn't sure whether the rice and lentils should be pre-cooked (I'm not at all intuitive with cooking) but assumed correctly from the amount of liquid and time cooked, they should be raw. I didn't need to adjust the cooking time but I did use a slightly larger pan (11x8). I used colby-jack cheese but may use something sharper next time. This would probably also be good with spicy turkey sausage crumbles or another posters suggestion of spinach and baked tofu to make it a little more hearty for DH. We ate almost the whole pan between the three of us for dinner so there was nothing left for lunch today!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
demonstrations.review: Best turkey burger I've had to date. I used a shallot instead of scallions,  Bragg's liquid aminos instead of soy sauce, flax seeds instead of sesame seeds and I completely forgot the sesame oil. I broiled them in the oven and they turned out perfectly. Very moist and flavorful. This will be my standard preparation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm eggplant  aubergine  salad

tasty warm eggplant salad, great served with yogurt and my "fennel and sea salt pita bread crisps".

1. preheat oven to 200c
2. peel strips off the eggplant skin with a vegetable peeler , slice eggplant into 1cm thick slices
3. brush both sides with the extra olive oil , then place in a baking dish and sprinkle with sea salt
4. cook for 30 minutes
5. remove from oven , if eggplant is a little dry , sprinkle with water , cool for 5 minutes , then cut into 1 cm cubes and set aside
6. heat olive oil in a skillet over medium-high heat , add tomatoes , garlic , spices , chilli , sugar and salt
7. simmer for 10 minutes , remove from heat and add juice , vinegar and black pepper
8. add to the reserved eggplant , stir through herbs
9. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: This was a hit at a Moroccan-themed party I attended. I didn't know until after I made the dish that the party was catered so I brought it anyway (thought we could never eat it all but, in hindsight, we probably could have!). The guests kept asking the caterer about it and she rather sheepishly admitted she didn't make it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach sorbet

you can peel or not peel the peaches. without the peel, the texture will be smooth and pure yellow. with the peel, the sorbet will have more texture and tiny flecks of pink.

1. in a small saucepan , combine the sugar , water , and corn syrup
2. place pan over medium heat and stir until the sugar dissolves
3. boil without stirring for 1 minute
4. remove form heat and cool to room temperature
5. place the peaches in a blender or food processor with the lemon juices , salt , and cool sugar syrup
6. process until the mixture is smooth
7. if the puree is too thick to blend properly , add water , 1 tablespoon at a time until mixture blends easily
8. freeze immediately in an ice cream maker according to the manufacturers directions
9. when finished , the sorbet will be soft but ready to serve
10. for firmer sorbet , transfer to a freezer safe container and freeze several hours
demonstrations.review: I had to resort to frozen peaches since quality fresh peaches are a rarity where I live. I added ground ginger to spice it up a bit and may add cinnamon next time as well. I also used brown rice syrup instead of the corn syrup and 1/4 c agave syrup in place of the sugar (reduced water to 1/4 c) due to dietary restrictions. Very easy, tasty treat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I used a spelt crust recipe I have, peas and carrots and vegetable broth instead of chicken. This turned out very nicely. My DH ate half of it in one sitting and DD cleaned her plate without bribery--she even asked for leftovers today! I will probably add mushrooms the next time I make this and will use turkey more often than chicken.

target.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin brownies bars

adapted from taste of home. i think they are more cake/bar-like than brownie-like.  i substitute freshly ground whole grain flour for the all- purpose. **please note**. if you substitute store-bought wheat flour for the all-purpose, you do not need to add the additional amount of flour - just use the same amount as all-purpose.

1. in a large mixing bowl , beat the pumpkin , eggs , oil and vanilla until blended
2. combine dry ingredients
3. gradually stir into pumpkin mixture
4. pour into a greased 15-in
5. x 10-in
6. x 1-in
7. baking pan
8. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
9. cool in pan on a wire rack
10. in a small mixing bowl , beat the butter , cream cheese , vanilla , milk and salt until smooth
11. gradually add confectioners' sugar until smooth
12. frost brownies
13. store in the refrigerator
14. yield: 5-6 dozen
target.review: This was good I used whole wheat flour and really like the heartiness it goes nicely with the pumpkin flavor I only had applesauce with cinnamon in it so I didn't add anymore cinnamon I kept the rest recipe the same but I'm tempted to experiment and use splenda in place on the sugar and see how that works...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free zucchini brownies

no one will guess that these are fat free or that they contain zucchini

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees and grease 9 x 13 pan
2. mix together first four ingredients
3. add remaining ingredients
4. spread in pan
5. bake for 40 - 50 min , or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
6. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I enjoyed these and brought half the batch to a party where my friends although skeptical at first enjoyed them too. Or they were just to drunk to know better. I found the zucchini added alot of liquid to mixture but I still add some applesace too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry date squares

a delicious variation of an old favorite.

1. place dates , raspberries and water on the stove over medium heat to soften , add water as needed to make a thick date butter
2. combine margarine and flour with pastry blender until crumbly
3. stir in oats and sucanat
4. stir in vegetable oil and press 2 / 3 of mixture into a 9 x 9 pan
5. spread date mixture over and top with remaining crumbs
6. press lightly and bake at 350f for 20 to 30 minutes , or golden brown on edges
demonstrations.review: The bars were very good, but I had some problems when making them. The crust mad what seem to be way to much and I ended up throwing some away because I think the oats would have overpowered the recipe if I used the whole thing. The filling made just enough for a very light layer of filling. It also took alot longer than the stated cooking time for the bars to be done. I think with some adjustments it would be a good recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry walnut white fudge

fruity taste too an old fashion fudge recipe.

1. line 9 inch square pan with foil
2. spray lightly with cooking spray
3. melt vanilla chips in small saucepan over low heat , stirring until smooth
4. remove from heat
5. combine powdered sugar , cream cheese and frosting
6. blend well
7. stir in melted vanilla chips , walnuts , cranberries and orange peel
8. spread in sprayed pan
9. refrigerate about 1 hour or until firm
10. remove fudge from pan by lifting foil
11. cut fudge into squares
12. serve
demonstrations.review: I made this for friends for the holidays. I'm a big white chocolate and cranberry fan so I really enjoyed. My friends really liked the creamy texture of it, probably from the frosting. It was better cold than warm because it sat out for awhile at my friends house. I nliked that this was an easy fudge recipe, no candy thermometer needed and I had my friends convinced I did it all from scratch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken   veggies

ok, so i couldn't think up a good name.  i came up with this on the spur of the moment and we all loved it -- even the veggie haters of the family ;)  amounts are approximate; i really just tossed everything in there, so adapt to your tastes!  oh, and if broccoli slaw isn't available in your area, sub shredded veggies of any type or just regular cole slaw mix (without dressing)

1. heat a teaspoon of olive oil in a skillet
2. toss the diced chicken and flour together in a bag to lightly coat with flour , then shake off all excess flour
3. cook chicken , stirring occasionally , until fully cooked and golden brown
4. remove chicken from skillet
5. add another teaspoon of olive oil to skillet
6. add squash and garlic
7. saute until tender-crisp
8. add broccoli slaw and saute another minute or two
9. add everything else , including the chicken , and cook until heated through , stirring frequently
demonstrations.review: I really enjoyed this recipe even though I totally forgot to add the italian seasoning. I was cooking in a hurry tonight. I love recipes that secretely add veggies, though these veggies aren't secret it's easy to fool someone who might not eat broccoli. I used whole weat flour to the dip the chix (I used tenders so they cooked quickly) in. I served it with roasted potatoes with thyme and a waldorf salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
terra chip chicken breasts

this is a quick, easy and yummy recipe that is like a gourmet version of chicken schnitzel. from the cookbook, "gatherings: creative kosher cooking from our families to yours" (netivot hatorah).
tips: to crush chips and still maintain texture, put them into a sealable plastic bag and use a rolling pin for crushing. for a finer texture, crush chips in a food processor.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a small bowl , combine flour , garlic powder , salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken breasts in mixture
4. set aside
5. in another small bowl , beat egg , mustard , lemon juice and lemon and herb spice together
6. set aside
7. place crushed chips in a large bowl
8. dip chicken first in egg mixture , then in crushed terra chips
9. place chicken breasts in roasting pan
10. in a small saucepan , melt margarine
11. drizzle on top of chicken
12. place roasting pan , uncovered , in oven
13. bake for 30 to 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wow this recipe is awesome. The colors of the terra chips look beautiful coating the chicken. I was out of the lemon pepper seasoning so I left that out but it was still very good and simple to make. Since I do not keep kosher I actually melted some parmesan cheese on top as well, it was a nice addition.

target.recipe_text:
indian style meat marinade

it's nice to put a twist on the usual foods like a roast. this recipe will add zing to your beef and covers up to a 6 pound roast. enjoy!

1. mix ingredients well and place in large resealable bag
2. add meat
3. squish meat around in marinade to coat well
4. marinate for 4 to 24 hours
5. the longer the tastier !
6. a
7. fill sink with enough water to cover bag
8. with the open side of bag up , gently place in water
9. you will notice that all of the air will be squeezed out of the bag
10. when the water is nearing the top of the bag , seal the bag
11. take out of sink , pat the bag dry and place in refrigerator
12. let it marinate ! :)
target.review: I used the marinade for a flat iron steak and grilled the meat after a 4 hour bath (for the steak, not me!).  A very nice change of pace without being overpowering.  I served it with steamed carrot/parsnip mixture and sauteed kale with malt vinegar.  Recommended.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new years good luck soup

a combo of "good luck" ingredients in a great soup.  from sweet tea and cornbread.

1. in a large stock pot or dutch oven , brown sausage along with onion and garlic
2. when the sausage browned add all of the other ingredients and mix well
3. bring up to a boil
4. reduce heat to simmer and cook for 45 minutes to an hour
5. if you want to do this in your slow cooker
6. brown the sausage with the onion and garlic first in a skillet
7. when browned place the meat with the other ingredients in a 5 - 6 quart slow cooker and cook on low 6-8 hours or on high for 3-4 hours
8. serve with your favorite cornbread
9. letting this soup sit a day or 2 will meld the flavors even more
demonstrations.review: This was a good basic bean soup but I felt it would be helped a bit with a larger range of flavors.  I added one finely diced carrot, 1 tbsp sesame oil and 1 tsp soy sauce to the mixture.  I feel lucky already and it's only the 2nd of January!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and chorizo  leftovers in tasty disguise

from the *best ever chicken* cookbook edited by linda fraser & per the intro -- "the perfect way to use up leftover cold meats, this spicy dish is a fast & fortifying meal for a hungry family." a cook's note attached to the recipe further states "you can also add cooked ham (or pork), smoked cod (or haddock) & fresh shellfish to this dish." (10-15 min time was allowed for ingredient prep. cooking time includes 5 min standing prior to serving). *enjoy* !

1. heat the oil in a lrg saucepan
2. add onion , celery + red bell pepper & cook to soften , but do not allow to caramelize
3. add rice , chicken stock , tomato puree & tobasco sauce
4. simmer for 10 min , uncovered
5. stir in chicken , sausage + peas & simmer for a further 5 minutes
6. turn off heat , cover & allow to stand for 5 min b4 serving
demonstrations.review: A nice family meal with just enough kick and variety.  In place of tomato puree, I just used a hefty squeeze of 2X strength tomato paste in a tube.  For the chorizo, I used two hot lean turkey sausages cut into 1 inch pieces.  Finally, I added 1/2 tsp turmeric for color.  Dinner for several and lunch for me tomorrow!  Enjoyed it very much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: I used a non-stick sheet [Silpat] to encourage browning and make it easier to make.  To make this into a more complete meal, I added the following for a tomato-based sauce: Finely diced eggplant (the ends of my monstrous eggplant), [1 medium tomato, 2 T onion, 1 tsp ground allspice, 2 T sherry vinegar, 1 T finely diced medium-hot pepper, 1 tsp sugar, 1/2 tsp salt, 1/4 tsp fresh-ground black pepper] all blended.  Then, the sauce is simmered to reduce by half.  Spoon it over the baked eggplant.  A nice way to keep a healthy vegetable healthy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled tuna steak with worcestershire

i cooked these about 4 minutes on each side.
it turned out very nice.
cook to your liking.

1. combine all sauce ingredients together
2. set aside
3. season the tuna steaks with salt
4. coat with ground black pepper
5. grill the tuna over a hot charcoal grill , cooking each side for 2 minutes
6. arrange on serving plates
7. serve with the sauce on the side
8. serve with steamed potatoes , and garnish with a sprig of parsley
demonstrations.review: I followed Slacky5's notes and served the tuna on pasta with minced garlic, olive oil and a dash of parsley.  I also added 3 tbsp of finely minced cilantro and 3 finely minced seeded cheyenne (hot) peppers.  The sauce went into individual ramikins as a dipping sauce. Spicy and savory!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alton brown s chipotle smashed sweet potatoes

this is a recipe from alton brown's show good eats.  (he is my hero!)  it is modified from the original by using 1/2 tsp instead of 1 tsp of adobo sauce and extra salt.  a great side to go with a steak and a salad!

1. put cubed potatoes into steamer basket and place steamer into a large pot of simmering water
2. steam potatoes for 20 minutes or until the potatoes are fork tender
3. add butter to potatoes and mash with potato masher
4. add peppers , sauce , and salt and continue mashing to combine
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Here's a solution to the chipotle in adobo problem--when you use this product, you invariably never use the entire can.  Take a plastic ice cube tray and place one pepper in each well and then distribute the adobo sauce among the set of peppers.  Freeze and store in a poly bag.  Now, when you need chipotle in adobo, take one cube and dice it. (Also works for tomato paste!).  Enjoy!

target.recipe_text:
chicken  mushroom and cheese quesadillas

in my opinion, you can't get a better flavor combination than chicken, mushrooms and onions sauteed together. mmmmm! this recipe is adapted from cooking light magazine.

1. heat olive oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
2. combine ground cumin , 1 / 8 teaspoon salt , and 1 / 8 teaspoon black pepper
3. sprinkle over chicken
4. add chicken to pan , and saut 5 minutes or until browned
5. remove chicken from pan
6. set aside
7. add onion , mushrooms , garlic , 1 / 8 teaspoon salt , and 1 / 8 teaspoon black pepper to pan
8. saut 5 minutes
9. remove from pan
10. let stand 5 minutes
11. wipe pan with paper towels
12. heat pan over medium heat
13. sprinkle each tortilla with about 1 / 3 cup cheese
14. arrange 1 / 2 cup mushroom mixture over one-half of each tortilla
15. arrange chicken evenly over mushroom mixture
16. carefully fold each tortilla in half
17. add 2 quesadillas to pan
18. cook 2 minutes on each side or until lightly browned and cheese melts
19. repeat procedure with remaining quesadillas
20. serve immediately
target.review: Our family loved this recipe.  It was fast, easy, the chicken was moist, the flavors were good but most importantly BOTH my children liked it.  My son, who never eats much, ate his whole quesadillas and said this was his favorite.  Thank you. I will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato and ham soup

found on 30 day gourmet.

1. assembly directions:
2. place potatoes , carrots , celery , onion , water , chicken bouillon , thyme , parsley and ham in a large stock pot
3. bring to a rolling boil
4. reduce heat to medium and boil for 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
5. in a separate bowl mix together the evaporated milk and flour until there are no lumps
6. add to the soup and stir in completely
7. continue to cook until the soup has thickened slightly
8. freezing directions:
9. cool soup completely
10. divide into family-sized portions in freezer bags or rigid containers
11. seal , label and freeze
12. serving directions:
13. thaw completely
14. reheat over low in a saucepan or reheat in the microwave
15. comments:
16. you can reduce the sodium in this recipe by using reduced sodium chicken bouillon
17. serve this soup with a big salad to round out the meal
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very easy and 3 out of a family of 4 enjoyed it.  My kids are very picky and if one likes dinner I consider that a success.  We did make very few changes. First we were out of celery so we added more carrots, second I used a evaporated milk subsitute, (6 TBSP's soy milk powder to 1 cup of boiling water; use amount called for in recipe) and third we cooked it in a crock-pot.  It was wonderful smelling and cooked away while we were busy.  I changed the servings from six to four and still have enough leftovers for tomorrow night.  One thing that we all agreed on was that it was to salty.  I would suggest cutting back on the bouillon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover mashed potatoes and turkey casserole

a lovely way to use hard-to-reheat potatoes and gravy, and good alternative to the same-old leftovers after thanksgiving. someone should try it with bacon bits under the cheese.

1. put the ingredients in the order given , layered: turkey , gravy , potatoes , and cheese
2. try not to squish the potatoes into the gravy , but this is a casserole , so there isn't any worry if you do a bit
3. the cheese adds a nice bite and flavor , so try not to skip out on it
4. cover and bake 350 degrees for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: My kids didn't like the way it looked and one refused to even try it.  It turned into a mush after being cooked, like a stew.  However it tasted very good and my husband LOVED it.  We tried it half with cheese and half without.  It was very good both ways but better with the cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streusel topped key lime squares

from cooking light (june 2005).

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. crust:
3. place first 5 ingredients in a medium bowl
4. beat with a mixer at medium speed until creamy
5. gradually add 1 cup flour to butter mixture , beating at low speed until mixture resembles coarse meal
6. gently press two-thirds of mixture into bottom of an 8-inch square baking pan coated with cooking spray
7. set remaining 2 / 3 cup flour mixture aside
8. bake for 12 minutes or until just beginning to brown
9. filling:
10. combine 2 / 3 cup sugar , 3 tablespoons flour , baking powder , and 1 / 8 teaspoon salt in a medium bowl , stirring with a whisk
11. add lime juice and eggs , stirring with a whisk until smooth
12. pour mixture over crust
13. bake for 12 minutes
14. remove pan from oven
15. sprinkle remaining 2 / 3 cup flour mixture evenly over egg mixture
16. bake an additional 8 to 10 minutes or until set
17. remove from oven
18. cool in pan on a wire rack
19. sprinkle evenly with powdered sugar
demonstrations.review:
This recipe was fast and super easy.  I did have to make a few changes because of what I had on hand.  I used bottled lime juice and since no fresh limes I didn't have any zest.  So I added extra lemon extract in the crust.  This turned out tangy and sweet, but not overly, which IMO lots of citrus baked goods are.
