I used three overripe bananas and crush one up to really infuse the banana flavor and slice remaining two and folded into the pudding/custard before pouring into the shell.  Did not take a long time to thicken, I would say as soon as I added scalded milk to sugar, flour mixture it was less than ten minutes to thicken to a right consistency.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
veronica s lemon buttercream frosting

this frosting is to die for if you love lemon! perfect as the frosting on a white or lemon cake. i think i found this in betty croker's cookbook, but can't remember. very very lemony!

1. beat butter , lemon peel and lemon juice in medium bowl on medium speed until smooth
2. gradually beat in powdered sugar
3. beat 2 to 3 minutes longer or until light and fluffy
4. however , when eaten the next day , it isn't as lemony and still very good
5. will cover a 9 x 13 cake or bunt cake
demonstrations.review: This was very very good.  I used 2tsp of dried lemon rind and 3-4T of "Real lemon juice" from the bottle.  It was VERY lemony (and I'm a lemon fanatic), perhaps it might have a "softer" taste with real rind and lemon juice. I will cut back on my own improvisations for this recipe as the kids said "Too Much Lemon".  My frosting was VERY fluffy - tip is to have the butter so soft that it's glossy -- seems like it will melt if you heat it up anymore.  Even my husband enjoyed this when he announced that he wanted me to make vanilla frosting; he didn't like lemon.  This made enough to put a thick layer in the middle and generously frost the sides and top of Cake. Thank you very much for a nice frosting recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne russo a la vodka with basil cream sauce

this receipe was adapted from marianne. it is a rich dinner, elegant enough to be served at a dinner party. i serve it with an individual anti-pasta salad as a first course and crusty french bread.

1. cook pasta in a large pot of boiling lightly salted water for about 8-10 minutes or until al dente and then drain
2. heat oil in large skillet or wok over medium heat
3. saute garlic , prosciutto , and red pepper flakes for 1 minute
4. stir in tomatoes and tomato paste and cook for 3 minutes
5. stir in vodka and cream and simmer for 15 minutes
6. stir in parmesan and chopped basil
7. add pasta and toss until evenly coated
8. serve with additional parmesan cheese if desired
demonstrations.review: I saught this recipe out because I recently went went to a local restaurant and ordered what I usually ordered there (but it's not on their regular menu), tortollini ala vodka.  They must have a new cook because they left out a few key ingredients.  So, not having satisfied my taste for it, I turned to recipezaar.  Obviously it's the prosciutto that makes the dish, along with the basil.  I added chopped onion (about 1/4 c), and a little chopped roasted bell pepper (less than 1/4 c).  I omitted the parmesan - saved it to be put on the top.  I used dried basil because I didn't have fresh - that would have been wonderful, but then added a bit of fresh spinach leaves to add the green.  I served this over handmade fettucine egg noodles. I thought it came out GREAT; the taste I had been looking for at the restaurant.  My children also thought it was wonderful (although they were concerned about the word "vodka" in the title - that I was feeding them alcholhol!  I didn't get into it about it cooking out - just told them that was just a fancy name...;)  )  Thank you for a really good recipe. I will make this often.  And it was easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
clam chowder   stew

best ever, lots of clams!!  lots of flavor! recipe can be cut in half.
if you would like to make this chowder really special, i have made it adding clams in the shell and mussels in the shell, with pealed prawns added at the very end, did this for christmas eve, served with cranberry scones, delicious!

1. fry bacon in a large dutch oven until crisp , remove with slotted spoon and set aside
2. add onion to pot , saute until softened , then add potatoes and chicken stock
3. season with salt and cayenne , cover and cook for 15 minutes
4. in a second large saucepan , melt butter , whisk in flour , whisking to make a roux
5. cook for 1 minute , then add cream and milk while whisking
6. cook over low heat until thickened
7. pour into onion and potato mixture , add clams , 2 cans undrained , add clams only , from the other cans reserving the juice
8. add worcestershire and bacon
9. add the other 2 cans of reserved juice a bit at a time to reach desired consistency and only if you want the soup less thick
10. stir and gently cook over moderate heat until heated through
11. transfer to soup tureen and garnish with parsley and paprika if using
demonstrations.review: I've used this recipe for a couple of years, but tweeked this recipe a bit though. Added 1/2 t thyme, 1/2 - 1 t red pepper flakes, a pinch or so of oregano, a few more potatoes, skimmed back just a tad on the onion (do not grate these-did this once BIG mistake), use whatever milk I've got on hand and at the end 1 short can of shoepeg corn.  Anyway, I've dazzled many with this recipe; it's on permanent file in my cookbook. Thanks for a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chickpea flour pizza

source: food and wine magazine archive by madhur jaffrey
note:  after two reviews regarding the size of this, i have changed this to serving one.

1. preheat the broiler
2. sift the chickpea flour with the salt into a medium bowl
3. slowly add 1 / 4 cup of the water , whisking constantly to form a paste
4. beat with a wooden spoon until smooth
5. whisk in the remaining 1 / 4 cup of water and let the batter stand at room temperature for 30 minutes , then stir in the rosemary
6. heat 1 tablespoon of the olive oil in a 12" nonstick ovenproof skillet
7. stir the batter once , pour it into the skillet and drizzle the remaining 2 tablespoons of olive oil on top
8. cook the pizza over moderately high heat until the bottom is golden and crisp and the top is almost set , 2 to 3 minutes
9. burst any large air bubbles with the
10. sprinkle the tomato , onion , parmesan and pepper over the top , then place the skillet under the broiler and cook until the pizza is golden and crisp , 4 to 5 minutes
11. slide the pizza onto a work surface , cut into wedges and serve hot
target.review: This was good, although I baked it rather than did it on the stovetop. We also made a real pizza from it, with pizza sauce and cheese and everything. A great-tasting alternative to pizza dough. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with fennel

this medieval chicken recipe, with its subtle flavor of fennel, is remarkable. it is a light dish that will not be out of place on the most inventive of modern menus. the original medieval preparation and cooking instructions (translated from the medieval language) read: 

1. cut the chicken into serving pieces and pat dry
2. melt the lard in a casserole over medium-high heat and brown the chicken
3. when it is golden brown , add the water and salt to taste
4. lower the heat and simmer , covered , for 40 to 45 minutes or until tender
5. meanwhile , wash and thoroughly dry the herbs
6. grind the almonds finely in a mortar and pestle or food processor , and then add the herbs and blend to a paste
7. remove the chicken from the casserole and keep it warm in a very low oven , covered loosely with aluminum foil
8. add the almond mixture to the casserole and reduce over medium heat until the sauce has thickened
9. arrange the chicken on a serving platter and strain the sauce over the chicken
10. sprinkle with the spices to taste and serve
demonstrations.review: We used ground almonds, which may be why our sauce didn't thicken much, so we  used it on the side for dunking. My extraordinarily picky daughter ate and ate, then asked "What is in this sauce?" That's never happened before, so thanks for the change of pace.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken almendrado

this is a delicious mexican dish that has a garlic sauce that is thickened with almonds, a definite spanish influence. adjust the spiciness to your taste.

1. brown chicken on all sides in oil in a large pot
2. add onion , garlic , and serranos to the pot
3. season chicken with salt and pepper
4. add stock , then simmer , covered , over low heat , for about 1 hour , or until chicken is tender
5. in a blender or food processor , combine almonds , sliced garlic , and 1 / 2 cup of cooking liquid
6. process into a coarse paste
7. remove chicken from pot and add paste to the pot and cook until sauce has reduced and thickened
8. place chicken on a platter and cover with sauce and sprinkle with chopped cilantro
9. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: I made this dish years ago and really liked it and was glad to find the recipe again. I wish I could give this three and a half stars -- it's pretty good, but a little bland and it didn't really thicken up. Also, it's pale and somewhat colorless without the cilantro. Maybe I could have browned the chicken more. Or used a spicier peppper and more cilantro. On the positive side, the kids liked it. Thanks for posting. I'll try it again some time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat hot fudge spoon cake

yummy wet chocolate cake.

1. whisk milk and chocolate pudding in a slow cooker until pudding is completely dissolved
2. in a large bowl , whisk cake mix , water , applesauce and egg whites until well-blended
3. pour the cake batter into the middle of pudding mixture in the slow cooker
4. cover and cook on low for 2 hours
5. serve hot , topped with ice cream
demonstrations.review: Strange and delicious! The mixture "bakes" in the slow cooker to a cake layer, a pudding center, and a layer underneath that seems liquid at first but thickens to a sauce. Very chocolatey and dense. Our applesauce jar broke, so we used some vegetable oil. And we found it needed more like 3 hours to cook. Fun, memorable recipe -- thanks qwerty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
so easy caramel rolls

caramel rolls were a favorite treat growing up in pa dutch country.  these are sinfully delicious and amazingly simple!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. combine all topping ingredients except pecans in ungreased 9-inch round cake pan
3. stir until well mixed
4. sprinkle with pecans and set aside
5. combine 1 tablespoon sugar and cinnamon in a small bowl and set aside
6. unroll dough and separate into 12 strips
7. spread each strip with 1 / 2 teaspoon softened butter , sprinkle evenly with sugar-cinnamon mixture
8. roll up loosely
9. pinch seam to seal
10. place rolls evenly in pan and bake for 18-23 minutes or until golden brown
11. cool 5 minutes
12. invert onto serving platter
13. let stand 1 minute before removing pan
14. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Prepped these at 5:30 a.m. and ate one as I drove to a 6:30 a.m. hike. They were so good I ate two more after the hike. I only got six rolls, not 12 -- maybe I was supposed to make very small rolls. Does that mean I actually ate 6 caramel rolls, not 3?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cashew burfi

nan

1. soak cashew in milk for an hour& grind finely along with saffron
2. in a casserole mix sugar with 1 / 2 cup of water& stir well
3. microwave it on high for 4 minutes to dissolve the sugar , stirring once in between
4. micro high , ghee in a cup for 1 minute
5. to sugar syrup , add cashew paste& hot ghee
6. micro high for 12-15 minutes , stirring thoroughly twice in between
7. test for soft ball stage
8. if not done micro high again for 1 or 2 minutes more
9. add spices , mix well , & pour onto a greased plate& cut when slightly cool
demonstrations.review: I really love cashews, and these are great with a cup of tea especially. Cut the sweets in small pieces, because they are rich. I especially appreciate the microwave directions, as I usually make the sugar syrup on the stovetop, but my kitchen is very hot in warm weather.

target.recipe_text:
quickest south beach breakfast

i needed a quick, fresh, easy breakfast before i go to work. i did not like the south beach cookbooks idea of making a bunch of egg muffins and freezing them. this can be changed a million ways - using different veggies, adding salsa...

1. spray microwave safe dish with butter spray
2. put spinach in dish
3. put cheese on top
4. pour in egg whites
5. microwave for 2 minutes - whites will start to puff up
6. take out dish and stir
7. microwave another minute - cook until looks dry on top
target.review: I make something very similar to this.  I like to quarter a tomatoe or two, put a little olive oil on it, sprinkle it with salt, pepper (and what ever else I'm in the mood to try) and roast them.  I love the taste of the roasted tomatoes with the spinach and eggs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar free banana split cake

a lovely dessert that will pass for the real thing and satisfy everyone's sweet tooth.  i found this dessert at a weight watcher's meeting and it quickly became the favorite dessert of several family members who are diabetic.

1. combine graham cracker crumbs and melted butter
2. pat into a 9x13 baking dish
3. spread sliced bananas over crust
4. mix pudding and milk according to package directions
5. spread over bananas
6. drain pineapple as dry as possible and spread over pudding
7. spread whipped topping over pineapple
8. top with sliced strawberries
9. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: When my kids were growing up I made this quite often during Spring and Summer. It was a family favorite. Mine was a Weight Watchers recipe but it seems to me that my recipe didn't call for milk. We added the crushed pineapples to the pudding mix instead of using milk. and we made 2-3 layers (bananas, pudding/pineapple, strawberries, whipped topping and again ...)   I don't recall if we put the whipped topping only on the top or in the layers.  Thanks for posting this. I'm going to make it VERY SOON!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 2 points santa fe salad with chili lime dressing

from ww site.

1. to make dressing , whisk together mayo , cilantro , water , scallion , lime juice , sugar and chili powder in small bowl until smooth
2. transfer to a jar or a plastic container with a tight fitting lid and refrigerate until ready to use
3. in a large bowl , layer remaining ingredients in order listed
4. cover and refrigerate
5. to serve , spoon salad ingredients into a bowl
6. shake dressing and then drizzle over salad , toss well to coat
demonstrations.review: This is an awesome salad. I roasted my corn and cooled it before throwing this together and it was really good. I will definitely make this again, especially on my menu #16207  I also like the fact that you put the dressing on each serving.  This will hopefully keep my leftovers good (there is only my husband and me now) for the next few days.  :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato basil soup

this is one of my favorite soup recipes, especially in the fall when it's just getting crisp and cool outside. however, it's also great in the summer when my basil is going nuts (like it is right now!)

1. heat the olive oil in a large soup pot over medium high heat
2. add the onion and garlic and cook , stirring often , until softened , about 10 minutes -- be careful not to burn garlic
3. add the tomatoes and the stock
4. bring to a boil and then reduce to a simmer
5. cook until soup is slightly thickened , about 20 minutes
6. season with salt and pepper
7. stir in the basil
8. place the pot of soup directly in sink , and using a stick blender , blend until smooth
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is EXACTLY what I was looking for. I love the "cream style" tomato soup, but I wanted something that tasted FRESH and without all the calories. Even better on day 2. I tried it cold and loved it that way, too. I am going to try to drain some to use as Bruchetta. I think it will be PERFECT. I melted some cheddar cheese in one time and boy was that awesome. This will be something I will keep in my refrigerator as a "go to" food. Thanks so much for sharing. :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sorbet de fraises et de framboises   strawberry   raspberry

a refreshing light dessert, serve with light cookies. originally from "french cooking - eileen reece".

1. hull the fruit , save a dozen whole berries for garnish
2. liquidize or mash them and pass them through a fine sieve to remove pips
3. beat in the sugar until dissolved , add water and strained lemon juice and pour into a freezing container
4. freeze for 40 minutes
5. remove and beat with a "silver" or "wooden" spoon and freeze again for 4 hours
6. serve in tall glasses
7. garnish with whole berries
demonstrations.review: I made up a recipe several years ago that was very similar to this. It is one of my favorite, most refreshing desserts. I use frozen fruits (so I didn't need to put in freezer) and I used Splenda. I didn't think of adding the lemon juice. Can't wait to try it with Lime juice (as I have a lime tree and not a lemon tree ) I will try this with fresh berries (as written but will use Splenda. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers mexican chicken breasts

this is a yummy easy recipe. 1 breast is 4 pts. i often used the flash frozen breasts for this. i use 4 4oz breasts.

1. place chicken breasts and taco seasoning in a seal able plastic bag
2. shake to coat well
3. spray casserole dish with pam
4. place breasts in casserole
5. bake 30 minutes at 375 degrees
6. top with salsa about 5 minutes before breasts are done
7. top with sour cream before serving
demonstrations.review: I'm in shock at how easy and good this recipe was... and to top it off a good choice for all those of us watching our weight.  I'm surprised I never thought to try this because of the simplicity.  I made it along with a southwest type salad and a WW desert.  It was a hit.  menu #16207 .  Thanks for posting

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review: I have hated meatloaf my entire life as my mother made the most disgusting meatloaf EVER.  My Husband loves meatloaf and I SO wanted to make it for him.  I found this recipe and it is SOOOOOOOO gooooood!!!!!   I LOVE it!  I usually make 6 at a time, have one that night and freeze 5 for future dinners.  I just make them as the recipe suggests, wrap tightly in foil, and freeze.  Then defrost and reheat in the oven, and make more of the sauce the night we're going to eat it!  Thank you for giving me a meatloaf my husband AND I love!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized butternut squash

this is a delicious butternut squash recipe from ina garten / the barefoot contessa. we really enjoy this during the holidays. it is best when the squash is cut in medium to large chunks so that the outside gets a maple-flavored crust, and the inside stays soft and delicious.

1. preheat the oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of each butternut squash and discard
3. peel the squash and cut in half lengthwise
4. using a spoon , remove the seeds
5. cut the squash into 1 1 / 4" to 1 1 / 2" cubes , and place them on a baking sheet
6. add the melted butter , brown sugar , salt and pepper
7. with clean hands , toss all of the ingredients together and spread out in a single layer on the baking sheet
8. roast for 45 minutes to 55 minutes , until the squash is tender and the glaze begins to caramelize
9. turn the squash while roasting a few times with a spatula to be sure it browns evenly
10. adjust seasonings if needed
11. serve hot
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely DELICIOUS! I only had maybe 1/8 cup of brown sugar so I added a little pure maple syrup....other than that I followed the directions and cooking time exactly. Hubby loved it too! I have another butternut squash (wish I had made both!!) and an acorn squash, I think I'll do those together and make another batch of this tomorrow!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato leek soup

the idea for the recipe came from a soup i had at biltmore estate in asheville, nc. it is easy to prepare, but tastes gourmet!

1. bring broth to a boil and reduce to medium
2. add leeks , potatoes , and onion
3. simmer , covered , 25-30 minutes
4. add seasonings and cream
5. simmer 5 minutes more
6. slightly mash with a potatoe masher to desired consistency
7. serve with salad and crusty bread
8. a snap to make , but tastes gourmet !
demonstrations.review: Pretty decent...good, creamy flavor. I have had better, but not by much. Gave it 5 stars due to impressive flavor with such an easy and QUICK preparation. I grow my own leeks and herbs so I didnt have much to buy. I tthought it was still a little anemic, flavorwise, so added a chickeb bouillon cube. Went a little mad with the immersion blender and didnt leave any chunks, but that's MY fault, not the recipes. Next time I make this,and there WILL be a next time, I will cut up and brown several slices of thick bacon in the pot prior to adding the chicken broth. Very good all around for a quick soup, very hearty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twice baked potatoes

easy and good. feel free to add any ingredients or spice that you like. i like to make extras, freeze wrapped in foil and add the cheeses later when potatoes are thawed and reheated.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. clean and scrub baking potatoes
3. pierce skin with a fork once or twice
4. bake at 350f 1 hour or until tender
5. let potatoes cool slightly
6. cut baked potatoes in half and scoop out within 1 / 4 inch of edge
7. mash with milk , green onions , s&p , and butter
8. stuff shells with mashed potato
9. sprinkle tops with cheeses
10. place on a baking sheet and bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until cheese is melted
11. serve with sour cream
demonstrations.review: Awesome! My only change was I added maybe 1/4 cup, maybe a little less, of sour cream to the mashed part before restuffing the shells.  I also did about 6 scallions because I really love them.  Everyone LOVED them, will make again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review:
This was AWESOME!! I had to use cornflake crumbs rather than bread crumbs as I'm a Celiac. I had HUGE chicken breast halves so I cut them in half and pounded them to a more equal thickness so they'd cook the same time. I added some smokey seasoned salt to the butter/garlic mix as I don't have regular seasoned salt. I used some crisco (butter flavor) to generously grease the pan. I preheated the oven and they baked 45 minutes at 350 and were perfect! I did not top with additional cheese as I'm not a big cheesy fan..the amount in the coating was more than adequate for my tastes, I'd think using Colby Jack would be lovely. One thing I did, just to not be wasteful, was any butter mix left in the bowl I drizzled over the pre-baked, prepared breasts prior to baking. My husband LOVED these, as did I. They are super quick and easy and look nice enough for company.

To the person who had trouble with them taking too long and then being dry...try pounding them a little thinner, and make sure they barely touch or don't touch in the pan. If you still have the same problem, I'd recommend having your ovens thermostat/temperature checked....and don't give up! This recipe really IS excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boneless pork chops with spicy rub

from dr. atkins quick & easy new diet cookbook

1. in a small bowl , combine olive oil , chili powder , paprika , garlic , salt , oregano , cumin and pepper
2. rub the mixture evenly over the pork chops
3. cover and refrigerate for 15 minutes
4. heat broiler
5. broil pork chops for 5-6 minutes on each side , until browned and cooked through
6. or you could also bake the chops at 375 degrees for 20-25 minutes or till done
7. serve immediately , with 2 wedges of lime for each chop
demonstrations.review: These were real good! I doubled recipe as I had 8 pork chops, I think I shall make extra next time to coat the chops more heavily.  I also squeezed the juice of half a lime into the rub as another reviewer did, will use a whole lime next time, will add maybe a dash or two of cayenne and/or Ginger next time too.  I washed and dried the chops, then rubbed them all over with the mix, covered and refrigerated for maybe an hour until I was ready to cook them.  I think they'd benefit from being in the fridge longer, maybe even overnight.  I seared them 2 minutes each side (they were one inch thick) and placed in a glass 13 x 9 dish, then added a little water to the bits left in the pan and drizzles over the chops, then covered tightly with foil and baked at 350 for 35-40 mins. I let them rest, keeping them covered, for about half an hour until the rest of the meal was done.  They were PERFECT and tender, just think that rub needs a little somethingl. By the way,  squeezing a little lime on the chops on your plate,,,really adds some zing! Very good! I served with twice baked potatoes and steamed broccoli with parmessan.  Very nice meal.

target.recipe_text:
fresh fruit with vanilla custard sauce

this makes a luscious light dessert, a change from all the heavy dishes over the holidays. looks wonderful in a stemmed glass. any fresh fruit can be used.

1. scald milk in a large saucepan over medium heat , set aside
2. combine eggs , egg whites , and sugar in a medium bowl , beat with a wire whisk until blended
3. gradually stir about one-fourth of hot milk into egg mixture
4. add to remaining hot milk , stirring constantly
5. cook stirring constantly , over low heat until mixture thickens and coats a metal spoon , about 30 minutes
6. immediately pour sauce into a large bowl , stir with a wire whisk until cool
7. stir in vanilla and salt , cover and chill 2 hours
8. serve over fresh fruit
target.review: Really good - you need to add the hot milk to the egg/sugar mixture very slowly in order to ensure nothing cooks, and the window between "thickened" and "overcooked and slightly grainy" is very short, but the recipe works beautifully.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy black beans and rice with mangoes  crock pot

this is so good and it's easy too. this recipe was found in fresh from the vegetarian slow cooker.

1. heat oil in large skillet over medium heat
2. add onion , bell pepper , garlic and jalapeno , cover , and cook 5 minutes until softened
3. add in seasonings , mix well and cook for 1 minute
4. transfer mixture into a 3 1 / 2 to 4 quart slow cooker
5. add bean , water , brown sugar , salt and pepper
6. stir well
7. cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
8. add the cooked rice and the mangoes
9. allow to cook another 10 minutes
10. serve and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was really good - I added some red pepper flakes to increase the heat a little.  Because I kept the crockpot on after adding the mangoes, they had time to stew a little, which made the bean mixture a little sweeter and really brought everything together.  Next time, I'll add them about an hour before the cooking time is over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno red bean bbq burgers

moist, delicious vegetarian alternative to boring frozen veggie burgers. these are easy to make and taste wonderful on whole-grain buns with some cheddar cheese, tomato and lettuce for crunch. be watchful while cooking these ... the sugar content in the barbecue sauce can cause the burgers to blacken kind of quickly. tastes great on the grill, too ... just keep an eye on them!

1. heat oil in nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. add next onion , plum tomato , jalapeno , garlic and chili powder
3. saut 5 minutes
4. cool slightly
5. using fork , coarsely mash beans in bowl
6. combine with onion mixture , breadcrumbs , 2 tablespoons of the barbecue sauce and egg white
7. shape mixture into four 1 / 2-inch-thick patties
8. it will look as though these little burgers will just fall apart and turn to mush , but they stay together really well once they"hit the pan" !
9. if grilling , oil the rack or spray grill rack with nonstick spray , then fire up coals to medium heat
10. if pan-frying , heat a little olive oil over medium heat
11. place patties on grill or in skillet and cook until golden brown and heated through , about three minutes per side
12. place burgers on buns
13. serve with more barbecue sauce , and cheese , tomato , lettuce , avocado , or whatever topping you like !
demonstrations.review: Good flavor, but these really need another egg white as binder to hold together.  It would be a lot easier to cook them in a skillet or on a griddle using a spatula with a sharp edge to flip them; you wouldn't leave so much good tasting stuff on the grill.  We'd make these again, with modifications.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean orzo salad with feta vinaigrette

from cooking light (june 2005)

1. cook the orzo according to package directions
2. drain
3. rinse with cold water
4. combine orzo , spinach , and next 5 ingredients in a large bowl
5. drain artichokes , reserving marinade
6. coarsely chop artichokes , and add them along with the reserved marinade and 1 / 2 cup of feta cheese to orzo mixture , tossing gently to coat
7. sprinkle each serving with remaining feta cheese
demonstrations.review: This is excellent; very flexible, and unfailingly delicious.  We find it really helps keep the salad fresh-tasting and less greasy if you squeeze almost all of the oil out of the tomatoes with paper towels.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creole black beans and rice

this one of my favorite recipes. it is a crockpot recipe but i'm sure you  could cook it on the stovetop also. it's pretty spicy.  

1. brown sausage in a skillet over med
2. heat
3. drain fat and transfer to crockpot
4. combine remaining ingredients in crockpot
5. cover and cook on low 8 hrs
6. or on high 4 hrs
7. remove bay leaves
8. serve over cooked rice
demonstrations.review: A co-worker of mine has been making this for our office holiday party for years - I love it, but she's retiring, so I'm delighted to see it here for safekeeping.  This recipe is terrific and easy - a crockpot recipe that's not mushy or bland.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry oatmeal muffins

nan

1. heat oven to 400f
2. line 12 medium muffin cups , 2 1 / 2x1 1 / 2 inches , with paper baking cups , or grease bottoms only of muffin cups
3. mix all ingredients except blueberries just until flour is moistened
4. fold in blueberries
5. divide batter evenly among muffin cups
6. bake 20 to 25 minutes or until golden brown
7. immediately remove from pan
8. high altitude : heat oven to 425f
9. decrease brown sugar to 1 / 3 cup
10. bake about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are nice!  Instead of blueberries, we substituted a cup of fruit compote that had been languishing in the freezer, and that worked well - I think this recipe would hold up nicely to other fruit substitutions.

target.recipe_text:
cream cheese poppy seed pound cake

this is a dense delicious flavoursome cake from the better homes and gardens cake book. it is quite filling so i don't bother frosting it and cut thin slices.my dh doesn't like cakes much but he loves this cake. note that it also freezes beautifully.

1. bring butter , cheese and eggs to room temperature before you begin
2. grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan and preheat oven to 160c or 325f
3. combine the flour , baking powder and salt in a bowl and set aside
4. in a large mixing bowl , beat butter and cream cheese until softened
5. gradually add sugar 2 tablespoons at a time beating on medium speed about 5 minutes until very light and fluffy
6. add poppy seeds and vanilla essence
7. add eggs , one at a time , beating on low to medium speed 1 minute after each addition and scraping bowl frequently
8. gradually add flour mixture beating on low speed until just combined
9. pour batter into prepared pan and bake for about 1 1 / 4 hours or until a wooden skewer comes out clean
10. cool in pan on wire rack for 15 minutes and then remove from pan and allow to cool completely before serving
target.review: Have been looking for a pound cake type poppy seed cake for some time.   Most of the recipes seem to have a cake mix as a base and we do not like using those because of all the added preservatives.   This is wonderful and keeps very well without freezing.  Thank you for submitting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange ginger tea loaf

another typical new zealand recipe. a loaf tin for this is 25cm x 11cm.

1. preheat oven to 180c
2. cream together sugar and margarine
3. add eggs , beat till light and fluffy
4. combine dry ingredients in another bowl
5. mix together orange juice and milk
6. add the orange juice mixture alternately with the dry ingredients to the batter , beating till blended
7. fold in orange rind and walnuts
8. bake in a loaf pan about for 45 minutes or until the cake is cooked when tested with a skewer
demonstrations.review: We love this type of bread/cake and this is no exception.   For taste bud reasons we prefer to use butter and also added more orange rind.    Lovely little cutting cake so thank you for a good addition to my files.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked flounder

an easy and delicious way to prepare flounder.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a large baking pan with cooking spray
3. rub the fillets on both sides with lemon juice , then salt and pepper them to taste
4. place the fillets in the baking disk and sprinkle evenly with tarragon
5. cover evenly with sour cream
6. bake for about 15 minutes until fish is done but not over cooked
7. sprinkle with chives and parsley
demonstrations.review: Very simple and tasty way to prepare this fish, i.e. if you like tarragon and it is one of my favorite herbs.    Felt that it needed just a little "something" so topped each piece of fish with a slice of well drained bottled roasted sweet red peppers.     Also gives it some color.    We tend to use a lot of these.   Thanks for a good addition to my files.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raisin cupcakes

these cupcakes are so moist and delicious, perfect with coffee and to guests, i like the adult rum version but orange juice will work fine also :)

1. set oven to 325 degrees f
2. line 16 standard-size muffin cups
3. in a saucepan , bring raisins and rum just to a simmer over medium heat
4. remove from heat
5. in a small bowl combine the flour with baking powder and cinnamon
6. in another bowl beat together butter and sugar until light and fluffy
7. add eggs and vanilla , beat well
8. alternately stir in flour mixture and milk into butter mixture beginning and ending with flour mixture
9. drain raisins and discard soaking liquid , then stir raisins into batter
10. spoon batter into prepared muffin pan filling three-quarters full
11. bake cupcakes about 20 minutes or until lightly browned and cupcakes test done
12. cool then transfer to a rack
demonstrations.review: If I could rate these 10 I would. They are a wonderful adult treat (because of the rum I tend to say they are for adults).  Whatever, they are moist, flavorful and  a treat anytime of the day.  Thanks for submitting and I am sorry that it took me so long to find the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maid of honour squares

a crunchy almond topping,soft cake-like filling and crisp shortbread base are texture sensations for your mouth.

1. base
2. in bowl , beat together butter , sugar and salt until fluffy
3. stir in flour
4. press into parchment-paper lined or greased 13 by 9-inch metal cake pan
5. prick dough with fork
6. bake in center of 350f oven for about 17 minutes until golden
7. let cool on rack
8. in bowl , beat butter with granulated sugar until fluffy
9. beat in eggs , one at a time , beating well after each
10. beat in milk and lemon rind
11. beat in ground almonds
12. stir in flour and salt
13. spread jam over base
14. pour almond mixture over jam
15. sprinkle with slivered almonds
16. bake in center of 350f oven for about 30 minutes or until golden and cake tester inserted in center comes out clean
17. let cool in pan on rack
18. sprinkle with icing sugar
demonstrations.review: Delighted to see this recipe in print because it seems to have disappeared from any books I have had.   Somehow or other I misplaced mine (almost identical) and never could find one like it until now.  Thanks so much for submitting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy microwave chocolate glaze

this makes a wonderful glaze for all kinds of cakes. must use only whipping cream!

1. in a microwave-safe bowl place the chocolate squares , whipping cream and butter
2. microwave on high for 1-2 minutes or until the butter has melted
3. remove and whisk or stir until the chocolate has melted and the mixture is well blended
4. whisk in vanilla until combined
5. let sit at room temperature to thicken more if desired before drizzling on cake
demonstrations.review: Highly recommend this recipe because I have used it for several years.   It is almost failproof and very versatile.     Good over icecream too. Look no further for a quickly made glaze that does not require many ingredients.   Thanks Kittencal......

target.recipe_text:
japanese pumpkin soup  kabocha soup

a lovely pumpkin soup posted in response to a recipe request from an online source.

1. cut pumpkin into large blocks and remove seeds
2. place pumpkin on a plate and heat in microwave for one minute
3. slice pumpkin thinly
4. heat butter in saute pan and cook onion slices until softened
5. add pumpkin slices to the pan and saute
6. add chicken bouillon and water and simmer vegetables until softened
7. when cooked , whirl the vegetables and broth in a blender or food processor until smooth
8. return to the pan and add milk
9. heat the soup over low heat
10. season with salt and pepper to taste
target.review: I just happened to have some kabocha sitting in my fridge from a dish my mother prepared and had no clue what to do with the rest of it. This soup fit the bill. Spooned over some leftover couscous and topped with grilled shrimp. The perfect lunch. I now ask my mom to bring over kabocha from her garden so I have it around to make this soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best orange dreamsicle  cake

if you love the taste of orange cream popsicles you'll love this cake. i made this for a cookout in the summer and there was no leftovers to go back home.

1. set out cool whip to thaw
2. prepare cake mix according to directions for a 9x13 pan ,
3. after the cake is done and you bring out of oven , poke holes throughout the cake with a fork
4. prepare orange jello with 1 cup of boiling water and pour over the cake
5. allow to cool in pan for 30 minutes
6. in a large mixing bowl , mix together with hand mixer instant vanilla pudding with 1 cup milk
7. stir in orange and vanilla extracts , mix well
8. fold in cool whip spread over the cake and chill for 2 to 3 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: I've made this for my DH company get together twice now & he brings home an empty pan everytime! I haven't tried the cake myself, but it smells great & looks soo pretty & it gets tons of rave reviews. Awesome recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu   egg  salad

this is my favorite recipe for sandwiches. the kids love it too!

1. mash the tofu with a fork and add all ingredients together
2. mix until well combined
3. refrigerate
4. it is best if left overnight for the flavors to combine
5. is great served on toasted bread with pickles and lettuce ! enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great starting point! I had a little less than a pound of tofu that I pressed for about an hour to let out the excess moisture. Mashed with my potato masher and just put in a dash of this and a dash of that to achieve the flavor I wanted. Used all of the ingrediants except for the dill. I chopped some vidalia onions and used half mayo & half non-fat plain yogurt and extra sweet pickle relish just cause I love it. Taste great right of the mixing spoon but decided to wait to let the flavors blend. I'm going to attempt to feed this to the DH without telling him what it's made of! I may never have egg salad again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: This meatloaf really is great! My DH liked it & he doesn't care for meatloaf. Served with green bean bundles & a potato casserole. I also made a gravy with the drippings for the potatoes. This meatloaf is very tender with a sweet & tangy sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini tacos

these can be a easy appetizer or a light dinner. i received this recipe in an email from the campbell's site, and after we made these for a tasty dinner, i knew i had to share!

1. cook hamburger until browned
2. drain the fat and stir in taco mix and 1 / 2 cup salsa / picante sauce
3. simmer for 3-5 minutes
4. press wonton wrappers into mini muffin cups
5. spoon beef mixture in cups and top with the 3 tbsp of salsa and cheese , evenly divided
6. bake in preheated 425f oven for 8 minutes , or until the wontons are nicely browned
7. serve with extra salsa , sour cream , olives and guacamole if desired
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Huge hit! I pre-baked the wonton wrappers in the mini muffin tins prior to stuffing them and cooled on a rack to keep them crisp. Topped with sliced olives, chopped grape tomatoes & sliced green onions. I got compliments on how cute and colorful they looked...oh yeah they tasted great too! Thanks ~Bekah~!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kao pad  thai style fried rice

from sundays at moosewood.

1. choose and prepare vegetables
2. select a combination with a variety of colors
3. in a wok , heat the oil and stir fry the ginger and garlic until golden
4. remove them with a slotted spoon and save for later
5. in the same oil , stir-fry the vegetables until just cooked
6. add the harder ones first , and the tender ones last
7. remove the vegetables from the wok and set aside
8. add the rice to the wok and heat thoroughly
9. with your stirring spoon , make a hole in the center of the rice , down to the wok and put in the eggs
10. stir until they are pretty well set before you mix them into the rice
11. the more you cook the eggs before stirring them into the rice , the drier the dish will be
12. add the tomatoes , the reserved ginger and garlic and the stir-fried vegetables
13. finally , mix in the chili sauce , soy sauce and lime juice
14. for serving , top each serving with thin slices of scallions
15. put thin slices of lime on the side
demonstrations.review: Reduced the serving for two and used a short grain brown rice. I also took the other reviewers suggestions and added the tomatoes at the very end. Used a combination of carrots, bell pepper and peas. I added more soy sauce at the end took it off the heat and topped with sliced green onions, cilantro and more lime. This rice went well with Thai marinated pork chops, recipe #30861. A keeper for sure!

target.recipe_text:
mom s best soft gingerbread cookies  new  gb house directions

this is my mom's recipe that just can't be beat. i don't know where the recipe came from, i just know they're good! i like them plain with raisins for decoration, but you can go all-out if you want! have fun and enjoy!!
*i used this recipe to make my gingerbread house, but the directions are slightly different for this. **see bottom of page.

1. place cloves in hot water
2. set aside
3. cream shortening and sugar
4. add egg and beat
5. add molasses , beat
6. remove cloves from water , discard cloves
7. add clove water , beat
8. dough will look "curdled"
9. add rest of ingredients , except the last 4 cups flour , and beat
10. gradually beat in last 4 cups flour
11. chill dough
12. roll out to 1 / 2" thick or slightly less
13. cut into shapes
14. decorate with raisins if desired
15. place carefully on ungreased cookie sheet
16. bake at 375 for 8-10 minutes
17. do not over bake
18. gb house directions:
19. make dough the same as above , but roll dough out thin , 1 / 4" at most
20. bake in 325 oven for about 20 minutes
21. remove to racks to cool , and let harden / dry out a bit overnight for sturdiness if making large pieces
22. doors and windows need to be cut out prior to baking
23. fill any with crushed hard candy before baking , too
24. and pieces filled with hard candy baked the best on foil
25. non candy-filled pieces were baked on parchment paper
target.review: Great recipe, lots of flavor! Although I must have screwed up on the flour somehow (I KNOW I added 5 cups altogether!! lol), it was overly sticky.. So after making a couple of cookies, I decided to add some more flour and let it sit back in the fridge overnight again.. They all turned out good in the end, my whole family LOVES them. (Especially my Mom!) I frosted them with a white buttercream frosting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: LOVED IT!! I used 1 lb of sweet Italian Sausage and 1 lb of Spicy Italian Sausage, tasted awesome! Only thing I didn't add was the crushed red pepper.  This will be my new staple spaghetti sauce recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry chicken with coconut and peanuts

when i was in college, i worked in an asian restaurant. my boss made the best curry i have ever tasted, and after much prodding and bothering the poor man, he finally fessed up! i have worked for years to get the recipe right, and i think this is it! i hope you like it as much as i do.

1. cut chicken into cubes , and sprinkle with salt and pepper
2. slice onion in julienne , and mash garlic
3. in a large wok , , heat oil to just below smoking
4. add garlic and stirfry til golden , and quickly add onions , and stir
5. when the onions begin to soften , add chicken , and stir fry until cooked through and browned a bit--liquid from chicken should all be evaporated
6. add wine and reduce a little , then add peanut butter , boullion , ginger , curry and cilantro
7. stir to coat well , and until peanut butter has melted
8. add water , and simmer about 15 minutes , or until flavors have blended well
9. add coconut milk and heat to just below boiling , then add cornstarch slurry to thicken as desired
10. serve over steamed rice , with chopped cilantro and peanuts to garnish
11. i like it a bit spicy , so i also add chopped chilies , or cayenne to the dish
demonstrations.review: This was a very good curry chicken recipe.  I had a wonderful dish at a restaurant in Port Angeles, WA called Nine Flavor Chicken.. This was almost the same, but not quite.  I'm not sure what is missing exactly, all the same this was pretty good. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flawless sesame chicken  restaurant style

this is the recipe you've been looking for!  it makes a perfect sesame chicken.  this excellent recipe comes out perfect every time with little fuss and inexpensive ingredients you probably have on hand.  this recipe is truly restaurant quality... try it, you won't be disappointed! (recipe courtesy of "reykjaviky" at all recipes)

1. cut the chicken into 1-inch cubes
2. mix the marinade ingredients and marinate the chicken for 20 minutes
3. to prepare the sauce:
4. mix together all of the sauce ingredients
5. pour them into a small pot and bring to a boil , stirring continuously
6. turn the heat down to low and keep warm while you are deep-frying the chicken
7. to deep-fry the chicken:
8. add the marinated chicken pieces a few at a time , and deep-fry until golden brown
9. drain on paper towels and then place chicken in warm oven while you continue frying
10. repeat with the remainder of the chicken
11. just before you are finished deep-frying , bring the sauce back up to a boil
12. place the chicken on a large platter and pour the sauce over
13. sprinkle with sesame seeds
14. serve the sesame chicken with rice
demonstrations.review:
Absolutely wonderful!! I've made this a few times now, and the family loves it! Tonight I decided to make it a little different and cooked the chicken whole, then cut it up into slices afterwards, which worked out great. 

When I mix the marinade, I will usually do half wine and half dry sherry.  And I don't have any chili paste, so I've just used my chili oil, which I think works just as good. I just realized I forgot to write the garlic down, so I've been using this recipe w/out garlic!! lol :) Oh well it still tastes good w/out it! Thanks for the great recipe, the whole family thinks it is even better than getting it at a restaurant.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: Made this for the family last night, even my FIL thought it was really good & he normally doesn't like different things like this. I used whole grain saltine crackers instead of just normal ones, I almost used brown sugar splenda but didn't know if it would leave a funny aftertaste or not, so I opted to not use it. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pesto

this was my daughter's favorite dish (along with some of her friends). she enjoyed it so much that we had to make it a weekly recipe.

1. prepare pesto sauce according to package direction
2. heat oven to 350 degrees
3. spray rectangular dish with no-stick spray
4. moisten chicken with water , shake off excess , and coat complete with bread crumbs
5. place chicken in baking dish
6. spread pesto sauce evenly over chicken breasts
7. cover each breast with slice of provolone cheese
8. spread mushrooms over cheese
9. bake in oven for 45- 50 minutes
10. serve with pasta
demonstrations.review: Chicken Pesto is now one of my favorite new dishes, I will be keeping this one in my favs for dinner.  I made it with homemade alfredo sauce & fettuccini.  I also used a homemade pesto sauce from this site, recipe #13044. Everything was SOOOO GOOD!! Thanks for sharing a favorite! :)

target.recipe_text:
better than sex cake iii

it is my understanding that there are a variety of recipes masquerading under this name, but this is the one that my friends like most.  overnight chilling not included in preparation time.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and lightly flour 13" x 9" cake pan
3. mix cake as directed on package
4. bake the cake about 35 minutes or until it tests done
5. as soon as it comes out of the oven , poke holes all over it with a fork and pour sweetened condensed milk evenly over the cake , followed by caramel sauce
6. refrigerate overnight
7. shortly before serving , spread whipped topping over cake and sprinkle with crushed heath bars
8. enjoy
target.review: This cake is easy to prepare, rich, gooey, and oh sooo good!  I mixed the sweetened condensed milk and caramel together before pouring over cake and this worked out well. Thanks for a great recipe.  It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot round steak

nan

1. combine all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high for 5-6 hours
3. goes well with mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was delicious and so easy!  I omitted the mushrooms as my husband doesn't like them, and added some sliced onions to the soup and dried onion soup mixture.  I browned the meat before I put it in the slow cooker, seasoning with pepper.  I didn't find it bland at all.  As a matter of fact, I didn't salt anything because of the salty taste of the dried onion soup mix.  The meat was very tender and flavorful.  I served it with mashed potatoes and the gravy was excellent.  I'l  make this dish again.  Thanks for posting it, Clairissa!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacardi rum cake

this bacardi rum cake is lovely and moist. i usually make it around new years, makes a nice looking dessert for a buffet and the taste is rich and wonderful. from a magazine add, many years ago.

1. sprinkle nuts over bottom of greased 10 inch tube pan or 12 cup bundt pan
2. stir together cake mix , pudding mix , eggs , water , oil and rum
3. pour batter over nuts
4. bake at 325 in oven for 1 hour
5. cool 10 minutes in pan
6. invert onto serving plate and prick top
7. glaze-----------------
8. melt butter in saucepan
9. stir in water and sugar
10. boil 5 minutes , stirring constantly
11. remove from heat
12. stir in rum
13. brush glaze evenly over top and sides of cake
14. allow cake to absorb glaze
15. repeat until glaze is used up
demonstrations.review: I served this over the holidays and it was a great success!  The rum flavor is wonderful and the nut crunch on top is delicious.  Very easy to prepare.  This will be my only recipe for rum cake from now on.  Thanks Derf!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mary s zucchini bread

this is my mother-in-law's favorite recipe and for very good reason!  this recipe makes two very moist and flavorful loaves.  i hope you will enjoy it!

1. place eggs , oil , zucchini and vanilla extract in blender and puree
2. sift together sugar , flour , baking soda , salt and baking powder and cinnamon
3. pour liquid ingredients into dry and mix
4. add nuts
5. divide batter into two loaf pans
6. bake at 325f degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This bread turned out beautifully.  It rose nicely in the loaf pans and it was very moist.  I usually have trouble with zucchini bread getting done in the center, but this recipe was right on.  Nice in the center and not burnt on the outside.  This is my "keeper" recipe for zucchini bread.  Thanks Bev!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican rice casserole

a great way to use a pound of ground beef and make a dinner that all will love.  it's so easy too!  if you cannot find mexicorn by green giant, you can use a regular can of corn or frozen corn.  to control the heat of the dish, you can choose mild, medium or hot salsa!

1. place the 2 cups of water and long grain rice in a medium sauce pan and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to a simmer , place a lid on , set timer for 20 minutes and cook rice until done
3. preheat oven to 350f
4. in a skillet , brown ground beef and drain
5. place in a large mixing bowl
6. in large mixing bowl , add the jar of salsa to the ground beef
7. also add chili powder , mexicorn , rice and salt
8. mix with a wooden spoon until combined well
9. spray a 2 quart casserole dish
10. put rice mixture into dish
11. cover with a lid or foil and bake in preheated oven for 30 minutes
12. at 30 minutes , take off lid / foil
13. add shredded cheddar cheese evenly over top and bake for an additional 5 minutes
14. remove from oven and serve
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something different to do with hamburger, as I get tired of the "same old menu".  I tried this and loved it.  I used Minute Rice and frozen corn.  I also stirred some of the cheese in the casserole, in addition to putting it on top.  I served it with a salad and corn bread.  Hubby liked it too.  I will make this again.  Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast with pears  brie  and cinnamon

a delicious twist on french toast that can be made-ahead and chilled for up to 24 hours. great for brunch, holidays, and special occasions.

1. grease a 9x13 baking dish
2. set aside
3. in a large skillet cook pears , brown sugar , and rosemary in 2 t butter over medium heat for 4-5 mins or until pears are tender
4. arrange 7 or 8 bread slices in a single layer in prepared dish
5. spoon pear mixture and arrange brie on bread slices
6. top each stack with a bread slice
7. brush bread with melted butter
8. combine sugar and cinnamon
9. sprinkle evenly over bread
10. in a medium bowl whisk together milk , eggs , vanilla , and salt
11. slowly pour over bread slices
12. cover and chill for 1-24 hours
13. preheat oven to 375f bake , uncovered , for 40-45 mins or until edges are puffed and golden
14. let stand for 10 minutes
15. serve warm with maple syrup , berries , and honey , or cranberry conserve
demonstrations.review: I made this for guests over the holidays and it was a hit!  I made it exactly as submitted.  The pears and rosemary are a great combination.  The leftovers heated up nicely the next day in the microwave.  Some guests suggested syrup with the leftovers and that tasted great too.  Thanks for an awesome recipe!

target.recipe_text:
broccoli salad with apricots

this is another recipe that my sister and i came up with for our home study group.  the tartness of the dressing and the sweetness of the fruit make a wonderful combination.  we found, for us anyway, that by adding a little miracle whip to the dressing we could cut down on the amount of sugar.

1. dressing:
2. mix together the vinegar , mayo , miracle whip and sugar and mix well
3. combine the remaining ingredients except nuts and bacon bits and mix with the dressing
4. mix in the bacon bits and pecans just before serving
5. chill before serving for about 30 minutes
6. fell free to add additional fruit to taste
target.review: Great salad!!!  Made during ZWT3 when I was dying for something crunchy and green...this fit in with a picnic-themed supper perfectly.  I am not familiar with "Miracle Whip" and to be honest have thought it WAS just a type of mayo until now (oops..I'm bad) -  I used a bit of honey sweetened low-fat plain yogurt instead and liked the results just fine!!!  I will make the effort to check out what "Miracle Whip" is about for the next time and there will most definitely be a next time!!  I loved the tender sweet tart of the apricot and raisins with the crunch of the onion and toasted nuts.  I also loved the fake bacon soy crisps with their touch of salt and the way that flavor played with the sweet and tart.  Not a big mayo eater, but I really liked this...it was just a nice light touch that did not "mask" the great natural flavors at all...I skipped additional sweetener because I had already used that bit of honey - I thought it was the perfect balance of flavors!!! Thanks ~Nimz~!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caf de olla  sweet cinnamon coffee

found for the world tour 2005, this looks like something dh would love!  a mexican recipe, it has been called ' "funeral coffee" because it is always served at the velorios - all-night wakes - with large trays of sweet rolls.'

1. bring the water to a boil
2. add the coffee , cinnamon and sugar , and continue boiling for 30 seconds
3. stir and strain into hot mugs
demonstrations.review: This is a great, easy coffee recipe...works wonders for me because we are "between" coffee makers and this makes a nice rich brew without the equipment.  I use more coffee (about 5 teaspoons)and usually more cinnamon, and less sugar ( I think it works well adjusting it to personal taste)...because of the sweetness of this blend I am able to drink it black...even iced - ( I'm usually a cream user!!!)  Wonderful for after dinner...a dessert all by itself!  Discovered during ZWT3 and now a keeper for constant use!!!  Thank you Elmotoo!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal souffle with crunchy topping

this is a wonderful way to get your oatmeal for the day. it has a wonderful brown sugar topping that adds a nice crunch.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray four 5-oz souffle molds , custard cups or ovenproof bowls with nonstick cooking spray
3. place in 15x10x1 inch baking pan
4. in a small saucepan bring the milk and butter just to a boil
5. gradually add oats while stirring constantly
6. reduce the heat to medium-low
7. cook 1 to 2 minutes or until oats thickened , stirring often
8. remove from heat
9. pour the oat mixture into a large bowl
10. add sugar , salt , cinnamon , sour cream and 1 egg yolk
11. stir until smooth
12. add dried fruit and set aside
13. in a medium bowl beat all 3 egg whites until stiff but not dry
14. gently fold egg whites into oat mixture using a rubber scraper
15. do not overmix
16. small lumps of egg white will remain
17. gently spoon the mixture into molds
18. sprinkle the tops with brown sugar
19. place in preheated oven and bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until souffles are puffy and a knife inserted in center comes out with a few moist crumbs
20. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at souffle and I was quite pleased with the results!!  I love my oatmeal so I thought this would be a perfect starter for me.  I found this while playing ZWT3 and enjoyed it during my "visit" to France!!  I used dates and worried about it being overly sweet so went easy with my brown sugar crust - I wish I had been a bit more heavy handed with that...not so much a taste issue - the sweetness was perfect - but my cup tops did not look as pretty as PaulaG's picture.  I thought this was wonderful...like a bowl of creamy milk and cookies - sooo yummy!!!  I am more comfortable about souffles now...I think I had a fear of them "falling" or something (??) but there is nothing to fear here!!! - The instruction is right on!  Thanks for sharing this!!  This is a winner recipe!!!  ***** 5 stars and MORE PLEASE!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot blush

this recipe is courtesy of hallelujah acres. the beet gives it a nice sweetness. great healing juice!

1. scrub organic carrots or peel the carrots if they are not organic
2. clean and cut beet into slender wedges , and wash and dry lettuce and spinach leaves
3. juice half of the carrots
4. add the beet
5. you may use the remaining carrots to help push the lettuce and spinach through the juicer
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: An exceptional juice recipe!!  Thank you so much Sharon123 for sharing this.  I juice quite regularly, but have never followed a recipe and I was thrilled with this outcome.  I was so happy to see someone else using a beet and carrot combo.  I use the beet, carrot and romaine and mix it up with either spinach or cabbage (or as RitaL suggested the beet greens work nicely as well!!)  The beet really makes this rock!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
live garden burger  raw foods

from sergei and valya boutenko's eating without heating: favorite recipes from teens who love raw food. they say about it: "you can make nori rolls, cabbage wraps, spread it on crackers, stuff mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, and more."  i have adapted it to fit in my little oscar food processor.

1. grind the nuts in a food processor
2. add the rest of the ingredients and grind it up or put the rest of the ingredients in a "champion juicer with the blank plate in" and then combine with the ground nuts
3. form into balls , cutlets , or fillets and sprinkle with a little paprika before serving
4. if the mixture is not firm enough , add one or more of the following: dill weed , dried garlic , dried onion , dried parley , nutritional yeast , psyllium husk powder , or ground flaxseeds
demonstrations.review: I LOVE this recipe...I wish I could even rate it more stars...it is off the charts good and good for the body and the soul :)...what I find most delightful about "LIVE FOOD" recipes is their versatility...their "chameleon-like", ever changing, ever evolving quality...every time you revisit a "live" recipe will be a slightly different experience...it is not so much of making something as it is creating it...experiencing it; and the experience of creating and experiencing it  :) :) :) {{lol}}...I tagged this for the Healthy Choices game and this particular time used the suggested walnuts, with "black nannas: (super ripe and frozen), extra nutritional yeast, some ground flax (I was after "extra body" because I wanted to form pretty solid little "meatballs" (for lack of a better word :) {{lol}} in addition to the "poultry seasoning" I added some chili powder...and a mix of chopped garlic and pineapple (a chutney type thingy if you will)...I got a dozen tasty little bites that were served up all sorts of ways all week at lunch and dinner... (they had a staring role with recipe#170557 in a weekend raw vegan feast !!)~~~Wonderful, just wonderful~~~ :)I can not wait to start my next batch and my next after that and so on and see what happens again and again...Thanks miliss, YOU ROCK!!!  This is a staple recipe must for a veg. head diet and should be kept on hand for a GO TO treat at all times!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy new york deli coleslaw

you may sustitute celery seeds for the caraway seeds if you like. adapted from the america's test kitchen family cookbook, that i just got for my birthday!

1. toss the cabbage with 1 teaspoons salt and let sit in a colander for at least 1 hour or up to 4 hours
2. meanwhile , toast the caraway seeds in a small skillet over medium heat until fragrant , about 3 minutes
3. rinse the cabbage and pat dry with paper towels
4. whisk the toasted caraway seeds , mayonnaise , vinegar , mustard , sugar , and 1 / 4 teaspoons pepper together in a large bowl
5. add the cabbage , carrots , and onion and toss
6. chill for at least 1 hour before serving
7. season with salt and pepper to taste
8. enjoy !
9. the coleslaw can be prepared , covered and chilled a day in advance
10. before serving , freshen the salad with a spoon of mayonnaise and a dash of vinegar
11. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Delish!!-I made sort of 1/2 batch...had about 8 cups of all green cabbage...so used the eyeballs to grate carrot and onion with "microplane" zester...used a homemade vegan-mayo-ishy with all the rest of the suggested mix-ins, including the fabulous caraway seeds (LOVE-YUM! )...I made it to go with mr. free-free's left-over corned beef from St Patrick's Day :) and as a prelude for a batch of ;)cultured cabbage;) I am working on...(the first hour is the same prep)- HUGE HIT!! :) Thanks again Sharon!

target.recipe_text:
chucumber  indian cucumber salad

this salad comes from north india and tastes excellent served with beer as a first course. i have also eaten it as a packed lunch. a lovely combo of flavours and textures. the original recipe calls for unroasted and unsalted peanuts, but i find the roasted, salted and esily available peanuts work great and that's what i use. omit or reduce the chillies if desired. recipe source is a book i borrowed from the library. the book is written in german but has been previously published in english with the title 'food of india'.

1. mix red onion , cucumber , tomatoes , cilantro , chilli , lemon juice , oil , pepper and chaat masala in a bowl and mix well
2. this could be done some hours in advance as the flavours will improve
3. just before serving , add the chopped peanuts and taste if extra salt is necessary
target.review: Delicious and tasty!!  I had no chillies except dried, but it still came out beautifully.  I used garam masala also as I did not have chaat.  Highly recommend this one as an alternative to a plain salad!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin streusel muffins

another great pumpkin muffin recipe. made these last night--ooh baby!!

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and the sugars
2. add the next 5 ingredients
3. stir to mix well
4. mix together the dry ingredients
5. gradually add the dry ingredients to the creamed mixture and stir just until combined
6. fill greased or paper line muffin cups two-thirds full with batter
7. for streusel topping: mix together the flour and brown sugar
8. cut in the margarine with a pastry blender until resembles coarse meal
9. sprinkle evenly over each cupcake batter
10. bake at 375 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until tests done
11. cool in pan for 5 minutes , then remove to a wire rack
demonstrations.review: These are almost perfect imo - or perfect if you don't like your muffins too sweet!  They rise beautifully, they look stunning, but they were not sweet enough for me and I couldn't taste the orange.  Next time I'll use more sugar and double the orange.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
demonstrations.review: Can't speak, mouth too full!  These are the such delicious muffins, took them to class today and everyone raved about what a good cook I am, hah!  I added walnuts and cardamom for my own twist, next time I'll add more apple too.  Thankyou so much for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
socca  provencal savory chickpea pancake    gluten free

soccas are a garbanzo flour pizza-like flatbread from the southeastern france. it is naturally and traditionally gluten-free and easy to make. they can be served with any kind of topping... try it with kalamata tapenade ("recipe #156988"), ratatouille, or sauteed vegetables and herbs. the best one i've ever had was topped with carmelized onions, black olives and anchovies. adapted from a recipe by mark bittman of the new york times. gluten-free - dairy-free - kosher: pareve. this recipe makes 1 large socca pancake, the diameter of a 10" cast iron pan. when sliced into quarters, it should serve 2 people as a main dish or 4 people as an appetizer.

1. place heavy skillet in oven and preheat to 450
2. in a large bowl , sift chickpea flour , pepper and salt together
3. after sifting , add rosemary leaves
4. whisk in warm water and 2 tbsp olive oil
5. cover the bowl and allow the batter set for at least 30 minutes , which should have the consistency of thick cream
6. stir sliced onion into the batter
7. remove skillet from oven
8. add 1 tbsp olive oil to the hot pan , pour batter into pan and bake for 12-15 minutes or until the pancake is firm and the edges are set
9. set socca a few inches below your broiler for 1-2 minutes , just long enough to brown it in spots
10. cut into wedges and serve hot , with toppings of your choice
demonstrations.review: Fantastic recipe - I wanted to try this after having it in a restaurant - this recipe came out even better! I only had coarse chickpea flour and the result was lovely and rustic, and I used herbs de Provence as I had no rosemary. Scattered it with roast cherry tomatoes, and arugula leaves - c'est bon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpea curry  garbanzos

with a picture! a delicious, easy, stovetop vegetarian indian curry that makes a yummy lunch! based on a recipe i got from mrcurrys.com with a sample of their wonderful curry seasoning powder.

1. saute onions in olive oil for 3 minutes
2. add ginger , garlic and curry powder , stir and cook for another minute or so
3. add chickpeas and salt and a tablespoon or so of water
4. cook and stir about a minute
5. add tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes , stirring gently
6. add another spoonful of water if it seems dry or if it's burning or sticking
7. serve with flatbread and rice
demonstrations.review: Quick, tasty, filling, and cheap - what more could I ask!  This is a great recipe, I used 2.5 tsp of curry powder, a little spicy for me but if I had some yogurt handy it would be fine.  I was hunting for something to make with the very few ingredients I had and this fit the bill perfectly - thanks Sarafish!  I also mashed the chickpeas (it's a personal preference, I just dont like them whole) till there were only a few whole ones left, and used dried onions because I'm out of fresh.  Personal preference aside - this dish is just perfect as is!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini cake

top this with cream cheese frosting for a special treat.

1. mix dry ingredients
2. combine oil and eggs with vanilla
3. add to dry ingredients , mix well
4. add zucchini , stir until combined well
5. fold in walnuts
6. place in greased 13x9 baking pan
7. bake at 350 for 40 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Perfect zucchini cake recipe!  I used self raising flour (plus a quarter of a teaspoon of baking powder to counteract the densifying properties vegetable oil).  I also added the zest of 1 orange - it came out beautifully.  Many thanks for this one!

target.recipe_text:
bacon crescent roll appetizers

this is a toh favorite.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix cream cheese , bacon , parmesan cheese , onion , parsley and milk until well blended
3. set aside
4. separate each can of dough into 4 rectangles
5. firmly press perforations together to seal
6. spread each rectangle with 2 rounded t
7. of the cream cheese mixture
8. cut each rectangle into 12 wedges , starting at short ends
9. place , seam down on greased baking sheet
10. bake 12-15 minutes or until golden brown
11. serve warm
target.review: These are great and fairly easy to make. I recently found the crescent dinner roll dough without the perforations, so that troublesome step of pressing the perforations together (which doesn't always work very well) can be eliminated. I have tried various sizes, and the smaller the better so the dough can cook through. Also, the cream cheese needs to be spread evenly over all the dough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked sweet potatoes

nan

1. layer potatoes , brown sugar and margarine in a casserole
2. sprinkle with cinnamon
3. bake uncovered at 375 degrees for 30 minutes
