demonstrations.review: Finally, a sweet potato recipe that doesn't require cooking the liquid before hand. Last time I tried that it came out like hard candy. This way is fool-proof and so much easier. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german creamed spinach

my oma's recipe from the old country. great for people who hate spinach.

1. wash spinach and steam together with onion for 5 to 10 minutes
2. finely chop cooked spinach and onion together with the garlic and place in a medium pot
3. combine flour and oil and and heat in a small sauce pan until golden brown
4. combine flour mixture with spinach stirring until evenly blended
5. add milk to spinach stirring to combine with flour mixture
6. bring to a boil over medium heat , then reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes or until spinach thickens
7. salt to taste
8. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I also made a couple of tweaks, but the taste was great. I had always been afraid to cook spinach, but this was very good. I sauteed 1/2 and onion and 1 clove of garlic in oil before adding the flour. Then had to add 1 cup of milk, then added the steamed, chopped spinach. I don't think it needs to simmer for 1/2 hour either, since the spinach is already cooked. Thanks for sharing it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous mini meatloaves fiesta style

food & family fall 2005 issue.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix meat , stuffing mix , water and chili powder together
3. spray a 12 cup muffin tin with cooking spray and press meat mixture into each cup
4. make a well in the center of each cup and spoon the salsa evenly into each of the twelve cups
5. bake 30 minutes or until meatloaves are cooked through
6. top with the cheese and return back to the oven until melted , about 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Great dish for a quick weekday meal. These are so easy to fix and taste great. I like to change it up with the BBQ version: substitute 1 tsp. garlic powder for the chili powder, 3/4 cup BBQ sauce for the salsa, and cheddar cheese instead of Mexican blend. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
large batch baked meatballs

makes a large batch, perfect for freezing.  i have used mixed ground meats in this recipe: italian sausage, veal, pork, lamb or a bit of everything...what ever i have in the freezer.  always start off with half ground beef.

1. combine bread and milk in a small bowl
2. let soak for 10 minutes
3. squeeze bread to release milk
4. discard milk
5. combine rest of ingredients , shaping into small balls and placing on roasting tray sprayed with pam
6. bake in 350 oven for 20 - 30 minutes , depending on size of meatball
7. remove from oven and tilt tray to drain fat
8. let meatballs cool before packaging
9. freeze up to one month
demonstrations.review: These are great, I have made them several time, but neglected to review them, shame on me! I only use 1/4 cup of milk and don't squeeze it out. I also add 1 Tbsp. onion powder, take the garlic powder down to 1 Tbsp. and reduced the salt/pepper. Thanks for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double coated chicken

i got this recipe off a box of kellogg's corn flakes.

1. place corn flakes in shallow dish or pan
2. set aside
3. in small mixing bowl , beat egg and milk slightly
4. add flour , salt and pepper
5. mix until smooth
6. dip chicken in batter
7. coat with cereal
8. place in single layer , in foil-lined shallow baking pan
9. drizzle with margarine
10. bake at 350 for 1 hour or until chicken is tender , no longer pink and juices run clear
11. do not cover pan or turn chicken while baking
demonstrations.review: We liked how crunchy this came out - maybe too crunchy - I might crush the flakes in the food processor next time (7 cups made more than 1 3/4 cups crushed). My son thought is was a little bland, so I might add some poultry seasoning too. Otherwise, a good find for changing up the same old chicken. Thanks! Made for Spring 2010 Pick A Chef. You've been adopted!

target.recipe_text:
frito pie in the bag

great for outdoor events, easy for kids!

1. slice bags of chips open along one side
2. spoon chili con queso over chips
3. top with lettuce , tomato , onion or pico de gallo
4. enjoy !
target.review: This was a favorite of my mother's when she was a child as well...  Mom used to take me to a local drive-in where we would both get Frito Pies.  Yum! Yum!  I'm really glad to find this recipe posted and hope lots of people try it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
popeye s fried chicken copycat

this recipe started very similarly todd wilbur's copycat, so food.com changed the name to his. however, with the help of some great commenters, with the help of others have modified this recipe to where it has nothing to do with his anymore. special thanks to navarro and elainerivhaywood- this recipe works best in a dutch oven or a deep fryer for that crunch everybody wants. also make sure the chicken and batter are cold for better adhesion.

1. mix all ingredients except the oil , flour , paprika , and eggs & milk , marinate overnight in an airtight container
2. in a large bowl , combine flour , salt , peppers , and paprika
3. break the eggs into a separate bowl and beat until blended slowly adding the milk
4. dip each piece of chicken into the egg and milk mixture , then coat generously with the flour
5. once the chicken is coated , place on a rack to allow the pieces to dry , 20 to 30 minutes
6. allowing the pieces to dry will provide for more even browning of the chicken
7. to fry , heat oil in dutch oven or deep fryer to medium
8. place the chicken pieces in the oil , skin side down , one piece at a time
9. leave enough space between pieces so that they are not crowded
10. this allows the pieces to cook and brown more evenly
11. continue to cook over a medium heat , turning until all sides are golden brown and the meat is cooked thoroughly
12. when the pieces finish cooking , they should be removed and placed on a paper towel to allow grease to drain
demonstrations.review:
Luvvv me some Popeye's Chicken... so I HAD to try this recipe.  I wasn't disappointed!  It was extremely easy.  
I used peanut oil instead of vegetable oil, but otherwise I followed the recipe exactly.  
It definitely did have that Popeye's flavor, although it wasn't as intense a flavor as Popeye's.  Perhaps this is attributed to their fryers getting hotter? I dunno.  What I DO know is this:  I'm not easily impressed with fried chicken recipes, but this one is gonna be MY new recipe!  
The chicken came out beautiful, juicy, and had a great tasting crust that was comparable to Popeye's.
Fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best cookies aka that 70s elusive cornflake cookies

this wonderful recipe was in circulation when i was a kid in the 70s. years later, a woman brought a tray of these to the office, which i instantly recognized as those cookies from my childhood, and she refused to give me the recipe (said it was her babysitter's secret recipe)! i searched online (tried several recipes) and asked my friends and family off and on if they'd heard of it, for 10 years. i finally just found this online! they are so good! bake them for your friends and family and share the recipe with the world! note, the number of cookies you get will vary - depending on how big you roll the balls.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. cream butter , sugars , vanilla and egg
3. add oil
4. mix in dry ingredients
5. form dough into walnut sized balls
6. place on cookie sheet and flatten with a fork dipped in water
7. bake for 10- 12 minutes
8. cool on pan for a minute or two , then transfer to a rack to cook
demonstrations.review: I substituted with Special K cereal instead of corn flakes, because it's what I had on hand.  Everyone gobbled these up very quickly.  They reminded me and a few other ppl very much of the pecan sandie cookie that is sold in stores.  I'm hanging on to this recipe and will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
miss daisy s deviled eggs

these are the best deviled eggs i have ever tried. i usually have to double this recipe because they are gone almost as soon as i put them out.

1. cut eggs in half lengthwise , remove yolks , and reserve whites
2. mash yolks until smooth
3. combine yolks , mayo , worcestershire sauce , mustard , salt , pepper , and mix until smooth
4. stir in onion , and pickle relish
5. spoon mixture into center of egg whites
6. sprinkle tops with paprika
demonstrations.review: These do not last long at my house.  My mother was visiting and raved over them as well, stating they were the best she ever had!  I agree.  The addition of the green onions is critical... really sets these delicious gems apart from the rest.  Will make deviled eggs this way forever.  Thanks for the recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
our secret sirloin steak

great steak--mmmm.

1. combine 1 / 4 cup of the lea& perrins , lemon juice , oil , minced onion , salt and minced garlic
2. mix well and set aside
3. place steak in tight-fitting bowl or plastic bag
4. pour lea& perrins mixture over steak
5. marinate 2 hours
6. remove steak from marinade
7. place on rack
8. grill over hot charcoal or broil under preheated hot broiler for 7 to 10 minutes on each side or until done as desired , brushing occasionally with leftover marinade
9. remove steak to serving plate
10. in a small saucepan melt butter
11. stir in parsley and remaining 1 teaspoon lea& perrins
12. pour over steak
13. slice and serve
demonstrations.review:
This is the first time I can say that I cooked a delicious steak at home without grilling it outside on a grill.  The flavor of this steak is no joke!  

I cut the marinating time down to 1 hr because of time constraints, and I cooked the steaks for about 5 minutes total on a George Foreman grill, after scraping off the excess onion and garlic marinade.  Delicious, juicy, and barely pink in the middle!  YUM!!

Thank you for a fabulous steak recipe that I'll be using many times again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach   mushroom pasta

love mushrooms, love pasta, love spinach. need i say more?

1. in large non-stick pan over med-high heat , cook garlic , onion& thyme in oil for about a minute
2. add mushrooms , cook about 8 minutes , stirring often , until the mushrooms begin to brown& their juices begin to run
3. sprinkle with flour& stir about one minute , then slowly begin to add the milk , and bring to the boil , stirring constantly for about 3 minutes , or until the sauce thickens
4. stir in the spinach , basil , salt& pepper& cook until the spinach begins to wilt
5. toss sauce with cooked pasta& grate fresh parmesan cheese over individual servings
demonstrations.review:
Oh, yea.  This one's a winner.  
I made this recipe with the following modifications:
After sauteeing the onions and garlic, I added the mushrooms for a few mins, then tossed in a couple splashes of balsamic vinegar into the pool.  I used a cup of cream and a cup of milk instead of just milk.  I'm serving this over egg noodles with crusty french bread and roasted asparagus.  I've already been sampling the spinach mushroom sauce along the way, and can't wait to eat!  Yum!!!

target.recipe_text:
lemony lima beans with parmesan

this is a great side dish that is easy to prepare.

1. bring a large saucepan of salted water to a boil
2. add lima beans and cook
3. stirring occasionally , until tender , about 4 minutes
4. drain , rinse with cold water , then drain again , and pat dry with paper towels
5. transfer lima beans to a bowl
6. stir in oil , lemon zest and lemon juice
7. season with salt and pepper
8. divide among four serving plates and sprinkle with parmesan
target.review: Wonderful, fast recipe.  I didn't even think I liked Lima beans.  My husband even tried them thinking he was going to hate them...I am making them for the 4th time tonight.  My whole family loves them!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braided sweet bread

this recipe comes from my best friend's aunt. it is a wonderful, chewy sweet bread that i can't keep my hands off of whenever i make it! just a great, simple sweet bread recipe.

1. mix together water , warm milk , and yeast
2. add melted margarine , sugar , salt and flour
3. knead dough , place in bowl , cover and let rise in warm place 1 hour
4. divide dough into 6 parts
5. shape dough into 6 long pieces
6. on baking sheet , braid 3 of the pieces together like you would hair , then braid remaining 3 pieces together
7. cover and let raise 1 more hour
8. brush beaten egg on top and bake at 350 degrees for 30-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and easy recipe.  I have made this three times now and each time I get better at braiding!  I do a four strand braid (I think it looks prettier).  Though, this tastes so good out of the oven that the taste pales when it's been out of the oven for more than a couple of hours.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy bananas foster

classic new orleans dessert, made simple for the folks at home. the alcohol is optional.

1. melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat
2. add sliced bananas and stir for 2 minutes
3. add brown sugar , vanilla , cinnamon , and salt
4. lower heat and continue cooking , stirring constantly for 2 more minutes
5. serve over a scoops of ice cream
demonstrations.review: Great recipe.  I added the bananas last, and they were still a little overdone, but they were full yellow, not any green.  Next time I'll try bananas not so ripe.  I used rum, and flamed it on purpose.  Oh and CAUTION, the rum flames up high!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat oatmeal pumpkin spice muffins

this is a recipe i adapted from an old favorite, applesauce muffins.   they are high in fibre and low in fat.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. oil or spray muffin tins with cooking spray
3. sift together the dry ingredients
4. add the rest of the ingredients and stir until just moistened
5. divide into 12 muffins and bake for 15-20 minutes until cooked in centre
6. remove from pan after 5-10 minutes and let cool
7. place in a airtight container and try not to eat for 24 hours as they will become more moist
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I took them out at 20 minutes and let cool, and the centers were still gooey.  I put them back in the (cooled off) oven and baked for another 15 minutes.  Not sure what went wrong.  I have an oven thermometer so it wasn't the temp...But they still turned out delicious!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple collard greens

this is my own recipe. this is what i think all collard greens should taste like. the fresher the collards used the more tender and quick cooking they'll be. if they are "elderly" as my great-grandmother would say, you will have to cook them longer as they will be tougher. wonderful with bbq tempeh, mac & cheese and corn bread.

1. heat butter or oil in a large skillet over medium-high
2. add onions
3. while onions are cooking wash collards leaving them damp
4. after about 5 minutes when onions are lightly browned add collards and cover pan with a lid
5. after about 5 minutes add maple syrup , bbw sauce , a pinch of salt and a few dashes of pepper
6. mix together and cook covered over medium for about 10-15 minutes or until greens are tender
demonstrations.review: I added a splash of cider vinegar at the end as was suggested in the reviews and that kicked it up for me, also I added an extra teaspoon or so of maple syrup at the end.  My greens took an extra 5 minutes to cook fully.  Great recipe, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
demonstrations.review: Absolutely moist and wonderful, and EASY!  The batter is VERY thin, thanks for noting that or I would have been concerned!  :) I used 3/4t salt and IMO could have used 1/2t, it's a tiny bit salty.  I also had to bake this cake for an extra 10 minutes.  But, um, YUM!  To die for.  Thanks for posting this recipe!  Oh yes, the cake FILLED my 9x13 pan to the brim.

target.recipe_text:
kalamata lemon chicken

this is a very good mediterranean style chicken dish that i love (lemon lover here). you just brown the chicken for a few mins and add the rest of the ingredients and place it in the oven while you go about making a salad (or whatever).

1. preheat oven to 400 degree f
2. in a 4-quart dutch oven brown chicken in hot oil over medium-high heat for 5 minutes , turning once
3. stir in orzo , olives , the can of broth , lemon wedges , lemon juice , greek seasoning , 1 / 4 teaspoon salt , and 1 / 4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
4. cover and bake for 35 minutes or until chicken is tender and no longer pink
5. serve in shallow bowls with additional broth , if desired
6. top with snipped oregano
target.review: This was very good, and I am sure I will make it again.  I used bone in thighs and I think that was a good choice, they were falling off the bone tender.  I loved the tangy flavor that the olives and lemons provided, but next time, I will include even more.  The lemon wedges were a little bitter, so next time I will remove them before serving, but I would like even more lemon flavor.  Maybe adding more lemon juice would do it.  Thanks for posting!  Made for ZWT9

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and black bean quesadilla

i recently attended a lowfat, high fiber cooking class at the hospital and this was one of the wonderful recipes we made.

1. in a large bowl , stir together all ingredients except tortillas and spray
2. spread about 1 / 4 cup of filling on half of each tortilla and fold in half
3. spray both sides of each tortilla with cooking spray
4. place on a non-stick skillet and brown on each side until filling is heated or bake on a baking sheet for 10-15 minutes at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: What a delicious and easy lunch!  I cut the recipe down to two servings and substituted jalepenos for the green chilis, and it was great. I loved the black beans in it, and it was so easy to make it in the oven.  I flipped it over once and it came out nice and crispy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon mocha coffee from taste of home

using fresh brewed coffee and cocoa powder - not a syrup.  from taste of home cooking school notes.

1. in a coffeemaker basket - using a filter - combine the coffee grounds and ground cinnamon
2. prepare 4 cups of coffee as directed on your coffee maker directions
3. as coffee is brewing , in a medium saucepan , combine the milk , sugar , cocoa and vanilla and cook over medium-low heat , stirring occasionally , for 5-7 minutes - do not boil
4. pour the hot milk mixture into four coffee cups / mugs , then add the cinnamon brewed coffee
5. optional , garnish with cinnamon sticks and a dollop of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: Wow!  This is delicious!  You can't go wrong with coffee and chocolate in my book, but it is the cinnamon that takes it over the top in this one!  I had it warm with brunch today, and it was smooth and spicy and perfect.  I have a little saved that I am chilling, and I will try it cold over ice tomorrow.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian marinated flank steak

i originally got the idea for this out of sunset magazine, and have tweaked it to suit my family and friends.  it makes a great oamc entree for the grill, or to take camping.  i've used this on chicken and salmon as well as beef, just reducing the marinating time appropriately.  don't use ground (dry) ginger in this- the flavor is not the same.

1. place all ingredients except for steak in a gallon size zip top bag , and mix well to combine
2. add steak to bag , remove all of the air , and seal
3. marinate for up to 24 hours , turning bag occasionally
4. remove meat from marinade , and grill or broil to desired degree of doneness
5. thinly slice steak against the grain and serve
6. to oamc , freeze bag for up to 6 months , and pull from freezer at least 24 hours before using
7. you can substitute garlic for the ginger
8. if you like it spicy , add more chili flakes !
demonstrations.review: This was good but probably not my favorite marinade for grilled steak.  My steak was a little on the thin side, and I did marinade for a little over 24 hours, but the ginger flavor was a little strong for my taste and it was a bit salty.  I think it would be a good marinade for a stir fry perhaps, but next time I will use less ginger and soy and marinade for a shorter amount of time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tropical baked bananas

from epicurious, nothing melts in the mouth like baked bananas. served with any kind of cream topping or ice cream, it is a simple, unsurpassed dessert. adjust the ingredients and flavors to your personal taste.

1. preheat the oven to 400f peel the bananas and slice in half lengthwise
2. lay the pieces into a buttered 9x13x2-inch ovenproof dish
3. pour the lime juice and rum evenly over the bananas
4. sprinkle on the cinnamon , nutmeg , and brown sugar
5. dot on the butter , if using , and bake for 10 to 15 minutes
6. serve hot , topped with a tablespoon of fresh cream or ice cream
demonstrations.review: Oh wow!  This was really good!  It is kind of like a spicy Banana Foster, but different.  Lime is one of my favorite flavors and it was a great addition here.  I had it with ice cream and a sprinkle of coconut.  Made for ZWT9

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry milk finland

in finland, they eat lots of berries, blueberries being one of their favorites. i have made this vegan by using non dairy milk, but in finland they use fresh cow's milk.  adapted from gimme some oven.

1. in a small saucepan , heat blueberries , sugar and water over medium high heat until boiling
2. reduce heat to medium-low , and let simmer for 10-15 minutes to reduce until it is thickens slightly and makes a syrup
3. remove from heat and strain through a fine-mesh strainer if desired
4. refrigerate
5. whisk together 1 / 4 cup blueberry syrup with 1 cup cold milk to serve
6. this recipe will also work with strawberries , blackberries , lingonberries , and cherries
demonstrations.review: It is at the beginning of our wild blueberry season in Alaska, and they were so good in this!  This reminded me of the flavored milk powder that comes in a can, but a million times better! I used regular 2% fat cows milk this time, but I'll bet this would be delicious with almond milk!  I would like to try the syrup on waffles too!

target.recipe_text:
blueberry filling for pies

you will never have soggy crusts again if you make your pie like this. you can make this and freeze it for using later. update: i just finished doing it in the microwave, so much easier than standing over a pot stirring. it took about 15 minutes, stirring after the first 5 min and every couple minutes until thick and clear looking. i added the cornstarch mixture after the first 5 minutes. 

1. in a heavy saucepan mix together blueberries , sugar and lemon juice
2. over medium heat bring to boil , stirring frequently
3. mix cornstarch with water to make a paste
4. pour into berry mixture , stirring constantly until thick
5. remove from heat and let cool
6. you can now freeze it or use for pie
7. bake at 400f for about 35 minutes
target.review:
Oh My Goodness, I've died and gone to blueberry heaven! I made this (#100281) and WAS going to use it in a pie and WAS going to use it to top a cheesecake BUT it never made it to the cool stage.... while I was making it I noticed my lemon ice cream was just not melting fast enough and .....is there nothing better than warm blueberry topping on frozen lemon ice cream? I think not. And yes, I have a sweet tooth and ...... let me stop and eat my ice cream..... 
Thank you!!!!!
Life is good to meeeeeee.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy blue  bleu  cheese dressing

this recipe (adapted from the joy of cooking) is one of my favorite blue cheese dressing recipes.

1. process all ingredients except blue cheese in food processor until smooth
2. empty ingredients into bowl and mix in blue cheese
3. taste and adjust seasonings
4. cover and refrigerate
demonstrations.review: I've never rated this one because this is the one that's identical to the one in my head minus the tabasco and load up on the blue cheese. Love blue cheese. So, that said, this is the only way I make blue cheese dressing, it is good on salad and my favorite--- PIZZA. Also try it with those pretzel chips from Sams club or Cosco, they're heavy duty enough. Thank you bobo for putting this in print!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot and cracker salad

this recipe originally hails from a 1977 cookbook called 

1. mix the first five ingredients together
2. add enough mayonnaise to achieve the consistency you desire
3. add seasoning to taste
4. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
Oh my goodness,I grew up with a version of this and had never seen it in print till now! 
The family version:
1 pkg saltines
3 boiled eggs
1 lb. carrots
run through meat grinder, ad 1 pint miracle whip.
a carrot lovers dream :)
thanks! As a kid I'd always get stuck grinding :(

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted kielbasa   potatoes

another recipe from mom. these are good and easy to throw together.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. pour into a 9x13" baking pan
4. cook in oven , covered with foil for approximately 1 hour
5. you can stir after 1 / 2 hour of cooking
demonstrations.review:
It is a keeper and a recipe that goes in the "I like trying new recipes but I'm ready for a dinner I KNOW will be GOOD" file!!!! 
It's so simple that it ruins the chase of preperation,measuring,timing and hoping it'll turn out okay. As my outspoken hubby would say "That was pretty good". Holy cow, he can talk?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab meat casserole

this is so good and smells wonderful while it is baking! i got it from a virginia country cookbook. its a great company dish that can be prepared several hours in advance.

1. mix first 8 ingrdients in a bowl
2. spray a 9x13 baking dish with non stick cooking spray
3. pour crab mixture into baking dish
4. combine eggs and milk and pour over mixture in dish
5. sprinkle cheese over top
6. bake at 350 degrees for approximately 1 hour
demonstrations.review:
OMG. I love the crabmeat casserole I get on the buffet at my favorite chinese resteraunt so I thought I'd try your recipe (sounded close). Wow, Bingo, we have a winner!
I also WAS going to take a pic and post it, but I ate it. Yes, I ate it all. Sorry, maybe next time...
Very simple, and boy is it GOOOOOOD! I didn't have real crab so I had to use my imatation, OMG is this Goooooood.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean roast chicken thighs

not sure where i found this recipe, but make it monthly for my family. i have used vegetable oil in place of the sesame oil and it still tastes great.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place chicken skin side down in a large baking dish
3. combine the remaining ingredients in a bowl and then pour on top of the chicken
4. bake uncovered for 45 minutes
5. turn the chicken over in the dish and bake for another 15 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Boy I follow directions like a 5 year old before Christmas....
First I was out of soy, so I used teriyaki(it says soy on the ingredients:) then I used regular onions then I (think) tripled the garlic. And out of black pepper. And OMG it is to die for.I made bbq chicken alongside just in case and this dish was devoured! 
One more thing, when it was done I drained the juice and added a little cornstarch for thickness then poured it on for dramatic affect.....as their eyes widened like saucers....mmmmmmmm
Thank you Petunia!!!!

target.recipe_text:
easy chiles rellenos

we have an awesome authentic mexican restaurant in our little midwestern town.  i fell in love with their chilies rellenos, and this is the closest i come to duplicating it.  (it can also be made with red enchilada sauce for an entirely different flavor.  can sizes are approximate)i serve these with shirleen mccorkle's refried bean recipe and they go wonderfully together!

1. blanch poblano peppers for 5 minutes in boiling water
2. meanwhile , brown ground beef , drain and return to the pan
3. add tomatos and enchilada sauce to pan and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat and simmer while preparing the peppers
5. remove pepper from water and remove the tops and seeds
6. cut the pepper into four similar sized pieces
7. lay pepper slices in a greased baking dish
8. place a spoonful of sauce over each pepper , then top with a spoonful of cheese
9. bake 35 minutes at 350 degrees or until cheese is browned
10. allow remaining sauce to simmer on the stove-top and serve with completed peppers
target.review: A quick and easy to put toghter. I roasted the chilies on the barbee,they were the easiest peppers that I have peeled ever. I think I will use this method from now on. The next time I make this I am going to put some diced onions in it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: As usual a 5 star icing. I haven't made icing in years, this was very easy and very good tasting. This is the very best chocolate icing that I have eaten ever. I don't like chocolate and hardly ever eat it, but this may change my attitude toward chocolate. My wife thought it was the best chocolate icing she has ever eaten.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic and cracked pepper rib eye steaks

nan

1. mix the first six ingredients together in a ziplock bag and add the steaks
2. put in the refrigerator at least two hours to marinate
3. put them on the grill and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: there was too much worcestershire sause for me. I didn't think it was possible to ruin a good steak excipet by over cooking, but this came close. i followed the recipe to the letter. this was not for my tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
glazed corned beef brisket   veggies

boiled corn beef always good, but this simple addition of a tasty glaze makes it even better. this whole "meal in one" is not that complicated, and can be cooking all at the same time easily. no fuss, and a simple clean-up!

1. slow boil corn beef brisket about 3 hours or until fork tender along with spices that come normally packaged with the corn beef
2. remove the cooked brisket and place it in a shallow baking dish lined with tin foil , fatty side up
3. score the fatty side of the corn beef
4. in a small bowl mix all the glaze ingredients together and spread on the scored brisket
5. bake in hot oven 400 degrees approx 45 minutes or until the glaze bubbling has almost stopped
6. in the mean time get a head start on the veggies
7. the cabbage and carrots cooked in slow boiling water until firm tender
8. the potato's and onions are placed on a cookie sheet lined with tin foil
9. bake potato's and onions in hot oven 400 degrees 35 minutes , or until potatos and onions are fork tender
10. season potato's and onions with kosher salt or seasoning salt and pepper while hot
11. butter the hot cabbage and carrots if you wish
12. suggestion
13. arranged on a large platter with all the veggies surrounding the hot sliced corn beef , this always looks so appetizing-- enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I have tried this twice. the roast veges wtih the corned beef were great, but the second time i made it icut the amount of cloves in half. more suited to my taste. i love corned beef this is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef   corn your own

the traditional irish dish - just in time for st. paddy's day! this requires 48-60 hours curing time in your fridge, but you get great-tasting corned beef in the end.

1. trim all but inch of fat from meat
2. wash and pat dry
3. rub with cup salt
4. in large saucepan , heat water , salt and sugar and stir to dissolve
5. place beef in large glass bowl and pour salted water over
6. add 2 bay leaves , 8 peppercorns , 2 tsps pickling spice and 2 garlic cloves
7. place weighted plate over so meat is completely immersed
8. refrigerate 48-60 hours
9. remove meat and rinse thoroughly
10. place in large saucepan and cover with boiling water
11. add remaining bay leaves , peppercorns , pickling spice and garlic
12. cover and simmer for 4 hours , or until meat is tender
13. serve hot with boiled potatoes and cabbage or cool the brisket and slice thinly to serve with rye bread and mustard
demonstrations.review: This is a very good corned beef recipe. However when I went to school 60 hours was 2.5 days not 5 days, so this was about right time to brine the brisket. It is better than most corned beef that you can buy ay wally world or most stores. thanks for the recipe Evelyn

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
demonstrations.review: I used this for a base for my volcano cakes. It has worked the best for my volcano cakes for my parties. Every one that has eaten them think it is the best they have ever eaten. Also it makes a great chocolate cake. Pared with Kittencal's Really Easy Chocolate Buttercream Icing makes it over the top.

target.recipe_text:
chow gai laan  jade green broccoli

adapted from a chinese cookbook by jim lee that was published around 1970. this is one of my all-time favorite cookbooks; i was introduced to it by friends who were chinese students i knew at university of virginia. the gai laan which the chinese eat is not actually broccoli, but broccoli is a good substitute which works well in america, where most of us don't have access to gai laan.

1. mix together sugar through soy sauce plus 1 / 2 cup water and put aside
2. heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium heat and add the garlic
3. when garlic is golden brown , add the broccoli
4. turn the heat up and stir-fry 2 minutes
5. add sherry , cover quickly and cook 2 minutes
6. lift cover& add the soy sauce mixture
7. when sauce thickens , remove and serve
target.review: Loved the flavor !!! Only thing I did different was to use rice vinegar instead of rice wine. Turned out great. I served this with Sesame Chicken recipe #44321. I will be making this again. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic  shrimp angel hair

easy and quick to prepare.  this is from all recipes.

1. cook the pasta according to the package directions
2. meanwhile , in a large saucepan , melt 4 1 / 2 tsp butter over medium heat
3. stir in flour until smooth
4. gradually add cream
5. bring to a boil
6. cook and stir for 2 minutes or until thickened
7. stir in the grated parmesan cheese , pesto sauce , 1 t garlic , worcestershire sauce , hot pepper sauce , salt , and pepper
8. keep warm over low heat
9. in a large skillet , saute broccoli in remaining butter for 5 minutes
10. add shrimp and remaining garlic
11. cook and stir until shrimp turn pink
12. stir in the cream sauce
13. drain pasta
14. add to shrimp mixture and toss to coat
demonstrations.review:
The good:   Very tasty and impressive dish. I made it exactly as stated.  My husband loved it.

The bad:  It's not exactly heart healthy. Full of fat and Cholesterol.

The ugly:  What my kitchen looked like after I made it.

If I make this again, I will use low fat ingredients.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted potatoes and green beans

this recipe is an adaption of a recipe found in williams-sonoma essentials of healthful cooking. the roasting blends the flavors and produces a delightful side dish.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. spray a 13 x 9 inch casserole with non-stick cooking spray and set aside
3. brush mushrooms clean and trim the ends of the stems
4. cut the mushrooms in half through the stem
5. cut potatoes into 1-inch pieces
6. cut the onion into wedges approximately 1 / 2 inch thick
7. seperate the garlic into cloves and peel
8. trim ends from green beans , wash and break into 1-inch lengths
9. set green beans aside
10. in prepared casserole , combine the mushrooms , potatoes , garlic and onion
11. drizzle with olive oil , tossing to coat evenly
12. roast vegetables until they begin to brown on the edges , about 30 minutes
13. add the broken green beans to casserole dish and carefully turn and rearrange vegetables in an even layer
14. sprinkle with 1 / 4 teaspoon salt and a few grinds of pepper
15. return to oven and continue to roast until the vegetables are browned and tender when pierced with a knife , about 15 minutes longer
16. sprinkle the grated parmigiano-reggiano and thyme over the vegetables
17. return to oven and cook for 5 minutes longer to melt the cheese
demonstrations.review: I've made this twice.  First time I used carrots, since my beans were past their prime.  It was great with the carrots.  Second time I used beans, which took forever to cook and became kinda dry.  Next time I think I will parboil the beans before roasting. Love the roasted garlic.  I will be making this again.  Thank You.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: Easy and Delicious !!! I used 1/2 cup half and half,  sauteed onions & 1 minced clove of garlic before hand.  <br/><br/>For the sauce 1/2 cup ketchp with 2 tablespoons O & Co Balsamic vinegar.   (If you like balsamic vinegar, this is absoulutely the best ever.  $32 a bottle, but worth every dime) This really added to the flavor of a great basic recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pomegranate glazed cornish game hens

i have not tryed this yet. but i will. pomegranates are a great souce of vitiamin c and potassium. sure sounds good hope you all will like it. i got this recipe out of the sunday newpaper in the coupons.

1. preheat oven to 375 deress season game hens with salt , pepper and thyme cook on rack for 1 hr
2. or until done
3. brush pomegranate glaze on hens
4. roast another 5 mins
5. sprinkle with fresh pomegranat arils
6. serve wigth remaining glaze as a sauce
7. pomegranate glaze to juice pomegranate slice in half crosswise and use a citrus juicer
8. in stainless stell sauce pan simmer juice with a pinch of salt until reduced to a syrupy glaze about 10 mins
demonstrations.review: This was soooooo good and easy. I used pomegranate juice, not concentrate, so used 1 cup and reduced.  So easy to eat.  Only problem is I wish I had made 3 birds instead of 2 for my DH and myself, and I'm not a big eater !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked balsamic chicken

love balsamic vinegar, hope you enjoy this chicken. note; i have found that it's better with boneless, skinless  chicken breast or  boneless, skinless thighs. baking time may be less due to size.

1. preheat oven 400 degrees
2. arrange the chicken bone side down in a 9-by-13 inch glass or ceramic baking dish
3. pour the vinegar over them and sprinkle evenly with the oil , oregano , salt and pepper
4. bake the chicken 20 minutes and baste with the vinegar juices
5. bake 20 minutes more or until juices run clear
6. serve chicken with juices spooned over them
demonstrations.review: Great chicken, DH and I both loved it. I cooked 6 chicken drumsticks, bone in, added whole peeled garlic cloves, and small whole red potatoes. I sprinkled a smaller amount of oregano, so it would't overpower the dish. I turned over the chicken after 20 minutes. Wow, easy and fit for company. I used premium Premium Balsamic vinegar from O & Company (Oliviers), it's syrupy. with and tart and sweet flavor, the juices turned into a glaze. Next time I will add some sliced onions. Fantastic !!!!!

target.recipe_text:
sweet curry chickpea casserole

this is an adaptation of dreena burton's recipe from vive le vegan.  it is fantastic, especially served over jasmine rice.  you can either bake it or put it in the slow cooker.  it keeps very well in the refrigerator--i think it tastes best a day or two after it is cooked. alternatively, you can make sweet curry chickpea bisque by adding two cups of water and pureeing most of the mixture with a hand blender after cooking (adjust salt and spices to taste).

1. mix all of the ingredients into a casserole dish
2. cover
3. bake , covered , for 60-70 minutes at 375 degrees , stirring occasionally
4. alternative: slow cook for 6 hours on low instead of baking
5. alternative: add two cups of water
6. simmer , covered , for 30 minutes instead of baking
7. puree 3 / 4 of mixture with a hand blender and serve as a bisque
target.review: I don't give out many 5s, but I LOVED this!  It had this mysterious tang to it that was just perfect.  I am guessing because I used Granny Smith apples.  I used more like 1 cup coconut milk and 3/4 cups water, because I love coconut milk!  I also used more sweet potatoes.  It was a 12 oz precut bag, so maybe more like 2.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
live garden burger  raw foods

from sergei and valya boutenko's eating without heating: favorite recipes from teens who love raw food. they say about it: "you can make nori rolls, cabbage wraps, spread it on crackers, stuff mushrooms, peppers, tomatoes, onions, cucumbers, and more."  i have adapted it to fit in my little oscar food processor.

1. grind the nuts in a food processor
2. add the rest of the ingredients and grind it up or put the rest of the ingredients in a "champion juicer with the blank plate in" and then combine with the ground nuts
3. form into balls , cutlets , or fillets and sprinkle with a little paprika before serving
4. if the mixture is not firm enough , add one or more of the following: dill weed , dried garlic , dried onion , dried parley , nutritional yeast , psyllium husk powder , or ground flaxseeds
demonstrations.review: I thought these were great!  I was glad for the Old Bay rec, because I thought they were just perfect that way.  I also used a full TB of raisins as I thought a little sweet boost sounded good tonight.  :)  They definitely weren't a burger in the sense that you could pick it up, but it did form together.  I am fairly new to raw foods, so thinking even if I added something, it wouldn't have gotten much firmer, but I may experiment in the future!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw brownies

i found this recipe online and really wanted to try it. it comes from a website called 28 cooks. you may substitute the dates and cherries for other dried fruits. the cooking time is freezing time.

1. process all ingredients in a food processor or blender
2. press into a small square baking pan and freeze for 1 hour
3. slice brownies into 12 pieces
4. store in fridge
demonstrations.review: I made these tonight, and they are great!  I wasn't sure as walnuts are my least favorite nut, but I guess ground up they worked for me.  I processed them a bit before adding the other ingredients, but still ended up with some chunky pieces, so I am going to try to do it even more next time.  Also, based on the other reviews, I only used 2 TB of honey, and that seemed fine!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw cashew cheesecake from vegetarian times magazine

this rich, dairy free, no bake cheesecake is flavored with agave nectar, a raw sweetener derived from the agave plant. agave nectar is sweeter than honey with a milder, more floral taste—ideal for desserts or drinks.

1. place macadamia nuts in large bowl , and cover with cold water
2. place cashews in separate bowl , and cover with cold water
3. soak nuts 4 hours , then rinse , drain , and set aside
4. pulse macadamia nuts and dates in food processor to a sticky crumb-like consistency
5. sprinkle dried coconut on bottom of 8-inch pie pan
6. press macadamia nut mixture onto coconut to make crust
7. place cashews , coconut oil , lime juice , agave nectar , and 6 tbs
8. water in bowl of food processor
9. scrape seeds from vanilla bean into food processor bowl , and pure until smooth
10. pour mixture onto crust , and freeze 1 to 2 hours , or until firm
11. remove from freezer , slice while frozen , and transfer to serving platter
12. defrost in fridge 1 hour , or on countertop 30 minutes
13. top with berries
14. and serve
demonstrations.review: Giving this 5 stars based on the texture and how well it held together.  But I used raw honey instead of agave, so I can't officially rate the taste it would have had.  The flavors of coconut and honey were great together.  But I don't think it was anything like an actual cheesecake, at least flavorwise.  But it was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw spaghetti with marinara sauce

another raw main dish from my friend.

1. process sweet potatoes or zucchini through a fine vegetable shredder so it looks like angel hair pasta
2. for sauce
3. combine all ingredients in a blender and process until smooth and creamy
4. add a little of the sun dried tomato soak water if needed
demonstrations.review: I thought this was pretty good, but not great.  My main complaint is that the sauce was really watery.  Maybe seeding the tomatoes would help.  It also makes a TON of sauce, so when they say large on the sweet potato or zuke, they ain't kidding!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw cauliflower korma

i found this recipe on goneraw.com written by katyuk. i have changed it a bit to my tastes but is raw and awesome!

1. to make the base: chop cauliflower into small pieces , add raisins and mix
2. set aside
3. to make sauce: put all remaining ingredients in a blender and mix at a high speed until combined and sauce-like add more water if required
4. to serve: pour sauce over cauliflower and eat ! the curry sauce is so good !
demonstrations.review: This is my favorite raw dish I have made so far!  I went ahead and used a full head of cauliflower because I needed to use it up, and it seemed like plenty of sauce.  I also added some unsweetened coconut flakes.

target.recipe_text:
andes crme de menthe cookies   andes mint cookies

i found this recipe on the back of andes crème de menthe baking chips. i made a few small changes and am really pleased with the results! these cookies taste very similar to the girl scouts thin mint cookies!

1. preheat oven to 350f do not do this until after dough has been refrigerated
2. blend butter , brown sugar , white granulated sugar , baking soda , baking powder , vanilla and eggs until ingredients are mixed
3. add andes baking chips and mix
4. add flour and continue to mix until all ingredients are well blended together
5. cover and chill in the refrigerator for 45-60 minutes
6. spoon out approximately 1 oz of dough per cookie
7. form a ball and then slightly flatten
8. place on non-stick baking pans and bake for approximately 8-10 minutes
9. cool on pans for 2 minutes , then remove
target.review: There was nothing wrong with the recipe, I just didn't care for the flavor. They were not at all sweet, and very very minty. I couldn't taste any chocolate. If you want a not sweet, minty cookie, then these are for you. Thanks anyway!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shredded chicken and walnut sauce

this is from a penzey's cooking magazine.  i think i'll be trying it very soon!

1. in a large pan , simmer the chicken with water and 1 / 2 tsp salt until cooked , 20-50 minutes , depending on whether it is bone in or not
2. strain through cheesecloth or a fine strainer and set chicken aside to cool
3. boil the water stock down until you have 1 1 / 2 cups
4. remove the cooled chicken from the bones while the stock is reducing and chop into 1-inch pieces
5. in a food processor or blender , blend the walnuts , onions and cooled , reduced stock
6. break the bread into chunks and add to the blender , along with 1 / 2 tsp paprika , 1 tsp salt and the pepper
7. blend to a smooth paste
8. put the chicken pieces in a bowl , pour the walnut paste over , and toss gently to combine
9. garnish with the remaining paprika and sliced black olives
10. particularly nice served with fresh fruit
demonstrations.review:
This was good. It definately has sort of a baby shower/tea room brunch kind of taste. I added a little minced garlic and toasted the walnuts first for more flavor.
While I cooked some noodles to pour this over, I got out the pita chips and dipped into it. I think it would make a lovely dip with maybe some melted feta over the top. I agree with a previous reviewer that this recipe has a lot of possibilities.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bagel bites  oamc

great to keep on hand for a quick snack!
for extra kick add jalepenos or other hot peppers to the mix.

1. lay bagels on large cookie sheet
2. combine remaining ingredients and mix well
3. top each 1 / 2 of the bagel with about 2-3 tbsp of mixture
4. flash freeze on cookie sheet for about 3 hours or until topping on bagels is firm
5. transfer to large freezer bag , label and freeze
6. to serve: bake from frozen at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until heated through and cheese melts
demonstrations.review: These are amazing! I cooked the meat and taco seasoning along with some minced onion, cooled it, and added the cheese, and peppers.These froze so well. I actually forgot the salsa, and they were still amazing. Thanks, I will be definately be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vermicelli soup  sopa de fideos

this is a mexican version of the old-fashioned chicken noodle soup.

1. heat oil in large saucepan over medium heat , add pasta
2. cook stirring constantly for 3-4 minutes or until it begins to brown
3. stir in broth , water and salsa , bring to boil
4. reduce heat to medium and cook for 10-15 minutes or until pasta is tender
5. add chicken , cook for 2-3 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was delicious. I didn't expect a lot, since there were so few ingredients. I cooked mine in the crockpot, and used bone- in chicken...removing it and shredding the chicken. I added some salt. Wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden garlic alfredo sauce

this recipe is posted by request and was found on the net-no name attached.

1. in a medium to large saucepan melt the butter over medium heat
2. add the cream cheese and whisk to smooth and melted
3. whisk in the heavy cream
4. season with the garlic powder , salt and pepper
5. bring to a good simmer and whisk frequently until sauce thickens , around 25 minutes
6. remove from heat and stir in cheese
7. taste and adjust seasoning's
demonstrations.review: What's not to love? If you want a fattening fest this is the recipe for you! It was delicious, and like most of the reviewers we stepped up the cream cheese a lot. ( we added half a block). It still has that authentic taste, but was a LOT creamier than other alfredo's I have tried or made.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best ham sandwiches ever

this recipe was given to me by my mom and i made them the first time for a football party.  everyone liked them so much that i ended up making more that day.  now they are what i have to take everywhere.  they are wonderful, easy to make, and are loved by everyone.  you can't go wrong!

1. you will need two 9 x 13 pans
2. place the bottoms of 12 rolls in each pan
3. place ham on the rolls
4. cut the cheese slices into 4 parts and place 2 small pieces on each sandwich
5. put the dinner roll tops on
6. in a sauce pan , mix butter , dijon mustard , worcestershire sauce , and dried onions
7. wait until all butter is melted and then pour the melted mixture over the ham sandwiches
8. sprinkle the buns with poppy seeds and cover with foil
9. let refrigerate overnight
10. preheat oven to 350 and uncover sandwiches
11. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes and serve
12. they are great hot and even at room temperature enjoy !
13. i have made these with turkey also and they are good
14. not as great as the ham , but they are good
demonstrations.review: Lordy, these are good. I cut the recipe in half for dinner for our family of four. ( along with a salad). I had to leave the poppy seeds out, because they were almost five dollars for a tiny container, but otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. YUM. I could eat twenty of these!

target.recipe_text:
brownie truffles

what could be a more romantic way to end a dinner than with truffles. i came across this quote recently-
"the truffle is not exactly an aphrodisiac, but it tends to make women more tender and men more likeable." -  by french gastronome brillat-savarin

1. preheat the oven to 350f butter an 8x16-inch pan
2. make the coating by combining the 1 cup sugar , the powdered coffee , and the cocoa
3. set aside
4. in a heavy saucepan , or the microwave , melt the chocolate and butter together
5. beat the eggs until they are light and then gradually beat in the 2 cups sugar
6. stir in the chocolate mixture
7. gradually add the flour , salt , and vanilla
8. this mixture is not meant to be light and fluffy , just fully incorporated
9. pour the mixture into the prepared pan and bake 25 minutes
10. the brownies will be slightly underdone and very moist
11. allow to cool in the pan
12. when cool enough to handle , cut the brownies into 1x1-inch squares
13. roll each square in the palms of your hands into balls about 1 inch in diameter
14. roll the balls in the coating mixture
15. pack in tins or plastic containers with wax paper between the layers and store in the refrigerator for up to a week
16. or place them in a single layer on a cookie sheet in the freezer until frozen , pack in containers , and store in the freezer up to 4 months
target.review:
These are DELICIOUS.
The only issue I have with them are the edges. You've really gotta crush them well, in order for them to ball up nicely, whereas the more central squares, were overly moist. Tasty nonetheless.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
intensely chocolate cocoa brownies

a rich brownie that is mixed in a sauce pan on the stove. easy, dense and soooooo good!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. melt butter in sauce pan
3. when melted remove from heat
4. add cocoa and stir well
5. add sugar , eggs and vanilla
6. mix until shiny and smooth
7. add flour , baking powder and salt
8. mix well
9. add choc chips or walnuts if desired
10. pour into an 8 inch or 9 inch pan
11. bake for 15-20 miutes
12. do not over bake
13. look for edges slightly pulling away from pan
14. cool and cut
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I didnt bother with the saucepan. I just microwaved the butter, and added the remaining ingredients. Used a 9 inch pan, but once I poured in the mixture it looked too thin... so I doubled it :D. These made the most amazingly dense brownies. mmmmm... I added a couple tablespoons of instant coffee mix, and sprinkled some white chocolate chips in. They're wonderfully fragrant. This recipe is a KEEPER.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portuguese coconut custard tarts    pastis de coco

this rich little dessert is a cross between a custard and a macaroon.

adapted from david leite, leitesculinaria.com

1. preheat the oven to 375f
2. adjust the rack to middle position
3. line a 12-cup muffin tin with 10 paper cupcake liners
4. dissolve the cornstarch in 1 / 4 cup of the milk
5. set aside
6. in a food processor fitted with a metal blade chop the coconut flakes for 30 seconds , or chop well by hand
7. in a large mixing bowl , stir the eggs and sugar together with a wooden spoon
8. one by one , add the cornstarch mixture , remaining milk , coconut , melted butter and lemon and other extract , stirring well after each addition
9. ladle the custard into the paper cups , filling to 1 / 4 inch from the top
10. bake for 25 to 30 minutes or until the coconut is nicely toasted
11. cool completely in the tin before serving
demonstrations.review: These are pretty delicious. The only issue I have with them is: they rose really beautifully (and i expected them to sink, of course) but they sunk in quite considerably. :/ Not pretty at all. But tasty nonetheless, a little on the sweet side. Goes well with hot tea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bok choy stir fry

this is a wonderful side dish for an asian style entree. bok choy has a wonderful, crisp texture that is reminiscent of celery. you can easily add shrimp or chicken to make a main dish, but i recommend doubling the sauce if you do so. simple and yummy:)

1. heat oil in saucepan over medium heat
2. add garlic , ginger , black pepper , and bok choy
3. stir fry about 3 min
4. in bowl , combine dissolved boullion and water , soy sauce , sugar , and cornstarch
5. whisk well
6. add cornstarch mixture to skillet and stir fry until sauce thickens and cabbage is tender , about 3 min
7. serve hot
demonstrations.review: I'd love to give this a higher rating, but it was way sweeter than I had anticipated. I enjoyed the flavor combination, but found there was a bit too much sauce. Next time I'd definitely add double the bok choy, hopefully thatd even things out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
demonstrations.review:
these are so amazing!
i made my first batch without the addition of nutmeg, and i was a bit worried about the baking soda-ee taste, but by the next day (when they were served) i proclaimed them my favorite cookie of all time. even my grandmother agrees that they are to die for.
my next 2 batches i added in about a teaspoon or so of nutmeg as i saw others had, and that really fixed the baking soda problem, making them scrumptious out of the oven, but they werent exactly "to die for," the next day like my first batch was.
im sticking to the original recipe from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baking powder biscuits  drop type

i get this recipe from my pillsbury family cookbook that was published in 1963. it was my mothers, a graduation present i believe, and i refer to it on a regular basis for the classic preparation of many foods.

1. sift flour salt and baking powder into mixing bowl
2. cut in shortening until the particles are fine
3. add milk all at once and stir just until dough clings together and flour disappears
4. drop by spoonfulls into greased muffin cups
5. bake 450 deg for 12 / 15 min
demonstrations.review: I felt like theses had too much of a baking powder taste to them. They were pretty tasty and all, even then, but that taste just kind of lingered. I would recommend adding some sort of herb to it. Nonetheless, it was super simple, and the result is a beautiful biscuit. Thanks for this recipe, it's a good basic for sure.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate cheesecake chunks

if you love cheesecke and chocolate, you'll love these.  i include these in my christmas cookie tray and everyone loves them.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. melt butter in 9-inch square baking pan
3. stir in crumbs and 1 / 2 cup nuts
4. press to cover bottom of pan
5. in a small bowl , beat cream cheese , sugar , cocoa , egg , and vanilla at medium speed until smooth
6. pour over crust and sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup nuts
7. bake 20 minutes
8. let stand at room temperature 2 hours
9. cut into 1-inch squares with a sharp knife
10. store covered , in refrigerator
11. these cookies are best presentted in a single layer
target.review: Wow! These are just fantastic. Chocolate and cheesecake how can you go wrong? But seriously, these were incredibly easy to whip up and decadent to eat. I'm so going to have these on my cookie tray for Christmas this year. Thanks Viviane for a delicious dessert! Made this for Spring PAC 2008.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
please eat your veggies   soup

this soup is the perfect remedy for those fussy eaters who refuse to eat their vegetables, yet will eat all sorts of vegetables when served in soup. this recipe was created for the rsc #14 cooking contest.

1. in a 4-quart pot or dutch oven add peanut oil
2. saute sliced sweet onions on medium low heat until tender , stirring frequently
3. then toss in the mushrooms and saute them for about 5 minutes stirring frequently
4. add garlic and green onions
5. saute for an additional minute
6. add vegetable stock , carrots , napa cabbage , wax beans , soy sauce , dill , sesame oil , worcestershire sauce and rosemary
7. bring to a boil and then drop the temperature down to simmer , cover and cook for 60 minutes
8. salt & pepper to taste
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: We liked this soup, but just felt that it needed something. I added a bit more worcestershire too. I think this is a great base to add things to, like more veggies, pasta maybe. Thanks for creating this and good luck!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai red chicken curry

this is a recipe i got from my sister years ago and i still make it on a regular basis.  it is the most delicious red curry that i have tasted.  i hope you like it too!
i usually serve it in a bowl on top of steamed white rice and it goes together great. enjoy...

1. saute` onion and curry paste in a medium pan
2. add chicken in batches and cook over medium heat until browned
3. add stock and potatoes
4. simmer covered for 20 minutes
5. stir in remaining ingredients
6. simmer uncovered for 5 minutes and serve
demonstrations.review: This was a delicious curry! The coconut milk and the basil paste were great in it. Everyone loved this for dinner tonight. I wasn't sure what size can of potatoes to use so I ended up using 2  15 oz. cans drained, and that worked great. Made for Fall PAC 2008, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichoke  spinach   sun dried tomato dip

update: my recipe was just published in the taste of home holidays & celebrations 2011 cookbook.  
tangy & creamy, this artichoke dip boasts the colorful addition of sun-dried tomatoes. serve with plain or multi-grain baked tortilla chips.  developed for ready set cook #11 - january 2008
update 2/27/2013:  thanks to racrgal for a really productive conversation regarding making this recipe in advance.  that led me to run a series of tests.  *i made four versions and found that it can be made a day in advance and refrigerated before baking, or made months in advance; frozen and then thawed before baking.  both oil-packed and dry-packed sun-dried tomatoes were tested to make sure the oil did not cause bleeding during thawing.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 2 quart baking dish with cooking spray
3. in large bowl combine cream cheese , mayonnaise , shallots & garlic
4. stir in artichoke hearts , spinach , tomatoes & cheese
5. at this point you can wrap the baking dish in saran wrap and refrigerate overnight , or wrap in 2 layers of aluminum foil and freeze for 2 months
6. when ready to serve , remove from fridge or freezer and thaw on counter before baking as directed
7. bake uncovered for 25-30 minutes , or until the cheese that sticks out the top of the mixture begins to brown slightly
8. serve with fresh vegetables or baked tortilla chips for dipping
demonstrations.review: This dip was just amazing, yum! It was creamy and delicious, and the sun dried tomatoes were a great twist on the restaurant version. We served this with tortilla chips and veggies, and it was loved by everyone. Definitely making this again, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate brownie cupcakes

from 125 best cupcakes recipes.

1. preheat oven to 325f and use muffin pan lined with paper liners
2. in a small bowl , mix together flour , cocoa powder , baking powder and salt
3. in a large bowl , whisk together granulated and brown sugars and butter until smooth
4. whisk in vanilla and almond extract
5. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
6. add flour mixture , beating until combined
7. stir in chocolate chips
8. scoop batter into prepared pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 28 minutes or until a tester inserted into center comes out with a few crumbs attached and a little melted chocolate
10. the tops of cupcakes will not spring back when touched
11. let cool in pan on rack for 10 minutes
12. remove from pan and let cool completely on rack
13. top cooled cupcakes with favorite frosting
demonstrations.review: YUM! These cupcakes were soooo good! Fudgey and delicious in their own right and loved the hint of almond extract. Then I frosted them with peanut butter cream cheese frosting, heavenly! Thanks for sharing :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german restaurant steak

i went with my parents to dinner at a german club restaurant called the maennerchor, in columbus, ohio.  i was in my teens and everything on the menu looked totally strange to me at that age.  i found a steak on the menu, don't remember what they called it, and decided to order that, despite the fact that i didn't like steak.  well am i glad i ordered this steak because i loved it and this is the only way i eat steak to this day.  this is my copy of this restaurants dish.

1. season steak with salt , pepper and seasoned salt to taste
2. in a large skillet , melt butter and add sliced onion
3. cook on medium low heat , cook until onions become tender and lightly browned
4. about 10 minutes
5. meanwhile , cook steak on the grill until it reaches your desired liking
6. add sourcream to the onions and stir to combine
7. pour the mixture over the top of the grilled steak
8. variation: you could add mushrooms with onions during the saute
9. this restaurant did not to my recollection , but that would also be yummy
demonstrations.review: This dish turned out really delicious from very simple ingredients. My whole family loved this steak and the yummy sauce was a perfect compliment. Thanks for sharing this! Made for ZWT 6 Queens of Quisine.

target.recipe_text:
double the streusel coffee cake

this coffee cake really packs a wallop of extra streusel flavor! a family favorite.
easy to double recipe for a 9x13" pan.

1. in a large bowl , sift together the flour , baking powder and salt
2. add the sugar
3. blend the 1 / 4 cup oil into the flour and sugar mixture until it is like cornmeal texture
4. in another bowl , combine the egg , milk and vanilla
5. add to the flour mixture
6. stir only enough to mix
7. pour 1 / 2 mixture in a greased 8" pan
8. combine the streusel ingredients , and sprinkle 1 / 2 of the streusel on the cake batter
9. add remaining batter on top , and sprinkle with the other 1 / 2 streusel
10. bake in a 350 degree oven for 25 minutes
11. you may drizzle with a thin powdered sugar icing , if desired
target.review: Loved that it was small, quick & easy.  But, we found it way, way too sweet.  I used 1/2 whole wheat pastry flour & 1/2 white flour.  If I made it again, I'd probably use half the amount of streusel and maybe cut down on the white sugar too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn fritters with chives

i usually deep fry my corn fritters, decided to try out the pancake version of cooking them and they turned out great!

1. sift flour , baking soda , salt and pepper together
2. in a seperate bowl add all eggs and lightly beat
3. combine dry and wet ingredients together and mix until you have a pancake mix consistency
4. add corn and stir until blended
5. add chopped chives and blend
6. preheat girdle to 350 degrees f
7. drop mixture by tablespoons fills onto pre-heated girdle
8. cook on one side for 4 - 5 minutes or until golden then flip to do the other side for 4 - 5 minutes
9. turn heat down to 200 and flip again for 1 minute on each side
demonstrations.review: i was looking for a way to use some fresh chives & came across this recipe.  I added some grated carrots & a little bit of water - i found the batter a tad dry.  I also threw in some dry parsley & thyme for added flavor.  I cut back on the black pepper - 1 full tsp is quite a bit & it was still pretty peppery.  I'd probably stick to 1/4 to 1/2 a tsp next time.  All in all, they were really, really good & fluffed up quite nicely.  Something different that can be served as a side or as a main dish.  I served mine with sour cream for dipping.  Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
its the great pumpkin cookies  charlie brown

these are wonderful cookies for the fall.

1. cream butter with both sugars until light and fluffy
2. add in egg , pumpkin , and vanilla and mix
3. then add flour oats , baking soda , cinnamon , and salt and mix well
4. then stir in chocolate chips and cinnamon chips
5. bake at 350 for 18-20 minutes or until firm and lightly brown
6. you can shape these into pumpkins before baking and when done and cooled decorate with frosting or peanut butter
7. i usually eat mine when they are totally cooled
demonstrations.review: I"ve made these a few times, but have yet to rate them.  YUM!  I subbed 1 cup of whole wheat pastry flour for white, used butterscotch, white and semi-sweet chocolate chips.  I aslo threw in a dash of pumpkin pie spice.  Mine were perfectly soft after cooking for 15 minutes.  Next time, I'll try subbing out some of the butter with applesauce.  Some chopped pecans might be a nice addition as well.  Thanks for a great fall cookie recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana oatmeal bars

these can be eaten for breakfast or anytime. kids will eat them before the realize how much oatmeal they contain.

1. combine flour , salt , soda and spices and set aside
2. in a large bowl , beat butter , sugar and egg until fluffy
3. add bananas and vanilla beat until smooth
4. gradually stir in flour mixture and oats until well combined
5. if using fruit or nuts , add them now
6. pour into a grease 9x13 baking pan
7. bake at 425 for about 25 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: These came out moist and delicious!  I used 1/2 c of applesauce for 1/2 of the butter, used 1 c of whole wheat flour & 1/2 c of white, threw in some raisins & sunflower seeds (for crunch).  I'm eating them right now, warm out of the oven & they really are yummy.  Not too sweet (I used 4 pretty ripe bananas).  What a great change of pace your typical banana bread/muffin circuit.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry banana bread

use up the leftover cranberries, freeze the loaf for later.
i often make half of this into a loaf and half into small muffins.

1. preheat the oven to 350f degrees
2. grease an 8 1 / 2 by 4 1 / 2 inch loaf pan
3. mix sugar and butter in a medium mixing bowl until completely blended
4. add banana , milk and eggs , mixing well
5. add dry ingredients , mixing just until moist
6. stir in nuts and cranberries
7. spread batter evenly in the loaf pan
8. bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the centre of the bread comes out clean
9. remove from pan , cool on rack
demonstrations.review: Although I found the crust to be a bit too crunchy, the inside was moist and delicious!  I made the usual changes - applesauce for butter & whole wheat flour for white.  I also added a bit of dried orange peel to add to the flavor.  I was worried because the batter completely fills up the loaf pan, but the bread rose nicely and cooked evenly throughout.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy foil bbq potatoes

quick and easy to prepare, pop on the bbq and forget them,'til the rest of dinner is ready, delicious!!!

1. scrub potato and make 4 slits almost through to bottom
2. slice onion into 4 slices to fit into slits in potato
3. dot with butter or margarine
4. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste
5. drizzle olive oil over all
6. wrap tightly in foil , as if to freeze
7. place package on rack in bbq and close the lid
8. in a hot bbq they should be done within an hour , depends on what else you are bbqing
9. open packages , adjust seasoning , serve in opened foil
10. repeat process for as many potatoes as needed
demonstrations.review: A nice variation on your standard foil wrapped potato.  I used russett potatoes and red onion.  The onion really shrinks down, so next time I'll really shove more in there.  I also sprinkled some Mrs. Dash and could have used more.  Garlic would be a nice addition.  Served right in the foil with sour cream.  Delicious!

target.recipe_text:
weight watchers avocado and tomato pasta salad

i love the flavour of guacamole so i came up with this simple, quick recipe for a pasta salad incorporating the same flavours. you can add a variety of other ingredients, cooked chicken would work particularly well. serves 2 as a main dish or 4 as a side dish.

1. first , cook the pasta
2. meanwhile , put the mayonnaise and lime juice in a large bowl and stir
3. chop the baby plum tomatoes and avocado and add to the bowl
4. finely dice and add the red onion
5. you may also like to add some cooked chicken
6. when the pasta is cooked , drain it , then pour cold water over it for a few minutes to cool it quickly
7. drain it again and add it to the bowl
8. finely chop as much fresh coriander as you like and sprinkle it over the top
9. season with salt if desired and stir the pasta salad thoroughly to mix all the ingredients together
10. if you are using properly ripe avocadoes , stirring the mixture should blend some of the avocado flesh into the dressing to develop the flavour
11. serve and enjoy !
