1. in a parfait or sundae glass , layer some fruit salad , top with 1 / 2 of the yoghurt per serving , and layer more fruit on top
2. drizzle with 1 tblsp honey per serving , sprinkle with 2 tblsps of walnut pieces per serving and a sprinkle of cinnamon
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Like a typical tourist I made this for breakfast - I felt very virtuous, but it was delicious! I used a combination of strawberries, apricots, seedless red grapes and orange. I also added a bit of orange zest, as I hate to waste it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan seared moroccan salmon

adapted from healthy women's magazine, this dish has plenty of flavor!

1. in a medium bowl , combine all ingredients except the salmon
2. stir to make a paste
3. rub the paste to evenly cover the salmon fillets
4. place on a plate , cover with plastic wrap , and refrigerate for 5 minutes up to 2 hours
5. preheat a 10" nonstick pan over medium high heat
6. spray with oil and add salmon
7. cook 2 minutes per side , then lower heat to medium
8. continue cooking until inside is no longer translucent , about 3 minutes per side
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was delicious, and really easy. I also added a bit of mint to the marinade as I had some floating about. I served this with couscous. My only criticism is that the portion size given was definitely not enough for 2.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp in chipotle sauce  camarones enchipotlados

this recipe comes from the art of mexican cooking.  very authentic.
update:  some may find this recipe a bit on the 'spicy' side so i've made notations to "adjust to taste" on some ingredients.  on ocassion i have substituted canned tomatoes.

1. season the shrimps with salt and pepper and lime juice and set aside to marinate for about 30 minutes
2. heat the oil in a frying pan
3. add the drained shrimp , and sliced onion and fry , shaking the pan and tossing the ingredients , for about 3 minutes
4. remove the shrimp and onion with a slotted spoon and set aside
5. in a blender jar , blend the tomatoes , chipotles , and their liquid , and garlic to a textured sauce
6. reheat the oil , and add the sauce , and fry over high heat stirring and scraping the bottom of the pan to prevent sticking for about 8 minutes
7. add the wine , oregano , marinade and salt to taste and cook for another minute
8. add the shrimp / onion mixture and cook for about 2 minutes--for the shrimps should be just cooked and not rubbery
demonstrations.review: These were delicious! Smoky, spicy tomatoe-y shrimp mmmm! I made this pretty much as posted (for a change) apart from I had to use ready-peeled raw tiger prawns (shrimp!) as whole ones were impossible to find.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple milk drink  sharbat

a moroccan drink.

1. peel and cube the apples
2. place in the blender with sugar , rose water and milk
3. whirl at high speed 15 seconds
4. serve , with ice if desired , in small glasses
demonstrations.review: I made a glass of this to have with breakfast, which might not be the traditional thing, but it tasted delicious! Light, fruity, frothy. Really good. I used Orange water, but will give rosewater a stab next time I have some in.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
target.review: We thought this was pretty good. Even my crockpot hating hubby thought it was ok, but the chicken was a little bland. I think I'll try marinading the chicken before hand and see how that goes. Other wise, it was great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
demonstrations.review: The taste was outstanding, problem I had was with the "Crust" on the top and bottom got really brown before the rest was done (only after 45min) but other wise the taste was outstanding after I picked off the bottom layer LOL

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy salisbury steak

you will love this quick and easy recipe! this seems to be a favorite among the men but of course everyone will love it. id make a side of mashed potatoes and pick a fresh veggie to go along. you can make your own brown gravy or use a different mix, but this is what i've used. i hope you enjoy.

1. combine first four ingredients in a large bowl
2. the meat will seem thin
3. roll the mixture into 4 or 5 balls depending on how big you want your patties
4. and place in fridge for 30 minutes
5. flatten the balls into patties and in a large frying pan brown each side
6. do not cook all the way
7. remove from pan and set aside
8. empty the pan from anything left over and add the brown gravy mix as instructed on the package
9. when the gravy comes to a boil add the patties and allow to cook uncovered on low for about 15 minutes--the longer the more tender
demonstrations.review: This is very good, I did make some subs as I used Italian breadcrumbs instead of crackers and I used 1 can of Brown gravy (already made) Also, I finished in the oven. Very easy and tasty! great with potatoes and corn

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: YUMMY! This is the best recipe I have found on here. I used 1 cup milk, 1 cup half and half.  I used half mild cheddar, half sharp cheddar. I also added lots of pepper and garlic salt. For the bread crumbs, I did Italian bread crumbs in butter . YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden chicken nuggets

this is one of my kids favorites. they have said, 'mom, your chicken nuggets are the best!!' for such picky eaters, that is a huge complement.

1. heat deep fryer
2. cut chicken into bite size pieces
3. soak chicken in milk
4. mix flour and seasoning in large bowl
5. dip chicken into flour
6. cook about 12 pieces at a time in fryer for 360 degrees for 6 to 9 minutes or until golden
7. serve with sweet and sour sauce or honey mustard !
demonstrations.review: This was great!!! My Dh and I and the kids LOVED them! So crispy and tasty. (and my son is a PICKY eater) We are going to experiment with different seasonings. Much healthier then getting Mc Nuggets from the Golden Arches...lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast ii

here's the way french toast has been made in my family for at least 4 generations - but until i got into high school, we called it 

1. whisk the eggs till frothy
2. add remaining ingredients , and mix well
3. over medium heat , lightly grease skillet with shortening
4. i use a paper towel , so i can use it repeatedly , with every 2 or 3 pans of french toast
5. dip each slice of bread into the egg mixture , on both sides
6. do this quickly , so as not to completely soak the bread
7. cook in skillet over med / med-high heat for approx 5 min per side
8. you may need to flip more than once to get th e desired golden-brown color
9. serve with butter and powdered sugar , or preserves or syrup
demonstrations.review: Wow!! This was wonderful! I scaled the recipe in half and used regular white bread. And it was enough for me, my DH and my two young sons. It was so good! nice and sweet how we like it! the first thing dh said was "what did you do different, this is great!" Will definatly make again and again!

target.recipe_text:
indian butter chicken

this is my family's favourite butter chicken recipe - it came about after my youngest son stayed at a friends house and they bought indian take-away.  youngest says this is just like the one he had at his friend's. this is one of favourite dishes.
butter chicken was created in the 1950s at the moti mahal restaurant in delhi.

1. heat a wok until really hot , add 1 tbsp oil
2. add half the chicken and stir-fry for about 4 minutes or until chicken is a nice colour
3. remove to plate
4. add extra oil and cook remaining chicken
5. remove from wok
6. reduce heat and add the butter
7. when melted add all of the spices and stir-fry until fragrant- about 1 minute
8. return chicken to wok and stir to coat with the spices
9. add the tomato and sugar and simmer for 15 minutes- stir occasionally
10. add the yogurt , cream and lemon juice and simmer for 5 minutes or until the sauce thickens a bit
11. serve over rice
12. this dish can be frozen
13. after step nine cool completely then store in a zip-lock bag in the freezer
14. to reheat , thaw in bag in fridge overnight then add contents to saucepan
15. reheat gently , then simmer for 8 minutes - add the yoghurt , cream and lemon juice and simmer for 5 more minutes
target.review:
Amazing! I have tried many butter chicken recipes and this one is restaurant quality. The whole family loved it so it's going in the keeper file. 
My only comment is that it was a little on the salty side, must be from butter since there is no added salt. I think I might do half unsalted butter next time.
Thanks Fairy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix extender

a simple way to make a bigger and better cake mix. makes a 13x9 pan come out very high and moist.

1. mix all together
2. add to your already mixed cake mix batter
3. bake per directions but may need and additional 5-10 minutes longer to become done
demonstrations.review: Excellent. Was in need of a dense and moist cake recipe that would hold up to fondant. This recipe is fast and easy. I also mix all dry ingredients together and wet together first. Although I love sugar I do cut back on the sugar by about a tablespoon. I also add some dry cocoa powder when extending chocolate cake.Thank you Laurie, this will be a treasured recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy enchiladas  beef or chicken

these easy enchiladas are my husband's favorite recipe of mine. because of the many different options, it is very versatile.

1. if using chicken , boil chicken in water
2. then rinse and shred with fork
3. add onion and garlic
4. if using ground beef , brown with onion and garlic , drain
5. add next 7 ingredients
6. in another skillet , heat oil
7. add tortillas , one at a time , for 10 seconds on each side
8. drain on paper towel
9. in 10x13 baking pan , pour just enough enchilada sauce in the bottom to coat the bottom of the pan
10. fill each tortilla with a spoonful of meat mixture
11. cheese , onions , and / or olives can be put inside each enchilada at this time , if desired
12. roll tortilla and place seam side down in pan
13. continue with remaining tortillas
14. pour remaining enchilada sauce over tortillas and top with cheese
15. at this time , pan may be refrigerated for several hours or overnight
16. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
17. top with sour cream
18. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
I know this recipe already has a lot of 5 star reviews but I just had to add one more.
FYI this recipe works well even if you skip the oiled tortilla step. We just heated them in our tortilla warmer to soften (And save calories), then followed the recipe as stated. Just make sure each tortilla has sauce covering it on top, even just a thin coat.
Excellent! Thank you IBShirley!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Even though it's #414, I still had to add a review. I was looking for something quick to fix with hope of having the ingredients on hand.
I entered roasted chicken (Had a precooked one from the deli in my fridge) and this was one of the recipes listed.
I just threw everything in a pot (I used Herdez salsa, I think it's more authentic and less sweet than most), simmered for awhile and added cream cheese at the end. We threw some corn and flour tortillas in the warmer and dinner was served.
Enjoyed by the whole family, thanks Jen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh blueberry cobbler

easy and too good for words.

1. add flour , 1 / 2 cup sugar , salt , and baking powder to a mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add in milk and butter
4. stir to combine
5. spread batter into a greased 8-inch square baking pan
6. sprinkle blueberries evenly over batter
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 cup sugar and drizzle with vanilla
8. bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until a pick comes out clean
9. can serve plain or with ice cream on top
demonstrations.review:
Loved it! I was looking for a dessert recipe that didn't use a lot of sugar so I gave this one a try.
I experimented by cutting the first round of sugar to only a 1/4 cup (Used unprocessed sugar) and the topping sugar (Regular white) was way under 1/3 cup, I just sprinkled it over the top.
I also used 2 % milk because that's all I had and cut the butter by about a tablespoon. Maybe next time I can cut a little more without compromising the recipe?
The cake was so soft, light and fluffy I would have thought it had buttermilk in it.
We topped with a little whipped cream from the can.
Next time I will definitely double the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornflake crusted baked chicken

this recipe is from everday foods. i just tried it out and it is soo good & crispy! i was impressed!!!! the recipe calls for bone-in legs and thighs, but i just used 4 breasts each cut into 3 diagonal strips.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. rinse chicken , and pat dry
3. season generously with salt , garlic powder and pepper
4. in a small bowl , whisk egg with 1 tablespoon water
5. in a large bowl , mix cornflakes with oil , cayenne , and 1 teaspoon salt
6. working with one piece of chicken at a time , dip chicken in egg mixture , then coat with seasoned cornflakes , pressing flakes to help them adhere
7. transfer coated pieces to a rimmed baking sheet
8. bake until golden brown and crisp , about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This one is going in the keeper file. I used 6 boneless breasts sliced about an 1 to 1 1/2 inch thick. I doubled the cornflakes (even added a tad more because I seem to run a little short.) Instructions indicate garlic so I added about a teaspoon of powdered garlic.
I have been making other versions of baked tenders for a long time but I think this is the only one I will use from now on.
Thank you Japanese Delight!

target.recipe_text:
auberge cheddar cheese and ham breakfast buns   muffins

these are what the french call "cakes" - they are little savoury buns or muffins - and are always requested for breakfasts in the auberge. they are delicious split and spread with herb and garlic cheese when warm - or serve them alongside hot soups, stews, chilli or casseroles! i have also made these with grated gruyere cheese as well as emmenthal....the trick is to use a mature and strong tasting cheese. i have suggested using smoked ham in this recipe - it just gives a wonderful extra flavour to these delicious buns/muffins. they freeze well and are easily reheated, if you have any left! we often have these for christmas morning breakfast or brunch with the optional chives added, and then spread with smoked salmon butter - divine!

1. pre-heat an oven to 200c / 400f / gas mark 5
2. grease a 12 hole muffin or bun tray / pan
3. sift the dry ingredients into a large bowl and mix well
4. season with salt and pepper - but be careful not to over salt as the stock powder will contain salt
5. stir in the ham and cheese , and chives if using , mix again
6. add the egg , milk and olive oil - mix well - but do not over mix - just enough to combine the ingredients together
7. adjust the consistency if too dry by adding a little more milk - the mixture should be a soft dropping consistency
8. spoon mixture into the prepared muffin / bun tray / pan and bake in the preheated oven for 20 to 25 minutes , or until the muffins are well risen and golden brown
9. remove from the oven and allow to cool slightly on a wire rack
10. serve whilst warm - delicious if spread with butter or soft cheese !
target.review: These little cakes are truly fantastic. They have a lovely savoury flavour that hits the spot for breakfast. I made a batch of these intending to use them for my children's breakfasts. They didn't make it to the freezer...we ate them all in a few days. I didn't have chives so I used spring onions and that worked out well. The use of mature cheddar does give them a little more zing than any other cheese would. These will certainly be made again soon...I'll just have to double the recipe so I don't run out. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
albondigas con salsa de tomate  spanish style meatballs

these spanish style meatballs with tomato sauce are fabulous....can't remember where i got this recipe.

1. combine meatball ingredients in a bowl
2. shape mixture into balls
3. cook in 2 tbspns olive oil , turning frequently
4. add sauce ingredients to pan
5. cover and cook gently , about 15 minutes
6. until tomatoes are pulpy and meatballs are cooked through
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe, thanks for posting! I used ground pork because that's what I had defrosted and instead of fresh tomatoes I used one tin of diced tomatoes with liquid. Alternatively, I could have used one tin of Spanish style tomato sauce and substituted the cilantro for the rosemary.
I served it over white rice with some steamed vegetables on the side. My family loved it!

Thanks again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bed and breakfast spiced pumpkin scones with honey butter

gorgeous spiced pumpkin scones with honey butter - what a treat for the tea-time table during autumn and winter. i have made these twice now and love the combination of the honey butter with the scones, although they are also delicious with plain unsalted butter. this recipe came from an australian "olive" magazine that was sent to me, apparently, queensland is famous for its blue pumpkins where this recipe originates from - i added the spices as well as the honey butter! a wonderful recipe for the cooler months, but as it uses tinned or frozen pumpkin, these can be made all year around. if you don't want to serve these with the honey butter, just split them whilst warm and spread with normal butter or cream. mixed spice is a british spice mixture, i have a recipe for this on rz: recipe #266688

1. preheat oven to 200 c / gas 6
2. lightly grease a baking tray
3. cream together butter and sugar , then beat in egg , pumpkin puree and 4 tablespoons milk until smooth
4. add the mixed spice to the pumpkin mixture , taste and adjust the spices to taste
5. stir in flour until a dough forms , then knead a few times on a well floured surface until the dough holds together
6. add more flour if dough is too wet or sticky
7. press the dough into a flat circle 1 to 1
8. 5cm thick
9. cut into 6 wedges , place onto greased baking tray , and brush the tops with 2 tablespoons of milk
10. bake in the preheated oven until golden brown on top and bottom , 10 to 15 minutes
11. once done , wrap scones with a clean tea towel and allow to cool for 15 minutes before serving with the honey butter
12. honey butter: mix the butter and honey together , adding the honey a spoon at a time until the right consistency is achieved
13. mix well
14. best served fresh with the pumpkin scones
demonstrations.review:
Mmmmmm good! The weather this weekend called for scones so I made two batches of these .
I think I did something wrong though, because I had to add quite a bit of flour to the mixture. I used 250g tinned pumpkin and 250g self rising flour. I was really careful to measure everything so I don't know what happened. In the end, they turned out wonderfully. I dusted them with a bit of icing sugar and served them with the honey butter and jam. Incidentally, I used your spice mixture....much better than what the shops sell.
Two friends came for Sunday afternoon tea and they complimented me several times. All the while, my two children were looking at the table counting the scones to make sure we'd left some for them. :-)
Karen, thanks again for another winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s crispy garlic baked chicken

if you don't have panko just use dry breadcrumbs

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. set oven rack to lowest position
3. grease a small baking sheet
4. in a shallow bowl combine melted butter with 1-1 / 2 teaspoons garlic powder and 2 teaspoons dijon mustard
5. in another bowl combine all breading ingredients
6. dip the breast into the melted butter turning a few times to coat generously , then coat in the breading mixture pressing down firmly with hands to adhere the coating to the breast
7. place on baking sheet
8. continue with remaining chicken adding in more breading to the bowl as needed to coat the chicken
9. bake for about 35-40 minutes or until the chicken is cooked through
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic, flavourful chicken dish! The garlic, Italian seasoning and cayenne blend so well together. I used real butter and panko. The panko is a must in my opinion. It bakes up so well in the oven but the inside was still very moist! Thanks for another wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steak  or chicken  fajitas

these are so quick and tasty. you can use strips of boneless chicken breast instead of the beef. feel free to double the marinade. the flavor is so great for such a short marination time. you can can do them up ahead of time and have the meat sit longer if you wish.

1. slice steak into thin strips
2. in bowl , mix together 1 tablespoons olive oil , lime juice , garlic , chili powder , cumin , hot pepper flakes , black pepper & salt
3. add beef strips and stir to coat , set aside
4. wrap tortillas in foil and place in 350 oven for 5-10 minutes or until heated through
5. cut onions in half lengthwise and slice into strips , cut your peppers into strips
6. in large non stick skillet over medium high heat , heat remaining tablespoons of olive oil
7. add onions & peppers stirring for 3-4 minutes , until softened
8. transfer to a bowl and set aside
9. add beef to skillet , cook , stirring for 3-4 minutes or until they lose their red color
10. return onions and peppers to skillet
11. stir for about one minute
12. to serve , spoon a portion of the beef mixture down the centre of each tortilla , top with your desired toppings , fold bottom of tortilla up over filling , fold the sides in , overlapping
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavour! I made these on a weeknight when I didn't have a lot of time to marinade the meat and was surprised because they were super tasty. The lime juice is what really brings all the flavour out. My family voted this as a keeper recipe! Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ann s close to wendy s style chili recipe

i really enjoy wendy's chili                    
so i have been playing around trying to make a clone for a long time. i have read other clones on the internet for the recipe and here is where i stand with the recipe.
i think it is pretty close to the taste  wendy's chili has.

i would love any comments or suggestions to improve this chili

enjoy  =)

1. brown the hamburger and drain the grease
2. add seasonings and frozen vegetables when frozen vegetables start to heat up
3. add the rest of the ingredients
4. simmer the longer the better i like to simmer at least a couple of hours
5. remove the bay leaf before serving
demonstrations.review:
This is by far the best chili recipe I have ever tried! Whenever I've made chili before it was either too "chili-ey", too tomato-ey or just not quite right. I feel like Goldilocks! I've finally found the right one.
I didn't have frozen Kroger veggies so I used onion, garlic, celery, red and green peppers. I made a few changes and used one tin of great northern beans because that's all I had and I also added one poblano chili as well as 1/2 teaspoon of smoked paprika. I served it with cornbread muffins and shredded cheddar cheese. My family really enjoyed it and I was lucky to have some leftovers for lunch tomorrow. Thanks for posting and congratulations on a wonderful recipe. I shall definitely make this again!

target.recipe_text:
mama bear s porridge

this is almost like rice pudding, it's a stick-to-your-ribs breakfast! don't worry about adding raw eggs, they will cook completely in the porridge! this can also be made in the microwave, but you will need to remove a couple of times to stir.

1. in a large heavy-bottomed saucepan bring 3 cups water to a boil
2. in another bowl mix together powdered milk , oats , cinnamon and sugar quickly stir into the boiling water
3. return to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer for about 6-10 minutes or until the mixture is desired thickness
4. remove from heat and mix in the raisins and vanilla
5. beat in eggs one at a time , mixing well after each addition
6. divide the porridge between 3 or 4 bowls , then top with a teaspoon of butter and then about 1 / 4 cup of cream or milk
7. drizzle with honey as desired
target.review: This is wonderful! I used brown sugar and the eggs did completely cook with the heat of the porridge. I am a hot cereal freak and appreciate the protein count in this as I don't eat every day. Thank you for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tater tots casserole

needed something last minute to take to a potluck so i threw this together. didn't have hashbrowns or regular onions on hand so i substituted! turned out great!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x 13 inch baking dish arrange tater tots in the prepared baking dish
3. in a mixing bowl , combine sour cream , cheese , and mushroom soup
4. pour this mixture over the tots
5. sprinkle onions over the top of the casserole
6. bake in 350 degress oven for 45-60 minutes
7. if it starts browning too much cover with foil
demonstrations.review: I am not a vegetarian anymore but I loved this as a meatless meal! I am just not that into meat and only eat small amounts anyway. Nice to have another meatless meal that is SOO comforting! I halved the recipe and had the rst a few days later reheated in the oven. It was still yummy. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest yellow   zucchini squash   beef casserole

this is a yummy, warming casserole that is meant to be a side dish, but since it has meat in it, can also be served as a main dish. this is the version i came up with after significantly reducing some of the heavier ingredients, that were in the original version i saw on lucy classic cajun & cuisine, a pbs cooking program. but don't let that scare you - this is not a spicy dish at all. i make this often in the end of summer to use up fresh squash.  if you don't have both types of squash, just use 2 of whichever type you do have.

1. cook sliced squashes in a small pot with the water until tender but not mushy
2. drain and return squash to the pot
3. add butter and allow it to melt in the pot and saut all together for 10 minutes , stirring occasionally , over medium to medium-low heat
4. meanwhile , spray a large deep skillet with nonstick spray and cook the beef and onions
5. drain any fat , then season meat mixture with salt and pepper to taste
6. add the squash to the beef using a slotted spoon , and reduce heat to low
7. beat together eggs , then whisk in mayo- add this mixture to the skillet
8. stir in the cheese and the cooked rice
9. pour into a large oval casserole and sprinkle with enough cracker crumbs to cover
10. bake in a preheated oven at 350 f for about 15-20 minutes
11. i have always used at most the 1 / 2 stick and as little as 2 tablespoons
12. -it is based on your preferences
13. i also always use real , unsalted butter
demonstrations.review: Being in Maine now we always seem to have a glut of summer squashes. I have many recipes I created for these but found this one to be a yummy addition to my repetoire! I omitted the meat and enjoyed it very much. Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of oatmeal

i often make this for my husband, who loves his hot cereal in the morning! one morning i was out of cream of wheat cereal, so came up with this! i hope you enjoy it! this is also good added to cream of wheat. you may also add chopped or sliced fruit(banana, peaches, apples, etc.), dried fruit(raisins, craisins, figs, dates, etc.) or other spices(nutmeg, cardamom, mace, etc.). i add a teaspoonful of ground flaxseed to mine sometimes.

1. place oatmeal in the food processor
2. process until finely shredded
3. place in a small saucepan along with the wheat germ , wheat bran , salt , water and milk
4. bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer till liquid is almost all absorbed , about 3-5 minutes
5. stir often so it won't stick to the bottom
6. pour into a bowl and place a little pat of butter on top , if desired
7. pour a little milk on , then brown sugar to taste
8. sprinkle with cinnamon , stir it all up and serve !
9. add whatever optional ingredients you like
10. :)
demonstrations.review: Love it love it! I use REAL Scottish Porridge Oats (1:3 ratio) for this as they are already finely milled though not pre-parched like quick oats. Using these I don't have to process the oats and I love hot cereals. I had no wheat bran so I doubled the germ using the honey kind. Bulk sections, health food stores and Bob's Red Mill all have Scottish porridge oats. Thank you for a winner Sharon!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 0 point weight watchers cabbage soup

you can eat as much of this 0-point weight watchers cabbage soup as you like. it's so good for you.

1. spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes
2. add broth , tomato paste , cabbage , green beans , basil , oregano and salt & pepper to taste
3. simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes
4. i have tried different variations
5. leaving out green beans
6. adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion
7. all very good
8. you can customize it a bit
demonstrations.review: I have the flu right now. I live in Morocco and got hubby Mohamed to make this for me. We didn't have green beans, basil or oregano so he spiced it using red sweet paprika, a pinch of ground ginger and plenty of fresh black pepper! It was sooo good! I think I wil get the flu again! He also used red onion as that is the onion in season at the moment.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ricotta bread for bread machines  1 pound loaf

a favorite i have been making for years. this isn't a very tall loaf and yes - the amount of flour is correct. note: (these days, most bread machines have much bigger pans, so if you have a larger capacity machine, you may instead wish to only mix the dough in the machine,let it rise, then bake the bread itself in a loaf pan (at 350 f for perhaps 30 minutes is a guess).  this can still be baked in a larger capacity machine, it will just have an odd shape.

1. place all ingredients into a 1-pound capacity bread machine according to the directions in your manual
2. select the basic bread cycle and light crust
3. after about 5 minutes , take a peek inside your machine to see if your dough is forming up a ball- if it is too wet , add up to 3 tbsp additional flour , a spoonful at a time , if too dry , add a little water
demonstrations.review: YUMMMM! This is a very nice bread and I love to make cinnamon french toast with it, bread pudding and/or toast it. I set my crust to medium as I always do and it was lovely! Thank you for a keeper! Am going back to live in the US and searching out bread maker recipes as I have a barely used one awaiting me that I left behind. Great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
spinach  tomato and feta quiche

this is an impressive looking quiche that's easy to personalise to your own tastes. you may like to try red peppers instead of the tomato, add a few mushrooms, maybe some asparagus...you get the idea! i served this with a nice salad, a vegetable side dish and a cheese plate for a nice summer meal.

1. two hours before you want to make the quiche , take the dough out of the freezer to defrost
2. when you're ready to start , lay the dough into either a 10 inch quiche or springform baking pan , making sure you have enough dough to form a crust around the edge
3. the crust should come 1 to 1 1 / 2 inches up the side of the pan
4. crumble the feta cheese onto the bottom of the crust
5. pour the olive oil into a saucepan and , when it is heated , throw in the spinach and cook until wilted
6. spread the spinach over the feta cheese
7. beat the eggs , garlic and creme fraiche together
8. pour over top of the feta cheese and spinach
9. place cherry tomatoes on top of the quiche
10. sprinkle chives and ground pepper on top
11. bake at 350 f or 180 c for 45 minutes
target.review: Very good! I added 1/2 cup of feta, instead of 1/3, and it could possibly have used a bit more. I bought a 5 ounce package of washed spinach, and just used that, without measuring to see if it was 3 cups. I had some roasted onions in the fridge, and used those instead of the chives, which was excellent. I doubled the number of cherry tomatoes, and that was just about right. Everyone raved. My only complaint -- and this is sort of a warning for you, if you're considering using the springform pan -- is that mine leaked, even through the pie crust.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal bars

my grandson prefers these to chicolate chip bars!  they're easy and oh so good.

1. cream butter and sugars together
2. mix in the eggs and vanilla
3. combine the flour , salt , cinnamon & baking soda
4. mix into creamed mixture
5. stir in the oatmeal
6. press into 9x13 " ungreased pan and cook @350 for 30-35 minute
demonstrations.review: Quite easy to make, though the creaming of butter and sugar is work. I added some craisins and chocolate chips, and it was still a little bland for me, which is why it only gets 4 stars. My guests loved it, though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy homemade cream of spinach soup

this is so easy to make. i've also used broccoli and am planning to try asparagus. i love this recipe-it's so quick!

1. in a medium saucepan combine water and spinach
2. cook till tender
3. do not drain
4. in a large saucepan melt the butter on medium low heat
5. stir in flour until smooth
6. whisk in hot milk and bouillon
7. cook until beginning to thicken , then add spinach mixture
8. season to taste
9. i sometimes add allspice instead of the garlic in the winter months
demonstrations.review: This is fabulous! I used fresh spinach and homemade chicken stock instead of the water, and omitted the chicken bouillon. Also, I used a hand blender to make it an actual cream soup -- the recipe never says to do this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s szegendiner gulyas

my grandmother brought this recipe from eastern europe. she served it with crusty homemade bread. as kids we loved to dunk our bread into the juice. what a treat. we couldn't wait until it was done.

1. heat the lard and saute the onion to a dark golden
2. add the pork and saute briefly only until it loses color
3. remove pan from heat and add the paprika , and water
4. put it back on the heat and add salt , caraway seed , and garlic
5. cook gently 1 / 2 hours
6. stir occasionally
7. add sauerkraut and cook until well done
8. your meat should be tender
9. stir the flour into the sour cream then add it to stew
10. let it simmer only about 10 minute
11. take out bay leaf
12. it's ready to eat !
demonstrations.review: This was amazing! My husband bought waaaay too much pork at the store, so I tripled the recipe. I added 1# of mushrooms and 2 full jars of sauerkraut (packed down, it wasn't even the 9 cups required, but it was plenty. My husband gobbled it down, and there's only 1/3 left (the normal recipe size) 2 days later. Next time, I'll add even more mushrooms, and a few juniper berries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german cabbage casserole   kohl und hackfleisch

cabbage and meat mildly seasoned with garlic and onions in a creamy cheese sauce and topped with breadcrumbs for a pretty presentation! a real comfort food. even those who say they hate cabbage will eat this and like it! i have even made this without the meat- using bulgur and veggie broth. here is how: just replace the meat with the same amount of bulgur- (for 1 lb of meat sub 1 cup bulgur) you will want to soak the bulgur according to the instructions on the package- if you bought it in bulk here is how...

bring 2 cups of veggie broth ( can use bouillon and water) per 1 cup bulgur

when broth is boiling stir in bulgur. cover and simmer about 15 minutes or until bulgur is soft. all the broth should be absorbed. fluff the bulgur with a fork as you would rice and add to your recipe.

i have used beef, pork, turkey and chicken  with great results too.

*see note for freezing, make ahead and left over tips*

1. brown meat , onion and garlic until meat is no longer pink and onion has turned clear
2. drain grease from pan and discard
3. add cabbage and cover
4. cook until cabbage is clear
5. add cheese and sour cream mixing well
6. pour all into greased casserole and top with bread crumbs
7. bake at 375 for 40 minutes
8. this freezes excellently and if anything tastes even better after ! i reheated it by melting a little butter in a skillet and then crumbling the partially thawed casserole into it , cooking and stirring until it was heated through
demonstrations.review: I was cleaning out the fridge and had a LOT of cabbage and some sour cream, so I found this recipe. Based on all the comments that it was a bit bland, I doubled the onions, tripled the garlic, added some red pepper flakes with the garlic, added sliced fresh mushrooms and some smoked paprika with the cabbage. Also used manchego and Romano cheese, instead of cheddar, because that was what I had. Turned out great! Even better the second day. In fact, it didn't last 24 hours in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian white bean and spinach soup

diabetic friendly
serve with parmesan, if you like.

1. in 3-quart saucepan , heat oil over medium heat
2. add onion and celery
3. cook , stirring , until celery is tender , 5 to 8 minutes
4. stir in garlic and cook 30 seconds
5. add beans , water , broth , pepper , and thyme
6. heat to boiling over high heat
7. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
8. roll up several spinach leaves together , cigar fashion , and thinly slice
9. repeat with remaining spinach
10. with slotted spoon , remove 2 cups beans from soup mixture and reserve
11. spoon one-fourth of mixture into blender
12. cover , with center part of cover removed to let steam escape , and puree until smooth
13. pour into bowl
14. repeat with remaining mixture
15. return puree and reserved beans to saucepan
16. heat to
17. boiling over medium-high heat
18. stir in spinach and cook until wilted , about 1 minute
19. remove from heat and stir in lemon juice
demonstrations.review: Very easy, very good, and I think it will be even better tomorrow. I used 2 cans pintos, because I had no white beans, 5 cups home made chicken stock and added a chopped carrot & 3 cloves of garlic. The lemon juice and thyme are very important; the thyme makes it fragrant, and it was really flat before I added the lemon juice.

target.recipe_text:
4 layer cream cheese pudding dessert

this is a wonderful recipe. it is so easy and no one would ever know! the great thing is you may use any flavor you like for the pudding. i would use chocolate or vanilla 8)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine the flour , nuts and margarine
3. press mixture into a 13x9-inch pan
4. bake 10-15 minutes
5. while cooling , combine the cream cheese , powdered sugar and 1 cup cool whip
6. spread over first layer
7. mix the pudding and milk
8. pour on creamy layer
9. chill
10. spread with remaining cool whip
11. you may sprinkle with toasted coconut if you like
target.review: What I'm rating here is the crust. I should have doubled or 1 1/2x the crust ingredients. When I spread the cream cheese layer over the crust, it just fell apart and crumbled.  No one will see it, but when one is putting in time, effort, and $$ for ingredients, it should be good looking in appearance besides tasting good.  I used lemon pudding and grated lemon zest into it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted cabbage with balsamic vinegar

yum!  cabbage and balsamic vinegar!!  found this in everyday food.

1. preheat oven to 450f cut cabbage into 12 wedges
2. remove thick core and discard
3. pull wedges apart
4. toss on a large rimmed baking sheet with oil , 2 tsp salt , and 1 / 4 tsp pepper
5. cover sheet tightly with foil
6. bake until cabbage is crisp-tender , about 20 minutes
7. remove foil
8. continue cooking , tossing occasionally , until tender and browned in spots , 20 to 25 minutes
9. toss with vinegar and serve
demonstrations.review: I made this last week-end as the recipe stated, except I sauteed in a pan. It was lacking  something. Today I sauteed some chopped red onion, added 1 1/2 tsp of sugar and the balsamic, and sautwith roasted lamb shanks and a pan gravy. Thanks for posting the basic resipr.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned banana cream pie

before cool whip and instant pudding, this was how a cream pie was made. if you leave out the bananas, you have vanilla cream pie. if you add 1 cup shredded coconut to milk as it's being heated, you have coconut cream pie.

1. have baked 9-inch pie shell ready
2. in a large saucepan , scald the milk
3. in another saucepan , combine the sugar , flour and salt
4. gradually stir in the scalded milk
5. over medium heat , stirring constantly , cook until thickened
6. cover and , stirring occasionally , cook for two minutes longer
7. in a small bowl , have the 3 egg yolks , slightly beaten , ready
8. stir a small amount of the hot mixture into beaten yolks
9. when thoroughly combined , stir yolks into hot mixture
10. cook for one minute longer , stirring constantly
11. remove from heat and blend in the butter and vanilla
12. let sit until lukewarm
13. when ready to pour , slice bananas and scatter in pie shell
14. pour warm mixture over bananas
15. if desired , make a meringue to top the pie , or just let the pie cool until serving
demonstrations.review: I don't understand all the raves about this recipe. It was soup!!  As I was making this, I kept telling myself that this was way too much liquid for the amount of flour. I should have trusted my judgement.  It tasted fine, but I won't be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
4. pour over the chicken
5. bake in preheated oven for one hour , or until sauce is caramelized
6. could also use wings or pork ribs
demonstrations.review: I used 5 thighs and added 1 haeping tsp of sambal oleek. At the end of baking I turned the oven to 500 for a few minutes to crisp the skin and caramelize the sauce. Delicious. I will make again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm greek style rice salad

this is from my cookshelf rice and risotto cookbook. i have not tried it. cook time is estimation of time it takes to cook the rice. it looks yummy!

1. cook rice till tender
2. drain and rinse under hot water
3. drain again
4. whisk together the lemon juice , olive oil , oregano , mustard , salt and pepper
5. add the tomatoes , bell pepper , olives , feta , cheese , capers and parsley
6. stir to coat
7. toss along with the rice in a large bowl
8. garnish individual servings with feta cheese and diced cucumbers
demonstrations.review: This was a great salad! I served it cold, and it was so colorful. I used orange, yellow, and red peppers. Had some leftovers for breakfast this morning. I didn't use the capers. I will make again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country bean  beef and cabbage soup

this is similar to a stuffed cabbage soup, with beans substituting for the rice. i am on the south beach diet and this soup can be eaten on phase i of the plan. it's very tasty and easy to prepare. even if you are not watching your carb/sugar intake, it's a healthy good for you soup. this recipe originated from the good carb cookbook.

1. spray inside of a large size dutch oven pot with non stick cooking spray
2. add ground beef
3. cook beef over medium heat until it's crumbly and no longer pink
4. add beef broth , tomatoes , onion , thyme , pepper and bay leaf
5. bring to a boil over high heat
6. cover and simmer for about 15 minutes
7. add cabbage and beans , turn heat up to high and bring to a boil
8. cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes
9. remove bay leaf and serve
demonstrations.review: This is the same recipe I use from Sandra Woodruff's Good Carb Cookbook, except she uses 12 oz. of lean ground beef. I added a chopped clove of garlic and canellini beans instead of red kidney beans, and some boullion granules and extra water because we like our soup to be more liquidy. I've made this simple soup many times and it's always good.

target.recipe_text:
my really good beef roast  crock pot

i don't think i've ever made crock pot roast the same twice but this one was really good so i decided i would post it so i could remember it next time.  few ingredients for an easy supper. makes an excellent au jus or gravy.

1. rinse roast under cool water
2. add roast to crock pot
3. sprinkle brown gravy mix on and around roast
4. add 1 / 2 cup water around roast
5. add quartered potatoes around roast
6. sprinkle ranch mix over roast and potatoes
7. season potatoes with salt
8. set crock pot on high for 3 hours
9. cut carrots same size as quartered potatoes or if using baby carrots , use whole
10. add carrots and additional 1 / 2 cup water if you like a thinner gravy or au jus
11. change setting to low for 2 more hours
12. slice roast on serving platter , surround with veggies
13. serve gravy or au jus on the side
14. any cut of roast would probably work , but this is a good , lean cut that doesn't require trimming and also slices nicely
15. a larger roast may also be used
16. cooking: you can also add the carrots after step 7 and cook on low for 6-8 hours total
17. the carrots will just be a little softer than the other method
target.review: Made this yesterday and it was really good.  The ranch dressing mix gave it a really unique taste. Only thing I changed was the use of regular salt instead of kosher salt and I added a little extra water in order to cover the potatoes and carrots.  But when done, removed veggies and roast and added a little cornstarch to thicken gravy.  Turned out excellent.  This is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
split pea soup  crock pot    dairy free

very little prep, just layer in crock pot/slow cooker, leave it for the day and a filling, delicious soup will be ready for dinner.

this recipe is a very versatile base split pea soup.  for a vegan option, omit the meat. i have made this recipe using ham, ham hock, and bacon. i have used veggie broth, chicken broth and water... each tasting different but yummy! i have reduced the salt but have not adjusted the recipe as written. this soup is even better the next day, it freezes well. this tends to be a thicker soup (especially once it has cooled) so adjust liquid after cooking to desired thickness.

1. layer ingredients in crockpot
2. pour in water , so don't stir
3. cover and cook on high 4-5 hours or on low for 8-10 hours
4. remove bay leaf
5. serve with some nice crusty bread or buns
demonstrations.review:
Made this yesterday which was my first attempt at split-pea soup. Noted BrittBall's comment about being thick so I added 1 extra cup of water and a 14 oz can of chicken broth.  Also added a dash of thyme and majoram and 3 bay leaves instead of 1.  Came out excellent!!
Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
favorite croutons

after trial and error this composite of spices seem to suit most of my family members. some want it spicy hot, some can't abide any spices. i wouldn't want any fewer spices than these few basic ones. the croutons should be watched closely while cooking as they will burn quickly.

1. pre-heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spread aluminum foil over a cookie sheet and set aside
3. in a medium sized bowl , mix together the oil and spices
4. stir well to blend
5. add bread pieces and toss to coat well
6. spread bread pieces out in single layer on foil lined cookie sheet
7. drizzle any remaining oil over bread and place in oven
8. bake for about 15 minutes , or until lightly browned
9. turn once halfway through baking time to brown , evenly
10. watch closely to prevent burning
demonstrations.review:
Made these croutons and used French bread. They got just a little dark since I got a phone call in the last 5 minutes after turning but they were still really good. Served on a Caesar salad with chicken and the  dressing by Mille #15913.
Excellent! Put the remaining croutons in a large zip-lock freezer bag to keep fresh.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy granola bars

i "borrowed" this recipe from the kitchen at my college because i fell in love with these bars. they are so much better than store-bought, and you can add or subtract ingredients as you wish. they make a perfect on-the-go snack; a much healthier alternative to chips or cookies, especially for kids (great for lunch boxes!)

1. preheat oven to 350 and lightly grease or spray 9 x 13 pan
2. in large bowl , beat brown sugar , sugar , and butter until light and fluffy
3. blend in honey , vanilla and egg
4. in separate bowl , combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda , and salt
5. add flour mixture gradually to sugar mixture and beat until combined
6. by hand , stir in almonds , chocolate chips and oats until well mixed
7. press mixture firmly in bottom of greased pan , and bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes , or until light golden brown
8. cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I made this a couple of months ago and everyone loved them. I just made them again today using half whole wheat flour and regular flour. Also I used walnuts this time instead of almonds. Still tasted really great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: I have been getting a lot of Tilapia lately at my local Costco and trying several different recipes. This is my hands-down favorite so far and I have made it about 5 times. I have even substituted romano for the parmesan on 1 occasion and it was still really good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caesar salad

my all-time favourite salad. no other even comes close - well, maybe a spinach/bacon/egg one.

1. mince and mash the garlic with the anchovies to form a paste and , in a bowl , whisk together paste , yolks , vinegar , mustard , worcestershire sauce , salt and lemon juice
2. add oil in a stream , whisking , until it is emulsified
3. toss romaine with parmesan and croutons in a bowl
4. add dressing and toss well to coat
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made a Casesar salad with chicken yesterday and used this recipe.  It was great. For me this also was the closest to restaraunt taste that I've found. Store bought just doesn't come close. However, I was out of fresh garlic and used powder. Next time though I will use fresh and I may adjust the vinegars a little and maybe try anchovy paste instead of fillets since it will spread better throughout the dressing. Still it was excellent!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
target.review: Delicious!  I made this even easier, by using frozen chicken breast, place in pan.  Mix wet ingredients in a bowl and pour over chicken.  Mix dry ingredients in a bowl and sprinkle over chicken.  Fast, easy, and just as delicious.  I also tried this with chicken thighs and it was very good (use less garlic!! just 1 tsp of the garlic powder).  Everyone I served this to, really likes it!  Thanks for a new favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww 6 points   sweet and sour pork

from ww take-out tonight. "the sauce in this dish is extremely versatile. try substituting chicken, shrimp, scallops, or even skinless duck breasts for the pork in this recipe."

1. combine the pork with 1 tablespoon of the cornstarch in a medium bowl
2. toss well to soat and set aside
3. combine the remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch , the water , vinegar , sugar , ketchup , and soy sauce in a small bowl
4. set aside
5. heat a nonstick wok or a large , deep skillet ower medium-high heat until a drop of water sizzles
6. swirl in the oil , then add the pork
7. stir-fry until almost cooked through , 2-3 minutes
8. add the ginger and garlic
9. stir-fry until fragrant , about 30 seconds
10. add the bell pepper and pineapple
11. stir-fry until crisp-tender , about 3 minutes
12. add the vinegar mixture and cook , stirring constantly , until the mixture boils and thickens and the pork is cooked just through , 1-2 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yes, this is a good one!  Great alternative to chinese sweet & sour pork.  Very tasty!  You wouldn't know its good for you!  Looks different from picture, more red sauce in the one I made.  I would make this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai grilled chicken thighs

this is my first recipe - please be kind! my kids love it and when i take it to a bbq everyone wants the recipe. it is a variation on one i found in epicurious a while ago. it is very easy and very yummy!!

1. combine all ingredients except chicken in a bowl
2. mix thoroughly
3. add chicken and leave to marinate at least one hour , preferably longer
4. grill chicken on the bbq , hotplate or in the griller until golden brown and cooked through
5. ususlly you would expect 12 thigh fillets to feed 4 to 6 people- in my family the kids eat 4 each so this recipe serves 3
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  I didn't have cilantro or fish sauce, but added a little water to make up for it, and it turned out excellent!  Also, I steamed frozen chicken breast till almost fully cooked, added the ingredients and then threw it on the BBQ for 5 min.  This way it was tender on the inside, nicely BBQ on the outside, and favour was delicious throughout!  Great recipe, the whole family loved it!  A new favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
belly buster

this recipe is in about its third or fourth generation, passed down from grandma to mom to me. it became my children's favorite, and now my grandchildren love it. it was a staple in each household, with or without the hamburger. the children named it 

1. this recipe can be made vegetarian , leave out the hamburger and add 2 cups of fresh mixed vegetables , i
2. e
3. broccoli , mushrooms , spinach , carrots , etc
4. cook elbow macaroni "al dente" , according to instructions on box , drain , add to large casserole
5. scramble fry hamburger with spanish onion and garlic , if using , until no longer pink , drain any fat through colander , add drained mixture to casserole
6. add cheese soup , no water , to casserole
7. add tomatoes to casserole
8. add salt and pepper to taste
9. mix thoroughly , in casserole , to evenly distribute ingredients
10. spread grated or sliced cheddar evenly over top of casserole
11. preheat oven to 400 degrees , bake , uncovered for 30 minutes or util bubbling around edges of casserole and cheese topping is melted and slightly browned
12. serves 4-6 or with a salad 8
demonstrations.review: I've made this recipe at least two dozen times.  Simple and delicious!  Its my toddler's favorite dish and my husband loves it too!  It tastes similar to Hamburger Helper, only a lot healthier.  I use cherry (baby tomatoes) and cut them in half (so they don't explode when you poke your fork into them), instead of stewed tomatoes.  I find it tastes fresher!  This recipe is worth giving a try, especially if you have picky eaters!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
5. reduce the heat to medium-low and continue simmering and mixing until thickened remove from heat and allow to sit at room temperature while making the chicken balls or you may cool to room temperature then refrigerate until ready to use
6. to make the chicken balls: in a large bowl combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda , garlic powder
7. add in water and sesame oil
8. whisk vigorously until smooth
9. add in chicken pieces
10. using clean handsand mix until well coated
11. heat oil in a deep-fryer or dutch oven to 375 degrees
12. carefully dip the battered chicken pieces in hot oil and fry until golden brown
13. remove to a paper towel
14. sprinkle with seasoning salt immediately after frying if desired
15. serve immediately with sweet and sour sauce
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This one is just for the chicken balls also.  Great batter! perfect!... but I used less cornstarch (only 1/2 C instead of one cup).  Use vegetable oil for deep frying!! (I used canola, bad aftertaste).  For the sauce... I would highly recommend True Lemon Chicken #51884 for the sauce.  Tastes just like takeout but without the MSG!  I will make this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best sweet and sour sauce

this came from taste of home's quick cooking and is much better than anything i've created on my own. the sauce is thick and gooy and goes well with so many things.

1. combine all ingredients in a sauce pan
2. cook over medium heat until thick , stirring constantly
3. pour over chicken , meatballs , smoked sausage , veggies , etc
demonstrations.review: This was good, but not sensational.  I used it to go with Chicken Balls (Chinese).  My family thought it was pretty good, so I'm giving it a higher rating.  Maybe its the way it mixed with that other receipe that didn't taste outstanding.

target.recipe_text:
chicken salad for sandwiches

simple old-fashioned chicken salad which is perfect for sandwiches or stuffing tomatoes. although the recipe calls for boiling uncooked chicken leftover chicken would also work fine and give wonderful flavor to the chicken salad. recipe source: local newspaper

1. place chicken , celery stalk and onion in saucepan with water to cover
2. bring to a boil and simmer 20 minutes or until chicken is done
3. drain and discard onion and celery
4. let chicken cool
5. in a food processor chop chicken
6. in a medium sized bowl combine chicken with mayonnaise , salt& pepper , parsley , dill seed , chopped celery and lemon juice
7. cover and refrigerate until chilled
target.review: I used meat from some fried chicken we had left over, so it wasn't boiled with onion & celery.  But it was still great using the last 3 steps in your recipe.  Great way to use left over chicken!  Thanks!  :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden chicken scampi  yummy    copycat

this is just as good as the olive garden.  on a difficluty scale from 1-5 this is a 3 to make. we just love it! please note: this is an adopted recipe and i hope to make it soonest. if you make it before i do than i would appreciate your feedback. thanks ! zwt region: italy.

1. for white sauce: heat 1 tablespoons butter in sauce pan , add 2 tablespoons flour and cook for 2 minutes on med
2. heat
3. heat stirring constantly
4. slowly add 3 / 4 cup hot milk
5. set aside
6. for scampi sauce: heat butter over low heat
7. add the garlic , italian seasoning , crushed red pepper and black pepper
8. cook for about 2 minutes on low heat
9. add the wine and chicken broth
10. stir until combined
11. add 1 / 4 cup white sauce and cook till slightly thickened
12. flatten tenders , coat w wondra flour & brown in a large skillet , in a little olive till nearly done
13. add the peppers and onions , saute till chicken is done
14. add the sauce
15. saute until everything is warmed
16. add roasted garlic cloves
17. serve over pasta
18. roasted garlic: separate head of garlic into individual cloves still in 'paper'
19. toss in olive oil and wrap tightly in aluminum foil or a small pint sized dish with a lid
20. bake in 350 oven for 30 minute when the garlic has cooled to the touch you should be able to squeeze it out of the 'paper' shell of the individual cloves
demonstrations.review: To make it easier I made the white & scampi sauce all at once, just adding the ingredients for the scampi once the white sauce was ready.  It was a bit thin, so I added 3/4 cup of grated parmesan.  This gave it somewhat of an alfredo flare, but it was very very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I made with hershey's cinnamon chips I'd had around forever (b/c I couldn't find a good recipe for them.)  This was excellent!  Thanks for such a delicious & simple recipe.  I love it that it's rated so high & yet has very basic ingredients.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ice cream cone cupcakes

this is an excellent treat for the kids; sure to bring a smile to their faces!

1. heat oven to 400f
2. prepare batter for cupcakes per instructions on the box
3. pour scant 1 / 4-cup batter into flat-bottomed ice cream cones so they are a little less than half full , or about half full
4. if you fill the cones too much , the cakes will not have a nice , round top
5. place the cones on a baking sheet and bake for 15 to 18 minutes
6. cool and frost , then decorate with sprinkles as desired
demonstrations.review: I took this to a recital (everyone was asked to bring treats) & they were gone before anything else!  I baked as long as I could without burning them, & there was no problem with sogginess when they were eaten 4 hours later.  I also baked in a cupcake pan to avoid the domino effect should one tip over while I placed in oven.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cream of broccoli soup

this recipe is thick and flavorful. simple, delicious, and quick to make. hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. i have added chicken to this soup, very good

1. melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot , and saut onion , garlic and celery until tender
2. add broccoli and broth
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
4. pure soup or mash with potato masher
5. return to heat
6. in small saucepan , over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter , stir in flour and add milk
7. stir until thick and bubbly , add to soup
8. add cheese
9. stir until melted
10. season with pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: I just threw all of the ingredients in the crock pot in the morning, set on high,  & then served for lunch.  This was an easy way to fix your excellent soup for me.  I recommend others try the same approach. Thanks for this great recipe Barb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef roast

very tender, very juicy. makes lots of gravy great over mashed potatoes simple to make. melts in your mouth everyone who's tried this recipe agrees you won't find an easier or better tasting beef roast recipe anywhere.

1. mix gravy , mushrooms , soup mix and italian dressing
2. pour over beef roast
3. bake , covered , for 1 hour 15 minutes per pound at 300f
4. add carrots and / or potatoes during last hour , if desired
5. cooking time is approximate , depending upon how big your roast is
demonstrations.review: I used chicken gravy (it's what I hand on hand) & it was still wonderful!  The roast made the gravy end up very beefy & it smelled incredible while cooking!  (I love recipes that make my home smell great!)

target.recipe_text:
downunder cheese puffs

these are not popovers and have nothing to do with bread. these are very quick snacks that you can whip up during commercial breaks when you are watching tv and you feel like something cheesy. vary the taste with different types of cheeses.

1. beat the egg in the milk
2. mix together with the flour , baking powder , salt and grated cheese
3. put large teaspoonfuls on a cold greased tray
4. bake for 10 minutes in a hot oven 400 degrees fahrenheit
target.review: Love these! So easy to make. They're slightly dense when done, but not as dry as a scone. I was a bit worried when I spooned out the mixture and it was rather wet and not dough like at all but it turned out perfect! Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: great recipe! I used chicken thigh meat diced and added 400g of mushrooms and 3 tomatoes chopped. Though I didn't use the butter. I just added the raw chicken in to the pasta sauce and cook it that way. Would be a great recipe for freezing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: Great, simple recipe. Very easy and they tasted fantastic! I stuck a hersheys kiss in the middle just to add a little extra sweetness and didn't bother with icing. Just one question, the batter was a little too thick so I added a little (3 tbsp) of milk, and later a few of the cup cakes overspilled out?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of applebee s oriental chicken salad by todd wilbur

this recipe is from www.topsecretrecipes.com. this actually tastes like the salad from applebees. it is a bit of work, but worth every second!!

1. preheat oil in deep fryer or deep pan over medium heat
2. you want the temperature of the oil to be around 350 degrees
3. blend together all ingredients for dressing in a small bowl with an electric mixer
4. put dressing in refrigerator to chill while you prepare the salad
5. in a small , shallow bowl beat egg , add milk , and mix well
6. in another bowl , combine flour with corn flake crumbs , salt and pepper
7. cut chicken breast into 4 or 5 long strips
8. dip each strip of chicken first into egg mixture then into the flour mixture , coating each piece completely
9. fry each chicken finger for 5 minutes or until coating has darkened to brown
10. prepare salad by tossing the chopped romaine with the chopped red cabbage , napa cabbage , and carrots
11. sprinkle sliced green onion on top of the lettuce
12. sprinkle almonds over the salad , then the chow mein noodles
13. cut the chicken into small bite-size chunks
14. place the chicken onto the salad forming a pile in the middle
15. serve with salad dressing drizzled over it or on the side
demonstrations.review:
An amazing dressing! Although I did cut down a little on the mayo and honey, added some extra virgin olive oil and some lemon juice. 

For the chicken instead of frying used a piece of brined chicken breast, pounded it thin then crumbed and oven baked it to save on the oil. Definitely will make this again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pete s scratch pancakes

it was the fall of 1987 when pete nyhus walked into our office, just to visit. we started talking about breakfast, and he reached into a wastepaper basket and pulled out a scrap of teletype paper. he wrote out this recipe, and my family has never used pre-mix since.

1. mix the dry items first
2. combine the eggs and melted butter to the milk and slowly stir into the flour mixture
3. let sit at least 10 minutes while heating the pan
4. these will be high , but light and fluffy --
demonstrations.review: Just like everyone says, this is a top notch recipe. WOW they're fluffy, soft and just fabulous. I had to run back to the computer to double check that it was tablespoons not teaspoons when it came to the baking powder part, but now I know why it's like that! Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
malva pudding  south african baked dessert

this is more delicious than the sum of its parts! it's a real traditional oldie. retested on 22 oct 07: after reading the reviews, i have just made this again. i cut down a little on the sugar in the sauce (it was 5 oz originally), but it should actually be a sweet pudding!! the sauce was quite enough to moisten the entire pudding -- it should not be dripping with sauce, as you can see in the photographs. do not serve immediately, but let it stand, keeping warm, to give the sauce a chance to soak in properly. real cold-weather comfort food. it's rich, so a little goes a long way, and this pudding yields up to 6 servings. this winter you must try this!

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f / 180 deg celsius
2. grease an oven dish
3. i used a 7 x 7 x 1 1 / 2 inch pyrex dish
4. beat or whip the sugar and eggs
5. it's quickest in a food processor , or use electric beaters
6. beat until thick and lemon coloured , then add the jelly and mix through
7. melt the butter and add the butter and vinegar to the wet mixture
8. sieve , or simply mix together: the flour , soda and salt
9. add this mixture with the milk to the egg mixture in the processor or mixing bowl
10. beat well
11. pour into an oven-proof dish and bake until pudding is brown and well-risen -- depending on your oven and oven dish this will be between 30 - 45 minutes
12. in a pot , melt together the ingredients for the sauce , and stir well
13. pour it over the pudding as soon as it comes out of the oven
14. leave to stand awhile before serving
15. serve warm
16. because it's rich it does not really need enhancement , but if you want , serve with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: A delicious recipe, very much for the super super sweet toothed. South African's love their desserts very, very sweet so if you're not used to that much richness I'd cut back on the syrup amount. I didn't find the cake too dry with only half the amount of syrup and it was very rich with the full amount. A great vinegar/baking soda recipe. I'd say this is very similar to a sticky date pudding or butterscotch pudding. Thanks so much for the recipe, will be making more of this in the future!! Oh yes and make sure yo have a mug of cold milk on hand when serving this, yummy!

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate pie

this is a very good recipe for peanut butter chocolate pie. freeze this for storage or for a summer treat.

1. in a large bowl beat cream cheese until smooth
2. add peanut butter and 1 cup of the sugar
3. beat until well blended
4. in a small bowl beat 1 / 2 cup of whipping cream until soft peaks form
5. gradually beat in remaining 1 / 4 cup sugar and vanilla
6. slowly fold cream mixture into peanut butter mixture
7. pour into cooled pie shell
8. for the topping-in a double boiler over hot but not boiling water melt chocolate and cream together , whisking until smooth
9. cool to luke warm and then pour over pie
10. you may need to rock the pie back and forth to get even coverage
11. one inch in from the edge form a circle with the chopped nuts and then chill for at least 2 hours
12. once topping has set you can cover with plastic wrap
13. you can freeze this pie for storage or for a frozen summer treat
