target.review: Made this for a coworkers birthday party today at the office. Total hit! I used a pre-made chocolate crust to make it even easier -- definitely DECADENT. So stick to slimmer slices to keep from chocolate overload, but you'll probably revisit the pie often....if it lasts!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry cheesecake bars

easy summer dessert from kraft. i actually made these as blackberry, rather than blueberry, and substituted a 21-ounce can of blackberry pie filling i had on hand for the jam and the blueberries.

1. preheat oven to 350f combine butter and graham cracker crumbs and press firmly and evenly onto bottom of 9 x 13-inch baking pan
2. beat cream cheese until smooth
3. add sugar , eggs and vanila , beating until well blended
4. set aside
5. stir jam until softened and spread evenly over crust
6. sprinkle with blueberries
7. top with cream cheese mixture
8. bake 30 minutes or until slightly puffed
9. cool completely in pan
10. refrigerate leftover bars for up to 3 days
demonstrations.review: These were a big hit at a BBQ I took them to. There were lots of expletives being thrown around about them (but in a good way). I had a similar problem to others though -- the crust was a bit soggy and so they were hard to cut out and keep their square-ish shape. However, they tasted just fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moldavian potato  feta and scallion salad

this salata de cartofi cu brinza is a delightful alternative to traditional potato salad. the recipe calls for red skinned potatoes, but it's grand with others too. originally from please to the table, a russian cookbook.

1. clean and cook potatoes in boiling water until tender , 18-20 minutes
2. chop , press and crumble other ingredients
3. cool potatoes until they can be handled , then dice into 3 / 4-inch cubes
4. toss with olive oil and garlic , then let fully cool to room temperature
5. add feta and scallions and drizzle with vinegar
6. add dill , salt& pepper , and toss gently
7. let rest for at least 1 hour to allow flavors to mingle
8. add optional garnish and serve
demonstrations.review: Brought this to a picnic -- huge hit! I had a little leftover that I shared with some Russian friends to get their opinion, and they were into it, too. They were glad it wasn't the typical mayo-saturated American potato salad. Very easy to prep and has a nice flavor with the added feta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buffalo chicken filled tortilla cups

these are a fun little appetizer or snack from rachael ray

1. place a small sauce pot over low heat , add hot sauce
2. whisk in the butter until melted
3. in a medium-size bowl , mix the pulled chicken with the hot sauce mixture and set aside
4. in a small mixing bowl , mix the sour cream and blue cheese and season with salt and pepper
5. to assemble the cups , place a spoonful of the buffalo chicken mixture in a tortilla cup and put a little dollop of the blue cheese sour cream on top
6. sprinkle with chives and serve
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very good! I didn't do the individual chips b/c I had to feed a huge crowd but this combo worked great for a big platter of nachos. I also used unsalted butter, like TeresaS, to cut down on the possible saltiness and loaded up on the hot sauce (I like it spicy). The blue cheese-sour cream dressing was a big hit with my nacho noshers. I bought a block of blue cheese (rather than the store bought dressing) and mixed it with the sour cream. Very good. I used the leftover chicken and sour cream sauce the next day on a baked potato.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip peanut butter ball cookies

these wonderful cookies stay in a ball shape and are fantastic! my sister shared this recipe with me and her hint was to keep them stored in the refrigerator, which i have to agree- almost tastes like candy! very good! we both double this recipe each time we make it.

1. combine all the above ingredients and roll into balls , then roll into sugar
2. place on cookie sheet
3. bake at 350 for 10 minutes , no longer !
4. let cool , if you can--
demonstrations.review: These were very easy and very good. I only had chocolate chunks (not chips) and the two cups proved too much -- made them hard to roll together. Next time I'll cut out a half cup -- just so they form more solid balls and there's more peanut buttery goodness. I also had to cook them for another 3 or so minutes, but I believe that's my oven. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scandinavian almond bars

this has become a family favorite every year! if i don't make it my whole family teases me. i am sure that your family will love it too!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. stir together flour , baking powder and salt
3. in a large bowl beat margarine or butter till softened
4. add sugar and beat till fluffy
5. add egg and the 1 / 2 teaspoon of almond extract and beat well
6. add the flour mixture and beat till well mixed
7. divide the dough into fourths , form each portion into a 12 inch roll
8. place 2 of the rolls 4 to 5-inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten each roll till it is about 3 inches wide
10. repeat with the remaining rolls
11. brush each flattened roll with milk and sprinkle about 2 tablespoons of almonds each
12. bake in a 325 oven for 12-14 minutes or till edges are lightly brown
13. while still warm , cut crosswise on the diagonal into 1 inch strips
14. cool completely on a wire rack
15. stir together the powdered sugar , the almond extract and enough of the 3-4 teaspoons of milk to make a drizzling consistency
16. drizzle over the cool bars
demonstrations.review: I like that they were chewy and no one flavor was overpowering the rest. Rocket K, Food.com's awesome designer, brought these for a cookie tasting at our office this past week. They looked and tasted wonderful!

target.recipe_text:
kentucky chocolate gravy

my dad told me how my great-grandmother would make chocolate gravy and biscuits and my curiosity was piqued. this is the recipe we worked together to create. it is very simple and takes only a few minutes.

1. in a medium saucepan , melt the butter over medium-high heat
2. add cocoa powder and stir together
3. add the sugar and 2 cups of milk to the pan---add the milk slowly , stirring constantly
4. mix the cornstarch and remaining 1 / 4 cup of milk until smooth
5. stir into pan
6. allow the contents to boil , but stir constantly until the mixture thickens into a gravy-like consistency
7. it shouldn't take more than 1 or 2 minutes
8. add more milk , if necessary
9. serve over hot biscuits and butter
target.review: My motherinlaw also made chocolate gravy for her children and grandkids.The only thing different was that she used flour instead of cornstarch.Iam afraid I never tried it myself ,but the kids liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp for one

i was fumbling around the kitchen today looking for a quick bite to eat. when my kids aren't here is when i get to experiment. this is an easy shrimp recipe. most of the ingredients are pre-cooked which saves on clean up time.

1. in a small skillet add the olive oil , garlic , crushed red peppers and minced onion flakes
2. heat on medium high heat for 5 minutes , stirring ocassionally
3. in a separate sauce pan cook the fettuccine noodles per package directions
4. add the chopped red and green peppers to the skillet and saute for another couple minutes
5. reduce heat to medium and add the shrimp and bacon
6. cook the shrimp until most of the liquid is gone
7. when the noodles are done , drain them and place them on an oven safe plate
8. spoon out the shrimp mixture onto the noodles and sprinkle the parmesan cheese and italian seasoning on top
9. sprinkle the shredded mozzarella cheese over all and place under the broiler at 500 degrees until the mozzarella just begins to melt
10. remove from the oven and enjoy
demonstrations.review: I got some cooked shrimp on sale and found this recipe to try.This was so good and pretty also.I used roasted red bell pepper.Also added some mushroom and 2c.chopped broccoli cooked.This served two.Thanks SJM

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla puff pancake

this is such a wonderful breakfast.  it's sweet and comforting, yet packed with protein to give the kids a good start to the day.  super easy to make.  you can even make the batter the night before and throw it in the oven the next morning.  for a variation, omit the vanilla bean and add a chopped granny smith apple.

1. place butter in a baking dish and pop into a 200c / 400f oven
2. whisk eggs and add milk , sugar , flour and vanilla extract
3. slice vanilla pod in half and use a knife to extract the seeds
4. add seeds to batter and mix to disperse
5. remove baking dish from oven and swirl to coat sides with butter
6. pour batter into it and return to oven
7. bake for 20-25 minutes or until puffed up and golden
8. serve immediately as it will deflate once out of the oven
demonstrations.review: I hope everyone will try this,it is so good and could not be easier to make.I used 1 TBS. of good vanilla and it smelled and tasted wonderful.I baked it 9" heavy non stick round cake pan.Thank you for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shortbread cookies with jam or jelly centers

do not be fooled by this little recipe.  so few ingredients but believe me!  it-is-a one right after another pop it in your mouth oh i cannot stop eating these.  before you know it, you will have to make another batch for the rest of your family.  i got this from my best friend robin who got it form her taste of home cookbook.

1. cream butter and sugar
2. beat in extract
3. gradually blend in flour
4. cover and refrigerate for an hour
5. roll into one-inch balls and place one inch apart on un-greased cookie sheet
6. with the end of a wooden spoon make a indention in the ball and fill with jam
7. i have used variety of jams and jellies raspberry being the best ! but apricot is yummmie too , along with apple , blackberry , blueberry the possibilities are endless
8. bake at 350 for 14 to 18 minute
demonstrations.review: These are very good.I didn't fill with jam.I added 1 cup dark chocolate and raspberryswirled chips,rolled into balls and baked .Then sprinkled with pwd sugar.I know the jam would be good also. Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
good  n  gooey fresh peach cobbler

this is a real texas peach cobbler with an abundance of juicy fruit and a sweet, biscuit-like batter topping that is crunchy on the surface and doughy inside. this recipe comes from cheryl and bill jamison.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a bowl , mix together all the filling ingredients
3. set aside
4. the filling will be a bit juicier than most pies
5. melt butter in a 9x13 baking dish in the oven
6. in another bowl , stir together flour , sugar , and baking powder , and then add the milk
7. mix until lightly blended
8. spoon the mixture evenly over the melted butter
9. do not stir
10. pour the peach filling evenly over batter
11. bake 45 minutes
12. serve warm , with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream if desired
demonstrations.review: Miss Annie,This is delicious.I used 8 very large peaches that were ripe and juicy sweet so I added juice of one lemon and omited ginger.I used brown sugar splenda in peaches and half sugar and half granular splenda in the batter.About fifteen minutes before done I sprinkled top with raw sugar and let melt in oven till done. Thank you for a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s tater soup

not my granny, she was too busy shopping at bloomingdale's! if we ever do find the granny that invented this soup we want to adopt her, this is super comfort food, very popular during the winter in our house.

1. place all ingredients , except chives and milk , in a 4 quart slow cooker
2. cover and cook on low for 7 to 8 hours or on high for 3 to 4 hours
3. stir in milk and chives during last hour of cooking
demonstrations.review: Theres nothing better than potato soup on a cold day!To make a full meal I like to add some cooked ham,smoked sausage or crisp bacon and stir in some cheese at the end.I just make mine on the stove,its done in less than 30 min.

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin chocolate chip bread muffins

this was originally a bread recipe, but i always make them as muffins! it's definitely a favorite, and can easily be halved. cooking time is for the bread.

1. mix all ingredients
2. if making loaves , pour into greased pans and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour or until knife comes out clean
3. if making muffins , fill greased or paper-lined tins 3 / 4 full and bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until set
target.review: This was quite good.  (Although I sent it in to DH's work for a company bake sale, so we didn't get to enjoy it ourselves too much!)  I didn't have any chocolate chips, so I used white chocolate chips instead.  My DH loved it that way!  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best pumpkin cookies

what can i say about these amazing pumpkin cookies... they are absolutely delicious! let me put it this way. i baked these every year at thanksgiving time for my job. my co-workers would come up to me two months in advance to make sure i was making them. one girl who resigned actually called me and asked what day i was bringing them in so that she could stop by - just for these cookies! another co-worker said she didn't even like pumpkin, but she loved these. the consistency is more cake-like than cookie. the glaze on top of these cookies is fabulous! at least, i think so. i noticed a few of you who rated this recipe said it was too sweet. that is why i suggested it may be omitted, or if you wish, use your own icing. lots of you have added nutmeg.. hey, make it all your own. that's what this is all about! : )

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. have ready some ungreased baking sheets
3. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and the sugars together until light and fluffy
4. blend in pumpkin , egg and vanilla extract
5. in separate bowl , stir together flour , baking soda , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg and salt
6. mix flour mixture into butter-sugar mixture
7. drop tablespoonfuls 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. bake the cookies for 10-12 minutes until golden around the edges
9. remove warm cookies and transfer to racks
10. let cool completely for a least one half hour , then frost with glaze
11. for glaze:
12. in a medium saucepan , heat butter and brown sugar over medium heat until bubbly
13. cook , stirring constantly , for one minute or until slightly thickened
14. beat in the milk
15. blend in confectioner's sugar until the glaze is smooth and spreadable
16. using a silicone basting brush , which i love and use religiously now , or a butter knife to spread glaze on cookies is the best
17. please
18. i suggest that you keep the saucepan over the stove on the lowest heat possible to prevent it from hardening
demonstrations.review: Wow, these are yummy.  I sent the ones I didn't eat into work w/ dh for his Christmas party.  He had a few requests for the recipe.  Don't pass on the glaze, it really sets these cookies apart.  Do be careful when you are putting the glaze on, it's extremely HOT!  I burned myself a couple of times not paying attention :).  These are going to become a Christmas classic at my house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lunch in a loaf

my brother is in construction and needs an easy, high-protein, low mess lunch each day. i started making these for him in large batches and freezing them. he just takes one out of the freezer each morning and it's ready to eat by lunchtime!

1. combine 1 1 / 2 c flour , yeast , sugar , salt and basil
2. beat eggs and oil together
3. add egg mixture and hot milk to dry ingredients
4. mix and then add remaining flour , turning out onto a board to knead when consistency allows
5. return to bowl and set in warm place to rise
6. punch down dough , divide into four balls
7. roll each ball out into a 8" circle
8. add filling to one half , fold over , pinch edges shut like a pie crust
9. bake 20- 25 minutes at 350f
10. filling suggestions:
11. i use whatever is left in the fridge ! beans , stew , veggies , meat
12. here are a few "recipes"
13. cooked chicken breast , chopped in small pieces , canned corn , barbecue sauce
14. tuna salad , cheddar cheese
15. canned beef stew cheddar cheese
16. make up your own !
demonstrations.review: This recipe is amazing!  My hubby loves the crust, and I love the chance to use up leftovers in the fridge and have his lunch ready in the freezer.  I've made them with ham and bean and pulled pork so far, but the possibilities are endless!  Thanks for a great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the fix for leftover mashed potatoes

this is a tasty way to fix leftover mashed potatoes so they don't feel like leftovers. sometimes i make too many potatoes on purpose, so i can make this up and refrigerate it for later in the week.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. mix the potatoes , green onions , onion powder , black pepper and sour cream
3. spread mixture evenly in a greased baking dish and sprinkle with bacon and grated cheese
4. bake approximately 20 minutes until mixture is hot and cheese melted
demonstrations.review: I used some leftover ham instead of bacon.  So yummy!  What a great way to use up these leftovers... I've always thrown them out since they don't reheat well.  Now we'll be sure to make leftovers ;).  Even my 3 year old liked them and he never eats mashed potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was just ok.  Thought DH would love it since he is a mayo fanatic, but even he thought it was just ok.  I probably won't be adding this to my usuals pile.  Guess we just have different taste than many other people on this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple core and peeling jelly

posted in response to a request. i haven't tried this, but love the idea of using that which would normally be tossed to make something delightful. cook time is approximate and does not include water bath time.

1. cook peelings and cores in 6 cups water for 20-30 minutes
2. strain through prepared cheesecloth or jelly bag
3. add water as needed , to strained juice , to obtain 7 cups liquid
4. add pectin and bring to a rapid boil
5. add sugar , boil hard for 1 minute
6. pour into sterile jars , leaving 1 / 8" headspace
7. wipe jar rims , adjust lids and rings
8. water bath 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at jam and jelly.  I used the leftovers from my jam to make this jelly, and it turned out yummy!  It was very easy to make, and my boys just love it.  I did boil it for 2 minutes, but even then it's not quite as thick as I like.  Next time I may reduce the juice by 1/2 a cup or so?  Other than that, I LOVE this recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
thanksgiving pumpkin crunch cake dessert

my family will give up a pumpkin pie for this! ---- two teaspoons of pumpkin pie spice may be used in place of the cinnamon, nutmeg and allspice --- i have made this using both the white and yellow cake mix i have to say that the yellow is better to use.

1. set oven 350 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a bowl combine the pumpkin puree , evaporated milk , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice and salt
4. mix until well combined
5. pour into prepared baking pan
6. sprinkle the cake mix evenly over the top of the pumpkin mixture
7. sprinkle the chopped nuts over the cake mix
8. drizzle the melted butter or margarine evenly over the top
9. bake for about 55-60 minutes
10. cool completely , then pipe the whipped cream over the top of the cooled cake
target.review: Made this last night to see if I wanted it for Thanksgiving.  Let my 4 yr old daughter have it for breakfast because she usually has pumpkin bread.  She said, Mama, you should make this instead from now on.  I think that says everything! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken katsu

katsu are boneless strips of chicken,or pork that are breaded; fried and served with a dipping sauce.  a staple at hawaii restaurants, it has its roots in japanese cuisine

1. to make katsu sauce , combine catsup , soy sauce , sugar , worcestershire sauce and red pepper in a small bowl and set aside
2. flatten chicken pieces into 1 / 4 inch thick pieces
3. season chicken generously with garlic salt , and let stand 15 to 30 minutes
4. set up three dredging pans
5. place flour in the first , beaten eggs in the second and panko flakes in the third
6. heat about 2 inches of oil in a skillet to 350 degrees
7. dredge chicken in flour , dip in eggs and coat with panko in that order
8. fry chicken in batches until golden brown on both sides
9. drain on paper towels
10. cut into one inch slices and serve hot with katsu sauce
11. pork can be substituted for chicken
demonstrations.review: I get to go to Hawaii for the first time in a month, but I'm lucky enough to have an L&L restaurant where I live and this is just as good as theirs!! So glad I found this! My husband lives it and my BIL says it's the best chicken he's ever had! I ALWAYS double the sauce and it's barely enough!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buffalo chicken for sandwiches

this is based on a tyson foods recipe that i tried and loved!! feel free to use wraps instead of deli rolls

1. place chicken between layers of plastic wrap or waxed paper
2. pound lightly with rolling pin or meat mallet to flatten
3. place 3 tablespoons blue cheese salad dressing in shallow baking dish
4. coat chicken lightly with dressing
5. dip in flour to coat
6. melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat
7. add chicken to skillet cook , 5 minutes on one side to brown cook 5 minutes on the other side to brown
8. when cooked through , remove chicken from skillet
9. drain butter from skillet except for 1 tablespoon
10. add hot pepper sauce and stir to mix with butter
11. return to heat and add chicken
12. cook chicken 2 minutes on each side in pepper sauce
13. serve chicken on toasted buns with spinach leaves
14. serve blue cheese dressing on the side
demonstrations.review: My 4 year old daughter loved this chicken (w/out hot sauce) and ate it all.  I just put salt and pepper in the flour.  My DH who rarely says anything loved it and said it was most definitely a "make again".  Thanks for the easy, delicious dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy tuna or chicken noodle casserole

this is a delicious casserole that can be made using either tuna or 1-1/2 cups or more of cooked cubed chicken or even cooked turkey
 --- for a thinner sauce use 1 cup of milk or half and half instead of 3/4 cup, prep time includes boiling the egg noodles, if you are not a garlic-lover then you may omit the garlic powder and to zing the flavor up even more add in 1-1/2 tablespoons of lemon juice

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. grease a 2-quart casserole dish
3. cook the egg noodles in boiling salted water
4. drain then toss with 2 tablespoons butter
5. in a large saucepan , mix the undiluted mushroom soup , garlic powder , parmesan cheese milk or half and half , sour cream , salt , pepper , chopped onion , pimiento , bell pepper and celery
6. cook over low heat , stirring frequently for 15 minutes
7. add in the tuna or chicken
8. mix to combine
9. combine the mixture with the cooked egg noodles
10. transfer to prepared greased baking dish
11. sprinkle top with the broken ritz crackers
12. bake for about 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: As if this needed another review..but this was so good. I was craving the classic from childhood and found it. I did leave out all the veggies, did not have parmesan, and forgot to butter the noodles and used two cans of tuna and it came out exactly how I remembered my mom making! I too wanted to add peas but didn't have any buy will next time. Thanks again for another winner Kittencal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mustard baked pork chops w brie

swift & company provides this recipe which surely would have to rank in the "top 10" of ways to turn the ordinary pork chop into something extraordinary. it's an easy fix & the use of dijon mustard & brie cheese provides its "french connection".

1. in a sml bowl , combine seasoned breadcrumbs , parsley , melted butter , garlic & thyme
2. set crumb mixture aside
3. in a wide , shallow bowl combine flour , coriander , salt & pepper
4. evenly coat both sides of ea chop w / mustard & then coat w / flour mixture
5. heat oil in skillet over med-hi heat
6. brown chops well on ea side & place in a shallow baking dish
7. cut brie in half & then cut again horizontally to form thin half-circles & place 1 on ea chop
8. spoon crumb mixture on top of cheese-covered chops
9. bake in a 400f oven for 20 minutes or till breadcrumbs are golden & chops just done
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: WOW! This is AMAZING.  My 4 year old ate it (without the brie) and LOVED the "crunchies" on top.  She ate every single piece.  My DH who is a cheese fanatic was really impressed also.  Thank you for helping me make something potentially boring spectacular!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork and vegetable lo mein  easy and delicious

my family loves this hearty main dish. i get requests for it often. it's very quick and easy to prepare, great for when you're in a hurry. you can buy a couple of the ingredients already prepared in the produce section of the grocery store, if you like.

1. already shredded--a real time saver
2. heat 2 tbsp olive oil in a large skillet or wok
3. saut pork , onion , garlic and pepper flakes until meat is no longer pink
4. remove this mixture from pan and keep warm
5. add remaining tbsp of oil to pan and saut cabbage , bok choy or celery , carrots and peppers until crisp tender
6. add spaghetti to cooked veggies in the pan
7. stir in soy sauce and add pork mixture back to the pan
8. cook for 5 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was really good and really quick.  Pork came out bland, so I think next time I will add some soy sauce in the beginning stage, but the noodles were awesome.. even leaving out the celery/bok choy, and bell pepers (personal tastes).  Thanks! Will definitely use again!

target.recipe_text:
comfort food rice pudding

it's perfect if you are craving rice pudding and have no milk or eggs. i love this, rich and flavorful but it's best if you eat it on the first day.

1. put rice in the top of a double boiler set over simmering water
2. add salt and 3 c water
3. coverand cook till rice is tender , about 30 minutes
4. stir in the sweetened condensed milk , butter , and raisins if desired
5. cook and stir frequently over simmering water till the puddings thickens slightly , about 20 minutes
6. remove the top dish with the pudding in it from the heat and stir in the vanilla and cinnamon
7. spoon into custard cups and eat warm or chill
8. we like ours with a little raspberry sauce or jam
target.review: I found this recipe while going through some recipes of my Grandmothers. I remembered how good it is and was going to post it but, here it is!  This pudding is so easy to make, you can't mess it up. It is absolutely delicious! I highly recommend it!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate creme brulee

dark and decadent.  a must for the true chocolate lover!  make a day ahead as this requires overnight chilling time - but well worth the wait!  this recipe comes from the enchantment resort in sedona, arizona.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees f
2. bring cream and half and half to boil in heavy sauce pan
3. reduce heat to low
4. add chocolate and whisk until melted and smooth
5. remove from heat
6. whisk yolks and 1 / 3 cup sugar in large bowl to blend
7. gradually whisk in hot chocolate mixture
8. strain
9. divide custard among eight 3 / 4-cup custard cups
10. place cups in large baking pan
11. add enough hot water to pan to come halfway up sides of cups
12. bake until custards are set , about 50 minutes
13. remove from water
14. chill 2 hours
15. cover and refrigerate overnight
16. preheat broiler
17. sprinkle each custard with 1 tbs sugar
18. broil until sugar turns golden , watching carefully to avoid burning , about 3 minutes
19. refrigerate until custards are set , 1-2 hours
demonstrations.review: Oh my!  This is to die for and is a must for chocoholics.  I received a Creme Brulee Gift Set for Christmas and was excited to try out my little butane torch and I am so happy I chose this recipe to do so.  I only made one half of the recipe since I only had 4 of the Creme Brulee dishes. I will get 4 more and serve this at my next dinner party. I know everyone would be very happy. Thank you Bev...Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the lady and sons easy peach cobbler   paula deen

it was an instant hit on the first day paula deen offered this dessert at the lady & sons, and remains so today. this delicious cobbler can be found on their dessert trays at both lunch and dinnertime.
 it's so easy to make you won't believe it! cooks notes: if they are available by all means use fresh peaches. in a saucepan, mix two cups fresh peach slices with one cup sugar and one cup water. bring to a boil, reduce heat, and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring occasionally. an almost equally good product is frozen peach slices. simply follow the instructions for the fresh peach slices. note: this is an adopted (late in 2006) recipe and there was already some discussion about the amount of butter necessary in reviews made previous to my inheriting this recipe: now that i have made it myself, i can say that for me at least, 60 grams (1/4 cup) of butter was fine, (by all means use a little less if you prefer) and my dumplings didn't turn out doughy at all... what i did mess up was using a larger can of peaches (non-metric sizes of canned fruit don't translate perfectly into metric ones), so i thought that the extra wouldn't matter much, mine was swimming rather a lot in the juice at the bottom and next time i will use all the peaches but only half or 3/4 of the juice from my metric sized can.. taste was excellent and guests devoured it. i'm delighted to have inherited this recipe, so to both paula deen and the previous zaar owner: thanks for an excellent recipe !!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. place butter in oven in a 2-quart baking dish to melt
3. stir sugar and flour together and mix well
4. slowly add milk and continue to stir to prevent the batter from lumping
5. being careful not to burn yourself , remove hot baking dish containing melted butter from oven
6. pour batter directly over butter in baking dish
7. spoon fruit on top of batter , then gently pour syrup on top
8. sprinkle with cinnamon , if using
9. the most important part of this dish is not stirring the mixture
10. bake for 30 to 45 minutes or until golden brown
11. your batter will rise above your fruit , producing the most wonderful of crusts
12. serve warm with vanilla ice cream or fresh whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I made this cobbler following the same recipe that is in my “Paula Deen’s Kitchen Classics” cookbook.  I didn’t see the need in printing it from here, as I assumed they were one in the same.  I guess the recipe in Paula’s Cookbook is incorrect.  It has the same five ingredients and the same method of preparation, but calls for one stick of butter.  In my review, which was honest but negative, I commented that one stick of butter was too much for us.  This chef was quick to point out my error, and I promptly changed my review, pointing out my mistake and gave it two stars.  In the spirit of fairness, I made another cobbler using the correct amount of butter (4 tablespoons) as the above recipe calls for.  I am sorry to say, we still did not care for it. It was still lacking in taste and still doughy.  When I went to change my review again, I noticed this chef is asking you to disregard my review.  I just what to give my honest review and point out the error in Paula’s cookbook.  I would hate you to make the mistake of using the wrong recipe, thus ruining your cobbler.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruth s chris steak house creamed spinach

love their steaks, and i love their version of this classic side dish to a thick, juicy steak. sometimes i cheat and use 2 10 ounce packages of frozen, chopped spinach which i thaw and drain.

1. melt 4 tablespoons butter in heavy medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add flour and stir until light golden , about 7 minutes
3. stir in onion , bay leaf and clove
4. gradually whisk in milk
5. whisk until mixture boils and thickens , about 10 minutes
6. reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes longer , whisking frequently
7. remove bay leaf and whole clove
8. cook spinach in large pot of boiling water just until wilted and tender , about 2 minutes
9. drain
10. transfer spinach to bowl filled with ice water to cool
11. drain well
12. roll up spinach in kitchen towl and squeeze out as much liquid as possible
13. transfer spinach to processor and finely chop
14. add spinach to warm sauce , simmer over low heat until spinach is heated through , stirring often , about 5 minutes
15. stir in remaining 2 tablespoons of butter
16. season to taste with salt and pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: I had to make this for myself, as I am the only spinach lover in the house. They don't know what they are missing!  I didn't and wouldn't change a thing! The only thing that would have made it better; a piece of Ruths Chris Carmelized Banana Cream Pie, for dessert! Thanks yooper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This was awesome! So tender, it melted in our mouths.  I cooked mine on low. After adding rinsed bean and corn, I put my  chunky salsa into a bowl and mixed in 1 pkg. taco seasoning mix, 4 large cloves minced garlic and 1 seeded & chopped jalapeno. After about 8 hrs. I removed the chicken, turned crockpot to high and added room temp cream cheese. When melted, I stirred utill cream cheese was totally incorporated and returned chicken to pot.  Served over rice and topped with lots of cilantro. Also served corn bread #86228
and Fresh Express Southwestren Salad. Picky son loved it! This recipe will now join the other 2 in my "JT Food" cookbook. Thanks Jen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country white bread or dinner rolls  bread machine

we think this is the best white bread recipe ever! it is a tender bread with a slightly sweet taste. my dinner rolls using this dough are so good, everyone always loves them. it doesn't take to long to make them when the bread maker does most of the work. the cook time is listed for the rolls only because everyone's bread makers cooks at different rates. mine is older and a regular loaf will take 4 hours and 10 minutes. i have found that 15 balls of dough fit perfectly in the 9x13 pan with sides touching after raising the 2nd time but they can be made whatever size you want. i hope you enjoy this great bread as much as we do.

1. in bread machine pan , place all ingredients from flour through yeast in order as recommended by the manufacturer
2. select the basic bread setting
3. check dough after 5 minutes of mixing , if needed add 1-2t of water or flour
4. bake as normal
5. for dinner rolls
6. mix in bread machine but use only the dough option
7. lightly grease a 9 x 13 baking pan
8. when dough is finished shape into 15 uniformly sized balls
9. i always grease my hands with shortening to smooth the dough out and it helps keep the dough from drying out
10. cover and let the rolls rise in a warm , draft free place until risen to the desired size
11. i let them about double in size
12. bake in a 350 oven about 12-15 minutes until golden brown
13. after removing from the oven , brush the tops of the rolls with melted butter
14. take out of pan and let completely cool before storing
demonstrations.review: Very quick, easy, and yummy. Made on dough cycle using Bread Flour and ABM yeast.  Had to add an additional 1/4 cup of flour. Beautiful dough, made 4 small loaves. I used my oven setting for proofing bread (100F about 30 mins) then baked about 20 mins. We all loved it, especially DS who has requested another batch today. Thank you DDW for sharing your recipe! 10/20 Update: I made another batch today and baked in my ABM.  My loaf was so large that is covered the air vent in the lid.  I had to open and make a small indentation in the vent area.  The bread I baked in the oven was PERFACT! The crust on the bread machine loaf was tough and the texture was waaaay too dense.  It didn't have enough room to bake.  My ABM is a Hitachi and looking at my manual it suggests 3cups of flour for a large loaf.  It could be my bread machine can't handle the recipe. Still a 5 star recipe but I will only bake it in the oven from here on out.  Thanks again DDW for the great, easy recipe.

target.recipe_text:
wiener schnitzel with sauce

i like this recipe as it can be made in one pan & comes with a sauce. from cuisine at home.

1. slice pork into eight 1"-thick pieces
2. pound each piece with a meat mallet to about 1 / 4" thickness
3. season with salt and pepper
4. place flour , eggs , and bread crumbs into three separate shallow dishes
5. dredge each medallion first in flour , then in eggs , and finally in bread crumbs
6. place breaded pork on a baking sheet or plate
7. heat oil and 3 t
8. butter in a large saute pan over medium-high heat
9. saute pork until golden brown , 23 minutes on each side
10. remove from pan and keep warm in a 200 oven
11. deglaze pan with wine
12. add lemon juice and simmer 3 minutes
13. add heavy cream and simmer until reduced by half , about 1 minute
14. off heat , whisk in butter 2 t
15. at a time
16. stir in parsley
17. spoon sauce over medallions
18. serve with lemon wedges
target.review:
Wonderful.
I didn't have any pork but had some turkey cutlets that I didn't know what to do with and I thought "Why not?"
Why not indeed, one of my more successful experments.
Thank you for sharing, this will become a household favorite, the kids loved it.
Lydia

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried blueberry corn fritters

much better for you than deep fried fritters. they go well with any fruit--canned with light syrup are good, but i like just fresh fruit as well, especially strawberries.

1. heat oven to 250f degrees
2. mix together cornmeal , flour , sugar , and baking powder
3. combine egg whites , milk and margarine , mix well
4. pour milk mixture into the dry ingredients , stir until just smooth
5. in a large non stick skillet heat the 2 tbsp oil , heat until quite hot but not smoking
6. drop in a 1 / 4 cup of batter for each fritter
7. cook approx 4-6 minutes on each side
8. keep warm in the oven covered with foil until you have cooked all the fritters
9. serve with blueberries or other fruit
demonstrations.review:
LOL........Wasn't paying attention and did not read the recipe through before starting.......hence a booboo!!!!
I mixed the blueberries into the batter!!!
A "good" mistake, the fritters were still (or maybe even more so)wonderful.  Will make them againg using the "Booboo method".
Thanks for sharing.
Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef egg rolls

this is my first post to zaar.  here's a really tasty recipe from my aunt rose.  what a winner!

1. saute garlic and ginger in oil til brown
2. add onion and cabbage
3. saute until the cabbage is wilted
4. add mixture to the raw meat , carrots , soy sauce , pepper , and 2 eggs
5. mix
6. make an egg wash with the remaining egg
7. brush the edges of the egg roll wrapper
8. put 2t of the filling in the wrapper
9. roll up and fry at 375 degrees til brown
demonstrations.review:
Hey Cruby,
I looked and searched for an egg roll recipe and finally settled on three of them of which yours was one of them and the first one to be made.  Happy happy, never tried the other two as this is a very basic recipe which lends it's self to changes very easily.  Now if I can just find a good sweet and sour sauce and or plum sauce to go with it, I will have it made, shall continue my quest.  Thanks so much for sharing, into the keeper file it goes.....Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger gravy my way

inexpensive way to feed a crowd. definately one of our favorite comfort foods! we love it over baked potatoes!

1. in a large frying pan , brown hamburger , crumbling as you go
2. add minced onion and cook until translucent
3. sprinkle flour over cooked beef , and stir thoroughly
4. cook for 1-2 minutes
5. add 2 cups milk , stir well and add all seasonings at this point
6. simmer , adding more liquid as gravy thickens
7. cook to desired consistancy , and serve over any style potatoes , pasta , rice , or toast
demonstrations.review: I use to do this for the kids when they were small, we called it SOS back then. Didn't use the mustard but if I could afford it added mushrooms.  Thanks for the memories, might fix it again soon.....not now though, to full after doing the eggs and cheese thing.......lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry ranch salad dressing mix

i needed a package of ranch salad dressing mix to make recipe #203830  ...but did i have one?  of course not!  found this recipe on line: i had all the ingredients on hand and went with it!  since there is a dearth of recipes here for dry ranch salad dressing mix, i thought i'd share it!  (from:  cooksrecipes.com)

1. combine all ingredients in the container of a food processor or blender and process on high speed until well blended and powdery smooth
2. store in air-tight container
3. to use mix: combine 1 tablespoon dry mix with 1 cup milk and 1 cup mayonnaise , mix well
4. makes 2 cups
demonstrations.review:
And thank you so much for sharing.
MY twin boys were starving, as usual (had just finished a substantial dinner a couple of hours before)/  I had chips on hand and veggies but no dip.  Went on a hunt and found this one which looked and sounded good, also had everything on hand. Quickly put it together and saved the day.  
Had some left over and it was twice as good this morning.  So I guess the trick here is to make it the day before you need it.
Thanks for a keeper my dear, and my boys thank you too.
Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa  potato  and onion skillet

this one-pot, easy dish is warm and satisfying. serve with a crisp green salad. i use yukon gold potatoes, but any potato will work.

1. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
2. add potatoes , onions , garlic , and pepper
3. fry until potatoes are golden and onions are translucent , about 8 minutes
4. add kielbasa and cook 1-2 minutes until warm
5. add broth and cover skillet with lid
6. lower heat to medium-low
7. cook until broth is mostly evaporated , 5-10 minutes , and potatoes are tender
8. be careful not to overcook the potatoes
9. if potatoes are not done and broth has evaporated completely , add more chicken broth and continue to cook until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: I too have made this for years with one small addition of shreaded cabbage in porportion to the potatoes, covered it and let it make it's own liquided as it cooked, no oil, I also swithched off the sausage to what ever happened to be on hand but our favorite is smoked. We are garlic lovers so had to add that and celery seed also.  A very good comfort dish and easy to throw together, I use red skinned baby potatoes so they don't need to be peeled (I'm lazy)

target.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
target.review: This was sooo easy to get ready (truly only 5 minutes), and VERY good!  I forgot to add the water... and did not cut the ingredients at all.  My chuck roast was 4.5 lbs & I cooked for 9 hours.  The meat was amazing!  It tasted like oven roasted, and was not overly "mushy".  My uncle used an electric slicer and this meal looked and tasted elegant. I would definitely make again and serve to company!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken garlic bites

simple and fun to make, great to eat! prep time includes marinating the chicken.  use matzo meal instead of the breadcrumbs and this is good for passover as well.

1. place chicken in shallow dish
2. in small bowl , mix olive oil , garlic , and black pepper
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and marinate 30 minutes
5. drain
6. preheat oven to 475f
7. mix bread crumbs and cayenne
8. coat chicken
9. arrange in a single layer on cookie sheet
10. bake 10 minutes or until brown
demonstrations.review: This recipe is soooo easy (I used kitchen sheers to cut my chicken), quick and delicious!!!  Will be making this again.  I doubled the recipe, except for the pepper (I have young kids).  We loved these.  Thank you for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted salmon and rhubarb

with all the rhubarb lovers here i decided to post this recipe from williams-sonoma. if you prefer a thinner sauce, add a splash of white wine.

1. preheat oven to 500 degrees , or its highest temperature
2. in a small saucepan , combine rhubarb and sugar
3. cover and cook over low heat until rhubarb is falling apart , about 20 minutes , adding water if necessary
4. stir in the lemon juice
5. the sauce should be the consistency of applesauce
6. arrange salmon filets , skin side down , on a foil or parchment-lined baking pan
7. season to taste with salt and pepper
8. bake until almost opaque throughout , about 17-20 minutes
9. spoon rhubarb onto center of warmed plates
10. lift fillets from pan , leaving skin behind if desired
11. place fillets on rhubarb
demonstrations.review: I grilled salmon steaks on my George Foreman grill and just followed the rhubarb sauce part of this recipe, minus the lemon juice.  The taste of the salmon and rhubarb together is AMAZING!!!  It was easy too.  I added a little water (about 1/4 cup) and actually boiled it till it fell apart due to shortage of time.  It was delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pampered chef taffy apple pie

mmm what a great blend of flavors! i got this recipe from a friend who served it at a pampered chef party.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. shape dough into a ball at the center of a baking stone or large round pizza pan
3. lightly flour dough and pat out , flattening to 1 / 4 in thick circle
4. bake 16-18 minutes , or until lightly golden brown
5. cool completely
6. mix cream cheese , peanut butter , and vanilla until smooth
7. add brown sugar to the mixture and completely blend
8. spread mixture evenly over cookie
9. arrange apple slices over cream cheese and sprinkle with desired amount of cinnamon
10. heat caramel and drizzle over the top
11. sprinkle with chopped nuts
demonstrations.review: This is one of my favorite recipes to demo at shows and make for my own family.  The combinations of flavors will really make you happy ~ I always share half with my best friend so I don't eat it all myself. Try it is soooo yummy and easier than you think!  I'll try to remember to take a picture the next time I make it. You can find it in All The Best Cookbook, page 92, and in the Use & Care instructions that come with one of the products (I think the Apple, Peeler, Slicer, Corer).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot apricot chicken

posted in response to a request; from company's coming slow cooker recipes.

1. in a bowl , whisk together dressing , jam and soup mix
2. brush each piece of chicken with sauce and place in slow cooker
3. cover chicken with any remaining sauce
4. cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or on high for 3 to 4 hours
demonstrations.review: REALLY good!  I used FROZEN boneless/skinless breasts and chicken remained moist and sauce was perfect.  My 3 year old loved it.  I served with a brown/wild rice, broccoli and romaine lettuce salad.  A wonderful meal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon caper sauce for chicken or fish

a simple sauce to compliment fish, seafood and chicken

1. put broth and garlic in skillet and bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 1-2 minutes til garlic is tender
2. stir in lemon juice and capers
3. remove from heat and add butter stir til melted , add parsley
demonstrations.review: I doubled this recipe and served over flounder (that I grilled on my George Foreman grill - takes 2 minutes).  It was the quickest meal ever, and very elegant!  Yum. I look forward to trying it on chicken or shrimp next.

target.recipe_text:
cast iron skillet baked cornbread

this is the result of the highly successful method of 'trial and error' to find the "perfect" cornbread for my 10" cast iron skillet. enjoy!

this can be baked in other dishes (8x8, 9x9, muffin tins, larger or smaller skillets etc and the doubled recipe fills a 9x13) but i do not have baking times for those.

*updated directions 2/16/2015*

1. position oven rack in the middle of your oven , preheat oven to 350 , place skillet in cold preheating oven in center of the middle rack
2. in a medium bowl combine all dry ingredients
3. in a separate smaller bowl combine wet ingredients , mixing thoroughly
4. combine wet ingredients into dry and mix until well blended
5. slide the oven rack , with the skillet on it , out and place last of the butter into hot skillet
6. immediately pour batter into hot skillet , and slide oven rack into place
7. bake for 18 - 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted into center comes out clean
target.review: Is there anything better than finding a perfect recipe??? This is fabulous cornbread - light, sweet and the directions are spot-on. I only did one thing differently, and that was to swirl the butter in the hot cast iron skillet to coat the sides before adding the batter. My skillet is new and not seasoned for long so I expected the batter to stick. Not so. And by the by, I used butter all the way because, of course, everything IS better with butter. DH loved it and considers it cake (oh these Italians who don't get the concept of sweet/savory.) That said, I may reduce the sugar a bit next time (tonight!) just to see. A thousand thanks Doodle Pirate for working this one out. I now have a happy future without dry or gummy or gritty cornbread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby greens with hazelnut parmesan crisps

fresh peppery salad greens, lemon vinaigrette garnished with hazelnut parmesan crisps.

1. preheat oven to 350f line a baking sheet with parchment paper
2. combine parmesan and hazelnuts
3. drop 12 spoonfuls of parmesan mixture onto baking sheet 3 inches apart
4. bake crisps for 8 to 10 minutes , or until golden
5. cool on baking sheet
6. whisk together lemon juice , oil and maple syrup
7. season with salt and pepper
8. toss lettuce with vinaigrette and pile on individual plates
9. coil each slice of prosciutto into a rose shape and set a rose in center of each mound of greens
10. garnish each serving with two parmesan crisps
demonstrations.review: My oh my is this a wonderful dish.  The hazelnut parmesan crisps are divine.  I skipped the prosciutto (it was vegetarian night), but will try in the future.  The vinaigrette is perfect, though next time I'll drizzle and taste instead of adding it all at once as we like a drier salad.  Thanks for such an easy/elegant creation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aloo mutter   indian potatoes with peas

this is a great indian recipe i got from the betty crocker indian cookbook. great tasty recipe and easy to make for a nice side or main dish. i also add chickpeas and cauliflower for more vegetables.

the calories from the book per serving are: 85 cal 2g fat 420mg sodium 17g carbs 3g protein

1. spray saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add onion and stir fry for 1-2 minutes till golden brown
3. stir in tomatoes , salt , ground pepper and turmeric , stir fry for 1-2 minutes till tomatoes are tender
4. stir in remaining ingredients , except the garam masaala , boil , then reduce to medium-low
5. cover and simmer 5 minutes
6. uncover and cook for 5 minutes until sauce is thick
7. add garam masaala
demonstrations.review: Wonderful and easy side dish, especially good for giving a diet meal some punch.  Other than using canned tomatoes and parsley in place of the cilantro, I made this as written and we enjoyed it thoroughly and will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern living basic yellow cake recipe   or chocolate

i found this is an older southern living cookbook- "heritage cakes" .
this is a basic yellow cake that yields 2 layers. the recipe is as found: my only changes have been direction clarifications.
for chocolate cake: add 3 ( 1 oz.) squares of unsweetened choclate, melted in a double boiler, to the creamed mixture.

1. 1
2. cream butter then gradually add sugar , beating well
3. 2
4. add eggs , beating well after each addition: this mix should be fluffy yellow
5. 3
6. in another bowl , combine the flour and baking powder: the add mix to the creamed mixture alternating with milk , beginning and ending with the flour mix
7. mix well
8. 4
9. stir in vanilla
10. 5
11. pour batter into 2 greased / floured 9" pans
12. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center come out clean
13. 6
14. cool in pan for 10 minutes then remove layers from pans and cool completely
demonstrations.review: This beautifully tall cake needs a double recipe of frosting, as another reviewer noted.  We enjoyed ours with Chocolate Buttercream Frosting and refrigerated due to the hot summer weather. This is the go-to yellow cake recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply potatoes brunch bake

ready, set, cook! special edition contest entry. light flaky phyllo dough holds a warm and nutritious filling of eggs, potatoes, spinach and sausage. hearty enough for breakfast elegant enough for brunch. so simple that even the novice cook will appear experienced. serve with fresh fruit or an arugula salad and voila' bon apetit!

1. cook bacon , crumble and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees
3. dice red pepper and chop spinach
4. in a non-stick pan heat oil on medium heat , add package of simply potatoes diced potatoes , cook for 3 minutes add turkey sausage to pan , cook turkey about 1 / 2 way add diced red pepper and seasonings to pan
5. cut sausage into small pieces during cooking process
6. when turkey is thouroughly cooked add eggs and 1 / 4 of cheese , crumbled bacon chopped spinach -- scramble lightly still runny
7. in 9x12 baking dish cut parchment paper to fit bottom , butter or oil pan and paper
8. melt remaining butter
9. lay 8 phyllo sheets one by one buttering in between to cover bottom of pan and sides
10. pour mixture into pan cover with remaining cheese put into preheated oven 25-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I agree with LoriDori...this is a wonderfully delicious dish enjoyed by the whole family. I too had to substitute fresh potatoes (3 diced and boiled to almost-done) and pork sausage, but did all else as written. I also agree that it would be fine without the phyllo or made with a regular crust as well. We had this for dinner with arugula and DH enjoyed a left-over slice today. Microwaved for 90 seconds, it was hot and the crust still crispy. Thanks for a dish that will surely enter into rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linzer bars

a friend brought this to one of my cookie exchange parties.  i have tried the raspberry version, but she said that apricot jam could also be used, so i am including both.  great flavor and really nice presentation!  a food processor comes in handy for the walnuts, or you can finely chop them.

1. preheat oven to 325f grease a 9x9" square pan
2. cream together butter , sugar , egg , lemon zest , salt , cinnamon , and cloves in a bowl
3. mix in flour and walnuts
4. reserve 1 / 4 of the dough , and pat the remaining into the prepared pan , going up about 1 / 2 inch on each side
5. spread chosen jam flavor in a layer over top of the dough
6. flour a flat surface
7. use reserved dough to create a lattice top for the bars by dividing it into pencil-shaped strips and rolling it on the floured surface
8. arrange in a lattice pattern across the top of the jam , criss crossing the strips and pressing the ends against the dough on the sides of the pan
9. bake 45 mintures , or until lightly browned
10. cool in the pan on a wire rack before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review: These are wonderful.  The zest, cinnamon, and ground cloves give a lovely difference to the dough.  I had a sugar-free jar of apricot preserves that needed to be used up and it was just right.  I think practically any jam would work and I plan on making this many, many times.  Thanks so much.

target.recipe_text:
honey garlic pork ribs

delicious!! marinade time not included in prep time.

1. cut ribs into serving size pieces
2. place in a large resealable plastic bag
3. combine remaining ingredients
4. pour over ribs
5. seal bag
6. turn serveral times
7. refrigerate for several hours or overnight , turning bag occasionally
8. drain ribs , reserving marinade
9. return marinade to the refrigerator
10. place ribs on a rack in a greased shallow baking pan
11. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 1 1 / 2 hours
12. drain
13. pour the marinade over the ribs
14. bake , uncovered , 45 minutes longer or until meat is tender , brushing occasionally with pan juices
target.review: Very yummy!  I didn't have the ginger & mustard and I only cooked 1 lb of ribs, but I don't think it hurt the recipe any.  I added some jerk seasoning b/c it has the ginger in it & then a splash of orange juice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: My eldest daughter loved this, she couldn't get enough....the younger one is a bit pickier.  I omitted the celery and added one zucchini & carrot, shredded.  I didn't have dry mustard so I didn't put that in either.  Ran out of ketchup, but had the packets of ketchup from drive thru meals...so if anyone is interested...8 packets of ketchup equals 1/4 cup of ketchup.  ; )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork and potato hash

perfect for leftover pork loin -- even better if you have a little leftover juices (gravy or pan drippings) from your roast pork.  our family loves this.  it's a jacques pepin recipe.

1. place the sliced potatoes , 1 1 / 2 cups water , onions , and juice from pork roast in a 12" nonstick skillet
2. bring to a boil , cover , and boil over medium heat for 10 minutes
3. add garlic , scallions , olive oil , tabasco , salt , worcestershire and pork
4. mix well and cook , uncovered , over high heat , stirring , for about 5 minutes
5. most of the moisture will have evaporated by now and the mixture should be starting to sizzle
6. since the hash will begin to stick at this point , use a heat-resistant spatula to scrape up the crusty bits sticking to the bottom of the pan and stir them into the uncooked mixture
7. continue to cook over medium heat for about 20 minutes , stirring every 3-4 minutes
8. the mixture will brown faster in the last 10 minutes of cooking and should be stirred every 2-3 minutes
9. turn out onto a large platter and serve immediately
10. garnish with fried egg on top , if desired
demonstrations.review: A good basis for what I was looking for.  Tweaked the recipe a bit: used shallots instead of onions b/c it is what I had, added mixed veggies, added some barbeque sauce & called it Cowboy Hash.  Thanks!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla  buttercream frosting  from sprinkles cupcakes

my sister got this buttercream frosting off the box of a sprinkles cupcake mix, made famous by oprah.  my sister said this was amazing.  update:  i have finally gotten around to making this myself.  i will say, that i don't like my desserts overly sweet and. though this was very good, i think i would probably decrease the amount of sugar for my personal taste.  i'm glad everyone else has liked it as-is, though.  :)

1. in a bowl add sugar then add butter
2. beat till blended
3. next add salt
4. then add the milk and vanilla and beat for an additional 3 to 5 minutes or until smooth and creamy
demonstrations.review: Easy to make & yummy.  It is, as some have posted, a bit too sweet for my tastes but the kids were not complaining.  I needed to add some milk to make it more spreadable (my house might have been too cold), but it worked out great on our cupcakes.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread men from a cake mix

easy to make and wonderful to eat.  decorate as you wish.

1. combine cake mix , flour , eggs oil and molasses and ginger in a large bowl
2. stir until thoroughly blended
3. refrigerate 2 hours
4. preheat oven to 375
5. roll dough to 1 / 4-inch thickness on lightly floured surface
6. cut with gingerbread man cookie cutter
7. place cutout cookies 3 inches apart on ungreased baking sheets
8. decorate as desired using raisins or candies
9. bake at 375 for 8-10 minutes or until edges start to brown
10. remove immediately to cooling racks
11. cool completely
12. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe as shown a couple of times & the cookies cracked on the surface every time.  I tried putting a pan of water on the bottom level to add some moisture, same result.  Lower oven temperature, baked for less time, no fail, it always cracked.  After making, 50 gingerbread men cookies, I gave up & ended up covering the tops with icing.  The children didn't mind & they tasted fine, but it was an awful experience.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled chicken breast with barbecue glaze

a delicious way to cook chicken and quite low fat as well! prep time doesn't include marinating.

1. combine sauce , honey , mayonnaise , garlic and ginger
2. add chicken fillets to bowl and until well coated with the marinade
3. cover and refrigerate for 3 hours or overnight
4. put chicken on oiled grill plate and bbq for approximately 5 minutes each side , brushing occasionally with the marinade
demonstrations.review: This recipe has nice results.  My family enjoyed the chicken.  I broiled skinless, boneless chicken instead of grilling it, I think I will try chicken thighs instead next time.  I think this will be a regular this summer.  thanks!

target.recipe_text:
kung pao chicken with broccoli

a classic, and a snap to put together.

1. blend water , soy sauce , cornstarch , sherry and sugar in bowl , set aside
2. toss chicken with 1 tblsp cornstarch to coat
3. heat 2 tblsps oil in wok over high heat
4. add chilies and cook until blackened , about 2 minutes
5. add chicken and cook until browned , stirring frequently , 1-2 minutes
6. remove chicken using slotted spoon
7. set aside
8. add remaining 2 tblsps oil to wok
9. add green onions , garlic and ginger and stir-fry 1 minute
10. add broccoli and stir-fry 2 minutes
11. stir sauce and add to wok
12. cover and cook until sauce is thickened and broccoli is crisp-tender , about 3 minutes more
13. mix in chicken and peanuts and heat
14. serve with rice
target.review: Flavor was very good.  Only complaint was that it was more steps than I normally like to do.  Not really hard - I just found it a bit tedious.  That's just me though.  I recommend anyone who likes Kung Pao to try it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lisa s swirled chocolate chip cookies

this is a chocolate chip cookie recipe that my friend delynn's best friend gave to us. this is the recipe i use for normal chocolate chip cookies, but i've recently been making them with nestlé's new white & milk chocolate swirled chips. this is a yummy soft and delicious cookie!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix butter , granulated sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs in a large bowl
3. stir in the flour , baking soda and salt
4. stir in 2 cups of swirled chocolate chips
5. drop dough by rounded measuring tablespoons , about 2-inches apart , onto ungreased cookie sheet
6. place the several of the reserved swirled chocolate chips on top of each cookie
7. bake 9 to 12 minutes or until light brown
8. cool slightly
9. remove from cookie sheet
10. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: WOW!  These were fabulous.  Let me just say, that I made a mistake and put in 1/2 a stick of butter less than called for and they still turned out great!  Probably not as gooey as they would have been if I'd used all the butter, but the flavor was wonderful.  It was hard to keep my hands off of them.  I used chocolate chunks as that is what I had on hand.  This makes a lot of cookies, so I froze half of the dough and will make them again soon.  Thanks for the wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy blue cheese hamburgers burgers

if you are a lover of blue cheese then you will love these burgers! they are at their best when cooked on the grill --- yield is only estimated depending on the size of your burgers you should get 6 good size burgers -- you may add in about 3 tablespoon finely grated raw potato for even more juiciness but no more than 3 tablespoons ---plan ahead the patties must be refrigerated for 24 hours to develop the flavors --- also see my recipe#208583

1. mix all the ingredients together
2. shape into 6 balls
3. cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours to blend the flavors
4. grill or cook as desired until cooked through
5. serve with your favorite condiments
demonstrations.review: I made these when my in-laws were visiting.  Unfortunately, I had a cold and my taste buds weren't up to par, but everyone else commented on how good they were.  I will make this again so I can get the full effect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom stuffed hamburger steaks

easy and delicious.

1. melt butter in a large skillet
2. add onion and mushrooms , and saute over medium heat 2 to 3 minutes or until tender
3. remove from skillet
4. combine ground beef and next 7 ingredients in a large bowl
5. shape into 8 patties
6. top 4 patties evenly with onion mixture
7. cover with remaining patties , pressing edges to seal
8. wrap each with 2 bacon slices , securing with wooden picks
9. place on a rack in a broiler pan
10. broil 5 1 / 2 inches from heat 10 minutes on each side or until beef is no longer pink
demonstrations.review: These were wonderful!  The flavors blended so nice together.  My husband raved about these and kids ate them right up.  Thank you so much for sharing this recipe.  This will be a regular meal at our home from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hash browns hotdish

this recipe is from an old cookbook from my mother's home town. very hearty and tasty.

1. butter a 9x13-inch pan
2. cover bottom of pan with hash browns
3. add hamburger , salt pepper and onions
4. sprinkle peas on top
5. mix soup and milk together and pour over peas
6. top with cheese
7. cover with foil and bake at 350f for one hour
8. sprinkle with french fried onions and return to oven for ten more minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  This was very easy to put together and the whole family loved it.  I did add some salt to flavor after it was done, but no need for that the next day.  The leftovers are excellent.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken and noodles

i started making this a few years ago for my family. it is one of my son's favorite meals. i take it to families with new babies and it's always a much-appreciated, comfort food.

1. place the washed chicken in the crock pot
2. cover with 1 cup of water , salt , and pepper
3. cook on low for 8-10 hours or on high for 6-8 hours
4. let cool and debone the chicken
5. separate the chicken into bite-sized pieces
6. set aside
7. prepare the egg noodles according to the package
8. mix the drained noodles and the chicken together
9. add about 1 cup of the reserved liquid leftover from the crock pot
10. you can add more if you like them extra moist
11. this freezes quite well too
12. it makes a lot at once
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to prepare and the chicken was so tender from being in the crockpot.  I added some Lawry's seasoning and liquid smoke to the crock.  I still found that it was a bit bland when served with the noodles.  I will experiment more with spiced next time.  My son absolutely loved this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
uncle bill s petite pea salad

a very light salad to add to any dinner meals. i developed this recipe in 1995 and it has been a highly rated salad.

1. in a microwave-proof dish , microwave peas on high for 2 minutes
2. stir
3. continue to microwave for an additional 2 minutes on high
4. drain and cool completely with cold water and ice cubes
5. then drain
6. in a large mixing bowl , mix together peas , sour cream , mayonnaise , dill weed , onions and celery and mix well to blend
7. chill for at least 30 minutes in refrigerator
8. meanwhile , fry bacon until well done and crispy
9. do not burn
10. place fried bacon on paper toweling to drain
11. crumble bacon and garnish salad when serving
target.review: Uncle Bill, I really liked this. I've made it twice already and the second time I subbed fennel for the celery and bits of ham for the bacon. It was good,too. I love those sweet little peas. Thanks for the inspiration .

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linguica  kale  and potato soup

this tasty recipe is similar to one i saw on the food network. this soup is full of texture, and is not pureed like a traditional caldo verde. i often use 

1. heat olive oil in a deep , heavy pot over medium high heat
2. add potatoes and onions , cover and cook for 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. add garlic , bay leaves , and kale
4. cover and wilt greens about two minutes
5. season with salt and pepper
6. add beans , tomatoes , linguica , & broth and bring to a full boil
7. reduce heat to medium , cover and cook 15 minutes or until potatoes are tender
8. remove bay leaves
9. serve soup with a dollop of sour cream and some of your favorite crusty bread
demonstrations.review:
This is very tasty Caldo Verde and I like the texture
better than the pureed version. I didn't have the linguica (darn) so I had to sub another hard-cured sausage, but I think it was fairly close in flavour. I will be making this again. (Got lots of kale in the garden. Thanks, TigerJo.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
not chicken soup

this veggie chicken soup is based on a mollie katzen recipe. instead of discarding the vegetable i sometimes mash them, add some eggs, oil and matzo meal and make them into a kugel.

1. combine everything in a large pot
2. bring to a boil , lower heat , and partially cover
3. cook slowly for 1-2 hours
4. turn off heat and let soup cool to room temperature
5. strain out and discard all the vegetables
6. heat gently just before serving
7. we cook matzoh balls separately and add them to the soup as we serve it
8. matzoh balls cooked or reheated in the soup will turn a beautiful golden color thanks to the turmeric
demonstrations.review: This is a really good veggie broth that can be made in a crockpot and used for a variety of clear broth style soups. After the simmering vegetables are removed I added diced carrots, cauliflowerettes, and a quarter cup of French lentils, simmering until the lentils were just tender. Garnish with finely minced parsley and chives. Very nice! Thanks, Mirj.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna and parsley tagliatelle

this is one of those dishes that i can always knock up when i haven't had the time to get in the shopping - it's a real store cupboard saviour and it's very tasty too.  like most fishy pasta dishy, hold the parmesan.

1. cook the pasta in a large pan of salted water
2. meanwhile , heat 4 tbs of the oil in a large frying pan and cook the onion , garlic and chilli for 2-3 minutes
3. add the mushrooms and cook for a further 3-4 minutes until beginning to brown
4. stir in the tuna and 4-6 tbs of boiling water from the pasta pan
5. add salt and pepper to taste
6. drain the pasta well and return to the pan
7. stir in the tuna mixture , the parsley and remaining tbs of olive oil
8. divide between 4 bowls and serve topped with a good grinding of black pepper
demonstrations.review: Lene, You've got a new fan here.  I hope to getting around to reviewing many of your recipes. This one is quick, easy and delicious, and I imagine bumping it up with homemade pasta when time is not an issue.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean summer breeze cold yogurt soup

you and your friend are sitting at a quaint outdoor café on the greek island of mykonos.  the sun is setting and the feel of the summer breeze on your sun tanned skin is so soothing. you have just finished eating a tasty shrimp appetizer, it was mouth watering  but a touch on the spicy side.  a cold creamy yogurt soup would just hit the spot.  enjoy!

1. for each individual bowls
2. put 1 / 2 cup of yogurt in a bowl and then add 1 / 8 to 1 / 4 cup cold water , 1 / 8 cup cream , 1 teaspoon salt , 1 tablespoon lemon juice , 1 teaspoon minced garlic all to taste
3. then blend until creamy smooth
4. add to each individual bowl , 2 tablespoons feta cheese , 1 tablespoon olives , 2-3 tablespoons bell peppers , 2 tablespoons spring onions
5. mix slightly
6. sprinkle on top 2 tablespoons of ground pistachio nuts
7. chill prior to serving , enjoy
8. you can also serve individual cups instead of bowls of this soup
9. simply , reduce the amount of ingredients in each cup
10. finally , you can add or substitute some of the vegetables
11. for example , cut up strawberries , tomatoes or chopped up hard boiled eggs
demonstrations.review: This was oh so nice after working in the garden all day. I made only one change and that was to cut back on the salt, but that is a matter of personal taste. There's just the two of us so halving the recipe was no problem.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
malawah

this is a flaky yemenite bread that my friend yechiel taught me to make in israel. it is delicious with puréed tomatoes and zhoug (a spicy condiment--i posted the recipe separately) or with honey. well worth the effort! (cook time is rest time).

1. sift the baking powder into the flour , make a well in the center and add water , 1 tablespoon of the butter , salt , sugar and vinegar
2. knead to a smooth elastic consistency
3. cut into 6 equal portions , and allow to "rest" in a cool place for 20 minutes flatten each piece to a 6-inch round
4. brush each round with the melted butter , then roll it into a tight sausage shape allow the rolls to rest for 20 minutes
5. repeat the flattening , rolling and brushing procedure twice more , waiting 20 minutes between rolling and re-flattening
6. using a non-stick skillet / frying pan , fry the malawah on both sides until golden brown , flipping them over at half time
demonstrations.review: I'm always a little nervous trying a new bread recipe but it turned out quite well and is rich and tasty with all that butter. I did use the vinegar but I'm wondering if using yogurt as part of the liquid would work as well? I'm tempted to try.

target.recipe_text:
creamy chicken chowder

creamy, cheesy comfort food just the way i like it. not a hot, spicy dish but well seasoned.

1. in a 4-quart slow cooker , add the chicken , corn , potato soup , chile peppers , cilantro , chili powder , cumin , and garlic powder
2. stir to combine
3. add the chicken broth
4. stir to combine
5. cover and cook on low for 4-6 hours
6. in a small bowl , stir about 1 cup of hot soup into the sour cream
7. add sour cream mixture back into the slow cooker
8. add in velveeta cheese cubes
9. stir to combine
10. cover and let stand 5 minutes
11. stir with a whisk to combine
target.review: Very tasty soup. Cooking with my crock-pot lets me get a home-cooked meal on the table so we don't have to order take-out all the time since I work until 6pm almost every night. This soup was sure creamy in texture and flavor and also have good tex-mex seasoning. Had some toasted tortilla chips to go with it. A very nice meal. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
anything goes stir fry

garlic and ginger give this real zip. use anything you have in the fridge. a great way to use up left over veggies from a party platter.

1. heat oil and add garlic and ginger
2. cook half a minute in skillet or wok
3. add carrots , cauliflower first& any other firm vegetable
4. cook covered one minute or until it steams
5. add medium veggies beans , onions , peppers , etc
6. cook covered one minute or until it steams
7. add meat
8. cook covered two minute or until it steams
9. add broccoli
10. cook covered two minute or until it steams
11. serve w / rice
demonstrations.review: This is a great basic stir-fry recipe. I used carrots, green onion, zucchini, pea pods, broccoli, cauliflower, and mushrooms. I used soy sauce and a little balsamic vinegar. Didn't add any meat but I think chicken, beef, pork, or shrimp would be good. The ginger and garlic added so much to the flavor. Served over rice. Thanks for a recipe that is fun and good for cleaning out my vegetable bin.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage mushroom appetizers

a favorite appetizer of my family's. easy and makes a lot so you may want to half the recipe.

1. remove stems from mushrooms and discard
2. set mushroom caps aside
3. in a mixing bowl , mix together the remaining ingredients
4. stuff mixture into mushroom caps
5. place stuffed mushrooms into two greased 13x9 inch baking dishes
6. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 16-20 minutes or until heated through
