this a provencal recipe from the new york times. i live in wa state where we have bing cherries, and i can't wait to try this recipe. new york times (9.3.03)

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. butter a 9-inch round glass dish or an 8- to 10-inch ovenproof skillet , preferably nonstick
3. pit about half the cherries , and arrange them , with unpitted cherries , in dish
4. combine flour , cornstarch and sugar in a bowl
5. whisk in eggs , milk and vanilla extract until smooth , but do not overbeat
6. pour over cherries
7. sprinkle with a little more sugar and dot with butter
8. put in oven
9. bake until puffy and firm , about 25 to 35 minutes
10. when done , let rest on a rack for a few minutes , then invert onto a plate
11. sprinkle with a little more sugar and serve warm
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I was trying to use up some cherries in my frig, and this was the perfect dessert for that! I'm just thinking about another piece tomorrow night with a nice cup of hot tea...great comfort food after work!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough pecan drop biscuits

a quick and easy way to use your sourdough starter. yummy for breakfast or just a snack. add a little grated orange or lemon zest for a burst of citrus flavor.

1. mix together flour , baking powder , salt , baking soda and 1 1 / 2 tbsp sugar
2. using a pastry blender or fork , cut in shortening until mixture remsembles coarse crumbs
3. stir in pecans
4. add beaten egg to sourdough starter and add all at once to dry mixture , stirring with a fork just until mixed
5. drop by heaping spoonfuls onto greased baking sheet
6. bake at 425 degrees f for 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
7. immediately upon removing from oven , brush with melted butter and sprinkle with with a mixture of the remaining sugar and cinnamon
8. you could drizzle with a powdered sugar glaze instead of the cinnamon-sugar topping , if desired
demonstrations.review: I have made these to bring to work multiple times and I always get rave reviews. I usually use walnuts instead of pecans due to the cost difference, and I always add about 1 tsp of cinnamon and 2 tbsp more sugar to the dough. To make them extra-good I do the cinnamon-sugar-butter topping, then once they cool top them with a vanilla glaze (I use the one from Betty Crocker) and drizzle over top - they look pretty and they're always gone by mid-day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best lemon bars

this recipe comes from gourmet magazine. it is very simple and delicious.

1. shortbread base:preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cut butter into 1 / 2 inch pieces
3. in food processor , process all ingredients until mixture begins to form small lumps
4. press mixture evenly into 9x13 baking pan
5. bake in middle of oven until golden , about 20 minutes
6. while shortbread is baking , prepare topping
7. topping: in bowl whisk together eggs and granulated sugar until combined well
8. stir in lemon juice and flour
9. pour lemon mixture over hot shortbread base
10. reduce oven temperature to 300 degrees and bake in middle of oven until set , about 30 minutes
11. let cool completely in pan then sprinkle with confectioner's sugar
demonstrations.review: I have made lemon bars before, but these were phenomenal! My mom loved them and she isn't even a lemon fan. They had just the right balance of tart & sweet with a strong lemony flavor. The shortbread was great - very buttery but not overpowering and the right balance of crust to topping. I did add in 2 extra egg yolks and the zest of 2 of the lemons I juiced to give a little extra kick, and it was perfect. I will definitely keep using this recipe, especially since it was so easy using the food processor for the crust! Thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat honey banana muffins

these muffins are delicious and have a great texture, and they are 100% healthy! no refined flour or sweeteners. we have a big family, so this recipe makes a lot of muffins, but it is easily halved for a smaller group. to make the muffins lower in fat, replace half of the oil with unsweetened applesauce. i also use "white whole-wheat" flour, which is softer than that made with red wheat (but has the exact same nutritional value).

1. stir together dry ingredients
2. beat oil and honey together
3. add eggs and beat well
4. add bananas and beat to combine
5. add dry ingredients to wet , alternating with hot water
6. mix well after each addition
7. spoon batter into 24 greased muffin cups
8. bake at 325 degrees for 15 minutes , or until muffins are golden brown and test done
9. remove from oven and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: These were excellent - even if I did forget to put in the bananas!! Guess I had too much on my mind :0( I added 1 cup chopped walnuts & 1 cup raisins, however. Texture was nice & light while firm - just what a muffin should be!! Guess next time I"ll have to try them WITH the bananas!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer cherry cake

this delicious summer cake is a hybrid cross between a classic french clafouti and a coffeecake.  it has a very moist, dense crumb due to the butter and eggs and low flour ratio.  it is a perfect afternoon dessert to serve with tea as well as a brunch or dinner dessert, especially as it can be made a day ahead of time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and dust with flour a 9-inch cake pan or tarte pan with removable bottom
3. shake off any additional flour
4. pit the cherries , then blend in a bowl with lemon juice and cherry brandy and let stand at least 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. cream the butter and sugar , lemon peel , nutmeg and vanilla until fluffy , then beat in eggs , one at a time
6. add flour
7. pour into pan and spread batter evenly
8. lift cherries from juices with a slotted spoon and distribute over batter , rounded sides up
9. drizzle cherry juices over fruit
10. bake until cake around fruit springs back firmly when lightly touched , about 30 minutes
11. let cool , then serve slightly warm or at room temperature , sprinkling with powdered sugar before serving if you wish
12. cake is best served 1- 2 days after baking as the flavor mellows and intensifies
13. this cake freezes well
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Just right for a "not too sweet" dessert - or maybe even breakfast?!? I macerated the cherries in almond liqueur since I did not have cherry, and it turned out great - that cherry/almond combo is always delish. Next time I'll try it with white wheat flour and see if I can convince myself it's healthy enough for breakfast! (I actually doubled this for a crowd but still used one stick of butter - and it was plenty)

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
target.review: The flavor was great, however the onions were still crunchy which is a major turn off for my family.  I will leave them out and use onion powder next time.  ***I also used puff pastry because we don't have crescent rolls here in South Africa.  They didn't cook through.  Next time I will bake them for awhile before topping with the sauce.  This part did not  change the rating!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
utah s cafe pork barbasco

this recipe is in response to a request.  i found it in a utah newspaper.  the restaurant serves this sweet pork in burritos and in salads.  for the burrito garnish with chopped tomatoes, salsa, lettuce and sour cream.

1. cut pork into large cubes and place in slow cooker with 1 / 3 cup water
2. season with salt and pepper and garlic salt
3. cook on high temperature for 4 hours or low for 8 hours , until meat is well done
4. remove from cooker and drain
5. shred meat and place in a bowl
6. stir in 1 / 2 cup green chili sauce and brown sugar
7. heat oven to 350 degrees
8. spray a 9-by-13-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray
9. warm the tortillas in a microwave to make them easier to roll
10. pour 1 / 2 cup green chili sauce into prepared pan
11. place 1 / 3 cup meat mixture down the middle of each tortilla
12. sprinkle 1 to 2 tablespoons of black beans and 1 to 2 teaspoons of chopped cilantro
13. roll burrito and place seam-side down in baking dish
14. repeat with remaining tortillas
15. pour 1 1 / 2 to 2 cups of green chili sauce over burritos and sprinkle with monterey jack cheese
16. cover with foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes or until cheese is melted and burritos are warmed through
17. serve with desired garnishes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful meal!  I was in a rush so I  rolled the burritos then put them on our plates and covered them in sauce and cheese and nuked it in the microwave. I know, I know That is totally Gringo.  But it was delicious anyway! ;)  It was a tad sweet for us but I think baking them in the oven would have fixed that.  I will try these in the oven next time. Made for Cookbook tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian chicken  or shrimp  w tomato cream sauce

this dish is great and easy for an everyday family dinner and great, easy and fancy enough for company. you can mix and match with chicken or seafood or both combined. serve with a salad and your choice of warm bread. i've gotton many compliments on this one! if you want some leftovers, double this recipe for dinner serving of 4.

1. cook pasta
2. cook chicken , onion& garlic in hot oil until no longer pink
3. drain and return to pan
4. stir in undrained tomatoes , sauce& seasonings
5. bring to a boil , simmer uncovered until thickened slowly add cream and stir constantly
6. serve over pasta
7. you can garnish with black pepper and green onions
8. to help thicken sauce , dredge chicken or seafood in flour prior to cooking it
demonstrations.review: Delicious! We will have this again.  I pureed my tomatoes because we don't like chunks and I also used a 4 oz can of tomato paste with 4oz of water in place of the tomato sauce. Made for cookbook tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrabba s italian grill parmesan dressing

found this on recipe secrets and can't wait to try it.

1. gradually blend milk into mayonnaise
2. mix in cheese , vinegar and worcestershire sauce
3. chill
4. serve on tossed salad greens
demonstrations.review: At first taste I thought this was going to be very boring.  But by the time dinner was on the table it had perked up.  I really enjoyed it on my salad and we also dipped our chicken in it as well! ( it was on the bland side).  I will be making this again.  Made for photo tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barb s crowd pleasing cookies

delicious chunky cookies that are easy to make and disappear in a snap! my long-time friend barb brought them to our new year's eve party and they were the hands-down favorite of a huge buffet table.

cook's note: the pretzels should be about the size of the chocolate chips, not pulverized. you want to taste bits of pretzel as you munch. this is a crunchy cookie. i use a food processor and just pulse until the desired size is achieved.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugars until light and fluffy
3. beat in egg and vanilla
4. in a medium bowl , combine the flour , baking soda and salt
5. blend into creamed mixture
6. stir in chocolate and peanut butter chips , peanuts and pretzels
7. drop by heaping tablespoons about 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet
8. bake 10 - 13 minutes , or until edges are lightly browned and centers are still soft
9. do not over bake
10. cool one minute on baking sheet
11. cool completely on wire racks
12. store in tightly covered container
demonstrations.review: Wonderful cookies!  I used pretzel sticks broke in 1/3rds.  And I left the peanuts out of 1/2 and added chopped caramels instead.  Those were also great.  The caramels did run a bit but came off the pan easy and had a toffee like taste and crunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic mashed potatoes

an easy way to make garlic mashed potatoes. i like to leave the skins on. i've found that a pastry blender works great for mashing potatoes; it seems even better than a masher.

1. toss potatoes , water , butter , salt , pepper , and garlic and put them into the crock pot
2. cook the potatoes for 4 hours on high or 7 hours on low in the crock pot
3. add milk and mash the potatoes
demonstrations.review:
I had a bit of trouble with these.  First of all This recipe only made 5 servings for me.  I cooked them on low for about 5 hrs. and some of them, not sure if they were the ones on top or on the bottom) got rubbery and didn't mash.  I also had to use more than 1 cup of milk to get them to a correct texture.  They were very stiff with the amount called for.
   That said, I really enjoyed the connivence and they tasted great. I will use this again when I want a quick meal when we get home from church.

target.recipe_text:
homemade crock pot macaroni   cheese

yum

1. toss cooked macaroni in 2 tablespoons oil in large bowl
2. add all remaining ingredients
3. pour into lightly greased crock-pot
4. stir well
5. cover and cook on low for 3-4 hours
6. stir occasionally
target.review: lovely and tasty and so easy.  i used the fresh pasta (from the chilled cabinet) and didn't pre-cook it.  it came out fine, although i left it for the full 4 hours.  my little ones loved it.  thankyou for a great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best blasted rapid roast whole chicken

blasting with high heat will shrink the skin and seal in all the juices to create an extremely moist and tender chicken with lovely crispy skin - and it will be on your table in about an hour. this method will also work with a larger chicken, but cooking time will need to be increased. you may adjust all seasonings to taste. if you are not a lemon lover, then you may omit the lemon juice. you really can use whatever seasoning that you like for this. i like to use seasoned salt. make certain to use a fork and poke holes all over in the lemon, then place it into the cavity of the chicken. roast roast as stated. the chicken with be moist and have a faint lemon flavor. for more of my tried-and-true recipes, visit my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com.

1. rinse the chicken inside and out well under cold water , then pat dry using a paper towel
2. in a small bowl mix the lemon juice with oil and melted butter until blended , then rub all over the chicken
3. using clean hands rub the inside and outside of the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder , black pepper and cayenne
4. place the lemon / s inside the cavity
5. place the chicken into a baking dish
6. using cotton string tie the legs together tightly
7. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 6 hours
8. set oven to 450 degrees f
9. roast the chicken at 450 degrees for 20 minutes , then reduce the heat to 400 degrees and continue roasting for about 40 minutes
10. cover with foil and let sit for 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Came out perfect. My chicken was 2kg and I left it in the oven an extra 10 minutes. I did notice when I pulled the carcas to bits (to make stock) that there was some little bits of red inside the legs so would leave it slightly longer next time. The meat was definitely juicier than my normal sunday roast and I will use this method next time. Thanks Kittencal

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger hot pot  crock pot

this is very good, and inexpensive to prepare

1. in skillet , lightly brown ground beef , drain well
2. add seasonings
3. set aside
4. place half the potatoes and onions in greased crock pot
5. add browned beef
6. top with remaining potatoes and onions
7. combine mushroom soup and water and spread over top -- being sure to moisten and cover evenly
8. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours
demonstrations.review: A lovely meal, tasty despite the basic ingredients. Made it as per the recipe. i warmed up the condensed soup with the water before adding. this meant it wasn't lumpy at all and, being warm at the start of the cooking time, got the flavours merging in the crockpot sooner.  thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts with pecans

a new, more exciting way to eat 

1. melt butter in skillet
2. add onion and garlic and saute until lightly browned
3. stir in sprouts , saute 2 minutes
4. add broth and sugar , cooking until liquid is almost evaporated , stirring frequently
5. add salt , sprinkle with pecans and serve
demonstrations.review: These were good. I too cut back on the amount of sugar - I used about half. I also used brown sugar and this seemed to give an even nicer flavor (I made previously exactely as written as I have a real  'thing' about people who are negative about a recipe when they  have changed basically everything!' I also think it is important not to brown the garlic - even slightly - as this does give a slight bitterness.  A fab recipe though, well done Just Married, you have been successful in getting my son to eat some.... and seconds. Previously he would rather have eaten nuclear waste than sprouts. A big thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bea s baked lentils

a quick and delicious meatless entree or side dish that we all love out here at the river. originally posted back in nov 13 1996 in the juniata sentinel, a local paper and shared by my wonderful mil.

1. bring water to boil in a pot
2. add lentils and simmer for 20 minutes or until water is absorbed
3. add rest of ingredients
4. place in baking dish and bake at 350 degrees for one hour or more
demonstrations.review: i was pleased with this one if only for the simplicity of the ingredients and how adaptable the end result is. it uses ingredients always on hand and really is very healthy. we have been using in packed lunches this week - sliced and put in a wholemeal bread bun with lots of lettuce, cucumber, tomato and red onion. i am going to try it hot next with some onion gravy and mashed potatoes. a lovely recipe. thank you,

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mozzarella bruchettas

this is my different twist on typical bruschettas. everytime i go to a party or pot luck at work, i am asked to bring this dish. not only does it taste great and get outstanding compliments... it is pretty and colorful!
especially for christmas!

1. slice baguettes into 1" pieces and place on platter
2. cut mozzarella balls in half and place 3 to 4 on each slice of bread to cover
3. top the mozzarella with sliced grilled red peppers
4. drizzle olive oil with fresh green basil , garlic , and sundried tomatoes with a spoon onto each bruchetta
5. sprinkle generously with parmesean cheese
6. shake on some italian seasoning and oregano
7. cover and refrigerate until ready to serve
8. you will get rave reviews !
demonstrations.review: MMMMMMmmmmmmmmmmmmmmm. Very good!! Simple and delicious. I prepared these today to take to a party tonight and I am almost ashamed to go as we have eaten most of them lol. Only amendment would be to say make at least double what you need..........they will go FAST!!! thanks.

target.recipe_text:
fresh spinach mushroom frittata

i had some fresh spinach that i needed to use and this recipe was born. uses all the good stuff that i always have on hand.

1. melt butter in an oven proof skillet
2. add garlic , onions and mushrooms cooking until onions are translucent
3. add spinach , sautee for 2 minutes
4. beat eggs , salt& pepper together
5. pour over mixture in skillet , stirring to combine
6. cook eggs for about 4 minutes , eggs will be almost but not quite set still moist on top
7. sprinkle with cheese and put in oven
8. broil 6" from heat for 3-4 minutes or until eggs are set and cheese is lightly browned
target.review: This has such wonderful flavor!  I must confess to changing it up quite a bit, however.  In order to make it more Ph-friendly, I upped the veggies and reduced the eggs.  I also used cooked collard greens in place of the spinach and onion salt in place of the onion and salt.  I will definitely be making it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country apple squares

i found this recipe in a newspaper a number of years ago, and i have been making it ever since. the apples go so well with the crumb and cream cheese layers. when fall comes around, this dessert is a real hit! hint: many reviewers have suggested doubling the amount of cream cheese!

1. combine flour , brown sugar and cinnamon
2. cut in butter to resemble coarse crumbs
3. add walnuts
4. measure 2 cups crumb mixture and set aside
5. press remaining mixture into a greased 9" x 13" pan
6. beat cream cheese and milk until smooth
7. mix in egg , sugar , and vanilla
8. pour over crumb mixture , and top with apples
9. sprinkle with the reserved crumbs and bake for 30 minutes at 350f
demonstrations.review: The changes I incorporated worked quite well.  I subbed xylitol in place of both the brown and table sugar and only half of what was called for.  I also took the advice of a previous reviewer and doubled the cream cheese layer.  Oh, I also layered the apple slices first, then the cream cheese mixture topped with the crumbs.  It got compliments all around, so we're definitely keeping this one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scooter s stuffed cornish game hens

i got this recipe from my nephew. a special occasion dish.

1. in a skillet , melt 3 tablespoons butter
2. saute onion and celery until tender
3. add next 7 ingredients
4. remove from heat and mix well
5. place stuffing into cavity of hens
6. place hens on a rack in a shallow baking or roasting pan
7. soften remaining butter and spread over the skin of the hens
8. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 1 hour or until the juices are clear
demonstrations.review: The stuffing was okay...a bit too sweet for our tastes though.  I'll stick with the more savory flavors of traditional stuffing next time--but I'm going to keep the brown rice instead of the bread cubes.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cauliflower soup

that's why i love soup. you can do almost anything with them. if you want this soup heartier, set aside some chunked, cooked veggies. then add them back to the pot with the pureed veggies.

1. in a 5-quart saucepan , add all ingredients except salt and white pepper
2. cover and simmer until vegetables are tender
3. strain off and reserve most of the liquid
4. place vegetables in a food processor and puree
5. add pureed vegetables and reserved liquid back into the pot , add salt and white pepper , and reheat
demonstrations.review: Didn't have any stock/broth, so I used all water and added salt, white pepper, marjoram, rosemary, thyme, paprika, celery salt and hot sauce...after pureeing, I threw in some corn and chicken and it was deliciously thick and tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice and lentil casserole

this is a great meal that we eat here often in the winter time. with some dark bread and maybe a salad it is a really hearty meal, though we have been known to eat just this for dinner. the recipe is adapted from amy dacyczyn's "the complete tightwad gazette"

1. preheat the oven to 300 degrees
2. mix all ingredients except the cheese in a baking dish
3. cover with foil and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes
4. then remove the foil , add the cheese , and bake for an additional 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Exactly what I was expecting it to be!  My husband described it as "earthy" and my 18 mo. old who hasn't had much of an appetite lately due to teething ate an entire bowl!  The one minute tweak I made was grating two large garlic cloves instead of the powder.  I also omitted the cheese and we all thought it was wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
danish bubble

the rough translation of this dish means "scrambled food" and is a great dish to use up leftovers from the night before.
we have had this for breakfast as well as supper.
serve with ketchup, hp sauce and toast.

1. chop onions finely and dice meat and potatoes into 1 inch cubes
2. heat a third of the oil or butter in frying pan
3. brown the meat until golden brown and remove meat from pan
4. add another third of the oil or butter and brown the potatoes at high heat until they are golden and crispy on the outside
5. remove potatoes from pan
6. add the remaining oil or butter to pan and cook the onions until clear
7. add meat , bacon , chives and potatoes to pan
8. and heat through
9. season with salt , pepper and worcestershire sauce
10. fry the eggs in butter , sunny side up and place on top of meat mixture
11. top all of this with the grated cheddar and serve hot
demonstrations.review: What a perfect combination of flavors!  I made this with red potatoes (they seem to hold together better), and I used half butter and half EVOO.  I used six eggs instead of four and it probably wouldn't have hurt to use eight--just for a better balance of ingredients.  The taste was perfect, and there's even some leftover for hubbie's breakfast!  Thanks for a keeper.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chops that will make you eat til you pop

these have to be, hands down, the best meal i have ever made in a crock pot. i borrowed a friend's crock pot one weekend and made this for my honey. low and behold, i got a crock pot for my next birthday along with a request for this recipe to be the first thing i made. i really wish i know where i got the recipe from because i would love to give credit for it. i beg of you, do yourself a favor and try this. you will not regret it. let me know what you think!!

1. salt and pepper pork chops if desired
2. add all ingredients except water and cornstarch to the crock pot
3. cook on low for 5 1 / 2 hours
4. mix cornstarch and water together and stir into crock pot
5. cook 30 minutes more
6. serve over rice
target.review: If you find sweet and sour pork appetizing you should like this recipe. The pork chops are very tender and the sauce goes great with white or brown rice. We eat pork chops a lot so this is a nice way to mix it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian turkey sausage and peppers with bow tie pasta

i just threw this together one night with ingredients i had on hand. we loved the flavor and it's now a favorite after work meal.

1. saute onion , peppers and pepper flakes in olive oil until onions start to brown
2. add garlic , salt , pepper , basil and oregano
3. set aside
4. prick sausage links with a fork
5. saute in skillet with a little olive oil over medium heat until brown
6. add wine vinegar and canned tomatoes
7. add the sauted vegetable mixture
8. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
9. meanwhile cook pasta al dente
10. add cooked pasta to sausage and pepper mixture
11. stir and serve
demonstrations.review: I reeeeeally liked this. I used turkey kielbasa, but look forward to trying it with Italian style turkey sausage. It was fine with dried basil, and you HAVE to use the red wine vinegar--totally made the dish. I like that it's heavier on the vegetables than most Italian pasta fare. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
freakin  good guacamole

this is how i do it.

1. peel and mash the avocados
2. mix in all ingredients
3. try not to think too hard
4. just do what feels good
5. eat it all yourself before your family gets to it
demonstrations.review: I went from being someone who had barely let guacamole pass my lips, to eating guacamole just about every other week since I first tried this recipe. Fresh lime juice and cilantro are musts. I use most of the juice from a whole lime. Haven't bothered with salsa yet, and instead add extra tomato and some minced onion. A little Tabasco is good too. When it comes to making this recipe I think following the directions is more important than sticking to the ingredient list :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan lentil and chickpea soup

one of the best vegetable soups i've had in ages!  extremely easy to make and very cheap (leave out the saffron if you don't already have any)!  this lemony, peppery soup is traditionally enjoyed at the end of a day of fasting during the muslim holy month of ramadan.  this is a vegetarian version of the thick and aromatic soup.  more like a stew.  from the 2/2007 issue of canadian house & home.

1. in large heavy saucepan or dutch oven , melt butter over medium heat
2. stir in onion and celery and cook , covered , for 7-10 minutes or until onion is tender , stirring occasionally
3. add cinnamon , turmeric , salt , pepper , ginger , hot pepper sauce and saffron
4. cook , stirring , for 2 minutes
5. add tomatoes , lentils , chickpeas and broth
6. bring to boil , reduce heat , and simmer , covered , for about 40 minutes or until lentils are tender
7. stir in noodles and simmer , covered , about 7 minutes longer or until noddles are just tender
8. in bowl , whisk flour , and 1 cup water until smooth
9. whisk flour mixture into soup and simmer , stirring often , for 2-4 minutes or until soup is thickened and no raw flour taste remains
10. stir in half of the parsley and cilantro , and all of the lemon juice
11. taste and adjust seasoning , adding up to 1 / 2 tsp more salt if needed
12. garnish with remaining parsley and cilantro
demonstrations.review: Loved this soup! I didn't use the saffron or fresh herbs. I ate leftovers at work for two days and my coworker wanted the recipe because it smelled so good. She made it that night and agreed it was fantastic. We both thought the lemon juice really brought the flavors of the soup together. Will definitely be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried chickpeas and black beans low fat

this is a quick and simple vegetarian curry with lots of flavor, tons of protein, and not alot of fat. i recommend using a real flavorful, mild curry powder, or one that you've mixed yourself. my "simple, sweet and mild curry blend" works well with this dish. however,if you do like heat, feel free to add some cayenne or crushed red pepper to suit your taste.

1. heat oil in a large , non-stick skillet over medium heat
2. add onion and ginger and saute about 3 minutes , or until tender
3. add curry powder and stir to coat onions evenly
4. add tomatoes with their juices and cook 1-2 minutes or until mixture seems slightly thickened , stirring well
5. add black beans , chickpeas and salt to taste
6. stir to coat beans evenly
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 5 minutes or until chickpeas are heated through
8. turn off heat , and stir in fresh cilantro , and lemon juice
9. serve warm
10. this dish goes nicely over some jasmine or basmati rice
demonstrations.review: I really enjoyed this. Ate it straight with no rice but I look forward to trying it again with some rice. It was very flavorful and seemed pretty healthy! Didn't use the cilantro or parsley, and my husband threw in bottled lemon juice before I could remind him we had a fresh lemon, but still tasted wonderful in the end.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
california quinoa salad

my step mom brought this to our family's weekly lunch and visit. it was enjoyed by all ages (which ranged from 1 to 71! i am not sure where she got this recipe, but it is definitely going in my "tried and true" recipe file. very good, very flavorful...and good for you! it has a nice, colorful
presentation, too.

1. whisk together the first five ingredients in a small bowl to make the vinaigrette
2. boil the water and add the quinoa
3. simmer for 15 minutes until the water is absorbed
4. stir in the spinach and remaining ingredients
5. add the vinaigrette and toss gently
6. serve at room temperature
7. suggest doubling recipe if making for a larger group of people
demonstrations.review: This was a really tasty dinner. The vinaigrette was perfect, and I especially like the addition of the kalamata olives and fresh basil, really helped bolster the flavor. I realizing I'm just not big on avocado so I won't use it again, which I guess negates the "California" aspect of this dish, but hey, it's still really good!

target.recipe_text:
ww 1 point  ww  warm chunky apple  pie

i was given a bunch of apples and wondered what to do with them. i searched all of my cookbooks and found a similar recipe. i just changed it to be weight watchers "friendly". it tastes just like warm apple pie without all the guilt! i am going to try it over pancakes too!

1. peel and cut apples into chunks and place in a crockpot
2. in a small mixing bowl mix splenda , water and cinnamon
3. pour over apples
4. cook on low setting for 4-5 hours stirring occasionally
5. serve warm with ice cream or cool whip
6. 1 cup= 1pt
7. delicious and very filling too !
target.review:
My family and I LOVED this "crustless" apple pie.  That says a lot because they are a hard crowd to please.

I didn't use Splenda (personal issues with it), and subbed 3/4 cup of sugar.  I also added a little bit of ground clove and about 2 tablespoons of organic flax seed meal to add some fiber.  No one even noticed I put it in!

I will make this time and time again.  My brother (and biggest critic) even agreed that it was good enough to serve to company!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chili pork chops     a must try

i found this recipe on the web somewhere and decided to try it. it is absolutely wonderful and the meat just falls off the bones. as my husband describes it "they are succulent!" this is a must in our family at least every other week!

1. cook onions in oil until lightly brown
2. add garlic , worcestershire sauce , chili powder , water , ketchup and salt and pepper
3. cover and simmer the sauce for 10 minutes
4. arrange pork chops in crock pot , pour sauce over the chops
5. cover and cook on low heat for 6-7 hours
6. i find that the longer you cook them , the more tender they are
7. i normally serve them with mashed potatoes and a vegetable
8. i put the sauce over the mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: I made this for a family of picky eaters, except I only had pork tenderloin on hand.  I followed the recipe, including using the water in the sauce which was important.  I put 3 tenderloins in the crock pot with the sauce for about 7 hours on low.  It was so moist and delicous- the whole family loved it!  Thanks for a great recipe- this one's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey or lean beef meat sauce  optional crock pot

no added fat just lots of flavor in this chunky meat sauce. not just chunky from the meat but from the diced vegies which adds flavor and keeps the fat down without adding to much meat! you can sweeten the sauce if the tomatoes are not sweet enough but wait till it simmers for 1/2 an hour then taste and season as you like. the carrot has a way of taking any tang from the sauce and the onions sweeten it. this make alot so you can have some for dinner and freeze some for the future.

1. in a large heavy hot pot over medium high heat brown meat
2. add onions , garlic , pepper , carrot , and celery and cook till meat is lightly browned being sure to stir often
3. add rest of ingredients and bring to a boil then simmer over very low heat for an hour or two
4. can be placed in a crock pot and cooked on low for 6-8 hours
5. stirring to prevent the sauce from burning
6. serve over your favorite pasta topping with cheese , or use for baked ziti , lasagna or use to top a pizza
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor and so quick to make!  I'm never going back to store bought sauce, and my family agrees this is a keeper.  Only thing keeping my away from 5 stars was the thinness of the sauce.  I added tomato paste to thicken it up to stick to the pasta better.  YUM!  THanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
decadent and easy crab bisque

this is an easy and quick recipe that my sister and i devloped. it's definitely not in the low fat category but it sure is satisfying!

1. saute onion in the butter , over medium heat , until translucent
2. add 2 t
3. of the flour to the onions , mixing well with a wooden spoon
4. cook for about a minute
5. add 3 cups of the half-and-half , heavy cream , salt and pepper
6. whisk while bringing up to a boil
7. shake 2 t
8. of the flour and 1 cup of the half-and-half - using a jar with a lid
9. shake until the flour is blended well
10. add to the soup by whisking
11. keep whisking until the soup thickens
12. stir in the crab and cook for about 5 more minutes
13. ladle the soup into the bowls and garnish with snipped chives , if desired
demonstrations.review: LOVE this recipe.. I just alter it a little. I add 2 cans of corn, a can of tiny shrimp, and a whole scallion right to the soup.  I only use jumbo lump crab meat, and it is absolutely out of this world!  Oh, and white pepper!  That is my secret ingredient that everyone loves!!!  Thank you so much for posting this recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin cream cheese muffins  like starbucks

these delicious muffins are very close to the kind you can get at starbucks. if you want to cut back on the fat, substitute some or all of the oil with natural unsweetened applesauce.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. mix cream cheese with one egg and 3 tablespoons of sugar
3. put the entire mixture on a piece of wax paper or parchment paper and shape it into a long log
4. put it in the freezer while you mix and fill the pans , up to an hour
5. unwrap and cut with a sharp knife so each cream cheese disk equals 1-2 teaspoons
6. if the cream cheese disks are too big around , cut thick slices and then cut them in half
7. this lets you push it down into the batter easier
8. mix all ingredients together
9. fill muffin tins half full
10. put cream cheese disc in the middle , pressing down
11. sprinkle with 1 tsp chopped nuts
12. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes , until a toothpick comes out clean from the muffin part
13. let cool in pans for 5 minutes , then remove to racks to cool completely
14. do not touch the cream cheese until it cools
demonstrations.review:
I usually have a hard time baking ANYTHING, but these came out PERFECT!  My family absolutely loves them, and are always asking me to make more.  

I did add vanilla to the cream cheese, although, people told me they couldn't taste the difference between the two batches.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian salmon

this is very quick to prepare; i have marinated the salmon for as little as 1/2 an hour, yet it has plenty of flavor. for ease of preparation, we buy individually portioned salmon from a big-box store. we prefer to grill it on our indoor contact because it's so quick. i've used straight brown sugar, splenda brown sugar blend, and straight splenda - and they all work very well. but i think the brown sugar or the brown sugar blend will give you a little better color.

1. whisk together olive oil , sesame oil , rice wine vinegar , soy sauce , brown sugar , pressed garlic , pepper , and minced onion
2. pour marinade over salmon
3. cover and refrigerate at least 1 / 2hr , or up to two hours
4. if using an indoor contact grill: after pre-heating , grill salmon on lowest setting for four minutes , or until the fish flakes easily with a fork
5. if using a conventional oven: preheat oven to 350
6. bake salmon , uncovered , for 15-18 minutes , or until it flakes easily with a fork
demonstrations.review: WONDERFUL dish!  This is a keeper.  I had to triple the sauce for the amount of salmon I served.  I might double that next time for the extra sauce- it was so good all over rice and veggies, too.  THANK YOU!  My 14mo old son couldn't get enough!

target.recipe_text:
show off roast pork

my favorite do-ahead party dish. excellent taste, very easy to make, and perfect for everything from a casual to a formal dinner party, or even a buffet. it's great served with braised belgian endive or lightly sauteed broccoli rappe, green salad, wine, and even pasta. versatile and easy dish. my go-to dish when we've got friends coming over, and i can't think of what to make.

1. mix together butter , prosciutto , garlic , rosemary , parmesan , and black pepper and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. cut slits about an inch or so long and a half inch or so deep all over the top of the roast
4. spread butter mixture over the roast , using the handle of a spoon to get it into the slits you made earlier
5. put prepared roast in a roasting pan , pour wine slowly over it , and cook for about 1 1 / 4 to 1 1 / 2 hours , depending on the size of the roast , basting about every 30 minutes or so with pan drippings
6. remove from oven , cover with aluminum foil and let rest for about 15 minutes
target.review: WOW! I had company for dinner last night and made this pork roast, everyone was very impressed.  Great presentation and amazing flavor.  I substituted parsley for the rosemary and it was truly delicious.  This will be a recipe I make MANY times.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken cordon bleu over rice

nan

1. place ham and chicken in bottom for greased 3-quart casserole dish
2. mix soup , sour cream and cheese and pour over meat
3. bake at 350f for 35-4o minutes
4. remove from oven and top with bread crumbs
5. bake another 5 minutes
6. serve over cooked rice
demonstrations.review: KEEPER!  Yummy stuff.  I have a daughter who doesn't like anything except pizza and filet mignon, needless to say she is not pleased with dinner many nights.  Tonight she had SECONDS, she is 19 years old and I would venture to say her taking seconds was a first :-).  I served it over rice with buttered green beans and Garlic bread with mayo and cheddar #22103, a totally successful meal as the bread was great too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry  feta and walnut salad

a tasty and beautiful salad. you may choose to substitute the walnuts with almonds - just as good!

1. toss greens , cranberries , cheese and walnuts in large bowl
2. mix vinegar , honey , mustard and pepper with wire whisk until well blended
3. gradually add oil , whisking constantly until well blended
4. pour over salad
5. toss to coat
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  I served this salad with a turkey dinner and it really complemented the meal.  To my dismay I realized I did not have honey so I substituted honey mustard for the honey and the mustard and the dressing was delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled clams with garlicky white wine sauce

yum! make sure to serve with more wine and a great crusty bread to get all the delicious broth! this is also great with a squirt of fresh lemon or some chopped green onions as a garnish. some even love to add a small dab of horseradish or even some good smoky bbq sauce. experiment and try what you like. to really get the clams to cook quickly sometimes i will even place an old pot with boiling water or broth in it on the grill to add some steam. adding some aromatics to the pot also seems to add to the flavor or the clams really well. this serves 6 as an appy or 2 as a meal if you include some bread and a green salad. of course i could probably finish the whole lot of them off all by myself! lol hope you enjoy this simple yet delicious dish!

1. heat olive oil over medium heat
2. melt butter then add garlic and saute for about 1 minute or until garlic is fragrant
3. pour in the wine and bring to a boil , cooking until the wine has reduced to about half its original volume
4. taste and season with salt and pepper as desired
5. i use sea salt and fresh ground peppercorns
6. set sauce aside and keep warm
7. get grill as hot as you can for best results
8. place the clams on grill
9. grill until the clams have opened and discard any clams that do not
10. remove from grill and pour clams and juice into a shallow bowl
11. pour sauce sauce over the top
12. top with parsley and any optional garnishes as desired
13. serve immediately with some good crusty bread to soak up all the yummy juices
14. have another glass of wine and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  There is a local restaurant that I go to when craving steamed clams with crusty dipping bread, I decided to try this one night instead so we could eat home on our deck.  This recipe was all I hoped for and more, my husband and I feasted on grilled clams and shrimp with crusty bread.  Making it again today for company.  Thank you for submitting a wonderful recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marvelous muffins

a tasty muffin recipe that it easy to make and looks great!

1. mix the flour , baking powder and salt in a large bowl
2. stir well and make a well in the center of the mixture
3. in a small bowl combine the spice mix ingredients- stir well and set aside
4. in a separate bowl combine the butter , sugar and egg and beat well
5. pour this mixture into the well of the flour mixture
6. mix just until moist
7. grease the muffin cups
8. fill the muffin cups 1 / 3 full and then sprinkle spice mix over top
9. spoon the rest of the batter over the filling to 2 / 3 full
10. bake at 400 oven for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made these yummy muffins as part of a muffin basket.  I have a friend who has been at a rehab center for a few months and I know he likes to share treats with other patients and the staff so I whipped up a bunch of these muffins along with Mini Pumpkin Muffins, recipe#76894,and Pecan Pie mini muffins, recipe #49381, I made them all as mini-muffins and they complemented each other nicely as a lovely fall basket of muffins to which I added fall wrapped candies and a big bow.  Made a great presentation for truly delicious muffins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curley s old fashioned cornbread

this is my mother's recipe. it was on the menu at every cafe she cooked. this cornbread has a great crisp crust yet the inside is soft and tender. it is a perfect accompaniment to soups, stews and the southern standard, 

1. preheat oven to 375 in a large bowl , combine flour , cornmeal , baking powder , salt , baking soda , and sugar
2. stir well to combine
3. in a small bowl , whisk together buttermilk , egg , and oil
4. place the butter in a 9 or 10 inch skillet and place in the oven and heat until the butter melts and is sizzling seriously
5. tilt the pan to coat the sides of the skillet
6. as the butter's melting , quickly pour the wet ingredients into the dry , and , using a wooden spoon , stir the wet and dry together with as few strokes as possible--- only as many as are needed to combine the two
7. don't beat it !
8. scrape the batter into the hot , buttery skillet
9. it should sizzle
10. place it in the oven immediately
11. bake until golden brown on top , about 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy stuff!  I made this cornbread to accompany my Hungarian Goulash recipe and was NOT disappointed.  I liked the idea of cooking it in my cast iron skillet, gave it a nice crusty outside, moist inside.

target.recipe_text:
olive garden copycat zuppa toscana

this is a clone of the olive garden zuppa toscana. tried and true, approved by former olive garden chefs.

1. chop or slice uncooked sausage into small pieces and cook until browned and meat is ground in bottom of your soup pan over med-high heat
2. add onions , garlic , salt , pepper , and red pepper flakes to sausage and cook until onions are clear and aromatics of the seasonings blend together
3. reduce heat back to medium and place , potatoes , in the pot
4. and slowly add the chicken stock and water and stir
5. cook on medium heat until potatoes are done and stir occasionally
6. once potatoes are done , add flour or cornstarch and simmer for another 15 minutes
7. reduce heat to lowest setting and sprinkle in your kale and cooked bacon and slowly pour cream while stirring
8. check for taste and then serve
target.review: I used venison sausage for this recipe to keep it a little less fatty.  This is so good.  I loved it.  My family really loved it too.  They were a little worried when I served it.  My husband thought it looked "too green" for his liking, but he loved it.  I asked my family to rate it and my 8 year old son was disappointed that I gave him a range of 1-5 stars because he said he'd definetly give this a 6 star rating!  I had to make a little extra so that I would have left overs the next day.  So next time I will make a bigger batch.  I forgot to add the bacon bits the first time so I added them to the second batch.  I was good both ways.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeo bites

these are a bit reminiscent of stuffed jalapeño peppers but much easier to make. i found this in the junior league celebrations cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine the cream cheese , parmesan , jalapeo peppers and egg yolks in a bowl and mix to form a paste
3. shape a 1 / 2 tablespoonful at a time into 1 / 4-inch rounds and roll in the bread crumbs
4. place on an ungreased baking sheet and bake for 10-15 minutes or until golden brown
5. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I decided to make these for a holiday get together.  I did double the amount of jalapeno.  When I was mixing these up I did not believe that I would be able to make them without them melting all over, so I adding about 1/4 cup of the bread crumbs to the batter.  I was still a little doubtful, but they did bake wonderfully and they were quite tasty.  I do wish that there was more jalapeno flavor, so I will probably add more jalapeno the next time I make these and omit the extra bread crumbs. This was an interesting and tasty treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: this was was great. My family and I love, love, love it! I added more potatoes, because I cant ever get enough pototo, I added some frozen petite peas and corn. I also added a couple of bay leaves, because that is what my dear friend mrs. chance suggested. Depending on my mood I add spices like basil, majorum, thyme, celery seed,or sage.  I double or triple  this so that I can freeze a pie for another meal. I also have made this recipe and topped it with biscuits. This recipe is SO GOOD that the word spread about it and I have people friending me on facebook, just to find out where to get the recipe LOL :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini chocolate cake

don't you just love it when you can get your daily vegetable requirements from the dessert you eat? and a chocolate dessert at that!

1. cream butter then add oil and sugar
2. mix
3. add next 8 ingredients
4. mix well
5. fold in the chips and nuts by hand
6. put in a greased and floured 9 x 13 pan
7. bake at 325 for 1 hour or until done
demonstrations.review: I made this cake months ago and never reviewed it.  It was delicious my only complaint was with the frosting I made for the top.  Next time I will try frosting that is a tad less sweet or maybe no frosting at all

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halloween worms

notes: use a cleaned 1-quart milk or orange juice carton to hold straws

1. in a bowl , combine gelatins
2. add boiling water
3. stir until gelatins completely dissolve
4. chill until lukewarm , about 20 minutes
5. meanwhile , gently pull straws to extend to full length
6. place in tall container
7. blend cream and food coloring with the lukewarm gelatin mixture
8. pour into container , filling straws
9. chill until gelatin is firm , at least 8 hours , or cover and chill up to 2 days
10. pull straws from container
11. pull straws apart
12. run hot tap water for about 2 seconds over 3 to 4 straws at a time
13. starting at the empty ends , push worms from straws with rolling pin , or use your fingers
14. lay worms on waxed paper-lined baking sheets
15. cover and chill until ready to use , at least 1 hour or up to 2 days
16. worms will hold at room temperature up to 2 hours
demonstrations.review: What a cool idea!  I love it.  Until it came time to get the worms out of the straws.  Way too time consuming.  I ran out of time and gave up. They look just like real worms though.  May try again next year and start early just because it is so gross - I mean cool!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese enchilada chowder

from bhg. a slow-cooker chowder.

1. add the black beans , tomatoes , frozen corn , onion , bell pepper , and jalapeno pepper to a 4 quart slow-cooker
2. stir to combine
3. in a mixing bowl , add the enchilada sauce and cream soup
4. whisk together
5. gradually whisk in the milk until mixture is smooth
6. pour over vegetables in slow-cooker
7. cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours
8. add cheese and stir until melted
9. ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls and top with sour cream , guacamole and broken tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review: When my DF Mrs. Chance came for a visit we made this dish together before we went out shopping for the day.  We doubled the recipe and I froze half the ingredients for and even faster crock pot recipe for another day!  We added chicken and more pepper.  When we came home from shopping we were o so pleased with our dinner.  This is a recipe that we will make regularly in my house!

target.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin with port sauce

saw this on martha, this tastes soooooo good!

1. heat oil in a medium , heavy-bottomed skillet over high heat
2. pat pork dry , and season with salt and pepper
3. cook pork in oil until brown , about 4 minutes or until cooked to desired doneness
4. transfer to a warm platter
5. set aside
6. remove skillet from heat
7. discard fat , and add port
8. return skillet to heat
9. deglaze pan , scraping with a wooden spoon to loosen the browned bits from the bottom
10. continue cooking until sauce is reduced to about 2 tablespoons
11. add stock , and cook until sauce is lightly syrupy , about 4 minutes
12. whisk in butter , a little at a time , gently shaking pan while whisking
13. stir in vinegar
14. taste , and adjust for seasoning
15. spoon sauce over pork , and serve immediately
target.review: This was excellent!! Next time I make it I am going to double the recipe for the sauce and serve it on the side. It was soooo good we all want extra so we aren't sopping it off of the serving platter!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: I LOVED this recipe! We eat a lot of salmon and are always looking for new ways to prepare it. This is now my favorite salmon recipe. It was so good! I made it exactly as the recipe stated but in the future I will try it with different nuts, especially pistachios that Marchellabella did! Thank you for this great recipe! It's super easy and fast too, so it's a great weeknight dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoky jalapeno bites

i love a jalapeno popper, but i always hate when i bite into the peppers that are cut in half lengthwise and all the yummy cheese pulls off, or you don't get a piece of bacon in every bite, etc.  the 2-3 bite process really ruined the deliciousness for me, so my husband came up with a great solution.  the flavors in this tasty treat are much the same as many other jalapeno appetizers, but these are cut to be perfectly bite-sized.  note:  these can be fully assembled a day ahead of time and baked when it's time to serve.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. prepare broiler pan by spraying with a non-stick spray
3. remove stems from peppers and cut each pepper into 1 / 2" to 3 / 4" rounds
4. using a paring knife or an apple corer , remove seeds and ribs from the inside of each pepper round
5. i rinse off the pepper after they're seeded to remove some of the spicy oils
6. lay out the halved bacon slices
7. place a pepper round in the middle of each one
8. stuff each pepper round with cream cheese and top with a sprinkle of cheddar cheese
9. fold each end of bacon over the pepper round , overlapping the ends and securing with a toothpick
10. place on broiler pan and bake for 20-25 minutes or until bacon is fully cooked
demonstrations.review: These were so good! If you are making these for a crowd, you had better make a LOT as they go fast! I served these as appetizers with B.L.A (bacon, lettuce, apple) Bites # 252447 and everyone LOVED it! The two complimented ewach other nicely!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the original cabbage soup diet

i got this out of the national enquirer in 1995-1996 when the soup diet originally came out. i don't remember the rules of the diet other than you could eat as much of this as you wanted.

1. place all in large stock pot and bring to a boil
2. simmer for 1 hour
3. refrigerate all leftovers
demonstrations.review: This is the best soup ever! I remember eating it back when I was younger when my mom was trying to lose weight and I thought it was sooo good then! I use hardly any balsamic though as it makes it way too tangy for my taste, but a tablespoon or two gives it a nice flavor. We usually have this soup on hand since the recipe makes so much that we'll freeze a bunch of it. And it freezes very well! Once we run out we'll end up making another batch a week or two later. Thanks for finding this and posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan jambalaya

this is from a great new vegan cookbook that my sister got me. i always looked at vegan food as earthy and grose, but this really changed my mind.

1. cube and marinate tempeh in broth , olive oil , cajun seasonings , cayenne , and tabasco overnight
2. brown tempeh and tempeh sausage in pan with additional olive oil
3. remove from heat
4. add artichoke hearts
5. in large pot , put 2 t
6. olive oil , 1 t
7. cajun seasonings , onion , peppers , and garlic
8. saute until onion is clear
9. add 1 cup of rice and stir over high heat until rice is translucent
10. add 2 cups of water and juice from can of rotel
11. stir and then cover
12. reduce heat to medium-low and cook for 25 minutes
13. once rice is cooked-- remove from heat
14. stir in tempeh mixture , can of rotel , and salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I printed this up for my boyfriend and he ended up making it. So the recipe was made as-is and it turned out fantastic! We like spicy foods so this didn't seem that hot to us and had a nice flavor! This is going ot be our new jambalaya recipe that we use! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan fried chicken vegan chicken nuggets  gluten free

i served these to some non-vegan friends (one of whom "hates tofu") and they seemed to really like them. based on a recipe from vegweb.com.  the original called for crushed cornflakes, but when i went to make this, somebody had eaten all my cornflakes so i used lay's baked potato chips instead.  i like the salty taste of the chips better than the sweet of the cornflakes, but feel free to used crushed anything here and add other seasonings to your heart's content.  you can find vegetarian chicken bouillon at your local health food store.

1. put hot water in a bowl and stir in bouillon
2. soak tvp in this liquid for 10 minutes
3. it will expand
4. stir in just enough instant mashed potatoes to make a doughy mixture that can be formed into patties
5. mix in salt , pepper , and other seasonings to taste
6. dip patties in crushed baked potato chips , covering completely
7. fry in oil until crispy , turning occasionally
demonstrations.review: This was so very good! I'm new to the vegan thing so I was looking for TVP and couldn't find it and used tempeh instead which could very well be the TVP! But It turned out and I was surprised at how much it tasted like chicken! I will make this again, and yes, some of my nuggets fell apart and some stayed together nicely. I think I am going to try and bake them, like the other reviewer did, next time I make them and see how that works! Great recipe though!

target.recipe_text:
southwest sausage and pasta casserole

this is very simple to make and (when using mild salsa) kids love it.  you can make it as spicy as you like!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease a 13 x 9 dish
3. set aside
4. cook shell pasta according to package
5. set aside and keep hot
6. while pasta cooks , brown the sausage in a skillet with the onions until no longer pink
7. drain well
8. return the cooked sausage and onions to the skillet
9. stir in the salsa , salsa con queso , and fat free sour cream
10. stir in the cooked shell pasta and mix well
11. pour into the prepared casserole dish
12. sprinkle with the cheese
13. bake at 350 for about 20 - 25 minutes
target.review: This was very good, quick and easy to make.  I didn't have enough salsa so I added a can of Rotel tomatoes and boy was it spicy! I will make this again but next time I'll make sure I have enough salsa, lol. Thanks Parsley.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken chimi chimies   chimichangas

this is an easy chimichanga, great for a busy day. i like to cook the chicken ahead, so that dinner can be ready in under 30 minutes. one chimi is good for smaller eaters, two for those hearty appetites. this is a mild dish, unless you add lots of cumin, which makes it great for kids. if you like spicy add a few dashes of hot sauce or a diced jalapeño. after reading a couple of reviews i realized that i too was increasing the sour cream without paying exact attention to the recipe this adapted from. i don't always start with the same amount of chicken so, you want the mix to be slightly wet and gooshy without being drippy, it should cling together.  i sometimes add 1/2 cup of shredded cheese to the mix, but you can leave it out to avoid the extra fat.   serve with your favorite side dishes, i like spanish rice and fruit with this.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. boil chicken in water until done , about 15 minutes
3. for extra flavor add some onion & garlic , and salt and pepper to the water
4. shred chicken
5. saut garlic and onion in the oil about 5 minutes , don't brown
6. stir together chicken and all the ingredients except for butter , tortillas and cheese
7. brush tortillas one at a time with melted butter , to the dry side and a spoon a generous scoop of chicken mixture in a line about 1 inch from one edge of the tortilla , tuck in sides as you go and roll up tortilla , and place seam side down on a cookie sheet , repeat until all you mixture is used
8. bake 15 minutes or until golden brown
9. option:
10. if you prefer your cheese melted , a few minutes before removing from the oven , sprinkle each chimi with shredded cheese
11. serve chimis with shredded cheese , also good with sour cream , chopped tomatoes and black olives
demonstrations.review: All of us thought this was very good. After reading the reviews, I decided to replace the tomato sauce with salsa. I thought it gave the kick that some of the other reviewers thought was missing. I used 2 tsp. cumin and I also sprayed them with Pam, as another reviewer suggested.  For the chicken breast, I used chopped meat from a purchased rotisserie chicken. I will definitely make this again. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin gooey cake

another yummy one from turkey hill just in time for fall!  wonderful served warm and topped with ice cream.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine cake mix and egg and butter mix well , pat the mixture into the bottom of a lightly greased 13x9 inch baking pan
3. filling: beat cream cheese and pumpkin until smooth , add eggs , vanilla and butter and beat together
4. next , add powdered sugar , cinnamon , nutmeg , cloves and mix well
5. spread pumpkin mixture over cake mixture and bake for 40 to 50 minutes
6. do not over bake
7. the center should be gooey
demonstrations.review: You get 5 stars from my co-workers! They kept commenting on how good the crust was. I still have quite a few butternut squash from my garden so I used it instead of the pumpkin. Personally, I thought this was very similar to a pumpkin pie, so since this is loaded with fat and calories, I think I will only make this occasionally.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever chocolate zucchini cake

i've been making this recipe for ions now.  it was a collaboration between myself and a friend about 25 years ago.  i haven't found one i like better. i hope you will agree.  these loaves also freeze very well.    note:  you could try using applesauce for some or all of the oil in order to reduce the fat content.  however....i haven't tried it myself.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. in a large bowl mix together eggs , both sugars , oil and both extracts
3. stir in grated zucchini
4. set aside
5. in another bowl mix flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cocoa powder
6. add to the zucchini mixture , mixing well
7. fold in nuts and raisins
8. pour into greased loaf pans
9. bake for approximately 75 minutes or until tested done with a toothpick
demonstrations.review: I have made this cake twice now.  I didn't add the nuts or raisins and I used the dark Dutch processed cocoa.  Very good taste and texture and not too sweet.  I brought some to work and everyone loved it.  Even those who wont eat zucchini tried it and loved it too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
clamato caldo verde

clamato is very popular in canada.  one of my hubby's favourite drinks is a bloody caesar (a canadian version of a bloody mary, made with clamato juice), so i am always on the lookout for clamato recipes.  this is from www.clamato.com

1. heat a large saucepanon medium-high
2. saute the onion and garlic in a little oil for about 3 minutes
3. add the potatoes and saute for another 2-3 minutes
4. add clamato and broth , cover and let simmer for 20 minutes
5. while the potatoes simmer , hear a skillet over medium-high heat and saute chorizo for about 10 minutes
6. drain fat and reserve
7. when potatoes are soft , mash them in the pan , then add chorizo and greens
8. season with salt and pepper and let simmer for another 10 minutes
9. add shrimp and let heat through
demonstrations.review: I had a lot of collards to use up after cleaning out my garden for spring planting. To be honest, I was a little bit skeptical and hesitant about trying this recipe. I'm so glad that I did because I thought this was fabulous! The chorizo gave it a little kick, but not too much. It didn't have a strong collard taste like I thought it would. Thank you for posting. I will definitely make this again next fall!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple cheese cake

wonderful summer treat!
everyone loves it and asks for the recipe.
it's fast,cool & yummy!
what more could you ask for??

1. mix margarine & crumbs together
2. press into a 13x9x2" pan
3. bake @ 350f for 5-8 minutes
4. cool
5. mix powered suger & cream cheese well
6. blend in cool whip & fold in pineapple
7. pour over graham cracker crust
8. spread evenly & refrigerate
9. crumble graham crackers on top
demonstrations.review: You were right! Every one loved this pie.  It's more like a fluffy cheesecake instead of a traditional heavy cheesecake. I only changed one thing: I didn't have a 12 oz. can of pineapple, I only had a 20 oz. can, so instead of wasting 8 oz. I threw in the whole can.  Probably all it did was give it a more intense flavor. Thanks, this is a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
baked trout amandine

from coup de pouce.  this is an healthy recipe that i plan to try soon.  and also it's done in less than 30 minutes.

1. put the buttermilk in a shallow bowl
2. in another shallow bowl , mix breadcrumbs , parsley , mustard powder , salt and pepper
3. dip the trouts in buttermilk , letting drain the excess , then put in the breadcrumbs flipping them to coat well
4. put the trout fillets on a baking sheet that has oiled foil on it
5. sprinkle almonds on them and drizzle with butter
6. cook in a preheated oven of 450 f 8 to 12 minutes per inch of thickness or until it flakes easily with a fork
target.review:
Once I read this recipe, I knew I had to try it right away! Could not find trout fillets, so decided to buy tilapia instead. I used Panko bread crumbs, dried parsley and lemon pepper. It is so easy to put together and it tastes delicious. I can't wait to make it again. My husband says it's definitely a keeper. Thanks for posting this one, Boomette!

P.S.  I forgot to mention that I used the rest of the ingredients as listed.  We especially loved the toasty taste of the slivered almonds - it gave the fish just the right crunch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boursin stuffed chicken breasts with pistachio crust

i found this on the internet and it is a great company meal.  every time i have made this i have been asked for the recipe.

1. cut any bits of fat or skin off chicken breasts
2. lay breasts flat on cutting board and make a small pocket on the side
3. stuff each breast with a quarter of the cheese
4. coat each breast completely with 1 tablespoon mayonnaise
5. place chopped pistachios on a plate and press each breast into the pistachios to coat completely
6. lay the chicken on a baking sheet and bake at 350 for 30 minutes or until interior temperature reads 160f
7. serve with white wine sauce
8. white wine sauce:
9. in a heavy saucepan , melt butter and saute onion until translucent
10. add wine , and boil on medium heat until more than half of the wine has evaporated , stirring occasionally
11. add chicken broth and boil again until half the stock has evaporated , stirring occasionally
12. add heavy cream and boil until half the liquid has evaporated , stirring occasionally
13. remove from heat
14. add salt and pepper
15. serve with chicken
demonstrations.review: This is a yummy recipe!  Because we are watching calories and fat contents, I served it without the sauce and used light boursin and mayonnaise -- it still tasted great!  Thank you for posting.  Will definitely keep and make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin with balsamic cranberry sauce

nan

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. melt 1 / 2 tablespoon butter in heavy large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat
3. sprinkle pork with salt and pepper
4. sear pork on all sides , about 2 minutes
5. place skillet with pork in oven
6. roast pork until thermometer inserted into center registers 155f , about 10 minutes
7. meanwhile , melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter in heavy medium skillet over medium-high heat
8. add onion and rosemary
9. saut until onion softens , about 3 minutes
10. add broth , cranberry sauce and vinegar and whisk until cranberry sauce melts , about 2 minutes
11. transfer pork to work surface
12. scrape any juices from large skillet into cranberry mixture
13. boil until sauce has reduced enough to coat spoon thickly , about 6 minutes
14. season with salt and pepper
15. slice pork and serve with sauce
demonstrations.review: This made a delicious Sunday dinner for the two of us.  It is easy to prepare and the flavors are simply wonderful.  I served it with a butternut squash risotto and steamed green beans.  Try this one, you will love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: I made these for the first time today.  I doubled the recipe and I did not use the electric mixer --maybe I should have!!   The mixture was quite thick when I was done.  I will add that extra egg yolk next time as someone recommended.  I found that the cookies were a bit dry but they still tasted good.  I used my cookie dough scoop and baked them in regular size muffin tins like I usually do.  They came out thick and chewy and friends seem to like them.  Will definitely make these again.  Thank you for sharing this recipe with all of us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed pork tenderloin

this special pork is tender and juicy and seasoned just right.

1. mix the first 11 ingredients
2. rub over the pork
3. put on a rack in a shallow roasting pan
4. bake , uncovered , at 400 for 45 minutes
5. remove from oven , cover with foil and let set for 10 minutes
6. slice into servings
demonstrations.review:
Easy, easy, easy, yummy, yummy, YUMMY!!!!!  How could you go wrong with all these spices?  We practically licked our plates....
Thanks for a great recipe that is going straight to "my favorites" folder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herb roasted pork tenderloin

got this recipe from southern living magazine. oh so good and easy.

1. stir together first 11 ingredients in a shallow dish or heavy-duty zip-top plastic bag
2. prick pork with a fork , and place in marinade , turning to coat
3. cover dish , or seal bag
4. chill 2 hours
5. remove from marinade , discarding marinade
6. place pork on a rack in a roasting pan
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes or until a meat thermometer inserted into thickest portion of pork registers 160 degrees
demonstrations.review: This was the easiest to prepare and it tastes absolutely delicious.  Since there are only the two of us, I used one single tenderloin and halved all the other ingredients.  I chilled it for several hours and decided to grill it on the BBQ.  I seared the meat on all sides, dipped it one more time in the marinade and then used the indirect method of grilling for about 20 minutes.  It was moist, tender and great tasting.  We both loved it and thank you for sharing this easy way of preparing pork tenderloin.  A keeper for sure!

target.recipe_text:
hodas authentic hummus

hummus like my fav restaurant

1. mix tahini with olive oil pour in a little at a time until tahini is more of a thick cream not a paste make sure before you scoop out the tahini that it is not seperated in the container
2. start with 2 lemon's juice
3. mix tahini and 2 lemons with all the other ingredients and blend until smooth in a food processor
4. add salt and lemon to taste
5. i like to make a dip with a large spoon and add a little more olive oil to the center of the dish
6. always better with warm bread or falafel
target.review: This was good. My DH thought it was a little too lemony (which coming from the guy that eats lemons like most people eat oranges is a little odd). I only added the 2 lemons like it says to start out with too. My MIL liked it just the way it is though. I will be making this again because it's really easy and much cheaper than what you pay at a restaurant. Thank you for posting. Made for Alphabet Soup Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green chile cilantro pesto sauce  pasta

this comes from cook's country and i love everything from their magazine. i'm always looking for new pasta recipes, and i adore cilantro.

1. puree cilantro , cheese , green chile , jalapeno , pine nuts , and garlic in food processor until smooth , scraping down sides as necessary
2. with processor running , add oil in steady stream until emulsified
3. season with salt and pepper
4. toss pesto with cooked pasta and reserved pasta cooking water , if necessary
demonstrations.review: This pesto is the best! Living in AZ I've had and made my fair share of cilantro pesto, this is my go to recipe from now on. The jalepenos in the store were huge so I used half of one and it's got a really nice kick to it. I'm already thinking of how to use this with things other than pasta. Can't wait to try it with grilled pork loin... Thank you so much for posting this. (I love cilantro too)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monkey meat

this recipe goes real well with my lumpia recipe. this came from the same party as the lumpia did. awesome, tender and very tasty. no monkeys were harmed in any way in the preparation of this recipe. enjoy!

1. mix 7up , soy sauce and garlic in a large bowl
2. place pork loin strips in bowl
3. cover and refrigerate overnight
4. weave meat on skewers
5. grill until done
6. for me , it takes about 15 minute to cook
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: This is really good. The meat is super tender and I love the flavor the soy sauce leaves in the meat. Next time I'm going to add some fresh ginger and chile paste to it . I think we will also sprinkle with cilantro too. It's great as it is and I'm really glad we tried it. Looking forward to playing around with it too! Thanks for posting. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
macaroni and beef

this i have not tried but certainly does look scrumptious! from gourmet.

1. simmer chuck in broth in a 2 qt saucepan , uncovered , stirring occasionally , until meat is very tender , about 1 hour
