2. while meat simmers , break up tomatoes by squeezing them into a bowl with puree
3. cook onion in half of butter in a 4 qt saucepan over moderate heat , stirring , until softened
4. add tomatoes with puree , worcestershire sauce , and sugar , then simmer stirring occasionally , 15 minutes , or until slightly thickened
5. preheat oven to 400
6. to make topping , toss together bread crumbs , 1 cup cheddar , remaining melted butter and salt and pepper to taste
7. cook macaroni in boiling salted water until al dente , then drain in a colander
8. cool macaroni 3 minutes , then tranfer to a large bowl
9. toss with tomato sauce , beef with broth , remaining 3 cups cheese and salt and pepper to taste
10. transfer macaroni mixture to a buttered 13x9x2" glass baking dish and spoon topping evenly over
11. bake in middle of oven , uncovered , 25 minutes or until topping is golden brown and mixture is bubbling
12. makes 8-10 servings
demonstrations.review: This was ok, a little bland and I think it would be better with ground beef, texture wise and time wise. I really liked the cheese mixed with the breadcrumbs, I've even used the technique in other recipes with tasty results. I'm going to make this again and try some tweaking with it. Good recipe to start with, thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy rice

i got this recipe years ago from a kraft magazine ad.  it is a family favorite and a great way to use up left over rice.  makes a great side dish to grilled meats. prep time includes time to steam rice.  prep time using leftover rice is about 5 minutes

1. in a greased baking dish , mix together all ingredients
2. bake at 350 degrees until heated thru and cheese is melted
3. about 20 min or so
4. dig in !
demonstrations.review: This was good. I was happy with how quick it was and how it was made with ingredients that I had on hand. I do think that I'm going to be playing around with it though. My DH didn't like how much he could taste the sour cream in it. I think next time I'm going to add ham cubes, green onion and some garlic salt. I also want to top it with some crushed ritz crackers, think the texture will compliment the creamy rice. Thanks for posting an easy recipe, it made a nice dinner. Made for Alphabet Soup Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli ritz cracker casserole

this is really good and a great way to get the kids to eat broccoli !!

1. par boil the broccoli for approx 5-10 minutes ,
2. cut broccoli into bite size pieces and put in 9x13 baking dish
3. mix mushroom soup , mayonaise , onion , eggs , cheese and seasonings together
4. pour over broccoli
5. top with crushed ritz crackers
6. dot with butter
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes uncovered
demonstrations.review: This is out-of-this-world!!!! Didn't know what I was going to do for dinner tonight and happened to have all the ingredients. Sooooo yummy! Will definitely be making this again.  Would be great with rice and chicken added too for a complete meal. Thanks so much for posting.

target.recipe_text:
banana chocolate chip muffins  light

kids will ask for more!  if you love the mix of banana and chocolate you will love these light muffins!  a r. reisman recipe. i have made this recipe both with plain yogurt and sour cream and they always turn out great.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. spray a 12-cup muffin pan with cooking spray
3. in a large bowl and using an electric mixer , beat together bananas , sugar , oil , egg , and vanilla until well mixed
4. in another bowl , stir together flour , baking powder , and baking soda
5. stir flour mixture into banana mixture
6. stir in yogurt
7. fold in chocolate chips
8. divide among prepared muffin cups
9. bake in centre of oven for 15 minutes or until a tester inserted in centre of muffins comes out clean
target.review:
Made double version. Got 18 muffins that were good size. I divided double version without addition of chocolate chips and divided it in three bolls. In one I added chocolate chips; Another coconut flakes and last raisins. Chocolate chips went first. Coconut addition was OK, more for adults; raisins went in school lunches as chocolate is not allowed.
I was worried that muffins would be too heavy or overly moist, but it had a nice light texture without being crumbly. My family loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
radish sandwiches

these tasty little sandwiches are great for appetizers, tea parties, ladies luncheons, etc., but my husband ate two full size sandwiches for lunch, and loved them.  the recipe is from one of a kind, a mobile junior league community cookbook i received from sweetpea burgess in the recent cookbook swap.
note for the world tour participants - this recipe is included in the british category.  these are ideal little sandwiches to be served with tea, as is common in britain.

1. for the filling , finely chop the radishes in the food processor
2. place in a large sieve or colander
3. press with paper towels to drain and squeeze out any excess liquid
4. cream the cream cheese and butter together until fluffy
5. add drained chopped radishes , parsley , chives , lemon juice , salt and pepper to taste , and cream again
6. cut crusts from bread and cut into small squares or rounds
7. spread with filling , and garnish with sliced or whole radishes coated with coarse salt
8. chill thoroughly before serving
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved the spread. My husband was skeptic about radishes but was coming back for seconds, thirds and so on... I made the spread in less than 5 minutes. I shredded radishes on fine shredder in food processor, then changed shredder to mixing attachment, put the rest of ingredients and voila - spread was done. I forgot to drain juice from radishes but I don't think it affected the spread: spread was not runny at all. Thank you for the spread, I will make it again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat cinnabon  for the bread machine

oh my husband loves me to make these!!! got it off the copykat site

1. place all ingredients in your machine in order recommended by your machine's manufacturer
2. place the pan in your machine
3. select the dough cycle and press start
4. when cycle is finished , remove the dough , knead enough to punch down and roll to 17x10
5. combine first three filling ingredients and mix well
6. heat in microwave 10 seconds to make it spreadable
7. spread over rolled out dough with rubber spatula
8. get as close to the edges as possible
9. sprinkle nuts or raisins over dough
10. starting with widest end , roll the dough into tight log
11. cut into 1 / 2-1" slices
12. place in a lightly greased baking dish with sides
13. put in warm draft free place and allow them to raise until double
14. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes
15. when the rolls are done top with frosting of your choice
16. yield: a full 9x13 pan
demonstrations.review:
I made this recipe many times and everyone loves it. I do not follow much filling directions: I just butter rolled dough, sprinkle little bit of brown sugar, cinnamon and raisins. I also do not put any icing on top because I like it less sweet, but I powder icing sugar on top. 
Also I found that if I leave dough to rise for extra 2-3 hours I would end up with more fluffier buns.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: It was good week day supper. I added more whole seed cumin and sliced black olives on top of the cheese. Also next time I would put some sauce on the bottom of dish before putting tortillas down, because mine were sticking to the bottom. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham

a delicious ham. different from the usual pineapple ham.

1. with the fat side down , score the top of ham with four strokes across and then turn 1 / 2 turn and score again with four more
2. place ham in a baking dish and smother with the mustard
3. next pat the brown sugar over the mustard until covered
4. then pour the maple syrup over the brown sugar and mustard until covered
5. pour 1 cup apple juice into bottom of pan and cover
6. bake at 350 degrees f for about 1 1 / 2 hours
7. serve with scalloped potatoes
demonstrations.review: Good basic ham. It would be good for party when people have different test and you want to please everyone. I did the ham in slow cooker and had very nice sauce. I did not have maple sirop so I used pancake sirop and ham still turnout great. Next time I would plan to have maple sirop on hand and this ham would be even better. Was very easy to make. I used fancy style mustard (dijon with mastard seeds). Thanks for simple, tasty and no fail recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vietnamese beef stew  bo  kho

my mom and dad make this dish in the winter a lot. every time they do, the whole house smells wonderful. one time my mom came to visit me in boarding school in england. she cooked one pot, i ate for a whole week and got on the black list of all asians in school. it taste good steaming hot with french bread, and also very good in sandwiches. some ingredients are available at normal grocery stores. you can get star anise and thai basil at asian stores, natural food stores

1. mix lemongrass , fish sauce , 5-spice powder , ginger , brown sugar and bay leaf , marinate the beef for 30 minutes
2. over high heat , heat oil in a heavy-bottemed 5-quart pot , sear the beef quickly then remove , reserve lemongrass and bay leaf for later use
3. reduce heat to medium , cook onions till translucent , then add tomato and cook with lid on for another 12-15 minutes
4. if sauce is too thick , add a bit of water
5. add back the beef , lemongrass , bay leaf and star anise , cook uncovered for 5 minutes then add water
6. bring pot to a boil , then reduce heat to simmer for 1 hour and 15 minutes
7. add carrots and simmer for another 45 minutes until beef and carrots are tender
8. remove bay leaf , lemongrass and star anise before serving with cilantro and thai basil
9. taste great with steam rice or french bread
demonstrations.review: I made your stew tonight. My husband and I loved it. The smell was wondeful. Taste has a good balance between salt and sugar. Fish sauce gives extra nuance but does not smell fishy at all. I added little bit of corn starch to make sauce thicker. What a great and different way to use  stew meat. Thank you very much for your posting.

target.recipe_text:
seared salmon with balsamic glaze

i saw this on sara's secrets and couldn't wait to try it! the sauce brings out the sweetness in the fish. enjoy!

1. stir together balsamic vinegar , water , lemon juice , and brown sugar in a small bowl
2. pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium high heat , not smoking
4. increase heat to high , add salmon skin side up , and sear until well browned , about 4 minutes
5. turn fish over and sear until just cooked through , 3 to 4 minutes more
6. transfer salmon to plates and carefully add vinegar mixture to skillet
7. simmer , stirring , until thickened and reduced to about 1 / 3 cup , about 2 minutes
8. spoon glaze over salmon
9. serve and enjoy !
target.review: This was excellent! I followed the recipe exactly...although I used frozen fillets w/o skin. I served it over a salad of Italian greens w/cold peas. It was really wonderful and it will most definitely be used again...and again! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet  cinnamon yellow bread

this recipe makes 2 loaves of the best sweet bread. we eat it for dessert.or with our morning coffee. its my father-in-law's favorite.  he says it's more cake than bread. freezes wonderfully for those last-minute guests.  enjoy!

1. beat cake mix , pudding , eggs , oil , water and extracts together for 8 minutes
2. mix sugar and cinnamon together
3. set aside
4. pam spray loaf pans
5. pour 2 / 3 batter into pans equally
6. pour cinnamon mixture equally over both loaves
7. using a knife swirl cinnamon through batter
8. top with remaining batter equally over both
9. bake at 350f for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This is pretty good --- got better as it sat. i think the next time i bake it i will change up the filling as that's the part that just isn't quite all it could be....maybe add some nuts or even try a date filling. thanks for the jumping off point!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat recipe for carrabba s chicken marsala

a clone dish from carrabba's restaurant. i have not tried this yet, but will soon and add more comments. sounds wonderful!

1. pound chicken breasts to even out thickness and lightly salt and pepper
2. in large skillet , saute chicken in 2 t melted butter until lightly browned , about 2 minutes per side
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. melt remaining butter in pan and add shallots and mushrooms
5. cook until mushrooms are lightly browned
6. add marsala and bring to a boil , scraping browned bits from bottom of pan
7. add cream and lemon juice and return to a boil
8. season with salt and pepper
9. return chicken to pan for about 3 minutes to reheat and finish cooking
10. serve with buttered fettucini
demonstrations.review: This is pretty much delicious ---- i subbed half and half for the cream and green onion for the shallots .... served w/garlic smashed potatoes it was an excellent meal. i would suggest one does not skimp on the salt/pepper or the marsala.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate heart cookies

i found this last year in the "taste of home" magazine. they were an instant hit and left everyone craving more. excellent for valentines especially, but they are good any time of the year. i dip them in the milk chocolate and drizzle white - though the recipe calls for it the other way, you can chose to reverse the amounts between white and milk chocolate chips according to your taste.

1. in a small mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. beat in vanilla
3. combine the flour and cocoa
4. gradually add to creamed mixture
5. on a lightly floured surface roll the dough to 1 / 4-inch thickness
6. cut with a heart-shaped cookie cutter placing 2-inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake at 350f for 8-10 minutes
8. remove to wire racks to cool
9. in a microwave safe bowl , heat vanilla chips and 1 tablespoon of shortening until melted , stirring frequently
10. dip both sides of the cookie into melted mixture
11. in another microwave safe bowl , melt chocolate chips and remaining shortening , stirring frequently
12. drizzle over the cookies
13. place on wire rack to dry
demonstrations.review: Easy cookies to make in a relative short period of time. I used 1/2 cup of butter and 6 generous ounces of cream cheese instead of all butter....I only dipped a generous half of the cookie in chocolate, drizzled the white. Cookies were gone in an evening....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana cookies  with dates and nuts

yummy cookies!! great when you have leftover bananas that are too soft to eat .. they smell heavenly while baking, and keep well in the fridge ... i don't add the nuts, but you can if you like ..

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , sugar and eggs
3. add bananas and vanilla , mix well
4. add the rest of the ingredients , with dates and nuts last
5. drop dough onto cookie sheet , and flatten slightly
6. bake 12 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: Fabulous!! These were exactly what i was looking for. They are tender and the perfect consistency. I used butter flavored crisco and creamed that with the sugar til fluffy before adding the eggs. I also combined all the dry before adding, finally stirring in 1 3/4 cup oatmeal and probably 2/3 cup of chopped pecans and a generous cup of dates. These would be good with a dab of chocolate frosting...although i'll leave them alone...this time! These will be added to my fav's list - thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican pork cubes

simple, yet delicious meat.  this is something i came up with one night when i was craving the usual mexican flare and had pork on hand.  i served it with my recipe #150134 and a side of corn.  good eats!

1. sprinkle meat with spices and place meat in saucepan with onion and butter and brown on both sides of pork chops
2. then add in the salsa and red wine vinegar and remove pork chops one at a time cutting into cubes , and place back in pan when finished cutting
3. once all pork is cooked through take off heat and sprinkle with cheese and place lid on pan and leave until melted
demonstrations.review: i came across this while looking for something to put with tomalitos...i ended up combining this recipe w/#172900 pork machaca... i omitted the salsa and used tomato paste, no cumin and no shredded cheddar. the two recipes together were more than outstanding. i've had numerous requests to repeat - like daily!!! thanks so much!!!

target.recipe_text:
asparagus with wasabi mayonnaise dip

adapted from cooking live, this is excellent! you may add more wasabi if you want more kick! this is good with other vegetables, meat, sandwiches and crackers!

1. blanch the asparagus in 2 batches in a large saucepan of boiling salted water for 1 minute
2. move to a colander and rinse under cold running water to stop it from cooking
3. drain well and pat dry
4. whisk together mayonnaise , soy sauce , sugar , lemon juice , and wasabi paste until sugar is dissolved
5. serve asparagus with dip
6. this dip is also good as a spread for sandwiches and as a topping for cooked veggies ! enjoy !
target.review:
This was soooooo good!  I made this with our ham on Easter Sunday and served with asparagus and brussel sprouts.  I have to make more and use it as a vegetable dip or chip dip.  We'll dip anything into it.  I added 2 tablespoons (misread the "teaspoons") and it was excellent.  We love wasabi and it was not overpowering.  It added such a nice flavour.  I will definitely recommend this to anyone!  Thanks for posting.
I just made this again a couple of weeks after my original review and we actually used it as a salad dressing and always use leftovers for fresh veggies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanishing oatmeal raisin cookies

oatmeal raisin cookie recipe from the quaker oats box.  bar cookie variation included.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. beat together margarine and sugars until creamy
3. add eggs and vanilla
4. beat well
5. add combined flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
6. mix well
7. stir in oats and raisins
8. mix well
9. drop by rounded tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
11. cool 2 minutes on cookie sheet
12. remove to wire rack
13. makes about 4 dozen
14. bar cookies: bake 30 to 35 minutes in ungreased 13x9-inch metal baking pan
demonstrations.review: These were exactly what I was looking for.  I didn't read all 40 ratings, but what I did read, no one mentioned that they were chewy.  That's what we love - CHEWY oatmeal raisin cookies.  I did have to lower my oven to 325 F and they baked for 10 minutes.  They did not spread much so you can load them up on your cookie sheet.  My daughter loved them too so the two of us made another batch the very next day for her to take to her co-op work place.  Great recipe!  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach pinwheel appetizers

these are pretty to look at, but even better to eat! enjoy!! i can't remember how many pinwheels you get, but i know it makes a lot.

1. in medium mixing bowl , combine cream cheese , sour cream and mayonnaise
2. beat in dip mix
3. add green onion , bacon bits and spinach
4. mix thoroughly
5. spread mixture onto tortillas , leaving a 1 / 2" space around edge
6. roll up each tortilla tightly , and wrap each in plastic wrap
7. chill for several hours or overnight
8. to serve , cut off ends and cut into 1 / 2" slices
demonstrations.review: I have made these a few times and keep forgetting to rate them.  They are real easy to make and are a favorite appetizer among so many people.  I buy the flavoured tortilla wraps (spinach, sun-dried tomato, whole wheat) anything but the plain flour tortillas.  I've also made them to store in the freezer.  I roll them up tightly in waxed paper, twist the ends and then put them in a large ziplock baggy.  I then have a quick appetizer on hand for those emergencies when unexpected guests show up.  Just take out however many you need, let sit for a few minutes, unwrap, and slice. They are much easier to cut when they are still half frozen and they don't take much longer to completely thaw.  Sometimes my DH and I just want something to munch on so I'll defrost one, take out pickles, cheese, olives and we have a nice variety of tastes for a weekend lunch.  I've worked up an appetite for these now.  I'll have to go buy the ingredients and make a batch of them.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham broccoli quiche

oh this is so yum!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a skillet over medium-high heat , saute' mushrooms and garlic in butter until tender
3. sprinkle swiss cheese in pie crust
4. top with mushroom mixture , ham and broccoli
5. in a mixing bowl , beat together eggs , milk , flour , white pepper and nutmeg
6. pour into pie crust
7. sprinkle with romano or parmesan cheese
8. bake 35 to 40 minutes or until a knife inserted near center comes out clean
9. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night. It was a huge hit and I absolutely loved it.  I had leftover ham from the day before and I wanted to use some of it up.  I made just a couple of small changes.  I used a mix of mozzarella and cheddar for the cheese. I also added chopped onion so I fried the mushrooms and garlic with onion and the fresh broccoli.  I didn't have any nutmeg so that was left out.  I had 2 pie crusts in the freezer so I made 2 quiches.  I'm glad I did.  One's in the freezer now ready to be reheated for a quick dinner.  This was my first time making quiche and definitely not my last.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I forgot to rate this when I made it a couple of months ago.  This went over really well in my family and has an excellent flavour.  I shredded the leftover chicken and we used it as a dip with tortilla chips.  Man, was it ever good.  We even ate it cold right out of the fridge.  I will make this easy recipe again and again.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked brie pastries with artichoke and prosciutto

i needed an appetizer for a dinner last night, and had all these ingredients at home.  these came out wonderfully well!  very tasty.  :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. if you have frozen puff pastry , allow it to thaw
3. cut the sheet into 9 squares
4. push the squares into 9 of the spaces a lightly sprayed muffin tin
5. in the food processor , whir enough artichoke hearts to make 1 cup of them when they are very finely chopped
6. in a bowl , combine the artichoke , basil , vinegar , salt , and pepper
7. place about 3 / 4 to 1 teaspoon brie in the bottom of each puff pastry in the muffin tin
8. add about 1 1 / 2 teaspoon of the artichoke mixture on top of the brie
9. top each with the chopped prosciutto and sprinkle with parmesan
10. bake at 350 degrees f for about 15 minutes , or until the puff pastry is golden
11. let sit for about 5 minutes before serving
12. makes 9 appetizers , about 6 servings since some people will have two
demonstrations.review: I made these for a get together with two of my best friends.  What a nice presentation.  Very flavourful and great for company.  We ate them all.  They were impressive and my friends thought I slaved over them.  I will be making them again.  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
apple pannekoeken

history in the baking.  they have a place here that makes them up at mayo clinic. that's what they make up here in minnesota. if you like popvovers you will like this it fast and easy

1. melt butter in an 8x8 inch pan
2. mix milk , flour , and eggs until smooth
3. pour into pan
4. spoon on apple filling
5. bake at 400 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
6. serve immediately
7. it will fall
target.review:
We can't get apple pie filling in Belgium so I used apples cut up finely and mixed with brown sugar instead. The directions are very good (maybe you would like to check after 25 min., mine was a bit too brown at the bottom, every oven is different of course).
For me this tasted a bit too eggy, but I'm glad I tried it! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai coconut curry noodles

i found this recipe on the back of a noodle pack while wandering in the grocery store one day.  we really enjoyed it, but added more veggies to make it a little healthier.  it's a great weeknight meal, as quite quick to prepare.

1. separate noodles in hot water , as per instructions on the packet
2. drain & keep warm
3. in a medium saucepan , heat the coconut mild on low heat and slowly stir in the curry paste
4. when it begins to simmer , add in the remaining ingredients , except for the port and snow peas
5. stir for around 2 minutes then add the port and heat until the pork is cooked
6. stir in the noodles and snow peas and serve
demonstrations.review:
For the first time ever, my kids liked an asian dish. I was stunded! Usualy they don't care for anything oriental, but this time they emptied their plates. What more could I want? DH and I enjoyed this dish very much too. I did use regular frozen peas, but it tasted great. A keeper!
Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favourite chicken curry

this is a winner with my family. 
i like to serve this with onion pilau #108305. i also like to throw in a handful of red lentils towards the end whilst it is simmering. pumpkin and baby spinch chucked in towards the end is nice also.

1. remove skin from chicken pieces , discard skin
2. toss chicken in flour , shake off excess
3. heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large pan , cook chicken , in batches until browned
4. drain on absorbent paper
5. heat remaining oil in pan , cook onion , garlic , chilli , cumin and curry powder until fragrant
6. return chicken to pan with the undrained tomatoes , paste , sugar and stock
7. bring to the boil , simmer uncovered for 30 minutes or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: I halved the recipe and made it as stated. It was really wonderful. As it reminded me of a moroccan recipe, so I added some zucchini, dried apricots and a handful of lentils. I served it with couscous. This is a very versatile recipe, you can easily add some new ingredients (veggies). Is is quickly made and both meat and veggies are in one dish. Fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fennel  smoked salmon and orange salad

a lovely, light, summery salad.  the citrus, the lightly licorice-flavoured fennel, and the smoked salmon are an amazing combination!  my daughter practically inhales this!

1. in a small bowl , whisk together the olive oil , orange juice , sea salt and black pepper
2. set aside
3. place fennel in a bowl and toss with about half of the dressing mixture until evenly coated
4. set aside
5. arrange orange slices attractively on four salad plates
6. mound the fennel mixture on top , divide and top with the smoked salmon , sprinkle with green onions and parmesan , then drizzle sparingly with the remaining dressing
demonstrations.review: Very refreshing and original salad! We liked it very much, but I would try to give it some more of a kick by using another dressing a next time. Perfect for hot summer nights, when you don't want to do too much of a cooking. Be sure to use the best ingredients you can afford!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country barbecue muffins

i got this recipe from a friend that served them at her son's birthday party. these are easy, delicious and a big hit with kids.

1. separate dough into 10 biscuits
2. flatten into 5 inch circles
3. press each into the bottom and up the sides of a greased muffin cup
4. set aside
5. in a skillet , brown ground beef
6. drain
7. add diced tomatoes to meat if desired
8. in a small bowl , mix ketchup , brown sugar , vinegar and chili powder
9. stir until smooth
10. add to meat and tomatoes
11. mix well
12. divide the meat mixture among biscuit-lined muffin cups , using about 1 / 4 cup for each
13. sprinkle with cheese
14. bake at 350 for 18 to 20 minutes or until golden brown
15. cool for 5 minutes before removing from tin and serving
demonstrations.review: These were a big hit in our family. Everyone absolutely loves them. I certainly will be making them again. Thanks for this great recipe. I used puff pastry instead of the buttermilk biscuits (never seen those in Belgium), and it turned out great, I just had to bake them for 5 min. longer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish angel crisps

a swedish cookie that you can adapt to your tastes easily by changing the ingredients around.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream together the shortening , sugars , and butter until smooth
3. stir in the egg and vanilla extract
4. sift together the flour , baking soda , and cream of tartar
5. stir into the sugar mixture
6. roll dough into walnut sized balls
7. roll the balls in chopped nuts then in sugar
8. place on an ungreased cookie sheet and bake for 12 to 15 minutes or until cookies are golden brown
9. cool on a wire rack completely before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a good cookie but it contains a bit too much suger to my taste. If you use the amount in the cookie, it gets a little too sugary when you roll them in sugar before baking. Other than that I wouldn't make any changes and it's a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
jen s low fat high fiber bran muffins

i have gone through pretty much all the bran muffin recipes on the zaar (and there are a lot!) and i could not find one like mine. we really enjoyed these, and i think if i don't write it down i'll forget all the substitutions i made! this makes 2 dozen regular or a lot of mini! (i made 1 dozen regular and 2 dozen mini.)

1. put 1 cup of the wheat bran in a bowl with the 1 cup of boiling water
2. stir and let it sit until the water is absorbed
3. in a large bowl put the flour , the baking soda , and salt
4. combine the sugar , splenda , oil , and applesauce
5. add the sugar mixture to the flour along with the wet bran and the remaining 2 cups of bran and the 2 eggs
6. combine the milk and the vinegar and then add this to the flour mixture
7. mix until totally combined
8. put into muffin pans you have sprayed with cooking spray
9. cook for about 15 minutes or until done
target.review: If you like bran muffins, you must give these a try. They are moist and light and kept well for a couple days in our pantry. Great substitutions to make these healthier than some bran muffins that have lots of oil. And the flavor is good and earthy. Thanks for a sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
city farm vinaigrette

this delicious salad dressing can be made from ingredients most people have right in their pantries. this dressing was served by one of the farms that comes to local farmer's market on saturday mornings. it was published this week in our local paper. our city has given plots of land for two local inner city farms to grow organic vegetable and herbs. the gardens are tended by the people and children of the community, and have been a great success. this yummy dressing goes wonderfully with the fresh greens that i'm able to get there in the summer

1. mix ingredients together in glass jar
2. shake well
3. serve over any fresh garden salad of your choice !
demonstrations.review: This dressing is awesome! I am so glad to find a homemade vinaigrette that has the perfect balance of sweet and tartness along with the character the soy sauce and garlic give it. Thank you for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish chili

i found this recipe in 'favorite recipes from quilters'. we love it.

1. brown ground beef , onions and celery , then drain excess fat
2. add flour and heat through , stirring constantly
3. add all remaining ingredients and mix well
4. cover and simmer 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Chili is about my all-time favorite food and I've been making it in a wide variety of ways for 29 years since I first learned how to cook. I have made this amish recipe every week for about 6 weeks now and I love this style of chili. I reduce the sugar just a little because it's very sweet but since my grandmother cooked that way, the sweet version brings back great memories. This is a really good way to eat chili. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy granola

this granola makes a great, filling snack. good dry or with milk. it is very addictive, but it's good for you, so enjoy!

1. heat oven to 275 degrees f
2. line 2 cookie sheets with parchment paper
3. combine brown sugar and water in a 4 cup microwave proof cup
4. microwave on high 5 minutes until sugar is completely dissolved
5. remove from microwave and stir in vanilla and salt
6. in large mixing bowl , mix oats , nuts , and brown sugar mixture
7. mix thoroughly
8. spread onto cookie sheets and bake 45 minutes-1 hour until golden brown
9. when granola has cooled completely , add fruits if you wish and store in airtight container
demonstrations.review: This recipe is fantastic. A nice, crunchy granola without any fat. Terrific! Tasty! Try it! Thanks for posting exactly what I was looking for in a granola. I might even try reducing the sugar content a little next time so I don't eat so much of it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dutch apple pie

this is from the first apple hill cookbook attributed to alice naslen.  alice,  i've made many, many pies by request and shared your recipe with many people.  i humbly thank you.  i always keep an extra bottle of bitters now.  when i open one, i buy another. once when i ran out of bitters, the store didn't have any!  thanksgiving was not the same!

1. combine crust mixture
2. reserve 1 cup and press the rest in a pie tin
3. put apples in crust
4. in a small pan mix water , sugar , salt , and cornstarch
5. cook while stirring until mixture gets thick
6. remove from heat and stir in vanilla and bitters
7. pour hot custard over apples
8. sprinkle reserved cup of crumbs over pie
9. bake at 350f for 50 to 60 minutes until crust is crunchy
demonstrations.review: I wanted to love this pie because it's different. The bitters add a great flavor and I found the custard/syrup to be really good. The finished product, however, was too sweet for my taste, and I wanted more apples than crust. I love the filling, so I'm wondering if it would be good in traditional pie crust. Thank you for a different kind of apple pie recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttered egg noodles  best ever

the creamiest buttered egg noodles you will ever taste. always a hit and easy to prepare.

1. bring water , 2 boullion cubes and 1 / 2 stick of butter to boil using med to high heat
2. add egg noodles
3. cook until noodles are desired texture
4. during last minute of cooking add remaining 1 / 2 stick of butter
demonstrations.review: I can't believe this many reviews for such an easy recipe! It's great! Without knowing this was a new recipe, my husband declared upon his first bite "These are the best noodles I've ever eaten." I asked him if he had read the print-out of this recipe with the comments and he had no idea. Thanks for this great method.

target.recipe_text:
seafood jambalaya

i learned this recipe from a restaurant in a town named opelousas, lots of paprika are called for here, i recommend starting small, then adding more. there are no tomatoes in this recipe, so it is faster than normal jambalaya.

1. heat butter and olive oil , add onions and peppers and cook for 8-10 minutes
2. add sausage or andouille and cook for 2-3 minutes
3. add paprika and garlic
4. add shrimp , cook for 6-7 minutes
5. add crawfish , cook for 2-3 minutes , if not dark enough add more paprika
6. add rice & season to taste
target.review: This was so delicious!  We'll definitely be making it again. We didn't have crawfish in our area, so we used lobster instead, which made it pricey.  I think if we made it again we would just make it with more shrimp instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chestnut and chorizo soup

a tasty, flavourful soup perfect for christmas starters or a lunch for the days when you've eaten too much :) and fancy a healthier alternative - so simple, really tasty and a bit spicy, yum!

1. heat the oil in a heavy bottomed pan and add the onion and garlic and saut for 4-5 minutes , until soft
2. add the tomatoes and simmer for five minutes
3. then add the chestnuts and simmer for a further three minutes
4. add the stock , bring to the boil and simmer until everything is tender
5. allow the soup to cool a little , then liquidise it in batches
6. return the soup to the pan , add the chorizo and simmer for a few minutes , or until hot
7. serve with the parsley as garnish
demonstrations.review:
A very creative recipe, and quite tasty. However, the chorizo dominates the flavor. I was looking forward to getting to taste chestnuts for the first time, but I'm still not sure what they taste like.

Also, one thing I would change is the prep time. We started making this recipe at 6:50 p.m. and couldn't eat it until 8 p.m. We had just harvested the chestnuts from our tree, and it took about 30 minutes to score them, boil them and peel their shells off. Then it also takes a while to chop the garlic, onion and tomatoes. Definitely more effort than 25 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
russian borscht

this is a meatless (not vegetarian) borscht, and even my husband, who must have meat with every meal, loves this! sometimes we make it in summer and serve it cold. it's very tasty! it came from a cookbook many years ago, but i can't remember which one. and i've changed it over the years and i do my own thing, there is no need to measure any of the veggies, it always turns out wonderful. so eyeball it! (your food processor will come in mighty handy for shredding all these veggies!) enjoy!

1. cook beets , carrots and onion in the 3 cans beef broth for 20 minutes
2. add cabbage and butter , and cook uncovered for about 20 minutes
3. season to taste
4. stir in lemon juice
5. now let it sit , for an hour or so
6. reheat or leave at temperature and serve with sour cream
7. this is better the next day !
demonstrations.review: When life gives you beets, make borscht!  We got a ton of beets in our CSA this year and I generally don't like beets, I think they literally taste like dirt.  But I ventured out on a limb and tried this recipe.  I am so glad I did!  For being so simple, this is a great soup.  Like a beety french onion soup.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot carrot soup with honey and nutmeg

excellent as an accompaniment to falafel in pita pockets.

1. heat the oil in a large skillet over medium heat
2. add the onions and cook until softened , 6 to 8 minutes , stirring often to cook evenly
3. put the potatoes , carrots , garlic , and herbs in the slow cooker
4. add the onions and oil , scraping them out of the pan
5. add enough of the water or broth to cover everything
6. cover and cook on high for 1 hour
7. turn the cooker to low and cook until the vegetables are soft , 5 to 7 hours
8. puree in batches in a food processor or right in the slow cooker with a handheld immersion blender
9. the soup will be nice and thick
10. stir in the honey and grate the nutmeg right over the crock
11. season with salt and pepper
12. keep warm on low without letting it come to a boil until serving
13. ladle the hot soup into bowls and enjoy
demonstrations.review: I have had this recipe on my "to cook" list for almost 3 years!  I finally got around to it tonight, and it was great!  The honey and the nutmeg are a great addition.  Without it it would just taste like any other autumn stew.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german pfeffernusse cookies   gluten free

a traditional german cookie for christmas..or any time of the year. commonly served with wine. should make 30 to 40 biscuits.
if not using a blended flour with xanthan or guar gums added- then add one teaspoon of gum with your flour to the recipe. these biscuits remind me of a ginger snap cookie from arnotts (or at least what i remember them tasting like!)

1. preheat oven to 190c line baking trays with greaseproof or baking paper
2. mix all ingredients in an electric mixer on a medium speed , until roughly mixed
3. do not overbeat
4. using a spatula then , scrape down the sides of the bowl and mix until well combined
5. leaving the mixture in the bowl , knead with your hands until all of the ingredients are well mixed
6. roll mixture into balls , about the size of walnuts
7. place on baking sheets about 1 / 2 inch / 1 cm apart
8. bake for about 10 minutes at 190c
9. allow the biscuits to cool completely on the trays
10. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: My husband is of German descent and asked for these cookies for Christmas.  I was nervous I wouldn't find a decent gluten-free recipe, but these are great!  I couldn't find self-rising gluten-free flour here in the United States, so I substituted with 2 cups gluten-free flour, 2 ½ teaspoons baking powder, ½ teaspoon salt and an extra egg.  To keep the cookies from sticking to my hands, I also rolled them in sugar before putting them on the baking tray.  They turned out awesome!  My two year old is currently asking for more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and egg jambalaya

a recipe from tony chachere's cajun country cookbook that we picked up in new orleans several years ago, where we fell in love with cajun & creole cooking.  i normally make this with bacon instead of ham.  a great brunch or lunch meal - also reheats well in the microwave.

1. in a large skillet , melt margarine and cook ham and onions until onions are wilted
2. add steamed rice and cook until hot
3. add eggs , mix well and stir thoroughly
4. season with tony chachere's creole seasoning
demonstrations.review: My husband and I have now made this recipe twice.  We've made it with bacon instead of ham, which is delicious.  It's such a great way to make eggs in the morning interesting again!  It's also great reheated.

target.recipe_text:
chicken shepherd s pie

traditionally shepherd pie is made from lamb (hence shepherd) but since i don't eat red meat, i'm making it with chicken.  you can use lamb if you wish. vegetarian can replace the meat with variety of beans or tvp.  you may use dried herbs if you don't have fresh herbs. mushroom i used comes in a can and is sliced and pre-made in butter sauce

1. preheat oven to 180c / 350f
2. to make mash potato: boil the potatoes in salted water , drain , add milk gradually , butter , season with pinch of nutmeg and mash set aside
3. to make the filling: in a large pan set over low heat , add oil and heat the oil until sizzling
4. add the onions , carrots , celery , peas and garlic
5. saut until the onions are transparent and the carrots begin to soften , about 10 minutes
6. remove from the heat and stir in the mushrooms in butter sauce , worcestershire sauce , rosemary , sage , thyme , marjoram , shredded chicken and salt & pepper to taste
7. allow to cool
8. place the shortbread pastry into a pie tin
9. don't cut the pastry yet , pour over cooled chicken filling , remove excess pastry by cutting the edge set aside
10. spread your mash potato over chicken filling and scored with a fork or you can use an icing kit
11. bake for 30 to 40 minutes or until the topping is golden and the sauce is hot and bubbly
12. allow to cool for 15 minutes before serving
target.review: Chef floWer this warmed me through to my core for dinner the other night. There is nothing I like more than a good pie with plenty of mash and this was simple and delicious. Everyone commented that it should become a regular at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pesto and potato tart

this is from a nz magazine called taste and is really easy to do and looks impressive.

1. heat oven to 190 degrees celsius
2. simmer sliced potatoes for 3 minutes , drain , set aside
3. spread pasrty base with pesto
4. sprinkle with parmesan - as much or as little as you like
5. lay sliced potatoes over top of cheese
6. season with salt and ground pepper
7. glaze pastry borders with beaten egg
8. bake 35-40 minutes till pastry is golden and crisp and potatoes are tender
9. sprinkle with basil
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic! I served it with a salad for lunch. Everyone loved it and thought I'd had to work hard to get it looking so beautiful. But it was so easy. This is made with things I always have on hand and will be something I can very easily throw together when I need to feed unexpected guests.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice pilaf with herbs

especially good pilaf. the celery and onion add a nice touch.

1. in skillet , saute rice , celery , and onion in butter until the rice is browned
2. place in a greased 2 quart casserole
3. combine all remaining ingredients
4. pour over rice
5. cover and bake at 325f degrees for 50 minutes or until rice is done
demonstrations.review: This was FANTASTIC!!! Everyone loved it. I didn't change and thing and wont in the future. Served this as a side with fish and the mild flavours of the herbs and celery complimented so perfectly. Will be making this again and again. Thank you MizzNezz for this wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
all day beef stew

easy no-brainer. have a hearty dinner waiting for you when you get home in the evening.

1. stir all ingredients together in slow cooker / crockpot
2. cover and cook all day on low
3. stir gently and serve with green veggies
demonstrations.review: I was comming home from work yesterday and got caught in the rain. I was grumblind and didnt want to cook dinner. To my suprise my BF had seen this recipe (left open on pc) and decided to make us dinner. This never ever happens. The house had a wonderful smell and it tasted great. Wasnt as thick as I expected but it had only cooked for around 6 1/2hrs by the time I got home starving. 4 Stars for flavour and an extra for getting my BF to cook for me. Thanks so much

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bangja gui  korean bbq beef in a lettuce wrap

i found this on a korean website.  serve with rice and side dishes or as an appetizer with drinks.

1. cut the steak into thin slices 3 inches long and 2 inches wide
2. this can be done easily if the steak is half frozen
3. mix the steak with salt , 1 tb sesame oil and the pepper
4. put seasonings into the meat
5. set aside for 15 minutes
6. soak the scallion slices in ice water for 15 minutes
7. drain well
8. mix together the soy sauce and the remaining 2 teaspoons sesame oil and toss this with the scallion slices
9. set aside
10. mix the chili powder , sugar and sesame seeds together
11. rub this seasoning on the inside curl of the lettuce leaves
12. set aside
13. grill the steak for 1 to 3 minutes until done according to taste
14. take 1 lettuce leaf put several slices of steak in the center add about 1 tablespoon of the seasoned scallions a sliver or two of garlic fold the lettuce over the steak and eat
demonstrations.review: Oh my gosh did I love this one. I knew I was in for a treat and I was not disappointed. The marinade is to die for. I'm a massive fan of san choy bow and thought this was an interesting play on the idea. But this beats it hands down. Thanks so much Elmotoo I can't wait to have ppl over and serve this to them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple grilled pears with brown sugar and cinnamon

this is a recipe from ken kostick's cookbook

1. in a large bowl spoon lemon juice over pears
2. in another bowl , combine brown sugar and cinnamon
3. sprinkle brown sugar cinnamon combo over the pear slices
4. set indoor grill on high and grill for 4-5 minutes or until golden
5. to serve , evenly distribute pear slices on to 4 serving dishes and drizzle with maple syrup
demonstrations.review: The guys at my house went crazy over this and were disappointed when there werenâ€™t any leftovers for seconds. I served with vanilla ice cream and even though I am not a lover of pears (unlike the guys) I enjoyed it a lot. The BF and brother asked that this be made regularly now that the colder weather has started and told me that I HAD to rate it 5 stars. Thanks Chef at Heart

target.recipe_text:
one pan pasta and meatballs

this recipe is from a betty crocker email that i received. a few ingredients, little time to make, and sounds very good!

1. using a 10 inch skillet bring water and pasta sauce to a boil
2. add macaroni , meatballs , olives and return to a boil
3. lower heat to medium and cover skillet
4. cook approximately 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally , or until macaroni is tender
5. sprinkle cheese if using and serve immediately
target.review: This was quick and easy to throw together. I left out the olives (personal preference) and added lots of shredded cheddar cheese to my dish and the sauce turned out so cheesy and yummy! It's a nice change of pace from the way I usually make my spaghetti and meatballs. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter oatmeal chocolate chunk cookies

another bakers baking chocolate recipe. quick cooking oats can also be used without compromising the recipe.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. mix flour , oats , baking soda , baking powder and salt
3. set aside
4. beat sugars , butter and peanut butter in large bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy
5. add egg and vanilla , mix well
6. gradually add flour mixture , mixing until well blended after each addition
7. stir in chopped chocolate
8. drop heaping tablespoonfuls of dough , 2" apart , onto ungreased baking sheets
9. bake 12-13 minutes or until lightly browned
10. cool 1 minute
11. remove from baking sheets to wire rackes
12. cool completely
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I really enjoyed snacking on these. They are really light! Perfect amount of peanut butter and chocolate. I used semi-sweet chocolate chips since I didn't have chunks on hand. They baked up just right and mine came out slightly crumbly but great nonetheless. I will make these again. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cookies and cream freeze

this sounds yummy and easy.  from kraft food and family.  cooking time includes freezing

1. melt chocolate as directed on package
2. set aside until ready to use
3. line 8-1 / 2 x 4-1 / 2-inch loaf pan with foil , with ends of foil extending over sides of pan
4. arrange 8 of the cookies evenly on bottom of pan
5. crumble remaining 6 cookies
6. set aside
7. beat cream cheese , sugar and vanilla in medium bowl with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended
8. stir in whipped topping
9. remove about 1-1 / 2 cups of the cream cheese mixture
10. place in medium bowl
11. stir in melted chocolate
12. spread remaining cream cheese mixture over cookies in pan
13. sprinkle with crumbled cookies
14. gently press cookies into cream cheese mixture with back of spoon
15. top with chocolate mixture
16. cover
17. freeze 3 hours or until firm
18. remove from freezer
19. invert onto serving plate
20. peel off foil
21. let stand at room temperature to soften slightly before cutting to serve
demonstrations.review: This is delicious! I made into individual servings by using a muffin pan lined with cupcake holders for easy removal. I really enjoyed the chocolate cream part of this dessert, probably because I have an extreme sweet tooth. Will definitely make this again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bailey s irish cream brownies

i found this recipe several years ago but i don't remember where i got it from. these are really yummy brownies. time does not include the cooling time.

1. melt unsweetened chocolate with butter in microwave and mix well
2. cool
3. beat sugar and eggs together in mixing bowl
4. add bailey's irish cream and cooled chocolate mixture
5. mix well
6. stir in flour , salt and chocolate chips
7. pour into greased and floured 8-inch square baking pan
8. bake at 325f for approximately 20 minutes
9. cool completely
10. pierce brownies with a wooden pick randomly
11. drizzle 3 tablespoons bailey's irish cream over brownies , then frost
12. frosting:
13. in mixing bowl , combine liqueurs and butter
14. mix well
15. gradually add confectioners' sugar and beat until spreading consistency
16. frost cooled brownies
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I got a bottle of Bailey's for Christmas and this was one of the first recipes I decided to make. It was absolutely delicious and looked as pretty as the picture. I also made only half the frosting and it was enough. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecue chicken roll ups

.

1. preheat oven to 375f degrees
2. bring large pot of water to boil
3. turn off heat and add lasagna noodles
4. let sit 5 minutes
5. remove lasagna noodles to platter to cool
6. to prepare roll-ups , place lasagna noodles on flat surface
7. divide chicken and bell pepper strips among lasagna noodles
8. sprinkle each lasagna noodle with about 1 tablespoon cheese and roll up , being careful to keep ingredients wrapped inside
9. spray 9x 13-inch baking dish with cooking spray
10. spoon 1v2 cups barbecue sauce into baking dish and spread evenly to cover bottom
11. place roll-ups into dish
12. pour additional barbecue sauce over roll-ups and sprinkle with remaining cheese
13. bake 40 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted
14. place under broiler for 1 to 2 minutes to brown cheese , if desired
15. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: MMM, this was great! I ended up shredding my chicken breast instead of leaving them slices, I found it easier to spread out over the noodles that way. Loved this recipe - simple but delicious. Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
puppy chow or monkey munch

kids love this and it makes a lot.  i got this recipe from a friend of mine.

1. measure cereal in large bowl
2. set aside
3. microwave chocolate chips , peanut butter and butter for 1 minute on high
4. stir
5. cook for 30 seconds longer or until smooth
6. add vanilla
7. pour mixture over cereal , stirring until coated
8. pour mixture into large ziploc bag and add powdered sugar
9. shake until well coated
10. spread on waxed paper to cool
11. store in ziploc bags or large sealed bowl
12. recipe
demonstrations.review: Oh my gosh! Best snack recipe ever! I took so long to try this after seeing so many people talk about how good and addictive it is and boy, why did I wait so long?! I think my most favourite part about this recipe is the fact that I can cut it down to one serving using just one cup of cereal when I want a small snack for myself. Thanks so much for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
steven s world famous to die for sour cream chicken

i've modified my grandmother's recipe for the 21st century. i can't have a dinner party and not asked to make this simple dish. enjoy!

1. clean chicken and pour sour cream over it and let marinate for about an hour in the refrigerator
2. meanwhile , take crackers and crush into medium course crumbs , mix in parmesan cheese and tarragon / marjoram
3. melt half of the butter and pour on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
4. dredge chicken in the cracker mixture and set in baking dish
5. repeat until complete
6. melt rest of butter and pour on top of chicken
7. bake@ 350 for 35-45 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: We really liked this recipe.  Since we are on a lower calorie diet, we substituted the regular sour cream for low fat sour cream and sweet butter for "I Can't Believe It's Not Butter" and since we did not have tarragon or marjoram we used paprika.  Even with these substitutions, it was really delicious.  We will be making this many times to come.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken roasted on sweet potatoes and garlic

i adapted this recipe from donna hay's flavours cookbook. in her recipe she used normal potatoes instead of sweet potatoes. but i prefered it with the sweet potatoes. a very delicious and simple recipe. quick whip up.

1. preheat oven to 200c
2. place oil , sweet potatoes , oregano , garlic , salt and pepper in baking dish and toss to combine
3. bake for 25-30 minutes or till potatoes are almost cooked
4. while potatoes are cooking , brush chicken fillets with a little oil and sprinkle skin with extra salt and pepper
5. heat frying pan over medium-high heat , add chicken skin side down , and cook for 3 minutes till well browned
6. place chicken skin side up , on top of potatoes and garlic in baking dish
7. bake for a further 10 minutes or till chicken is cooked through , and juices run clear in the thickest part
8. to serve , place the chicken and sweet potatoes on serving plates
9. squeeze the garlic from its skin and spread on the potatoes and chicken
10. serve with steamed beans and a squeeze of lemon
demonstrations.review: We just ate this and absolutely LOVED it.  The only thing we changed was that we coated the chicken in Italian seasoned breadcrumbs (we dipped it in an egg white to save calories and then coated it) which we thought added a fantastic flavor to the chicken.  Thank you so much for this - we'll be making this for many years to come.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dijon steak

a perfect quick meal for a rushed day. your family will think you've been in the kitchen for hours! dijon adds a delightful flavor to this favorite dish.

1. melt butter in large skillet
2. brown steaks quickly on both sides
3. remove , set aside
4. reduce heat
5. add gravy , half-and-half and mustard to skillet
6. heat , stirring , till bubbly
7. return steaks to pan with gravy
8. turn heat down
9. cover and let simmer about 30 minutes , or until done
10. sprinkle fresh parsley over steaks just before eating
demonstrations.review: Loved the recipe.  We changed the meat from cube steak and used a sirloin strip.  We then used Boston Market beef gravy which was awesome.  For our sides, we made garlic mashed potatoes and we also simmered sliced mushrooms and onions (with two cloves of sliced garlic) in a mixture of water, balsamic vinegar and dijon mustard (a perfect complement to this steak recipe).  Everything came out perfectly.  Good job.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with chickpeas and garlic sauce

another great veggie pasta dish from cooking light magazine.

1. heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add crushed garlic , saute 1 minute
3. add salt , pepper , chickpeas and broth , bring to a boil
4. cover , reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
5. while garlic mixture simmers , cook pasta in boiling water 9 minutes , drain well
6. place chickpea mixture in a food processor and process until smooth
7. combine chickpea mixture , pasta , tomatoes , minced garlic , parsley and lemon juice , toss well
8. sprinkle with cheese
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Surprisingly good.  After following the recipe we were a little nervous about the way it looked but the taste and texture proved to be absolutely delicious.  We were able to prepare and enjoy this meal in less than 30 minutes which was a huge plus.  Thank you so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken sausage farfalle

we developed this recipe after we had something similar at an upscale italian restaurant.  we made it the way we like it.  it is simple, the kids love it and you can play with the ingredients to your liking.

1. slice and fry sausage in the listed spices , as much as you like
2. cook noodles until el dente
3. fry onions and garlic , with some of the above spices in olive oil until onions are just translucent
4. turn off onions and gently mix in tomatoes
5. you do not want to cook the tomatoes
6. mix together the sausage , onion mixture , cheese , basil , cream and noodles
7. cook gently over med high heat
8. you may not want to add all the cream at once
9. cook for a little and then adjust the amount of cream to your liking
10. adjust the spices and add more as you need it
11. serve and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This meal was deliciously different.  The only alterations we made were substituting the 2 large tomatoes for grape tomatoes and using fat free half and half for the full fat version.  This was really excellent and only took 40 minutes!  Thank you so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: We used Panko instead of the regular breadcrumbs and loved this recipe.  Even my boyfriend (who doesn't really like eggplant) loved them.  We served them with a side of sliced cooked red potatoes.  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
roasted cauliflower   16 roasted cloves of garlic

i find it totally amazing, that children and men all  love this recipe!  as for the female of our species we just love this for the flavor and the health benefits it brings our families.
roasted brings out a wonderful sweetness in this dish. the garlic is roasted to a tan color is creamy good. you can just pop them in your mouth. or you can spread them on your florets or fresh bread. just be sure to scoop up some of the rosemary, olive oil and black pepper that may have escaped to the bottom of the dish.
for halloween check out recipe #396674 version of my recipe.

1. mix oil , rosemary , salt , pepper and garlic together
2. toss in cauliflower and place in a large casserole dish in one layer
3. roast in a preheated oven at 450 degrees for 20 minutes
4. give a toss and bake for 10 more minutes
target.review:
I found this flavor to be too intense. The garlic is a bit overpowering. But then my picky husband liked it. So go figure!

Edit: And I like garlic.  :(  I've been thinking about this and I think I roasted mine too long.  I reduced the heat because it is a convection oven.  But sometimes even at a reduced heat the convection oven does TOO good a job.  I think the garlic got too dark.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory braised short ribs

this is hearty comfort food.  serve with mashed potatoes, a veggie and good bread for sopping up the sauce. yum!

1. brown short ribs well on all sides in dutch oven over medium heat
2. add broth , onion , 1 c water , peppercorns , worchstershire sauce , garlic , bay leaf and marjoram
3. bring to a boil
4. reduce heat , cover and cook slowly 2 to 2 1 / 2 hours or until tender , turning once
5. meanwhile , prepare horseradish sauce
6. place short ribs on serving platter and keep warm
7. skim fat from cooking liquid
8. combine flour with 1 / 2 cup water , mixing until smooth
9. combine with cooking liquid , bring to a boil , stirring constantly , reduce heat and cook slowly 3 minutes
10. strain , if necessary , and serve with short ribs
11. garnish platter with tomato wedges and parsley
12. serve horseradish sauce with short ribs
13. horseradish sauce
14. 1 / 4 cup dairy sour cream 1 t prepared mustard 2 1 / 2 t prepared horseradish 1 / 8 t salt combine sour cream , horseradish , mustard and salt in small bowl
15. cover and refrigerate
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious.  This gravy has a lot of depth to it.  I could drink the gravy as a soup.  To reduce the fat quite a bit I trimmed excess fat from the ribs, removed the ribs from the broth after cooking and chilled until the next day and I strained the broth and chilled it until the next day.  I was able to remove a very large slab of beef fat from the top of the broth.  I then thickened the broth slightly and added the ribs and baked at 350 for 30 minutes in a dutch oven.  Decadent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tender and juicy marinated chicken

this is great because its easy, and once the chicken is marinated, very quick. i can pop it in the oven and finish other things while it bakes. this is without a doubt my husbands favorite chicken, he likes it even better than my fried chicken, which is wonderful because its sooo much easier.

1. combine italian dressing and soy sauce
2. mix well
3. pour marinade into a gallon sized resealable plastic bag
4. add chicken
5. marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight , turning several times
6. place chicken in a shallow baking dish
7. sprinkle chicken liberally with onion powder and garlic powder
8. sprinkle with salt , to taste
9. bake for 45-60 minutes at 350 degrees , or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Excellent and easy!  I made up several bags and froze them.  I take thaw them overnight and either bake or grill the chicken the next evening.  Delicious.  This has become a frequent OAMC recipe for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai basil vegetables

nice and flavorful with aromatic basil.

1. in a small bowl , combine the fish sauce , soy sauce , lime juice , ginger , garlic , sugar , and sambal oelek for the sauce
2. set aside
3. the sauce in this is thin from the veggies
4. if you like a thicker sauce , add 1 tbsp
5. cornstarch to your sauce , but it won't affect the flavor either way
6. heat oil in wok or large skillet over medium-high heat
7. add zucchini , mushrooms , and carrots to pan
8. stir-fry for 3 minutes
9. add sauce in bowl to pan
10. stir to mix well , and continue cooking for 5 minutes , until vegetables are crisp-tender
11. stir in herbs and serve
demonstrations.review:
This is very good!  It is best to adjust the flavors, especially lime and pepper, as you go.  I put in the juice from half a lime and mine was a bit too sour.   I used snow peas, onions, napa cabbage, mushrooms, red pepper and water chestnuts.  Delicious!

It should be noted that this can also be made without the cilantro, if basil is all you have on hand.  It is very good with just basil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bow ties with sausage  tomato  and cream

a very easy pasta dish for busy evenings. i like it served with crusty bread (to dip in the sauce) and a tossed salad. i have even doubled the recipe and served it to guest on a casual evening.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. cook pasta in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes , or until al dente
3. drain
4. heat oil in a large , deep skillet over medium heat
5. cook sausage and pepper flakes until sausage is heated and browning around the edges
6. stir in onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
7. stir in tomatoes , cream , and salt
8. simmer until mixture thickens , 8 to 10 minutes
9. stir cooked pasta into sauce , and heat through
10. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review:
Excellent!  Small changes I made.. I didn't use any oil.  I drained the kielbasa after cooking and before adding the onions.  When adding the onions, I had to add a little water to scrape up the browned bits of meat.  I added the garlic 30 seconds before the tomatoes so it would not burn.  AND I added basil instead of parsley because that is what I had.  I also found I did not need to add salt.  

The family says this is to go in the favorites folder!  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
restaurant quality chinese chicken fried rice

i created this recipe out of desperation last night when it was getting late and everyone was hungry now, so i call it one of my desperation dinners! it is really pretty and tastes as good as something you order in a restaurant!  it was very cheap to make.  you buy the chicken on sale and boil it and shred it and put in freezer in baggies till you need it and it's all ready to use in recipes at last minute!  you can get the canned water chestnuts for $1 or less on sale and keep on hand in pantry! hope you like this as much as we do!

1. make rice first
2. add all ingredients together in saucepan and bring to boil
3. turn to simmer and cook 20 minutes with lid on
4. set aside to cool
5. in large skillet pan melt butter
6. in a small bowl stir egg and water
7. add to skillet on medium low heat in one big thin pancake formation
8. cook for 1-2 minutes or until set
9. take out carefully with spatula
10. cut egg into long thin shreds on cutting board
11. set aside
12. heat oil in same skillet over medium high heat and put in onion , bell pepper and drained water chestnuts
13. cook until soft
14. add rice , chicken , soy sauce and pepper
15. mix all together to warm through and then add shredded egg to mixture
16. cook a few minutes more and serve hot
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  I think one of the keys to the good taste of the recipe is the rice cooked with the flavorings and using plenty of egg (I used 2).  The cook can easily vary this recipe to there own liking.  I added chinese cabbage (Napa).  Delicious!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s 5 minute cinnamon flop brunch cake

except for the the milk and small amount in the egg, the cake itself has very little fat and using low-fat milk will keep the fat to a minimum, i have stated the egg as optional, i strongly suggest to add it in for a more cake-like texture --  if you are looking for a fancy cake to serve then this is not it however for the ease of this cake it is darn good and makes a great weekend brunch cake, it's like a combination of a cake and cinnamon bun all in one,  ridiculously simple to make as it's all mixed by hand and takes like 5 minutes to throw together, try adding in some chopped strawberries, apples or blueberries, raisins or dried cranberries, this recipe is a blank canvas, so go ahead and add in fruit, nuts chocolate chips whatever you wish, and to kick this up a notch drizzle recipe#120835 on top :) --- servings are only estimated

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. prepare a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish , or two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans
3. in a bowl mix the 2 cups flour , 1-1 / 4 cups white sugar , milk , vanilla or almond extract , baking powder , pinch of salt and egg until just combined careful not to overmix
4. pour into prepared baking pan / s
5. generously spread brown sugar and cinnamon on top
6. if desired sprinkle chopped walnuts or pecans over top
7. drizzle melted butter over top
8. bake for about 20-25 minutes for 8 or 9-inch round cake pan , and about 30 minutes for a 13 x 9-inch pan
target.review: The cake was yummy yet spongy.  Although it was still a nice cake to make...Remind me of a cinnamon roll yet in a cake form... I used a bundt pan and I did not have milk therefore I substituted evaporate milk and water and it still was good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best grilled pork chops

this is a simple recipe i have adapted from company's coming.it is simple to throw together the marinade in the morning before going off to work and coming home to an easy dinner to prepare at night.

1. in deep bowl mix all marinade ingredients
2. marinate at least 2 hours
3. remove from marinade and cook over medium-high heat on greased grill for no more than 15 minutes or until done
4. cooking time for second side is shorter by 1-2 minutes
5. 3 / 4" or thinner , 5-6 minutes maximum per side , thicker than 3 / 4" 6-7 minutes maximum per side
6. do not over_grill , chops will become tough
7. after 2 minutes grilling on a side , rotate chops 45 degrees for even cooking
8. turn over when juices pool on upper surface and meat appears to be cooked half-way through
demonstrations.review: the best! Only way to describe this recipe! I only marinated for 30 minutes as I was cooking the chops on the same night.  they were was moist, not dry...the lemon pepper taste was not overwhelming! the soy sauce was not tooo salty, it was just right!! I will make this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops   southern style

simple, quick and tasty. something i threw together with the 'scraps' in my fridge and surprised me with how great it tasted. feel free to remove as much 'fat' from the pan as you need to... the more you leave, the better it tastes! great with mashed potatoes!

1. in 12" skillet , cook bacon on med hi heat
2. remove bacon from skillet , but leave bacon drippings
3. add 1 tbsp butter and diced onion
4. when transparent , remove from skillet
5. reduce heat to medium , lightly salt and pepper both sides of pork chops and place in skillet
6. brown both sides
7. chop up bacon , and add both bacon and cooked onion to skillet
8. add 3 / 4 cup water , 1 tbsp butter , cover and simmer until cooked
9. just before serving , mix 2 tbsp cornstarch with cool tap water
10. place pork chops on plates , add corn starch / water mixture to gravy / drippings in skillet and bring to quick boil stirring frequently to form thick gravy
demonstrations.review: It was a little bland, but it was good.  I added mushrooms, green onions, garlic, and parsley.  I used a half pack of center cut bacon. I tasted the bacon flavor but it was not as strong as i thought it would be.  I gave it 4 stars because of the bland flavor.  I would make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked steak

a nice change to broiling or grilling, the gravy is delicious. i always serve this with mashed potatoes.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. pound steak to tenderize
3. dredge both sides in flour , salt and pepper
4. in heavy oven proof skillet heat oil , add steak and brown on both sides , remove add stock , bring to boil , scraping bits off pan
5. add worcestershire sauce , more salt and pepper to taste
6. remove from heat
7. layer half the onions in pan , add steak , layer rest of onions , broth , spoon some broth on top
8. bake for 2 hours , covered , basting steak after 1 hour
9. remove to cutting board and slice
10. serve with the gravy
demonstrations.review: First off it was delicious! I used thin cut ribeyes, sprinkled tenderizer, zatarains season, garlic, paprika, parsley, before frying with the flour.  As far as the beef broth, and worcheshire, I added onions, 2 green onions, and fresh mushrooms. I baked for 45 minutes, while turning at least every 10 minutes. The steaks were tender, juicy and flavorful.   I still had gravy leftover, as the gravy dryed out slightly.  I added garlic pasta with chicken and veggies by viola.  the hubby and I had a wonderful dinner, and I will definitely cook it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot garlic rosemary chicken breast

this is a nice simple way to prepare chicken in the crock pot, but it tastes like you put a lot of work into it!

1. place butter and garlic in microwave-safe bowl and heat until butter is soft
2. blend together
3. roll chicken breasts in garlic-butter mixture and place in crock pot
4. sprinkle chicken breasts with salt , pepper , parsley and rosemary
5. add broth to bowl with remaining garlic-butter , reheat if necessary to allow smooth blending , and add mixture to crock pot
6. cook on low setting for 6 - 8 hours
7. serving size is approximately half a chicken breast and a small amount of sauce
demonstrations.review:
one word-DEEELICCIOOOUS! 
I made the recipe slightly different.  I used garlic powder instead of minced garlic.  I used italian seasoning which has rosemary in it instead of rosemary.  My hubby thought it was good too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
demonstrations.review: i used drumettes, and I have to say the flavor was yummy!  The taste is more like terriyaki or bourbon chicken you would get from a chinese restaurant.  Instead of the garlic clove i used garlic powder with parsley.  I added black pepper and zatarains season.  While the drumettes were baking i turned them several times to make sure they were coated well.   I would recommend the recipe to anyone that want a different flavor added to their chicken and don't have all the time in the world to marinade.

target.recipe_text:
moist oatmeal pumpkin muffins

since i discovered my husband has diabetes, i have been trying to add more fiber rich foods to my families diet. the oatmeal in this recipe helps with this, and the kids and everyone else realy like these moist treats. try them!!!

1. heat oven to 375f
2. grease and flour muffin tins , or use paper liners
3. in large mixing bowl , mix together all ingredients except nuts , blend until just combined
4. do not over mix
5. stir in nuts
6. fill prepared muffin tins three fourths full
7. bake for 18 to20 minutes , or until muffins test done
8. cool in pan or on a wire rack
9. enjoy !
target.review:
I've made this several times so far. it's been enjoyable.
The first thing I did was drop the oil and water in favor of 2 sticks of butter.
I like to add 1 cup of whole frozen cranberries, which add a nice juicy tart pop to some bites.  Dried cranberries or 2 tb of finely chopped candied orange peel are also complimentary flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate panna cotta

this comes from iga's list of recipes. to vary the flavour you can replace the chocolate with 2 teaspoons instant coffee or 1 teaspoon finely grated orange or lemon peel.  cook time does not include refrigeration time.

1. sprinkle gelatine in milk snd allow to soften for ten minutes
2. heat cream with sugar
3. add chocolate and stir until it is dissolved
4. remove from stove add softened gelatine and stir
5. por mixture into coffee cups and place in fridge for 2 hours to set
demonstrations.review: This was super easy.  Everyone in the family really liked it.  I will definitely make this again.  I'd add some coffee, orange or cinnamon to the chocolate in the future.  I also will add a bit more chocolate and remove some sugar (but that's my taste, there was nothing wrong with the proportions as written).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy creamy rice pudding

best rice pudding that i have ever tasted. good sprinkled with nutmeg or cinnamon.

1. in a medium saucepan , bring 1 1 / 2 cups water to a boil
2. add rice and stir
3. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 20 minutes
4. in another saucepan , combine the cooked rice , with 1 1 / 2 cups milk , sugar and salt
5. cook over medium heat until thick and creamy , 15 to 20 minutes
6. stir in remaining 1 / 2 cup milk , beaten egg and raisins
7. cook 2 minutes more , stirring constantly
8. remove from heat , and stir in butter and vanilla
9. serve warm
