demonstrations.review: I was looking for something that's more of a custard.  This worked reasonable well and came out creamy and tasty, but I'm still looking for perfection.  It was too thick and dry when it was done and cool.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was great. I made a few changes. First of all, mashed potatoes are always my last leftover from Thanksgiving, after getting carried away I'm done with carbs until christmas, I also used some cauliflower, just because it was sitting around. most importantly, I had bought leeks intending a potato leek soup, but found this recipe first, they made a great sub for the onion. I used the last of my turkey stock from the holiday, and now have a clean fridge and a happy tummy. I'll be cooking a ham next week just because I want the leftover for another round of this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried lentils

this recipe might sound a little strange but if you fix it once you will fix it often. it also freezes fine.

1. wash and sort the lentils and cook until they are tender but firm
2. 4 cups of water high heat 10 minutes and low / medium heat 15 minutes
3. heat the olive oil in a large skillet
4. when it is hot , add the garlic and saute over moderately low heat for 1 minute then add the spinach and cook about 2 mins or so until all the leaves are wilted
5. add the lentils and the remaining ingredients to the skillet
6. cover and simmer over very low heat for 15 minutes
7. this is good over mashed potatoes , rice or couscous
demonstrations.review: Loved it.  Our kids loved it.  Easy to make.  I used frozen chopped spinach because I had some on hand.  It needed a little more seasoning, the recipe omits salt and pepper but I added some red pepper flakes.  I will definitely make this again  The instructions could use some work - my garlic does not have leaves.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage cornbread stuffing

my family's favorite- great with gravy too.

1. saute onions and celery in butter , set aside
2. saute sausage meat until browned , drain
3. preheat oven to 350f
4. mix veggies and sausage in large bowl
5. add cornbread , broth , thyme , salt and pepper , and toasted pecans
6. bake 30 minutes covered , 15 minutes uncovered
demonstrations.review: This worked really well for me. It came out very dry because I used a large recipe of cornbread. I used sage instead of thyme because it tied into my other dishes, and I used extra (but not enough) homemade turkey broth. I had some extra apple slices that didn't fit in the pie, so I though them in too.

target.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
target.review: Tilapia is such a versatile fish... it can be cooked all types of ways. This recipe is my favorite so far! I dredged the fillets in lemon juice then arranged them on the pan. Before putting them in the oven, I sprinkled garlic & onion powder over them. I made the sauce as the recipe stated, minus the basil and green onions because we didn't have any. I baked the fish for about 12 minutes, added the sauce, then another 13 minutes or so. The fillets was tender and so incredibly flavorful! DH and his brother inhaled this dish. I will definitely be cooking this again! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review: This recipe is *flawless*... and if possible, it comes out more and more delicious every time I make it. I have made it exactly as it was written, and I have also made it with a few slight changes. I find that adding garlic powder and onion powder to the milk/cream mixture really amps up the flavor. Also, adding just a pinch of cayenne pepper really gives the entire dish a feeling of warmth and comfort. My family members are cheese-a-holics, so I also increase the amount of cheese. These changes are more about personal preference, though, because the recipe rocks, as is!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s crispy honey chipotle chicken crispers bytodd wilbur

these sweet and spicy chicken tenders can be served as either an appetizer or an entree.  this recipe was created by todd wilbur from top secret recipes - www.topsecretrecipes.com.

1. make honey-chipotle sauce by combining all ingredients in a small saucepan over medium heat until boiling
2. reduce heat and simmer for 2 minutes
3. remove from heat
4. heat shortening or oil in fryer or dutch oven to 350 degrees f
5. whisk together all ingredients for the batter , excluding flour , in a shallow bowl for at least 30 seconds
6. whisk in the flour
7. make the breading by combining all ingredients in another shallow bowl or pie pan
8. when you are ready to fry the chicken , dip each piece of chicken into the batter
9. lift the chicken out of the batter and let some of the excess drip off
10. toss the chicken into the dry breading and coat completely
11. repeat with 2-3 other pieces
12. carefully drop the breaded chicken into the hot oil and fry for 4 minutes , or until golden brown
13. remove chicken from oil and allow to drain on paper towels
14. repeat steps 8-13 until all the chicken tenders have been cooked
15. when all the chicken tenders are done , drop them into a large glass or metal bowl
16. pour the sauce over the top , and toss gently until all the chicken tenders are coated with sauce
demonstrations.review: This chicken is outstanding-- and really really easy to make, too! I am not a chef. I am not a spectacular cook, either. But a good recipe helps a novice cook like yours truly whip up something incredibly delicious. A few alterations: I did not have any broth, so I left it out. I also had only about 1/2 cup of honey, so I added some maple syrup to make the 2/3 cup I needed. Also, I did not have the chipotle powder, so I added a dash of chili powder. Last, I added some panko bread crumbs to the flour mixture to give it extra crunch. Those were basically my small changes. And believe me, the entire batch was polished off in 30 minutes flat! I made some baked beans and cornbread and voila! A nice, southern, comfort-filled meal! I will be adding this into my weekly rotation for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ultimate no fail lasagna

i love this lasagna recipe because it never fails me, even though i'm a rookie cook!  this is so easy to make and it makes tons so i always freeze half and eat it for a month!  if you want to make a small pan, divide the recipe in half and it'll still turn out great!

*edited to add: this can be made without the eggs!  the cheese mixture will still be delicious without the egg.

1. brown meat and drain off fat
2. add spaghetti sauce , pizza sauce , salt and pepper
3. cook noodles in boiling water until tender
4. preheat oven to 350f
5. in separate bowl , mix together ricotta , 2 cups mozzarella , parmesan , eggs and herbs
6. in a 9x13 pan lay down layer of cooked noodles only slightly overlapping
7. cover noodles with 1 / 3 of meat sauce and 1 / 2 cheese mixture
8. cover with another layer of noodles
9. cover with 1 / 3 meat sauce and rest of the cheese mixture
10. cover with another layer of noodles
11. cover with remaining meat mixture and top with remaining shredded cheeses
12. bake at 350f for 30 minutes
13. remove from oven and let stand for at least 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was my first time cooking lasagna and it was a hit (especially with the men in the house, lol). I found that 2lbs of ground turkey made the lasagna a bit meaty, but the flavors of the cheeses, herbs and spices blended together wonderfully. I only slightly altered this recipe by using 48 oz of spaghetti sauce. It was delicious and my family is already asking me when I'm going to make it again! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review: I decided to make chicken quesadillas for the first time, and this was the recipe I decided upon. Boy, was it a HIT! Even my mom, who could really care less for Mexican food, devoured hers and asked for more. The family keeps asking when I'm going to make them again! :) I altered this recipe by doubling the sauce. Also, I used the Mexican 4-cheese blend, and didn't use the sliced cheese. It tastes delicious as is, or served with sour cream! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle casserole

this is really tasty! i love the addition of the sour cream and cream cheese. mmmmmm! prep time approximate. i got this recipe from southern living cookbook that i bought back in the 70's. it did not give number of servings, but i fed a family of 5 with a couple of them having seconds.

1. combine first six ingredients and saute until meat is done
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 20 minutes
3. cook noodles according to pkg
4. directions
5. blend cream cheese and sour cream together
6. add scallions to cream cheese mixture
7. in a slightly greased casserole , place 1 / 3 of the noodles , then 1 / 3 of scallion mixture , then 1 / 3 of the meat sauce
8. continue this two more times
9. top casserole with the shredded cheese and bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: As a mom of two toddler boys, I find quick and easy recipes like this one so helpful! I did make a couple of "mommy-friendly" tweeks, such as swapping garlic for garlic powder, leaving out the scallions, and adding the sour cream/cream cheese mixture to the meat sauce mixture. (If I would have had a larger pot, I would have combined the noodles with the sauce mixture. That would have saved me from layering all together!) Anyhow, I did use egg noodles and layered the noodles with the sauce/creamy mixture. Topped with shredded cheese and presto! My picky toddlers feasted! Very delicious.

target.recipe_text:
plum upside down cake

this is a slightly altered version of a recipe i got from a fitness magazine. it is a dense cake, very different and yummy! using the light ingredients i specified, it's relatively guilt-free.

1. heat oven to 350 f
2. coat bottom of 9-inch round cake pan with melted butter and top evenly with brown sugar
3. arrange slices of plum to cover pan , very slightly overlapping
4. sift together dry ingredients
5. beat together"wet" ingredients in large bowl
6. gradually beat together wet and dry ingredients until smooth
7. pour mixture over plums
8. bake for 35 minutes , or until inserted toothpick comes out clean
9. cool for 5 minutes , then invert onto plate to serve
target.review: My family really loved this cake! It came out so pretty to! It has a lot of flavor and is moist...hard to believe this was homemade and not out of a box! Thanks for sharing it, my neighbor gave us a lot of plums from his tree!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww core   bubbling pizza casserole

this delicous weight watcher core program recipe counts as 4 point per serving to the the core member.   you can really add any vegetables to taste to this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in skillet , brown meat over medium heat , stirring to crumble
3. stir in onion , tomato sauce , basil , garlic , and italian seasoning
4. add veggies
5. add quartered biscuit dough to the pan of sauce & meat
6. stir gently until biscuits are covered with sauce
7. spray a 9 x 13" casserole dish with cooking spray
8. dump the mixture into the dish
9. bake for 25 minutes
10. sprinkle with cheese , and bake an additional 10 minutes or until biscuits are done
11. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This is delicious! So quick and easy to make to! Just wanted to add-to make it even more low cal use Morningstar Farms veggie crumbles instead of meat. Just saute them in a pan on stovetop for a few minutes first with a little olive oil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry banana loaf

want to try something a little different?

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. beat eggs
3. stir in the oil , sugar , strawberries , and banana
4. stir together flour , oats , baking powder , soda and salt
5. dump it into the egg mixture
6. stir to moisten
7. dump it into a greased 9"x5"x3" loaf pan
8. bake at 350f
9. for 1 hour or until done
10. cool 10 minutes
11. remove from pan
12. cool on a rack
13. let ripen 1 day before cutting
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! I didn't have strawberries so I substituted frozen raspberries(defrosted and smashed) and it was equally great.I did like the other poster and added more fruit than recipe called for about 1 1/2 cups each fruit and it was perfect and flavorful.Very pretty bread! Awesome recipe, I am definitely making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
armenian rice and noodles

my daughters call this 

1. break noodles into small pieces
2. melt butter in med-large saucepan
3. cook noodles in butter 5 min , stirring frequently
4. add remaining ingredients
5. bring to boil , stirring a few times
6. reduce heat
7. simmer , covered , 14 min remove from heat , fluff with fork
8. cover and let steam 5-10 min
9. garnish with snipped parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: wow this was really good and so easy to make! Thanks for sharing this great dish! I added a little garlic and parsley just for funsies and I think it really enhanced the flavor. This is a keeper for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin tofu pie  or pumpkin tofu custards

i love this recipe because no one has a clue it has tofu in it. it was in an old american heart association cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. prepare pie crust and bake for 5-7 minutes
3. remove from oven and cool
4. reduce oven temp to 350f combine all other ingredients in a blender or food processor , blend until very smooth
5. pour into prebaked pie shell
6. bake for 1 hour or unti a knife blade inserted in the center comes out almost clean
7. cool on a rack and serve at room temperature
8. store unused portions in the refrigerator
9. variation: you can also serve this as a custard
10. spray 8 custard cups and divide the blended mixture equally
11. set cups in 9x13 pan in the oven and add hot water to custard line
12. bake at 325f for 45 minutes or until blade of knife comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This is really good! You can't see or taste the tofu at all! It has a nice smooth texture and tastes exactly like pumpkin pie! Thanks for a healthy dessert recipe! I agree with the other poster...it needs 1 cup sugar..I know thats a lot but it really needs it :) Also a dollop of Cool Whip on top sweetens it up immensely to she was right.Give this one a try!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot dog bean balls

this is a weird sounding one that the kids might like.  i haven't made it yet.  i got it out of a fundraiser cookbook.  these can be made ahead of time and then can be heated later.

1. mix the beans , dogs , cheese and garlic together in a bowl
2. use 1 whole package of the crescent rolls and 1 / 3 of the second package
3. to make the "balls" , flatten 2 triangles to make a rectangle and then press the rectangle into a muffin tin
4. fill the dough cup about 1 / 3 of the way and then fold the 3 corners of the dough over the top
5. fold the 4th corner completely over the top to seal it
6. bake these at 375 for 20 minutes or until golden brown
7. if it browns too fast , cover with foil so that they continue to heat up
8. serve warm
demonstrations.review: My kids loved these! I just substituted soy hot dogs for the meat ones. Very easy and quick to make too. They smell delicious when they bake! These are great for school lunches or "fast food" lunches in the car that you don't want a mess made and does not need utensils! Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
uncle bill s vegetarian minestrone soup

a hearty and healthy soup. excellent on chilly days. very easy to prepare.

1. heat oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add chopped onion and saut for 4 minutes or until just lightly browned
3. add water , zucchini , carrots , canellini beans , celery , basil , oregano salt , pepper , tomatoes and garlic
4. bring to boil
5. reduce heat , cover and simmer on medium-low heat for 25 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. add macaroni , cover and cook an additional 10 minutes
7. adjust spices to suit your taste
8. serve hot
target.review: This is a great soup recipe! It's easy, nutritious and full of flavor. I used vegetable stock and served the soup with grated parmesan cheese. It was wonderful on this rainy night! I will make this recipe on a regular basis. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww turkey chili

this is a delicious low-fat turkey chile recipe i came up with. it is only 3 pts. for a 1 cup serving. if you like it hot, add 1/2 - 1 tsp of tobasco sauce.

1. brown ground turkey with onion , pepper and garlic until no longer pink
2. do not drain
3. add tomatoes , chile powder , salt and worcestershire sauce
4. stir to combine
5. bring to a boil and then cover and simmer for 1 hour
6. stir in kidney beans and simmer another 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was quick and easy and very good! We like it hot, so I added 2 chopped jalapenos from our garden. I also added some chopped cilantro that I had leftover from other recipe. Also, it says that  it makes 7 servings, but it was 4 servings for us. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate greek salad

this is the most delicious salad - fresh and wonderful-tasting.  fyi, lettuce can very much be a part of any greek salad - if you want it to.  we like lettuce in my family and i often add it.  it would not be 'authentic' in a horiatiki (village) salad, but who cares?

1. whisk dressing ingredients together until blended
2. season to taste
3. drain onion from ice water and pat dry with paper towels
4. combine all salad ingredients , except cheese , in large bowl
5. toss with dressing
6. sprinkle cheese over and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful salad, every bit as good as the Greek salads I've eaten in restaurants! I used some freshly picked Romaine lettuce from the garden and cut the recipe in half for two large servings. I look forward to making it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
death by caramel

this gooey rich dessert bar was made by taking an old recipe i found and tweaking it a little!

1. combine cake mix , oil and eggs
2. mix well
3. pat 2 / 3 of the mixture in bottom of greased 13 x 9 baking pan
4. in microwave safe bowl combine margarine , sweetened condensed milk and chocolate / caramel chips
5. melt until creamy
6. pour over top of cake mixture
7. sprinkle remaining cake mixture over top
8. bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until brown
9. chill 2 hours and then cut into bars
demonstrations.review: Everyone enjoyed these bars. The guys practically inhaled them! They are very rich and gooey. I had to go to five stores before I found the milk chocolate and caramel swirled morsels! I wish I could rate these a 4.5. They weren't quite a 5, but still very good! Thanks for another tasty recipe! Made for Spring PAC 2009.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light crustless pumpkin pie

this is a recipe for pumpkin pie which i have sort of concocted myself. it is absolutely delicious, and unbelievably lowfat/low-calorie. it's perfect for diabetics or those watching their weight, but it tastes so yummy that most people would love it! it is a bit spicy, so if you don't like spices very much, leave out the cloves.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. in a small bowl , combine splenda , cornstarch , cinnamon , ginger , cloves , and salt
3. in a separate large bowl , beat egg whites well
4. stir sugar mixture into the large bowl
5. stir in the can of pumpkin
6. slowly stir in skim milk
7. stir well , until all ingredients are uniformly mixed
8. pour into a 9-inch round pie plate that has been lightly coated with nonstick cooking spray
9. bake at 425f for twelve to fifteen minutes
10. reduce temperature to 350f
11. bake pie an additional 30-35 minutes at 350f
12. remove pie from oven and cool
13. serve immediately or refrigerate until serving
demonstrations.review: This is wonderful and the bonus is that it's VERY low calorie and virtually sugar free! I made it as written. Splenda is the perfect sweetener for this recipe because there was no after taste and even my sugar loving guests couldn't tell the difference. I topped each slice with a dollop of whipped cream. DELICIOUS!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach lasagna

no boiling the noodles.  this is non-fussy lasagna that goes together quickly with satisfying results.  it's yummy.

1. in medium bowl , combine ricotta , 1 cup mozzarella cheese , egg , spinach , salt , pepper and oregano
2. stir well
3. spread 1 / 3 spaghetti sauce in a greased 9x13" baking dish
4. place 1 / 2 of lasagna noodles over sauce
5. spread with 1 / 2 ricotta cheese mixture
6. then again: sauce , noodles , cheese mixture
7. sprinkle remaining 1 cup mozzarella over
8. save a bit of sauce to dribble over top
9. pour water around edges
10. cover securely with foil
11. bake at 350 for 1 hour and 15 minutes
12. let stand 10 minutes and serve
demonstrations.review: This was really easy to put together and was very good. My family enjoyed it and the meat lovers didn't miss the meat at all. I used Barilla No Boil lasagna noodles and they worked perfectly. I will make this again.

target.recipe_text:
ohio shaker lemon pie

gourmet november 1993  

note if you are seeking another recipe, it is not here.  google the name of the other recipe and i bet it shows up.   the reviews are not for this one. also click my name.  go to my homepage.  read the directions [wink]

1. blanch the lemons for 30 seconds then drain and rinse with cold water
2. trim the ends of the lemons , toss them , cut the lemons crosswise into paper-thin slices
3. in a bowl cover the lemon slices with the sugar and let the mixture stand , stirring once after 1 hour , for 8 hours or overnight
4. preheat the oven to 425f remove the lemon slices from the sugar and arrange them in the shell
5. add the eggs and salt to the sugar , whisk the mixture until it is combined well , and pour it over the lemon slices
6. cut slits in the crust with a sharp knife , forming steam vents , and bake the pie in the middle of the oven for 25 minutes
7. reduce the temperature to 350f and bake the pie for 20 to 25 minutes more , or until the crust is golden
8. let the pie cool on a rack and serve it warm at room temperature
9. you might want to do a search engine search for the other pie if you bookmarked it
target.review: Wowww!  This pie is *fantastic*. I've tried tons of different recipes for Key Lime Pie, and this one tastes the best by far, and it uses ingredients that I always have on hand. I love this recipe because it's so old-fashioned and it actually has a history/story to it. And it was easy!  Much thanks to Jessie and to you to, philocrates!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple homemade applesauce

this makes just 1 1/2 cups of applesauce.  from great american home cooking (collector's issue 1998)

1. place apples , water , and cinnamon in a heavy saucepan
2. bring to a boil over medium heat
3. reduce heat
4. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
5. mash sugar into the apples
6. cook for another 5 minutes
7. remove cinnamon stick
8. cool and store in a tightly covered bowl in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review:
I did the same as the other two reviewers, used brown sugar and I did double the recipe.

Everything turned out perfect, best applesauce I've ever had. :D

And dare I say it... Even better than mom's! ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato salad  barefoot contessa  ina garten

really tasty mustardy flavor. ina garten, 2006. didn't allow for chill time.update: 12/03/2008 - after much deliberation as to how to do this, i decided to warn those of you who are going to make this recipe - to ignore the 2 teaspoons of salt that the recipe says to add just before you toss the salad; also, i think you should only use 1-1/2 t of salt when boiling the potatoes for the salad. better to add salt than to have too much! ok lauralie? :)

1. place potatoes and 2 tablespoons of salt in large pot of water
2. bring the water to a boil , then lower the heat and simmer 10-15 minutes , until the potatoes are barely tender when pierced with a knife
3. drain the potatoes in a colander , then place the colander with the potatoes over the empty pot and cover with a clean , dry kitchen towel
4. allow the potatoes to steam for 15-20 minutes
5. meanwhile , in a small bowl , whisk together the mayonnaise , buttermilk , dijon mustard , whole grain mustard , dill or parsley , 1 teaspoon of salt , 1 teaspoon of black pepper , and a pinch of crushed red pepper , if using
6. set aside
7. when the potatoes are cool enough to handle , cut them in quarters or in half , depending on their size
8. place the cut potatoes in a large bowl
9. while the potatoes are still warm , pour enough dressing over them to moisten
10. add the celery and red onion , 2 teaspoons of salt and 1 teaspoon of pepper
11. toss well , cover , and refrigerate a few hours to allow the flavors to blend
12. serve either cold or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe, made it tonight from Ina's cookbook. I use about half the salt in the boiling water that the recipe calls for, and let people add salt if desired afterwards. I also omit the dijon and use all grainy mustard, because we like the texture so much, and use green onions instead of red onions. I love this recipe because it isn't globby and overwhelmed by mayonnaise, and the dill adds a really fresh taste. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern lima beans with rice

i was born and raised in the south, and we eat a lot of beans.  here is a easy and basic lima bean recipe.  we've been doing it this way for years. you can use ham hocks, hambones, smoked bacon or smoked sausage for the pork flavor in this dish.  also fresh, frozen or even canned beans can be used--they just won't have to cook as long.

1. i know the bag says to soak the beans overnight , but you really don't have to
2. wash the beans , and then put them in a large pot
3. cover with water and bring to a boil
4. boil for 3 to 5 minutes , then turn off the heat , cover and let it sit for 1 hour
5. after the beans have sat , drain the water and sit the beans to the side
6. add the oil to the pot and saut the ham hocks and onions together , until onion is clear and tender , add garlic and saut about 2 minutes more
7. add the beans and cover with water
8. add pepper and salt--only about 1 teaspoon of salt at first
9. bring to a boil
10. stir , reduce heat and cover and simmer for about 2 hours
11. keep checking the water level and stirring every once in a while
12. add more water if needed , but not too much
13. just enough to keep about 1 inch of water above the beans as they cook
14. cook until beans are tender , adding more salt if needed
15. the water will turn into a wonderful gravy
16. serve over rice
demonstrations.review:
OH my goodness that was soooooo good! I just had it for dinner tonight, and my dad, who is usually quite discriminatory, well he loved it just as much as I did. :D Wish we made more! 

I didn't have any ham hocks or anything like that on hand, so I used some salt pork, and that worked just fine. Thanks so much for posting the recipe! 

I just can't understand how so many folks think so poorly of lima beans... lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
starbucks blueberry muffins

here's a recipe for the blueberry muffins at starbuck's. this recipe originated from www.ca.answers.yahoo.

1. cream butter and sugar together until light and fluffy
2. add egg and mix well
3. sift dry ingredients together
4. add flour mixture to the butter mixture , alternating with milk
5. toss blueberries with lemon rind and gently fold into batter
6. do not over-mix
7. fill 12-cup muffin tin with paper cups or grease with butter
8. fill 2 / 3 full with batter
9. bake in preheated 375f oven for 15-20 minutes
10. remove from tins and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: I *loooooooved* these (so did my dad and boyfriend!). I have to tell you, I've been searching for YEARS to find the perfect muffin recipe, consistency-wise. The pastry flour really makes this recipe. I'd never used it in muffins before, and the texture came out just like the kinds of muffins you buy at a bakery/coffeeshop. Nice and light and fluffy, and moist! I subbed dried currants for blueberries, and it came out wonderfully. I will definitely continue making/switching up this recipe for ALL muffins. :D Great recipe overall, and it works really well as a general base for so many other kinds of muffins. Thanks so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese chocolate squares

this is a favorite in my family. i made it for the holiday christmas party at work and everyone wanted the recipe. it is the best of cheese cake and chocolate in one.

1. microwave 3 / 4 cup of margarine and 2 oz
2. chocolate squares until melted
3. stir together
4. stir in graham cracker crumbs , coconut and peanuts
5. press mixture onto bottom of 13x9 inch backing pan
6. chill 30 minutes
7. mix cream cheese , sugar , vanilla until well blended
8. spread over graham cracker crust
9. chill 30 minutes
10. microwave reamaining margarine and chocolate squares until melted
11. mix well , and then spread over the cream cheese layer
12. chill until chocolate is hardened
13. cut into squares and serve
14. hint: warm a knife with warm water to cut without cracking the chocolate topping
15. the review reminded me that i do double my chocolate topping
16. it just makes it that much better !
demonstrations.review: I recently had to cater a Christmas party and used this as one of my sqaure/bar recipes. These were one of the first things to go, and I actually saved a bunch for myself, because they were the tastiest of all our desserts. The only problem I ran into was that the graham crumbs, coconut and peanut section didn't hold together as nicely as I would have liked. Added a little bit of butter and baked that layer briefly in an oven (as you would with a graham cracker pie crust), it seemed to help a little, but still, a lot stuck to the pan. Next time, I will bake a little longer, or line the pan with foil first. Still, this recipe is a keeper and I will definitely make it again. Very easy and very delicious results!

target.recipe_text:
mojito cake

from a betty crocker  'super moist cakes' mini recipe mag. posted for safekeeping.

1. heat oven to 350
2. spray bottom of 13x9 pan with baking spray
3. beat cake ingredients in large bowl on low speed for 30 seconds
4. increase to medium speed and beat 2 minutes
5. pour batter into prepared pan
6. bake about 30 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool 15 minutes
8. meanwhile , mix glaze ingredients in a medium saucepan and heat to boiling over high heat , stirring frequently
9. reduce heat to medium , boil for another 2 minutes , stirring frequently , until glaze has thickened slightly
10. poke warm cake with fork every inch
11. pour glaze slowly over cake
12. cool completely , about 1 hour
13. in a small bowl , beat whipping cream and powdered sugar on high speed until soft peaks form
14. garnish each serving with whipped cream , mint leaf , and shredded lime peel
15. store loosely covered at room temperature
target.review: I just made this for Mother's Day and it is Soooo good! Just a note: I did'nt have rum (shame on me!) so I used 1 teaspoon rum extract + 1/4 cup water for the cake.  For the glaze I used 2 teaspoons rum extract + 1/2 cup water.  The glaze smells like hot buttered rum, yum!  I used regular whipped cream from a squirt can, which was easier.  This is a great cake to use when you want something a little different than the usual.  Thanks for posting it so I don't have to!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana rum brownies   d

here's is a super fast, diferent kind of brownie.  betcha can't eat just one!

1. pre-heat oven to 350f
2. please ignore the 2 eggs and 1 / 2 cup milk
3. the ingredients for the brownie mix are bogus
4. i had to put in something so recipe would be accepted
5. please use appropriate added ingredients for your particular brownie mix
6. directions:
7. prepare brownie mix as directed on package in large bowl
8. set aside
9. heat milk and extract in medium saucepan , until hot
10. add bananas and stir for 1 minute to heat through
11. pour banana mixture and nuts into brownie mix and stir
12. pour into lightly greased 9-inch square pan
13. bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
14. sprinkle with powdered sugar , if desired
15. cut into bars
demonstrations.review: I thought they were great - very moist and did not dry out.  My kids however didn't like them too much...they saw and tasted the banana bits and they prefer the more traditional type of brownie.  But if you can get kids to try them, then that's one more way to get some fruit into their diet!  Thanks for submitting the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy sausage balls

you can use these in pasta dishes. or put them on a platter and supply toothpicks for great appetizers.

1. mix all ingredients together well
2. form into 1in balls
3. place on ungreased shallow pan
4. bake at 375 for 15 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was a winner at the Christmas family get togther-I made 3 batches!  By the 3rd batch I had made a couple of adjustments...mind you these are wonderful as is - the taste vaguely reminds you of stuffing...by the 3rd batch I had to use minced green pepper b/c I ran out of celery, I used a little minced garlic as suggested by some other reviewers, and upped the Bisquick and cheese to 1 C. each.  That was my own personal favorite combination.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon shortbread cookies

my ex m-i-l had this recipe scribbled on the flyleaf of one of her family cookbooks and no one knew what it was, one year we made it and it was her mom's infamous shortbread cookies. i thought i'd lost the recipe when i divorced, but i found it online (with food processor instructions no less!) and wanted to share. i like bigger cookies so i don't get as many out of the recipe, some friends can get 5 dozen out of theirs. prep time includes chilling, and it can vary.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease baking sheets
3. place flour , cinnamon , and salt in work bowl of food processor
4. pulse five or six times until blended
5. remove to a small bowl
6. process butter and brown sugar about 30 seconds , scraping down sides once or twice , until light and fluffy
7. add egg yolk and process about 10 seconds to blend
8. add flour mixture and pulse six to eight times , just until blended
9. wrap dough in plastic wrap and chill at least one hour or overnight
10. roll out dough , half at a time , to 1 / 8-inch thick
11. cut with cookie cutter and place cookies two inches apart on baking sheets
12. sprinkle with sugar
13. bake seven to eight minutes until firm and just beginning to darken at edges
14. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review:
This was an excellent recipe - it tasted GREAT.  My kids love it!  It was crumbly and a little difficult to roll out, but we managed to get stars and circles out of them.  Thanks for sharing this!
Rebecca

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula deen s chicken and wild rice casserole

i found this in one of my paula deen cookbooks.  it's so easy and so fast, and can definitely be made after a long day at work.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cook rice according to package directions and spoon into greased 2 quart casserole dish
3. layer chopped chicken over top of rice
4. mix soup , mayonnaise and curry powder and pour over chicken
5. top with dry stuffing mix and dot evenly with butter
6. bake for 30 minutes , or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: Wonderful casserole! I didn't use curry b/c my hubby doesn't like that. But I put a cup each of diced onion and celery, and used the regular Pep. Farm stuffing mix on top.  The mayonnaise is amazing with it - it adds a tangy taste.  The butter on top is awesome too.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple butter pumpkin pecan streusel pie

i recently discovered the merits of apple butter as a baking ingredient, and wanted to share my discovery.

1. preheat to 375 degrees
2. combine pumpkin , apple butter , brown sugar , cinnamon , ginger , nutmeg , salt , eggs , and evaporated milk
3. pour into the pie shell
4. bake 50-60 minutes or until knife inserted two inches from center comes out clean
5. meanwhile , mix together butter , flour , sugar , and pecans until they resemble coarse crumbs
6. top pie with streusel topping and bake for an additional 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: If I could give this 10 stars I would.  My 13 yr old daughter makes the pumpkin pie every Thanksgiving and Christmas with my help.  We've always used the "traditional" recipe but some of our family don't prefer it.  This time we tried yours and everyone raved over it.  I happened to have some "apple-rum" butter which made the texture so terrific.  Not watery at all.  Thick and rich!  The taste of the pie and the topping made it really sensational.  Thank you so much for publishing this receipe - my daughter has now adopted it for all future pumpkin pies!

target.recipe_text:
sweet potato and lentil curry with rice

i discovered this many years ago and will even get my husband to eat it, even though there is no meat..........lol

1. heat a medium saucepan and add the curry paste
2. cook , while stirring , for 1 minute or until fragrant
3. add the lentils , bay leaves , onion , and sweet potato , ginger and chicken stock
4. bring to the boil and reduce the heat to low
5. or until the sweet potato is cooked
6. season with salt and black pepper
7. place the cooked rice on 4 serving plates , spoon over the curry and scatter with coriander leaves
target.review: Great, great, great.  I browned the seasonings along with the onion, ginger, and added a bit of garlic.  After a couple minutes, I added everything else into my dutch oven and just simmered for 20 - 30 minutes.  I added a huge bunch of fresh spinach at the end, covered and waited for it to whilt.  It was just fabulous.  My DH who is a VERY picky veggie eater really enjoyed this.  I thought it got even better the next day when I ate it at luch.  Good job!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
payday bars

yummy version of the candy bar.

1. grease 9x13 pan
2. pour 1 / 2 peanuts on bottom of pan
3. melt margarine and chips
4. add milk and then marshmallows
5. pour over peanuts , pat down
6. put rest of peanuts in and pat down
7. chill
demonstrations.review: I would give these ten stars if I could.  I made these as a part of my Christmas treat selection this year and they were a hit!  They don't taste exactly like a payday (not as tough nougat consistency) but they taste GREAT, nonetheless!  DH wasn't crazy about them, but he doesn't like Payday bars either.  He said they would be better with some sort of chocolate component.  I will most definitely add this to my collection and make time and time again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed white sweet potato bake

found this in the kraft food & family and i thought this would be great for the holidays! i love the idea of the layers being visible through a clear casserole dish if possible.

1. preheat oven to 375f place white and sweet potatoes in separate bowls
2. add half each of the cream cheese and sour cream to the potatoes in each bowl
3. season with salt and pepper
4. mash with potato masher or fork until creamy
5. stir half of the parmesan into the bowl of white potato mix
6. mix half of the cheddar cheese into the bowl of sweet potatoes
7. alternately layer half each of the white potato mixture and sweet potato mixture in a 2 qt clear glass casserole dish
8. repeat layers
9. bake 15 minutes
10. sprinkle with remaining cheeses and continue baking 5 minutes or until cheeses are melted
demonstrations.review: I made this for Thanksgiving to avoid the high sugar typical sweet potatoe dish.  I have to say it was pretty good.  All comments noted they liked the change in potato dish.  However, most noted that that you couldn't really taste the sweet potato.  I think if I made it next time I would use 3 sweet and 2 white potatoes.  That is also because I do not like white very much nor the high gylcemic index of it either.  I think this is a great dish if you are looking for something different.  Oh, I also added way mroe cheese than suggested - what can I say, I love cheese!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate dipped krispies peanut butter balls

these are lighter then the ones without the rice krispies. i got the recipe from the "classic holiday cooking" cook book. you can shape into eggs for easter!

1. melt butter and while hot , stir in peanut butter
2. mix well and add vanilla , powdered sugar and rice krispies
3. work in with hands until it will form balls
4. if using paraffin shred on a box grater then add to the chocolate in a double boil and heat till melted and combined
5. dip into melted chocolate and paraffin or shortening with toothpick
6. cool on waxed paper
demonstrations.review: ********** - That's 10 Stars! Wow, this was my most coveted Christmas Treat! People went nuts over these things! I followed other reviewers suggestions and only used 2 cups of powdered sugar. They were very sweet and cannot imagine using an entire box of powdered sugar. I also slightly crushed the Rice Krispies before adding them. Finally, I also rolled the balls and then covered with plastic wrap and placed in the freezer as I went about making other sweets. I used 2 tbs. of shortening instead of paraffin wax as well. ****These are a great sweet treat and the Rice Krispies give them such a neat twist. You will not be disappointed!****  I have made these 2 more times and still continue to get RAVE reviews!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dijon broccoli

nan

1. steam the broccoli until it is barely tender
2. combine all other ingredients and heat until butter melts
3. stir to blend
4. pour over the hot broccoli
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful!  I made as a side dish for Thanksgiving and it was a hit.  I don't think I had quite enough broccoli, but it wasn't a big deal.  Great flavor, healthy, and less fattening than a casserole.   This is going in my recipe book!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead wraps   oamc

i was thinking that if you can make breakfast burritos to freeze than you have to be able to make a healthy wrap for lunch. here is the result. feel free to change it up to whatever sounds good to you!

1. combine rice , southwest seasoning and water in a saucepan , and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to low , cover , and simmer for 35-40 minutes , or until tender
3. remove from heat , and cool
4. place black beans and pinto beans into a colander or strainer , and rinse
5. transfer to a large bowl
6. add corn , onion , spices and salsa , and toss to mix
7. mix in rice and cheese
8. divide the mixture evenly among the tortillas , and roll up
9. freeze wraps in single layer on lightly greased cookie sheet
10. when fully frozen , wrap individually
11. place wraps in large zip-top freezer bags
12. freeze
13. to serve: unwrap wraps from foil or plastic wrap that you used for freezing
14. wrap in a paper towel
15. cook in microwave until heated through
16. or thaw wrap , put foil , and bake at 350f for ten minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  I am just floored at how amazing these are.  I used basmati rice (only rice I ever used) and a rasberry chipotle salsa I found at my local Kroger.  I have to keep my co-workers out of the freezer to keep them from stealing these tasty treats.  These will be a MUST have in my freezer for the future.  THANKS!

target.recipe_text:
no flour cornbread

this recipe was the one my mother used, and her mother before her. beyond that i can't go! it spoiled me for anything calling itself "cornbread" that has flour or sweeteners in it -- i call those "corn cake." this is great with chili, stew, and other hearty dishes. my dad used to crumble it up into buttermilk and eat it with a spoon. it's a requirement for our family's new years day dinner, along with the roast pork and black-eyed peas. it's also the main ingredient in thanksgiving/christmas/anytime turkey stuffing.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. put first 5 ingredients in mixing bowl
3. mix with large spoon or whisk
4. put bacon grease in well-seasoned 10-inch cast iron skillet over medium to high heat
5. just as the bacon grease is about to start smoking , pour it into the other ingredients , stirring as you pour
6. leave enough in the skillet to coat the bottom and sides
7. pour entire mixture into the skillet
8. place skillet on middle rack of oven
9. bake until cornbread is springy in the middle , browned and pulling away from the skillet on the sides
10. remove from oven and invert skillet over serving plate
11. if cornbread does not drop easily , you may need to run an icing spatula or even a flexible metal egg-turner around / under it so it comes loose
12. recipe halves well , just remember you can't cut the bacon grease by half because you still need to coat the skillet
13. serve hot , with plenty of butter
14. or margarine , if you insist
target.review: My mom and I don't eat wheat flour, so we love this. But not just because of that - it's also a great recipe that the rest of our family loves. It's a little crumbly, but the yummy flavor totally makes up for it! We use margarine or butter, not bacon grease, and it's still awesome!!! Oh, our skillet isn't oven-proof, but we always cook it on the stove at medium-high heat for about 15-20 minutes and it cooks just fine!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
purple oatmeal

this is so easy, delicious & healthy!  we tried this with raspberries & didn't like it as much.  i found this on a vegetarian website & made a few minor adjustments.  enjoy!  your cholesterol levels will thank you, lol.

1. bring water to a rapid boil
2. stir in oats , lemon zest , cinnamon , flaxseed , & nutmeg
3. reduce heat to a simmer
4. cook for about 20 minutes , stirring occasionally , until it is the consistency you like
5. add blueberries & cook 5 minutes longer
6. add walnuts , shut off the heat , put the lid on & let stand 5 minutes
7. serve & enjoy ! we do sprinkle a little vanilla sugar on ours
8. )
demonstrations.review: Oh my GOSH!!!! This is FANTASTIC!!! Tastes a lot like a blueberry muffin in the form of oatmeal! I halfed the recipe because only 4 of us were eating it - my parents don't eat breakfast and my brother for some reason didn't want to try it. I've made this type of thing before. Almost idental recipes, but no flax seeds or lemon zest in mine. I didn't use flax seeds in the recipe today - we didn't have it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calzone  bread machine

you can create your own fillings for this very easy calzone. i don't use the pepperoni, but substitute cooked, chopped spinach. you can also add sauteed onions and peppers, olives, ricotta cheese...etc. i have also made small individual calzones to dip in marinara sauce...heaven! kids love these.

1. place water , salt , basil , oregano , garlic powder , bread flour , dry milk , sugar , and yeast in the pan of the bread machine in the order suggested by the manufacturer
2. select dough cycle
3. after cycle ends , roll out dough on a lightly floured surface , shaping into a 16 x 10 inch rectangle
4. transfer to a lightly greased cookie sheet
5. in a small bowl , mix together chopped pepperoni and mozzarella
6. spoon pizza sauce in a stripe down the center of dough lengthwise
7. add sausage and cheese filling
8. make diagonal cuts 1 1 / 2 inches apart down each side , cutting within a 1 / 2 inch of the filling
9. criss cross strips over filling , sealing with water
10. brush top with melted butter
11. you can just fold over the sides without cutting the strips to make this process easier
12. it will taste just as good , but not look as nice
13. be sure to seal the edges well
14. bake at 350 degrees f for 35 to 45 minutes
demonstrations.review:
OH MY GOSH!!!!!!!!! THIS IS THE BEST EVER!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! All my family LOVE LOVE LOVES this!!!!!!!!!!!! I made a mixture of about 2 tablespoon of  melted butter, some garlic salt, and some Italian seasoning and brushed it on top before baking. I made six individual calzones, two for each person (only 3 of us were eating) with a little extra dough that I used for little breadsticks in the shape of our initials. Thanks for the fantastic recipe!!!!!!!! I am making this again tonight!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!
-Indiana State Fair Girl

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Ten stars for this recipe!!!! I've been eating all whole wheat/grain breads, pastas, etc., so I tried out this recipe (I'm only eating it if it has at LEAST 50% whole wheat in it), only to find out that my whole family LOVED it!!!! I served one with dinner and froze the rest. Now we have two left. It's a great, hearty, healthy-tasting and lightly sweet bread. Thanks for this fabulous recipe!!!! Will totally make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review:
GROSS!!!!
I'm really sorry to say this, because this is the first 1-star review I've ever posted. It was really dry and nasty and had the worst flavor.....it ended up in the trash after staying in the fridge for a week. 
Sorry, but we did NOT like this!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: Extremely good! Used it on a cake mix - wanted to try your chocolate cake, Kittencal, but my mom wouldn't let me. Very very very yummy!!! My Aunt's birthday party's tomorrow and I'm making the cake! (Yeah, I snitched a bit while frosting...smelled so good and I couldn't resist :) ) My aunt'll LOVE this!!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
hamburger stroganoff

thick, rich goodness

1. brown hamburger meat
2. add onions and cook until tender
3. add onion soup mix , cream soup , milk and seasonings
4. mix well
5. simmer until bubbly and then for 5 minutes more
6. remove from heat
7. stir in sour cream
8. serve over cooked egg noodles or sliced baked potatoes
target.review: This was quick, used up many items in need of use and was absolutely delicious!  From picky to 8 year old it was loved by all :).  I used that 2lbs ground out 2 days, subbed a cream of celery for one mushroom, shorted the sour cream by 1/3 and it was still saucy, creamy and delicious over 16 oz. egg noodles cooked to perfection buttered and peppered!  Thanks Ruth for saving dinner tonight!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cilantro jalapeno hummus

a wonderful combination of flavors. this is always a huge hit at parties.

1. in food processor , pulse garlic
2. add beans , lime juice and salt
3. puree
4. slowly add olive oil and blend until thick , 1-2 minute
5. add cilantro and jalapeno , pulse 10 seconds
6. transfer to bowl , and chill a few hours to allow flavors to meld
demonstrations.review:
Totally delicious!  I took a few liberties, couldn't resist ;)  I made a half batch using a huge garlic clove, juice from a big lime (love the stuff), 2T. olive oil and drizzled in water until the consistency was smooth enough.  I didn't measure, just used a sm. handful of cilantro (another love!).  This was so good on tortilla chips I didn't even realize until 1/3 of the way through the bowl that I forgot the peppers!
Thanks C - I'll make this one again for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut ginger rice

great side dish, just a little bit different.

1. heat broth , coconut milk and ginger to boiling in saucepan over medium-high heat
2. stir in rice
3. heat to boiling , reduce heat
4. cover and simmer 15 minutes or until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed
5. add lemon rind and green onions
6. fluff rice lemon rind and onions lightly with fork to mix
7. garnish with coconut and lemon slices
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I used this as the base for a very simple but not overly sweet dessert.  I was out of lemon and left out the onion.  After the rice cooked, I drizzled a little coconut milk around an individual serving, topped with diced mango and the flaked coconut~ delicious and cooling after our lentil soup! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s lasagna

like my father's rib recipe which i've also posted, this is a recipe which some old buddies of mine recently requested that i post. back when we all were a little younger, the guys used to come over everytime my dad made his lasagne. maybe it was the free meal or maybe it was just that good but this recipe is the reason why lasagna has always been one of my favorite foods. i know that you can substitute ground beef for the sausage (or use both combined) with equal success. i've posted this as 6-10 servings but i know from experience that 4 big guys can polish this off and still ask for more.

1. remove sausage skins and break up the sausage in frying pan
2. brown meat slowly and spoon off excess fat
3. add garlic , basil , 1 1 / 2 teaspoons salt , tomatoes and tomato paste
4. simmer , covered for 15 minutes
5. stir often
6. set aside when finished
7. meanwhile , cook noodles in boiling salted water until tender
8. drain
9. rinse
10. in a large bowl , beat eggs
11. add ricotta , parmesan , parsley , pepper and a tsp of salt
12. mix well
13. now in a 13x9x2 inch baking dish
14. layer half the noodles
15. spread with half the ricotta cheese / egg mixture
16. add half the thinly sliced mozzarella and then half the meat sauce
17. repeat
18. bake at 375 f degrees for about 30 minutes
19. alternatively , you could refrigerate until later and then bake for 45 minutes
20. either way let the lasagna stand for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
Ok, I'll admit it I needed to make some substitutions and minor changes, yet I don't think they affected the core recipe.  I didn't have sausage, I had ground pork so I added 1t. fennel seed, 1t. oregano, 1t. garlic salt and dash pepper while slowly browning the meat.  
We're the kind of girls who like a saucy lasagne; for the garlic bread of course.  I only had one 14.5 oz. can of tomatoes, so I used that, the 2 sm cans of tomato paste, and added a small can of tomato sauce and one 14.5 oz. can water.  I let all this simmer with the spices when the recipe indicated to add tomatoes.
I layer different than Nurbel's dad, always starting with sauce (so noodles don't stick)and always topping with the mozzarella cheese.  This time I added a twist: I discovered this spinach in the refrigerator (fresh leaves) that needed to be used so I added them in a single layer to the center of the lasagne.  (You all realize I'm including all this so I can replicate it, right?)  I will never go to that fancy restaurant downtown that charges $12.50 for only one piece again, never.  This is authentic enough for my Italian friend. My daughter was upset because zaar only goes to 5 stars!  Many more stars to you!! Thank you Nurbel, please tell your dad his lasagne ROCKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef and broccoli

i learned to cook this recipe from stephen yan many years ago. he was famous for his television shows -wok with yan.

1. in a mixing bowl , mix together soy sauce , pepper , sambal oelek , sesame oil and corn starch
2. add sliced beef , coat well and let marinate for 15 minutes
3. in a wok , heat 2 tablespoons of peanut oil until smoke begins to rise
4. add broccoli florets and salt , stir well
5. now add 1 / 2 cup of water , cover with a lid and cook on high heat for 3 - 4 minutes or until steam starts to escape from the edge of the lid
6. remove broccoli and any liquid to a bowl
7. reheat wok to high heat , add the remainder 2 tablespoons of peanut oil
8. when hot , add garlic and brown for 1 minute , stirring often
9. add sliced beef and marinade and stir-fry until the color of meat changes , about 1 minute
10. return broccoli and liquid to the wok and mix
11. stir-fry for 30 seconds
12. serve hot
demonstrations.review: We rarely eat beef anymore and when we do I want it to be special... this recipe will go in the keeper file to be specifically modified to our tastes!  Additionally, I'll use this method for meat in any and all future stir fry dishes I prepare... I used the tapioca starch vs cornstarch and got the benefit of succulent tender beef and the velvety mouth feel in the sauce that you normally get with take out!  I added a pinch of red pepper flakes for some heat and next time will add brown sugar for a note of sweetness.  Finally, I'd like to speak to method particularly given some of the comments in the reviews... with the broccoli already in the wok, as per the instructions, I didn't find adding water to the pan to be either scary or dangerous ;)  TY for the best attempt at Chinese I've ever made in my own kitchen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pineapple nut bread

a wonderful sweet bread. i always eat this with whipped cream cheese on top and a cup of coffee. mmmmmm....

1. combine flour , sugar , soda , cinnamon , pecans and salt in large bowl
2. set aside
3. in another bowl , mix vanilla , eggs , oil , bananas and pineapple
4. after blending , add liquid mixture to dry mixture and stir until well blended
5. pour into two greased and floured loaf pans
6. bake at 350 degrees for 60-70 minutes or until toothpick inserted near center comes out clean
7. cool in pans on wire rack for 10 minutes before removing
8. continue to cool on wire rack
9. store in airtight container or plastic wrap
demonstrations.review: This is very similar to my mom's tropical quick bread, to which she adds coconut.  I added 1 t. dried orange peel, 1/2 t. each ginger and nutmeg.  This bread really needs one day wrapped before slicing to mature and blend flavors.

target.recipe_text:
old time baked beans

these are the beans my french-canadian mother used to make. she never measured anything making these so i've estimated the amounts. these taste great with fresh bread. a good dish to keep in mind for pot-lucks. you can add pork or weiners to it if you like. bacon strips on top work well.

1. soak beans overnight in water , then boil until tender
2. drain water and put beans in a large heavy pot or crock
3. add all ingredients together and mix
4. add enough water to cover beans
5. cover and bake at 325 degrees for about 6 hours
6. check beans while they are baking to add water to ensure they do not go dry
target.review: Oh, yum!! These were the best baked beans I've made ever, and I've made a few. I only had 1# beans, but kept the 'sauce' ingredients the same volume. In addition to the bacon on top, I chopped up a few slices and added them to the beans when they went in the oven. Today is weekly bread baking day, so when the beans came out the bread went in; beans stayed nice and hot on top of the oven. Your beans and my bread made a perfect winter meal. Thanks for a great recipe, Paul!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted ratatouille

ratatouille is usually a savoury vegetable stew cooked on top-of-the-stove ... but roasting in the oven intensifies the flavours. for a main course, serve this with salad and crusty bread. (i enjoy it on top of shredded lettuce with a dollop of yogurt cheese.) the recipe comes from bonnie stern's more heartsmart cooking.

1. spread onion , garlic , eggplant , zucchini , tomatoes , fennel , mushrooms and sweet peppers in large lightly oiled roasting pan
2. sprinkle with rosemary , thyme , salt and pepper
3. stirring occasionally , roast vegetables in pre-heated 400f oven for 45 minutes , or until tender and browned
4. toss with basil , olive oil and vinegar
5. taste and adjust seasonings if necessary
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Roasting the vegetables for a good long time (I usually go 90 minutes or so) concentrates their flavor and really elevates this Ratatouille. I use your recipe as a starting point, and add or subtract veggies according to what's in the CSA box. So today no fennel but added in a patty-pan squash and an extra summer squash. I usually serve this on linguine with lots of Romano cheese. Leftovers will be topping pizzas next week. Thanks for a versatile, super-healthy way to eat our vegetables.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
demonstrations.review: This was a great soup! Spicy and flavorful and hearty. The different types of chili pepper all complemented eachother. I omitted the onion and added a handful each of chopped celery, carrot and corn. As the crockpot was busy, it cooked on the stove just fine. Thanks, Jill4man!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: Delicious sauce! I doubled the sauce and cooked my chops (covered) for 45 minutes after browning, and they came out very tough and dry. Seems chops should either cook quick or a long braise. So next time they'll go in for a quick 25-30 minutes and we'll see how that goes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Hey now, this was good bread! I used all freshly ground whole-wheat flour (about half and half red/white wheat), and dropped the temp about 10*... other than that followed the recipe exactly. Nice and light, with a good dark crust.
This will probably become my standard every-day bread.
Thanks for sharing, Karen!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
demonstrations.review: I've been making this chicken for years now, forgot to review -- <br/>So juicy, tender and delicious! I don't use the trash-bag -- just set the chicken in a small roasting pan and cover it with plastic wrap for the overnight. I rarely have garlic or onion powder in the kitchen, so chop-fine fresh and make more of a 'paste'.  Also, I use vinyl food-handler gloves to keep the mess down when applying the rub.  Tomorrow's chicken will be served with garlic smashed potatoes and broccoli.

target.recipe_text:
mexican crock pot roast

add some ole! to your pot roast. you can adjust the spice by using hot or mild salsa and you can substitute jalapenos for the chilis.

1. combine salsa , paste , water , seasoning mix and chilis
2. spoon 1 / 2 the mixture into the bottom of a crock pot
3. add the roast and top with the remaining mixture
4. cover and cook 8-10 hours on low
target.review: great taste and texture! There was definently some spice but it was complementary and didn't overwhelm the dish. Made this 2 weeks ago for my appreciative wife, we are reheating the leftovers for tonight to stuff in pitas with lettuce/tomatoes/etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caribbean cucumber salad

i like this salad in the summer with our bbq evenings. it is tart and a little hot. if you don't do hot so well, use one pepper.

1. slice the cucumbers lengthwise and remove seeds with a spoon or melon baller
2. slice each half into 1 / 2 inch slices
3. place in a bowl and sprinkle with the salt
4. toss gently and let sit for 30 minutes
5. drain well
6. place the cucumbers in a serving bowl and add the chilies , lime juice , and garlic
7. toss well
8. cover and let sit at room temperature for 1 hour before serving
demonstrations.review: I don't normally enjoy cucumber, but this was fantastic. The raw garlic was Very sharp, in future I may try it either roasted first or pre-soaked in the lime juice to break down some of the harsher flavors. Was a nice compliment to our meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared scallops with asian lime chile sauce

nan

1. soak skewers in water 30 minutes
2. pound garlic , chile , and sugar to a fine paste with a mortar and pestle
3. stir paste together with vinegar , fish sauce , water , and lime juice
4. pat scallops dry
5. thread 4 on each skewer then brush both sides with oil
6. season scallops with salt and pepper
7. brush a 12-inch nonstick skillet with remaining teaspoon oil and heat over high heat until hot but not smoking
8. sear scallops , turning over once , until just cooked through , about 6 minutes total
9. serve scallops with sauce spooned over
10. cooks'
11. bring to room temperature before serving
demonstrations.review:
Very nice flavors, I opted for no skewers and served it over some thai rice noodles that I briefly cooked in the pan (after removing the scallops) with a bit of the sauce. 

love4culinary's idea with the lime zest really brightened up the dish and made for a nice presentation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced black beans

really good and spicy bean dish that goes well with grilled beef and pork. add a few splashes of hot sauce towards the end of cooking time.( without the bacon, this is very good as a  vegetarian dish; or, an ounce or two of chorizo sausage can be used instead of bacon)

1. saut the bacon until almost crispy , don't drain
2. add vegetables , spice blend , garlic and bay leaf
3. stir and simmer until veggies are tender
4. add the beans , coffee , rum , curry , lime juice
5. simmer until hot
6. add salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This recipe worked mindblowingly well. Very easy, suprisingly fast to throw together, and the *flavor* exploded out of the dish. I like beans, but often have to convince myself to eat a healthy amount -- not so with these. We had lots of dishes out there ('carribean' feast) -- this was the only one scraped clean.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle cornbread

i found this recipe on the internet. i haven't tried it yet, but it sounds pretty good.

1. preheat oven to 450 , allowing the cast iron skillet to heat up with it
2. in the mixing bowl , combine the cornmeal , flour , sugar , salt , and baking powder
3. fold in the egg , buttermilk , milk , oil , and chipotles
4. spray cooking spray on cast iron skillet and pour in the batter
5. bake for 25 minutes
6. when cornbread is taken out of the oven , immediately run a knife around the edges and flip the skillet over onto a plate
7. serve with butter
demonstrations.review: Wahoo! I have a hunch that my 12" skillet was way too big, I got more of a cornbread pizza crust in terms of dimensions and it cooked through REALLY fast... other than that this was amazing. I used canned chipotles (chipotles en adobo) -- next time I think I'd cut them to 2 or maybe 3, or possibly skip the seeds... definently hot. Interestingly, this played the opposite role than cornbread usually does, e.g. with a spicy chili, providing some cooling to the meal. All in all a great recipe, though it might be nice to have the intended size of the cast iron skillet posted.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot and sour cabbage salad

i made this recipe as a side dish this week end. qick and easy, from gourmet mag

1. put cabbage and scallion in a bowl
2. heat remaining ingredients to boil and lower heat , cook until sugar is dissolved
3. pour over cabbage , toss to combine
demonstrations.review: Fantastically light and crispy, a big favorite at the table even amongst those who "didn't like cabbage." The heat of the dressing just took the edge off the rawness of the cabbage, very delicious and fresh tasting/feeling.

target.recipe_text:
spinach egg drop noodle soup

an easy delicious one pot soup to enjoy for a quick lunch or dinner. original recipe was found on the internet, but like always, i tweaked it a bit.

1. im medium saucepan , bring chicken broth to a boil
2. stir in egg noodles and cook per package directions
3. beat eggs , water , parmesan cheese and pepper together
4. stir spinach into the broth and reheat to boiling
5. pour egg mixture into soup slowly while stirring constantly with a fork
6. cook 30 seconds
7. check seasonings and add salt if desired
target.review: This whipped up in minutes.  So healthy & delicious.  I skipped the noodles and added some ginger-in-the-tube, which gave it that tiny bit of mellow spice.  MAKE THIS SOUP, whoever is reading this review!!  For the photo, I drizzled some shredded parm on top :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot corsican chicken

i nice crockpot recipe for a great chicken dish. i use this recipe #18553 recipe for what is called for. it's great to have made up ahead of time just for dishes like this. the use of chicken thighs instead of breasts makes the dish cheaper and more flavorful. don't let the long ingredient list scare you away. it only looks like a fancy pants recipe. once you throw it all together in the crockpot, the most work you have to do is in making the sauce at the end.

1. mix butter , herbs , salt and pepper , and garlic
2. rub on chicken pieces
3. put into crock pot
4. add onion , tomatoes , consomm and vermouth
5. cover
6. put on low for 4-5 hours
7. add olives and peel
8. recover
9. put on high for 30 minutes
10. remove chicken and keep the pieces warm
11. pour juices into saucepan or skillet
12. in separate cup , combine cornstarch and water
13. mix until smooth
14. stir into juices
15. bring to a boil , and cook for 2 minutes
16. pour over chicken
17. sprinkle with basil , parsley and pimentos
demonstrations.review: Decided to make this in my new cast iron Dutch oven because I started it too late in the day.   It was done in about an hour and a half.  I slightly browned the chicken with the butter and onions (used both boneless breasts & thighs cut cross-wise).  Then, I pretty much followed Jess4freedom's instructions, except I omitted olives & the last three ingredients.  The herbes de Provence were very flavorful & provided just the right "French feel" to this marvelous dish!  Fantastic on a cold winter day served with a loaf of fresh, crusty bread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom n  cheese omelet

yummy

1. mix eggs and milk
2. cook sliced mushrooms in small pan
3. add onion and garlic to mushrooms
4. melt margarine into frying pan or skillet , then pour eggs into it
5. let cook for a moment
