I also added 1 tsp of the red pepper flakes because we like spice! I added all the water, in fact I had to add more water because I simmered it for 6 hours. I also added 1 cup of a good red wine, makes all the difference in the world. I'll never buy another jar of spaghetti sauce again, this recipe is so simple and it makes a lot of sauce. And it's even better the next day. Thanks for a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic fried catfish

from southern living magazine, 1982. excellent!

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a large shallow dish
2. sprinkle fish with 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
3. dredge in cornmeal mixture , coating evenly
4. pour oil to a depth of 1 1 / 2 inches into a deep cast-iron skillet
5. heat to 350 degrees
6. fry fish , in batches , 5 to 6 minutes or until golden
7. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe. I added a little extra red pepper for some zing. Made Deely's Hush Puppies to go along with the fish. I used striper fish because the neighbor had given me a huge bag of filets. Doubled the recipe as I had a lot of fish to fry. Will use again. Thanks, Bev!!!

target.recipe_text:
nepalese vegetable pulao

this is a lovely dish that is pretty easy to put together, and is full of flavor. :)

1. rinse rice thoroughly , and then soak it in water for about 45 minutes
2. heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a pan , and add cumin seeds , allowing them to heat until they begin to change color
3. then add turmeric , bay leaf , cloves cardamom pods and cinnamon
4. then add ginger , garlic and chilies
5. cook on medium heat for just a minute
6. next , add the onion , tomato and green peas , and cook for 3 minutes
7. now , drain the water from rice and add rice , stirring gently for a minute to combine thoroughly
8. add 2 and 1 / 2 cup of water , and add salt to taste
9. cook on high heat , stirring gently but continuously
10. when water is almost absorbed , add lemon juice
11. lower your heat , cover the pan , and allow it to continue cooking for approximately 7 minutes or so , until the rice is completely cooked
12. serve immediately
target.review: I cooked 5 cups of rice and increased all of the ingredients.  I think I may have used a little too much water, because my rice was just a touch overcooked.  I think if I would have followed the recipe exactly it probably would have turned out better, but the flavor was still good.  I wanted to try this dish for company and they seemed to like it despite the overcooked rice.  By the way, I also added a couple of potatoes in there and I think next time I'll add some red chili powder just for that extra kick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish and tomato curry

from the book hot and spicy that belongs to a friend

1. spice mixture:
2. heat the oil in a wok or skillet over medium heat
3. stir-fry the spice mixture ingredients until fragrant
4. add the tomatoes with their juice , salt and sugar
5. reduce heat to low , cover and cook for 5 minutes
6. add the fish , cover and cook a further 5 minutes or until the fish is just cooked
7. remove from the heat , divide into serving bowls and sprinkle with the fresh coriander
8. serve with rice and the lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: Made this for dinner tonight and served with naans.  Delicious!  Here are just a few changes I made: I fried the onions, garlic and ginger for a little bit before adding the rest of the spices,  I didn't have enought tomatoes so I used 1 chopped tomato with 2 tbsp tomato sauce, I didn't add the sugar but I did add one seeded Serrano pepper sliced length-wise.  I don't think my changes affected the true taste of your recipe which was just wonderful.  thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin crescent rolls

a unique pumpkin recipe ideal for breakfast, brunch or simply an autumn afternoon treat served with steaming mugs of spiced apple cider. recipe courtesy of a cooksrecipes e-mail i received.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in large bowl , blend cream cheese , pumpkin , eagle brand , flour and spices until combined and smooth
3. unroll crescent rolls
4. separate and lay flat
5. evenly spread 1 tablespoons of pumpkin mixture over the uncooked dough
6. sprinkle 1 teaspoon chopped nuts over the pumpkin layer , then roll into crescent shape
7. sprinkle top of rolls with sugar
8. bake 11 to 13 minutes or until slightly golden brown
9. store leftovers covered at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I was just about to post this recipe, but I see it's already here.  I made these yesterday and they were delicious.  I skipped sprinkling them with sugar.  They are perfect for breakfast or an afternoon snack.  Easy to make and very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy coconut pie

i received this recipe from a really good friend of mine. she is a cancer survivor and gave me this recipe to put into a cookbook that we printed to raise money for the american cancer society. it is really quick and easy and oooohhhhh sooooooo gooooooood!!!!!!

1. mix all ingredients well
2. pour into pie shell
3. bake@ 350 degrees f for 50 minutes or until golden brown and set
4. i use the flour to assure that the pie sets good , but it is not required
demonstrations.review: If you're a coconut lover, this is absolutely wonderful!  It was sooo easy to make.  I followed the recipe exactly using unsweetened coconut and it was just perfect.  I didn't think the pie was too shallow.  It may be because I used extra large eggs.  I wish I could have taken a picture of the whole pie because it really was picture perfect!  Thanks Jellyqueen!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
clear fruit glaze for cakes

i knew this recipe wouldn't be here at zaar because it's very very old.  it came from my ex-boyfriend's aunt suzie.  she was different from the rest of the family (she a baptist, they were catholic) which made her the black sheep.  she and i got along like peas and carrots.  i commented that i loved to cook and she gave me this recipe.  it was her husband's grandmother's recipe.  she said it was his favorite.

1. bring the sugar and 1 / 2 cup juice to a boil
2. dissolve the cornstarch in the remaining juice
3. add to the boiling juice and cook till thick
4. stir in the corn syrup
5. bring back to a boil and remove from heat
6. cool and drizzle over cake
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much for posting this.  I was pressed for time and needed something quick.  Recipezaar to the rescue!  I used this glaze for raspberries and blueberries that I used to top mini cheesecakes (recipe by RecipeNut).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
va voom veggie burgers

i got this recipe when i worked at colonial pines inn, a bed and breakfast in highlands, n.c. delicious! feel free to put in what you like, maybe some chopped mushrooms,wheat germ,seasonings, etc.

1. mix ingredients all together
2. shape into patties
3. fry on low heat in olive oil , till each side is browned
4. serve with lettuce and tomato and grilled onions on a bun , with your favorite toppings
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I really wanted to make this recipe but I didn't have oats or cornbread stuffing on hand.  I just used a mixture of bread crumbs and cornflake crumbs.  I think I might add some red pepper flakes next time for a little kick but my husband enjoyed them as is.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.  Always looking for a good veggie burger as we are trying to cut back on meat. I used "Recipe#416331" and it was a nice combination.

target.recipe_text:
egg salad sandwich   simple and delicious

egg salad that is tasty and satisfying. it is the most requested sandwich in our household.

1. place boiled eggs into a small bowl , mash about half of them with a fork
2. stir in the green onions , miracle whip and dry mustard powder
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper to suit your tastes
4. makes 2 sandwiches
target.review: I hadn't had an egg salad sandwich in years,,,this is as great as |I remembered them. I took Emilee's suggestion and used a spicy brown mustard like my granny used. Thanks for sharing Chef Dee ! I will certainly have this on my menue more often now that I have such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham chowder

creamy ham chowder. perfect for winter nights and quick dinners. this is another of my mother's geraldine lefever recipes she used while we were growing up. our children have loved it too!

1. cook onion in butter til soft , not brown
2. combine with all else , and heat
3. serve
demonstrations.review: Have you ever observed 3 teenagers and a grown man trying to lick their bowl? This is wonderful: great flavor, texture,simple to make!. I normally follow the recipe exactly however, today I was trying empty the fridge and added 3/4 cup cooked floweerets from cauliflower, 1 1/2 ounce of cream cheese and 1/3 cup of sour cream at the end just melting the cheese and blending in the sour cream. WOW!! Thanks Ann for sharing this great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast chicken with yogurt sauce

chicken will never taste the same once you try this roast chicken prepared with yogurt and turmeric sauce.

1. wash and pat dry chicken
2. prick the skin with a fork
3. rub it with a mixture of pepper and ground ginger
4. with string , tie legs and tail of chicken
5. place chicken breast side-up on rack in open roasting pan
6. roast at 180c for 10 minutes
7. heat sauce in a pan over medium heat
8. brush skin with sauce
9. roast the chicken for about 1 1 / 2 hours , basting frequently with sauce
10. keep the sauce warm while basting
11. place the chicken on a heated platter , arrange rice or bread stuffing around it if you desire
12. mix some dripping from the roasting pan with yogurt sauce and pour some over the chicken
13. serve the remaining sauce separately
demonstrations.review:
Perfect dish !!! Simple,moist,tender and mildly aromatic. I found this wonderful chicken delicate in tast and attractive with its' light golden color derived from the turmeric. I followed the recipe exactly each of the three times I have made this; using chicken leg quarters. I used my gas grill each time placeing  the flame on low with the chicken in a roasting pan, uncovered.  

I served this with #48037; Spiced Califlower on one occassion and with #10524; Carrot Berfi the next two times.  Thank you for sharing this recipe  ! I love it !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drago s brunswick stew

this dish might take awhile but it is worth it.

1. place chicken and 1 1 / 2 tsp salt in large dutch oven
2. add water to cover
3. bring to a boil
4. cover then reduce heat and simmer 2 to 21 / 2 hours or until done
5. drain and reserve broth
6. remove and discard skin from the ckicken
7. next bone and shred the chicken
8. set aside
9. skim the fat from the broth and return it to the dutch oven
10. bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer until the broth is reduced to 2 cups
11. add potatoes and simmer 10 minutes
12. add tomatoes , lima beans and onion and simmer 20 more minutes
13. stir in chicken , corn and remaining ingredients and simmer 10 more minutes or until vegetables are tender
demonstrations.review:
If you are looking for a wonderful Brunswick Stew then you have found the best recipe right here. I have made this as printed several times now and received wonderful compliments from family and friends. A side salad, crusty bread or corn bread and you have a hearty winter meal.
The left overs the next day are even better . I serve peach cobbler as dessert which is a perfect compliment. As mentioned in another review, this can be put in the freezer with ni problems. Make , eat, enjoy... !!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken papadoris

this is an excellent light curry dish to be served over cooked rice. i developed this recipe in palm springs, ca and it has been a big success with everyone who has tried it. the recipe name is very original as i named it after some friends of mine. her name was "doris" and i called her husband "papa". therefore, "chicken papadoris". you can also use chicken drumettes, wings or thighs.

1. remove all fat from chicken breasts and discard
2. cut chicken breasts into bite size pieces
3. in a large frying pan , melt butter , add onion and garlic and saute' until onions are translucent
4. add chicken pieces , cover and fry until cooked through and have turned white , about 6 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. stir in pine nuts , soy sauce , paprika , coconut milk , cumin and curry powder
6. cover and continue cooking for about 5 more minutes , stirring occasionally
7. in a cup , mix together tapioca starch and water until dissolved
8. near the end of cooking the chicken and while sauce is bubbling , add cornstarch mixture , small amounts at a time , stirring constantly until the sauce thickens
9. use only enough tapioca mixture so that the sauce has the consistency of gravy
10. adjust seasonings to taste
demonstrations.review:
An excellent curry dish! India cusine is a favorite of mine and this was supurb.I made this tonight for my son who is visiting and he gives it two thumbs up also. 
 I only use Basmati rice which is perfect with this dish as it is a firmer rice. I made exactly as posted with excellent results. As I only use Penzy's spices I normaly use half the amount in a recipe as their spices are some stronger than those purchased at the grocery. In this I used exact amounts which was perfect. I suggest using the roasted pine nuts as they add such as wonderful flavor. I purchase pine nuts at an Italian Market where they are less expensive and I can chose smaller amounts. 
 Having several more chicken breasts I made a second batch after supper tonight. To this batch I added 1/4 teaspoon Garam Masala which gave a slighty more intense India flavor however, the recipe is perfect as is. 
 Thanks for another great recipe Uncle Bill. Your becoming a household name here. 

Samijo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best banana bread

this is one of the recipes i am known for. super moist and super yummy. i have tried many over the years and always come back to this. i often give it as a gift around the holidays. just may be the last banana bread recipe you ever try! can also make 3 mini-loaves

1. cream butter and sugar
2. mash bananas and add by hand to creamed mixture
3. by hand add eggs , vanilla , baking soda , flour and salt
4. gently stir in buttermilk and chocolate chips
5. pour into a greased loaf pan
6. bake at 350f for 1 1 / 4 hour or until it tests done with a toothpick
7. i find that coarsely mashing bananas is best and make sure they are over ripe for best flavor
8. i also find that doing the majority of the mixing by hand makes for better texture in the end
9. even though the recipe says it makes 1 loaf , i usually use 2 loaf pans or 3 mini loaf pans because it seems to yield a moister bread
10. just adjust baking time down
11. if you do not have buttermilk you can put 1 teaspoons vinegar into a 1 / 2 cup measuring cup and fill to top with milk
12. let rest 5 minutes before adding to recipe
13. this freezes well
demonstrations.review: Another 5 stars for this delicious moist banana bread. I cut the sugar back to 1 cup per some suggestions and used chopped pecans as that's what my Grandmother always used and I was in need of some nastalgia. This made one nice loaf in my Pampered Chef clay bread pan. I set the heat back to 325 and checked the bread more often since this pan seems to bake faster. It took about 50 minutes to bake. I suspect I'll be hiding bananas now just to have over ripe ones to make this wonderful bread often. Thanks for sharing Tracy and thanks to all the others that sent comments.

target.recipe_text:
2 minute microwave fudge

all i have to say, is that i'm obsessed with this recipe... i've never tasted better fudge! it's so good... although it's very sweet and very rich! prep time includes chill time.

1. sift powdered sugar , cocoa , and salt into a 1 quart microwave safe bowl
2. stir in milk and vanilla
3. mix well
4. place butter on top
5. microwave on high , 2 minutes
6. beat with wooden spoon until smooth
7. stir in nuts
8. spread in 8 x 8 x 2 inch baking pan
9. chill about 1 hour or until firm
10. cut into 36 pieces
target.review: Late one evening I developed such a craving for chocolate I could barely think straight.  I remembered saving this recipe and literally ran downstairs to make it.  Licking the bowl satisfied my craving a bit and I tossed it in the freezer to harden.  I delayed going to bed b/c I had to try the finished product.  It was fabulous.  My boyfriend ended up eating almost the entire pan the next day and was asking for more.  Thanks for a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheat n  eat vietnamese chicken soup

sometimes you just don't have all day to make vietnamese soup! you can have this made and in your hands in 15 minutes!

1. soak noodles in very hot tap water
2. while noodles are soaking , cut chicken into thin julienne strips
3. heat oil in deep skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. garlic , ginger , and pepper flakes
6. cook , stirring for 1 minute
7. then add broth and fish sauce and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat to medium and simmer until chicken is done , about 8 minutes
9. drain noodles and cut into short pieces , about 1-1 1 / 2 inches long
10. arrange noodles in bottom of bowls
11. ladle soup over the top and sprinkle with cilantro , onion , and basil
12. serve with"tuong ot sriracha" , or chile paste , if desired
demonstrations.review: I have a pretty awful cold and I automatically thought of this recipe I had been meaning to make.  I used leftover chicken kabobs so it was even quicker to make.  Unfortunately, I did not have any fresh basil on hand, but I loved the cilantro garnish.  I wasn't in the mood for noodles, so I tossed in some shredded cabbage for more substance.  I can't wait for leftovers tomorrow!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared salmon with balsamic glaze

i saw this on sara's secrets and couldn't wait to try it! the sauce brings out the sweetness in the fish. enjoy!

1. stir together balsamic vinegar , water , lemon juice , and brown sugar in a small bowl
2. pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium high heat , not smoking
4. increase heat to high , add salmon skin side up , and sear until well browned , about 4 minutes
5. turn fish over and sear until just cooked through , 3 to 4 minutes more
6. transfer salmon to plates and carefully add vinegar mixture to skillet
7. simmer , stirring , until thickened and reduced to about 1 / 3 cup , about 2 minutes
8. spoon glaze over salmon
9. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Awesome, Sharon! I loved how quick this was to throw together and with all ingredients I'd have on hand. I tossed in a few mushrooms along with it and bam! Dinner's done! Thanks!  Update:  I've made this a few times now and have found that it's important to use a large shallow skillet if possible.  I tried jamming everything in a smaller pan and that fabulous glaze just refused to set up.  Serves me right for trying to get out of washing a bigger dish...  ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portobello mushrooms with thyme and parmesan cheese

this is a scandinavian recipe adapted from tina nordstrom's recipes in new scandinavian cooking. i love mushrooms and this is so good with the thyme and parmesan! great as a side dish and it's also good on toast or with pasta. enjoy!

1. place the oil and butter in a large skillet
2. saute the mushrooms , garlic and thyme for 3-5 minutes
3. season with salt and pepper
4. mix in the onion and saute for 3-4 more minutes , or till done to your liking
5. pour over the balsamic vinegar and remove from heat
6. sprinkle with the dill and parmesan cheese
7. add some freshly ground black pepper to taste
8. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I was short on time and needed a quick recipe.  This was excellent.  Be sure to follow the recipe and serve two mushrooms each as they shrink a lot more (it seemed) than when you cook them whole.  Normally we have one each as a main course but this definitely would need to be served as a side or with the accompanying carbs to make you feel like you had a meal.  We served ours with eggs.  Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: I took this pie to Thanksgiving with about forty people and in the middle of dessert someone yelled, "Hey!  Who made the caramel apple pie?"  I claimed it from across the room and he yelled back a request for the following year, with others chiming in with the same.  It was my first Thanksgiving with the boyfriend's family, so thank you for making me look good!  This is definitely an easy, impressive dish not to be passed over!  Gold star recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super healthy hummus

taken off a website, don't have the reference. an excellent hummus, the only one i make anymore. you really need a blender or food processor to get the consistency right. 1/4 cup = 1 point ww.

1. combine everything in blender or food processor and process until smooth
2. the blender gives the best result
3. if you need more liquid to make a nice consistency , add a bit more yogurt
4. chill
5. serve with pitas or as a veggie dip
demonstrations.review: We've made this three times in three days.  Speaks for itself, doesn't it?  :)  We had impulse dinner guests both Friday and Saturday and this was the perfect whip it together appetizer.  Thanks for saving me!

target.recipe_text:
a  pork marinade

i have been searching for a pork marinade that is not too lemony for my husband but not too sweet for myself. i finally found it...enjoy!

1. trim all visible fat off of pork
2. combine all ingredients except the pork in a mixing bowl
3. stir until honey / maple syrup is dissolved
4. put pork into a gallon plastic freezer bag and pour marinade over top
5. seal the bag and shake to make sure you coat your pork pieces
6. marinate in the fridge for at least 4 hours turning once an hour -- best if left overnight
target.review: Absolutely wonderful!  I used this at Christmas, and forgot to write a review...  using it again tonight.  I don't think there is a better marinade out there, honestly.  THANKS soooo much for the recipe.  It RAWKS!  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun chicken alfredo pasta

this dish can be made two ways: 1. the easy weeknight throw together way, 2. the good for company restaurant style way. i thought this way extremely spicy, my husband thought it was perfect so, spice to taste. serve with salad and bread! i made the cream cheese a range, i prefer it with less but have added more to cut the spiciness when making it for both of us, so taste and add as desired.

1. prepare noodles according to package directions and set aside
2. trim chicken breasts of fat and cut into bite sized pieces
3. saute chicken in butter
4. if you are doing restaurant style us only 1-2 tbsp of butter , reserving the rest
5. add cajun seasoning to chicken while it sautes , adding the ingredients to taste , you can always add more later
6. for family style , once chicken is cooked , stir in half and half or cream and cheeses
7. bring to a low boil and stir until melted and creamy
8. toss with pasta and serve !
9. for restaurant style , melt remaining butter in a medium sauce pan , add half and half or cream
10. melt in cheeses , stir to combine
11. toss with pasta and place chicken on top
demonstrations.review: Sooooooo very, very GOOD!  We had this over cheese ravioli, only used 4 oz of cream cheese.  We thought the spice was wonderful, as we love spicy food.  I actually forgot the parmesan, and honestly we didn't miss it.  I added mushrooms, red onion, and omitted the onion powder (personal preference).  Thanks for posting.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pot roast cooked in beer so tender it falls apart

it's fall apart good. serve with my roasted garlic mashed potatoes and cauliflower  recipe #46925 or mashed potatoes with roasted garlic and caramelized onions recipe #93000 





1. in a dry cast iron pot brown fat side down , then continue to brown all sides
2. your kitchen will be smokey !
3. season with salt and pepper
4. add 1 can beer
5. and pour the other can for yourself !
6. add rest of ingredients except butter and flour
7. put pot with cover into 325 degree oven for 3 hours
8. melt butter in micro and flour
9. remove roast and vegies from pan
10. add some drippings to butter then add back to pan
11. cook 5 minutes till nice and thick
12. add veggies back to sauce
13. plate the sliced roast {if it`s not already falling apart} top with the veggies and serve with your or my favorite side !
demonstrations.review: Absolutely AMAZING! I was a little concerned about the beer taking over the taste, but it did not.  It was very simple to make, very tender, and I have already forwarded the recipe to others!  Thanks so much for posting, it's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kona inn banana bread

i got this from a garden center favorites cookbook quite a few years ago.  it is the best banana bread i have made--and i have tried a bazillion recipes. i keep coming back to this one!!  i hope you like it.

1. cream together butter and sugar
2. add bananas and eggs
3. sift dry ingredients
4. blend wet and dry mixtures but don't overmix
5. bake in a loaf pan at 350 for 45 minutes
6. makes 1 20-ounce loaf
demonstrations.review: I've never made banana bread before, even though I really love it.  I tried it tonight for the first time, using mini-loaves.  They turned out PERFECT!  I'm giving them to my family and friends as gifts for Christmas (although I definitely made extra for home).  Thank you for posting.  =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple cream cheese sausage puffs

i found this recipe on the back of a tube of jimmy dean maple pork sausage.

1. brown sausage in a dry skillet over a low to medium flame
2. when the sausage starts to brown , add chopped apple
3. stir fry until sausage is thoroughly browned
4. season with salt and black pepper to taste
5. drain excess juice , transfer sausage filling to a bowl
6. add cream cheese to the warm filling and mix well
7. separate crescent rolls into triangles and place one tablespoon of filling on wide edge of triangle
8. roll wide edge of dough towards the point of the triangle , enveloping the filling
9. fold edges of dough over so that filling is completely enclosed with dough
10. bake at 375 degrees for 11-13 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I was given some Maple Sausage and this was perfect for breakfast.  I used flaky butter biscuits, instead of crescent rolls (didn't have any), they worked just as well IMO.  I also added cinnamon and brown sugar, personal preference.  My husband absolutely loved it!  I would have preferred more apples and less sausage, but that's just me.  Real easy to make, and it makes A LOT - I had quite a bit of leftover filling!  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
individual cream cheese danish

small danishes that make a great addition to a brunch buffet. you can also make fruit and cream cheese danishes by adding a spoonful of your favorite pie filling prior to baking. there are never any leftovers when i make these.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. slice crescent roll dough into 1 / 4 inch slices
3. place slices of dough on cookie sheet and make slight indention in the middle
4. in a large bowl , mix together cream cheese , white sugar , lemon juice , vanilla extract and sour cream
5. add a tablespoon of filling to each roll
6. bake in preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes
7. in a small bowl , stir together confectioners' sugar , milk and butter
8. after danish has cooled , drizzle with icing
demonstrations.review: sooooooo GOOD!   I used Grands flaky butter biscuits instead of crescent rolls.  I made some plain, some with orange marmalade, and some with melted chocolate drizzled over the top.  They were all absolutely delicious.  Everyone who tried them RAVED!  Thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
potluck macaroni salad

traditionally a side dish, the addition of baked beans to macaroni salad turns this wonderful salad into a complete main course. this recipe makes enough to serve a crowd, so take it to your next picnic supper, you'll be glad you did. recipe came from mealtime.org.

1. cook macaroni according to package directions
2. drain well
3. in large bowl , combine macaroni and beans
4. toss to combine
5. add celery , onion , bell pepper , vinaigrette , and basil
6. toss lightly
7. let stand at least 15 minutes before serving to allow flavors to blend , or cover and refrigerate up to 4 hours
8. garnish with the basil or parsley before serving
9. prepare as directed , using 4 ounces elbow macaroni , 1 can undrained baked beans , 1 cup each of the vegetables , 1 / 3 cup prepared herb vinaigrette and 1 / 4 cup chopped herbs
target.review: It's the weirdest thing...I LOVE this recipe and have made it several times for different events.  The problem is that although some people liked it, most of them didn't.  I did encourage people to try it.  Maybe it's the visual of beans mixed in pasta salad...I just don't know.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty shrimp in butter beer sauce

herby, spicy shrimp with a kick, in a buttery-beer "sauce". fast, easy and delicious, serve as an appetizer, or a dinner over rice or with lots of crusty french bread to soak up all the tasty, herbalicious sauce!

1. saute garlic and herbs in butter until garlic is slightly browned
2. add shrimp , stirring constantly , until shrimp are pink and done
3. pour in beer , simmer 1 minute more , and serve !
demonstrations.review: The neighbors gathered for "Shrimp Night" and I brought this.  I cooked it at home and brought it in the crockpot.  It never made it to dinnertime because everyone dug into it early.  I followed the recipe except for decreasing the cayenne and red pepper for personal tastes.  Good one, EdsGirlAngie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german potato pancakes

this recipe was passed down from my grandfather to my mother (and i assume someone passed it on to him.) while the grating and frying can be somewhat labor intensive, the results are great. just make sure to get the oil to the right temperature. my mom can do this like a pro, but i have to admit i am still learning. ;) she also used to occasionally experiment with various additive

1. grate the potatoes
2. i do two on the very fine side and one on the coarser side for the best texture
3. they may turn brown
4. squeeze out the excess liquid
5. grate the onion on the finest side and add
6. stir in the rest of the ingredients
7. heat a generous amount of oil in a heavy skillet
8. drop the mixture in by spoonfuls
9. the tops will get slightly drier and you will see browned edges
10. when this happens flip the pancakes carefully
11. serve on their own , or with applesauce or sour cream
demonstrations.review: My husband had been wanting me to make these.  I used my Salad Shooter.  The first time I grated once.  The next time I grated part of the potatoes twice to make them finer.  I liked results when grating once better.  So far mine aren't real pretty, but they sure taste good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red  white  and  blue jello flag

we had a block party for memorial day and i brought this jello dessert.  you can buy the actual mold from www.kraftfoods.com/jello/ for $3.50.  i got the jello mold free for buying jello at my local grocery store, which included several recipes. if you don't have the mold, use a pan that has a 10 cup capacity.
follow directions as closely as you can as the consistency of the jello is very important.
please note that you can use (2) 4 serving size packages or (1) 8 serving size packages of jello for the red and blue layers.
this will be a hit at your next holiday gathering!

1. add 1-1 / 2 cups boiling water to dry berry blue gelatin mix in medium bowl
2. stir at least 2 minutes until gelatin is dissolved
3. dissolve dry red gelatin mix in 1-1 / 2 cups boiling water in separate bowl
4. stir 1-1 / 2 cups ice cold water into dissolved gelatin in each bowl
5. spray 10-cup flag mold with cooking spray
6. place on baking sheet
7. pour red gelatin into mold
8. refrigerate 45 minutes until set but not firm
9. meanwhile , refrigerate berry blue gelatin in bowl for 45 minutes
10. meanwhile , stir remaining 1 cup boiling water into dry lemon gelatin mix in bowl at least 2 minutes until dissolved
11. refrigerate 25 minutes or until slightly thickened , stirring occasionally
12. stir in whipped topping with wire whisk
13. gently spread over red gelatin in mold
14. refrigerate 10 minutes or until set but not firm
15. gently spoon thickened berry blue gelatin over lemon gelatin mixture in mold
16. refrigerate 4 hours or overnight until firm
17. unmold
demonstrations.review: I have been making this recipe for years.  I also got the Jello mold as a free promo.  The recipe is delicious!  I tried using spray whipped topping one year and it melted fast.  I suggest you pipe on Cool Whip or another brand from a tub.  Try this if you want to impress your friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian sausage  tomato  and cream with bow ties

submitted for the 'zaar world tour 2005. ciao!

1. heat oil in heavy large skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and pepper flakes
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , olives , cream , salt and parsley
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling salted water until just tender but still firm to bite , stirring occasionally to prevent sticking
8. toss with mixture and sprinkle with parmesan
demonstrations.review: I didn't follow this recipe all the way, but it was a great one to use as a guide.  I could tell by looking at it we would like it.  My 10 yr. old was saying "Yum!"  all through dinner.  I used hot Italian sausage and no red pepper.  I also added shrimp which was an awesome addition.  Changes I made were using a whole med. onion, half n half, petite diced tomatoes, and added a can of mushrooms. I used cellentani pasta which made it fun.  Next time I will add capers and maybe chicken.  I am looking forward to using this again in the future.  It was quite delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best beer margarita

i make these all year around for my parties they are the best margarita,  don't worry you won't even taste the beer, you can double or triple this recipe if desired, if the mixture tastes too sweet you can add in a little more water, use the limeade can to measure out all ingredients

1. pour the limeade , tequila , seven-up , water and beer into a large glass pitcher
2. stir with a long-handled spoon until completely blended and the frozen limeade has completely melted
3. add in lots of ice
4. adjust with extra water if the mixture is too sweet
5. serve each glass with a lime wedge on the end
demonstrations.review: Made at the DH's request and it was a hit with all who tried it!  Smooth, no heartburn, and not too sweet.  I made it with 6 oz. each of 7Up and water.  Next time we'll try all 7Up.  We also flavored some with an orange liquor which made it tasty!  It was a wonderful match to the Cinco de Mayo taco bar party we had!

target.recipe_text:
southern mashed potatoes

everyone always tells me that they have never heard of miracle whip in mashed potatoes but i grew up on this recipe in south georgia. maybe it's a local thing; maybe it's just a family thing but everyone who tries them likes them. i have never measured the ingredients for these so you might want to start off with a little and adjust to your taste. and let me know what you think! p.s. these go great with my cheesy meatloaf also on this site.

1. peel and chop potatoes
2. boil in 4 quarts of water in till soft
3. drain and put in large mixer on low
4. add miracle whip , maargarine , and milk
5. mix until smooth
target.review: I've used this recipe for years...but with regular mayo and no butter.  I also hand mash instead of whip - I like it slightly chunkier.  I originally tried this because I ran out of butter one time and needed a creamy consistency.  It's been a family favorite since.  I think the vinegar in the mayo gives it a bit of a punch although it's not noticeable.  Thanks for sharing your version!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potatoes with afritude

walt disney world (boma, animal kingdom lodge)

1. wash potatoes well , and cut into wedges
2. in a large bowl mix the spices and olive oil
3. add the raw potatoes
4. coat the potatoes with the spice mixture
5. place the potatoes on a baking sheet , place in a preheated 350f oven and bake for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a wonderful change from the norm!  I used only 4 med. red potatoes and reduced all else (except olive oil) to 1/3 of what recipe indicates.  Cooked 30 minutes as stated, then "crisped" them a bit under the broiler for a few minutes.  Especially excellent with a topping of butter mixed with a little mustard & a few drops of worchestershire sauce!  Heavenly.  Will definite make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy pasta with bacon

i have to admit whenever i first saw this i was skeptical...but after one bite, i was hooked. it has a flavor that i didn't expect, especially after hearing the ingredients. i don't know where it originally came from as i got this recipe from my mom. unsure of serving amount...makes quite a bit though.

1. cook pasta and drain
2. fry bacon , drain off grease , and crumble into small pieces
3. saute mushrooms , garlic , and green onions in bacon grease
4. add pasta , parmesan , bacon pieces , whipping cream , and black pepper to sauted mushroom mixture
5. simmer until slightly thickened
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Great, easy dish for a quickie dinner after working in the yard all day.  I tweaked it by using lots more mushrooms (like a previous rater), and used a can of low-fat 2% evaporated milk instead of cream.  Added a handful of leftover peas, and used mostly Asiago cheese along with Parmesan.  Yummy!  Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey pot pie with biscuits

i have a collection of cook books and usually look up a few of the same recipes and combine the ingredients i like from each recipe so that it makes it my own. this one called for chicken but works for either or just as well. so hope you enjoy experiementing with it as i did.

1. grease a 3 qt casserole dish
2. in lg
3. saucepan , combine carrots and broth
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and cover
6. simmer for 5 minutes or til crisp-tender
7. heat oven to 400f in small bowl , mix 1 1 / 2 cups milk& 1 / 4 cup flour
8. mix the milk mixture , sage , 1 t marg
9. and 1 / 2 t salt into carrot mixture
10. bring back to a boil , constantly stirring
11. boil for approximately 1 min , add chicken and corn
12. pour into greased casserole dish
13. in medium bowl , mix together the 1 cup flour , onions , baking powder , and 1 / 4 t salt
14. once mixed well stir in the 1 / 2 c milk and 1 t melted or soft marg
15. until soft dough forms
16. drop dough by spoonful evenly onto chicken mixture
17. bake at 400f for 20-25 minutes or till top is golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yummm...I'm sitting here eating leftovers right now!  To the chicken broth, in addition to carrots, I added some chopped celery, a handful of frozen peas, and a handful of leftover green beans as well as a few chopped onions (left out the corn).  I also doubled both parts of the recipe. This will definitely be a keeper here!  Thanks, Vet!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey pot pie

this was a recipe i was a little nervous trying as i am not a pie maker...what a pleasant surprise- it turned out delicious and was a good stick to your ribs meal on a cool fall day. update- i tried it this year with the new pillsbury refrigerated pie crusts, it turned out wonderful, see the photo i took!

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. melt 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium heat
3. add the onion , celery , carrots , parsley , oregano , and salt and pepper
4. cook and stir until the vegetables are soft
5. stir in the broth
6. bring mixture to a boil
7. stir in the potatoes , and cook until tender but still firm
8. in a medium saucepan , melt the remaining 2 tablespoons butter
9. stir in the turkey and flour
10. add the milk , and heat through
11. stir the turkey mixture into the vegetable mixture , and cook until thickened
12. cool slightly , then pour mixture into 1 unbaked pie shell
13. cover with remaining crust
14. flute edges , and make 4 slits in the top crust to let out steam
15. place on a cookie sheet
16. bake in the preheated oven for 15 minutes
17. reduce oven temperature to 350f , and continue baking for 20 minutes , or until crust is golden brown
demonstrations.review: We loved this (well, except for my DH who wouldn't even try it).  Made it pretty much as shown except I had no parsley so added dried basil, Italian seasoning, and garlic powder.  I think it would've been a bit bland for our tastes if I hadn't added these extra spices.  Oh, and I had no carrots so used frozen peas and corn. Used my own pie crust recipe. I'm thinking of making some small pot pies with this recipe for my college daughter who is a great fan of them.  She can freeze and then pull them out whenever she needs a quick and tasty meal.  Thanks, Debbie, for a great dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast cereal muffins

wonderful breakfast, brunch, or mid-morning snack. this recipe is very versatile. any kind of cereal works, and you can substitute dried fruit and/or nuts for part of the cereal. if using a cooked, hot cereal like oatmeal, combine with wet ingredients instead of dry.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease 12 medium sized muffin cups
3. in a mixing bowl , beat egg and whisk together with oil , milk and honey
4. in a large bowl combine the dry ingredients
5. mixed well
6. pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir just until flour is moist
7. fill muffin cups 2 / 3 full with the batter , and bake for 20-25 minutes
8. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I would've given this a 5=star because of the flavor alone, but when I removed them out of the pan as indicated, they fell apart into a crumbly mess.  Otherwise, they tasted GREAT! I used Post's Selects Great Grains, raisins/dates/pecan cereal.

target.recipe_text:
streamlined chimichangas

this is a great tasting recipe and so easy that even my daughter doesn't complain when i ask her to make it.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. brown meat with onion and garlic
3. drain , but do not rinse
4. stir in picante sauce , cumin , oregano and salt
5. simmer 5 minutes or until most of the liquid has evaporated
6. brush one side of the tortillas with butter
7. on unbuttered side spoon heaping 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture into center
8. fold 2 sides over filling , fold ends down
9. place seam side down in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish
10. bake for 13 minutes or until golden brown
11. to serve , top with sour cream , guacamole and additional picante sauce
target.review: Yum!! I made a double batch, with 10 chimichangas per batch. We ate one pan, and I'll freeze the other for another day. I used canola oil instead of butter, which worked very well. I served them with shredded lettuce, shredded cheese, sour cream, guacamole, and salsa. My DH and DS loved them (and so did I)! DH ate half the pan himself, and was longing for more. My picky 2-year old son made all kinds of happy yummy noises when I served it up, too - always a good sign. UPDATE: These froze and reheated well, although I cooked them a little too long the first cooking. Next time I'll cook them for a shorter time prior to freezing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef and horseradish bonbons

very simple, yet very delicious. a must for any party! a blink and they are gone dish!

1. cut each slice of beef into 8 strips
2. combine butter , herbs and horseradish
3. brush a sheet of phyllo with the butter mixture , top with another sheet of phyllo and brush with more butter mixture
4. cut the pastry into quarters and each quarter into quarters again
5. top each quarter with a strip of beef
6. roll up from narrow sides and pinch ends to form bonbon shapes
7. repeat with the remaining pastry , butter and beef
8. place bonbons on a lightly greased tray and bake in a hot oven for about 8 minutes until crisp and brown
9. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Delicious! A bit fiddly to make, especially since they are not really something you can make ahead. But very good. I used deli roast beef, stacked the slices, cut into strips and then into small squares. I lay these little stacks onto the prepared filo squares, folded over once, then tucked the sides around and continue to roll up--kind of like rolling up a chimichanga or something. These took a bit longer than 8 minutes at 350 to bake to a golden brown, and they ended up a bit dark on the bottom, but not so dark that it affected the flavor. Everyone liked these "beefy bites" and they held their own--even against a 1-kg wheel of warm, melty brie! Thanks so much for posting, Noo! Made for Photo Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef with soy sauce and ginger

from jamie oliver....i love this guy!

1. on a very hot griddle pan , cook your seasoned piece of sirloin steak until medium or to your liking
2. place in a plate and allow to rest for 2 minutes
3. now cook your greens in salted boiling water until tender
4. while hot , douse with a good couple of tablespoons of soy sauce , and sprinkle with the garlic , ginger , chilli , lime juice and olive oil
5. when the greens are cooked , simply divide onto two plates , thinly slice up the sirloin steaks , place on top of the greens and drizzle with any of the infused sauce left on the resting plate
demonstrations.review: Excellent! The flavors went very well together. I used reduced-sodium soy sauce and omitted the salt, and it was still plenty salty enough for our tastes.  I did make one mistake--I bought baby bok choy out of habit, and so there wasn't nearly enough greens--but what greens we had were wonderful with the dressing and beef. I made this with Recipe #342901 served beforehand, Recipe #340293 on the side, and Recipe #113064 along with dinner. It was a fabulous entree for a fabulous pan-Asian meal. Thanks so much for posting, Lorrie! Made for Holiday Tag Game.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty sesame chicken

the measurements for sugar and sesame oil are the way i found the recipe--they can be adjusted according to your taste.  yummy served with fried rice.

1. mix marinade ingredients in medium bowl
2. add chicken cubes and marinate at least 20 minutes
3. meanwhile , mix sauce ingredients in medium saucepan
4. bring to a boil , stirring continuously
5. reduce heat to low while cooking chicken
6. heat peanut oil for frying
7. add marinated chicken pieces , a few at a time , to the hot oil
8. cook until golden brown
9. drain on paper towels
10. bring sauce back to boil
11. place chicken in serving bowl and pour sauce over
12. sprinkle with sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: This definitely has potential, but it was way to sweet for our taste. It was different from the sesame chicken at our favorite Chinese restaurant. It tasted like a cross between their sesame chicken and sweet and sour chicken. Instead of the hot sauce and the garlic, I used a couple of squirts of sriracha chili-garlic sauce. It was as hot as my 3-year old will eat food--he ate with a fork in one hand and a glass of milk in the other! I definitely like it, and will try reducing the sugar to see if that helps. Thanks for posting, CookinMamaof2!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
limeade  nam manao

in very hot weather, this cold, refreshing drink is a welcome relief. it is popular in thailand, and is a perfect accompaniment to spicy thai foods such as curry.

1. with your hands or a reamer , squeeze the juice from limes to make 1 cup of lime juice
2. set juice and lime rings aside
3. pour water into a 2-quart microwavable glass measuring cup
4. microwave , uncovered for 6 to 8 minutes on high until almost boiling
5. little bubbles will form on the water surface
6. add sugar and salt and stir until dissolved
7. add lime rinds and let the mixture stand for 10 minutes until cool
8. squeeze the remaining juice from the rinds into the limeade through a sieve into a pitcher
9. add reserved lime juice and stir well
10. refrigerate until ready to serve
11. to serve , fill a tall glass with ice and add limeade
12. garnish with a slice of lime and a sprig of mint
demonstrations.review: Oh my! I love Thai limeade, with its sweet-sour-salty flavors, but this is by far the best I've ever had! It was very easy to make, too. The only change I made was to use 6 limes instead of 7 (miscounted at the store) and made up 1 cup of juice with bottled. The flavor didn't seem to suffer, although I'll know for sure next time! I also skipped the garnishes for expedience's sake. Thanks so much for sharing, morgainegeiser! Made for Everyday is a Holiday tag game.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
piemontese capsicums

a flavoursome and visually stunning recipe which will serve you equally well as an appetiser, as a light lunch or as part of a nearly vegetarian meal from australian chef iain hewitson.  this is a recipe which allows the key ingredients to be the stars: make sure you use the best quality ingredients you can find.

1. preheat oven to 190c
2. cut the capsicums in half lengthways and remove the ribs and seeds
3. place them on an oven tray , with the cut side up
4. then place the tomatoes , garlic , thyme , anchovies and pepper in the centre of each half , capsicum and spray generously with oil and cook in the oven for about 40 minutes or until they are tender
5. when they are almost ready , place a slice or two of goats cheese on top of each capsicum and briefly return the capsicum to oven
demonstrations.review: Wow! I was so impressed with how easy and how supercalifragilisticexpiali-delicious this recipe was! I halved the recipe, using 1 each yellow and orange bell peppers (smallish ones). I used heirloom cherry tomatoes instead of large tomatoes, halving or quartering them into small bite-size pieces. I used chevre. DH also loved this recipe, and even DS liked the bite I gave him. The only (really minor) changes I can think I might like to try would be to increase the anchovies (we love them so) and possibly decrease the chevre to maybe 1/2 the amount called for. However, I was very impressed with these and can't wait to make them again. They were just perfect with grilled steaks! Thank you so much for posting, bluemoon! Made for Newest Zaar Tag game.

target.recipe_text:
basic machine french bread

this is my winner with tammiev and our friends. this recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. i think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.

1. add to the bread pan in the order yours needs
2. for mine it is water first
3. then i add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top
4. this will run well on the normal , rapid , and delay start cycles
target.review: I cooked mine in the machine and I was sure it wasn't done and I'd ruined it because it didn't look cooked.  I think I used a light setting.  Anyway, I dumped it out and it was crispy all around.  I let it cool a little then sliced it and it was perfect.  This morning I had some toast for breakfast and it was WONDERFUL.  I couldn't believe the texture and flavor.  You will love this.  I'm sure baking it in the oven vastly improves it's appearance but as lazy as I am, I will just slice it before I let anyone see it. lol

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mile high crispy bacon and onion bread   bread machine

i could not believe how high this bread was - and it was an experiment too! wonderful flavours of bacon & onion with just a smidge of mixed herbs. just crisp up your bacon & fry your onion, and then it all goes in the breadmaker for a delectable bread! just think - you can have an english breakfast just by adding some scrambled eggs on top of a slice of this bread!

1. fry your bacon in it's own fat in a frying pan and when nearly crispy & cooked , add the diced onion
2. stir around thoroughly & continue to cook until the bacon is crispy & the onion soft
3. drain well & allow to cool slightly
4. put the ingredients into your bread machine in the order that is written in your manual
5. mine is wet first & dry last
6. make sure that the yeast does not come into contact with the liquid
7. select the 1 kilo or 2lb setting on white rapid or white normal
8. choose your crust finish
9. do not add the bacon and onion to the extras tray - there is too much !
10. add the bacon & onion when extras are added in the cycle - towards the end of the kneading time
11. when cooked , take out straight away with oven gloves & turn out to cool on a wire cooling rack
12. if the paddle stays in the bread - remember to take it out before cutting the bread
13. serve with butter , eggs , cheese or by its self with salad
14. this is also wonderful toasted too !
demonstrations.review:
Oh my, Oh my, O my.
This is sooo good.
As per others, I used bacon pieces from Costco (really good) I warmed them in a frying pan and added the red onion just as directed.  Used 2 1/2 teas yeast.
I used Herbs of Provence and white bread flour.  I will use less salt, it could be that the bacon was too salty.  I did have a problem with the amount of flour.  I used 3 1/2 c of flour but it was too wet so added extra.  I just kept adding until it started to combine, probably about  an additional 1/4 c..  I also used regular milk instead of water and dry milk.  DELICIOUS

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef and cabbage in guinness

the irish butcher at my market gave me a new (to me anyway) recipe for corned beef & cabbage; he told me to cook it in guinness draught. (guinness stout will make the dish bitter).  since everyone raved about it, i thought i'd share the recipe he gave me. 

note: some reviewers have mentioned that the broth/sauce is very salty. it is important to rinse your corned beef in cold water before cooking it to remove some of the excess salt from the corning process. (i usually soak mine in cold water for a bit depending on the brand - some are much saltier than others).  --- i have tried 5 times today to change the wording of the last ingredient on the list from "1-2lbs carrot, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces" to "1 - 2 pounds of carrots, peeled and cut into 3-inch pieces". every time the change "goes through," it does not reflect the new wording. grrrrrrr!

1. rinse corned beef under cold water , and pat dry
2. in a dutch oven , or other large pot with a cover , brown corned beef well on all sides over high heat
3. pour guinness over the meat , and add enough water to just cover the brisket
4. add the onion , garlic , bay leaf , cinnamon , cloves , allspice and pepper to the pot
5. bring pot to a boil and skim off any foam
6. reduce heat to a simmer
7. cover pot and simmer for 3 hours
8. add carrots , then potatoes and then the cabbage wedges to the pot
9. cover pot , and continue cooking until meat and vegetables are tender
10. remove meat and vegetables to warm serving platter / dishes , leaving the cooking liquid / sauce in the pot
11. over high heat , bring the cooking liquid to a boil , and cook until the amount of liquid is reduced by half
12. slice the corned beef
13. serve with the vegetables and the sauce on the side
demonstrations.review:
This is a keeper. We loved it. After I finished cooking the brisket, I removed it and wrapped it in Saran (as one of the posters recommended) Then I put in the potatoes, parsnips and carrots. When they were done, I removed them to a bowl and put in 2 heads of cabbage. I love veggies so doubled them. They were so good cooked in the broth. I did rinse it (the brisket) yesterday and put it in a Ziplok with water and put it in the fridge overnight. So, I had no problem of it being too salty. But, this was wonderful
I was at the store and they still had some corned beef left so I bought 2 to put in the freezer.  I was telling the butcher about it and printed out the recipe for him.  I will make this again and again.
MaryAnne

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesecake factory cheesecake

i feel sad for anyone who has never been to a cheesecake factory restaurant. this cheesecake is out of this world! i think you will find the nut crust quite unusual. sometimes i double the crust portion of the recipe just so i can have a thicker crust.

1. crust: mix all nuts and vanilla wafer crumbs with melted butter and press into a 9 inch buttered springform pan , trying to line the sides as much as possible about 1 1 / 2" up the sides of the pan , set aside
2. cheesecake: all above ingredients should be at room temperature before your begin
3. start by beating the cream cheese until light and fluffy
4. keep the mixer on a low setting throughout the beating and mixing process
5. add the sugar a little at a time and continue beating until creamy
6. add one egg at a time and beat after each egg
7. when eggs have been mixed into the cream cheese add flour , vanilla and lemon juice , mix well
8. add the sour cream last and beat well
9. pour cream cheese into the spring pan
10. place on the top rack in the middle of a 325 degrees preheated oven for one hour and 15 minutes
11. when time is up , turn oven off , prop open oven door and leave in oven for one hour
12. after one hour , remove from oven
13. let cool enough before the cheesecake is put into the refrigerator for 24 hours
14. a cheesecake should season
15. the wait is worth it
16. the flavor ripens and becomes enriched
demonstrations.review:
I didn't make this myself but sent it up to my SIL in NY who loves to bake.  So, I'll give you her report.

She said she'd give it more than 5 stars if she could.  My SIL lives on LI and has been to the Cheesecake Factory about 20 miles away.  BUT, the news is, when I was there last summer, they were building about 10 min away.
For those of you who have been to Cheesecake Factory, they are VERY expensive by the slice.  She has 6 children  ages 30 down to 16 and they loved it too.

I'm going to visit in May and will have to try this place.

But SIL said the whole family loved it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese enchilada chowder

from bhg. a slow-cooker chowder.

1. add the black beans , tomatoes , frozen corn , onion , bell pepper , and jalapeno pepper to a 4 quart slow-cooker
2. stir to combine
3. in a mixing bowl , add the enchilada sauce and cream soup
4. whisk together
5. gradually whisk in the milk until mixture is smooth
6. pour over vegetables in slow-cooker
7. cover and cook on low heat for 6-8 hours
8. add cheese and stir until melted
9. ladle hot soup into individual serving bowls and top with sour cream , guacamole and broken tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review:
Yummy!Yummy!Yummy!
I used 4cups Mex 4 cheese mix.
I chopped up extra peppers and they are in the freezer waiting for the next time.
Tortillas are a must.
I will definitely make this again.
Just love those Crock Pot recipes.
MaryAnne

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted cauliflower   16 roasted cloves of garlic

i find it totally amazing, that children and men all  love this recipe!  as for the female of our species we just love this for the flavor and the health benefits it brings our families.
roasted brings out a wonderful sweetness in this dish. the garlic is roasted to a tan color is creamy good. you can just pop them in your mouth. or you can spread them on your florets or fresh bread. just be sure to scoop up some of the rosemary, olive oil and black pepper that may have escaped to the bottom of the dish.
for halloween check out recipe #396674 version of my recipe.

1. mix oil , rosemary , salt , pepper and garlic together
2. toss in cauliflower and place in a large casserole dish in one layer
3. roast in a preheated oven at 450 degrees for 20 minutes
4. give a toss and bake for 10 more minutes
demonstrations.review:
YUMMY!
I used 3 heads of cauliflower (and I'm glad I did)  I didn't even peel the garlic, just smashed it a little with my knife and threw it in.  It just squeezed out in the mouth and seperated from the peel.  I often roast veggies this way but I will start thinking about not mixing them.  The cauliflower was delish on it's own.
MaryAnne

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin donut drops

this recipe comes from a dude ranch in northern michigan. the chef served these with hot chocolate after a hay ride. cook time is for the whole recipe.

1. heat oil for deep frying
2. in large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , cinnamon , ginger , and nutmeg
3. mix pumpkin , milk , oil , vanilla and egg
4. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
5. drop by teaspoonfuls into hot oil 5-6 at a time
6. fry 1-2 minutes , on each side , until golden brown
7. drain on paper towels
8. mix sugar and cinnamon
9. roll warm donuts in mixture
target.review: I made these for an evening treat while hubby and the kids played video games. It is a cooler night than is usual for August, it is getting dark earlier,  and with pumpkins and back to school just around the corner, these really hit the spot with our family. It was pretty quick to throw everything together, not much longer than making pancakes really. I have tons of butternut squash growing in my garden, and I am thinking that these might be great made with those. Will have to try it out. Thanks for the recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s 100  whole wheat air buns  rolls   for abm

i find most 100% whole wheat buns are very dense, and let's be frank, taste like the floor of a barn. this recipe is an adaptation of my "mom's air buns" #168628, and makes delicious, soft, healthy,and easy to make rolls. i think the unusual addition of vinegar is what makes the difference.
edited to include links to recipe#419620, and recipe#419622 for those of you who wish to make whole wheat loaves instead of buns...same great taste and texture!
for those unfamiliar with how to shape rolls, you may find it helpful to look at the following links for instructions: http://www.recipetips.com/kitchen-tips/t--1121/shaping-rolls.asp 
http://www.finecooking.com/articles/shaping-dinner-rolls.aspx

1. put water , butter , honey , salt and vinegar in the machine
2. in the bottom of a one cup measure , put 2 tablespoons of gluten , and then fill the cup with w
3. w
4. flour
5. put that , and another 3 1 / 2 cups of flour on top of the liquids
6. add yeast to surface , and programme for "dough" cycle
7. i make two 9 inch pans of rolls , each with 9 rolls per pan , and let rise until double
8. bake at 350f for approximately 20 minutes
9. rolls will be deeply golden and oh so yummy
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic. I'd given up on wheat bread because every attempt came out too heavy or dense, but these are amazing. I used the shortening and sugar instead of honey and butter, and I brushed a little melted butter over them before and after baking. I adapted the directions a bit to use my Kitchenaid. Using the mixer, and with my kitchen being so dry this winter, I did not use all the flour called for. I'd say I used about 1/2 cup less, and I let the dough hook knead for about 5 min. I also used about a 1/2 tbsp more gluten than stated. I did put them into 2 round cake pans, but I shaped them into 4 rolls for each pan for hamburger buns. This dough was very easy to work with, and I'd recommend this recipe to anyone who has been hesitant about the taste and texture of whole wheat. I'll be making some more tomorrow, I'm sure these won't last long at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hershey s no bake chocolate cheesecake

this quick and delicious cheesecake can be made in just a few minutes with just a few ingredients.

1. place chocolate chips in small microwave-safe bowl
2. microwave at high 1 minute
3. stir
4. if necessary , microwave at high an additional 15 seconds at a time , stirring after each heating , just until chips are melted when stirred
5. set aside to cool
6. beat cream cheese , sugar and butter in large bowl on medium speed of mixer until creamy
7. gradually add melted chips , beating on low speed until blended
8. fold in whipped topping until blended
9. spoon into crust
10. refrigerate until firm
11. garnish as desired
12. cover
13. refrigerate leftover cheesecake
demonstrations.review: This is my favorite chocolate cheesecake recipe. Very easy, very very rich. I was going to post when I saw it was already posted. I haven't made this for awhile, guess I know what's for Easter dessert this year!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry supreme

this is my dad's all time favorite dessert. i always make it for him for his birthday, but it still is oh-so-easy!

1. put oven on 350 degrees f
2. grease a 13x9 inch pan
3. put both cans of cherry pie filling in
4. top with cake mix
5. press butter throughout dish
6. sprinkle with nuts
7. bake for 1 hour , or until it looks done
8. serve warm , also is good with vanilla ice cream or whipped cream-- or both
demonstrations.review: I've made this several times now and it has turned out great every time. It is a real treat for my son who has an egg allergy. I've made the recipe according to the directions, and I've also tried it in an 8 inch square pan using only one can of cherry pie filling (all I had on hand at the time) and the whole box of cake mix. It gave it a thicker crust, but I actually liked it even better that way. And we ALWAYS go with the vanilla ice cream on top. YUM! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned beef stew for your crock pot

take the hassle out of dinner tonight by letting this scrumptious stew simmer in your crock pot all day. from bh&g.

1. place flour in a plastic bag
2. add meat cubes , a few at a time , shaking to coat
3. in a large saucepan or dutch oven brown meat , half at a time , in hot oil
4. drain off fat
5. in the bottom of a 3-1 / 2- or 4-quart electric crock pot layer onion , potatoes , green beans , corn , carrot , and meat
6. combine vegetable juice cocktail , bouillon granules , worcestershire sauce , marjoram , oregano , pepper , and bay leaf
7. pour over meat and vegetables in crock pot
8. cover and cook on low-heat setting for 10 to 12 hours or until meat and vegetables are tender
9. discard bay leaf
demonstrations.review: This was very very good. My kids hate veggies, so it didn't go over so big with them, but who cares. I am following Weight Watchers again, and it is 8 points per serving. If I had eliminated the oil, I think it would be much lower. Anyway, the recipe was great and it worked well for me. Thanks for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
demonstrations.review: We liked this alot. I could not find Pepperidge Farm Stuffing so I used Whole Wheat Stove top instead. I also used Campbell's Healthy requests for the soups to lighten the calories and salt a bit. This is a keeper, and a great recipe for my crock pot. Even though it is hot outside, we still like a hot dinner without heating up the whole house. Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
lunch in a loaf

my brother is in construction and needs an easy, high-protein, low mess lunch each day. i started making these for him in large batches and freezing them. he just takes one out of the freezer each morning and it's ready to eat by lunchtime!

1. combine 1 1 / 2 c flour , yeast , sugar , salt and basil
2. beat eggs and oil together
3. add egg mixture and hot milk to dry ingredients
4. mix and then add remaining flour , turning out onto a board to knead when consistency allows
5. return to bowl and set in warm place to rise
6. punch down dough , divide into four balls
7. roll each ball out into a 8" circle
8. add filling to one half , fold over , pinch edges shut like a pie crust
9. bake 20- 25 minutes at 350f
10. filling suggestions:
11. i use whatever is left in the fridge ! beans , stew , veggies , meat
12. here are a few "recipes"
13. cooked chicken breast , chopped in small pieces , canned corn , barbecue sauce
14. tuna salad , cheddar cheese
15. canned beef stew cheddar cheese
16. make up your own !
target.review: This was so fun to make!  The dough turned out beautifully.  I doubled the recipe & made the whole thing in my Kitchen Aid Mixer. I used part whole wheat, part white flour, rolled it out, & filled it with diced parmesan-pesto ham and shredded cheddar cheese.  I used my circle-sandwich cutter to seal the pocket.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: Oh, this is so good...and a very quick meal to make.  I was suprised how fast it was.  We omitted the red pepper for young taste buds and used half and half instead of whipping cream.  I also adjusted the recipe to fit for a larger family.  Worked great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon blueberry scones

my family loves these, they get eaten up right away. i like them with butter and honey right out of the oven. the recipe came from my grandmother.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. mix the first four ingredients in a bowl
3. cut in shortening
4. add lemon rind
5. add egg and milk and work in gently and quickly with hands
6. add blueberries and gently fold in
7. pat into round one inch thick on a baking sheet score into 8 pieces
8. brush with milk and sprinkle with sugar
9. bake 15 minutes or until slightly golden--do not over bake
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe.  Perfect for a late afternoon snack or weekend breakfast.  my 8 year old daughter has this recipe down pat & can make it in a flash.  We used frozen blueberries and a round stone pan for baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
big breakfast cookie

i put the dry ingredients into baggies and store several baggies in the cupboard.  all i have to do in the morning is add the wet ingredients and bake while i am doing my animal chores and i have an amazingly filling breakfast.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray cookie sheet with baking spray
3. mix all ingredients together
4. spoon 1 large mound on the baking sheet
5. bake 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This has become a staple recipe in our house.  The kids love it as much as I do.  I mix up a big ziplock bag and make as needed.  These also freeze well.  Sometimes I add just a couple of chocolate chips to make it a little more enticing for the kids.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I absolutely love this roast.  I seem to always be able to remember the few ingredients it uses & pick it up at the grocery store when I'm at a loss for dinner ideas.  I add some potatoes, onions, & carrots...fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
demonstrations.review: I love this recipe and find myself coming back to it time and time again.  It's so easy to remember the ingredients and just whip it up for dinner.  I use a cut up whole chicken (kept on hand in the freezer) and just sprinkle all purpose seasoning salt in with the cheese and bread crumbs.  Wonderful!  Served with brown rice or garlic bread & veggies. Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
ruggles reese s peanut butter cup cheesecake

this was a best selling dessert for ruggles grill, in houston.  it's a little different than some peanut butter cheesecakes--very good---with that winning combo, chocolate and peanut butter!  hope you enjoy.

1. please
2. to make the crust:
3. combine crushed oreo cookies and peanuts that have been ground in a food processor with the melted butter
4. pat the crust mixture onto bottom and sides of a 10-inch springform pan
5. to make the filling:
6. beat cream cheese in bowl of electric mixer until smooth
7. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
8. add sugar , peanut butter and cream
9. mix until smooth
10. stir in vanilla , then fold in peanut butter cup pieces with a rubber spatula
11. pour filling into prepared crust
12. place springform pan into a larger baking pan
13. pour hot water into the larger pan so that the water comes 1 inch up the sides of the springform pan
14. bake at 275f 1-1 / 2 hours , or until firm and lightly browned
15. for the topping:
16. combine the sour cream and sugar and spread on the cheesecake
17. return the cake to the oven for 5 minutes
18. remove from the oven and allow to cool on a wire rack for one hour
19. you may run a knife along the edge of the cake to loosen it from the pan somewhat
20. refrigerate for at least 4 hours
target.review: I made this recipe as something different.  However, I never got a chance to taste it.  From my experience it was a quick and fun cheesecake to make - it looked amazing.  I just got an email from the people I made it for saying that they finished every last bit, and requesting it for a baby shower - so it must have been pretty good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped jalapeno poppers

these bacon-wrapped jalapeno poppers are unbelievably good! you'll love them!

1. cut stems off of peppers and cut them all in half longways
2. remove seeds from peppers
3. fill each pepper with cream cheese and sprinkle cheddar cheese on top
4. wrap 1 / 2 slice of bacon around each pepper half
5. place on baking sheets and place in 450 degree oven for 10 to 15 minutes or until bacon is fully cooked
6. remove and serve when cooled
7. enjoy !
8. i always freeze them after they are made for about 20 minutes to a hour before putting them in the oven or on the grill
9. doing this will keep the cheese from melting out as much
demonstrations.review:
This tasted amazing!  My husband is a Texan up here in Canada, so any chance I have to add spice to his life, I take it.  He requested that i put some of the seeds from the jalapenos in the cheeses, which I did.  They certainly had a bite, to me, although he said they could have had more!  
Also, I found that 1/2 slice of bacon to wrap didn't turn out quite right (hubby says bacon is longer in the states) so next time I'll use a full slice to keep them nice and wrapped.

Again, AMAZING recipe, they sort of melt in your mouth and taste divine!  Thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wilton stabilized whipped cream

i have been using this method for 30 years, no more thin runny whipped cream and your whipping cream will hold up for days this,  is fabulous on cakes --- for 2 cups whipping cream use 2 tsp gelatin in 2 tbsp cold water.

1. in a small pan , combine gelatin and cold water
2. let stand until thick
3. place over low heat , stirring constantly , just until the gelatin dissolves
4. remove from heat
5. cool
6. whip the cream with the icing sugar , until slightly thick
7. while slowly beating , add the gelatin to whipping cream
8. whip at high speed until stiff
demonstrations.review: I've made this a few times now with excellent results every time.  It's easy, and tastes great!
