I decorated a cheesecake with it, and everything I piped on held up beautifully for days.  I love that this will last and hold itself for a few days without compromising taste and texture!  This will be my go-to whipped cream recipe!  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shake a pie crust

my mother always told me the less you handle dough, the better it will be. this is too simple! and it makes the flakiest crusts for pies.

1. put flour , sugar , salt and crisco shortening in a plastic bowl with a lid
2. seal and wink
3. shake until it sounds like sand
4. add water
5. seal and wink
6. shake until it sounds like a rock
7. roll out for your favorite pie or pastries
demonstrations.review: This was really easy and fun to do - a great quick way to make a pie crust.  I felt there was something missing though, but can't quite put my finger on it.  I didn't let that affect my rating though, because i loved it nonethless!  When i need a quick easy pie crust - this is  where I'm going! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
demonstrations.review: I made this for my Mom's birthday this year - she's a chocolate cake fanatic and says that it was easily the best chocolate cake she's ever had, home made or otherwise!!  I topped it with Recipe #89207 - Kittencal's Chocolate Buttercream and it was absolutely fabulous!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s extreme chocolate brownies

if your looking for an everyday run-of-the-mill cake-style brownie then pass this by, this is a a moist chewy extreme chocolate bakery-style brownie that takes little time to make and tastes even better the next day, it's everything a good brownie should be!  --- i have even made these using half brown sugar and half white sugar, the amount of sugar listed will give you a sweet brownie you may reduce the sugar by 1/4 cup or more if desired or if you have a sweet tooth use amount stated --- add in a couple of tablespoons of coffee-flavored liqueur in place of the vanilla if desired -- according to a reviewer oil may be used in place of the butter successfully --- these brownies freeze very well,  they are so simple to make just mix everything by hand, they bake out so rich and sinful! --- see recipe#89207

1. set oven to 325 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. in a heavy saucepan , bring butter , sugar and water to a boil , stirring constantly until the butter is melted and sugar is dissolved
4. remove from the heat , with a wooden spoon , stir in 2 cups chocolate chips until melted
5. cool slightly , beat in vanilla
6. in a mixing bowl , whisk eggs , gradually add in the chocolate mixture , beating with a wooden spoon until completely mixed
7. mix together flour , baking soda and salt
8. add to the egg / chocolate mixture
9. mix well to combine
10. stir in the remaining chocolate chips
11. spread into prepared baking pan
12. bake for 35-40 minutes
13. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I made these brownies today - mostly because I needed an excuse to make your recipe for Choc0late Buttercream - and they are DELICIOUS!!  When my mom found out I was taking some to a friend, she told me that it would be better if I just brought more to her house - so I think she liked them too!  Thanks so much!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s fried parmesan zucchini sticks

these have been a long time family favorite, use only dry breadcrumbs for this as fresh will not stick to the zucchini, the cayenne is only optional add in for some heat --- if desired you may slice the zucchini into rounds instead if sticks--- also see my recipe#244592

1. in a shallow bowl whisk the eggs with water
2. in another shallow dish combine dry bread crumbs , flour , parmesan cheese , italian seasoning , dried parsley , seasoned salt , black pepper , garlic powder and cayenne pepper
3. dip the zucchini sticks in egg / water mixture then coat into the breadcrumb mixture
4. heat oil in a skillet until hot
5. fry zucchini in hot oil until golden brown and crispy , turning occasionally
6. transfer to a paper towel-lined plate
7. serve immediately
target.review: Wonderful as always kittencal! I used italian breadcrumbs so left out most of the spices except for the garlic powder. Loved the mixture of the flour with the breadcrumbs, made for a great batter texture. Only change I would make is more salt, but that's about just personal preference. Will definitely do again, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chilean salsa

after trying this salsa, it is hard to go back to store-bought salsa. i could eat my weight in this stuff, along with tortilla chips. yum!!

1. in a mortar , crush the garlic , chile peppers , and salt and make a paste , using a circular motion with the pestle
2. transfer mixture to a serving bowl
3. add the remaining ingredients and stir to combine
4. will keep in the refrigerator for 2-3 days
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, absolutely wonderful. I substituted olive oil for vegetable oil and the juice from one lime for the red wine vinegar. Thank you very much for sharing this recipe, it will definitely made again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new red potato salad

we can't wait for those lucious little new red potatoes to be ready in our garden so we can fix this great potato salad!!

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil
2. drop in the new potatoes and reduce to low
3. cover and cook for 20 min , or until potatoes are done
4. dice potatoes into a lg bowl
5. add onion
6. mix all remaining ingredients in sm bowl
7. pour over the potatoes and mix well
8. best if refrigerated for 1-2 hours
demonstrations.review: The sauce alone for this deserves five stars. Amazing! My husband insisted on hard boiled eggs being added which didn't negate the flavor at all. Wonderful recipe, thanks for sharing! Can't wait to wow my family with it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic baked ziti

this baked ziti recipe is a simple italian casserole dish that my family enjoys.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large skillet , cook ground beef , onions , and garlic over medium-high heat for 6 to 8 minutes or until beef is browned
3. stirring frequently
4. stir in spaghetti sauce , chicken broth , and oregano
5. reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
6. stir 1 cup of the sauce into the cooked ziti noodles
7. spoon 1 / 2 of the ziti mixture into a 13x9x2-inch baking dish
8. sprinkle with 1 1 / 2 cups mozzarella cheese and 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
9. top with 2 cups sauce , then remaining ziti mixture and remaining sauce
10. cover and bake 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella and parmesan cheese
12. return to oven and bake uncovered for 10 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: I used two pounds of ground beef instead of one and some homemade sauce my husband made over the summer, and subbed egg noodles for ziti. Did not have as much mozzarella as I though so had to use a lot of monterey jack, but it still turned out fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat recipe for carrabba s chicken marsala

a clone dish from carrabba's restaurant. i have not tried this yet, but will soon and add more comments. sounds wonderful!

1. pound chicken breasts to even out thickness and lightly salt and pepper
2. in large skillet , saute chicken in 2 t melted butter until lightly browned , about 2 minutes per side
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. melt remaining butter in pan and add shallots and mushrooms
5. cook until mushrooms are lightly browned
6. add marsala and bring to a boil , scraping browned bits from bottom of pan
7. add cream and lemon juice and return to a boil
8. season with salt and pepper
9. return chicken to pan for about 3 minutes to reheat and finish cooking
10. serve with buttered fettucini
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious. I was out of heavy cream and substituted 1/4 c. sour cream and 1/4 c. whole milk, left out the lemon juice, and it turned out great! The kids (1 & 3) are eating it as I type, and they don't like anything but hot dogs & chicken nuggets. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streamlined chimichangas

this is a great tasting recipe and so easy that even my daughter doesn't complain when i ask her to make it.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. brown meat with onion and garlic
3. drain , but do not rinse
4. stir in picante sauce , cumin , oregano and salt
5. simmer 5 minutes or until most of the liquid has evaporated
6. brush one side of the tortillas with butter
7. on unbuttered side spoon heaping 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture into center
8. fold 2 sides over filling , fold ends down
9. place seam side down in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish
10. bake for 13 minutes or until golden brown
11. to serve , top with sour cream , guacamole and additional picante sauce
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness, my husband and I could NOT get enough of these! Thanks so much for sharing! YUMMY! Oh, and I actually used taco seasoning instead of the cumin, oregano and salt; olive oil instead of butter; and Ortega thick & chunky salsa instead of the Picante sauce. And I didn't have sour cream so used ranch dressing. We were snowed in so I had to use what was on hand. LOL Still absolutely fabulous and will definitely make again!

target.recipe_text:
balsamic roast

i picked this recipe up from a local market while on vacation.  this is a delicious dish!

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. generously season roast with coarse ground black pepper
3. place the onions in high sided roasting pan and place roast on top
4. in a large bowl , mix the vinegar through bay leaves , pour into roasting pan
5. cover and cook for 3 to 3 1 / 2 hours , adding the prepared vegetables 45 minutes before the end of cooking time
6. if desired the meat and vegetables can be removed from the cooking liquid when done and the liquid brought to a boil , reduced and then thickened with arrowroot starch or cornstarch
7. serve the gravy over the cooked meat and vegetables
target.review: Excellent flavor!!  I cooked it in the oven - cooking time was perfect for the roast, but I would increase the time for the veggies a little bit.  We served the leftover meat on mashed potatoes - yummy!  Next time I will be making this in the crockpot. Thanks for a delicious pot roast!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle roast for tacos   sandwiches

crock pot recipe. beware - this is spicy, but is an excellent shredded beef for tacos, sandwiches or enchiladas!

1. place chuck roast in large crock pot and sprinkle with the salt and pepper , chili powder and cumin
2. add the remaining ingredients and simmer on high for 5 hours or on low for 7-8 hours
3. shred the meat with a fork and simmer on high for additional 10-15 minutes
4. serve in enchiladas , tacos or on crusty rolls with the juice for dipping
demonstrations.review: Absolutely THE best recipe for beef in Mexican dishes. I have made this countless times now and everyone loves it!  I add 5-6 chipolte chiles in adobo, but my family is into the "spicy" stuff! Thanks for a wonderful recipe. (Oh! And DH uses the leftovers over pasta with a can of drained corn - yummy!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot special

this is from a handwritten recipe card, so i don't know where it is from.  i do know that it is simple and delicious.  great served over egg noodles, mashed potatoes or rice.

1. mix soups together
2. place roast in crock pot and pour soup mixture over
3. cook on low 8-9 hours
4. serve over egg noodles , rice or mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review:
Love the simplicity of this recipe! So easy to put on in the morning as you are trying to run out of the door! Easy, tasty, and no leftovers (ROFL) - the family inhales it all!! Thanks KelBel.
Valina

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun fish fillets

make the rub as hot or mild as you wish. from heart healthy cooking by becel

1. in a small bowl , combine paprika , garlic powder , thyme , salt , black pepper , cayenne pepper and oil to make a paste
2. pat fish dry with paper towels
3. using the back of a spoon , rub paste mixture evenly over the entire surface of the fish
4. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for 2 hours
5. preheat bbq to medium high and grease grill
6. bbq halibut , turning once , until cooked through , about 3 to 5 minutes per side
7. cooking time may vary depending on thickness of fish
8. remove fish to a serving plate and serve with lemon wedges
9. this rub works equally well with salmon , sea bass or tuna
demonstrations.review: Very good flavor!  I used about 1/2 tsp. ground chipotle pepper instead of cayenne - we like things spicy!  I used this on Tilapia but want to try it on halibut and tuna. Thanks so much for posting!  Valina

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: Hehehe - Chef #725332, EXACTLY what I did!  I used "Recipe #136292" as the marinara sauce and this as the eggplant...tossed a little shredded mozz during the last few minutes of cooking the eggplant and slathered it in pasta and sauce - super delicious!  Of course, it was so tasty that I ate 2 of the smaller pieces as I fixed the plates!  Yummy!! I also used regular mayo and fresh onion.  I also used Italian-style breadcrumbs - since I had them in the house - and omitted the italian seasoning. Awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy potato salad

have you ever posted a recipe and just love reading the reviews for it?  this is my signature potato salad.  whenever there is a pot luck function at work, i am told that i have to bring the potato salad.  no one else is allowed to and i am never given a choice.  thank you everyone who ever tried this potato salad and for leaving such glowing reviews for it.  you all have made me look so good.  i personally can not stand eggs or raw onions, so i leave them out but i know most people don't think a potato salad is complete without them.  thanks again for so many wonderful reviews. (psssst....check out my recipe #123107 as well.  it shares the dressing with this recipe but tastes much much different because of the different ingredients) please see recipe #242966 for bacon bit tips.

1. cook potatoes in boiling , salted water until tender
2. drain well
3. peel and cube potatoes
4. transfer to a large bowl
5. add celery , onion , sweet relish and bacon bits
6. combine mayo , sugar , celery seed , vinegar , mustard , and salt
7. add mayo mixture to potatoes
8. toss lightly to coat potato mixture
9. carefully fold in the chopped eggs
10. cover and chill thoroughly
11. bacon bit
12. use a sharp knife and cut the frozen bacon into long strips about 1 / 4 inch wide
13. turn the bacon and cut the strips into pieces also about 1 / 4 in wide
14. you now have perfect raw bacon pieces to fast fry
15. no need to separate
16. they will separate during cooking
17. perfect bacon bits
demonstrations.review:
Awesome flavor - the whole family loved it! I doubled the recipe using 5 lbs. of potatoes.  Boiled them whole, skin on, then cooled them on counter...then put them in fridge overnight.  The next morning, I peeled and cubed and added the doubled ingredients. (Cutting them into cubes when they are cold helps them keep their shape, not getting so mushy) After tasting, I added 1 more tsp. of mustard, because of our taste. 
I also diced the onions and the celery very fine - again for our taste.
The family loved it! Thanks for the great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
pipin  hot bakery whole wheat tortillas

these flavorful tortillas were used at the bakery for our breakfast burritos, which had scrambled eggs, cheese, salsa, fried potatoes, and sour cream.  i also use them  to make bean burritos, quesadillas, and as an accompaniment with a bowl of pinto beans.

1. combine flours , baking powder , and salt
2. stir in the oil and water all at once , using mixer or a fork , and toss quickly
3. when dough can be gathered into a soft mass , turn onto floured surface and knead a few times
4. form 8 balls of dough , dredge in flour , and store in a plastic bag to prevent drying until ready to be used
5. flatten first ball of dough into a disk
6. roll out dough on floured surface until 7 inches or larger with even strokes that do not reach to the edge , turning over frequently
7. place tortilla in ungreased , frying pan that has been preheated to medium-high heat
8. cook 30-40 seconds on one side , turn over with spatula and cook 30-40 seconds on other side
9. , first side should be pale and sprinkled with brown spots and the other side will be blotched
10. repeat process with other balls of dough
11. stack tortillas on a plate as they are cooked and cover them with a dish towel , which will keep them soft
target.review: These were excellent. They were quick to put together, tasted great, and I liked the fact that they were a little healthier with the whole wheat flour and lack of hydrogenated oils. I used them to make wraps for tempeh soft tacos. My 5-year-old daughter said they were the best tortillas she's ever had.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review: I had some brussels sprouts that I needed to use up from the last of our CSA share (they're not a typical purchase in our household). These are the best brussels sprouts I've ever had. I was afraid I'd roasted them too long because they were quite brown, but they tasted perfect. The outside was a bit crispy and the inside was tender, almost creamy. The roasting also gave them a sweeter flavor than they get when sauteed, steamed, or boiled. I won't wait until next year's CSA share - this recipe is worth purchasing brussels sprouts!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue plate special halibut or salmon

this comes from "seafood twice a week". it was my first attempt at cooking fish. it always turns out great and gave me the confidence to try other fish preparations. it's also great for those nights when you're just too tired to cook. the next day, leftovers mashed and mixed make a good halibut-salad sandwich. my favorite is halibut with this preparation, but salmon is good this way, too.

1. lightly oil or spray a baking dish before placing fish in a single layer
2. mix remaining ingredients
3. spread over fish
4. bake at 400 degrees f for 15-20 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: I made this with a salmon fillet. It was so fast to put together and was pretty tasty too. Next time I'll cut the amount of mayo in half...there was a little more than suited our taste, but that's just personal preference. This is a great recipe for a busy weeknight dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wilted spinach with raisins and apples

here's a little different twist on spinach salad.

1. heat oil in a large saute pan over medium heat
2. add raisins , pine nuts , apples , and onion , and cook about 5 minutes , stirring occasionally , until raisins plump
3. stir salt into raisin mixture
4. add spinach , tossing until spinach is just wilted
5. serve immediately , with wedges of lemon to squeeze over spinach if desired
demonstrations.review: This was knock-your-socks off delicious. If you are even a slight fan of these ingredients, try this combination; it's fantastic! Everything melds together to give you just the right combination of textures and flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
canary island cilantro soup

the 

1. in a med-large soup pot , heat about 2 tblsp of olive oil
2. sautee onion , garlic , tomato , potatoes , and paprika over fairly high heat until the onions are translucent
3. add boullion , 1 / 2 of the green pepper 2 / 3 of the bunch of cilantro , tied with a string , and the salt to taste
4. add enough water to cover vegetables completely , with about 1-2 inches above the veggies
5. bring to a boil , cover , reduce heat and simmer for about 20-30 minutes
6. about half way through cooking time , add the rice
7. adjust salt , remove green pepper and bunch of cilantro , discard
8. chop the remaining green pepper and cilantro and serve each soup plate with fresh chopped green pepper and sprinkle with cilantro
9. serve with"queso fresco" and baguettes
demonstrations.review: Great soup that I'll definitely make again. The house smelled fantastic while this was cooking! I had already chopped my entire bunch of cilantro, so I threw in approx. 1/2-3/4 bunch of the chopped and left it in. I was a little worried that the cilantro would overpower, but it was just right for our tastes. Thanks for posting this Canary Girl!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary tomato parmesan bread

this flavorful bread has a nice texture for sandwiches. it also makes wonderful croutons when cut into squares and toasted. adapted from a recipe in 

1. add all ingredients except tomatoes to bread machine in the order listed , making a little indention in the flour for the yeast
2. turn on machine
3. if tomatoes are packed in oil , first blot them dry with a paper towel
4. cut or snip tomatoes into small pieces-- but do not add them until after the first knead
5. if your machine has a fruit& nuts setting , add them when that beeper goes off
demonstrations.review: This bread is divine. It tasted great fresh out of the breadmaker, and was even better toasted. I used some of it to make grilled cheese sandwiches, and they were the best grilled cheese sandwiches I've ever tasted. Thanks for such a great recipe, Moxie.

target.recipe_text:
coconut beer battered shrimp with mango orange chutney

emeril strikes again!!! these are great!!!!!!!!!!

1. in a deep saute pan or pot , heat the oil to 360 degrees
2. combine the flour , sugar and essence in a medium bowl
3. slowly add the beer and whisk to form a smooth batter
4. place the coconut flakes in a shallow bowl
5. one at a time , holding them by the tail , dip the shrimp into the batter to coat , then dredge in the coconut , turning to coat evenly and pressing to make the flakes adhere
6. fry in batches in the oil until golden , 3 to 4 minutes
7. drain on paper towels and season lightly with essence
8. place the chutney in a bowl on a large platter
9. arrange the shrimp on the platter around the bowl and sprinklewith the chopped cilantro
10. serve immediately
target.review: I made mean chef's version of this with his recipe for chutney. I don't remember where I got it from, maybe recipecircus but this is basically the same recipe and I REALLY love it. I use sweet coconut cause I like most everything sweeter! Great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoky chicken corn cakes

this recipe has become a family favorite!  we will be having this often during football season!  great corn cakes!!! 
note -- turn down the heat in this dish by omitting the chipotle or reducing it by half and using just 1 tablespoon of the adobo sauce.

adapted from real simple.com

1. using a fork or your fingers , shred the chicken meat , discarding the skin and bones
2. in a medium bowl , combine the meat , chipotle , lime juice , 1 / 4 teaspoon of the salt , the onion , tomatoes , and cilantro
3. set aside
4. in a large bowl , whisk together the flour , cornmeal , baking powder , pepper , and the remaining salt
5. stir in the eggs and ricotta until no lumps remain
6. fold in the corn
7. heat the oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
8. for each corn cake , spoon about 1 / 4 cup of the batter onto the skillet and cook until golden brown and set on one side , 2 to 3 minutes
9. using a spatula , flip the cakes and cook 1 minute more
10. divide the cakes among individual plates and top with the chicken mixture
11. serve with sour cream , if desired
demonstrations.review: Made this for a BBQ at my house and everyone loved it. The chicken salsa as I called it was tasty and had alot of good flavor going on. The corn cakes were the biggest hit of the day with the guests. I used a pack of jiffy mix instead of flour and corn meal. I also added a dab of honey and threw in some grated cheese. They came out great. Together the chicken and corn cakes make a great dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet meatball goulash

this is a delicious meal that my family loves!

1. spray 12-inch nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray
2. heat over medium-high heat until hot
3. add bell pepper and onion
4. cook and stir 2-3 minutes or until crisp-tender
5. add gravy , broth , water , chili sauce and meatballs
6. mix well
7. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally
8. reduce heat to medium
9. cover
10. cook 5 minutes or until meatballs are thawed
11. add uncooked noodles
12. mix well
13. cover
14. cook about 10 minutes or until noodles are tender and meatballs are thoroughly heated , stirring occasionally
15. remove from heat
16. stir in sour cream until well blended
17. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: I just finished making this and I am very impressed. It was so easy and done so quickly. I am just waiting on my bread to finish cooking and then it's TIME TO EAT!! I didn't have chili sauce but I just used the ingredients that recipezaar has listed as a substitute and I used egg noodles. Tastes Great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy scalloped corn casserole

nan

1. beat eggs slightly
2. add sour cream , butter and corn
3. fold in dry jiffy corn mix
4. put in baking disk
5. sprinkle cheese on top
6. bake at 350 for 45-60 minutes
7. make sure center comes out clean
8. another rendition is to mix in the cheese-- this was very good since it spread the cheese throughout the corn
demonstrations.review: I have been trying to remember how to make this for a while. I just never remembered the sourcream. I have used your recipe a few times since I found it and I have to admit that around my friends and family this is now MY corn casserole. I even have a request to make it tomorrow! I love this recipe especially with the cheese. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amy s favorite chicken

i made this up, loosely based on a chicken dish i had at a friend's house. you can always experiment with different cream soups and veggies. i buy a frozen bag of seasoning vegetables-onions, bell peppers and celery. i keep a bag of this on hand and use it for a lot of recipes.  this cuts down on a lot of prep time. i also buy fresh mushrooms when they are on sale and freeze them, too.

1. pound the chicken breast to even thickness
2. heat olive oil in a large deep skillet
3. season breasts as preferred and then brown
4. remove breasts , set aside
5. add more oil if needed , then saute all veggies for about 5 minutes if using bacon , add that too , it takes longer to cook than the prosciutto
6. after 5 minutes add the diced prosciutto and garlic
7. saute for another minute or 2
8. add cream soup and wine , stir until well combined
9. return chicken to pan , cover and simmer for 20 minutes
10. i usually turn the chicken once
11. you can season sauce further if needed
12. i think that it only needs a little fresh ground pepper to top it off
13. this goes great with long grain and wild rice
demonstrations.review: I decided to make this for dinner since you were the chef of the day and I am very glad I did. the whole family loved it. I couldn't find cream of onion soup so I mixed golden mushroom and french onion together. I think that I probably doubled the recipe also. The addition of the wine is what sets this aside from other "cream of" and chicken dishes. Thanks for a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy hot wings

i was so tired of soggy skinned hot wings or too much vinegar in commercial hot wings, so i made this recipe up. i serve it with ranch dressing and sliced fresh veggies. great to take to parties.

1. cut wings into pieces discarding
2. wash and pat dry with paper towels
3. pre-heat cooking oil to 350 degrees
4. slowly add 1 / 2 of the wing pieces to hot oil
5. fry until golden brown
6. in the meantime , in a large pan , melt the butter on a very low heat
7. add bottled hot sauce and bbq sauce
8. keep sauce warm
9. add the cooked wings to the sauce
10. stir to coat
demonstrations.review: I really love this recipe. I can control the heat level of the wings with the BBQ sauce by adding more or less. My hubby doesn't like spicey foods but he'll eat these if I lower the heat. I never would have thought of the BBQ sauce.....thanks

target.recipe_text:
stove top tamale pie

this is a quick and easy one-dish meal.

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef over medium-high heat
2. drain
3. stir in tomato sauce , beans , water and taco seasoning mix
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat , cover and simmer 5 minutes
6. prepare corn muffin mix according to package directions
7. drop small spoonfuls of muffin batter over meat mixture in a skillet
8. cover and cook over medium-low heat 15-17 minutes or until corn bread is done
9. top with cheese and green onion
10. cover and cook over low heat until cheese melts
target.review: This was great. As it was cooking, I was starting to have dubts, but it turned out great. We don't like kidney beans, so I used canned yellow corn instead, I also used a Mexican 4 cheese blend instead of plain cheddar.Our meat dept. has ground beef already seasoned ( quality, that the butchers season, not pre-packaged.), so I bought that, and I still used the taco seasoning packet, for a little more flavor. I will be making this again. And, I can see lots of possibilities for things you can add to it, or ways to change it around. You could add onions, canned tomatoes, jalepeno, use ground turkey instead, regular cornbread, etc. etc. Great dish. Thanks Fluffy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best fried ravioli

i got this recipe off of "everyday italian" with giada de laurentiis.  talk about good!!  i made it for my husband (who is a only meat and potatoes kind of guy) and he flipped!  it's even better than cheese sticks...and who can top that?

1. pour enough olive oil into a large frying pan to reach a depth of 2 inches
2. heat the oil over medium heat until a deep-fry thermometer registers 325 degrees f
3. while the oil is heating , put the buttermilk and the bread crumbs in separate shallow bowls
4. working in batches , dip ravioli in buttermilk to coat completely
5. allow the excess buttermilk to drip back into the bowl
6. dredge ravioli in the bread crumbs
7. place the ravioli on a baking sheet , and continue with the remaining ravioli
8. when the oil is hot , fry the ravioli in batches , turning occasionally , until golden brown , about 3 minutes
9. using a slotted spoon , transfer the fried ravioli to paper towels to drain
10. sprinkle the fried ravioli with parmesan and serve with a bowl of warmed marinara sauce for dipping
demonstrations.review: Wonderful! I had never had fried ravioli before, and this was excellent. I thought I had dry breadcrumbs in my pantry, but I didn't so I put some bread slices in my blender, grinded them very fine, and added, basil, garlic, oregano, onion powder. It came out great. I used a different marinara, recipe # 58246, they went wonderful together. This recipe is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon pie

i love cinnamon anything.  this is one of my favorite pies and is really easy.  you are sure to have all the ingredients in your kitchen too.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix all ingredients together with a whisk
3. batter will be slightly lumpy
4. pour into the shell and bake for 45 minutes or until set
demonstrations.review: The flavor of this was good, but there were a couple of things I didn't like, the texture of the filling was mushy (which could have been my fault, although I followed the recipe exactly), and my crust seemed like it would have benefitted by being baked blind first. Thanks for the recipe though, I will probably try again, and see if I can get it right.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seven layer rigatoni

can substitute 3/4 pound of bulk turkey italian sausage and reduced fat mozzarella cheese if you prefer a less fattening dish.

1. heat oven to 375
2. spray rectangular baking dish , 13x9x2 inches , with cooking spray
3. cook and drain pasta as directed on package
4. while pasta is cooking , cook sausage in 10-inch skillet over medium heat , stirring occasionally , until no longer pink , drain
5. mix tomatoes , garlic and basil
6. layer half each of the pasta , sausage , mushrooms , bell peppers , parmesan cheese , tomato mixture and mozzarella cheese in baking dish
7. repeat layers
8. bake uncovered 35 to 40 minutes or until hot and cheese is golden brown
demonstrations.review: Very good. The simplicity of the flavors was excellent, nothing had to compete with anything else, you could taste each seperately, but they blended very well together at the same time. Very good, thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s salsa

you can make this sauce easily at home. from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. in food processor place jalapenos and onions
2. process for just a few seconds
3. add both cans of tomatoes , salt , sugar , and cumin
4. process all ingredients until well blended but do not puree
5. place in covered container and chill
6. a couple of hours of chilling will help blend and enrich the flavor
7. serve with your favorite thin corn tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: This is great, the texture is perfect, because I don't like chunky salsa. I added fresh garlic, a fresh jalepeno pepper (which made it quite hot), fresh cilantro and some parsley. I didn't have garlic salt, so i used garlic powder, and added just a little kosher salt. It wasn't too garlicky with the fresh garlic and the powder. I also put some pepper in it. I will defintely make this again, and it was really close Chili' Salsa, now if I could just find chips, like the thin, and crispy ones they serve!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq pork steak

easy to do, tasty combination of flavors. i was just playing around, had a pork steak and threw this together. hope you try it and like it. preparation time does not include marinating time.

1. mix all the ingredients except pork steaks
2. rub spice mix all over the steaks
3. wrap tightly in plastic wrap and put in fridge overnight or 2 hours at room temperature
4. have the bbq hot and sear the chops for 2 minutes each side
5. turn bbq down to medium and continue cooking apprx 6 minutes each side or until internal temperature reaches 160-170f
demonstrations.review: Very, very good. I am not a fan of pork chops, but my husband likes them alot, so I decided to give this a try. I am glad I did. The only change that I would make is, that next time, I would probably use only 1/2 a teaspoon of salt in the marinade, as it was a little saltier than we would have liked, but other than that excellent. Thanks, Bergy.

target.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
target.review: I have made this twice now and we really enjoy it.  I never use quite as much lemon, but that's just a personal preference.  I don't usually make potatoes cause I hate doing alot of prep for dinner.  These are so easy and so tasty.  Even "the chef", aka DH, loves these.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot ham and beans

this is cheap eating at it's best. really good for scraping by at the end of the month if your cash gets low. goes best with freshly baked corn muffins drizzled with honey.

1. sort beans and soak in enough water to cover overnight
2. or you may sort them and place in a saucepan with 2-inches of water to cover
3. bring them to a boil , boil for 3 minutes , then cover and remove from heat
4. allow to sit for one hour after boiling
5. whichever method you use , rinse and drain the beans before placing them in the crock pot
6. put the rinsed beans , garlic , onion , salt , pepper , parsley , cloves , ham or ham hocks into the crock pot along with 6 cups water or broth
7. cover crock , and cook on low for about 8 hours , or until beans are tender and creamy
8. skim any excess fat , if necessary , before serving
demonstrations.review: Have I not rated this?  DH absolutely loves this, especially with greens.  Now that I am going to school at night, this is the perfect meal: cheap, easy, and I don't have to be here!  Thank you for a real life saver!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: YUMMY!  DH, the chef, told me the night before I made this that he is "always disappointed by people's decision to make roast".  Too few steps for him, I guess.  I added veggies and 1 cup of water.  He ate seconds and thirds.  Guess I changed his mind!  Thank you for the easy, hubbie-pleasing recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern baked spaghetti

this is an easy, yet very tasty spaghetti casserole, which reminds me of the spaghetti they used to serve us in elementary school. i loved their spaghetti! i normally only brought my lunch, but not on spaghetti day!

1. cook spaghetti per package direcions
2. combine milk and egg , mix well
3. combine drained spaghetti , milk and egg
4. mix well
5. pour spaghetti mixture into a buttered 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. brown ground beef with onion , bell pepper and garlic in a large skillet
7. drain
8. return drained meat back into the skillet and add seasonings
9. cook for 2 minutes
10. stir in tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes
11. spread meat mixture over spaghetti
12. sprinkle with cheese
13. bake at 425f for 10 minutes or until cheese melts and is bubbly
14. remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was really good and super easy to put together.  Hubby ate almost all of it.  Picky four-year-old THANKED ME for dinner, and newly-picky two-year-old didn't even try it.  Oh, well, still a success in my book.  Next time I'll add mushrooms.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked spaghetti with ground turkey meat

this is so very good, i make it for my people all the time and people ask all the time for the recipe. it uses ground turkey and low fat ingredients for a healthy meal with a great flavor.

1. cook spaghetti noodles until done and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees and grease a 9x13 casserole dish
3. cook the turkey breast , green peppers and onions in a skillet on medium heat until turkey is no longer pink
4. add the drained jar of mushrooms and the can of diced tomatoes to skillet
5. simmer for 15 minutes
6. in a small bowl mix the can of cream of mushroom soup with the water
7. in the casserole dish place half of the cooked noodles , then topped with half the meat mixture , then 1 cup cheese
8. repeat
9. then finally the cream of mushroom soup mixture
10. top with the grated parmesan cheese
11. cook on 350 for 35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I took some liberties with this and it turned out OK.  I used sweet Italian turkey sausages (all they had at the store) and half yellow, half red onion.  I also added some more spices.  I used milk instead of water for the soup.  I would not recommend that, as it turned out WAY too creamy and rich.  If I were to make this again I would add some tomato sauce, cut back just a tad on the cheese, and use the water.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy drumsticks

another easy and delicious chicken recipe from mr. food

1. spray a 13x9 inch baking pan with cooking spray
2. put drumsticks in the baking dish and sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. bake at 375 degrees for 30 minutes
4. in a bowl , mix together the remaining ingredients
5. take drumsticks out of the oven and pour sauce mixture over them
6. bake the drumsticks for 30 minutes or until juice run clear
demonstrations.review: Mmmmmm....  We loved this and it couldn't be easier.  It wasn't very spicy, but did have a little kick.  Perfect for the kids and next time we'll do 2 sauces and make our's a little hotter.  This will be a regular at our house from now on.

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian lasagna

i first had veggie lasagna when i was in hospital, and i just had to find a better recipe! here it is.

1. mix carrots , oregano , and spaghetti sauce together
2. mix ricotta , spinach , and eggs together in separate bowl
3. spread cup spaghetti sauce in bottom of 9 x 13 inch baking dish
4. layer 3 lasagna noodles , remaining sauce , ricotta mixture , sliced zucchini , sliced mushrooms , mozzarella , and parmesan
5. repeat layers with remaining ingredients
6. bake in 350 degrees oven for about 45 minutes
target.review: Wonderful and easy.  Even my non-veggie hubby ate it up with no problem :)  I used fresh spinach and it came out just fine.  Just be sure if using fresh spinach to make sure it is covered with sauce or it will dry out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese sauce  vegan

this is the simplest and best tasting vegan cheese sauce recipe we've found.  we got it from our cousin diana p. who got it from who knows where.  we like it best for nachos.  it works well for mac'n'cheese as well as enchiladas or any recipe that calls for a cheese sauce.

1. rinse cashews with hot water while combining the remaining ingredients in a blender
2. add cashews to blender and process on high for 1-2 minutes
3. cook in a sauce pan over medium heat , stirring constantly , until thick
4. add chiles and serve or use in other recipes that call for cheese sauce
demonstrations.review: This is a really nice gravy.  I call it a gravy because I do not find it cheesy what-so-ever.  It does look like cheese, but definitely does not taste like cheese.  It does taste very good on a variety of things, just don't expect it to be cheese.  Also, I like to use carrots for coloring instead of piment.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blockbuster vegetarian crock pot black bean soup

this soup is really yummy and healthy too! this makes a main dish accompanied by tortillas, or crusty french bread and a nice salad!caribbean, cuban, mexican and spanish influences! it really is best if the beans are soaked overnight.and depending on your cooker, the soup might need to be cooked longer.

1. soak beans overnight in water to cover
2. if you don't soak the beans overnight:
3. in a large pot over medium heat , place the beans in three times their volume of water
4. bring to a boil and let boil 10 minutes
5. cover , remove from heat and let stand 1 hour
6. drain and rinse
7. in a crock pot , combine soaked beans and 1 1 / 2 quarts fresh water
8. cook for 3-7 hours on high , depending on how hot your cooker gets
9. stir in carrot , celery , onion , garlic , bell pepper , jalapeno , lentils and tomatoes
10. season with chili powder , cumin , oregano , black pepper , red wine vinegar and salt
11. cook on low , 2 to 3 hours
12. stir the rice into the crock pot in the last 20 minutes of cooking
13. puree half the soup with a blender or food processor , then pour back into the pot before serving
14. serve with lime wedges , sour cream , and cilantro
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.  I really enjoyed all of the flavors.  We topped it with some spicy cilantro dip, sharp cheddar cheese, and chopped fresh red onion and cilantro.  Served some tortilla chips on the side and it was great!  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale chips

light and crunchy "chips" that are practically guilt free. found this recipe on radicalhealth.com.  i reduced the amount of salt called for in the original recipe thanks to some of the reviews.

1. cut kale into 2 to 3 inch pieces
2. mix vinegar , oil , and salt in a large bowl then add kale and mix by hand
3. try to get all the leaves covered
4. place on baking sheets and bake at 350 f until they are crispy
5. after about 20 minutes , if it looks like they are not sizzling a bit or getting a little crispy , turn up the heat to 400f
6. time for baking varies depending on the size of your chips and desired crispness
7. the outer edges cook quicker than the pieces from near the stem
demonstrations.review: Wow! I had no idea these would come out so crisp.  There is no need to run for a bag of potato chips again.  These definitely satisfy the need for crunch and salt.  I used much less salt than called for and would still reduce it even further.  Quick and easy snack.  I will definitely try playing around with other seasonings as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpeas with spinach  greek

nothing fancy about this dish - just good eating. round off with some feta cheese and crusty bread.

1. in a large saucepan , over medium heat , saute the onions and garlic in the olive oil until the onions are tender
2. add the chickpeas , tomatoes , pepper flakes , and oregano , and paprika
3. cover and simmer for about 18 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. add spinach and cook about 7 minutes longer , or until spinach is cooked
5. add the lemon juice , salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Surprisingly tasty.  It seemed kind of plain and boring so I wasn't convinced to make it, but it was really good.  I would make it again.  I made the garbanzos from dried and I think that made a big difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potluck orzo pasta salad

i made this for a work potluck- and was asked repeatedly for the recipe, so i put it up here. i didn't take home very much of it! the sesame oil and pine nuts are a bit expensive, but i think they are what makes the recipe. it's very easy and fairly quick to prepare.

1. cook orzo in 6-8 qt pot of boiling water according to pkg directions drain and rinse with cold water
2. drain well
3. toss in large bowl with 1 1 / 2 t olive oil
4. add chopped vegetables , beans , and olives in separate small bowl , combine olive juice , sesame oil , lemon juice , vinegar , garlic , oregano , dill weed , mustard and curry
5. gradually whisk in remaining 1 / 2 cup olive oil
6. add salt and ground pepper to taste
7. add dressing to orzo mixture and blend well
8. at this point taste the salad , and add more of whatever you prefer
9. toast pine nuts on a cookie sheet in a 350 degree oven for 5-10 minutes
10. sprinkle on top of salad just before serving
11. can be made 1 day ahead
12. makes approximately 10 cups
demonstrations.review: Really tasty.  I like the orzo pasta because it's not too "pasta-y".  I didn't have bell peppers so I used some shredded carrots, spinach, and tomato.  It was very nice, but I think I would use less oil next time; it was a little greasy.

target.recipe_text:
buttery shrimp and pasta

this is a really simple dish to make and it's quite elegant.

1. have pasta ready
2. in lg skillet , heat butter
3. add shrimp and garlic
4. saute 4 minutes , remove shrimp from skillet
5. add half and half
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes , stirring frequently
8. add shrimp , basil , cheese , pepper and pepper flakes
9. pour sauce into a bowl
10. add pasta and toss well
target.review: As is often the case I was drawn to this recipe by the photo. Lucky for me, easy to prepare, looked great, smelled great and was delicious. I doubled everything except the black and red pepper, used Shell shaped pasta and light cream because I forgot to buy half and half. The sauce didn't thicken but that was no problem because we mopped it up with  italian bread. 5 stars plus for a recipe that I plan to make often. So nice of you to share it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked grilled cheese

my family loves grilled cheese so when they asked for it i wanted to try something new.  this was the best grilled cheese, nice crunchy bread with melted cheese.  i had to post this so i wouldn't forget it.  family loved it served with homemade milkshakes and fries. this is a great way to make a bunch at one time and the clean-up was nothing. ;)

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. lightly butter one side of each slice of bread
3. place on a cookie sheet butter side down
4. place 2 slices cheese on each piece of bread
5. place other piece of bread on top , lightly butter side up
6. bake for approximately 5 minutes
7. then flip each sandwich over
8. bake additional 3-4 minute until done
demonstrations.review: What better meal to serve on a very rainy day, Baked Grill Cheese and Pasta Sausage Soup!(184501)This recipe makes the most delicious grilled cheese. I combined cheddar and mozarella and it was so good. I have also tried this for the last few weeks with Tortillas instead of bread. It comes out perfect both ways with the tortillas a bit crispy. A great method to make many sandwhichs at once. Everyone loved it. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
famous butter chicken

chicken breasts are dipped in beaten eggs and cracker crumbs, then baked with butter. this chicken is really tender, moist and delicious! a real favorite in my household.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place eggs and cracker crumbs in two separate shallow bowls
3. mix cracker crumbs with garlic salt and pepper
4. dip chicken in the eggs , then dredge in the crumb mixture to coat
5. arrange coated chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
6. place pieces of butter around the chicken
7. bake in the preheated oven for 40 minutes or until the chicken is no longer pink and the juices run clear
demonstrations.review: This recipe is wonderful. I used the new Ritz Crackers with Garlic. It was easy and very tasty, my family said it's keeper. Thanks for posting it, I served it with another wonderful recipe, baked potatoe wedges by dj101, great combination!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp parmesan

my husband favorite. a one dish meal. you can prepare everything up to putting in the oven, chill, till ready to heat. serve with a nice crusty bread. or skip the pasta and make shrimp parmesan sandwiches. check out the step x step for this recipe http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewtopic.zsp?t=223776

1. open the shrimp up like a book and remove the dark vein
2. in a zip lock bag , place flour seasoned with salt and old bay toss in shrimp and shake to coat
3. remove shrimp
4. to the same bag with the rest of the flour add panko , breadcrumbs , and parmesan cheese
5. in a small bowl whisk well eggs and mayonnaise
6. dip floured shrimp into egg mixture then bread crumbs
7. in a large heavy bottom pan heat oil
8. brown shrimp in batches and drain on paper towel to remove excess oil
9. spread 1 / 3 the sauce on bottom
10. spread cook pasta on top of sauce
11. spoon 1 / 3 sauce on pasta
12. lay shrimp in a baking dish 1 layer
13. sprinkle with with mozzarella cheese
14. top with rest of sauce
15. top with grated parmesan cheese
16. bake in 350 degree oven till cheese is melted
17. about 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: We just had this delicious dish for dinner. I made it as written except for not having panko so I just used the italian bread crumbs. The whole family loved it and asked that it be made again soon. It tastes like it came from a fine restaurant. The pictures are a mini cooking lesson and made the dish look as delicious as it tastes. Thanks Rita for sharing this recipe with everyone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
restaurant teriyaki sauce

you know the nice, sweet, thick teriyaki sauce you get from your favorite takeout joint? now you can have it at home.

1. mix all but cornstarch and 1 / 4c water in a sauce pan and begin heating
2. mix cornstarch and cold water in a cup and dissolve
3. after sauce is simmering , add cornstarch and water mixture , whisking well until sauce thickens
4. heat until sauce thickens to desired thickness
5. add water to thin if you over-thick it :)
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner today. I cooked some shrimp in butter with garlic and poured this sauce over the shrimp and served it with rice. It was delicious and everyone really enjoyed it. I like that I had all the ingredients and it tasted so much better than the bottled kind. It was the perfect thickness too. Thanks for sharing, I will use it on chicken next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: I would love to give this more than 5 stars. It is so moist and delicious. I followed it exactly and we tasted it with and without the fabulous icing. both were a hit. It also looks very apetizing. I think you are right, putting it in the freezer must be the trick. thanks for sharing a recipe that I will make often.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter cup cookies  tarts

i first saw these at a bake sale and was so impressed. you bake a ball of dough in a mini-muffin tin, bake, and press a reese's peanut butter cup into it after you take it out of oven. you are left with a picture-perfect tart, receiving "oohs and aahs" and "how did you do it?" you could even use the refrigerated sugar/peanut butter cookie dough too.

1. cream peanut butter , butter , sugar and brown sugar until fluffy
2. add egg , vanilla , flour , baking soda and salt' mix well
3. roll into 1-inch balls and place in miniature muffin tins or in mini cupcake wrappers)
4. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f
5. when tins are removed from oven , immediately press 1 peanut butter cup into the center of the cookie
6. allow to cool completely before removing cookies from the tin
target.review: These were so easy to make and delicious! I had problems getting them out of the pan though.  I tried Pam-ing them and everything but they were still sticking.  That won't keep me from making them again and again though! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crab broccoli bake

here's a quick, easy and healthy casserole for dinner. add some brown rice, or whole grain bread - and a salad for a great meal!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray 8x8-inch baking dish with cooking spray
3. place broccoli in bottom of dish
4. add flaked crab and onion
5. combine mayonnaise , mustard and italian seasoning
6. spread over top of crab mixture
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake for 20 minutes , or until heated through
demonstrations.review: I followed directions exactly and my family of 5 just didn't care for it.   It could be because we're from Maryland and crabs just aren't crabs without Old Bay seasoning.  Maybe next time I'll use Old Bay instead of Italian seasoning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft snickerdoodle cookies

these snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. they are so fast to put together too! i actually got it from an old recipe that my great grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. grandma always knows best!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix softened butter , 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl
3. combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt in a separate bowl
4. blend dry ingredients into butter mixture
5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: The best Snickerdoodle cookie, by far.  My hubby is addicted to the Snickerdoodles made at the mall at the Great Cookie, and out of ALLLL the recipes I've tried this is it!!  He was so happy!! Lol!!  Thanks for a great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amanda s cheese pound cake

my daughter amanda found this recipe in a old church cookbook, that i have had for years. its the kind of cake that you want to stick your face in the pan and never come up for air.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. cream butter , cream cheese and sugar together
3. add eggs one at a time
4. add vanilla and then flour slowly
5. pour into a bundt pan or tube pan
6. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours
7. important: do not try and rush by cooking faster in a hotter oven
demonstrations.review: This was REALLY good! I'm not much of a pound cake person, but I made it for a bake sale at work.  After 4 people came back to tell me how good it was, I decided to give it a try.  Wow!  I will be making this at home for myself now! Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cider beetles

get ready for the holidays!! i know a company that sells these for $7 each but i like to include them in holiday baskets. i like to make these for the kids to have cider during the fall and winter holidays as a tradition in our very new household.  they are very cute and great as a gift. tie with a festive ribbon and attached to a bottle of apple juice along with the directions. also these can be made inexpensively if you purchase your spices from a store selling them in bulk by weight.

1. adult portion:
2. slices oranges in half and scoop out pulp without breaking the orange rind
3. reserve pulp for another use or discard
4. place orange halves cut side up on a wire rack on a baking sheet
5. bake at 250f for 2 hours until dry and hard
6. let cool
7. kid portion:
8. pack brown sugar firmly into each orange half , mounding slightly
9. arrange spices in the brown sugar to resemble beetles: use a cinnamon stick as the body , a nutmeg as the head , 2 allspice for the eyes , and 6-8 cloves for the legs / feet
10. cover tightly with plastic wrap and store in the refrigerator
11. directions for use:
12. unwrap the beetle and drop into 1 1 / 2 quarts apple juice or cider
13. simmer 30 minutes
14. strain whole spices and orange rind from cider to serve
15. may add 1 / 2 cup of brandy , and heat well
16. store leftover cider in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I made one to try before making a bunch for Christmas baskets.  Everyone in my house gave it 4 stars, so needless to say it's a keeper and I'll be making them for baskets.  We tried it with the cider, next we want to try it with juice to see what the taste difference is.  Thanks for a great recipe MommyMakes! :o)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s hot chocolate mix

my mom's favorite hot chocolate mix. a little different from other mixes as this one has a box of instant chocolate pudding.

1. mix all together
2. store in airtight container
3. use 1 / 3 mix to 2 / 3 water when making hot chocolate
demonstrations.review: All 3 of my daughters loved it!!! (Mommy tried some too, and she also gives it 5 stars! lol)  This one is definately a keeper, no doubt about it!  I will also be adding jars of the delicious hot chocolate mix to Christmas baskets this year!  Thanks for the best hot chocolate recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
calypso pineapple bean pot

i can't remember were i originally got this recipe, but it has been a favorite around here for a long time.  the flavours blend very well together and it is very filling.

1. in a large , non-stick skillet , combine pineapple , onion , garlic , and brown sugar
2. cook over medium heat , stirring frequently , 15 minutes or until mixture becomes brown and onion starts to brown
3. add remaining ingredients , mixing well
4. reduce heat to medium low , cover , and cook 30 minutes
5. stir several times while cooking
6. serve over brown rice , or cooked grain of your choice
target.review: Awesome!  Instead of fresh tomatoes I used a can of diced tomatoes.  My husband doesn't like chickpeas so I used a blend of pinto, kidney, and black beans instead.  It was so delicious!  It made great left-overs too!  Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage cheese roast  vegetarian meatloaf

great vegetarian comfort food! don't be fooled by the ingredients; the flavor is very much like meatloaf. kitchen alchemy at its finest!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a loaf pan
3. in a large bowl , combine cottage cheese , eggs , vegetable oil , soup mix , walnuts , cereal and onion
4. spoon into prepared pan
5. bake for 60 to 70 minutes
6. let the 'roast' rest for 5 to 10 minutes
7. turn out onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: AWESOME!  This is a weekly staple at our house now.  So easy and delicious.  My meat-eating husband loves it too.  I don't care for onions much so I leave them out.  The onion soup flavors it enough for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calypso chicken casserole

island flavors in an easy and healthy casserole.  you can just hear the steel drums play...

1. combine chicken , peppers , beans , corn and pineapple in 2 quart glass casserole dish
2. dissolve cornstarch in pineapple juice and stir it in along with remaining ingredients except lime and coconut oil
3. bake at 350 for 30 - 40 min until chicken is done
4. stir in coconut oil
5. serve with lime wedges , or add fresh squeezed lime juice before serving
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: SO GOOD!  I'm a vegetarian so I just used frozen veggie chicken.  I also omitted the pineapple tidbits and just used about half a can of pineapple nectar since my husband does not like fruit in his savory dishes.  It turned out great and was a huge hit!  Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheesy vegetable casserole

a quick, easy casserole made with frozen vegetables, soup and cream cheese. there are lots of ways to alter this recipe by using alternate soups, vegetables, etc. (update 12/08) after reading the reviews that some chefs thought this dish was too soupy, i made it again using 2 packages of frozen veggies, it wasn't soupy at all, so i've edited the recipe from 1 pkg. to 2 packages of veggies. i think this will correct the problem.

1. prepare frozen vegetables as package directs
2. cook until just tender as they will continue to cook as casserole bakes in oven
3. place cooked vegetables in a large bowl , stir in soup and cream cheese
4. transfer to a greased 1 quart baking dish , sprinkle with croutons
5. bake 25 minutes at 375f or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: So good and easy!  I followed the recipe exactly and loved it.  I was afraid it was going to be a little soupy but the croutons soaked it up  and it was sooo good!  I think this is going to become a weekly dish at our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty italian crescent casserole

this is a very good, easy dish that's sure to impress.  i've had great results from others when i've made this.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. in large skillet , brown beef and onion then drain
3. return meat to pan
4. add spaghetti sauce
5. meanwhile , in a medium bowl combine mozzarella cheese and sour cream
6. pour hot meat into an ungreased 12 x 8 inch dish
7. spoon cheese mixture over meat
8. unroll crescent roll dough over the top of the mixture
9. mix parmesan cheese and butter together , then spread over the top of the dough
10. bake 18-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy, and good.  I substituted vegetarian grounds for the beef, and it worked fine.  I had to cook it about 10 extra minutes to cook the crescent rolls all the way through, but when it was done it was very tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked orzo with peppers and cheese

this is a great side dish. very similar to macaroni and cheese, but then again...not!!

1. boil orzo in boiling , salted water 10 to 12 minutes until tender
2. drain
3. mix orzo peppers , chiles and mozzarella cheese
4. place in buttered casserole dish
5. spread sour cream evenly over top , sprinkle with parmesan and dot with butter
6. bake at 450 for 15 mintues until golden and puffed
7. cool slightly
demonstrations.review: I was scared to use the diced green chilies since I don't like spicy food, but they added such a great flavor and were not spicy at all!  Thanks for introducing them to me!  It was a little dry for me so next time I might add a little more sour cream.  Very tasty dish though!

target.recipe_text:
raw apple crumble  no bake

from march 7th's ottawa citizen. the woman featured is a vegan who promotes raw living (raw living consists of no food being cooked at temperatures higher than 46c (115f). she (and many studies) claim food is healthier this was and retains more nutrients. well i don't know about the claims, but this sure sounds good!

1. to make filling , in a food processor , place 2 apples with raisins , cinnamon and nutmeg , process until smooth
2. in a bowl place remaining chopped apples and toss with lemon juice
3. pour pureed filling mixture over top , mix well
4. spoon apple mixture into a med sized lasagna pan and set aside
5. for crumble , in a food processor , pulse walnuts , dates , cinnamon and salt until coarsely ground
6. do not over mix
7. crumble the mixture over the apples with your hands and press lightly
8. serve immediately or let marinate for a few hours for extra flavor
target.review: This is a real keeper.  I love desserts that have no added sweeteners, and this one is yummy.  I had to halve the recipe as I only had a few apples (which were Galas).  The only change I made was leaving the skin on the apple that got pureed.  I peeled the ones that were chopped.    Will definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smooth sweet potato bisque

smooth and mellow, with an undertone of sweet and spicy. great comfort food, colorful and beautiful.

1. in a medium saucepan , saut onion in butter till translucent , about 5 minutes
2. add sweet potatoes , carrots and chicken broth
3. simmer about 15-20 minutes , until tender
4. add sugar , nutmeg and cumin , and stir to combine
5. cool 15-30 minutes and place in blender or food processor to puree
6. you might want to do this in two batches
7. pour puree back into saucepan
8. reheat , then take off heat and add cream
demonstrations.review: This just didn't work out for me.  A lot of the liquid cooked off, so that when I pureed it, I came out with a baby food thickness.  I thinned it out with water, and found the flavor not so good.  I added some cinnamon, brown sugar, and maple syrup.  It made it edible, but I will not be making it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean burger

very easy to make. i got this one from mark bittman.

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. combine the beans , onion , oats , chili powder , cumin , salt , pepper , and egg in a food processor
3. pulse until chunky , but not pureed
4. the mixture should be moist , but not sticky
5. add a little liquid if needed
6. grease a baking sheet
7. use your hands , a spoon , or an ice-cream scoop to make patties
8. drop these onto the baking sheet
9. bake for about 15 minutes , or until the bottoms are nicely colored and lift easily from the baking sheet
10. flip and bake for 15 more
11. you can also broil these burgers , or cook them in a hot cast iron skillet , or on the grill
12. they cook a lot faster using these other methods , so just be sure to keep an eye on them
demonstrations.review: These are good.  The consistency is just right, and they don't fall apart once they're cooked.  I cooked mine on a griddle.  I would recommend using a coarse chop for the onion rather than simply quartering--my food processor didn't handle it well and I had to fish out huge chunks of onion when I was making the patties.   The second time I made these, I played with the recipe a little--I first pureed several baby carrots, a stalk of celery, and some roasted peppers, then added the other ingredients.  My family liked this version better, as there was more flavor than just bean.  We'll add this to our rotation!  Serving note:  We like these best with guacamole!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s salsa

this has been a favorite in our family for as long as i can remember.  i use it on tacos, chimichangas, with chips, tamales, enchiladas, burritos, scrambled eggs, taco salads, mexican rice, huevos rancheros, fried potatoes...you get the point.  this recipe is an attempt to get the spices right since mom doesn't measure the ingredients.  (nor do i.) ;)  feel free to adjust seasonings to your taste.  please note: the salsa needs to sit in the fridge for at least 2-3 hours for the flavors to meld.

1. combine all ingredients in a large bowl
2. cover and refrigerate until ready to use
3. put all the ingredients in the jar , cover and shake well
4. stick in the fridge to have on hand whenever you need it
demonstrations.review: This is a nice, very simple recipe.  Takes just a couple minutes to whip up.  It would be perfect for tacos or enchiladas, as it's more of a sauce than a salsa.  Adding some chopped tomatoes and onions would chunk it up, which is what I think I'll do.  Huevos rancheros, as mentioned in the header of the recipe, sound like a winner of a choice for it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced bubble and squeak

a different twist on the great classic ...perfect for those left over veggies, but worth cooking  some for too!

1. mash together the cooked veggies , but not too much
2. heat the oil , add the cumin and chilli flakes
3. once sizzling , add the veggie mix with the spices and press down firmly to brown the underside
4. cook , stirring occasionally , until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good.  I didn't get it to brown as nicely as I'd have liked--my error, I'd guess.   The flavors were like a toned-down take on Indian food.  I used potato, carrot, celery, zucchini, onion, peas broccoli, and cauliflower.  I like strong flavors, so I think I would play around with the spices to get more oomph out of it--probably coriander, garam masala, and other Indian flavors. EDIT:  The leftovers were great!  I smooshed them out thin and put under the broiler at 400 degrees, letting them get browned and crisp on top.  Then drizzled with a sweet hot chutney.  Yum!  Would make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried red lentils

for me, this is comfort food. it only take about a half hour to make, and with some fresh pitas, it's a fantastic meal by itself.

1. rinse the lentils in cold water until the water runs clear
2. add lentils and enough water to cover to a saucepan and simmer until the lentils are tender
3. add water if necessary
4. while the lentils are cooking , caramelize the onions in the vegetable oil in a large skillet
5. combine the curry paste , spices , garlic and ginger in a bowl
6. mix well
7. when the onions are cooked , add the curry mixture to the pan
8. cook over a high heat , stirring constantly for 1-2 minutes
9. stir in the tomat puree and reduce the heat to a simmer
10. cook the curry base until the lentils are ready
11. when the lentils are tender , drain off any exceess water and add the lentils to the curry mixture
12. combine thoroughly and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yum, this was much tastier and easier to prepare than I thought it would be.  I'd never cooked red lentils before, and this came out so delicious.  Hubby didn't like it but I had seconds.  So glad I have leftovers for tomorrow!

target.recipe_text:
homemade pie crust

a nice all purpose pie crust. when i need a crust for a cobbler, i change it to self rising flour because i like lots of crust in my cobblers.

1. put flour into a mixing bowl with the butter
2. using a pastry cutter , cut the butter into the flour
3. add salt and water
4. mix until dough is formed
5. roll out on flat surface
6. bake at 375 degrees until brown
7. prick crust prior to baking for non filled baked pies
target.review: The very fact that I made a decent pie crust says volumes about this recipe!  I can book/bake nearly everything else... but NOT a pie crust.  I didn't have enough shortening, so I used 1/2 butter, 1/2 shortening, and I did do it all in a food processor, but it was still really good!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish apple pie

this is a "no crust" apple pie that my mom used to make. it is great served alone or with vanilla ice cream. this is a "must" for our family at holiday gatherings.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. fill pie pan 3 / 4 full with apples
3. mix 1 / 4 cup sugar and 3 tsp cinnamon
4. sprinkle over apples
5. in saucepan , melt butter and remove from heat
6. add remaining ingredients
7. pour evenly over the apples in pan
8. bake 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  It was a little too heavy on the cinnamon for me (and I love cinnamon), so next time I'll but back on it by a tsp.  Also, I found the sugar directions a little confusing due to only 1/4 Cup of the sugar goes on the apples.  I made the dough and realized that I hadn't added the extra sugar.  I had to scrape it off my apples and add it in.  Still... yummy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy meat   potatoes casserole  our version of hamburger pie

an easy, yummy, satisfying 1-dish meal of seasoned hamburger, mashed potatoes and cheese. you probably have all these ingredients in your house right now! nothing fancy or expensive and it's real good!

1. brown the meat with the onions
2. drain
3. add seasonings and green beans
4. spray a 2 qt casserole dish with pam
5. spoon meat mixture into bottom of dish
6. spread mashed potatoes over meat
7. sprinkle cheese over potatoes
8. lightly sprinkle paprika over cheese
9. bake uncovered in preheated 350 oven for 25-30 minutes until cheese is melted and top of casserole is slightly puffed
