1. cream shortening , butter , and sugars in large mixing bowl
2. blend in eggs and vanilla
3. combine dry ingredients and add to butter mixture
4. mix until well blended
5. stir in chocolate chips
6. drop by rounded teaspoon onto ungreased baking sheets
7. bake at 375 for 7-10 minutes until golden brown
8. i like chewy cookies and if you do too , adjust the baking time accordingly)
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  The cookies turned out perfect.  I did some chewy (for me) and crunchy (for the kids) so everyone was happy.  I love making American recipes for my French friends and they loved them!  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet parmesan chicken

this is real comfort food. a family favorite. if you can, buy the fresh mozzarella. you won't believe the difference and it's worth it. the texture isn't rubbery like the typical mozzarella. i got it from watching an emeril show on the food network.

1. pound the chicken breasts between two slices of plastic wrap until about 1 / 4" thick
2. season with salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken in flour and shake off excess
4. dip in egg / milk mixture , then in breadcrumb / parmesan mixture
5. heat the butter and olive oil in a large deep skillet
6. brown the chicken breasts over medium heat until golden on each side
7. remove to a plate and keep warm
8. add the marinara sauce to the skillet
9. heat to boiling and simmer 10 minutes
10. add the chicken breasts to the sauce and sprinkle parmesan over them
11. place a slice of mozzarella on each piece of chicken
12. cover and simmer about 8- 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the chicken is tender
13. serve with your favorite pasta- we like linguine
demonstrations.review: My family really enjoyed this one!  It was easy too.  I made it exactly as directed with fresh,soft mozzarella.  I served with pasta to my family but I ate it without (trying to watch the carbs)and it was delicious.  Thanks for the recipe.  I will definitely make this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: Just add my voice to the chorus--this was VERY good!  I made as directed (except using milk/vinegar substitute for buttermilk).  I have what I consider to be a "slow" oven and it took 1 hour and 30 minutes to bake at 275.  I agree with other posters that this cake would be very good without the frosting.  Thanks so much for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive mexican stew

my mother gave me this recipe.  she found it while clipping coupons.  it is from s&w.  this is the best stew i have ever eaten and my family requests me to make it quite frequently.  it has become a 

1. cook onion and garlic in oil in large saucepan until tender
2. add cooked chicken , taco seasoning , tomatoes , beans , corn and chilies
3. blend broth and cornstarch
4. add to saucepan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
7. stirring occasionally
8. serve with cornbread for a hearty meal
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  I used two large breasts from a roti-chicken.  I didn't have any cornstarch, so I used a tbsp of flour instead.  Very easy to make and a great option for leftover chicken. Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
whiskey marinade for chicken  pork or steak

i used this marinade on ribeye steaks cooked on the grill.

1. place brown sugar in bowl
2. add whiskey to brown sugar and mix
3. add olive oil to whiskey and brown sugar mixture
4. add remaining ingredients
5. place meat in air tight container
6. pour mixture over meat
7. seal in air tight container
8. shake container
9. place meat with marinade in refrigerator for 3 hours to overnight
10. cook meat on grill
target.review: This is so yummy! I halved the recipe for 4 chicken thighs and used lite (low sodium soy sauce), 1t salt, 1t garlic powder marinated chicken thighs for 6hrs, and baked @ 350 degrees (I didn't know if the bourbon would ignite at a higher temp) for ~45 minutes. The salt level was perfect and the meat didn't have an overpowering alcohol taste at all (as other reviewers mentioned, I think the key to avoiding the alcohol taste is to not marinate overnight!). With the changes, this is a definite keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  chicken   greek style

i'm not greek, but love the food. this is my take on one of their dishes. update: after the first two reviews of chicken being a little dry (perhaps breasts too thin), i suggest stacking dinner as follows in the directions:

1. night before dinner , place potatoes in large ziploc bag with olive oil and toss well
2. rinse chicken in cold water and shake off excess water but don't dry
3. place in bowl with garlic and oregano and toss
4. put potatoes on bottom of cooker
5. add chicken , followed by the onions
6. add water and lemon juice
7. sprinkle with seasonings
8. cook on high 5-6 hours or low 8-9 hours
demonstrations.review: This is good. I used a whole chicken, 3 large potatoes, and 3t dried oregano. I also cooked it on low for 8.5 hours.  I didn't use sea salt, just regular salt (no measurement, just by taste). Also, I marinated the chicken in the salt, garlic, pepper, and oregano overnight. The only thing is the chicken could have used more flavor but I don't know what else would have been good to add.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple baked fish

this is a quick and easy recipe.  all ingredients you probably already have on hand.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. lightly grease or spray a 13" x 9" baking dish
3. rinse fish filets and pat dry
4. set them in a single layer in the prepared baking dish
5. in a small bowl , combine melted butter , lemon juice , garlic , sugar , pepper , thyme and parsley
6. stir well
7. pour evenly over fish filets
8. sprinkle with the breadcrumbs
9. bake at 425 for about 20 minutes or until filets are opaque and flakey
demonstrations.review: This is so good! I used 1T lemon juice, 2 cloves garlic, and marinated the fish overnight in everything except the breadcrumbs and butter. Before going in the oven, I added the breadcrumbs and melted about 1T butter (and drizzled over the fish). I would recommend baking for 12-13 minutes then broiling for 3-4 minutes (just to get the crumbs nice and crispy). This is a definite keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
doro wat  spicy chicken stew

posted for the african part of the tour 2005.
check out niter kebbeh, recipe #140755 and berbere, recipe #140767

1. mix lemon juice with salt in a small bowl , and rub over chicken pieces
2. let stand at room temperature 30 minutes
3. heat oil in a large , heavy or non-stick skillet and add onions
4. simmer over moderate heat about 5 minutes , until onions are beginning to soften
5. stir nitir kebbeh into skillet and heat until melted
6. add garlic , ginger , fenugreek , cardamom , berber and paprika
7. stir well after each addition
8. cook , stirring , over low heat for about 5 minutes
9. pour in wine and water , bring to a boil , and simmer uncovered for five more minutes , until mixture is beginning to thicken
10. add chicken to sauce , turning to coat on all sides
11. cover tightly , lower heat and simmer 15 minutes
12. pierce holes all over the eggs with a fork , then add to the sauce
13. cover and simmer another 15 minutes on low heat , until chicken is cooked through
14. serve with injera check my recipe or rice
demonstrations.review: This recipe was okay but no one really cared to have it again. I used my own recipes for berbere and spiced butter. It seems like there's too much dry spices, I had to add almost a cup of water extra so that the sauce didn't seem grainy. It was also  bitter (maybe from all the paprika in this recipe and the berbere) so I added about 2.5t of sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot indonesian beef or pork

created for my crock pot and very easy to make! indonesian food is very much part of the dutch cuisine and food culture and goes back to colonial days, it is very popular in the netherlands. this is good when just made but even better the day after or after freezing. add as many chilies or sambal to bring it up to your own desired spiciness. if you cannot get lime leaves sub with some lime zest, it's not the same but it's the best substitute.

1. put all ingredients in your food-processor except the meat , oil and the lime leaves
2. process until almost like a paste
3. heat the oil in a large frying pan and fry the onion mixture on medium heat for approx 5 minutes
4. turn up the heat and add the meat , stir and fry for another 5 minutes
5. transfer to the crock pot , add the lime leaves and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours , depending on your crock pot
6. when done taste and add more sambal if desired
demonstrations.review: I wasn't sure how to rate this. On one hand, I thought that the pureed sauce was smelled fabulous and delish before it was cooked but after cooking in the crockpot (I used beef but no sambal or lime leaves), the result was very bland/boring. So I felt like rating the stew a 3 but the sauce was a 5 (I made more and mixed some with ground beef, breadcrumbs, and egg to make a meatloaf - which was fab!). So I think the cook time kills the sauce/flavor, but it's definitely a keeper. Maybe I'll try to make this dish over the stove instead.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken

this is a simple recipe for chicken. the recipe comes from a lable on a can of butterball low sodium chicken broth.

1. in a bowl , combine chicken broth , cornstarch , mustard and dill weed
2. mix well and set aside
3. heat butter in large skillet
4. saute chicken and onion until lightly browned
5. slowly add chicken broth to chicken , stirring constantly over medium heat , bring mixture to a boil
6. reduce heat and cook until slightly thickned
7. pour chicken mixture over hot cooked noodles and toss , serve
demonstrations.review: I made this in my crockpot using 1t dry dill, 1.5t dry mustard, 2 potatoes, 2c chicken stock, no butter or egg noodles and cooked on low for 8 hours and put the cornstarch in during the last 10 minutes. This really is delicious!

target.recipe_text:
healthy peanut butter balls

these don't have chocolate, but they have flax, oat bran, rolled oats etc.  my 3 yo helps me make these and can easily take a few out of the fridge when he's hungry.

1. in a large bowl , mix together all ingredients
2. you may have to mix by hand
3. i've found it helps to mix with your hands much like kneading dough
4. it's a little dry , so you may have to add a tiny bit of milk or oil to keep it together
5. roll into 1-inch balls and store in airtight container in the fridge
6. you may roll them in wheat germ or powdered sugar if you like
target.review: I have made these three times now and I really really like them. The first time I made them I followed the recipe and I found them really dry. Still good, but definitely dry. I've modified the ingredients only slightly and I love the way they turn out now. I only use 1 cup of flour and I increase the peanut butter to two cups. I also found the addition of a little cinnamon and vanilla delightful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy pumpkin pasta

a delicious recipe for pumpkin that's not a dessert! i usually make my own pumpkin puree in the blender with a little water. this dish is mild and warming; my kids like it because it looks like mac and cheese!

1. in a large skillet , saute the onion and garlic in butter , over medium heat , until soft , not brown
2. whisk in the pumpkin , broth , creams and seasonings to taste
3. simmer 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. meanwhile , boil the pasta in salted water until al dente
5. drain pasta and stir into pumpkin , simmering 2-3 minutes more until thick
6. stir in parsley and garnish with romano , more parsley and pumpkin seeds if desired
demonstrations.review: This has become a new comfort food for me. My husband detests pumpkin but loved this dish. He even requested left overs for his lunch! I used homemade chicken stock, used half & half in place of cream, and omitted the parsley (didn't have any). Also, I added 1lb of turkey breakfast sausage. I think this dish would be great with peas or broccoli & cauliflower for a more rounded meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco cheesecake

this appetizer proves that cheesecake is not just for dessert. very good and the presentation of this is impressive. enjoy! helpful hint: when cutting or seeding hot peppers, use rubber or plastic gloves to protect your hands and avoid touching your face. prep time includes overnight refrigeration.

1. sprinkle bottom of greased 9-inch springform pan with cornmeal
2. set aside
3. in mixing bowl , beat cream cheese until smooth
4. add the taco seasoning , sour cream and salsa
5. stir in the eggs , pepper jack cheese and chilies
6. fold in olives
7. pour over cornmeal
8. place pan on a baking sheet
9. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until center is almost set
10. cool on a wire rack for about 10 minutes
11. carefully run a knife around edge of pan to loosen
12. cool for 1 hour
13. refrigerate overnight
14. remove sides of pan
15. spread sour cream over top and sides of cheesecake
16. arrange olives , onions , tomatoes and jalapeno slices on top in a circular motion
17. i do tomatoes on the outer edge , then green onion , jalapeno , then scatter black olives randomly , within the circle
18. serve with assorted crackers
demonstrations.review: I made this for a large family BBQ and it was a hit. I served this with frito scoops. I did find this a tad bit salty for my taste, especially with the chips. Next time I will use a homemade taco seasoning with less salt rather that a store bought packet. Thanks for a great way to enjoy a cheesecake that's not sweet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken tortilla soup

this recipe has been a huge hit with everyone who has ever tried it. we make it almost weekly, and the leftovers are eaten immediately. it is also very healthy! it is a little spicy, so if you don't have too much of a tolerance for spicy foods, you may choose to leave out the seeds of the jalapeño. if you love spicy, like we do, extra cayenne pepper adds even more zing. enjoy!

1. saut onion , garlic , jalapeo and green pepper with olive oil in a large pot until soft
2. add all the rest of the ingredients to the large pot and bring to a boil
3. after about 15 minutes , remove the chicken breasts and shred
4. return shredded chicken to the pot and simmer an additional 45 minutes
5. serve , topped with crushed tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review: This was very good soup but I did make some changes. I used store bought rotisserie chicken, subbed two Anaheim peppers instead of the green pepper, added a can of drained, rinsed, black beans, added 1/2c uncooked brown rice (really couldn't tell though) and I used 6c of homemade chicken stock. Also, I doubled the spices, as I thought it was a little blah with how it was written. All in all, this is a very yummy and satisfying soup. Thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta fazool   pasta and beans with sausage

this is a delicious dish that includes beans, pasta and sausage meat all in one, topped with cheese then baked in the oven, it's a very popular italian dish and there are many versions of this recipe, this one is a family favorite, i hope you enjoy this as much as my family does! --- if you prefer a dryer mixture then drain the tomatoes, ziti pasta works well in place of penne, please adjust the cayenne pepper to suit heat level, prep time includes cooking the pasta.

1. set oven to 400 degrees f
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan
3. cook the pasta until just al dente
4. drain , do not rinse and immediately toss with 1-2 tbsp oil to prevent sticking
5. set aside
6. in a large fry pan , saut the sausage , ground beef , onion , garlic , dried oregano and thyme , over med-high heat , until the sausage and the ground beef are brown , crumbling with a fork while cooking
7. add in the undrained tomatoes , tomato paste and the cayenne pepper
8. simmer for 5-6 minutes
9. add in the kidney beans , and heat through
10. season with salt and pepper
11. add in the cooked pasta , parmesan cheese and parsley
12. toss to combine
13. transfer the mixture to a prepared baking dish
14. top with grated cheese
15. bake for 25 minutes , or until cheese melts and the mixture is hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: I really really liked this. I used mild itailan turkey sausage. My store doesn't have hot turkey sausage. I should have upped the pepper to make up for this. I used a whole small can of tomato paste instead of trying to find another way to use it all up. I accidently bought mozzarella instead of provolone. Very very good. I have been having leftovers all week for lunch amd have enjoyed every bite, especially the cheesy top :) Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gg s lace cookies

my grandmother had two cookies she was famous for...this is one of them.  they are crunchy, rich, fancy and almost a bit like brittle candy.  these are sandwich cookies and great for parties and having with tea.

1. place butter , shortening , syrup and sugar in the top of a double boiler and bring to a boil over direct heat
2. remove from heat and blend in flour and nuts
3. drop by teaspoonfuls on a greased , foiled line cookie sheet
4. bake at 325 degrees for 8-10 minutes
5. cool slightly before removing from sheet
6. place chocolate in new pan and melt over double boiler
7. when almost melted , remove from heat and stir until melted
8. brush one cookie with chocolate and cover with another
9. refrigerate til set
demonstrations.review: I really liked these. The flavor reminded me a bit like almond rocca. My cookies didn't turn out very round so I didn't make sandwiches out of them, I just brushed each one with chocolate. Instead of using walnuts I used almonds. To the chocolate mixture I added a little vanilla and some milk to make it a little creamer. I will definitely make these again.

target.recipe_text:
my own cube steak and gravy

this recipe is a old family favorite that i get asked to make at least twice a month and serve with my cream potatoes.

1. in a bowl or plastic bag add flour , salt , onion powder , garlic powder and black pepper
2. add cubed steak in flour mixture and coat well
3. heat oil and butter in a large frying pan
4. add cubed steak and brown on both sides for 15 minutes
5. remove cubed steak and drain grease out of pan , leaving some dripping grease in pan
6. add can of mushroom soup , water and heavy whipping cream or milk to the pan drippings and mix well
7. add cubed steak back to pan and simmer on low heat for 30 minutes
8. turning cubed steaks once during simmering
target.review: I made this last night for dinner, and everyone, including my picky teenage son, really loved it. It was relatively simple, used ingredients I had on hand, and got rave reviews from the family. I call that a success!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno chicken wraps

i've been playing around with this recipe from taste of home back yard grilling and think i've got it right for our taste.  this is so good, it can be a meal in itself.  it's a little heat intense, but we like it that way.  we loved the combination of spices.  hope you try it.

1. cut chicken into 2 in strips that will fit the size of your pepper
2. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the garlic powder , onion powder , pepper , seasoned salt and paprika
3. add chicken and shake to coat
4. place a chicken and onion strip in each jalapeno half
5. wrap each pepper with a slice or two of the shaved smoked ham , enough to cover the entire pepper and place on baking sheet
6. you will need toothpicks if you use bacon or the prosciutto
7. preheat oven to 350 degrees
8. bake peppers for 20-25 minutes or until the ham is slightly browned and chicken juice runs clear
9. you can also grill these:
10. spray your grill with pam
11. grill peppers uncovered , over indiredct medium heat for 20-25 minutes or until chicken juices run clear and ham is slightly brown
12. serve with blue cheese or ranch dressing
13. for a variety , try sprinkling some italian bread crumbs on top before adding the ham it adds to the flavor
demonstrations.review: I have made these twice for parties and they have been devoured! The first time I made exactly by the recipe, but the second time I made some changes. I did saute the onion the 2nd time (we like that better)and I stuffed a tiny bit of pepper-jack cheese into the mix because everything is better with cheese! Also, I wrapped some in ham, some in bacon. Next time I will use a leaner bacon, but other then that this is a GREAT recipe. Oh, and for what it's worth, I cook them and then stick in my crock pot on the warm or low setting and keep them toasty warm...and it gives them a roasted, tenderness that everyone seems to really enjoy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
daytona wings    baked teriyaki style chicken wings

growing up in a family of race fans, watching the daytona 500 on tv was something we always looked forward to. mom always made these wings to snack on during the race. once upon a time these were called wing dings, but somewhere along the way they were renamed daytona wings.

1. combine all ingredients except the wings in a large pitcher
2. mix well
3. place chicken wings in single layer in a 9" x 13" pan
4. pour the liquid mixture over the wings
5. marinate at least 2 hours , flipping wings once
6. keep wings refrigerated while marinating
7. bake at 350 degrees for 1 1 / 2 hours
8. flip once during baking
demonstrations.review: Made these last night for our Friday Night Bonfire and they were a hit with everyone. They were super easy to fix. I bought one of those 4 lb. bags of frozen chicken wings and mixed up the marinade and poured it in the bag the wings came in (still frozen) and then left them to marinate and thaw in the fridge until the next day when I cooked them. The taste was fantastic! Will absolutely be making these again. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dads sausage  peppers and onions

my dads recipe, personally i can't get enough of this, very easy and fast too. it uses the jars of red peppers along with fresh.

1. remove casings from sausage
2. cook and crumble till brown in a large pot along with fresh bell pepper , onion and garlic
3. chop jarred red peppers smaller and add to sausage with their juice
4. simmer on low
5. prepare the linguini according to package instructions , drain
6. add to sausage mixture and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night. I had the ingredients on hand, and it was a relaxed Saturday evening. I didn't want to extend myself too much in the kitchen...so I put this together in just a few minutes, fixed some bruschetta to go along with, and it was excellent. I'm adding this to my "keeper" file!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini muffuletta kabobs

my aunt mary alice made these yesterday for a puppy shower we held at her house.  they were very yummy!

1. layer 1 slice each of smoked ham , provolone cheese , and genoa salami
2. tightly roll up , and slice into 4 equal pieces , repeat procedure 5 times
3. thread 24 wooden skewers with 1 of each: pepperoncini salad pepper , meat-and-cheese roll , 1 -inch-long roasted red bell pepper , and pimiento-stuffed spanish olive
4. place in a 13- x-9-inch baking dish
5. pour dressing over skewers , and chill 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for our weekly bonfire party last night and everyone seemed to really enjoy them...there weren't any left at the end of the evening and that's usually a good sign that they were a hit! When a recipe is simple, takes just a few ingredients, and everyone likes it, I add it to my keeper list! Thanks for a neat recipe :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cabbage roll casserole

yummy and less work than the real cabbage rolls.  there is no rice in this recipe, because i don't like rice in my cabbage rolls.

1. spary crock pot with nonstick cooking spray
2. crumble the raw ground turkey and spread along bottom of crock pot
3. add the onions , green pepper , garlic , salt , pepper , thyme and cabbage
4. pour the diced tomatoes over top
5. mix the sugar into the tomato sauce and pour over everything
6. if you like more sauce , add another 8-oz or 15-oz can of tomato sauce
7. cover and cook on low for about 8 hours or on high for about 4 hours
8. when done , remove lid and stir to mix well
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night. I only had regular ground beef and I was afraid there'd be a boatload of grease if I didn't modify for that, so I precooked the meat about 70% in the microwave prior to adding it to my crockpot. Other than that I followed the recipe exactly and both my husband and I loved it. It was simple, uses a lot of fresh handy ingredients, smelled lovely cooking and tasted wonderful. Would have been great with rice, but we currently have a lot of squash and zucchini coming from the garden so we grilled some of them and made that our meal. Lovely, just lovely!

target.recipe_text:
green beans  black eyed peas salad

nan

1. steam and drain the green beans and allow them to cool completely
2. drain and rinse the black eyed peas
3. combine all ingredients and mix well
4. may be served chilled
target.review: This was so simple and good!  I only had frozen cut green beans and I ommitted the parsley.  I let it sit at room temperature for about an hour and the flavor just kept improving.  It was light and refreshing, and I think it would be great with fresh green beans.  Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style turkey burgers

the best turkey burgers i have ever tried .... i freeze left-overs, and heat in the microwave later ...

1. combine all the ingredients in a large bowl
2. form into 4 patties , then grill
3. i have served this on regular burger buns with tomatoes and mayo , and on pita with tahini , tomatoes and lettuce
demonstrations.review: I made this exactly as is except I used 1 Tb fresh oregano, 1 Tb fresh parsley and omitted the dried basil.  I served on pita bread with tzatziki, red onions, tomatoes and lettuce and ended up removing it from the pita and eating it with just tzatziki.  The other ingredients just detracted from the burgers which were great on their own!  This is so good and will definitely become a regular recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb hungarian mushroom soup

although this recipe is easy to make, it has a great, complex taste-and it's low carb too. my family loves it, and i hope you do too.

1. melt butter over medium heat , using a large pot
2. add onions and saute for 5 minutes
3. add mushrooms and saute for 5 more minutes
4. stir in the chicken broth , paprika , soy sauce and dill weed
5. reduce to low , cover and simmer 15 minutes
6. pour heavy cream into soup and blend well
7. simmer , covered , for 10 more minutes
8. stir in salt , pepper , lemon juice and sour cream
9. heat through for 4 or 5 minutes
10. serve garnished with fresh parsley
demonstrations.review: This soup was a nice change from your standard creamy mushroom soup.  I only used 1 can of chicken broth (about 1.5 cups) and milk, because I didn't have any cream.  I added slightly more sour cream to compensate.  It was delicious!  The only change I will make next time is to chop the mushrooms.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsukimi udon  full moon udon

literally translated, tsukimi means "viewing the moon". the egg in this dish represents the "full moon" surrounded by "clouds" of noodles. it is traditionally served in the autumn but i love it all year long. for some reason, i find it very romantic.lol.

1. add noodle to a pot filled with boiling water
2. stir and , as soon as water begins to boil again , add 1 / 2 cup of the cold water
3. bring back to a boil and add remainder of cold water
4. cook noodles until al dente , rinse under lukewarm water and drain
5. very thinly , diagonally slice enough of the leeks to equal about 2 tbsp
6. , using the white part only
7. add chicken broth , soy sauce , mirin , sugar and salt to the pot and bring to a boil
8. divide noodles among 4 oven proof bowls
9. add the sliced leeks to the noodles and pour the hot broth over
10. break an egg in the center of each bowl and bake in a preheated 350f [180c] oven for a few minutes , just enough to cook the egg
11. garnish with sliced green part of leeks and sprinkle with pepper
demonstrations.review: This was so quick, easy and delicious!  I made a few changes to simplify it a bit.  I cooked udon noodles per package directions until al dente and rinsed with cool water.  I simmered 2 cans chicken broth, 6 Tb soy sauce, 2 Tb dry sherry, 2.5 tsp sugar and the whites from 1 bunch of scallions.  I added the cooked noodles and poached the eggs in the noodles and broth while covered until just set.  I garnished with green onions and Asian chili powder.  SUPER EASY AND GOOD!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s  ramadan  sandwiches

yummy breaded sandwiches my mom made during ramadan. can be served as an appetizer, but use a small cutter. use different fillings if you like, next time i plan to try salami, cheese and salsa .. can be fried, baked or broiled, whatever you prefer ..

1. cut out a circle out of the bread slices
2. shred the chicken breast into small pieces
3. prepare the sandwiches: spread with mayo , layer with chicken , tomato and lettuce
4. press down the sandwich using your hand , this makes the next step easier
5. dip into the egg , then the breadcrumbs
6. be sure to cover the sides of the sandwich as well
7. fry in a little oil until golden-brown
8. can be baked or deep-fried as well
demonstrations.review: I made with chopped turkey, tomatoes and mayo.  They were pretty good, and I will definitely make circular grilled sandwiches in the future.  They seemed to fry more uniformly without the crusts.  It was fun to try, but I donâ€™t think I will be breading the sandwiches in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa with tomatoes and white beans

a polish-italian quick fix main dish!

1. heat oil or butter in a large skillet , add kielbasa and cook over medium high heat until lightly browned , remove with slotted spoon
2. reduce heat to medium , add onions and cook until transparent
3. reduce heat to low , add garlic and herbs and cook 1 minute
4. add kielbasa , tomatoes and white beans , bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I did not add oil/butter and I cooked the meat, onions and garlic together.  Other than that, I made exactly as written and it was VERY good!  Normally I am not a big fan of rosemary, and I almost substituted thyme, but I am glad I did not.  As others have written, the flavors blended well and the sauce was delicious.

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: Very good!  A new favorite around here. I used olive oil instead of the margarine and it resulted in crisp on the outside just like the fried ones.  We topped with sour cream and had some Mexican rice on the side.  We will have again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
martha s blue ribbon sugar cookies   christmas

these cookies are by far "the best" sugar cookies i have ever had, and the amazing flavor is in the secret ingredient :)  i guarantee if you do make them, you will never use another recipe.  try them and see for yourself! they are delicious plain or decorated with frosting, or glaze and holiday jimmies or sprinkles or colored sugar granules. you can substitute lemon or lime peel in place of the orange peel if you wish.  they are all awesome!  you can easily double this recipe to make a larger amount of cookies for the holidays!  the amount of cookies really depends on the size of the cutters you use, so it is only a guesstimate.  the cooking time is for 2 sheets of cookies.

1. in a large mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar until well mixed
2. add 2 eggs to the creamed mixture
3. mix well
4. in another large bowl , mix sifted flour , baking powder and salt together
5. add to creamed butter mixture
6. mix well
7. add in grated orange rind , and mix well
8. make into a ball , and chill in bowl covered with saran wrap , for at least 2 hours , or overnight in the refrigerator
9. when ready to bake preheat the oven to 350
10. with a floured rolling pin , roll out the dough to about 1 / 4" thick on a very lightly floured surface
11. make into desired shapes using cookie cutters
12. if you don't have cookie cutters , you can use the bottom of a glass instead
13. brush off any excess flour before putting them on the cookie sheet , if there is any
14. place cookies on ungreased cookie sheet about 2" apart
15. you may use parchment paper if you like
16. bake for 8 minutes
17. let cookies cool on wire racks
18. decorate
19. store in a covered plastic container , or cookie tin
demonstrations.review: The cookies themselves were delicious but were messy looking due to runny icing that took forever to harden and in the meantime dripped down the sides of the cookies and ruined the looks.  I ended up putting them on my Christmas dessert table instead of giving them to coworkers and neighbors as planned.  I will be looking for another good icing that really does harden for the next batch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s chunky garlic mashed potatoes

oh man, these are a comfort food that goes with just about anything!  i have been known to eat them by themselves :)  this is definately one you will want to add to your recipe collection!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cut the top of the garlic bulb , and place on the middle rack in the oven
3. bake until bulbs start to pop out of the skins , about 20-25 minutes
4. after the garlic bulb is roasted in the oven , remove , and squeeze the bulb , and the garlic will pop out of each finger
5. put roasted garlic pieces into a dish , and mash , or chop up fine
6. set aside
7. meanwhile:
8. while the garlic is roasting , cook potatoes in a lg
9. pan , just covering with water for about 25 mins
10. , or until fork inserts easliy when inserted
11. drain well , put cover on , and set aside
12. to drained potatoes , add roasted garlic , butter , sour cream , salt , and pepper
13. mash with a hand masher
14. i use a rubber spatulda to break up potatoes a little more
15. you don't want them completely mashed like regular mashed potatoes
16. serve
demonstrations.review: These were so good with our pork chops and coleslaw!  These mashed potatoes are filled with garlicy deliciousness that we all totally enjoyed!  With a little salt and pepper when serving they were the bomb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mimi s raspberry and lemon muffins with streusel topping

this was given to me by my daughter several years ago and has been an a+++++ favorite of ours.  it has a hint of lemon and chocked full of raspberries.  the streusel topping just makes the whole thing come together as a super, yummy muffin.

1. in a small bowl combine yogurt , oil , lemon juice , and egg whites
2. blend well
3. in a medium bowl combine the 1 1 / 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup of sugar , baking powder , lemon peel , and salt
4. mix well
5. stir in frozen raspberries
6. add yogurt mixture to flour mixture stirring just until dry ingredients are moistened--one direction only for muffins
7. line muffin tins with cupcake papers
8. spoon batter evenly into the papers
9. in a small bowl make the streusel topping using the 1 / 4 cup sugar , 2 tablespoons flour , and 1 tablespoon butter , using a fork till crumbly
10. sprinkle evenly over batter in muffins tins before baking
11. bake at 400 degrees for 16-20 minutes or until muffins are golden brown
12. immediately remove from pan and serve warm
demonstrations.review: Lovely and delicious muffins that I have now made more times than I care to count!  I made these for a bake sale and they were one of the first things to go.  My grandchildren love them and request them when they come to stay for the weekend.  I love that they are so flavorful, and easy to make.  You are right up there with Kittencal as far as good recipes go Mimi... I hope others try all your recipes!  I plan to :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s mexican meatloaf

i love meatloaf, and love creating new ones to try.  this is one that i created with a mexican twist in mind...  it is just wonderful, and is a winner for sure!

1. mix the hamburger , minced onions , bread crumbs , beaten egg , and italian seasoning together well with your hands
2. add in the ketchup , 1 / 2 the can of tomato sauce , and 1 / 2 the can of ro-tel tomatoes
3. mix well
4. put 1 / 2 the mixture into an oven-proof baking pan , making a square or a circle , whichever you prefer
5. cover the top of the meat mixture with a generous amount of cheese , not coming quite to the edge
6. top the cheese with the rest of the hamburger mix , and pat down to make a loaf
7. press the sides together a little so the cheese won't drip out when cooking
8. mix the tomato sauce and ro-tel tomatoes together and spread on top of the meatloaf
9. bake in a 350 oven , for about 30 minutes before taking it out , to drain off the juices in the pan
10. put back in oven for 30 more minutes then take out , and cover to top of the meatloaf with the rest of the cheese
11. put back in the oven , and watch carefully for the cheese to melt on top
12. remove , cut , and serve
demonstrations.review: We all agree that this meatloaf rocks!  My kids and I have had it a few times and they eat every bite every time I make it!  I have to say it is very very good and I just love it.  The combination of flavors really adds to the overall taste and the spices are perfectly balanced and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry nut cake

if you like cake and you like strawberries, then you will love this cake.  yum!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. prepare 2 9" cake pans
3. cream shortening and sugar
4. add eggs , one at a time , beating after each addition
5. add vanilla
6. sift dry ingredients together
7. add dry ingredients alternately to shortening mixture with buttermilk
8. stir in nuts and strawberries
9. bake at 350 , for about 30 minutes , or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I tried your cake for Recipe #308627 and it was amazing, so I wanted to try this too.  It is excellent as well!!  I used Strawberry Glaze Icing for the top and layer inbetween the 2 cakes.  We loved it!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s no more watery meringue

using this method will prevent your meringue from "weeping" and will hold up well for days, it's great for lemon meringue pies --- prep time does not include cooling time. cornstarch/water mixture. if you are making two pies and using 6 or more egg whites, just double up and use 2 tbsp of cornstarch, 4 tbsps cold water and 1 cup boiling water, and follow same method.

1. in a saucepan , blend the cornstarch with the water
2. add the boiling water , and cook , stirring until clear and thickened
3. let stand until completely cold
4. with an electric mixer , at high speed , beat the egg whites until foamy
5. gradually add in the sugar
6. beat until stiff , but not dry
7. turn the mixer to low speed
8. add in the salt and vanilla
9. gradually beat in the cold cornstarch mixture
10. turn the mixer onto high again
11. beat well
12. spread the meringue over cooled pie filling sealing the meringue to the pie crust
13. bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes , or until the meringue is lightly browned
target.review: Well I am giving you a 5 star b/c I just love ALL your recipes!!!  Mine turned out watery for some reason...but it was my first ever attempt at meringue, so I am saying user error!  It tastes SOOOOOO yummy!  I left it on the pie..we'll eat it anyways lol  The method for preparing it was simple and I will definintely try this again..it's insanely hot and humid in Savannah so I am thinking that might have something to do with it as well!  Thanks for all of your amazing recipes Kittencal! :)  Oh, I also loved that the chocolate pie I made used 3 egg yolks..so this was perfect for using the whites!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: This was a good recipe for an easy soup!  I did jazz it up a tad for my taste (extra spices, bacon, and cheddar).  I used about 8 palm sized potatoes and it was just perfect for the broth.  I used a whole yellow onion b/c I love onion.  It's a very easy one to throw together and next time I think I'll use the advice of someone else and use a bag of the frozen cubed hashbrowns!  That will make this a seriously quick delicious dinner!  The cream cheese melted in just fine and while it cooked on the stove top I stuck bacon in the oven and they both ended up being done at the same time!  Oh, and my potatoe masher broke so I used the spoon that you can use to lift things out of oil that has the big mesh grate (not fine but a really big one) and mashed it with that and the back of a wooden spoon lol  Thanks for the easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter pumpkins

be a nut and putter your bumpkins. have your own pumpkin patch right in your kitchen. after reading melanie's helpful review, i thought it best to emphasize that you should add sugar to the dough until it is very stiff and leave it at that.

1. melt butter in a large bowl and add a few drops of yellow and red food coloring , until mixture has a nice orange color
2. add the peanut butter and confectioners sugar and mix together until a doughlike consistency is reached
3. shape dough into small balls shaped like pumpkins
4. make ridges on the pumpkins with a toothpick
5. add a small amount of green decorators icing to the top of each pumpkin for a stem
6. refrigerate , if desired , to allow pumpkins to firm
7. serve on a plate lined with toasted coconut and halloween decorated cookies , if desired
8. these also look good on top of cupcakes
demonstrations.review: These were SO easy!!  I was a little afraid to try to make them, but they came out PERFECT!  I used all but maybe 3/4 cup of the powdered sugar.  They were a huge hit at our bake sale!  I think it's important to know to use the side of the toothpick and not the actual tip to make the ridges...it took me a few tries to figure this out lol  But the great thing is if you mess up you can just re roll and start that one over :)  Thanks for this adorable recipe!  Oh, with one recipe I got close to 30 pumpkins...I guess mine were smaller but they were golf ball sized!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soup mix in a jar

i made this for xmas gifts last year and everyone raved about this soup. while similar to other recipes it has additional ingredients in the mix and in the preparation. i had space left in the jars i was using so i added baggies with goldfish crackers and directed that they be removed with the macaroni.

1. place the alphabet macaroni in a sealed plastic sandwich bag
2. in a 1 1 / 2 pint jar , layer the ingredients in the order given
3. attach the following recipe to the jar
4. ingredients
5. 1 jar soup mix
6. 1 pound ground beef
7. 2 garlic cloves , minced
8. 1 can diced tomatoes
9. 3 quarts water
10. fresh ground black pepper to taste
11. directions
12. remove macaroni and set aside
13. in a large pot , brown ground beef with the garlic and drain excess fat
14. add tomatoes , water and soup mix
15. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low , cover and simmer 45 minutes
16. add macaroni , cover and simmer 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are SO cute put together!!!  I couldn't find any barley at my store, which is weird b/c I have bought it before so they must have been out.  So I got red kidney beans instead so it was a pretty color!  I cut the recipe in half like Mrs. Emily said and tried going a tad heavier on the onion.  I did add a tad bit more rice and pasta to each to fill up some of the space.  I'm getting ready to make a pot of this soup for lunch, but wanted to review it at least to this point before I forgot!  Also, one bag of each dried item, 1 lb. each, and a 1 lb box of pasta, 2, 2 oz. containers of onion flakes, and 1 jar of beef bouillon were enough to fill 9 pint jars.  And maybe half a container of Italian seasoning.  Thanks for a great recipe :)  UPDATE:  This was so tasty!  I am so very glad I made it!  I actually used beef stock instead of water and added some Tastefully Simple Onion Onion to the beef while it was cooking.  I definitely won't use kidney beans again...they were just too big compared to everything else and didn't cook the whole way through by the time everything else was done cooking.  I actually think I'll make this recipe again, not only for gift giving!  Thanks again :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot shredded chicken breasts for freezing   oamc

great to have on-hand for recipes. just place as many chicken breasts as you can fit into your crock pot as long as the lid fits on properly. i use bone-in, skin-on but i'm sure boneless, skinless would work too.

1. place the chicken breasts in the crock pot , mix water and spices together and pour over the chicken
2. cook on the low setting for 8-10 hours
3. remove chicken breasts , shred or pull the meat from bones , removing skin
4. place meat in individual freezer bags or containers and freeze until needed for recipes
5. defrost and add to any recipes that call for cooked chicken
6. great for casseroles , quesadillas , pizzas , burritos , pastas , soups , etc
7. or heat with bbq sauce for hot barbecue chicken sandwiches
demonstrations.review: This was so simple, I can't believe I haven't done this before!  I used four very large bone in/skin on chicken breasts, stuck them in my crock pot this morning, and by 5 they were perfect!  I started using forks to pull it apart, once it cooled off I just used my fingers and it was great!!  I yielded 4-2 cup baggies of shredded chicken!  Thanks so much, I wish I knew about this before I had my kids when I worked all the time!! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried sweet potatoes

when we first got married my husband wouldn't go near sweet potatoes. now he asks me to specifically make these for him.

1. cut the potatoes into thin wedges
2. pile them in a bowl and cover them with cold water
3. let rest 15 minutes
4. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
5. coat a baking sheet with vegetable spray
6. set aside
7. drain the potatoes and dry them with paper towels
8. press the potatoes with paper towels to remove all water
9. transfer the potatoes to a large bowl
10. sprinkle the potatoes with oil , tossing the potatoes to disburse it
11. then sprinkle with pepper , salt , paprika and cayenne pepper
12. bake the potatoes at 375 degrees f for 20 minutes
13. turn over the potatoes
14. sprinkle potatoes with garlic and continue cooking for another 15-20 minutes or until crisp and brown
15. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: These are so delicious!  We make them at least once a week.  When I make them into wedges them seem to burn, so I cut mine into about 1 inch wide and 1/2 inch thick fries.  And they usually don't take quite as long to cook this way...maybe half the time.  I especially love the chunks of garlic at the end....Amazing...Will be making these FOREVER! :)

target.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
target.review: This was  definitely a 5 star+ recipe. I made it with all the said ingredients(except coconut, because I didn't have any, also I used chopped macadamia nuts) and it came out just heavenly!  I used the frosting with powdered sugar (not sure if that's icing sugar?) and it was very good as well!  The only thing I would do different next time is leave out the pineapple do to my family's  preference.  This is a keeper forsure!  Thansk for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wonderful filling!!!!  The gravy it's in is just wonderful!  Made this tonight and a big hit!  Who knew you could whip up a homemade pot pie with such little effort.  Big on flavor, thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shake a pie crust

my mother always told me the less you handle dough, the better it will be. this is too simple! and it makes the flakiest crusts for pies.

1. put flour , sugar , salt and crisco shortening in a plastic bowl with a lid
2. seal and wink
3. shake until it sounds like sand
4. add water
5. seal and wink
6. shake until it sounds like a rock
7. roll out for your favorite pie or pastries
demonstrations.review: Really great pie crust!  I have used this several time since I found it here.  Sometimes I use 1/2cup butter 1/2 cup shortening, either way is great and really good for a pot pie! Thanks for sharing, so much better than a premade store bought one!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy enchiladas  beef or chicken

these easy enchiladas are my husband's favorite recipe of mine. because of the many different options, it is very versatile.

1. if using chicken , boil chicken in water
2. then rinse and shred with fork
3. add onion and garlic
4. if using ground beef , brown with onion and garlic , drain
5. add next 7 ingredients
6. in another skillet , heat oil
7. add tortillas , one at a time , for 10 seconds on each side
8. drain on paper towel
9. in 10x13 baking pan , pour just enough enchilada sauce in the bottom to coat the bottom of the pan
10. fill each tortilla with a spoonful of meat mixture
11. cheese , onions , and / or olives can be put inside each enchilada at this time , if desired
12. roll tortilla and place seam side down in pan
13. continue with remaining tortillas
14. pour remaining enchilada sauce over tortillas and top with cheese
15. at this time , pan may be refrigerated for several hours or overnight
16. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
17. top with sour cream
18. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Awesome recipe! I was a little leary seeing the worcestershire sauce on the ingredient list but it came out sooooo goood! The shredded chicken was the best! In fact I"m making the chicken tonight and putting on tostada's, it's that good! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth pumpkin bread

i got this recipe out of a church cookbook many years ago. it is a simple and delicious pumpkin bread. my daughter who hates coconut loves this bread. it is so moist and tasty that it really does melt in your mouth.

1. mix oil , eggs and pumpkin
2. combine remaining ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture
3. bake in a 9x5x3-inch pan at 325 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Holy cow this is really good, even better with some butter on it!  It didn't rise like a normal sweet bread but it is very dense and still very good. Mine cooked well in a stoneware pan 9x13.  I used instant vanilla and doubled cinnamon and added 1 tsp nutmeg. Soooooo good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy fried eggplant  aubergine

no more soggy eggplant!the secret is in the cornstarch.it keeps the eggplant crisp.

1. peel eggplant and slice into 1 / 4 inch slices
2. add salt to egg and beat
3. add cheese to breadcrumbs
4. dip eggplant slices into cornstarch and shake off excess
5. dip into egg
6. press breadcrumb onto slices
7. fry till golden
8. salt to taste
demonstrations.review: I used flour instead of cornstarch because it's what I had and wow!  What a nice change to try something new for dinner.  I just told my 6yr old son it was a cheese stick and he dipped it in the marinara sauce and loved them!  Nice golden brown and crispy is how mine came out, next time I will definetly add some Mozzerella cheese on top and broil for a bit, then it would be even better (agrees my dh).  Thanks for sharing this great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
chocolate  butterscotch  pb rice  krispies treats

born with a rice krispie treat in my hand, you better believe i know my krispies. even if you are not a rice krispie fan, this will become one of your regular "goody" recipes!

1. mix peanut butter , karo syrup , and sugar in a pot , and bring to a slight boil
2. stir until creamy
3. take mixture off the burner , and mix with rice krispies cereal
4. spread mixture in 13 x 9 inch pan
5. melt chocolate and butterscotch chips together in microwave
6. spread melted chips over rice krispie mixture
7. refrigerate until chocolate-butterscotch mixture hardens
8. cut into 2x2-inch squares
9. enjoy !
target.review: This is a recipe our family has been making for years and years.  We call the Grandpa's Krinkles and everyone loves Krinkles.  When we make them we always leave the topping off of one strip along the side for a couple people in the family that are allergic to chocolate.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vietnamese ground pork

posted for zaar world tour 2

1. in a oil on medium heat fry the garlic slices until fragrant remove garlic and set aside , then add the pork and stir until well cooked , and dark , making sure to separate a finely as possible
2. add sugar , and fry until browner in color
3. add msg and fish sauce and taste
4. add crushed pepper , or black pepper if
5. desired
6. add the garlic slices , add 1 / 2 cup of water , and let simmer until water has almost evaporated
7. remove garlic and ginger , and serve with rice
demonstrations.review:
We are on a restricted diet so no MSG or Accent for us, honey instead of sugar.  With changes this was super good...I loved the flavors!  We served this with rice and I wish I had cucumbers to make a slaw or fresh spring rolls to serve with it.  
Will certainly make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy creamy rice pudding

best rice pudding that i have ever tasted. good sprinkled with nutmeg or cinnamon.

1. in a medium saucepan , bring 1 1 / 2 cups water to a boil
2. add rice and stir
3. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 20 minutes
4. in another saucepan , combine the cooked rice , with 1 1 / 2 cups milk , sugar and salt
5. cook over medium heat until thick and creamy , 15 to 20 minutes
6. stir in remaining 1 / 2 cup milk , beaten egg and raisins
7. cook 2 minutes more , stirring constantly
8. remove from heat , and stir in butter and vanilla
9. serve warm
demonstrations.review:
A good standard recipe that tastes perfect.  I was able to make as stated and with alternative sweetners and got wonderful results all three times.

For those wanting to use leftover rice, simply add 2 1/4 cup cooked rice into the milk, sugar, and salt step.  Proceed as before making sure to not skimp on the 15-20 minute cooking time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
milk rice

this is a delicious rice dessert.

1. bring water to a boil in a large saucepan
2. wash the rice and drain it
3. add the rice to the boiling water , and cook for 5 minutes
4. in a separate saucepan , bring the milk to a boil over medium heat
5. remove the cooked rice and drain it
6. slowly drop the rice into the boiling milk
7. lower the heat and add salt , vanilla bean , and sugar
8. cover and simmer 15 - 20 minutes , stirring occasionally , until the milk is absorbed
9. add more milk , if necessary for a tender rice
10. serve warm , cold or room temperature - your preference
demonstrations.review:
Very tasty, perfect for a cool night or breakfast! 

We used Grade B maple syrup instead of sugar (6 TBSP) and also let each person pick a spice to put on their bowl -full (cinnamon and nutmeg are both great choices!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mafe  senegalese beef stew

this traditional stew, with peanuts (groundnuts) can also be made with lamb, chicken or just vegetables.  the amount and heat of the peppers you use can be varied to suit your palate.

1. whisk together peanut butter and stock and reserve
2. season the meat with salt and pepper
3. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
4. brown the meat well on all sides
5. do not crowd the meat
6. saute in batches if necessary
7. remove meat and keep warm
8. add the onion , garlic , peppers , and carrots to the pan and saute until the onions are translucent
9. add the peanut butter and broth mixture , scraping all the brown bits up from the bottom and sides of the pan
10. return the reserved meat to the pan with the tomatoes and their liquid , the thyme and bay leaf
11. stir well and bring to a boil
12. reduce heat to low and simmer , stirring often , for about 1 hour or until the meat is tender
13. taste for seasoning
14. remove the thyme sprig and the bay leaf and discard
15. serve hot over rice
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe.  We upped the veggies a bit, but chopped up fairly find just to help the little ones eat them without complaints (onion, celery, bell peppers, and carrots.)  I wish I had thought to add mushrooms as they would be good with it as well.  I didn't have a chili on hand, so I added 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper (powder form) to the mix.  Starting at step 8 I put everything into a low crockpot for about 3-4 hours.  Very yum served up with brown rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sourdough whole wheat biscuits

this is from one of those other sites. i am always looking for ways of putting more fiber in the diet. usually i mix whole wheat flour and white. these work well with all whole wheat. cooking with sourdough is wonderful and produces great results. hope you enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. spray a cookie sheet with non-stick cooking spray
3. mix all dry ingredients in a medium size bowl
4. cut in the butter and work in starter until well blended
5. turn out onto floured surface and knead gently for 2 minutes
6. roll dough to 1 inch thickness
7. cut into 2-inch rounds with biscuit butter and place on prepared cookie sheet
8. bake for 10 minutes and serve hot from the oven
demonstrations.review:
This is as good as it gets for a whole wheat biscut!  I had ot add a little extra flour, but I know this is because my starter tends to be on the runny side and the weather when I was making them.

They make great hamburger buns in a pinch!

target.recipe_text:
campfire hamburger and beans

although i did make this "car camping", when my sons were young, it is a quick and easy, at home, top of the stove, one skillet dish. sometimes, i use bacon, sometimes not. you might want to use less catsup, sugar, and molasses if you want it less sweet.

1. if using bacon , cut into 1" strips crosswise and saute over medium heat with onions until translucent , then add beef
2. otherwise start with next step
3. cook beef and onions over medium high heat until onions are done , about 5-10 minutes
4. drain fat
5. add remaining ingredients , stir , mixing throughly , and turn heat to low
6. continue cooking until hot and bubbly , then serve in bowls
target.review: These were very good and simple baked beans.  I made them when we went up to the mountains.  I prefer the ones with a bunch of different beans but my husband likes ones like these that just have one kind in.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared salmon with balsamic glaze

i saw this on sara's secrets and couldn't wait to try it! the sauce brings out the sweetness in the fish. enjoy!

1. stir together balsamic vinegar , water , lemon juice , and brown sugar in a small bowl
2. pat salmon dry and season with salt and pepper
3. heat oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium high heat , not smoking
4. increase heat to high , add salmon skin side up , and sear until well browned , about 4 minutes
5. turn fish over and sear until just cooked through , 3 to 4 minutes more
6. transfer salmon to plates and carefully add vinegar mixture to skillet
7. simmer , stirring , until thickened and reduced to about 1 / 3 cup , about 2 minutes
8. spoon glaze over salmon
9. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I am not an expert at cooking fish and especially salmon.  This came out perfect!  I made it for my DH for Valentine's Day. He loved it, though he preferred it without the glaze. I really enjoyed the glaze.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
upside down pepperoni pizza casserole

fun and easy take on pepperoni pizza - one of my sons favorites.  great one-dish meal!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees and prepare baking dish
2. over medium heat , combine the ground beef , onion and garlic in a large skillet until beef is browned
3. add the mushrooms , olives , pepperoni and tomato sauce and heat through
4. pour mixture into prepared baking dish
5. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese
6. top randomly with biscuit pieces
7. bake 15-18 minutes until biscuits are browned and casserole is bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was very good and easy.  I will be making this more in the future. Update: I forgot how delicious this is and easy.  I need to figure out how to get the biscuits done in the middle, maybe cut them smaller.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
autumn spice cupcakes with pumpkin spice frosting

this is an easy, festive recipe for autumn.  i made this recipe with our nursing home residents in celebration of our october birthdays.  they really enjoyed the aroma of the baking cupcakes and frosting them.  we inserted pretzel sticks into the center of each orange-colored frosted cupcake to make them look like little pumpkins.  what fun we had!  this would also be a fun children's project.  enjoy! (note: preparation time does not include time for cupcakes to cool.)

1. cupcakes:
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. sift cake mix into a medium mixing bowl until all lumps are removed
4. then add water , pumpkin and eggs and thoroughly combine with a hand-held mixer
5. spoon batter into muffin pan cups lined with paper liners , filling each cup 1 / 3-full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into center of thickest cupcake comes out clean
7. allow to cool on a wire rack for one hour
8. frosting:
9. in a medium mixing bowl , combine butter , pumpkin , milk , vanilla , cinnamon , nutmeg and cloves
10. add powdered sugar one cup at a time , blending with a hand-held mixer and scraping sides of bowl with a rubber spatula until a smooth and spreadable texture is met
11. if desired , add food coloring for an extra festive orange color
12. frost cooled cupcakes
demonstrations.review: These were very good and full of flavor.  I followed the recipe to a T and they turned out wonderful and were very easy to make.  I thought the frosting was extra special since it had pumkin in it and my son liked the orange frosting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s pizza crust

this is an excellent crust that requires no time to rise. why order out when you can just throw this pizza together?

1. combine yeast and warm water
2. stir until dissolved
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. let rest 5 minutes
5. roll out to size and shape you need
6. bake at 450 for 15 minutes or until golden
7. a couple
8. instead , i add several good shakes of italian seasoning mix
9. use your imagination , this is hard to mess up
demonstrations.review: This is the only pizza crust recipe I use anymore.  It is quick, easy, and turns out right as long as you make sure to prebake it long enough.  Last time I made it I didn't let it bake long enough and then even though I baked it again with toppings on it came out a little soggy.  I like it with the Italian herbs in it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef stuffed green bell peppers with cheese

we had these not too long ago and we both decided that they needed a little more seasoning. we put a little hot pepper sauce on them and they were much better. i would probably include 2 teaspoons in the meat mix the next time that i make them.

1. cut off the tops of green peppers
2. discard seeds and membranes
3. chop enough of the tops to make 1 / 4 cup , set aside
4. cook the whole green peppers , uncovered in boiling water for about 5 minutes
5. invert to drain well
6. sprinkle insides of the peppers lightly with salt
7. in a skillet cook ground beef , onion and 1 / 4 cup chopped pepper till meat is browned and vegetables are tender
8. drain off excess fat
9. add drained tomatoes , salt , worcestershire , and a dash of pepper
10. in a separate pot put water bring to boil add rice cook until rice is soft
11. if needed add more water
12. add rice to beef mixture
13. stir in cheese
14. stuff peppers with meat mixture
15. place in a 10x6x2 baking dish
16. bake , covered in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
17. in the last 5 minutes add any remaining cheese to the top of the peppers
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  I did not add in the chopped peppers but instead saved it for another use.  I also needed to add a little extra water to cook the rice mixture.  My husband said he doesn't usually care for stuffed peppers, but really liked these and that is saying a lot!

target.recipe_text:
buttery shredded beets

a nice mild side dish.  season at table with lemon if desired.
i don't remember where i got this from.

1. using medium grater - grate beets into a skillet
2. sprinkle with seasoning and dot with margarine
3. cover , simmer until tender
target.review: So simple,  but this recipe delivers.  I used 6  beets and 6 tsp of real butter.  It was amazing.  Kinda messy grating the beets (i wore rubber gloves) but well worth it.  Shahana, thank you for posting this great recipe.  Sue

demonstrations.recipe_text:
opal s pumpkin pie

this recipe makes 2- 9" pies.  if you make one large pie instead you will have to add time to the baking to get it done.  this recipe was given to me by opal beebee, several years ago. this is a handed down family recipe. it was once prepared in the white house for one of the former presidents. opal's daughter had served in the national guard and had met a pastry chef who later worked at the white house and called opal to ask for the recipe for thanksgiving dinner at the white house. do not eliminate the heavy cream in the pie...the cream and the amount of spices listed is what makes this pie so special. it is good hot or cold. i never tasted hot pumpkin pie until i tasted this one.  

i found out this past christmas (2009) that this bakes well without a crust as well.

i had to make 3 pumpkin pies to take to my son's home.  i had enough mixture left over make another pie but not enough pie dough for a 4th pie.  so i spray oiled a round casserole dish, filled with mixture and baked.

1. combine first 8 ingredients in a large bowl , mixing well
2. combine the evaporated milk and the heavy cream in a small saucepan
3. heat the milks to the scalding point
4. add scalded milks to the other ingredients , mixing well
5. pour equally into the two unbaked pie shells
6. bake 350 degrees for about 1 hour
7. pie is done when a knife inserted into the middle comes out clean
8. top with desired topping
demonstrations.review: A wonderful, wonderful pumpking pie.  I chose this recipe well before Thanksgivng, and was comforted to see that it was rated as one of the best pumpkin pie recipes on zaar.  I had only made pumpkin pie from Libby's mix before; I was very very pleased with the creamy texture and spice blend.  It was the best pumpkin pie I have ever made.  It even rivals my mom's pie.  (Sorry Mom).  I will be making this for many future Thanksgivings and anytime I want a delicious pie!  Thank you for posting, Carrol, a true treasure.  Sue

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: I know I give a lot of recipes 5 stars, but this one truly deserves it for ease and taste!  It took less than 30 minutes to put together and the aroma of it cooking away in my crockpot drove me into the kitchen all afternoon anticipating.  the flavor was wonderful, the gravy was a great texture.  I served it with rice, but mashed potatoes or noodles would be good too.  Thanks, Buttercup

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best darn sugar cookies ever

i don't care for sugar cookies at all and i thought these really were the best darn sugar cookies ever! these cookies are so light and have a fabulous texture. everyone is sure to love them.

1. cream sugar , butter , powdered sugar , and oil
2. then cream in eggs and vanilla
3. in a separate bowl mix baking soda , cream of tartar , and flour
4. start adding dry ingredients to creamed ingredients less than 1 cup at a time
5. chill in refrigerator at least 2 hours
6. drop 1-2" balls on the cookie sheet
7. if you would like , you can flatten the balls with the bottom of a drinking glass that has been dipped in sugar
8. bake at 350 for 10-12 minutes or until the edges are browned
9. you can also sprinkle on cinnamon and sugar , colored sugar sprinkles , etc
demonstrations.review: Shannon, I don't know about the best darned sugar cookies ever, but the are the best I have ever made.  I made them for an Elementary School Dance.  I didn't roll them and cut, I made balls and flattened them with a sugared glass.  Then I frosted and decorated them with sprinkles.   I haven't taken them to the dance yet but I know the kids will love them.  Thanks for posting such a good recipe.  Sue

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and kielbasa

my husband didn't think he liked cabbage until i served this. the bacon and onion really give this recipe a lot of flavor.

1. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
2. remove bacon
3. crumble , and set aside
4. add next 7 ingredients to bacon drippings
5. cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes , turning cabbage once
6. add sausage and cover and cook an additional 5 minutes or until sausage is heated
7. transfer to a serving dish with a slotted spoon
8. sprinkle with the crumbled bacon
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic!  We love cabbage and kielbasa and I am always on the lookout for a quick weeknight meal.  The bacon, onion, and season salt flavored the cabbage superbly.  I served it with mashed potatoes (my grandson's favorite food).  I will make this again.  Thanks Chef 316618

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applesauce pie

this is dd's favorite pie.  the topping makes this pie wonderful.  if you are looking for that different dessert to take to potluck, picnics for family gatherings give this a try.

1. cook applesauce , raisins and brown sugar slowly for 20 minutes
2. add butter and salt
3. cool
4. beat eggs and add to mixture
5. pour into pie shell
6. bake at 375 for 20 minutes
7. mix sugar , flour , cinnamon and softened butter with a pastry blender
8. sprinkle on top
9. continue to bake another 20 minutes or until golden brown
10. cool before serving
demonstrations.review: I chose this recipe because I had all the ingredients on hand.  I used frozen pie crusts and was able to squeak two pies out of one recipe.  One I am taking ot a PTA function and the other I am keeping from home.  This was super easy to make; and tastes delicious!  A definite keeper.  Thanks, mommyoffour, for posting a great recipe.  Sue

target.recipe_text:
vegetarian tacos

a vegetarian alternative to this mexican favorite. my parents are a little leary of my non-meat dishes, but they love mexican food. and this was a big hit. i was happy...

1. in large fry pan , heat oil over medium heat
2. cook the onion , celery , red or green pepper , jalapeno , and garlic until softened
3. add garbanzo beans , spices , and a couple tsp of salsa
4. stir until heated through
5. i like to fit the taco shells in a baking pan , spoon in filling evenly into the shells and bake in a 300f oven for 5 minutes or so
6. it helps the shells from falling apart when you take the first bite
7. remove from oven and top with your favorite toppings
target.review: Wow these are excellent, great combination.  My Husband does not even like Tacos but he loved these.  My Son's girlfriend is a vegetarian so these worked perfectly.  I also cooked some hamburg for those who missed the meat.  Personally I did not miss it one bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
famous barr s french onion soup

one of st. louis's favorite soup recipes was recently printed in the  post-dispatch.  i remember going to st. louis when i was young and my family  going into the department store's restaurant for this famous soup.  enjoy!  famous-barr's french onion soup

1. peel onions and slice 1 / 8 inch thick , preferably in a food processor
2. melt butter in a 6-quart stockpot
3. add onions
4. cook , uncovered , over low heat for 1 1 / 2 hours , stirring occasionally
5. stir in pepper , paprika and bay leaf
6. saute over low heat 10 minutes more , stirring frequently
7. pour in 6 cans broth and wine
8. increase heat and bring to a boil
9. dissolve flour in remaining 1 can broth
10. stir into boiling soup
11. reduce heat and simmer slowly for 2 hours
12. adjust color to a rich brown with caramel coloring , season with salt
13. refrigerate overnight
14. to serve , heat soup in microwave or on stove top
15. if desired , pour into ovenproof crocks or bowls
16. top with a slice of bread and a sprinkling of grated cheese
17. heat under the broiler until cheese melts and bubbles , about 5 minutes
18. leftover soup can be frozen
demonstrations.review:
Fantastic! The best French Onion soup I have ever made.  It was thick, rich, beautiful colour and the flavour was outstanding.  
I have deleted all other recipes  saved to try............this is the ONLY one I will ever make from now on.
I would not change a thing, why mess with perfection.
