Thank you so much my Husband
could not stop raving.  I can't wait to make this for company.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot water pastry

this is a recipe from an old dutch cookbook. it works out so well.you can use lard or shortening. i suppose you can also use butter too, although i have not tried that yet.

1. put shortening in a medium bowl and boil the water
2. pour water over shortening and blend till all the water is absorbed and the mixture is smooth
3. add the flour , salt and baking soda
4. i put the soda and salt in the first cup of flour and mix in one cup at a time in case you don't need all of the flour
5. usually you do
6. once it is mixed and in one large ball , you can then cut this down to 3 individual balls of dough , wrap in plastic wrap and chill for at least 2 hours
7. if you want a larger pie crust , just do 2 balls of dough
8. if you do not use all the dough it can be kept in the fridge for about a week or so or even frozen
9. bake these pie crusts up as you would any others
10. i usually bake them at 350-400 for 12-15 minutes , or till golden brown
11. follow instructions for double crust fruit pies when using those recipes
demonstrations.review:
Thank you, thank you, thank you 
I always made this pastry when I was first married and lost the recipe.  I always had such luck with it and can't wait to start making it again.  I always used lard but I know I added in probably a teaspoon of  vinegar  to the lard and water which made it creamy.
Always foolproof.
Right on Elaine!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mark bittman s pasta with garlic  tomatoes and anchovies

i'm an anchovy-lover.  if you are one too, you will like this.  if you know an anchovy-hater, don't tell them and i bet they won't even know.  the anchovies completely break down into the sauce.  of course you need excellent anchovies, and that means ones that are packed in olive oil, preferably from italy or spain.

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil and salt it for the pasta -- you should be able to make the entire recipe as the pasta cooks
2. put olive oil in a medium skillet over medium heat
3. a minute later , add garlic and chilies , if using -- cook garlic so it bubbles gently
4. when it is lightly browned all over , add anchovies and cook , stirring occasionally , for about a minute , until anchovies begin to fall apart , then add tomatoes
5. adjust heat so tomatoes bubble nicely , and cook until mixture becomes saucy , about 5 minutes
6. taste and add salt and pepper as necessary
7. meanwhile , cook pasta until tender but not mushy
8. when it is done , drain it , reserving a little cooking water to thin sauce if necessary
9. serve pasta with sauce and parsley
demonstrations.review:
I am not a huge lover of anchovies, except for Ceasar Salad.  My Husband, however, adores them  so I thought I would give this recipe a try.
Well thank you, thank you,  
I will be making this often.
It is just the right balance of flavors.
I was out of parsley so I used fresh basil and it was wonderful.
A definite keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tikka spice mix

hi tikka spice mix is easy to make....maybe you'd want to reduce the quantity as this makes 200g :)

1. the idea is you mix all these together and then keep the powder mixture for when you need it
2. if you couldn't get garlic powder you could replace it with fresh garlic when you added the required amount of mix to a dish
3. i've left the mint out too and it was perfectly ok :)
demonstrations.review:
Excelent spice mixture.
I love it because depending on how hot you like your food you can use accordingly. 
My guys like really spicy food so I can't wait to try this out on them.
I can then sit back and say 
"Oh it's a Jacqui Creation"
Thank you so much for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cream of broccoli soup

this recipe is thick and flavorful. simple, delicious, and quick to make. hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. i have added chicken to this soup, very good

1. melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot , and saut onion , garlic and celery until tender
2. add broccoli and broth
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
4. pure soup or mash with potato masher
5. return to heat
6. in small saucepan , over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter , stir in flour and add milk
7. stir until thick and bubbly , add to soup
8. add cheese
9. stir until melted
10. season with pepper and serve
demonstrations.review:
Just what you need another review on your wonderful soup. 
My Husband & I each brought home 2 heads of broccoli from the store.  Yikes what was I going to do with all that broccoli?
I found your recipe and I am
so thrilled I did.  
Superb flavor.
I used Old White Cheddar cheese because that is what I had on hand, and it was out of this world.  
Thanks Barb.
Joan

target.recipe_text:
baked turkey and jack cheese chimichangas   weight watchers

5 points a serving. ridiculously easy. great with a black bean and corn salad (not included in points.)
please note - this is 9 points with the new weight watchers !!!!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. coat a large skillet with cooking spray
3. coat a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish with cooking spray
4. add turkey to skillet and cook over medium-high heat until lightly browned , about 5 minutes
5. drain any excess liquid from pan and then add beans , 1 3 / 4 cups of salsa , chili peppers , chili powder and scallions
6. cook until heated through , about 3 minutes
7. stir in cheese
8. meanwhile , wrap tortillas in foil
9. warm in oven for 10 minutes
10. assemble chimichangas by spooning about 1 / 2 cup of turkey mixture onto each tortilla
11. fold in sides and roll up
12. place chimichangas in prepared baking dish
13. bake uncovered until tortillas are crisp and browned , about 20 minutes
14. serve each topped with 2 tbsp of salsa and 1 tbsp of sour cream
target.review: Well when I read KHLQuilts comment my heart sank! I am making these tonight!! I went to my WW eTools to check it out, hoping to prove her wrong... and to my surprise, after plugging in the recipe exactly as stated here on the recipe builder, and putting in 8 servings it came out to 4 POINTS PER SERVING!!!! YAY!! Can't wait to try them!!!!! Will be on tonight to give my stars!! *After Eating*  BEST DINNER EVER!!  I WAS IN HEAVEN!!! *Another note*  Wrote this review a year ago!  Before points plus!  For some reason it was saved but never posted!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chris s pueblo green chili sauce

this recipe comes from southern colorado and i have been making it for over 20 years. it is my favorite thing to cook and eat. if you like hot and spicy mexican food, this is a recipe for you! i made it for our friends and it has become a hit here in corpus christi, texas! the great thing is you can also make it hotter or milder, depending on your taste! in pueblo, colorado, we served it over burritos, or enchilada's. my personal favorite way to eat green chile (especially on a cold day) is by placing a hamburger bun in a bowl, add a plain hamburger (with or without cheese), smother it with the green chile sauce, then top it with diced onion and oyster crackers. in colorado we call these green chili sloppers! they are great served with a beer!

1. in large stainless kettle , brown pork in bacon fat or vegetable oil
2. cook on medium heat till meat is slightly pink
3. add diced onion and garlic , cook till soft
4. add flour and stir , browning flour as you would a roux
5. add some of your water if flour is too thick , keep stirring till it bubbles
6. add chicken broth
7. add the rest of the ingredients and bring to a bubble , then turn heat to low
8. cook uncovered for 2-3 hours , stirring occasionally
9. if your chile is too thin , add more flour
10. if your chile is too thick , add more chicken broth
11. taste often and add more spices or peppers to your liking !
12. if you do not like chunks of tomato or peppers , place the rotel , tomatoes and canned diced green chile's into a blender and puree them !
demonstrations.review: I have family in Colorado, and several years ago when my Aunt and her now ex-husband came home to Ohio for a visit, he made us green chili.  He showed me how to make it and I made it once soon after that, but never wrote it down.  This recipe is very similar to what I remember, and it was soooo good!  I didn't use the serrano chilies because I like just a mild heat, and this was still pretty spicy for me!  I made it with your chicken enchiladas and they made a perfect pair.  Thank you so much for this recipe, I can't wait to make it again and again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers stuffed shells

received this from a meeting.  very tasty!  they point value we were told from our meeting leader was 4/serving.  some of the reviews people have recalculated it saying 8.  to be safe, i would refigure it so your comfortable knowing the points.

1. preheat oven 375
2. cook shells until al dente , rinse and set aside
3. mix cheeses , salt , garlic powder , oregano and pepper
4. spread a few spoonfuls of tomato sauce on bottom of 9x13 dish
5. when shells are cool enough to handle , fill each shell with cheese mixture and place in baking dish
6. when all shells are in dish , spoon remaining tomato sauce over shells
7. cover pan and bake for 20 minutes
8. yields about 4 shells per serving
9. servings 6
demonstrations.review: I'm wondering if I did something wrong!!  My filling didn't even fill half of the box of shells, so I had to double the batch, and then all the filling cooked right out of my shells!  It ended up more like a soupy casserole for me. :o(  We still ate it, and still LOVED the flavor.  It makes me sad because I really want to make this again, it was delicious.  Am I really the only one who had this problem???  I double checked the recipe, and followed it to a tee.  Well thanks for posting, and I will try again, hopefully with better results!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake caramel popcorn

easy to make, no-bake caramel popcorn!! even kids can make it! takes less than 15 mins

1. pop the microwave popcorn and set aside in a pan or bowl lined with wax paper
2. combine butter , brown sugar and salt together in a saucepan
3. heat until completely melted
4. pour over popped corn immediately
5. may be eaten warm or cool
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Perfect for what I was looking for!  I wanted caramel corn NOW not in an hour or two!!  My family gobbled up the whole bowl so fast I had to make another!!  If you are looking for a quick easy way to get a caramel corn fix, this is the way to do it!!  Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers chicken pot pie

4-6 points per serving

1. preheat oven to 400
2. spray 8x8 casserole dish with cooking spray
3. mix together veggies , chicken and soup
4. pour into casserole dish
5. in another bowl , mix bisquick , milk , and egg
6. pour over top of chicken mixture
7. bake for 30 minutes , or until crust is golden
8. 6 servings=4
9. 5 points
10. 4 servings=6
11. 5 points
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  Like other people, I used the cream of chicken because we are not mushroom fans, and I also seasoned it with salt, pepper, garlic powder and onion powder.  I won't use frozen vegetables next time either because we just don't care for them.  BUT OTHERWISE  sooooo good.  Creamy, good crust, so fast and EASY... doesn't taste like it's low in points and doesn't taste like it's that easy!!!  Will make VERY OFTEN!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula s mexican rice

this is a meatless rice dish. it is very good and pretty spicy.

1. saut onion , butter , celery
2. add all other ingredients
3. bring to boil , reduce , cover and cook until liquid is absorbed about 20 minutes
4. transfer to serving dish and add cheese
demonstrations.review: This was very good rice.  I've always wanted to make my own mexican rice from scratch rather than buying the packaged kind.  I was very happy with how this turned out, used regular Rotel and still too spicy for the kids to eat, but I loved it!  Didn't have the worcestershire sauce so just didn't put it in, will try it next time though!

target.recipe_text:
lemon cilantro eggplant dip

the light, nutty flavor of tahini, an essential ingredient in hummus, pairs perfectly with rich roasted eggplant in this delicious mediterranean dip.  from good housekeeping.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. line a 15 1 / 2" by 10 1 / 2" jelly-roll pan with nonstick foil
3. place eggplant halves , skin-sides up , in foil-lined pan
4. wrap garlic in foil and place in pan with eggplants
5. roast vegetables 45 to 50 minutes or until eggplants are very tender and skin is shriveled and browned
6. unwrap garlic
7. cool eggplants and garlic until easy to handle
8. when cool , scoop eggplants' flesh into food processor with knife blade attached
9. squeeze out garlic pulp from each clove and add to food processor with tahini , lemon juice , and 3 / 4 teaspoon salt
10. pulse to coarsely chop
11. spoon dip into serving bowl
12. stir in cilantro
13. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours
14. serve dip with pita and vegetables
target.review: This was good, but I don't know if I'd say amazing. My husband, who hates eggplant even liked it (before I told him it was eggplant!) I used fresh parsley instead of cilantro but will try again as written. I was more generous on the lemon juice as I like things lemony! Would be very good on top of falafel instead of hummus.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornmeal blender waffles

cornmeal just adds that extra crispness that i love so much! i love these with some good quality all-fruit preserves. yum!

1. preheat your waffle maker and set oven temp to"warm"
2. place all ingredients in a blender container
3. cover and process at med-high speed until dry ingredients are moistened
4. do not overblend
5. pour 1 / 2 cup batter over grids
6. close waffle maker gently and bake until steam no longer escapes
7. remove waffle with a fork and place on baking sheet to keep warm in the oven
8. garnish as desired and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
These were delicious! Probably the best waffles I have ever made. I did however alter the recipe to make it lower in fat and sugar. I doubled all the ingredients to make more, EXCEPT ---
- Used 1 cup skim milk and 1/2 cup fresh squeezed orange juice
- Used 1/4 cup oil and 1/4 cup applesauce for other half
- Only used 2 tsp sugar instead of doubling it
The only problem was my blender wasn't really big enough (or powerful enough) to accommodate twice the ingredients. Maybe I need a bigger blender or could just do it in bowl?
Served with nonfat plain yogurt and strawberries! YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
demonstrations.review: I make minestrone soup without a recipe but it always seems to be missing something. This was just about perfect! I didn't have frozen green beans so used a can, and didn't have celery. I chopped the carrots finely instead of shredding because I was too lazy! The spices were perfect but I let it sit a little long and the broth was absorbed so next time I'll add more or eat it more quickly! Very Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yellow split pea dal

"dal" in indian cooking refers to porridge like dishes made from dried legumes, usually split peas or lentils. dal is often served in a thinned state as a soup, but equally often it will be a thick, hearty side dish. this is a thick dal, comprehensive and highly spiced enough to be the focus of a meal. from one of the moosewood cookbooks. prep time includes 2 hours for cooking dried split peas. serve with rice and raita.

1. place split peas in a saucepan with 5 cups of water
2. cover and bring to boil
3. lower heat and simmer very slowly , partially covered until soft melt butter in large skillet
4. add crushed garlic , cumin , mustard seeds , turmeric , and cinnamon
5. cook , stirring , over medium heat for 3 minutes
6. add cooked peas and stir until everything is well mixed
7. keep stirring and cooking as you gradually add an additional 1 / 2 cup water
8. you want a creamy consistency but not soup
9. add salt , black and red peppers
10. cook and stir another 5 minutes over low heat
11. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Fantastic is an understatement! This was amazing especially considering that I really thought I'd screwed it up. I wanted to double it, so used 2 cups peas and 10 cups water and added a little onion powder to the water.  Well about 2 hours later, I kind of had forgotten about it, and the peas were cooked to mush and there seemed to be WAY too much water. I almost scrapped the project but decided to proceed. I doubled the spices (since I'd doubled the peas)used a bit of olive oil (no butter) and used jarred crushed garlic (about 1 TBS), cumin powder (about 1.5 tsp) and used garlic salt instead of regular. I omitted the pepper and red pepper flaked but added a bit of red chili pepper. I added the very watery pea mixture back to the spices and prayed! I didn't need to add any additional water, just let it sit for a bit after mixing the peas in... it thickened up perfectly and had the best tasted and texture. I did a little more garlic salt in the end and sprinkled some garam masala too. Served on brown rice. This is mild (not spicy like some Indian dishes) but we LOVED it. My 3 year old did too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan chocolate orange muffins

this came from a vegan website.

1. mix your dry ingredients reserving about a third of the chocolate chips for topping
2. then add the wet ones and stir well
3. divide between 12 cake or muffin cases , topping with the remaining chips
4. bake at 200c / 400f for 15 to 20 minutes until well risen and browning
demonstrations.review: Very good.... and I made quite a few changes, so not sure if this is a fair rating.  First off, I was a little confused by the "1/2 - 1 cup liquid" and after making them, wondered if it should state "1 1/2 cups" of liquid? I used about 1/4 cup sugar, as I am always trying to reduce calories/sugar. I was too lazy to zest the oranges, and actually used 2 oranges, juicing them by hand and adding a bit of the pulp after juicing. I think next time, I will take the effort to include the zest as I would have liked them more orange-y.  I tried substituting apple sauce for the oil, but it was very very dry, so ended up adding about 1/4 cup oil and a total of about 1 and 1/4 cup soymilk (which is I why I wonder if the recipe should call for 1 1/2 cups?) Next time, I'll include the zest, use orange juice, and start off with more liquid. And I think chopped nuts would be great too! Thanks for a good vegan muffin!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cilantro tofu dressing

trying to get more soy into your diet???
or want no eggs or dairy????
try this.!!!!
try as a dip!!!for vegies or grilled chicken!

1. place the tofu , lime , garlic , shallot , mustard , cilantro into food processor with metal blade and blend till pureed
2. combine the water to prcessor while machine is still running , follow with the oil salt and pepper
3. serve immediately on your favorite salad or grilled meat
demonstrations.review: Really good dip/dressing! I didn't have shallot but used a bit of onion, and completely omitted the oil to make it healthier. I also used a whole box of silken tofu (12 oz) so tripled the rest of the ingredients (except for the garlic - used about 4 big cloves total).

target.recipe_text:
fantastic taco casserole

i originally found this taco casserole recipe in a taste of home magazine.  since then, i have made this recipe at least 50 times.  i love it because the ingredients list isn't complicated and, based on the layers, i can readily remember all ingredients when i am at the store without my recipe card.  i have served this for myself and had wonderful leftovers or many times i have made it for company with a nice green salad to accompany it.  i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. add taco seasoning and cook according to package directions , adding proper amount of water
3. put corn chips on bottom of 8x8" dish
4. cook refried beans on stove until hot
5. add 1 cup cheese and 1 cup salsa
6. stir until combined
7. pour beans over corn chips in dish
8. add beef to top of beans
9. sprinkle remaining cheese over top
10. sprinkle green onions and black olives over cheese
11. bake in a 375 degree oven until the cheese is sufficiently melted
12. take out of oven and sprinkle chopped tomatoes on top
13. wait 1-2 minutes and then serve
target.review: This was WAY too salty.  Next time I will skip the chips at the bottom and just use this as a dip or taco filler.  I would also suggest salt-free refried beans or low-sodium taco seasoning.  I liked the texture and even though I'm only giving it 2 stars, I thought it has great potential.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic bistro style gratin dauphinois   french gratin potatoes

this classic french potato gratin dish is world famous, and rightly so! i am quite happy to have this as a main meal, with just some crusty bread and a large mixed salad on the side. i have heard that this famous dish was created as a way of encouraging the "dauphin" (the young prince destined to become king henri ii), to eat up his vegetables, hence the name! maybe - it is certainly just as popular with children, as it is with adults. try to slice the potatoes as thinly as possible for the best results. a wonderful accompaniment for all sorts of roast meats, stews, casseroles and poultry.
this recipe is not strictly french, using as it does a swiss cheese.

1. preheat the oven to 300f / 150c / gas mark 2
2. take a heavy-bottomed dish or an ovenproof gratin dish , and grease it will with some of the butter
3. layer the potato slices in the dish , slightly overlapping each other , seasoning lightly with the salt and pepper , and sprinkling a liberal amount of cheese on each layer
4. sprinkle cheese on the top of the last layer
5. put the double cream , garlic and sprigs of thyme in a pan and bring to them gently to the boil , then remove the thyme and pour hot cream over the potatoes
6. dot the top of the gratin with the remaining butter and some extra cheese if you wish , and bake for about 1 hr to 1 1 / 2 hrs , or until the potatoes are soft , and the top is crispy and golden brown
7. serve bubbling hot as a main meal or as an accompaniment
demonstrations.review: WOW....these are absolute perfection.  I followed the recipe exactly (though I'll only put the salt on the top layer from now on) and I could not make myself stop eating them.  Absolutely worth the effort!!!!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the bomb burgers

awsome burgers if i do say so myself!

1. in a bowl combine beef , bread crumbs , green onions , coriander , hoisin sauce , garlic , ginger and egg
2. mix well
3. make 5 burgers
4. poke a hole thru the middle
5. in a small bowl mix together water , hoisin , and sesame oil
6. place burgers on a hot grill and brush the top with the previous mixture
7. flip after 7 min or so and baste the other side
8. serve with condiments of choice
demonstrations.review: I cooked 4 different types of burgers at a BBQ and the Bomb burgers rated in the top 2 almost every time.  I made them exactly to the recipe and they were so full of flavor that I wouldn't change a thing.  Wonderful DiB's!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drunken garlic crock pot roast

don't be afraid of all the garlic in this! it gets really mild from the long cooking process and gives the meat a wonderful flavor. this is a favorite for me, and i hope it will be for you, too. different brands of beer will give you different amounts of sweetness ranging from bitter to malty (common beer characters). try going with less sugar until you know how your beer will taste (as most of them add some amount of sweetness regardless).

1. in a large skillet , heat 1 tablespoons of the oil and brown roast on both sides , seasoning with salt and pepper
2. remove to a platter and keep warm
3. add the remaining tbsp of oil to the pan and add the onions , cook until they just start to wilt then add the garlic , them cook until the onions are tender , a few minutes more
4. add the bouillon cubes to the hot water and stir to dissolve
5. add that to the skillet along with the beer , brown sugar , mustard , and vinegar
6. stir to mix well
7. pour mixture into the bottom of the crock pot
8. place roast on top of liquid , cutting into pieces if it doesn't lay flat
9. set the crock pot on low and cook for 7-8 hours
10. remove meat from crock pot and pour liquid into a pan on the stove
11. heat to a boil , and mix a slurry out of the cornstarch and water
12. thicken pan liquid with slurry to make a gravy
13. serve gravy over meat or with potatoes or noodles
demonstrations.review: This was SO good. I followed the recipe to a T and it turned out perfectly. The only Lager I could get was Red Stripe, I can't wait to try this with other Lagers to see if there is a difference. The garlic really mellows out(I was concerned about that). I paired this with mashed parsnips and potatoes from the Sept issue of Cooks Illustrated. What a pair! This is totally going on the rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bourbon sweet potatoes  yams

made in my house for every family gathering and holiday. possibly the most delicious thing you'll ever eat--even if you don't like yams, which i don't.

1. in a skillet , brown the pecans
2. in a big pot , boil the yams for 12 minutes with water just covering them
3. after 12 minutes , drain the water and replace with ice cold water to stop the cooking--peel and slice the potatoes
4. in a big pan melt the brown sugar and butter together until saucy
5. add the bourbon and optionally flamb
6. add heavy cream , blend together
7. add the sliced yams to the pan and mix around with the sauce
8. add the pecans and mix together while heating for a little bit , but not to cook the yams completely
9. pour everything into a casserole dish and heat in the oven at 375 for 25 minutes or until potatoes are cooked
demonstrations.review: WOW!  I followed the recipe (except I didn't put butter on the top) and this dish turned out wonderfully!  This makes a TON and it gets better as it ages.  My husband has already requested that next Thanksgiving we should make this a week ahead of time.  This is definatley going on the rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
overnight french toast casserole

great make-ahead breakfast casserole.

1. melt margarine in a 9 x 13 baking pan
2. put 6 slices of bread in bottom of pan
3. in a bowl mix 1 cup brown sugar with 1 tsp cinnamon
4. sprinkle 1 / 2 of this sugar mixture over bread
5. add another layer of 6 slices of bread
6. in a bowl , whisk eggs with milk until well blended
7. pour over bread layers
8. sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture
9. cover and refrigerate overnight
10. bake covered at 350f 30 minutes
11. uncover and continue baking 15 minutes or until set and browned
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  I only made a half order and I used whole grain bread and it turned out pretty well.  My 2 yr old went to town on it.  I used 1/2 cup br sugar and 3 eggs.  I will make this again but maybe shake things up with some added vanilla or cardamon.

target.recipe_text:
adult popcorn

here's a great, economical snack for those sports fans. it's quick & easy too

1. combine parmesan , salt , cayenne , cumin& thyme
2. this is best done in the processor with the blade , process for 3 minutes so the mix is very fine
3. pop the corn
4. toss with the butter
5. toss with the cheese mix
6. best served now but may be prepared up to 4 hours in advance and served at room temperature
target.review: The first time I made this I made it twice. the second time I made it I made it three times. I am starting to think that my hubby's friends want to have poker here because they now they will get this popcorn. So good and it literally takes 5 min to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chinese corn soup

you won't even bother ordering this soup from a chinese restaurant anymore, this is so easy to make and very good! for a thicker soup use more cornstarch, i like to add in some sesame oil also and if i am serving this to guests i also add in a few drops of yellow food colouring for a nicer presentation.

1. in a saucepan combine the creamed corn and broth
2. bring to a boil over medium-high heat
3. in a small bowl or cup whisk the cornstarch and water
4. add to the simmering corn soup and continue to cook for about 2 minutes or until thickened
5. gradually add the beaten eggs while stirring or whisking the soup constantly
6. add in the corn niblets and heat though
7. season with salt and pepper
8. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: as always when you see Kittencal you know it is going to be a winner and this is no exception. The flavor is nice a sutle and the time it takes to make is really the best part. It is also made with all things that I have on hand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black cake

this is an old fashioned cake that is very easy to make and is very good.

1. heat water and butter in small saucepan until butter is melted
2. mix remaining ingredients in lg bowl
3. add water and butter
4. mix well
5. pour into greased and floured 13x9 baking pan
6. bake at 350 for 30 minutes , or until a pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I have used this cake for every Birthday now for well over a year. I guess it is time I say I love it. It is easy to make and always moist. Not too sweet just lovely. I usually use cream cheese icing on it and it is great. I really don't like super sweet cakes so this is great. I always get compliments thanks Mizznezz another great riecpe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect perogy casserole

i found this recipe in the flyer of a food store, and later found it on the cheemo perogies website. it's a great dish to serve perogies with a different twist on them. i've substituted sausage for the ham and that works just as good. i've never microwaved this dish so i can't tell you how well it would turn out.

1. in a small skillet melt butter or margarine and saute onion and green pepper for 5 minutes
2. in a medium size casserole dish , combine frozen perogies , onion , green pepper and ham
3. combine milk and mushroom soup and pour over casserole
4. top with cheddar cheesse
5. bake 35 minutes at 175c or microwave until heated through
demonstrations.review: I love this and really there about 100 subsitutes I can think of. My husband loved this and said we will never eat perogies any other way again thanks. I added a little spice to taste, garlic, cummin, and pepper. No salt because the soup has more then enough.Thank you so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf  hey virginia  mine is better

ha-ha, i do love the "meatloaf: yes virginia, there is a great meatloaf" recipe, however i believe mine is just a hint better.  you be the judge.  i made this for my husband’s birthday- party of 15, and everyone raved over it- so, hey everyone- give it a shot, i would love some feedback.  i use dried onion as opposed to fresh because i didn't like the bite of fresh onion, it's much more subtle yet still flavorful to use dried... you be the judge though- use 1 small fresh yellow onion chopped if you like. by the way- some of you may be wondering- this is not a 'sweet meat'... it may be confusing with all the brown sugar and sweetened condensed milk- but i assure you- this is not sweet- if you want to- just omit the savory sauce and make it on the side to use as a dipping sauce the first time around... i'm highly confident in this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. mix all ingredients thoroughly in mixing bowl and pat into a 9" round pie plate and pat flat
3. mix the "savory sauce" in a separate bowl and spoon over the meatloaf
4. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I made mine with one part pork and two parts beef I also sub milk for sweetened condensed milk because I had none. We all liked it except for my daughter but she hates everything. I will make this again. I really liked the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rack of lamb

i made this for dinner last night and it was awesome. the baked breadcrumb topping mixture is to die for! recipe found on the internet.

1. sear rack of lamb all over in skillet that can be used in the oven
2. with food processor running , drop shallot and garlic into top tube and process until finely minced
3. add parsley and process until finely chopped
4. add pieces of fresh bread and process to fine crumbs
5. remove from processor to a bowl and mix in melted butter
6. pat bread crumb mixture onto top of rack of lamb
7. roast at 450 for 15 to 20 minutes
8. if crumbs brown too quickly , turn oven down to 425
9. test with oven thermometer until done to your liking
demonstrations.review: the flavor was amazing so yummy. the only issue I had was the bread wouldn't stay on the lamb. I think maybe  a little more butter. I just eyeballed it. The flavor was yumm and the meat was a beautiful pink color.

target.recipe_text:
addictive mexican stew

my mother gave me this recipe.  she found it while clipping coupons.  it is from s&w.  this is the best stew i have ever eaten and my family requests me to make it quite frequently.  it has become a 

1. cook onion and garlic in oil in large saucepan until tender
2. add cooked chicken , taco seasoning , tomatoes , beans , corn and chilies
3. blend broth and cornstarch
4. add to saucepan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
7. stirring occasionally
8. serve with cornbread for a hearty meal
target.review: A keeper.I served it with corn bread, and a dish of sour cream on the side....my son ate his bowl with corn bread, the took another bowl with sour cream and ate it with tortilla chips...needless to say I'll be making this often. Thanks so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snapple iced tea  5 flavors

quick, easy and refreshing!

1. for any of the flavors , boil the water in a large saucepan
2. when the water comes to a rapid boil , turn off the heat , put the tea bags into the water , and cover
3. after the tea has brewed about 1 hour , pour the sugar or sweetener into a 2 quart pitcher , then add the tea
4. the tea should still warm , so the sugar or sweetener will dissolve easily
5. add the flavoring ingredients
6. chill
demonstrations.review:
I followed the recipe using generic brand orange pekoe tea bags, sugar and freshly squeezed lemon juice.It was soooooooooo good.Then I made it again adding 1/8tspn pure orange extract-couldnt taste the orange at all...so I kept adding more extract 1/8tspn at a time and finally could taste the orange at 1 tspn-not a strong orange taste but faintly there.
In any case, the recipe is awesome and I have made it 4 times in the past day and a half and the pitcher is empty again!
I squeezed my lemons and froze the juice so its handy...will be trying the no sugar version soon.THANK YOU so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana oat muffins

nan

1. combine first 6 dry ingredients in large bowl
2. mix well
3. beat egg , banana and melted butter together in small bowl until smooth
4. add banana mixture to dry ingredients
5. stir just until moistened
6. stir in nuts , if desired
7. fill greased muffin cups almost full
8. bake at 375f for 20-25 minutes , or until top springs back when lightly touched
demonstrations.review:
These are great!
I used melted margerine,(was out of butter), and added a mixture of sliced almonds,sunflower seeds and chopped walnuts,(wanted to use up the little bits I had left of them).
I froze some in baggies and take one or two of them with me when I go out and know I will be late getting home for supper.
Excellent texture and flavor.
My son loves them too.
I will use this recipe often 
Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sassy s beef and broccoli

this is a great week-day supper. fast and delicious! we always have this with a big bowl of rice, and everyone just loves it - even the kids! you can add any other veggies that your family likes!

1. marinate steak in mixture of 1 / 2 of water , soya sauce , sugar , vinegar , garlic , ginger and cornstarch
2. drain well , reserving marinade
3. heat oil in wok or skillet
4. add steak and brown
5. add broccoli and onion
6. cook at medium-high heat , stirring for 1 minutes
7. add remaining water , cover and steam for 3-4 minutes until broccoli is tender-crisp
8. add marinade and cook until sauce is hot and thick
demonstrations.review: Very easy.I added sliced carrots( my son needs to eat lots of veggies for a medical condition),used frozen broccoli and omitted the ginger( was all out!). I served it with whole wheat spaghetti( as thats the only noodle I had in the house).Next time I will add some dried crushed red pepper to the marinade because we like the heat, but the flavour was just perfect as written.A definite keeper.Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new and different  taco salad

this tastes nothing like a normal taco salad. it is so different that it will wake up your taste buds. kids will love it.

1. fry and drain 1 pound of ground beef
2. put beef back in pan and add taco seasoning and water
3. cook until no longer watery
4. chop up lettuce really fine
5. dice 2 tomatoes
6. put all ingredients in a big bowl
7. add a small bag of fritos regular chips
8. add big bag of shredded cheddar cheese
9. add one chopped green onion
10. add one big bottle catalina french dressing
11. mix well
demonstrations.review: I made this for supper using the catalina dressing. I thought it was ok, my son did too but my daughter hated it...I think it would have been much better with a different dressing...I am going to try it again,(scaled down by half until I find a dressing we like).I think it would be good with sour cream and maybe some chopped jalepenos...Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick yellow cake

you can mix this up in a hurry.

1. heat oven to 350
2. mix dry ingredients in lg bowl
3. add shortening , milk and vanilla
4. beat on med for 2 minutes
5. add eggs and beat for 30 seconds more
6. bake in greased 13x9 pan for 35 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
demonstrations.review:
My son wanted to bake a cake last night,(his first), so I gave him this recipe.
He put all the ingredients in one bowl and beat it with an electric hand mixer till smooth and baked it in a greased 8" square pan.
It was great!
Moist,not too fluffy,great flavor,easy and quick...a definite keeper.
Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
orange french toast ii

tasty:)

1. combine eggs and orange juice
2. beat really well
3. dip bread into egg mixture , then into crumbs
4. in a large frying pan , melt butter
5. pan fry on both sides until lightly browned
6. serve with syrup or honey and top with powdered sugar or fresh fruit
target.review: I am always searching for interesting recipes to try out at the restaurant I work at for specials and your recipe was just the ticket to turn ordinary french toast into something special. everyone who ordered it loved it!! I did one slight modification, I used texas toast (slightly trimming off the crust) instead of regular bread and I added 2 tsp. of fresh orange zest to the egg mixture. I also premade these the night before. the grilling brought back the crunchiness of the vanilla wafers. we served them with a homemade orange syrup. thank you so much for sharing your recipe!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy strawberry crepes

these are our favorite crepes, perfect for christmas morning.

1. in a large mixing bowl , beat the eggs , milk , water , butter and salt
2. add flour , beat until smooth
3. cover and refrigerate for 1 hour
4. in an 8-in non stick skillet , melt 1 tsp butter , pour 2 tbsps of batter into the center of skillet
5. lift and tilt pan to evenly coat bottom
6. cook until top appears dry
7. turn and cook 15-20 seconds longer
8. remove to a wire rack
9. repeat with remaining batter , adding butter to skillet as needed
10. when cool , stack the crepes with waxed paper or paper towels in between
11. for filling , in a small mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese , confectioners' sugar , lemon juice , peel and vanilla until smooth
12. fold in 2 cups of berries and whipped cream
13. spoon about 1 / 3 cup filing down the center of 15 crepes
14. roll up
15. garnish with the remaining berries
16. freeze remaining crepes for another use
demonstrations.review: I made these for a Sunday special at work.....and I have to say that all of my customers that ordered it just LOVED it!!! fantastic recipe!! the filling is to die for...light with a wonderful hint of lemon and sweetness without being overpowering. thank you for sharing!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
featherweight buttermilk biscuits

very light and delicious! try with your next breakfast or ham dinner!

1. preheat oven to 450f degrees
2. sift together first 6 ingredients into large bowl
3. add butter and rub in with finger
4. add buttermilk and stir until dough forms
5. turn dough out onto floured surface
6. knead until smooth , about 8 turns
7. roll out the dough to 1 inch thickness
8. using 2 inch diameter biscuit cutter , cut out biscuits
9. gather scraps and roll out to 1 inch thickness and cut out additional biscuits
10. transfer biscuits to large ungreased baking sheet
11. bake until golden , about 12 minutes
12. serve warm
demonstrations.review: awesome biscuits!!! I made these for our restaurant and had to multiply the recipe by 12 times....lol but they made the best biscuits ever and our customers loved them on biscuits and gravy and biscuits with chicken fried steak and eggs...this is a keeper!  thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom and almond rice pilaf

a wonderful side dish to almost any meat entree. this works well with any type of rice - brown or white, long-grain or short-grain.

1. brown onions in margarine
2. mix together with remaining ingredients in a shallow baking dish
3. bake for 1 hour at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: wonderful! I made this to go along with chicken divan crepes at our restaurant for a lunch special and it was a great accompaniment. the only thing I did differently was use chicken stock instead of the soup since it was a chicken dish I was serving. thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s baked potato salad casserole  or cold potato salad

this may be served hot as a casserole or reduce the melted butter amount down to 2 tablespoons and serve as a cold potato salad, either way it's delicious! --- if you are serving hot as a casserole i strongly recommend to have the potatoes cooled to room temperature before using in this recipe or use cold potatoes that have been cooked a day ahead, i have even made this using about 5 cups of thawed frozen hash browns, the complete casserole may be assembled and refrigerated for up to 2 days ahead before baking although it's so delicious cold it might not even make it to the oven, and also makes a large amount which makes this *perfect* dish for potlucks --- if you are baking as a casserole use only mayonnaise such as hellman's using salad dressing will not be as good.

1. to serve hot as a casserole
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. set oven to 350 degrees f
4. in a large bowl , mix mayonnaise , sour cream and melted butter , garlic powder , seasoned salt and black pepper until well combined
5. mix in green onion and yellow onion
6. add in the cooked cubed potatoes , cubed cheese and ham mix with a large spatula until well combined
7. transfer / spread the mixture to prepared casserole dish
8. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours until ready to bake
9. bake 25-30 minutes or until hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and sprinkle the grated cheddar on top
11. return to oven and bake 5-8 minutes more or until the cheese has melted
12. to serve as a cold potato salad
13. make as stated in steps 3-5 reducing the melted butter to 2 tablespoons
14. place in a bowl , cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or more before serving
15. delicious !
demonstrations.review: you are awesome kitten!!! this is to die for! I made this for the restaurant to serve instead of french fries with our sandwiches and it was a big hit! (I knew it would be, your recipes are the best). I baked my potatoes the night before and cubed them with the skin on..instead of boiling them. and I used 1 1/2# of cooked bacon pieces in place of the ham..mmmmmmm thank you for the recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple crepes

i just love to make them!

1. combine all ingredients below crepe mixture until smooth
2. make shells like you would make manicotta shells
3. yield 16-18 crepes
4. prepare pudding as directed
5. saute apples about 10 minutes
6. add sugar and seasonings
7. combine apples and pudding
8. mix well and chill
9. makes enough filling for 8 dessert crepes
10. just before serving , divide mixture evenly on crepes and pocket fold
11. serve with whipped cream and powdered sugar
demonstrations.review: I made these for a sunday special at the restaurant I work at. they are spectacular! I modified it slightly by making my own tapioca pudding (cheaper when you need to make a large quantity) and I substituted carmel extract for the brandy. they were served warm with sauteed granny smith apples on top and drizzled with a homemade carmel sauce....rave reviews from all of my customers!!! thank you so much for the recipe. I will definetely make these again!!!

target.recipe_text:
cousin jim s amazing apple pie

this is the best apple pie i have ever had. this is one of those pies where everything just blends together on the palate beautifully and makes your mouth want more. i was not an apple pie fan until i tasted this! it is better than any bakery, restaurant, or grocery store bought (duh) apple pie i've tried. oh - and by the way, it is worth the effort to roll out the dough...mmm, mmm! you can use this light, flaky dough with tons of other fruit pies.

1. prepare the apples: peel , core , and slice apples thinly , and place in a large bowl
2. cover apples with sugars , flour , vanilla , and spices , and mix well with apples
3. set aside
4. at this point , preheat oven to 350
5. prepare the dough: mix salt , flour , and shortening in mixer- then add ice cold water
6. remove dough , divide in half , and roll out one half using flour to keep from sticking- reserve the other half for top crust
7. line 9 inch pie pan with half dough
8. allow 1 / 4 inch extra dough to stick out- you'll pinch it with the top crust later
9. put apple mixture into crust-lined pan
10. roll out top crust and cover apples
11. finish the pie: gently pinch bottom and top crusts together , and flute edges of dough
12. poke several fork holes in top crust , and dot crust with butter and sprinkle with sugar
13. bake at 350 for 65-70 minutes
14. allow to cool 20 minutes before serving plain or with vanilla bean ice cream , cool whip , or whipped cream
15. this also warms up great in the microwave
16. and , by all means , enjoy !
target.review: Like virtually everyone else who's reviewed this recipe, I have to say that it's absolutely the best apple pie I've ever tasted, let alone made!  I made it exactly according to the recipe, save for substituting Instant Clear Jel for the flour...as I do in all my pies.  What a spectacular recipe!  Thanks so much for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot flank steak with linguini

nan

1. pound the flank steak to about 1 / 2"
2. spread 3 tbsp of butter on the steak and sprinkle with the thyme , sage , basil , garlic& season with salt and pepper
3. with the long side towards you roll up the steak and secure with skewers or toothpicks about 1" apart
4. heat olive oil in skillet and brown the outside of the steak , place steak in your crock pot
5. in the same skillet brown onions& mushrooms , when browned add tomatoes , tomato paste , chilies , soy sauce , sour cream , bay leaf& worcestershire sauce , mix well and pour over the steak in the crock pot
6. turn to low and cook 5-6 hours
7. add half the parsley after 5 hours
8. meanwhile cook the linguini so it will be ready in time to serve with the flank steak , drain the linguini , add 2 tbsp butter& remaining parsley
9. toss
10. cut the flank steak into 1" slices and put on individual plates along with the pasta , serve with sauce over the steak& the pasta
demonstrations.review: Outstanding recipe for flank steak!  The only change I made--by necessity--was to increase the cooking time to about 10 hours.  It didn't seem to adversely affect the recipe at all: the meat was incredibly flavourful, tender, and lovely to look at when sliced.  I thickened the sauce with a bit of cornstarch/water and served all with egg noodles (I'm thinking the leftover sauce will make a perfect soup base).  Fantastic mid-week meal, but would also be ideal for company!  Thanks so much for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger buns

this has a nice backstory to it (don't all my 
recipes ha ha:-) a friend of mine who lives way out in washington state told me about her fleischmann's yeast breads booklet. she got it in a mixer she received as a wedding gift over 25 years ago. she says the recipes in the booklet are sooooo good she has worn her booklet to a frazzle-pages are coming loose, dog-eared, you know what i'm talking about. anyway, i decided i'd try to find her a new one (or a good used one)  i spent weeks searching the web looking on ebay, amazon, alibris and every little site i knew of to find a copy. finally after 3 months of looking i found two copies on ebay-bid on em and got both of em for a real good price! boy was she happy. she told me about this bun recipe and how great it was and that i should try making them. she was right (she usually is:-) these make very good buns. you can add sesame or poppy seeds to the tops with an egg wash. with summer fast upon us i thought i'd send this one in. i use these all the time when i make my blue mill tavern sandwiches i've posted to this site. enjoy! makes 8 buns. p.s. i'm very sad to say my friend who told me of this recipe has gone on to be with the lord. i shall miss her very very much but i know she is now with her beloved husband and family who passed before her. thank you kath for making me a better person (and a better baker!).

1. place warm water in large warm bowl
2. sprinkle in yeast
3. stir until dissolved
4. add warm milk , sugar , butter , 1 1 / 2 tablespoons minced onions , salt , and 2 cups flour
5. blend well
6. stir in 2 eggs & enough remaining flour to make soft dough
7. knead on lightly floured surface until smooth and elastic , about 4 to 6 minutes
8. place in greased bowl , turning to grease top
9. cover
10. let rise in warm , draft-free place until doubled in size , about 30 to 45 minutes
11. punch dough down
12. remove dough to lightly floured surface
13. divide into 8 equal pieces
14. form each piece into smooth ball
15. place on large greased baking sheet
16. flatten balls to 4-inch rounds
17. cover
18. let rise in warm , draft-free place until doubled in size , about 20 to 40 minutes
19. lightly beat remaining egg
20. brush on rolls
21. if desired , sprinkle with minced onions or poppy or sesame seed
22. bake at 400of for 10 to 15 minutes or until done
23. remove from baking sheet
24. let cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: What an outstanding recipe for truly soft, tender sandwich/hamburger buns with a lovely crumb!  I made them exactly per the recipe, with the exception of substituting Baker's Special Milk Powder (mixed with dry ingredients) and water for the milk called for in the original recipe.  As you can see from the photo, the buns rose incredibly high and finished with a nice sheen.  The rise time was spot on for me, as was the bake time, and I love that this is such an uncomplicated recipe--it was remarkably quick with the KitchenAid.  My husband announced that we shall never again purchase store-bought hamburger buns!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zesty low fat chicken breasts

very tasty, you can make it as hot or as mild as you want. quick easy dish - no muss no fuss

1. put the breasts in a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. whisk remaining ingredients together until they are well blended
3. pour over the breasts
4. coat both sides of the breasts with the sauce
5. bake in 400f oven for approx 30 minutes or until the chicken is done
6. remove breasts , keep warm
7. pour the sauce into a sauce pan stir in the cornstarch that has been mixed with a tbsp of water , bring to a boil and allow to thicken whisk constantly
8. pour over the chicken & serve
demonstrations.review: This is the second time I've made this and I have to say, it's an ideal middle-of-the-week option for us.  The flavour is quite amazing and the chicken is *unbelievably* fork tender.  Mine hasn't needed thickening either time, as the sauce reduced nicely on its own in the oven.  My husband is profoundly anti-sauce, but even he loves this recipe!  Also, it seems to lend itself to adaptation: I mistakenly doubled the honey last night, added some vinegar to offset the additional sweetness, and it turned out just fine.  Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bakery style bran muffins

i love a good bakery bran muffin and have tried countless refrigerator bran muffin recipes, which always come up short. this recipe is from cook's illustrated and promises the best bran muffins. what is different about the ingred. is the ratio of white and wheat flours and wheat bran. the molasses, dark brown sugar help make up the great flavor and you will love the bakery crusty top. it is a little more work, but i would never bake any other recipe!

1. adust oven rack to lower middle position and heat oven to 375
2. beat butter in large bowl of electric mixer at medium speed until light and fluffy , 1-2 minute
3. add brown sugar , increase speed to medum-high , and beat until combined and fluffy , about 1 minute longer
4. add eggs one at a time , beating thoroughly before adding the next
5. beat in vanilla , molasses , and sour cream until thoroughly combined and creamy , about 1 minute longer
6. reduce speed to low and beat in buttermilk and half the flour mixture until combined , about 1 minute longer
7. beat in remaining flour mixture unil incorporated and slightly curdled looking , about 1 minute longer , scraping sides of bowl as necessary
8. stir in bran and raisins
9. spray a twelve mold muffins tin or a six mold muffin tin with cooking spray
10. divide batter evenly using ice cream scoop or spoon
11. bake until a toothpick inserted into center withdraws cleanly of with a few moist particles adhering to it , about 25 minute set on wire rack to cool slightly , about 5 minute remove muffins from tin and serve warm
12. makes 12 small muffins or 6 jumbo muffins
demonstrations.review: Without doubt, the best bran muffins I've ever tried!  Not particularly caring for the recipes utilising bran cereal, I prepared these exactly according to the recipe and was delighted: the muffins are light, moist, and possess a rich, almost caramel-like flavour.   This has become my holy grail of bran muffin recipes.  Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
demonstrations.review: Excellent chicken salad!  I made the recipe exactly as posted the first time, then with mayonnaise and a touch of lemon juice the second: both were equally good (it's just that we don't generally have Miracle Whip in the house).  This recipe is easy, quick, and delicious whether served as a sandwich filling, as a stuffing for tomatoes or green peppers, or even on its own with toast or crackers.  A definite 'do again' for us, and an outstanding use for leftover baked chicken breast!

target.recipe_text:
pork roast over sweet potatoes for the crock pot

my husband always requests this recipe. i cook it 11 hours so the meat barely holds together. works for low glycemic index diets.

1. combine first 6 ingredients
2. rub into pork
3. put potatoes in the crock pot
4. place pork on top of potatoes
5. pour broth over all
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
target.review: made this twice -- there's just two of us now so a small pork loin goes along way. frist time with the fennel seeds the next I used caraway seeds (whole didn't bother to crush them)This is a good one it has two things going for it; 1--the crockpot for that instant dinner when i get home from work and 2--takes care of hubby's love of sweet potatoes. the frist time we found the potatoes were a little to mushy to his liking so the second time i cut them in quarters then cut the quarters into inch slices.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bombay beef   cauliflower

nan

1. combine first 4 ingredients and pepper to taste in a small bowl
2. stir well with a whisk and set aside
3. heat a large oiled non-stick skillet over high heat
4. add meat and saute 3 minutes or until browned
5. remove from skillet and set aside
6. add cauliflower and broth
7. cover , reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes
8. return meat to skillet
9. stir in yogurt mixture
10. add snow peas and bring to a boil
11. cook 2 minutes , stirring gently
12. toss with pasta before serving
13. garnish with toasted almonds , if desired
14. good served cold as a luncheon salad
demonstrations.review: The honey mustard added a different punch to the sauce. Didn't have any snow peas so I used plain old frozen peas which worked out fine. Served it over pasta, but next time it's on rice...think it would go better with the curry. But Dancer^ was right it's great cold with the pasta!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portabella  pizzas

for hors d'ouevres (serves 4), cut the portobellos in half. to serve this as a meal (serves 2), leave the pizzas whole.

1. preheat the oven to 350f lightly spray baking sheet with cooking spray
2. wipe the portobellos with a damp paper towel , but do not rinse under water
3. spray each with cooking spray and place on baking sheet
4. bake for 10 minutes
5. meanwhile , cut the tomato into eigths
6. cut the basil into thin strips
7. remove from portobellos from the oven and top each with the cheese , tomato wedges , basil , and pine nuts
8. return to oven and bake for an additional 5 minutes , until the cheese melts slightly
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review:
This is a good quick meal with a little salad on the side. I've made it a few times and thought maybe it was time to give it a review!
I also love the whole tomato and I have also added alittle roasted red pepper strips or fresh green peppers when you add the tomato.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
demonstrations.review:
A frist rate winner with brussel sprouts lovers and even won over a few who "hated them".
An added plus...very easy to fix.
I did mine with just cracked pepper instead of lemon pepper and added some baby carrots to stretch the veggies as we had an unexpected guest for dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked sole fillets

sole is my favourite white fish; serve this with rice and a green vegetable for a quick, healthy meal.

1. preheat oven to 375f degrees
2. butter a shallow baking dish and arrange fish pieces in it
3. cover fish with onion slices
4. in a small bowl , whisk together sour cream , wine , flour , lemon juice and the seasonings
5. pour over the fish and onions
6. bake , uncovered , for 25 minutes or until fish is tender
7. do not overcook or fish will dry out
demonstrations.review: Wonderful...found my self with only 3/4 cup of sour cream so made up the difference with a little more wine. Forgot to add the paprika till after I had poured the sauce on my fish...sprinkled it on top. Thought the onions would be too much...but I followed your recipe there. I will repeat... wonderful

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauerkraut and apples

goes great with sausages steamed in beer. my husband is always after me to make kraut, and this is one of the many ways i do.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. rinse sauerkraut and wring dry
3. heat margarine in a large skillet
4. saute onion and garlic until onion is tender
5. add kraut , cider , stock , apples , and juniper
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. bring to a boil
8. transfer to casserole dish
9. cover with lid or foil and bake at 350 degrees f
10. for 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This would be a great recipe to introduce someone to sauerkrurt! It is wonderful. I make sauerkrurt alot, my Husband loves it too, but never like this... Not sure what the secert is but the taste is very balanced and doesn't have an overpowering sauerkrurt taste. I've always used caraway seeds in my kraut, but the juniper berries caught my eye. Maybe that's your secert??? I did have to bake it a little longer to get it bubbling, and just a little bit browned on the edges, but every oven varies. I will make it again.

target.recipe_text:
tsr version of red lobster cheddar bay biscuits by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. the cold butter is the secret. it's not included in other copy cat recipes.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine bisquick and cold butter
3. don't combine too thoroughly
4. there should be small chunks of butter about the size of peas
5. add cheddar , milk and 1 / 4 tsp garlic
6. mix by hand until combined , but don't over mix
7. drop 9 equal portions onto greased cookie sheet
8. bake for 15-17 minutes or until tops are light brown
9. melt 2 tbsp butter in a bowl
10. stir in 1 / 2 tsp garlic powder and parsley flakes
11. use a pastry brush to spread garlic butter over tops of biscuits
target.review: For a Feast of the Seven Fishes seafood potluck I thought it would be awfully clever of me to make this copycat version of Red Lobster's signature biscuits. The recipe is quite easy with minimal ingredients and the results were very tasty. Admittedly I haven't had real Red Lobster CB biscuits in quite awhile, but these seemed to hit the mark. A friend arguably more well-versed in the Cheddar Bay biscuit genre agreed. I needed to add just a touch more milk than what the recipe specifies but other than that I followed it to the letter.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red cabbage with apples and spices   crock pot

you can braise this on the stove top as well in the crock pot! this is a long cooking recipe to make a very tender texture. the braised red cabbage of alsace, counterbalances the fattiness making pork, duck or a traditional christmas goose a great to serve with it. seasoned with apples, ginger, cinnamon, coriander and nutmeg. try even some lavender in it!

1. place all ingredients into a large crock pot
2. it will be full but will cook down to about 1 / 5
3. cook for 5 hours on low
4. stirring occasionally adding water if needed
5. optional: or you can cook stove top saute onions in some butter till softened add rest of ingredients and simmer 1-2 hours or bake at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: I have made this at least twice now, and it is always a hit! It works great as as side dish for a German meal of bratwurst, but we also just enjoyed it with Swedish meatballs and mashed potatoes for Christmas Eve dinner. I make the recipe exactly according to the instructions. It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german dark rye bread

this is one of 2 rye bread recipes i posted in answer to a request for a "marbled rye" bread. my suggestion for making the "marbled rye" is to knead the dark rye dough together with a "light" rye dough (recipe # 43286), before shaping the loaves. (of course that will make 4 loaves, since each recipe makes 2 loaves).this recipe makes a wonderful dark rye bread! (90 minute prep time includes rising time).

1. in large bowl , combine all-purpose flour , salt , cocoa , yeast , and caraway seed
2. heat and stir molasses , butter , sugar , 2 cups water and 2 tablespoons oil until warm
3. add to dry mixture
4. beat at low speed on electric mixer 1 / 2 minutes , scraping bowl
5. beat 3 minutes at high speed
6. then by hand , stir in enough rye flour to make a soft dough
7. turn out onto lightly floured surface
8. knead till smooth
9. cover , and let rest 20 minutes
10. punch down dough
11. divide in half
12. shape into 2 round or oval loaves on greased baking sheets
13. brush with small amount of cooking oil
14. slash tops with knife
15. cover
16. let rise until double
17. bake at 400 degrees for 25-30 minutes
18. remove from baking sheets , place on racks to cool
19. proceed with the recipe as stated
demonstrations.review: So, this was my first time making bread! I followed the recipe to the letter with one exception...apparently I am kind of a wimp because I had a tough time stirring in the rye flour by hand. I returned the dough to my mixer bowl and used the dough hook to mix in the rest of the rye. The end result was excellent! I didn't find the bread to be too dense at all...it seemed just right. I took part of a loaf to my culinary student neighbor and he agreed it was wonderful. Thanks for a great recipe that made a beginner feel more confident about baking bread!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
praline brownies

brownies with a crunchy praline topping.  i cut them into squares and freeze what we don't eat in the first couple of days.

1. preheat oven 350 degrees
2. grease the bottom only of a 13x9 inch baking pan
3. place brownie mix into a large bowl
4. stir in eggs , oil and water
5. mix until well combined
6. spread evenly over bottom of baking pan
7. in a separate bowl , mix together praline topping ingredients until crumbly
8. sprinkle evenly over the top
9. a small corner may be left uncovered with the topping as a spot to test for doneness
10. bake 28 - 30 minutes
11. do not overbake
12. check corner with a pick for doneness
13. it should come out clean with no crumbs attached
14. cut into squares
15. freezable
demonstrations.review: These were delicious and a hit at our Super Bowl party! I did find I had to add several more tablespoons of butter in order to get the sugar mixture to the consistency I wanted...but it's not like I was trying to make a low-fat treat. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw tuscan kale salad with pecorino

from the ny times. eating this was the first time i'd had kale, and it was simply delicious!! the only change i had made from the original recipe is that i added lemon zest and it turned out even better! for the bread crumbs, coarsely crushed homemade croutons would work also. instead of bread crumbs, you can use a nice thin slice of toasted country bread. zaar wouldn't let me enter the word crusty/chewy country bread into the ingredient list. if you have a microplane, that works good for grating the garlic instead of finely chopping it.

1. trim bottom 2 inches off kale stems and discard
2. slice kale , including ribs , into 3 / 4-inch-wide ribbons
3. you should have 4 to 5 cups
4. place kale in a large bowl
5. if using bread , toast it until golden on both sides
6. tear it into small pieces and grind in a food processor until mixture forms coarse crumbs
7. chop or microplane the garlic and transfer to a small bowl
8. add 1 / 4 cup cheese , 3 tablespoons oil , lemon juice & zest , salt , pepper flakes and black pepper , and whisk to combine
9. pour dressing over kale and toss very well to thoroughly combine
10. let salad sit for 5 minutes , then serve topped with bread crumbs , additional cheese and a drizzle of oil
demonstrations.review: A tasty, healthful salad! I made this tonight for a New Year's get-together and it was a hit. I had to use a dark Red Kale as the grocery store didn't have any Lacinato Kale in stock. And, I used Parmesan rather than Pecorino as that's what I had on hand. Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blue cranberry sauce

i wanted something different than just cranberry sauce- but still wanted the 'tradition' of it. i have made this sauce for thanksgiving 3 years in a row and it gits rave reviews from- what seems like- everyone that eats it-  even from people who don't like 'traditional' cranberry sauce.  i recommend that you make this a day ahead (refrigerate)  to let flavors mingle.  i serve it cold- as far as the spices go-  i don't really measure... i know 1/8th of a tsp of cloves seems like a lot-  i just shake a bit in... but if you don't like cloves- just omit them!  enjoy!!! :)

1. wash and pick over cranberries
2. place in a medium saucepan with water and sugar
3. bring to a boil , reduce heat , stir and simmer for 10 minutes or until cranberries burst
4. slightly mash the cranberries with the back of a wooden spoon to insure all skins are broken
5. add the cinnamon , nutmeg and cloves
6. mix well
7. remove from heat and mix in the blueberries
8. the sauce will thicken as it cools
9. transfer to a bowl , cool slightly and place plastic wrap directly on top of sauce to cover
10. refrigerate until chilled
demonstrations.review: I made this today for Thanksgiving and it was a hit! I am not the biggest fan of cranberry sauce but I LOVE blueberries, so this recipe was a great find. I did find I wanted it to be a bit sweeter, so added around 1/4 cup of agave syrup in addition to the sugar as directed. I didn't have ground cloves so threw in a couple of whole cloves...I don't recommend this, however, as I couldn't find them later! I thought the dish improved in flavor after being allowed to cool (I put mine in the refrigerator, but it was probably near room temperature when we ate it). Thanks for a nice twist on traditional cranberry sauce!

target.recipe_text:
jb s classic belgian waffles  and variations

we love weekend breakfasts around our house. belgian waffles has always been a favorite, especially for my son, jb! you will find all sorts of variations for this recipe, one of which i'm sure will suit your needs! these waffles will come out light, crisp and toast to a golden brown. we love to top ours with strawberries or blueberries, powdered sugar and whipped cream, blueberry syrup & real maple syrup!... and you didn't think weekends could get anymore special!

1. place all ingredients in a large mixing bowl and combine until well blended
2. allow batter to rest 5 minutes before using
3. use in your belgian waffle maker according to manufacturer's suggestion
target.review: What a great recipe!  I used half whole wheat flour and half white flour and it worked just fine.  I did add a bit more flour to give them a thicker texture, but that's just how I like waffles.  I think next time I'll try adding a bit of vanilla as other reviewers did.  Topped them with strawberries and whipped cream and my family loved them.  Can't wait to try some of the other variations (raspberry syrup here I come!).  Thanks, Bev!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey whole wheat oatmeal cookies

these cookies use honey instead of white granulated sugar. also, 100% whole wheat flour used instead of all purpose flour. tempature is lowered on purpose beacause honey burns at higher tempatures. this is suppose to be a healthier alternative to cookies made with white sugar.

1. mix all ingredients until well combined- except oats , raisins and nuts
2. mix in oats , raisins , and nuts
3. mix well
4. drop onto lightly greased baking sheet using ice cream scoop
5. bake at 325 degrees for 18-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made these last night and my family's requesting them again tonight!  They were a great alternitive to regular oatmeal cookies.  I didn't add the cinnamon as we don't like it in our oatmeal cookies.  Otherwise I didn't change a thing.  Great recipe, thanks for submitting.  Kindcook

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger oat cookies  no white sugar added

recipe was posted in the carbo canteen at www.coolrunning.com.  i have made both the banana and the pumpkin versions.

1. mix all ingredients , drop by spoonfuls onto greased cookie sheet and bake at 350f 10-15 minutes
2. you can add nuts and raisins too
3. for pan cookies , i use a greased 9" x 9" pan and bake for 20-25 minutes at 350f
demonstrations.review: I made the pumpkin version and it turned out pretty well, considering there is no oil or white sugar added.  I made it in a 9" x 9" pan, and they turned out very moist with a nice, chewy texture.  My only critique is that I felt the bars could use a little more flavor, like a kick of something - more spices perhaps. Other than that, pretty good for such a healthy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato veggie burgers

tasty and easy to put together. because the potatoes are mashed with the beans, everything stays together nicely. easy to add other seasonings to your own taste.

1. microwave potatoes until done , let cool
2. mash the potatoes and black beans together
3. add the remaining ingredients , except the oil and mix until combined
4. shape into patties
5. heat about 2 tablespoons of olive oil and cook each patty until they are done , about 3 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: These reminded me of healthier version of hash browns rather than burgers, but they were quite tasty regardless!  I had intended to serve them as burgers, but I ended up serving them as hash browns with some jelly on toast on the side.  I think next time I'll make scrambled eggs to complete the whole "breakfast for dinner" theme.  Only thing I changed was I used one large regular potato rather than the three new potatoes.  Also, this made 12 4 x 4 inch patties for me, so I shaped the remaining mixture into patties and stored them in the fridge until the next day.  When I wanted to serve them the next day, I popped them in the microwave 20 seconds, just to take the chill off, and then cooked them as usual.  Worked like a charm!  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach delight   lana s spinach salad

this is my favorite salad. this is easy to put together and it is always adored by everyone. i could make a meal out of this salad alone. another great recipe from my mother-in-law!

1. mix dressing ingredients together in jar
2. place all salad ingredients in a large salad bowl and toss together
3. toss in salad dressing just before serving
demonstrations.review: Mmm mmm MMM!!  This was absolutely fabulous.  We had it as the main dish with orange slices on the side.  I wasn't sure how the ingredients would combine, but I trusted the reviews and boy, was everybody right!  I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach garlic soup

this soup turns to a brilliant green color. my kids take leftovers to school for lunch and ask me to often make this easy soup. i have substitued skim milk for the cream with good results

1. in a 5qt dutch oven , bring spinach , broth and carrots to a boil
2. reduce heat
3. simmer 5 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. remove from the heat
5. cool to luke-warm
6. meanwhile , in a skillet , saute onion and garlic in butter until onion is soft , about 5-10 minutes
7. add flour
8. cook and stir over low heat for 3-5 minutes
9. add to spinach mixture
10. puree in small batches in a blender or food processor until finely chopped
11. place in a large saucepan
12. add cream , milk , and pepper , heat through but do not boil
demonstrations.review: Who knew you could make cooked spinach so tasty!  I remember being a little hesitant the first time I tried this, what with it being green and all, but I'm so glad I did!  I was actually fighting the family for leftovers the next day!!  To make it healthier, I used 1 1/2 tablespoons of butter, 1 tablespoon of oil, and a cup of milk instead of the heavy cream/milk ratio, and we think it's fine like that.  Thanks MissPenny!

target.recipe_text:
lemon mustard chicken

received from a friend.

1. place chicken pieces on an unheated broiler pan , broil 4 inches from heat for 15 minutes , until light golden brown
2. while broiling -- in a bowl stir together oil mustard lemon juice lemon pepper oregano red pepper salt & pepper
3. brush mustard mixture onto chicken turn chicken brush with remaining mixture
4. broil for 5-10 minutes longer , until chicken is no longer pink
5. edited to changed red peppers to red pepper flakes
target.review: I don't know if my lemon pepper has more pepper than normal, but this was almost too peppery to eat. I used a scant 1/8 tsp. cayenne pepper-I guess that was what was meant by "red peppers". I also used several shakes of salt & pepper, but not what I'd think of as "out of the ordinary". I may try this again, using no extra pepper & much less lemon pepper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bed   breakfast baked eggs

a very easy and very yummy egg dish to serve for brunch or even dinner.  can be made ahead and kept in refrigerator overnite if needed. don't be afraid of the low fat ingredients- you'll never be able to tell.

1. mix together the eggs , milk and sugar
2. add the cheeses and butter , followed by the flour and baking powder
3. pour into a greased 9x13 pan
4. refrigerate until needed
5. bake at 325 for 50 minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I gave this 5 stars because my teenage daughters and I really liked it. My picky DH said it was OK & ate it. It's really easy, and sort of tastes like southern cheese grits. I thought it was very tasty. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s company baked egg frittata

my mom rarely cooked us breakfast, but when we had company she went "all out". this is a very simple recipe.  there are probably lots of similar ones out there, but this one is dear to my heart because it was truly a "special occasion" whenever my mom made this. i still love it to this day, although i've embellished it plenty from time to time--yum! note for zaar world tour ii:  frittatas are italian in origin.

1. fry bacon until crisp , then remove strips and drain
2. crumble bacon
3. whisk all other ingredients together except cheese , and pour into an 8x8-inch greased glass pan
4. sprinkle bacon and cheese evenly over top
