5. bake in a preheated 400f oven for 20 minutes , watching so that it does not get too brown
6. garnish with chopped , fresh parsley
7. i serve it with pillsbury crescent rolls , butter and honey
demonstrations.review: This was a really easy & yummy recipe. My family really liked it, and I liked how easy it was. I used 2% milk and low-fat cheddar cheese. To make things easier, I used the pre-cooked bacon & cut it into bits with my kitchen shears. I forgot to add the green onion until I had the frittata already assembled, so I just sprinkled it on top. It was great! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach and black eyed peas

a quick and easy side-dish that's both delicious and helpful.  a hint of lemon and spice makes this a dish that's sure to delight.  can also be eaten cold, if preferred.

1. chop onions and saute in olive oil over medium heat until soft
2. add drained , rinsed black-eyed peas , lemon , salt and allspice and mix well
3. place two "bricks" of spinach on top and continue to cook on medium heat until spinach is cooked through , stirring occassionally
demonstrations.review: This was a STRANGE-looking recipe, but it really tasted good. It was really different, but we liked it a lot. I really liked that I didn't have to thaw and drain the spinach, just threw it on top & let it cook! The allspice added a nice touch, too. I'll be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
diet cola chicken

very simple to prepare but very tasty.

1. spray your pan with cooking spray
2. place chicken breasts in pan
3. brown lightly on each side
4. mix ketchup and diet cola together
5. pour over chicken
6. cook for about 45 minutes or until chicken is tender
7. very yummy ! oven degree ?
demonstrations.review: This chicken is so good and tender. The only reason I gave it 4 stars is that it seemed too sweet to me, as written. The second time I made it, I used 8 oz. tomato sauce instead of the ketchup. I also used the Splenda-sweetened Diet Coke. It was PERFECT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best chicken pot pie

i've tried a lot of pot pies, but this is my favorite. i once was making it and realized i didn't have any chicken, oops, oh well i made it any way and didn't miss the chicken one bit.

1. mix all ingredients except pie crust and egg
2. pour into unbaked pie shell and brush egg on top
3. bake at 375 for 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have been making this recipe for several years, only my recipe calls for 2 cans cream of potato soup. I'm going to try the celery soup next time. I'm sure it will be even better. I've had many complements on this recipe. It's great to make & take for a sick friend or a new mom. I had 1 new mom call me months later asking for the recipe. Her husband had raved about it, and she had tried to reproduce it by chopping veggies and doing lots of extra work. I was embarrassed to tell her how easy it is. I use refrigerated crusts to take to someone. Just for us, I use a deep dish frozen crust for the bottom and a regular-sized frozen crust for the top.

target.recipe_text:
one point pumpkin pie  crustless

i got this recipe from my weight watchers group. i admit i do prefer traditional pumpkin pie but this is pretty good. all the ingredients are core, too, even though baked goods don't qualify as core due to abuse potential.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine all ingredients
3. spray 9" pie plate with pam
4. pour mixture into pie plate
5. bake at 400 f for 15 minutes
6. reduce heat to 325 f and continue baking for about 45 minutes or until a knife comes out clean
7. slice into 8 pieces
target.review: I make this pie every winter--I love it! Today I made it using butternut squash puree and it's just as good as the pumpkin. The only thing I do different is add 1/2 cup self-rising flour.  I've never tried it without.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat pumpkin cornbread

higher in fiber and nutrients than the usual cornbread. makes a good breakfast item. original from an old mag, but i don't know which one.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 9 inch square baking pan with nonstick cooking spray and coat lightly with flour
3. combine the first 8 dry ingredients
4. in another bowl , beat the butter and sugar together until fluffy
5. add eggs and pumpkin and combine thoroughly
6. add dry mixture and milk alternately until all are incorporated and the mixture is smooth
7. pour into pan
8. bake 60-70 minutes , until tester inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Yum! I was making pumpkin puree today, wondering how in the world I would use it all (I made about 15 pounds!), when I came across this recipe and decided to give it a try.  I was already making a batch of cornbread for my father, so I whipped this one up along with it.  It's a very hearty bread b/c of the whole wheat (and I used stone-ground cornmeal as well), but moist and sweet. I'm thinking about making this to serve with Thanksgiving dinner.  The only thing I changed in the recipe was I substituted buttermilk for the milk since that's all I had, but it turned out great, nonetheless!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrot pancake

i always try to make meals as "healthy" as possible for my 1 and a half year old daughter. so, for breakfasts i've played around with ideas for pancakes. i decided to be adventurous and add carrots. your first reaction might be "gross!" but it actually tastes rather good. my daughter loves them and eats them up.

1. in a bowl , mix together the dry ingredients [flour , sugar , b
2. powder , salt
3. ]
4. mix in the milk , egg , and applesauce
5. put raw , uncooked carrots in a food processor until very fine
6. stir the carrots in with the batter
7. spray your griddle or frying pan with cooking spray , then heat to 375 or medium heat
8. use 1 / 4 cup to measure out your pancakes
9. cook pancakes until bubbly on top , then flip over until the other side is also cooked and golden
demonstrations.review: I made one as intended, then added vanilla, cinnamon & raisins to the batter and cooked the rest that way, which I found tastier. This is a very moist pancake and tasty--especially for being so healthy. I used almond breeze for the milk & opted for applesauce instead of oil. I made a cream cheese spread for the topping made with 4 oz reduced fat cream cheese,  1/4 cup powdered sugar, 3 tbsp milk & 1 tsp vanilla.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whole wheat cornbread

this bread is great with chili or stew

1. combine the corn meal , flour , baking powder , and salt
2. add the honey , oil , milk and eggs
3. mix just enough to moisten the batter
4. pour the batter into an oiled 9 by 13 inch baking pan
5. bake at 375 degree oven for 20-35 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Yum! I made this for my Dad, who is a cornbread fanatic, but I couldn't help myself from nabbing a piece before I delivered the pan to him.  Can't say that I'm sorry, b/c it turned out really yummy.  I'll definitely be making this again--and not just for my Dad, either!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter truffle brownies

for those of us who crave peanut butter and brownies together! from the betty crocker website.

1. heat oven to 350f grease bottom only of 13x9-inch pan with cooking spray or shortening
2. in medium bowl , stir brownie mix , pouch of chocolate syrup , water , oil and eggs until well blended
3. spread in pan
4. bake 28 to 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted 2 inches from side of pan comes out almost clean
5. cool completely , about 1 hour
6. in medium bowl , beat filling ingredients with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth
7. spread mixture evenly over brownie base
8. in small microwavable bowl , microwave topping ingredients uncovered on high 30 to 60 seconds
9. stir until smooth
10. cool 10 minutes
11. spread over filling
12. refrigerate about 30 minutes or until set
13. for brownies , cut into 9 rows by 4 rows
14. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: These are my new favorite brownie. They are perfection!! An offset spatula really helps with spreading the filling (since it is fairly thick and hard to spread) and topping (since it has to be spread very thin).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Obviously I'm in the minority here, but I don't see what all the fuss is about. This chile tastes more like baked beans with meat in it and although it's nice, I like my chile to taste like chile.  The sweetness was the only drawback for me--it had a nice flavor otherwise & you couldn't even tell there was beer, coffee and chocolate in it. But that might be because of the sweetness! If I ever make it again, which is doubtful, I would omit most or all of the sugar.

target.recipe_text:
no bake sugar plums

my kids love to make these cookies, and they make wonderful gifts! a great cookie for vegans or people who are lactose-intolerant.

1. in a food processor or by hand , finely chop apricots , pecans , figs or dates , raisins and coconut
2. add liqueur or orange juice and almond flavoring
3. stir until well blended
4. roll into 36 balls , about 1-inch , by placing a small amount of the mixture between the palms of your hands
5. roll each ball in granulated sugar
6. layer in an airtight container , placing waxed paper or plastic wrap between each layer to prevent sticking
7. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
8. serve on a glass plate lined with a paper doily
target.review: This is a wonderful recipe, and it deserves every one of it's five stars. I used dates and orange liqueur, and rolled 1/2 tablespoon sized balls in a mixture of plain coco and hot chocolate mix. I put the balls into little candy cups, and they looked like chocolate truffles! I gave them out as Christmas gifts, and had great feedback. I'll be making these every Christmas from now on. Thanks for a fantastic recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan apple crisp  no margarine

at christmas, my mom always baked an apple crisp in her deep glass pie dish, and we unashamedly scarfed it down. the apples made it healthy, sure, but what about all the hard fat? when we went vegan and couldn't buy a dairy-free margarine, that was a dilemma. thankfully, we don't have to resort to crisco. we found and modified this recipe on vegweb, and now our holiday apple crisp is every bit as sinfully sweet, appley and crispy as it ever was.

1. first of all , feel free to use any type or combination of apples
2. if you are using a very firm variety- granny smith for instance- it is a good idea to cook them for a couple of minutes , with as little water water as possible , just to warm and slightly soften them
3. otherwise they will stay rather firm instead of half-melting as they bake
4. preheat oven to 350
5. mix the other ingredients , with a spoon , then with fingers , until the texture is crumbly
6. if too dry , add more oil or soymilk
7. if too wet , add more flour
8. transfer the apples to a medium casserole or pie dish
9. sprinkle the dry mixture over them and even it out a bit with a spoon
10. bake for 1 / 2 hour , checking occasionally , till the "crisp" is golden and crispy ! allow to cool a little before devouring with a scoop of vanilla ice cream -- enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a GREAT apple crisp recipe!! I used unsweetened almond milk, and reserved a third of the sugar to mix with the apples before sprinkling on the topping. I also served it with some banana-date syrup (recipe # 192974). What a scrumptious dessert!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan spelt banana bread

vegan banana bread made with spelt flour, pecans, and maple syrup

1. heat oven to 350f
2. oil a loaf pan
3. in a bowl , mash bananas and mix in the maple syrup , canola oil , and vanilla
4. in a separate bowl sift the dry ingredients together , adding the nuts last
5. blend the wet and dry mixtures and pour into the loaf pan
6. bake for 42 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was so impressed with this recipe! The texture was perfect, and it tastes wonderful. I baked the loaf for exactly 42 minutes. I took the advice of White Rose Child and used 1 tsp of vanilla, and halved the maple syrup. I also added 1/2 tsp of cinnamon. Thanks for a super recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw vegan fruit tart

a healthy tart consisting of almonds, medjool dates, and fruit!

1. food process the almonds , medjool dates , and salt until they become coarse crumbs
2. get a 9 in pie pan and using your hands or a rubber spatula , press the almond mixture into the form of a crust
3. plastic wrap the crust and put in the freezer for about 15-20 minutes
4. meanwhile , blend the mango and the soaked dried mango until smooth
5. leave in refrigerator until ready to assemble tart
6. pour the filling over the crust and top off with fruit
7. cover the entire tart
8. refrigerate for at least an hour
9. preferably , overnight
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: A fantastic recipe! I made a couple of changes. I used half almonds, half pecans for the base and used a dried fruit mix instead of mango. I also increased the amount of dried fruit to firm up the filling. I topped it off with some strawberries, bananas and blueberries. Super yummy!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted balsamic beets

even if you don't normally like beets, you'll love the sweet and tangy taste of this easy recipe.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. wash and peel the beets
3. slice each beet in quarters lengthwise , and then slice each quarter into three chunks
4. line a baking sheet with foil , and place the beets on top
5. drizzle with the olive oil and vinegar , and then add salt and pepper
6. gently stir to coat the beets
7. cover with more foil and roll the edges of the two layers to create a pouch for the beets
8. cook for 20 minutes
9. remove the beets from the oven , and raise the temperature to 400 degrees
10. take off the top layer of foil , and stir to mix the juices
11. return to the oven and continue to cook for 35 minutes , stirring occasionally
12. serve warm or cold , or add to a salad
demonstrations.review: This is an absolutely fantastic recipe!! With the advice of the other reviewers I decided to leave the foil on the entire time. I cooked them for 20 minutes at 350, stirred the juices, and then cooked them for 20 minutes at 375. Finally, I stirred them again, turned down the heat to 325 and cooked for approx 15-20 minutes. They turned out great!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana date syrup

adds a simple, sweet touch to hot pancakes, cooked grains, scones  or... i suspect anything else! this basic idea can be endlessly varied, of course.

1. combine the banana , dates and juice in a blender , and puree until very smooth
2. add more juice if you want it thinner
3. sprinkle in a bit of cinnamon if you like
4. serve immediately
5. this gets sweeter if you store it very long in the refrigerator but it tastes best fresh
demonstrations.review: What a fantastic and super versatile syrup!! My family and company loved it. I tripled the recipe and added about a teaspoon of cinnamon. I served it over an apple crisp, which was a big hit. We can't wait to have it on some pancakes tomorrow morning. This is a definite keeper!

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: Just made these last night for supper using leftover roast chicken. Delicious! Tasted sinful and knowing they're not, made it all that much better. Made them exactly as posted except I also used olive oil brushed on them before putting them in the oven. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quiche lorraine

as we all know, this is one of the greatest lunch or brunch dishes ever invented. prepare in advance, freeze, and bake when needed. this is one of the best recipes for quiche i know of. recipe source, "the country innkeepers' cookbook".

1. combine the cheese and flour and sprinkle into the pie shell
2. spread the ham evenly over this
3. combine the eggs , milk , salt and mustard
4. beat until smooth and pour evenly over the cheese and ham
5. bake at 375 degrees for 45 minutes , or until the custard is set
6. serve warm , garnished with chopped parsley
7. to freeze: prepare recipe through step 4
8. wrap well with saran wrap and then foil
9. freeze
10. to serve: thaw in fridge overnight
11. bake as directed
demonstrations.review: Just made this for Valentine's day brunch.  It was very good and so easy.This was the first quiche I've ever made. I especially like that it is made with milk and not whipping cream as many other quiche recipes seem to call for.  I also used a deep dish pie crust and agree that it was perfect.  Thanks for submitting Tweeky,will definitly make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey pot pie with stuffing crust  using leftovers

this is my favorite pot pie to use up those holiday leftovers. i tend to make more stuffing and gravy then i need for the meal so that i can use up the leftover turkey in this way. i love the crispy stuffing crust on the top. the gravy keeps the potpie from being dry.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook vegetable mix according to package instructions
3. drain well
4. mix together turkey , vegetables , garlic powder , sage , salt and pepper in a large bowl
5. if using a bottom pie crust , line a 9 x 13 rectangular cake pan with crust
6. prick all over and pre-bake until light brown
7. spoon vegetable and turkey mixture into the 9 x 13 rectangular cake pan
8. pour gravy over the vegetable / turkey mixture
9. top with stuffing , spreading evenly over all
10. bake for 30 minutes or until hot and the stuffing crust is brown and crispy
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to make and used up all those leftovers.  I didn't have any leftover stuffing so I used stovetop.  It was still good but I think it would have been better with homemade stuffing. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch chicken thighs

needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. this is adapted from an old taste of home magazine. the chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. you won't miss the skin!  
eta -- some say this is too bland.  the ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  i do add season salt to taste (nature's seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine crumbs , parmesan cheese , cornmeal , italian seasoning , and seasoned salt
2. dip chicken into salad dressing , then coat with crumb mixture
3. place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: Kelly this tasted great!  You don't miss the skin at all.  I didn't use the cornmeal and I used light ranch dressing and it turned out fantastic. I will definetly make again, in fact I'm planning on trying it on chicken breasts next.  Thanks for this very easy, and very tasty recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: I just realized I hadn't rated these yet!  Not that you need another 5 star rating!! These were fantastic.  I actually made these and took them to a work Christmas party in December, it is now July and people are STILL talking about them.  Going to a bbq tonight and am planning on making these for dessert.  I made these exactly as posted with 2 cups of chocolat chips.  Then I melted some chocolate chips and peanut butter chips together and frosted the brownies with the mixture.  Amazing!!!  Delicious! Would definitely give this more than 5 stars if I could.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish with bell peppers

a long time ago i was flipping through one of my mother's cookbooks, which happened to be from weight watcher's. i found this dish and find it very easy to make and is healthy for you. i have used several types of fish and it always tastes good. i hope you enjoy it.

1. if fish are large , cut into 4 servings
2. heat oil in 10-inch non-stick skillet
3. layer onion and bell peppers in skillet
4. sprinkle with half of thyme and pepper
5. place fish over bell peppers and sprinkle with remaining spice
6. cover and cook over low heat for 15 minutes
7. uncover and cook until fish flakes easily with fork , 10 to 15 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! I used haddock and only about 1/8tsp of pepper because I'm not that fond of black pepper. It's so healthy, tasty and simple how can I not put it into my "keepers" file. Can't wait to try it with other types of fish.  Thanks for posting such a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
dried cherry scones

wonderful scones served at a local bed and breakfast here in my town. prep and cook times are a guess, since i only tasted, but haven't made yet.

1. combine 1 / 2 cup of dried cherries with 2 tablespoons brandy or apricot nectar
2. let stand for 15 minutes
3. combine dry ingredients
4. cut the shortening into the dry ingredients well
5. add pecans
6. make a 'hole' in the center of the dried mixture
7. stir together well beaten egg and half-and-half
8. add egg and fruit mixtures to dry ingredients all at once
9. using a fork , stir just until moistened
10. turn dough onto a lightly floured surface
11. knead for 12 to 15 strokes
12. form dough into a 7 inch circle , and cut into 8 wedges
13. place scones 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking sheet
14. brush tops with 1 tbsp half-and-half , sprinkle with 2 tsp sugar
15. bake in a 400 degree oven for 12 to 15 minutes
16. cool on a wire rack for 5 minutes
17. serve warm with maple-nut butter posted on this site , if desired
target.review: I made your recipe for Mother's Day, Keen 5, and it was just delicious!  I used unsalted, dry-roasted almonds instead of pecans, and butter instead of shortening.  Next time I make these I will add a dash of almond extract.  I found that applying the half-and-half and sprinkle of sugar to the round of dough before cutting it into wedges made the process easier.  I also found that a bench scraper worked really well for cutting the dough.  Thank you for this classic of a recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot and sour salmon soup

from the new zealand magazine cuisine. i haven't made this, but plan to.

1. place the stock and ginger in a large saucepan , bring to the boil , lower the heat and simmer for 5 minutes
2. strain to remove the ginger
3. discard
4. return stock to the pan , add salmon strips , bok choy and chilli to the stock , simmer gently for 2 minutes
5. lastly add soy sauce , and sugar and lime juice to taste and to achieve a balanced hot , sweet , salty , sour flavour
6. ladle into serving bowls and garnish with torn coriander leaves
demonstrations.review: I halved this recipe and used U.S. measurements for the broth and salmon: 3 1/4 cups low sodium chicken broth, and 3/4 lb. fresh salmon cut into 1/2 inch cubes. I also used 3 baby bok choy instead of 2, slicing them horizontaly, added an 8 oz. can of bamboo shoot strips, drained, and added a dash of sesame oil. Not finding fresh, small red chilies in my grocery stores, I used a combination of crushed red pepper flakes, ground white pepper, and Asian hot chili oil (all three are often used in traditional hot and sour soup)for the 'heat'. Instead of following the directions, I didn't add the salmon until the bok choy had cooked, because the minute I added the salmon to the hot broth, it was cooked! Using farm-raised salmon and adding it at the end of the cooking process made for very succulent, fully cooked, poached salmon pieces. Thank you so much for this recipe, JustJanS/JanRoundOz. I will make the soup often, because it has  light, clean, fresh flavors, and is extra delicious with the additions I made. Lynnie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pulehu tri tip steak

here's a recipe i got when i went to hawaii - tri-tip steak is one of the newer cuts of beef, and is pretty tender.

1. combine spices and rub into meat
2. let sit for 30 minutes
3. broil or grill the steaks , turning every 4 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this using about 6 oz. of tri-tip and about 1 tsp. each salt, sugar and coursely ground black pepper, with a couple of good shakes of garlic powder. I grilled the steak on my Le Creuset grill pan, cooking for 4 mins. on each side.  Great flavor, and easy, too.  Thanks, Chris!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai style roast chicken

tender chicken roasted in thai flavours.

1. wash and dry chicken
2. combine all ingredients except chicken
3. pour mixture inside and over chicken
4. cover and allow to marinate in fridge for at least 1 hour
5. move to a wire rack baking tray
6. bake , uncovered , in preheated 180c oven for 1 1 / 2 hours or until cooked , brushing occasionally with pan juices
demonstrations.review: Very  juicy and flavorful fresh out of the oven, as were the leftovers.   I used low fat coconut milk, increased the chopped cilantro (stems and all) to 1/2 cup, decreased the fish sauce by half (to lower the sodium content), and increased the green curry paste to replace the heat and flavor from the small fresh chili I didn't have on hand.  Since my chicken was over 4 lbs., I roasted it 1.5 hours at 350* and 30 minutes at 375*.  Leftover meat was great in a salad with Thai flavors and in a soup (I cooked the chicken carcass  in chicken broth for an hour, removed the bones, skimmed off the fat, and added green curry paste, fresh minced cilantro stems, cut green beans, white corn kernals, slivered bamboo shoots, the last of the leftover chicken meat, and a cup of leftover cooked rice to the broth.  Brought it to a simmer, and it, too, was fabulous.   I can't wait for the weather to cooperate so I can roast  the chicken outdoors on my charcoal grill.  Thank you so much for sharing  this recipe, Jewelies! It's a real favorite.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
freezer margarita

easy, blender free, slushy, margarita. perfect for camping, the rv or just to have on hand for a quick and yummy frozen drink! just dump it all into a tupperware type container and freeze! the alcohol prevents it from freezing solid. prep time does not include freeze time.

1. place everything into a sealable container
2. freeze until firm
3. brake / stir the concoction until its a yummy , slushy drink !
demonstrations.review: What an easy, tasty recipe!  I made it during a recent "heat wave" here in the N.W.  I had no triple sec on hand and used Grand Marnier instead, with good results.  When I tasted the mixture before freezing it, I thought it was going to turn out too watery. But, the flavor was great after freezing it!  I love having this on hand for guests, and that I don't have to use a blender to make it.  Thanks for the recipe, dukeswalker!  Lynnie

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached eggs

i have been poaching eggs in the microwave for many years.  for me this is the best way to prepare poached eggs for 2.  it is quick, easy and almost foolproof.  please make sure you use a toothpick to pierce the yolk before cooking or it will explode!

1. add the water and white vinegar to a 6 ounce custard cup
2. break egg into cup , pierce egg yolk with toothpick , and cover dish loosely with plastic wrap
3. place in microwave and cook for 1 minute or until desired doneness
4. you may need to experiment with cooking times based on the wattage of your microwave and taste preference
5. immediately remove egg from hot water with a slotted spoon as it will continue to cook
6. serve with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: The thing I like best about this recipe is the ease of clean-up after making it.  But I really struggled to get the eggwhite to cook beyond runny without over-cooking the yolk.  After a half-dozen tries, I decided to heat the water/vinegar mixture for about 30 seconds before adding in the egg, which produced better results.  I still have more experimenting to do to get it just right, and I think the water's temp. when you add the egg plays a big part in this recipe's success.  I didn't use plastic wrap - I don't believe it is necessary.  Thank you, PaulaG, poaching eggs in the microwave is a great idea!  Lynnie

target.recipe_text:
you like cheese   garlic bread spread

this is fantastic. this was posted on a canning list, and this is a definite staple in my fridge. the best thing about it is that you make it, and it keeps in the fridge for up to 2 months. the taste is fantastic!

1. in large mixing bowl , mix all ingredients together
2. fold until all is blended
3. keep refrigerated in mason jars with lids , or in containers with tightly fitting lids
4. to make garlic bread , slice french bread and place on cookie sheet
5. spoon spread onto bread
6. toast , bake , or broil until cheese is bubbly and nicely browned
target.review:
Very good spread recipe! I think next time I will leave out the lemon juice. I did not care for the lemon taste so much but the garlic was heavenly! I am making this for company tomorrow night.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mountain dew jelly

nan

1. pour mountian dew and lemon juice into a large pot
2. bring to boil
3. boil 3 minutes
4. cool slightly
5. then follow the sure jell directions
6. process for 10 minutes in a boiling water bath
7. you can use more mountain dew and reduce it to 3-1 / 4 c
8. for a more concentrated flavor
demonstrations.review:
I was so happy to see this recipe! I am originally from Marion, Va which is the birthplace of Mountain Dew. I can't beleive I have never heard of this jelly before. What a great gift this will make for friends and family back home!
Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pinto beans

my family loves this recipe after trying many different ones. when i'm short on time i use canned beans and just add the rest of the ingredients, i cook the bacon up when using canned beans. enjoy!

1. clean beans and wash well with water
2. put beans in large pot , add water
3. bring beans to boil and let boil for 1 hour
4. check closely , as beans cook , you will probably need to add more water
5. run tap water until very hot before adding to beans
6. add bacon pieces and cook another 45 minutes
7. add spices and reduce heat to low and cook another 20 to 25 minutes
demonstrations.review:
My DH requested pinto beans for his birthday and when I saw this recipe I decided to try it. It was great. The only thing different I did was to use fresh garlic and onion. I also made Garlic-Onion Dinner Muffins #50973 and the combination was heavenly...just good ole comfort food!
Thanks. You posted this one just in time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my dill dip

this is a great tasting dill dip that i have used for years. i usually double this recipe and keep it on hand. cook time is chill time

1. mix ingredients together , until well blended
2. chill several hours or overnight
3. serve with chips or raw vegetables
4. the longer it sits- the better it gets !
demonstrations.review:
What a great dip! I just whipped this up in a matter of minutes and it is absolutley delicious. My kids love raw veggies and I always try to have dip for them as well. No more store bought dip mix packets for me!
Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatballs stuffed with pineapple chunks

i got this recipe from a microwave cookbook i bought my mother 25 years ago.  i love to serve these as appetizers for parties, and also with rice for dinner.  this is a quick, tasty, easy recipe.  give it a try!!

1. drain pineapple well , reserving syrup
2. mix together beef , egg , bread crumbs , onion , salt , cloves , allspice and 2 tbsp syrup
3. mold small amount of mixture around each pineapple chunk
4. place meatballs in 12x8x2" glass dish
5. cover with wax paper
6. mirowave at high 4 minutes
7. pour off meat juices
8. stir together 1 / 3 c reserved syrup , ketchup and brown sugar
9. pour over drained meatballs and microwave at high 3 to 5 minutes longer , or until done
demonstrations.review:
I couldn't wait to try this recipe. It was wonderful!! I added 1/2 tsp of garlic powder and baked them in the oven instead of the microwave. I can't wait to serve these at my next party.
Thanks for sharing a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock goldfish cheese puffs

saw this made on a foodtv show and thought it would be fun to make with ds.  we tried the other day and he had a glorious time.  they are quite tasty too.  make these as spicy or salty as you want.  change the seasonings for totally different snack.  please note that they can quickly go from baked to burnt.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. stack the slices of cheese and cut into 16 small squares
3. separate the pieces and place next to each other on a flat surface
4. combine the salt , chili powder and garlic powder
5. sprinkle seasoning mix onto cheese
6. toss the cheese to thoroughly season both sides of cheese
7. arrange the cheese squares on a parchment-lined baking sheet , leaving a little space between the squares
8. bake about 7 - 7 1 / 2 minutes , until well-browned and crispy
9. cool completely
10. store in airtight container on countertop
demonstrations.review:
These are wonderful! What a great idea for an after school snack.
My kids loved them. They all thought they tasted like pizza. I can't wait to experiment with some different seasonings too.
Thanks Ducky!

target.recipe_text:
mustardy green beans

i think green bean recipes are like pairs of shoes....you can't have too many! here's a real quick and easy one.

1. bring water to a boil
2. cook beans until crisp-tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. drain
4. heat oil in the same pan
5. stir in mustard and salt and pepper to taste
6. add beans
7. toss to coat and serve warm
target.review: Mmmm!  I only had canned green beans, so I didn't have to cook them first.  I also cut the recipe in half because I just used one can.  The garlic adds a nice touch, but it would be delicious without!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
i hate ricotta meat   2 cheese stuffed shells

my non-ricotta cheese-eating husband always raved about "the meat stuffed shells his mom used to make." his grandmother recently wrote to the tv guide (where this recipe originated) and they were kind enough to send back the recipe, dated september 13, 1976. i have to agree, these are delicious! serve with a tossed salad and garlic bread. the prep time includes the pasta/beef cooking; the cook time is the baking time for the casserole.

1. boil water for pasta
2. meanwhile , in a large skillet , brown ground beef , onion and garlic
3. drain and cool
4. cook pasta in water , drain
5. preheat oven to 400 degrees
6. meanwhile pasta is cooking , combine meat , mozzarella cheese , bread crumbs , egg and parsley
7. season with salt and pepper
8. mix spaghetti sauce with tomato sauce
9. cover bottom of a 13x9 casserole dish with 1 / 4 of the sauce
10. stuff cooked , drained shells with the meat mixture and place on top of sauce in dish in a row
11. add red wine to remaining sauce and mix well
12. cover shells with sauce and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
13. bake in oven for 20-25 minutes or until bubbly and browned
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  I didn't believe all the filling was going to fit in 18 shells, so I made more.  I wasted the extras because indeed, it fit perfectly in 18 shells.  I think next time I will cook the spaghetti sauce and wine because 25 minutes in the oven was not enough time for the wine and sauce to meld together.   I used high quality wine, but it stood out too much alone in the sauce. I also used ground venison instead of beef.   Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot bbq beef moose venison

this is great shredded with chopped greens and served in tortillas or served as the main course with rice.

1. in a bowl add 1st 8 ingredients
2. reserve 1 / 2 cup for sauce later
3. trim excess fat from meat if using chuck roast
4. put meat and onions into a 4 quart crock pot or dutch oven
5. pour liquid over meat
6. crock pot: cover & cook 5-6 hours on high
7. dutch oven: cook covered for 3 hours at 325f
8. remove meat from liquid and serve with sauce
9. sauce: heat reserved spiced liquid , ketchup , and butter in a sauce pan until heat until butter melts
10. set aside in fridge
11. heat through and serve with meat
demonstrations.review: We eat a lot of venison in our house and I am always looking for new ways to serve it.  Unfortunately, this isn't exactly what I was hoping for.  BBQ led me to believe it would be a bit tangy, but I didn't feel this had much of a BBQ taste.  The onions overpowered the venison.  I even added only one onion, and they were still too overpowering, and we even like onions :)  I could see where this recipe would be really good with a really "gamey" piece of meat as the onions would disguise the game flavor.  We did enjoy it, hence the 4 stars, but it wasn't quite what we were looking for.  I served this with Parmesan-mustard Mashed Potatoes Recipe #49073 and they seemed to be a nice mix in flavors.  Thanks a bunch! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer battered fish  for fish n chips

i love fried fish.. always have. when dining out, nine times out of ten, i will order fish n'chips. it's getting to be very hard to find a restaurant that serves good fish n'chips anymore..so i just had to learn to make them myself.

1. sift together flour , salt , and paprika
2. stir in enough beer to make batter so it is barely thick enough to coat a spoon
3. usually somewhere between one and two cans
4. set batter aside while you heat your deep-fryer or deep pan of oil to 375 degrees
5. use a candy thermometer if you need to
6. peanut oil is best but any vegetable oil will do
7. cut the cod fillets diagonally into 2 inch wide strips , and remove any pin bones from fish
8. lightly coat fish in flour and shake off excess
9. this will allow batter to stick to fish
10. when oil is heated , dip fish in batter , let excess drip off , then fry fillets 2 or 3 at a time until golden brown
11. drain on paper towels
12. serve with fries and tartar sauce
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent beer battered fish recipe!  I make fish and chips a lot and I have searched high and low for a recipe I like.  This takes the cake! I only had to use one can of beer, and for fish, I used lingcod.  Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
satay ayam  chicken satay

this looks incredible. another recipe sent to me from my mother (who knows i loooove ethnic cooking!) i will be posting the katjang (spicy peanut) sauce separately. (prep time is marinade time). this is an appetizer recipe, so the serving sizes may be small compared to what one would need for a main course.

1. combine the garlic , salt and pepper in a deep bowl and mash them to a paste with the back of a spoon
2. mix in the soy sauce , molasses and lime juice
3. add the chicken cubes and toss until they are evenly coated
4. marinate in the refrigerator for 2 hours , stirring occasionally
5. remove the chicken from the marinade and thread it tightly , 4 or 5 pieces at a time , on small skewers (preferably oriental wooden skewers about 6 inches long)
6. brush the oil evenly over the chicken
7. cook over charcoal or under the kitchen broiler for 5 to 10 minutes , turning occasionally , until the chicken is crisp and brown
8. serve at once , with the meat still on the skewers , accompanied by katjang sauce presented separately in a bowl
demonstrations.review: My husband gave me three hours notice that we needed a dish for a retirement potluck!  I quickly thawed some chicken breast and had this dish ready to serve from thaw to finish in three hours! It was inhaled by everyone.  I made the peanut sauce that accompanies this dish.  Everyone was very impressed with the presentation, and I didn't have a crumb left over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
donny s asian noodles

this dish is a great way of using up leftovers, and is very versatile re: what meat/fish you use. my friend donny made these for me and i loved them, i think the recipe originated in one of the company's coming cookbooks, but both donny & i have adjusted some stuff to our taste. great pot luck addition.

1. heat water in large covered sauce pan until boiling , add noodles , bring back to a boil , stirring occasionally to prevent sticking , then turn heat off and let stand until ready to use
2. heat oil in wok , adding garlic& ginger , cook until tender
3. add meat , then cayenne , green onions , oyster sauce& curry powder
4. stir thoroughly
5. drain noodles , add to wok and toss may be served now , but re-heats really well
demonstrations.review: My lips are still on fire from this one!  This was really good.  I wanted to make this a main course, and I didn't want to make a side vegi dish, so, I threw in some scallops as well half of a mixed bag of frozen "stir fry" vegis.  The result was fantastic!  Next time I might add only 3/4 tsp. cayenne.  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
creamy pork tenderloin

this is adapted from taste of home's best of country cooking 1999. my dh loves it and that's all that matters!

1. cut tenderloin into 3 / 4" slices
2. in a shallow dish , combine egg , water , rosemary , pepper , and garlic powder
3. dip pork slices into egg mixture and then into bread crumbs
4. in a large skillet over medium heat , brown pork in oil and butter for 5 minutes on each side
5. remove pork to a 13x9 baking dish
6. in the same skillet , combine soup and sour cream
7. heat through
8. pour sauce over pork
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
target.review: Very Good, very rich!  It needs a side dish like rice or potatoes. The flavor is yummy.  I used Progresso Italian breadcrumbs and chopped fresh rosemary and it was really delicious.  Lots of flavor for the effort.  I will try with thin boneless pork chops next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan grilled chicken with avocado and red onion salsa

a wonderful combination of flavors and color. quick and easy for week day meals and a wonderful entree for a dinner party. joining zaar has reunited me with many old favorites long lost in my 35 year old collection of recipes. this recipe, written on the back of a sales slip, probably came from a doctor's or dentist's office as i looked through magazines while waiting to be seen.

1. whisk marinade ingredients together and pour over chicken , marinate 20 minutes
2. add oil and chicken to a hot heavy skillet and brown on both sides , reduce heat and cook until juices run clear
3. while chicken is cooking , mix salsa ingredients together , season with salt and pepper , and stir in coriander
4. serve chicken and salsa on individual plates garnished with red onion , lime and cabbage
demonstrations.review: Easy to make, didn\'t have the red pepper flakes so I used a little cayenne pepper.  The salsa was great, boyfriend loved it.  Next time I will reduce the oil in the salsa, it really didn\'t need that much. This one is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken suiza cornbread bake

a wonderful mexican inspired casserole. i got this one from my aunt. she's been making this for years, and it's one of my uncles favorites, and he usually doesn't like mexican cuisine!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. grease a 9 x 13-inch baking dish
3. melt butter in small skillet over medium-high heat
4. add onion and garlic
5. cook and stir 4 to 6 minutes or until tender , stirring constantly
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , combine corn , cream style corn , eggs and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
8. mix well
9. add corn muffin mix-mix well
10. fold in cooked onion mixture
11. pour into greased dish
12. in a large bowl , combine all topping ingredients , except cheese , mix well
13. spoon over corn bread to within 1 inch of edges
14. sprinkle with cheese
15. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes or until edges are golden brown
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, I used non sweet conrbread mix and thought it was great.  Next time I'll use the whole can of chopped green chiles and may throw in some chopped jalapenos.  I used a mexican blend of cheeses which had monterey jack in it.  I didn't have mushrooms so I threw in chopped black olives instead. It was easy to make and if you use less butter and fat free sour cream I don't think you would be able to tell the difference.  I don't think the recipe would be enough for 12 servings, it's too good and everyone will want seconds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato salad with chipotle peppers a man s salad

warning warning !! this tex mex salad is very spicy !!!  use your best judgment in how much chipotle peppers you use. taste as you add just don't dump them all in. each pepper has it's own heat level. yes us girls love it too! ;)

1. mix first 7 ingredients together
2. toss in remaining ingredients except 1 tablespoon bacon and salt and pepper
3. mix well
4. taste to see if you need to add salt and pepper
5. i myself like lots of pepper
6. top with bacon bits
7. chill& serve
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved it, I made as written, second time I didn't have red pepper and was still delicious.  I can't decide if I like cilantro or parsley better.  The heat doesn't hit you until you've a had couple of bites.  I like things hot but don't think more would be better.  It's a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 layer cream cheese pudding dessert

this is a wonderful recipe. it is so easy and no one would ever know! the great thing is you may use any flavor you like for the pudding. i would use chocolate or vanilla 8)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine the flour , nuts and margarine
3. press mixture into a 13x9-inch pan
4. bake 10-15 minutes
5. while cooling , combine the cream cheese , powdered sugar and 1 cup cool whip
6. spread over first layer
7. mix the pudding and milk
8. pour on creamy layer
9. chill
10. spread with remaining cool whip
11. you may sprinkle with toasted coconut if you like
demonstrations.review: I make this all the time everyone always loves it,  I use 1 cup of nuts in the crust and only add 1/2 cup of powdered sugar to the cream cheese layer. I use chocolate and vanilla pudding mixed together while in powder form and only add 2 1/2 cups of milk, I also add 1 teaspoon of vanilla to the pudding mixture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple cream cheese ball

the best cheese ball i've ever had. i got the recipe from a caterer

1. combine all ingredients , savings some pecans to roll cheese ball in
2. pack mixture into a bowl or mold
3. chill until firm
4. remove and roll in pecans to coat exterior
5. serve with crackers
demonstrations.review: Glad I found this one, my aunt used to make this at Christmas.... yummy!  Everyone at work wanted the recipe, it's a great combination of flavors, you've got to let it chill for a while to blend flavors.  I like it with baked pita chips.

target.recipe_text:
spinach stuffed chicken

moist and juicy, with a lucious filling! this is a very elegant dish that is also very easy!

1. in lg skillet , cook spinach in water until wilted , 2 minutes
2. drain and set aside
3. in same skillet , saute onions , mushrooms , and garlic in oil for 1 minute
4. stir in the seasonings and spinach
5. set aside
6. flatten chicken
7. spread spinach mix down center of chicken breasts
8. roll up tightly
9. secure with toothpick
10. mix crumbs , cheese , and paprika
11. beat egg with water
12. dip each roll in egg , then crumbs
13. place , seam side down , in 13x9 baking pan coated with cooking spray
14. drizzle with butter
15. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 25 minutes
target.review: What a wonderful way to serve chicken!  It looks very 'professional'.  My family seemed very impressed.  I followed the directions perfectly and it came out perfectly.  My family really really really enjoyed this recipe.  This awesome recipe is DEFINTELY a keeper and I would suggest that everyone try it! Thank you for the awesome recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy chicken and asparagus

from quick cooking magazine. this tastes wonderful and looks great on the table. a great way to get the kids to eat asparagus too :)

1. if desired , partially cook the asparagus
2. drain
3. place the asparagus in a greased 9 inch square baking dish
4. in a skillet over medium heat , brown the chicken in oil on both sides
5. season with salt and pepper
6. arrange chicken over asparagus
7. in a bowl , mix soup , mayonnaise , lemon juice and curry powder
8. pour over chicken
9. cover and bake at 375 for 40 minutes or until the chicken is tender and juices run clear
10. sprinkle with cheese
11. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I was going to post this recipe because it is my FAVORITE dinner dish! Since I was 5 I begged my mom to make me this all the time! She never used the curry though, but I still loved it.  Everyone loves this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
2  handed kitchen sink tomato sandwich

i got this recipe from an old georgia boy that was transplanted in tennessee, he is 72 and says he grew up on this sandwich.

1. in the peak of tomato season , chill 1 very large or 2 medium size tomatoes that have been vine-ripened and have plenty juice
2. take 2- slices of bread and coat them with 1 / 4 inch good mayonnaise
3. add layer of tomatoes cut 1 / 4 inch thick
4. salt & pepper to taste
5. add another slice of tomatoes and salt and pepper to taste again
6. add the other piece of bread on top of this
7. roll up your sleeves and start eating over the kitchen sink while the juice runs down your elbows
demonstrations.review: This really is my favorite sandwich.  I think the key to it is having good tomatoes, not the orangy-red yucky ones!  There's nothing like nice big red tomatoes from the garden!  Sometimes I also add a slice of american cheese, but I don't think it is needed! yum yum

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my grandmother s fresh peach cobbler

my grandmother used this recipe every summer when the peaches were ripe. she got the recipe from her church cookbook. you can use any almost any kind of fruit in the cobbler, it will still be good.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into an 8x8 pan
3. whisk together the flour , 3 / 4 cup of sugar , baking powder and milk
4. pour over melted butter
5. cover with peach slices
6. cover with 3 / 4 cup sugar
7. bake until batter rises to top and forms a nice brown crust , about 20 - 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: WOW! Was this delicious or what!?!?! Oh my! Very simple to make and everyone loves it! We wish we could give it more stars!I used the extra peach juice as the previous reviewer did and that turned out great! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry tart   couldn t be easier

this blueberry tart is so simple to make yet packs a great taste. everyone always loves this and it is a great way to use blueberries. this recipe comes from the "i can't believe it's kosher" cookbook. note: tart may also be made in a 10-inch pie plate or a 10-inch quiche dish. a little extra care is needed to get the first piece out of a quiche dish.

1. preheat oven to 400f and spray 10-inch springform pan with non-stick cooking spray
2. combine flour , salt and sugar
3. cut in the butter with pastry blender or fork
4. mix in the vinegar
5. pat crust onto bottom of springform pan and 1 inch up side
6. for filling combine sugar , flour and cinnamon
7. add 2 1 / 2 cups blueberries
8. place evenly on top of crust
9. bake for 1 hour
10. remove from oven and put remaining 2 cups blueberries on top , lightly pressing in blueberries
11. cool completely
12. remove rim and serve from springform bottom
demonstrations.review: Wow! We really loved this recipe! I loved how simple it was!!! I was short about a half a cup to a cup of blueberries so in the picture it may appear a little flat.  I was quite suprised how amazing it taste because it was so easy to do!  Sorry that the picture isn't great, as I am new to taking picture, however I WILL be making this again and will take another picture! Thanks for the awesome recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peaches   cream muffins

these are delicious peach flavored muffins with a delightful cream cheese filling and cinammon sugar topping. recipe courtesy addie's attic bed & breakfast

1. dice the drained peaches to about the size of peas
2. set aside
3. in a large bowl , mix flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
4. in separate bowl combine eggs and oil
5. then whisk in the milk
6. combine egg and flour mixtures
7. then fold in diced peaches
8. for filling , beat cream cheese , sugar , peach juice and almond extract
9. fill greased muffin tins half full of batter
10. drop 1 teaspoon of the filling into each muffin cup of the batter and top with 1 1 / 2 tablespoons more batter
11. for topping , mix cinnamon and sugar
12. sprinkle over muffins
13. bake in a preheated oven at 350 for 20 minutes
14. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These muffins were wonderful! I loved them!  What a nice suprise when you bite into one!  I loved the almond flavor also.  I think it went well with the peaches.  Now I know what I will make when I have canned peaches around! Thanks for this delightful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
buttermilk chocolate cupcakes

moist chocolate cupcakes that are always a hit!  cooking time will vary according to the size of your muffin pans and oven.  the cupcakes between 15 and 18 minutes to bake.

1. cupcakes:
2. combine all the cupcake ingredients in a large mixing bowl
3. beat at low speed of an electric mixer just until blended
4. then beat at high speed for 2 minutes
5. spoon the batter into paper-lined muffin pans , filling 2 / 3 full
6. bake at 350 degrees for 15 to 18 minutes , or until a wooden pick inserted in the center comes out clean
7. remove from the pans , and let them cool completely on a wire rack
8. once cool , spread frosting on top of each cupcake
9. frosting:
10. combine all the frosting ingredients in a mixing bowl
11. beat at low speed of an electric mixer until smooth
12. yield: 2 1 / 2 cups
target.review: Very, very moist.  Good thing it's a cupcake recipe, because if you tried to make this as a cake, you'd never be able to slice and serve it.  I made them mint chocolate chip by adding mint chocolate chips to the batter and sprinkling some over the frosting.  I think I must have messed up the frosting, because it came out more the consistency of a thick glaze, but it was still good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian style tuna pasta bake

mouth-watering tuna pasta baked topped with grated cheddar and grated mozzarella!  different from the usual tuna pasta bake which calls for condensed soup.  very easy and very yummy!

1. heat oil in a fairly large pan and add the onion until it softens
2. about 2-3 minutes
3. then add the tuna and saut for another 3 minutes
4. add the chopped tomatoes , tomato puree , italian herb seasoning , oregano , garlic granules and salt & pepper to taste
5. simmer for about 15 minutes-20 minutes or until the sauce has thickened stirring from time to time
6. while the sauce is simmering , heat the oven at 200 degrees or 180 for fan-assisted ovens
7. and cooked the pasta shells 2 minutes less than the directed time on the packet
8. it needs to be a little bit tougher as it still needs to be cooked in the oven
9. do not overcook
10. drain and set aside
11. when the sauce has thickened add the chopped fresh basil and the drained pasta shells and stir until thoroughly mix
12. transfer into an oven-proof dish and topped with grated cheddar and mozzarella
13. bake for another 20- 25 minutes or until the cheese on top has turned golden brown
14. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Yummy and different from cream based tuna casseroles. We really enjoyed it.
NOTE: 06/12 Just wanted to say that I usually use a one pound package of pasta and that works well for us. Also last time I made it I added a can of pumpkin puree. I know that may sound weird, but it doesn't really affect the taste and it adds a little bit of a richer texture to the sauce. Plus it ups the vitamin quotient.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creole black beans  n  sausage

a want-to-try recipe from best of country cooking.

1. in a large skillet , brown sausage over medium heat
2. drain
3. transfer to a 5-qt
4. slow cooker
5. in a large bowl , combine the beans , onion , celery , green pepper , water , tomato sauce , garlic , thyme , bouillon , white pepper , cayenne and bay leaves
6. pour over sausage
7. cover and cook on low for 6 hours or until vegetables are tender
8. discard bay leaves
9. serve with rice
10. yield: 10 servings
demonstrations.review: I made this on Sunday (love using the slow cooker for Sunday Lunch) and we both enjoyed it.   I used turkey sausage and omitted the white pepper to suit my husband's diet.   I also made a 1/3 of the recipe, as it was just my husband and I and that fit well into my 2 1/2 qt. slow cooker.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and swiss dijon braid

this is incredibly yummy!!! it's a dijon flavored bread braided over layers of ham, swiss and dill pickle. it's a great party bread-beautiful and different.

1. combine 3 cups flour , sugar and salt in a mixing bowl
2. in a small saucepan heat water , dijon mustard , and butter to 120-130 degrees
3. stir yeast into liquid
4. let set 5-10 minutes until yeast is foamy
5. add liquid to dry ingredients
6. stir in remaining 1 cup flour to form a stiff yet pliable dough
7. knead 6-8 minutes
8. roll into a 12x14 inch rectangle on a greased baking sheet
9. layer 1 / 2 lb of ham over the dough
10. top with the cheese
11. add the pickle
12. arrange the remaining 1 / 2 lb of ham on top
13. starting on a long side , cut 1 inch wide strips about 3 inches long toward the center
14. repeat on the other long side
15. starting at one end , fold strips at an angle across filling , alternating sides , tucking ends under next strip
16. pinch ends to seal
17. cover with a cloth and let rise for 15-20 minutes
18. brush with the egg
19. bake at 375 degrees for 30-35 minutes
20. serve warm with dijon mustard
demonstrations.review: I made this for supper last night.   I liked it and my husband really enjoyed it.    The flavor combos are very nice.   It is neat to have the Dijon in the bread.   I think this would be great on a party or buffet table.    I would give it 5 stars if the bread part of the recipe was better, the flavor was good but the texture seemed lacking to me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
golden tilapia

this tasty recipe for tilapia is quite easy to make. i got it off of foodnetwork.com. and just slightly modified it. the recipe calls for the fish to marinade for 20 minutes, but i bet it would be even better if marinated for longer. enjoy!

1. simmer in a saucepan over medium heat the sugar , soy sauce , water , lemon zest and lemon juice
2. add the ginger , garlic , and pepper and cook until the sauce is reduced by half
3. allow the sauce to cool and then marinade the fillets in 1 / 2 of the sauce for 20 minutes in the refrigerator
4. reserve the remaining sauce
5. remove fillets from the marinade
6. season with salt and pepper if desired
7. preheat oven to 375 degrees
8. heat skillet to medium high
9. add oil to skillet and saute the fillets for about two minutes on each side until golden brown
10. reheat the reserved sauce
11. place fillets on baking dish or cookie sheet and finish in oven for 5-7 minutes or until done
12. serve with reserved sauce
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this.  I did let the fish marinade longer.  I prepared it in the morning and the fish marinaded until supper.  While we enjoyed it we will probably lessen the amount of or omit the cloves as that flavor seemed a little overpowering.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blackberry bunt cake

a dear friend from church gave this to me after i had gone blackberry picking.  we were living in the seattle wa. area at the time and they grew wild all along the roads.

1. grease and lightly flour a 10 inches bunt pan
2. combine dry ingredients
3. in a mixer beat butter for about 30 sec
4. add sugar and vanilla and beat until fluffy
5. add eggs 1 at a time , beating after each addition
6. add dry ingredients and buttermilk alternately to beaten mixture until combined
7. fold in blackberries
8. turn batter into prepared pan
9. bake at 350 for about 1 1 / 4 hours
10. sift powdered sugar on top when cake is cooled
demonstrations.review: Made this last week to use up some blackberries and flour.   I only made half of the recipe (I didn't have enough flour for the whole cake) and baked it in a 8 by 8 pan and it turned out well.   I found this recipe in an old book called Better Homes and Gardens Treasury of Country Crafts and Foods.   The recipe said to combine the powdered sugar with milk to make a glaze, but the ideas of just dusting with powdered sugar seems nice too.   I also thought it would be nice to top the cake with a jarred berry topping, but the cake was gone before I thought to try it that way.   If I make again I think I might add more berries to the batter.

target.recipe_text:
low carb oatmeal pancakes

very satisfying!!

1. place all ingredients in a blender
2. blend until smooth
3. spray a frypan with veggie spray
4. pour batter into frypan making two large cakes or 4 smaller cakes
5. cook until bubbles aprear around the edges and the edges look dry
6. flip and cook the other side
7. serve hot with margarine and lemon or syrup or jam or freeze and reheat in a toaster
target.review: They were decent.  I would add splenda next time.  This is my first time making oatmeal pancakes, and after a few adjustments, these are a very different and satisying meal. I spread the pancakes with light butter and sprinkled with a cinnamon and splenda mixture, yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked oatmeal creme brulee style

this is a basic recipe, be it breakfast or dessert. add fruit, nuts or even mini chocolate baking bits. it's so good, adjust any amounts you prefer.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly oil a 9 x 13 baking dish
3. in a large bowl , combine dry mix
4. in a medium mixing bowl , whisk wet mix well
5. add wet mix to dry mix , stirring well
6. pour mixture into prepared dish
7. bake 40- 45 minutes- centre will be jiggly
8. remove pan from oven , place pan on a cooling rack
9. hand sprinkle brown sugar over top of oatmeal
10. return pan to oven , bake until sugar melts , 2- 3 minutes
11. remove pan to cooling rack
12. set oven to broil
13. set pan under broiler 3 inches from heat till sugar bubbles and browns slightly , 1- 2 minutes
14. remove pan from broiler and spoon mixture into serving bowls
demonstrations.review: Very good! I downsized the recipe to 2 servings, and I cooked it a lil too long because the center was not 'jiggly' but the taste is still great.  This is a keeper and will make again and had my own spin on it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato chowder

another of my aunt's recipes. great for those cold nights.

1. combine potatoes , onion , broth , and cream of chicken soup in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 8-10 hours or until potatoes are tender
3. add cream cheese and blend
4. top with bacon and chives before serving
demonstrations.review: Delicious!! This is one of the best potato soups I have ever made. I had to leave out the bacon because Lent but I will definitely be adding this to the leftovers.  Will be making this again and again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers general tso s chicken

great ww recipe from a meeting. 8points plus per serving.

1. in a medium bowl , whisk together broth , cornstarch , sugar , soy sauce , vinegar and ginger
2. set aside
3. heat oil in a wok or large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add scallions , garlic and pepper and cook 2 minutes
5. add chicken and cook until browned all over , about 5 minutes
6. add reserved sauce and simmer until sauce thickens and chicken is cooked through , about 3 minutes
7. serve chicken and sauce over rice
8. yields about 1 cup of chicken and sauce and 1 / 2 cup of rice per serving
demonstrations.review: Very good! More like a typical chinese brown sauce than General Tso's.  I made 1.5 recipes of the sauce and added two heads of broccoli and served it with brown rice instead.  Very tasty!! Great way to get a healthy, Chinese fix at home!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach artichoke cheesy tortellini

this is from rachael ray, and oh soooo good!! like having artichoke dip in a pasta. my son even ate his on top of toasted french bread!

1. heat a deep skillet over medium heat with the oil and butter
2. when butter melts , add garlic and grated onion
3. saute for 5 minutes
4. sprinkle the flour into the skillet and cook for 1 minute
5. whisk in the broth , then the cream and bring to a bubble
6. season the sauce with nutmeg and reduce heat to low
7. separate spinach into pieces as you add it to the sauce
8. stir in the artichokes and cheese and season to taste with salt and pepper
9. cook the tortellini in salted boiling water according to package directions , about 7 minutes
10. drain and toss with the spinach artichoke sauce
11. serve immediately with additional grated cheese and diced tomatoes , if desired
demonstrations.review: This is a very good recipe.  I used half Three Cheese Tortellini and half Spinach Tortellini.  Also I used Fat Free Evaported Milk.  I had to add a little bit of milk before serving to make it a bit more liquidy.  Very good and very filling!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast casserole

make certain to use 1 to 2 day-old bread for this, i strongly suggest not to double the amounts and bake in a larger baking dish, make two separate recipes and bake in two 8 x 8-inch casserole dishes, if you prefer a sweeter taste then increase the sugar amount.

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. generously grease an 8 x 8-inch baking pan
3. sprinkle the bread cubes into the baking pan , then sprinkle the raisins over the bread
4. in a bowl whisk together the eggs with milk 2 tablespoons brown sugar , salt and vanilla
5. pour evenly over the bread cubes
6. sprinkle the butter cubes over the top
7. allow to stand for 15 minutes
8. in s small bowl combine the remaining 2 tablespoons brown sugar with 1-2 teaspoons cinnamon
9. sprinkle over the top
10. bake for 45-50 minutes or until golden
11. serve warm with maple syrup or pancake syrup
demonstrations.review: Very Good, and so easy! It went together in a flash.  We used soft Italian bread, cubed up.  I drizzled mine with syrup and loved it.   Great way to serve French Toast to a larger group of people in a flash!! Its a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
chicken with fettuccine alfredo

juicy chicken with a great creamy alfredo sauce. very easy to make!

1. cook fettuccine according to package
2. drain
3. while fettuccine is cooking , prepare chicken
4. heat 12-inch skillet
5. add 2 tbsp butter
6. flatten chicken slightly
7. salt and pepper chicken
8. roll in flour , add to skillet
9. cook and brown until juices run clear , about 10 minutes
10. remove from skillet
11. add to skillet 2 tbs butter , onions , and garlic
12. cook 1 minute
13. add cream , cook for 3 minutes until reduced a bit
14. add cheese , parsley , and red pepper flakes
15. stir well
16. add last 1 tbsp butter and stir well
17. bring back chicken and coat with sauce
18. place chicken on plates , put fettuccine in sauce and swirl around to coat well
19. add to plate with chicken
target.review: If I could give 100 stars I would!  Fettucine Alfredo is my all time FAVORITE meal and this was SO PERFECT!  The chicken was SO juicy and the sauce was absolutely incredible.  This is the ONLY alfredo I'll be making for a LONG time.  THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk cookies

these are impossible to stop eating.

1. cream the butter and peanut butter together until fully incorporated
2. add the sugars and cream on medium speed
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until completely incorporated
4. add the flour and baking soda , mix until no white remains , then add the chocolate and mix on low just until everything comes together
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 9 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Just felt like baking something for my mother-in-law and decided to make cookies.  SHE LOVED THEM!  Everybody did.  These cookies are absolutely perfect.  They're not too sweet and are perfectly chewy and crunchy at the same time!  I've never made such yummy home made cookies ever!  Thanks MEAN CHEF!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest beef enchiladas ever

best enchilada recipe i've found. we love the spicy, cheesy flavor of these.

1. brown meat and onions in large skillet
2. add 1 cup enchilada sauce and 1 cup cheese
3. mix well
4. put filling along center of each tortilla
5. roll up and place seam side down in a 9x13 pan
6. pour remaining sauce over
7. sprinkle remaining cheese over
8. bake at 350f degrees for about 30 minutes till cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: Really easy and very good!  I'd like to try using a homemade enchilada sauce some day.  I added cumin in the meat and the sauce for an extra little something and it was great.  Quick and easy recipe for lazy night!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf barbecue style

this is our favorite meatloaf recipe. it's easy to make, moist and delicious!

1. mix together beef , crumbs , onion , egg , salt , pepper and 1 / 2 can tomato sauce
2. form into loaf and put into loaf pan
3. combine rest of tomato sauce , water , brown sugar , prepared mustard and worcestershire sauce
4. pour over loaf
5. bake in 350f oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes
6. makes 4-6 servings
demonstrations.review: I made this for my ENTIRE family (I usually only cook for my husband) and they LOVED IT!!  I was pretty nervous trying a new recipe for them because they're pretty critical but, it was SO easy to make and it tasted WONDERFUL!!  It was VERY moist and the sauce was EXCELLENT!!  I'll never try another meatloaf recipe.  THANKS FOR A KEEPER!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno roll ups

this recipe came from a co-worker years ago, she brought these in for a birthday. they are absolutely addictive. i am requested to make this all the time and have given it out too many times to count. enlist some helpers with the spreading and rolling.  *note: i have found that fresh jalapenos can be tricky finding out if they have the right amount of heat.  i buy 4-6 peppers, process 3 of them & add them to the cream cheese mixture.  if i have the desired heat i stop, if not i add 1 more pepper at a time.  i've never had to use more than 6.  hope this helps :)

1. in a medium sized bowl soften cream cheese to room temperature
2. add to the cream cheese , the jalapenos , deli meat and onion mixing thoroughly
3. spread mixture onto tortillas , then roll them up and then slice
4. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: I LOVE THESE ROLL-UPS THEY ARE THE BEST!!  Pooh Bear makes these for us at work for every occasion and they're ALWAYS the first to go!  You gotta be fast or you won't get any (trust me.. I know)!  Thanks for an awesome treat at work (and for my birthday), Pooh Bear!!  :o)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patti labelle s macaroni and cheese

got this off of the "good morning america" website after i saw her cook this on the show. this is the best macaroni and cheese i have ever tasted!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly butter a deep 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish
3. fill a large pot with water and bring to a rapid boil
4. add macaroni and the 1 tb oil
5. cook for 7 minutes , or until somewhat tender
6. drain well , and return to the pot
7. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , melt 8 tb of the butter
8. stir into macaroni
9. in a large bowl , combine all of the shredded cheeses
10. to the macaroni , add 1 1 / 2 cups of shredded cheeses , half and half , the cubed cheese and the eggs , and the seasoned salt and pepper
11. transfer to the prepared casserole dish , and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
12. dot with remaining 1 tb of the butter
13. bake for 30-35 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and bubbly
14. serve hot
15. serves 8
demonstrations.review: I wish there was a picture of this recipe so that I could see if mine turned out right.  Mine was not very yellow in color it was pale and creamy colored so, I wasn't sure if I made it right.  This recipe was ok if you like baked macaroni.  I guess I'm just the stove top mac 'n' cheese type.

target.recipe_text:
curry dressing for rice or potato salad

this is a versatile dressing with a refreshing flavour that brings out the best in a rice salad.  i am always asked for this recipe once people taste it, as rice salads can generally be very boring.  the curry powder is the old fashioned one my mum has bought for years simply called indian curry powder.  it is not curry paste or masala but a milder type our grandma's used for making curried sausages and eggs.  do not use floury potatoes, they need to hold their shape when being mixed with the dressing etc. cooking times are for the rice and potatoes and are approximate.

1. whisk dressing ingredients together and set aside
2. if you can leave it to stand for at least 1 / 2 an hour the flavours will come together better
3. for the rice salad i brown a chopped onion and half a chopped red or yellow capsicum
4. then i add other veges of choice e
5. g
6. precooked carrot , corn , peas , beans etc
7. pour dressing over about 15 mins before serving
8. for the potato salad i use pre cooked large chunks of potato , the browned onion and capsicum and beans , but also add chopped hard boiled eggs
9. both salads are much nicer if served warm , but not hot
target.review: Wow! This was soooo tasty! I served the dressing with a potato salad using egg, onion (and a little sping onion) green, red and yellow capsicum and corn. As I made extra, the second time I ate this salad I added some unsweetened yoghurt and it was DELICIOUS! I highly recommend this! Regardless, thank-you so much for a recipe that I will use over and over and over....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese salad dressing ii

japanese salad dressing    the pungent miso also adds vitamins, protein, and nutrients to this healthy,  low-fat dressing, which contains just a 1/4 teaspoon of sesame oil. serve  drizzled on top of a simple salad of iceberg lettuce and shaved carrots.

1. in a small bowl , combine miso and sugar
2. add mirin , water , soy sauce , sesame oil , and sesame seeds
3. stir until well blended
4. serve over lettuce and carrot slices
5. toss to combine
demonstrations.review: Great! Very tasty and not too salty or too overpowering. I must admit I am a fan of miso though, so perhaps if you don't like miso give it a miss, or try it with Shiro (white) miso for a milder flavour? I used Awase miso which was really tasty! I served this with a very Japanese-style salad of cabbage and tomato, with a bit of carrot, spring onions and green pepper! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean chicken and rice pilaf

nan

1. in large deep skillet , heat the oil over medium-high heat
2. add the chicken and brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
3. add the onions , curry powder and garlic salt
4. saute until onions begin to soften
5. about 3 minutes
6. add the soy sauce and hot sauce
7. simmer 2 minutes
8. add the rice and mix to coat with spices
9. pour in the stock
10. reduce the heat , cover and cook until all the liquid is absorbed , the rice is tender and the chicken is cooked through
11. about 35 minutes
12. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: SUPER tasty! I love curry so I couldn't go wrong really, but I also added eggplant and pumpkin which made for a really, really tasty meal! I cut out the hot sauce, and I made sure I washed the rice really well before adding it. I've already made it twice! Thanks a bunch!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese eggplant with miso

a recipe passed on by australian chef simon bryant which he obtained on a trip to japan.

1. in a bowl mix together miso , sugar , sake , mirin , sake and egg yolk
2. wash eggplant and cut lengthways in 1cm thick pieces
3. sprinkle with salt and leave hour
4. rinse , pat dry then brush with a little veg oil on both sides
5. either bbq , grill or panfry eggplant until soft
6. spread one side with miso mix , and sprinkle with sesame seeds
7. grill for a few minutes until the miso bubbles on top
8. serve , garnished with a little julienned spring onion greens
demonstrations.review: I have now cooked this recipe about 4 times and I LOVE it! I have used white and awase(mix of red and white) miso and both turned out really well. I find that if I put the lid on my frypan when I'm cooking the eggplant before adding the miso it draws out more of the bitterness. I also use brown sugar and serving with spring onions is a MUST for me! Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese beef and rice bowl  gyudon

this recipe is from the "japanese cooking class cookbook" by the editors of consumer guide.

1. cut beef into 1 / 8 inch thick slices
2. cut slices into strips about 1 inch wide and 2 or 3 inches long
3. cut green onions crosswise into 1 inch lengths
4. reserve
5. wash rice with cold water
6. cook rice with 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and 2 3 / 4 cups of water
7. about 10 minutes before serving , heat remaining 1 / 4 cup water , the mirin and soy sauce to boiling over medium high heat
8. add beef and boil until beef reaches desired doneness
