9. add green onions and boil 30 seconds
10. remove from heat
11. divide rice among 4 individual serving bowls
12. place equal amounts of beef and onions over rice in each bowl
13. ladle equal amounts of cooking liquid into each bowl
14. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is so simple, but SUPER tasty! I used regular onion instead of sping onion, and substituted beef mince for beef strips. Not only does the mince cook cuper quickly, but it is really flavoursome! I served with Japanese Okayu infused with garlic.. Thank you so much! This is a great recipe, expecially for winter!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian noodle salad

this is yet another version of asian salad.  i love snow peas when they are in season so i cannot resist adding them to this salad.  we enjoy this dish in the summer and spring for our main dish, and absolutely love it.

1. make sesame dressing by shaking all ingredients in a tightyly covered container
2. set aside
3. cook noodles as directed on pkg , adding snow peas for last 1 to 2 minutes
4. drain
5. pinse with cold water
6. drain
7. spray 10 inch skillet with cooking spray
8. cook pork and gingerroot in skillet 4 to 6 minutes , stirring occasionally , until pork is slightly pink in center
9. toss noodles , bell pepper , carrots , onions and pork with half of the dressing
10. sprinkle with sesame seed
11. serve with remaining dressing
demonstrations.review: This recipe is a great summer recipe. I used rice noodles instead of soba. I did find the dressing a little bit too 'vinegar-y' so I would probably recommend more oil and less vinegar? I will definately make this one again though! Thank-you!

target.recipe_text:
baked salmon with mustard dill sauce

very easy and wonderful if you like mustard-dill sauce. one of my favorites.

1. in a small bowl , whisk together the first 4 ingredients
2. add salt and pepper to taste and blend well
3. allow to stand at room temperature for 1 hour
4. lightly grease or oil a baking sheet
5. put salmon , skin side down , on baking sheet
6. sprinkle with garlic , salt and pepper
7. spread with 1 / 3 cup of sauce
8. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until just opaque in the center
9. serve with the rest of the sauce
target.review:
Great recipe!  I took a picture of it when I was done making it, so as soon as I get my film developped and scan it in, I'll post that too.

I really enjoyed this and I think I'll be making it for my family when I go home for Christmas :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple potato curry

the following curry is very simple and has become a family favourite,it does,t use any fancy spices and both my sons can make it from scratch!

1. saute onions , ginger and garlic in melted butter til soft
2. add potatoes
3. sprinkle over curry powder , toss well
4. stir in stock , bring to boil
5. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 15 minutes
6. add peas , cook 5 minutes
7. add coriander , wine vinegar and lemon juice
8. season to taste with salt and pepper
9. heat through
10. i serve this with basmati rice , sliced banaas tossed in plain yogurt and chutney
demonstrations.review:
This was fantastic, it really hit the spot on this miserable winter day.

I made a few substitutions, and left some ingredients out, though I don't think it affected the taste too much.

Instead of the butter, I used 2 tbsp of canola oil.  This was for health concerns.  I left out the ginger, coriander, white wine vinegar and lemon juice because I didn't have any on hand.  I bet it's outstanding if you include these items (although I'm likely to simply double up on the lemon juice and leave the vinegar out entirely)

Finally, next time I make this I will try to get the potatoes to fry a bit in the oil before adding the stock, as I found the potatoes disintegrated a bit more than I would have liked, and I hope searing them on the outside will help avoid this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lentil curry

a simple vegetarian curry. split peas can be used instead of lentils. and the curry seasoning should be adjusted to taste.

1. wash lentils several times
2. heat oil in a pot and add chopped onion
3. when onion is light brown in colour , add the lentils and about half of the water
4. stir
5. now add curry powder , chilli powder , mustard and salt
6. simmer until lentils are cooked , adding more water of needed
7. add milk about 5 minutes before removeing pot from the stove
8. split peas can be used instead of lentils
demonstrations.review:
This is so easy and quick to make, I make it for lunch all the time now!

It's also ridiculously healthy, (check out the fibre and protein on this baby!) and by using cooking spray instead of oil and using only water instead of milk, you can cut out a lot more calories - meaning since I've started eating this regularly I've lost some weight!  Awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
2  handed kitchen sink tomato sandwich

i got this recipe from an old georgia boy that was transplanted in tennessee, he is 72 and says he grew up on this sandwich.

1. in the peak of tomato season , chill 1 very large or 2 medium size tomatoes that have been vine-ripened and have plenty juice
2. take 2- slices of bread and coat them with 1 / 4 inch good mayonnaise
3. add layer of tomatoes cut 1 / 4 inch thick
4. salt & pepper to taste
5. add another slice of tomatoes and salt and pepper to taste again
6. add the other piece of bread on top of this
7. roll up your sleeves and start eating over the kitchen sink while the juice runs down your elbows
demonstrations.review: During the summer my father brings these as his lunch to the office.  It's a sharp change from his usual left-over dinner fare (that his coworkers generally oooh and ahh over) and the first few times he did it someone took him aside and asked him if he was having problems with his wife!  Turns out not everyone knows how great these sandwiches are...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pasta with asparagus  pasta al forno con asparagi

i love fresh asparagus recipes.  got this one out of 100 pasta sauce recipes.  serve with some crusty bread and a salad and you have a great dinner. it turns out great!


1. wash asparagus
2. remove any tough stalks and cut into short lengths
3. you may want to split the length in half
4. melt about 3 tbs of butter in pan and cook the asparagus over a low heat for about 20 min
5. every so often , add a little chicken stock to keep it moist
6. when the asparagus is done , season to taste
7. while the asparagus is cooking , process the ricotta cheese with the oil
8. cook the pasta for half the time stated on the package
9. drain and immediately toss in the remaining butter and half the parmesan
10. butter a deep oven dish
11. make a thin layer of pasta , then one of asparagus , then one of pasta again and then one of ricotta
12. repeat , finishing with the layer of pasta
13. beat together the eggs and the remaining cheese and pour over the top
14. sprinkle with black pepper
15. bake in a medium oven , 350 degrees for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Asparagus was nowhere to be found in this godawful place (the North West of Ireland) and so I used Broccolli instead.  I thought it was good, I added a lot of salt to make up for the lack of salt in ricotta.  I think it could have used some garlic though, and I will add some next time I make it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
molasses bread

easy to make, great with cream cheese. make ahead and freeze for future use.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. spray 9x4 inch loaf pan with non stick spray
3. sift dry ingredients together
4. mix liquid ingredients together , then add to dry mixture
5. blend well with electric mixer
6. pour into prepared loaf pan
7. bake for 1 and 1 / 2 hours
8. cool for 10 minutes in pan , then turn out and cool completely
9. delicious with cream cheese
10. freezes well
demonstrations.review: I really liked this recipe.  I only had skim milk on hand and I thought it still worked wonderfully.  I added two teaspoons of cinnamon and 3/4 teaspoon of nutmeg.  It is very easy to make and I enjoyed the fact that it uses whole wheat flour.  Next time I make it I will add raisins, I would have this time but I didn't have any on hand.

target.recipe_text:
cranberry oatmeal muffins

these are moist, tasty muffins which are especially nice to serve around christmastime.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. soak oats in yogurt or sourcream just enough to make it moist
3. sift dry ingredients into a bowl
4. in a separate bowl , add oil , sugars , and egg
5. beat until well blended
6. gradually fold in dry ingredients
7. add chopped cranberries and orange zest
8. put in greased muffin tins
9. bake for 20 minutes
target.review: These muffins are baking in the oven right now and I was looking forward to the delicious smell others described, but unfortunately all I am smelling is burnt batter on the oven floor.  These muffins rose tremendously and spilled over my muffin pan.  It looks like a big cake in there, as opposed to 12 muffins.  Next time I will only half - fill the muffin tins.  As for the recipe, I was a bit disappointed by the lack of direction in the recipe.  Brown sugar isn't mentioned to be "packed", so I just assumed it should be.  Dry ingredients didn't include sugar, but I didn't realize this until I had already mixed the sugars with the flour mixture.  Also, the oatmeal yogurt mixture was just sitting off to the side and is nowhere mentioned again in the recipe.  I just added it at the end with everything else.  Also, no direction is given with regards to the orange zest.  When and where do you incorporate that?  I just added at the end.  So, all in all, a good simple recipe but be advised that you will have to fill in the blanks where direction is lacking.  Ok they just came out of the oven, and the flavors are indeed good.  The orange is perfect although when I tasted the batter it came through really strong.  Looking forward to making these again with less confusion and less spillout.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
plain lentil soup  vegan   and low fat too

delicious, hearty, low fat and high protein soup that doesn't use meat or bones for flavor - just fresh veggies and spices.

1. wash lentils
2. put all ingredients in large pot
3. bring to boil then reduce heat and simmer 40 minutes til lentils are tender
4. blend in blender in batches until all soup is smooth
5. season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: As healthy as lentils are, and as health conscious as I am, I really wish I enjoyed eating them.  I do eat them, but I can't say that I enjoy it.  So, needless to say, I was hesitant with this recipe and wondered if there was a chance this recipe would make a lentil lover out of me.  I made exactly as directed, with the addition of 1 cup of chopped zucchini and extra cayenne pepper.  I cooked it for about 45 minutes, and then used an immersion blender to puree.  I tasted it and felt so-so about it, but after another sprinkle of sea salt and further pureeing... voila!  Delicious soup, and I've had 2 bowls of it already!  Thanks for making me like lentils!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
p  f  chang s chicken lettuce wraps by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes 2" (penguin random house 2007). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

another version of the chicken lettuce wraps.

1. make the special sauce by dissolving the sugar in water in a small bowl
2. add soy sauce , rice wine vinegar , ketchup , lemon juice and sesame oil
3. mix well and refrigerate this sauce until you're ready to serve
4. combine the hot water with the hot mustard and set this aside as well
5. eventually add your desired measurement of mustard and garlic chili sauce to the special sauce mixture to pour over the wraps
6. bring oil to high heat in a wok or large frying pan
7. saute chicken breasts for 4 to 5 minutes per side or done
8. remove chicken from the pan and cool
9. keep oil in the pan , keep hot
10. as chicken cools mince water chestnuts and mushrooms to about the size of small peas
11. prepare the stir fry sauce by mixing the soy sauce , brown sugar , and rice vinegar together in a small bowl
12. when chicken is cool , mince it as the mushrooms and water chestnuts are
13. with the pan still on high heat , add another tbsp of vegetable oil
14. add chicken , garlic , onions , water chestnuts and mushrooms to pan
15. add stir fry sauce to pan , saute mixture a couple minutes then serve in lettuce leaves
demonstrations.review: These were ok... I thought they'd be fabulous considering they are supposed to be like PF Changs, but as it turns out I prefer my lettuce wraps with other stuff in them... like nuts, scallions, and those styrofoamy curly Asian noodles.  This recipe was ok, but I thought the "Special Sauce" was way too watery, and the stir fry sauce was small in quantity and flavor compared to the amount of food it had to cover.  Oh well... glad I tried it, and still enjoyed the meal.  Thanks...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot collard greens and ham

an excellent choice as a side dish for fried catfish or pulled pork. also goes well with cornbread to soak up the juices which are called "pot likker". when you eat this kind of food, you know you are living!

1. remove any thick stems and tear or chop leaves into strips
2. cook bacon in a skillet until the fat renders and bacon becomes translucent
3. place bacon , with its drippings , into the bottom of the crock pot
4. add the greens , ham hock , salt , pepper , and water into crock pot
5. cover and cook on low for 6 hours or on high for 3 hours
6. remove ham hock , discard skin and shred meat , returning meat to crock pot
7. serve greens with minced onion , vinegar and tabasco , if desired
demonstrations.review: Wow! Great recipe! I skipped the meat because I didn't have any in the house, and skipped the onion for dietary reasons. I did add a little bit of hickory smoke powder for the bacon flavor. I sprinkled in a little olive oil right before cooking. I cooked on low for about 5 hours and on high for another hour. The texture was perfect... that melt in your mouth feeling. I added a little red wine vinegar and Tabasco upon serving. Hubby wasn't crazy about them (this was his first greens experience) but he ate them anyway. Will make again!! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate flan cake

this recipe calls for mexican cajeta (caramel topping). if you cannot find this in your supermarket, substitute smucker's caramel topping, however the mexican cajeta has a richer flavor. this is very easy to make, and super good. use it with your next mexican fiesta!!

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray a large 12-cup bundt pan with nonstick coating
3. soften the cajeta in the jar in the microwave and pour into the prepared pan
4. prepare cake mix according to package directions
5. pour the cake batter into the cake pan over the cajeta
6. to make the flan: pour condensed , evaporated and fresh milks into a blender with the cream cheese , vanilla and eggs
7. mix well
8. pour the flan mixture very slowly over the cake batter
9. spray aluminum foil with non-stick spray
10. cover the pan tightly with aluminum foil
11. set the bundt pan into a large pan and set on the oven rack and slide into the oven
12. carefully pour hot water into the larger pan to a depth of 2 inches
13. bake cake for 2 hours
14. do not uncover during this time
15. after two hours , remove cake from water and allow to cool for 15 minutes
16. peel off the aluminum foil
17. invert cake onto a large plate with rim
18. the cajeta will drip down the sides of the cake
19. cool completely then refrigerate
20. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: Amazing! What a beautiful, unique, and delicious cake!! I did use authentic cajeta and HIGHLY recommend that instead of the caramel. The cajeta has the signature flavor of goats milk, almost a bit tart but sweet, and adds another dimension to the fabulous flavors of chocolate and creamy flan. The texture is outstanding!!! I will make this again and again! Thanks!!! ****Ah, just made this again and it came apart after inverting it and removing the bundt. Oops... I forgot to spray the pan with Pam.  Now I know for next time!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight for hubby, and it was great!  Let me say that I HATE HATE HATE pot roast and other "gray" overcooked meats, BUT... this was delicious.  The meat was so tender that I had to use a spatula to pull it out of the crock pot because it was falling apart.  The flavor was excellent, and yes, quite salty, but I love salty food.  I'm really not a fan of "short-cut" cooking, but this was fantastic.  Thanks for a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
mom s famous potatoes

this is out of a local tv cookbook by kcts cooks (favorite recipes). sent in by a bellevue, washington viewer. she said it's always requested for special family gatherings, and  can be prepared ahead of time.

1. boil potatoes in salted water until not quite done
2. drain , cool and scrape off peels
3. grate potatoes into a large bowl , using the big holes of the grater
4. peel onion , cut in half and slice very thin
5. mix onions with potatoes
6. add salt , pepper and nutmeg
7. grate cheese and add to potatoes saving about 1 cup for top
8. add sour cream and mix well
9. taste and adjust seasonings
10. pile into a 9 x 13-inch baking dish and top with remaining cup of cheese
11. sprinkle with paprika
12. bake for approximately 1 hour at 350 degrees
13. if prepared ahead and refrigerated , allow more baking time
target.review:
This was a delicious potato dish.It really made a change not to use cheddar.I used Emmental in mine,so it had that lovely nutty flavour to it.Next time I may well add a little garlic or garlic salt to it,just for personal taste.
Oh,by the way,I didn't bother to scrape the skin from my potato,as when you grate it it tends to come away from the potato,and you're left with it in your hand.
A lovely recipe,again,Teresa.Thanks for sharing.Made for 1-2-3-4 Hit Wonders.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barefoot contessa s turkey meatloaf

this is an ina garten recipe from the barefoot contessa cookbook. my husband is fussy about his meatloaf, but really likes the texture and flavor of this.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. saute onions in olive oil until translucent , about 15 minutes
3. add salt , pepper , thyme , worcestershire sauce , chicken stock and tomato paste and mix well
4. allow to cool to room temperature
5. combine ground turkey , bread crumbs , egg and onion mixture in a large bowl
6. mix wll and shape into a rectangular loaf on an ungreased sheet pan
7. spread the ketchup evenly on top
8. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours until the internal temperature is 160f and the meatloaf is cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.I halved the recipe as it was too much for us.I coated half of the loaf with the ketchup (for the children) and half with spicy Jack Daniels marinade-heavenly! Leftovers reheated beautifully too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled pepper chicken

i got this recipe back in 1989 out of a betty crocker cookbook called "make it light" it's a quick and easy dish to prepare (using boneless chicken) and has a nice kick to it. i have made it even lighter and quicker by using skinless chicken breast with out bones. cooks up in half the time. this is a great dish to make after a hard day at work.

1. cut chicken into pieces: cut each breast half into halves
2. mix oil , marjoram , red pepper , margarine and salt
3. brush chicken on both sides with margarine mixture
4. place chicken , skin sides down , on rack in broiler pan
5. set oven control to broil
6. broil chicken with tops 7 to 9 inches from heat 30 minutes
7. turn
8. broil until brown and thickest pieces are done 20 to 30 minutes longer
demonstrations.review:
What a fantastically quick,easy and totally delicious dish!
I was dubious about the marjoram and chilli fusion,but hey,it works really well.
I used skinless chicken breast,brushed on the mixture and threw it into the George Foreman for a few minutes..served with a crisp green salad,recipe #289258#289258 and a well chilled glass of wine,it completely rescued a bad day at work!!
I'm keeping this one,thanks Teresa...I loved it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon nachos

this recipe is inspired by appleydapply bacon and onion nachos.  we had unexpected company come by and i wanted to make lunch for them.  this is the result i got.  it's hot and spicy but you can decrease the amount of jalapeno peppers.  if you do not like crisp vegetables, microwave them to the desired consistency you like.  we like crisp.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. line a baking sheet with aluminimum foil
3. spread 1 / 2 bag of tostitos over the foil
4. sprinkle with half the bacon , onion , peppers and 1 cup of cheese
5. spread the remaining 1 / 2 bag of tostitos on top
6. top with remaining bacon , onion , peppers , olives and tomatoes
7. top with 1 1 / 2 cup remaining cheese
8. bake for 5-10 minutes or until the cheese is melted and slightly browned
demonstrations.review:
A really quick and simple dish,that really lends itself to the contents of your fridge/larder.
The bacon makes for a nice change of pace,from more conventional nacho recipes.
This would be great with some guacamole thrown into it too (next time),and I love the idea of sour cream too!
I have tried Appleydapply's original recipe,and we enjoyed it very much,as we did this one.
Thanks Nimz,for a recipe that can be tailor-made to keep everybody happy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried crispy chicken

this chicken comes out moist and delicious with a crispy coating.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment paper or foil
3. in shallow bowl or pie plate , combine the rice cereal , parmesan , oil , paprika , cumin , 1 / 2 t salt and 1 / 4 t pepper
4. brush both sides of the chicken with the yogurt and coat with the cereal mixture , pressing gently to help it adhere
5. place on the prepared baking sheet
6. bake until golden brown and cooked through , 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Moist succulent chicken with a crispy coated outer layer...deeelicious!!!
I used Rice Krispies, and sour cream in lieu of natural yogurt. As my chicken was so thick, I sliced the breasts in half before coating, and turned them halfway through the cooking time to crisp up the underside.
They turned out beautifully...a very easy and totally tasty supper solution after a busy day.
Thanks Lainey..we loved it. Made for PRMR.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
secret recipe chocolate chip cookies

these cookies are tall and hold their shape. i have tried bunches of recipes and after a little tweaking it is my favorite. the lemon juice helps to activate the baking soda, producing a softer, chewier cookie. the original recipe calls for putting the oats into a blender or food processor until finely ground. i have never done that as i think the oats add texture. the prep time is a guess as i have never really figured it out. these freeze great too.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. the original recipe suggests lining the baking sheets with parchment paper
3. i use my silicone liners
4. but they have also turned out great without using any lining at all
5. combine oats , flour , baking soda , and salt in a mixing bowl
6. in a larger bowl cream butter , sugars , vanilla and lemon juice , using an electric mixer
7. add eggs and beat until light and fluffy
8. stir the flour mixture into the egg mixture , blending well
9. add the chips and nuts , mix well
10. place dough by rounded tablespoons onto cookie sheet about 1-2 inches apart
11. bake the cookies until lightly browned , about 10 minutes
12. remove from cookies sheets after a couple minutes
13. when completely cooled store in a sealed container to keep them soft and chewy
14. in fact i think they are even better the second day
demonstrations.review:
This is an absolutely wonderful cookie recipe. I used a mixture of white and dark chocolate chips, and slivered almond for the nuts...the resulting cookies were beautfully soft and chewy, and more than a little addictive.
They started disappearing at an alarming rate off the cooling racks ( and that was just me, before the kids got a whiff of them!!).
Just delicious,....this is a real winner,thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
3 corn casserole

if you like the 5-star sour cream cornbread recipe from nursedi, you will love this creamy side dish version! it is, in a word i use to describe it, food-gasmic!! definitely a comfort food on cold winter days! easily doubled with excellent results! enjoy! yanni

1. in large bowl , mix together butter , sour cream and egg
2. stir in cans of corn and corn muffin mix
3. spoon mixture into buttered 2-quart casserole dish
4. bake in preheated 375-degree oven , about 45 minutes
5. remove from oven , add cheese , stir well
6. return to oven , bake additional 15 minutes , or until dish is slightly puffed , bubbly , and browned around the edges
target.review: This is also one of my favorites, but have never tried it with the cheddar. Except I put in 2 eggs, beaten and 2 Tblsp. sugar. This not only a kid pleaser, but the adults go back for seconds too.. Diets are forgotten at that point! Isn't food wonderful!.. glitter

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with hot tomato   bacon sauce

great change from regular pasta sauce. fast to assemble--40 minutes to the plate. kick it up by adding extra red pepper flakes if you like--i do!

1. fry bacon till crisp
2. drain on paper towel
3. pour all grease from pan except 1 tablespoon
4. add olive oil and onions
5. saut till onions wilt , about 5 minutes
6. stir in garlic , tomatoes , salt , sugar , basil and red pepper flakes
7. crumble bacon in and add parsley
8. simmer 30 minutes
9. remove from heat
10. cook pasta while sauce is simmering
11. drain well
12. toss sauce and pasta together
13. serve
14. pass cheese to garnish
demonstrations.review: IB I really like this sauce because it is a tasty change. I have made it often the only difference I add a little nutmeg to it while it's cooking. But we like it both with and without. And of course, it's always nice to have that little bit of a bite from the pepper flakes..you feel like your eating. Thank you for sharing...glitter

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review:
Miss Annie as usual fantastic! My dh and I really loved these. I did make a slight difference this time when I made them. I used a peach salsa that really went well with the chicken and along with the cheddar I happened to need to use up some mozzerella which I never would have thought to use on this but I thru it in for good measure and I didn't have the heart to throw away. It was really good which made me only think a mexican cheese mixture with the the cheddar would be so good.

Either way I have now had this recipe twice made as specified and with the change and it is a keeper. My dh took all the leftovers with him for lunch today..He just kept on saying ..this is really good. Thanks a bunch for this easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken breasts

mmmmmm--this is so good and so creamy.  you will enjoy this dish.

1. butter a 13x9-inch baking dish and arrange breasts in dish
2. top with cheese slices
3. mix soup and apple juice together till well combined
4. spoon evenly over chicken breasts
5. sprinkle stuffing mix over soup
6. drizzle butter over crumbs
7. bake at 350 for 50 minutes to an hour , or till chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: I've made this many years.A family favorite. I sear the chicken for a few moments on each side and I prefer broccoli and cheddar cheddar soup. If I use the cream of chicken I add a can of cream of celery also. Goes well with rice or noodles. Great when your in a hurry. If I make it on top of the stove I leave the oleo and stuffing out.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sopapillas

this is a mexi.  to guarantee they puff, it is important to keep the oil at 375°f.

1. combine the first 4 ingredients
2. cut in the shortening with a pastry blender until the mixture is just crumbly
3. add milk stirring with a fork until dry ingredients are moistened
4. shape into a ball
5. turn dough out onto a lightly floured surface and knead gently until smooth
6. cover dough and let rest 1 hour
7. roll the dough into 1 / 16 inch thickness with a floured rolling pin
8. using a pizza cutter cut the dough in to 3 inch squares , cover dough with a damp towel or cloth
9. pour oil to 2 inches deep in a heavy pot
10. heat to 375f drop the dough a few at a time into the hot oil turning immediately to allow even puffing
11. turn back over and cook until both sides are light golden brown
12. drain on paper towels and repeat until all dough is used
13. serve immediately with honey and cinnamon sugar
demonstrations.review: These are positively addictive and out of this world! I love these. The first time I had them was in Denver, Co. I am so glad you shared the recipe with us. They just are so perfect! And of course the honey and cinnamon is definite plus!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and eggs   schinken mit ei

german dish, ham and eggs. came from a friend of mine who is german.

1. melt the butter
2. fry the ham in butter real quick on both sides
3. open the eggs directly into the pan over the ham
4. salt slightly
5. cover the pan with and let the eggs sit until they are the desired consistency
demonstrations.review: I make this all the time..never even gave it a thought as a recipe. In Germany, Bavaria, and the German towns thruout Europe this dish is extremely popular in the morning (or sometimes we even made it for a Sunday evening meal) with homemade crusty bread. I love this for breakfast much better than bacon.Yummy!

target.recipe_text:
saffron scallion couscous

this is from food to live by. everyone loves this side dish. i noticed there is one other recipe posted on recipezaar that is very similar to this one. there are a slight change of ingredients and the preparation is a bit different.

1. place couscous in a medium size shallow heat proof bowl and drizzle olive oil over it
2. rub the couscous between your palms until all the grains are coated with oil
3. heat the stock in a small saucepan until just begins to boil
4. remove stock from heat and add the saffron , stirring to blend
5. add half the stock to the couscous
6. keep the remaining stock warm over low heat
7. stir and fluff the couscous with a fork
8. cover the bowl with a plate or plastic wrap and let sit for 5 minutes
9. add the remaining stock to the couscous
10. using a rubber spatula , scrape up an saffron that may be stuck to the saucepan and add it to the couscous
11. fluff the couscous with a fork , and recover the bowl
12. let it sit for 5 minutes longer
13. season the couscous with salt and pepper to taste and stir in the scallions just before serving
target.review: I made this over a year ago and never rated it!  It's as easy as making jell-o and very tasty.  I lived in Morocco as a Navy Brat and we leared to love cous-cous as a main meal with chicken and as a dessert with cinnamon and crushed rock sugar and mint. Thanks for posting and for the memories.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker beef short ribs

you won't believe how good these ribs are!!! i think we could have these every other night with no complaints! they're yummy!!!!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a bag
2. add ribs and shake to coat
3. brown ribs in butter in a lg skillet
4. put in slow cooker
5. in same skillet , combine remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil , stirring
7. pour over ribs
8. cover and cook on low for 9 hours
demonstrations.review:
Very, very good!  I made potato bread to go with this.  I made this to pack for DH's lunch for tomorrow with a nice rice side dish.  He will be so surprised.  For me it was just a little bit tangy but the rice side will help with that.  Sauce to spare so make lots of rice or mashed potatoes!  Thanks MizzNezz!  SA;)
PS I should add that I made half of a recipe since it was just the two of us.
PPS Gee, I hope that calorie count is wrong!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamed mushrooms on multigrain toast

for breakfast, brunch, lunch, or a light dinner.

1. melt the butter in a saute pan over medium heat
2. add in the shallots
3. stir / saute 1-2 minutes or until the shallot begins to soften
4. stir in the mushrooms
5. cook 6-8 minutes or until they are limp and have given up much of their liquid
6. add in the stock , cream , salt , and pepper
7. cook until the liquid reduces by about half
8. arrange toast on 4 plates
9. top each with an equal portion of mushrooms and sauce
10. dust with paprika and serve
demonstrations.review: I made this twice but made some changes that I really liked in the second batch.  I added a tablespoon of tomato paste and a splash of vermouth.  It was so wonderful, so very wonderful... It's 4 AM and I am thinking about the 'shrooms I have in the fridge and breakfast....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tre s pickled onion rings

"good with hamburger, cheese sandwich, egg salad sandwich and as a pickle with regular meals."

1. cut onion into thin slices
2. separate into rings and put into a two cup sterilized jar
3. pour boiling water over to cover onions
4. allow to cool , then drain
5. mix together vinegar , water , sugar , salt and hot pepper sauce and bring to a boil
6. pour over onion rings
7. cover tightly and refrigerate for at least 2 days before using
8. store in refrigerator up to 2 months
demonstrations.review:
Almost as easy as making tea!  I used cider vinegar and a little extra tabasco.  5 stars for simplicity and 6 stars for flavor even after a few hours let alone a few days.  Do yourself a favor and make two pints of these because they won't last long once they are on the table.  Thanks for posting - I love pickles!
SA UPDATE ON THIS: My friend Patty tasted these onions and swiped the whole jar for her hubby.............

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drunken cranberry sauce

a delicious holiday (or not) whole berry sauce that is so simple (if you don't sneak a sip of the liquid while you are acquiring the ingredients) that you'll be amazed.

1. combine first 3 ingredients
2. cook over low heat until most of berries have "popped"
3. add zest and cinnamon
4. remove from heat
5. cool and store in refrigerator or freeze until wanted
demonstrations.review: Whoa!!  A little too much booze for me!  Still good, but an acquired taste, methinks.  I usually make my cranberry sauce with juice (different kinds) and lemon peel or orange peel and I am not a drinker so take this review for what it is and decide for yourself.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice cooker   risotto  with carrots and onions

this is a very simple risotto-style side dish that i make in an on-off rice cooker. i use knorr chicken broth powder if i don't have chicken stock handy. if your broth is unsalted, you will need to add salt to taste.

1. put oil and butter in rice cooker pot , switch on
2. when butter is melted , add carrots and onions
3. cook until softened , 3-5 minutes
4. add rice , stir until it is coated with oil
5. add chicken stock and switch to cook
6. check consistency when rice cooker switches to warm
7. if it is too chewy , add 1 / 4 cup water and switch on again
8. this is very altitude dependent
demonstrations.review: We used CalRose and added some fresh chopped parsley.  It did need a little more broth, but was yummy, easy and great with chicken.  Next time I will add a teaspoon of curry powder for a different flavor - Thanks Lille!

target.recipe_text:
mom s pork tenderloin

the marinade sauce for this recipe is amazing!

1. mix soy sauce , chili sauce , honey , vegetable oil , green onions , curry pwder , garlic , tabasco and worcestershire sauce together
2. place meat in a ziploc bag
3. pour in sauce
4. marinate overnight , turning every few hours
5. grill marinated tenderloins 5 minutes on each side
6. cut on a diagonal to serve
7. serve over rice
8. refrigerate overnight while the meat is marinating and heat before serving
target.review: I didn't have all of the ingredients to make this properly, but we were still blown away by it! I didn't have chili sauce, curry powder, or tabasco sauce. I substitued a tablespoon of chili powder, paprika and red pepper flakes. I marinated the pork for two days and I have never had a more tender meat! It was like slicing butter!!! Delicious and made the whole house smell nice. My husband and daughter both gobbled it up and asked for seconds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast ii

here's the way french toast has been made in my family for at least 4 generations - but until i got into high school, we called it 

1. whisk the eggs till frothy
2. add remaining ingredients , and mix well
3. over medium heat , lightly grease skillet with shortening
4. i use a paper towel , so i can use it repeatedly , with every 2 or 3 pans of french toast
5. dip each slice of bread into the egg mixture , on both sides
6. do this quickly , so as not to completely soak the bread
7. cook in skillet over med / med-high heat for approx 5 min per side
8. you may need to flip more than once to get th e desired golden-brown color
9. serve with butter and powdered sugar , or preserves or syrup
demonstrations.review: I had never had french toast like this until 3 years ago. My mom has a rather bland style of cooking, and french toast was white bread dipped in egg/milk. Period. This is almost exactly how my mother-in-law makes her french toast. She was kind enough to make it for me whenever we stopped by during my pregnancy. She just sprays her pan with a cooking spray like Pam. This is how I have been making it ever since. My husband and daughter love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss cheese bacon smoked almond dip

awesome dip!!!  always the first to go at parties.  it is also great served in pre-packaged phyllo cups

1. fry the bacon
2. let drain and crumble
3. mix all ingredients
4. bake in 350 degree preheated oven for about 15 minutes
5. until golden and bubbly
6. top with some crushed almonds
7. for a twist , put the cold dip in pre-packaged phyllo cups and bake for about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this for our housewarming party and recieved more compliments on it than anything I have ever made! In fact, my husbands entire family stood around the counter gorging on it and barely had room for dinner. They have asked that I bring it to all family functions! I used chive cream cheese, as its what I had. I also used smoked apple flavored swiss and plain almond slivers. It was EXCELLENT!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: My husband LOVES garlic, and this dish really did it for him. I thought it was really good, but I'm not a cheddar cheese fan, so I will try it w/out next time. I think it will still be great! We found it flavorful and moist, a new addition to our rotation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy turkey tetrazzini

this is a great way to use leftover cooked turkey or chicken. it's also an easy one dish casserole that everyone in the family enjoys. the recipe started life as a cooking light recipe in a recent issue. i made modifications to suit our taste.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. melt butter in saute pan
3. add onion , celery , pepper , salt , carrots , and mushrooms
4. saute until vegetables are tender
5. add flour and stir until vegetables are coated
6. add wine , and stir quickly until flour is absorbed
7. gradually add broth , stirring constantly
8. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes , stirring frequently
9. remove from heat
10. add 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese and the neufchatel cheese , stirring until cheese melts
11. add the peas , turkey and pasta
12. stir until blended
13. coat a casserole with non-stick spray and transfer mixture to the casserole
14. combine breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
15. sprinkle mixture evenly over the top of the casserole
16. bake at 350 for 30 minutes until lightly browned
17. let rest for 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this with a lot of changes (picky husband). I didn't use any vegetables except onion and red bell pepper. I used vegetable flavored low-fat cream cheese and didn't remember the breadcrumbs. Anyway, it was delicious. I also used the spiral pasta noodles. I will make this again tonight and freeze it for busy days this month! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pink stuff     cherry pie filling  pineapple dessert

my husband and children would literally die without this for the holidays!  and it is so easy!  my husband says it is a side dish.  i say it is a dessert.

1. combine all ingredients and mix well
2. serve chilled
3. your family and friends will go nuts
demonstrations.review: My husband's aunt made this for Thanksgiving and I immediately asked her for the recipe, and here it is!!! I think I added drained mandarin oranges too though. Delicious, simple, and should def. be a dessert (IMO)!!!

target.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
target.review:
Thank You Bev for a great recipe.
The sauce is rich,full bodied and...easy to make. I did add a extra tsp. of oregano but folowed the recipe otherwise as it was written. I like to add also that you can freeze it very well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with black beans and rice

this is a variation of a cuban dish. the balsamic vinegar gives it an exceptional flavor!

1. in a large pan , heat olive oil and add red pepper flakes
2. add onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
3. increase heat , add chicken , stirring until cooked
4. lower heat to medium , add 1 tsp oregano , 1 tsp cumin , and simmer 1 minute
5. add black beans , pimentos , remaining spices , and balsamic vinegar
6. blend and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes , reseasoning if needed
7. while beans are simmering , bring broth to boil in a pan , add rice
8. lower heat to simmer , cover , and cook 20 minutes until rice is fluffy
9. serve bean mixture over rice
demonstrations.review:
Perfect!! Easyto fix and wonderfull taste.
I made 1/2 the recipe since it is just the two of us and only 1 chickenbreast ,also in Holland you can not find pimientos jars so I used 1 lgr. red bell pepper.
The result was great and I will most likly fix  this dish very often.
Oh and I did sprinkle it with fresh  coriander (cilantro?) before serving it.Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arabic salad

this is the standard palestinian salad -- they eat it with just about anything but especially to accompany and give colour to rice dishes -- it might take a little getting used to, but you'll get used to it!

1. dice cucumber and tomatoes
2. place in bowl
3. add parsley and onion
4. just before serving , add the salt , lemon and olive oil and combine all ingredients
5. serve in small bowls to accompany rice dishes
demonstrations.review:
Lovely salad! I am sure I will fix this many times over the summer.I did use a little more oil and used a red small onion,very good. Next day ( we had some leftovers!) I added a few spoons creme fraiche and that was good also.
Nice picture Sue Lau,mine salad looked just like that!
Thanks for sharing Baraahnz.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick boston baked beans

from australian super food ideas may 2007.  low gi, great breakfast or brunch or light supper.  they recommend to make a double batch and freeze for later use eg as jacket potato topping.  9th november 2008 update made this today and have made changes to timing and serving size, i have upped to 5 serves based on that i got 5 cups of 250ml,  weighing 200gram each.  i've increased the prep time but then my knife skills are slow especially on a day of pain.  update june 2010 - to make vegetarian omit the bacon and if you want try other canned beans (though white light coloured ones work best) and herbs.  you could use dried beans but you would need to cook these first which doesn't make the recipe quick but very cheap to make.

1. heat oil in a deep non-stick frying pan over medium heat
2. add bacon and cook for 4 to 5 minutes or until crisp
3. remove bacon from pan using a slotted spoon and set aside
4. add onion to frying pan , cook stirring for 3 minutes or until onion is tender and light golden , add garlic and paprika continue to cook stirring for 1 minute
5. return bacon to frying pan and add the tomatoes , sugar , tomato paste and beans
6. cook stirring often for 5 minutes or until heated through
7. season with salt and pepper
8. split muffins and toast
9. spread with butter
10. place on serving plates and spoon baked beans over the muffins and sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review:
Very good and easy! We do not have english muffins in the Netherlands so I used crusty country bread instead,put a poached egg on top and a green salad on the side for a nice comfort-food-dinner!
Thank you Pat for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect vodka sauce with prosciutto

i adopted this recipe in aug. 2006 & will add input whenever i prepare it. it originally was posted dec 11, 2002. original comments: "the best vodka sauce i've ever had. restaurants wish they had this recipe. really, it's true."

1. in a large frying / saute pan add oil , butter and garlic , saute on low flame until oil starts to bubble
2. add tomatoes , salt and pepper
3. cook covered on a low flame for about 30 minutes
4. add vodka
5. cook uncovered for 25 minutes
6. add prosciutto-- cook 5 more minutes
7. add basil and heavy cream-- cook just 5 more minutes
8. serve it now !
9. i like this over penne pasta
10. i only use barilla
demonstrations.review: true...a perfect sauce! I have made it several times and every time it was a hit.Once I made it with sliced porto bello mushrooms,once with shrimp and once with prosciutto,my favorite was with the shrimp I must say. I used 4 Tbsp. olive-oil.I like to use the roma tomatoes,peeled and seeded them,it is worth the extra trouble since you will get a wonderfull smooth sauce this way.I will defently make this sauce often,thank you very much for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy grilled lime chicken  w  oamc directions too

thaw and marinate your chicken at the same time in this wonderful concoction! toss it all in a zipper seal bag and throw in the refrigerator. ready the next day to throw on the grill! use bone in or boneless. this marinade will cover about 4 lbs of chicken.

1. mix together and pour over raw or frozen chicken in zipper seal bag
2. toss in refrigerator overnight
3. drain marinade and grill until chicken is no longer pink in middle
4. use less cayenne- or none- to reduce heat !
5. oamc: to freeze: place chicken and marinade in a large freezer bag
6. seal , label and freeze
7. to serve: place in fridge to thaw overnight
8. grill or broil until done
9. thanks lucid for these great instructions !
demonstrations.review:
Oh so good and easy!
I did indeed just as you said, put the frozen chicken in the bag with everything(just used 1/2 of everthing since it is just the two of us) than browned them in a pan with adding now and than the marinade,and it was great!
Served with baked potato and sugar-snaps! thanks for a wonderfull easy recipe.

target.recipe_text:
tomato kielbasa penne

one of my favorite easy fix dinners. the recipe originally came from the back of a kielbasa package years ago but i doctored it up with many different ingredients to make it my own. everyone in my house loves it.

1. cook penne pasta as directed in separate pot
2. in a large skillet add olive oil , onion , garlic , and sliced kielbasa over cook over medium heat until onions are tender
3. stir in diced tomatoes , tomato sauce , oregano , parsley , vinegar , and cooked pasta
4. cover and simmer for 15 minutes
5. serve topped with parmesan cheese , if desired
target.review: This was a hit with my family.  The only thing different I may do next time is put in some green pepper to give it a little more color.  I used 2 packages of keilbasa in mine also.  It was quick and simple to make and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken spinach salad with warm bacon dressing

simple, fast and easy to make and its delicious!

1. place the bacon , dressing and water in small microwavable bowl
2. stir
3. microwave on high 30 seconds or until warm
4. toss spinach , chicken breast strips , onion , mushrooms , cashews and eggs with dressing mixture in large bowl
5. serve immediately
6. substitution:
7. 1 t parmesan cheese & 2 t bacon grease in place of the catalina dressing
8. for an even faster version use precooked chicken and bacon
9. those such as oscar mayer ready to serve bacon & louis rich grilled chicken breast strips
demonstrations.review: This is very good.  The salad has a very fresh taste and the dressing is just right.  I did add some grape tomatoes to it to add some color and some freshly grated parmesean cheese.  Very good for a quick lunch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk muffins with variations

this is a basic muffin recipe. you can vary the taste according to which fruit you choose to use. other combinations are strawberry, cranberry/orange, and blueberry/lemon.  it may be necessary to use more flour depending on which fruit you use.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. prepare muffin cups by spraying with non cooking spray or lining with paper muffin cup liners
3. mix together all streusel ingredients with a fork to make a crumbly mixture
4. set aside
5. for the batter , whisk together the oil , brown sugar , zest and egg
6. stir in the buttermilk and vanilla
7. stir together 2 1 / 2 cups flour , salt , baking powder , soda and cinnamon in a bowl
8. add to the wet ingredients and blend
9. fold in your desired fruit
10. the use of frozen fruit may help firm up the batter
11. if the batter seems too loose , add 1 / 4 cup more flour to make the batter stiffer
12. fill the muffin cups to the top
13. sprinkle streusel topping over each muffin evenly
14. bake for 15 minutes , lower the oven temperature to 350f and bake for another 12 to 15 minutes or until the muffins spring back when pressed lightly
15. let cool in pan for 5 minutes before unmolding onto wire racks
demonstrations.review: These muffins are very good.  I used lemon zest and blueberries in mine.  I only used 2&1/2 cups flour in the batter and used an additional 1/4 cup on the blueberries before I folded them into the batter.  The strusel topping is to die for.  Thanks MarieAlice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ranch chicken thighs

needed a quick & easy weeknight meal. this is adapted from an old taste of home magazine. the chicken is tasty & juicy, with a nice crunchy crust. you won't miss the skin!  
eta -- some say this is too bland.  the ranch dressing is not enough seasoning.  i do add season salt to taste (nature's seasonings) to the bread crumb mixture for more flavor.  hopefully as a cook, you will know what to add to suit you and your family's taste.

1. in a shallow bowl , combine crumbs , parmesan cheese , cornmeal , italian seasoning , and seasoned salt
2. dip chicken into salad dressing , then coat with crumb mixture
3. place chicken in a greased 13x9 baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 375 degrees for 45 minutes or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: The chicken was very moist and tasty.  I made this for dinner and took mine with me to work and heated up in the microwave later and it was still very moist.  It is a very easy recipe and very inexpensive, had everything on hand already.  Thanks Keywee for a great chicken recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chop rice skillet

my mom use to make this all the time for us when i was a kid. the secret is hot sauce.you could also use chicken.

1. trim and season pork chops
2. melt butter in large frying pan brown chops on both sides
3. remove from pan
4. saute rice and onion in same pan
5. add soup mix and water and add hot sauce and oregano
6. blend well
7. bring to a boil and place chops on top bring down to a simmer and cook covered for 30-35 minutes
8. or until liquid is gone
demonstrations.review: I loved the simplicity of this recipe. The only think I found was that 2 & 1/2 cups water was a little bit too much.  I will cut some of the water next time and  when I make it I will add some garlic to the onions and rice mixture.  I used bonless, skinless chicken thighs instead of pork as that was what I had and the chicken was very tender.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hacienda pork chops grande

these are really fun!! taste great and a nice way to use up any leftover taco "fixin's"!! not dry at all, and look really pretty, too! top with your own favorite toppings! just have fun! :)

1. rub taco seasoning mix on both sides of all four pork chops
2. or make your own taco seasoning ! )
3. in large skillet , melt butter with vegetable oil , heat over med-high heat
4. lightly brown chops on both sides
5. transfer to shallow , lightly greased baking dish
6. top each chop evenly with salsa
7. place in 350 oven for about 30-35 minutes or til done
8. chops are done when very slightly pink inside and juices run clear
9. don't overbake ! bake less if chops are thinner !
10. top with cheese during last 5 minutes or so of baking
11. serve topped with rest of ingredients
12. serve with spanish , mexican or green rice and refried beans if desired
demonstrations.review: This was a wonderful change for pork chops.  The flavors all worked great together.  I topped ours with sour cream, lettuce and green onions.  I would have used tomatoes too if I had them.  Reviewed from ZWT4

target.recipe_text:
cranberry feta pinwheels

from ocean spray and very good!

1. combine all ingredients except tortillas , mix well
2. divide and spread mixture evenly among tortillas
3. roll up tightly , wrap in plastic and refrigerate at least one hour
4. to serve cut into 12 slices
5. a nice variation is to add thin slices of ham on top of the spread before rolling
target.review: OMG! These were amazing! I actually ended up placing 2 slices of bacon instead of the suggested ham in each one of these and I had to seriously FORCE myself to stop eating them before everyone came over. They were soooooo good!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexicali casserole

i like this recipe because it is not only low-fat but tasty. it is excellent warmed over but can eaten cold-very versatile dish for people on the go.

1. start browning meat in a large skillet adding the chopped onion and green pepper-drain excess fat
2. after browning meat , stir in taco seasoning mix , corn , and entire jar of picante sauce
3. simmer mixture on med heat approximately 10 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. while meat is simmering , preheat oven to 375f
5. mix mexican cornbread mix and your 2 / 3 cup milk in a medium mixing bowl
6. set aside
7. pour about 1 / 2 of mixture into 9-inch casserole dish then cover with 1 / 2 bag of shredded cheese
8. repeat-layering the two cover top with cornbread mixture-spreading over entire casserole
9. bake in oven for approximately 25 minutes or until brown
10. cool for 5 minutes then serve
11. add sour cream to taste
demonstrations.review: This recipe was a hit! My husband said it was the best meal I had made yet! I only used 1/2 an onion, a jalapeno pepper as the "green pepper" and the 8.5oz Jiffy cornbread mix as previous posters suggested. All in all, it was an easy and delicious recipe. I will be making this over and over again! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perky olive penguins

these tuxedo-clad tidbits are actually ripe olives stuffed with a mildly seasoned cream cheese filling.

1. cut a slit from the top to the bottom of 12 jumbo olives
2. set aside
3. in a mixing bowl , combine the next six ingredients
4. mix well
5. fill a small heavy-duty plastic bag with cream cheese mixture
6. cut a small hole in the corner of the plastic bag
7. carefully pipe mixture into jumbo olives
8. set aside
9. cut a small triangle out of each carrot slice
10. press triangles into small olives for a beak
11. on each notched carrot slice , position a jumbo olive so the white chest is lined up with the notch for the feet
12. place the small olive , hole side down , over the jumbo olive so the beak , chest and feet are aligned
13. carefully insert a toothpick through the top of the head into the body and carrot base
14. wrap a pimento around the neck for a scarf
demonstrations.review: These have got to be the most adorable thing I have ever seen! It was so much fun putting these together and seeing them "come to life". People didn't even know that they were food! But the filling was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
demonstrations.review: This was sooooo easy! And sooooo delicious! Everyone loved it and complimented me on how great it tasted. I can't believe I never made a ham before. Now that I know how easy it can be, I'll be making them for EVERY holiday meal! Thanks Boopster!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blt nibbles

if i get asked for this recipe one more time, i will scream - just kidding! this is a great do-ahead appetizer. a good recipe to have for your summer garden abundance (and parties!). only 145 days til july!

1. cut a thin slice off the top of each tomato
2. scoop out and discard the pulp
3. invert tomatoes on paper towels to drain
4. in a small bowl , combine all remaining ingredients and mix well
5. spoon into tomatoes
6. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: These were delicious! A bit difficult to do the stuffing, but only because I put my DH in charge of chopping the bacon, so it turned out a little thick which made it difficult to push through the ziplock. But I had a request for the recipe, which is always a great sign.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach balls  appetizer

very handy to have in the freezer for the holidays - easy to make

1. cook spinach according to instructions , drain in a sieve , use back of a wooden spoon to press the spinach against the sieve to get as much moisture as possible out in a bowl combine the spinach , stuffing mix , cheese , eggs , butter , salt& pepper mix thoroughly& roll into small balls 3 / 4 to 1" size
2. place on a cookie sheet& freeze
3. when frozen place in a plastic zip lock bag
4. to serve place frozen balls on a cookie sheet and bake at 350f 10-15 minutes or until lightly browned if you are doing them fresh or thawed only bake for 7-10 minutes
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: These were great! They were the last thing I made at my party, so people were pretty full by the time they came out. Try to make them early if you are making multiple finger foods. However, the people who tried them raved!

target.recipe_text:
snow peas with cashews

only 1 ww point.

1. in nonstick skillet , heat oil
2. add orange peel and cook over low heat for 2 minutes
3. add snow peas and salt and pepper , to taste
4. turn heat to medium
5. stirring constantly , cook 3 to 4 minutes or until snow peas are bright green and crunchy
6. sprinkle with cashews and serve
target.review: This is a delicious veggie dish - the crispy snow peas and the smooth crunch of of the cashews are a nice contrast!  I used olive oil rather than canola.  This recipe is from "The New American Plate Cookbook," by the American Institute for Cancer Research and was in the Oregonian newspaper in March of 2005.  Note: To toast the cashews, put them in a small skillet over medium-high heat and stir frequently for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly brown; immediately transfer the nuts to a small dish and cool.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dump truck cakes

enjoy this fabulous dessert in cake or cupcake form for breakfast lunch or dinner!!!!

1. mix all ingredients together
2. add more buttermilk if needed
3. bake for 40 minutes at 325f degrees
4. bake until golden brown and a toothpick stuck into the center comes up clean
demonstrations.review: I made it in loaf form, and it just wasn't very appealing.  It was lumpy from some ingredients and smooshy in other places from the pineapple and strawberries.  It might be a fun thing to make with kids, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
egg and brown rice salad

found this recipe about 10 years ago in the "working woman's cookbook" it makes alot, and has been a hit at picnics.

1. rinse peas under cold water to separate
2. drain
3. in a very large bowl mix together peas , eggs , rice , celery , onion , cheese , and pimiento
4. in a small bowl combine mayonnaise , mustard , lemon juice , salt , pepper , and dill weed
5. toss with egg mixture
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours , but no longer than 24 hours
demonstrations.review: A good summer staple for picnics and potlucks, I've made this many times in years past.  I usually add a bit of garlic, use chopped green onion instead of white or yellow, Dijon, and add a sprinkle of cayenne for a little kick.  Thanks for reminding me of the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halibut onion crunch

excellent recipe. try adding a high quality aoli to the finished dish as a sauce.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. combine the oil , lemon juice , marjoram , garlic salt , dry mustard , and pepper
3. pour over halibut
4. marinate 20 minutes , turning once
5. transfer fish to buttered baking dish
6. sprinkle with cheese and onions
7. bake 15 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: Yum!  This recipe was a nice change of pace from my usual method of cooking fish.  I don't usually use "French fried onions" but I had some left over from the holidays and decided to try this out.  I didn't use halibut, figuring any nice white fish would do, and it came out quite tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with fava beans and lemon sauce

i think this is such a fabulous dish to celebrate spring!!  fava bean (also called broad beans) season is late spring and after the beans are ready to use this prepares so fast, you'll have more time to spend outside in the lengthening daylight.  if you don't have access to fresh or frozen fava beans, you can substitute lima beans (not my favourite, but some like them) or edamame.  this recipe is from organic style, 5/2005, i added a bit of garlic and garnished with a little mint.  the prep time mostly is shelling the fava beans, the cooking time includes removing their outer skins.

1. shell fava beans and cook in a medium pot of boiling salted water 2 minutes
2. drain and immediately plunge into a large bowl of ice water
3. peel off outer skins of beans---there is a dark green , thick ridge on the rounded side of the beanstarting there , pinch the skin and pull it open , once the skin opens a bit you can squeeze the bottom and the bean slips out into your bowl
4. cook pasta in boiling salted water according to package directions until al dente
5. reserve a half cup of the water the pasta has cooked in and drain pasta in colander , you don't have to worry about excess water in the "little ears" as it will help tie the pasta sauce together
6. return pot to medium heat , add butter and garlic , cook until garlic is soft
7. add half-and-half , heat one minute
8. stir in lemon juice , zest and pepper
9. add pasta and cheese , stirring until pasta is coated and cheese is melted
10. add favas and toss , adding a few tablespoons of reserved pasta water if pasta seems dry
11. serve immediately in warm bowls , garnishing with mint if desired
demonstrations.review: These fava beans are *so* good!  We didn't have  orecchiette, and used elbow macaroni instead, which worked fine (and I forgot to put them in the photo too - sorry).  This is now my favorite way to prepare fava beans!  Delicious, Bikerchick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
malaysian style oxtail soup

this broth is so flavorful and so authentic. it tastes sort of like the vietnamese 

1. place the oxtails , onion , garlic , cilantro sprigs , cinnamon stick , cumin , coriander , and chile in a heavy soup pot
2. add the broth and water to cover the ingredients by 1 1 / 2 inches
3. bring to just a boil , reduce the heat , and simmer covered for 2 hours , skimming any foam that rises to the surface
4. season with salt and pepper and cook uncovered for another 15 minutes
5. the oxtail should be very tender
6. remove from the heat
7. remove the oxtails and shred the meat from the bones , discarding the bones and any fat
8. set the meat aside strain the broth through a very fine strainer
9. cool for at least 1 hour so that the fat rises to the top
10. skim off all the fat and discard
11. return the broth to the soup pot
12. add the ginger and slivered garlic
13. bring to a boil , reduce the heat , and simmer for 10 minutes
14. return the shredded meat to the broth and cook another 5 minutes
15. stir in the cilantro and cook 1 minute longer
demonstrations.review: I made this soup in my crockpot, simmering it on low for about 15 hours before straining - it was outstanding!  I added the garlic and ginger and simmered another hour.  If you have the opportunity to make oxtail soup, MAKE THIS!  I'll be using it for years to come.  Thank you, Grace Lynn!

target.recipe_text:
kid friendly tuna casserole

only 4 ingredients makes this an easy recipe for a hectic evening.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. boil and drain pasta
3. combine all ingredients in 13x9 in pan
4. bake for 10 minutes , then remove and stir
5. continue to bake for 10 more minutes or until cheese is entirely melted
6. stir and serve
target.review: It was kid-friendly, as promised.  I was also a little short on time, so it nice to have something so simple to throw together.  My husband thought it was a little strong fish flavor (we used 3 cans), but I thought two cans seemed too few for a family of six.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican sunset bread  bread machine

from toh. yield: 1 loaf (about 2 pounds).

1. in a bread machine pan , place all ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer
2. select basic bread setting
3. choose crust color and loaf size if available
4. bake according to bread machine directions
demonstrations.review: I liked this bread, but it didn't rise quite right.  That may have been my own fault for having used fat-free sour cream.  It is a nice flavor, and something a little different.  Thank you for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy low fat chicken enchilada casserole

this was an experimental meal, but when my guys tasted it, they said it was a winner.  very quick and easy, suitable for beginning cooks.  you can embellish this basic version however you choose by adding chopped green chilies, black olives, etc.  i like to add fresh lettuce, onions, tomatoes, and salsa on top at serving time.  

1/8 of the casserole is 7 ww points.  after obtaining calorie counts for each ingredient listed in the recipe from my fitness pal, the entire casserole comes in at 2200 calories.  one serving would be 275 calories.

1. grease a 9x13 pan with shortening or spray
2. in saucepan , add chicken , soup , water , taco seasoning , and black beans
3. heat slowly and stir until heated through and bubbly
4. cut tortillas into quarters
5. cover the bottom of the 9x13 pan with about 1 cup of the chicken mixture
6. piece half of the tortilla wedges , jigsaw-puzzle-like , so they cover the chicken mixture on the bottom of the pan
7. spread half of the remaining chicken mixture on top of the tortillas
8. spread 1 cup of the shredded cheese on top of the chicken mixture
9. repeat layers
10. bake at 350 degrees f for 30 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: It was good, but a little bit too salty for my taste, but that might be the taco seasoning to blame.  It was warm and nice to have on a cool evening.  I used chili beans which did make it a little more spicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn dogs

here's a good basic recipe for corn dogs. i'm looking forward to trying some of the suggestions from reviews as to adding dry mustard or other seasonings to the batter.

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt and egg
2. mix well
3. stir in milk to make a thick batter
4. place in a tall narrow glass
5. let stand 4 minutes to thicken
6. meanwhile , heat oil to 375 degrees f
7. pat hot dogs dry
8. dust with flour if desired
9. insert sticks in hot dogs
10. dip into batter
11. let excess drip off
12. fry until golden brown , about 5-6 minutes
13. drain on paper towel
demonstrations.review: This turned out pretty good!  We made them without sticks, which turned out just as easy to do.  Our oil had gotten hotter than 375, so they only took about 2 minutes to cook. We had leftover batter, which we dropped into the oil to fry too, and they turned out as delicious little pastries!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker french onion soup

i made this fantastic recipe for a big batch of onion soup that you can freeze in portions to use later.  serve this with a lovely red wine and salad and voilà for a romantic meal.  these are 14 large servings so if you are serving this before a meal reduce the amount of soup in your bowl.

1. over medium heat saut the onion in butter until soft and translucent and caramel colour
2. make this in 3 batches
3. place onions in slow cooker
4. deglaze cooking skillet with some of the beef stock
5. this is the secret to that taste
6. add to slow cooker along with the remaining beef broth
7. add worcestershire sauce , thyme and bay leaf
8. cover
9. cook on high for 4 hours or on low for 6-8 hours
10. add salt and pepper to taste
11. remove bay leaf
12. divide soup into appropriate containers
13. seal and freeze
14. when ready to enjoy your french onion soup
15. remove from freezer and place in a microwave dish with 2 tbsp sherry
16. heat for 5 minutes
17. add parmesan cheese to your onion soup bowl
18. place one slice of toasted bread over the cheese
19. fill bowl with soup
20. top with shredded gruyre cheese
21. place under broiler to melt your cheese
22. use the processor to slice your onions
23. i once read 'if i use my food processor just to make onion soup it will be worth the cost"
24. bon appettit !
demonstrations.review:
Loved this recipe. I pared it down a little bit--just four pounds of onions and about ten cups of broth.

Just before serving it, I dished it out into ramekins. Then I sliced the French bread, laid a slice on top of the soup, but partially sticking out of the bowl too. I sprinkled mozzarella cheese over top (didn't have any other variety at the moment) and broiled it for about 3 minutes. Turned out perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french country casserole

i am sure that the french used actual dried beans, soaked and cooked. however, this one is very quick to make if your evening is hectic.

1. combine all ingredients in a bowl
2. transfer to an ungreased 3-quart baking dish
3. cover and bake at 375f for 60 to 70 minutes or until carrots are tender
demonstrations.review: This is a good recipe.  I've made it several times--I have it in a cookbook.  I have used canned carrots so that the baking time is reduced a little.  I also omit the brown sugar, because we don't care for sweet beans.

target.recipe_text:
leftover ham casserole

i threw this together today with a bunch of leftovers we had in the kitchen.  my picky son liked it.  i made it low in fat by using light and low fat products.  i served it with a green salad.

1. oven at 400 f
2. set aside 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
3. steam the broccoli until tender-crisp
4. in a lightly sprayed casserole dish , combine noodles , broccoli , onion , cream of mushroom soup , ham , 1 cup of cheese and pepper
5. stir to combine
6. top with extra 1 / 2 cup of cheese
7. bake for 30 - 35 minutes , until hot and bubbly
target.review: EASY EASY EASY! This was as easy as 1, 2, 3.  Could not have asked for an easier recipe.  It tasted good and I think the vegetables could be very versatile. Next time will probably add some steamed carrots and cauliflower. My family and I had some left over ham from Easter and did not want it to go to waste, we are sure glad we found this recipe.  This will be a future reference recipe for when we have left over ham.  Thanks for a wonderful dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked potato wedges

we love these potatoes, they are simple to make and taste great!

1. wash potatoes , cut into wedges
2. place potatoes skin down in a baking dish
3. mix the next 6 ingredients together and brush onto potatoes
4. bake at 350 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Just WOW! These are awesome!  I don't see how these could possibly have less than 5 stars.  It was easy and fast.  The only difference I did was shake them in a bowl in stead of brushing the sauce on the potatoes.  I was just in a hurry.  Very tastey, crunchy on the outside and soft on the inside.  You could also easily add maybe some dried rosemary leaves to the mix.  Or simply play with the spices.  Way to go, this is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
a really good tomato recipe

here is a recipe to try with those delicious homegrown tomatoes. provolone cheese is also good with this.

1. line the bottom of a 9-inch pie or quiche pan with a single layer of the croutons
2. alternate 1 / 4-inch slices of tomato with mozzarella slices on top of the croutons
3. sprinkle with the red wine vinegar and then the dried basil
4. put in a microwave oven for 5-8 minutes or until the cheese has melted
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a REALLY GOOD TOMATO RECIPE!!!!!  This was perfectly quick and easy for someone without a lot of time.  I have made this a few times now and the only thing differnt I've done is add some ricotta cheese to it.  Other than that it's perfecto as is!  Served up nicely the next day too, had eveyone in the breakroom asking what it was and how to make it.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice cooker spanish rice

this is an easy no mess spanish rice that is a great addition to any mexican meal! thanks for the review chef #792090, i have edited my recipe according to your recommendations.

1. spray rice cooker with cooking spray
2. add rice , 1 cup water , and all other ingredients
3. stir
4. when the cycle is almost completed check the rice
5. if necessary , add additional 1 / 2 cup water
6. the amount you need will depend on what kind of rice you use
demonstrations.review: I will never make spanish rice on the stove again.  This was so yummy!  This was right up my families alley they loved it!  Even my mom wanted the recipe!  I did add some diced green chilies, chichen broth, real onions, and a pinch of salt.  Very flavorful and I'm sure a litle healthier since you're not browning the rice with oil first. Great post, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy lamb marinade

a tasty dish, which teases the taste buds and has everyone crying out for more.

1. combine all the ingredients
2. add the chops and marinade for as long as possible
3. great cooked under or in the grill or the bbq , served with salads
4. gujerati potatoes , spicy tomatoes or any choice of your own
demonstrations.review: Excellent taste! This was wonderful! I've never had lamb before and was told it's very hard to cook. So when it came out tender I was quite pleased. This was very easy to make. I had this mairinating for 12 hours before tossing on the bbq. This was just wonderful. VERY tender!
