3. reduce heat to medium low and add remaining oil
4. add onion , celery , bell pepper and garlic
5. cover and cook , stirring occasionally , until veggies start to soften
6. stir in cayenne , paprika , oregano , bay leaf , salt , black pepper and rice
7. cook and stir for 1 minute
8. add broth
9. bring to boil , reduce heat and simmer , covered for 15 minutes
10. turn heat back up to medium and stir in shrimp
11. cover and cook for 2 minutes
12. remove pan from heat and let stand covered until rice and shrimp are done
13. remove bay leaf and stir in scallions
demonstrations.review: Fantastic! Didn't have any shrimp on hand so I just used beef sausage, left the celery out, but added broccoli. The flavor was phenomenal. Just enough of a 'kick' to make it really exciting, but not so spicy that we couldn't feed it to the kids. AMAZING recipe. I'll be making this again and again. Ty for posting.

target.recipe_text:
faux ground beef stroganoff  turkey

this is made with ground turkey, which has a lot less calories and fat than ground beef. even people who don't like ground turkey like this! as usual, fast, easy and tasty, and a nice comfort food.

1. brown turkey well in a large frying pan
2. when brown , add the brown gravy mix , water , herbs and pepper bring to a boil , then reduce heat and let slow boil for 15-20 minutes to thicken the sauce
3. add sour cream , mix well and serve
4. you can add mushroom , peas , onions or whatever to this
5. if i add onions and mushrooms , i usually saute them with the turkey
6. serve over egg noodles , with a big salad and a slice of french bread
target.review: This was pretty good, we had it last night.  Easy, too!  I think it would be great, though, with the onions and mushrooms, mainly because I LOVE mushrooms.  Thanks for a good recipe, this one will be going into my recipe box for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
trevor s chex party mix

we worked years to perfect the seasonings as most mixes were too salty for our taste. we laugh everytime we make it as the dogs go crazy. they know i have mixing issues (it goes all over), so it's like pavlovs dogs every 15 minutes while it's cooking! everyone goes racing into the kitchen! yikes!!

1. preheat oven to 250 degrees
2. place butter in a 13x9 inch pan
3. melt in oven
4. add all seasonings and mix well
5. add remaining ingredients , mix well
6. bake 15 minutes , stir well
7. bake another 15 minutes , stir well
8. bake another 15 minutes , stir well
9. bake another 15 miutes
10. take out of oven and let cool on paper toweling
11. beware of poachers !
demonstrations.review: I picked this recipe mostly for the "sauce".  I love how, like you said, it's not too salty. I did my own mix, however, to suit my family and what I was trying to accomplish: a healthy salty/sweet snack to keep around for my children.  Here's what I put in, just in case anyone else want s to know.  4 cups Rice Chex, 2 cups wheat chex, and one cup each of multigrain cheerios, pretzels, peanuts, raisins, dried cranberries and dark chocolate chips.  Followed your instructions, leaving out the dried fruit and chocolate, then added those once the entire mixture was completely cooled.  Needless to say, it turned out PERFECT, and now my 3 year old won't leave me alone to give him more.  Thank you!  PS, the whole thing fit EXACTLY perfectly in the container I had been dying to use, so if I could give you more stars just on that point, I would.  ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss chicken supreme

smothered in a thick sauce and topped with buttery cracker crumbs, this entree is a hit.

1. place the chicken in a greased 13-in
2. x 9-in
3. x 2-in
4. baking dish
5. sprinkle with minced onion , salt , garlic powder and pepper
6. top each with a slice of cheese
7. in a large bowl , combine the soup , sour cream and water
8. pour over chicken
9. toss the cracker crumbs and butter
10. sprinkle over chicken
11. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 30-40 minutes or until chicken juices run clear and crumbs are golden
demonstrations.review: My husband always has an opinion when I serve up dinner, and he had nothing but good reviews for this recipe.  This was really delicious!  I served with mashed potatoes, and it made for a great gravy to top them as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy garlic lemon potatoes

a delicious low fat potato dish which i found in the november 2005 issue of the 'australian good taste' magazine, as an accompaniment to recipe #145704. i have posted both recipes for the post-zwt healthy for the holidays challenge.

1. preheat the oven to 220c
2. cook the potatoes in a large pan of salted boiling water for 6-7 minutes or until just tender , and drain well
3. place the potatoes , oil , lemon zest , garlic , and salt and pepper , to taste , in a large roasting pan and gently toss to combine
4. roast in the oven for 20 minutes or until golden brown and crisp , and serve with italian beef rissoles with fresh tomato salsa recipe #145704
demonstrations.review: I may change my rating at another time when I get it right.  I wrote this down a couple months ago and it's been posted on my refrigerator ever since.  Well, I finally got around to trying it, and it really didn't have much flavor.  Now that I have come back to it, it seems my measurements must be off.  We'll see how it goes next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel brownies

the best brownies ever made! very simple.

1. preheat oven 350
2. melt butter and let cool slightly
3. stir in brown sugar
4. beat in eggs and vanilla , then dry ingredients
5. bake in a 9 x 13 pan for 30 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These brownies are SOOOOOO good!  My husband just loves them (they remind him of a certain aunt), so I try to bring out the recipe once and awhile.  I made a batch a month ago and took half of them to my dad's house.  He ate three of them while we were sitting there chatting, before he even knew what hit him!  Great recipe, Heather; thanks for posting!!! ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy biscuits

this is the easiest biscuit recipe i have ever used.  i came up with it when i had no shortening.

1. mix dry ingredients
2. put oil in measuring cup and add milk
3. do not stir
4. add to dry ingredients
5. mix lightly to moisten ingredients and knead one or two times to form ball
6. roll out between two sheets of plastic wrap to about 1 / 2" thick
7. cut into 2" biscuits
8. bake on an ungreased pan at 475f for 10-12 minutes , until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: These tasted good, but I think I rolled them out too thin.  I will definately try it again later.  They worked well for what we needed though.  Usually we cut a biscuit in half and make a sandwich with eggs and bacon.  Two of these worked perfectly.  Thanks for the recipe, I'm sure it'll go better next time.

target.recipe_text:
jollof chicken and rice

this originated in french colonial africa. i found this in a cookbook under nigeria. it's very similar to jambalaya.

1. in a large skillet brown chicken on both sides in hot oil about 15 minutes
2. remove from skillet
3. set aside chicken , reserving drippings
4. add the onion to drippings
5. cook till tender but not brown
6. drain off fat
7. return chicken to skillet
8. combine undrained tomatoes , broth , and seasonings
9. pour over chicken
10. do not stir
11. bring to boiling
12. reduce heat
13. cover
14. simmer for 30 minutes
15. skim off fat
16. add rice , making sure all the rice is covered with liquid
17. cover
18. simmer for 30 minutes more or until rice is tender
19. remove bay leaf
20. sprinkle with parsley
target.review: This was a very flavorful and satisfying meal. The flavors complimented each other very well. While this is nothing like the jollof rice I enjoyed in Chicago at Vee Vee's restaurant, it was still pleasant nonetheless. It is more like jambalaya as you mentioned. Thank you for the recipe, I'm sure I'll be cooking it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted habanero chicken

a chicken recipe that highlights the spicy sweetness from roasted habanero peppers. from life's ambrosia.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. place habanero pepper on a baking sheet and roast for 10 15 minutes or until soft
3. combine roasted habanero pepper , olive oil , vinegar , garlic , salt , cilantro and lime juice in a food processor
4. process until well blended
5. place chicken in a bowl
6. pour marinade over the top
7. cover and refrigerate for at least 2 hours
8. when ready to cook
9. preheat oven to 400 degrees
10. place chicken in a baking dish or oven proof pan
11. pour marinade over the top
12. lay sliced onions around chicken
13. cook in preheated oven for 35 40 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and browned
14. transfer chicken to a serving platter and spoon sauce over the top
15. serve
demonstrations.review: I saw this recipe on the Life's Ambrosia blog page. I have made this dish twice and my family loves it. I absolutely love using habanero peppers in my meals so I'm always looking for recipes that incorporate them. This meal is definitely not too spicy and it really highlights the sweetness of the habanero. Should be a classic recipe. I serve this with cilantro lime rice and a salad. Love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lobster cajun chicken pasta

this is a copycat recipe.

1. place chicken an cajun seasoning in a bowl or resealable plastic bag
2. toss or shake to coat
3. in a large skillet over medium heat , saute
4. chicken in butter until almost tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
5. reduce heat
6. add cream and seasoning
7. heat through
8. add pasta and toss
9. heat through
10. sprinkle parmesan cheese if desired
11. adjust the cajun seasoning if you like it spicier
demonstrations.review: Tasted pretty good. Maybe I used a bit too much flour to thicken up the sauce?... Maybe too much parm? Oh well, I'll be trying it again but I'll stick to the way its listed here for the best results. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
intensely chocolate cocoa brownies

a rich brownie that is mixed in a sauce pan on the stove. easy, dense and soooooo good!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. melt butter in sauce pan
3. when melted remove from heat
4. add cocoa and stir well
5. add sugar , eggs and vanilla
6. mix until shiny and smooth
7. add flour , baking powder and salt
8. mix well
9. add choc chips or walnuts if desired
10. pour into an 8 inch or 9 inch pan
11. bake for 15-20 miutes
12. do not over bake
13. look for edges slightly pulling away from pan
14. cool and cut
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These were YUM! I added a smidge of instant coffee and my daughter added a small handful of chocolate chips to the batter and then another small handful spread on top of the brownies as they cooled. I ate 4 brownies, my daughter had to drag me away from the pan. Excellent recipe:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kip met kerriesaus  baked chicken with curry sauce

this is a different and delicious way to serve baked or rotisserie chicken. it's a dutch recipe.  we never have left overs. the prep and cook time does not include the time to bake a chicken. i usually start with a fresh hot rotisserie chicken from the grocery store.

1. slice and saute onion in butter until lightly browned
2. add curry powder and flour and stir for a few minutes to absorb the butter and brown a bit
3. slowly add stock , stirring constantly to avoid lumps
4. simmer for approximately ten minutes or until thickened
5. meanwhile cut chicken into serving pieces and arrange on platter
6. add creme or milk to the sauce , stir and pour sauce over chicken
7. serve with rice
demonstrations.review: Pretty good curry sauce. I baked some chicken leg quarters and then made the sauce, making a little bit more than shown here. Next time I will be sure to add some cayenne to the sauce, we like it hot! Decent addition to a meal of chicken, mixed vegetable blend and rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
special baked chicken

this is very good! it is best with corn flake crumbs, but it is good however you do it.

1. brush with miracle whip
2. combine crumbs , cheese and seasoning
3. coat chicken with this mixture
4. place in an 11 3 / 4x7 1 / 2 inch pan or dish
5. bake at 350 for 1 hour or till done and juices run clear
6. may use other crumbs such as crushed potato chips , crackers , etc
demonstrations.review: This chicken was a little bit sweet. In reality I'd give it 3.5 stars. It was very moist and put you in the mind of fried chicken, if it weren't for the sweetness and the slippery crust. We prefer our chicken spicy, but I wanted to try something new tonight. It was still a satisfying and affordable meal with mashed potatoes and spinach. I dont think I'd make this again, unless I was running low on ingredients.

target.recipe_text:
bev s sauteed yellow squash

this is the way i have been serving summer squash to my family to years. it is so easy and tastes great. i hope you enjoy it too!

1. melt butter in large skillet
2. add onion and cook just till tender
3. add yellow squash and continue cooking over medium heat , stirring until squash begins to soften
4. cover and continue cooking over low heat until nice and tender
5. i add lots of salt and pepper
target.review: This is how I've been making squash for years.  It is delicious.  I usually add zucchini squash and lots of garlic, though.  And sometimes I even throw in mushrooms if they're in danger of getting too old in  the refrigerator.  Very good recipe, but definitely add the garlic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red snapper parmigiana

i think this came from cooking light around five years ago. it is really good, even for those like me, who aren't that crazy about fish.

1. combine the first 4 ingredients in a large zip-lock bag
2. add fish
3. marinate in the fridge for about 30 minutes , turning occasionally
4. remove fish from bag and discard the marinade
5. combine the flour , parmesan , salt & pepper in another zip-lock bag
6. add the fish
7. seal and shake to coat the fish with the flour mixture
8. coat a large skillet with cooking spray and add the olive oil
9. heat over medium until hot
10. add the fish and cook for about 7 minutes on each side or until it flakes easily
demonstrations.review: OH MY GOODNESS!!!  So good.  We've had this twice now.  I tried it for the first time early this week and then we had company last night.  My boyfriend requested that I make this for our company.  I used Yellowtail the first time and Mangrove Snapper the second that we caught last week.  Very good!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried brussels sprouts

i've only eaten brussel sprouts steamed, until i found this recipe. this is from my mom's 500 low-carb recipes' cookbook by dana carpender. i added the lemon juice.
this recipe has lots of possibilities!

1. remove brown outer leaves of brussel sprouts
2. cut the brussel sprouts in half
3. it's your choice to cut in half or leave whole
4. in sauce pan , heat olive oil over medium heat
5. add the brussel sprouts and fry , stirring occasionally , until very dark brown , almost charred , but not burnt
6. the last minute of cooking , add the garlic and stir in to combine
7. be careful not to burn the garlic !
8. season to taste with salt , white pepper and lemon juice if using
9. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I'm not a huge fan of brussel sprouts, but my boyfriend likes them, so I made these for him.  I ended up enjoying them very much.  I didn't have white pepper, so I just used fresh ground black.  The lemon juice is good, but be careful not to use too much because the flavor can be too strong.  Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary roasted salmon

nan

1. place half of rosemary sprigs in a single layer in the center of a baking pan
2. place sliced red onion ontop of the rosemary
3. place salmon filet on top of the onion with skin side down
4. sprinkle salmon with salt and pepper
5. cover salmon with remainder of rosemary sprigs
6. place lemon slices over rosemary
7. drizzle olive oil over filet
8. sprinkle with salt
9. in a preheated 500 degree oven , roast salmon for about 20 minutes or until cooked through
10. serve salmon with onion and lemon
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.  I used the onions I had in the refrigerator instead of the red onion the recipe calls for.  It was really good, but I do think next time I will go for the red onion.  Really easy to make and makes a great presentation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan seared tilapia with chile lime butter

nice, fresh-tasting dish that comes together in a snap. make it even quicker by preparing the chile lime butter ahead of time. it can be made 1 day ahead, covered and chilled. just make sure to bring to room temperature before using. i like this served atop jasmine rice. -adapted from gourmet

1. make chile lime butter:
2. stir together butter , shallot , zest , lime juice , chile and salt in a bowl
3. prepare fish:
4. pat fish dry and sprinkle with salt
5. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over moderately high heat until just smoking
6. saute 3 pieces of fish , using a spatula to turn once , until golden and just cooked through , 4 to 5 minutes
7. transfer to a plate and saute remaining fish in same manner
8. serve each piece of fish with a dollop of chile lime butter
demonstrations.review: This is a recipe that my boyfriend found on this site and asked me to make.  We had to go to 3 grocery stores to find fresh tilapia, but it was well worth it.  We cooked only 4 steaks, but used all of the sauce.  The 2 we had left over we ate the next day after re-heating in a toaster oven.  They were just as good as the night before.  I think next time, though, I'll use more chilies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with sun dried tomato mushroom sauce

this is my adaptation of a superfast cooking light recipe. i can get this on the table pretty darn fast after work!

1. heat 2 tsp
2. oil in a large non-stick skillet over medium-high heat
3. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper
4. add chicken to pan
5. cook 4 minutes on each side or until done
6. remove from pan
7. keep warm
8. reduce heat to medium
9. add 2 tsp
10. oil , mushrooms , and shallots
11. cook 2 minutes , stirring frequently
12. stir in broth , chopped tomatoes , and wine
13. cook for 1 minute
14. spoon sauce over chicken
15. sprinkle with parsley
16. serve over pasta
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe to the letter and thought the sauce was lacking something.  It was a little too thin and lacked something.  It needs extra flavor.  I may try it again and take some of the suggestions from other comments and add sour cream or reduce the sauce further.

target.recipe_text:
not really stuffed stuffed pork chops

attention:  several reviewers have had to add additional water to make this recipe work.  i decided not to change the recipe itself, because i was afraid that it would confuse others who may be reading the reviews.  please take the time to read the reviews to see comments on additional liquids....thanks!!!  this is a recipe that i got out of the cookbook aunt paula sent to me in the cookbook swap. i made a few minor changes to make the recipe work for me and dh. i did change the name from mom's stuffed pork chops to the name i chose because they are really not stuffed, but you have the same effect. hope you enjoy this recipe as much as we did.

1. brown chops quickly
2. place chops in bottom of casserole dish
3. pour water and chicken granules in pan that chops were browned in and stir
4. mix remaining ingredients in bowl
5. pour water mixture in bowl and mix well
6. mound stuffing on top of chops
7. cover and bake@ 350 45 minutes
target.review: Very easy to make. I didn't have enough bread crumbs and I was in a rush so I used some crushed crackers and it worked fine.  Great easy recipe.  I could not believe how fast this came together.  Tastes like you worked for hours on it and it only took moments to make! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dry rub pork ribs

a simple, no hassle, no mess and delicious method for 

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. cut pork ribs into sections of 3 or 4 bones
3. mix remaining ingredients well , sprinkle on both sides of ribs and rub into the meat
4. seal rib sections in foil with a tablespoon of water in each package , and bake for 2 hours on a cookie sheet in the center of the oven
5. open foil carefully as steam escapes
6. can be crisped on a hot bbq if desired but will be great just the way it is
demonstrations.review: GREAT!!!!  Made this tonight when we didn't feel like saucy ribs.  DH said they were perfect. He said they took a while but it was so worth it! (he is impatient when he smells something good cooking) I will be making this again very soon.  They would probably be over the top on the BBQ....I didn't have that luxury but I did open the packets at the end and broiled them for 5 min.  Great and they really did fall off the bone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: SO EASY AND TASTY!  I put a few mini chocolate kisses on the top when they came out of the oven.  These were so good that we ate the whole batch in one night between the two of us!  I have tried making this before and they didn't turn out great but that is because I was not flattening the dough with a fork before baking it.  As another reviewer wrote, dipping the fork in water really helps.  I will be making more of these ASAP! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate skor squares

this is an easy five ingredient recipe. toffee and chocolate on an oreo crumb base, what could be better?

note: skor bits come in a bag like chocolate chips, they are basically toffee mini-chips. i don't think this is the same as a chopped up skor bar...

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spray a 9" square pan with cooking spray
3. mix 2 tablespoons of the butter with the condensed milk in a large microwaveable bowl
4. mix the remaining butter with the oreo crumbs and press into the prepared pan
5. microwave the condensed milk for 5 minutes , stirring every 30 seconds
6. warning: make sure your bowl has enough room for this to expand 5-6 times the original volume as it boils up
7. stir in the skor bits and spread over the oreo base
8. bake for 12 minutes
9. sprinkle chocolate chips evenly over top of squares and return to the turned off oven for 1-2 minutes until just melted
10. spread the chocolate to make a smooth topping
11. cool and cut into 25 squares while still slightly warm
12. cool completely before removing from pan
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very good!  We couldn't eat them fast enought (only 2 of us) so I put them in the freezer. I would like to try this with a different crumb base next time (maybe graham??) Very good and a nice treat! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked buffalo thighs

just like hot buffalo wings but with more meat! adjust the 

1. coat a non-stick skillet with cooking spray
2. add oil
3. place over medium-high heat until hot
4. add chicken
5. cook 4 minutes on each side
6. transfer to an 11x7 baking dish coated with cooking spray
7. combine hot sauce and next four ingredients
8. pour over chicken
9. bake , uncovered , at 400 for 25 minutes
10. serve with blue cheese dressing
demonstrations.review: Made this for my husband who like hot wings and he loved this dish. I made it as is and removed the chicken from the sauce and broiled it to get a crispy skin. Poured some hot sauce on it after it came out and I was begged to make another batch!  Will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice krispies treats with a twist

these are not your ordinary crispy rice cereal marshmallow treats. they are so much better! once i tried these i don't make them the old way!

1. bring karo syrup and sugar to a boil
2. add peanut butter and vanilla and stir
3. add cereal and stir well
4. pour into 9x13-inch greased pan and smooth out
5. melt both flavors of chips and frost top
6. slice and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These are wonderful!  I have found that when I make the "traditional" squares that include marshmallows, they always seem to become rock hard the next day.  Not these ones!  I had to make these in a jiffy and they are great!  Instead of butterscotch and chocolate chips, I melted some chocolate chips and caramel sauce together and drizzled it all over the top.  I have been instructed to make more ASAP!  Thanks for the great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
cheeseburger mini muffins

you can enjoy the delicious taste of a cheeseburger without having to resort to fast food. these little appetizers are the perfect 'finger food' and can be frozen after baking. (cook time reflected is for two batches; add 15 minutes for each additional batch)

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. in a skillet , cook beef and onion over medium heat until meat is no longer pink
3. drain
4. in a mixing bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
5. in another bowl combine ketchup , milk , butter , eggs and mustard
6. stir into the dry ingredients just until moistened
7. fold in the beef mixture and shredded cheese
8. fill greased miniature muffin cups three-fourths full
9. bake for 15-18 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center of a muffin comes out clean
10. cool for 5 minutes before removing from pan to wire rack
11. refrigerate leftovers
target.review: I wanted to do a "trial run" before serving these at a party.  Followed the recipe exactly.  We enjoyed these very much, but next time I will increase the ketchup to 1 cup because we like a more pronounced "ketchupy" taste.  Also, we liked these minis warm, so I will put them on a warming tray at the party.  Thank you for a great addition to my appetizer collection.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichoke wonton cups

if you adore artichokes, you should adore this cheesy appetizer. this takes your next gathering to the sophisticated level. great for special occasions, if you are having a large get together you will probably want to double this recipe, and keep it warm.

1. in a small mixing bowl , combine the parmesan cheese , mayonnaise , onion powder and garlic powder , mix well
2. stir in the mozzarella cheese and the chopped artichokes
3. set aside
4. coat one side of each wonton wrapper with non-stick cooking spray
5. press greased side down into miniature muffin cups
6. bake at 350' for 5 minutes or until edges are lightly browned
7. watch carefully to prevent over-browning !
8. fill each cup with 1 tablespoons artichoke mixture
9. bake 5-6 minutes or until golden brown
10. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Was making this to take to a TGIF yesterday, but our plans changed at the last minute, so...my husband and I ate these for dinner!  Today my husband is snacking on the leftovers as I write this! Very nice, easy and tasty.  I subbed 1/2 c. Asiago for the parmesan and used marinated hearts.  Thanks for sharing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian chopped salad in shells

i just found this on recipegoldmine.com. haven't made this yet, but they sound like an incredible appetizer for a cookout or picnic. prep time includes 2 hour chilling time.

1. cook pasta shells as directed on the package
2. drain and cool
3. place remaining ingredients except vinaigrette in a medium bowl
4. pour vinaigrette over the salad , toss to coat
5. stuff the shells with the salad
6. cover and refrigerate 2 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: I doubled the recipe and took these to a party -  brought home the empty serving platter!  Very impressive looking and tasty. I cooked the shells the night before and let them set empty overnight in the refrigerator.  They were very easy to stuff while the pasta was cold.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese pound cake with strawberries and cream

use my recipe for strawberry sauce (recipe #43690) with this recipe. you won't be disappointed.  it's a winner! from southern living.

1. sprinkle sliced strawberries with 2 tablespoons sugar
2. cover and chill until ready to serve
3. beat butter and cream cheese at medium speed with an electric mixer until creamy
4. gradually add 2 1 / 2 cups sugar , beating well
5. add eggs , l at a time , beating until combined
6. stir in flour by hand just until moistened
7. stir in salt and vanilla
8. pour batter into a greased and floured 10-inch tube pan
9. bake at 300 for 1 hour and 50 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
10. cool in pan on a wire rack 10 to 15 minutes
11. remove from pan , and let cool completely on wire rack
12. cut into slices
13. beat whipping cream and 3 tablespoons sugar at high speed with an electric mixer until stiff peaks form
14. serve with cake
15. top with strawberry mixture , and drizzle with strawberry syrup
16. garnish , if desired
17. high-powered stand mixers can over beat some pound cakes , giving them a tough texture
demonstrations.review: Another winner, Bev!  I made this exactly as written, except I baked it in a Bundt pan for 1 hour 15 minutes.  Perfect!  My husband couldn't even wait until it had cooled properly...he was seriously salivating!   This recipe is in my "keepers" file.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy shrimp kabobs

chipotles give a zippy flavor honey giving it a sweetness making it a perfect finger licking food for entertaining. tweeked from weber. serve as an appetizer or over rice for a main meal. i served this with lime cayenne mayonnaise recipe #120459. it went great with it!

1. in a large bowl , combine the honey , chile pepper , garlic and salt
2. add the shrimp and toss to coat
3. cover and marinate at room temperature for 20 minutes or in the refrigerator for 1 hour
4. remove from the marinade and discard any remaining marinade
5. thread the shrimp through the tail and head onto small metal skewers or soaked wooden skewers
6. strong rosemary stems are good to use as skewers
7. grill over direct high heat for 2 to 4 minutes , turning once halfway through grilling time
8. arrange skewers on a serving dish and sprinkle with the cilantro
demonstrations.review: I had only cooked shrimp in the freezer and REALLY wanted to try this recipe, so I marinated the cooked shrimp in the sauce for a few hours.  Then I removed the shrimp, heated the sauce (to a boil) in a big frying pan.   I then lowered the heat, added the shrimp just to take the chill off being careful not to overheat them.  OH MY!!  Wonderful!  We found the shrimp is great as a hot dish or at room temp.  I am already planning to make this as an appy for our next party.  Thanks so much for this very tasty, easy dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s hot fudge sauce

grandma used to make this on sunday nights, it is the best!  even if you are usually not a big chocolate lover, you will love this.

1. heat medium sized sauce pan at medium heat
2. put chocolate and butter into the pan , melt
3. mix sugar into butter and chocolate mixture
4. in a separate bowl , beat eggs with a few tablespoons of milk
5. stir egg mixture into chocolate sauce as fast as you can !
6. don't take too long because the eggs will scramble-mixing half of the egg mixture in at a time makes it easier
7. add enough milk to dissolve the sugar and make a smooth sauce
8. use more than called for , if necessary
9. add salt and vanilla
10. enjoy !
11. store left overs in the fridge for up to a week
12. you may be tempted to eat it out of the jar !
demonstrations.review: Oh yes!!!  This is wonderful!  I followed the recipe exactly as posted and used a portion of it as the topping for Cream Puff Dessert # 51713.  Sent the rest home with our daughter who could not stop smacking her lips!  I know I will be making this a lot!  Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
southern macaroni and cheese

a recipe i gladly received from my husband's grandmother. true comfort food!

1. spray a flat bottomed casserole dish with vegetable spray
2. put half of the macaroni in the dish , top with half of the shredded cheese
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper
4. repeat
5. mix the melted butter and enough crushed saltines to absorb the butter , together
6. spread on top of cheese layer
7. pour milk slowly over all
8. bake at 350f for 35-45 minutes or until milk is no longer liquid
9. let set for at least 10 minutes before serving
target.review: Made it as a Thanksgiving side dish and my husband loved it. The crust is what makes this recipe stand out. He says it reminds him of the mac and cheese his mom made him as a boy. The kids are more of a soft,creamy, and cheesy type of mac so next time I'll add a more creamy cheese like Velveeta maybe. We'll see.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
foolproof  one bowl banana cake

made for those of us who often only have time to bake in the wee hours of the morning (or when we are half asleep), this super easy banana cake offers a great way to use up the      , overripe bananas sitting on the top of your refrigerator, and still make something that everyone will enjoy.  it can be frosted or not, but i usually don't bother; it stands on its own.  another winner from "the makings of a meal."

1. mix all the ingredients together in a large bowl until smooth
2. pour into a greased or sprayed 9"x13" pan
3. bake at 350f for 30-40 minutes
4. can be frozen for later use
demonstrations.review: I'm in love! So easy to make and delicious. I added all spice, cinnamon, butter instead of margarine, and almond extract.  Mixed in a little whole wheat flour with the white but used exactly 2 cups total, and finally included walnuts. It turned out awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fast and easy coconut custard pie

this is a fabulously easy pie that looks like you worked really hard! it makes its own crust and can be prepared and in the oven in no time. i found the original recipe in the 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray a 10 inch pie plate with cooking spray and then dust with flour
3. in a blender place everything but the coconut
4. mix until it is blended
5. add the coconut and blend for a few seconds or until it is all mixed
6. pour it into the pie plate and bake for 50-60 minutes
demonstrations.review: This dessert is beautiful in appearance with a wonderful pie crust like shell, but taste wise it turned out very bland. I expected more sweetness. Also the filling was not custard in texture but more like a "Budin" ( a Spanish dessert made with old bread that has a fruit cake type of center but softer) I did made a change to the recipe since we have our own coconuts growing in our property. I substituted the sweet coconut flakes for fresh coconut shavings, but to compensate for the lack of sugar in the natural coconut I added more sugar, so this shouldn't have been as dull in flavor. I followed all instructions in the recipe with the above exception.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: So easy and delicious! Restaurant pulled pork or chicken sandwiches have nothing on this one. Added a little honey mustard and spicy barbecue sauce along with Baby Rays and Tadaaaaa! Perfect leisure meal for a weekend afternoon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: The name says it all, and with good reason! Moist,sweet, and delicious. I added pecans to the top before baking and a little nutmeg to the mix, but the recipe stands for itself. Doesn't require any changes. I didn't put any frosting on it since I don't care much for it and the cake is sweet enough. If you haven't tried it, go for it. You will not be disappointed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best belgian waffles

these waffles are super crisp on the outside, light as a feather inside and so scrumptious! avoid removing them from the waffle iron too soon; they should be a golden brown. enjoy!

1. oil the waffle maker
2. sift the dry ingredients together in a large bowl
3. in separate bowl , separate egg whites and beat until stiff peaks form
4. in a separate bowl , mix together the egg yolks , milk , oil , and vanilla , stir slightly
5. add to dry ingredients and mix well
6. fold in egg whites
7. cook in waffle iron on medium-high heat for around 5-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is 10 stars worthy! Everything good all the other reviews say about it is true! Added some pecans to the batter, ate the waffles with maple syrup, and if I closed my eyes it felt like eating breakfast on vacation at a five star resort...luxurious.

target.recipe_text:
awesome slow cooker pot roast

i found this on the all recipes site. this is a very easy recipe for a delicious pot roast. it makes its own gravy. it's designed especially for the working person who does not have time to cook all day, but it tastes like you did. you'll want the cut to be between 5 and 6 pounds.

1. in a slow cooker , mix cream of mushroom soup , dry onion soup mix and water
2. place pot roast in slow cooker and coat with soup mixture
3. cook on high setting for 3 to 4 hours , or on low setting for 8 to 9 hours
target.review: This was a great recipe, though I am not sure I can rate it fairly. I used a 3 lb. chuck roast and the dry onion soup mix along with 1/2 cup of water but no cream of mushroom soup. I cooked it in the crock pot along with carrots, celery, potato and onions. I usually buy those expensive pot roast seasoning packages but did not have one and tried this. The onion soup mix is more affordable. I cooked it on low for 9 - 10 hours. Thank you for sharing, it was tender and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger   tots green bean casserole

makes a lot, so this is perfect for potlucks. quick and simple to make also.

1. brown hamburger
2. mix hamburger , soup and green beans
3. put this mixture in a buttered 9x13-inch cake pan
4. layer the tater tots over the top
5. bake at 350f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good. I make one very similar to this. It doesn't have green beans. I used 1 lb. of hamburger, 1 can of cream of mushroom soup and also added some chopped onion to it. The green beans were a nice change. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple upside down bundt cake

i love bundt cakes because they are so easy to serve. i found this recipe on a camping website and adapted it for use in the home kitchen instead of on the camp fire! it comes out great and it will be the easiest pineapple upside down cake you'll ever serve!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter in bundt pan in oven
3. spray cooking spray on the parts of the pan that aren't covered by the melted butter
4. sprinkle brown sugar over melted butter
5. place maraschino cherries on top of sugar
6. spread crushed pineapple over all
7. mix cake ingredients according to the package directions regarding time and mixer speeds
8. pour cake mix over topping ingredients in pan
9. bake for 40 minutes , until golden brown
10. test for doneness , knife or toothpick inserted should come out clean
11. immediately invert onto serving platter and remove pan carefully so none of the topping stays in the pan
12. cool completely before serving
demonstrations.review: This was really good. I added extra butter to the bottom of the pan and left out the cherries. I used all pineapple juice instead of part water. My first time to ever make a bundt cake and it turned out wonderfully. Thanks for the recipe. Will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
doctored up vanilla pudding casserole

this pudding is so good, it has a very good texture and the taste is to die for.

1. line the bottom of a 13 by 9 by 2-inch dish with 1 bag of cookies and layer bananas on top
2. in a bowl , combine the milk and pudding mix and blend well using a hand held electric mixer
3. using another bowl , combine the cream cheese and condensed milk together and mix until smooth
4. fold the whipped topping into the cream cheese mixture
5. add the cream cheese mixture to the pudding mixture and stir until well blended
6. pour the mixture over the cookies and bananas and cover with the remaining cookies
7. refrigerate until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: Excellent! This was the first time I have added cream cheese and sweetened condensed milk to my banana pudding and it adds great flavor. I will be making my banana pudding this way from now on. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan bow ties

kid favorite.

1. cook noodles according to package directions
2. drain
3. transfer to a serving bowl
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. toss to coat
demonstrations.review: This was very good. I didn't have any Italian dressing so I used raspberry vinaigrette. A little sweet but still good. I didn't even think it needed salt and pepper. I added some sliced black olives to it. Thank you, will definitely make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel s hash browns casserole   copycat

my parents worked on a cracker barrel training video (which they use to train the chefs) and got this recipe a few years ago. cracker barrel's recipe seems to have changed a bit over these few years but not for the best. this is their recipe though and has become a family favorite. we usually have it now for easter and thanksgiving and its also great for a brunch. happy cooking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix potatoes , onion , celery and mushroom soups , and 1 / 2 of the cheese
3. coat a 9" x 13" baking dish with spray oil
4. spread mixture into dish
5. sprinkle other 1 / 2 of cheese evenly over top
6. dot margarine evenly over the cheese
7. bake at 350f for 45 minutes to 1 hour or until cheese starts to brown at peaks
demonstrations.review: This was very delicious and easy to make. I made exactly as directed except instead of dotting margarine on top of the cheese, I just sprayed it with Pam butter spray (fat & calorie free). It was warm, creamy and very good. Will make again. Thank you for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
creamy scrambled eggs with diced bacon

my daughter in law from france made this egg dish for me and it is so good. simple and quick to prepare.

1. cook bacon pieces in skillet until crisp
2. remove from pan and drain on paper towels
3. remove bacon grease from skillet , wash and dry pan and return to heat
4. scramble eggs and add half and half and mix well
5. add butter to heated pan and add egg mixture
6. let the eggs set a bit and then sprinkle bacon over
7. stir eggs until soft set or until they are done to your liking
8. then proceed with recipe
target.review: WOW! Such a simple recipe but so delish. I used Recipe #208501 for the bacon, which worked like a charm so I didn't have to dirty two pans. ;) DH never likes scrambled eggs, but he LOVED these! I used fat free half & half and cooking spray instead of butter. It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog coffee  non alcoholic

a great way to use that eggnog! don't ya just love the holidays?

1. place coffee in filter in brew basket of coffee maker
2. sprinkle with nutmeg
3. place sugar in empty pot of coffee maker
4. add 2-1 / 2 cups cold water to coffee maker
5. brew
6. when brewing is complete , stir in eggnog
7. pour into 4 cups
8. serve immediately , topped with dollops of the whipped topping
9. sprinkle lightly with additional nutmeg , if desired
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: What a great holiday treat! :) I used low-fat eggnog and splenda for the sugar. The nutmeg sends this over the edge delicious!! I will enjoy this all holiday season -- thank you so much for sharing it, Sharon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus and veggie wrap

this is one of the most popular dishes at the cafe i work at-there you can get it on 3 different choices of wrap; sun-dried tomato, spinach, or flour.  it's really good

1. microwave tortilla for a few seconds to make it pliable
2. spread hummus over tortilla
3. add assorted veggies
4. add lettuce last
5. roll up and slice in half or eat whole
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: yum!!! I went searching for this recipe after I had one similar to this at whole foods. this is a great combination of flavors! and I love that the recipe is designed for one, cause my hubby won't go near something as healthy as this. ;) this is a perfect lunch/snack for these hot summer days! I made mine on a garlic flavored wrap, and left out the tomatoes cause I was all out, and left out the onions cause I was so excited to eat my wrap I forgot to slice them up and add them. ;) all in all, thanks for a great keeper! loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
batter dipped deep fried cauliflower

great appetizer or snack.  the breading is not too heavy.  the only time i've seen guys eat cauliflower during a football game is when it's this recipe.

1. preheat fryer oil to 375
2. place the beaten eggs , milk and salt in a shallow bowl
3. in a separate shallow bowl , mix together flour , cheese , garlic powder , thyme , oregano , paprika , cayenne , and pepper
4. place flowerets into egg mixture and toss to coat well
5. remove and place into flour mixture and toss to coat well
6. fry in batches for 4 - 6 minutes or until golden brown
7. drain on paper towels and lightly salt
8. serve w / dipping sauces such as marinara , ranch or blue cheese
demonstrations.review: wow! this an outstanding recipe.  I had been looking forward to making this recipe on my day off all week -- and it was well worth the wait! I put half the batch into a bagged caesar salad (got the idea from 'everyday italian' on the food network) and had the other half for snacks. both were great! I didn't have ranch to dip in, but they still were fantastic plain. thanks for a wonderful keeper! looking forward to trying this with other fresh veggies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potato pancakes southern style

on a rare occasion we have leftover mashed potatoes.  using recipe #27361 (the best), i added a modern twist to my mom's old southern recipe. increase or decrease onion, garlic, hot sauce, and s&p as to your preference. crispy on the outside, soft on the inside.  bet you can't eat just one!

1. in medium bowl combine all ingredients
2. whisk together until combined well
3. consistency should be similar to cornbread mixture
4. heat skillet with a light layer of oil on medium-high heat
5. spoon batter to form 3 1 / 2 to 4 inch rounds
6. brown each side to a rich dark golden brown
7. potato pancakes should look like a thick regular pancake
8. place on paper towel to drain excess oil
9. don't stack on top of each other or the bottom pancakes will become soggy
demonstrations.review: Yum! I hardly ever have mashed potatoes in my house, but we had some leftovers today so I decided to make this recipe. Let's just say I am stuffed.... I enjoyed these a little too much, lol. :) I cut the recipe in half and it worked well, was hard to flip for me too like another reviewer said, and got a little messy, but it tasted so good I didn't care. Thanks so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken caesar pasta casserole

i finally decided to post this.  i have made this recipe for years.  last year, i transformed this recipe and created recipe#195066!  i like to use a store-bought roasted chicken and an assorted bag of pasta that has penne, spirals, bowties and shells!!  this recipe also works well with tortellini!  i can't remember where this recipe originally came from...  enjoy!

1. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients except croutons and parmesan cheese
2. pour mixture into a greased , 2-quart casserole dish
3. top dish with croutons and parmesan cheese
4. bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until casserole is heated through and croutons are golden brown
demonstrations.review: YUM! I used a similar recipe from Holly Clegg's "Freezer Friendly" cook book. I made it ahead of time, froze, and reheated it in the oven. Fantastic! I used whole wheat pasta, no green onions, light dressing, and low-fat cheese. It all tasted great! Next time I might add a little more dressing just to really bring that Caesar flavor up a notch. This is definitely a keeper -- thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
chicken breasts stuffed with goat cheese and arugula

quick, easy and will look like you spent the day in the kitchen.

1. combine cheese and garlic in a small cup
2. trim excess fat from chicken
3. season with salt and pepper
4. using a sharp knife , cut a horizontal slit through thickest portion of each breast to form a deep pocket
5. stuff each pocket with an equal amount of cheese mixture and arugula
6. press edges of chicken together to seal
7. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
8. brown chicken , 4 minutes per side
9. reduce heat to medium
10. add broth to pan
11. cover and simmer , about 6 minutes , or until chicken is cooked through
12. serve immediately , discarding any remaining broth
target.review: I had this tonight for supper.  The combination of the goat cheese and the arugula was a really nice contrast to the chicken.  I'll definitely make this again.  The only big deviation I made was that instead of discarding the broth after simmering the chicken, I added a spritz of lemon juice, a pat of butter and a bit of cornstarch slurry to make a pan sauce to spoon over the chicken.  Served with a side of pan fried home-fries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrots   potatoes roasted w  onion and garlic

i came up with this recipe after having done a search on zaar and came up empty handed. it is a simple recipe and turned out exactly as i had hoped. i hope it will work for you as well as it did for me!

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. combine carrots , potatoes , onion and garlic with melted butter in 8x8" square glass pan
3. season generously with salt and pepper , toss
4. cover pan with aluminum foil and bake for 45 minutes
5. uncover , stir and continue baking for another 30 minutes , stirring occasionally to lift bottom portions to top to allow to brown and crisp
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  As a recent convert to many veggies, I needed the direction on roasting carrots without having charcoal.  The only thing I did differently from the recipe was to add a little salt and oregano.  I had planned on picking out and eating only the potatoes and onions, but I really did like the flavor of the carrots so I ate them, too.  Go figure.  I'm nearing 50 and I'm finally eating the veggies, voluntarily, that my mother tried to feed me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
everyday is thanksgiving in a loaf

ground turkey and a box of chicken or turkey seasoned stuffing makes anyday thanksgiving.  this is a favorite in my household.  we buy ground turkey instead of beef for a healthier lifestyle, unfortunately we always seem to over eat with this recipe.  serve this "meat"loaf with any of your favorite thanksgiving side dishes, we usually do mashed potatoes and corn.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. combined ground meat , stuffing , egg , pinch of pepper and sage , and 1 / 2 can gravy in a gallon sized freezer bag
3. with above ingredients in sealed bag , mush together with hands until all ingredients are mixed well
4. form into loaf shape while still in bag and drop into a loaf pan
5. top with remaining 1 / 2 can gravy
6. place in oven and cook for approximately 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is comfort food at its best for a carb lover.  I especially liked the texture that the loaf had because of the box of stuffing.  It was more "stuffing"ish than "meat"ish which was perfect for me.  If you prefer a meatier loaf, I could see this working just as well with 2 lbs of ground meat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade mayonnaise

when you're out of mayonnaise, blend a batch of this homemade mayonnaise in under 1 minute. because of the raw egg, this is not recommended for very young children or elderly persons, although washing the egg shell reduces the chance for contamination.

1. serving size is 1 tablespoon
2. recipe makes 1-1 / 4 cups mayonnaise
3. wash the outside of the egg shell with soap and water
4. rinse and dry
5. in blender , add egg , dry mustard , vinegar , and 1 / 4 cup oil
6. turn on low for 1-2 minutes
7. turn blender off , and scrape sides if necessary
8. turn blender on , and while it is running , slowly add the remaining 3 / 4 cups oil
9. blend until the consistency of mayonnaise
10. refrigerate in non-reactive container
11. for variation: add 1 / 4-1 / 2 tsp of your desired seasoning , such as , basil , tarragon , or parsley
demonstrations.review: My husband is a Miracle Whip guy and I don't touch mayo or Miracle Whip  but I needed some mayo to make some ranch dressing.  I started to make his in my food processor and nothing was happening and I was sure something was wrong.  Then POOF all of a sudden it was mayo!  I was so proud of myself.  I did a little taste and it tasted like mayo.  How cool is that????  Thanks for much for posting this recipe.  It was great just to have enough mayo on hand without buying a jar and having it go to waste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade rice a roni

this is a big hit at my house and pretty cheap to make too!

1. in medium skillet saute' broken spaghetti pieces in butter , stirring constantly , until the spaghetti begins to brown
2. add rice , stirring until the rice is well coated with the butter and the spaghetti browns a little more carefully pour in broth
3. simmer until liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: Made this for supper tonight and it was a big hit.  I used Knorr's Chicken Bouillon (powder) for the broth.  I don't normally like it as a broth but it did really well in this recipe and I was able to almost duplicate Rice-a-Roni.  Thanks for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
northwest creamy smoked salmon fettuccine alfredo

this is my fav. comfort food. i got this recipe from my mother and changed it just a bit. you can use shrimp or any other seafood

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 mis or until al dente
3. drain
4. in a medium saucepan , combine cheeses , margarine , milk , garlic powder , basil and stir over low heat until smooth and creamy about 10 to 15 minutes
5. toss sauce vegetables , smoked salmon , sauce and pasta in a large bowl
6. sprinkle with nutmeg
demonstrations.review:
This review is solely based on the sauce flavor.  To be honest, I'm not sure how I felt about the whole meal -- a bit fishy for me -- but I'm basing my review on the flavor of the sauce before the fishiness (which was a product of the salmon not the recipe)

I made a few alterations to the recipe.  I used only 4 oz of the cream cheese and about 75% of the parm called for.  Also instead of 1/2 cup of milk, I used just shy of 1 cup of heavy cream.  These changes made a tasty sauce.  As the recipe was written, it would have been far too.. too.. cream cheesy for our tastes.  Sometimes less really is more.

I didn't have a tomato on hand, but I used about 1/2 can of petite diced tomatoes, drained, and that really was a nice touch.

For the salmon, I used about 5 oz. of smoked salmon.  I found that a bit too fishy for my tastes but since the amount of salmon for the recipe wasn't noted in the directions, the fishiness didn't detract from the amount of starts given.

All in all this was a good pasta meal.  But I'm not sure if it was good enough that I'll make it again.

target.recipe_text:
holiday mushrooms

this dish is always requested at christmas and easter.i always make two because one is never enough!

1. clean and slice mushrooms
2. layer about a third of mushrooms in a 2-quart baking dish
3. layer with a third of bread crumbs and drizzle with a third of melted butter
4. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste
5. repeat for second layer
6. cover with remaining mushrooms
7. sprinkle with salt and pepper and wine
8. cover and bake in 325 degree oven for about 35 minutes
9. mix remaining crumbs and butter and spoon over mushrooms
10. bake , uncovered 10 minutes or until crumbs are toasted
target.review: I made this for our family Christmas dinner yesterday.   It is very good.  DH & I will make it again but because we like to experiment we're going to try different wines to see how each one changes the flavor.   I'm thinking that marsala would be good to try.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili s fajitas by todd wilbur

update: this recipe was created by todd wilbur for his cookbook "top secret restaurant recipes" (penguin random house 1997). www.topsecretrecipes.com. 

serve on flour tortillas with cheese, guacamole, sour cream, tomatoes, and lettuce.

1. combine the lime juice , water , oil , garlic , soy sauce , salt , liquid smoke , cayenne pepper , black pepper and either the sirloin or the chicken in a tupperware container , cover , and refrigerate at least 2 hours or overnight
2. discard leftover marinade
3. grill meat over medium flame 4-5 minutes on each side
4. cut meat into thin strips
5. set aside and keep warm
6. combine the 2 tbls
7. water , soy sauce , lime juice , salt , pepper and olive oil
8. set aside
9. cook onion and peppers in oil until brown
10. remove from heat
11. pour reserved mixture over onions and peppers
12. combine meat , onions , and peppers
demonstrations.review: The flavor of these is outstanding.  We went to dinner at the Outback one night and used our leftover prime rib from dinner in this.  Wonderful!  Thanks so much for posting - we'll be making these again - and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry cranberry salad  with sour cream cream cheese topping

this yummy recipe is and has been a staple and favorite dish in our family esp. at thanksgiving and christmas for many years. we like the tang of the cranberry softened with the other ingredients. it makes a wonderful side dish and can pass as a dessert, too. it would be good anytime you were serving a turkey, chicken or ham dish.

1. mix jello with the two cups of boiling water till disolved
2. add the can of pineapple including the juice and the whole cranberry sauce and nuts
3. let set in bowl or mold of choice
4. blend the cream cheese , sour cream and sugar well
5. after jello has set , spread on top
demonstrations.review: We make this in a 9x13 dish instead of a bowl.   Other than that, it is exactly like our traditional Thanksgiving cranberries.   It's one of my absolute favorite ways to eat them.   The topping is a nice contrast to the jello/cranberry layer.   Even the cranberry haters started eating them when we started making this dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brats and sauerkraut

had this at a farm sell. the sauerkraut on top of the brat was just great! this can easily be made for a large crowd and keep in a roaster.

1. saute onions in butter
2. when the onions are caramelized add garlic , saute for 1 minute
3. add undrained sauerkraut , sugar , celery seed and bay leaf
4. cover and simmer 1 / 2 hour
5. add meat and simmer for 45 minutes
6. serve on bun and top with sauerkraut
demonstrations.review: This was so good, I didn't cook my brats ahead of time either.  They took on the flavor of the kraut which had mellowed from the sugar and other additions.  I made a double batch because I used a bag of kraut instead of a can, when I mentioned leftovers tomorrow night everyone said they would be back.  That's how good it was, DH said this is a definite keeper.  Try Mini Ravindran's Warm Mustard Sauce with these - awesome!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge rice crispy sandwiches

these no-bake cookies take rice krispy treats to a new level. almost all of the prep time involves chilling the cookies in the refrigerator. i suggest doubling the recipe to keep everyone happy.

1. melt butterscotch chips and peanut butter over very low heat , stirring constantly until well blended
2. remove from heat , then stir in rice krispies until well coated
3. press half of rice krispy mixture into buttered 8x8 pan and chill in refrigerator
4. combine water , chocolate chips , powdered sugar , and butter and melt until well blended using a double boiler or a mixing bowl atop a saucepan of boiling water
5. spread chocolate mixture evenly atop chilled rice krispy mixture , lightly press into place , then chill in refrigerator
6. spread remaining rice krispy mixture atop chilled chocolate layer , then chill again
7. remove from refrigerator and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: First off, the taste was great but I too had a bit of a problem with the rice krispies sticking so next time I will press down harder...maybe they'll stick better...I too think the chocolate layer could be halved.  They were easier to cut once they had sat out of the fridge for a bit.  I have some peanut butter chips and I'm thinking that they will work well in place of the butterscotch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lite salmon   pasta casserole

i like to spice this up a bit more with garlic and jalapenos etc but it is very tasty the way it is - this will stretch to 6 servings but i think 4 is realistic. surprisingly low in fat and calories. good budget stretcher

1. cook pasta according to directions or try recipe#30358 perfect pasta with no watching& no sweating in a large saucepan combine soup , milk , swiss cheese , dill , lemon zest , mustard powder& black pepper cook over medium heat until the cheese has melted
2. stir in the salmon and cooked pasta shells
3. spray a 2 quart casserole lightly with veggie oil and pour in the casserole ingredients heat oven to 350f
4. sprinkle with parmesan& parsley
5. bake covered with foil for apprx 20 minutes remove foil and continue baking for 5 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I really liked the flavor of this dish - the lemon zest gave it a freshness that was totally unexpected.  It's not a real saucy dish so if you like lots of sauce you might want to double it.  We thoroughly enjoyed it with some fresh asparagus.  Also I baked this in a 9x13 instead of a 2 quart casserole.  This will definitely be made again and again around here.

target.recipe_text:
downunder cheese puffs

these are not popovers and have nothing to do with bread. these are very quick snacks that you can whip up during commercial breaks when you are watching tv and you feel like something cheesy. vary the taste with different types of cheeses.

1. beat the egg in the milk
2. mix together with the flour , baking powder , salt and grated cheese
3. put large teaspoonfuls on a cold greased tray
4. bake for 10 minutes in a hot oven 400 degrees fahrenheit
target.review: I made these w/ sharp cheddar and about half a teaspoon of dried mustard.  Now I'm hooked!!!!  If, for some strange reason, they haven't disappeared immediately after being baked, it's definitely worth it to heat them up again before serving them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chinese pineapple chicken with cashew nuts  ginger  spring onion

this is sure to satisfy all your cravings for chinese food, it's a great recipe.  be brave with the ginger, it mellows out as it cooks and is helped along by the sweetness of the dish.  the cashew nuts are optional but i am yet to make it without them as i love their crunchy texture and creamy taste.   be sure to serve it with plenty of white fluffy rice.  quicker than waiting for takeout. update - i have decreased the amount of water used in the sauce from 1/2pt to 1/4 pint but i find it does tend to get a bit too thick and needs a drop or 2 more.  use your senses, if you think it needs it then add it!  adding frozen veggies will water the sauce down considerably.  this particular recipe does not adhere much to tweaking and i suggest you try it as stated below first.  thank you

1. first of all make the sauce
2. combine everything , mix well until smooth and set aside
3. fry the chicken in the oil with the onion and ginger for 5 minutes over a medium high heat
4. add the green pepper and the pineapple chunks and fry for another 5 minutes adding half of the spring onions after 2 minutes
5. add the crushed garlic and the cashew nuts , fry for 2 minutes then pour over the sauce and bring to the boil
6. after a minute or 2 , the sauce should thicken and stick to the chicken
7. it it looks too thick , add some water , little by little until desired consistency is acheived
8. utterly delicious
demonstrations.review: This is an easy and tasty treat!  I used a bag of frozen stirfry veggies i lieu of the green pepper (added them in frozen with the chicken), and used pineapple tidbits instead of the chunks.  The sauce was a little bit bland for my tastes, but this is definitely worth tweaking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh strawberry cake

i make this cake at least once every summer, when fresh strawberries are in season. it's delicious! i found the recipe in a cook book titled, 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. for cake: sift together: flour , salt , and baking powder
3. in a separate bowl , combine butter , sugar , eggs , and vanilla
4. beat for a total of 3 minutes , scrapping the sides of the bowl
5. then add flour mixture to creamed mixture , alternating with strawberries
6. beat for two minutes
7. pour batter into two 8-inch round greased and floured cake pans
8. bake in pre-heated oven for 25-30 minutes , or until cake tests done
9. turn out on to wire cooling racks to cool
10. when cool , top with strawberry glaze
11. for strawberry glaze: mix together all ingredients
12. use enough strawberries to thin mixture
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavor!  I halved the recipe to make a dozen cupcakes for work.  The batter seemed stiff, so I ended up increasing the amount of strawberries to a half cup.  I mixed this using a stand mixer, and next time may cut down on the mixing time in step 4 a little.  I iced the cupcakes with Cream Cheese Icing (recipe #22932).  My coworkers are already asking for the cake recipe, which is always a good sign!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy potato bell pepper chowder

a belly-warmer!  makes a lot, but is easily halved. serving size is a guess.

1. in a large soup pot , melt butter
2. add onion , bell peppers and garlic and saut until tender
3. briskly stir in the flour
4. add the chicken broth and stir well
5. stir in the potatoes , chives and pepper
6. bring to a soft boil
7. reduce heat and gently simmer for about 20 minutes or until potatoes are tender
8. stir frequently to prevent sticking on bottom
9. add half and half and cheeses
10. stir constantly until cheese is melted
11. add salt
12. if needed to taste
13. serve
demonstrations.review: I made this for a potluck, and it was a huge hit.  Great choice for these below zero days!  I used orange and yellow peppers, and substituted 2% evaporated milk for the half-and-half, but omitted the swiss.  I had to simmer 30 minutes insead of  20, but some of my potato pieces were a bit on the large size.  The leftovers were divine as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian lentil and barley soup

this is a surprisingly filling, vegetarian, crock pot soup. it is very good, and easy to prepare the night before, or chop the veggies in advance and turn it on before you leave for work in the morning. goes great with a crusty bread.

1. sort through lentils to remove debris and shriveled beans , then rinse
2. add lentils to crock pot , along with barley , carrots , celery , onion , garlic , dried herbs and bay leaf
3. pour in broth , water , and tomatoes
4. cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 14 hours , or on high heat for 5 to 6 hours
5. discard bay leaf and just before serving stir in parsley and vinegar
6. lentils aren't like dried beans
7. they don't require soaking and cook pretty quickly when you do it right
8. when you buy your lentils , go somewhere that has a decent turnover so your lentils haven't been sitting on the shelf for years
9. also , don't add any additional salt to the soup while it is cooking , and don't add lentils to already boiling water as either one can make lentils tough
demonstrations.review: What a fabulous, versatile recipe!  I've made it several times now as printed (even with the celery, which I'm not a fan of usually!), and most recently with a diced sweet potato added for fun. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
five spice chicken noodle soup

try this spicy asian-inspired take on the traditional soothing chicken noodle soup. recipe comes from better homes and gardens.

1. in a large saucepan combine water , chicken broth , green onions , soy sauce , garlic , five-spice powder , and ginger
2. bring to boiling
3. stir in bok choy , sweet pepper strips , and noodles
4. return to boiling , reduce heat
5. boil gently , uncovered , 3 to 5 minutes or until noodles are tender ,
6. stir in chicken , heat through and serve
demonstrations.review: I doubled this for dinner for 8 picky eaters, and it was a definite hit.  I used all chicken stock instead of cutting it with bullion, subbed in udon noodles instead of somen, and added a handful of thinly sliced carrots as well as some white pepper.  Not a good soup to make if you're hoping for leftovers!  ;)

target.recipe_text:
kentucky biscuits

i got this recipe from a small free recipe book  from kfc    

1. preheat oven to 425
2. sift into mixing bowl flour , salt , sugar and baking powder
3. make a nest in the flour mix and add milk
4. add shortening and begin kneading with hands the vegetable shortening and flour in the milk until thoroughly mixed
5. add milk - if needed - to form , and mix
6. turn onto floured board , and knead gently 6 to 8 times
7. pat dough to 1 / 2" thickness
8. cut into biscuits
9. place on baking sheet and brown in oven 10-13 minutes
target.review: can you say WOW!? theese biscuits were wonderful and I can't emphasize that enough. I was addicted and eating them like chocolate chip cookies. These are my new dinner biscuits that I'll be making again and again! I think i'm going to go make some more :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili sauce  homemade

this is an easy recipe for chili sauce using fresh ingredients.

1. add all ingredients to heavy pot
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce to a simmer and let cook for 1 hour
4. add ingredients to a blender and blend until smooth
5. return to pot and simmer for 30 minutes more
6. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was absolutely wonderful! So much better than anything store bought. The smell as this simmered in my kitchen for an hour and a half was just so tantilizing!!! I used this to makde a crock pot pulled pork recipe, #76273, and I'm already planning on making this for our church potluck on sunday!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted mediterranean vegetables

a lovely, filling dish from my mom.  i believe she got it from a market.  you can use any color bell peppers - i like to use two different colors.  i usually leave the skins on the potatoes and eggplant, but feel free to peel them before making the recipe, if that is your preference :)

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. prepare a shallow roasting dish with nonstick cooking spray
3. combine potatoes , eggplant , both bell peppers , and the red onion slices and place in roasting dish
4. whisk together the olive oil , balsamic vinegar , basil , oregano , chives , garlic and salt and pepper
5. drizzle sauce over the mixed vegetables and toss to coat
6. roast vegetables until tender , about 45 minutes
7. stir halfway through the cooking time
demonstrations.review: Yummy recipe. I didn't have eggplant so I substituted with yellow squash. I also used from herbs from my garden and added some parsley as well. I recommend cutting your potatoes smaller than the instructed size. I had a few that could have been cooked a little bit longer.  Made & enjoyed for Zinga ZWT6.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Chimichangas are my favorite thing to get at mexican restaurants and this was my first attempt at making them at home. I enjoyed these a lot! I added half a packet of taco seasoning for a little extra kick and some fresh cilantro.  I loved the crispyness of the tortillas! One thing I'll probably do differently next time is shred the chicken. Thats just a personal preference. I will be making these frequently from now on! thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brie bread

this is an outstanding addition to your tapa table and so easy to make. i received this recipe from my friend pat who i had met in sint maarten.

1. melt the butter in a sauce pan and onion and basil
2. cut the brie into small pieces and add to the butter mixture
3. stir until the brie is melted
4. slice the french bread in half lengthwise
5. take each half and cut almost all the way through into slices about 1 1 / 2 inches each
6. spread the melted brie mixture over each half of the loaf
7. place each half of the under the broiler until the cheese is bubbly
8. tear the individual pieces completely off the loaves and place on serving platter
demonstrations.review: As in Julie & Julia- you can never have too much butter! Loved this recipe but discovered that I am not a fan of brie cheese (this was the first time ever trying it). I would make this recipe again with a different type of cheese, maybe feta or gouda ??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chop suey con casuy

authentic filipino meal of stir fried chicken, vegetables, and cashews.  serve over rice.

1. cut chicken breasts into paper thin slices
2. combine with cornstarch , 1 tablespoon soy sauce , and egg white
3. heat 1 tablespoon oil in skillet over medium high heat
4. add vegetables and saute for 3 minutes
5. add remaining soy sauce
6. transfer to platter and set aside
7. add remaining oil into same skillet and turn to high heat
8. saute chicken for 2 minutes until cooked
9. return cooked vegetables to skillet
10. add hot broth
11. stir to combine all ingredients thoroughly
12. cook for one minute
13. garnish with cashews
demonstrations.review: Growing up I never liked cabbage but here lately I've grown to really enjoy it in some recipes. I really enjoyed this one! The flavors of all the vegetables just came together nicely and were not overpowered by any other spice. It had a very natural easy going flavor!! Made for ZWT6 Asia Region!

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin white chocolate cake

i got this recipe from a resident's grand-daughter. she made it as a birthday cake and everyone inhaled it. i was thrilled when i found out it started out with a cake mix.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350 degrees grease and flour 12 cup bundt pan , i use bakers joy spray
2. in a large bowl
3. combine cake mix , eggs , pumpkin , evaporated milk and oil
4. beat on low speed until moistened
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in chips
7. pour into prepared pan
8. bake for 45 minutes or until wooden toothpick inserted in cake comes out clean
9. cool in pan for 25 minutes then invert on wire rack to cool completely
10. place on serving plate
11. glaze when completely cool glaze: heat evaporated milk in small saucepan over medium heat until it just starts to come to a boil
12. remove from heat
13. stir in white chocolate chips and stir until smooth
14. add cinnamon and stir in well
target.review:
This is a very nice, moist cake. I did not have a spice cake mix so I used a yellow cake mix and added the spices myself. Turned out fine.
The whole family liked it. Even my son that never eats anything veggie.
Thanks for the recipe. Its a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
