4. drain the zucchini well between the palms of your hands and add to the mixture
5. mix lightly
6. put the oil in a frying pan and heat well
7. to make each fritter use a tablespoon to take a scoop from the mixture and with the aid of another spoon push it into the frying pan
8. fry the fritters for a few minutes until they are nicely browned
9. drain on towels on a plate
demonstrations.review: These were mostly delicious.  Universally in our grou at least, these were a bit too salty.  I didn't add any extra salt, and didn't use much salt for the zucchini.  Next time I'll cut back on feta and may rinse the zucchini before use.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted broccoli with lemon

the heat concentrates the flavors and caramelizes the natural sugars. a touch of olive oil gives a crispy, delicious finish. (eating well, winter 2004)
this is an easy and yummy alternative to steaming. something about the oil and salt combination that makes this so good.

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. toss broccoli with oil , salt , and pepper
3. place on a large baking sheet
4. roast until broccoli is tender and blackened on the bottom , 10-12 minutes
5. serve immediately , with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: This is awesomely delicious.  I was looking for this exact recipe, but had already eye-balled the amounts.  I think I went heavier on the olive oil, but if you let the broccoli flowerettes get a little browned it's got a wonderful carmelly crispy taste that is great with the salt, lemon and olive oil.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
target.review: This is exactly the same taste that I was looking for. The recipe had a great taste and delicious and yummy.Before this recipe network, i will follow the ( https://www.sooperchef.pk/pakistani-recipes/ ). Video Tutorial also available for cooking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: Good taste &amp;amp; So delicious and yummy -Amazing recipe. i also made this meal. This meal recipe same as the recipe of. Must visit ( https://pakistanirecipesinurdu.wordpress.com/ ) to find more Recipes like this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best oatmeal cookies

this is a family favorite that i have been making for years. it's the most requested oatmeal cookie recipe i've ever made. i found it somewhere years ago, but have lost the source. the secret is soaking the raisins which makes all the difference.

1. this is a very important first step that makes the cookie: combine eggs , raisins and vanilla and let stand for one hour
2. cream together butter and sugars
3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: Oatmeal dish is my favorite dish. I made it with my mom and enjoy whole family.This is great website for food lovers. I am share a link with people to find the Oetmeal pakistani recipe video here. Thank you sharing yummy recip. https://pakistanirecipespoint.wordpress.com/

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  rice  and spices bake

i got this recipe from my friend kasey a long time ago (i have adjusted the spices to my taste) and it is very easy--even for those that just can't seem to get basmati rice to cook "just right". so long as you cover the baking dish tightly with foil, it will not fail! i brought this to a pot-luck at work one day and ever since this dish was always requested by everyone at all of our potlucks.***i am cutting the salt to around half since there are quite a few reviews saying it is too salty. i don't measure the spices when i cook so i think i guessed the amount wrong.***
*** the cinnamon amount should be 1/2 tsp to 3/4 tsp only, not 2 teaspoons.  i have tried changing it twice now and get email confirmation that the changes have been approved but it still says 2 tsp of cinnamon.

1. preheat oven to 375f and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. bring water to boiling and add chicken bouillon cubes , lower heat and simmer till dissolved--keep it hot
3. sprinkle chicken with half the spices
4. heat the olive oil in a large skillet on med-high to high heat and fry the chicken till both sides are brown , lower heat to medium and remove the chicken to a plate
5. in that same skillet saut the onions for 2 minutes , then add the garlic and remaining spices and saut another 2 minutes , then turn off the burner
6. add the rice and stir for about 30 seconds to 1 minute , till well coated
7. spread rice in the baking dish and place the chicken thighs over the rice
8. gently pour in the chicken stock and cover tightly with foil
9. bake for 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy! This one is good and easy to make. I made this with my mom according to instruction and add more chicken & Masala to make taste delicious and yummy. I also made this recipe before itself from recipe network ( https://www.sooperchef.pk/pakistani-recipes/ ).Thankyou!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: Yummy and Delicious Dish. This is my favorite dish. I just made it at home with my mom. So tasteful, I loved your cooking recipes and way of cooking it's amazing Before I will also find the same soup recipe from one website sharing a link with you::: http://sooperchef.blogspot.com/

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Great Meals so delicious & yummy.I just made it with my mom & enjoy with family. I loved your method.I am following you and another websites for cooking. Sharing a link ( https://cookingrecipesnetwork.blogspot.com/ ).

target.recipe_text:
crook s corner shrimp and grits

crook's corner is a restaurant in chapel hill, nc. this is a dish served at the restaurant and i found the recipe in the latest southern living magazine. i made this last night for dinner and my husband and i went nuts for it, it's the ultimate comfort food. don't let the long list of ingredients throw you off, this goes together quickly and easily.

1. bring first 4 ingredients to a boil in a medium saucepan
2. gradually whisk in grits
3. reduce heat and simmer , stirring occasionally , 10 minutes or until thickened
4. add cheddar cheese and next 4 ingredients
5. set aside but keep warm
6. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
7. remove bacon and drain on paper towels , reserve 1 tablespoon of drippings in skillet
8. crumble bacon and set aside
9. sprinkle shrimp with pepper and salt
10. dredge in flour
11. saute mushrooms in hot drippings in skillet 5 minutes , or until tender
12. add green onions and saute 2 minutes
13. add shrimp and garlic and saute 2 minutes or until shrimp are lightly brown
14. stir in chicken broth , lemon juice and hot sauce and cook 2 more minutes , stirring to loosen browned bits from skillet
15. divide grits into 4 large , shallow soup bowls
16. divide shrimp mixture into four servings and place on top of grits
17. top each serving with crumbled bacon and serve with lemon wedges
target.review:
** May 25, 2009 -- Made this again last night!!!  It is amazing!  Just wanted to say thanks again for my most favorite meal!!!**

YUM!!!!  SOOOOO good!  I am originally from the mid-west, so I kind of had to get used to grits (which is a staple here in NC), but this recipe was beyond awesome.  My husband has not developed a taste for grits, so he ate his over white rice and loved it.  We had company over for dinner, so there were NO leftovers and that made me very upset!  I can't wait to make it again!!  I didn't have white pepper, so I used black and added a bit more tabasco to give it some more spice.  My friend makes this and adds diced tomatoes to the mix, so I might try that addition next time!  Thank you for posting!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
steven s world famous to die for sour cream chicken

i've modified my grandmother's recipe for the 21st century. i can't have a dinner party and not asked to make this simple dish. enjoy!

1. clean chicken and pour sour cream over it and let marinate for about an hour in the refrigerator
2. meanwhile , take crackers and crush into medium course crumbs , mix in parmesan cheese and tarragon / marjoram
3. melt half of the butter and pour on the bottom of a 9x13 baking dish
4. dredge chicken in the cracker mixture and set in baking dish
5. repeat until complete
6. melt rest of butter and pour on top of chicken
7. bake@ 350 for 35-45 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Excellent!  I cut the butter to about 4 TBS and used 4 large chicken breasts sliced into strips.  used reduced fat parm. cheese and FF sour cream.  I also substituted 2 TBS Italian seasoning for the tarragon.  We really enjoyed it with green beans and potato rolls.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy ham and potato soup

comfort soup at its finest!  i usually make this to use up leftover ham.  this is easy to adapt with other ingredients.  i don't put celery in mine.  i have added garlic sometimes as well.

1. combine potatoes , celery , carrots , onion , ham , and water / broth in stockpot and bring to boil
2. then cook over medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. stir in the chicken bouillon , salt , and pepper
4. in separate saucepan , melt butter over medium-low heat
5. whisk in flour and cook stirring constantly until thick
6. slowly stir in milk as not to allow lumps to form and all milk is added
7. turn up to medium heat
8. continue to stir until thick
9. add in cheese and stir until melted
10. stir the cheese mixture into the stockpot and cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: OMG!  That is amazing!  I made it tonight since it is sooooo chilly here, and we ate it with some crusty rolls....the kids even loved it!  I used evaporated milk (2%) and onion powder instead of 1/3 c onion.  I boiled the potatoes on the stove in the stock, made the cheese sauce, then transferred everything to a crock pot where it kept warm (and thickened) until it was time for dinner!  Sooooo good!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cooker chicken

this recipe is from the 

1. combine soup mix , sour cream , and cream of mushroom soup in crockpot
2. add chicken , submerging it into sauce so it's covered
3. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
4. serve over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: This was super easy to throw together and really tasty!  I used a package of chicken breast tenders, a can of sliced mushrooms, 1 C. sour cream, and 1/2 envelope ranch dressing mix (because I was out of onion soup mix) in addition to the cr. of mush.....it was great over noodles!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This is a really good idea, however, it was way too salty for us.  I think the saltiness came from the cr. of chicken soup being undiluted.  I did not bake these with the sauce, and tomorrow, with the leftovers, we will probably omit the sauce all together. The rolls are fine without it.  Thanks for an interesting recipe, though!
**edited 10/15/07 - made this again tonight and it was excellent!!  I used healthy choice cr. of chicken soup, light cream, and baked the rolls without sauce, adding it after they came out of the oven.  I cut the butter to 2tbs and used about 3/4 c. cheddar cheese total. So, I am changing my rating to 5 stars!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I made this with Belinda's Mexican Rice #241947 as a side and it was a great meal!  I used fat free/reduced fat versions of beans, sour cream, soup, and cheese and it turned out perfect! Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
amazing whole wheat oatmeal cookies

these cookies are really good! and they only have a little bit of butter in them! you can add raisins to them, or you can use chocolate chips instead!  they are moist and tasty.  one healthy recipe my family actually liked! makes 4 dozen

1. heat oven to 375
2. combine the flour , cinnamon , baking powder , baking soda , and salt in one bowl
3. mix the brown sugar , applesauce , eggs , margarine , and vanilla in another bowl
4. mix the two bowls into one bowl
5. then add in the oats and raisins
6. drop rounded teaspoons of the dough onto a baking sheet
7. cook for 10-12 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: These were great cookies! So much better than a lot of lower fat cookies out here. The only thing I did differently was use 1 whole egg instead of 2 egg whites because I only had one egg left in my fridge! Thanks for sharing such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutella biscotti

i have not tried this recipe yet, so i'm putting it here for safe keeping.  i love nutella and biscotti and figure you can't go wrong to combine the two.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. sift together flour , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda and salt in a medium bowl
3. beat eggs in a large bowl until frothy
4. add sugar and continue beating on high for 2 minutes
5. stir in nutella
6. add flour mixture to egg mixture and stir until well combined
7. stir in chocolate chips and hazelnuts , if using
8. divide dough into 2 or 3 logs with well floured hands and arrange on a parchment lined baking sheet
9. press logs into rectangles approximately 1 / 2 inch thick
10. bake at 350f for 20 minutes
11. remove from oven
12. turn down oven heat to 300f
13. using a serrated knife , cut logs into 1 / 3-1 / 2 inch slices
14. arrange on baking sheet and return to oven
15. bake for 10-12 minutes , turn biscotti over and bake an additional 10-12 minutes
16. remove to a wire rack to cool
17. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: I'm in love with this recipe! I made this exactly as directed and they turned out wonderfully. My only problem was that I didn't make my logs thin enough, so mine took longer to bake. Yum, I can't wait to make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
get up   go  bars

i found these at the mr. food site. my friends says they really are called get up and go bars because with all the fiber, you really will have to get up and run! especially if you have one of these bars with your first morning cup of coffee!

1. line a 9" x 13" baking dish with foil and coat the foil with nonstick cooking spray
2. in a large saucepan , combine the sugar , corn syrup , and peanut butter over medium-high heat
3. bring to a boil and cook for 1 minute , stirring constantly
4. add the remaining ingredients
5. mix well then spread evenly into the prepared pan
6. let cool then cut into bars and serve , or cover until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: This recipe is amazing. My husband always requests I make a new pan as he eats the last bar out of the old pan! I omit the sugar in the recipe, as I think the peanut butter and dried fruit make the recipe sweet enough. Thank you for such a yummy recipe, Mirj.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread pudding

vanlig brodpudding

1. mix together stale bread pieces , hot milk and butter
2. set aside until cool
3. heat oven to 350
4. beat eggs well , add sugar and milk and stir
5. stir in spices if desired
6. mix cold bread mixture with egg mixture
7. pour into buttered casserole
8. bake 30 minutes until pudding has set and is turning golden brown
9. serve warm
demonstrations.review: This was my first time making bread pudding. The recipe was easy to follow, and I ended up with fantastic bread pudding! I reduced the amount of sugar to 1/2 cup and adding about a 1/2 cup of raisins. Otherwise followed recipe. Will be making again, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
snack mix squares

cool kid's snack

1. in a large bowl , combine the pretzels , cereal and m&m's
2. in a large saucepan over low heat , melt butter and peanut butter
3. add marshmallows
4. cook and stir until marshmallows are melted and mixture is smooth
5. pour over pretzel mixture
6. stir to coat
7. press into a greased 13x9 inch baking pan
8. cool until firm
9. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: I was really disappointed that this never set that well. It was like there was too much butter; the squares were really gooey, and the marshmallow mixture just sank to the bottom. The taste was good. I might consider making this again but tweaking the recipe... 1/2 cup butter just seems like too much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low calorie apple cinnamon pancakes

these are my own creation, and since my boyfriend and i love pancakes we make them often!!

1. heat skillet and coat in cooking spray
2. combine ingredients in medium size bowl
3. ladle out 2 tbsp of batter per pancake and lightly brown each side of the cake
4. try leaving the very center gooey for a different texture and flavor
demonstrations.review: I have made these pancakes several times now, and they always turn out great. Mine do not turn out heavy like some other reviewers have stated. Lately I have been adding frozen blueberries to my pancakes. Once I pour the batter into the pan, I sprinkle the blueberries on top and push them into the batter. They cook up perfectly! Thank you for such a great, low calorie pancake.

target.recipe_text:
spicy meat and cheese stromboli

this is from 30 minute meals on food network.  a simple, quick snack for the sunday football game or movie night.

1. pre-heat oven to 400 degrees
2. break open the tube of dough and remove it from container
3. dust your hands and lightly coat the dough with cornmeal then roll out onto work surface
4. stretch out dough , then cut the thin rectangular dough into 4 equal square pieces
5. cover each piece of dough with: 6 slices pepperoni , 1 1 / 2 slices cheese , 1 1 / 2 slices hot ham and 2 slices genoa salami
6. roll each piece on an angle from corner to corner making a long roll that is thicker in the middle and thinner on each end
7. brush rolls with extra-virgin olive oil then mix sesame seeds , cheese and seasonings in a small cup , sprinkle and pat the mixture into the dough
8. bake until evenly golden , 12 to 15 minutes then serve
9. if desired , serve with marinara sauce
target.review: This recipe has become my 'go to' stromboli recipe. It's so easy and yummy! I add a little bit of sauce to mine but otherwise I make it just as the recipe directs and we just love it. I've tried using bread dough and it does ok in a pinch but the pizza dough is much easier. I've also tried making one large stromboli and prefer the 'individual' ones since the dough in the middle never seems to be cooked in the large one. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
redneck casserole  aka comfort casserole

this recipe came about after reading a thread about spam and velveeta, so i thought i would come up with this, not bad if i say so myself (but i like spam and velveeta :)).  the prep time might be a little shorter or longer, had to guess at it.

1. in a large saucepan , cook pasta according to package directions
2. in a medium sized skillet over medium heat add oil when oil is hot , add spam , carrots and onion
3. stir until spam is brown and onion and carrots are softened , about 10 to 15 minutes
4. remove from heat , in same skillet add pasta and peas mix well
5. in a lightly sprayed 8 by 11 inch dish , add pasta and spam mixture
6. in a medium saucepan over medium heat add milk , velveeta and flour
7. with wire whisk , whisk until smooth and slightly thickened
8. pour over the pasta and spam mixture , salt and pepper to taste then mix well
9. evenly sprinkle shredded cheese over the top bake at 350 until top is golden brown , about 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have to say that, like other reviewers, I was a bit skeptical about this recipe but I was pleasantly surprised. This recipe was easy and yummy - just the way I like 'em! Hubby REALLY liked it and it will certainly be made again in our house! Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic saffron rice

this is easy, simple and wonderful.  the original recipe which was printed in the spring 2005 penzeys catalog, calls for long-grain rice; however, i liked it much better with basmati. also, the original recipe called for minced onion but i found it worked very well with dried onion.  i indicated that the butter is optional, because i did not add it.

1. rinse the rice well , drain
2. in a medium size saucepan , add the rinsed rice and remaining ingredients
3. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat
4. simmer for 15 to 20 minutes or until stock is absorbed and rice is tender
5. fluff with fork and serve
demonstrations.review: I somehow found myself without saffron when making this recipe but even without it, the result was very yummy. I used regular white rice and onion powder as that's what we had on hand. Thanks for a new, quick take on the same old rice!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry orange quinoa salad

quinoa (pronounced 'keen-wa') is a whole grain originating from central america. it has become very popular recently for it's health benefits as a complete protein substitute for vegetarians. quinoa is similar in texture to couscous and very versatile. this particular recipe is a wonderful and flavorful side dish for any occasions.

1. melt butter to saucepan and add quinoa
2. on medium heat , toast quinoa until light golden brown
3. add oj and water to pan and bring to a boil then simmer on low for 30 min until liquid is absorbed
4. in mixing bowl , combine cranberries , chopped green onions , toasted pine nuts , and chopped apple
5. in a measuring cup , mix olive oil , vinegar , spices , and honey
6. blend well
7. add cooked quinoa to bowl and toss well with the dressing
8. chill in the refrigerator for at least 30 min before serving
9. refrigerate for up to 4 days
demonstrations.review: This recipe was full of new flavors and a nice change to the usual salads I take to pot lucks! It smelled delicious while cooking and was very easy to put together. They only thing that went wrong was totally my fault. I halved the salad recipe but made the whole dressing recipe and didn't realize it until I put them together! It was still good but the vinegar flavor was a little overpowering, the salad was very moist and I felt like the orange flavor (I used orange mango juice - yum!) was completely overwhelmed. I'd definitely like to try this again and see how it tastes when made properly! Thanks for a fun, new way to use quinoa!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever bbq chicken

the bbq sauce on this juicy grilled chicken is out-of-this world! we "wow" people with this recipe every summer during outdoor entertaining. i always double the sauce recipe to have extra on the side for dipping. the original recipe calls for 2 small boiler chickens quartered but we prefer using bone-in, skin on chicken breasts. slow cooking on the grill gives it the best flavor. i hope you enjoy this as much as we do - it's a favorite at this house.

1. in a saucepan , saute the garlic in butter until tender
2. add the next 8 ingredients
3. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
4. remove from the heat and set aside
5. grill the chicken , covered over medium heat for 30 minutes , turning occasionally
6. baste with sauce
7. grill 15 minutes longer or until juices run clear
8. continue basting and turning during the last 15 minutes of cooking
9. serve with any extra sauce you set aside for dipping
demonstrations.review: This recipe *is* just delicious! I didn't have the chili sauce so I left it out and it was still very yummy. This is definitely my 'go to' BBQ sauce recipe from now on! Thanks for a great recipe - now to defrost the ribs!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolutely great  secret  simple mashed potatoes

this is a recipe shared with me by my southern gentleman friend. he made them for me one evening and i couldn't believe how great they were, when asked why they were soooo good, he remarked simply "it's just a can of evaporated milk, that's the only way to make them". so here it is. i'm so used to adding milk, butter, sour creme, yogurt, whatever i can find to make them creamy and tasty, that the simplicity of this is a nice change. it makes them wonderfully creamy and rich, the last time i made them i only used about 4t of butter (which is a lot less than i normally do) and i didn't miss it at all, it still tasted very rich, i also added 4 roasted garlic cloves, so you can play around with your preferred variations, while still enjoying the base creamy richness of this recipe. yet another example of how great something simple can be, (it took me a long time to learn that lol).

1. boil salted water , add potatoes
2. drain when tender
3. mash by hand or with an electric mixer depending on your preferred texture
4. add butter
5. add evaporated milk gradually as you mash , until you reach your desired consistency
6. the 4t of butter , and almost 1 can of milk was based on approximately 8 med sized potatoes
7. add any other ingredients , and salt and pepper to taste
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: So easy and what a wonderful way to use up the evaporated milk the I never know what to do with! We added some garlic and Parmesan. I know I'll be using this recipe over and over and over again. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
unleavened whole wheat bread

this is a whole wheat communion bread recipe that our kids used to love out of the freezer in the summer.this is also authentic to the early centuries, if you use olive oil in place of the veggie oil and goats milk, as the staple bread of the times.

1. mix honey and oil and warm slightly
2. mix egg yolk in warm milk
3. add honey and oil to flour and salt
4. then add egg and milk mixture gradually to the flour mixture
5. divide dough into three equal pieces
6. working with one piece at a time , roll out very thin to dinner plate size
7. score dough using a shot glass for the center , then a saucer and next a salad plate
8. then score twelve spokes out from the center circle
9. bake on cookie sheet for 10 minutes at 350 degrees
10. wrap while still warm
11. store in refrigerator or freezer
12. makes three flat loaves
target.review: Followed the directions exactly except for subbing the olive oil and goats milk.  Very easy recipe.  Nice soft texture and taste.  Next time will shape into more sandwich friendly pieces.  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell mexican pizza copycat recipe by todd wilbur

a friend gave me this recipe and it was an immediate hit with our family and friends. adapted from www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. cook the ground beef over medium heat until brown , then drain
2. return meat to pan and add the salt , onions , paprika , chili powder and water
3. let mixture simmer over medium heat for 10 minutes , stirring often
4. heat oil in frying pan over medium-high heat
5. when oil is hot , fry each tortilla for about 30-45 seconds per side and drain on paper towels
6. be sure to pop any bubbles that form when frying so that the tortilla lays flat in the oil
7. tortillas should become golden brown
8. heat refried beans
9. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
10. stack each pizza by first spreading 1 / 3 c beans on one tortilla
11. next add 1 / 3 c meat , then another tortilla
12. top the second tortilla with 2 t of salsa
13. divide the tomato , cheese , onions and olives evenly and top in that order
14. bake for 8-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe saved my life.  I was pregnant and living overseas where they *gasp* do not have Taco Bell!!!  Naturally since I couldn't get it anywhere in that or any of the surrounding countries - that's what I was craving most.  This recipe is so close to the real thing it exactly hit the spot and kept me from creating an international incident.  :)  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: This is almost exactly what spanish rice should taste like.    The only thing that is missing is the peppers.  Other than that it was perfect!!  Excellent, color, texture, smell, etc. Next time we'll sautee a little green pepper and stir in.  Served this with refried beans, pollo con crema and flour tortillas.  Garnished with a little fresh avocado and sour cream.  Looked just like a meal at your average mexican restaurant.  Thanks for posting this recipe.  We'll definately be making it again and again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super fast   easy tuna noodle casserole

yummy, nutritious and easy as can be.  a great week-night dinner.

1. fill a 4
2. 5 quart pan about two-thirds full of water , add 1 tsp salt per quart of water , and bring to a rapid boil
3. add noodles and boil until al dente
4. meanwhile , open a 7 oz can of tuna , drain it , and break tuna into flakes
5. mix with cream of mushroom soup and 1 / 2 cup milk
6. open 10 oz package of frozen peas and empty into colander
7. when noodles are done , drain them through peas in colander to thaw peas
8. combine everything
9. turn heat to medium-low and warm until hot
demonstrations.review: Excellent basic recipe.  I used 5oz tuna instead of the 7 because that's what was on hand, and whole wheat tri-color rotini for the pasta.  I also traded the peas for some mixed veg (peas, carrots, green beans and corn).  Oh, and I used cream of celery instead of mushroom.  Also added a thin layer of shredded cheddar and crumbled whole wheat crackers and then broiled in the oven for about 5 minutes or so to melt the cheese.  Came out delish!  I would say the recipe seems to serve more like 8 than six though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pollo a la crema

my favorite dish at our local mexican restaurant. chicken, mushrooms & onions in a spicy cream sauce, yum! very rich, but so delish! a real comfort food. i have been playing with the recipe for some time, just trying to get close to what they serve.  i think i'm finally as close as i can get.  5/30/08 update: if you can find mexican crema (dairy case at my grocer) it is thicker and works better than cream.  this is also good served over rice or noodles.  ***i discovered that my paprika had gotten old and lost strength, when i bought new, i also had to reduce the amount.  the recipe now reflects the reduced amount.

1. heat oil in large frying pan
2. saute chicken and onion until chicken is no longer pink & onions are translucent
3. add cream , mushrooms , paprika & chicken base
4. bring to a boil and simmer for 5-7 minutes or until chicken is tender
5. remove from heat and stir in sour cream
6. mixture will be somewhat thin , but should be a creamy texture like the consistency of a white sauce
7. serve hot with warmed flour tortillas and spanish rice
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe!!  We are definately adding it to our collection of family favorites and making it a regular part of our cooking routine.  The only thing I would change is to halve the amount of paprika and maybe use a thicker cream as we had trouble getting the sauce to thicken like it should.  (Although that may have been the fault of the cook not the recipe :P).  We served this essentially the same as CompulsiveCook did, except instead of the salad we served fresh flour tortillas and avocado slices.  Deeeee-lish!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried deviled eggs

let me tell you that the secret ingredient will add that special something that will get people asking what you did to make these so good! i'm not good at a bunch of ingredients so this is bare bones...you can fiddle with the spices if you like but try them this way first...you may never go back!

1. lay the eggs in the pan and add cold water to cover
2. set over high heat and bring just to the boil
3. remove from heat , cover the pan , and let sit exactly 17 minutes
4. when the time is up , transfer the eggs to the bowl of ice cubes and water
5. chill for 2 minutes while bringing the cooking water to the boil again
6. transfer the eggs to the boiling water , bring to a boil again , and let boil for 10 seconds remove eggs , and place back into the ice water
7. chillingthe eggs promptly after each step prevents that dark line from forming , and if time allows , leave the eggs in the ice water after the last step for 15-20 minutes
8. chilled eggs are easier to peel , as well
9. the peeled eggs will keep perfectly in the refrigerator , submerged in water in an uncovered container , for 2 to 3 days
10. leaving egg whites intact , gently remove yolks
11. in medium bowl , mash yolks with fork
12. stir in all remaining ingredients
13. spoon rounded tbs of the mixture into each egg white half , or pipe mixture with large star
14. cover and refrigerate
15. remove from refrigerator 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I followed the egg boiling instructions to the letter and ended up with unuseable eggs.  Once I re-boiled the eggs the recipe was divine.  The filling is absolutely delicious!!!  We served them at my sons 1st b-day party (jungle theme) as 'wild boar eyes' and they were a HUGE hit!!!

target.recipe_text:
red lentil   caramelised onion soup

from an aww magazine, thick and satisfying soup.

1. rinse the lentils and rice in cold water and drain
2. combine the 4 cups of stock and the water in large saucepan and bring to boil
3. add the lentils , rice and cumin and return to the boil
4. reduce heat and simmer uncovered , stirring occasionally until just tender , approx 15 minutes
5. meanwhile , melt butter in large fry pan , add onion and cook until softens , add sugar and vinegar and cook stirring until onion caramelises , remove from heat
6. stir the cayenne , coriander and parsley into the lentil mixture and bring to the boil
7. stir in the caramelised onion mixture and the extra cup of stock , cook , stirring , until heated through
target.review:
We really liked it but found the caramelised onions a bit strong tasting. Next time I will reduce the amount of vinegar and sugar. 
I took stardustannie's advice and cooked the rice longer which was necessary.
The lentil, rice, stock and cumin combination is simple but really wholesome tasting and the rice gives it texture.
The kids wouldn't eat it but who's surprised!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frazipan  danish almond cake

i got this recipe from odense website (they produce the almond and marzipan paste). it's super easy, it's very light, very almondy.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grate the almond paste
3. add butter and sugar , mix well
4. add eggs gradually , stir with whisk until fully incorporated
5. use a spatula to fold in the flour
6. pour cake batter into a 10-inch tart pan , bake for 30 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean
7. sprinkle powdered sugar or top with fruits
demonstrations.review: An excellent light and flavoursome almond cake. I had some trouble grating the marzipan as it is quite soft. I considered cooling it but instead I threw it into the food processor with the sugar and that did a good job. I was surprised at the amount of flour but it was fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry marzipan coffee cake

this is so yummy - and really easy. i found it in betty crocker's new cookbook, and avoided it for years because of the almond paste (to me, it's an exotic ingredient). i was really missing out!

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray bottom and sides of 9x9-inch square pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. cut firm margarine into 1 / 3 cup flour and 1 / 4 cup sugar using a pastry blender until crumbly
4. stir in almonds
5. set aside
6. beat 2 cups flour , 3 / 4 cup sugar , softened butter , milk , baking powder , vanilla , and egg with an electric mixer on low about 30 seconds until blended
7. beat on medium about 2 minutes , scraping down the bowl occasionally
8. spread half the batter in the pan
9. sprinkle with half each of the almond paste , raspberries , and the "streusel" that you set aside
10. repeat with the remaining batter , almond paste , raspberries and streusel
11. bake about 50 minutes
12. this is hard to test with a toothpick , because if you hit some almond paste you might think it isn't cooked yet--mine was perfect after 50 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Yum. The cake was fabulous. The only tricky bit was doing the two layers (they both need to be quite thin) and chopping up the marzipan (it was very soft).
Next time I think I will be more generous with the raspberries, maybe a cup and half.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango chicken

this is an old "canadian living" recipe that has become a family favourite. we all love it, and sometimes i increase the amount of curry paste, depending on who is coming for supper! i normally make it with a pot of rice and a salad. it's a nice "different" dish when you have company. everyone seems to love it!

1. cut chicken into three 4 inch pieces
2. seed , core and cut peppers into 1-inch pieces
3. slice onions into 1 1 / 2-inch lengths
4. peel and pit mangoes and cut into 2 / 3-inch pieces
5. whisk together stock , sugar , soy sauce , vinegar , cornstarch and curry paste
6. in wok or skillet heat half of the oil over high heat
7. stir fry chicken for 4 minutes or until no longer pink inside
8. transfer to plate
9. add remaining oil to wok
10. stir-fry peppers for 2 minutes
11. stir in ginger , cook for 30 seconds
12. add stock mixture and chicken , cook stirring for 2 minutes or until sauce is thickened and chicken is hot
13. stir in onions and mango
14. sprinkle with cashews
demonstrations.review:
This one was a winner for the family and will be a regular at our house in the future. I used thighs instead of breasts, added a slightly different mix of vegetables and cooked it a bit longer (being thighs).
This dish is quite sweet and gingery. For those who do not like too much sweetness or ginger, I would drop it down a bit.
I used a mild korma curry paste and it was perfect for our family (we like mild dishes).
Curiously the kids noted that the mango didn't match the dish although they enjoyed eating it. If you don't have any mango, don't let this stop you making this dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lamb and rice casserole

in spring, lamb is plentiful. this casserole recipe came from a greek cookbook and is reproduced here for you lamb-lovers.

1. trim fat from lamb shanks
2. in a heavy pot , brown well in butter
3. add onions
4. saute until soft
5. add 2-1 / 2 cups water , tomato paste , allspice , cinnamon , 1 tsp
6. salt and pepper
7. bring to a boil
8. cover and simmer 1-1 / 2 hours
9. when lamb is tender melt butter to bubbling in saucepan
10. saute rice , stirring constantly , untillightly browned and butter begins to foam between rice kernels
11. add remaining salt
12. set aside
13. remove lamb shanks from pan
14. measure broth and add water to measure 2-1 / 2 cups
15. return shanks to pan
16. bring to a boil
17. stir in sauteed rice and butter
18. simmer , covered , 30 minutes
19. allow to stand , covered , 10 minutes before serving
20. spoon yogurt over top of rice
demonstrations.review: I didn't use shanks but 4 pieces from the top of the shank (big chops with bones). I used half the butter and salt  and I had to add extra water to the rice (as I always seem to do). The dish was really good. It is a mildly flavoured wholesome dish. I used freshly ground allspice and pepper and the flavour just blended in. I had to stir so the rice didn't burn.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hungarian noodles and cabbage

a jewish recipe, originally from "foods from eastern europe add variety to purim menus" which i have adapted from one i found on www.jewish.com.  posted for the 2005 zaar world tour.

1. heat the oil in a large non-stick pan
2. add the sugar and heat gently until the sugar browns
3. add the onions , garlic and leeks
4. cook until they start to wilt
5. stir in the cabbage
6. saut , stirring frequently , until the cabbage has softened , about 20 minutes
7. season to taste with pepper , and transfer the cabbage mixture and pan juices to a large bowl and keep warm
8. cook the noodles according to the packet instructions , then drain
9. quickly toss the noodles with the cabbage mixture and the poppy seeds
10. serve immediately
11. it's certainly delicious with the sour cream
12. opt for a lower fat dish another night !
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I'm giving 5 stars to a noodle and cabbage recipe! It is a really good dish and I don't think we can eat goulash again without it. The only ingredient I omitted was the poppy seeds. I have used both sour cream and butter and prefer the butter. I did cook the cabbage longer as I like it slightly browned. Once I missed out the leeks and realised how important they are for the flavour. I do recommend seasoning with salt and pepper at the end.

target.recipe_text:
crispy salmon cakes with lemon  caper mayonnaise

this recipe was published in cooking light. i make it a bit different than it originally appeared, though (i don't use fat-free mayonnaise, saltines, etc. and also add some additional ingredients to suit my taste). if you would like to make the original version, just stick with the fat-free items and omit the last 4 items in the ingredient list (mayo through tabasco) and you will have the original recipe. prep time includes 20 minutes chilling time for the salmon cakes.

1. mayonnaise:
2. combine first 6 ingredients in a small bowl
3. cover and chill
4. salmon cakes:
5. heat 1 teaspoon oil in medium nonstick skillet over medium heat
6. add onion and celery and saute' 4 minutes , or until tender
7. combine onion mixture with 1 / 2 cup crackers , mustard , 1 / 4 teaspoon black pepper , salmon , egg , mayonnaise , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce and tabasco in a medium bowl
8. divide into 4 equal portions , shaping each into a 1 / 2-inch thick patty
9. coat each patty with 1 tablespoon crackers
10. cover and chill 20 minutes
11. heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot
12. add patties and cook 5 minutes on each side or until lightly browned
13. serve salmon cakes with flavored mayonnaise
target.review: This was outstanding. I halved the recipe and I, too, added the onions and celery to the mix without sauteeing (didn't read the directions thoroughly) but it still came out great. Plus the mayo is excellent.  This will be served frequently in our house.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican casserole   6 5 weight watcher points

this is a delicious mexican casserole recipe with only 6.5 weight watcher points per large serving!  yum!  (on the new, points plus system of weight watchers, this recipe is 9 points)

1. brown ground beef and chopped onions in large skillet
2. brown 10 to 12 minutes or until thoroughly cooked , stirring constantly
3. drain well and rinse with warm water to remove all fat
4. return beef / onions to skillet
5. add corn , black beans , tomatoes , chilies / jalapenos and taco seasoning mix
6. mix well
7. reduce heat
8. simmer 5 minutes
9. meanwhile spray 12x8-inch baking dish with nonstick cooking spray
10. cut each tortilla in half
11. place 8 halves in bottom of sprayed baking dish , overlapping slightly
12. spoon half of beef mixture evenly over tortillas
13. spoon sour cream over beef mixture
14. spread evenly
15. top with remaining 8 tortilla halves and remaining beef mixture
16. heat oven to 350f
17. bake at 350f for 25 minutes
18. remove from oven
19. sprinkle with cheese
20. cover
21. let stand 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
22. sprinkle with chopped cilantro and serve with fresh chopped lettuce , tomatoes , salsa , black olives , etc /
23. makes 6 large servings at 6
24. 5 weight watcher pts / each
demonstrations.review: I just finished off the half of this recipe that I froze.  It was really good.  I left out the cilantro since I don't care for it but otherwise followed the recipe.  I'll put this in regular rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french potatoes

this is a no-fuss microwave potato dish that really makes a hit. i serve it for special occasions, as well as any old time. it's from the book microwave cooking by beverley piper.

1. put the potato slices to soak in cold water
2. put the onion rings into a bowl
3. cover with plastic wrap , and pierce
4. microwave on high for 1 minute
5. grease a five cup casserole dish with a little of the butter
6. layer the drained potatoes and onions in the dish , starting and finishing with the potatoes
7. season each layer with salt and pepper
8. pour the milk over the potatoes and dot with the rest of the butter
9. sprinkle the top with paprika
10. cover with plastic wrap , and pierce
11. microwave on high for 13 minutes
12. rotate half-way through cooking time
13. allow to stand , covered , for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was great. Frankly I forget about my microwave and it was really nice to use it while I grilled chicken.  I did make a couple of changes after reading the reviews.  I used a bit of Montreal Steak Seasoning on the potato layers and grated some parmesan on the dish when it came out of the microwave.  Delicious.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
san  francisco pork chops

something a little different. the red pepper flakes give it just a little kick.

1. trim fat from pork chops
2. heat 1 t oil in skillet
3. brown chops on both sides
4. remove chops and saute garlic for one minute being careful not to burn
5. combine 2 t oil , sherry or broth , soy sauce , brown sugar , and pepper flakes
6. return chops to skillet
7. pour mixture over top
8. cover tightly
9. simmer over low heat till chops are tender and cooked through
10. add 1-2 t water , if needed , to keep sauce from cooking down to much or burning
11. turn chops once
12. remove chops to platter
13. stir in cornstarch
14. cook till thickened
15. pour over chops and serve with buttered egg noodles
demonstrations.review: I made the following changes, which I don't think are substantial enough to keep me from rating this fantastic, easy recipe:  I didn't have fresh garlic so I used a rosemary garlic seasoning that my sister gave me (yum!);  I reduced the soy to 3T; I reduced the cooking time to 25 minutes.  The chops are moist and the sauce is delicious.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beefy macaroni and cheese bake

one of the best quick family-style mac and cheese casseroles i have run across.

1. cook macaroni in large pot of boiling salted water until done
2. drain
3. meanwhile , heat oil in large frying pan and saut onion until softened
4. add ground beef and cook until browned
5. add tomatoes , thyme , oregano and salt to taste
6. cook about 5 minutes to blend flavors
7. in a small saucepan , whisk together flour and milk
8. cook over medium heat , stirring , until mixture comes to a boil
9. continue cooking 1 minute
10. remove from heat and stir in 3 / 4 cup cheese
11. stir until cheese is melted
12. stir into meat sauce
13. combine with macaroni
14. pour into prepared baking dish
15. top with remaining 1 / 4 cup cheese
16. bake at 375 until golden , about 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe exactly except I added garlic and a few red chili flakes to the meat as it browned.  I also made a traditional bechamel sauce and added cheddar and mozzarella cheese to it for the cheese sauce.  It was great, and even better the 2nd day.  We'll make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice and lentil casserole

this is a great meal that we eat here often in the winter time. with some dark bread and maybe a salad it is a really hearty meal, though we have been known to eat just this for dinner. the recipe is adapted from amy dacyczyn's "the complete tightwad gazette"

1. preheat the oven to 300 degrees
2. mix all ingredients except the cheese in a baking dish
3. cover with foil and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes
4. then remove the foil , add the cheese , and bake for an additional 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I haven't reviewed this.  It's outstanding.  I added dried mushrooms and used the liquid from reconstituting them for half of the stock.  I also added grated carrots. I also raised the oven temp to 375.   I make this at least twice a month.

target.recipe_text:
cheesy chicken quesadillas

these are yummy, quick, easy and cheesy :) you only need 4 ingredients to make these delicious pockets and they can be served as a main dish or as appetizers.

1. preheat oven to 425
2. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper and cook in lightly greased skillet until cooked through and juices evaporate , stirring often
3. add soup and salsa and heat through
4. spread about 1 / 3 cup of mixture on half of each tortilla , leaving a 1 / 2 inch edge
5. moisten edges with water , fold tortillas over and press edges to seal
6. place on baking sheets
7. bake 5 minutes
target.review: I made the filling, and then made sandwiches out of it. It is excellent, warm and cold, and makes a change from the normal chicken salad sandwiches in your lunch! I also added some shakes of chili powder to the mixture, as I didn't think it was spicy enough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy olive bread

over-the-top bread for your next bbq. you can make this right on your grill or in the oven.

1. mix all ingredients except extra olives
2. toast bread on grill or in oven
3. spread cheese mixture on top cover and grill cheese side up 5-7 minutes or until hot and melted
demonstrations.review: This was great!  I loved the hint of olive in this, and I think if you added a piece or two of pepperoni on top of the spread, it would be even better!  Will definitely add this to my "eat again" files!  Made for PAC Fall 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kolacky

we've been making this cookies on the slovak side of my family for generations and they are my favorite! they take a lot of work but taste much better than the kind you can get in the store and well worth it!
also, the filling can be made or bought (we find solo brand is best), but it is often hard to find the nut kind so i have included instructions for that as well.

1. mix softened cream cheese , softened butter , baking powder , and egg yolks with a pastry blender
2. mix in sour cream and sift in flour
3. add vanilla and knead the dough until your hands are clean
4. roll into 1 / 4 cup balls and refrigerate overnight
5. prepare the filling
6. beat the egg white until it is foamy
7. mix with crushed walnuts , melted butter , sugar , brown sugar and cinnamon
8. store in the refrigerator
9. preheat the oven to 350
10. roll dough flat , using flour to prevent sticking to surface and rolling pin
11. only remove what dough from the refrigerator that you are currently rolling
12. use a square-shaped cookie cutter to cut squares out of the dough
13. place a little filling in the middle of the square
14. then pinch 2 opposite corners together
15. fold this over and pinch again
16. bake 9-12 minutes on a non-stick pan , or until light brown
demonstrations.review: This recipe produced nice little filled cookies.  It wasn't precisely what I was looking for however.  Here in the Hinterlands, I know a kolacky to be a sweet bread roll with filling, and this recipe was far from that.  Made for Spring 2008 PAC.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ziti chicken casserole

i got this off an email list years ago. we really like this casserole.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in large pot , cook ziti as directed on package and drain well
3. combine all ingredients except parmesan cheese and spoon into a greased 2-quart casserole dish
4. top with parmesan cheese
5. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes or until hot and bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was both good and just okay.  I'm leaning more towards the okay side right now, but we'll see what it's like as leftovers.  I may change my mind.  It has a comfort food flavor and consistancy that I really liked, yet it was very bland too.  My boys didn't enjoy it at all, which doesn't put it into the dinner rotation.  We'll see how reheating treats it.  I may add some tabasco or some other hot sauce to spice it up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy buffalo chicken pasta

your chicken, your hotness and your bleu cheese dip all in one creamy concoction atop your favorite pasta.

1. cut chicken breast into bite-size pieces and sprinkle with paprika , garlic powder , salt and pepper
2. saute chicken until cooked
3. add hot sauce to your liking
4. remove chicken from skillet
5. saute vegetables
6. combine mayo , dressing and milk
7. add to skillet
8. add chicken and heat through
9. serve with pasta of your choice
demonstrations.review: I thought this was great, but the boys weren't as sold on the recipe.  It'll definitely have to be something I make when they're not around.  I think bleu cheese crumbles would add a lot to this recipe.  I took it to work for lunch, and it was as good cold as it was warm.  I think the buffalo wing flavor was a little more pronounced in the cold version, which isn't a bad thing as far as I'm concerned.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leighdear s buffalo chicken dip goes main course  low carb

as i have stated before i mostly gather, modify and review recipes instead of designing them and this is one of those recipes. the recipe came from leighdear at lowcarbfriends.com and is one i did not modify at all. it is a really good dish that my family loves and has been getting great reviews. thanks for the great recipe leigh!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. season chicken with salt and pepper
3. saut in oil til browned
4. place in greased 13x9 baking dish
5. beat the cream cheese with a hand mixer until very smooth , then beat in ranch dressing and hot sauce
6. stir in shredded cheese
7. spread over chicken in baking dish
8. bake at 350f for approximately 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: While we love the buffalo chicken dip, for some reason, none of us were thrilled about this.  The plates were cleaned, but no one asked to have this added to the rotation.  I was surprised, as the boys love all things buffalo, but...sorry Soozie!  Made for PAC Fall 2007.

target.recipe_text:
a unique and delicious braided bread

i got this from my relative a few years ago and now everyone loves it!

1. combine the yeast , honey , milk , and butter , stir , and leave for 15 mintues to dissolve
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour and salt
3. make a well in the center and add the yeast mixture and egg
4. with a wooden spoon , stir from the center , incorporating flour with each turn , to obtain a rough dough
5. transfer to a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic
6. place in a clean bowl , cover , and leave to rise in a warm place until doubled in volume , about 1 1 / 2 hours
7. grease a baking sheet
8. punch down the dough and divide into three equal pieces
9. roll to shape each piece into a long thin strip
10. begin braiding from the center strip , tucking in the ends
11. cover loosely and leave to rise in a warm place for 30 minutes
12. preheat the oven to 375f
13. place the bread in a cool place while oven heaats
14. brush with the glaze and bake until golden , 40 to 45 minutes
15. set on a rack to cool completely
target.review: This is a delicious bread! I expected a same old same old, but it was tasty and easy. I wish that I hadn't made the three strands so thin and long, the finished pieces weren't very big. I didn't glaze it either, but the crust was almost flaky! Thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super nutty cookies  wheat free lactose free

my mother-in-law is allergic to everything. this cookie is an adapted skippy peanut butter recipe. it is wheat-free, white sugar free, and dairy free.... and most important super soft and very yummy.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine all ingredient in a medium sized bowl , using a wooden spoon or heavy duty mixer
3. after throughly mixed add any additional optional ingredients--my favorites: cracked nuts , chocolate chips , or carob chips
4. roll into very small balls and place 2 inches apart on cookie sheet
5. bake 9 minutes in the oven or until puffed and golden
6. cookies will be very soft until cooled completely
demonstrations.review: These were too sugary for our tastes. In small doses, they are good, like candy, but the 24 cookies were too big. If I make them again, I would make them smaller, and add the nuts to give them more texture. I had to "drop"them, they were too runny to roll into balls.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut garlic shrimp

if you love caribbean food, then this is for you.  its good for you, and definately full of flavor!  i hope you like it as much as i do!

1. precook the shrimp in a skillet over medium heat until barely pink
2. let cool and peel , set aside for later
3. in a large skillet , mix the olive oil and butter and heat until the butter has melted
4. stir in the garlic , scallions , and ginger and make sure everything is coated evenly
5. saut over medium-low heat until the garlic and scallions are soft but not brown
6. stir in the rum , and lime juice
7. cook for one minute , and then add the tabasco sauce , garlic pepper , and coconut milk , stirring well
8. reduce heat and cook for two minutes
9. meanwhile combine the cornstarch with the 2 tablespoons of water and mix to make a paste
10. when you are done combine the cornstarch mixture to the sauce and stir well
11. add the shrimp and cook for a minute or two until the sauce slightly thickens
12. serve right away over white rice , and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to make, although I would recommend getting all the ingredients together before you start. The taste was fine, but I thought it could use more lime. I guess Caribbean food is just not my thing. Thanks for the experience though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
palestinian lentils and rice with crispy onions

this is so delicious and so simple. it's a little exotic, very flavorful, and will make your kitchen smell wonderful as it cooks - and my preference is to add extra cumin! i've never made it without first soaking the rice and lentils, but the dish could surely be adapted to no-soaking if you're looking to cut some of the prep time.

1. soak lentils in water for 3 hours
2. drain
3. soak rice in water for 1 / 2 hour
4. drain
5. saute onions in a large skillet for about 15 minutes , or until very brown and crisp
6. remove onions to a plate lined with paper towels to drain
7. turn heat to medium-high and add lentils and rice to skillet
8. saute quickly in the browned-onion-flavored oil , adding cumin , salt and pepper
9. add 3 cups of water and bring to a boil
10. cover very tightly and then cook on very low heat for about 20 to 25 minutes
11. to serve , fluff up rice and lentils and top with the crispy browned onions
demonstrations.review: This sure was tasty. I don't have a very big skillet, so by the time all the onions were browned, most of them were burnt. So next time I will cook them in 2 batches at least. Also, I used whole pepper corns, about a tsp of them. The taste was great, but next time I will grind them so that the heat is more even. My carnivore DH even liked this, and my 1 year old loved it! The rice and lentils cooked up mushy enough for him, he couldn't get enough. I did everyhting up to the browning the rice and lentils stage as directed, and then poured it all in to my rice cooker with the 3 cups of water. Very easy and tasty. I think I might make it again tomorow for my Vegan sister. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken agrodolce  an italian sweet and sour chicken

this is such a unique italian chicken dish. chicken breasts are briefly sauteed, then simmered in a sauce of honey, balsamic vinegar, wine, orange and lemon juice. toss in a few toasted pignoli, and you've got a quick and delicious dinner with risotto or cappellini.

1. in a large plastic bag , combine flour and chicken breasts , toss to coat
2. in a large skillet , saute floured chicken breasts in olive oil with the whole garlic , bay leaves and allspice berries until chicken is browned
3. remove chicken to a plate
4. to the skillet , add honey , vinegar and wine
5. cook to reduce slightly , about 10 minutes on medium-high heat
6. return chicken to skillet , add orange and lemon juices , salt and pepper , and cook about another 20 minutes or until chicken is done and sauce is reduced slightly
7. remove garlic , bay leaves and allspice berries from sauce
8. add pignoli and heat through , another 5 minutes or so
9. delicious with angel hair pasta or a nice risotto
demonstrations.review: The sauce on this is amazing. I had no honey on hand, so I used corn syrop, which tasted fine. DH says the chicken is tender, like me, just how he likes it! Easy to make, and definately going to be a staple around here, and not just for company!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex meatloaf

this is my origional recipe. it is so good, you'll be lucky if there is any left over for sandwiches! my grandma always requested this for get togethers. after she passed away, i decided to write a cookbook in her honor. this is in there. you can get more info at www.countryconfections.net

1. preheat oven to 375
2. in a small bowl mix ketchup , cumin , and chilli powder
3. set aside
4. next , mix beef , salt , oats , salsa , and eggs
5. place mixture in a large glass baking dish
6. form into a loaf
7. spread ketchup mixture on top of meatloaf
8. bake on middle rack for 45 minutes
9. remove from oven and place pepper rings on top
10. return to oven and cook for 15 minutes more
11. let rest for 5 minutes
12. makes great sandwiches
demonstrations.review: I tried this recipe when looking for a meat loaf that didn't taste like meat. DH and I loved it! I made the salsa myself with roma tomatoes, green peppers and green onions, otherwise I followed the recipe exactly. It was great hot, but the left overs were a bit salty. I will cut back the salt next time.

target.recipe_text:
chicken breast with tomato olive sauce

i got a calendar for 2007 with a recipe and food picture on each month.  this is the first one that caught my eye!

1. mix basil , garlic powder , thyme and pepper and rub into both sides of chicken
2. cover and let stand for 30 minutes
3. melt 2 tbs
4. butter and olive oil in a heavy skillet over high heat
5. add chicken and saute until golden brown , about 5 minutes per side
6. transfer to plate
7. melt 3 tbs
8. butter in heavy skillet over medium-high heat
9. add onion and saute until softened
10. add garlic and tomatoes and cook 2 minutes
11. add olives and cook 5 minutes more , stirring frequently
12. season with salt and pepper to taste and serve over chicken breasts
target.review: Delish! Served with a side of whole wheat pasta tossed in olive oil and parmesan. I usually just do black olives, but the green were a nice addition. My bf doesn't even like green olives, but he sure did gobble them up. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best asparagus lemon pasta

i came across this at epicurious and fell in love, and its been elsewhere. years of looking for the lemon pasta i remembered as a child, and finally found it. tweaked it a little to my own taste, replacing parsley with fresh basil and using linguine.  if you don't have  tender asparagus, the europes best frozen ones are far better than woody fresh ones.  do not substitute lighter creams, it just does not work that well.

1. cut the asparagus into 1 / 2 inch slices on the diagonal , or just into 3 pieces
2. in a steamer set over boiling water steam asparagus , covered , until crisp-tender , about 3 minutes
3. drain and rinse under cold water to stop cooking
4. set aside
5. in a 6-quart kettle bring 5 quarts salted water to a boil for pasta
6. in a deep 12-inch skillet heat butter and cream over moderately low heat until butter is melted and stir in zest , lemon juice , and salt
7. remove skillet from heat and keep sauce warm , covered
8. add pasta to boiling water and boil , stirring occasionally , until al dente
9. ladle 1 / 4 cup pasta water into sauce and drain pasta in colander
10. immediately add pasta and asparagus to sauce and cook over moderate heat , tossing , 1 minute , or until heated through
11. add basil and salt and pepper to taste and toss well
12. sprinkle pasta with a little parmesan and serve more parmesan on the side
demonstrations.review: I'm have mixed feelings about this dish. Maybe I did something wrong, however I added everything you said. Maybe my palate is used to more intense flavors. I too sauted the asparagus in the butter instead of steaming, used whole wheat linguine, went back to the parsley, and even added 14 oz of shrimp. My bf liked it so much he had seconds.  I on the other hand needed and extra squirt of lemon, salt, and fresh cracked pepper. It was good, but not goooood. Let's just say this is not something I myself would crave. But thank you for helping me broaden my horizons.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old bay steak fries

mmmm..potatoes!  these are baked in the oven with some old bay and they're a change of pace.  serve with steaks, burgers, whatever.  yum!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. coat baking sheet with cooking spray
3. in a large bowl , combine potato wedges with oil , seasoning , and salt
4. toss to coat well
5. spread potatoes in a single layer on the baking sheet
6. bake without turning until tender and browned , about 40-45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I did regretfully cut back on the Old Bay myself. I like my food spicy and should have stuck to the recipe. My bf thought they were perfect, as he has a lower heat tolerance than I. Next time no cutting back on the Old Bay.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grapefruit pie

i saw this on the food network,it was from a festival in fl. i haven't made it but it looks great and all the judges raved about it.

1. in medium saucepan , combine sugar and cornstarch , add water and cook over medium heat until thick and clear
2. add strawberry gelatin and stir to dissolve
3. let cool , and add grapefruit sections
4. pour mixture into baked pie shell and chill until firm , about 2 hours
5. top with whipped cream and serve
demonstrations.review: Very refreshing! After reading the other reviews I decided not to include the 1 cup sugar and used regular jello but not by choice. I've been cutting sugar from my diet and it turns out I have zero granulated sugar in my apt anyway. Regardless, my BF and I were still happy with the result and the added sweetness from the cool whip really helped. I don't even wanna know how sweet it should really be. (Used reduced fat cool whip, reduced fat graham cracker crust, and no added sugar)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dave s perfect pasta

simply delicious! very quick and easy to make! everyone will think you cooked for hours, don't tip them off.

1. add olive oil to large skillet , warm using medium heat
2. saute garlic and crushed red pepper together about 5 minutes until garlic is golden
3. add tomatoes , pepper , and salt , continue to cook until tomatoes are tender 10-15 minutes
4. add fresh basil cook 5 additional minutes
5. pasta should be cooked"al dente" and well drained
6. combine all ingredients and serve hot topped with 1 / 2 oz of imported shredded parmesan cheese
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Loved the flavor, bf did too. I did add the bell peppers as suggested. Wish I had fresh basil, only dried on hand. I think I'll cut back a little on the olive oil next time around, cuz i definately will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
african tilapia

this marinated tilapia is grilled hot while basted in the marinade to give it lots of extra flavor. it's a favorite around my room mates!

1. combine all ingredients except for the tilapia
2. mix well until the salt is disolved
3. place tilapia in a glass dish and cover with marinade
4. turn to coat and set aside for 20 minutes
5. preheat grill
6. pour marinade into a saucepan and bring to a boil
7. allow to cool
8. grill tilapia fillets of a medium high heat for about 4 to 5 minutes per side or until the fish flakes easily and has an even appearance all the way through
9. serve by pouring a small amount of the sauce over the tilapia fillets
demonstrations.review: Tilapia is so boring and bland, but this recipe gives this fish so much oomph. It was delish!! My bf says it tasted better than most we've eaten at restaurants. He says he looks forward to eating this every friday. I wouldn't mind it either. The only thing I changed was using olive oil, left out the lemon b/c I didn't have any on hand, and halved the recipe to make for 2. Also you didn't state what kind of vinegar so i used rice vinegar. I think I will use less oil next time too. Thank you for all that flavor!

target.recipe_text:
chicken and rice stew gone wild

another easy crock pot meal!

1. place mushrooms , carrots , leeks and rices in bottom of crock pot
2. place chicken on veggies and rices
3. top with seasonings and pour broth over all
4. cover and cook on low 7-8 hours or on high 3 1 / 2-4 hours
5. stir in cream of mushroom soup at end of cooking
target.review: I used an onion instead of the leeks, and added a finely chopped stalk of celery. I didn't pay attention to the directions and added the mushroom soup with the rest of the ingredients - still tasted great. Even better the next day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry peach pudding cake

little is better than a hot fruit dessert covered in a scoop of slowly melting vanilla ice cream and this is no exception

1. spread blueberries and drained peaches in the bottom of a 9-inch square pan or an 11x7-inch rectangular baking pan
2. sprinkle with the lemon juice
3. heat oven to 350
4. in another bowl , blend flour , baking powder and soda , salt , and 1 cup sugar
5. in a separate bowl , whisk together the milk , egg , melted butter , and vanilla
6. combine the dry ingredients with egg mixture just until blended
7. spoon over the fruit layer and gently spread
8. combine the 3 / 4 cup sugar with cornstarch
9. spread evenly over batter
10. carefully pour the boiling water over all
11. bake for 40 to 50 minutes
12. spoon into dessert dishes and top with ice cream or whipped topping
demonstrations.review: The kids say full stars! I used frozen saskatoon berries instead of the blueberries, and replaced half of the vanilla extract with almond extract to enhance the flavour of the saskatoons. I also reduced the sugar in the cake batter to 3/4 cup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit preserve bars

nan

1. cream the butter and the brown sugar together
2. add the flour and the baking soda
3. mix well
4. blend in extract
5. stir in oats
6. spread mixture in bottom of greased 13x9 inch pan
7. spread with preserves to within 1 / 2 inch of outer edge of pan
8. sprinkle with almonds
9. bake at 375 degrees for 22 to 25 minutes
10. cool and cut into bars
11. preheat oven to 350 degrees
12. grease 13x9 inch pan
demonstrations.review: Very popular in our house. A great way to use up last year's jam when the new batches look more enticing for toast. I used huckleberry jam. I reserved some of the crust to put on the top in place of the almonds because nuts are banned at our school.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken shwarma   chawarma lahme

as part of a mezze, or as the main ingredient in a sandwich, or pita wrap, this is a flavorful, homey recipe.  this recipe is translated from cuisine du liban by pomme larmoyer.

1. cut the chicken breasts , or just white chicken meat , into long , slim strips , then into lengths that are about an inch long
2. put them into a bowl or other container , and allow them to marinate in the lemon juice , olive oil , crushed and diced garlic , yoghurt , tomato paste , salt , pepper and spices
3. allow 24 hours for the flavors to develop
4. the following day , remove and drain the chicken pieces from the marinade , and saute them for 10 minutes
5. serve hot as a mezze or for sandwiches along with thinly sliced onions , deseeded tomato , and any other crudites , or pickled crudites
demonstrations.review: I substituted buttermilk for the yogourt, ketchup for the tomato paste and oregano for the coriander because that's what was on hand. Very tasty both freshly grilled and cold in a sandwich the next day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheddar drop biscuits

this was in the dallas morning news.  the original source is diabetes comfort food.  
exchanges:  1 starch, 1 fat

1. preheat oven to 400f coat a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray
2. combine flour , baking powder and salt
3. cut in butter to make coarse crumbs
4. add cheese and chives
5. stir in milk to make a soft , sticky dough
6. use a 1 / 4 cup measure to drop 15 portions onto the prepared baking sheet
7. sprinkle with chives
8. bake on middle rack for 18 to 20 minutes , or until edges are golden
9. transfer biscuits to a rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Great recipe. I use medium or old cheddar and add 1/2 teaspoon garlic powder. I use a 1 1/2 tablespoon mini ice cream scoop to get about 25 little biscuits. This recipe is from Johanna Burkhard and is also in her 400 Best Comfort Food Recipes (my all time cookbook!).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
family favorite beef stew

really easy and inexpensive dinner that the entire family enjoys. even my picky four year old! this recipe is a mixture of many other recipes i have tried in the past. i have also used red cabbage at the end, and found it tasty for the adults, the children weren't terribly impressed with that addition though. edit*** i have used this recently after trying new experiments and this recipe needs something i think. something savory, maybe a couple anchovies? i do not know, but please experiment! i am also cutting the v8 to 2 cups as the 3 cups in the slow cooker seems to be too watery.

1. place vegetables in bottom of crock pot
2. toss beef with flour , shake off excess
3. saut beef in hot oil , optional step but recommended
