4. place beef on top of vegetables mix juice , onion soup mix , garlic powder and worcestershire sauce
5. pour on top of mixture
6. cover and cook on high 20-30 minutes
7. finish cooking on low for 8 hours
8. mix in salt and pepper to taste and serve
demonstrations.review: Even our picky DD's ate this all up! I lightly dusted the pieces of stew meat with instant (Wondra) flour, but placed them directly in the crockpot without browning. I only added about 2 teaspoons of worcestershire sauce since it's not my favourite. This is a great beef stew that I will make again.

target.recipe_text:
speedy salsa chicken quesadillas

from kraft foods.

1. combine salsa , dressing and chili powder
2. spread evenly onto bottom halves of tortillas
3. top with chicken and cheese
4. fold tortillas in half to enclose filling
5. cook in skillet sprayed with cooking spray on medium heat 4 to 5 minutes on each side or until both sides are golden brown and cheese is melted
6. cut each quesadilla into 3 wedges to serve
7. makes 4 servings , 6 wedges each
target.review: Very easy and delicious!!!! I did use the Miracle Whip, and I think that's important for the nice zip of the salsa!!! I didn't have a blend, so I just used cheddar cheese. I also sprinkled some diced jalapenos on my hubby's cuz he likes the heat!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh strawberry pie

this is my favorite summertime pie!

1. arrange strawberries nicely in pie crust
2. mix cornstarch and sugar in pan
3. add water
4. boil til clear
5. add jell-o
6. pour over strawberries
7. chill
8. serve with cool whip !
demonstrations.review: My cooking-challenged hubby made this cuz he lost a bet to another coach in Little League! I wasn't allowed to help (part of the rules of the bet), so I'm not sure he followed the directions correctly, cuz it didn't gel very well. I'm not gonna blame the recipe, cuz it tasted delicious!! Well, the little bits that I could sneak off the cover, cuz we had to give it away! We used a prepared graham cracker crust, cuz a homemade one woulda pushed DH over the edge!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy empanadas

these are more sweet than spicy and there are a few surprise ingredients that really make these little beef bites quite delicious!  my husband is a "dipper" and created the tomato-based sauce that perfectly complements these non-traditional empanadas.  the recipe makes 24 bite-sized appetizers, or you can make them twice as big and eat them for dinner. :)

1. for the sauce:
2. combine all ingredients and whisk till smooth
3. for the empanadas:
4. take the pastry sheets out of the freezer 40 minutes before your empanadas will be ready to be filled
5. preheat the oven to 400 degrees
6. peel the potatoes and dice them fairly small
7. cover them with water and simmer for 10-15 minutes , or till tender
8. meanwhile , mince the onion and place in a large bowl with the beef , all the sugar and spices , and the milk
9. knead with your hands until the mixture is very soft
10. cook the meat mixture in a skillet over medium heat until the beef is browned
11. drain the potatoes and mix them in with the meat
12. drain any excess fat
13. cut the pastry into 24 equal rectangles and divide the mixture between them
14. divide the cream cheese into 24 portions as well and squish it on top of the meat so it evenly covers
15. fold the pastry over and seal the edges by folding or pinching
16. place on baking sheet and bake for 13-15 minutes , or until puffy and golden brown
17. remove from oven , place on serving plate , and dip in the sauce if you desire !
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed the heat of this, and my DH really enjoyed the dipping sauce. The piece of cream cheese bothered some in the family. Maybe if it was blended in with the meat mixture it would have worked better. Thanks for creating this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blood orange lemonade

one of our favourite summertime drinks.

1. in a pitcher , blend water and sugar until the sugar dissolves
2. add orange blossom water , blood orange juice and lemon juice
3. stir
4. add what remains of one lemon and one blood orange
5. let chill for 30 minutes
6. serve over ice
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I don't have orange blossom water, but it was great without it! I used two Meyer's lemons from my yard and 2 blood oranges. I just added sugar as I saw fit, way less than the 1 cup, cuz my lemons are very sweet. My boys loved it! And strange thing...it looked PINK!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
terrific tonkatsu  japanese pork cutlet chops tenderloin

tonkatsu is tasty, quick and easy to prepare, and fiercely popular... think of this as the japanese chicken nugget, only tastier!  i like mine dipped in the delicious sauce and served over a simple white rice with crisp apple chunks folded in.  a green alongside accompanies well for a full meal.

1. combine applesauce , ketchup , worcestershire , mustard , and vinegar in medium saucepan and bring to a boil , stirring constantly
2. remove from heat and allow to cool
3. bread pork: dredge in flour , shake excess , dip in egg , drain excess , press into panko
4. add 3 t
5. of oil to large skillet over medium heat
6. cook pork for ~5 minutes each side , until golden brown
7. add reserved oil to pan prior to flipping pork
8. remove golden brown and delicious chops from pan and allow to rest for 3 minutes before cutting into strips ~1-1 1 / 4 inches wide
9. serve immediately with sauce
demonstrations.review: The review is based solely on the sauce recipe. This was very good, but I doctored it up a little, trying to get to a taste I had in my mind. Added a little brown sugar, and some apple cider vinegar. Hubby loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry feta pinwheels

from ocean spray and very good!

1. combine all ingredients except tortillas , mix well
2. divide and spread mixture evenly among tortillas
3. roll up tightly , wrap in plastic and refrigerate at least one hour
4. to serve cut into 12 slices
5. a nice variation is to add thin slices of ham on top of the spread before rolling
demonstrations.review: I was leery about the amount of feta, but it was perfect. I whirled mine a bit in a food processor before spreading. The tart/saltiness of the feta was perfectly offset by the sweetness of the cranberries!

target.recipe_text:
skillet parmesan chicken

this is real comfort food. a family favorite. if you can, buy the fresh mozzarella. you won't believe the difference and it's worth it. the texture isn't rubbery like the typical mozzarella. i got it from watching an emeril show on the food network.

1. pound the chicken breasts between two slices of plastic wrap until about 1 / 4" thick
2. season with salt and pepper
3. dredge chicken in flour and shake off excess
4. dip in egg / milk mixture , then in breadcrumb / parmesan mixture
5. heat the butter and olive oil in a large deep skillet
6. brown the chicken breasts over medium heat until golden on each side
7. remove to a plate and keep warm
8. add the marinara sauce to the skillet
9. heat to boiling and simmer 10 minutes
10. add the chicken breasts to the sauce and sprinkle parmesan over them
11. place a slice of mozzarella on each piece of chicken
12. cover and simmer about 8- 10 minutes or until the cheese has melted and the chicken is tender
13. serve with your favorite pasta- we like linguine
target.review: OH my GOSH!! My family of 7 absolutely adored this recipe!! Everyone cleaned their plates after seconds EACH!! My son even claimed that if he had to eat it every night for the rest of his life he would be happy. As usual I had to double the recipe to accomodate the family. Since I had so much chicken to cook I used an electric skillet and tripled the butter and olive oil. I also put the chicken in the oven while waiting for the marinara sauce to warm up. I used Prego marinara sauce and served over angel hair pasta, garlic bread sticks, and green beans. This is a KEEPER!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
daisy mae s fried apples

each fall, i use these with pork chops, pork roast - whatever.  they are wonderful, and so easy to make, from my grandma daisy's kitchen.  

1. melt butter in large skillet over medium heat
2. add apples
3. sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
4. stir until apples are blended with sugar / cinnamon
5. cover and cook for approx 15-20 minutes , frequently stirring gently
6. serve them warm , right on the pork chop or pork roast
7. they also double for a dessert dish served over vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: we have tons of frozen apples to eat up.  i used part of them to make this for my 7 year old on her waffles (she does not like syrup).  She ADORED them and i now know how i will be cooking the rest of the frozen ones!!!!  thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato mushroom chowder

big taste in this hearty soup.

1. saute onion in butter
2. add flour and seasonings
3. slowly add water , stirring
4. bring to a boil , cook 1 minute
5. add remaining ingredients , reduce heat and simmer for 30 minutes
6. add cream and cheese
7. heat through
demonstrations.review: I am making this for the third time and I noticed that I never reviewed it.  My family absolutely adores this soup and 3 out of 5 of the kids aren't big soup eaters but they sure love this!!  I have even served this to my in-laws who are picky eaters and they have asked for the recipe!!!  Thanks for sharing this keeper!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jello smoothie

a low-fat low cal smoothie/milkshake option...use orange jello for a dreamsicle flavor or lime for key lime pie

1. in blender , mix boiling water and jello mi until dissolved
2. combine cold water with ice
3. add with cool whip to mixture in blender until smooth
4. serve immediately
5. makes 2 large or 4 small servings
demonstrations.review: Recently diagnosed with diabetes I was needing a "sweet" this evening.  I truly see this as a very regular treat in my house!  All 4 kids LOVED this and my 16 year old added a 1/2 banana blended to hers.  YUMMY!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruzicka chicken

this is a great chicken recipe that i found on one of the bed&breakfast inns sites. we love it and so easy to make

1. mix cream cheese and onions
2. divide into 8 balls
3. salt and pepper chicken and place cheese-onion ball in center of each piece
4. wrap each piece of chicken in 2 strips of bacon , so that cheese is completely sealed inside
5. bake at 350 degrees for 30-50 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: This was a winner in our house!  I had five chicken breasts and halved them...2 pieces of bacon each.  My husband rarely says something is "great" because he is so not picky and doesn't really care what he eats.  This chicken recipe actually made him ask what it was!!   I served with green bean casserole and hot dinner rolls.  The five kids loved it as well...even the seven year old who isn't into the green onions so much!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
top secret recipes waffle house waffles by todd wilbur

try the recipe that has sold millions of waffles. if you prefer pecan waffles, add 1/4 cup chopped pecans before pouring the batter onto the waffle iron

recipe created by todd wilbur www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. combine flour , salt and baking soda in a medium bowl and stir to combine
2. lightly beat the egg in another medium bowl and combine with sugar , butter , and shortening , mixing well until smooth
3. add the half & half , milk , buttermilk and vanilla and mix well
4. add the dry flour mixture to the wet mixture while beating and mix until smooth
5. if you can , cover and chill overnight , though the batter can be used right away
6. rub a light coating of vegetable oil on a waffle iron , and preheat it
7. leave the batter out of the refrigerator to warm up a bit as your waffle iron is preheating
8. spoon 1 / 3 to 1 / 2 cup of batter into the waffle iron and cook for 3 to 4 minutes or until the waffles are light brown
demonstrations.review: Wow!! I rec'd a professional waffle maker for Christmas and used this recipe tonight!  My kids LOVED it and it will be our new waffle recipe from now on!!  I served this with pats of butter and cinammon syrup #37023!  YUMMMMMY!

target.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
target.review:
I can't believe I haven't written a review. This is my standard chocolate cake. I don't want to go back to boxed. Turns out rich and moist.

It just takes a couple of minutes more than making a boxed cake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barilla no boil lasagna

this is the best lasagna ever!! the noodles are so nice and thin and there is no preboiling!! i will never purchase any other lasagna other than barilla. i've been making this now for 3 years and everyone agrees--the recipe makes the very best! the instructions are right on the back of the lasagna box. i usually make multiple batches and freeze them. its a great housewarming or "new baby" meal for a friend!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. in bowl , combine beaten eggs , ricotta cheese and two cups of the mozzarella cheese and parmesan
3. if you choose not to use the parmesan , just add more mozzarella
4. set aside
5. in a 13x9x3 pan , spread 1 cup of sauce on bottom of pan
6. layer in the order , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , then 1 / 3 part of the ricotta cheese mixture , half the browned meat , 1 cup mozzarella cheese , and 1 cup of spaghetti sauce
7. next layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , 1 / 3 part of the ricotta cheese mixture , and 1 1 / 2 cups sauce
8. next layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , remaining ricotta mixture and remained meat , 1 cup of sauce
9. for top layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , remaining sauce , and remaining 1 cup mozzarella
10. bake covered with foil for 50-60 minutes
11. uncover and continue cooking until all the cheese is melted on the top
12. let stand 15 minutes before serving
13. if you are using a 13x9x2 pan---just make 3 layers to avoid boiling over
demonstrations.review:
This is our standard, quick lasagna. I love the recipe. I can't count the number of times people have asked for the recipe and I tell them to buy a box of barilla lasagna noodles and follow the directions. I've tried other recipes from time to time but finally decided: why bother! This one works great. It freezes nicely too, so it's a good dish to take to a new mother or someone else needing a lasagna. This amount of lasagna fills a 9x13 pan and an 8x8 pan, so I make the 9x13 and we eat that one night and then the leftovers a couple of nights later. The 8x8 either goes to someone or goes in the freezer. 
When I make Jo Mama's World Famous Spaghetti Sauce (#22782) I save half for this lasagna.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef roast

very tender, very juicy. makes lots of gravy great over mashed potatoes simple to make. melts in your mouth everyone who's tried this recipe agrees you won't find an easier or better tasting beef roast recipe anywhere.

1. mix gravy , mushrooms , soup mix and italian dressing
2. pour over beef roast
3. bake , covered , for 1 hour 15 minutes per pound at 300f
4. add carrots and / or potatoes during last hour , if desired
5. cooking time is approximate , depending upon how big your roast is
demonstrations.review: This recipe was fine. The meat was very tender. The mushrooms were a very nice addition too. I left out the onion soup mix (shook a little bit of dried onions in instead) and it was plenty salty. I thickened the gravy a little with a flour water paste. I used a three pound roast and would estimate 8 to 10 servings. I will go back to my regular roast recipe (#134203), since this was like what you would get at an American-style restaurant, and I prefer a more homemade taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry sour cream pie

nan

1. mix sugar and flour together in bowl
2. beat in sour cream , egg , vanilla and salt together until smooth
3. fold in blueberries
4. pour into pie crust , and bake at 400f for 25 minutes
5. meanwhile , combine topping ingredients
6. remove pie from oven after the 25 minutes , and sprinkle on topping
7. return pie to oven and bake 10 minutes more
8. chill before serving
demonstrations.review: Great pie! Very unusual--similar to a pecan pie with custard underneath and blueberries on top. This is a family of pie lovers, and it passed our exacting standards! I used light sour cream, so I increased the flour to 3 tablespoons. It also took longer to bake than listed, more like 45 or 50 minutes, probably due to the use of frozen blueberries. Great topping!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mole  mo lay  sauce

this is my version of mole sauce. it can hold its own against the mole at our great local mexican restaurant. i usually double this recipe, but that's just me. the original recipe calls for 5 tbsp(yes, 5)of chili powder. i cut it in half, but you can take it from there. and don't judge the taste until you add the chocolate. it's just not done until you finish this step! serve it over good chicken, over enchiladas,or burritos. i think it is good with lots of things. i served it the other night over leftovers from canarygirl's chicken verde, and it was superb!(her recipe stands on its own as a great dish, i just enhanced my leftovers! thanks, canarygirl!)

1. heat oil in a large saucepan over med
2. low heat
3. add onion , garlic , oregano , cumin and cinnamon
4. cover and cook until onion is almost tender , stirring occasionally , about 10 minutes
5. mix in chili powder and flour , stir for 3 minutes
6. gradually whisk in chicken broth
7. increase heat to med
8. high
9. boil until reduced , about 35 minutes , stirring occasionally
10. remove from heat
11. whisk in chocolate
12. season with salt and pepper , if desired
demonstrations.review: Excellent. It's not absolutely perfect, but the taste is right. I used cocoa (almost 2 Tb) and put it through the blender when it was done cooking. I should have cooked it down further than I did, and used less salt, but it is very good and I think I will cook some chicken in the leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken curry in a hurry

watch out or you might get pulled over for a speeding ticket in the kitchen! ready in 20 minutes. :)

1. mix together flour , salt and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
2. add chicken in small batches , shaking to coat
3. heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken and cook until lightly browned
5. then add curry powder and toss to coat
6. remove from pan
7. add onion and garlic to pan , adding a little more oil if necessary , and cook for 2 minutes , then add broth , raisins , and tomato paste
8. return chicken to pan and simmer uncovered for 8 minutes or until chicken is cooked through and sauce has thickened
9. garnish with cilantro and a dollop of yogurt
10. serve with quick cooking minute rice , if desired
demonstrations.review: Very nice. I used garam masala instead of curry powder. Right amount of spiciness, and all. I left out the golden raisins and yogurt because I didn't have them, but it was still excellent. I gave it four stars instead of five, because the children didn't care for it. It must be a grown-up food in our house.

target.recipe_text:
quick and easy cinnamon rolls  yeast free

i made these today in 'home ec' class. these are super yummy and quick to make because they have no yeast, so you don't have to wait hours for them to rise.
my friend is vegan so our group used powdered milk instead of actual milk.
you do not need to use a mixer at all ^_^
sorry for the form of measurement, the recipe was written in ml's instead of cups-tsp-tbsp.

1. preheat oven to 250c
2. mix flour , sugar , salt , and baking powered in large bowl
3. cut in margarine until mixture looks like oatmeal or small peas
4. add milk gradually , stirring with a fork
5. dough should come away from sides of bowl
6. knead 3-4 times and then roll into a rectangle on lightly floured counter
7. -filling-
8. smear margarine over dough coating it not to thick but not to thin
9. sprinkle desired amount of cinnamon on top
10. sprinkle desired amount of brown sugar on top
11. sprinkle desired amount of raisins
12. roll up like a jelly roll , starting from the long edge
13. slice into 1-inch slices and place cut side down in a grease muffin tin
14. bake 12-15 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: This was pretty good.  Tasty, but texture wasn't quite as good as some other recipes I have tried.  Also, the glaze didn't turn out at all.  Not sure whether I did something wrong.  I had to throw that out and make my own.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best vegan oat   walnut waffles  or pancakes

our sunday tradition entails that my hubby make waffles for me and the boys (3 and 5). we tried this recipe this morning and it was the best waffles he's made by far!  this recipe is from moosewood resturant and is listed exactly as they wrote it. here are my adaptions: we omitted the walnuts due to allergies. we used all unbleached flour. we decreased the soy milk by 1/3 cup and added a glob of vanilla yogurt instead. we used sugar instead of maple syrup. lastly, we doubled the recipe for the four of us because we love leftovers for the next morning! (though i only added one tbsp of oil instead of two) this could be used for pancakes also. follow-up: since posting this recipe, i tried as pancakes. while the taste was good, i prefer the waffles.

1. if toasting walnuts , toast in a single layer on an unoiled baking tray at 350 for 5 to 10 minutes , until fragant and golden brown
2. in a large bowl , sift the flours , salt , baking powder , cinnamon , and nutmeg , stir in the walnuts and oats
3. in a separate bowl , stir together the milk , oil , and maple syrup or sugar
4. make a well in the dry ingredients and pour in the wet ingredients
5. stir until just combined
6. do not overmix the batter
7. when combining wet and dry ingredients , it is better to leave a few lumps than to stir too much
8. after mixing , let the batter sit for a few minutes until bubbles form on the top
9. this 'rest' gives the baking powder time to start working so the waffles will be lighter
10. preheat waffle iron and lightly oil to prevent sticking
11. use 1 / 3 cup of batter for each waffle and bake accoring to the directions for your waffle iron
demonstrations.review: I made these according to the recipe, except I used 2% milk instead of soy (I'm not a vegan - just a dude who ran out of eggs).  I have to disagree with a couple of other posts in that I didn't miss the eggs at all.  The waffles were just as crispy as any others I have made.  My suggestion to anyone making waffles of any type is not to stack them after they're cooked.  That makes them soggy.  I wouldn't recommend this recipe to anyone who doesn't like walnuts (which I do), as that seemed to be the dominant flavour to me.  We liked them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat banana oatmeal chocolate chip muffins

i am now actually "watching" my diet, and in the process am trying to make my favorites in a "low fat" manner. i took my favorite muffin recipes and combined them, made some adjustments and came up with this great recipe. hope you enjoy them!

1. add sugar to mashed bananas and mix
2. add beaten egg and mix
3. in a separate bowl mix all dry ingredients
4. add dry ingredients to the banana mixture and mix well
5. mix in applesauce
6. add chocolate chips and stir
7. spoon into medium size muffin tin and fill 3 / 4's full
8. bake for 20-25 minutes at 350
9. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Wonderful muffins!  I halved the sugar, which was sweet enough for my liking.  I also used a greased muffin pan, rather than the paper liners.  They came out of the pan without issue.

They were wonderfully moist and tasted great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat dq ice cream cake

posted in response to a thread.  i asked the sweet gals at our local dq about making these cakes.  this is it.  simple as it may seem, this is exactly the recipe.  the three hours is freezer time.

1. butter the cake pan of your choice , then press wax paper over the bottom of the pan
2. allow one of the flavors of ice cream to soften , then spread one flavor on the bottom of pan until the pan is almost half full
3. sprinkle with crushed oreo cookies
4. heat the hot fudge in the microwave until pourable
5. let cool slightly then spoon hot fudge sauce over the top of this
6. set in freezer until frozen
7. fifteen minutes before removing the pan , soften the second quart of ice cream
8. smooth it evenly with the top of the cake pan
9. return to the freezer and freeze until very hard
10. remove from freezer and frost with a mixture of equal parts vanilla ice cream and thawed frozen whipped topping beaten together
11. return to freezer until serving time
demonstrations.review: This turned out pretty well for me, though I had some issues with the cookie/fudge layer.  I used a whipped cream icing (http://www.recipezaar.com/39013), which was perfect for the cake.  I used Smucker's microwavable fudge, which was a mistake.  It was much too runny, made the cake messy, and was probably responsible for the fact that I was unable to cut out nice, full pieces in tact.  I also put the cookies in a blender, which I wouldn't do again.  It seemed like the crumbs might have been too small, which also might have been responsible for my slices falling apart.  For those wondering (as I was) whether you should read the ingredients list as containing 2 quarts or 4, I used 2 (one chocolate and 1 vanilla) and it seemed right.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
three pepper pizza

a colorful pizza.  a great way to use up summer produce. you can use a store bought pizza dough or make your own.  from williams-sonoma with some minor changes to fit our taste.

1. roll out the dough into a 12 inch round and lay the dough on top of a lightly greased pizza pan
2. lightly brush the dough with the olive oil and spread the tomatoes evenly on top , leaving a 1 / 2 inch border
3. lay the cheese slices evenly over the tomatoes
4. scatter the bell peppers and sausage evenly over the cheese
5. sprinkle with half of the oregano and season with salt and pepper
6. bake at 450 degrees f until the bottom of the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbly , about 15 minutes
7. remove from the oven and sprinkle with remaining oregano
8. let cool for 5 minutes , then cut into slices and serve
demonstrations.review:
Wonderful pizza!  With the olive oil and tomatoes instead of tomato sauce it had the feel of a gourmet pizza.  I would strongly recommend including all the tomato called for in the recipe, as it gives the pizza a sweet flavour.

We will certainly use this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: I know this recipe has a lot of very positive reviews, and I don't like to be difficult, but I honestly didn't like it.  I didn't like the bottom (peanut butter) portion - it didn't have the peanut butter taste I was expecting.  I probably would have let my own opinion slide, but when my 8 year old and 6 year old wouldn't eat them (and they are not picky eaters), I thought I should probably mention it.

target.recipe_text:
tsr version of applebee s oriental chicken salad by todd wilbur

this recipe is from www.topsecretrecipes.com. this actually tastes like the salad from applebees. it is a bit of work, but worth every second!!

1. preheat oil in deep fryer or deep pan over medium heat
2. you want the temperature of the oil to be around 350 degrees
3. blend together all ingredients for dressing in a small bowl with an electric mixer
4. put dressing in refrigerator to chill while you prepare the salad
5. in a small , shallow bowl beat egg , add milk , and mix well
6. in another bowl , combine flour with corn flake crumbs , salt and pepper
7. cut chicken breast into 4 or 5 long strips
8. dip each strip of chicken first into egg mixture then into the flour mixture , coating each piece completely
9. fry each chicken finger for 5 minutes or until coating has darkened to brown
10. prepare salad by tossing the chopped romaine with the chopped red cabbage , napa cabbage , and carrots
11. sprinkle sliced green onion on top of the lettuce
12. sprinkle almonds over the salad , then the chow mein noodles
13. cut the chicken into small bite-size chunks
14. place the chicken onto the salad forming a pile in the middle
15. serve with salad dressing drizzled over it or on the side
target.review: We ate at Applebee's on Friday night and actually had this salad.  Then we made this recipe on Saturday as a side salad and left off the chicken.  It was very good, but did taste a little different than Applebees.  Maybe too much mustard....  I'm not sure.  Next time, I think I'll go lighter on it and try the chicken too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut clusters

i make these alot.. people have asked for them so i tend to put them in gift baskets.

1. in a large saucepan , melt peanut butter and butterscotch morsels on
2. medium heat
3. remove from heat
4. stir in peanuts and cornflakes
5. mix well and drop
6. by spoonfuls onto waxed paper
7. chill until set
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very good!  I've made them with butterscotch chips (mmmm - my favorite) and with semi-sweet chocolate chips (my hubby's favorite.)  I even sent them in gift baskets this year and had a coworker ask for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite way to cook asparagus

the best thing about this method is that it is completely and easily do-ahead!   great for company!  since his favorite way to eat asparagus is as a separate course on buttered toast, at the end of the 8 minutes cooking time, i drain almost all the water out of the skillet, add a chunk of butter, heat slightly until the butter melts and serve on (yes) buttered toast.  edited to say:  call me crazy, but i peel my asparagus with a potato peeler unless it is under 1/4" thick!

1. snap off bottom third of stalks or where they snap easily
2. arrange the thoroughly washed stalks in 2 or 3 flat layers in a 10-12" skillet
3. cover with cold water until it stands " above the asparagus
4. add a tablespoon each of salt and sugar
5. bring uncovered to a rolling boil
6. let boil from 2-4 minutes depending upon the thickness of the asparagus and whether you like it very crisp or not quite so chewy
7. remove from the heat and let stand , still uncovered , in the water at least 8 minutes or until ready to serve
8. if the wait to serve is too long and the asparagus gets cold , simply bring to a boil once more , drain and serve immediately
9. sometimes i get crazy and sizzle the stalks in the butter for a couple of minutes
10. still have to put that on toast , though
11. cooking
12. start with frozen , cover with cold water , bring to a boil separating stalks
13. boil 1 minute , take off the heat and let stand for 4 minutes
14. maybe you would like a smashed garlic clove and / or red pepper flakes in the water
15. i haven't tried that yet
demonstrations.review: Excellent and Easy!  I served this to my kids (6 and 4) last week and they cleaned the dish.  Today, I bought two bunches of asparagus and can't wait to serve it to them again.  We're getting our veggies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
south pacific island chicken  from a crock pot

i was playing in the kitchen again and this was the creation. my hubby loves it and i can't go home to my family's house without them hounding me to make it....thank goodness it's easy!

1. in a large bowl combine pineapple juice , orange juice , and 3 tablespoons of the ground ginger
2. put 1 / 2 of the liquid in a large zipper seal bag
3. reserve rest of liquid in bowl or other covered container
4. rinse chicken and pierce with a fork in several places of each breast
5. place chicken in zipper bagand refrigerate at least 4 hours to overnight
6. drain the mandarin oranges and put in container with reserved liquid , cover and marinate for the same amount of time as the chicken
7. chop peppers and onion
8. when ready to cook , place chicken in bottom of crock pot , discard the marinade
9. layer the onions and peppers on chicken and salt and pepper to taste
10. drain pineapple chunks and add fruit to crock pot
11. add undrained crushed pineapple to crock pot as well as the mandarin oranges with the liquid
12. set crock pot to high and cook 6-8 hours , depending on when the chicken is done
13. when ready to serve cook rice according to package directions and serve chicken with sauce over the rice
14. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I just finished dumping my left-overs down the garbage disposal.  Nope, we didn't like this one much at all.  I was able to choke it down the first round, but couldn't bear the thought of it a second time, hence two only stars.  BTW, if you do decide to try this recipe, make sure you use a large crock pot or only make half.  My crockpot ended up being too small.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rejuvenated rustic turkey  artichoke panini

similar to one of my favorite selections at panera bread restaurant--this one will work for lunch as is with a few carrot-sticks on the side or add a cup of soup or small salad for delicious dinner-time fare. i don't have a panini-maker--so my two large cast-iron frying pans get called into action.

1. lightly toast pine nuts in cast-iron frying pan or oven
2. pour nuts into small bowl
3. set aside to cool
4. melt butter in empty pan , saut shallots , stirring lightly
5. set aside
6. coarsely chop artichokes , then add to shallots in warm pan
7. set aside
8. cut focaccia bread into four equal sandwich portions , then slice horizontally
9. spread each slice with one tablespoon of mayonnaise
10. layer spinach and tomato slices equally on four of the bread slices
11. add the grated cheese and toasted pine-nuts to the artichokes-shallot mixture in the pan
12. quickly divide into four portions and spoon over the spinach and tomatoes
13. add one fourth of the turkey breast meat to each of the sandwiches , lightly add salt & pepper and cayenne pepper flakes to taste
14. put the lid on the sandwich and press lightly
15. place sandwiches into panini-maker and heat per manufacturers suggestions
16. or
17. place sandwiches into large buttered medium-hot frying pan , place another heavy frying pan on top
18. then press down firmly to heat sandwich like this for 1-2 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I made a few changes to it.  I skipped the pine nuts and pepper flakes.  I also couldn't find plain asiago cheese, so I used an italian cheese mix with asiago in it.  Next time, I'll use much less mayo.  I am a fan of mayo, but this sandwich tasted like a LOT of mayo.  Next time, I'll just spread it like I usually do - without measurement.  My hubby gave this sandwich a big thumbs up, too.  I've had the panera version - it's a favorite.  This is pretty close.  I think it'll be closer with less mayo.  Can't wait to have it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy asian beef   noodles   ww recipe

this is delicious. it satisfies my craving for lo-mein. i have made with chicken and shrimp as well, just adjust the ramen noodle flavor to match.  from ww cookbook cooking for two, it makes a huge 10 points serving.  i am satisfied with 1/2 a serving.

1. trim fat from steak
2. cut steak diagonally across grain into thin slice
3. heat 1 tsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium high heat
4. add steak and green onions
5. stir fry 1 minute
6. remove steak mixture from skillet
7. keep warm
8. heat remaining 1 tsp oil in skillet over medium high heat
9. add slaw
10. stir fry for 30 seconds
11. remove slaw from skillet and keep warm
12. remove noodles from packages
13. reserve 1 seasoning packet for another use
14. add water and remaining seasoning packet to skillet
15. bring to a boil
16. break noodles in half
17. add noodles to water mixture
18. cook noodles 2 minutes or until most of liquid is absorbed , stirring frequently
19. stir in steak mixture , slaw , and soy sauce
20. cook until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: We LOVE this recipe!  I have the WW magazine and have been making this for years.  We use half a bag of cole slaw mix and save the other half to have it again in a few days.  You can also make this with CHICKEN and chicken flavored ramen noodles.  5 stars either way!

target.recipe_text:
the only chocolate cake recipe you ll ever need   devil s food

this chocolate cake is absolutely thee best we have ever had. it is so moist and rich, i never make anything else (unless i am short on time :) the frosting recipe included goes perfectly with this cake, but you can use any frosting you like. try this once and you'll see why i call it "the only chocolate cake recipe you'll ever need"!!  adding 2/18/06: i want to note that i recently used sweetened whipped heavy cream with vanilla and it was just as fabulous as the frosting recipe listed, plus much easier.  i also used hazelnut coffee in the cake and it added even more of a little extra something!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. in a large mixing bowl , sift together dry ingredients
3. add oil , coffee and milk and mix at medium speed for 2 minutes
4. add eggs and vanilla and beat 2 more minutes
5. expect batter to be thin
6. pour into a 9" x 13" greased and floured pan or 2- 9" round pans
7. bake 9 x 13 pan for about 45 minutes or 9" pans for about 30 minutes
8. cool in pans for about 15 minutes and then cool completely on racks
9. while cake is cooling make the icing: combine the milk and flour in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick , whisking constantly
10. cover and refrigerate until chilled
11. in a medium bowl , beat butter , shortening , sugar and vanilla until creamy
12. add chilled milk and flour mixture and beat for 10 minutes
13. frost cooled cake and enjoy ! the frosting sounds intimidating , but it is worth it ! by the way , for some reason , we prefer this cake chilled , right out of the refrigerator
14. the rich chocolate and cool frosting just seem to taste best this way
target.review: I have been using this cake recipe for over a year now.  I'm sorry I didn't review it sooner.  This is by far the best chocolate cake ever!  The name says it all.  I passed the recipe on to my mom and now its the only chocolate cake recipe she ever uses too.  I love using different flavors of coffee in the recipe too.  I have done many variations of this cake trying different icings and such.  Once I used the frosting listed here as a filler for a layer cake and used chocolate butter cream on the outside.  It turned out wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental mini meatloaves with honey garlic sauce

a yummy variation on traditional meatloaf. i have also made this mixture into meatballs as well.

1. meatloaves-combine all ingredients in a large bowl
2. mix lightly but throughly to blend
3. divide into 12 muffin cups
4. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes
5. or remove from pan and serve with honey garlic sauce immediately
6. sauce-combine ingredients in a sauce pan
7. cook and stir on low heat until hot and bubbly
8. serve with rice or oriental noodles
demonstrations.review: Someone suggested this recipe to me when I posted that I was in search of a ground turkey recipe.  I am so glad I tried it. The only thing I did differently was that I made meatballs instead of meatloaf.  I served them over rice and it was very delicious.  Will be using this recipe again very soon. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberries   cream bread  strawberry or blueberry

a wonderful recipe using fresh strawberries from netherhill strawberry farm in australia. this recipe also yields a tried and true (and reviewed) great blueberry & cream bread.

1. combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
2. set aside
3. in small bowl , beat butter until creamy
4. gradually add sugar , beat 1 minute or until light and airy
5. add brown sugar
6. beat in eggs , one at a time
7. beat in sour cream and vanilla
8. stir into flour mixture only until dry ingredients are moistened
9. fold in strawberries and nuts
10. pour into a greased 8 x 4 inch loaf pan
11. bake at 350f for 60 to 65 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean
12. let stand 10 minutes in pan
13. turn out on rack to cool
demonstrations.review: The only word for this bread is ADDICTIVE!  It is so delicious I guarantee you cannot eat just one slice.  My little one loved this as an after school snack.  This is going to be a recipe I'll use often.  I can't wait to try it with blueberies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pronto pups aka corn dogs

these are also known as corn dogs, but our school and church term for them are pronto pups. my family loves these friday nights, i can never seem to make enough for the kids!

1. combine cornmeal , flour , baking powder , salt , egg and sugar
2. add milk until batter has a pancake type consistency
3. dry off hot dogs with paper towels , coat with flour , and skewer through the center of the corndog
4. heat 2" deep oil to 370 degrees f
5. dip skewered hot dogs into batter mix and coat evenly
6. fry until golden brown about 2 1 / 2 minutes
7. let cool and drain on a paper towel
8. with left over batter drop like dumplings into the oil until golden brown and drain
9. serve with ketchup , mustard tarter sauce or a dressing of your choosing
demonstrations.review: My hubby loves corn dogs and I thought I'd like to make my own rather then keep buying the store bought frozen ones.......good idea!  My hubby adored these dogs.  This recipe is going to be a summertime favorite I'm sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth pumpkin bread

i got this recipe out of a church cookbook many years ago. it is a simple and delicious pumpkin bread. my daughter who hates coconut loves this bread. it is so moist and tasty that it really does melt in your mouth.

1. mix oil , eggs and pumpkin
2. combine remaining ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture
3. bake in a 9x5x3-inch pan at 325 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe...but not as a bread.  After trying it the first time as a bread I decided it would taste better as a cake.  I doubled the recipe, and baked it in a bundt pan at 325 for about an hour.  I then topped it with cream cheese frosting.  It was one of the best cakes I have ever made!  Also I chose to use french vanilla pudding rather than coconut.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: I used to use another banana bread recipe and loved it as well.  But I thought I would test out this one.  I will never go back to my other recipe again!  This bread is so moist and so banana-y.  Its great for breakfast or for dessert!

target.recipe_text:
creamy bacon salad dressing

delicious!  i make up a quart jar and keep it in the fridge.  makes a delicious blue cheese dressing base as well.  just add the blue cheese!

1. i put all the ingredients in my mini food processor
2. if you want to mix by hand , the bacon should be minced fine
3. this is a thick dressing to toss with a salad
4. if you prefer a thin dressing to pour over the salad , substitute milk for the cream
target.review: Very good dressing!  It is nice and thick, so it did double - actually triple - duty for me.  I had some on a salad last night, served some as a dip with pretzels as a snack for my kids after basketball today and then added the rest to our cole slaw tonight to make Creamy Bacon Coleslaw - YUM!  I did double the amount of garlic powder and added about 1/4 tsp. liquid smoke that gave it a Smokey Bacon flavor.  I will have to try the blue cheese next....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach spoon bread   crock pot

excellent side dish.

1. combine all ingredients in large bowl , mix well
2. pour batter into oiled , preheated slow cooker
3. cook , covered but with lid slightly ajar to allow excess moisture to escape , on high 1 3 / 4 to 2 hours or on low 3 to 4 hours or until edges are golden and knife inserted in centre of bread comes out clean
4. serve bread spooned from slow cooker , or loosen edges and bottom with knife and invert onto plate
5. cut into wedges to serve
demonstrations.review: Okay, this was really, really, really ridiculously good!!  I've never made spoon bread before and you can bet your bottom dollar I'll be making this one again!  So yummy....I could make a meal out of it.  I didn't have a red bell pepper and couldn't find a 5 1/2 oz. box of cornbread mix.  I used an 8 1/2 oz. box of yellow muffin mix (just the store brand) and used only 1 egg and omitted the seasoning salt for personal preferences.  I also used only 1/2 cup butter.  It turned out perfectly and was so good...thanks so much for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic cabbage rolls

i believe i got this recipe in one of my "tast of home" cooking magazines. it is a really good recipe for cabbage rolls.

1. in a dutch oven , boil cabbage for 10 minutes or until leaves are tender
2. drain
3. rinse in cold water
4. drain
5. remove 8 large outer leaves , set aside
6. in a large saucepan , saute 1 cup of the chopped onion in butter until tender
7. add tomatoes , v8 juice , garlic , brown sugar and 1 / 2 tsp
8. of the salt
9. simmer for approximately 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
10. meanwhile , in a bowl , combine rice , catsup , worcestershire sauce , pepper and remaining onion and salt
11. add beef and sausage
12. mix well
13. place about 1 / 2 cup meat mixture on each leaf
14. fold in sides
15. starting at an unfolded edge , roll up each leaf to completely enclose filling
16. place seam side down in a skillet
17. top with the sauce
18. cover and cook over medium-low heat for 1 hour
19. reduce heat to low
20. cook 20 minutes longer or until rolls are heated through and meat is no longer pink
demonstrations.review: These were the first cabbage rolls I had ever made and we loved them - my DH especially. I have to admit they are still the only ones I have ever made, but they are always welcome at our dinner table!  Thanks for posting!  : )

demonstrations.recipe_text:
springtime spinach salad

from taste of home march 2005

1. place asparagus in a foil lined 1
2. 5 inch x 10 inch x 1 inch baking pan
3. sprinkle with olive oil and toss to coat
4. bake , uncovered , at 400 degrees for 15 minutes or until crisp-tender , turning occasionally
5. cool
6. in a large bowl , combine the spinach , strawberries , walnuts , asparagus
7. in a jar with a tight fitting lid , combine the vegetable oil , vinegar , sugar and salt
8. shake well
9. drizzle over salad and toss to coat
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Wonderful salad - we loved everything about it - even though I forgot to get the asparagus at the store, and several other things I needed....the two kids with me rolling around in their Heelys and another trying to put everything I didn't need in my cart could have had something to do with it.....but I digress....! I know the asparagus (I love roasted aparagus!) would have only sent it over the top and I will make it again soon with it included!  My family couldn't get enough of this salad - like SweetsLady,  I could also see putting grilled chicken on it, but it is just great as-is!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna turnovers

this is one of those recipes that is so beat up that it fell out of the book - the more with less cookbook by doris janzen longacre.  i learned a lot from this cookbook when i was a newlywed and new mother figuring out how to plan meals.   these are great if you make your own biscuit dough but they're super easy if you use the refrigerated kind!

1. combine all ingredients except biscuit dough
2. prepare biscuit dough - or open the tube :)
3. if homemade dough , roll out to 1 / 8-to 1 / 4 inch thickness
4. if premade biscuit dough , flatten out each biscuit a bit - i divide them in half if they're the big fat type
5. cut into 4-inch squares or rounds
6. place about 2 1 / 2 t filling onto each dough piece , fold over and pinch to seal
7. i don't bother sealing these all the way - just roll them up and pinch closed across the top
8. some of the filling may sneak out the ends , but i prefer them this way
9. bake 15 minutes in a 400 degree oven
10. to freeze: bake as directed and allow to cool
11. wrap in plastic wrap and then place in a freezer bag
12. seal , pushing out as much air as possible
13. label and freeze
14. to serve: allow to thaw in fridge or microwave
15. good warm or cold
demonstrations.review: These were good - my children especially enjoyed them!  I have made up something similar to this before so I know we would like it- if you don't feel like or have the  time to form the individual turnovers, you can also make a casserole - pat the biscuit dough in the bottom of a baking dish, top with tuna mixture, sliced tomatoes and cheese and bake.  I do like the individual turnovers - makes it fun to eat!  :)  Made and reviewed for Aus/NZ Swap #16.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolaty double crunchers

this came from taste of home.

1. in a mixing bowl cream butter and sugars
2. add egg and vanilla , mix well
3. combine flour , soda , and salt
4. add to creamed mixture and mix well
5. add oats , cornflakes and coconut
6. shape into 1 balls and place 2 inches apart on greased baking sheets
7. flatten with glass dipped lightly in flour
8. bake at 350 for 8-10 minutes or until lightly browned
9. remove to wire racks to cool
10. for filling: beat cream cheese and sugar until smooth
11. add chocolate and mix well
12. spread on cookies to make sandwiches
13. keep in the fridge
demonstrations.review: We love oatmeal and chocolate around here, so that makes this a popular recipe for us!  It is often requested by my children when they have friends spend the night.  Many of the steps are very kid-friendly: rolling the balls, flattenig the cookies (my boys can get a little carried away with this), and then spreading the filling and making the "sandwiches".  I got it from Taste of Home and was about to post it, but found you already had.

target.recipe_text:
i can t wait for chole

a nice spicy indian chickpea recipe. i know, i know. the beans come from a can. yeah, yeah. but i was so hungry, and i was in a hurry! remember this little dish the next time you're short on time, too! to serve as a vegetarian main dish, increase the quantity. reheats well, too.

1. in large saucepan over medium heat , heat cumin seeds , bay leaf and cinnamon until very fragrant , swirling around to prevent burning
2. add ginger and garlic , cooking until the smell of those fills the air , then add onions
3. saute onions , stirring frequently , and adding drops of water to prevent sticking , until they are translucent
4. add the tomatoes , coriander , turmeric , salt , and cayenne
5. check for seasoning , adding more as you prefer
6. bring to a boil
7. add garbanzo beans , cover , and reduce heat
8. simmer on low for 10-15 minutes
9. stir in garam masala and lemon juice just before serving
10. garnish with a sprinkle of chopped cilantro if you desire
11. serve with rice , or indian breads or pitas
target.review: I made this, adding some chicken to meet hubby's definition of dinner. It was pretty good. I don't know if I did something wrong, but the spices just didn't last thru the cooking. But not bad. Thanks. This was a great recipe for my son who's allergic to milk & eggs.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
redroadhome s pizza dough

whole wheat pizza dough sweetened with honey.

1. place yeast in warm water and allow to dissolve for 10 minutes
2. combine flour , wheat germ and salt
3. add honey and yeast mixture
4. stir well
5. allow the mixture to sit at room temperature for 10 minutes
6. put on a floured pan
7. bake at 350 for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: WOW!  This was fabulous.  I was wanting a meatball pizza today, and I have only whole-wheat flour, so I tried this recipe.  This recipe completely blew me away.  I used 2 Tbs of honey.  I made it thin-crust, and got 2 14" pizzas.  Definitely my new pizza dough recipe.  Simple, quick and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Fabulous for OAMC.  I made the full batch & froze in 2-serving bags.  I've used it in casseroles, on ravioli and with pasta.  I just thaw under running water for 10 minutes & reheat with pasta.  SO easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal apple cookies

these delicious cookies are chock full of chewy yummy and mostly healthy ingredients. enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 375 and grease cookie sheet
2. combine shortening , sugar , egg , milk and vanilla in large bowl
3. beat at medium speed until well blended
4. combine flour , cinnamon , salt , soda and nutmeg in a small bowl and mix into creamed mixture at low speed until just blended
5. stir in oats , apples , raisins and nuts
6. drop rounded tablespoonfuls of dough about 2-inches apart onto prepared cookie sheets
7. bake for 13 minutes or until just set
8. cool for a minute or 2 on cookie sheets and then remove to a wire rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review:
These were really good cookies!  A great way to use up apples & oats.  I used butter and old-fashioned oats, and they still turned out just fine.

Not only do my kids keep asking for more, but my husband as well!  Definitely a repeat-recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked pasta with sausage and tomato pesto

the smoked gouda can sometimes be hard to find, but it adds a great flavor and texture.  the hot italian sausage adds some spice.  got this one from "the best american recipes 2003-2004."

1. in a large dutch oven over medium-high heat , add the sausage and onion
2. cook , breaking sausage up with a spoon , for about 5 minutes , or until softened , stirring frequently to cook onion evenly
3. add garlic and cook for 1 more minute
4. add marinara sauce and reduce heat to medium
5. simmer for 10 minutes , or until sauce begins to thicken
6. stir in pesto and season with salt and pepper to taste
7. set aside
8. cook penne in a large pot of salted boiling water for about 10 minutes , or until al dente
9. drain well
10. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
11. oil a 9-x-13-inch baking dish
12. spread a thin layer of sauce over bottom of dish
13. in a large bowl , combine pasta with remaining sauce , the gouda or mozzarella , 1 / 3 cup of the parmesan , and spinach , mixing well
14. spoon mixture into prepared dish and sprinkle with remaining 2 / 3 cup parmesan over top
15. bake for about 30 minute or until casserole begins to bubble and cheese is browned
16. serve hot
demonstrations.review: FABULOUS!  I made it as a side & skipped the sausage.  Instead, I used finely diced mushrooms sauted in hot chili oil.  I've made it twice since then.  What a fabulously easy & delicious recipe.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin french toast with toasted walnuts

this has the nicest autumn-y flavor. i like it served drizzled with maple syrup, but the topping possibilities are endless with this.

1. combine first six ingredients in a shallow bowl
2. heat a skillet until water droplets dance
3. grease the skillet
4. dip one slice of the bread in the mixture , make sure it is fully coated
5. put coated bread in greased pan and cook about 3 minutes each side , or until golden brown
6. repeat with other slice
7. throw walnuts in the pan and stir until they are toasted
8. put them on top the toast
demonstrations.review: WOW!  This was really good.  I tripled the recipe and used just regular sandwich  bread instead of thick-sliced.  I got 7 pieces of toast, and they went fast!  Even the guys (who normally fuss over anything remotely healthy) loved it.  Definitely a repeat-recipe!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
chicken with mustard and tarragon cream sauce

make sure to serve this with steamed rice to soak up all this delicious sauce! from bon appetit.

1. melt butter with oil in heavy large skillet over high heat
2. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper
3. cook , skin side down , until brown , about 5 minutes
4. turn over
5. cook 1 minute
6. using tongs , transfer chicken to plate
7. add shallots to same skillet
8. reduce heat to medium-low
9. saute until soft , about 3 minutes
10. add brandy
11. simmer until liquid is reduced , scrapping up browned bits , about 2 minutes
12. whisk in broth
13. return chicken to skillet , skin side up
14. reduce heat to medium low
15. cover , and simmer until shicken is cooked , about 20 minutes
16. transfer to platter
17. reserve skillet
18. whisk cream , tarragon and mustard into same skillet
19. increase heat to high
20. boil until sauce is thickened , about 2 minutes
21. season with salt and pepper
22. pour sauce over chicken
target.review: This is a wonderful dish!  I used just chicken breasts and DOUBLED the sauce which I am so glad I did.  Outstanding!  This is definitely a dish worth serving company.  Impress your friends, make this dish for them. Thanks AGAIN Heather for sharing this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer cheese soup

this recipe came from the coburg inn in coburg, oregon.  we had this soup on our wedding night.

1. saute vegetables in butter until done , but not browned
2. blend in flour , dry mustard , and chicken stock
3. cook 5 minutes
4. blend in cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese , m and beer
5. let simmer 30 minutes
6. season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: This hearty soup is a real crowd pleaser.  We loved the combination of the dry mustard, beer and cheese.  Very flavorful and comforting.  The extra added bonus is that it is easy to make too.  Great recipe, Lavender Lynn.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked cinnamon applesauce

very yummy!

1. in a 3 1 / 2-quart electric slow cooker , toss together the apples , brown sugar , and lemon juice
2. cover and cook on the high heat setting 3 hours or until the apples are very tender
3. mash up the apples with a potato masher
4. stir in the cinnamon
5. serve over vanilla ice cream , if desired
demonstrations.review:
This dish was made for a "Crockpot Picnic" I hosted.  Everyone raved about how good it turned out for being cooked in a crockpot rather than on the stove.  Everyone asked for the recipe and said, "no more slaveing over a hot stove for me"   Thank you Bev for your help in making my picnic such a success!
:-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than traditional green bean bake

we prefer this cheesy version of the traditional bean bake.

1. combine soups , milk , pepper in a large baking dish
2. stir in beans
3. bake at 350 degrees for 45-60 minutes
4. top with french friend onions
5. bake 5 more minutes or until onions are golden brown
demonstrations.review: I was going to make our "traditional" green bean casserole for Easter when I found this and decided to try it instead.  (I was putting my life in my own hands).   Everyone LOVED it, Shelli!!!  The cheddar cheese soup was a nice variation to an old favorite.  Thanks so much for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super moist italian meatballs

craving some tender and juicy meatballs?? give this recipe a try! the two secrets are the extra eggs, and cooking the meatballs in the sauce, instead of pre-baking or frying them. ground chuck or a 50/50 mix of chuck and sirloin work best for full flavor and moistness.

1. in a bowl , combine beef , bread crumbs , cheese , eggs , garlic , pepper , salt , and wine
2. mix well
3. shape mixture into 1-1 / 2" or 2" meatballs
4. in a large pot , bring sauce to a boil
5. add meatballs one at a time , and simmer over medium-low heat for 40-45 minutes
6. serve over pasta , or on hoagie buns for meatball subs
demonstrations.review: These are by far the BEST meatballs I have ever tasted. Wish I could give them 10 stars. They turned out so tender and flavorful.  I followed your instructions exactly and would not change a thing.  All my other meatball recipes are out the door.  Thanks so much for sharing, ItalianMan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy fruit dip

mmmmmmmm--very creamy dip with a caramel taste to it.

1. combine cream cheese and brown sugar , beating till smooth
2. add remaining ingredients one at a time , beating well after each addition
3. cover and chill at least an hour
4. makes 3-1 / 2 cups
demonstrations.review: Who needs fruit!  I could eat this right out of the bowl!!!  I've tasted many variations of fruit dip but particularly liked the vanilla pudding that is added to this.  An added plus is, I mixed this all up in the morning and it keeps very well until you are ready to serve.  I served this with a variety of fruits and it made a beautiful presentation.  My strawberries weren't very good, but who cares, when you dip them in such a wonderful dip, ha, ha, ha.  Thanks Darlene Summers, for sharing this with us.

target.recipe_text:
strawberry cheesecake ice cream  for electric ice cream machine

posted by request. recipe is from the recipe book that came with my ice cream machine. prep time includes 1 hour chilling and 1/2 hour freezing times.

1. blend all ingredients until smooth
2. chill ingredients for about 1 hour , or until cold
3. turn on ice cream machine and set it to chill the freezing / mixing bowl for 5 minutes
4. spoon the cooled mixture into the freezing / mixing bowl of machine
5. set the freezing timer to the 30 minute maximum setting
6. push start button
7. when timer rings , spoon ice cream into dishes and enjoy
target.review: Love it! Rave reviews from all who tasted. Used freshly picked strawberries and mashed them, and doubled the recipe using 1/2 cup amaretto flavored creamer and 1 cup heavy cream since it was what was on hand.  Blended all in a processor but the heavy cream (didn't want it to whip) and reserved half of the berries and stirred those in after so I could have strawberry chunks throughout.  In the last 5 minutes I added broken pieces of graham cracker crust.  Tasted like a frozen strawberry cheesecake!  Subbed low fat cream cheese and you'd never know... guess the heavy cream made up for that.  It made too much to fit in my icecream maker, but the first batch was gone in minutes so I was happy to have another ready to go!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
copycat recipe for carrabba s chicken marsala

a clone dish from carrabba's restaurant. i have not tried this yet, but will soon and add more comments. sounds wonderful!

1. pound chicken breasts to even out thickness and lightly salt and pepper
2. in large skillet , saute chicken in 2 t melted butter until lightly browned , about 2 minutes per side
3. remove from pan and set aside
4. melt remaining butter in pan and add shallots and mushrooms
5. cook until mushrooms are lightly browned
6. add marsala and bring to a boil , scraping browned bits from bottom of pan
7. add cream and lemon juice and return to a boil
8. season with salt and pepper
9. return chicken to pan for about 3 minutes to reheat and finish cooking
10. serve with buttered fettucini
demonstrations.review: I doubled the sauce but will triple it next time, my DH loved it so much.  I too will add prosciutto and rosemary next time as others have suggested, and will try it with half and half to reduce the fat as it is pretty rich! Great for OAMC if you don't mind, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth pumpkin bread

i got this recipe out of a church cookbook many years ago. it is a simple and delicious pumpkin bread. my daughter who hates coconut loves this bread. it is so moist and tasty that it really does melt in your mouth.

1. mix oil , eggs and pumpkin
2. combine remaining ingredients and add to pumpkin mixture
3. bake in a 9x5x3-inch pan at 325 for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: Definitely lives up to its name! Can't wait to try it with the pumpkin flavored pudding mix I picked up over thanksgiving. Did take my oven longer to cook than suggested, but worth the wait. My mother in-law loved it so much she wanted the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest mac  n  cheese

the easiest and tastiest macaroni and cheese recipe...so easy my 10 year old can make it! also the only mac and cheese my very picky 7 year old will eat. make sure to use extra sharp cheddar, it makes all the difference. best of all, no need to pre-cook the noodles! adapted from moosewood low fat favorites.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. place cottage cheese , buttermilk , and mustard in a mixing bowl
3. using a stick blender , puree until smooth
4. add cheddar cheese and uncooked macaroni to pureed mixture and stir until well mixed
5. spray a 8x11 baking dish with non-stick spray , then pour mixture into dish
6. in a small bowl , mix together bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
7. sprinkle over top of mixture in the baking pan
8. bake for about 45 minutes , until edges are nice and bubbly and top is browned
demonstrations.review: I love that it was super easy with no pre-cooking of the noodles. I used mini penne and it worked perfectly. It was not as creamy and cheesy as I like my mac n cheese to be, but I happened to have buttermilk and cottage cheese on hand that I needed to use. If I try it again will cover it like The Squid Grrrl recommends and maybe that will help. My family enjoyed it though!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry crumb pie

after looking around for this recipe and not finding it, i kind of adapted one on my own. it comes out pretty and delicious and a dollop of cool whip on top is lovely.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. place pie crust into pie pan and crimp edges as desired
3. in a mixing bowl , combine all filling ingredients gently
4. pour evenly into pie plate
5. combine flour and sugar for topping and cut in butter until mixture resembles course crumbs
6. sprinkle evenly over filling
7. bake for 40-50 minutes until filling starts to bubble and crust is lightly browned
8. cover edges with foil if crust is browning too quickly
demonstrations.review: Great way to use the blueberries I picked and froze over the summer. I just let them thaw before baking. Can't wait to try this with fresh picked berries. Don't know if it's my oven, but I did have to bake this over an hour before it got bubbly and browned.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas red enchilada sauce

this sauce can be used with beef or cheese enchiladas. the amount of "heat" in the sauce depends on the type and amount of chili powder you use.

1. melt butter / margarine in a sauce pan
2. make a roux by browning flour in melted butter / margarine
3. add spices and tomato paste
4. stir until well blended into roux
5. add water gradually , stirring constantly
6. heat until boiling
7. continue simmering and stirring until desired thickness is achieved
8. taste every so often and adjust spices as needed
9. once desired consistency and taste is reached , coat the bottom of a pan with the sauce , add freshly rolled enchiladas , then pour the remainder of the red sauce over enchiladas
10. place pan in oven and cook until enchiladas are done
demonstrations.review: Great to make ahead and have on hand! Made it for a few tamales once and refrigerated the left-overs. A few weeks later I decided to make chicken enchiladas and it was quick, easy and delicious!  I did think mine was a little too thick for my tastes, maybe I didn't cook the roux long enough, so I added a small can of tomato sauce and cooked it down to the consistency I wanted. Very tasty!

target.recipe_text:
raspberry tilapia

a great sweet tasting dish that is a snap to make

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 11x7 inch baking dish
3. in a mixing bowl , whisk together the olive oil , raspberry vinegar , honey , mustard and dill weed
4. arrange the tilapia filets in a single layer in the prepared baking dish
5. pour mixture over the fish filets , coating the filets evenly
6. bake in a preheated oven , uncovered for 20 minutes or until fish is flaky with a fork
target.review: Made this recipe tonight for dinner and enjoyed it quite a lot. I didn't have tilapia, so I used it on salmon fillets instead. I marinated the salmon for about an hour beforehand in the sauce. The 20 minute cooking time was not enough since the salmon fillets were thicker than your average tilapia, so I finished them off in my stove-top grill pan. I also used raspberry preserves, rather than vinegar, and found it worked well. Very tasty. Will make this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for the world s best indian mango curry

this is one curry u dont want to miss. its one of the few really yummy curries subru uncle makes for us. the last 3 days, this has been my addiction. be it lunch/ midnight, if i'm not on my chair or exercising or asleep or outisde shoping, etc, i'm right in front of the fridge, hunting for this curry! even a drop is an ocean, i love this curry that much:)

1. put the mangoes in a skillet alongwith the whole seeds of the mangoes
2. add the curry leaves , green chillies and water
3. add salt , turmeric powder and red chilli powder
4. bring to a boil
5. cook on high flame for 8-10 minutes
6. remove from flame and keep aside
7. heat oil in a non-stick saucepan
8. add the mustard seeds and allow to crackle
9. add methi seeds and allow to sizzle
10. add the cumin seeds and allow to splutter
11. add few curry leaves and stir-fry for a few seconds
12. remove from heat
13. pour into curry
14. stir well
15. allow to cool for about 30 minutes on the kitchen counter
16. then , stir in the beaten yogurt
17. mix it well and serve with cooked white basmati rice
18. this is one lunch that you will eat licking your fingers and enjoying every morsel , i promise !
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe over the weekend and was quite pleased with it. I did, however, make some adjustments based on the previous reviewers' comments. First off, I started with frying the cumin, methi and mustard seeds first. I doubled the amount of those seeds (which might be too much for the average person, but wasn't too much for me), and then after frying them, I combined them with the turmeric, chili powder, green chillies and a little water, just enough to make it process smoothly in the food processor. Then I sauted the curry leaves in a little oil until aromatic, then added the mango cubes for a few minutes. Then I added the processed spice paste, and a little more water and simmered it for awhile. From there, I basically added a bit of water and cream (which I used instead of yogurt) at a time until the sauce was the consistency I wanted. One final note: I was unable to include the mango seeds in the recipe, because no matter how hard I tried, I could not split open the mango cores. The fruit I bought was pretty ripe, but still, the cores wouldn't open, either with a chef's knife or a serrated knife.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot artichoke and sun dried tomato dip

i cannot remember the origin of this recipe, but the blend of ingredients are phenomenal!

1. stir together all of the ingredients
2. spoon into a 9- inch pie plate
3. bake for 25 minutes at 350 degrees
4. serve hot with your favorite crackers
demonstrations.review: I first got this recipe from a friend back in college who made it for all her parties. Loved it then, and love it now, though I add more hot pepper now that my tastes have gotten spicier. Also, I like to process the tomatoes and artichokes in the food processor because I prefer this dip a little less chunky than the original recipe. It makes the sun-dried tomato flavor more prominent, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted red pepper coconut soup

from the moosewood restaurant! i took home an entire tray of roasted red peppers from a reception we had at work.  this was the perfect recipe to use up a good portion of them.  feel free to adjust the heat to suit your tastes.  the original recipe is listed below, however, i actually used less crushed red pepper (which is totally not like me) and it was perfect!  this was so quick, easy and delicious!

1. warm oil over medium heat in large stock pot
2. add the onions , garlic , red pepper flakes , and salt and saut for about 15 minutes , until the onions are very soft and translucent
3. remove the pot from the heat and add the tomatoes , coconut milk , water , and the roasted red peppers
4. in batches in a blender , puree the soup until smooth
5. return it to the soup pot and cook on medium heat until hot
6. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made this soup exactly as directed, and then tasted it. The soup didn't have enough coconut flavor and wasn't cream enough for my liking. I was expecting something more like a bisque. In the future, I think it would be better to make this soup with coconut cream rather than coconut milk. In order to make this soup more bisque-like, I ended up adding some dairy cream and some cream cheese; that made it creamy enough, but the side effect was that the coconut flavor was subdued.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian inspired coconut crab cakes

i got the idea for this recipe taking an international cooking class in college..  i adapted it til it was perfect..

1. preheat oven to 375
2. place coconut in a mircowave safe dish and mircowave 3-4 minutes stirring often til lightly toasted
3. combine crab , ginger , green onions , pepper , carrot , lemon juice , may , egg , rice vinegar and garlic and mix well
4. combine bread crumsb and cayenne pepper and fold into crab mix
5. sprinkle half of the coconut on cutting board
6. with a measuring spoon form 16 even sized balls of crab mix
7. roll in coocnut mixture and sprinkle remianing coconut on top
8. flatten and place on cookie sheet
9. bake 20 minutes until coconut is golden brown
10. serve with asian style hot mustard
demonstrations.review: I tried these last night and was a little disappointed. They made a fine crab cake, but they just didn't have the zing I was hoping for. Aside from the coconut, they just really didn't taste any differently than an ordinary crab cake. I'm definitely going to make a spicy sauce for eating the leftovers. I'll probably go back to my usual crab cake recipe after this attempt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeo bites

these are a bit reminiscent of stuffed jalapeño peppers but much easier to make. i found this in the junior league celebrations cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. combine the cream cheese , parmesan , jalapeo peppers and egg yolks in a bowl and mix to form a paste
3. shape a 1 / 2 tablespoonful at a time into 1 / 4-inch rounds and roll in the bread crumbs
4. place on an ungreased baking sheet and bake for 10-15 minutes or until golden brown
5. serve warm
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty, however, they did not keep their shape in the oven.
