festive black bean soup in the crock pot

this is nice to come home to any time of the year.

1. place beans in slow cooker
2. add other ingredients
3. add water just to cover
4. cover
5. cook on high 8 hours
6. mash some of the beans for a thicker consistency
7. if desired , garnish with fresh cilantro , and cheese or sour cream
8. leftovers freeze well
demonstrations.review:
This is really good. I used chicken broth because it is what I had on hand, and I added some carrot, fresh jalepeno and a little cayenne pepper. YUM! ("Some Like It Hot" *wink*)
Thanks, Prose, for the recipe! It was great, but the photos weren't.  ~Made for PAC FALL 07

target.recipe_text:
chocolate jelly roll

a friend gave this recipe to my a long time ago and i have really enjoyed making it. you can always make it in advance and store in the freezer without filling. when you want to serve it, take it out and fill with your favorite filling, like ice cream.

1. prepare a large cookie sheet with lining it with wax paper
2. mix together sugar , whole eggs and water
3. beat in remaining ingredients
4. pour into prepared cookie sheet and bake at 375 degf for 12-15 minutes
5. remove from oven and turn out onto a clean , moist teatowel springled with icing sugar
6. quickly remove the wax paper and trim off crisp edges
7. while still warm , roll cake into tea towel into a roll , rolling the towel with the cake
8. when cool , unroll the cake carefully and spread with jelly , or ice cream or your favorite filling
9. roll up again
10. if using ice cream , store in the freezer until ready to serve
11. slice into serving pieces
target.review: Great recipe, exactly what I needed. Although next time when I roll it up in the tea towel I might put some more icing sugar, or some corn starch or something on the towel. The cake stuck to the towel really badly. It cooked up perfectly though, I didn't even need to trim any edges. I filled it with raspberry jam and whipped chocolate ganache and then covered it with more ganache. It was amazing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa greek salad

i got this recipe from a co worker after having it at a potluck.

1. in a saucepan , bring stock to a boil
2. stir in quinoa
3. reduce heat to med low and cover
4. cook 15 minutes , until liquid is absorbed
5. transfer to a large bowl and cool
6. stir veggies and cheese into cooled quinoa
7. whisk together dressing ingredients
8. pour over quinoa mixture and toss
demonstrations.review: I love the texture of this, it was a fantastic dish but I think that it had too much lemon juice. Next time I will use a greek salad dressing, balsamic vinegar, and red wine vinegar as the dressing. But we very much enjoyed this. I used kalamata olvies instead of black and my red onion was bad so I had to omit it. Other than that I made it as per the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fondant

this recipe is from www.thecookduke.com and it actually tastes good!  
tips from the website:
   1. when you make fondant, both the dough and the icing, make sure to make it in room temperature – too cold or too warm room will hurt the dough
   2. when you calculate the quantity of fondant icing required, it’s better to have too much fondant icing rather than too little, as leftover icing can be stored and used at a later date, or used for extra decorations
   3. make sure you make fondant on a clean and smooth working surface.
      jewelry on your fingers or wrists or fluffy clothing could hurt the fondant’s surface

1. sprinkle the gelatin over cold water in a small bowl
2. let it rest for two minutes to soften
3. place the bowl in a microwave for 30 seconds on high , until the gelatin dissolves
4. add the flavoring
5. add the corn syrup and the glycerin and stir until the mixture is smooth and clear
6. sift 1 1 / 2 pounds of the sugar into a large bowl
7. make a hole in the sugar and pour the liquid mixture to it
8. stir with a wooden spoon until the mixture becomes sticky
9. sift some of the remaining 1 / 2 pound of sugar onto a smooth work surface and add as much of the remaining sugar as the mixture will take
10. knead the fondant , adding a little more sugar if necessary , to form a smooth , pliable mass
11. rub the vegetable shortening on your thumbs and knead it into the fondant
12. wrap the fondant in plastic wrap and place it in a tightly sealed container to prevent it from drying out
13. if the icing dries out and harden it can often be revived by popping it into a microwave oven for a few seconds and then kneading it back to life
demonstrations.review: This is an easy to make recipe, and it takes color very nicely. It makes more than enough fondant and, I'm not a huge fan of the taste of fondant but as far as fondant goes it's the best tasting I've tried. Also the texture isn't rubbery which is important. It is very sticky to work with and I put shortening and icing sugar on my working surface to stop it from sticking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww baked yams with pineapple   3 points

this has been marked in my ww cookbook called "simply the best" as great. darla from los angeles sent this in. very yummy indeed. hope you enjoy.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. in a 2-quart casserole dish , combine the yams , orange , pineapple and its juice , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. dot with the margarine
4. cover and bake until the yams are tender , about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: this was very good but there was too much liquid in the bottom of the dish when it was done, which kind of made a mess on the plates etc. I think next time I might try adding cornstarch to help with that or maybe I'll add crushed pineapple and mash it at the end - that might be really good! I will be trying this recipe again, it was very tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy ham casserole

nan

1. heat oven to 350f degrees
2. mix all ingredients except 1 / 2 cup of the cheese
3. spoon into 1 1 / 2-quart casserole
4. sprinkle with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
5. bake for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated
6. sprinkle with seasoned croutons , if desired
7. microwave: prepare as directed
8. microwave on high 8 to 10 minutes or until thoroughly heated
9. sprinkle with seasoned croutons , if desired
demonstrations.review: My husband could not get enough of this. I cubed the cheese, and added seasonings, mrs dash, and Cajun. I thought it was about 3.5 stars. Easy and good enough for a quick dinner. But my husband over ate at dinner. He loved it so much. And then had the leftovers for breakfast. So because of that I gave it 5 stars. The kids also ate it without complaint. So I will be making it again that's for sure. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony rice pilaf

this takes plain ol' rice to a new level. goes particularly well with chicken. if you don't use chicken stock, this side dish is vegetarian/vegan.

1. in a heavy saucepan , heat oil over mediumheat and cook onion for 5 minutes , or until softened
2. stir in rice , then stock , and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and cover
4. let simmer for 20 minutes , or until rice is tender
5. stir in lemon zest , lemon juice , and parsley
6. taste and add pepper if you wish
demonstrations.review: The best rice ever! I love lemons! I had 3 helpings. My 3 yr old loved it too. He said it was the best. My husband found it a bit bland and added ranch dressing but he adds ranch dressing to everything so we will just ignore that haha. Thanks so much, I'll be making this again and again.

target.recipe_text:
country ribs   crock pot

mouthwatering classic!!

1. place onion rings in bottom of a 3 1 / 2 quart
2. crock pot , place ribs on top of onions
3. make sure ribs are trimmed of all excess fat
4. in a small bowl , whisk together the remaining ingredients , reserve 1 cup for sauce , cover this reserved portion and refrigerate
5. pour remaining tomato mixture over ribs , cover pot
6. cook at high setting for 5 to 6 hours , drain ribs , discarding cooking liquid
7. in a small saucepan , simmer reserved sauce for 10 minutes , serve over cooked ribs on heated plates
target.review: These ribs were quite tender, and the sauce was tasty. The recipe was quite easy, but a adjusted for our altitude (7,200 feet) and unfortunately cooked them for too long. I will make them again according to the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and pasta in white wine garlic sauce

this is simple and a crowd pleaser! intense combination of flavors that will have them back for seconds!

1. cut chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces
2. combine chicken in large skillet with water , olive oil , mushrooms , onion , garlic , and spices
3. cook until onion is tender
4. add tomatoes , wine , salt and pepper to taste
5. reduce heat , cover , and simmer about 15 minutes while preparing pasta , stirring occasionally
6. drain pasta al dente , place into serving dish and toss with olive oil
7. pour chicken mixture over pasta
8. serve with fresh salad and garlic toast
9. i am very generous with my spices when i make this dish and usually add more than the recipe calls for , but it is quite delicious as written
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe for unexpected guests because I knew it would stretch.  It was loved by all.  I particularly like the way the olive oil and seasonings come together.  It was finished in 1/2 hour and ready for all of my hungry people.  I used raw chicken breast cut small and simmered them in the sauce as directed.  We mixed the chicken with the pasta and served with Parmesan cheese.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish cream bundt cake

this is a great cake to celebrate st. patrick's day!

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. grease and flour a 10 inch bundt pan
3. sprinkle chopped nuts evenly over bottom of pan
4. in a large bowl , combine cake mix and pudding mix
5. mix in eggs , 1 / 4 cup water , 1 / 2 cup oil and 3 / 4 cup irish cream liqueur
6. beat for 5 minutes at high speed
7. pour batter over nuts in pan
8. bake in the preheated oven for 60 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into the cake comes out clean
9. cool for 10 minutes in the pan , then invert onto the serving dish
10. prick top and sides of cake
11. spoon glaze over top and brush onto sides of cake
12. allow to absorb glaze repeat until all glaze is used up
13. to make the glaze: in a saucepan , combine butter , 1 / 4 cup water and 1 cup sugar
14. bring to a boil and continue boiling for 5 minutes , stirring constantly
15. remove from heat and stir in 1 / 4 cup irish cream
demonstrations.review: This cake is delicious and so easy to make. I used all of the glaze, but let it cool first so that it thickened up. At my altitude (7,200 feet above sea level), I added 1/4 cup flour to the recipe, and it didn't fall.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
n  y  c  irish soda bread

classic irish soda bread

1. in a mixing bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , brown sugar and teaspoon of salt
2. cut in the butter until the mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. combine 1 beaten egg , raisins and buttermilk
4. add to mixture above and stir until just moistened
5. on a lightly floured surface , knead gently for 12 strokes
6. on a greased baking sheet , shape the mixture into a 6 inch round loaf and cut a cross in the top
7. brush with the other beaten egg
8. bake at 375f for 35 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: This bread has a wonderful flavor and texture. It is quite easy to make. I added an extra egg and 1/4 cup more flour to adjust for my altitude (7,200 feet). I cooked it on my baking stone, and it was perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable gumbo  crock pot

low calorie and filling vegetable soup which makes an easy dinner by itself or with grilled cheese sandwiches. this recipe needs a large (5 quart or larger) slow cooker/crock pot. recipe source: the healthy slow cooker

1. in a skillet over medium heat , heat oil for 30 seconds
2. add onions and celery , cook stirring until soft
3. stir in garlic , thyme , peppercorns , and bay leaf , cook stirring for 1 minute
4. stir in tomatoes and bring to a boil
5. transfer to large crock pot insert
6. stir in rice and broth
7. cover and cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3 hours or until rice is tender
8. discard bay leaf
9. in a small cup mix together the paprika and lemon juice
10. add paprika / lemon juice mixture , okra and green pepper , stirring in well
11. cover and cook on high for 20 minutes or until pepper is tender
12. add a dash or two of hot pepper sauce if desired
demonstrations.review: This has become a family favorite. I brought a batch to a baby shower, and there were not any leftovers. Sometimes I add a few chicken breasts. I find that the rice cooks better if I add the tomatoes with the paprika and lemon juice instead of right away. I throw in frozen okra about two hours before serving.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hummus amongus

there's a large middle eastern population in bayridge brooklyn and amazing restaurants line the avenues...hummus is served with every dish on the menu...it's one of my favorite things in the whole wide world...if you haven't tried it, please do. i think you'll love it!

1. drain beans
2. reserve water
3. in a food processor or blender add beans and all the ingredients
4. process until smooth
5. if mixture is too thick , add some of the reserved liquid from the beans to dilute to a desired consistency
6. serve at room temperature with pita bread , grilled pork , lamb or chicken
demonstrations.review: We love this hummus! I used dried beans (about 1/2 pound) cooked and reserved the cooking liquid for the moisture. We also added more garlic (four cloves total) because we are garlic lovers. Easy to make and very tasty.

target.recipe_text:
praline pecan pie a la virginia hospitality

this is a tasty pecan chess pie, but its custard is the color and taste of pralines, and it is a little less intense than dark pecan pie - virginia hostess style (although dh prefers the "dark" version).  this recipe came from virginia hospitality by the junior league of hampton roads.  it took my pie 60 minutes in the oven.  be sure to put pie pan on pizza pan to catch any spillage.  i added the perfect pecan halves just before baking; they improve the look of the pie for entertaining.  i learned through zwt5 that the french created the pecan pie after settling in new orleans and being introduced to the pecan by the natives, so it is considered a creole dish.

1. sort through pecans to select 1 / 2 cup of perfect pecan halves
2. set aside until pie is otherwise ready for the oven
3. preheat the oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
4. mix corn syrup , sugar , milk , lightly beaten eggs , flour , vanilla , and salt and mix well
5. stir in chopped pecans
6. mix well
7. pour into unbaked pie shell
8. create decorative pattern with perfect pecan halves
9. place pie on pizza pan to catch drips
10. bake at 400 degrees fahrenheit for 10 minutes
11. reduce heat to 300 degrees fahrenheit and bake for 30 minutes or until firm in the middle
12. cool on wire rack
13. refrigerate
target.review: This pie is very good. I used undiluted canned milk for the extra richness and I had to cook it for about 50 minutes instead of the 30 called for in the recipe. I think next time I will use buttermilk and brown sugar just to see what happens. I love buttermilk pralines so I bet it will be great. Thanks, This is a keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex goulash

this recipe makes much more than i anticipated when i made it. if you have a larger group it works out perfect. you could also freeze leftovers and just re-heat them in the oven. be sure not to top the whole dish with torillia chips unless you are going to eat the whole thing right then. otherwise just top each plate that is served with the crushed tortillia chips.

1. start by boiling the elbow noodles
2. while elbow noodles are boiling brown the ground beef and strain off any fat
3. add taco seasonning , onion , strained can of corn or frozen corn , rotel , and jalapeno black eyed peas
4. keep warm while noodles finish cooking
5. strain noodles when cooked and add them to the meat mixture
6. blend well then add cheese and sour cream
7. stir well and keep warm serve when its dinner time
8. add crushed tortillia chips to the top of each served plate
9. then just eat !
demonstrations.review: Thanks for this one! I did make few changes only because of personal taste. I used a can of Hoppin John which is black eyed peas with tomatoes, onions and jalapenos. I used spiral macaroni because that is what I had and  I used the sour cream and cheese as a garnish instead of adding it to the pan. This is really a good recipe and I will make it again. I am giving this 5 stars because it was so easy and so very flavorful. The church potluckers are going to love this. Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flourless brownies  sugar free  low carb

source is unknown, but probably a low carb venue

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees
2. melt the chocolate and butter together on stovetop or in microwave
3. add the splenda , eggs , egg yolks , vanilla and cocoa , stirring until well blended
4. pour into a 9 x 13 inch pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 50 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I gave this recipe 0 stars because I think it is posted incorrectly. When I read this I thought WOW that is alot of chocolate so I printed it, then pulled it up again on the site to make sure I was reading it right. 12 ounces of unsweetened chocolate and 6 T of cocoa. HMMMMM. Well I had my doubts but I proceeded and it turned out like bitter dirt. It was a very expensive mistake. I am pretty sure it is supposed to be 2 ounces of unsweetened chocolate. I may try it again with only 2 and come back with a different review but if you make this as is, it is not good. I threw it directly into the trash. Just wish I could get a refund. 8 eggs and all of that chocolate was not cheap.
OK, I went back and tried this recipe again using only 2 ounces of unsweetened chocolate and I substituted margarine in place of butter just in case it turned out bad again. This time it was very different. It is a very good recipe. I really enjoyed these brownies. well as much as you can enjoy something with no sugar or flour. It is definately a keeper. I HIGHLY recommend using only 2 ounces of the unsweetened chocolate though. Someone really should correct the amount of chocolate. It is very expensive to make and throw away as it it listed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome artichoke dip

my friend made this at a party and i just had to have her recipe. this is the best artichoke dip that i have ever tasted. you might want to double the recipe because this stuff will go very quickly!  i've made this several times now and the key is to rinse the spinach well before putting it in the recipe.  otherwise you will have green dip!  other cheeses, and cheese blends work fine in place of the parmesan.  however, i feel the parmesan gives the best flavor combination.  fresh lemon juice really makes this recipe different from other spinach artichoke dips and adds a much needed zing to the recipe.  its also best to use the freshest garlic you can get your hands on.

1. preheat your oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a 7x11 baking dish in a medium bowl mix cream cheese and mayo until smooth add chopped artichokes , chopped spinach and parmesan
3. add lemon juice and minced garlic mix together well
4. for a smoother texture , pulse in a food processor until the desired texture is achieved
5. this will also help mix things more completely and give a better fusion of flavors
6. bake covered with aluminum foil for 20 minutes
7. during the last 5 minutes of baking remove the foil
8. the top should be golden brown around the edges when it is done
9. serve while hot with tortilla chips , fresh veggies , or italian bread
demonstrations.review: This is an AWESOME recipe. Easy to make. I always order this when I go out and this is better than ANY that I have ever had. I did add a cup of mozzerella cheese and garnished with finely chopped tomatoes. Then served it with thin garlic cheese toast and chips. Everyone went WILD. You will not be disappointed with this recipe. Thanks for this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
another good pound cake

this cake has a nice texture and a crust that is just crunchy enough. i hope it is not already posted on recipezaar. i looked at many pound cakes and could not find an exact match. some called for 2 cups of powdered sugar but this one uses a whole pound.

1. cream butter or margarine and sugar well
2. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
3. add flour 1 / 2 cup at a time , beating in each addition before adding the next
4. when well blended , add the vanilla and lemon extracts
5. turn into a well greased and floured bundt pan
6. bake in preheated 350 degree oven for 45 to 55 minutes
7. cool briefly , then turn out onto serving plate
demonstrations.review: I have been looking for this recipe forever. My grandmother used to make this for me when I was a little girl. It is super easy and delicious.The powdered sugar and real butter make a wonderful difference in this cake. Definately a keeper. Thank you so much for posting this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pecan pie cake

this is absolutely to-die-for!!! once you try this delicious cake, you will want to make it again and again!!

1. combine cake mix , 1 egg , and melted butter together
2. set aside 2 / 3 cup of this batter
3. spread the rest into a greased and floured 9 by 13-inch baking pan and bake at 325 degrees fahrenheit for 15 minutes until lightly browned
4. mix reserved 2 / 3 cup batter with syrup , 3 eggs , brown sugar , vanilla and pecans
5. pour this filling on top of crust and cook for 50 to 60 minutes at 325 degrees fahrenheit or until set
demonstrations.review: I tried this and it was so good!!!! I substituted regular pancake syrup for the KARO as I do in all recipes that call for KARO and my family and coworkers went nuts. I will definately make this again and again. Super simple and no fail. GREAT RECIPE. I could eat the whole pan by myself. It is better the next day after it sets and all of the flavors mix and mingle.

target.recipe_text:
oven scrambled eggs for a crowd

cooking for a crowd? a really big crowd? use this easy recipe for an easy egg dish.

1. divide butter among four 13 x 9 inch baking dishes
2. combine eggs and salt
3. mix well
4. gradually stir in milk
5. pour evenly into baking dishes
6. bake , uncovered at 350f for 10 minutes
7. stir
8. bake 10-15 minutes more or until eggs are set
9. serve immediately
target.review: These were a hit!! So wonderful--it puffed up just a like a souffle! I just added 2 tablespoons of sour cream after I poured in the milk and some sliced swiss cheese on top whil it was baking. I did not stir it while baking since I wanted a casserole type consistency. I adjusted the recipe to serve 20 ladies this AM and they all loved how light and tasty it was! Thanks Miss Annie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gooey cinnamon rolls  bread machine recipe

this is the homemade version of the famous rolls you can buy at the mall.  for best results, serve fresh out of the oven.

1. rolls:
2. place ingredients in machine following the specifications of that particular machine
3. set for dough cycle
4. after complete on dough cycle , remove from machine and roll out to about 17x10" rectangle
5. filling:
6. mix together brown sugar and cinnamon
7. moisten the dough by brushing with milk
8. sprinkle brown sugar and cinnamon mixture over top
9. roll tightly from long end , pinching edges closed when completely rolled
10. slice rolled dough into 1 / 2" slices
11. place into greased cake pans or a cookie sheet
12. if using cake pans , use 3 9" pans
13. let rise until doubled
14. bake at 350 for 15-20 minutes , until golden
15. do not overbake
16. frosting: spread on very warm rolls
17. they are best when eaten fresh , but we have found that 10-15 seconds in the microwave rejuvenates them
demonstrations.review: Sublime! These cinnamon rolls were delicious and DH said they were the best he's ever had. The texture of the roll was soft and moist not dry like some handmade rolls. Thank you for sharing this terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twelve layer jello

kids and adults alike love this 'salad!' nice to slice & serve on a lettuce leaf (for presentation)- the colors can be varied to suit any holiday - greens & reds for christmas, varying shades of red for valentine's day, etc.. enjoy! this sounds like a lot of work, but it's really not. this is one i like to make when i'll be working around home all day, and can stop to do step after step. :)

1. add 1 cup boiling water to cherry jello
2. stir until dissolved
3. divide in half
4. to 1 / 2 the jello , slowly add 1 / 3 cup sour cream& stir until smooth
5. pour into a 9x13 pan
6. chill 25 minutes
7. add 2 tablespoons cold water to remaining jello& pour over first layer
8. let set 15 minutes
9. repeat process for each flavor , using flavors in given order for color effect
10. when completely cooled& firm , slice into squares& serve
demonstrations.review: This was so great WJKING! I made this for Thanksgiving weekend and everyone loved it and was in awe of the layers. So creamy, light and fruity! Not to mention beautiful! Thanks for sharing the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy quiche lorraine   wow  em

this recipe was shared with me by my friend marilyn, who is an amazing cook! enjoy!

1. prepare 9-inch pastry shell and bake for approximately 10 minutes until the crust seals to the bottom of the pie plate
2. cool completely
3. beat the eggs and add all other ingredients
4. pour into the cooled pie shell
5. bake at 325 for 35-40 minutes until custard is set
6. let cool for 5-10 minutes to finish 'setting' , and then serve
7. this quiche freezes well
8. the possibilities are endless !
demonstrations.review: This was delicious WJKING! I made this for brunch and another time for a light dinner with a salad. I added turkey bacon one time and made a veggie one with mushrooms, peppers, and onions. Both turned out great. What an easy recipe yet scrumptious results! My husband loved it too. Real men do each quiche! Thanks for sharing this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rich french onion soup

for all of those french onion soup lovers out there, here's one that can cook while you are doing everything else you have to do during your day. i got this one from quick cooking magazine.

1. in a large skillet , saut onions in butter until crisp-tender
2. transfer to an ungreased 5-quart slow cooker / crock pot
3. add the broth , worcestershire sauce , and bay leaves
4. cover and cook on low for 5 to 7 hours or until the onions are tender
5. discard bay leaves
6. top each serving with french bread and cheeses
demonstrations.review:
Delicious! I didn't have the time to let it simmer in the crockpot but it was just as good cooked on the stove!
I used half olive oil instead of all the butter and also added some thyme.
Great recipe Wjking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican beef enchiladas

a slightly different twist on an old favorite. just lovely served with spanish rice, beans or refritos, and guacamole or pico de gallo. posted in response to a recipe request.

1. prepare meat filling:
2. saute ground chuck in a medium skillet with next five ingredients over medium heat until no pink remains and meat is broken up into crumbles
3. stir in undrained kidney beans
4. make tomato sauce:
5. saute garlic and onion in oil over low / medium heat until golden
6. remove from heat
7. stir flour into garlic / onion / oil until smooth
8. stir in tomato puree , vinegar and dissolved bouillon cube broth
9. bring mixture to boiling point , stirring frequently , over medium heat until thickened
10. add chiles , cumin , salt and pepper
11. simmer , uncovered and stirring occasionally , about 5 minutes
12. to assemble enchiladas:
13. preheat oven to 350f and spray your pan with cooking spray
14. place about 1 / 3 cup filling in center of each tortilla
15. roll up
16. arrange , seam side down , in a 13 x 9 x 1-inch baking dish
17. pour tomato sauce over all and sprinkle with cheese
18. bake 25 minutes
19. reheat slightly to serve
demonstrations.review: This was really great. I just loved the Enchilada sauce. I pureed it and used chicken base since I didn't have beef bouillon --still tasted delicious. I also used chicken thighs and refried beans instead of ground chuck with flour tortillas since we prefer those over corn and everyone loved it. Thanks for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
evans farm inn apple crisp

this recipe comes from the evans farm inn, which used to be in mclean, va. the 40 acre farm is now being developed into apartments and houses. serve this wonderful crisp with a scoop of your favorite vanilla ice cream or a dollop of whipped cream.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a 2 quart rectangular baking dish
3. in a large bowl , blend apples with 3 / 4 tsp cinnamon , 1 cup sugar , and 2 tbs flour
4. place apples in the baking dish and dot with butter
5. in a medium bowl , place remaining sugar and flour , baking powder , remaining 1 tsp cinnamon , and salt
6. stir in egg until mixture is crumbly
7. sprinkle topping over apples and bake 30 minutes , or until apple mixture is bubbly and browned
target.review:
I used 4 Tbsp of flour to thicken the McIntosh apples I used which did the trick. 
I think the topping should call for 1 lg egg & a yolk or something.  My large egg didn't moisten all of the dry ingredients and so the dry flour just sat on the top like powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review:
I must've done something wrong.  I doubled everything and while it was easy, I never achieved a sticky glaze. Maybe I didn't have the gas turned up high enough?  The chicken was cooked thru so we at it.
I don't think the family want me to try it again, though I think I'm missing out on a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy double chocolate pudding

this is one of the best homemade puddings, forget about the boxed stuff this takes minutes to make and is much better! if you want deeper-flavored chocolate then use regular semisweet chocolate chips instead of milk chocolate chips --- this will yield 2-3 and may be doubled.

1. in a medium heavy-bottomed saucepan whisk together the sugar , cocoa , cornstarch and salt
2. add in the half and half and whipping cream
3. set the saucepan over medium heat and cook whisking constantly until the mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. remove from heat and add in vanilla and gently add in the milk chocolate chips and vanilla let stand for 5 minutes , the mix until the chocolate is completely mixed in
5. divide the mixture into 3 or four small dessert dishes
6. chill until cold
demonstrations.review:
This was a wonderful easy chocolate pudding.  I doubled it and used whole milk and Tropical Source semisweet chocolate chips from Whole Foods.  My chips weren't completely melted so my son thought I had small soft lumps!
Thanks for sharing your wonderful recipes with us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate icicle cookies

i have not made these into the icicle shapes but i have made this recipe into less time consuming shapes and still used the glaze and glitter (you can order the glitter online from king arthur flour). very yummy and pretty no matter what shape you choose. i put 24 cookies but that depends on how big you make them and i can't say how long it will take to make the icicles as i've not done that, so don't go by that it says below. i just had to put something in. prep time includes 4 hrs of chill time.

1. mix sugar , butter , milk , vanilla , egg and melted chips in a large bowl with a spoon till creamy
2. stir in flour , baking powder and salt
3. cover and refrigerate at least 4 hours until chilled
4. heat oven to 375f for each cookie , divide 1 round teaspoons of dough in half
5. roll each half into a 5" rope , tapering the ends
6. twist the ropes together
7. place 2" apart on ungreased cookie sheet
8. to hang icicles , poke a hole in the top of each cookie with a toothpick
9. bake 5-7 minutes or until set and very light brown
10. cool 2 minutes
11. remove from cookie sheet to a wire rack
12. cool completely
13. brush with white glaze and sprinkle with glitter or sugar
14. thread string through the hole in each cookie to hang if desired
demonstrations.review:
I've made these and they taste delicious.  I used a good quality white chocolate-Lindt Swiss White Bar.  I had trouble forming icicles and asked experts for their tips (read on).  I may try again using a little less flour.

From Katrina's Cookie Swap 2000 where I found the original recipe
"WORD OF WARNING: These are time consuming. On a positive note, Karen baked these for a cookie exchange and was told by many that they were quite delicious. An elegant Christmas cookie, but they take time."

I did have trouble making icicles. Here's some advice from experts: Chill dough very well. Work in a cool room. Work on a slap of marble chilled in the refrigerator for a few hours before working with the dough. If you don't have marble, fill a big tray of ice and a bit of water and leave it on your counter until it melts, dry well and work directly over it. Repeat as necessary.
Taste of Home has icicle directions: For icicles: Cut log into 1/4" slices; roll each into a 9â€� rope, tapering from the center to each end. Fold each rope in half; twist pinching the ends to a point. Place 2â€� apart on ungreased baking sheets.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread cake  spicy

adapted from a gourmet recipe, this spicy gingerbread originated from the gramercy tavern. it's excellent warm, and even better after one day. if you like a deep, spicy gingerbread, you might try this one!

1. butter a 10-inch bundt pan well and dust with flour , shaking out excess
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. generously butter bundt pan and dust with flour , knocking out excess
4. bring stout and molasses to a boil in a large saucepan and remove from heat
5. whisk in baking soda , then cool to room temperature
6. sift flour , baking powder , and spices in a large bowl
7. whisk together eggs and both sugars
8. whisk in oil , then molasses mixture
9. add to flour mixture and whisk until just combined
10. pour batter into bundt pan and bang pan sharply on counter to eliminate air bubbles
11. bake in middle of oven until a tester comes out with just a few moist crumbs adhering , about 50 minutes
12. cool cake in pan on a rack 5 minutes
13. turn out onto rack and cool completely
14. you can serve the gingerbread immediately , dusting lightly with confectioners sugar , and / or adding whipped cream
15. you can also hold the gingerbread for a day before serving , as the flavors develop with some time
demonstrations.review: Great gingerbread!! I've made this many times.  I use Guiness Stout.  I try to boil the Guiness stout and molasses early in the day and let it cool on the stove so the smell dissipates.  Very moist and addictive.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: I just made Oreo Truffles into little pumpkins.  My co-worker brought them in.  She dipped 1-inch balls in Wilton Orange Candy Melts and took a toothpick to pre-drill a hole before inserting a short broken straight pretzel for the stem!  She placed them on a plate with easter grass.  Too cute.

target.recipe_text:
corn dog cake

i got the idea from a corn dog muffin recipe. i did not have the correct ingredients. so i had to make due. my kids love it. they always have an extra piece. you can also substitute veggie hot dogs for the regular hot dogs. the brown sugar makes it a bit more sweet.

1. preheat oven to 350 f and lightly grease baking pan
2. combine flour , brown sugar , corn meal , baking powder , and salt in a bowl
3. mix together
4. set aside
5. combine milk , eggs , butter
6. mix well
7. add dry mixture to wet mixture , stir until just blended
8. pour into baking pan
9. cut hot dogs into bite size pieces
10. sprinkle hot dogs into mixture
11. bake at 350 f for 35 minutes or until golden brown
target.review: Have made these a couple of times now. Kids have loved them as muffins and as cake. They didn't seem to notice that I substituted whole wheat flour and added a little wheat germ and flax seed. lol Sneak it when  you can when it comes to the kids!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted pork loin

very yummy! we really enjoyed this.

1. preheat the oven to 375
2. season the pork and place in a roasting pan
3. in a separate bowl , mix together the honey , juice , oil and thyme
4. pour over the pork
5. add the broth to the pan
6. bake until internal temperature reaches 150
7. baste frequently
8. strain the pan juices into a saucepan small amount gravy flour
9. reduce until slightly thickened
10. serve over the sliced pork
demonstrations.review: Tasty. I made in the crockpot and the house smelled good.  I cooked it on high for 3 hours, next time I would probably do it on low as it was a little dry, but I just put some of the sauce drizzled over it and it was fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas best cheese dip  chile con queso

this is a delicious cheese dip that my daughter makes.  the cream cheese gives it a wonderful consistency. all the fresh ingredients make this a dip that you will be asked for over and over again! please note i have put "to taste" on alot of the ingredients as it depends on how big your bunch of veggies are.  if you actually get lucky enough to have any left it keeps in the fridge a good while and reheats great. i usually serve/take this dip in a crockpot so it stays warm.

1. melt cheeses together in microwave or on stove top
2. stir in all other ingredients
3. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Doubled the recipe and took it to a potluck. Everyone really liked it and I imagine it will be requested. I may never buy the stuff in the jar again. A trip to the farmers market got us fresh peppers and tomatoes. Yum. We used 1 lb. reg. velveeta and 1 lb. mexican velveeta just because we knew kids would be eating it also. Had a side of chopped up jalapenos if anyone wanted to kick it up a notch.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot   style loaded baked potato soup

if you like loading your baked potatoes will all those delish dairy ingredients, then you'll love this soup recipe, too! original recipe calls for only four slices of bacon, but i -- being a little piggy -- love the bacon, so we always use more like 8 to 12 slices. you decide which you prefer.

1. combine first seven ingredients in a large crock pot
2. cover and cook on high for 4 hours or low for 8 hours
3. mash mixture until potatoes are coarsely chopped and soup is slightly thickened
4. stir in cream , cheese and chives
5. top with sour cream , sprinkle with bacon and more cheese
demonstrations.review: This was excellent. Will make again and again. Might be one of the better soups I have ever made. I did as one reviewer suggested and put the potatoes in the food processor as we don't like the big chunks. The kids liked also. That is always a bonus.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled breakfast burrito

a soft flour tortilla, rolled and lightly grilled, filled with scrambled eggs, sausage, potatoes, onions, peppers, and two cheeses.

1. heat 1 / 4 cup of vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat
2. fry potatoes until almost cooked through , then add onions and peppers , continuing to cook until vegetables are tender
3. drain , set aside
4. in the same skillet , melt butter or margarine over medium heat
5. scramble eggs , adding potatoes , vegetables , and sausage during the last few moments of cooking
6. add salt and pepper to taste
7. top each tortilla with cheese and part of the egg mixture , roll into a burrito
8. spray a hot grill with cooking spray
9. grill for approximately 10 minutes or until lightly browned
10. serve hot with homemade pico de gallo , salsa , sour cream , or perhaps spanish rice and refried beans
demonstrations.review: Everyone enjoyed. Easy to make. I made 2 batches. I crushed up bacon instead of sausage and didn't have a grill, so put them in a 350 degree oven for 5 minutes to melt the cheese. I have never made burritos before and they were very easy, tasty and filling.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal  raisin  cookies

this was a long lost recipe that i got back at work. the activity lady made it for the patients in the health center and i tasted a cookie and got real happy. finally my long lost oatmeal cookie recipe. i think it is the best! i hope you do too.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl beat butter with an electric mixer on medium for 1 / 2 minute
3. add brown sugar , granulated sugar , baking powder , baking soda and cinnamon and cloves if desired
4. beat until well mixed , scraping sides of bowl occasionally
5. beat in eggs and vanilla extract until combined
6. beat in as much flour as you can with mixer , then stir in remaining flour with a wooden spoon
7. stir in rolled oats , mix well
8. if using raisins , stir in now
9. drop dough in rounded teaspoons 2 inches apart on ungreased cookie sheet
10. bake at 375f for 10-12 minutes or until edges are golden brown
11. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: These turned out great. Using a medium scoop I made 36 cookies. Everyone loved. I used the Pampered Chef cinnamon plus which as among other things has clover in it and I loved the hint of flavor that it added to the cookies. I also added 1 cup white chocolate chips instead of raisins. Nice flavor combiniation.

target.recipe_text:
easy baked macaroni and cheese

this is a family favorite that i learned from my mom. it has been passed down and i am sure it has changed over the years, but everyone that has it loves it.  i use it anytime i need a nice side dish in a pinch!! the left overs reheat nicely and never stick around more than a day or so!  i tend to cook by sight, so i did my best to approximate the measurements. i like to make this with fried chicken, grilled salmon, pork roast,etc with a fresh salad or veggie. it really is a versatile dish that leaves you free to tend to your main dish or dessert prep!!

1. pre-heat oven to 400
2. bring water to boil , then add pasta
3. cook uncovered for 8-10 minutes
4. while macaroni cooks , chop onions to desired consistency
5. drain pasta and rinse with hot water
6. place pasta back into pot with 2 tbsp butter and stir to cover so pasta does not stick
7. stir in onions and cheese
8. pour in heavy whipping cream and stir until nicely mixed
9. add garlic powder and black pepper to taste
10. scoop mixture into covered casserole dish and bake for 30 minutes , then check for desired bubbliness
11. )
12. enjoy !
target.review: I tasted this while vacationing with MD's family when MD made this specially for us.  It is super easy to prepare and makes a perfect sidedish to bbq meats or as a main dish for kids. I liked the creamy flavor of the sauce (it can be made thicker by adding more cheese or less cream).  Recipe makes a large batch.  I loved it as leftovers (and had it for breakfast and lunch).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
v s tri tip marinade

this is it! family favorite... :) in my family we eat this at least once a week. makes a nice sunday dinner. i prepare the marinade on saturday and let it sit until we're ready to bbq on sunday. i was absolutely honored when bobby flay did a show with this recipe slightly modified of course!  easy....delicious and the most tender flavor you'll never expect  prep time does not include time to marinade. the longer .... the better if you like a melt in your mouth tri-tip this is how i make it.

1. mix all of the ingredients except for the beef in a large mixing bowl to make the marinade
2. place trimmed tri-
3. let stand in the refrigerator for at least 6 hours heat grill to medium temperature
4. place tri-
5. remove the tri-
6. serve with your favorite side dishes
demonstrations.review:
I had this as part of a 4th of July bbq menu. The marinated tri tip was perfect off the grill. The meat was juicy and the flavors of the marinade didn't overpower the meat but added rich smoky flavors. Also, grilling the marinade created a bit of a crust that was excellent. The simplicity of the ingredients makes the recipe a keeper. Update: Over the weekend, I wanted to serve a casual dinner for my family that wouldn't be too difficult. I instantly thought of Chef V's marinated tri tip cooked on the grill. It turned out delicious--again--and got rave reviews from my mom who knows that I am truly just a fry cook. Don't be intimidated by amount of salt, it acts to tenderize the meat and cure it so that the meat comes out super flavorful. Excellent for making an impression on guests!
Update 2009 -- Still the best.  The meat is so tender.  Great for sandwiches the next day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon basil chicken and vegetables

this is a quick, simple one skillet chicken meal. this has an asian feel and taste, but my grandkids enjoyed it, nice way to get them to eat their veggies.

1. cook rice as directed on package
2. while rice is cooking , cut chicken into 2 x 1 / 4 inch strips
3. spray 12-inch nonstick skillet with cooking spray
4. heat over medium-high heat
5. add chicken to skillet
6. sprinkle with pepper and garlic powder
7. stir-fry 4 to 6 minutes or until brown
8. add onion
9. stir-fry 4 to 6 minutes or until brown
10. add onion
11. stir-fry 2 minutes
12. stir in frozen vegetables and water
13. heat to boiling
14. reduce heat to medium
15. cover and cook 5 to 6 minutes , stirring occasionally , until vegetables are tender
16. mix stir-fry sauce and cornstarch until smooth
17. stir into mixture in skillet
18. heat to boiling , stirring constantly
19. boil and stir 1 minute
20. divide rice among bowls
21. top with chicken mixture
demonstrations.review: I couldn't find the stir fry sauce in my local grocery store so I substituted bottled lemon pepper marinade and added fresh basil.  Not sure if this still constitutes the recipe but it was delicious!  Keeping with the Asian feel, I used (frozen) mixed vegetables with snap peas, green beans, water chestnuts, carrots and red peppers.  I even used brown rice in a packet that steamed in 5 mins.  The sauce very lightly coats the chicken and vegetables enabling you to taste all the flavors.  Very quick and easy to prepare recipe.  I think this is the perfect dish for spring and summer meals when you want something substantial yet light.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
v s chile verde

i'm always challenged to come up with my family's favorite mexican food. this is a tried and true recipe that is so easy to make that no one knows how simple but delicious chile verde can be. ***** served with recipe#282467 makes a complete meal ;)

1. mix all seasonings together in small bowl
2. mix beef boulion with water and pour in crock pot first
3. rub meat with seasoning , place in crock pot ,
4. cover and set on 6-8 hours
5. one hour before serving , drain pork drippings out leaving about 1 / 2 cup with meat
6. pour salsa verde on top and stir to break up meat
7. continue to cook
8. just before serving i add a cornstarch slurry to thicken it up
9. serve with spanish rice and beans and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was the hands down favorite meal prepared by Chef V for our group of friends during the 4th of July vacation.  The pork was juicy and had a wonderful Southwest picante flavor.  Served inside warm tortillas with salsa made it a filling meal.  And we had leftovers so in the morning for breakfast we burros with scrambled eggs. Yum, Yum, Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick honey mustard pork stir fry

a really easy pork stir fry that goes well with either rice & stir fried veggies or with potatoes & salad.
*note: i sometimes add 1 tsp minced garlic and/or 1 tsp minced ginger to the marinade to kick it up a notch!!

1. slice pork thinly
2. mix together the honey & mustard
3. marinate the pork in honey mustard mixture for at least 15-20 minutes
4. heat oil in nonstick wok or pan
5. add meat & stirfry with high heat until cooked , stirring & tossing all the time
6. serve with stir fried veggies & rice or potatoes & salad
demonstrations.review: My review echos Wildcook's: this recipe is tasty and easy to prepare.  I marinated the meat for more than an hour and also doubled the honey & mustard mix for extra sauce.  I added minced red chillies on top for some zing.  I bought mixed Asian vegetables for the side dish.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco salad   our way

this is the way my family enjoys our taco salad (and i sneak in a few veggies while we are at it!!)  it may vary a bit from time to time dependant on the ingredients on hand, but the basics are the same.
http://www.broccosprouts.com/

1. brown turkey and season with taco seasoning , black pepper and garlic to taste
2. on each plate spread desired amount of greens evenly
3. layer cooked turkey , peas , tomatoes , sprouts , and cheese in desired amounts then top with salsa for dressing
4. garnish with sour cream , black olives , jalepenos / green chiles and corn chips as you wish
5. enjoy !
6. )
demonstrations.review: I had this while visiting MD in Portland.  She omitted the broccoli and snap peas but the salad was still very filling; the turkey seasoning was just the right amount of spicy/heat and the turkey was the healthy alternative to beef.  Prepping the dish was so quick and it was easy to assemble.  We had the hot salsa which perfectly accentuated the meal.

target.recipe_text:
chipotle pork roast

a little bit spicy, a little bit sweet. definitely moist. it's the best roast i've ever made.

1. place pork roast in baking dish
2. in a separate bowl , assemble the remaining ingredients , stir well
3. pour marinade over roast , cover and place in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour
4. in a preheated oven , cook at 500 degrees for 10 minutes , then reduce heat to 300 degrees
5. cook until roast reaches an internal temperature of 170 degrees
6. allow to cool five minutes before serving
target.review: This was wonderful, i used chipotle chiles in adobe sauce, and minced them finely, I also covered the roast for the last 1/2 hour and this resulted in a lovely juicy sauce to pour over the pork when served. I will definately be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive mexican stew

my mother gave me this recipe.  she found it while clipping coupons.  it is from s&w.  this is the best stew i have ever eaten and my family requests me to make it quite frequently.  it has become a 

1. cook onion and garlic in oil in large saucepan until tender
2. add cooked chicken , taco seasoning , tomatoes , beans , corn and chilies
3. blend broth and cornstarch
4. add to saucepan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer 15 minutes
7. stirring occasionally
8. serve with cornbread for a hearty meal
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty, i didnt have green chilies, and used fresh chopped hot peppers instead, I served over rice, sprinkled cilantro over the top and added cheese and sour cream. This was devoured by four hungry teenagers with plenty left over for the rest of us.Now i have a great recipe to use up all the turkey at thanksgiving and xmas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jalapeno relish

this recipe has been in our family since 1976.  it was my dad's recipe given to him by a friend.  he won 3rd place at the southern new mexico state fair in 1978.  he passed away that month and never knew he won.  so you can say this a very special recipe in our family.  it is like a canned pico de gallo.  you can eat it with tortilla chips or mix in with scrambled eggs or whatever you prefer.

1. chop jalapenos , tomatoes and onion
2. mix vegetables together with garlic and oregano
3. set aside
4. mix together vinegar and water
5. set aside
6. fill jars with vegetable mixture to 1 / 2 inch from top of jars
7. to each jar add 1 tsp each of salt and sugar
8. then add liquid to jars to 1 / 2 inch from top
9. seal jars and process in water bath for 45 minutes
10. start counting when water comes to boil
demonstrations.review: Great stuff, we consumed half a jar in one sitting and my DH asked me to make another batch, so we would have plenty for the winter. To be honest i guestimated the amount of tomtoes and peppers. I used fresh cayenne peppers ,so i had to be cautious adding theses as they are really hot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4th of july grilled salmon  or chicken

a friend of mine made this at last year's 4th of july celebration, and after much begging and groveling, shared this super-easy, fun, and very yummy recipe, which you can easily double or triple for a big crowd!   the cold left-overs (if any) the next day are fabulous!  try this with chicken!!  grill 4 chx breasts 4-5 min ea side, then finish in 350 degree oven in covered pan with butter & olive oil for +/-20 min.  oh!  magnificent (great sandwiches w/tomato, cream cheese, and avocado).

1. into a large zip-lock bag , make marinade out of peanut oil , soy sauce , vinegar , onions , brown sugar , garlic , ginger , red pepper flakes , sesame oil and salt
2. combine well , and insert fish or chicken
3. seal and marinate in refrigerator 4-24 hours
4. oil and preheat grill on medium-high heat
5. grill fish ~5 minutes per side , until fish just flakes with a fork
demonstrations.review: This was amazing, I tried it on salmon and chicken and loved both. the marinade is just slap youre' Momma GOOD, will be using this over and over again. I turned the grill up to high for the last minute to caramelize it. i used chicken breast and marinated it for 6 hours and it was so juicy and tender, it was amazing. Yhanks for posting a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
terrific iced tea

this delicious iced tea is a real thirst quencher on a hot summer's day.  cook time is chill time.

1. steep tea and mint leaves in boiled spring water for 10 minutes
2. strain
3. zest orange and lemon rinds , avoiding the white pith
4. squeeze the juice of the orange and lemon into a large jug , add the strained tea , fruit zest and sugar
5. stir well to make sure sugar is dissolved
6. chill and serve over ice
7. hint: freeze some of this mixture into ice cubes !
demonstrations.review: I made a batch of this ,this morning and now i cant stop drinking it, i admit to using a family size tea bag, instead of the loose tea; I just love the fruit rind in it.Being a Brit in America, it has taken a few years for me to get used to my tea being cold , but i love this recipe, very refreshing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smothered pork chops

this is a delicious way to do chops, fall off the bone tender.

1. brown chops in microwave , cut off any fat
2. mix remaining ingredients and pour over chops
3. bake in 350 degree oven for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I loved the flavors of this recipe..it saved our dinner last night:I had started a sauerkraut and pork chops recipe and half way thru I decided I didnt like the look of it so quickly whipped together this sauce and poured it over my previously browned chops, and served it with garlic mash potato and suerkraut cooked with apples and onions ( the aborted recipe )

target.recipe_text:
deluxe spiced tea mix

i keep this in my pantry year round. wonderful pick-me up. great to give as gifts

1. combine all ingredients , stirring well
2. store in an airtight container
3. to serve , place 1 tablespoon plus 1 teaspoon mixture in a cup
4. add 1 cup boiling water , stirring well
target.review: I have made this for many years except for out the red hots. Adding them sounded like a wonderful idea so I tried it. Fabulous. Just adds more intense cinnamon flavor which I really liked. I am going to make another batch and give this out as Christmas gifts to my co-workers and friends. Thanks Nurse Di.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli and wild rice casserole

this dish has become a family holiday favorite. i have tried many broccoli-rice dishes and this one is the best in my opinion. see what you think.

1. cook rice according to package directions
2. cook broccoli according to package directions
3. when broccoli is cooked , use paper towels to absorb any excess water
4. mix together rice , broccoli , cream of chicken soup , cheez whiz , and water chestnuts
5. pour into casserole dish
6. bake in pre-heated oven at 350 degrees for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have tasted many a broccoli-rice casserole and this one in my opinion is the best. I think the seasonings in the wild rice mix really zest this up. I also think the water chestnuts are a huge plus. We loved the crunchy texture. Rich and cheesy which is what you would expect.  Very yummy!! Thanks Nurse Di.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled rib eye steaks

the marinade is asian-flavored.

1. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the first 7 ingredients
2. add the steaks
3. seal the bag and turn to coat
4. refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight
5. drain and discard marinade
6. grill steaks , uncovered , over medium-hot heat for 8-10 minutes or desired doneness
demonstrations.review: My husband has grilled almost every meal we have eaten this summer. This recipe has become a favorite of ours. The marinade is delicious and produces very juicy, tender, mouth-watering steaks. He has made these about once a week and we haven't gotten tired of them yet. Thanks Nurse Di.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s gingersnaps

another one of my grandmother's incredible recipes. this was a special treat when i was a little girl.

1. in a large mixing bowl , cream the shortening and sugar
2. beat in the egg and molasses
3. combine the flour , baking soda , ginger , cinnamon , and salt
4. gradually add to the creamed mixture
5. roll teaspoonfuls of dough into balls
6. dip one side of each ball into sugar
7. place with sugar side up on a greased baking sheet
8. bake at 350 degrees for 12-15 minutes or until lightly browned and crinkly
demonstrations.review: These cookies were so wonderful. I made them during Christmas. Intense smell while baking. Very tender and soft in the middle. Wonderful ginger-molasses flavor Not only did my family enjoy them, but we put them on a plate for Santa. They were all gone on Christmas morning so he must have liked them too. Thanks Nurse Di.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican stuffed shells  oamc

you can add jalapeños, hot sauce or green chilies to this to add a real kick! **edited on october 24 to add instructions for once a month cooking. i usually make these during a cooking blitz and freeze until i need them**

1. brown ground beef and drain
2. add seasoning , water , onion , and 1 / 2 cup of salsa and 1 / 4 cup cheese
3. mix together remaining salsa , tomato sauce , and chili powder
4. spread a thin layer of sauce on the bottom of a 9 x 12 baking pan
5. fill each shell with the ground beef mixture and place in pan
6. pour remaining sauce on top
7. sprinkle on the rest of the cheese on top and garnish with green onion
8. cover and freeze at this point
9. defrost overnight and bake at 350f for 30 minutes
10. if desired sprinkle additional cheese on top after baking and return to oven for 5 minutes longer or until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I have been in a cooking rut and wanted something different for dinner. This was perfect and my family and I thought it was delicious. I used cheddar cheese because that is what I had but I think pepper-jack cheese would be a great idea, too. Will try it with that next time. The recipe worked as written. I wouldn't change anything. Thanks Pamela.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
festive cranberry salad

cook time includes freezer time.

1. in a bowl , combine milk and lemon juice
2. mix well
3. stir in pineapple , cranberry sauce , marshmallows , pecans , and cool whip
4. spoon into a 13x9 inch baking dish
5. freeze until firm , 4 hours or overnight
6. cut into squares
demonstrations.review: This frozen salad was outstanding. Had a sweet-tart flavor and a luscious creamy texture. The cranberry flavor was the perfect accompaniment for our pork dinner. Kids and adults all liked this at my house. Thanks for this one.

target.recipe_text:
rachael ray apple cake

this is called "my sister maria's easy apple cake".  it is a quick and yummy cake for dessert. good warm and topped with ice cream. it bakes in a 9x9 pan, so you do not have a ton of cake. just enough for a nice weekday dessert.  **please note the size of the cake mix.  it is a little box, i use the jiffy cake mix.  i have made this cake many times to take with a meal i have made for a friend that has been sick or had a baby.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9 by 9-inch square cake pan with 1 tbs butter
3. prepare cake mix as described on cake box , with 1 / 2 cup water and the egg
4. peel and dice apple into small bits
5. sprinkle apples with cinnamon and sugar and mix well
6. pour cake batter into prepared cake pan
7. spread apples on top of cake batter , evenly covering the entire top of the cake
8. bake 20 to 25 minutes
9. best if served warm with ice cream
10. very good at room temperature though
target.review:
Really, really good!  

Would you believe the grocery store didn't have the Jiffy cake mixes?  I bought a Pillsbury one and just measured out 9 oz of mix and then used one egg and the 1/2 cup of water per your instructions. I ended up having to bake it for twice as long as you indicated, but that was probably due to the different cake mix.  It turned out moist, yummy and was soooo good warm.  We really liked how quick it was to make and how it doesn't make too much at one time.  This is definitely a keeper.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best blasted rapid roast whole chicken

blasting with high heat will shrink the skin and seal in all the juices to create an extremely moist and tender chicken with lovely crispy skin - and it will be on your table in about an hour. this method will also work with a larger chicken, but cooking time will need to be increased. you may adjust all seasonings to taste. if you are not a lemon lover, then you may omit the lemon juice. you really can use whatever seasoning that you like for this. i like to use seasoned salt. make certain to use a fork and poke holes all over in the lemon, then place it into the cavity of the chicken. roast roast as stated. the chicken with be moist and have a faint lemon flavor. for more of my tried-and-true recipes, visit my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com.

1. rinse the chicken inside and out well under cold water , then pat dry using a paper towel
2. in a small bowl mix the lemon juice with oil and melted butter until blended , then rub all over the chicken
3. using clean hands rub the inside and outside of the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder , black pepper and cayenne
4. place the lemon / s inside the cavity
5. place the chicken into a baking dish
6. using cotton string tie the legs together tightly
7. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 6 hours
8. set oven to 450 degrees f
9. roast the chicken at 450 degrees for 20 minutes , then reduce the heat to 400 degrees and continue roasting for about 40 minutes
10. cover with foil and let sit for 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Good Lord, woman! I don't need to repeat anything that hasn't already been said. I will say this. I do not like breasts/white meat.  This was the most amazingly juicy and tender chicken I have ever made.  While the kitchen did get a bit smokey (forgot to turn on the fan), that's the only negative I'd have to say and that won't make me deduct a star. I took the leftovers and made them into chicken salad for sandwiches for the rest of the week. My husband thinks I'm more of a Goddess than he already believed.  You rock.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy swiss chard pasta

quick - easy - tasty from lakeside organic gardens.

1. wash swiss chard , cut into small pieces
2. heat oil in large 2 quart saucepan over medium high heat , 1 to 2 minutes
3. add swiss chard , garlic and onion
4. cooking 1 to 2 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. add tomatoes , sour cream , milk , parmesan cheese , cooked fettuccine , salt and pepper to taste
6. stir well
7. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I joke that if the DH wants it again, it's a 5 star review.  No joking.  This was amazing.  After reading all the reviews I was really worried about the clumping of the chard.  (Also, it was my first time cooking/eating chard.)  After making this dish, I'm of the belief that the reviewers who experienced "clumping" cooked the chard too long initially.  I can really see how that could happen.  This recipe was so easy, fun to make and fairly healthy!  I served it with some garlic bread.  Sooo yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brioche loaf   breadmaker 1 1 2 lb  loaf

this recipe is from fleischmann's yeast company. i love egg breads, especially for french toast and bread pudding.

1. measure all ingredients into bread machine pan in the order suggested by manufacturer
2. process on sweet or basic / white bread cycle
3. use light or medium / normal crust color setting
4. remove bread from pan
5. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: 5 stars for sure.  I loved this recipe.  It was easy and filled the breadmaker.  I set it for 2 pounds, white & light crust.  About half the loaf was gone within the first hour after it was done.  Sooo yummy.  DH has already requested another loaf of it 24 hours later.  This will be a staple in our home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reese s peanut butter bars

this is the recipe my husband always requests when he is having a lunch event at work. they are foolproof and have a rich, homemade flavor.

1. heat oven to 350
2. grease 13x9 pan
3. melt butter
4. add peanut butter , stir until melted
5. stir in sugar and vanilla
6. add eggs
7. with spoon , stir until well blended
8. add flour , baking powder and salt
9. stir until blended
10. stir in chocolate chips
11. spread batter into prepared pan
12. bake 35 minutes or until top is golden brown and edges are firm
13. cool completely in pan on wire rack
14. cut into bars
demonstrations.review:
I'm not sure what I did wrong here, but the chocolate chips melted immediately in the batter.  Perhaps the I misread the instructions and should have transferred things to other mixing bowls.

That being said, the bars turned out very yummy, melted chips and all and we've been enjoying them since Christmas.  I'll deifnitely try making these again, this time allowing things to cool or using more mixing bowls.

Thanks1

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kung pao shrimp with cashews

chiles add heat to succulent shrimp with cashews. it is essential to have all ingredients cut and ready before you start. from food & wine magazine.

1. in a bowl , mix the orange juice , vinegar , soy sauce , sugar and cornstarch
2. in a wok or large frypan , heat the oil over high heat until smoking
3. add the chiles and salt
4. stir-fry until browned , 45 seconds
5. add the onion , ginger and garlic
6. stir-fry until fragrant , 15 seconds
7. add the peppers and cook until crisp-tender , 30 seconds
8. add the shrimp and stir-fry until nearly cooked through , about 5 minutes
9. stir the sauce , add to the wok and cook until thickened slightly , 30 seconds
10. stir in the cashews and sesame oil
11. serve
demonstrations.review: Really, really good and the DH said, "Definitely a keeper."  I was a bit skeptical about the orange juice in it, but it added such a great flavor.  We loved the zip the chilies gave it.  You were absolutely right about it being essential to have everything chopped, prepped and ready to go before cooking as it all comes together quite quickly and would have been a disaster if we hadn't prepped beforehand.  Thanks for a definite keeper.  Beats a restaurant hands down - especially because we could add as many shrimp and cashews as we wanted!  :)

target.recipe_text:
five  or more   ingredient garlic quinoa

this makes such a nice side dish. i even like it cold as a salad the next day! 06/28/08 - update!!  as i have already said, i like this for a salad too.
today i added some chopped egg whites, chopped black olives, some scallions (green and white). i then tossed with one tbls each of evoo and red wine vinegar.  realllllly good!    07/24/08 - another update!  wow, instead of using the fresh garlic, use roasted!  i had several bulbs roasting while i was making dinner. they smelled sooo good and that is when i figured it could only make this dish better. just leave out the minced garlic and when the dish is finished, stir in about five squeezed out chopped cloves and then serve. yum!  07/29/08 - still another update!  i have really gotten on the quinoa bandwagon. put together two more recipes, so if you like quinoa as much as me, take a look. i'm not bragging, just sharing a good thing....recipe#316192 and recipe#316159.

1. make sure you rinse the grain under cold running water several times to remove coating
2. spray medium size saucepan with vegetable oil
3. add onion & cook about 3 minutes , add garlic & cook another 2 minutes
4. add rest of ingredients & bring to a boil
5. reduce heat , stir and cover
6. simmer 15 minutes or until all the water is absorbed
target.review: This was the first time I had tried quinoa and it was very tasty.  Thanks for adding the toasted quinoa recipe/suggestion.  I used sweet onions but no carrots and it still tasted great.  I made this with Veal Cutlets with Balsamic Sauce (Recipe #49051) and Roasted Broccoli Florets with Toasted Breadcrumb Gremolata (from Epicurious.com).  Very good dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
100  whole wheat buttermilk pancakes

most whole wheat pancake recipes sneak in some refined flour, but not these!  
great to make ahead and freeze for later.

1. preheat non-stick skillet over medium heat
2. using whisk , combine all ingredients until smooth
3. pour approximately 1 / 4 c batter into skillet
4. when edges begin to bubble and lift from skillet , flip pancakes
5. cook both sides until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These pancakes are yummy.  I've made them a couple of times now and this past time made them for my roommate.  She was surprised at how good they were (with the whole wheat and flaxseed).  I love flaxseed and this is one ingredient that made the recipe attractive for me.  I like to freeze these and heat them in the microwave (one minute, wrapped in a paper towel) for a quick breakfast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: This was a great, simple recipe for tilapia.  I've had something similar once before and I remember loving it.  I didn't have any seasoning salt or hot pepper sauce so I just used table salt and a pinch of cayenne pepper.  I served it with Creamy Parmesan Leeks (Recipe #23959), Lemon Herb Quinoa (Recipe #65131), and Caesar salad (for those who refused to the eat the leeks).  The fish was a great success!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
comfort food baked custard

easy to make,easier to enjoy! this custard is done when it appears set but still jiggles slightly. the custard will firm up as it cools. bet you can't just eat a little!

1. heat oven to 350
2. in large bowl , combine eggs , sugar , salt and vanilla
3. blend well
4. gradually stir in milk
5. pour into 6 ungreased 6-oz
6. custard cups
7. sprinkle with nutmeg
8. place custard cups in 13x9 inch pan
9. pour boiling water into pan around custard cups to a depth of 1 inch
10. bake at 350 for 45 to 55 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
11. serve warm or cold
12. store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I didn't really like this but it was probably because I've never really had custard before and I didn't know what to expect.  It did have a strong egg flavor and it was really watery.  I added extra sugar before cooking but then had to add more after it was cooked.  This looks so good.  I wish I had liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frijoles negros  cuban black beans

ay caramba, these are good!

1. fry the onion and pepper in a little oil
2. add the garlic and saute a little
3. introduce a little of the bean liquid until all previous ingredients are soft
4. add the beans with the remaining liquid
5. add spices and simmer about 30 minutes
6. add the vinegar just before serving
7. these are quite good when served over a bed of rice seasoned with just lime
demonstrations.review: These were absolutely amazing! I didn't think I liked black beans, but I found a can in the pantry so I thought I might as well use them for a quick lunch. This turned out to be a very quick lunch, and one of the best I've had in a while! I had to omit the onion and green pepper because I didn't have any and I drained and rinsed the canned beans that I used to take away some of the extra sodium. I just added water in place of the liquid. I made some tacos with the beans, Low Carb Taco Shells (Recipe #85258) and some tuna (mixed with a little over a Tbsp. mayo, the juice of half a lime, salt, and a great deal of cracked black pepper). Fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with chicken in creamy garlic sauce

wonderful pasta dish in a great creamy garlic sauce. i also have used crab meat instead of the chicken.

1. boil pasta in lightly salted water
2. fry chicken in canola until lightly browned , set aside
3. in large pot saut garlic in butter or margarine , do not brown
4. add flour , salt , pepper , and nutmeg to garlic and butter or margarine and mix to form a roux
5. slowly add milk , whisking to prevent lumps
6. add parmesan cheese and mix well
7. cook over medium heat stirring often until sauce thickens
8. add chicken , mushrooms , and peas to the sauce
9. drain cooked pasta and mix into sauce
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic recipe!  I used angel hair pasta instead of shell pasta and skim milk and whole wheat flour.  I also omitted the mushrooms and peas.  (I know, I know - I changed everything!).  This has such a great flavor and it was so easy to make.  I love that it's not so bad for you as alfredo, but it tastes similar.  In my opinion, better than alfredo.

target.recipe_text:
moroccan chicken tagine  crock pot

i'm always looking for new ways to spruce up my monthly menu. this is a great twist to plain ole chicken.

1. place chicken in crock pot slow cooker
2. combine broth , tomatoes with juice , onions , apricots , garlic , cumin , cinnamon , ginger , coriander , red pepper and cilantro in medium bowl
3. pour over chicken
4. cover
5. cook on low 4 to 5 hours or until chicken i no longer pink in center
6. transfer chicken to serving platter
7. cover to keep warm
8. combine cornstarch and water in small bowl
9. mix until smooth
10. stir cornstarch mixture and beans into crock pot slow cooker
11. cover
12. cook on high 15 minutes or until thickened
13. pour sauce over chicken
14. sprinkle with cilantro and toasted almonds
15. sever with couscous or rice
target.review: Wow, this was a great discovery!  I was trying to find a slow cooker recipe that would help me get rid of a pantry full of chick peas.  I don't even like dried apricots but they really added a delicious and unique flavour to this dish.  I made the recipe as outlined and served it on couscous.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mandarin orange spinach salad

delicious, refreshing salad that can really be adapted to your tastes. i got this from a friend and have had many rave reviews whenever i serve it.

1. in a jar , combine all ingredients for the dressing
2. shake well and refrigerate for at least one hour to blend flavours
3. in a heavy skillet , cook almonds and sugar over medium heat until sugar melts and coats almonds , stirring frequently
4. cool
5. break apart if necessary
6. in large bowl , combine spinach , celery and green onions
7. just before serving , add almonds and orange segments
8. toss gently
9. pour dressing over salad and toss
10. p
11. s
12. i always double the amount of almonds because they really add a wonderful flavour to the salad-- and because some mysteriously disappear before they make it to the salad !
demonstrations.review: Mmmm, this is a nummy salad and a great way to use up a few of those leftover Christmas mandarins!  I changed the dressing a bit by adding a few slices of fresh ginger and running it through the blender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
leftover steak skillet
