this is the name that my daughter came up with, for my most requested lamb dish! she did not realise how easy it was to cook, as the results are so sophisticated and special! i have never made it other than in the crock-pot, but i am sure it would cook very well in an aga or wood burning range......long and slow. this is an all year around recipe, as we have cooked this in the summer and served this meltingly tender lamb with salads and crusty bread - as well as in the winter with mountains of mashed potatoes! the redcurrant and honey glaze is sensational, and makes the most divine gravy or sauce. do not be tempted to use a cheap and low fruit content redcurrant jelly, it gives nowhere near the same taste and results as a high fruit jelly. i always use a leg of lamb for this dish - but i suspect that shoulder of lamb would work extremely well. be warned......this is a fall off the bone, moist and very succulent way of cooking lamb!!

1. if the leg of lamb is too big for your crock-pot , cut through the joint between the main leg and shank
2. put 2 tablespoons water into the crock-pot and place the lamb inside
3. spoon the honey , dijon mustard and redcurrant jelly over the top of the lamb
4. sprinkle the crushed garlic / powdered garlic , salt & black pepper over the top of the lamb
5. cook on high for at least 6 hours and up to 8 hours - yes , on high ! if it is a 4lb to 5 lb leg of lamb , these are the perfect timings - it falls off the bone and is moist and tender
6. about 30 minutes before serving , carefully ladle most of the juices out of the crock pot and into a large mixing jug
7. allow the juices to cool and skim the fat that rises to the surface
8. place the juices into a saucepan and bring to the boil , boil vigorously until it has reduced by about a half - you now have the most wonderful gravy or sauce to serve alongside the lamb !
9. take the lamb out and allow to "rest" for about 10-15 minutes before carving and falling in love !
target.review: Made this for Christmas Dinner. Got up at 4:30 am to put it on and was back in bed by 4:40. Spectacular! The meat literally fell off the bone (I had even forgotten to add the water). The family members who sniffed they would never eat lamb devoured it. My lamb-loving kids asked me to fix it every day. I did add a couple of rosemary sprigs, as other reviewers suggested. Next time I will use some of my home made plum jam, instead of the store bought red currant jelly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christmas broccoli salad

great at christmastime!  red and green colors make this salad so festive!  so easy to make and looks great in a trifle dish or glass bowl.

1. in a large bowl , combine the first five ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine the mayonnaise , cider vinegar and pepper until smooth
3. pour dressing over broccoli mixture
4. toss to coat
5. cover and refrigerate until serving
demonstrations.review: Although there a lot of great broccoli salad recipes on the Zaar, I tried this one because of the "Christmas" in the name. I particularly liked the addition of the sweet red peppers. I used red onion instead of green; rice vinegar instead of cider vinegar; sunflower seeds instead of pecans, and added dried cranberries (to make it even more Christmas-y). Like another reviewer, I added sugar -- 1 TBSP of organic sugar to the dressing. Also used Light Hellman's mayo and center cut bacon to cut down on the fat and calories. My dinner party group snarfed it down!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango lassi frozen yogurt  for ice cream maker

mango lassi happens to be one of my favorite dairy treats, so the combination of "frozen" and "lassi" seemed like an obvious one. i hope you enjoy this frozen treat as much as i do on a hot day.

1. first begin by pureeing two fresh mangoes in a blender with just enough water as was necessary to grind them to a smooth mixture
2. combine 16 oz of greek yogurt together with the mango mixture and 1 / 2 cup sugar in the ice cream maker
3. while the mixture was churning in an ice cream maker , add 1 / 2 tsp cardamom and 3 drops yellow food coloring for a vibrant yellow color
4. also add 1 / 2 tsp vanilla extract
5. after 30 minutes of churning , the frozen mango lassi will be ready to be frozen in a freezer
6. allow to freeze for at least four hours before serving
demonstrations.review:
I used homemade yogurt, which I let drain for a few hours until it was thick and creamy; added 3 to 4 Tbsp of frozen orange juice concentrate; and pureed partially thawed frozen organic mangoes -- this was very good, and not too sweet! It has frozen to a very creamy texture, not icy.
I might try a bit  of fresh grated ginger next time and a tad less of cardomom.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s chicken soup

this isn't my dad's chicken soup recipe, it's just what it was called. i think this originally came from bon appetit. i have always made it with pasta instead of rice. the thyme in this is what makes it tasty. prep time does not include cooking the chicken.

1. bring first five ingredients to boil in heavy large pot or dutch oven over high heat
2. mix in rice and thyme
3. return soup to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium and simmer uncovered until rice is tender , stirring occasionally , about 30 minutes
5. add chicken and simmer until heated through , thinning with additional broth if desired
6. season with salt and pepper
7. transfer soup to large bowl
8. garnish with parsley and serve
9. i like corkscrew pasta in this
demonstrations.review: Excellent flavor. Used home-made chicken stock, extra fresh garlic cloves, and Lundberg's wild rice blend. Sauteed the veggies with the thyme in a splash of olive oil, then added the broth and rice. Next time will try with fresh thyme.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean and chile stir fry sauce   oamc

skip the high-sodium, low-taste soy sauce and make a big batch of this sauce instead. you can freeze individual servings into plastic baggies or an ice cube tray so that you can use it as needed. from "can i freeze it?" by susie theodorou.

1. after you've sliced and diced everything , thoroughly mix all of the ingredients in a bowl
2. serve immediately with a stir-fry as appropriate , or freeze
3. to freeze , allow the sauce to cool and portion it out into ice cube trays or freezer-safe plastic baggies
4. alternatively , you can use it as a marinade for the meat of your choice , and freeze that instead
5. make sure that you get all of the air out of your plastic bag , and that it is laying flat and fully squished while freezing
demonstrations.review: I purchased some preserved black beans (called salted black beans at my oriental market) and was looking for ways to use them up so decided to make this sauce. 6 inches of ginger sounded like a lot to me, so I used a big toe's worth, grated (I keep mine in the freezer). Also used organic sugar, and a liberal sprinkling of red pepper flakes since I didn't have fresh red chilies. Assumed the rice wine was supposed to mean sake. Taste is fantastic -- like a jazzed up teriyaki sauce!! I just haven't decided what to marinate with it yet but will update my review when I do!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried red lentil dahl

when i first posted this recipe, i hadn't made it, i had posted it for a tag game,  but encouraged by the positive reviews it has received,  i made it this weekend, and took it as a gift for my friend, who loves hot curries and dahls.   its a little hot for my personal taste, but she loved it!     easy and quick to make, it comes from the 
very easy vegetarian cookbook, by simon & alison holst

1. heat the oil in a large pan
2. cook onion and garlic , stirring frequently , until the onion has softened and is turning clear
3. add bay leaf and spices and cook , stirring continuously , for 1 to 2 minutes longer
4. cover the pan with a lid whilst simmering , so that the liquid does not evaporate too quickly
5. cook until the lentils are tender , about 25 - 30 minutes
6. stir in the coriander and serve
7. suggested accompaniments , steamed rice , naan bread , poppadoms
demonstrations.review: I really liked this recipe as a side for a roasted pork with mango curry sauce dish -- I used red split lentils (known as Masoor Dal). And, after sauteing the onion, garlic and spices in a cast iron skillet, I put the lentils, just water (had no broth on hand) and the onion-spice mixture into a rice cooker on the rice setting just for fun, to see what would happen. I ended up added another 1/2 to 2/3rds cup of water, and had to open the cooker to stir the lentils  a couple of times while it was cooking, but it turned out really well. Next time, I may add some fresh grated ginger and more freshly ground black pepper, but overall, a very nice accompaniment to pork, in particular.

target.recipe_text:
roasted brussels sprouts

i got this from the barefoot contessa cookbook. so good.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cut off the ends of the brussels sprouts and pull off any yellow outer leaves
3. mix them in a bowl with the olive oil , salt , and lemon-pepper seasoning
4. transfer them to a sheet pan and roast for 35 to 40 minutes , until crisp outside and tender inside
5. shake the pan from time to time to brown the brussels sprouts evenly
6. sprinkle with more kosher salt , if you like , and serve hot
target.review: This is one of my new favorite recipes! So easy to make! I cut the oil a bit, and no lemon pepper (just black) and a bit of salt. The crispy parts are the best! Never thought i'd say i love brussels sprouts, but these are beyond delicious :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bestest hamburger soup

i think this is our #1 all time family favorite and it's often requested for birthday dinners. it's the 'bestest' because my daughter described it as such when she was little.  this freezes well and i've added directions for that and for reheating.

1. in a large saucepan , brown meat , drain excess fat
2. add salt , pepper , oregano , basil , seasoned salt , and onion soup mix
3. stir in boiling water , tomato sauce , and soy sauce
4. cover and simmer for about 15 minutes
5. meanwhile , prepare celery , celery leaves , and carrots
6. then add to simmering mixture with split peas and continue to cook for 30 minutes
7. add macaroni and simmer for 30 minutes longer , adding more water if necessary and stirring occasionally
8. serve sprinkled with parmesan cheese over individual servings
9. to freeze: place soup in a rigid container and freeze
10. to reheat: remove from freezer and thaw
11. place soup in saucepan and heat , stirring , until hot
demonstrations.review: good stuff! this is my kinda food! my hubby isn't a fan of soup, and after reading all the reviews i was hoping he'd like this, but no go lol.. soup is soup.. i will definitely be making this again! my only changes were i didn't have any seasoning salt and i halved the salt (the soy and onion soup scared me so i waited to taste, but it was perfect without) and i cooked the pasta on its own and threw it in near the end.. perfect! thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
split pea soup  crock pot    dairy free

very little prep, just layer in crock pot/slow cooker, leave it for the day and a filling, delicious soup will be ready for dinner.

this recipe is a very versatile base split pea soup.  for a vegan option, omit the meat. i have made this recipe using ham, ham hock, and bacon. i have used veggie broth, chicken broth and water... each tasting different but yummy! i have reduced the salt but have not adjusted the recipe as written. this soup is even better the next day, it freezes well. this tends to be a thicker soup (especially once it has cooled) so adjust liquid after cooking to desired thickness.

1. layer ingredients in crockpot
2. pour in water , so don't stir
3. cover and cook on high 4-5 hours or on low for 8-10 hours
4. remove bay leaf
5. serve with some nice crusty bread or buns
demonstrations.review: this was my first attempt at making any type of soup, let alone using the crock pot. oddly enough i was missing half the ingredients, yet it still came out great! used bacon instead of ham, had no celery or carrots,  so i diced a few potatoes and threw them in after the first few hours. no bay leaf, and used bullion instead of just water. i'm ready to make this again, except now i have all my veggies (will still use the potatoes, they cooked perfectly), and bought bay leaves! thanks for the recipe :) cant wait to have this again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
unbelievable chicken

copied from allrecipes.com to keep my collection in one place.

1. in a large non-reactive container , mix the cider vinegar , mustard , garlic , lime juice , lemon juice , brown sugar , salt , and pepper
2. whisk in the olive oil
3. place chicken in the mixture
4. cover , and marinate 8 hours or overnight
5. preheat an outdoor grill for high heat , or preheat your broiler
6. lightly oil the grill grate
7. discard marinade
8. place chicken on the prepared grill or under broiler , and cook 6 to 8 minutes per side , until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I too found this on All recipes originally. Love this stuff! I cut the recipe in half for 3 chicken breasts, so - I didnt have lime, so used 1 lemon, 1tbsp dry mustard, white vinegar, and only 1tbsp EVOO. Kept garlic the same as we love garlic. I actually made two batches of this. I marinated the chicken for about 5 hours or so, then used the other (cut the sugar and oil on this batch by a bit) to bake it in. 350 until done. This was so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple cake filling

i got this recipe from my cake decorating instructor.  it's very simple, but absolutely delicious.  we also like to spoon it over ice cream.  this recipe will fill a 9", 10" or 9x13 cake.

1. in heavy saucepan combine cornstarch , all of the sugar and salt
2. add pineapple with juice and mix well
3. cook over medium heat until mixture comes to a bubbling boil , stirring constantly
4. once mixture comes to a boil continue stirring constantly for approximately 5 minutes , or until thickened and its looses it's "milky" look
5. remove from heat and add butter , stirring to melt
6. let cool then store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I decided last minute to make my daughters birthday cake, and had a can of pineapple slices, and this sounded perfect. And it was! I used my hand held chopper/blender to chop up the pineapple, and didnt have cornstarch so I used wondra instead. Worked perfectly.  Was very sweet! I *might* cut down the sugar a tad next time, but it was so good I just may leave it! My husband was literally eating it out of the bowl as is!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake rice krispies peanut butter granola bars  lower fat

this is a delicious lower fat bar if using reduced-fat peanut butter, these are perfect for kid's lunch boxes, feel free to add in some chopped nuts or sunflower seeds or coconut in place of the raisins,

1. lightly grease 11 x 7-inch , can use a 13 x 9-inch baking dish but you will have a thinner bar
2. in a large bowl combine rice krispies cereal , oats and raisins
3. in a saucepan stir the corn syrup or honey and brown sugar until just at a boil
4. immediately remove from heat and stir in the peanut butter and vanilla until well combined
5. pour over the dry ingredients in the bowl
6. mix to combine
7. mix in mini chocolate chips work fast the mixture hardens quickly
8. transfer the mixture into prepared baking dish , then using slightly wet hands push evenly down into the pan
9. while the mixture is still soft , for easier slicing take a sharp knife and slice into desired size bars
10. chill until firm
demonstrations.review: I have made these about 4 times already, and we love them! made them exactly the same as stated the first time (with honey), but thought the raisins were too sweet (that possible?), second we omitted the raisins and peanut butter and used corn syrup - still perfect! third - no raisins and used corn syrup, and fourth no raisins, used corn syrup and added chopped up dried apricots (my favorite so far!)  nice fast, easy and cheap snacks!

target.recipe_text:
asian meatballs with rice noodles

submitted for rsc #9. this whole recipe was a new experience for me...i was so happy it worked out! i made it as a last effort for the contest after 2 failed recipes. i knew what fresh asian flavors i liked together so that is what inspired the meatballs. i was impressed with how flavorful they turned out! they did end up a little hot so feel free to cut down on the peppers. i loved the rice noodles so much that they will be come a regular quick meal in my home. i love the suggestions from reviewers to bake the meatballs. why didn't i think of that? i do think the sesame oil is a very important flavor enhancer for the noodles. thanks to everyone who tried this for the contest!

1. combine meatball ingredients in a large bowl , mix well
2. form 1-1 1 / 2" meatballs
3. place meatballs in a large 12" skillet in a single layer
4. cook over medium high heat until browned all over and cooked through , about 15-20 minutes
5. remove meatballs and set aside
6. drain grease
7. rinse rice noodles in cold water until they go slightly soft
8. set aside
9. cut green onions into 1 inch strips
10. peel carrots and then use your peeler to peel down the rest of the carrots to make long thin strips
11. chop cilantro
12. heat sesame oil in the meatball skillet over medium high heat
13. add vegetables and stir-fry for about 3 minutes until the carrots go limp
14. add beef broth and rice noodles , bring to a boil
15. cook for about 5 minutes stirring the noodles until the broth is all absorbed and the noodles are soft
16. push the noodles to the center of the pan and place the meatballs around the edges
17. heat for another 3 minutes until the meatballs are hot
18. serve with soy sauce , chili oil and fresh lime wedges if desired
target.review: This was fantastic. If I could give it 10 stars I would. I didn't use the red pepper flakes because I have small kids, but I didn't even miss it. I can see us eating this once a week! Even the kids liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rotel spicy skillet chicken

found this recipe in a magazine and it looked wonderful so i decided to try it and it's absolutely great.

1. in large skillet , cook chicken in hot oil until brown
2. add onion and garlic , saute until tender , about 5 minutes
3. add mushrooms and rotel tomatoes
4. reduce heat
5. cover and simmer 25 minutes , stirring occasionally until meat is done
6. sprinkle with cheese
7. replace cover and heat until cheese melts
8. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This was great! We put the chicken on our plate, topped it with the sauce, then put finely grated monterey jack cheese on top. The heat of the sauce melted the cheese. This would go really well with some spanish rice and tortillas on the side. I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buca di beppo chicken saltimbocca

from chef vittorio renda, buca di beppo

1. lightly salt chicken breasts
2. sprinkle evenly with chopped sage
3. place sliced prosciutto on top the chicken and pound it into the breast until the thickness of the chicken measures 3 / 8-inch
4. meanwhile , heat olive oil in a saute pan
5. lightly flour chicken pressed with prosciutto
6. place in heated oil , prosciutto side down
7. brown one side , turn and brown the other side
8. drain off excess oil , and deglaze with 4 ounces of white wine
9. add artichokes , fresh lemon juice , cream and butter and cook until sauce is thickened
10. on a large platter , place chicken breasts topped with reduced sauce and garnish with capers
demonstrations.review: This was horrible. The lemon juice and the artichoke hearts made the sauce so tart. We ate the chicken plain because the sauce was just unedible. I even tried adding more wine and heavy cream. Sorry. Just not a good one for us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poverty meal

when i was a child, my family used to eat this at least once a week due to the fact that it is inexpensive and a little goes a long way. we also added fresh herbs or sometimes whole kernel corn. its even better the next day and it freezes well.

1. saute onions and garlic in olive oil until translucent
2. brown ground beef and drain
3. add ground beef , tomatoes , water , raw macaroni , salt and pepper to the onion and garlic mixture
4. cook for 15 to 20 minutes or until macaroni is tender
5. if desired , top with parmesan cheese
6. serve with crusty bread and a salad
demonstrations.review: This was good. It's a little on the plain side, even though I added some corn. I will make this again, but maybe next time add more garlic, and melt some cheddar cheese over the top. I really liked how quick and easy this recipe is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ratatouille

this is another recipe i made a lot before the-girl-who-hates-vegetables joined us. one of our favotite summer dinners with a nice hunk of bread. i also added some tomato paste to this to reduce the acidity. came from we're cooking now - an old cooking show circa 1985.

1. heat oil in dutch oven or large saucepan , cook garlic and onions until tender
2. cut vegetables into 1-inch pieces
3. add the eggplant , zucchini , pepper , oregano parsley and stir well
4. saute about 5 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cover and cook over low heat for about 45 minutes
6. serve hot or cover mixture and refrigerate to serve chilled
demonstrations.review: I never have had Ratatouille before, but made it because my kids were curious because of the Disney movie. The only change I made was I used one green pepper and one yellow. This was better than I had expected. My kids didn't like it because it was all vegetables, but I expected that. I would definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage breakfast muffins  oamc

this is a recipe i found online and adapted to suit my family's taste. you can use either chorizo or regular bulk breakfast sausage, depending on your tastes. they're both good. if you like spicy foods, add a 4 oz can of chopped and drain green chilies.

1. line muffin tins with paper liners , and set aside
2. fry , crumble and drain sausage
3. preheat oven to 375 degrees
4. mix together bisquick , cornmeal , eggs , and milk
5. add drained sausage , and cheese , and stir well
6. ladle the filling into the prepared muffin tins , filling almost to top
7. bake for 11-15 minutes
8. allow to cool completely
9. store in freezer in a large airtight container
10. or place each in a sandwich bag , and then place a dozen in a large ziploc bag
11. microwave on high for approx 90 seconds
demonstrations.review: These were really good. I halved the recipe and used regular breakfast sausage instead of chorizo. Half the recipe made 19 regular muffins for me. They stuck to the liners pretty bad, so next time I will skip the liners, or spray them with some cooking spray. This is a nice alternative to sugar cereals in the morning for the kids, who happen to like these too.

target.recipe_text:
classic from the box all bran muffins recipe

the same recipe that used to be on the box years ago.

1. stir flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
2. set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine all-bran cereal and milk
4. let stand 5 minutes or until softened
5. add
6. egg and oil
7. beat well
8. add flour mixture , stirring only until combined
9. portion batter evenly into twelve 2 1 / 2-inch muffin-pan cups coated with
10. cooking spray
11. bake at 400 degrees for about 15-20 mins or until lightly browned
12. serve warm
13. yield: 12 muffins
14. this from the all-bran cereal box !
target.review: These were a bit bland for my taste. I think if I made them again I would incorporate molasses into the recipe (maybe cut back on the sugar and a bit of the oil and replace with molasses) and add some raisins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
english muffin bread

nan

1. combine flour , yeast , sugar , salt and soda in a large bowl
2. heat together milk and water until very warm
3. add dry ingredients and beat well
4. stir in remaining flour to make a stiff batter
5. spoon into 2 loaf pans that have been greased and sprinkled with cornmeal
6. sprinkle cornmeal on top
7. cover and let stand in warm place for 45 minutes
8. bake at 400 for 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: My mom used to make this, and I was searching for a good recipe: Thanks! Very nice on its own, and even better toasted. I think I might add a bit more salt next time to suit my taste, but otherwise it was perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french yogurt cake

in france, we make a cake, called "gâteau au yaourt / yogurt cake" very easy,
because you just need the container to weigh all ingredients. you can use the
flavor you want, or add fruits or chocolate chips. we usually bake this cake in
a regular pan, but i like to do it into cupcakes tins. you can use your blender
to make the dough !
here in france, a yogurt container is equal to 1/2 cup, but  you can adapt to your own container! you can double the recipe, or more ! it's very easy =) (i like to do this with apple sauce instead of yogurt) [3 march 2007 visiting a friend in the us, i made this cake using low fat dannon vanilla yogurt, brown sugar, bananas and frozen strawberries ! very good!]

1. preheat oven 300f
2. mix yogurt and sugar
3. add the 3 containers of flour , one by one and the salt , the dough will be hard
4. add the eggs , the oil and the flavor
5. finish with the baking powder
6. mix well
7. pour into a greased and floured cake pan
8. bake for 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: I love the versatility of this recipe! Most recently made it with vanilla and almond extracts, and used finely chopped pineapple (mixed with a little dark brown sugar) as the fruit component. Doubled the recipe and made it in a 9X13" glass pan. (Note: The cooking time varies a lot depending on the type of pan and if it is single or double recipe. Watch carefully after 30 minutes).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rock   roll bbq pit style beans for the crock pot

get that tasty bbq shack flavor in your kitchen

1. drain most of liquid from can of beans
2. put all ingredients into a crock pot and mix it up
3. turn mixture on high for 30 minutes , then reduce to low setting for 2 hours
4. this mixture can cook for hours on low during your party if need be
demonstrations.review: Excellent! The first time I made them I didn't heed the direction to drain the beans first, and they were a bit soupy. But when I made them as directed they were perfect. A lovely touch of Southern BBQ for those up us way up north!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer  n bbq braised country style pork ribs

this recipe comes originally from the 

1. brown the pork in a lightly sprayed skillet on all sides
2. place the ribs in an oven proof pan and scatter the onions all around them
3. pour in the beer and seal with a lid or tin foil
4. bake at 375f until the pork is tender 1 1 / 2- 2 hours
5. pour out the beer
6. slather the pork with the bbq sauce and bake uncovered for 1 more hour or until the meat is brown and the sauce is thick
7. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I made these for a holiday dinner in December and have been receiving requests for them (and the recipe) ever since. Rubbed them first with Theresa/Thunderbird's Southern Barbecue Rub (here on RecipeZaar). Usually use a President's Choice Mesquite BBQ sauce, but we tried a Smoky Chipotle Sauce from Superstore last time, and it was also very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish cardamom coffee cake

another lovely cardamom recipe, this one is adapted from the fantastic 'the great scandinavian baking book' by beatrice ojakangas. you can buy cardamom already ground but i prefer grinding it myself in a mortar and pestle, it's much tastier.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease a 9-inch tube or bundt pan with butter
3. dust with cookie crumbs , set aside
4. combine flour and baking soda in a small bowl
5. set aside
6. mix sugar and butter with an electric mixer until light and fluffy , about 3 minutes
7. add eggs , one at a time , beating after each addition , about 5 minutes total
8. beat in cardamom and cinnamon
9. add flour mixture
10. beat until just combined
11. add sour cream , beat until smooth , about 1 minute
12. pour batter into pan
13. bake until a toothpick inserted in the center of the cake comes out clean , about 50 minutes
14. let stand 5 minutes
15. turn out on a wire rack
16. cool completely
17. dust with confectioners' sugar
demonstrations.review: HeyJude speaks the truth: grind your own cardamom. I used some preground that was lingering in the cupboard, and everything about the cake was great...except that the flavour was flat. I was so mad at myself for taking the lazy route. Next time I'm going to do it properly! Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
black bean brownies  gluten free  dairy free

i love this recipe!  an easy, gluten free recipe for black bean brownies that have just the right combination of chocolate and cayenne to make you feel like you're having cafe and dulces in mexico!  using a food processor is the easiest method, but a blender or even a potato masher can be used instead.  my variation of a recipe found at livingwithout.com.

1. preheat oven to 350 and spray an 8-inch square baking pan with non-stick cooking spray
2. set aside
3. to the bowl of a food processor , add black beans and process until a paste forms
4. add eggs , oil , sugar , cocoa , flour , xanthan gum , vanilla , baking powder and cayenne
5. process until smooth and well combined
6. stir in chocolate chips and spread batter into prepared pan
7. bake for 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean
8. cool and refrigerate for easier cutting
9. store in sealed container or in refrigerator
target.review: I made these for a friend who was gluten- and dairy-intolerant.  She said they were great.  I thought so too.  This is a very dense brownie - loved the chocolate chips in it (found some that had no dairy products in them).  OK, I was nervous but I couldn't taste the black beans at all!  What a great recipe!  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
persimmon bundt cake

got a lot of persimmons you don't know what to do with? or have you always wanted to make something using this little-known fruit. here's your chance to make a wonderful, flavourful bundt cake that not only has luscious persimmons in it, but warm spices that make it extra-special.

1. position rack in center of oven and preheat to 350f
2. butter and flour bundt pan
3. peel persimmons
4. press pulp through coarse sieve into medium bowl
5. measure 1 1 / 3 cups persimmon puree into small bowl
6. mix baking soda into puree and set aside
7. beat sugar and butter in large bowl until blended
8. add eggs , 1 at a time , beating well after each addition
9. mix in vanilla
10. sift flour , cinnamon , salt , allspice and cloves into butter mixture
11. blend well using rubber spatula
12. mix in persimmon mixture , walnuts and currants
13. transfer batter to prepared pan
14. bake cake until tester comes out clean , about 55 minutes
15. cook cake in pan on rack 5 minutes
16. turn out cake onto rack
17. cool completely
18. sift confectioners sugar over cake
demonstrations.review: This was my first-ever cooking experience with persimmons...a positive one, I'm glad to add!  Delicious cake.  Other reviews were correct - the persimmon flavor isn't strong, but then persimmons don't HAVE a strong flavor!  Nice, moist cake perfect for the harvest season.  I took one reviewers suggestion to drizzle it with a glaze made of lemon juice, powdered sugar (and I added the lemon zest too)! Very nice recipe! Showy too! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kefir  buttermilk  salad dressing

adapted from a recipe from the gourmet cookbook.  original recipe used buttermilk, i have substituted plain kefir and made a couple of other minor changes.  the final product is a healthier, lighter, "buttermilk" style dressing.

1. put all of the ingredients , except the olive oil in a blender or food processor
2. puree until all ingredients are well incorporated
3. drizzle in the olive oil while processing
4. continue to blend for another 20 seconds or so
5. best if refrigerated overnight , as it allows the dressing to thicken slightly , and the flavors to mingle
6. i have , however , used it right out of the blender and it still tastes great
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  Nice to have another way to take advantage of this powerfully, healthy food (the kefir) without cooking it.  I'll be making this again!  It seems like it would be a great baseline from which to experiment with some other flavorings too!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real deal penne al limone

nice fresh lemon taste, quick and easy. this is a favorite recipe that my sister and best friend always ask me to prepare when i come home. it is a big hit in small dinner parties, but could not be easier to prepare.

1. in a large pot put the water to boil for the pasta
2. in a large saucepan melt the butter until is starts to foam , add the lemon juice and let it reduce a bit , maybe 5 minutes
3. set aside
4. when the pasta is ready , drain and keep aside
5. return the lemon sauce to the stove and add all of the cream and let it reduce by a half
6. mix the pasta with the cream sauce , add the cheese , salt and pepper to taste
7. garnish with fresh parsley stems ,
demonstrations.review: Wonderful flavor!  The butter/cream/lemon ingredients add interest and dimension to the pasta.  It didn't need to be swimming in sauce - all the flavor was there without all the calories (that would have been there with double or triple the sauce)!  DH loved it.  I loved that it was a dressed-up dish without a lot of ingredients, just used things I'd usually have on hand.  Don't forget that sprinkle of chopped parsley at the end - adds both color and flavor.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shaved brussel sprouts

i know that brussel sprouts usually get a bad rap, but they truly are a 
delicious vegetable.  give this a try and it may change your outlook!  they are tender, a little spicy, and slightly cheesy. all in all, a simple and flavorful side dish.

1. 1
2. cut out the core of the brussel sprouts and shave them so that they look like thin ribbons
3. 2
4. saute the brussel sprouts in olive oil for 2 to 3 minutes
5. 3
6. season with salt and pepper and add the crushed red pepper flakes
7. 4
8. add the water and continue to cook for 5 to 8 minutes , until the brussel
9. sprouts are tender
10. 5
11. mix in the cheese
demonstrations.review: Really fast! Really great! Loved the simplicity of this recipe even though it looked so fancy. I must admit that I was in too big of a hurry to cut out the cores. I trimmed the bottoms of fresh brussel sprouts then fed them into the hopper of my food processor with the slicing blade. I think it worked pretty well. I went "light" on the red pepper flakes but "heavy" on the parmesan. Will be making this over and over! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutty cheese tortellini

this is so easy and tasty! found it in taste of home magazine.

1. cook tortellini according to directions , drain
2. in the same pan , melt butter
3. stir in the tortellini , parsley and walnuts , toss to coat
4. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and pepper
demonstrations.review: This was SO delicious! It was fast and easy but your guests will never know it! It has such a great combination of flavors - buttery, fresh, sweet, savory, crunchy! It was exactly what I was looking for. (I didn't use all of the butter though -- just 6 Tbsp. -- that was plenty we felt.) Thank you so much for this awesome, tasty, wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
creamy chicken and stove top stuffing casserole

this recipe is the ultimate comfort food when paired with buttery mashed potatoes, corn or green beans, and hot rolls. wash it all down with a tall icy cold glass of milk!

1. oven@ 350
2. cook chicken and cut into bite sized pieces
3. place into a casserole dish
4. prepare stove top according to directions
5. heat both cans of soup with the milk in a saucepan until hot
6. pour over chicken
7. spoon stuffing over top of chicken and soup
8. bake for 30-45 minutes or until bubbly
target.review: Now this is my kind of recipe-- simple, easy and DELICIOUS. I did add a small can of sweet peas and used two cans of Costco's chunk chicken breast, but it worked out fine. Thanks for sharing this great dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review:
Wondered what had happened to 'Nurse Di'!!!!

Fixed this tonight for my wife and we both agree, it's wonderful.

Due to time restraints, had to cut back to 30 min on the 'simmer' portion of sauce, but was still as tasty as could be.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arielle s favorite tuna casserole

this is one of my family's favorite quick work night meals - i used to make this as a teen for my folks and have continued with my family. my kids (and hubby) request this one!!  fun ways to change it up are to bake crescent rolls in a ball/roll filled with cheese on top of the casserole (i like to start them out first so the bottoms cook a bit first), or top the casserole with fried onions, crushed potato chips (a great use for those old chips in the cupboard), etc.  i modify the amounts depending on what i have in the pantry - but it is always great!!!

1. cook pasta al dente or as directed on package
2. drain
3. combine in pot pasta , cream of mushroom soup , tuna , peas , salt , pepper and cheese
4. mix thoroughly
5. transfer into a covered casserole dish and bake at 400 degrees for 30 minutes or until bubbly
6. remove from oven and allow to cool for 5 minutes prior to serving
7. serving suggestions - serve with crusty bread and salad or green veggie
8. ) enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
At last I have found IT! After a lifelong search for the perfect tuna casserole, yours fits the bill. Cut back a bit on the cheese (that's a lot of cheese!) and put the onion rings on top. Enough there for a hungry Siberian army, so will cut in half next time.

Thanks Moma D for making my day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: Figured 227 folks couldn't be wrong. And I was right. This is one good meatloaf recipe. Had some green pepper on hand, so chopped and added it. This is the comfort food to beat all comfort food. Thanks, Nita.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini and ground beef lasagna

in a welcome change from all of the heavy lasagna noodles, this recipe may even be a great way to get the kids to eat their veggies. young and old(er)alike will enjoy this!

1. cut zucchini into strips , 1 / 4-inch thick
2. heat oil , add garlic and onion and cook until vegetables are tender but not browned
3. add meat and brown , stirring to keep meat crumbly
4. add tomatoes , tomato paste , mushrooms , wine , oregano , thyme , basil , and salt and pepper to taste
5. simmer , uncovered for 1-1 / 2 hours
6. place half of zucchini strips inside of an oiled , shallow casserole
7. top with half of the mozzarella and half of the ricotta
8. add half of the meat sauce
9. repeat layers
10. top with parmesan cheese
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes or until hot
demonstrations.review: Wife and I really enjoyed this dish tonight, but....the instructions on whether or not the zuchini should be sauted with the onions/garlic not real clear. I did not and the squash just did not cook enough for my taste in the baking process.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
minnesota chicken and wild rice soup

this is a great way to use up leftover chicken (or turkey) and whatever vegetables you have on hand. it is hearty, tasty, and pretty good for you, too. from better homes and gardens heritage of america cookbook.

1. in large pot bring to a boil: broth , carrots , potatoes , wild rice , green onion , bell pepper , thyme , and black pepper
2. cover and simmer 45 minutes or until rice is tender
3. stir in butter and half-and-half
4. slowly add flour , stirring constantly to prevent lumps from forming
5. stir in chicken and sherry and heat through
demonstrations.review:
Wife and I had your recipe for dinner last night and it was superb!! Leftovers tasted even better after night in the fridge. I added some celery that was on hand.

This is a real winner for a cold, winter night.

target.recipe_text:
vanilla scented granola

great snack for everyone, or the for kids lunches or even as an after school treat! serve for breakfast with yogurt and fruit or over ice cream for dessert. watch your time in the oven because sometimes it cooks a little quickly. this recipe came from bon appetit, march of 2002.
a few baking tips i have learned from making this recipe often: i use a jelly roll pan so the granola will have maximum exposure while cooking.  also, if you do like your granola to clump, do not stir while baking.  allow to cool in pan for about 10 minutes or so, then run a spatula between granola and the pan to loosen.  you will have so many clumps you will have to break them with your hands ; )

1. position rack to middle of oven and preheat to 300
2. lightly spray large baking sheet with nonstick spray
3. mix next 5 ingredients in large bowl
4. combine oil , honey and sugar in small saucepan
5. bring to simmer over medium heat
6. remove from heat
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour hot liquid over oat mixture
9. stir well
10. using hands , toss mixture until thoroughly mixed
11. spread granola on prepared baking sheet
12. bake until golden brown , stirring occasionaly , about 30 minutes
13. transfer sheet to rack
14. cool granola completely
15. makes about 8 cups
target.review: Great!  My family loved the crunchiness of the granola.  I also substituted light olive oil for the vegetable oil.  Instead of all honey, I used about half pure maple syrup.  For the nuts we had pecans on hand, so I used these.  It was some of the best granola we've had.  Loved the vanilla!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel pecan ice cream dessert

this lucious high calorie ice cream dessert is sooo good you may want to pass on dinner and get right to the dessert.  it is easy to make and disgustingly yummy. this recipe is 2 part so i have broken it down in ingredients and directions.

1. combine flour , pecans , sugar , and oats in a large bowl
2. add margarine and mix well
3. pat this mixture on a large baking sheet with sides
4. bake at 400f stirring occasionally for 15 minutes crumble while warm
5. cool
6. press half of crumb mixture into a 9 x 13 pan
7. drizzle with half the sauce
8. spread ice cream over crumb mixture and add remaining crumbs and sauce
9. cover and freeze
10. remove from freezer 10 minutes before serving
11. also , i cut it and wrap in saran individual pieces to take out of freezer when needed
12. this is an extremely rich dessert so i cannot judge portions
13. i would not serve more than about a 3" square per person
14. to make caramel sauce
15. in heavy saucepan , bring sugar , corn syrup , butter and water to a boil over med
16. heat , stirring constantly
17. boil 1 minute reduce heat and cook for 5 minutes
18. remove from heat and stir in vanilla
19. let cool slightly
20. stir in cream
21. sauce
22. will thicken
demonstrations.review: We made this recipe for a large group of teenage girls at a swim party.  They loved it.  Also served it to a group of college-aged guys.  We  also make the topping and just serve it on vanilla ice cream.  Some of our family thinks it is more delicious this way with the topping freshly made and served immediately.  Great!  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey pumpkin pie

nan

1. line 9-inch pie plate with pastry disk
2. flute the edge
3. with fork , prick shell all over
4. place in freezer for 30 minutes
5. line pastry shell with foil or parchment paper , then fill with pie weights or pie chains
6. bake empty shell on the lowest rack in 400 f oven for 10 minutes
7. remove both weights and foil
8. continue baking for about 10 minutes longer or until pastry is set
9. filling: meanwhile , in large bowl , beat eggs lightly
10. add pumpkin , honey , light cream , cinnamon , cloves , ginger , nutmeg and salt
11. combine thoroughly and pour into the pastry shell
12. combine sour cream with milk
13. pour into plastic dispenser with very , very , very narrow opening
14. hold finger over the opening and position the dispenser above the pie
15. remove finger and quickly drizzle mixture in spiral pattern over filling
16. beginning at centre , pull
17. beginning at outside , pull knife through middle of intervals toward centre to create web pattern
18. bake on lowest rack in 350 f oven for about 1 hour or until filling is set and point of knife inserted into centre comes out clean
19. let cool on rack
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed this pumpkin pie very much.  I especially like the decorative lace pattern which looked similar to a spider web or a flower on one of the pies.  We also made this pie with a rice flour crust so it was very healthy.  The honey made the pie not too sweet. This pie is a  good option for those on a sugar free diet. Thank you for submitting the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grannydragon s  really quick cream of asparagus soup

super quick using canned asparagus.

1. in the soup pot , melt the butter with the oil
2. add onion , cooking until transparent
3. add garlic and thyme , cook until the garlic smells aromatic , just a few minutes
4. put both cans of asparagus and their liquid in a blender to puree
5. add the pureed asparagus and chicken broth to the pot
6. heat through
7. add milk or cream to the pot , being careful not to allow it to boil
8. adjust seasonings to your taste
9. you might serve with a pat of butter in the center of the bowl
demonstrations.review: This soup was so delicious, Grannydragon.!  I used a large bunch of fresh asparagus, instead and it had such a fresh delicious flavor.  It was a very soothing soup on a chilly evening.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy peezy pizza dough  bread machine pizza dough

this is a really easy way to make a good "yeasty" pizza dough! as well as using this recipe for when i'm making pizza, i also use it for when i'm making a focaccia or a calzone. (the preparation time i have given includes the time it takes to make the dough in the machine and the time it takes for the pizza dough to proof - after removing it from the bread machine, 30 minutes.)

1. some pizza topping ideas
2. caramelised onions and roasted garlic
3. mozzarella cheese , camembert , romano and feta
4. equal parts of basil pesto and olive oil mixed together with parmesan or romano cheese
5. plus some roughly chopped sundried or semi-dried tomatoes , sliced black olives and lots of grated mozzarella cheese , salt and lost of freshly ground black pepper !
6. cranberry jelly , shredded chicken , sliced brie !
7. mozzarella cheese , shredded chicken and sliced avocado !
8. the bread
9. place all the above ingredients in the order i have listed into the bread machine
10. select the dough cycle and press start !
11. when the dough cycle is complete , take the dough out of the machine and place in well greased bowl , and roll the dough around thus 'coating' it in oil
12. cover and leave to rise in a warm place for about 1 / 2 an hour
13. knead the risen dough lightly
14. to shape and bake: roll the dough into a circle
15. place on well greased baking tray or pizza pan
16. then add a topping of your choice and bake at 225'c
demonstrations.review: Excellent Crust!  I did cook it differently.  I cooked a 425 degrees F for 20 minutes with no toppings.  Then I removed the crust and put my sauce on top with toppings and cheese.  The crust really puffed up when we cooked it.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried chickpeas with raisins

simple (especially with canned chickpeas), rich, and healthy.  serve with half a cup of cooked brown rice per serving and some spinach sauteed with garlic.  

edited 5/5/2011 - you are so right about the cayenne!  sorry about that!  that was some kind of typo.  i am not a tablespoon-of-cayenne sort of eater, either...

1. heat oil over medium flame
2. saute onion and bell pepper five minutes
3. add garlic and ginger and continue to cook until vegetables are soft
4. add curry , cumin , and cayenne and stir
5. add coconut milk and bring to a boil
6. reduce heat , add chickpeas , and simmer until thickened slightly
7. season with salt and pepper and garnish with raisins
demonstrations.review: This was really an exciting meal to eat!  It was so spicy.  I cut the cayenne to half and it was still to spicy for most in my family.  Next time I will cut it to one fourth and try it again!  It had an excellent flavor just too hot for my family.  Try it!!

target.recipe_text:
velveeta cheese sauce for cauliflower and broccoli

cauliflower and broccoli never had it so good! --- the amounts stated makes a huge amount if desired the ingredients may be reduced by half --- for cheese sauce with a kick add in some tabasco or cayenne pepper, of coarse this cheese sauce may be used with just about anything!

1. melt the butter in a small saucepan
2. remove from heat
3. blend in the flour until smooth using a wire whisk
4. return to heat
5. gradually whisk in the half and half cream
6. bring to a light boil , keep whisking until the mixture is smooth
7. add in the cubed velveeta , and contine to mix with a spoon until cheese is melted
8. remove from heat
9. add in the sugar , salt and pepper
10. mix until combined
11. pour over the veggies just prior to serving
12. sprinkle with paprika
target.review: As usual, Kittencal hits another one out of the park.  EVERYONE at dinner liked this sauce.  I only made 1/2 the recipe and had a good deal left over.  The next day I added it to some cooked elbow macaroni for mac-n-cheese.  Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh blueberry cobbler

easy and too good for words.

1. add flour , 1 / 2 cup sugar , salt , and baking powder to a mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add in milk and butter
4. stir to combine
5. spread batter into a greased 8-inch square baking pan
6. sprinkle blueberries evenly over batter
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 cup sugar and drizzle with vanilla
8. bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until a pick comes out clean
9. can serve plain or with ice cream on top
demonstrations.review: I doubled the recipe and cooked it in a 9 X 13.  I had to add 10 minutes to the cooking time.  It turned out perfectly!  I loved the "cakiness" of it.  I cooked it in a Glad plastic dish and the edges weren't over crisp at all.  The cobbler was a hit with my family and our guests.  There's no way I'm losing this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: Used this recipe as a reference for portions and the sauce.  I had leftover chicken and vegetables from dinner a couple of nights ago.  All I can say is WOW!!  This recipe is spot on and it will be the only one I use from now on.  Thanks!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rich buttery poppy seed muffins

a favorite muffin recipe i turn to often. adapted from one of my favorite community cookbooks, "enough to feed an army."

1. line 12 muffin cups with paper liners or grease tins well
2. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
3. mix together flour , poppy seeds , salt , baking soda
4. in another bowl , using a mixer , cream together sugar and butter
5. beat in eggs to the butter mixture one at a time , then beat in yogurt and vanilla
6. hand stir together the dry mixture and the butter mixture just enough to moisten ingredients- there should still be some lumps
7. spoon into prepared muffin tins and bake 15-20 miutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
8. let cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: WOW!  This is the perfect muffin recipe.  My kids love orange flavor so I exchanged the vanilla extract for 1 1/2 tsp. orange extract.  I also added a bit of orange zest.  I will be keeping this recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pressure cooked pork chops

got from another user.  loved it so so easy yet so so delicious.

1. brown pork chops in pressure cooker on both sides in 1 / 2 of the butter then salt and pepper well
2. have your potatoes and carrots already peeled and chunked into healthy meaty portions
3. have your onion diced into small peices
4. take out pork chops with tongs and set aside for a moment while you add the onions and rest of butter to pork fat
5. then add potatoes and carrots then pork chops add the cup of water and the steak sauce put lid on and lock bring to high pressure once pressure is established put timer on for 15 minutes , then use the regular release method and it is unbelievable a great dinner with soooo much taste in less than 30 minute
6. let me know if anyone likes it
7. serena
demonstrations.review: This was my very first recipe with my pressure cooker.  Now I know how the Ikea cafe cooks their potatoes - lol.  This recipe is wonderful.  I was petrified I'd do something wrong and have an explosion in the kitchen.  I must've read your directions 150 times.  Everything went off flawlessly.  I used the carrots and it worked just great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
drunken meatballs  with crock pot instructions

i found these on another website ages ago ad they have since become a regular at my parties. you can use any bourbon but i have done well using southern comfort.

1. combine the first three ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes , until blended
2. add meatballs and simmer , covered for about 45 minutes
3. crock pot: for the crock pot , prepare sauce as above
4. put meatballs into crock pot , pour sauce over and cook on low for 8 to 12 hours
demonstrations.review: I made this with frozen meatballs in a crockpot.  It's sooooooo good!!  This recipe is going in my permanent file :-)  I used Southern Comfort and chopped up one each red, yellow and orange bell pepper and added it.  It turned out perfect and was a hit with all my friends.

target.recipe_text:
barley lentil soup

canadian living recently featured a an article promoting recipes rich in grains. this soup looked so comforting and satisfying, i knew that as autumn arrived it would be the perfect meal. submitted for 'zaar world tour.

1. in large saucepan or soup pot , heat oil over medium heat
2. saute onion , garlic , carrot , celery , thyme , marjoram and pepper until onions are softened , about 5 minutes
3. add stock , water , lentils and barley to the pot and bring to boil
4. reduce heat , cover and simmer until barley and lentils are tender , about 40 minutes
5. stir in chopped parsley before serving
6. to serve , top each serving with a dollop of yogurt
7. sprinkle with finely chopped parsley
target.review: I just about double the veggies, and added a can of diced tomatoes along with the stock and water. I did not use the optional topping. Really delicious and satisfying. I like that it is a healthy vegetarian option, but still very filling. It's perfect for fall lunches. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blender caesar salad dressing

this is so easy and good.  i got this recipe years ago from a magazine.  i want to say it was sunset, but not sure now.  if you like caesar salad, this is quick to make and tastes great.

1. in blender add egg , cheese , lemon juice , garlic , worcestershire sauce , mustard , tabasco , salt and pepper
2. blend until combined
3. remove top and with blender on , on lowest speed , gradually add oil in thin stream until thick and creamy
4. pour into jar , cover and refrigerate 1 hours or up to 5 days
5. let stand at room temperature 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I really like this. DH absolutely LOVES it. I add anchovy paste because DH is an anchovy fan, but I find the paste easier to deal with and it gives it that extra little something. We usually use it over romaine hearts with grilled chicken, parmesan shavings and homemade croutons. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish soft honey whole wheat bread

i've been looking for a soft all whole wheat bread, and i finally found it!  this is in an amish cookbook that i have, and i am writing it as it is written. i mix it with my kitchenaid. :)  this is our sandwich bread that we have all the time on hand and the recipe can easily be cut into 1/3 to make just one loaf. :) 10/8/07 corrections made to make bigger loaves.  i usually use recipe #185778 to have a great rise.

1. mix water with yeast and sugar and let sit until foamy
2. in the meanwhile , put the 3 eggs in a bowl of hot water
3. put flour , salt , and gluten in bowl
4. pour in yeast mixture and stir until combined
5. add in honey , eggs , and crisco until combined , scraping sides
6. add more wheat flour and knead until smooth
7. let set in warm place for about an hour until double in size
8. divide into 3 loaves
9. let rise again in warm place until doubled
10. bake as regular bread
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a very tasty and soft whole wheat bread. I did sub butter for the Crisco because that is what I had on hand, but other than that, followed the recipe exactly. I turned one of the three loaves into a cinnamon raisin swirl bread by rolling into a flat rectangle, sprinkling with cinnamon, sugar and raisins and then tightly rolling into a loaf. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review: These were Amazing! I made a batch of another white chocolate-cranberry cookies last week, but I tried this recipe to see if there was any significant difference and I'm not sure what it was, but this recipe was so flavorful. Exactly what I was craving! Thank you so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwest chicken black bean soup

an extremely flavorful way to combine chicken and the ever growing popularity of black beans. lots of flavor and a great thick broth. its very healthy for you too! serve with recipe #43730.

1. in a medium sized skillet cook chicken that's been seasoned with seasoned salt until done and no longer pink
2. dice and set aside
3. finely chop bell peppers , onion and jalapeo slices in food processor or by hand if you like larger pieces
4. combine all peppers , onion and jalapeo and add lemon juice and a pinch of salt
5. melt margarine in a large stock pot
6. saut pepper and onion mixture until soft
7. add can of crushed tomatoes , stirring
8. add three cans of black beans , undrained
9. add chicken to pot , stirring carefully
10. then add chicken broth to soup and stir
11. next , add bay leaf , about a teaspoon of season salt , tarragon and cinnamon
12. let simmer until flavors are combined and peppers and onion are soft and tender about one hour , or until it smells so good you cannot wait
13. serve with recipe #43730
demonstrations.review: I really love this soup. I use regular jalepeno peppers rather than the pickled kind but other than that I use the recipe exactly and often make it for lunches. I've also made it without the cheicken and substitued veggie broth for the chicken broth for a vegatarian friend and that tasted excellent as well. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s marinara pasta sauce  vegetarian

this is a basic simple marinara but big on flavor, it can be ready in 1 hour or you can cook it longer and even tastes better the next day that is why i strongly suggest to make this sauce 1-3 days ahead and refrigerate as the flavors will blend and intensify ---this freezes well so make a double recipe and freeze a batch for the next meal, you may omit the wine but i strongly suggest to add it in, it really adds flavor to the sauce --- please make certain to purchase only good-quality canned italian roma (plum) tomatoes for this it will make a huge difference to the flavor of the sauce ---  all ingredients may be adjusted to suit taste, this sauce can also be simmered for a longer time in a crockpot, throw in some fresh mushrooms also if desired ---  also see my recipe#71273

1. in a heavy-bottomed stockpot or dutch oven heat oil over medium-high heat
2. add in onions , garlic and dried red pepper flakes , basil and oregano
3. saute for about 3-4 minutes
4. add in the tomato paste and stir for 2-3 minutes
5. add in the roma tomatoes with juice and wine
6. simmer uncovered over low heat for 1-2 hours stirring occasionally
7. season with salt and pepper and add in sugar if desired
demonstrations.review: Love the addition of the wine! That's really the only difference between this and more normal recipe, and that difference has made this my new normal recipe. I doubled the recipe and added the called for amount of sugar and the full cup of wine. It was a bit thick, so I did add just about a half cup of water. Thank you for posting your great recipes! Can't wait to try more!

target.recipe_text:
rocky road

yummy rocky road for chocky lovers. put a few in a cellophane bag and tie with green and red ribbon for a tasty christmas gift.

1. line a 30cm square tin with baking paper
2. melt chocolate and copha in a heatproof bowl over gently boiling water and stir until smooth
3. combine all other ingredients in another large bowl leaving aside 2 tblsp of coconut
4. pour in melted chocolate and mix well
5. pour completed mixture into the lined tin and spread
6. sprinkle on the remaining coconut
7. refrigerate then cut into chunky squares
8. enjoy
target.review: So easy to make and so yummy. I followed the basic recipe but as I was making this for christmas I put in some chopped red and green frog lollies (jelly Candy)and some chopped nuts. I will definately be making this in the near future, thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus cob dip

everyone i know likes this dip and ask for the recipe. it's quick and easy and tastes great. i got it from a friend of mine one christmas.

1. mix sour cream , cream cheese , spring vegetable soup mix& asparagus cuts in a bowel
2. cut the top of the bread cob
3. dig out the bread from the cob
4. fill the cob with dip and replace top of cob
5. cook in moderate oven until hot and crisp
6. cut french stick to dip with when cob cooked
demonstrations.review: I love this dip, and so it seems did my guests as there was nothing left on the platter at the end of the party. I made the mixture up the day before and refrigerated it in a microwavable container, then I heated up the filling slightly before putting it into the cob.It worked perfectly Thanks for posting this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mojo walleye

walleye is just about the best whitefish i know, and this marinade is fantastic! allow about 3 hours for marinating, and either grill or broil the walleye, or sometimes i like to coat it in a light mixture of dried unseasoned breadcrumbs with a little cornmeal and pan-fry.

1. in a plastic zipper bag , combine 2 large walleye fillets with the marinade ingredients
2. marinate for 3 hours
3. to cook , either grill , broil or pan-fry
4. total cooking time should be about 15 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, DH really enjoyed it and asked me to make this again, the kids thought it was a little spicy. I only had time to marinade for 1.5hrs, and I cooked the fish on a grill. Thanks for posting this yummy recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread pudding in the microwave

i have no idea where i got this recipe, but it is handwritten in a small book where i saved recipes back in the mid-80s. i haven't made this in ages, but i do recall i used to make it a lot. i think i will make it again today! :-) ordinary sandwich bread works fine, or use a spiffier bread to make a spiffier pudding. serve with a vanilla custard sauce, whipped cream, or even ice cream.

1. spread bread cubes evenly in an 8-inch round glass pan
2. sprinkle with the sugar , salt , and raisins
3. place milk in a 4-cup glass measuring cup and add the butter
4. microwave on high for four minutes , until butter melts and milk is warm
5. rapidly , stir in eggs with a fork or small whisk and combine well
6. pour over bread
7. microwave on medium-high for 9 to 12 minutes
8. when cooked , centre may still be slightly soft , but does set up as pudding cools
9. serve warm or chilled
10. your preference
demonstrations.review: We needed a fast dessert, this was certainly fast to put together, I didn't have raisins so I substituted with sultanas. I served with ice cream it went down really well. I will be holding on to this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
morrie s sausage casserole

when growing up, morrie was our next door neighbour. i remember my brother loving this recipe, in fact it was about all he would eat as a kid!!  please allow time to boil the sausages and stew the apple!

1. preheat oven to 120c
2. make a sauce with the boiling water , flour , sugar , vinegar , ketchup , butter , curry powder , salt and pepper
3. in an oven dish place sausages , carrot , onion and apples
4. add sauce mixing well
5. cover and cook for 1 1 / 2 - 2 hours
demonstrations.review: A great family meal, everyone liked the flavour,7yo has requested it again. I stewed the apple in the microwave otherwise cooked as per instructions, served with creamy mashed potatoes and brocoli.Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage pie simply the best

now this is real comfort food -  its simple to make and tastes wonderful and if necessary you can stretch it that bit further with more vegetables in the filling

1. heat oil in a medium saucepan
2. add the diced onion , carrot , garlic and mushrooms , stirring constantly for 2-3 minutes
3. add beef to pan and cook stirring with a fork until sealed and brown
4. add the stock , bay leaf , tomato puree , worcestershire sauce , bay leaf salt and pepper
5. simmer gently for half an hour , reducing liquid and thicken if necessary
6. place in ovenproof pie dish and allow to cool
7. cook potato , with the 1 diced onion
8. when cooked , mash the potato , adding the milk , parsley , pepper and salt to taste
9. spread the mash evenly over the meat
10. place in hot oven for approximately 30-35 minutes until golden brown
11. serve with other cooked vegetables
demonstrations.review: This is a really good recipe, I really enjoyed the addition of mushrooms, which I have never had in a cottage pie before. The kids ate it all up which of coarse made me really happy. This will be a regular on our menu. Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
cheese scalloped potatoes

this is a recipe by emeril lagasse (from the essence of emeril show) that my husband enjoys.

1. preheat oven to 350f fry the onion in butter until soft , add flour and whisk in with butter for 2 minutes
2. then whisk in the milk and cook until thick and bubbly
3. remove from heat and add 3 / 4 cup of cheese , stirring until melted
4. season with salt and pepper
5. layer half of potatoes in a small baking dish and sprinkle with salt and pepper
6. cover with half of sauce
7. layer remaining potato slices on top of sauce and season
8. top with remaining sauce and sprinkle with remaining cheese
9. bake , covered , for 30 minutes or until potatoes are tender
target.review: Made this tonight to have with our New Year's ham. These are fantastic and so easy to make. I used fat-free evaporated milk in place of the milk, as I had some to use up and our regular milk had gone bad. The rest was as per the recipe. I had to cook mine for about an hour, though. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiked banana bread

get ready to raid your liquor cabinet! a moist and delicious treat for any time of the day with ingredients you probably already have! my husband ate half a loaf in one sitting!! haven't tried freezing yet as it doesn't last that long, but stays for at least a week in the fridge :)makes 2 loaves.

1. mix together 1 / 8 cup triple sec and 1 / 2 cup sugar and set aside
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. mix together margarine and 1 1 / 2 cups sugar until creamy
4. beat in eggs and bananas
5. add flour , baking powder , salt and vanilla
6. mix well
7. while mixer is still mixing , slowly add 1 / 3 cup of triple sec and 2 tablespoons orange juice
8. mixture will be creamy but not too runny
9. pour into two greased 8 inch loaf pans
10. bake for 40 minutes
11. then , with loaves still on oven racks paint the bread with the topping
12. be sure to cover entire top
13. bake five more minutes
14. allow to cool in pans five minutes before transferring to cooling racks
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I just made this and had a slice - it's awesome. Okay, now I have to admit, I had no triple sec, but we did have coconut rum, so I used that instead, and it's still fantastic. The only other change was that I used light margarine (all that we have on hand) and it still worked out fine. Fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cheesecake ice cream  for electric ice cream machine

posted by request. recipe is from the recipe book that came with my ice cream machine. prep time includes 1 hour chilling and 1/2 hour freezing times.

1. blend all ingredients until smooth
2. chill ingredients for about 1 hour , or until cold
3. turn on ice cream machine and set it to chill the freezing / mixing bowl for 5 minutes
4. spoon the cooled mixture into the freezing / mixing bowl of machine
5. set the freezing timer to the 30 minute maximum setting
6. push start button
7. when timer rings , spoon ice cream into dishes and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is the best recipe for my ice cream maker - it sets so quickly and wow, does it taste fantastic! I used low-fat cream cheese and 1% milk and no one would know the difference. The first time I used fresh strawberries and tonight I made it again but used frozen blueberries - nice! Thanks so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast in a pan frittata

not knowing what to fix for breakfast can be a real chore. this was the result of "i'm tired of the same old thing". served this with homemade biscuits and sliced tomatoes. makes two generous servings.

1. using medium shredder blade of food processor , shred the potato
2. warm olive oil in non-stick skillet , add potato , bell pepper , green onions , mushrooms and bacon
3. cook and stir until potato is lightly browned and other vegetables are crisp tender
4. add salt and pepper to taste , pour egg mixture over vegetables
5. cook until eggs are almost set , running spatula around edges and allowing uncooked egg to run to bottom of pan
6. when eggs are almost set , invert onto a dinner plate and then slip back into pan allowing the bottom to cook completely
7. the last few minutes top with shredded cheese and cover until cheese melts
8. cut in half and slip onto serving plates
demonstrations.review: This was really tasty and my fiance ate all of his portion - the first time he has ever eaten all of his frittata! I think next time I will leave out the Canadian bacon - just a personal preference, though. It's the first time I've actually been able to flip a frittata, too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot panama pork stew

i'm so glad i found this recipe. it's a deliciously different combination of ingredients and flavors.

1. layer potatoes , corn , green beans , onion , and pork in the bottom of a crock pot
2. add tomatoes , chili powder , salt , coriander and water to a large bowl , stir to combine and pour over crock pot ingredients
3. cover and cook on low 7-9 hours
demonstrations.review: I made this on the weekend, and, while I was intending on using the crockpot, got tied up and ended up just making it on the stove-top. Next time (and there will be a next time!) I will try the crockpot. At any rate, I really loved this - it was the first time I have made anything with sweet potatoes, and I really liked their flavour and texture in this. I did add some cumin to this (I never measure - probably 2 tsp), plus about a tsp of cinnamon. Thanks for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese ice cream

luscious, tempting, creamy ice cream!!  something different this summer!

1. blend cream cheese , milk , lemon juice , sugar and salt in blender till smooth
2. transfer to bowl , then stir in cream
3. freeze cream cheese mix in ice cream maker , transfter to airtight container and put in freezer to harden , at least 2 hours
4. let ice cream soften 5 min before serving
demonstrations.review: Excellent, quick, and very tasty. I have made this successfully with light cream cheese and 1.5 cups of 1% milk (omitting the cream altogether). I also used vanilla extract in place of the lemon. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
quick butternut squash soup

here's a quick, light and creamy soup that warm you on the coldest night. add some hearty whole grain bread and a tossed salad to make a very satisfying meal.

1. add oil , garlic and onion to large stockpot over medium heat
2. saute for 3-4 minutes
3. add sage , salt , pepper , broth and squash
4. bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. use stick blender to lightly puree , leaving some chunks , or puree half of the soup in a food processor or blender and return to pot
7. garnish with parmesan cheese and more fresh sage
target.review: This was very flavorful. I'm not sure what the other reviewers were complaining about. Based on their complaints, I did make a few minor adjustments. I subbed 1/2 cup of water for the broth (I used bullion   water for broth) with dry white wine. I also tossed in about 1/4 teaspoon each of thyme and rosemary with the sage. Next time, I will probably cut back on the salt a bit, as I found it a tad bit salty for my taste. My husband, on the other hand, thought the salt was just fine. Thanks for a solid recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and kielbasa

my husband didn't think he liked cabbage until i served this. the bacon and onion really give this recipe a lot of flavor.

1. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
2. remove bacon
3. crumble , and set aside
4. add next 7 ingredients to bacon drippings
5. cover and cook over medium heat for 10 minutes , turning cabbage once
6. add sausage and cover and cook an additional 5 minutes or until sausage is heated
7. transfer to a serving dish with a slotted spoon
8. sprinkle with the crumbled bacon
demonstrations.review: Yum! We ate this over mashed potatoes, and it was a hit. It was a bit spicier than I expected, so next time I will halve the red pepper. I think we could also handle only using half the sausage. (We are not big meat eaters. It was a fun change of pace to be eating meat and potatoes.) I may also play around with using maple syrup instead of brown sugar next time. Thanks for a solid recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slovak potato dumplings with fried cabbage

this is pure comfort food. this was my mother's recipe. i hope you enjoy it.

1. dumplings:
2. in a mixing bowl , add grated potatoes , salt and egg
3. add flour , mixing well
4. add water if dough is stiff
5. drop dough from moistened spoon into a kettle of boiling water
6. cook partly covered for 7 to 10 minutes , stirring occasionaly
7. drain and rinse with cold water
8. cabbage:
9. in skillet , saute onions in butter / margarine until golden brown
10. add grated cabbage and salt
11. cover and fry over low heat stirring occasionaly until tender and golden brown
12. add to dumplings , mix well
13. you may need to add more salt to your taste
demonstrations.review: Delicious! Like the previous reviewer, I had just a bit of bacon that needed to be used. I fried two strips in a large skillet and used the drippings for frying the cabbage. Since I was using the bacon grease, I only used half the butter called for in the recipe, and I probably could have cut it even further. I chopped up the bacon and added it at the end when mixing everything together. This will definitely be added to my cold weather rotation. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dressed peas

this recipe is from "company's coming for christmas". we really like it as one of our veggies with christmas dinner.
