Cooked for 2 minutes on one of those sandwich grills. Perfect! Thanks Kimbearly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green cilantro rice

this is wonderfully flavored mexican rice. i love to serve it with chicken enchiladas. it is a must try if you love cilantro.

1. saute in butter the garlic , onion and jalapenos until soft
2. add uncooked rice
3. stir constantly until rice is slightly brown
4. pour in chicken broth
5. stir in the cilantro , cumin , salt and pepper
6. pour in a baking dish if you pan is not oven friendly
7. cover with a tight fitting lid
8. bake at 350 for 30- 45 minutes until rice is soft
9. fluff and serve hot
demonstrations.review: Very good. Will make again and again. Update: Have made twice now with brown rice and cannot tell it is brown rice. This is now my wife's favorite rice and I'm making it again today (Mother's Day). Leftover rice is good for using in stuffed peppers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredible oven fried chicken

this recipe is the most flavorful home made fried chicken i have ever had. also great picnic food.

1. whisk buttermilk , oil , hot pepper sauce , mustard , garlic , 1 tsp salt and 1 / 2 teaspoon pepper in a large bowl
2. add the onion and then the chicken turning to coat each piece with the marinade
3. cover
4. chill at least three hours or up to one day turning the chicken occasionally
5. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , flour , thyme , paprika , cayenne and 1 tsp salt in a large baking dish
6. remove the chicken from the marinade and roll in the breadcrumb mixture
7. set chicken on a rack to dry for about 30 minutes
8. preheat oven to 400f degrees
9. place chicken in large baking dish and pour butter over the chicken
10. bake until crisp and brown , approximately 50 minutes
demonstrations.review: I'd give more stars if I could. This chicken could be addictive! Best ever. Only changes I made was onion powder instead of onion slices and used Panko breadcrumbs. 24 hour marinade turning once. Thanks for posting Minx.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried tuna  carrot   hommus couscous

wowee wow, think you don't like cous cous, then try this recipe, i swear you'll be converted. a great healthy & tasty lunch. found in recipes +.

1. place couscous in a large heatproof bowl & stir in stock , add in curry powder , garlic & margarine and mix to combine
2. cover with plastic wrap & set aside for 5 mins or until all liquid has absorbed
3. fluff with a fork to separate grains
4. add tuna to couscous with capsicum , carrot , rocket , onions & lemon juice , season to taste & stir well to combine
5. top each serve with a generous dollop of hommus
demonstrations.review: We don't usually eat this kind of stuff in Texas, but hey I'm adventurous. This was good and healthy. I thought some red pepper hummus accented it nicely. I ate it as a meal since it has about everything in it you need. Thanks for posting Mandy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potato   cabbage casserole

i found this recipe on the internet awhile back and finally got around to trying it, and i'm glad i did. its very good.

1. preheat oven to 425f lightly oil a 3-quart baking dish
2. place potatoes in a large heavy pot
3. add salted water to cover and bring to a boil
4. reduce heat to medium and cook until tender , 10 to 20 minutes
5. meanwhile , drop cabbage into a pot of boiling salted water and cook , stirring occasionally , until tender , about 6 minutes
6. drain and set aside
7. drain potatoes and return to pot
8. place over low heat and shake , uncovered , for about 30 seconds to evaporate excess moisture
9. remoe from heat and mash potatoes with an electric mixer or a potato masher
10. add cream cheese and 1 teaspoon salt
11. mash until smooth
12. fold in scallions and reserved cabbage
13. adjust seasoning with salt and pepper
14. spread mixture into prepared baking dish 9x13 and top with cheese
15. bake casserole at 425 degrees uncovered , for 30 to 45 minutes depending on if the casserole goes into the oven warm or cold
demonstrations.review: I was a bit reserved about this recipe at first, but wanted a cabbage/potato dish to go with my homemade corned beef #85332. My wife and I both smiled after the first bite and had to go back for seconds, after all it's low calorie. Will make again and again. Thanks RecipeMonster.

target.recipe_text:
grilled vegetable kebabs

this is a great recipe. when i make the kebabs as a meal i serve them with a loaf of crusty italian bread. sometimes i grill up some italian sausage to complete the meal. if there are any leftovers i use them in my recipe for pasta sauce. they are also excellent toppings for pizza.

1. cut up the vegetables in chunks and put in large bowl
2. mix up the ingredients for the marinade
3. pour the marinade over the vegetables
4. cover the bowl with plastic wrap
5. refrigerate for at least 2 hours
6. after marinating put vegetables on skewers
7. grill for at least 10 minutes turning frequently
target.review: I'm not a veggie lover, but with the 50+ people at the party, this was a fair hit. Those that liked veggies, devoured these, and they were fun to make. I used baby bella 'shrooms, and I think should have used elephant garlic - if that was the intent (to skewer them too).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calico bean pot

my favorite bean casserole!!! i've taken this to many potlucks & picnics, & there's never a bean left. everyone asks for this recipe. this is from 'the best of the best' cookbook.

i always double this recipe & use a large crock pot; i cook for the same length of time listed below.

1. cut bacon into small pieces& fry till crisp
2. remove from pan
3. cook onion until soft in bacon grease
4. put all ingredients into 2 1 / 2 qt casserole
5. bake at 350 f for 1 hour
6. if you want them a little drier , don't cover
7. i prefer mine saucier , so i cover them
8. you may also cook in your crockpot for 4-5 hours , on low
demonstrations.review:
Thanks for the recipe. 
I have a similar one (no green beans, only 1/2 cup brown sugar, 1 teaspoon vinegar & 1 teaspoon prepared mustard, add 1/2 lb ground beef and the 1/2 cup ketchup as in earlier review.) It is outstanding even for those who don't like lima beans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mare s most delicious icing

this is a very light and fluffy icing..it is like whipped cream but it does not need to be refrigerated..important..to roosie..you must beat the sugar and butter and crisco for a full ten minutes..the hot(not boiling) milk must be added very very slowly..about 1/8 of a cup at a time all the while beating it well...

1. beat for a full 10 minutes the following 3 ingredients: butter or margarine , crisco , granulated sugar
2. heat milk in microwave till very hot
3. while beating
4. add hot milk to sugar and butter mixture very slowly
5. (i mean about 1 / 8 of a cup at a time -- all the while beating it well --
6. after all of the milk has been beaten in , beat in vanilla extract
7. this is delicious
demonstrations.review: It's almost pointless to add another 5-star to this, but WOW! I will NEVER use any other icing ever. I made a minor error of beating butter   crisco, adding the sugar after 10 mins. It gave the icing a bit of a grit but it was still off-the-wall good! I actually dripped the milk in very slowly because I didn't want it to break down as Roosie's did - Worked perfect for me! I'm gonna experiment with adding cocoa...hmmmm

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornbread with corn casserole

tasty!

1. mix first 3 ingredients together
2. add: margarine and jiffy corn bread mix , pour into well greased 8x8 casserole dish
3. bake for 1 hour at 375 degrees
demonstrations.review: Awesome recipe, and as everyone says, it's gone in an instant. I use 1/2 cup melted margarine and add 1 cup sour cream to mine. It also helps to keep it shallow so the casserole isn't too thick and can cook well all the way through without drying out the edges.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scandinavian almond bars

this has become a family favorite every year! if i don't make it my whole family teases me. i am sure that your family will love it too!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. stir together flour , baking powder and salt
3. in a large bowl beat margarine or butter till softened
4. add sugar and beat till fluffy
5. add egg and the 1 / 2 teaspoon of almond extract and beat well
6. add the flour mixture and beat till well mixed
7. divide the dough into fourths , form each portion into a 12 inch roll
8. place 2 of the rolls 4 to 5-inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
9. flatten each roll till it is about 3 inches wide
10. repeat with the remaining rolls
11. brush each flattened roll with milk and sprinkle about 2 tablespoons of almonds each
12. bake in a 325 oven for 12-14 minutes or till edges are lightly brown
13. while still warm , cut crosswise on the diagonal into 1 inch strips
14. cool completely on a wire rack
15. stir together the powdered sugar , the almond extract and enough of the 3-4 teaspoons of milk to make a drizzling consistency
16. drizzle over the cool bars
demonstrations.review: Me again. I just had to try this again, but I did two variations. I put chocolate chips on top of one batch. Didn't impress me, but some liked it. For the other, I used lemon extract with almonds on top. After baking, I added minced candied lemon (#116131)and lemon drizzle. Lighter tasting cookie for another set of taste buds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and sweet potato croquettes

lovely with a green salad

1. boil both potatoes together until tender , drain into large bowl and mash
2. stir in onions , seasoning , cheese , butter and chicken
3. mix well
4. shape mixture into 18 croquettes
5. cover
6. refrigerate 30 minutes
7. toss croquettes in flour , shake away excess
8. dip croquettes in eggs , then crumbs
9. shallow-fry croquettes in batches , in hot oil until browned
10. drain on absorbent paper
demonstrations.review: I also made them much smaller and ended up with a lot more. While you have to handle them VERY gently before and during getting a crisp cook to them, they were well received. Most were surprised at the sweet potato ingredient, but all loved it.

target.recipe_text:
grilled corn on the cob   beer

add grilled corn to your list of summer vacation or picnic traditions. this is a recipe everyone will be glad to help you with!! husk, soak, and grill the corn in anticipation of its sweet, smoky flavor.

1. peel husks back , but do not remove
2. using a stiff brush or your fingers , remove silk from corn
3. pull husks back up around corn
4. in an ice chest , cover corn with 12 pack of beer
5. then cover with bag of ice
6. soak for at least 1 hour
7. drink the beer
8. pull corn from cooler shaking corn to remove excess water
9. cover corn as much as possible with husks
10. if necessary , tie the
11. grill corn on an uncovered grill directly over medium-hot coals about 25 minutes or until tender , turning several times
12. carefully remove the husks and strings
13. meanwhile , in a small saucepan combine margarine or butter , lemon juice , and thyme
14. heat on the grill or stovetop until margarine is melted
15. brush mixture over the corn before serving
target.review: Really good. We followed your recipe to the letter, and had a most delicious meal and a most pleasant view of the nice summer evening.  It was just my husband and I, so there was plenty of everything to go around!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken soup verde

the verde part of the soup comes from the green vegetables in it - asparagus, peas and green onions.

1. bring broth and wine to a boil in a heavy large saucepan over medium high heat
2. add chicken asparagus and peas
3. reduce heat and simmer until chicken is almost cooked through and vegetables are crisp tender , about 3 minutes
4. add green onions and marjoram
5. simmer until chicken is cooked through and flavours blend , about 2 minutes longer
6. can be prepared a day in advance
7. cover and refrigerate
8. bring to a simmer before continuing
9. mix 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese into soup
10. season with salt and pepper
11. serve with remaining cheese
demonstrations.review: We really liked this. I didn't have marjoram, so I added a little basil and oregano to compensate. This is a different, easy, and GREAT chicken soup recipe. My daughter's home sick today, and she absolutely loved this. Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable rice pancakes

nan

1. combine all ingredients except oil
2. form into 12 thin patties , pressing firmly with hands
3. in large skillet , cook patties in heated oil until brown , turning once
4. serve with dairy sour cream or yogurt , if desired
demonstrations.review: These were very tasty... I used regular flour, but will have whole wheat next time.... I used lots of fresh onion and garlic, and made them a little more pourable with milk. I fried them like fritters in hot olive oil and they were a total hit. Whole grain rice, organic veggies, olive oil....healthy, yet tastes really decadent. Thanks for posting a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken

this is a family favorite recipe at our house that i usually make at least once per month. it's really like an oven-fried chicken, it should come out crispy and browned. i don't even measure the ingredients any more, i just dump the flour and spices in the bag and shake away - it's so easy! this is great with mashed potatoes (if you make gravy with the pan drippings) and corn (in the summer), carrots (in the winter). the original recipe is from gh illustrated cookbook, i've changed a few things.

1. in a large roasting pan , in a 425 oven , melt the butter or margarine
2. mix flour , salt , paprika and pepper in a heavy-duty plastic bag
3. shake chicken pieces in the bag , a few at a time , until evenly coated
4. in the pan , place the chicken , skin side down , in the melted butter
5. bake 30 minutes
6. turn chicken pieces and bake 15 minutes more until pieces are fork-tender
7. i usually make gravy from the de-greased pan juices , using some or all of the leftover flour and some chicken stock
demonstrations.review: This was really good and easy. My husband and I have spent a lot of time in Memphis, so I added some Rendevous seasoning. Also, I used chicken breasts and served roasted potatoes on the side. Yummy! Thanks Hey Jude!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion roll appetizers

these are really easy appetizers that you can make a few days in advance, and bake them the day they are needed. i am not a fan of onions, but these are delicious.

1. chop onions
2. place in frying pan with butter
3. fry for 20 minutes or until onions are limp
4. stir in cream cheese and grated swiss cheese
5. stir until melts
6. spread on tortillas
7. roll and refrigerate overnight
8. to cook: grease baking sheet
9. cut into 1" pieces
10. bake , upright , at 375 degrees for 10 minutes or until lightly brown
demonstrations.review: These were so great! I microwaved the onions with green peppers and minced garlic in no-transfat butter, then added low-fat cream cheese and 2% 4 cheese Mexican. I used whole grain tortillas...I'm a low-fat freak! After slicing, I sprinkled some gorgonzola and cayenne on top prior to baking.They were beautiful coming out of the oven!  My guests loved them, and I had way too few even for my small crowd! I will make these again, only I'll double or triple the recipe! Thanks leilani!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried bananas

serve at brunch or as a dessert.

1. slice each banana in half lengthwise and in half crosswise to end up with 8 banana halves
2. toss each half in melted butter and then in flakes
3. place on baking sheet coated with nonstick cooking spray
4. bake at 450 for 10 minutes
5. drizzle with honey
demonstrations.review: This is a great way to make fried bananas. I used Special K cinnamon pecan cereal, which I crushed in a gallon-sized ziplock bag with some frozen chocolate chips, added  a little brown sugar, and coated the bananas as instructed. I then refrigerated the coated bananas until time to bake.  I topped them with vanilla ice cream, and had a dessert that was so good it wasn't enough to satisfy my family. Next time, I'll double it. Thanks for the easy, wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
mean chef s asparagus with orange sesame butter

this is an adopted recipe, was originally submitted by the legendary mean chef. i have not made any changes to it (i wouldn't dare!)

1. snap the ends from the asparagus they'll break at the point of tenderness
2. or slice the ends off closer to the root end and peel spears with a swivel-bladed vegetable peeler
3. rinse , then soak for a few minutes in a couple of changes of cold , lightly salted water
4. agitate lightly to release grit that may be trapped
5. rinse well again
6. drain and pat with paper towels to absorb moisture
7. spread asparagus in a single layer on a large , rimmed baking sheet
8. drizzle with olive oil and sprinkle with 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
9. shake pan to distribute ingredients
10. roast in a preheated 425-degree oven 12 to 15 minutes
11. test for tenderness
12. while the asparagus is cooking , melt the butter in a small saucepan
13. whisk in the juice concentrate , sesame oil , teaspoon salt and several grindings black pepper
14. keep warm
15. transfer asparagus to a serving dish
16. drizzle with the butter , sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve immediately
target.review:
Finally found a store with fresh asparagus and have saved this to make again!  Thanks for sharing another great Mean Chef recipe!
We loved the sweet & salt taste paired with the toasted sesame seeds. Wonderful. Wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp   artichoke fettuccini

i found this recipe at allrecipe.com but made a bunch of changes to make it my own.  use any pasta of your choice.

1. cook pasta in boiling water
2. while pasta is cooking , saute onion and garlic in 2 tblspn oil for about 5 minutes
3. remove to bowl
4. add wine , chicken broth & lemon juice to the onion and garlic mixture , set aside
5. add shrimp and remaining 2 tblspn of oil to pan for about 3 minutes
6. stir in artichokes , onion & garlic mixture and heat to boiling about another 5 minutes on a low to medium flame
7. toss with pasta , parsley , salt and pepper
8. top with grated cheese
9. serve immediately -- enjoy !
demonstrations.review: 5 stars and 2 thumbs up from me and my son!  I changed the recipe slightly, using 2 cans of artichoke hearts and added some bay scallops.  Wonderful recipe, super fast, easy and great on a hot summer night!  Thank you for posting a recipe that will see lots of activity from here on out!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
outstanding chicken and wild rice soup

this is a recipe from a local coffee shop here in oklahoma. it's wonderful, and best with cornbread or just crackers. this soup is definitely a treat!

1. boil chicken in 6 cups of water until well done
2. take chicken out let cool a while
3. now you need to add your wild rice
4. add carrots cook 5 minutes then add in celery , onion and garlic
5. cook for 15 minutes
6. debone chicken pieces and pull apart using hands making small pieces of chicken
7. add to soup mixture
8. now it is time to add all your dry seasonings to your soup
9. it is also time to add your peas and corn
10. after this is the time to add your heavy cream
11. cook on a medium temperature , stirring often until you see it start to cook down or thicken up
12. this will be a process of about 2 hours cooking time
13. but may i state "well worth it" !
demonstrations.review: WOW - very flavorful soup!  I made using boneless/skinless breasts as that is what I had on hand.  I was leery of the peas (never had that in chicken & wild rice soup before) but they really added a nice punch of flavor. DH loved this soup.  Served with dinner rolls and a large salad. I will make this again for sure! Made this for January 2009 Belly Warmers: Soups And Stews.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog pancakes

i have not used the called for sesame oil in these. i have used walnut oil and that worked nicely (plain oil will do just fine). if the batter seems a bit dense just thin it slowly with more eggnog or a bit if milk till it seems right to you. very quick, easy and dh loved (mine will eat the whole batch)

1. in a bowl , combine flour , baking powder , baking soda , salt , egg , eggnog , vanilla , and sesame oil
2. beat until smooth
3. using oil as needed to grease , pour batter by 1 / 4 cup and cook on a 375f griddle
4. flip to brown slightly on other side
5. serve with maple syrup
demonstrations.review: Annacia, these are just absolutely wonderful.  I added the extra milk as other mentioned and also added a couple of grates of fresh grated nutmeg to the batter.  I served with Brown Sugar & Peppered Bacon with warmed maple syrup.  Thanks for posting, holidays or not, these will be served often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white trash hamburger gravy and breakfast biscuits

this was my sister's favorite thing to eat when she was growing up. she wouldn't let anyone but me make it for her.

1. cook and drain beef
2. melt butter in a pan and when melted and lightly sizzling add the flour
3. whisk until combined and gently simmer the butter / flour mixture for about two minutes to remove the flour / starch taste but don't let it brown any
4. add the 1
5. 5 cups of milk and quickly whisk until smooth
6. simmer until thick over medium heat stirring constantly
7. it will be quite thick
8. add the half and half cream and quickly whisk until smooth
9. cook over low heat until thickened
10. add the beef and adjust the seasonings
11. serve over good biscuits well buttered
12. this is a very creamy and rich gravy
13. you may use 2 cups whole milk if you need to omit the cream
14. if it is too thick for your taste -- then dilute with more milk -- but it usually is perfect the way it is written
15. leftovers are excellent
demonstrations.review: I think we are related!  My mother & grandma made this often when I was growing up.  This is one of those dishes that we never had a recipe, didn't even think of writing one.  It was just a regular staple at our house.  Sometimes we used canned biscuits, sometimes we would toast white bread (store bought of course, we would not think of wasting grandma's homemade white bread for this stuff!).  Thanks for the memories Potsie, I'll be making this again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lobster  or crab  newburg for two

this is another recipe from the dayton's-hudson's- and marshall field's cookbook. this one was submitted by leny sanders of marshall field's. it's sinfully delicious, and very easy.

1. in lg skillet , melt butter
2. saute shallot and red pepper
3. add flour and stir until mixed
4. add broth and sherry
5. simmer for 3 minutes
6. add mushrooms
7. simmer 5 minutes
8. add lobster or crab and half and half
9. do not boil , but let this mixture heat through
10. spoon into 1 qt casserole dish
11. sprinkle with breadcrumbs and parmesan cheese
12. place under broiler until breadcrumbs are light brown
demonstrations.review: Made this for the August 2008 Seafood Photo Challenge.  This is super easy and quick!  I did not have anything prepped other than the pre-cooked lobster and crab meat that I used.  Dinner was done and being served just at 30 minutes!  Other than the fact I had to mix the lobster & crab (limited availability where I am) I did make as written.  It did seem a bit lacking in a little flavor so I did season the bread crumbs with a little Old Bay Seasoning.  Perfect!  DH had 2 large helpings and said it reminded him of our trip to Maine.  Thanks MizzNezz for another recipe that will be a great classic for us!

target.recipe_text:
italian inspired potatoes

this was inspired by chef potpie's recipe#197754. i went to make it and thought it was missing tomatoes...i realized i had some sundried tomatoes and other flavorful add-ins and came up with this. it turned out very yummy. i love the tangy additions with the salami. to me this is a meal in itself! you could add onion to this also if you like. i might even try it with some capers next time. hmm...and perhaps feta cheese instead of mozzarella with shredded chicken or no meat for greek potatoes! it's so fun to experiment. this could also be made in the oven or with leftover roasted potatoes or canned potatoes. enjoy!

1. place potato halves cut side up in a single layer in a microwavable dish that has a lid
2. put 1 tablespoon of water in the bottom of the dish
3. sprinkle potato halves with garlic salt
4. cover and microwave on high 8-15 minutes until tender
5. meanwhile , mix together the cheese , oregano , salami and sundried tomatoes
6. when potatoes are done top them evenly with the cheese mixture
7. place one red bell pepper strip on each potato and arrange green olive rings around them
8. microwave for 1-2 minutes until the cheese is melted
9. serve with sour cream if desired
target.review: These were fantastically delicious!  I actually didn't have any sundried tomatoes, but I did have some leftover spaghetti sauce (no meat). After the potatoes were cooked through in the microwave, I spread a thin layer of the sauce over them (like a pizza) and then sprinkled the rest of the ingredients.  Threw the pan in the oven with my chicken that was almost finished baking.  The taters browned up nicely, cheese melted, and they were so so yummy!  Thank you thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerbread gingerbread cake

this is my grandmother's recipe from the 1930's. it's my favorite spicy gingerbread/cake recipe that's wonderful served warm with whipped cream or butter. prep time is estimated.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour an 8" square pan
3. the ingredients listed under "cream together" should be added one ingredient at a time , creaming in between each addition
4. when you have finished adding / creaming all the liquid ingredients , keep beating the liquid mixture , folding in the dry mixture , alternating with the 2 / 3 cup sour milk
5. once everything is mixed in , pour the batter into the prepared pan
6. bake at 350
7. check for doneness by inserting a toothpick in the middle
8. when it comes out clean , it's done
demonstrations.review: Yum yum yum!  We loved this recipe, even though my cake fell.  I live at high altitude and probably should have added another 1/4 cup of flour.  I used sour cream in place of the sour milk because it needed to be used (so, I suppose that could have been the problem, but I doubt it).  I doubled all of the spices.  Served it with Kittencal's caramel sauce (Recipe #78088) and whipped cream.  It was absolutely divine and we ate every last spec!  Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked southwest sandwiches

yummy sandwiches.

1. in a bowl , combine olives , chili powder , cumin and salt and set aside 2 tablespoons
2. add the mayonnaise , sour cream and onion to the remaining olive mixture
3. place the bread on an ungreased baking sheet and spread 1 tablespoon of mayonnaise mixture on each slice
4. top each with turkey and tomatoes
5. spread with another tablespoon of mayonnaise mixture and top with cheeses
6. sprinkle with reserved olive mixture
7. bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  We loved these sandwiches!  The sauce for these is so tasty - my whole family (including my two smallest) gobbled these up!  I did change a couple of things - didn't have any olives, so just left them out. Also, I wanted them to not be open-faced, so I put sauce on the other half of the buns, put the lids on, wrapped them in foil and baked them in the oven for 20 minutes at 375 degrees.  So delish!  Thanks bmcnichol!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef enchiladas

the sauce on these is very rich and full of flavor. everyone's favorite!

1. brown ground beef , drain
2. add next 6 ingredients , mix well
3. put 1 / 3 cup filling down middle of each tortilla
4. wrap , place seam side down in 13x9 baking pan
5. for sauce: heat oven to 350 degrees f
6. saute onion and green pepper in hot oil until tender
7. add next 4 ingredients , mix well
8. pour over tortillas
9. cover and bake 30 minutes
10. sprinkle with cheese and bake 7 more minutes
demonstrations.review: Yum!! We loved this casserole - it was delish!! I really like how the cottage cheese adds a creaminess to the recipe, and the enchilada sauce has the perfect flavor and consistency. And, I almost always have everything for this recipe in my fridge & pantry. I follow the recipe exactly except that I add a can of red or chili beans to the meat filling to make it go further.  Thank you thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate toffee crunch ice cream cake

i was perusing the ice cream cake recipes here and couldn't find what i had in mind so i made this one up. at our house we use gluten free cake mix, lactose free ice cream, and sugar free cool whip so please feel free to adapt this recipe to meet your dietary needs. the cake ingredients included are for the gluten free mix i make. if your cake calls for more or less, eggs, water, or oil, make sure to use the necessary changes. cook time is partly freezing time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine cake mix , eggs , butter , and water
3. pour into a well greased 13x9 pan
4. bake for 35-40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
5. allow cake to cool completely
6. when cake is fully cooled , using a serrated knife , cut cake in half lengthwise
7. place the bottom half of the cake back in the pan
8. top with the softened ice cream , and spread it evenly over the cake
9. sprinkle the toffee chips in an even layer over the ice cream
10. place the top layer of the cake on the toffee chips / ice cream
11. spread the softened cool whip over the top of the cake
12. freeze 2 or more hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Loved this super easy recipe! I halved this recipe by making 1/2 box of cake mix in a round, 9" springform pan (I weighed the mix and used half, then used half the oil, water, and 2 eggs).  After baking, I popped the sides off the pan, sliced the cake in half with a serrated knife, and put the sides back on. Then, I layered ice cream, toffee, and hot fudge topping in the middle before replacing the top.  So quick to make and the whole family loved it.  Thanks for such a simple, clear explanation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Wow!!! Yum! I have prepared pot roast for years, and it was never quite this good! I did only add 1/2 pkg of ranch dressing. Also, I didn't have brown gravy - only had turkey gravy mix. SO, we added that and it was just great!  I also put carrots & potatoes aroud it in the pot after I had sprinkled all the seasonings on the meat.  They also turned out so yummy! What a terrific, adaptable recipe that makes its own delectable gravy! Thank you Yooper!!

target.recipe_text:
ham and rice skillet

very simple and fast to fix.all in a skillet.

1. saute peppers with butter in the skillet
2. stir in flour slowly add milk stir
3. bring to a boil
4. stir until thickened
5. reduce heat to low stir in sour cream until blended
6. stir in remaining ingredients
7. heat thoroughly
target.review: YUM!  This was delicious! I added some peas and a bit of swiss to the mix, but other than that followed exactly.  It was creamy and extremely tasty, not to mention affordable to make.  This will definately be entered into our rotation.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cousin jim s amazing apple pie

this is the best apple pie i have ever had. this is one of those pies where everything just blends together on the palate beautifully and makes your mouth want more. i was not an apple pie fan until i tasted this! it is better than any bakery, restaurant, or grocery store bought (duh) apple pie i've tried. oh - and by the way, it is worth the effort to roll out the dough...mmm, mmm! you can use this light, flaky dough with tons of other fruit pies.

1. prepare the apples: peel , core , and slice apples thinly , and place in a large bowl
2. cover apples with sugars , flour , vanilla , and spices , and mix well with apples
3. set aside
4. at this point , preheat oven to 350
5. prepare the dough: mix salt , flour , and shortening in mixer- then add ice cold water
6. remove dough , divide in half , and roll out one half using flour to keep from sticking- reserve the other half for top crust
7. line 9 inch pie pan with half dough
8. allow 1 / 4 inch extra dough to stick out- you'll pinch it with the top crust later
9. put apple mixture into crust-lined pan
10. roll out top crust and cover apples
11. finish the pie: gently pinch bottom and top crusts together , and flute edges of dough
12. poke several fork holes in top crust , and dot crust with butter and sprinkle with sugar
13. bake at 350 for 65-70 minutes
14. allow to cool 20 minutes before serving plain or with vanilla bean ice cream , cool whip , or whipped cream
15. this also warms up great in the microwave
16. and , by all means , enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This pie was delicious. I actually made it twice already. The first time it had WAY too much liquid. I cut down the sugar to 3/4 cup of brown sugar and 1/3 of white and it turned out perfect this time. Thanks so much for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one dish chicken and rice bake

this recipe goes together in 5 minutes and bakes in 45. best of all it is mixed and baked in the same casserole! enjoy this recipe from american century cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix soup , water , rice , and 1 / 4 tsp each of paprika and pepper in ungreased shallow 2-quart casserole
3. lay chicken on top and sprinkle with remaining paprika and pepper
4. cover and bake until bubbly and chicken shows no signs of pink in the center--about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was really excited to try this recipe, but found that it really lacked flavor.  I wish I had taken some of the advice of other raters and added some other flavors.  I did add some mushrooms, but it really didn't taste like much at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: YUM!  This were light, moist, and delicious!! I used just under a tbsp of the vanilla and added a dash of almond extract!  The definitely could have made more than 12 cupcakes. These cupcakes are HUGE!!  Great flavor and consistency!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sherry buttered shrimp

this is so very simple, and so very tasty. elegant and perfect for a nice, romantic dinner.

1. in large skillet , cook mushrooms , garlic , and shallot in butter until tender
2. add shrimp , basil and pepper
3. cook and stir until shrimp are pink
4. stir in sherry
5. simmer for 3 minutes
6. serve with cooked rice
7. makes 4 servings
demonstrations.review: This was delicious.  I had to make it using what I had on hand so I did not add mushrooms and I used onion instead of shallot, but it was still wonderful!  I made this dish for 2 of us and there was not one shrimp left! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy skillet cheese topped chili macaroni

this is a quick and easy recipe for a weeknight meal. its very tasty and very filling. dh loves it when i make this and always takes leftovers to work!

1. in a large skillet , brown onion and garlic with ground beef
2. drain and return to pan
3. add kidney beans , tomato sauce , water , chili powder , and salt
4. cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes
5. add cooked macaroni and stir
6. add grated cheddar to top , cover and simmer just until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: This dish was OK.  I made it as directed and it turned out to be pretty bland.  I took the advice and added some sour cream and that definately helped.  Next time I will try adding a packet of taco or chili seasoning to give it some more flavor!  It was definately warm and comforting.  Despite the lack of flavor I wanted to keep eating more.  I will try it again with some more spices.

target.recipe_text:
postre de mango  mango dessert

this dessert is best made not too sweet. this allows the natural flavour of the mango to come through.

1. gently dissolve gelatin in warm water
2. pure the mango flesh
3. add the cream , sour cream , lime juice , and gelatin to the mangoes
4. process or blend
5. add the honey to desired sweetness
6. pour into serving bowl and chill
7. serve garnished with thin slices of lime and mango
target.review: I also used milk in place of the heavy cream and sweetener in place of honey. The dessert turned out nicely! Not so sweet, tangy and kinda mousse-like. I wasn't so fond of the texture but the taste was yum. Thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meethi lassi

from the city times!

1. blend everything well in a blender
2. serve chilied in a tall glass
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic! The yoghurt I used wasn't the set kind so I measured a cup of it into my blender along with a handful of ice cubes and added about a tablespoon of water (instead of half cup). I used artificial sweetener =) It was so wonderful, I looove cumin so I enjoyed this thoroughly. I can't wait for my friends to come over so I can serve them this drink! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
key lime sauce

my husband loves key lime pie.  after a recent trip to florida, he got a hankering for some, so luckily i found recipe #161578 kelly's rich & creamy key lime pie which is just delicious and easy to make.  but dh wanted me to drizzle a key lime sauce over the pie.  so here is a recipe i found that, if desired, goes great with peacefulnightdove's recipe. this would also be good drizzled over bread pudding, among other things.

1. in a small bowl , dissolve the cornstarch in the 3 tablespoons of water
2. in a small non-aluminum saucepan stir together the sugar , the lime juice and 1 / 4 cup of water
3. bring to a boil over moderate heat to dissolve the sugar
4. stir in the cornstarch mixture and boil , stirring , for about 30 seconds or until the lime sauce thickens
demonstrations.review: I've been craving a sauce like this for a loooong time, I'm so glad I found it here =) I used freshly squeezed key lime juice and added about half a tablespoon more of cornstarch to make the sauce a little thicker. I also added a drop of green food colouring and some cubes of Nata De Coco... It's SO good, I used it as a topping for vanilla ice cream, it's PERFECT for it! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the most ultimate buttery cream cheese pound cake

this is the most ultimate rich dense buttery pound cake! no lein this cake but the eggs--- for best results this cake should be baked a day ahead and wrapped in plastic, or it can be frozen for up to 3 months, servings is of coarse estimated ---  this is wonderful served with a blueberry or strawberry sauce :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. generously grease two 8 x 4-inch loaf pans or a 4-quart tube pan
3. in a bowl cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
4. add sugar
5. beat until light and fluffy , about 5-7 minutes
6. add the eggs one at a time beating well after each addition
7. mix in vanilla
8. with mixer on low add the flour and salt in two additions
9. immediately pour in batter into prepared pan
10. tap pans to eliminate any large air bubbles in the batter
11. bake 60-75 minutes , or until cakes tests done
12. cool in pans for 10 minutes
13. turn out the cakes then cool completely with the tops up on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: My uncle (who is VERY particular about butter cakes) asked me to bake one since he's been having a craving. I've tried some other recipes which he did not like at all so when I found this, I decided to give it a go yesterday. It turned out perfectly! I didn't tell a soul there's cream cheese in the cake and everyone had no clue how this "butter cake" turned out sooo buttery and creamy. Even my uncle was very impressed that he took home a large chunk! He says that this cake tastes just like the ones at 5-star hotels (now we know their secret lol), score! Anyway, I didn't have any loaf pans so I used a 10-inch cake tin and baked it for 45 minutes extra. I also reduced the sugar to 2 cups (it still turned out sweet, but not terribly). I love this cake and yes, it is going very very VERY fast! Thank you for the most wonderful pound cake recipe in the world =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s danish potato salad

a easy-to-make inexpensive potato salad. the homemade dressing for this is really good and i feel what makes it so good, and works equally well with macaroni salad. this is my mom's recipe, and her mom made it before her. i use about 6 hard-boiled eggs because i like my potato salad with more eggs. the prep and cook time is only a estimate, as i've never timed how long it takes to make this.
if you use mayo instead of miracle whip i'd suggest starting with only 1 t. sugar and adding more to taste as mayo is sweeter than miracle whip.
and of course please feel free to adapt this recipe ingredient-wise to your familie's preferences.

1. combine first 6 ingredients and bring to a boil
2. gradually beat in well-beaten eggs
3. cook , stirring constantly until slightly thickened
4. remove from heat and add salad dressing
5. mix well and pour over potato , egg , celery , onion and relish
6. add more salt and pepper if desired
7. refrigerate until well-chilled and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I've JUST made it and am currently eating it warm, it's sooo good. The rest will go into the fridge for tonight :) I used Mayo and decided not to add in any sugar. Perfect. Next time I'll add in a handful of crispy chopped up salami and perhaps a bit of macaroni. Thanks for a great recipe :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 minute no bake cookies

from a quaker oats newsletter.

1. in large saucepan , combine sugar , margarine , milk and cocoa
2. bring to boil over medium heat , stirring frequently
3. continue boiling 3 minutes , stirring frequently
4. remove from heat
5. stir in oats
6. drop by tablespoonfuls onto waxed paper
7. let stand until firm
8. store tightly covered
9. makes about 3 dozen
10. if using old fashioned oats , cool mixture in saucepan 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: I modified this recipe a wee bit - I didn't use the cocoa and added in some vanilla extract and used soft light brown sugar (was out of white). They were waayyyy too sweet and I think I need to cut down the sugar by half next time! Also, they needed to sit in the fridge for awhile to set (no problem there). I still thought these were yummy though, and I'll make them again with less sugar :) Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
lamu style mahi mahi

i received this recipe from my pastor's wife. it is too sophisticated for my kids, but if you like spicy food, i think you will enjoy this. i have only made it with mahimahi, but it should work with any firm white fish.

1. in a small bowl , mix garlic , lime juice , cumin , and pepper into a paste
2. spread mixture onto fish& let sit for 20 minutes
3. heat oil in a large skillet and saute fish over moderate heat for 8 minutes , turning it over halfway through the cooking time
4. drain onto paper towels
5. serve garnished with lime slices
target.review:
I'm normally not a fish fan,but this was amazing! I know I'll be making this alot.
I followed the recipe to the letter and it was absolutely perfect.I served it with white rice and there wasn't a drop of fish left at the end of dinner. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
date loaf candies

nan

1. in a medium sauce pan , mix sugar , dates , butter and milk
2. cook for 10 - 15 minutes
3. remove from heat and add walnuts , and vanilla
4. beat until it thickens
5. pour onto a cleaned dish towel
6. make sure the towel is wet but not soaking wet--little over damp
7. roll it lengthwise and put into fridge until it has completely cooled
8. unroll the wrap and slice
demonstrations.review:
My Grandmother made this EVERY Christmas! Brings back fond memories of the holidays.This is an amazing recipe and I'm sure I'll be making this for the entire famiy this holiday season!
Thanks guys!! I've been looking for this recipe for years!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s sour cream raisin pie

this is my mother's favorite pie recipe and it came from her mother. just wanted to pass along an old family favorite to my zaar family.

1. mix together filling ingredients and cook until thick
2. pour into pre-baked pie shell -- that's it , no more cooking
3. optionally you may top with meringue , lightly brown the meringue
demonstrations.review:
Wonderful recipe!
I made it for Thanksgiving and it was a big hit!
The nutmeg gave it an amazing taste!!
So creamy and rich tasting.
I will be making this pie quite often.
Thanks for posting such an excellent recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy shrimp ramen

i love shrimp flavored ramen and just shrimp period. i was looking for something quick so of course i reached for the ramen but then realized i had a few pieces of shrimp left in a bag from a dinner the night before. so i decided to try and make a "shrimp pasta" and it turned out so good! note: when i made this i just added the seasoning to my taste so im going to try my best to put it in measurements.

1. break noodles in half inside of packet
2. make noodles as directed on package
3. while noodles are preparing , heat a small pan over medium heat
4. add butter and shrimp
5. season with garlic powder , creole seasoning , and black pepper
6. cook shrimp for about 4 mins
7. when noodles are done drain them leaving about 1 / 4 cup of the water and place in a bowl
8. add seasoning packet , shrimp out of the pan , and hot sauce
9. mix together and enjoy =]
demonstrations.review:
OH my gosh!!!!
This makes AMAZING shrimp!!!!
I used the shrimp flavorings for my shrimp stir fry and it is wonderful!!
I'm looking forward to using it as you wrote with ramen noodles!

Thanks for a perfect recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon glazed popcorn

no corn syrup needed, i've left cinnamon out and added a 1/2 tsp vanilla or butter rum flavoring

1. spread popcorn over sided baking tray
2. in small bowl combine egg white , sugar , cinnamon , salt beat with fork til frothy
3. pour over popcorn and toss coating all
4. bake at 300f degrees for 20 minutes cool store in airtight container
demonstrations.review:
Oh my gosh!!!
I've got a new addiction!
I made half cinnamon and half vanilla.Wow!They were both amazing.I will be making this one alot!!!!!!!
I can't wait to play around with adding other flavors and food coloring for holidays and get togethers!
Kudo's for listing this LDJ!!
Many thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken crescent appetizers

my aunt serves these as an appetizer for family gatherings. they are yummy and disappear in a flash.

1. mix diced chicken , cream cheese , chopped chives , and margarine together
2. separate rolls in triangles
3. place chicken mix on top of each
4. roll up as directed and pinch ends together
5. bake according to package directions
6. optional: may brush with beaten egg before baking
demonstrations.review:
Excellent!!!
I've made these many times and just can't get enough.I've even made these for dinner by adding more filling to each one.
I added more chives and let the mixture sit over night.
I cannot recommend this recipe enough!
This has quickly become my favorite comfort food!

target.recipe_text:
blackened trout

my first time ever cooking trout, altho i've eaten it twice at o'charleys restaurant. delicious, easy, and tasty way to prepare trout.. found this online, but i did list the type of trout i just fixed. the cooking time depends on the thickness of your fillets. also, i've tried this with catfish fillets too, and its just as good.it would work on any of your favorite fish fillets.

1. preheat large , heavy skillet until very hot
2. combine paprika , salt , onion powder , garlic powder , cayenne pepper , white pepper , black pepper , thyme , and oregano in a small bowl
3. then place it in a shallow plate that's big enough to roll the fish inches
4. dip fillets in melted butter , then in seasoning mixture , and place in hot skillet and cook 2-5 minutes on each side until blackened
5. reheat melted butter to a simmer , and pour in small bowls to use for dipping
target.review: what a wonderful, uncomplicated recipe! And so tasty. This is such a great way to do trout. Its a real keeper, and I'll be making it again and again.Didn't realize I could enjoy any fish as well as I did when trying this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strong hot chocolate

knock your boots off hot chocolate! tastes like about 5 of the richest candy bars imaginable, melted into your cup! 
this is a recipe that appeared in our sunday paper. it is by pastry chef elizabeth falkner from her book, demolition desserts.

1. off the heat , in a 1-quart saucepan , combine the milk and cream
2. split the vanilla bean lengthwise and use the
3. whisk the cocoa powder and brown sugar into the milk , then place the saucepan over medium heat and whisk for 5 to 7 minutes , or until frothy and simmering
4. place the chocolate in a heatproof bowl
5. remove and discard the vanilla pod from the milk mixture , then pour the mixture over the chocolate
6. add the salt and whisk until the chocolate is smooth
7. divide the hot chocolate among cups and top each with 2 marshmallows or a dollop of whipped cream
8. can be cooled , tightly covered and refrigerated up to 3 days
demonstrations.review: Oh my, oh how rich! Just the perfect thing for the cold temps we're having. Perfect for cuddling up under a warm blanket and watching a favorite movie. And one is plenty. can't handle to much of something so rich and so delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet milk corn cakes with tennessee white bean salsa

great dish from martha white. i didn't have corn meal mix, so i did a search and found a recipe for making one cup of cornbread mix from regular corn meal. worked great!

1. prepare and cook sweet milk corn cakes as directed in recipe
2. heat oil in medium saucepan over medium heat until hot
3. add onion and garlic: cook about 5 minutes or until tender stirring frequently
4. stir in beans
5. cook until bubbly
6. mash mixture with potato masher or fork until thick and lumpy
7. spoon into serving bowl ,
8. set aside
9. combine tomato , chile , avacado , bell pepper , cilantro , and lemon juice in small bowl
10. mix well
11. add salt and pepper to taste
12. spoon tomato mixture over bean mixture
13. serve with sweet milk corn cakes
14. sweet milk corncakes:
15. beat egg in large bowl
16. add corn meal mix , sugar and milk: mix well
17. if batter is too thick , add additional milk
18. heat griddle or large skillet to medium heat grease lightly with oil
19. pour 1 / 4 cup batter for each corn cake onto hot griddle
20. cook until edges look cooked and bubbles begin to break on surface
21. turn and cook until golden brown
demonstrations.review: so different, and so good. I get tired of the same old same old. This is unique, and satisfying. A very good dish. I made it just as it is written with no problems. Martha White does indeed have a winner. A simple dish for a simple meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yellow squash dessert

wonderful way to get kids to eat squash. i've made this for years, and haven't found anyone who didn't like it. its creamy, easy and delicious.i used to tell my kids it was a dessert pudding, and it was years before they realized they were eating squash. it has a nice vanilla taste. you can use splenda as a substitute for the sugar.

hint: precook your squash by peeling, seeding, cubing and boil it in enough water to cover it, for about 20 minutes, then drain throughly.

1. add margarine , sugar , vanilla , salt , flour , eggs , and milk to squash and mix well
2. -pour mixture into a buttered 9" x 13" casserole dish
3. -bake in 375 degree oven for 25 minutes , or until slightly golden brown and a knife inserted in center comes out clean
4. -serve slightly warm with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: oh my Gosh! How wonderful! What an unusual way to eat squash. It tastes like a vanilla custard. Wow! Its so good with whipped Cream topping it. Don't tell your kids what it is, and they'll eat it up!!! thanks for this great recipe. I can't believe I'm the first to try it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb eggplant  aubergine  parmesan

i am on a low carb diet (south beach) and i've found this recipe to be best in satisfying my craving of pasta with red sauce or pizza....god, i miss those days! but this is just as good and healthy too; a good dish for a vegetarian that may also be watching their carb intake. serve this as a main dish (serves 3) or as a side dish (serves 6).

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. peel eggplant , if you wish , and cut into 1 / 4 inch thick round slices
3. lightly grease a medium sized casserole dish and place half of the eggplant on the bottom
4. top with 1 / 2 cup of parmesan , 3 / 4 cup mozzarella and 3 / 4 cup of sauce , sprinkle with spices
5. repeat layers and again , sprinkle with spices
6. cover with aluminum foil and bake for 40 minutes or until eggplant is tender
7. uncover and top with the remaining 1 / 2 cup of mozzarella and once again , sprinkle with spices
8. bake for about 5 more minutes or until the cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I agree... it definately al dente.. lets just say I cooked it 20 minutes longer and it was raw. It could have been good if it would have gotten done. Perhaps it was the egg plant... maybe it was old and tough.. who knows? If you do try this, plan on a long cook time.I peeled it too.I cooked it at least 15 minutes longer, and put it in the microwave for 3 minutes, and it was still raw. I doubt seriously if I will EVER make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
it s cold outside bean and sausage chowder

this is a great soup to make on cold winter days when you don't know what to make for dinner and it's too cold and snowy (or rainy) to go to the store -- this is the soup that is perfect for those days when i used to live on the east coast or when kids were sick--using ingredients that i almost always have on hand and which is very adaptable to subsitutions depending what is in the refrig.  we like this soup served with whole whole wheat bread or rolls. recipe source: bon appetit (october 1982)

1. in a large heavy skillet fry bacon until crisp , reserving 2 tablespons bacon drippings
2. drain on paper towels and crumble and set aside
3. transfer reserved bacon drippings to a large dutch oven over medium heat and add onion , green pepper and celery , cooking for 10 minutes or until vegetables are tender
4. remove from heat
5. stir in flour and next six ingredients and cook over medium-high heat until mixture comes to a boil , stirring constantly
6. reduce heat , cover and simmer over for 25-30 minutes
7. add sausage , cover and continue simmering another 10 minutes
8. ladle chowder into bowls and sprinkle with reserved bacon
demonstrations.review: wow, this was good! I used beef broth also in place of water. And it was even better the next day as leftovers. I simply added a little more water with beef bouillion, a little more onion, and a little bit of corn. Great stuff! I originally used a can of black beans and a can of pintos. I added a can of great northern beans to the leftover chowder.It was like a brand new dish! Thanks a lot for posting this recipe.

target.recipe_text:
zesty baked fries

low fat--high taste! so easy to make. these make great appys with low fat ranch or blue cheese dressing.

1. mix first 5 ingredients
2. cut potatoes in sticks
3. toss potatoes with cheese mixture
4. place on baking sheet coated with cooking spray
5. spray potatoes lightly with cooking spray
6. bake at 425 for 15 minutes , turn potatoes over and bake 15 more minutes , until crisp
target.review: These were pretty good -- however they didn't really "wow" us. I'll probably give them another shot though since they were so easy to make! I think I might add some fresh minced garlic next time -- we love our garlic :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
veggie crunch

my weight loss key!  :)   
this is a great way to eat fresh veggies.  it is light, easy to make, and best of all delicious.  cook time is refrigeration.  
i never get tired of this way of enjoying my veggies.

1. prepare all veggies and place in a cover able bowl
2. mix water , vinegar , salt , pepper , sugar , and basil in a separate bowl until everything is dissolved
3. pour over veggies
4. refrigerate at least 3 hours before eating , but this will get better and better as it marinates
5. i have never had a batch last more than 4 days , but i think that would be my limit for storage
demonstrations.review: I'm glad I found this because I was trying to find a good way to incorporate more veggies into my diet without having to dip them in salad dressing -- which starts to defeat the purpose. Anyways, the only thing I changed was I substituted yellow bell pepper for the celery since I don't care for celery. Thanks for a healthy snack idea!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ancho chile marinade for meat ala chipotle

this is a recipe from a great "gourmet" taco joint called chipotle. they have 2 things, tacos and burritos. this place it totally crave-worthy! if you ever get a chance, try their carnitas soft tacos. so good!

1. soak dried chilis overnight in water until soft
2. remove seeds
3. add all ingredients , except chicken to a food processor , puree until smooth
4. spread mixture evenly over chicken and refrigerate at least 1 hour , but up to 24 hours
5. heat grill to 400f
6. salt chicken breasts to taste
7. grill for about 4 minutes per side , until done
8. garnish with fresh cilantro
demonstrations.review: This was great! Chipotle's is one of my fav restraunts, so I wanted to try and duplicate a 'burrito bol' at home. I made this along with recipe #147335. Was close enough to the real thing to satisfy my craving.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free pizza crust

from carol fenster's "special diet solutions".

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. in medium bowl using regular beaters , blend all ingredients on low speed
3. beat on high speed for 3 minutes
4. dough will resemble soft bread dough
5. put mixture on lightly greased 12-inch pizza pan or 11 x 7-inch pan
6. liberally sprinkle rice flour on dough , then press dough into pan , continuing to sprinkle with flour to prevent sticking to hands
7. make edges slightly thicker to hold toppings
8. bake pizza crust for 10 minutes
9. remove from oven
10. spread pizza crust with your favorite sauce and toppings
11. bake another 20 to 25 minutes or until top is nicely browned
demonstrations.review: I absolutely love this pizza crust! I have been partial to kinnickiniks individual pizza crusts and especailly amy's rice crust pizza. But this is a lot cheaper and so easy to make! I will be using this one from now on. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick spanish rice

great side dish for your mexican fiesta. try with recipe #17130!  it is as good as you'll find in any mexican restaurant.  update:  1 teaspoon cumin was added to original recipe.  i took some of my reviewers suggestion and added 1 teaspoon of cumin to the recipe. they were right. cumin definitely adds to the taste.

1. in medium saucepan , combine all ingredients
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat to low
4. cover and simmer 25 minutes or until rice is done
5. garnish with green onions and / or cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: I'm glad I found this recipe because I needed a quick spanish rice recipe to bring to a family gathering, and I had all the ingredients on hand! I followed it exactly and it turned out really good. It was enjoyed by all! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black beans and rice with cheese

this is a wonderful black bean dish.  my husband and i enjoy this, especially when it's cold out.  this is also good for you!  serve with chips and salsa for a complete meal

1. prepare brown rice according to package directions
2. while brown rice is cooking heat oil in a medium saucepan over medium heat
3. add onion and bell pepper
4. cook 5 minutes or until tender , stirring occasionally
5. ladd garlic
6. cook 1 minute
7. add water and next 7 ingredients
8. bring to a boil
9. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 10 minutes or until thoroughly heated
10. place 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 cup rice in bowls and top with bean mixture
11. sprinkle each serving with 1 tbsp cheese
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe! I'm a big bean and rice fan, and this really hit the spot. I didn't have a bell pepper, so I left that out. I did add some sliced jalepanos to it for some extra spice. I topped the rice and beans with tortilla chips, low fat sour cream, and reduced-fat cheddar. I will be making this again!

target.recipe_text:
thai style pork in black pepper  moo pat prik thai dam

this dish has become popular in thailand few years ago, it has a strong peppery flavors which is quite appealing to the thai taste buds...i just had it for lunch so i thought of sharing it with zaar....enjoy!!

1. fry garlic in hot cooking oil until fragrant
2. add pork and keep stir fry until almost ready
3. add onions , ginger , bell peppers , chili peppers , fresh pepper and liquids
4. add fish sauce , oyster sauce sugar and black pepper , taste and adjust flavors
5. stir fry for a minute
6. serve hot with white rice
target.review:
Wow, I love thai food and this came out really good! Delicious! I can't stop eating it.. thank you VERY much and I hope to try some of your other thai recipes!
Edit:  I just tried this with ground pork instead, and by doing so 1tbsp is a LOT of pepper.. it was very spicy and I'm the only one in the house who can take it this hot.  I recommend cutting it to 1 -2 tsp of pepper if you are using ground pork.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatball soup ii

nan

1. combine ground beef , farina , minced onion , parsley , parmesan cheese , egg and tomato paste
2. form into 12 meatballs
3. bring beef broth and water to a boil , add meatballs , celery , carrot and sliced onion
4. cover and simmer for 45 minutes or until vegetables are tender
demonstrations.review: I think everyone liked this one a lot.. very similar to a mexican albondigas recipe but with a lot of different things.  My mother thought it was really good, except that I made the meatballs a little too big and so were a little rare(I used 3lbs of meat and got 20 meatballs).  O well, this was an excellent soup otherwise.  I would recommend on getting the leanest beef possible since none of the fat will be drained (like the kind of beef you would use in kibbee).  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked arroz con pollo

the original recipe was longer and used chicken pieces, but this is my quick and easy version! i hope you enjoy, it is packed with flavor!

1. saute veggies in oil
2. add broth , tomatoes and bay leaf
3. bring to a boil
4. spread rice in a 9x13 casserole pan
5. pour hot liquid over all , stir well
6. add chicken , mix
7. bake at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review:
This was really good and flavorful too!  I put a lot more tomatoes in it as well (maybe triple the amount) and it came out delicious! My family loved it too even though their initial response was "BAKED arroz con pollo??"  They suggested next time I could serve it in a burrito with beans and rice (inside or on the side).  
As for the chicken, I started with 6 chicken breasts and cooked them by boiling them in water and then using the broth with vegetables to make a chicken soup along with some more chicken boullion to taste. I shredded the breasts and put 2 of them in the soup and 4 of them into the arroz con pollo (doubled the recipe).  
Thanks again for a great dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hawaiian chicken kabobs

the marinade is the key to these great kabobs. they only need 1 hour in the refrigerator to marinate.

1. put chicken in large shallow dish
2. drain pineapple , keep 1 / 2 cup juice
3. set pineapple aside
4. mix juice with the next 7 ingredients in small pan
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes
7. pour over chicken
8. cover and chill for 1 hour
9. remove chicken from marinade , reserve marinade
10. alternate chicken , pineapple , green pepper , mushrooms , and tomatoes on skewers
11. grill kabobs over hot coals 20 minutes or until chicken is done
12. turn and baste frequently with marinade
13. serve over hot rice
demonstrations.review: I also thought that these were really good!  I made these for a medium sized party and together with a few friends, we probably assembled 40 kabobs, and they were ALL gone by the end of the night!  Thanks a lot!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini lasagna  lasagne    low carb

great for anyone going low carb or who has so many zucchini, they don't know what to do!! :) we found the sauce to be very mild. i think it would be better with twice as much garlic. i boiled my zucchini slices for about 3 minutes so they were partially cooked. i wanted to make sure they were soft in the finished dish or i knew the kids wouldn't eat them. ;) the cottage cheese provides a slightly tangy note. i think we would have preferred ricotta, but that is personal taste. i use my 11x7 baking dish and got 6 pieces the size of what you see in my photos. both of the guys ate two so it fed 4 of us, and i double the meat. adjust the recipe accordingly for your family.

1. cook zucchini until tender , drain and set aside
2. fry meat and onions until meat is brown and onions are tender
3. drain fat
4. add next 8 ingredients and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer , uncovered 10 minutes or until reduced to 2 cups
7. in small bowl slightly beat egg
8. add cottage cheese , half of shredded cheese and flour
9. in baking-roasting pan arrange half of the meat mixture
10. top with half of the zucchini and all the cottage cheese mixture
11. top with remaining meat and zucchini
12. bake uncovered at 375 degrees f for 30 minutes
13. sprinkle with remaining cheese
14. bake 10 minutes longer
15. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
Pretty good! I had double of everything except the cheese so mine was a bit more sauce and meat.  I used a can of tomato sauce instead of the fresh tomatoes and the sauce still came out quite good, just needed to cook a little longer for the liquid to evaporate.  Next time I might use both fresh tomatoes and tomato sauce.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken makhani  indian butter chicken

wow! i just finished making this and it tastes incredible! it tastes better than the chicken makhani at my favorite indian restaurant! you can make this as mild or spicy as you wish by adjusting the cayenne. serve with basmati rice and naan bread. i got the recipe from allrecipes.com.

1. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large saucepan over medium high heat
2. saute shallot and onion until soft and translucent
3. stir in butter , lemon juice , ginger garlic paste , 1 teaspoon garam masala , chili powder , cumin and bay leaf
4. cook , stirring , for 1 minute
5. add tomato puree and cook for 2 minutes , stirring frequently
6. stir in half-and-half and yogurt
7. reduce heat to low and simmer for 10 minutes , stirring frequently
8. season with salt , pepper and cayenne
9. remove from heat and set aside
10. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large heavy skillt over medium heat
11. cook chicken until lightly browned , about 10 minutes
12. reduce heat and season with 1 teaspoon garam masala and cayenne
13. stir in about 1 / 3 of the sauce and simmer until liquid has reduced and chicken is no longer pink , about 5 minutes
14. pour the rest of the sauce into the chicken
15. mix together cornstarch and water , then stir into the sauce
16. cook for 5 to 10 minutes , or until thickened
demonstrations.review: I made a few changes, but I thought it came out great, although didn't taste like the butter chicken I had a restaurant before (but most likely due to my changes). I didn't have yogurt or half and half, so I used sour cream and milk instead. I also used very little oil, and instead of 2tbsp butter I used 1tbsp ghee. I doubled the meat, and didn't need to add cornstarch since most of the sauce stuck to the meat instead. It was great, thanks a lot!

target.recipe_text:
philadelphia cream cheesecake

from the philadelphia cream cheese box

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. mix cream cheese , sugar and vanilla with mixer on medium until well blended
3. add eggs
4. mix until blended
5. spray 9 inch pie plate w / cooking spray
6. sprinkle bottom w / crumbs
7. pour in cream cheese mixture
8. bake for 45 minutes
9. to reduce cracking , place cookie sheet of water in oven with cheesecake while baking
10. cool thoroughly
11. refrigerate 3 hours
target.review: Great cheescake.  Certainly not for the fat gram conscious eater, but I splurged.  I added more crushed graham cracker crumbs because I like more crust.  Topped this with blueberry pie filling.  Delish!  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled  venison burgers

delicious venison burgers with that 

1. in bowl , mix dry ingredients
2. add venison and mix well
3. add liquid ingredients and mix well with a fork , until bread crumbs are barely noticeable
4. on plastic wrap , form into 8 patties , making them round and very flat-- like a fast-food burger
5. they can be cooked immediately , but i prefer to freeze them first
6. place them on a large cookie sheet and freeze them several hours
7. remove from freezer and place waxed paper between each burger as you stack them
8. i stack them in 2 1-quart freezer zip-lock bags
9. preheat cast iron skillet to very hot
10. cook frozen burgers until they are slightly charred on one side and then turn and cook until the other side is slightly charred and burgers are medium-well
11. do not overcook
12. turn burner off and leave burgers in the pan while you put condiments on your hamburger bun
13. if cooking thawed burgers , cook about 2-3 minutes per side
demonstrations.review: I've never made venison burgers before, chose this recipe.  Had to make a few modifications (i.e. real egg whites, etc.) that were minor due to items on hand.  Turned out great.  Cooked on the charcoal grill.  A little overdone, but that's the cook, not the recipe!  My son loved the burger and  that's enough proof for me.  Thank you, will make again for sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled cilantro pork tenderloin

this recipe is from easy taste of home grilling but has been modified a bit for my families taste. we love this and so has everyone i've ever made it for. i've also used this sauce on pork chops & chicken. still yummy!

1. in a large ziplock baggie , mix the first 7 ingredients
2. add pork and coat well
3. seal bag and refrigerate over night
4. grill over indirect heat , on low-med , for 25 to 40 minutes or until meat therm reads 160
5. slice & serve
demonstrations.review: Okay, I had my doubts- that's a lot of sweetness and soy sauce!  But my wife loves cilantro and we all like tenderloin, so I thought I'd try something different from the usual barbecue sauce kind.  We were not disappointed.  Grilled for approx 35 mintues, flipping and turning a few times.  Went great with grilled corn, mashed potatoes and rolls.  Next day was great on sandwich buns.  Will do again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cola ham

a popular, easy, and flavorful way to cook a small ham for the holidays, a dinner party or to have ham for sandwiches, soups or casseroles.

1. remove ham from packaging
2. lightly score ham in diagonal lines first one way , then crosswise , to form a diamond pattern , being careful not to cut any deeper than about a eighth of an inch
3. make a paste of brown sugar and mustard
4. rub paste into ham on sides that have been lightly scored
5. transfer to crock pot
6. pour in two cans of coca cola into bottom of pot , not pouring directly over ham to wash away brown sugar paste
7. cook on low 7-8 hours
demonstrations.review: Great ham!  We were looking for a small ham to slow cook to put mini-sandwiches together for our NYE "buffet" we do for the kids.  Really good, and leftovers made great lunch the next day.  I used a 3.5lb presmoked ham (to off set the sugar component, as opposed to the honey ham offered same brand).  Already scored.  Delish all put together.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled linguine and clam sauce

got this recipe from a friend and i found it so hard to believe that i had to try it! was the best linguine and clam sauce i have ever tasted! very easy. and you can cook and serve in the same pan!

1. preheat grill to high
2. place a large aluminum baking pan directly on grate
3. in the pan place butter and chopped onion and saute , stirring frequently until onion is translucent
4. add the garlic , half the parsley , and half the basil and saute for a few minutes more until the garlic just starts to turn color
5. add wine , 1 can of the chicken broth , salt and pepper and the clams
6. lower heat to medium , close the grill checking every few minutes and tossing the clams around for about 15 to 20 minutes , until clams open
7. add pasta the remainder of the parsley , basil , and broth , grated cheese and shake in as much hot pepper flakes to the heat you desire
8. mix well , close the grill and cook a few minutes more untill everything is heated through
demonstrations.review: Very good.  Reminds me of a meal my mother would fix when I was a child.  I used 2- 6.5oz cans of chopped clams, but skimped a lttle on the clam juice thinking it was too much-mistake.  Turned out a little dry, will use all next time.  And will certainly make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sage and garlic roast turkey

a great spin on the classic roast turkey! we loved this on thanksgiving 2004!

1. preheat the oven to 325f
2. prepare the turkey by fastening the neck skin to the back of the turkey with pins or a skewer
3. fold the wings to the turkey so the
4. mix all ingredients in a bowl except for the water , fresh sage , and apples
5. on a rack in the roasting pan , place turkey
6. brush with butter mixture
7. insert oven proof meat thermometer so
8. add water to the pan
9. cover turkey loosely with foil or the roaster top
10. roast for three hours
11. uncover
12. roast 45 minutes to an hour
13. turkey is finished when thermometer in thickest part of the bird reads 180f
14. let stand 15 minutes before carving
15. garnish with sage and apples
demonstrations.review: Just realized I've not posted a review for this after having cooked it so many times.  Best turkey I've ever cooked!  Only changes made:  stuffed cavity with chopped onions,celery fresh parsley, and added same seasonings used inside as on the outside rubbed well.  Basted occasionally with own juices.  Great turkey!

target.recipe_text:
chicken pot pie with 2 crusts

this is old-fashioned, from scratch, comfort food. this has been a family favorite for years. i like to take this to other families when they are in need of a meal. it's always a winner. i like making it with leftover turkey, too! i often add some cooked diced potatoes.

1. heat butter over low heat until melted
2. blend in flour , onion , salt and pepper
3. cook over low heat , stirring constantly until smooth and bubbly
4. remove from heat
5. stir in broth and milk
6. heat to boiling
7. stirring constantly
8. boil and stir one minute
9. stir in chicken and veggies
10. reserve
11. line pie plate with prepared bottom crust
12. pour in filling
13. top with top crust
14. cut slits in center to vent
15. flute edges
16. cook uncovered in 425f oven until crust is brown
17. approximately 30-35 minutes
target.review: This is the first time I have attempted to make chicken pot pie.  It was very easy and so delicious!I didn't wait for it to settle so it was a little runny when I cut into it, but that didn't really bother me.  The leftovers were just as good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
max   erma s chicken tortilla soup

goooooood!  nice and spicy.  this makes a lot.

1. add all to large pot
2. bring to a boil and simmer 1 hour
3. can be topped with:
4. flour tortilla chips , cut into strips and fried
5. or shredded cheese
6. i did not add the cilantro , red chili powder , salt or pepper
7. i also used fat free soups where i could
8. this was still delicious
demonstrations.review: We thought this was very good and did taste very similar to Max & Erma's soup.  We used canned chicken to make it a little easier.  Just some advice, if you're cooking for 2 you might want to cut the recipe in half.  This has literally lasted a week (1-2 bowls a day) and I still have more in the fridge.  Next time I might freeze some for a quick dinner later.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review:
*UPDATE*
I originally gave this 3 stars 2 years ago.  However, it is the most requested meal at my house still years later and it's so easy so I'm moving up to 5 stars.  I had a roast at a friends house yesterday and it was SO dry, I tried to giver her this recipe.

The meat was very tender and broke away with just a fork.  I used all of the ingredients and didn't find it too salty.  I used a small beef roast and cooked it on low for about 9 hours.  I also threw in some potatoes and onions.  I don't have anything to compare it to so I don't know if it is "to die for" but my bf and I enjoyed it and it was very easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian parmesan bread for bread machine
