i've been making this bread for years without measuring, and finally decided to write it down. my most requested bread from my bread-lovin' son. makes the house smell divine!! you can easily increase the amounts of seasonings to your taste. (note: many people seem to be needing to add extra water, so i'm adding an adjustment to the recipe.)

1. add ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer
2. mine is water first , then flour , then seasonings and cheese , lastly yeast
3. run on basic or delay cycle
demonstrations.review: I followed the directions to a T.  I lost track of time and didn't have time to put it in the bread machine for a full cycle so I used the 58 minute express cycle.  It tasted and smelled great!  I might increase the cheese and seasonings next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calzone  bread machine

you can create your own fillings for this very easy calzone. i don't use the pepperoni, but substitute cooked, chopped spinach. you can also add sauteed onions and peppers, olives, ricotta cheese...etc. i have also made small individual calzones to dip in marinara sauce...heaven! kids love these.

1. place water , salt , basil , oregano , garlic powder , bread flour , dry milk , sugar , and yeast in the pan of the bread machine in the order suggested by the manufacturer
2. select dough cycle
3. after cycle ends , roll out dough on a lightly floured surface , shaping into a 16 x 10 inch rectangle
4. transfer to a lightly greased cookie sheet
5. in a small bowl , mix together chopped pepperoni and mozzarella
6. spoon pizza sauce in a stripe down the center of dough lengthwise
7. add sausage and cheese filling
8. make diagonal cuts 1 1 / 2 inches apart down each side , cutting within a 1 / 2 inch of the filling
9. criss cross strips over filling , sealing with water
10. brush top with melted butter
11. you can just fold over the sides without cutting the strips to make this process easier
12. it will taste just as good , but not look as nice
13. be sure to seal the edges well
14. bake at 350 degrees f for 35 to 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were very good!  The only strayed from the dough recipe twice.  I only had all-purpose flour so I used that and I didn't have any powdered milk so I omitted it.  It still turned out great!  The dough was a little sticky but not unworkable.  Instead of making a braided calzone as pictured, I made 4 semi-circle calzones.  I filled mine with pepperoni, mushrooms, cheese and sauce.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: So easy and so much better than the stuff you buy in the tubs!  My chicken was frozen when I put it in and it was done in about 5 hours.  I turned the crock pot to warm until we were ready to eat.  Thanks for sharing this!

target.recipe_text:
baked tilapia with lots of spice

this is a fabulous recipe for oven fried tilapia slightly adapted from paul prudhomme's wonderful 

1. preheat the oven to 450 degrees
2. in a small bowl combine the spices from the salt through the italian seasoning and set it aside
3. in a shallow container mix the bread crumbs , dried parsley , and green onions
4. measure 4 tsp of the spice mix and sprinkle that all over the 4 fish fillets
5. add the remaining spice mix to the bread crumbs , mixing well
6. add the olive oil to the bread crumb mix , blending it in with your hands
7. dredge the fish in the breadcrumbs , coating well
8. shake off any excess breadcrumbs
9. place the fish on a baking pan that has been sprayed with non-stick spray
10. bake for 6 minutes
11. turn over and bake for 4 minutes
12. turn over again and bake until flaky , about 4 more minutes
13. serve immediately
target.review: Delicious! I can't believe how flavorfull this was...and healthy. I am so pleased to have a "go-to" recipe for a quick week night dinner. I used cod instead of tilapia and I served it with steamed broccoli and wild rice. Absolutely yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple cinnamon wontons

here's a great autumn dessert that's waist friendly. apples, cinnamon, brown sugar and a nice crunch. great alternative when craving apple pie.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. coat a large baking sheet with butter flavored cooking spray
3. in a medium bowl , combine apples , brown sugar , lemon juice and cinnamon
4. toss to coat apples
5. place wonton wrappers on a flat surface
6. drop apple mixture by teaspoonfuls onto center of each wrapper
7. moisten edges of wrapper with wet fingers , fold over one corner to make a triangle and press sides together to seal
8. transfer filled wrappers to prepared baking sheet and coat surface with cooking spray
9. bake until wontons are golden brown , about 15 minutes
10. place wontons on individual plates and sift with powdered sugar
11. serve with ice cream on the side
demonstrations.review: Very good and very easy too. Made these for DH for Valentines day and he really enjoyed them. They are a great low-fat alternative to apple pie. I sprayed them with cooking spray and sprinkled some sugar on top before baking. Really very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fillet of beef  beef tenderloin whole

how to cook a whole or large piece of beef tenderloin. note from unknownchef86: this is a recipe i adopted in 2006.

1. preheat the oven to 500 degrees f
2. place the beef on a sheet pan and pat the outside dry with a paper towel
3. spread the butter on with your hands
4. sprinkle evenly with the salt and pepper
5. roast in the oven for exactly 22 minutes for rare and 25 minutes for medium-rare
6. remove the beef from the oven , cover it tightly with aluminum foil , and allow it to rest at room temperature for 20 minutes
7. remove the strings and slice the fillet thickly
demonstrations.review: OMG! Sooooo easy. I followed the directions to the letter and it turned out amazing. I took a chance and made this for a formal dinner party for 14 and everyone loved it. I ended up giving the recipe to all of them! Thank you for making my party a huge success!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana streusel muffins

better than banana bread, and these freeze well too.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. lightly grease 10 muffin cups , or line with muffin papers
3. in a large bowl , mix together flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
4. in another bowl , beat together bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
5. stir the banana mixture into the flour mixture just until moistened
6. spoon batter into prepared muffin cups
7. in a small bowl , mix together brown sugar , flour and cinnamon
8. cut in butter until mixture resembles coarse cornmeal
9. sprinkle topping over muffins
10. bake in preheated oven for 18 to 20 minutes , until a toothpick inserted into center of a muffin comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I had some over-ripe bananas and needed a quick, delicious recipe. This looked good and the comments were all very positive so I tried it. Delicious! Simple to make and full of flavor. The crumb topping is the perfect touch. Mu hubby loved them and he is hard to please. Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my no roll pie crust

the only pie crust i will use anymore. its flaky and slightly sugary and oh so easy to do. note: due to some major discrepencies please use a good quality oil, preferably a vegetable and a good name brand like mazola, it may not seem like it will make a difference but in the end it will, also use new oil not something that has been sitting around for a while.

1. mix dry ingredients together with a fork in a pie pan
2. make a well in the center and add the oil and milk
3. mix with a fork til it makes a ball
4. flatten and press into the pan in pie crust shape and flute the edge
5. bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes until golden
6. one crust pie , excellent for cream pies and crumb topped baked pies
demonstrations.review: Very easy and tastes great too. I found it a bit salty the first time so I cut the salt in half the second time. It worked out well. This crust is extremely flaky so expect it to fall apart when you slice the pie but the taste and simplicity make up for the appearance.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: This is my stand-by cake for every function. I have made this several times in 2 round pans and I always leave on in the freezer for future eating. The second one always tastes just as moist and fresh as the first. The freezing is a very important step in the process. I believe it stops the cooking process so that there is no "leftover" baking time to dry the cake out. Genious!

target.recipe_text:
low cal veggie pizza

this is a very colorful and yet good treat. enjoy and please let me know what you think of this.

1. unroll cresent roll dough into a long rectangle
2. press onto a bottom of a 1392 pan coated with a non stick spray
3. seal seams and preformations
4. bake at 375 for 11 minutes or until golden brown
5. cool completely
6. in a mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese and salad dressing and milk until smooth
7. spread over crust
8. sprinkle with vegetables
9. cover and refrigerate at least 1 hour
10. cut in to 16 pieces
target.review: Took this to a super bowl party tonight and everyone loved it.  It was a little think on the cream cheese mixture for my liking though.  Next time I will cut down on the "sauce" for the pizza.  My toppings were olives, peppers, lettuce, onion, tomatoes.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
becky s tater tot casserole

i love this recipe, it's delicious, pretty much everyone enjoys it, good for family get togethers, pot lucks, etc. i got the recipe several years ago from an old friend.

1. preheat oven to 350 deg
2. fry hamburger until completely done
3. in small bowl mix cream of mushroom and cream of celery
4. mix until well blended
5. in large casserole dish , combine hamburger and cream mix
6. spread so it covers the bottom
7. sprinkle shredded cheese over top
8. place tater tots on top
9. place in oven until golden brown
10. cool for about 20 minute
11. serve
demonstrations.review: This is always a hit at my house.  Even my dd, who hates all things potato, will risk eating a tater tot piece just so she can have more of the "good stuff".    We add a veggie or 2 to the mix.  Pairs nicely with a small salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagna      homemade lasagna

this is really not al capone's lasagna, it's my very own! a friend of mine had a halloween party and ask me to bring al capone and my lasagna. al capone and his boy's would be very proud if he had some of this lasagna, if he wasn't full of holes. my spaghetti sauce is excellent,,,,,, after all, it's all about the sauce! recipe #106003, it can be made ahead and frozen. it can be used on any pasta.

1. boil the noodles as the directions say on the box
2. brown the beef and strain the grease , set aside
3. in the same skillet saut the onion and garlic until it's limp , set aside
4. mix the onion , garlic and ground beef in a bowl
5. in a 9x11 casserole dish , spread 3 ladle's of sauce across the bottom of the dish
6. put 3 noodles on top of the sauce
7. add ground beef on top of the noodles , about half of the mixture of beef , onion and garlic
8. dot with ricotta cheese , about 5-6 tablespoons
9. repeat the same steps
10. bake for 30-45 minutes at 350 or until golden brown
11. after 30 minutes top with mozzarella and parmesan cheese
12. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This was my first time making a red sauce meat lasagna and it was so simple and tasty!  I used the oven ready noodles and put everything together in a 9x13 pan.  I also used jar spaghetti sauce(actually 2 jars).  The kiddos loved this and it was even better as leftovers the next day for lunch.  This will become my lasagna recipe from here on, just don't tell my mom or aunt all the short cuts I take. :)  Their recipes take all day!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican corn and bean soup

really easy and inexpensive to make. delicious too!

1. combine beans , corn , diced tomatoes , tomato sauce , and water in a large sauce pan
2. add chili powder and garlic powder
3. simmer on medium heat for about 45 minutes , or until beans are soft
4. can be served with sour cream , tortilla chips , and grated cheese
demonstrations.review: I made this in the crock pot last night.  It was a quick and easy meal and I plan to make it again.  Only complaint it was alittle bland for our liking.  Next time I will add more garlic and maybe some red pepper flakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker tex mex chicken

from kraft food & family, fall 2007

1. mix chicken with seasoning and flour in slow cooker
2. stir in all remaining ingredients except the shredded cheese
3. cover with lid
4. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
5. stir just before serving
6. top with the shredded cheese
7. serve over rice and garnished with fresh green onions and cilantro
demonstrations.review: My husband and I ate this over tortilla chips with some cheese and sour cream.  It was good however we were expecting more of a meal not a dip or nacho topper.  I do plan to make this again.  I think it will be great for super bowl parties.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
one dish chicken and rice bake

this recipe goes together in 5 minutes and bakes in 45. best of all it is mixed and baked in the same casserole! enjoy this recipe from american century cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. mix soup , water , rice , and 1 / 4 tsp each of paprika and pepper in ungreased shallow 2-quart casserole
3. lay chicken on top and sprinkle with remaining paprika and pepper
4. cover and bake until bubbly and chicken shows no signs of pink in the center--about 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: My kids ate this!!!  My 6yo dd, who is very picky and claims to HATE rice ate everything on her plate.  She even had 2nds on the chicken.   I did add some extra water and sprinkled cheese on top for the last 10 mins of bake time.  Some of the other reviews said it was simple or bland so I added garlic and roasted red pepper seasoning to the mixture.  Very tasty!!!

target.recipe_text:
spinach salad with creamy dressing

cool and creamy but tangy dressing really complements the flavor of the spinach!

1. combine washed and torn spinach leaves , mushrooms and bacon in a large bowl
2. in a blender , combine the dressing ingredients
3. toss salad with the dressing and serve
target.review: very very good...would be good on any salad..i added homemade croutons and some sweet sliced onions.....will make it often....now i have another favorite besides my caesar dressing (which my family wants almost daily)...thanks for posting it and i'm sorry it took me so long to find...its a keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
romaine salad with creamy garlic dressing

i wish i had a nickel for every time i was either asked to make this salad for a gathering, or asked for the recipe for it! the dressing is irresistable! a good description for this is a caesar salad gone balistic. it travels well too; i prepare all the ingredients, except the avocado, and pack in separate containers and just assemble it when i get to my destination. so much of this can be done ahead of time that it makes this recipe an excellent choice for a dinner party. plan on having copies of the recipe available because you will be asked for them! i found this recipe in the sunset cookbook of favorite recipes ii.

1. tear lettuce into bite-size pieces , you should have about 12 cups
2. cover and refrigerate until well chilled
3. combine garlic and salt in a small bowl and mash with the back of a spoon into a paste , or , mash with a mortar and pestle and transfer to a bowl
4. mix garlic paste with lime juice , add egg and beat until foamy
5. stir in mayo and worcestershire
6. this can be made ahead , just cover and refrigerate
7. just before serving , peel , pit and dice avocado
8. in a large salad bowl , combine avocado , lettuce , cheese , tomatoes , onions and croutons
9. stir dressing and pour over salad then toss until well mixed
10. if you are pregnant or nursing , or have a compromised immune system you may want to consider using a purchased pasteurized egg product
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something different to use up my 6 heads of romaine that I bought....my husband and my 22yr old son couldnt stop raving over this one....requesting I make it again before they even finished eating it all....thanks for this post....smiles :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and delicious pumpkin bread pudding

some people might think this is even better than pumpkin pie lol! you can cut the sugar back a couple of tablespoons. serve this with my really easy and good caramel sauce#78088, or with whipped cream, this is so good! prep time does not include slicing the bread into cubes.

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. butter a11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl whisk together first 7 ingredients to combine
4. fold in bread cubes and raisins
5. transfer the mixture to prepared baking dish
6. let stand for 10-15 minutes for the bread to absorb the mixture
7. bake for about 40-45 minutes , or until done
8. serve with lots of whipped cream , or caramel topping
9. delicious !
demonstrations.review: thanks for this recipe, I don't normally like pumkin anything and this was just fantastic...my family loved it and it sure is a keeper...will pass along to others so that they can enjoy it as much as we all did...made it with the easy carmel sauce Recipe #78088 which I could have ate with a spoon, thanks again Kittencal..again another sure winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled mahi mahi

nice blend of flavors for this fish. this was a recipe i altered some from a cooking magazine. this recipe may also be broiled. leftovers are even better the next day if you have any left.

1. with mortar and pestle , mash garlic and salt to form paste
2. place in a gallon bag
3. add rum , lime juice , mint , cilantro , peppers , oil , honey , lime peel , cumin , salt and pepper
4. add fish
5. turn and rub to distribute marinade evenly
6. refrigerate for no more than 30 minutes so fish doesn't break down
7. place fish on grill over medium heat or 4 to 6 inches from coals
8. grill 8 to 10 minutes or until fish flakes
9. turn once and spoon remaining marinade over fish halfway through grilling time
demonstrations.review: well what a dummy I am, I forgot the hot chili pepper....but the men in my family loved it and said it was one of , if not the best fish that they have ever eaten.....so it is a keeper....thanks so much

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded brussels sprouts

brussels sprouts are quite often referred to as 

1. wash and trim brussels sprouts
2. cut an"x" in the stem , about 3 / 8 inch deep
3. in a medium size saucepan , add brussels sprouts and cover with cold water , add 1 teaspoon of salt and bring to boil
4. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 6 minutes or until just tender ,
5. drain
6. place sprouts in a six-cup oven proof casserole dish
7. sprinkle 3 tablespoons melted butter over the sprouts and mix well to coat
8. brussel sprouts should be in a single layer
9. meanwhile , combine parmesan cheese , dried bread crumbs , granulated garlic powder , black pepper , seasoning salt and remaining 3 tablespoons butter and mix well
10. sprinkle mixture over the brussels sprouts
11. place casserole dish about 3 inches below broiler in oven and broil on high for about 5 minutes or until the crumb mixture is lightly browned
12. serve hot
demonstrations.review: I am guilty of not liking these little guys, but I must admit I did enjoy them done this way...in fact another time I went to make brussel sprouts for dinner my son made me search my cookbook to find this recipe again....thanks for posting....I had better not misplace this recipe ever....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers 0 point tortilla soup

a great soup that fills you up and only 0 points on the ww program.

1. simmer onions , garlic & green onions in a pan until tender
2. put all ingredients in a pot , simmer until all veggies are tender
3. you can add chicken , divide the points by 9 servings
4. taste great with a couple toasted taco shells on the side , but count your points --
demonstrations.review: Great tasting soup...and low cal bonus for sure....I also added extra heat and left out the flour...have not tried it with a bit of sour cream but I bet the heat with the coolness will be a double bonus...thanks Janet...loved it...

target.recipe_text:
favorite amish cinnamon bread

i got this from my mom and as it was passed from person to person, i don't know where it originated.  this is a "sourdough" recipe.  it takes 10 days sitting out on the counter, but is absolutely wonderful.  my family eats this bread for snacks, breakfast, gives as gifts, a must have for holidays.

1. on day 1: combine 1 cup milk , 1 cup sugar , and 1 cup flour in a large ziplock bag and mush to mix ingredients
2. on days 2-5: mush the bag twice daily
3. on day 6: add 1 cup milk , 1 cup sugar , and 1 cup flour to the bag and mush to mix
4. on days 7-9: mush the bag twice daily
5. on day 10: squeeze contents of bag into large mixing bowl
6. add 1 cup milk , 1 cup sugar , and 1 cup flour and mix well
7. measure out 4 "starters" you may freeze the starters for future use if desired
8. to the small amount in the bowl add oil , milk , eggs , vanilla
9. mix well
10. next add remaining ingredients
11. mix well
12. then fold in nuts and raisins
13. spray 2 loaf pans with cooking spray
14. sprinkle generously with cinnamon and sugar
15. pour batter into pans and sprinkle tops with cinnamon and sugar
16. bake at 325 for 1 hour or until done
target.review: I love this recipe! A friend gave me a starter and I have been "culturing" it on the counter for about 6 weeks. Every 5 days, I add 1 cup of flour/sugar/milk and stir. When I want to make a bread, I just pull out a cup with out worring if it's been 10 days yet and it works out fine. To make pumpkin bread, I decreased the oil to 2/3 cup and added 1/3 cup of pumpkin, 2t cinnamon, 1t nutmeg and 1/2t cloves. I happened to have pumpkin spice pudding that they carried around the holidays and used that. For apple bread, use 2/3 cup oil, 1/3 cup applesauce, 1 cup diced apples, 2/3 cup walnuts and 2t cinnamon. I used vanilla pudding here. Also made banana using banana pudding, 2/3 cup of oil, 2/3 cup of bananas and 1 cup of walnuts. Coconut bread is also good with coconut pudding and 1 cup of toasted coconut. Once you have a good sized batch, say 4-6 cups, just feed it every 5 days and dip out a cup when you need. A lot of fun coming up with new stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix peanut butter squares

a cake mix, some peanut butter, a few chocolate chips and 30 minutes is all you need for this easy recipe!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. mix cake mix , peanut butter , margarine and egg together
3. place 2 / 3 of the mixture in a greased 9x13 pan
4. heat condensed milk , chocolate chips and butter until melted
5. spoon over mixture that is in the pan
6. cover with the rest of the cake batter
7. bake 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: I may have to "eat" my previous words. I had said these were good but not great. Well, I took them to work and everyone wanted the recipe. Some took a peice home to their spouse and THEY wanted the recipe so these are definantly worth trying.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: This was fabulous. I was worried that it would be grainy and I had heard that to get the full flavor of cocoa, you had to mix it with something hot so I brought whipping cream to a boil and added 3/4 cup Hershey's Dark cocoa. It immediantly made a firm ball but I tossed the ball in the with the soft butter and blended the powdered sugar and man, was it fudgy!! Caution in adding too much powdered sugar or the frosting will get hard. Just add more whipping cream to soften it up. I topped choc. fudge cupcakes with it and in the center of each cupcake, I piped about 1T of homemade Twinkie filling from Topsecretrecipes.com into the center of each. Fabulous! Won't use canned again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
top secret peanut butter frosting

adapted from a hershey's recipe, this heavenly concoction starts on the stove-top and ends with countless rave reviews. it has made me famous amongst co-workers and friends! i usually pair it with a buttery betty crocker cake mix and then top it off with chocolate curls or drizzled chocolate syrup which has been cut through for a marbled effect.


1. stir flour into milk
2. cook on low heat in a small saucepan until boiling , stirring constantly
3. transfer to a small bowl
4. cover with plastic wrap and let cool on the counter-top for 30 minutes
5. add the rest of the ingredients and beat with a hand-mixer until fluffy
6. store in the fridge
7. variations a softened 8-oz
8. block of philadelphia cream cheese may be beaten in for a richer frosting
9. hershey's unsweetened cocoa powder can be added a tablespoonful at a time until desired flavor / color has been achieved
10. this produces a rich-tasting chocolate / peanut butter frosting
demonstrations.review: I gave it 5 stars even though mine was flop. I too was afraid of grainyness so I added the sugar right off the stove. I waited 30 min and I did use 4oz of cream cheese but it was runny and never set up, even in the fridge. I'm sure it was because I "melted" the sugar. I may use butter Crisco next time also. It was smooth and glossy which makes me want to try this again and actually follow the directions!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake batter ice cream

i made this recipe after falling in love with coldstone and carvel's cake batter ice cream.

i recommend using splenda instead of sugar since there is sugar in the cake mix.

you can use 2 teaspoons of vanilla extract if you please. you can also use 3/4 cup of cake mix.

this recipe is to use with an ice cream maker (mine is by cuisinart)

1. place freezer bowl of ice cream maker into the freezer
2. it is better to keep it in there 24 / 7 that way it is always ready
3. in a medium bowl , whisk the milk and granulated sugar until the sugar is dissolved
4. stir in the heavy cream and vanilla to taste
5. stir in cake mix , making sure there are no lumps
6. pour mixture into the freezer bowl and let mix until it has thickened
7. remove ice cream from freezer bowl and place into a separate container
8. place freezer bowl and the ice cream into the freezer to further harden
demonstrations.review:
Fabulous! Used Funfetti cake mix and the full 3/4 cup of sugar. The 2/3 cup of cake mix was about 1/4 of the package so I took the rest of the cake mix and made a cake in a 9x9 pan to serve with it's matching ice cream. I have a Kitchen Aid attachment ice cream maker and noticed it wasn't firm after 40 min (it usually takes 25 min) so I went ahead and put it in a container in the freezer and it was perfect 6 hours later.

I also made this with caramel cake mix. I used 1 cup of mix, 1/2 cup of sugar and 1/4t of English toffee extract. Again, it didn't freeze very firm in my ice cream freezer but was fine after a time in the  freezer. This was INSANE! It didn't whip much air into it and it was like the super premium that you can only get at a specialty shop. Wisk your ingredients well to dissolve all of the cake mix and sugar before freezing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red lobster cheddar bay biscuits   copycat

cheddar bay biscuits
like red lobster's®

1. combine bisquick , milk , and cheddar and beat with a wooden spoon for about 30 seconds
2. -spoon onto a lightly greased cookie sheet
3. -bake in 450 degree oven for 8 - 10 minutes
4. -combine butter and garlic powder and pour over hot biscuits
5. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: I miss read the recipe and put all of the ingredients in the biscuits. I also upped the cheese to 1 cup. I melted the 1/4 cup of butter, mixed it with the milk and garlic powder and then stirred in Heart Smart Bisquick (no trans fat) and cheese. I used my largest cookie scoop (1/4 cup) and baked them about 11 minutes.. While baking, I read the recipe and realized what I had done. I melted another 1/4 of butter and added the garlic powder to it and brushed it on top of the freshly baked biscuits. They were very good. I think I got away with this because Heart Smart Bisquick is lower in fat than regular so the added fat was fine.  Thanks

target.recipe_text:
cucumber salad  acar ketimun

this is an indonesian salad.  i found the recipe in my extending the table cookbook, and since i have an explosion of cucumbers in my garden right now, i am trying every possible variation of cucumber salad! :) chilling time is the cook time.

1. mix all ingredients together
2. if you prefer a little heat , you can add slices of hot chili peppers to taste
3. chill and marinate at least 30 minutes before serving
target.review: Made per the recipe, using persian cucumbers which don't need to be peeled.  Nice balanced seasonings (I don't see any optional chilies - made per the recipe using black pepper).  So easy too.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy roasted red pepper and mushroom lasagna

based on the recipe on the back of the barilla no-boil lasagna noodles, but made meatless.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray a 9x13 baking dish with non-stick cooking spray
3. combine ricotta , spinach , 1 / 2 cup mozzarella cheese , and egg in a large mixing bowl
4. spread 1 cup of sauce on bottom of baking pan
5. layer 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , 1 / 3 of ricotta mixture , 1 / 2 of sliced mushrooms , 1 / 2 of roasted red peppers , and 1 cup of sauce
6. layer 4 uncooked noodles , 1 / 3 of ricotta mixture , and 1-1 / 2 cup sauce
7. layer 4 uncooked noodles , the rest of the ricotta mixture , remaining mushrooms and roasted red peppers , and 1 cup of sauce
8. layer 4 uncooked noodles , remaining sauce , and parmesan and remaining mozzarella
9. cover with foil and bake at 375 degrees for 50-60 minutes
10. remove foil and continue baking until cheese is melted , about 5 minutes
11. allow to stand for 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was so easy, and good.  Highly dependent on your choice of jarred sauce - I used Bertolli's Basil/Tomato Sauce.  (top rated by Cook's Illustrated taste test).  Next time I will add a bit of garlic, since the sauce didn't seem to have that.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy salmon cakes with lemon  caper mayonnaise

this recipe was published in cooking light. i make it a bit different than it originally appeared, though (i don't use fat-free mayonnaise, saltines, etc. and also add some additional ingredients to suit my taste). if you would like to make the original version, just stick with the fat-free items and omit the last 4 items in the ingredient list (mayo through tabasco) and you will have the original recipe. prep time includes 20 minutes chilling time for the salmon cakes.

1. mayonnaise:
2. combine first 6 ingredients in a small bowl
3. cover and chill
4. salmon cakes:
5. heat 1 teaspoon oil in medium nonstick skillet over medium heat
6. add onion and celery and saute' 4 minutes , or until tender
7. combine onion mixture with 1 / 2 cup crackers , mustard , 1 / 4 teaspoon black pepper , salmon , egg , mayonnaise , lemon juice , worcestershire sauce and tabasco in a medium bowl
8. divide into 4 equal portions , shaping each into a 1 / 2-inch thick patty
9. coat each patty with 1 tablespoon crackers
10. cover and chill 20 minutes
11. heat 2 teaspoons oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot
12. add patties and cook 5 minutes on each side or until lightly browned
13. serve salmon cakes with flavored mayonnaise
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious.  I find myself planning to grill salmon, just so I have leftovers to make these with.  The sauce and the patties are both "keepers" in my book.  Used bread crumbs in place of crackers, and it worked just fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun chicken jambalaya

this is an easy to prepare dish that brings out all the flavors of traditional jambalaya. you will like this one.

1. melt butter in a large skillet
2. saut the onion , garlic , celery and bell pepper until tender
3. add canned , crushed , tomatoes with liquid , rice , thyme , basil , cajun spices , cayenne pepper , chicken broth , chicken , tabasco and bay leaf
4. bring to a boil , then reduce heat to a simmer , and cook until rice is tender
demonstrations.review: Delicious.  My 17 year old son doesn't like rice, and he asked me to continue to make it.  I doubled this, and froze before adding the rice or broth.  To serve, I thawed, added rice and broth and heated until the rice was done.  Quick, easy, and very good.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
senate bean soup

this is an old recipe given to me by my mother. i have tasted different versions but this one is my family's favorite.

1. wash and sort beans
2. in large kettle , cover beans with 6-8 c hot water
3. bring to a boil
4. boil 2 minutes
5. remove from heat , cover , and let stand for 1 hour
6. add another 2 quarts of cold water and ham bone
7. bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer 1 1 / 2 hours
9. stir in remaining ingredients
10. simmer 20-30 minutes until beans are tender
11. remove ham bone , trim off meat and return meat to soup
12. remove bay leaf
13. serve hot
14. freezes well
demonstrations.review:
Delicious.  Nice balance of flavors, hearty and satisfying.  Wonderful winter comfort food.  Freezes well too, making this a great candidate for OAMC.  Served with crusty bread and spinach salad for a balanced meal.  Thanks for sharing.
Diane

demonstrations.recipe_text:
exotic indonesian style chicken

i found this recipe in an old cookbook published back in the 80's. i've never tried it, but hey...any new chicken recipe to try couldn't hurt

1. prepare the baste marinade: combine all ingredients in a saucepan
2. stir and heat , but only until sauce boils
3. remove from heat and cool to room temperature
4. season the chickens lightly with salt and pepper to taste
5. place them in a baking pan skin side down
6. cover with about 1 / 3 of the marinade
7. bake at 350 degrees for about 40 minutes
8. add a little water to pan if the marinade starts to burn
9. turn chicken over and spoon on 1 / 3 more of the marinade
10. bake an additional 30-45 minutes , or until chickens are tender
11. add more marinade and water as needed during the cooking
12. if there is any leftover marinade , gently reheat it and serve as a sauce to be passed around at the table
13. this recipe freezes with no problems
demonstrations.review: Wow!  This isn't just exotic, it's magical!  I cooked the chicken on our rotisserie BBQ, and cooked down the marinade to use as a glaze (made the color dark, but no impact to taste).  The marinade on it's own didn't taste too special, but on the chicken, something changed.  Delicious!   I will definitely make this again - thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
baked macaroni and cheese with stewed tomatoes

boy, does this bring back memories! when i was in high school, they served this every friday in the cafeteria. i guess they had to make sure we had our vegetables :) it sounds gross, but i couldn't wait until fridays, the macaroni and tomatoes were so good together. to this day, almost 20 years later, whenever i have baked macaroni & cheese, i crave stewed tomatoes. with this recipe, i don't have to.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cook macaroni according to package directions and drain , rinse and set aside
3. in a large saucepan , over medium heat , heat the 3 cups of milk , butter , salt and pepper until hot but not boiling
4. in a small bowl or cup , combine 1 / 4 cup of milk with the cornstarch and stir until dissolved
5. slowly add this to the hot milk mixture , stirring constantly with a whisk
6. when mixture has thickened , remove from heat and stir in 2 cups of the cheese until melted
7. pour pasta into a large mixing bowl and add the cheese mixture and the stewed tomatoes
8. mix well until macaroni is well coated
9. pour into a greased 9 x 13 baking dish or 3 quart casserole and top with remaining cheese
10. bake for 35 to 45 , or until golden brown
target.review: Wow! If your using the food.com iPhone app the recipe does not state 1 lb elbow or 1 lb shell macaroni.  The recipe reads like its 1lb of each!  Of course I didn't figure it out till the whole thing was in the pan. I had to make more sauce and add it to the mix. Turned out great thank god! When I went on the website the recipe is correct. Lesson learned. Now I have enough Mac and cheese for a week!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: To sum it up in one word AWESOME!  I made this in a 9x13 pan so it took a little longer to bake. I used both roasted chicken breasts and thighs. I added a small jar of pimento's to the mix. I can't wait to make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pesto

this was my daughter's favorite dish (along with some of her friends). she enjoyed it so much that we had to make it a weekly recipe.

1. prepare pesto sauce according to package direction
2. heat oven to 350 degrees
3. spray rectangular dish with no-stick spray
4. moisten chicken with water , shake off excess , and coat complete with bread crumbs
5. place chicken in baking dish
6. spread pesto sauce evenly over chicken breasts
7. cover each breast with slice of provolone cheese
8. spread mushrooms over cheese
9. bake in oven for 45- 50 minutes
10. serve with pasta
demonstrations.review: Wow! Made this for a dinner party last week and it was a hit!  I used fresh mushrooms under the cheese as previous reviewers suggested. Doubled the provolone and topped with roasted red peppers. Served the pasta with pesto sauce, roasted red peppers and topped with toasted pine nuts. You wont be disappointed with this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple crumb cake

my dh hates apple cakes and pies of all kinds but will eat this until i stop him and i love apple cake and pies of all kinds and will eat this until i stop myself; in other words everyone loves this cake. this is not a fluffy cake but a good heavy crumb cake with an almost cookie-like crust. the nice thing about this is that you really can use any kind of fresh or frozen fruit or any combination (except strawberries). my personal favorite is apple and apricot. it is especially good with a layer of fruit pie filling on top of the apples like cherry pie filling.

1. combine all dough ingredients and mix with mixer until moist and crumbly
2. spread half of the crumb mixture into the bottoms of two 9" pans or one 10x13 pan
3. layer the fruit filling over the crumb base
4. cover the fruit with the remaining crumb dough
5. bake in a 350 oven for approximately one to two hours or until nicely browned from edge to center
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe. I have made recipes similar to this before but  none of them had a crumb topping that retained it's crunchy texture. The recipe did not state what type of apple or size so I used 3 1/2 lbs of Granny Smith apples which is a  tart baking apple.I found 1/2 cup of sugar was not enough. If your using tart apples an omitting the canned filling you need to increase sugar to 3/4 to 1 cup. I also increased the cinnamon to 2 tsp. It took longer to bake in the 9x13 pan. approximately 1 1/2 hours overall. Thanks for the recipe,

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: I liked this recipe . The sauce complemented the pork chops extremely well. Like some other reviewers my pork chops were a little dry. I think I will use Country style spare ribs next time I make this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have been making this bread for the past year. It's worth the time and effort. I have baked it in 3 -10" loaf pans and also shaped into rounds on a cookie sheet. It comes out perfectly each time.

target.recipe_text:
plantation ribs

southern living

1. combine first 6 ingredients in a saucepan
2. bring mixture to a boil
3. remove from heat , and set aside
4. cut ribs into serving size pieces
5. place meaty side down in a large shallow baking pan
6. bake uncovered , at 450 degrees for 30 minutes
7. drain off excess drippings
8. reduce heat to 350
9. turn ribs over , and bake an additional 50-60 minutes
10. brush ribs with sauce during the last 15 minutes of cooking
target.review: The ribs turned out beautifully. I am so impressed. The meat was tender and we didn't break our teeth trying to get the meat off the bone (that is the way mine usually turn out). The sauce was a little spicy and a little sweet. Very yummy. I served with baked beans and potato salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard turkey meatballs

these are a little different. for all the honey-mustard lover.

1. in a bowl , combine turkey , egg , cracker crumbs , cheese , onion , ginger , and 3 tablespoons mustard
2. form into 30 balls , 1-inch each
3. place in a greased 13x9 inch baking dish
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes or until juices run clear
5. in a saucepan , combine pineapple juice , green pepper , honey , cornstarch , onion powder , and salt
6. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
7. cook and stir 2 minutes more
8. reduce heat
9. stir in remaining mustard until smooth
10. brush meatballs with about 1 / 4 cup sauce and return to oven for 10 minutes
11. serve with remaining sauce as a dip for meatballs
demonstrations.review: We made a feast off of these meatballs. I made them for our dinner instead of an appetizer. The meatballs were moist and tasty. The mustard sauce was out of this world. Very tangy. 5-stars from all in my family. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black eyed pea gumbo

this is so simple, either crock pot or stovetop! a friend of mine served this a few weeks ago on a very cold sunday and i've made it three times since! spice it up or tone it down as you like. i like spicy foods so i add a lot of tabasco? to my bowl! some people like to add okra as well for the real gumbo look...i hope you enjoy this!

1. slice bell pepper , celery and uncooked sausage
2. put all ingredients except rice in a crock pot
3. cook on high for at least 3 hours then add cooked rice and cook for an additional 30 minutes
4. if you make this on the stove top the cooking time will be approximately 45 to 60 minutes
5. i leave the rice out and allow each person to put in as much as they like in their bowl and pour the gumbo over it
6. if there is any left over , i add the remaining rice
7. if it is needing additional broth the next day , i add tomato juice or tomato sauce
demonstrations.review: This one got rave reviews from my family. I made it in the crock-pot too, and used rotel tomatoes because we like our spice. I also did as you suggested and added frozen okra for a more gumbo look and taste. This was a nice, hearty meal that I will serve often in my home. I served it with some Mexican cornbread and salad. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian chicken in a skillet

pasta and chicken with an italian flavor.

1. cut chicken into bite sized pieces
2. in lg skillet , brown chicken in oil
3. add onion and peppers , cook for 5 minutes
4. add broth , tomatoes , and spices
5. cook 2 minutes
6. add pasta , reduce heat and simmer , covered , for 10 min or until pasta is done
demonstrations.review: This was a delicious dinner, Mizz Nezz. Just stir a few ingredients in a skillet and dinner is ready. The seasoning was just right and best of all, my family loved it. Definitely will make this one again. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried egg sandwiches

this is something my grandmother used to make for my dad and us grandkids. my husband and i love it and are not ashamed. an old southern classic.

1. spread one side of each slice of toast with honey mustard
2. in a large skillet , cook bacon until crisp
3. drain on paper towels
4. crumble and set aside
5. pour drippings from skillet
6. over medium-high heat , melt butter in same skillet
7. crack eggs and let raw egg drop into skillet
8. cook until desired doneness , turning once
9. sprinkle with salt and pepper
10. using a spatula , place each egg on a slice of toast
11. sprinkle bacon evenly on top of eggs
12. top with remaining toast slices to make sandwiches
demonstrations.review: I LUUUUV fried egg sandwiches. My mom used to make them when I was a kid. She always spread mayonnaise on the bread and laid two bacon strips over the top of the fried egg. I like this version with mustard just as well. I added a slice a cheese. A heart attack waiting to happen but sooo good. Thanks and add me to your list of fans, Nurse Di. We love your recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fudge filled bars

i like to make these when i need something that travels well. very good! very easy!

1. mix oats , flour , brown sugar and salt
2. add butter and mix until crumbly
3. stir in pecans
4. set aside 1-1 / 2 cup for topping
5. press remaining into a greased 13x9 baking pan
6. in saucepan combine milk , chips and shortening
7. cook and stir over low heat until melted
8. spread over crust in pan
9. sprinkle with reserved topping
10. bake at 350f for 20-25 minutes , until edges golden are brown
demonstrations.review: An overwhelming success. I made these to take to a Sunday School party. The crowd went wild. The oatmeal-pecan crust was flaky and delicious. The fudgy chocolate was double delicious. So easy to make and they were gone before I could turn around three times. Thanks MizzNezz. You have a great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
pasta with fresh tomato sauce

starting with fresh tomatoes keeps the sodium levels low in this recipe. recipe is from family circle.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. drain and set aside
3. while pasta is cooking , heat 2 t of the olive oil in a medium-size saucepan over medium heat
4. add garlic and cook for 2 minutes or until fragrant
5. add tomatoes , vinegar , worcestershire sauce , salt , pepper and tomato paste to pan and turn heat to medium-high
6. cook for about 10 minutes or until tomatoes have begun to lose their shape
7. stir in remaining tablespoon olive oil and basil
8. place pasta in large bowl and stir in sauce and parmesan cheese
9. serve immediately
target.review: Awesome, awesome.  I didn't peel tomatoes but did seed them; used dried basil (a generous helping) and left out tomato paste as I didn't have any.  I can't wait to make this again.  It didn't make close to 8 servings though-- it was enough for two of us as the main course.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin butter muffins

this is a recipe i created to use the pumpkin butter i've had sitting around that i didn't know what to do with. the muffins turned out even better than i had hoped! they have an amazing flavor and moistness. will make a great breakfast muffin!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. combine all dry ingredients in a medium bowl
3. in a second medium bowl , mix together milk , egg , oil , and 1 / 2 cup pumpkin butter
4. make a well in the center of your dry ingredients and pour in milk mixture
5. stir together till just moistened
6. batter will be slightly lumpy
7. fill greased or paper lined muffin tin with half the batter-a little over a tablespoon in each cup
8. then top that with a teaspoon of pumpkin butter , then spoon the rest of the batter on top of that , so that the pumpkin butter is in the center
9. stir together topping ingredients and sprinkle heavily over muffins
10. bake them for 15-18 minutes or until a toothpick through the center comes out clean
11. allow to cool for a few minute before removing from pan and place on a wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: Easy, but not as moist as I had hoped (maybe due to the whole wheat flour?) and the flavor was slightly lacking.  They also got stale really quickly--were very dry the second day.  The pumpkin butter in the middle was a nice touch though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful bread salad

this is my version of tuscan bread salad. with tomatoes, garlic, cucumber and fresh mozzarella and herbs, how could you go wrong? cook time is sitting/refrigeration time

1. combine tomatoes , cucumber , garlic , and herbs in a large bowl
2. whisk together oil and vinegar , add salt and pepper to taste
3. pour the oil / vinegar mixture over the veggies and let them sit at room temperature for about 15 minutes
4. stir them well and add mozzarella and bread
5. refrigerate for at least 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was great.  I used some sandwich rolls that were on the verge of being stale and added a bit of rosemary to the oil/vinegar mix and thought it was just perfect.  Left out the parsley and didn't notice it not being there.  Good way to use up all those garden tomatoes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry lemon bread

nan

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
2. butter 8 1 / 2 x 4 1 / 2 x 2 1 / 2 loaf pan
3. combine first 3 ingredients in small bowl
4. using electric mixer , cream butter with 1 cup sugar in large bowl until mixture is light and fluffy
5. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
6. add lemon peel
7. mix in dry ingredients alternatively with milk , beginning and ending with dry ingredients
8. fold in blue berries
9. spoon batter into prepared loaf pan
10. bake until golden brown and toothpick inserted into center comes out clean , about 1 hour 15 minutes
11. meanwhile , bring 1 / 3 cup sugar and lemon juice to boil in small saucepan , stirring until sugar dissolves
12. pierce top of cake all over with toothpick
13. pour hot lemon mixture over loaf in pan
14. cool 30 minutes in pan on rack
15. turn bread out of pan and cool completely on rack
demonstrations.review: Few problems--all the blueberries sunk to the bottom.  I should have followed the other reviewer's advice to toss them with flour.  Half the cake stuck in the pan--be SURE to wait the 30 minutes.  And the lemon flavor was not very strong in the cake itself; the icing is necessary for lemon taste.  Even though it didn't come out perfectly, it did taste good and I would try it again with a few changes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wild mushroom risotto

i originally made this as a side dish for osso bucco.  the leftovers were fantastic all by themselves!  mushroom broth or vegetable broth can be substitutes.

1. bring chicken broth to simmer in medium saucepan
2. reduce heat to low
3. cover and keep broth hot
4. melt 3 tbsp butter with olive oil in heavy large saucepan over medium heat
5. add chopped shallots
6. saut 1 minute
7. add wild mushrooms
8. cook until mushrooms are tender and juices are released , about 8 minutes
9. add rice and stir to coat
10. add sherry and simmer until liquid is absorbed , stirring frequently , about 8 minutes
11. increase heat to medium-high
12. add 3 / 4 cup hot chicken broth and simmer until absorbed , stirring frequently
13. add remaining hot chicken broth 3 / 4 cup at a time , allowing broth to be absorbed before adding more and stirring frequently until rice is just tender and mixture is creamy , about 20 minutes
14. stir in parmesan cheese and chopped fresh thyme
15. serve warm
16. you may not need to use all the broth
demonstrations.review: Excellent, and not too complicated! I used extra chicken broth instead of sherry and a pound of assorted fresh mushrooms - crimini, oyster, and shiitake. Also used about 1/3 of a small onion instead of shallots.  It's a little time-consuming to cook but so worth it.  Add a sprinkle of fresh ground black pepper at the end.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat blueberry lemon charlotte

a friend of mine who lives up north and grows her own blueberries developed this when she decided to go on a diet.

1. in a large bowl , combine lemon gelatin with 2 cups boiling water , stirring constantly until completely dissolved , about 2 minutes
2. stir in 1 1 / 2 cups of the blueberries and the yogurt until smooth
3. cut the cake into 14 slices
4. cut each slice into 3 1-inch rectangles
5. arrange rectangles upright around edge of an 8-inch springform pan
6. arrange remaining pieces to cover bottom of pan
7. spoon in blueberry-yogurt filling
8. scatter remaining 1 / 2 cup blueberries over top
9. cover and chill until firm , about 2 hours
10. serve with blueberry honey sauce , if desired
11. to make the blueberry honey sauce:
12. in a small saucepan , combine honey and ginger and bring to a boil
13. stir in blueberries and return to a boil
14. remove from heat and stir in lemon juice
15. transfer mixture to a blender container and whirl until smooth
16. serve over blueberry lemon charlotte or spoon over cut-up fruits
demonstrations.review:
The recipe didn't come out as neat as it sounds for me-- the yogurt/jello mix was very thin (not spoonable) and when poured into the pan, the cake on the bottom floated to the top.  Also, cutting the cake as directed didn't leave enough to cover the bottom of the pan.  It came out looking very strange.  That said, it tastes great, even without making the sauce.

This is the same exact version on the Blueberry Council website.

target.recipe_text:
caramel pull aparts

yummy breakfast or brunch addition

1. grease a bundt pan
2. cut the rolls in half and roll in each in dry pudding mix
3. arrange in pan alternately with nuts
4. be sure to stack evenly as possible
5. sprinkle remaining pudding mix over the top
6. combine the brown sugar and butter together and heat until the butter is melted and syrup is formed
7. make sure it is stirred well
8. pour the syrup over the rolls
9. cover with greased plastic wrap let rise until double in size or even with top of bundt pan
10. remove wrap and bake at 350 deg
11. f 30-35 minutes
12. cover with foil the last 15 minutes of baking
13. immediately invert onto a serving platter
target.review: I made a crescent/brioche type dough in the bread machine and put it in the fridge overnight and made these rolls the next morning with about 2/3 of the dough recipe (halfway up the bundt pan.)  I rolled the balls roughly the size of a quarter.  I don't think I'd have them much bigger as there would be too much plain dough-to-caramel ratio.  :)  The dough I used is a bit richer than frozen bread dough but the best part of this recipe is the ease.  Nothing difficult about it and it would be great for company.  I would guess you could use different kinds of pudding-- ie vanilla or cheesecake, etc and get some interesting results as well.  I chose this variation of the recipe because the others have you starting with frozen dough and I knew mine would simply be refrigerated.  It's a great option to have instead of buying dough or freezing your own.  Almost any bread dough will benefit from an overnight rest in the fridge anyhow, to develop a depth of flavor.  Try it!  :)  Just make sure the butter mixture is not too hot when you pour it on the non-frozen dough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried bananas

just as south and central american countries have their fried plantains, the vietnamese have fried bananas, usually sold on the streets by women in front of their houses. the firmer the bananas, the better.

1. mix together the flour , sugar , egg , milk and salt to make a smooth , paste-like batter
2. leave to rest for one hour
3. peel the bananas and slice each one in half lengthwise , then across into chunks about three inches long
4. dip the banana pieces into the batter and shallow fry in hot oil for a few minutes or until golden brown all over
5. drain quickly on a wire rack or paper towel , and serve warm
6. if you like , serve them with real maple syrup , powdered sugar , or honey , for extra sweetness
demonstrations.review: I'm not sure what I expected from this recipe, but I thought the dough would be a little crunchy on the outside with hot sweet banana inside.  However, deep fried until the dough was nicely browned all over, once cool enough to eat-- the dough was soft and rubbery, and the banana inside was piping hot mush.  I did start with firm bananas.  I think they would be better in a crispy dough, but then I am not familiar with how this 'should' turn out, perhaps it is supposed to be non-crispy with hot mush inside.  It was not bad tasting with some caramel sauce, but texture was an issue.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monte cristo folds

i love the classic monte cristo that bennigan's serves with red raspberry preserves for dipping; but sadly, our bennigan's recently closed.  this is a variation from the 2002 pillsbury bake-off using grands buttermilk biscuits and baked instead of fried.

1. heat oven to 375f in medium bowl , mix ham , turkey and cheese
2. separate dough into 8 biscuits
3. press or roll each to form 6 to 7-inch round
4. place slightly less than 1 / 3 cup ham mixture on one side of each biscuit round
5. fold dough over filling
6. press edges to seal
7. place on ungreased cookie sheet
8. in small bowl , beat egg , milk , cinnamon and nutmeg
9. brush over tops of filled biscuits
10. bake 12 to 19 minutes or until golden brown
11. sprinkle with powdered sugar
12. serve with jam
demonstrations.review: These are great and every bit as tasty as the 'real thing!'  I too was missing Bennigan's...decided to make these on a whim.  Used deli meats and a chunk of Swiss all whizzed in the food processor.  Even used store brand flaky biscuits and they turned out a treat.  (And look pretty, too.)  Thumbs up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pinto bean bread

delicious, light, different high protein bread. a great use for leftover beans, if you ever have any. you can leave out the middle rising but the bread will be more dense.

1. combine the milk , beans , sugar , salt , shortening , and 1 tablespoon of the flour
2. stir in the yeast and wait for it to bubble
3. if it has not bubbled in 5 minutes , get new yeast
4. stir in 5-6 cups flour , to make a kneadable dough
5. knead 5-10 minutes , until satiny
6. place in a greased bowl , turning to grease dough
7. cover loosely with a clean damp cloth and let rise till double
8. punch down
9. let rise again
10. punch down
11. shape into 2 loaves
12. place in greased loaf pans
13. bake at 350 for 30-40 minutes , or until thumps hollow on bottom
demonstrations.review: This is a really nice recipe to have-- thanks!  It is surprisingly light and pretty with flecks of bean skins (I used pressure cooked mashed pinto beans.)  I made two batches, the first I used as wrapping for krautburgers and it was perfect.  The second time, I halved it and adapted it to the bread machine.  It worked great and it has absolutely no "beany" flavor, so you can use it for sweeter sandwiches like peanut butter and jelly or cinnamon toast.  It keeps well, too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pound cake cookies

once i tried these, i never bothered making 'traditional' sugar cookies again. a soft, flavorful cookie that is a must for me at christmas. note, the original recipe said they were cut-out cookies but i never was able to get them to work well that way. that is why i make the round ones as described.

1. heat oven to 375f mix half of the cake mix , the butter , almond extract and egg in large bowl until smooth
2. stir in remaining cake mix
3. divide dough into halves
4. roll each half 1 / 8 inch thick on lightly floured board
5. cut into desired shapes
6. or roll into 1-inch balls , place on ungreased cookie sheet and flatten with the bottom of a glass
7. bake until edges are light brown , 6 to 8 minutes
8. cool slightly before removing from cookie sheet
9. cool completely
10. ice with buttercream icing and decorate , if desired , with sprinkles etc
11. yields: 3 to 4 dozen cookies
12. then ice cookies as usual
13. they are now decorated without a lot of the mess !
demonstrations.review: This is a very good and very easy recipe. I was seduced by some comments which said it was close to Lofthouse cookies. I agree, tastewise, it is very close. However, the texture is not the same. Mine were quite crunchy on the outside, and slightly soft in the middle-- and that's cooking them BARELY beginning to golden on the edges. Lofthouse, of course, have no crunch at all. I did experiment with undercooking these a bit, and they were indeed more soft, but actually tasted undercooked. That said, as a sugar cookie not being compared to a famous brand, they are really outstanding unto themselves and super easy. I am posting the quick pink "Lofthouse" frosting I made for them. Try it out, it makes exactly enough for this recipe, and the cookies look outstanding. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ben   jerry s fresh georgia peach ice cream

the best way to capture the elusive flavour of summertime. ben and jerry prefer small peaches because they have more flavor and less water than the larger ones. prep is 2hrs 15 mins which is almost all chill time. freezing time is however long it takes for your ice cream maker to freeze it.

1. combine the peaches , 1 / 2 cup of the sugar , and the lemon juice in a bowl
2. cover and refrigerate for 2 hours , stirring the mixture every 30 minutes
3. remove the peaches from the refrigerator and drain the juice into another bowl
4. return the peaches to the refrigerator
5. whisk the eggs in a mixing bowl until light and fluffy , 1-2 minutes
6. whisk in the remaining 3 / 4 cup sugar , a little at a time , then continue whisking until completely blended , about 1 minute more
7. pour in the cream and milk and whisk to blend
8. add the peach juice and blend
9. transfer the mixture to an ice cream maker and freeze following manufacturer's instructions
10. after the ice cream stiffens add the peaches , then continue freezing until the ice cream is ready
11. makes 1 generous quart
demonstrations.review: This is right out of B&J's ice cream recipe book. They do not cook their custard base first...just how it is. Doesn't make it wrong. It's fine. If you get your eggs off of a farm, you might want to use a cooked base recipe but in 30+ years of making ice cream base with raw eggs from the store, which are cleaned and refrigerated...I've never once gotten sick. Remember in the Rocky film where he is swallowing eggs to train? And in the 50s one of the most popular drinks was an egg flip or an egg cream. I really hate to see people spreading paranoia re eggs. Did you know, PhytoMan, that the outside skin of cantaloupe has more chance of having salmonella, than storebought eggs? And when you draw your knife through it to cut it, you contaminate the fruit, and then eat it raw. But do you know anyone who has ever been truly sick from it? Ever handled a lizard or turtle? Their skin is full of salmonella. I don't mean to diminish the seriousness of someone who suffers from contracting it, but other than keeping such risks away from small children, it's just part of life. Take care, but don't lose sleep over it. And try this ice cream base-- it's fantastic! (All their flavors basically 2 cups cream, 1 milk, sugar, eggs and then all the good stuff.)

target.recipe_text:
cajun jalapeno poppers

this recipe came from taste testing poppers all over. i combined what i liked and discarded the rest. you can use fresh peppers or prepackaged peppers (not recommended,to soft). if i use fresh, i sometimes like to slice them in half, leaving the stem, de-vein and seed them and saute' them in my favorite beer to soften them up just a little (2-4 minutes). another tip is to always use protective cooking gloves when dealing with peppers.

1. halve the jalapenos leaving the stem attached , de-vein and seed them
2. setting the halved jalapenos and bread crumbs aside , mix all of the other ingredients together
3. take your mixture and completely fill the jalepeno cavities to their brim and set aside
4. put bread crumbs on a flat plate
5. take jalapeno halves , one at a time , and roll cheese side only in bread crumbs and place cheese / crumb side up on a baking pan once completed if you like a thick crumb layer , you can repeat this step
6. if you do not intend to bake finished product skip the rolling part and just lightly sprinkle the top of the jalepenos with the bread crumbs
7. bake at 350 for 15 minutes or until mixture starts to bubble
8. i like to refrigerate at least 1 hour prior to baking sometimes i prepare the day before , cover and refrigerate
9. serve warm , room temperature or chilled with any or all of the recommended sauces
target.review:
Who would have thought that making your own homemade Jalapeno Poppers could be this easy ... I sure didn't!  Our entire family LOVED them!  I have an abundance of jalapenos right now and have made this recipe twice.  The first time, I used Sargento's Mexican blend cheese and they were perfect!  The second time, I only had sharp cheddar on hand.  While still quite good, we much preferred the blend of cheeses.  Also, I didn't add any of the "optinal additions" because these little gems didn't need anything extra!

This is a recipe I'm keeping handy for the rest of my jalapeno season.  Thanks for sharing a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
venison tenderloin with cabernet sauce

another favourite venison recipe. this recipe considers farm-raised deer which is readily available in better butcher shops, or some larger super markets. a favourite cook offers up this recipe, and can be found in 

1. preheat the oven to 450 degrees f
2. rub the venison with garlic and sprinkle with salt and pepper
3. put olive oil in a heavy skillet
4. add venison and sear over high heat until browned on all sides- about 3 minutes place in oven and roast until medium-rare
5. for 16- 20 minutes , turning once
6. meanwhile , combine the wine with the vegetables and herbs and bring to a boil
7. reduce by half over medium heat- about 8 minutes
8. strain out vegetables and discard
9. in a saucepan , reduce broth by half over high heat- about 7 minutes
10. combine all the liquids
11. when meat is done , remove to cutting board and cover loosely with foil
12. pour any fat from the pan and deglaze with the reduced liquids
13. whisk in the cold butter and add salt and pepper
14. spoon a bit of sauce over each meat serving
demonstrations.review: We were so pleased with this recipe.  The directions for preparing it were very easy-to-follow and resulted in a very flavorful and tender venison steak.  The only change that we made to the recipe was that we used McCormick brand Montreal Steak Seasoning in place of the salt & pepper that you call for in the recipe.  Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: This is a super easy recipe to prepare and follow. I did not have enough balsamic vinegar on hand, so I substituted rice wine vinegar. This turned out fantastic even with the substitution! Next time I will try it with the balsamic vinegar. For the peppers, I used a couple dried, seeded Chiles de Arbol, which I had on hand. This was fabulous with just the right amount of heat. I served the chicken with white rice and steamed broccoli. Thank you for a great (last minute) meal!  UPDATE:  I've tried this recipe many times since my first review and wanted to say that we actually prefer the rice wine vinegar in this dish over the balsamic!  Still a great recipe!  Thank you Jan!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden copycat zuppa toscana

this is a clone of the olive garden zuppa toscana. tried and true, approved by former olive garden chefs.

1. chop or slice uncooked sausage into small pieces and cook until browned and meat is ground in bottom of your soup pan over med-high heat
2. add onions , garlic , salt , pepper , and red pepper flakes to sausage and cook until onions are clear and aromatics of the seasonings blend together
3. reduce heat back to medium and place , potatoes , in the pot
4. and slowly add the chicken stock and water and stir
5. cook on medium heat until potatoes are done and stir occasionally
6. once potatoes are done , add flour or cornstarch and simmer for another 15 minutes
7. reduce heat to lowest setting and sprinkle in your kale and cooked bacon and slowly pour cream while stirring
8. check for taste and then serve
demonstrations.review: AWSOME!  This soup was fantastic!  I have made this before on my own, but it was nice to find a recipe to follow!  I did add 2 extra potatoes to make the soup a bit thicker.  Even our kids liked it after tasting (they were leary on the kale).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
individual cream cheese danish

small danishes that make a great addition to a brunch buffet. you can also make fruit and cream cheese danishes by adding a spoonful of your favorite pie filling prior to baking. there are never any leftovers when i make these.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. slice crescent roll dough into 1 / 4 inch slices
3. place slices of dough on cookie sheet and make slight indention in the middle
4. in a large bowl , mix together cream cheese , white sugar , lemon juice , vanilla extract and sour cream
5. add a tablespoon of filling to each roll
6. bake in preheated oven for 15 to 20 minutes
7. in a small bowl , stir together confectioners' sugar , milk and butter
8. after danish has cooled , drizzle with icing
demonstrations.review: I made these for my daughter's birthday brunch and they were a huge hit!  It's a good thing the recipe makes alot, because everyone wanted to take extra home!  These were so easy to put together.  My children said they tasted like "toaster strudels".  A wonderful recipe sbsbea!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
danish cherry sauce

when cherry season hits, this one is worth preserving. great for cheesecakes or ice cream topping.

1. wash and pit cherries
2. in a large saucepan combine sugar , cinnamon sticks , almond extract , water and corn syrup
3. over medium high heat bring to a boil , stirring often to prevent scorching
4. reduce heat to a simmer and add cherries
5. simmer for 5 minutes
6. remove cinnamon sticks
7. ladle hot sauce into hot sterile jars , leaving 1 / 2 inch head space
8. wipe rims and adjust 2 piece caps
9. process 10 minutes in a boiling water canner
10. to thicken sauce for serving , combine 1 t cornstarch and 2 t's water in a medium saucepan
11. whisk well to remove any lumps
12. add 1 pint danish cherry sauce and bring to a boil , cooking until sauce reaches desired thickness
demonstrations.review: This sauce is fabulous!  I've made this many times over the past few years and just today realized that I hadn't reviewed it!  So easy to make and my family really enjoys it!  In addition to the uses that you mention, we enjoy it over pancakes.  I've also used it in coffee cakes, too!

target.recipe_text:
chicken   rice soup

nan

1. combine the broth , thyme , dill , bay leaf , carrots , celery and onion in a pot
2. bring to a boil , stir in the rice , cover and reduceto a simmer
3. cook 15 minutes
4. add the chicken and cook over medium heat for another 5 to 10 minutes , or until the rice and vegetables are soft and cooked through
5. season to taste with salt and pepper
target.review: This was very good.  I used brown rice so I cooked it a while longer.  Also, the brown rice must have soaked up more of the broth because mine was not very brothy...I didn't mind.  I added in some garlic and omitted the dill.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot steak fajitas

nan

1. brown the steak in oil
2. place the steak and drippings into the crock pot
3. add lemon juice , garlic , cumin , salt , and chili powder
4. mix well
5. cover and cook on high for 2 1 / 2 to 3 hours , or until meat is tender
6. add green pepper and onion
7. cover and cook for 1 hour more
8. warm the tortillas
9. spoon beef and veggies down the center of the tortillas
10. top each with cheese , salsa , sour cream , lettuce , and tomatoes if desired
11. fold in the sides of the tortillas and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I used boneless chicken breasts, I didn't brown them, just threw everything in before work and added the green pepper about 2 hours before we ate.
