I shredded the chicken and it made an excellent meal and leftovers!  This one's a keeper!  I'd love to try it with beef if I could get my family to eat some cow!  thanx for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s tuna salad sandwiches

this is a simple recipe but big on flavor and it even tastes better if left in the fridge a few hours to blend the flavors so i suggest to do that --- it's wonderful with a slice of tomato on top of the tuna and served between two thick slices of toasted whole grain bread or in a pita bread or served on a plate on top of a bed of lettuce --- i sometimes add in some chopped small sweet gherkin pickles or yum yum pickles also --- feel free to add in some cooked macaroni pasta and serve on a plate --- please only fresh lemon juice for this bottled is just not the same, i have left the mustard powder and tabasco as optional i most always add it in it takes this salad to another level :)

1. drain the tuna then hand-squeeze out any excess moisture
2. place in a bowl then flake with a fork
3. add in all remaining ingredients up to the tabasco sauce
4. mix until well combined , adjusting all seasonings to suit taste
5. cover with plastic wrap and chill for at least 2 hours
6. divide onto bread slices with lettuce leaves and slices tomatoes
7. delicious !
demonstrations.review: Oh yum!!! I was looking for a way to spice up my tuna sandwiches...thank you for posting this gem :)  I didn't have any onion or celery, but chopped up a bit of yellow pepper that I had in the fridge, the relish, tabasco, fresh ground pepper, season salt, ground mustard and lemon juice.  Delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot pepper butter  mustard  for canning

awesome mustard for anything from pretzels, sandwiches, or glazes on hams. i add more peppers than in the recipe for a hotter butter (approx 60 ranging med-large). also i am trying other peppers as well, habenero, maybe only 10-12...i'll have to let you know how it works :) you will not be disappointed! i have sold the canned product to many family and friends and they can only say this is the best! hope you enjoy!!

1. seed and chop peppers
2. mix everything together
3. boil for 5 minutes ! stirring constantly ! or until desired thickness
4. ladle into hot , sterilized jars
5. cap with hot lid and of course the ring and process in hot water bath for 10 minutes
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I hate to leave so few stars but I can't find a single soul who likes this stuff...it is soooo sweet.  I followed the recipe exactly, but used a variety of banana, jalapeno, and red chili peppers.  I am very disappointed...it was a lot of work.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy seven layer rice casserole

since there is no precooking the ground beef for this casserole it comes together quite easy, just layer ingredients and bake in just one dish, i always season the ground beef with seasoned salt, black pepper, fresh garlic and a few tablespoons of parmesan cheese but that is only optional, you can even sprinkle cheddar cheese in the middle also when layering :)

1. set oven to 450 degrees f
2. butter a 2 qt casserole dish
3. layer each ingredient in order given starting with the uncooked rice on the bottom of casserole dish , ending up with the bacon on top
4. cover , bake for 1 hour
5. uncover and continue cooking for 20-25 minutes longer
6. top with shredded cheddar cheese the last 5 minutes of baking
demonstrations.review: I modified this recipe by using black beans instead of corn and also a jar of salsa instead of green peppers and the diced tomatoes...and then I used a can of chicken instead of using ground beef.  And, no bacon.  We loved it!  Thanks for the inspiration!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coca cola pork roast

there are lots of cola/meat recipes on this site, this one is a little different. i found this in a crockpot cookbook that my folks gave me for christmas. i tweaked it a bit, but still--great stuff!

1. rub the roast with salt and pepper then place it in the crockpot
2. add soup mix and coke
3. cook on low 8 hours or high for 4
4. before serving dump liquid from crockpot into a pot
5. skim fat
6. to the remaining juices add salt and pepper to taste and a dash of kitchen bouquet
7. bring mixture to a boil
8. remove a cup of the liquid and add corn starch to thicken
9. add corn starch mixture to the rest of the juices
10. cook until it reaches desired consistency
11. wonderful gravy !
demonstrations.review: Made this today & my house smelled great!  The meat was so-so...nothing we were dying over. BUT, the gravy is out of this world! I would give the gravy 5 stars and the meat 3...that's how I ended up rating 4 stars.  If you decide to make this, make extra gravy! I followed recipe exactly except I used flour to thicken gravy because I didn't have any cornstarch.

target.recipe_text:
dry rub pork ribs

a simple, no hassle, no mess and delicious method for 

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. cut pork ribs into sections of 3 or 4 bones
3. mix remaining ingredients well , sprinkle on both sides of ribs and rub into the meat
4. seal rib sections in foil with a tablespoon of water in each package , and bake for 2 hours on a cookie sheet in the center of the oven
5. open foil carefully as steam escapes
6. can be crisped on a hot bbq if desired but will be great just the way it is
target.review: I have had ribs many times before made by some of my friends.  This was the first time I cooked them.  I was so Glad that I did.  These were the best ribs ever.  What I did differently was I halved the garlic powder and red pepper flakes and double the paprika and added a little more brown sugar.  After they cooked I took the top foil off and brushed on some Sweet Baby Ray's Honey BBQ sauce and put it back in the oven for another 15 minutes.  My BF couldn't stop eating them.  Thanks so much Dug for sharing this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked tilapia w  fondue sauce and crab

the sauce on this is so creamy...you would never guess that it is low in fat!

1. preheat oven to 400
2. for the sauce , melt the butter in a pan
3. stir in the flour and nutmeg until smooth
4. gradually stir in the milk
5. cook until smooth and thickens a little
6. add the cheese , and stir until melted
7. add in the sherry and crab meat , mixing well to coat the crab
8. season tilapia with salt and pepper
9. place the tilapia in an 8x8 pan
10. pour the fondue-crab sauce over the tilapia
11. sprinkle with the paprika
12. bake at 400 for 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: My bf and I thought that this was superb.  We just loved the fondue sauce.  This is definately gonna be my fav tilapia recipe.  It definately has the presentation from going to a quality restaurant.  Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: This was a really good meatloaf.  It was better than my mom's and that's a tough task to do.  I did do a couple things different.  Instead of the slice of bread, I used 3/4 cup of breadcrumbs and since I didn't have any onions at home I used a little bit of onion powder.  The sauce is really good too.  Though I would cut down on the vinegar.  It's my personal preference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy chicken tetrazzini

this recipe came from southern living, way back in 1987.  this is my favorite tetrazzini recipe.  a great way to use up leftover chicken or turkey.  also, i often find myself with extra pasta...this is a great way to use that up as well!

1. combine first 3 ingredients in a saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. cut chicken into 1 / 2 inch cubes
4. add chicken to saucepan
5. cover , reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes or until done
6. drain
7. combine 6 cups water , 1 / 2 tsp salt , and olive oil in a dutch oven , bring to a boil
8. add pasta , and cook according to package directions
9. do not overcook
10. drain well and set aside
11. saute green pepper in butter in a dutch oven until tender
12. add flour , and stir well
13. stir in milk , next 6 ingredients and 2 cups cheddar cheese
14. cook over medium heat , stirring constantly , 10 minutes or until thoroughly heated
15. stir in chicken
16. spread half of pasta in a greased 12x8x2 inch baking dish
17. spread half of chicken mixture over pasta
18. repeat layers
19. bake at 350 degrees for 15 minutes
20. sprinkle with remaining cup of cheese and top with almonds
21. bake an additional 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: My bf and I very much enjoyed this.  I used the thin spaghetti.  Instead of the wine/sherry, I used apple juice. I also added some peas to this as well.  I completely forgot to toast the almonds, but it was still good and like the cruch it brought.  Thanks for sharing this recipe. I will definately use it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers hot tuna melt on english muffin

this is a recipe that was printed in a ww coupon flier that i got.  only 5 points.

1. preheat broiler or toaster oven to high
2. combine tuna , celery , cream cheese , salt , pepper , and lemon juice in a small bowl
3. mix well until thoroughly combined
4. scoop equal parts tuna mixture onto each muffin half
5. sprinkle equal amounts cheese over each tuna-topped muffin
6. place both halves in broiler or toaster oven and heat until cheese is melted , 1-2 minutes , watching carefully so they do not burn
7. remove promptly from heat
demonstrations.review: I thought that this was just ok.  I just started on weight watchers so I'm getting used to trying new things.  But of couse I did do a boo boo.  I accidently used tablespoons instead of teaspoons of the lemon juice.  Thank goodness that I at least like lemon juice.  I bet it will be better next time if I used less LJ.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chicken crescent roll casserole

this will also work great with turkey; if you do not have chicken breasts, then use any leftover cooked chicken. if desired you can fill the crescents just with the filling mixture and omit the soup, just brush with butter before baking. they are wonderful just stuffed with the filling! a few members have experienced a soggy bottom, so you might want to consider just drizzling half (or even a little less) of the soup mixture on top and a little around the sides of the crescents, then save the rest of the soup mixture for another time (this will help prevent a soggy bottom). you may use the jumbo crescent rolls and stuff with more chicken mixture :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. butter a casserole dish
3. in a saucepan , mix half and half cream , 3 / 4 cup grated cheese and undiluted chicken soup
4. heat just until the cheese melts
5. for the filling --- in a bowl , mix the soft cream cheese with butter until very smooth , then add in garlic powder
6. add in the chopped chicken , onion and cheddar cheese
7. mix well until combined
8. add in 2 tablespoons whipping cream or mayonnaise
9. mix to combine
10. season with seasoned salt or white and black pepper to taste
11. unroll the crescent rolls
12. place 1 heaping tablespoon chicken mixture on top of each crescent triangle , then roll up starting at the thicker end
13. drizzle a small amount of soup mixture on the bottom of the dish
14. then place the crescent rolls seam-side down on top of the creamed mixture in the casserole
15. drizzle the remaining sauce on top and sprinkle with 1 cup grated cheese , or amount desired
16. bake for about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  My bf loved it even more....   I used the jumbo crescent rolls  and he ate all but one of them.  That says a lot to me.  All the ingredients worked so well together.  Thanks so much Kittencal!

target.recipe_text:
burger bites

this recipe came from kraft foods and the photo was so cute.  it showed these little "kabobs" made with meatballs, pineapple and peppers on wooden toothpicks.  it was adorable! i have not tried them, but wanted to share them with you. the serving number is based on using toothpicks as the skewers, with one meatball, one pineapple chunk and one piece of pepper per toothpick.  hope you enjoy!

1. mix barbecue sauce and jelly in large skillet
2. cook and stir on medium heat 2 minute or until jelly melts
3. add meatballs to skillet
4. cook 10 minute or until heated through
5. skewer each meatball alternately on long wooden skewer or toothpick with pineapple chunk and red pepper
target.review: WOW!! What a delcious dish!!! Easy to make and ever better to eat! I used Your Basic Meatballs and made them without freezing them! The sauce thickened up really nicle, and stayed on the meatball real well. Thanks for the recipe Bobtail!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
costco muffins   copycat

found on the net and posted so that it will be easier to find when folks ask for the recipe!  prep times are guess-timates.

1. mix all ingredients together
2. spoon into prepared muffin cups
3. bake at 375 for approximately 20 minutes or until tops are lightly browned
4. for almond poppyseed muffins: use a white cake mix , add 2 teaspoons poppyseeds , and 1 tsp almond extract
5. for chocolate muffins: use a chocolate cake mix and stir in 1 1 / 2 cup chocolate chips
6. create your own: use whatever flavor cake mix you want and add your own goodies
7. other suggestions:
8. + french vanilla cake mix and fresh raspberries
9. + lemon cake mix and poppyseed
10. + spice cake mix with cinnamon / sugar topping
demonstrations.review: Great!! My family loves costco muffins and i have been looking forever for a recipe! I made double chocolate chip muffins, but for the cake mix i used Moist Deluxe Dark Chocolate Cake Mix(Copycat-Duncan Hines) Recipe #129855  and it turned out great! Thanks so much for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog cookies

"what a delectable treat for eggnog lovers everywhere! these cookies have a wonderful spicy aroma and are great tasting. the fragrance of nutmeg and cinnamon will infuse your home with holiday spirit as you bake these cookies. they make delicious gifts and are a welcome addition to cookie exchanges. "

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. combine flour , baking powder , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. cream sugar and butter until light
4. add eggnog , vanilla , and egg yolks
5. beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth
6. add flour mixture and beat at low speed until just combined
7. do not overmix
8. drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet 1 inch apart
9. sprinkle lightly with nutmeg
10. bake 20 to 23 minutes until bottoms turn light brown
demonstrations.review: These cookies were very good and got me into the Christmas mood! I used light eggnog and it worked fine! These cookies have a cake like and puff up nicley in the oven. I bcaked mine less than 20 minutes and that was the only delema I faced! Thanks for the recipe RecipeNut!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 minute fudge

my favorite is the butterscotch but i have done the chocolate, too and they both turn out great.

1. mix milk , sugar and salt in a heavy saucepan , over med-high heat
2. heat to boiling
3. cook 5 minutes , stirring constantly
4. remove from heat , and add other ingredients
5. stir until marshmallows are all melted
6. pour into buttered 9" square pan
7. cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Great, easy and delcious! Instead of putting this fudge into a pan, I put each scoop into a muffin cup and worked very well! I didn't have to worry about cutting, and the servings were perfect! This made a great addition to our xmas tray! Thanks very much for the recipe bert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat brownie

i have adopted this recipe (feb 2006) and not made yet. if you make the recipe i would be highly interested in any comment on it.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. make the brownie cake by whipping the egg whites in a large bowl with an electric mixer until they become thick
3. add the sugar to the egg whites and continue beating until the mixture forms soft peaks
4. mix shortening , chocolate syrup , fudge sauce , water , and vanilla
5. in a separate bowl , combine the flour , cocoa , salt , and baking soda
6. while beating the wet mixture , slowly add the dry mixture and mix until smooth
7. fold in egg white mixture
8. lightly grease a 9-inch pie pan with shortening
9. pour the brownie batter into the pan and sprinkle the chopped walnuts over the top
10. bake for 35 minutes or until a toothpick poked into the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review:
I was curious to try this recipe because of the chocolate that you use. This was delcious! It was very moist and had a great chocolate flavor to it. Next time I would probaly add some chocolate chips to the batter-just for that little extra crunch. The cooking time was exact for me!
Thanks for the recipe Thorsten!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog coffee  non alcoholic

a great way to use that eggnog! don't ya just love the holidays?

1. place coffee in filter in brew basket of coffee maker
2. sprinkle with nutmeg
3. place sugar in empty pot of coffee maker
4. add 2-1 / 2 cups cold water to coffee maker
5. brew
6. when brewing is complete , stir in eggnog
7. pour into 4 cups
8. serve immediately , topped with dollops of the whipped topping
9. sprinkle lightly with additional nutmeg , if desired
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This was FANTASTIC!!!!! So easy to make and tastes delcious! Whenever I brew myself a cup of coffee in the morning, I'll probaly make this becuase its not that much more work!!!
Thanks for the recipe Sharon123!

target.recipe_text:
rustic salmon pie

delicious and easy, great for a special occasion or even a week day dinner. the pastry on this is lushious! i used frozen butter and grated it, made it sooo flaky and delicious!! i think one could use almost any filling, i used pink salmon, probably the sockeye would have looked prettier. i'm sure a meat/chicken filling would work beautifully too.
(from one of those little bakefest books, pullout from a magazine.)

1. pastry:
2. combine flour , butter and salt in the bowl of a food processor fitted with a metal blade
3. pulse until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
4. beat egg with lemon juice , adding enough ice water to measure 1 / 3 cup
5. add to flour mixture and process , until mixture begins to clump
6. form into a disk and chill
7. preheat oven to 375f degrees
8. roll pastry between two sheets of parchment paper , lightly floured , to about 1 / 4 inch thick
9. remove top piece of parchment and slide the pastry onto a large baking sheet or pie plate
10. filling:
11. measure 1 tablespoon of cream and reserve
12. stir mashed potatoes with salmon , cheese , remaining cream , onion , egg , lemon juice , dill , garlic , salt and pepper until well combined
13. spoon salmon mixture into the centre of the prepared pastry round
14. fold in the edges of the pastry , leaving the centre of the filling exposed
15. brush the crust with the reserved cream
16. bake for 50 minutes or until pastry is golden
target.review: Just wonderful. Made it for Christmas Eve dinner for my husband, his mom and her mother, and all loved it. I used 1lb of fresh salmon, pan-sauteed with a little butter and salt.  Used milk instead of cream ... NO need for that extra fat.  And if you can let it rest for 5-10mins before serving it firms up -- but not essential.  This was only the second pie crust I've made in my life and it was EASY. Thanks so much!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 vegetable casserole

my bosses wife swears by this recipe for leftovers. i have used it many times, make a good meal or sidedish.

1. scald milk with margarine
2. remove from heat , add bread veggies , salt , eggs and 3 / 4 cup cheese
3. mix together and pour into a 4 quart greased casserole , top with remaining 1 / 2 cup of cheese
4. bake at 325 for 40 min
5. want some extra flavour use half evaporated milk
demonstrations.review: Delicious, and even better texture when reheated the next day!!  I think 4-qt is a typo; mine fit in a 2-qt even with a little extra bread.  Picture seems to show a 2-qt. casserole dish.   And friends, please, use butter.  Margerine is NOT better for you and doesn't taste as good!  ;-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven barbecue

this is a recipe i had written down in an old cookbook and decided to try it one afternoon. it was a hit!! i fixed it with hashbrown casserole and a salad and it disappeared in a flash!

1. in roasting pan , cover meat with cream of chicken soup
2. cover with barbecue sauce
3. cover all with the dry soup mix
4. cover and bake in 350 oven for about 2 hours or until tender enough to slice
5. for shredded meat , bake about 3 hours or until very tender
6. drain off fat
7. slice or shred and serve on buns
8. spoon gravy from roaster over the meat in the sandwiches
demonstrations.review: Delicious, but needs more liquid to start -- at least half the soup can of water.  Probably also cover with foil for part of cooking time.  I used 5-lb meat and after 2hrs, there was no way to "drain off fat" and barely enough sauce even to spread over all the meat. BTW:  I used cream of celery because that's what I had!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penny s easy goulash

want something that you can throw together quickly and forget about for an hour?  this is it!  a "chili-mac" style dish that has great flavor and makes a ton!  perfect for a cold winter day...thanks penny (my mom)!

1. brown meat until done , drain grease
2. transfer to very large pot or dutch-oven
3. add the onion , green pepper , tomatoes , garlic , mushrooms , tomato juice and macaroni
4. do not add the oregano or basil yet
5. stir to mix
6. add salt and pepper to taste
7. cover
8. simmer on medium-low heat for ~45 minutes , stirring once or twice
9. check periodically during last 10-15 minutes for doneness
10. macaroni should be just a slight bit underdone as it will continue to cook after being removed from the heat
11. add oregano and basil at this time
12. stir & re-cover after each check
13. let sit for at least 5 minutes before serving
14. serve with italian bread and parmesan cheese !
demonstrations.review: Quick, easy and delicious.  Easy to make a half-recipe, and even a 20-minute simmer is fine (although longer would be better).  I substituted chopped zucchini for mushrooms, and note:  if you use dried herbs (smaller amount), you can add at any time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious ground beef pizza casserole

this is not hard to throw together, i make this quite often and my family loves this casserole!

1. grease a 13x9-inch baking dish
2. cook the gound beef in a medium skillet with the onions , green peppers , garlic , salt pepper until meat is browned and veggies are tender
3. drain fat , and mix in the parmesan cheese
4. stir in the 1 / 2-pound pepperoni , mushrooms , pasta sauce
5. stir well until combined
6. simmer for 20-25 minutes on top of stove
7. set oven to 350 degrees
8. place the cooked rigatoni pasta on the bottom of the greased baking dish
9. sprinkle with 2 cups mozzarella cheese over the pasta
10. layer with pepperoni slices evenly over the cheese
11. top with the ground beef / pasta sauce mixture
12. bake uncovered for 30 minutes
13. remove from oven , sprinkle with the remaining 2 cups mozzarella cheese
14. return to oven and bake for 10 minutes longer , or until bubbly
15. let stand for 10-15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: Diamond in the rough; recipe is artery-busting and too complex as written, but with lots of changes it yields a great dish results. (1) a pound of pepperoni would overwhelm; 6oz (turkey!) pepp. is plenty. (2) 3c mozzarella is also plenty. (3) Doesn't say if pasta measure is raw or cooked; simply use a 1-lb box rigatoni. (4) Green pepper isn't worth it; I sub'd a whole plastic tub of stemmed baby spinach, lightly chopped -- cooks way down and adds color and nutrition.  Now you're talking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Yummy chili, here.  My tips:
-- NO more than 2Tbl. brown sugar; might even cut it nexy time.
-- 2-3 cans of beans is plenty.  "Mostly drain" them (but not the diced tomatoes).
-- Don't skip the diced sirloin; it adds a great texture element alongside the ground beef.
-- Foster's isn't very dark, but very easy to buy one (large) can at a time for you non-beer households! 
-- Definitely store the chili overnight or longer before eating.  We ate our batch several times this week!

target.recipe_text:
mary s biscuits

these biscuits are a 

1. combine dry ingredients in a large bowl
2. cut in shortening with a pastry blender , until mixture resembles coarse crumbs
3. cover bowl& refrigerate for about 30 minutes
4. make a well in the center of the mixture& add milk all at once
5. stir just until dough clings together
6. preheat oven to 450f degrees
7. on a lightly floured surface , knead dough gently 10-12 strokes
8. roll or pat dough to 1 / 2" thickness
9. cut with a floured 2 1 / 2" biscuit cutter--cut straight down to the board , then twist& lift cutter--dipping cutter into flour after each cut
10. transfer biscuits to an ungreased baking sheet
11. place biscuits so they're almost touching , and press two fingers lightly into top of each biscuit
12. bake 10-12 minutes or until golden
13. remove to wire rack to cool completely
14. also , pressing your fingers into the center of each biscuit keeps the middles from rising higher than the sides
target.review: Biscuits are not a big thing in Alberta, Canada as restaurants serve dinner buns.  I've never made biscuits before and I am pleased with the results. They are high, light and fluffy and I brushed the tops with butter when they came out of the oven. Thanks so much for sharing your recipe. Katherine

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy glazed banana cookies 2die4

i believe that could quite possibly be, one of the yummiest cookies i have seen! if you are bored with baking banana bread, give this recipe a shot!

1. heat oven to 350
2. in large mixing bowl , mix 3 / 4 cup brown sugar & 3 / 4 cup butter
3. beat at medium speed , scraping your bowl often until mixture is creamy 1-2 minutes
4. add in the bananas , egg , orange zest & 1 / 2 tsp vanilla extract
5. continue beating batter until well mixed 1-2 minutes
6. reduce speed to low & add the flour , baking powder , baking soda & salt
7. beat until well mixed again , 1-2 minutes
8. by round teaspoons , drop the dough 2-inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets
9. bake 8-10 minutes or until edges have slightly browned
10. on medium heat , melt 2 tbsp butter in 1-quart saucepan , adding 3 tbsp brown sugar & cream
11. continue to cook , while stirring occasionally until mix comes to a boil 1-2 minutes
12. remove from heat & add powdered sugar & remaining vanilla , beat until well mixed
13. when cookies have cooled , frost them with icing
demonstrations.review:
These were wonderful, but I made a few changes.
I used margarine instead of butter and 1 tsp. of vanilla. 
Then I added 1 cup of chopped pecans and 1 cup of chocolate chips which truly enhanced the flavor of this cookie.  
I used 1 large Tbsp of dough per cookie and ended up with 24 cookies. 
Thanks again for this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hungarian pork chops

another one of my mom's recipes. what can i say, she was a great cook!

1. sprinkle chops with salt and pepper
2. sear chops in large skillet in oil or cooking spray
3. remove chops to a plate
4. saut onions and garlic in drippings until onion is limp
5. return chops to the skillet with broth , bay leaf , and paprika
6. cover tightly and simmer about 1 hour
7. remove chops from liquid again
8. mix water and flour in a shaker and whisk into liquid
9. heat to boiling , stirring constantly
10. stir in sour cream , if desired
11. return chops to gravy
12. serve with mashed potatoes or hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: Great and easy recipe to make, the pork chops were tender but the gravy was bland tasting and didn't have much flavor. The next time I will add a few more spices to enhance the flavor of the gravy. Otherwise very good recipe. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tex mex rice

this is a version of rice that you find at a tex-mex restaurant. it is way easier than it looks and after you have made it once or twice - you can do it by heart. my kids love it and i love that i can sneak a few veggies in! can be made vegan with veggie broth.

1. in a heavy pot , cook garlic in oil over high heat until browned , stirring often
2. discard garlic cloves
3. add rice to infused oil and reduce heat to medium high
4. stirring constantly , brown rice
5. add broth , salsa , carrots and corn and reduce heat to low
6. cover and cook for 20 minutes
7. fluff rice before serving
demonstrations.review:
Awesome rice with a wonderful flavor and I made this with Garlic Beef Enchiladas (#18387)....great together.  I used can corn since I didn't have frozen and mixed chicken OXO with water for the broth and it turned out perfect. 
Thanks for sharing this recipe Cindy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stroganoff meatballs

this is a favourite in my family, easy to put together and especially loved by children. i make it a least once every two weeks.

1. meat balls: combine all ingredients in large bowl
2. mix well and roll into balls of desired size
3. place on edged cookie sheet and bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes
4. remove from oven , drain and set aside
5. sauce: brown onion in butter , add flour , mix well
6. add ketchup and consomm , cooking slowly until thickened
7. add sour cream , then meat balls
8. place in casserole and heat in 300f oven until serving time
9. serve over broad egg noodles or rice
10. i usually don't add the full cup of sour cream , but just add a bit at a time until i think it is right for me
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe and the taste of the sauce is wonderful and really makes the dish.  I cut the recipe in half but still used 1/4 cup of onions as we love them and I added 1 tsp. of minced garlic and 1 tbsp. of parsley into the meatballs.  Next time I will use fresh mushrooms and saute them with the onions for the sauce. Thank you so much Bert for this terrific recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fannie farmer s classic baked macaroni   cheese

to me fannie farmer's recipe is the only "real" macaroni & cheese. it's from my 1946 edition of "fannie farmer's boston cooking school cookbook". with time on it's side - this recipe is hands down the best for traditional, homemade baked macaroni & cheese - comfort food.

please note: if you use cheap cheese you will end up with a bland and flavorless dish!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. cook and drain macaroni according to package directions
3. set aside
4. in a large saucepan melt butter
5. add flour mixed with salt and pepper , using a whisk to stir until well blended
6. pour milk and cream in gradually
7. stirring constantly
8. bring to boiling point and boil 2 minutes
9. reduce heat and cook 10 minutes
10. add shredded cheddar little by little and simmer an additional 5 minutes , or until cheese melts
11. turn off flame
12. add macaroni to the saucepan and toss to coat with the cheese sauce
13. transfer macaroni to a buttered baking dish
14. sprinkle with breadcrumbs
15. bake 20 minutes until the top is golden brown
16. (you can also freeze this recipe in zip-lock bags for later use - once you have mixed the macaroni along with the cheese sauce allow to cool to room temperature before adding to your freezer - i generally pull it out the night before and allow macaroni and cheese to reach room temperature
17. i then add the macaroni and cheese to a buttered baking dish , sprinkle with bread crumbs and then bake for 20 to 30 minutes , until golden brown on top and bubbling
demonstrations.review:
This was extremely tasty!
I added 1 tsp dry mustard, garlic & more milk to thin the sauce.  I did not put on any breadcrumbs as the family doesn't care for that.
Thanks so much for one of the best macaroni & cheese recipes.
Katherine

target.recipe_text:
chicken macaroni casserole

southern living: a simple homey casserole my kids like.

1. in a large skillet over med-high heat , saute onions in butter until onions are tender
2. add in soup and 1 cups cheese
3. gradually stir in milk
4. cook over medium heat until cheese melts
5. stir in chicken and macaroni
6. taste and adjust seasoning with salt and pepper
7. transfer mixture to a greased 2 quart casserole
8. sprinkle with cracker crumbs
9. bake in a preheated 350 oven for 30 minutes or until heated through
10. top with remaining cup cheese and bake 5 minutes
target.review: We loved this even with the few changes I had to make to use what I had on hand.  A 'traditional' rotisserie chicken was perfect for this!  I also used egg noodles, 1 can cream of chicken and 1 can cream of mushroom soup, didn't use onion but added a little garlic salt and pepper, then topped with buttered bread crumbs and cheese.  Thanks for sharing, I will make it by the recipe next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili dogs  college style

the perfect, cheap and easy way for people on a budget to make chili dogs, hence the title!

1. heat the chili and hot dogs in the same pan until hot
2. put the hot dogs in a split hot dog bun , cover with chili cheese and onion
3. eat !
demonstrations.review: Love me an occasional chili cheese dog!  Sometimes I make a pan full at a time, in the oven!  Hot, toasty, delicious!  Gotta have some yellow mustard on it too! The hot dogs and chili still need to be warmed first though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s cheese potato   smoked sausage casserole

this was another one of our favorites in the 70's  very inexpensive and very easy to make.  just recently found this recipe hand-written by my mom, and the warm feelings flood back to me, because this was a true favorite in our house.  little did i know that she was on such a tight budget, yet made things like this that we all loved!!  note:  the meat that was used in this recipe always varied, according to whatever we had available at the time.

1. cut skinless smoked sausage in half , lengthwise , and then chop into 1 / 2 inch "half moon" cuts
2. cook in a frying pan for about 15 minutes , turning frequently to slightly brown
3. meanwhile , put cooked & diced potatoes in 2 quart casserole
4. add cooked meat and give it a gentle toss
5. mix all remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until warm , melted and smooth
6. pour white / cheese sauce over potatoes and meat
7. sprinkle shredded sharp cheddar cheese on top , and then sprinkle paprika evenly over the top
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for 35-45 minutes
9. hot dogs , sliced into 1 / 2-inch slices or 1 / 2 lb
10. ham diced into 1 / 2-inch dices or 12 oz
11. can of spam diced into 1 / 2-inch dices , instead of the smoked sausage
demonstrations.review: After reading that the recipe made a lot of sauce,  I reduced the ingredients by 25%. I added a full teaspoon salt, a little garlic salt, and a good pinch of dry mustard to it as well.  I didn't measure my potato cubes, so I may have had a little more than stated.  After topping with the shredded cheese, I sprinkled about 1/3 cup buttered Panko crumbs over the top before baking.  Overall, it was a good casserole, but I will use a different smoked sausage next time..Echrich tastes like bologna to me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
loose meat sandwiches

these taste like a good old fashioned hamburger.  they are so good!  we usually double the recipe and use the meat in stuffed baked potatoes on the second night.

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , cook onions until brown and carmelized
2. add ground beef and cook until brown
3. add salt , pepper , garlic powder and beef broth to cover
4. reduce heat to low and simmer , uncovered , until broth is gone , 15 to 30 minutes
5. serve meat on buns topped with dill pickle slices and mustard
6. we steam the buns on top of the meat for a minute or two to get them nice and soft
demonstrations.review: Love loose meat sandwiches!!  I had to modify a little to use what I had on hand, 1 Tbl dried onions instead of fresh and beef bouillon dissolved in hot water for the broth.  Per personal tastes, I decreased the amount of garlic powder, added 1 tsp sugar, and 2 tsp Kitchen Bouquet for a better color.  And yes, "steamed" buns make all the difference!  Dill pickle slices, yellow mustard, and finely diced onions are our toppings of choice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatless italian macaroni bake

dont be deceived, this recipe looks singularly ordinary so one may be tempted to alter it...but then it'll have all the subtlety of mac 'n' cheese w/ tomato...please try it as written, discover the subtlety and simplicity of it all...as for me, this 'casserole' quickly became a favorite meal, particularly since i usually have all the ingredients already on hand...i imagine it could also be adapted to the microwave, but i'll leave that to the alleged experts lol

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a large mixing bowl combine the cooked marcaroni , stewed tomatoes , 1 / 2 cup of the mozzarella , italian seasoning and mayonnaise --
3. spoon the mixture into a 1 1 / 2 quart casserole dish
4. sprinkle with the remaining 1 / 4 cup mozzarella cheese --
5. bake in the preheated 350f oven for approximately 20 min until warm and all cheese is melted --
6. e
7. no salad dressing , no miracle whip , as the recipe is specifically tailored to the result that is created by the use of mayonnaise --
8. variation: use a different pasta such as rotini or penne rigati
demonstrations.review: This was good even though I thought it needed more seasonings since we like spicier foods. My additions were salt, pepper, a pinch of garlic salt, and a dash of cayenne pepper.  An easy way to chop the stewed tomatoes is to use kitchen shears while they're still in the can.  I used one cup of mozzarella in the mixture, and 1/2 cup on top to keep the macaroni from getting too dry. I will try it again with rotini and a different mayo, or maybe substituting part of it with a little sour cream or cream cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy brussels sprouts with bacon   onion

i came up with this myself. since brussels sprouts have a similar flavor to cabbage, i have adapted my cabbage recipe for them. my husband thought he did not like brussels sprouts until i made these. i usually have to do a double batch and we end up fighting over the leftovers!!!

1. cook brussels sprouts according to package
2. i steam mine in the microwave
3. while sprouts are cooking , in a pot on the stove , cook your bacon and onion together
4. cook until bacon and onion are thoroughly done
5. add brussels sprouts to bacon & onion
6. add margarine and salt & pepper to taste
7. when margarine is melted , you are done !
8. i like to cook mine until the sprouts get a little brown on the bottom
demonstrations.review: I love brussels sprouts!  I didn't have an onion so I used some onion salt and a pinch of garlic powder, very good subs.  I'm kinda glad that my DH doesn't eat brussels sprouts so I can have the leftovers!  I could make a meal off these and hot cornbread!

target.recipe_text:
chewy secret chocolate chip cookies

this is a take on the nestle tollhouse recipe. only one added ingredient, dark brown sugar, melted butter and a smidgen more flour make the difference... i had to sell my soul to my aunt so she'd tell me why hers tasted soooo good! chewy chocolate chip cookie heaven!!!!!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. melt butter
3. beat butter , granulated sugar , dark brown sugar , molasses and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
5. combine flour , baking soda and salt in separate bowl
6. gradually beat in flour mixture
7. stir in morsels
8. drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased baking sheets
9. bake at 375 oven for 9 to 11 minutes or until golden brown
10. let stand for 2 minutes , remove to wire racks to cool completely
11. after cooling , carefully hide a few so you have a chance to eat them !
target.review: These are not pretty cookies, but they sure do taste wonderful.  They came out flat and monochromatic, kind of like the color of the  milk chocolate chips I used.  However, they are very tasty, chewy and soft.  They were enjoyed by grownups and kids alike.  Great alternative to the Tollhouse chocolate cookie recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
alton brown s baked brown rice

this recipe comes from alton brown and it's the only way we have rice anymore.  my servings are quite a bit smaller than his, though!  you can use chicken or veggie broth in place of the water, or add herbs and spices.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. boil the water and add the butter and salt
3. stir to dissolve salt and melt butter
4. place the rice in an 8" casserole dish
5. pour the boiling water mixture over the rice and stir
6. cover with foil and bake on the middle rack for 1 hour
7. fluff with fork and serve
8. this rice also refrigerates and reheats fairly well , but it's best freshly made
demonstrations.review: This technique works great!  I tried increasing the water and using my rice cooker and the bottom of the rice burned.  Anyway, so this technique works great.  Next time I will add broth and herbs and spices for flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boston market cornbread

found this recipe on the internet... it called for yellow cake mix, but the butter mix adds a great taste. tastes just like boston market! (when i made it, i used 12 muffins and 4 mini loafs)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f and mix all dry ingredients
2. add remaining ingredients and mix well
3. pour into greased cupcake pans or mini loaf pans
4. bake 30 minutes or until golden brown on top and a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out clean
5. allow to cool slightly in the pan
6. remove from pan and serve warm
demonstrations.review: I made this in a 9x13 lasagne pan.  Half the pan was gone after dinner.  My kids and my husband loved this recipe.  It is wonderfully soft and sweet.  A great addition to our meal.  Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey chili for people who hate ground turkey

i totally hated ground turkey until i tried this recipe. people don't even know ground turkey is in it; until you tell them;so don't.this chili is mild so any one can eat it.

1. over medium heat spray a large dutch oven with non stick cooking spray
2. saute ground turkey , green pepper , and onion until lightly browned and onion and pepper are soft
3. add the remaining ingredients plus the water and stir well
4. cook over medium heat for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a great basic starter recipe.  I added an extra can of tomato paste and about doubled the spices.  The title is exactly right, you can't even tell it's ground turkey.  We are just starting to use ground turkey in our house and I was thrilled to find that you couldn't tell what the protein was in this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lite or light pumpkin chocolate chip muffins

a lighter version of recipe #3564. i also usually add a tsp or 2 of vanilla.

1. mix first 5 ingredients together
2. separately , mix dry ingredients
3. blend the two mixtures together , fold in chips
4. generously fill 24 greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees f
6. for 16-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: These are wonderful muffins.  I made them for an after school snack today, and the boys loved them.  I used the 1 1/2 cup sugar and regular sized chocolate chips.  I added a dash or two of cloves and a few runs across the microplane with a fresh nutmeg.  I got 21 regular sized muffins from my silicone muffin pans using a large ice cream scoop.  We will definitely be adding these to the regular rotation!  Thank you so much for these wonderful fall treats.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
president roosevelt s birthday cake

a lovely chocolate cake recipe as published in our local paper.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and dust an 8 x 8 cakepan with cocoa
3. cream butter and add sugar a little at a time
4. cream well
5. add eggs
6. sift flour , salt , soda and cocoa together 3 times
7. add coffee to batter alternatively with flour mixture
8. then add vinegar and vanilla
9. bake at 350 degrees about 30 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I made this cake in a deep 9inch square baking dish.  It took a while longer to bake up, and then the center never really did get completely baked.  However, besides my screw up by using this baking dish, this cake is a great lil cake.  Great flavor, nice and dense.  I will use this recipe again and again for a standard chocolate cake.  Thanks so much for posting!

target.recipe_text:
old fashioned corn and potato chowder

this really is old fashioned! it comes from 

1. combine , in a large pot , all ingredients except milk and flour / water
2. cook until potatoes are fork tender
3. add milk and flour / water , stirring well
4. bring to a boil and allow to cook for 10 minutes
5. serve with chopped green onion and shredded cheese as a garnish
target.review: I'm giving this a four because I ate more than I normally would.  There was too much corn for me and last minute sub was dried minced onions.  But, the flavor is very good.  This one is going in my hardcopy cookbook.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato crust quiche

tasty quiche recipe, and a bit different than your usual one. you can jazz it up with some herbs if you like. easy and tasty, without all the hassle of rolling out a pastry crust.

1. mix oil and potatoes
2. press into a buttered 9 inch pie plate
3. bake in a 425f oven for 15 minutes
4. spread onion in crust , then sprinkle on cheese
5. top with ham slivers
6. beat together egg , milk and seasonings
7. pour over ham
8. bake at 350f for 30 minutes , or until a knife inserted near the centre comes out clean
9. serves 4
10. p
11. s
12. after you have grated the potatoes , squeeze as much water as you can out of them with your hands
13. this makes a drier mixture and you won't have a soggy crust
demonstrations.review: I don't know.  Maybe I thought the potato crust would be crunchy.  The filling had a good flavor, but with the potatoes, it needs alot of salt.  I use a salt sub.  Will work with this again and see what happens.  Oh, I used three eggs because they were very small.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green tomato relish  hot dog relish

i found this recipe in a canning book. it look easy, so i tried it. it tastes like the relish in the store. plus, you can use all those green tomatoes you look at and hate going to waste.

1. combine tomatoes , onion , and pepper in large bowl
2. sprinkle salt over vegetables , mix in , and let stand 1 hour
3. drain vegetables
4. combine drained vegetables , sugar , mustard , and celery salt in a large pot
5. tie cloves in cheesecloth and add to mixture
6. stir in vinegar and simmer for 20 minutes
7. take out spice bag
8. pack hot relish into hot jars
9. leave 1 / 4 inch headspace
10. place canning lids on jars
11. process half pints for 10 minutes in hot water bath
demonstrations.review:
Now this is the chow chow I remember! The jars are sealing as we speak. Taste testing along the way allows me to rate it now. When this is made again, I'll try brown suger or a mix of the two. But other than that, I wouldn't change a thing. This is almost my granny's. Also, this is such a basic recipe you could do anything with it. Thanks for posting!

UpDate: 9/4/07.  This is my kinda relish/chow chow.  I've given some to others that also craved this taste and they love it!  The brown sugar batch is good also.  My sister wants more, my DH's co-worker brought his jars back cuz he knew he would get some more!  Yum Yum!
Thanks!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato pie vi

note: this is the best sweet potato pie recipe that i  have found. tastes great!  

1. combine all ingredients in mixing bowl
2. mix well
3. pour into pie shells
4. bake at 350 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  Made two small pies last night for an office get together.  They went over very well and the ones that didn't even like sweet potatoes came looking for more!  Easy prep time, short cooking time, but to find the perfect pie crust....on to another quest!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flour frosting

a great light frosting that is less sweet than the traditional buttercream frostings.

1. in a small saucepan blend flour and milk
2. cook stirring constantly until mixture bubbles
3. cool
4. in a large bowl , cream shortening , butter and sugar with a mixer until fluffy
5. add vanilla and salt , blending well
6. on medium speed beat in cooled flour mixture in small portions , beating well after each addition
7. continue beating until light and fluffy
demonstrations.review:
If you want a super rich frosting, don't use this one.  But, if you are looking for something that won't overpower your cake or in my case, cinnamon rolls, this is the one.  It is quite fluffy, but it has started to separate after one hour. But I'm sure the rolls won't mind. :)  Still, I will use again.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s no knead yeast rolls

these are wonderful rolls, especially when you slather them with butter. even i can make these and i don't consider making bread as one of my specialities. my aunt and i compete at christmas dinner to see who can eat the most. i'm not revealing my record. :)

1. dissolve yeast in the lukewarm water
2. sift together flour , salt and sugar
3. cut in lard
4. add yeast and water
5. mix until well blended and keep mixing until dough forms elastic strands
6. place dough in a greased bowl
7. cover and allow to rise 30 minutes
8. place dough on a floured board , smooth gently with your hands and roll out to desired thickness
9. cut out
10. place rolls in a greased pan
11. cover and allow to rise in a warm place for 45 minutes
12. brush with butter and bake at 450 degrees for 15 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I never have been able to do the dough thing, but this one really worked.  I did do a little mixing with the hands, but all in all, the rolls are wonderful.  And I won't ask how many you eat at Christmas dinner. 
Thank you very much!

Melody

target.recipe_text:
coney island chili dog casserole

this is a variation on chili dogs made into a casserole that pleases kids and adults alike! simple and quick for you on-the-go chefs! this was inspired by a casserole my mother used to make for me when i was a kid. her version is quite different, although just as good!! the original coney island casserole recipe #180894

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. remove biscuits from package and lightly press into the bottom and slightly up the sides of a lightly greased 9 x 13-inch baking dish
3. place biscuits in oven and bake for 10 minutes
4. in bowl , combine chili , hot dogs , cheese and onion
5. remove biscuits from oven and top with chili mixture
6. return to oven and continue baking for an additional 12 to 15 minutes or until biscuits are golden brown and filling is hot
7. cut casserole into squares and serve immediately
target.review: I made this last night for the family. I used a can of grands flaky biscuits and large can of chili beans sans meat. Turned out great. Everyone enjoyed it. Served with roasted onions and carrots. A great quick meal! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot apple butter

this is just one of my comfort foods. i love it slathered on homemade biscuits. mmmmmmmm...so good.

1. place apples in a large bowl
2. combine sugar , cinnamon , cloves and salt
3. pour over apples and mix well
4. place in crock pot , cover and cook on high for 1 hour
5. decrease heat to low
6. cover and cook on low for 9-11 hours or until thickened and dark brown
7. stir occasionally
8. uncover and cook on low for 1 hour longer
9. if desired , whisk until smooth
10. spoon into freezer containers , leaving 1 / 2-inch head space
11. cover and freeze
demonstrations.review: One word: perfect! I made this with a load of apples we got from the neighbors (golden delicious). I have since used the butter for homemade pop-tarts, homemade "nutra-grain" bars, and even a delightful kringle danish. Thanks for helping me to put all those apples to good use!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rigatoni with cheese and italian sausage

delicious! if you like spicy food, try it with spicy italian sausage and spicy marinara sauce!

1. cook rigatoni until tender in large pot , drain pasta
2. meanwhile , preheat broiler
3. cook sausage in large heavy pot over medium high heat until no longer pink , stirring frequently and breaking up with back of a wooden spoon
4. add garlic and saute until soft , about 2 minutes
5. drain off excess oil and return pot to medium high heat
6. add marinara sauce and crushed red pepper , then pasta
7. season to taste with salt and pepper
8. divide pasta among four 1 1 / 4-cup custard cups , or double recipe and put in one large baking dish
9. sprinkle parmesan and mozzarella over
10. place in broiler until cheese melts and begins to brown , watching closely to prevent burning , about 1 1 / 2 minute
11. sprinkle with parsley and olive oil and serve
demonstrations.review: Great verastile basic recipe. We didn't have italian sausage on hand, so I just threw in some smoked sausage that I had sauteed with onions. I also omitted the red pepper because not everyone likes the heat. I threw a cup of chopped zucchini into the sauce for some extra veggie action. Baked for about 25 minutes. The family loved it! I will be making this again. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almost nutra grain bars

these are great to take to work, kids lunch boxes, for a potluck or a bake sale, you can slice them and stick them in the freezer then wrap tightly in foil, put a frozen wrapped bar into your kid's lunchboxes, they will thaw out by noon, they are just as good if not better than the store-bought! ---this also works well using blueberry or other flavors of jams, for easy spreading heat the jam in the microwave until softened :)

1. set oven to 375 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl combine cake mix , oatmeal , cinnamon and brown sugar
4. mix with a spatula or a large wooden spoon
5. in a small cup whisk egg with lemon juice and vanilla until combined
6. add to the crumb mixture along with 1 / 4 cup plus 2 tablespoons melted butter
7. using a large wooden spoon toss to combine then use your fingers to finish the mixing
8. mix until the mixture clumps together
9. sprinkle a litle more than half of the crumb mixture into the pan then spread out evenly pressing firmly to cover bottom
10. spoon the jam carefully over the crust in the pan and spread evenly
11. cover with remaining crumb mixture over top of the jam then gently pat the mixture down slightly
12. bake for 20 minutes
13. cool completely , or semi-freeze before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review: Wow! I made a batch of these today using homemade apple butter. I used a reduced sugar yellow cake mix. I also used a combo of old fashioned oats, quick oats, and a 5 grain blend for a little more texture. I used oil instead of the melted butter as well. They turned out wonderful--much better than any store bought bar. Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh blueberry cobbler

easy and too good for words.

1. add flour , 1 / 2 cup sugar , salt , and baking powder to a mixing bowl
2. stir to combine
3. add in milk and butter
4. stir to combine
5. spread batter into a greased 8-inch square baking pan
6. sprinkle blueberries evenly over batter
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 cup sugar and drizzle with vanilla
8. bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until a pick comes out clean
9. can serve plain or with ice cream on top
demonstrations.review: Yummy! I made just a few small changes. I melted the butter into the pan then poured the batter over that (just how I always make my cobblers). I also simmered the berries in the sugar/vanilla for a bit to bring out the juices. Then I just dumped them into the batter and into the oven for 40 minutes! Simply delicious! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake granola bars

snack bars.

1. in large bowl , combine cereal , rolled oats and raisins
2. set aside
3. in small saucepan , combine brown sugar and corn syrup
4. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
5. stir in peanut butter and vanilla
6. blend until smooth
7. pour over cereal mixture
8. mix well
9. press into ungreased 13"x 9" pan
10. cool
11. cut into 24 bars
demonstrations.review: A great recipe for quick, easy granola bars. I used 2-1/2 cups of puff wheat cereal instead of the crispy rice . I divided the dry ingredients into 2 bowls and added coconut to one bowl (some don't care for coconut). I had to add a bit of honey to the mix for some extra stickiness. I then pressed each half batch into 8X8 square pans. They turned out great! I cut and wrapped the coconut bars in wax paper to give to dad for a nice lunch treat at work. Thanks for a yummy, easy recipe! I'll definitely be making these again and again.

target.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
target.review: A great apple pie - I press the pecans into the topping and bake them in (covering with foil for the first bit of cooking so they don't burn) and drizzle a generous amount of caramel at the end of cooking.  The topping keeps everything moist inside and the caramel adds that extra flavour.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dreamy cappuccino dessert

my variation of a recipe i found on the kraft foods website.  also try with chocolate flavored pudding!  enjoy!

1. mix milk , coffee and dry pudding mix in a medium bowl with a wire whisk for 2 minutes or until blended
2. pour into individual dessert dishes and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or until ready to serve
3. fold cinnamon into whipped topping
4. top each serving with a dollop of cool whip and a sprinkle of coffee beans !
demonstrations.review: Very good - I used chocolate flavoured pudding. I improvised a bit - I stirred 1 cup of cool whip and a dash of cinnamon right into the pudding mixture to lighten the mixture up a bit.  I served the dessert in tea cups, with a dallop of cool whip on top and drizzled with chocolate syrup.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic roasted yams

i just found this recipe in a cooking magazine and can't wait to try it!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place balsamic vinegar and brown sugar in a large skillet and bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring until sugar dissolves
3. reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes or until the mixture thickens slightly
4. add butter and salt and stir until butter melts
5. add yams to the pan , stir to coat and season with black pepper
6. spread evenly on a rimmed cookie sheet
7. bake 40 minutes , or until yams are tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: This turned out so well, I will definitely make it again!  I used a baking dish instead of a cookie sheet so that it could cook in the sauce, and I could stir it while it was cooking and recoat the yams.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly.  Yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy corn medley

this salad goes great with any meal, especially barbeque. the recipe is from the july/august 2000 issue of quick cooking. make in advance-needs to chill.

1. in a large serving bowl , combine the first 8 ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine vinegar , sugar , oil , salt and pepper
3. whisk until sugar is dissolved
4. pour over corn mixture
5. mix well
6. cover and chill for at least 3 hours
7. stir just before serving
8. serve with a slotted spoon
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe - I think it's way better than the standard marinated bean recipe!  I couldn't stop sampling it as it was marinading! LOL  I omitted the water chestnuts as I don't like water chestnuts, reduced the amount of green onion, and increased the amount of celery.  Yum yum yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy italian chicken  crock pot recipe

easy to make, wonderful to eat!

1. place chicken breasts and mushrooms in crock pot
2. mix together the italian salad dressing mix and water
3. pour over chicken and cover crock pot
4. cook on low for 3 hours
5. meanwhile set out cream cheese-i like to cube it while it's cold
6. when 3 hours is up , remove chicken and mushrooms with a slotted spoon
7. whisk the cream cheese with the liquid in crock pot
8. when well incorporated , return chicken and mushrooms to crock pot and cover
9. cook for 1 1 / 2 hours on low
10. plate and shred fresh parmesan to taste
11. serve
demonstrations.review: This was so good - super rich and the sauce super creamy!  I made a couple of changes, only because these were the things I had in the cupboard: I used dried Herb dip mix instead of the italian seasoning, with a splash of worcestershire; low fat cream cheese; button mushrooms.  I think this recipe would be versatile using any dressing mix. I also used 6 chicken thighs.  Altogether, I cooked on high for 1 1/2 hours and low for another 3.  The chicken was very tender.  I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and peppers stir fry  with sweet and sour sauce

we call this "ham and peppers" but there's onion and pineapple too. this is a great quick meal and an excellent use for leftover ham. the recipe was originally from a doubleday cookbook but has evolved during the past 12 years to suit our taste--we like the ham and onions slightly browned and the peppers crisp/tender. serve over steamed rice and add soy sauce to taste. note that this dish is best just after it's thickened and it doesn't reheat that well, but there's rarely any leftovers.

1. prepare the sauce by first stirring cornstarch with about 2 or 3 tbs
2. of the chicken broth in a small bowl
3. when the cornstarch is dissolved and smooth , stir in the remaining sauce ingredients and set aside
4. brown ham in 1 / 3 of butter over moderately high heat in a skillet or wok until it begins to brown
5. remove and set the ham aside
6. melt another 1 / 3 of the butter in the skillet or wok and saut the onions
7. when they start to soften and turn translucent , add the peppers and the final 1 / 3 of the butter
8. when the onions have somewhat browned , add the ham and the pineapple , juice and all
9. stir the sauce until smooth again and pour into skillet or wok
10. increase heat and stir until the sauce begins to bubble
11. reduce heat and stir for a minute or two until the cornstarch is fully cooked
12. if too thick , thin with a little water or broth
13. serve over steamed rice as soon as possible
14. i like to sprinkle some dried hot red pepper flakes over it
15. i love hot food and this gives the dish some zing !
demonstrations.review: I really liked this recipe, although my husband hated it (what does he know)! It makes a really nice thick sauce, good over rice too.  Next time I might reduce the amount of vinegar to 1/4 cup (my own personal taste), and cook the green peppers the same amount of time as the onions, as they were a little too crispy for me.  This was really satisfying and filling though, a good way to use up leftovers.

target.recipe_text:
herb crusted roast beef

nan

1. put the roast with the fat side up , in an ungreased roasting pan
2. mix together the cloves , mustard , lemon juice , oil , and worcestershire sauce
3. stir to mix well
4. pour over and evenly coat the roast
5. in a bowl , add the next 6 ingredients
6. mixing well
7. rub herb mixture over roast
8. bake roast , uncovered , at 325 degrees for 1 3 / 4 to 2 1 / 4 hours or until desired degree of doneness
9. remove from oven and place roast on a warm serving platter
10. let stand for 10-15 minutes
11. add 2 cups water and bouillon granules to pan drippings
12. bring mixture to a boil
13. mix together flour and 1 / 3 cup of water
14. stirring until smooth
15. gradually add to pan
16. cook until bubbly and thickened , stirring constantly
17. slice roast and serve with gravy
target.review: This roast was delicious.  I had two smaller rump roasts in the freezer, so I cooked both together in my large LeCreuset roasting pan.  There was plenty of both the marinad and the rub to cover both roasts.  I have a convection oven, so I roasted at 325 but they were done in an hour and a half.  Actually, I sort of blew it on temperature.  I am so paranoid of underdoing my roasts (as I've had problems with this in the past) and I should have taken it out sooner, so it was not quite as pink as we like our meat by the time I let it rest and then sliced it.  Nevertheless, it was moist and tender.  The gravy was wonderul!  I thought about adjusting the amount of lemon based on one of the previous reviews, but I didn't and we liked it just fine.  Thanks for a great new roast recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon basil shrimp

this is good done on the barbeque and can also be cooked using the grill. if you like basil you will like these prawns serve with some nice crusty bread. makes enough marinade for more then 12 prawns. marinating time not included.

1. place all the ingredients , except the prawns , in a shallow dish and mix well , taste or you want to add more mustard
2. add the prawns and toss to coat , cover , refrigerate for 1 hour
3. remove the prawns from the marinade and thread on skewers
4. cook over medium coals for 2-3 minutes on each side , basting with any remaining marinade from time to time
5. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this delicious shrimp last night.  I had seen the recipe on a thread about lemon recipes, and when I got to the market and found jumbo prawns on sale, I figured this was the day!  I got 31 shrimp from a 2 lb. bag of unpeeled "colosol" prawns.  I followed the directions as written, and they were moist and flavorful - and gone!  No leftovers here for the five of us.  The fresh basil is a must here in my opinion.  Thanks for a great treat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: We had these wonderful eggs for Easter day appetizers, and really enjoyed them.  I especially liked the dill flavoring that came through, as I'm not much of a sweet pickle fan as you often see in a traditional deviled egg recipe.  Thanks, Kitten.  These will definately be making a repeat showing at our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: This is a new family favorite!  I made it the first time at Thanksgiving and all the apple pie eaters raved.  No leftovers!  Made it again at Christmas and then DH requested it for his birthday 2/21.  I am really not much of a pie maker - I consider the weak point of my cooking skills - so to have a pie I made requested for a birthday dessert is a major kudo!  I used Granny Smiths and didn't put on the pecans since we aren't nut eaters.  This pie is very sweet and rich.  When I saw the caramel amount (1/4c) I thought it seemed like it wouldn't be enough, but a little really goes a long way and it covered well.  Thanks for a terrific recipe!  Steph

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s lemon cream cheese pie

a pie so good it is worthy of selling in a bakery!  prep time includes the refrigeration time --- see my recipe#66929

1. in a saucepan , combine sugar , cornstarch and pinch of salt
2. stir in water , lemon juice , lemon rind and yellow food colouring bring to a boil over medium-high heat
3. cook , and stir for 2 minutes , or until smooth and thickened
4. remove from heat
5. stir in butter
6. cool to room temperature for about 1 hour
7. meanwhile , in a mixing bowl , beat the cream cheese and the powdered sugar until smooth
8. fold in the whipped cream and the 1 tbsp lemon juice
9. remove 1 / 2 cup of the whipped cream / lemon mixture for the garnish
10. spread the remaining cream cheese mixture into the baked pastry shell
11. top with the cooled lemon filling
12. chill in the fridge for a minimum of 8 hours or overnight
13. when ready to serve , scoop the reserved 1 / 2 cup cream cheese mixture into a pastry bag with a star
14. pipe stars onto the pie , or garnish with the reserved cream cheese mixture or as desired
15. refrigerate until ready to serve-- delicious !
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic pie!  I made it for Easter dinner, and everyone raved.  I did have to cook the filling a few minutes longer than the directions stated, but I think this is because I've never made a cream pie from scratch before, and didn't know what the filling would look like when it was to the correct stage.  I Zaarmailed Kittencal and she and was very helpful.  I just needed to cook it a little longer, and it suddenly thickened up and cleared.  After that it was a breeze.  It has a very zippy lemon flavor, so will really please a true lemon lover like me!  I made it with a shortbread crust, but am going to try it with a traditional crust next time, as I found this particular crust to be a little "thick" for the pie.  Thanks Kitten for the terrific recipe and your help when I was fumbling my way through it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: Another 5 star review for this outstanding recipe!  We loved it.  I doubled it since I was feeding three people and my DD ate the leftovers the next day for lunch (there weren't many).  I did cut the red pepper because I have one kid who is picky about hot food.  Otherwise I followed the recipe word for word.  I have already promised my DS who is away at college that I will make it for him the next time he comes home.  Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
sugar pecans

these make good munchies and was received from a dear coworker back in louisiana.

1. mix the egg white , brown sugar and vanilla together
2. fold in whole pecans
3. place on greased cookie sheet and bake at 250 degrees for 30 minutes
4. store in an air tight container
target.review: Tasted good, but not the best looking...still tasted great on a salad with pears and feta.  I doubled the recipe and put on very large baking sheet, but did not increase time.  Nuts were not as crunchy as I hoped, but still good.  Next time, I will increase cooking time slightly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s slow cooker vegetarian chili

this is a rich, satisfying meal that freezes well. great on a cold winter day. serve it with tortillas, cornbread, french breadand/or rice! enjoy!

1. in a saucepan , saute the onion , bell pepper , zucchini , and celery for about 5 minutes
2. in a slow cooker , combine black bean soup , kidney beans , garbanzo beans , baked beans , tomatoes , corn , onion , bell pepper , zucchini , jalapeno , chilies , and celery
3. season with garlic , chili powder , cumin , parsley , oregano , basil
4. cook for about 6 hours on low
5. serve with tortillas , cornbread , rice , or french bread
6. enjoy !
7. this freezes well !
8. leftovers are good on top of nachos !
demonstrations.review: Loved this recipe--so filling and satisfying!  Great over corn bread/muffins.  I used plain black beans because I didn't have soup on hand and fresh chili peppers.   Carnivorous husband liked it, but didn't love it enough to eat leftovers (which there were a lot of!) so I had many frozen lunches to take to work--still just  as good as the first round!  Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean chef s vanilla buttermilk cupcakes

i adopted this recipe, which was originally submitted by mean chef. mean's original comment: "from sunset magazine"

1. beat butter and all the sugar on medium speed until well blended
2. add eggs and vanilla and beat on high speed until well blended
3. sift together flour , baking powder , and salt
4. with mixer on low speed , add one third of the flour mixture , followed by a third of the buttermilk repeat , alternating in thirds
5. when all the flour is incorporated beat mixture on medium speed just until well blended
6. fill paper-lined or buttered muffin cups about three-fourths full with batter
7. bake in a 350 oven until tops spring back when lightly touched in the center , 20 to 25 minutes
8. cool on racks 5 minutes
9. remove from pans
10. cool completely
11. decorate with your favorite frosting
demonstrations.review: Flavor was very good.  I added a tad extra baking powder and buttermilk after reading other reviews saying cupcakes were too dense and crumbly.  Even with these changes, I still found them fairly dense and crumbly...I only cooked mine for 20 minutes and they were more than done--15-18 minutes may have been better.  Overall an okay recipe considering how easy they were, but I probably would not make these again with all the other recipes out there to try.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almond roca  english toffee

a delectable confection from the kitchen of june oaks, wife of brigham young university president dallin oaks.  this was surprisingly easy to make and an absolutely delicious addition to my goodie plates for christmas.

1. spread almonds evenly on a buttered 12 x 17-inch jelly roll pan
2. mix sugar , butter and water in a large saucepan
3. cook over high heat until tan
4. it needs to be past the point where the mixture begins to turn tan
5. it will be a foamy , thick , medium tan
6. be sure to stir constantly with a wooden spoon
7. pour over sliced almonds and spread as much as possible
8. sprinkle chocolate pieces over immediately
9. let melt a minute or two and then spread evenly with knife
10. when completely cool and chocolate is solid , break into pieces
demonstrations.review: So easy and SPECTACULAR!  This recipe makes a lot, but that is a good thing because a bag/box of this makes a great gift for everyone and anyone.  I used milk chocolate on the first batch and spread some sliced almonds on top--very tasty! On the next batch I used semi sweet chocolate chips because that's all I had--this was good, too, but not as good as the milk chocolate. Next time I will try dark chocolate.  I brought the temperature up to exactly 295 and it was perfect.  Thanks Sharlene W.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced zucchini muffins

these are good for you muffins that are great as a coffee companion in the morning.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. grease and paper muffin tins
3. mix the eggs , oil , sugar , sour cream , and zucchini together in a large bowl
4. do not overmix
5. add the two flours , baking powder , baking soda , salt , cinnamon , nutmeg , cloves , fruit and walnuts , if using
6. do not overmix , but make sure that all the batter is mixed together
7. pour into muffins tins and bake approximately 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yummmm!  Even though I made a few changes to make these even healthier, they tasted wonderful.
