I used 1 cup egg whites, subbed apple sauce for almost all of the oil, used 1 cup whole wheat flour, 1/2 cup white flour and 1/2 cup oat bran, subbed nonfat plain yogurt for the sour cream, and reduced the sugar to about 2/3 cup.  Even with all of these changes, the muffins were wonderfully moist and delicious!  I will definitely be making these again!  Thanks for a great base recipe Tish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fabulous zucchini bread

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. cream together eggs , oil and applesauce
3. add sugar and vanilla
4. add dry ingredients and mix well
5. stir in zucchini
6. grease and flour loaf pans
7. large loaf pans bake for 50 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
8. small loaf pans bake approx
9. 25-30 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
10. remove from oven to cooling racks and let cool until slightly warm before removing
11. because this is a moist bread it freezes very well
demonstrations.review: Very flavorful and yummy!  I followed the recipe exactly and it was fabulous.  Next time, I will use more whole wheat flour and less white and a little less sugar--just for health reasons, but otherwise LOVED IT!

target.recipe_text:
chinese sesame limas

good hot, cold, room temperature.  these do not taste like lima beans.  they are from my favorite chinese cookbook, the key to chinese cooking, by irene kuo, copyright 1977.  i have made nothing from the cookbook that isn't entirely wonderful.

1. remove limas from package and let defrost a little and separate them with your fingers
2. heat a skillet over high heat until hot
3. add the peanut oil , swirl , heat for 30 seconds
4. scatter in the beans
5. stir-fry briskly for 30 seconds until the color turns icy green
6. sprinkle in the salt and sugar and stir rapidly for another 30 seconds to season them evenly
7. add the stock or water , even out the beans , turn heat to medium-low to maintain a strong simmer
8. cover and simmer for about 5 minutes
9. uncover , turn heat high and stir rapidly until the remaining liquid has evaporated
10. add the sesame oil , stir to distribute evenly and pour into serving dish
target.review: These were outstanding! Like many people, I don't like limas at all, but I trusted the description for this recipe. The unusual blend of salty, sweet and sesame appealed to me, as well as the ease of the recipe. The limas had a creamy "comfort food" rexture, almost like potatoes, and we slightly preferred them hot. For dinner with friends, I prepared 2 recipes ahead, following the recipes exactly, and nibbling all the while:-) The 4 of us started with them as appetizers (on tooth picks tee-hee) and finished them off as a side dish. So, you see, we ate 2 whole recipes - in addition to chicken, rice, vegtable and bread! Everyone wanted to keep eating them, and we all agreed they were fantastic. So, thanks, BarbryT! I will surely make these more at home - because they are sooo easy, and for gatherings - where they will impress people because they are addictively delicious and uncommon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ciocia s thai butternut coconut bisque

a delicious soup i invented from leftovers and a few additions.  it's very forgiving to feel free to use a squirt of lemon for lime juice, use a different herb, try ginger for lemongrass, etc. also, i used small handfuls, etc. and have estimated some ingredients.

1. preheat slow-cooker for 20 minutes on high
2. add onions to pot or carmelise onions in a frying pan
3. if carmelised , add later with stock
4. add butter and oil to slow-cooker
5. chop shallots
6. add to oil along with salt and pepper and thyme
7. allow to cook until translucent
8. add roasted butternut squash , broken into several pieces , stock and fresh lime juice
9. cook all day or overnight on low setting
10. remove lemongrass
11. add coconut milk and blend thoroughly with immersion blender or blend in batches in a countertop blender
12. serve hot with additional freshly ground black pepper , as desired
13. freshly chopped coriander leaves would be a nice touch and taste !
demonstrations.review:
Ten stars!  Truly outstanding recipe!  All eight grown-ups agreed, and even the 4 kids had seconds :-)  

I made this pretty much as stated, except:  I omitted the salt, as I was using a chicken base, I used dried thyme, my squash 1/2 was large, I used 3/4 the amount of coconut milk, and only 1/2 the black pepper.  The amount of pepper in the recipe would be extremely spicy.  Using 1/2 was still a bit spicy, but the kids ate it up, so use your own judgement.  

Two more things - Since I don't have a slow-cooker, I carmelized the onions and shallots until golden, then added everything through the stock, and "barely simmered" it on my stove for a few hours.  Also, since I was taking it away on a group vacation, I cooked it through step 7, pureed it and froze it.  When it was time to eat it, I defrosted it, at which point it had a "seperated" look that had me worried.  But after I heated it and added the coconut milk, it was fine.  The cilantro was a terrific garnish.  

I am so glad to have this recipe!  It is different, but not at all strange.  Of course, this is a fitting beginning to a Thai meal, but I would not hesitate to serve it at Thanksgiving (when you should probably watch the pepper) or any other time.  Especially when you want raves ;-)  Thanks again for this fabulous recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet ziti with chicken   broccoli

the sauce is amazing, all the girls in my office have cooked this recipe and we all agree it is by far one of our favorites! this recipe puts a full meal on the table using only one pan and 30 minutes of your time.  america's test kitchen cookbook.

1. season chicken with salt and pepper
2. melt 1 tbs butter in 12-inch skillet over medium heat
3. add chicken and cook until it is lightly browned but not fully cooked , about 4 minutes
4. transfer chicken to a bowl
5. add 1 more tbs butter , onion , red pepper flakes , oregano , & 1 / 2 tsp salt to the skillet
6. cook until the onion is softened , about 5 minutes
7. stir in the garlic and cook until fragrant , about 15 seconds
8. sprinkle the ziti evenly into the skillet
9. pour the broth and milk over the ziti
10. cover and bring to a simmer about 5-10 minutes or till al dente
11. reduce heat to medium low and stir in the broccoli and roasted red peppers
12. cover and continue to simmer , stirring occasionally , until the past begins to soften and the broccoli turns bright green , about 8 minutes
13. stir in the chicken and any accumulated juice
14. cover and continue to simmer until the chicken is cooked through , about 3 minutes longer
15. stir in the remaining 1 tbs butter , parmesan , and lemon juice
16. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Mmmm!  Tastes like I made restaurant food!  Besides being quite tasty, it was quick and easy - I love the idea of cooking pasta in the pan instead of boiling it in a pot of water.  Plus, the pasta takes on flavor that way.  I had cooked chicken from recipe #33104 (highly recommended, btw) and had asparagus on hand, which I steamed seperately and added in.  I used whole wheat pasta spirals, probably more than 2 1/2 cups, so I simply "barely covered" them with the milk and broth, stirred it a few times while cooking, and it came out perfect.  I omitted the peppers (personal preference.)  However, I feel like the lemon juice is what really made the dish stand out, so I highly recommend it.  Also, I added extra cheese, but it tasted better before I did that;do go easy there!  So, go make this already; everyone will love it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
clay pot chicken with garlic carrots and potatoes

this is our family’s favorite recipe. i created this recipe when i purchased my first clay pot. chicken will be very moist and tender; potatoes are done in the same pot. what more could you want? easy, delicious and great looking dish. i promise, that even your pickiest eaters will be asking for seconds.

1. soak clay pot for 15 min
2. rub chicken with garlic , salt , pepper , caraway seeds , parsley , italian dressing and marinate overnight you can rub your chicken and bake it right away , but it will taste much better , if marinated
3. in a clay pot , add potatoes , carrots and chicken on top
4. place your clay pot in the cold oven and roast at 430f for 1
5. 5 hours
demonstrations.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this, as did my husband, kids, and 2 guests!  It was very easy, and had a great flavor.  I surely will be making this again.  Some notes:  The caraway, which is optional, is what really made the dish delicious and a bit different.  I used chicken leg quarters, which I cut, removing whatever fat I could.  For ease, I used my food processor to chop the garlic and parsley, then added the Italian dressing, 1 t. salt and some pepper.  Marinated in a freezer bag overnight.  I cut the carrots into chunks and used lots more - they were the first to go, so I do recommend lots if your family eats them.   I added 3 small onions to my clay pot, and next time, I think I'll also add some cut up cabbage.  Also, the chicken will make its own juice in the pot.  After cooking, I put the chicken in a pan under the broiler for a couple of minutes to further brown/crisp it, removed the veggies to a serving dish, and defatted the chicken liquid to serve alongside.  Yum!  Thanks again, Angela, for a winning recipe.  This was one of my choices for Pick-a-Chef, and now I'm sure glad I played!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hearty beef and barley soup with root vegetables

nan

1. heat 1 tablespoon oil over moderate heat in a large pot
2. add the steak and brown well , stirring occasionally
3. remove steak and leave the juice
4. add the remaining teaspoon of oil , onion , bay leaf and caraway seeds
5. cook for about 4 more minutes
6. add the carrots , parsnips , turnip , rutabaga , barley , and thyme
7. stirring constantly , cook for about 5 minutes
8. stir in bouillon , water , tomato paste , salt , and pepper
9. bring to a boil over high heat
10. immediately reduce heat and simmer for 20 minutes
11. discard bay leaf , stir in the spinach and serve
demonstrations.review: The family really loved this soup; even both kids had seconds.  A tasty comfort food!  I would especially recommend it if you want your family to eat some different vegtables than the usual, or if you really like root veggies, as they definitely give the soup a different flavor.  I followed the recipe pretty closely, using sirloin tips.  Since the recipe didn't say, I added them with the barley.  They turned out very tender.  For the veggies, I mostly "pulsed" in my food processor, so they were pretty small, and that worked well - easy plus made a great texture.  Lots of flavor, but wasn't like biting into pieces of vegtables.  I did need to simmer the soup closer to 50 minutes.  I made the soup in the afternoon, and we ate it for dinner, but in my haste to eat it, I forgot to add the spinach.  We'll do that with the leftovers.  Anyway, the soup got better as it sat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory rugelach

found this in a 1997 southern living "home for the holidays" publication.  looks like a keeper.  chilling time required.  may be frozen unbaked for up to 1 week.

1. in a food processor , pulse flour , butter , cream cheese , and 1 / 2 teaspoon salt until dough leaves sides of bowl
2. divide dough into 8 equal portions
3. wrap separately , and chill at least 1 hour
4. meanwhile , prepare the pesto by baking the pine nuts in a shallow baking pan at 350f , 5 minutes or until toasted , stirring occasionally
5. pulse pine nuts , basil leaves , parmesan cheese , garlic , and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt in a food processor until smooth , stopping once to scrape down sides
6. pour oil through food chute with processor running , and process until blended
7. refrigerate until ready to use
8. on a lightly floured surface , roll one dough portion at a time into an 8-inch circle
9. spread each circle with 3 tablespoons pesto filling , leaving a 2-inch circle of uncovered dough in the center
10. cut each into 8 wedges and roll up wedges , starting at wide end
11. place , point side down , on a lightly greased baking sheets
12. may be frozen at this point for up to one week
13. bake at 350f for 15-20 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I have chosen to give 5 stars, based mostly on the delicious taste, and partly on the wonderful concept of savory rugelach! My mind is chock full of ideas for other fillings for this dough! However, I must tell you that I did not follow the recipe exactly. First off, I used already prepared pesto, instead of the recipe's. This was a big timesaver for me, since I didn't have to go to the store. Secondly, I didn't have quite enough cream cheese, so I subbed some sour cream. And thirdly, I subbed 1 cup of whole wheat flour for white. On balance, I thought all my subs were quite successful, but I also felt that the recipe, as written, would also generate 5-star taste. I did find the rolling, filling, and shaping to be a long process. Next time, I may use the same recipe, but shape it into a rectangle, fill, roll and slice. Another cooking note - I forgot to lightly grease my cooking sheets, but that was fine, because when baking, they expelled a LOT of oil, until they were practically swimming in it. It didn't affect the results in any negative manner. I am still not sure if I ended up with too much fat in my dough, or if it was from my pesto, which was a little loose. But, they were very delicious, esp. when warm! Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
spicy carrot and zucchini bhaji

posted for the asian forums eat your veggies december 2008/january 2009.  taken from the australian womens weekly new asian cookbook.

1. whisk besan , salt and the water in medium bowl until mixture forms a smooth thick batter
2. stir in spices , garlic , onion , carrot , zucchini and coriander
3. heat oil in wok , deep fry tablespoons of mixture , in batches , until vegetables are tender and bhaji are browned lightly
4. drain on paper towel
5. serve with mango chutney
target.review: Really loved these. No doubt they can be tweaked according to taste and I am looking forward to making more in the future. I found they were still a bit undercooked in the middle after I fried them but I finished them off in the oven and they were great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan bread salad

great way to use up stale bread! i have made this with and without the herbs and olives and both ways are good, just the one without is a bit simpler. maybe more of an appetiser than a main course.

1. preheat the oven to 220c or 425f
2. put the peppers into char
3. meanwhile , break up the bread into bite-sized pieces and place on a roasting tray
4. put in the oven for 10 minutes until lightly toasted
5. peel and tear the charred peppers into strips and make the dressing
6. in a bowl , mix the garlic with the cumin , vinegar , tomato juice , salt and black pepper
7. add the olive oil and whisk well
8. season to taste
9. when the bread is ready , transfer to a large salad bowl and pour over half the dressing
10. toss and let sit for a few seconds , before adding the peppers , tomatoes , herbs and olives
11. pour on the remaining dressing , toss again and check the seasoning
12. serve with a bit of extra olive oil drizzled on top , if you like
demonstrations.review: I have made this salad a couple of times and loved it each time. I have added shredded carrot as well as seeded sliced cucumber and celery. The toasted crushed cumin seeds and fresh herbs make this salad something special. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
aaloo fry  spicy  fried potatoes

this is an excellent side to many indian dishes but this is the best served with dhal curry. try it with my meat dhal curry.

1. after washing potatoes , add spices
2. toss potatoes in spices until well coated
3. heat oil in saucepan
4. when oil medium hot , add salt to potatoes and fry in batches until potatoes develop a crisp outer layer to it but soft inside
5. drain and serve hot with dhal
demonstrations.review: I made these to go with the Dhal Curry With Meat (Gosht Dhal) they were full of flavour but not overpowering in the amount of spices. Easy and quick to make!  I will definitely cook them again. Made for spring PAC 2014

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrabba s sausage and lentil soup

i've gone to carrabas many times just for this soup. a lady from my supper club happened to bring this in for our soup theme and it tasted exactly like carrabas! i've substituted italian turkey many times and you would never notice the difference. you might also want to sprinkle some fresh basil and parmesan cheese on top. its good with a crusty piece of bread!

1. brown sausage
2. drain off fat
3. in a large pot combine all ingredients bring to boil
4. reduce heat , cover
5. simmer for about 1 hour or until lentils are tender
6. add water if necessary , for desired consistency
7. i like to puree about 1 cup of the soup and add back to pot to give it a thicker consistency
8. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: Had to substitute haricot beans and red lentils for the brown lentils and eggplant for the zucchini so my soup was different to the one in the recipe. Nevertheless we loved it - added the red wine vinegar to our individual bowls. The vinegar adds another dimension of flavour. I'll definitely make this again - as stated in the recipe this time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portuguese custard cupcakes

this is a different take on the traditional portuguese custard cupcake.

1. preheat the oven to 300f grease cupcake tins with butter
2. beat the eggs until lemon coloured
3. add the sugar and butter and continue to beat until thick , then add the lemon rind
4. pour warm milk into egg mixture while continuing to beat
5. once blended , fold in the flour until well mixed
6. fill the tins half way up and bake for approximately 1 hour , or until a tester inserted comes out clean
7. cool in pans on a rack
8. cupcakes will sink during the cooling process
demonstrations.review: Yum! These little cakes were sweet silky and delicious - and they were so easy to make. The flour in the mix forms a light crust at the base and the centres are lovely and "custardy". We loved them - made for spring PAC 2014

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boiled date cake

a very simple cake, with very few ingredients, and quick clean up. just my sort of baking. it's not too sweet either.

1. combine butter , milk , sugar , dates and spices in a pan , stir over heat until butter is melted , bring to boil , remove from heat , stir in soda , stand 5 minutes
2. stir in lightly beaten eggs and sifted flour in two lots , mix well
3. pour mixture into a well greased 20cm ring tin , bake in a moderate oven for 40 minutes
4. turn onto a wire rack to cool
5. serve buttered
demonstrations.review: This cake has everything a basic cake should have. It is moist(we didn't need to butter the slices), not too sweet or rich and it is so very easy to make! We loved it and will definitely make again. Thanks Jan.

target.recipe_text:
turnip puff

this dish can be done ahead of time and any leftovers can be frozen. try this instead of the usual carrots and turnip for a holiday vegetable.

1. cook turnip until tender , drain and mash
2. add butter and eggs and beat well
3. combine flour , sugar , baking powder , seasoning and nutmeg
4. stir into turnip mixture
5. pour into a buttered casserole dish
6. mix breadcrumbs and butter and sprinkle on top
7. bake at 375 for 25 minutes or until light brown on top
target.review: Absolutely delicious!  My fiancee, who hates turnips, ate this after I told him it was mashed potatos.  I probably could have let him go on thinking it was potato, but I rarely miss an opportunity to say "Told you so."  Even after I told him, he finished off his helping, as did our 2.5 year old daughter.  Definitely a winner!  I used butter and egg substitutes to make it almost fat free and it was still great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp frittata

nan

1. in a medium bowl , add eggs and milk
2. whisk mixture until light and frothy
3. set aside
4. pour oil into a 10 inch nonstick skillet over medium heat
5. add the scallions and saute for 1 minute or just until they are soft
6. add the shrimp , thyme , parsley , oregano , salt , and pepper to the skillet
7. saute , stirring frequently , for about 2 minutes or until the shrimp are pink and firm
8. turn heat to low
9. pour in the egg mixture
10. make sure the shrimp and onions are evenly distributed
11. cover the skillet and cook without disturbing for about 8 minutes or until the eggs are set
12. cut the frittata in half and transfer to individual serving plate
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good, but it mostly just tastes like shrimp and eggs.  The spice and scallion flavor doesn't come through much.  I think it would be better with a butter or hollondaise sauce or something to give it a little more flavor.  Not bad and SO fast that I'll try it again with some changes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chamorro cucumber slices

from the southern pacific island of guam where we lived for 4 years! these were a favorite at our church potluck suppers and picnics with barbequed chicken and ribs! very refreshing in hot and humid weather! (the name "chamorro" comes from the native people of guam...very warm, and friendly people...)

1. pare the cucumbers and leave narrow strips of skin for color
2. slice into 1 / 4-inch slices
3. in a zip-lock plastic bag , combine onions , pepper , soy sauce , lemon juice , and water
4. add cucumber slices
5. seal bag securely
6. turn bag over and over to coat cucumbers
7. place bag in refrigerate for at least 15 minutes
8. a longer time will enhance flavor
9. serve in bowl
demonstrations.review: This was a really nice change of pace from "regular" cucumber salad!  I wasn't sure how I was going to like the soy sauce, but I gave it a shot.  I nearly threw the whole batch out when I first made it because it was so overpowering, but decided to let it marinate as per the recipe.  The key is really letting the cucumbers release their juice to mild down the flavor.  I made it about 12 hours in advance and it was so perfect!  I'll definitely make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli  ham and cheese manicotti

what an interesting change from tradtional manicotti! you'll love the creamy texture of the cheese sauce! note: if you slightly undercook the manicotti they will be easier to stuff.

1. saute onions until tender
2. add ham , broccoli , cheddar cheese , and mayo , when cheese is melted , remove from heat and cool slightly
3. stuff manicotti with ham mixture , dividing between shells evenly , and place in a greased 9x13 inch pan
4. melt butter in saucepan
5. add flour and cook 1 minute
6. add milk and cook , stirring constantly until thickened
7. remove from heat and add swiss cheese , stirring until smooth
8. pour sauce over manicotti
9. bake at 375 degrees for 30 minutes or until sauce bubbles
10. perfect supper with a crisp salad and garlic bread !
demonstrations.review: I thought this was a really great dish!  Instead of being spiced up, it's just simple ingredients that go great together!  It doesn't take as long to prepare as I thought, but I may toss it all with rotini next time like a casserole to make it even faster.  My box of manicotti had 14, so I just made them all instead of having 4 leftover.  I had enough mixture to loosely fill them all, but I could have used more cheese sauce.  It's not fine cuisine, but it's a great family dish and very kid-friendly!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian chopped salad in shells

i just found this on recipegoldmine.com. haven't made this yet, but they sound like an incredible appetizer for a cookout or picnic. prep time includes 2 hour chilling time.

1. cook pasta shells as directed on the package
2. drain and cool
3. place remaining ingredients except vinaigrette in a medium bowl
4. pour vinaigrette over the salad , toss to coat
5. stuff the shells with the salad
6. cover and refrigerate 2 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: I probably shouldn't rate this because I didn't follow the recipe exactly.  I had some vegetarians coming to my party, so I skipped the meats and added some walnuts and pecans.  It was still excellent and a terrific idea to get some salad into a finger foods menu!  Really a great idea!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato basil pork chops

these italian style pork chops are moist, tender, and delicious. serve with a tossed salad and garlic bread for an impressive dinner that you're sure to enjoy!

1. in large skillet or dutch oven , melt butter
2. add garlic and saute for 1 minute
3. brown pork chops on both sides , then add tomatoes , basil , salt , and pepper
4. cover and cook over low-medium heat until pork chops are cooked through and tender
5. remove pork chops from pan and keep warm
6. in small bowl , combine water and cornstarch , then pour into hot cooking liquid
7. add onions and green peppers , cooking over medium-high heat for 5-6 minutes , or until vegetables are crisp-tender
8. place pork chops on serving platter or dinner plates and pour sauce over the top , garnishing with fresh basil if desired , and serve
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  The sauce has such a nice flavor to it- like homemade spaghetti sauce. In fact, I only had 4 chops, but I kept the sauce measurements as written and used the rest the next day over pasta.  This one is a keeper!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
sausage and pepper baked ziti

found in quick & simple magazine. the total cost of this dish is under $1.00 per serving.

1. in a deep nonstick 12" skillet , cook sausage over medium-high heat , stirring occasionally , until browned on all sides , about 5 minute
2. reduce heat to medium
3. discard all but 2 t sausage fat
4. add garlic , pepper and onion to sausage in skillet
5. cook , covered , stirring occasionally , until vegetables are tender , 10 minute stir in whole tomatoes , tomato puree and salt
6. bring to a boil over medium heat , breaking up tomatoes with side of spoon
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover and simmer 10 minute
9. meanwhile preheat oven to 400 degrees f
10. in a large pot of boiling salted water , cook pasta 2 min less than cooking time recommended on label
11. drain pasta and return to pot
12. stir in sausage mixture to coat
13. add mozzarella and toss to combine
14. transfer pasta mixture to an ungreased 9x13" baking dish and spread it out evenly
15. sprinkle with grated cheese
16. bake , uncovered , until top browns and sauce is bubbling , 20 to 25 minute let stand 10 min before serving
target.review: This was a very tasty, simple recipe. I made some subtle changes - small green pepper and added a small red bell pepper, and used minced bottled garlic instead of sliced fresh. I also used a small amount of red wine to deglaze the pan after I cooked the sausage. The kids ate it up - minus the peppers - and the adults kept going for more. I'll definitely keep this one around ! Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
can do chicken and biscuits

i call this recipe "can-do", because if i can do it, anyone can!

1. combine the first six ingredients in a small skillet
2. cook for 10-15 minutes on medium heat , stirring occasionally
3. make the biscuits
4. when the biscuits are done , split them in 1 / 2
5. spoon chicken mixture on the biscuits
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! I was concerned that the soup mixture wouldn't be enough for the chicken and veggies but it was perfect. The husband said it was very good, and that doesn't happen very often. Thanks for posting. This one is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic potato salad

nan

1. in large bowl combine mayonnaise , vinegar , salt , sugar and pepper
2. add potatoes , celery , onion and eggs
3. toss to coat well
4. cover
5. chill to blend flavors
demonstrations.review: This will be my go-to potato salad recipe ! It went together painlessly, and got rave reviews from everyone at dinner last night. I made a couple of minor substitutions - used onion powder instead of chopped onion (DH doesn't like texture) and added garlic powder and bacon. I couldn't keep my fingers out of it while it was warm, and it only got better after it had been chilled in the fridge. Thanks for posting - this one's definitely a keeper !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
campbell s slow cooked pulled pork

easy pulled pork recipe from campbell's kitchen.

1. heat the oil in a 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat
2. add the pork and cook until its well browned on all sides
3. stir the soup , ketchup , vinegar and brown sugar in a 5-quart slow cooker
4. add the pork and turn to coat
5. cover and cook on low for 8 to 9 hours or until the pork is fork-tender
6. remove the pork from the cooker to a cutting board and let stand for 10 minutes
7. using 2 forks , shred the pork
8. return the pork to the cooker
9. divide the pork and sauce mixture among the rolls
10. can also be cooked on high for 4 to 5 hours
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious. It doesn't get better than this. I had a picnic roast that I had to use before it went bad, and was looking for something that I potentially had all ingredients for. This fit the bill perfectly. It's also versatile enough to use the meat in tacos, or just eat by itself if you're in a rush. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed bell peppers picadillo

a different type of stuffed pepper with a spicy/sweet combination of ingredients. looks like i found the recipe in an article on budget-friendly meals. pretty healthy, too.

1. heat broiler
2. arrange peppers , cut side down in a shallow baking pan and coat with nonstick cooking spray
3. broil 3 to 4 inches from heat source 10 minutes , turning once until lightly charred
4. set oven temperature to 375f
5. meanwhile , heat a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
6. add ground beef , chili powder and cinnamon
7. cook , breaking up chunks of meat , until no longer pink
8. drain off any fat
9. add remaining ingredients
10. bring to a boil , reduce heat , cover and simmer 10 to 12 minutes until barley is tender
11. spoon into pepper halves
12. loosely cover with foil and bake 20 to 25 minutes until peppers are tender
demonstrations.review:
Really liked the flavors in this. Roasting the peppers first mellows the flavor a bit, which was nice. Will probably add more chili powder next time; went a little light with hopes that my kids would eat it. I've got leftover filling, so I'll probably try to make a soup out of it somehow.
Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange caramel pecan biscuits

from pillsbury.

1. heat oven to 375
2. with 1 tablespoon butter , generously butter bottom and sides of 9-inch round cake pan
3. spread ice cream topping in buttered pan
4. sprinkle with pecans and orange peel
5. place frozen biscuits over pecans and orange peel
6. bake at 375 for 25 to 28 minutes or until golden brown and biscuits are no longer doughy
7. immediately invert on serving platter
8. spread any topping remaining in pan over biscuits
9. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Wow ! These are really yummy - I like the flavor the orange zest gives. These are a great alternative to the overnight sticky buns we usually make. My 9" round pan fit 7 biscuits. In a convection oven, I ended up cooking them for about 22 minutes at 350 degrees. Thanks for a keeper !

target.recipe_text:
heavenly apricot white chocolate chunk cookies

a must try. the butter and brown sugar give the cookies a caramel-like taste that is pure heaven when paired with the apricots and white chocolate. source: the neighborhood bakeshop by jill van cleave

1. preheat the oven to 350
2. cream the butter and brown sugar in a medium-size mixing bowl until smoothly blended
3. beat in the egg and vanilla
4. add the flour , baking soda , and salt , stirring the mixture into a smooth dough
5. add the apricots and white chocolate , stirring until the pieces are thoroughly dispersed
6. drop the batter by tablespoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheets , spacing 2 inches apart
7. bake for 10 minutes , until the edges are lightly browned
8. let the cookies set on the sheet for 1 to 2 minutes before transferring them with a spatula to wire racks to cool
target.review: I felt like baking cookies this afternoon, and this is the recipe I decided to try -- I'm SOOOOoooo glad!  I used mixed fruit bits, because that's what I had on hand, and also added macadamia bits per previous recommendations.  I think next time I will add a little more flour, because I prefer a softer cookie - that's just my personal preference.  This is one GOOD COOKIE, not only because it is delicious, but also because it is out of the ordinary.  I can't wait for my kids to come home from school!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn   black bean   mango salsa

nan

1. combine all the ingredients in a bowl and mix well
2. refrigerate in a covered container for up to 3 days
3. serve with crostini
demonstrations.review: Fantastic recipe!  I always double it now or there will be aquabbles at the table over who didn't get their fair share.  I do add a tablespoon of oil to it, just to help blend the flavors a little.  Thanks Dancer!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of twin dragon almond cookies by todd wilbur

www.topsecretrecipes.com i found this copycat recipe on the web and it's one of my all-time favorite cookie recipes. i don't know how many times i've made it. i use a cookie scoop so they come out nice and even, and they just look so nice on a platter. and they taste even better! i like the fact that unlike most almond cookie recipes i've found, this one contains ground almonds in the dough. depending on the size of the cookies, this recipe makes from 24-40 cookies. i usually make them into 3/4" inch balls instead of 1-inch, which result in about 40 cookies. i've written 30 cookies in the yield as an average.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. use ungreased cookie sheets in a bowl , mix the flour , baking soda and salt
3. in a blender , grind 1 / 2 cup of the almonds to a fine powder
4. add the ground almonds to the flour mixture
5. in another large bowl , cream the sugar , lard , almond extract , one egg , and the water
6. add to the dry mixture and mix thoroughly
7. form the dough into 1-inch balls and place on the cookie sheets , 2-inches apart
8. press one of the remaining whole almonds into the center of each ball , while flattening the cookie slightly with your fingers
9. beat the remaining egg well and with a pastry brush , brush each cookie lightly with the beaten egg
10. bake for 20 minutes , or until cookies are lightly brown around edges
11. wait a minute or two before removing from the cookie sheets to cool on a rack
12. also , if you can get pre-ground almonds , you will need 3 / 4 cup of the ground almonds
13. also , i don't like using lard , and have always substituted vegetable shortening with excellent results
14. recipe from todd wilbur's book top secret recipes
demonstrations.review: I give this recipe 5 stars with the following notes:  the 1/2 cup of ground almonds is measured AFTER grinding.  The water is not added to the dough, but to the second egg to make the wash. Bake for 20 minutes at 325 degrees, or for 13 minutes at 350 -- the key as noted is to take them out when they are just beginning to brown.  Also, I used a mix of half shortening/half butter, and I prefer these particular cookies on the small side.  Purely for greed's sake, I put TWO almonds on top of the cookies.  Enjoy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled herb polenta  with asparagus   tomatoes and parmesan

tired of your potatoes and pasta try polenta is a type of meal ground from sweetcorn, cornmeal or maize.

1. bring 2 of the cups of water to the boil and slowly add the polenta and herbs , whisking all the time
2. this ensures the polenta wont form lumps
3. reduce the heat to a simmer , stirring frequently with a wooden spoon
4. when the polenta becomes too thick , add the remaining water a little at a time
5. line a tray with cling film and spread the polenta about 1 inch thick using the back of a spoon
6. cool overnight
7. once cooled , cut into shapes brush with oil and season with salt and pepper and grill on hot grill
8. heat the balsamic vinegar , garlic and sugar in a saucepan
9. once the sugar has dissolved , add the asparagus and cook for 3 minute
10. to serve: arrange the polenta shapes on serving dishes , top with the asparagus and tomatoes , shave over the parmesan and drizzle with a little olive oil
11. garnish with fresh parsley
12. serve with lots of fresh crusty bread
demonstrations.review: I had to resort to pre-made polenta when I first tried this as time was short, but even so this is a delicious dish.  Makes a very welcome change from rice or pasta as a side dish.  Can't wait to try it with freshly made polenta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mandarin orange chicken delight

this is a light and easy chicken dish with a brightly-flavored sauce of mandarin orange juice, lemon juice, soy sauce, and honey. the chicken is then served with the oranges and topped with slivered almonds and chow mein noodles on a bed of rice. the whole thing takes about 15 minutes to prepare and about 30 minutes to cook, so long as you defrosted the chicken ahead of time. enjoy!

1. make the sauce by combining reserved orange juice with honey , soy sauce , lemon juice , , and ginger in a small bowl
2. blend well and set aside
3. combine flour with salt and pepper in a shallow pie pan
4. set aside
5. trim off any fat and white veins from chicken breasts and slice each breast into about three strips
6. dry between double layers of paper towels
7. heat butter and oil in large skillet or wok over medium-high heat
8. coat all sides of chicken strips in seasoned flour and brown lightly in skillet
9. reserve browned pieces on a plate lined with paper towels
10. when all chicken is browned , pour sauce into wok or skillet
11. place chicken in the sauce and turn to coat
12. reduce heat to medium-low , cover , and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes , or until chicken is tender and white throughout and sauce begins to caramelize on the chicken
13. turn several times during cooking to coat evenly with sauce
14. meanwhile , prepare rice
15. when chicken is done , remove from heat and quickly stir in the mandarin oranges
16. sprinkle with your chosen garnish and serve over rice
demonstrations.review: Simple and delicious -- even my picky eater cleaned her plate.  I used fresh ginger, only 1 pound of chicken, and replaced the butter with olive oil, but otherwise followed the recipe.  This recipe is going into our regular dinner rotation, but I wouldn't hesitate to serve it to company too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jb s classic belgian waffles  and variations

we love weekend breakfasts around our house. belgian waffles has always been a favorite, especially for my son, jb! you will find all sorts of variations for this recipe, one of which i'm sure will suit your needs! these waffles will come out light, crisp and toast to a golden brown. we love to top ours with strawberries or blueberries, powdered sugar and whipped cream, blueberry syrup & real maple syrup!... and you didn't think weekends could get anymore special!

1. place all ingredients in a large mixing bowl and combine until well blended
2. allow batter to rest 5 minutes before using
3. use in your belgian waffle maker according to manufacturer's suggestion
demonstrations.review: The family wanted waffles tonight, and I was too lazy to beat egg whites - I found this recipe and it exactly fit the bill.  I added some vanilla and a little extra salt as I thought the flavor needed a little pick-me-up, and I also cut the milk back to 2 cups as another reviewer said the batter was a little runny, and they were perfect.  These waffles rose high and light, and yet at the same time were nice and dense and filling.  Thanks so much Bev!!

target.recipe_text:
chickpeas with spinach  greek

nothing fancy about this dish - just good eating. round off with some feta cheese and crusty bread.

1. in a large saucepan , over medium heat , saute the onions and garlic in the olive oil until the onions are tender
2. add the chickpeas , tomatoes , pepper flakes , and oregano , and paprika
3. cover and simmer for about 18 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. add spinach and cook about 7 minutes longer , or until spinach is cooked
5. add the lemon juice , salt and pepper
target.review: We love this dish! My hubby is a vegetarian and I am always looking for easy vegetarian meals that make everyone happy :) The only think I do differently is I use fresh spinach as i do not like the taste of frozen spinach. Like many others I was thinking I was going to need to umph it up a little with more spice, so I had them ready but it was completely not needed. Perfect as is :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave peanut brittle

note your microwave needs to be 750 to 950 watt. if your microwave is higher need to lower your cooking times and if your microwave is less you will need to increase your cooking time. i'm sorry i did not update this sooner.

1. mix sugar and corn syrup together and cook on high for 4 minutes
2. add peanuts mix well and cook on high for 3 minutes
3. add butter and vanilla and cook on high for 2 minutes
4. add baking soda and mix well , mixture will foam
5. spread on well butter foil
6. when completely cooled break in to pieces
7. store in air tight container
demonstrations.review: This is exactly like the recipe (except mine calls for 2 cups of peanuts...makes it very peanutty...also mine calls for micro-ing 5 min with just the corn syrup and sugar then an additional 4 min after adding peanuts and butter and then mixing in baking soda and vanilla...no micro-ing after that) I use and it has been a hit for many holiday seasons. I like it because with minimal work I can have something that tastes great and makes a lot for teacher gifts. I'm all into recipes that yield decent amounts! One variation that is on the recipe I use (I'm not sure where I got it) is to melt semi sweet chocolate and dip half of the peanut brittle pieces in it (scrape the back of the brittle against your bowl to get off excess chocolate)...this makes it look very fancy. my youngest daughter's 1:1 aide at school loves it so much that she wants a tin of just brittle this year instead of the variety I usually do! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was so incredibly GOOD!!! I was a little short on time so I cut my chicken into bite sized pieces so they would cook in time and it was fantastic. I put everything in the crockpot and then ran out to run an errand...when I returned just a few minutes later the whole house smelled like an Indian restaurant..I knew we were in for a treat :) This is one I will make over and over

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera bread  black bean soup

this is my own version of panera bread's black bean soup. it tastes a lot like it, and i love it! use vegetable stock to make it vegetarian.

1. in a pot , combine the first six ingredients
2. simmer for 10 minutes
3. add half a can of beans , salt and cumin
4. cook for 5 minutes
5. puree soup
6. add the rest of the beans to the soup
7. combine the cornstarch with 1 1 / 2 tablespoons of water
8. add the lemon and the cornstarch to the soup
9. cook until thickened
demonstrations.review: I think for most people this soup will be spicy enough and have enough flavor so I gave it a 4. In our house it was more of a 3. Once I added about 6 more cloves of garlic, habanero pepper and black pepper we had a winner!! This is a very filling soup and low in WW pointss (I calculated 2 using the recipe builder

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange fudge

this is so easy and yet it is probably the best fudge i've ever had. i usually omit the pecans. my niece used this recipe, substituting 3-4 drops peppermint extract for the orange zest, and earned a blue ribbon at the county fair. even my 12-16 year old 4h girls had no problems making it. note: make sure you use fresh orange zest. dried will make the fudge bitter. also make sure you don't get any of the bitter white part of the rind when you are zesting your orange.

1. line a 8x8x2-inch baking pan with lightly buttered waxed paper or aluminum foil
2. set aside
3. melt chocolate chips with condensed milk in the top of a double boiler or in a bowl in the microwave
4. stir until smooth
5. remove from heat and stir in pecans and grated orange peel
6. spread in prepared dish and chill until firm
7. carefully remove fudge from pan using the edges of the foil
8. cut into squares
9. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I absolutely love how easy this is to make and it's really creamy and rich. I'm not crazy about orange and chocolate so I substituted about 3tsp of Peppermint extract (I say "about" because I was making a double batch and 6 tsp was almost the whole bottle of extract so I just dumped the rest in :) )Then I topped it with crushed peppermint pieces and OH MY GOSH!!! it was so good. I had to keep hubby and daughter off of it since I was making it as gifts..I let them have SOME, I'm not that mean. I was trying this out because I was wanting something that was easy but looked impressive and tatsed great to make for teachers and I definitely found it! This is going in my permanent file.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
really good vegetarian meatloaf  really

high in fiber and protein, low in fat, easy and really yummy! i've always thought meatloaf looks and smells so delicious and savory so, as a vegetarian, i decided to make a no-meat version! this is basically our favorite meatloaf recipe but with cooked mashed lentils instead of ground meat. the result is a very tasty dinner!

1. add salt to water and boil in a saucepan
2. add lentils and simmer covered 25-30 minutes , until lentils are soft and most of water is evaporated
3. remove from fire
4. drain and partially mash lentils
5. scrape into mixing bowl and allow to cool slightly
6. stir in onion , oats and cheese until mixed
7. add egg , tomato sauce , garlic , basil , parsley , seasoning salt and pepper
8. mix well
9. spoon into loaf pan that has been generously sprayed with pam or well-greased
10. smooth top with back of spoon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 30- 45 minutes until top of loaf is dry , firm and golden brown
12. cool in pan on rack for about 10 minutes
13. run a sharp knife around edges of pan then turn out loaf onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: This is really good. It's become something I make almost weekly and everyone enjoys it. I have made it with BBQ sauce and even chili sauce and both varations were really yummy. I do have to say that I don't think it can be called meatloaf. It doesn't have the same texture or even a similar taste. The only way it resembles meatloaf is that it is baked in a loaf pan. So, really quite good but not a meatloaf substitute in my opinion

target.recipe_text:
potato peanut cakes

an interesting way to jazz up plain ol' spuds. from cooking light magazine.

1. place potatoes in a saucepan
2. cover with water
3. bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes or until tender
4. drain and cool
5. shred into a large bowl
6. cook bacon in a large non-stick skillet until crisp
7. remove bacon from pan , crumble
8. add corn , onion , bell pepper and chopped thyme to drippings
9. cook until onion is tender , about 4 minutes
10. combine potatoes , bacon , corn mixture , green onions , peanuts , salt and egg
11. stir with a fork until well blended
12. coat a non-stick griddle or skillet with cooking spray
13. spoon about 1 / 3 cup potato mixture onto hot griddle
14. flatten slightly with a spatula
15. cook 5 minutes on each side or until golden brown
16. garnish with thyme sprigs if desired
target.review: THE best potato patty/cake I've ever had.  The crunchy peanuts and combination of vegetable flavors, textures and colors send this way over the top.This makes 8 patties which, at our house, is far less than 8 servings. I'm not going to change a thing next time.  These are perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cider poached apples with cinnamon yogurt

lovely diabetic dessert, or for all to enjoy! (from diabetic cooking) dietary exchanges 2 fruit, 1 fat

1. bring apple cider and cinnamon stick to a boil in small sauce pan over high heat
2. let boil , uncovered , about 20 minutes or until liquid is reduced to about 1 / 2 cup
3. add apples
4. cover and simmer about 10 minutes or until apples are just tender
5. gently remove apple halves and poaching liquid from saucepan
6. refrigerate until cooled
7. combine yogurt and ground cinnamon in small bowl
8. reserve 1 tablespoon
9. divide remaining yogurt mixture evenly among 2 dessert dishes
10. place apple halves on top of sauce
11. sprinkle each apple half with toasted pecans
12. drizzle with reserved yogurt sauce
demonstrations.review: What a lovely dessert and sooo delectable.  I just couldn't waste the poaching liquid so after placing the apples on top of the yogurt sauce, I poured on the syrup. I didn't need to use more sweetener in the yogurt. Definitely a keeper, Derf.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthier fruit muffins

great way to prepare any kind of muffins.  typical favorites have been blueberry, strawberry, cranberry, or a combination.  they are not greasy or overly sweet, nor are they too dry.  uses lots of healthy alternative ingredients.  i have been asked for this recipe everytime i make them.  depending on the fruit, you can also add 1/2 tsp cinnamon to the batter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. combine all the dry ingredients and mix together
3. then add the wet ingredients
4. carefully add the fruit last
5. pour batter into muffin cups , fill near to top
6. sprinkle the mixed topping over the muffins
7. the sugar will bake into a "glaze" and the oats are for texture
8. bake 15-20 minutes , until you can stick a fork in them and it comes out clean
9. muffins will only rise slightly
demonstrations.review: These are truly excellent,buelow. I made them with fresh Washington state cherries and they got RAVE reviews. That sugar makes up for a lot of missing fat but the whole wheat flour adds to the healthfulness  deliciously.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty turkey tortilla wraps

this is one of my favorite quick and easy meals. it's also versatile because you just use whatever veggies that you have on hand. yummy! good for dieters too - makes it easier to get your veggies into a fast meal.

1. steam you veggies so that they are to your liking
2. place 2 oz of turkey on each tortilla
3. top with 1 oz of cheese on top of turkey
4. top with 3 / 4 c of the veggie mixture
5. top with 1 t dressing and roll up like you would a burrito
6. if you want the cheese to melt better , zap in microwave for about 30 seconds
demonstrations.review: Thoroughly enjoyed this for lunch today after a walk out to the garden.  Used tiny patty-pan squash, squash blossoms, sprinkled the tortilla with baby shell peas and savored every bite.  Using Ranch Dressing Mix Plus #2836 made that part of the recipe easy to accomplish on the spur of the moment.  I keep the mix on hand for just such occasions.  This is terrific and oh-so-versatile, Mysterygirl.  Thank you for sharing it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
acorn squash with apple turkey stuffing

a wonderful, healthy main dish with a great combination of flavors.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. remove stalk stub if necessary , slice just enough off the bottom to make a level surface
3. cut in half and remove seeds
4. prick inside surface all over with a fork
5. combine remaining ingredients and fill the squash halves , mounding if necessary
6. place in a baking dish , add 1 / 2 inch of water and cover with foil
7. bake 45 minutes , remove foil and bake 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Yum! Made this just as directed, except I forgot what size squash I was supposed to buy and got one that was twice the recommended size.  So, naturally, it took twice as long to cook and by then the meat had dried out a bit.  I also didn't poke enough holes in the squash flesh.  Doing that allows the juices from the meatloaf to infuse the flesh and increase the flavor.  The recipe is perfect.  My ability to follow directions could use a little work.  Even with my mistakes this was delicious. Great combination of flavors.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili macaroni    crock pot

a recipe that never fails to please

1. in slow cooker , combine first 8 ingredients and mix well
2. cover and cook on low heat for 6 hours or til heated through
3. stir in macaroni and mix well
4. season to taste
demonstrations.review: This couldn't have been easier,made the house smell wonderful, and was a delicious homey meal.  I used recipe #47454 Chili Seasoning, and added a little adobo sauce and chicken broth since I used regular pinto beans rather than sauced hot chili beans.I've put the extras in the freezer where they'll save the evening next time I'm too hassled to make dinner.  Thanks for the husband pleaser, Bluenoser.

target.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
target.review: So good! Very simple to prepare as well. I had only the about half the proper amount of honey, so I substituted some brown sugar and syrup for the remainder. I used a teaspoon of minced garlic, and turned about three times during the cooking process. It smelled great while cooking, tasted delicious and didn't take much time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Made this for the first time for guests & all agreed it was very good.  I used 2 and 1/2 c of water because I was afraid it wouldn't make enough gravy for my 4 lb roast. That was a bit too much--maybe 1 and 1/2 c next time. I threw red potatoes & baby carrots in the pot too & they came out really well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beth s pizza crust

this is an excellent crust that requires no time to rise. why order out when you can just throw this pizza together?

1. combine yeast and warm water
2. stir until dissolved
3. add remaining ingredients and mix well
4. let rest 5 minutes
5. roll out to size and shape you need
6. bake at 450 for 15 minutes or until golden
7. a couple
8. instead , i add several good shakes of italian seasoning mix
9. use your imagination , this is hard to mess up
demonstrations.review: Pretty good pizza crust. I found I might have liked it a little more salty, but that's just me; I like everything to be salty. However, it was quick and easy, and a really good base for homemade pizza. I used my pizza stone & prebaked it for 8 minutes -- it stuck, but that may be because I had never used the stone before. Might try with italian seasonings next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with cherry tomatoes

this makes for a pretty dish and is easy to assemble. if you don't have the fresh vegetables on hand, you can easily adapt with canned goods. i get requests for the recipe all the time.

1. cook beans in water , until tender
2. in a fry , melt butter and add garlic salt , sugar , basil , salt and pepper
3. swish cherry tomato halves around until barely soft and heated , but not squishy
4. add the drained beans and mix well
demonstrations.review: Yummy and quick way to cook green beans. Makes a really nice side dish for company dinner. I used canned french beans and it cut the cooking time down to about 10 minutes. I liked the amount of sugar used, but I also added additional amounts of the other spices. I used fresh garlic and basil, and this had a really nice light taste.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: My husband said this recipe was a 10 and that it should be made all the time! I was a little nervous about the flavor combo, and told him to try the meat before he used barbecue sauce. He was shocked that it was delicious and didn't need any additional sauce. I followed the directions mostly according to the recipe. I did double the sauce -- used fresh ginger & garlic powder, and lightly browned the meat in an oven safe skillet before cooking slightly more than an hour at 350. It did need to be turned once or twice, but is an excellent recipe as is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe. I made basically according to the directions -- cooking time was a little longer than suggested, but I may not have thoroughly defrosted my tilapia beforehand. I omitted the green onions, which was fine, and added a little garlic. The only request I got was more sauce over the fish, but my husband said it tasted like dinner from a fancy restaurant.

target.recipe_text:
my favorite king ranch chicken

i adopted this recipe from recipezaar in september 2006.  it was originally submitted by moxie, but she is no longer a member of recipezaar.  i've been making moxie's recipe for several years now and i'm proud to give it a home.  the only change i make is that i use two cans of cream of chicken soup and omit the can of cream of mushroom soup, because my kids dislike mushrooms.  this casserole is a church potluck staple here in texas and there are as many versions of this dish as there are armadillos in texas.  however, this is the best king ranch chicken recipe that i've found! this casserole also freezes well.

1. steam or boil the chicken breasts until cooked through
2. when cool , dice into bite-size pieces
3. in a large saucepan over medium heat , mix the soups , onion , ro-tel tomatoes and cheez whiz until blended
4. preheat oven to 350 degrees farenheit
5. layer the bottom of a greased 9x12 casserole dish with crushed chips
6. next , layer half the chicken pieces
7. top with half the sauce
8. sprinkle with half the cheddar cheese
9. repeat the layers , but top with the cheddar and mozzarella
10. sprinkle paprika over the top to garnish
11. bake for 30-45 minutes , or until hot and bubbly
target.review: I liked it. Was simple to make and everyone ate it. The only thing was that my dish somehow did not have much of the sauce. I used 6 breast, maybe I should have used only 4 and placed in a smaller baking dish. Then would have been perfect amount of sauce for the amount of chicken I had. I used Doritoes and topped with shredded Mex cheese blend cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham   cheese quiche

you can serve this for dinner or for breakfast. delicious.

1. beat eggs with milk , salt and pepper in bowl
2. add ham and cheese
3. pour into pie shell
4. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
5. let stand for several minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I was a little sceptical of this at first because it was such a simple recipe. BOY WAS I WRONG. It turned out better than I would have EVER expected. I used some left over Honey Baked Ham, added an extra egg and a little extra cheese. Other than that I didn't change a thing. Served it with salted sliced tomato's on the side. YUMMY !!!!! My BF is probably eating the left overs for breakfast as I type this. Thanks for a keeper !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple   mandarin orange fluff

it's a light salad that is quick and easy to make.

1. in a large bowl , mix cottage cheese and jell-o mix
2. drain juice from oranges and pineapple , then add to ingredients
3. add in the cool whip a little at a time
4. refrigerate overnight is best
demonstrations.review: I have been making this SAME recipe for awhile now. It was passed down to me as well. I can not put into words how YUMMY this is. I have seen and made different variations of this without the cottage cheese, but it is not the same. I would suggest to everyone, do not make any changes to this. It is excellent just the way our mom's use to make it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
divine meatball sandwiches

the spread on these meatball sandwiches is what really sets them apart from others. you can experiment and customize by using your favorite meatballs, sauces and fresh bread. good for a party finger food, or for lunch or dinner. i promise no meatball sandwich will be the same again! cook time includes entire process.

1. in a large pot combine frozen meatballs and spaghetti sauce
2. heat over medium until meatballs are heated throughout
3. meanwhile , mix together cream cheese , mayonnaise , italian seasoning , pepper , and garlic powder and set aside
4. slice italian style bread loaves horizontally with serrated bread knife
5. cut loaves into three- or four-inch sections to make small sandwiches
6. spread cream cheese mixture on insides of each sandwiche's tops and bottoms
7. preheat oven to 350f
8. when meatballs are heated , spoon onto sandwiches and top with shredded mozzarella cheese
9. put sandwich tops on and place on a foil-lined baking sheet
10. bake about 10-15 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: well, my rating is for the spread only. I made my own meatballs, sauce and used italian sub rolls, moz cheese and parm cheese. I have been looking for something new to add to it and this was AMAZING. I saw "cream cheese" and knew I had to try it. Thanks a TON! I would have never though of that on my own

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cornflake crusted baked chicken

this recipe is from everday foods. i just tried it out and it is soo good & crispy! i was impressed!!!! the recipe calls for bone-in legs and thighs, but i just used 4 breasts each cut into 3 diagonal strips.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. rinse chicken , and pat dry
3. season generously with salt , garlic powder and pepper
4. in a small bowl , whisk egg with 1 tablespoon water
5. in a large bowl , mix cornflakes with oil , cayenne , and 1 teaspoon salt
6. working with one piece of chicken at a time , dip chicken in egg mixture , then coat with seasoned cornflakes , pressing flakes to help them adhere
7. transfer coated pieces to a rimmed baking sheet
8. bake until golden brown and crisp , about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Oh My....Where do I start. I made this last night. I used boneless, skinless chicken breast (fresh NOT FROZEN). I used chicken poultry seasoning instead of the cayenne. I put the seasoning as well as salt and pepper on the breast and in the cornflake mix. I used butter (land of lakes) instead of olive oil. I did lighly oil pan so bottom would crisp as well. GEEEE WHIZ this turned out so FREAKING GOOD. I will never make another breaded baked chicken any other way again. Even the leftovers I had for lunch was great!!!. I did have to make a little extra of the cornflake crust to put on tops of the chicken before I baked it. I served it with mashed potatoes and White peppered gravy. The gravy on the chicken was very similar to chicken fried chicken dish, but WAY less guilt. My daughter and hubby SOOOOO loved it too!!! I cant say enough good things here !!! THANKS

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
demonstrations.review: Oh My ! This was GREAT! The family loved it. The only thing I did differently is serve it topped with (green salsa verde, Melted Queso cheese and additional sour cream). I made it two weeks ago and am making it AGAIN tonight. This is better than my local Mexican Dive's version. Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini slaw

used the overabundance zucchinis to make this healthy slaw. i used a mandolin to create long julienned strips of zucchini, carrots and red bell peppers..
this is a healthy raw foods!

1. mix dressing ingredients together
2. mix slaw ingredients together
3. pour over slaw tossing to coat
4. chill for 1 hour
target.review: Excellent! Wanted something healthy and light for a side dish to grilled burgers for the 4th of July. This was perfect! I used a combination of zucchini and yellow squash but followed rest of recipe. Everyone loved it and said it is a keeper recipe. Thank you Rita!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey pot pie with biscuits

i have a collection of cook books and usually look up a few of the same recipes and combine the ingredients i like from each recipe so that it makes it my own. this one called for chicken but works for either or just as well. so hope you enjoy experiementing with it as i did.

1. grease a 3 qt casserole dish
2. in lg
3. saucepan , combine carrots and broth
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and cover
6. simmer for 5 minutes or til crisp-tender
7. heat oven to 400f in small bowl , mix 1 1 / 2 cups milk& 1 / 4 cup flour
8. mix the milk mixture , sage , 1 t marg
9. and 1 / 2 t salt into carrot mixture
10. bring back to a boil , constantly stirring
11. boil for approximately 1 min , add chicken and corn
12. pour into greased casserole dish
13. in medium bowl , mix together the 1 cup flour , onions , baking powder , and 1 / 4 t salt
14. once mixed well stir in the 1 / 2 c milk and 1 t melted or soft marg
15. until soft dough forms
16. drop dough by spoonful evenly onto chicken mixture
17. bake at 400f for 20-25 minutes or till top is golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was easy to prepare and tasted delicious. I did not put the green onions in the biscuits because I have a 9 yr old and a 6 yr old that are picky. I followed the recipe but I did double the amount for the biscuits. I baked this in a 9 x 13 pan so the dbld amount covered the top fairly well. My only recommendation is to double the turkey mixture as well. It will easily still fit in the pan and you will be glad you did. I served it with some steamed broccoli. My daughter proclaims this her new favorite dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ricotta  tomato and basil torte

a delicious light meal with a salad. great to take on picnics to serve instead of sandwiches or bread.
can be lightly heated and served warm.
recipe from australian coeliac society magazine nov/dec 09

cooking time does not include chill time in the fridge

1. preheat your oven to 180c oil side and line with baking paper the base of 20cm springform tin
2. beat ricotta , feta , eggs and garlic until smooth
3. stir in basil
4. put into prepared tin and smooth top
5. arrange tomatoes on top cut-side up
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until set and golden
7. cool completely before putting in fridge for at least1 hour to firm
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I used 15 oz. Ricotta because that's how it's packaged here. 4 oz of Mediterranean style feta because that's what I had and did the rest according to the recipe. It does smell amazing while baking! It is hard to resist cutting into it fresh from the oven, but we did. I served it chilled along with a tossed salad and Grilled Balsamic Asparagus by gaylaj. Everyone loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin with merlot mushrooms

this dish is full of flavor, one of my favorites.

1. rub the minced garlic into the tenderloins and sprinkle with the salt and pepper
2. heat the olive oil in a non-stick pan and sear the tenderloins on both sides until browned
3. place tenderloins in a shallow baking pan and add the wine to the saute pan and simmer for 1-2 minutes
4. add the tbsp of butter and heat until just melted
5. pour the half of the sauce from the saute pan over the tenderloins , reserving the rest of the sauce for the mushrooms
6. bake the tenderloins at 350 for 30-35 minutes
7. during the last 5 minutes of baking , heat 2 tsp butter and the reserved sauce in a saute pan
8. add 2 tsp minced garlic and the mushrooms and saute on high heat until golden brown
9. add the 1 / 2 cup merlot and simmer for 2-3 minutes
10. season with the salt and pepper
11. serve the mushrooms on the side or slice the pork tenderloins and serve a small amount of the mushrooms on top the tenderloins
demonstrations.review: Very easy and very good. I followed recipe but I did saute a some thin sliced sweet onion in the butter and merlot before adding mushrooms. Also if you want to splurge a bit, I sliced tenderloins, topped with mushroom mixture then garnished with a sprinkle of crumbled bleu cheese which set off the wine just perfect! Served with a salad and jasmine rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer  n bbq braised country style pork ribs

this recipe comes originally from the 

1. brown the pork in a lightly sprayed skillet on all sides
2. place the ribs in an oven proof pan and scatter the onions all around them
3. pour in the beer and seal with a lid or tin foil
4. bake at 375f until the pork is tender 1 1 / 2- 2 hours
5. pour out the beer
6. slather the pork with the bbq sauce and bake uncovered for 1 more hour or until the meat is brown and the sauce is thick
7. enjoy
demonstrations.review: My husband said to throw away any other rib recipes I had. This is the way I needed to cook them from now on. Followed recipe exactly. Used about 3-4 lbs of boneless country style pork ribs. I did line my pan with foil first which made clean up a breeze. My favorite bbq sauce is Tom's, a local restaurant brand. Unfortunately I did not have any so I tried this with Kraft honey bbq. It was really good. The ribs were so incredibley tender. Can't wait to make it again with my favorite bbq sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cube steaks au poivre

this is just plain good. i cannot remember where i had found this recipe, but i thank whoever came up with this!!!

1. sprinkle steaks with salt and pepper to taste
2. in a large skillet , melt butter and cook steaks 2 at a time on medium-high heat until browned on both sides , about 4 minutes for each set of steaks
3. reserve drippings in pan
4. arrange steaks on a platter and keep warm
5. into pan drippings , over medium high heat , add remaining ingredients
6. stirring often to losen brown bits on bottom of skillet , heat until warm
7. pour over steaks and serve
demonstrations.review:
This was quite good and a nice simple meal. I served it with mashed potatoes and steamed broccoli. The amounts in the recipe really didn't make enough sauce. My husband loves gravy so I sprinkled a little flour in the pan
after I removed the steaks and doubled the rest of the ingredients. It still did not make a whole lot so next time I will probably triple the gravy ingredients. Flavor was wonderful though and I have 2 picky elementary aged children that loved it.

target.recipe_text:
corned beef in beer  crock pot

the best corned beef i've ever made was in the crock pot. (you can substitute water for beer, but the flavor won't be the same)

note:  if you make more than 3-4 lbs., cook it on high.  i've made 6-7 lbs., and it won't be done after 9 hours on low.

another note:  this makes wonderful sandwiches if you cook it, then chill it before slicing.

1. place potatoes , onions , carrots , and bay leaf in crock pot
2. trim excess fat from brisket
3. put meat on top of veges
4. mix molasses with beer and pour over all
5. cover and cook on low heat setting 9-11 hours
6. if desired , place cabbage wedges on top of meat
7. to steam for last hour
8. slice brisket thinly across grain
9. serve with vegetables
target.review: This corned beef had good flavor and was very easy since I didn't have to add veggies later as with some recipes I have tried.  Next time though I will use a dark beer as I used a light beer the first time and couldn't taste any difference from other recipes I have used without beer.  I gave it 4 stars because it was so simple to put together.  You definitely need a BIG crock pot though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage  peppers  and potatoes

lots of flavor in a very easy supper.

1. in 12 inch skillet , heat oil and brown sausage
2. remove from pan
3. add peppers , potatoes , onion mix and water
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce to low and simmer , covered 20 minutes
6. return sausage and simmer another 5 minutes , or until potatoes are done
demonstrations.review: I cannot say enough about this recipe.  It was fantastic.  Great flavor and super easy.  The peppers...yum!  I used small red potatoes cut in half and reduced the simmer time by 5 min to compensate.  I already can't wait to eat the leftovers tomorrow.  I found this recipe as an alternative to using italian sausage with pasta and I'm definitely satisfied.  Next time I'm going to serve it over rice.Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marlboro country chicken fried steak  country fried

this is true southern cuisine, the flavors in this recipe are a little more complex than the basic chicken fried steak. not being a real texan i don't like mine with gravy, but it would be blasphemy not to post the gravy recipe as well.  this recipe also works well for venison (first soak meat in milk to remove the gamey taste). makes excellent sandwiches the next day (serve leftovers on texas toast).  storing this recipe on zaar cause i couldn't find it last time i had a craving!

1. trim steak , cut into 6 to 8 smaller pieces and pound thin
2. combine milk , green tabasco sauce , and salt in one bowl
3. add 1 cup of flour to a second bowl
4. combine remaining flour , paprika , garlic , salt and pepper in a third bowl
5. coat steak in first bowl of plain flour
6. dip floured steak into milk mixture then coat with seasoned flour mixture
7. set aside until all meat has been coated
8. heat 1 to 2 inches of oil or fat in a heavy fry pan
9. fry steaks approximately 2 min per side until golden brown
10. drain on paper towels , serve with cream gravy , mashed potatoes and biscuits
11. for the cream gravy:
12. pour off all but 6 tbsp of fat from the fry pan
13. using the leftover seasoned flour first , add 6 tbsp flour and blend well
14. gradually stir in milk
15. cook and stir over medium heat until thickened , season with salt and pepper
16. serve gravy over steaks
demonstrations.review: I have watched my dad may Chicken Fried Streak many times but until last week I had never made it or from scratch gravy.  This recipe was really easy and it came out good.  I didn't have tabasco so I used tapatio and I must mot have used enough because it didn't have quite the kick I wanted.  My gravy was also a little too thick and bland.  I will definitely be using this as a base again though.  Thank you...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
clock watchers chicken skillet

this is a quick and tasty one-skillet meal. just add a salad and garlic bread, and dinner is ready in no time. perfect for those busy nights when we had to run to hockey practice. those were the days!

1. in a large skillet , cook chicken and onion until onion is tender
2. remove chicken from skillet and keep warm
3. add tomatoes , broth , basil , garlic and pepper to skillet
4. bring to a boil
5. stir in spaghetti
6. reduce heat
7. cover and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes
8. return chicken to pan
9. cook until juices run clear and spaghetti is tender
10. sprinkle with parmesan and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good.  I also diced my chicken but still took it out.  Next time I will leave it in the whole time as it needed more flavor.  I used angel hair pasta broken in half and it worked well.  Love the all in one pan.  I will definitely make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
penne arrabiatta

this is my all-time favorite pasta dish, especially since it's non-dairy. i like it hot, but you can adjust the red pepper flakes to make it as hot or mild as you like.

1. saute garlic and onion in olive oil until transparent
2. add crushed tomatoes and spices and cook over low heat , stirring occasionally , about 30 minutes
3. cook pasta in lightly salted , boiling water until cooked el dente
4. drain pasta and place back in the pot and add some of the sauce and gently toss until coated
5. while serving , add additional sauce if desired and top with freshly grated parmesan cheese
6. left over sauce can be refrigerated or frozen and reheated
7. use a bit more red pepper if you prefer it hotter
demonstrations.review: We have this for dinner at least once a month.  My boyfriend can't get enough.  I have added more pepper flakes and it just gets better.  I do add a pinch of sugar to cut the tomato and it make a huge difference.  I LOVE this recipe.  So easy and CHEAP!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
atomic canuck chili

this is a canadian take on chili -- hope you like it hot and spicy!

1. in a large skillet over medium heat , brown ground beef together with onion , crushed red pepper , garlic powder , and seasoned pepper
