10. squeeze the juice of both the orange and the lemon over the whole fillet
11. grate the zest of both the orange and lemon on the top
12. wrap up the fish with all the ingredients in the foil
13. place the envelope in the grill and grill at 400f for 20 minutes
14. turn the grill off and let it sit in the grill for another 10 minutes
15. remove the envelope , cut an "x" on the top , place on plate and serve
demonstrations.review: My family enjoyed this dish, generally fish dishes are pretty bland but the mix of spices really gave this fish flavor. I did add salt as we add a bit to everything and used powdered ginger as thats all I had on hand but it turned out moist and delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage and beef soup

hearty, thick soup that tastes very much like stuffed cabbage rolls. this is sooo easy, and my family loves it. sure to please even the heartiest of appetites!

1. in large pot or dutch oven , brown beef and onion
2. add all ingredients except parsley
3. bring to boil
4. reduce heat and simmer , covered , for 1 hour
5. you may add extra water if you like a thinner soup
6. garnish with parsley to serve
demonstrations.review: Very good soup with a nice blend of flavors. We prefer a thicker soup so we didn't feel the need to add any of the water. The only changes made were a bit of chili p and cumin as well as more onion and we added a can of black beans plus the kidney beans. We also didn't use the beef bouillon because our cubes have sugar in them so we just threw a can of beef broth in instead. Thanks for a great hearty soup recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paradise pumpkin pie

looking for something different from the same old pumpkin pie? this is a wonderful alternative! how about a pastry shell filled with a creamy layer of cheesecake, a layer of sweet and spicy pumpkin,and topped off with a crunchy pecan praline topping.absolutely the best!

1. beat cream cheese until smooth
2. add sugar and vanilla
3. mix well
4. add egg , beat until smooth
5. spread over bottom of pie shell
6. chill 30 minutes
7. beat filling ingredients until smooth
8. carefully pour over cream cheese layer
9. cover edge of pie with foil to prevent crust from over-browning
10. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes
11. remove foil
12. bake 25 minutes longer
13. meanwhile , mix flour , brown sugar and margarine until crumbly
14. mix in pecans
15. sprinkle over pie
16. bake 10-15 minutes more or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: This was good but to my family it wasn't fabulous. The cream cheese part sort of blended in with the pumpkin and wasnt really very noticeable. It would be a really good pie for those who don't like their pies sweet, because if you don't get a bit of topping with the filling its really not too sweet at all. Overall, a good pie and very easy to make but I think in the future I'd stick to either pumpkin pie or cheesecake and skip mixing the two.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: Really what is there to say about this recipe that hasn't been said? I didn't actually eat any but I made them for work and all of the men came back 3 or 4 times for more. My 9x13 pan was gone in two hours! I added miniature candy bars, marshmallows and chocolate chips and everyone raved about them. Said they were rich and delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot old south pulled pork on a bun

this is a great dish for weekends in the country, friday night dinners or evenings when you have a house full of teenage boys who can't get enough of the rich, smoky sauce.

1. in a skillet , heat oil over medium heat
2. add onions and cook until soft
3. add garlic , chili powder and pepper and cook , stirring , for 1 minute
4. add chili sauce , brown sugar , vinegar , worcestershire sauce and liquid smoke
5. stir to combine and bring to a boil
6. place pork in slow cooker stoneware and pour sauce over
7. cover and cook on low for 10 to 12 hours or on high for 6 hours , until pork is falling apart
8. transfer pork to a cutting board and pull the meat apart in shreds , using two forks
9. return to sauce and keep warm
10. when ready to serve , spoon shredded pork and sauce over warm buns
11. make ahead: this dish can be partially prepared the night before it is cooked
12. complete step 1
13. cover and refrigerate sauce overnight
14. the next morning , continue cooking as directed
15. the 150 best slow cooker recipes j finlayson
demonstrations.review: This was SOOOO Good! We didn't actually cook it in the slow cooker, just threw it in the oven and cooked it for about six hours and the meat was just rediculously tender and moist! The sauce was also delicious though I added a touch more brown sugar as the chili sauce that I used was very tart.

target.recipe_text:
wild rice chicken casserole

easy and tasty rice and chicken dish for that leftover chicken or turkey. there is never any leftovers.

1. prepare rice mix according to package directions
2. while rice is cooking , cook onion and celery in butter until tender
3. stir in soup , sour cream , wine , and curry
4. stir in chicken and cooked rice
5. turn into a 2 quart casserole or a 12x7x2 inch baking dish
6. bake , uncovered , in a 350 degree oven for 35 to 40 minutes
7. stir before serving
target.review: This was a very good chicken and rice casserole -- even though I forgot to add the curry.  The wine lends a nice flavor.  I also added water chestnuts -- I love the crunch they give to a casserole.  Next time I may also add chopped fresh mushrooms to saute with the onion and celery.  And I will remember the curry! This was a great casserole!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado crab enchiladas with green sauce

this is a recipe i have not tried but really looks good! prep time includes refrigeration time. source: the california avocado commission. for avocado-chicken enchiladas substitute 4 skinned and boned chicken breast halves, cooked and shredded, for 1 pound crabmeat.

1. process 1 cup broth , next 5 ingredients , and teaspoon salt in a blender or food processor until smooth , stopping to scrape down sides
2. remove 1 cup sauce , and stir in crabmeat , next 3 ingredients , and remaining teaspoon salt
3. set aside
4. stir together remaining 2 cups sauce and remaining 1 / 2 cup chicken broth
5. cover and chill up to 4 hours , if desired
6. spoon crabmeat mixture evenly down center of tortillas
7. sprinkle evenly with 2 cups cheese , and roll up
8. place seam side down in a lightly greased 13- x 9-inch baking dish
9. cover and chill up to 4 hours , if desired
10. pour sauce mixture over top , and sprinkle with remaining 1 cup cheese
11. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
12. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: This recipe is good but very rich.  I substituted 8 oz of low fat sour cream for half of the cream cheese and still thought it was a little too rich.  I love cilantro but also would cut back on that -- maybe eliminating it from the filling and just using it in the sauce.  By the way, the sauce by itself, is fantastic -- would make a great dip.  I will probably make this again with a few adjustments.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole

we make this the night before and breakfast for christmas is ready in a snap. served with hash browns, juice and coffee and your not spending all morning in the kitchen.

1. trim crusts from bread , cut into cubes , cover bottom of a 12x7" casserole and sprinkle with cheese
2. beat eggs , add milk and mix well
3. stir salt , pepper and dry mustard into the egg mixture , add bacon and sausage , stirring until well blended
4. pour over cheese , cover with foil and refrigerate overnight
5. in the morning put in a 350f oven and bake for 50-55 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great and so easy.  I made it in the morning and put it straight into the oven.  Only change was cutting back the milk to 2 cups and that seemed to be plenty.  Used prosciutto instead of bacon and skipped the sausage.  It was so yummy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: We had this for dinner this evening and it was great!  Very easy too.  Since my husband doesn't like mustard in any form, I substituted herbs de provence and it was fantastic.  I served it over smashed new potatoes -- unfortunately, I didn't make enough for all of that wonderful gravy!  This one's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft cafe  cookies

these are the best cookies you'll ever eat. they are a tradition in our family, and are made every chance we get. very soft, chewy, and delicious. just like the kind sold for a $1.50 at coffee shops.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix together milk and eggs
3. add the brown sugar , vanilla , and white sugar
4. add flour , salt , and baking soda slowly to batter
5. last , but not least , add 1 / 2 to 1 cup of chocolate chip , or nuts ,
6. put tablespoons of batter on a greased baking sheet
7. bake these heavenly cookies for 8 to 10 minutes
8. warning: these will disappear in seconds , so hide a few for yourself before they're gone and you're begged to make more !
demonstrations.review: I thought these cookies were good.  They are definitely fluffier than most cookies (but not like a meringue).  I used 1/4 tsp salt and added chocolate chips then I baked them for about 8 minutes until they were slightly browned on top. I found them to be plenty sweet and not salty at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
artichokes  lamb  and orzo avgolemono

nan

1. in a dutch oven or large skillet heat the oil and brown the meat with onion and garlic till onion is tender
2. drain fat from the meat and return the meat to pan
3. add 3 / 4 cup wine or chicken broth , oregano , lemon peel , salt , and pepper
4. bring to a boil , reduce heat , and cover
5. simmer for 20 minutes
6. add fresh or canned artichokes and simmer 10 minutes more , or till tender
7. meanwhile , in a large saucepan or pasta pot bring 3 quarts water to boiling
8. add pasta and reduce heat slightly
9. boil for 5-8 minutes stirring occasionally
10. immediately drain and return to warm pan
11. keep warm
12. in a small mixing bowl combine egg , lemon juice , cornstarch , and 1 / 2 cup warm chicken broth
13. pour egg mixture into the lamb-artichoke mixture
14. cook and stir over medium heat for 1 minute , or till thickened and bubbly
15. cook and stir for 2 minutes more
16. serve lamb mixture over hot cooked pasta
17. garnish with parsley
demonstrations.review: I love orzo pasta and this was great!  I cooked the lamb with white wine and used dried oregano since I didn't have fresh on hand. My whole house smelled so good from this dish.  My only addition was a little bit of butter to the orzo after I drained it to keep it from sticking together.

target.recipe_text:
soft  chewy sugar cookies

i was never a huge sugar cookie fan until i went to a local bakery and bit into one of their frosted sugar cookies.  it had a fudgy texture that complimented the harder frosting and sprinkles on top.  so good!  i've been on a hunt for such a cookie since.  i haven't found the frosting yet, but here's a great cookie that delivers on texture and taste!

1. cream shortening , butter , sugar
2. add eggs , lemon , vanilla and sour cream
3. mix till creamy
4. add sifted dry ingredients: salt , soda , and flour
5. chill for several hours or overnight
6. roll into balls and flatten with bottom of sugar coated glass
7. bake at 350f just until the edges start turning color
8. time will vary depending on how large and thick you made your cookies
9. it is important not to overbake if you want the texture to remain chewy and soft
10. decorate as desired
target.review: Ok we absolutely love these cookies from the store so I decided to make up the dough tonight so I could bake them tomorrow. I can already tell that the cookies will be gone in less then a couple days as when my family got home they all decided to try the cookie dough and loved it! I will be making these over and over again! Will let you know how they turn out too :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried zucchini sticks

i love these.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. spray a cookie sheet with cooking spray
3. place bread crumbs , cheeses , garlic powder , oregano , basil , parsley in ziploc bag
4. shake well to combine
5. set aside
6. cut each zucchini lengthwise into 8 pieces
7. cut each piece in half horizontally
8. beat egg and milk in a shallow bowl
9. dip each piece of zucchini in egg mixture then bread crumb mixture
10. repeat until all of the sticks are coated
11. place them on prepared cookie sheet
12. bake for 10-15 minutes or until brown and tender
13. serve with warm spaghetti sauce or ranch dressing
demonstrations.review: I got some fresh zucchini from the Farmers Market and whipped these up to go with some Lasagna. They worked great as dipping sticks and just to mop up the sauce. I did shred up some of my own breadcrumbs along with store bought to make sure I had enough. Very good and glad to have tried zucchini in this way! Made for ZWT7!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
que que  chilean coffee cake

this is a low, dense coffee cake, with a hint of citrus. i recommend using the lemon extract vs the vanilla called for in the recipe. my cake tends to fall in the center as some of the posters have mentioned. i tried baking in a 9x9 pan and it helped, but still sank a little. if anyone has suggestions,  i love to hear them as this really is a delicious coffee cake --brenda.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix sugar and butter until light and fluffy
3. add egg mix well
4. stir in flour , baking soda , and baking powder , alternating with buttermilk
5. add lemon rind , vanilla or lemon extract , and pecans
6. stir to mix
7. pour batter into well buttered , floured loaf pan
8. bake for 45-50 minutes
9. check for doneness with toothpick
10. remove from pan and sprinkle with sugar
demonstrations.review: I first found this recipe when creating a Chilean meal for my family for a Spanish project and they loved this dish especially. It is so easy to make that I now have made it over ten times! This is a great snack or dessert and I love the combination of citrus and pecans.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and avocado panini sandwiches

the tastes of summer are terrific in this quick fix meal. you do not need a panini press for this sandwich.

1. heat panini press to medium
2. peel and remove pit of avocado
3. coarsely mash avocado in bowl using fork
4. add lemon juice and stir
5. stir in onion , cilantro , chopped jalapeos , and tomatoes
6. salt and pepper to taste
7. spread thin layer of mayo on bread slices
8. assemble sandwich by layering onto bread sliced jack cheese , chicken , bacon , avocado mixture , and grated cheddar
9. top with remaining slice of bread
10. grill until heated through and crispy on the outside
11. if using naan bread , slice into six triangles
demonstrations.review:
These were delicious! We have a half panini press so I flipped the sandwiches at the end. I made two with english muffin toasting bread and the other two with pita pockets. I wasn't sure which side to put the mayo but I found that putting mayo on the outside gave it a lighter press (not as crunchy) but of course the others still had a good flavor even with the mayo on the inside. The other adjustments I made was to use dried cilantro, all shredded cheese, and fajita grilled strips of chicken. 
Made for ZWT5, Dining Daredevils.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanish roasted red pepper sauce

try this with "party nut loaf" or a baked potato or mash, or pasta, or, or, or!

from linda mccartneys world of vegetarian cooking

1. put the peppers and tomatoes on a baking tray and roast them at 200c / 400f / gas 6 for 20 - 30 minutes , turning from time to time until the peppers have blackened and the tomatoes have cooked
2. cool the peppers in a paper bag for 10 minutes , then peel off the skins , core and de-seed them
3. skin the tomatoes
4. put the peppers and the tomatoes in the blender with the olive oil
5. blend to a puree
6. pour into a small saucepan and add the creme fraiche or soya cream
7. stir well , season to taste and heat through to serve
demonstrations.review: This was a delicious sauce! I didn't get enough time to peel all the peppers but they blended up fine and just made the sauce a little chunkier. Just make sure to season it as it gives it some great flavor, I used some garlic salt and it was delicious! I decided to use have an half for the creme which worked well. All on all this was a great pasta dinner sauce. Made for ZWT5, Dining Daredevils ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potatoes with creme fraiche and chives

these mashed potatoes are creamy, fluffy and slightly tangy thanks to the creme fraiche. a ricer is used on the potatoes to make them really smooth, but you could always mash by hand. simple goodness! from food & wine.
*note: the mashed potatoes can be made ahead of time and kept at room temperature for up to 3 hours. reheat before serving. (you may need to add a bit more milk.)*

1. in a large pot , cover the potatoes with cold water and bring to a boil over high heat
2. cover and cook over med-high heat until the potatoes are tender to a fork , about 20 minutes
3. drain
4. press the potatoes through a ricer into a large saucepan over low heat
5. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , combine the milk with 10 tablespoons of the butter and 1 tablespoon of salt and cook over medium heat until the butter is melted , about 3 minutes
6. pour the hot milk over the riced potatoes and cook over medium heat , stirring occasionally , until blended - about 2 minutes
7. stir in the creme fraiche , the remaining 2 tablespoons of butter and the chives and cook until the potatoes are heated through , about 5 minutes
8. season with salt and pepper and serve !
demonstrations.review: This is a very plain potato dish but still works well with main courses. I served this with meatballs which worked great! Unfortunately, my homemade creame fraiche did not set the way I wanted but I threw it in but this made it more like a chowder which bummed me out but my family still liked it, I may try this again but maybe after letting my creme fraiche set longer. ;) Made for ZWT5, Dining Daredevils.

target.recipe_text:
roasted garlic asiago dip

this is sooo good. very rich. if you like garlic, this is a must try. the prep time includes the time to roast garlic.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. cut the garlic head in half along the"equator"
3. place the garlic , cut side down on a foil lined baking sheet and roast uncovered 40 to 45 minutes or until tender
4. to remove the garlic , turn heads upside down and gently squeeze the garlic out of the skins
5. reduce oven temp to 350
6. with a food processor or electric mixer , blend cream cheese , asiago cheese , heavy cream , sour cream and parsley until well-blended add garlic and blend again
7. place mixture into a casserole or baking dish and top with shredded mozzarella
8. bake about 20 minutes until bubbly and golden brown on top
9. serve with firm crusty bread , crackers or other dippers of your choice
10. i have added artichoke hearts to the dip for a nice change
11. update: i have been replacing the heavy cream with sour cream and it comes out fine
target.review: I made some changes but it turned out AWESOME!!  I did not have any heavy cream so I just doubled the sour cream, I added another half a head of garlic, an addiction to it in the family and a sprinkle of cayenne to give a little bite... one final change, I mixed half asiago and half romano and skipped the parsley (personal preference).  If I can tear it away from the family it is going to the Super Bowl party.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review:
This was very good.  I did not have parmesan cheese so subsituted half romano and asiago.  

I had one pound of tilapia but kept the rest of the ingredients the same quantity.  It turned out just right.  My family loved the extra sauce.  

We served this with jasmine rice and roasted brussel sprouts and crusty french bread.  All the flavors combined beautifully.

Do toss this in the broiler for the last minute or two to crisp up the cheese.  This will definitely be a staple in our house.

Thanks for the wonderful recipe Crabbycakes!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best broccoli salad

i made this salad for an end of school year pot luck. the following year i was asked if i would bring it again. people remember this salad from year to year. it can be made the day before and chilled - which is very helpful. it uses a full pound of bacon. the cook time is actually 

1. combine all the salad ingredients , tossing well to mix
2. mix the dressing ingredients together then toss with the salad mix
3. let stand at least 1 hour in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review:
I was searching for a recipe like this.  I viewed a couple of the others but ended up with this one since it seemed to be what I wanted.

I did not have the sunflower seeds so substituted chopped pecans.  The other sub I made was instead of using the broccoli florets, I used broccoli slaw and rainbow slaw.  It was a 12 oz bag of each.  I used about a quarter of a medium red onion.  Not a huge onion fan but it does add flavor.

The results... FABULOUS!

I tasted it after about 15 minutes and it was wonderful.  An hour later and I wanted to eat the whole dish and not share.  The dressing was a just right for the two bags.  It coated it nicely without being soggy.

The dressing is sweet with a slight tang that blends well with the other flavors.  

I made this with pulled pork sandwiches.  I wanted something a little different than the traditional cole slaw.  This worked perfectly.

Thank you Trisha!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato cucumber salad  salad shirazi

for zaar world tour ii (middle east/persia) recipe source: the book club cookbook discussing "nine parts of desire: the hidden world of islamic women" by geraldine brooks. i haven't made this salad yet, but it seems like it would be a wonderful summer salad.

1. in a jar , whisk together the dressing ingredients
2. in a large salad bowl , combine salad ingredients , toss
3. add the dressing and toss
4. refrigerate at least 30 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
This was absolutely yummy.  I diced the pieces of tomato and cucumber very small hoping to let the flavors blend quickly.  I added the mint to the dressing in the food processor to get tiny bits.  I was not sure how I would like bigger pieces of it.  After letting it set in the fridge for an hour, it was sooo good I almost ate the entire thing myself.

Thank you for this recipe it will stay as a staple for a LONG time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini crisp  apple crisp

i found this recipe on the internet and can't wait to try it !! it is supposed to taste like apple crisp. i have never made this recipe, but am posting it here to share with you all and to keep it safe for future use. if you try it before i do, let me know how it turns out!

1. zucchini mixture:
2. in a large saucepan , over medium-low heat , cook zucchini and lemon juice for 15-20 minutes until zucchini is tender
3. add sugar , cinnamon and nutmeg and cook for a minute more
4. remove from heat and let sit
5. crust mixture:
6. for crust , mix flour , and sugar in a large bowl
7. cut in cold butter until mixture resembles pea size coarse crumbs
8. stir 1 / 2 cup of the flour mixture into zucchini and mix well
9. press 1 / 2 of remaining crust mixture into a greased 15x10 jelly roll pan
10. spread zucchini mixture over crust in pan
11. crumble remaining crumb mix over zucchini and sprinkle with the 1 teaspoon cinnamon
12. bake at 375f for 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very yummy and does taste like apples.  When I first saw the recipe I was a little nervous about all the lemon juice.  I cheated and grated the zucchini and skipped the boiling step since the peices were smaller.  When I added the lemon and sugar it smelled strong of lemonade and got a little concerned.  Once it baked in the oven, it was not lemony at all just tender and sweet goodness.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised cannellini beans with onions and arugula

canned beans are one of the few canned foods i really like, and i often use them instead of dried beans in soups, stews, and even salads to save on soaking and cooking time. 
in this easy recipe, i braise cannellini beans with onions, garlic, and a hint of tomato, and throw in arugula for an earthy flavor and silky texture.

1. heat the olive oil in a 1-quart pot over a medium-high flame
2. add the garlic and cook 30 seconds , stirring constantly
3. the garlic should become aromatic and just lightly golden
4. stir in the chili pepper and cook 15 more seconds
5. add the onion and cook , still stirring , about 2 minutes , or until the onion becomes translucent and soft
6. stir in the pepper and parsley and cook 1 more minute
7. fold in the rinsed and drained beans , and then stir in the tomato paste
8. add enough cool water to cover the beans by 1 / 4 inch
9. season with the salt and bring to a gentle boil , uncovered
10. cover and lower the heat to medium-low
11. cook for 5 minutes
12. uncover , stir in the arugula , and cover again
13. cook for another 15 minutes
14. adjust the seasoning if needed and serve hot
demonstrations.review:
I made this recipe almost according instructions.  I cut the onion down to 1/4 of a medium red onion.  I am not over partial to onions.  This was my first time cooking cannellini beans or arugula.

I definitely will be making this again and often.  I had planned on making this a side dish with grilled chicken but it quickly became the main course.

The butteriness of the beans is blended well with the slight pepppery flavor.  It keeps it from being bland.

Thanks Dancer for introducing me to two new ingredients!!

target.recipe_text:
linda s ham salad sandwich  sandwiches  or finger rolls

these are a big hit around the holidays when having parties or having baby, graduation and wedding showers!  this recipe uses left over ham from a smoked shoulder.  the flavor is wonderful, and so good!  this is a real treat!  my gram always made it for us growing up, as she made us smoked shoulder quite often...  i always helped her grind the meat, and that i was the "big cheese" getting to do that part lol...  now i just use my blender, and it works like a charm, as long as you don't overload it.  you can use chunks of chopped ham in this recipe, but it's not quite as tasty!  try some of my other delicious sandwiches: recipe #52284 recipe #218337 recipe #52286

1. grind the ham shoulder with a meat grinder
2. you can use a blender for this also , just make sure you don't put in too much at a time
3. put ground meat in a bowl and add mayonnaise , mustard , and relish
4. mix well
5. chill until ready to make sandwiches or rolls
6. when ready to make sandwiches , put a good amount of meat filling on the roll
7. add a slice of onion , or as much as you want
8. i love making these with vidalia onions , they are so sweet
9. put the top piece of bread or roll on , and serve
target.review: We made a ham shoulder for Sunday dinner and ground the leftovers for sandwiches for work.  These are so good!  My wife plans to use the filling for stuffed finger rolls for a baby shower that she is hosting in a few weeks.  Thanks for another great recipe Linda!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled marinated tuna steaks

this recipe was given to me to try not too long ago. thought it would be a good one to post since it's about that time of year!

1. for marinade , combine the above ingredients except fish
2. place fish in a plastic zip-loc bag and add marinade
3. seal bag and turn bag to coat fish well
4. chill 2 hours , turning fish once
5. remove fish and discard marinade
6. grill fish on a greased rack of uncovered grill over medium coals for about 12 minutes , or fish flakes easily when tested with fork
demonstrations.review: This was really enjoyed by my DW and I.  I marinated them for 2 hours then threw them on the grill.   Excellent taste from all the herbs.  DW says she would even attempt to make these because of the ease of preparation.  We will have these again when we can get the tuna cheap enough!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan catfish

i hate fish, but this tastes similar to chicken when fixed this way and isn't so bad for me to eat!

1. heat oven to 400
2. rinse fillets and pat dry
3. mix eggs and milk in a small bowl
4. combine remaining ingredients in another bowl
5. dip fillets into egg mixture , and then into bread crumb mixture , coating evenly
6. place fillets , rounded-side up , on a greased baking sheet
7. spray fillets lightly with non-stick cooking spray and bake , uncovered , for about 15 minutes , or until fish flakes when tested with a fork
demonstrations.review: We love fish, and I had this recipe for awhile so I decided to make it, and I am so glad we tried it because it was a great topping for our flounder.  With a few squirts of lemon on top the two of us ate  it all and enjoyed it very much too!  Rich

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinade for beef

this marinade gives an 

1. combine all ingredients in a glass deep or large zip-lock bag and mix well
2. add beef and marinate for several hours
3. grill steaks , basting with marinade to desired doneness or place roast along with marinade in a baking dish and bake@ 350 degrees for 40-50 minutes for rare
4. if whole tenderloin cook 45-60 minutes@ 425 degrees for rare
5. i bake the tenderloin@ 350 degrees for about 2 hours for medium well
6. let sit about 10 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: I am always looking for new ways to prepare steak and this was a great marinade we found here.  I marinated our sirloin steaks for about 8 hours and then grilled them, and they were very flavorful!  We will use this marinade on a roast too, and see how it works.  Thank you for sharing!  Rich

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple oat nut scones   starbucks

this is a copycat recipe from starbucks. i've altered the recipe a little so i could use a mixer instead of a processor....soooo very yummy!!!

1. preheat oven to 425f
2. using a food processor or blender , finely grind oats
3. in a mixer , mix flour , oats , sugar , salt and baking powder
4. add maple syrup and butter and mix well
5. in a small bowl , beat the egg with the cream and maple extract
6. pour the egg mixture into the flour mixture and mix well
7. add pecans and mix just to incorporate
8. place dough on a floured surface
9. knead and pat dough into a 8 to 10 inch circle and cut into 8 wedges
10. spray a baking sheet with cooking spray
11. place wedges on top and bake for 13 to 15 minutes , or until light brown
12. remove scones from oven to wire rack
13. let cool about 3 to 5 minutes
14. mix glaze ingredients until smooth
15. adjust the amount of water to get to the desired consistency
16. i like the glaze to be rather thick
17. spread lots of glaze over each scone and dry about 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: My wife made these for brunch this morning, and I was tickled pink when I bit into the first one.  They weren't dry and the flavor just about knocked my socks off!  I told her she better guard this one with her life, because we want it at hand to have again REAL soon.  Delicious!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s awesome grilled tuna steak

i love fresh tuna fillets, and i am always looking for new ways to prepare it.   here is one that i created one night when i wanted to experiment.  delicious and very easy to prepare.  try it!!!  it will make you a tuna lover too!

1. sprinkle both sides of fillet with tony's seasoning
2. top the fillets with 1 pat of butter on each fillet
3. squeeze the lemon and lime all over the fillets ,
4. turn heat on using high setting
5. wait for 20 minutes before adding fillets
6. grill on preheated grill , over indirect heat for 5 minutes per side , then serve
7. please
demonstrations.review: This simple but excellent recipe is one that I have made many times in the past several months.  It has awesome flavors from the seasonings and citrus.  If you enjoy fresh tuna this is one to try.  Everyone here raved about it!

target.recipe_text:
substitution for pumpkin pie spice

out of pumpkin pie spice and only need a little to get you through until you buy more? from hamilton beach web site a few years back.

1. stir or shake ingredients together
2. store in a closed small container
3. use in place of"pumpkin pie spice" in your recipe
target.review: I don't know what pumpkin pie spice is supposed to taste like, but I was making a cookie recipe today that called for a bit so I used this version.  Two of the spices in here are definitely not my favorites (cinnamon and ginger) so I was a bit worried about the taste of the cookies I was making, but they were excellent!  There was a bit of a spice flavoring, but not overwhelming and I couldn't taste any of the flavors that I don't like.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kelly s blueberry banana bread

not bragging, but everyone says this is simply the best banana bread they've ever had. blueberries are one of my fav fruits and i put them in everything!i love to make it, especially since it makes 2 loaves. we keep one and always give the other one away. :)

1. in large bowl , mix all ingredients except blueberries for about 30 seconds
2. fold in frozen berries
3. pour into 2 greased 8 1 / 2x4 1 / 2x2 1 / 2 loaf pans that have been greased on the bottoms only
4. bake in 350 oven for 55-60 minutes , til toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
5. cool slightly , loosen sides with knife from sides of pan , turn out onto rack to cool
6. when cool , wrap tightly with plastic wrap , keep refrigerated
7. best the next day !
8. ialways bake blueberries frozen in breads and muffins so they hold up perfectly , and you don't end up with a hollow blue hole , lol
demonstrations.review: I'm a bit torn on this review, but I decided to go with 4 stars instead of 3 after all.  I think I've made this recipe before and loved it, so decided to make muffins out of it for a potluck dinner. I didn't have any blueberries, but used frozen cranberries instead, also left out the coconut and pecans.  Although I can't say the muffins were bad, the parts without cranberry in it seemed bland.  That could be the left out ingredients, or maybe the dough cooked differently as muffins.  I got 12 muffins out of the recipe and they were decent size and many people complimented them, so maybe my taste buds were just off yesterday.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christie s chocolate chip cookies

i adapted this recipe from bev's recipe#35813 they are the most amazing biscuits and i wanted to see if they would taste just as good without the oats and raisins but with chocolate....they do :)   used 1 cup of m&m's and 1 cup of chocolate chips....but you may like to use something else.

1. beat the sugars and butter until smooth
2. add the egg and vanilla
3. sift the flour , biking soda and salt together and mix into the wet mixture
4. mix in the chocolate chips
5. roll into balls and place onto the baking tray
6. flatten slightly
7. bake at 180c for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: The only reason I'm giving this recipe a 4 instead of 5 is because although the cookies are good, there's nothing really special about them and they turned out a bit too sweet.  However, I scaled the recipe down and it seemed like I used too much chocolate chips.  I loved the idea of using M&M's, though!  PAC 2011

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frosted pumpkin walnut cookies

this is my adopted recipe.i have made these now and if you like pumpkin and walnuts you will like these. the original recipe didn't have any nuts in the ingredient list so i tried 1 cup and that seemed to be fine. no milk was listed so i used about 1 tablespoon in the icing. she/he also had 84 as the amount, i only got 58 cookies. even dh, the picky one, enjoyed them.

1. cream butter
2. gradually add brown sugar , beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating after each addition
4. stir in pumpkin and vanilla
5. combine flour , baking powder , salt , and pumpkin pie spice
6. gradually add to creamed mixture , mixing well
7. stir in walnuts
8. chill for at least 1 hour or until ready to bake
9. drop dough by teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto greased cookie sheets
10. i used a 1 1 / 2 inch cookie scoop and got 58 cookies
11. bake at 375f for 11-12 minutes
12. cool on wire racks
13. frost with maple frosting
14. cream butter
15. gradually add 1 cup powdered sugar , beating well at medium speed of an electric mixer
16. add remaining sugar alternately with milk , beating until smooth enough to spread
17. you may need to add a bit more milk
18. add maple extract , and beat well
demonstrations.review: These were excellent!  I was doubtful since I'm not a huge fan of pumpkin, but I had so much of the insides left over after carving that it seemed a shame to waste.  I used the rind of the pumpkin (the hard stuff closest to the skin, not the stringy insides) from a fresh pumpkin I bought and carved earlier that day.   I used maple syrup instead of maple extract, and for that and the milk I needed at least twice as much as is called for to get the right consistency for the icing.  Even then, you can see in my pics that the icing is quite a bit thinner than in the other pictures, although not sure why.  However, these were nice and soft with great subtle flavors and the icing was literally the icing on the cake, err... cookie!  Thanks for a great recipe and I'll be keeping this one for next time I have leftover pumpkin!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fasolakia ladera

this is a traditional greek recipe. i grew up eating this as a child, and i think it's fantastic. can be served both hot or cold.

1. heat oil in heavy large nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
2. add onion and saute 5 minutes
3. add green beans and cayenne pepper and saute until onion is translucent , about 3 minutes
4. add potatoes and parsley
5. pour tomato paste over vegetables
6. bring to boil
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer until potatoes are tender , stirring frequently , about 45 minutes
9. season with salt and pepper
10. remove from heat
11. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review:
Over all, good side dish.  I cut down on the oil and added some V8 juice as I was cooking so it stayed moist and didn't stick to the pot (although still stuck a little).

My only complaint is that the flavours of the tomato were quite mild, but I accidentally added Cayenne pepper instead of regular, so that's my fault =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian ham and cheese stuffed chicken breasts

this is a very easy dish to make, i promise.  very elegant dish, as well, and with only about 250 calories per serving.  i highly recommend using good quality prosciutto and muenster for this.  for novice cooks, if you freeze the chicken breasts for a bit before slicing them, they are much easier to slice.

1. slice chicken breasts horizontally without cutting all the way through
2. open so breasts are flat
3. place between 2 pieces of plastic wrap
4. pound gently with flat side of meat mallet
5. in small bowl , stir together parsley and mustard
6. spread over half of each chicken breast
7. top each with half slices of cheese and prosciutto
8. fold breasts to enclose stuffing
9. pressing edges together to seal
10. sprinkle with salt
11. place flour on plate
12. dip chicken in flour , tapping to remove excess
13. heat oil in large nonstick skillet over meium heat until hot
14. add chciken , cook 6-10 minutes or until golden brown , no longer pink in the center , and juices run clear
15. place of serving platter
16. increase heat to medium high
17. add wine to skillet
18. cook 30-60 seconds until slightly reduced , stirring to scrape up any browned bits from bottom of skillet
19. pour over chicken
demonstrations.review: I was worried that this would turn out to be a mess, but it was pretty easy to make and SOOO good!  I used fat-free deli ham and light Havarti (I had both in the fridge; I couldn't find Muenster, but that's my next mission =) and it gave the chicken a great smoky, creamy flavour.  I'm not a fan of dijon but it was just right in this recipe.  Note, it's much easier if you use a fairly plump chicken breast, as it flattens into a breast large enough that you can fold over easily.  I fried it for about 6 min per side, and had to add a bit more oil as I went along.  I will definitely be making these again! (PAC 2011)

target.recipe_text:
roast  sticky  chicken

beautiful and delicious, this incredibly moist roasted chicken puts kenny roger's roasters, boston market, and other rotisserie style chickens to shame! please don't let the word 

1. blend all spices together and set aside
2. remove neck and giblets from chicken cavity , rinse well inside and out , and pat dry with paper towels
3. rub with spice mixture , both inside and out , then stuff cavity with onions
4. wrap in a resealable"food grade" plastic bag , tie closed , and refrigerate overnight
5. remove from plastic bag and place in a shallow baking pan
6. roast uncovered in a 250 f oven 5 hours
7. if the chicken contains a pop-up thermometer , ignore it
8. this recipe is safe
9. according to the united states department of agriculture food safety and inspection service , a whole chicken should reach an internal temperature of 180 f
10. for more info check out their"thermy" campign web site !
11. baste with drippings every 30 minutes after the first hour
12. let rest for 10 minutes before carving
target.review: This was my first attempt at a whole roasted chicken so I have nothing to compare it to, but it was delicious. My friend and her kids all loved it too.  I used an organic bird and rubbed some of the spice under the skin too since I don't eat the skin. I also didn't have white pepper but I don't know if it mattered. The chicken was super moist and tender and flavorful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic roasted yams

i just found this recipe in a cooking magazine and can't wait to try it!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. place balsamic vinegar and brown sugar in a large skillet and bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring until sugar dissolves
3. reduce heat and simmer 3 minutes or until the mixture thickens slightly
4. add butter and salt and stir until butter melts
5. add yams to the pan , stir to coat and season with black pepper
6. spread evenly on a rimmed cookie sheet
7. bake 40 minutes , or until yams are tender , stirring occasionally
demonstrations.review: I tried these for friends at Christmas dinner and while I wasn't totally loving them, everyone else really liked them (mostly boys/men!).  But then, since I had leftovers, I ate them the next few days and I loved them!  Weird. So, I think I'll make them again.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach balls  appetizer

very handy to have in the freezer for the holidays - easy to make

1. cook spinach according to instructions , drain in a sieve , use back of a wooden spoon to press the spinach against the sieve to get as much moisture as possible out in a bowl combine the spinach , stuffing mix , cheese , eggs , butter , salt& pepper mix thoroughly& roll into small balls 3 / 4 to 1" size
2. place on a cookie sheet& freeze
3. when frozen place in a plastic zip lock bag
4. to serve place frozen balls on a cookie sheet and bake at 350f 10-15 minutes or until lightly browned if you are doing them fresh or thawed only bake for 7-10 minutes
5. serve hot
demonstrations.review: These were great - even after I modified them to lower the fat content. I used mainly egg whites instead of whole eggs and reduced the butter to roughly half I think.  Also, I used the cranberry Stove Top stuffing and they were yummy and different. I also used Asiago cheese cuz that's what I had.  AND I re-freezed the cooked leftovers, which tasted great the 2nd time around too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
will brink s chocolate protein bars

these are tasty, nutritious and easy to make.  the recipe is from a collection tasty fat loss and muscle-gaining recipes by will brink, a bodybuilder.  i use vanilla whey powder and add 1/4 c cocoa and mix it all in a food processor.  this saves mashing bananas and fighting with the peanut butter. they also freeze well.

1. preheat your oven for 5 minutes at 180 c
2. mix the oats , whey and cinnamon
3. add the peanut butter and stir in thoroughly
4. add the egg whites , mashed bananas , and the honey
5. add the nonfat milk slowly , while mixing thoroughly
6. spoon the mixture into a greased , lined cake pan and level with a knife
7. bake for 15 minutes
8. remove from oven and allow to cool slightly before cutting to reduce stickiness
9. cut into 8 bars
demonstrations.review:
These were great! I've tried a few different homemade protein bar recipes and this one is the best so far. I even halved the recipe and didn't measure most of the ingredients exactly and they were great. Took them to the beach to eat while everyone else ate junk! 

Additional Note:  I have now made these a few times and have successfully replaced the bananas with applesauce and added ground flax seeds. They came out good but needed something..... I think that ingredient is probably a pinch of salt. I think that will bring out the flavors more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh my d lux chocolate chip cookies

these are definitely not your standard chocolate chip cookies! they are of the "oh my" variety, which is what you'll say after the first bite! the addition of rice krispies may seem odd, but these are great and a favorite of kids of all ages. an extra plus...this recipe make about 7 1/2 dozen cookies :) (don't worry, you'll have no problem getting rid of them all!)

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream butter and add sugar , beating at low speed until light and fluffy
3. add eggs and vanilla and beat well
4. combine flour and baking powder and add to creamed mixture until well combined
5. stir in remaining ingredients
6. drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto baking sheets
7. bake for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned
8. cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: These sounded awesome but I didn't absolutely love them like I thought I would. To be fair though, I used crushed rice or corn chex (didn't have the box) instead of the rice krispies since that's what I had on hand, and I think that might have been the difference in taste that I didn't like.  I will definitely make again with the real rice krispies.  However, some friends loved them and wanted the receipe. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh basil corn salad

i am something of a basil addict, and this salad is the reason. even if you're tempted, don't use canned or frozen corn - it's just not the same! from barefoot contessa.

1. fill a large bowl with ice water
2. set aside
3. boil the corn in a large pot of salted water for 3-5 minutes , just until it loses its' starchiness
4. drain corn and prevent further cooking by plunging into the bowl of ice water
5. when corn has cooled , cut the kernels off the cob
6. toss the cut corn with the onions , vinegar , olive oil , salt and pepper
7. add the fresh basil just before serving
8. serve cold or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I can't even describe how happy my taste buds were when I ate this. Love, love, LOVE it! I omitted the onion cuz I don't like it. I also didn't even measure the vinegar or oil but used them sparingly, and used fresh corn that I grilled in foil - perfect! I had some super sweet orange cherry tomatoes from the farmer's market so I added those, along with some cubed mozarella that I had to use up. The flavors were so delicious that I can't even imagine using anything but fresh corn, fresh basil leaves, etc.  Heaven!

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon bun icing

this is just like the sweet, gooey icing that comes inside tiny tins inside those tubes of refrigerated cinnamon bun doughs. by changing the extract flavor, you can make orange cinnamon buns, lemon cinnamon buns, whatever you like.

1. mix together sugar and enough cream to achieve a spreading consistency
2. add extract flavor of your choice and salt
3. to use: spread over warm biscuits or sweet bread still warm from the oven or drizzle over gingerbread cookies
4. this also makes a nice icing for quick breads like banana bread or zucchini bread
target.review: I glazed Recipe #285374 with this icing and it was awesome.  The rolls are great as is, but the icing just adds that little something extra.  I added in about 1 tsp. cinnamon, just to give it more flavor.  I will use this again often!!!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s shepherd s pie

quick and easy to prepare, even the kids love this one, because it's yummy!  this recipe will have you going back for a 2nd helping for sure... lol  it's addicting!

1. in a lg
2. frying pan cook the onion until almost done
3. add beef and stir , cooking until meat is cooked through
4. add a sprinkling of salt , pepper , and garlic powder over the top of the mixture
5. spoon mixture into a 9x13" baking pan
6. top with the 1 can of whole kernel corn , spreading across the meat mixture , then add the 2 cans of cream style corn
7. cook and mash the potatoes until smooth
8. add the mashed potatoes over the top of the casserole
9. dot with pats of butter all over the top
10. put in a 350f oven , and bake for 30 minutes or until top is lightly brown
demonstrations.review: This is such a great one to have when it's cold outside and you want to warm your insides and please your belly!  I loved the infusion of the creamed corn into the meat and the potatoes were so good on top.  Though the ingredients are simple, the mix of flavors in so delicious and addicting.  I had to stop myself from having a third dish!  This is totally comfort food for us, and it's a winner all the way into my favorites!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s chunky garlic mashed potatoes

oh man, these are a comfort food that goes with just about anything!  i have been known to eat them by themselves :)  this is definately one you will want to add to your recipe collection!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cut the top of the garlic bulb , and place on the middle rack in the oven
3. bake until bulbs start to pop out of the skins , about 20-25 minutes
4. after the garlic bulb is roasted in the oven , remove , and squeeze the bulb , and the garlic will pop out of each finger
5. put roasted garlic pieces into a dish , and mash , or chop up fine
6. set aside
7. meanwhile:
8. while the garlic is roasting , cook potatoes in a lg
9. pan , just covering with water for about 25 mins
10. , or until fork inserts easliy when inserted
11. drain well , put cover on , and set aside
12. to drained potatoes , add roasted garlic , butter , sour cream , salt , and pepper
13. mash with a hand masher
14. i use a rubber spatulda to break up potatoes a little more
15. you don't want them completely mashed like regular mashed potatoes
16. serve
demonstrations.review: These potatoes really made the meal last night for supper.  I had them with some baked fish and sauteed green beans.  The kids loved the change of pace from regular mashed potatoes, and each forkful was a piece of heaven in my mouth!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s spinach salad with the works

this delicious extra special and quick to prepare salad is a true treasure to serve anytime... great to serve when entertaining and you want to impress your guests!

1. snap off the woody ends of the asparagus and discard
2. take the rest of the asparagus , and cut them into 1" pieces
3. blanch them in boiling , salted water for a couple of minutes , until just crisp-tender
4. drain the asparagus , and plunge in cold water until completely cooled
5. drain again
6. meanwhile , for the dressing , blend together poppy seed dressing , orange peel , and orange juice
7. in a salad bowl combine the spinach , asparagus , artichokes , and strawberries
8. lightly toss with the dressing
9. place on serving plates , and garnish with toasted nuts , and cheese
demonstrations.review: I loved everything that was in this salad and it was such a nice change from the same ole same ole!  The dressing is excellent and really compliments all the flavors in the salad!  I plan to make this again for company coming over the weekend.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s lobster rangoon

i made these for an asian themed party at my house, and they were delish! crispy and full of flavor, these are sure to be a treat at your next social event!

1. put your cream cheese in a glass dish and microwave for 45 secs
2. chop your green onions finely , and add to cream cheese
3. add your lemon and garlic juice , and mix well
4. chop your lobster finely , or use the blender
5. add to cream cheese mixture , and mix in well
6. put 30 won ton wrappers onto a lg
7. flat baking pan , i used a cookie sheet
8. place a teaspoonful of mixture into the center of each won ton wrapper
9. mix the egg and 2 t
10. of water together well
11. with 2 fingers , dip into the egg wash then rub around the edge of each won ton
12. taking the bottom right
13. when all 30 won tons are done , put in the refrigerator for at least 2 hours
14. when ready to deep fry , heat your oil to 350 degrees f
15. turn on your oven to 200
16. drop 6 won tons in at a time and fry on one side , then flip and fry on the other
17. place on a layer of 4 paper towels to absorb grease , then place in an oven proof dish , and put in oven to keep warm while the next batch is cooking
18. serve with duck or plum sauce for dipping
demonstrations.review: I splurged and bought a lobster to make this.  I had friends coming over for a Chinese dinner and I wanted to have something different and special.  This fit the bill, as they were amazing!  I served with duck sauce to dip them in and we ate every last one before dinner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my copycat shrimp paesano

this is my copycat version of paesano's restaurant signature dish. you will love this garlic shrimp dish. paesano's restaurant is on the riverwalk in san antonio, texas.

1. pre-heat oven to 400 f
2. soak shrimp in half& half for 30 minutes
3. drain shrimp and dust lightly in flour
4. saut shrimp for 5 minutes on one side
5. you will have to do in batches so that you do not overcrowd
6. do not turn shrimp
7. remove shrimp and place in a baking dish , sautd side down , and place in pre-heated oven
8. turn to broil and broil for 5 minutes
9. meanwhile , mix egg yolk and lemon juice in half the butter and stir over low heat until butter is melted
10. take off heat
11. add garlic and remaining butter and return pan to heat
12. stir briskly until butter melts and sauce thickens
13. add chives and parsley
14. pool sauce in plates and top with shrimp
15. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I made this and was thrilled that it came out so wonderfully!  I loved the flavors and it was a big hit with my company as well.  I made wild rice pilaf and candied carrots on the side and it was a wonderful dinner all the way around!

target.recipe_text:
diana s chicken casserole

when my dad passed away, someone brought this to the house. my son loved this so much, i was glad to be able to get the recipe.

1. put the chicken breasts in a 9x13 inch glass baking dish
2. put a slice of lorraine cheese on each piece of chicken
3. mix the soup , water and stuffing together pour the stuffing mixture over the chicken
4. melt the stick of butter and drizzle over the top
5. bake , uncovered , for 1 hour at 375 degrees f
6. i like the onion and sage stuffing myself and this is what i used
target.review: made this use lower sodium soup didnt use any butter at all. like the crunchy top but was thinking of useing low sodium chicken broth to moisten th top instead of butter. sprinled poultry seasoning on the top

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops dijon

nan

1. trim excess fat from chops
2. spray a 10-inch skillet with nonstick spray coating
3. brown chops on both sides in hot skillet
4. remove chops
5. add onions
6. cook and stir over medium heat 3 minutes
7. push onions aside
8. return chops to skillet
9. combine mustard , dressing and pepper
10. spread over chops
11. cover
12. cook over medium-low heat 15 minutes or till meat is tender
demonstrations.review: made this last night, DH was in the shower getting ready for the gym,when he came into the kitchen saying what are u making smells great. this was easy fast and very tasty. when he got home from the gym he told me it was hard for him to leave and go to the gym. think this would be good over  chicken.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern baked spaghetti

this is an easy, yet very tasty spaghetti casserole, which reminds me of the spaghetti they used to serve us in elementary school. i loved their spaghetti! i normally only brought my lunch, but not on spaghetti day!

1. cook spaghetti per package direcions
2. combine milk and egg , mix well
3. combine drained spaghetti , milk and egg
4. mix well
5. pour spaghetti mixture into a buttered 9x13 inch casserole dish
6. brown ground beef with onion , bell pepper and garlic in a large skillet
7. drain
8. return drained meat back into the skillet and add seasonings
9. cook for 2 minutes
10. stir in tomato sauce and cook for 2 more minutes
11. spread meat mixture over spaghetti
12. sprinkle with cheese
13. bake at 425f for 10 minutes or until cheese melts and is bubbly
14. remove from oven and let stand for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: just finished eating this and ate way to much. As pass reviews served extra sauce on the side for those who wanted it. Used sargento bistro blend nacho and taco cheese has taco seasoning mixed with cheese. thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple easy chesapeake bay rosy crab soup from the farm

being from maryland, i know very well homemade crab soup. this is not that recipe. this is a very quick crab and tomato soup recipe that is used to finish extra crab meat off. being a base recipe, please use this to be creative with, adding or subtracting ingredients and adjusting seasonings for you and your families enjoyment.  i haven't used canned crab in this recipe, but feel free to try it!

1. melt butter in a soup pot until tender
2. add minced garlic , cook for 30 seconds on medium heat
3. stir in remaining ingredients , except crab until heated thoroughly
4. stir carefully , add crab meat , making sure not to break up crab chunks
5. serve in warmed bowls , adding croutons to float on top
demonstrations.review: live on the east coast love blue crabs and yeaterday we had 40 mile per hr wind gusts. started with base soup added chicken broth for water, only had fresh veggies on hand so carrots onions celery potatoes and some spinach use 2 tablespoons of old bay. had whole wheat rolls.used can crab even now fresh even now crabs are flown in. love the flavor and the taste let the winds blow. Andi just wanted to note always check out your recipes because i love the "stories " or tales that go with your recipes

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatballs and gravy  spaghetti sauce

we used to have this every wednesday.  this is essentially my grandma's recipe, i just add more cheese to the meatballs than she did.  sometimes i leave the neckbones out and add some italian sausage.

1. place ground beef , pork , bread crumbs , romano cheese , eggs , milk , seasoned salt and basil into a large bowl
2. mix well with hands
3. shape into 24 balls
4. brown meatballs in pan , making sure to keep a thin layer of water on the bottom of the pan at all times to prevent burning
5. while meatballs are cooking , start the gravy
6. brown onion lightly in olive oil in a large pot
7. add garlic and cook 1 or 2 minutes
8. add tomato paste and water
9. stir until tomato paste is thinned
10. add remaining ingredients and mix well
11. bring to a slow boil and reduce heat
12. when meatballs are done , add to sauce
13. simmer , covered loosely , over low heat about 2 hours , stirring frequently to prevent burning
14. if sauce is too thick water may be added
demonstrations.review: made this up for daughter who is having back surgryand askedfor meals for her recovery. made good amount of sauce used beef bones no pork. made double the amount of meatballs. now in freezer two pkgs fo 10 meatball and sauce for her house but 2 pkgs of 6 for my house,and used the sauce to make her a baked ziti. will re edit when everyone eats , but i also eats a meatball after making them cooks treat. thanks again

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fabulous beef stew

my family thinks this is fabulous, and that is all that matters. made in the slow cooker.

1. put all ingredients except cornstarch in a slow cooker on low heat for 6-8-10 hours
2. add 2 tablespoons of cornstarch mixed with water
3. turn heat to high and stir until thickened
demonstrations.review: ok started this out tomake for my daughter who is having back surgry friday and asked for cooked meals for her recovery.so i doubled the amt as to feed two houses mine and her's crock put wasnt big enough so had to use stove top. now there are those who would say this i shouldn't rate the recipe but it i'll go ahead I have never used lipton onion soup mix in beef stew and believe that is what amkes it fabulous. have 2 bags in freezer, cupfull in there to cover hubby and haveing two bowls tonight for dinner. thanks for a great recipe.will rerate when dear d eats hers.daughter loved hers so did we thanks again

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon biscuit blossoms

found this on the back of a pillsbury biscuit dough wrapper. these are so simple to put together. making biscuits blossom and look like flower petals, sprinkle cinnamon & sugar on top and a scant of jelly in the center. tasty!

1. heat oven to 375f
2. separate dough into 8 biscuits
3. make 5 cuts evenly around outside edge of each biscuit to resemble flower petals
4. place each biscuit flower on ungreased large cookie sheet
5. in small bowl , combine sugar and cinnamon
6. mix well
7. sprinkle sugar mixture over biscuits
8. with thumb , make deep indentation in center of each biscuit
9. fill each with scant teaspoon jelly
10. bake at 375f for 11 to 17 minutes or until golden brown
11. serve warm
target.review: These tasted pretty good. They definitely were easy to make! Unfortunately I didn't have Grands biscuits, so I used the regular smaller buttermilk bisquits I did have. I didn't cut down deep enough. My knife wasn't very sharp. I bet you could almost use a scissors though to do it. Also, I think as a result of the smaller biscuit, the preserves I used got a little runny because I couldn't press down too far. These are a good change if you don't like carmel or cinnamon rolls and want something just a little bit sweet for breakfast.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir grilled fish tacos

i tried these when visiting friends in san diego. they are so delicious and great when the weather gets warm. they shared the recipe with me but i don't know where it originates from--don't really care. just know it is good eatin'

1. put halibut chunks in a bowl
2. sprinkle with cajun seasoning and toss to coat
3. transfer halibut to a well-greased grill wok
4. stir-grill over hot coals for 8-10 minutes , tossing while cooking
5. in a big bowl , add cabbages
6. mix well
7. in a smaller bowl , add vinegar , sour cream , green onions , and salt
8. stir to combine
9. add dressing mixture to cabbage
10. toss to coat well
11. for each tortilla , fill with 1 / 3 cup cabbage mixture and 4-5 chunks of halibut
12. fold up and serve with lemon wedges , salsa , tartar sauce , guacamole , and a pitcher of margaritas
demonstrations.review: I kind of combined this recipe with one I found on another site. I used salmon. Instead of cajun seasoning, I used a smoked chili powder and a pinch of cayenne pepper. I really think 3 tsp would suffice. I cheated and used coleslaw in a bag. I used the cider vinegar, but not the sour cream. I also didn't have any green onions, so I used red onions. The other recipe I saw called for fresh cilantro, so I added that also. I was short on fish, but they still were excellent!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken chow mein

this is fresh-tasting and easy to make. i enjoy it much better than take-out.

1. in a large pot , saute celery in oil for apx 5 minutes or until crisp-tender
2. add bean sprouts , mushrooms , water chestnuts , and chicken
3. in a large bowl , blend cornstarch with water
4. when smooth , add chicken broth and soy sauce to bowl
5. mix well and pour over meat and vegetables
6. bring to a boil , stirring until sauce thickens
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover and simmer 10 to 15 minutes
9. serve over hot , cooked rice and chow mein noodles
demonstrations.review: Every time I use a recipe from this site, I ask my husband how many stars it deserves. This time he looked at me and said, "Well duh! I could eat this every week!" Pretty high compliments from him...Even my 10 month old ate some. I did change the recipe up a little bit to what I had in the cupboards and our likes. A whole package of celery seemed like a lot to me, so I used what I had in the fridge which amounted to a little more than a stalk. Since I used less celery, I added the whole can of bean sprouts I had. I also used fresh musrooms, as opposed to a can. This really seemed to make a difference to us. I ended up not having water chestnuts after finding out that my can had expired, so I added a half of onion instead, and it added a lot of flavor. I think you could also could add bamboo shoots if you want. I hadn't realized that my soy sauce had run out, so I didn't add any, but I added the rest of my 14 oz can of broth instead. To that I added a couple splashes of worchestershire sauce just to add a little bit of a salty flavor. We couldn't tell the difference to be honest. It was over all a very good and simple recipe, which is always necessary around this mad house! We will definitely be making this again at our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick soft breadsticks

our family likes these breadsticks because they are soft and chewy. i like to make them when i am in a hurry because they rise quickly.

1. make dough using your favorite method- bread machine , mixer or by hand
2. roll out into a 10x12 inch rectangle
3. cut into strips about 3 / 4 inch wide
4. give each strip a twist and place on a greased cookie sheet
5. let rise for at least 20 minutes or more if you have time
6. bake at 375 for 10-15 minutes
7. brush with butter and sprinkle with garlic salt and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: These were soooo good! Talk about easy if you've got a bread maker! They are so light and fluffy! I too cut them in half so they weren't so long. I even forgot them in my bread maker for about an extra half hour while making my soup, and they still turned out perfect...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken tortilla soup

this recipe has been a huge hit with everyone who has ever tried it. we make it almost weekly, and the leftovers are eaten immediately. it is also very healthy! it is a little spicy, so if you don't have too much of a tolerance for spicy foods, you may choose to leave out the seeds of the jalapeño. if you love spicy, like we do, extra cayenne pepper adds even more zing. enjoy!

1. saut onion , garlic , jalapeo and green pepper with olive oil in a large pot until soft
2. add all the rest of the ingredients to the large pot and bring to a boil
3. after about 15 minutes , remove the chicken breasts and shred
4. return shredded chicken to the pot and simmer an additional 45 minutes
5. serve , topped with crushed tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review: I love soup, and I think this is my absolute favorite type! It's so versatile, and you can do whatever you want to it and it still turns out awesome. Love how easy it is just throwing in the chicken. I used fresh corn, which made it a bit more fresh tasting. It was what I had. A lot of times we skip the tortillas on top and just eat it with quesadillas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
40 minute hamburger buns

homemade hamburger rolls with only a 10 minute rising time.  these are really good.  recipe from taste of home.

1. in a mixing bowl , dissolve yeast in warm water
2. add oil and sugar and let stand for 5 minutes
3. add the egg , salt and enough flour to form a soft dough
4. turn onto a floured surface and knead until smooth and elastic , about 3 to 5 minutes
5. do not let rise
6. divide into 12 pieces and shape each into a ball
7. place 3" apart on greased baking sheets
8. cover and let rest for 10 minutes
9. bake at 425 for 8 to 12 minutes or until golden brown
10. remove from pans to wire rack to cool
demonstrations.review: These were awesome!!! I couldn't believe how easy they were to make and how close they came out to being from my bakery section at the grocery store. The next day they were less grocery store quality, but who cares, they hardly made it past day one, they were that good...My husband said the worst part about them was that the recipe didn't make more....I thought they were great the next day with left over pulled turkey and mayo. Reminded me of my Grandma's! Thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
extremely soft white bread   bread machine

this is the softest white bread i have ever baked.  it was sent to me via email and i cannot remember who sent it.  this is the only recipe i use for white bread.

1. put your hot water , yeast and sugar in your bread machine
2. let stand 6-12 minutes depending on the temp of your water
3. your yeast will foam
4. add remaining ingredients
5. use rapid or basic white cycles
6. or bake for 25 minute @ 350
target.review: I've been experimenting with different white bread (BM)recipes for awhile now and this is the winner. I meant to review this bread the first time I made it (2 months ago). It's perfect for my needs... lunchbox sandwiches. It's soft but not too soft and easy to slice once cooled. The two things I do differently are reduce the loaf size to 3/4 (.75) and reduce the yeast to 1 t. (so it fits in my bread slicer afterwards). I have made this bread twice a week since I found the recipe and will continue to do so. Thanks, TKDLVR, for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple meatloaf bursting with flavor

a simple and flavorful meatloaf recipe that is so easy to make!

1. preheat the oven to 350 and spray the meatloaf pan with olive oil
2. mix all of the meatloaf ingredients in a large bowl
3. transfer the meatloaf mixture into the pan
4. poke several holes through the meatloaf to help it thoroughly cook
5. place in the oven and cook for 1 hour
6. mix together the 3 ingredients for the sauce
7. cover the meatloaf with the sauce
8. put back into the oven and cook for 30 minutes
9. slice into 4 - 6 portions and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I went searching for a meatloaf recipe using ingredients I had on hand at the moment and this was the winner.  WOW!!  Delicious!  All 4 boys came back for seconds. I'll double the recipe next time so there will be leftovers. Followed the recipe exactly.  Thanks for posting, Herndons.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply awesome baked pork chops

tender and delicious!!

1. brown chops in butter
2. place in baking dish
3. sprinkle with soup mix
4. pour cream over all
5. bake , tightly covered , at 375 for 45 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: I've been making this recipe for a few years now and have neglected to review this amazing dish! A definite go-to for me as I always have the ingredients on hand and it always comes out perfect. Thanks Inez for another winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dee s pork chops casserole

yummy moist pork chops and pototoes that take no time at all to prepare. my young daughter loves this meal.

1. spray a 13x9 inch pan with cooking spray
2. slice potatoes and lay in the bottom of the pan
3. lay pork chops on top of potatoes
4. pour soup over potatoes and chops
5. sprinkle with onion soup mix
6. cover with foil and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
7. remove foil and bake another 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good! And easy. I used Cream of Onion soup (I usually sub this for Cream of Mushroom) and added a little milk, per other reviewers. I also kept it covered the entire time as I used thin pork chops (6 of them). Steamed broccoli on the side and you have a lovely dinner! I'll be making this again. Thanks for sharing this recipe. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken broccoli alfredo soup

here's a scrumptious soup served at dairy keen (three-time "best of state" winner) of heber city, utah. this is a recipe i've not had long, but have made over and over and over again. it is that good!

1. in a heavy stockpot over medium heat , saut onion and garlic in butter for 2-3 minutes
2. add flour and cook , stirring , for another 2-3 minutes until bubbly
3. gradually whisk in chicken broth and half & half
4. cook , stirring frequently , until thickened
5. meanwhile , in a separate pan , add water to broccoli and bring just to boiling then remove from heat
6. do not drain cooking water from broccoli
7. add parmesan cheese to soup-base in stockpot
8. cook over low heat , stirring , just until cheese is melted
9. add cooked broccoli along with its cooking water , chicken , seasonings , and bow tie pasta to the stockpot
10. heat through
11. also , decrease the salt by half if you happen to substitute full-sodium chicken broth in this recipe
demonstrations.review: This is SO good! I was wondering what to make for dinner tonight  and I happened to have all the ingredients for this... and it was a huge hit with the family, even the super picky husband. I will be making this often! Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy bean soup with kale

we've all heard how anti-oxidants fight cancer, save eyesight, and prevent clogged arteries. turns out lutein, a delicious 7 mg dose of which is supplied with each serving of this recipe, is even more beneficial than beta carotene. it delays lung aging and combats arthritis to boot! who knew improving your health could be so quick and easy, and taste so good? try it -- you'll see!
p.s. since i felt this lacked enough elements to chew on, i've been adding canned, sliced carrots (fast, easy & healthy!) for quite a while, and thought i'd update the recipe. also, sometimes i add another can of beans, for the same reason. glad so many of you have been enjoying this. there's a container in my frig right now - yum!

1. in a large pot , heat olive oil
2. add garlic and onion
3. saute until soft and the onion is transparent
4. wash the kale , leaving small droplets of water
5. saute , stirring , until wilted and a lovely emerald green , about 15 minutes
6. add 3 cups of the broth , reserving 1 cup , 2 cups of the beans , reserving 1 cup , all of the carrots , tomatoes , herbs , salt and pepper
7. simmer 5 minutes
8. in a blender or food processor , mix the reserved beans and broth until smooth
9. stir into the soup to thicken it nicely
10. simmer 15 more minutes
11. ladle into bowls
12. sprinkle with chopped parsley and shredded parmesan
13. serve with a nice loaf of crusty bread to soak up all the yummy broth !
14. for vegetarian use the vegetable broth
demonstrations.review: Delicious!! I've been trying to find ways to add kale to my diet and this soup is perfect. I've made it a few times now. Once I added diced chicken. Another time I doubled the amount of kale. And another time I used kidney beans instead of cannellini. Each time the flavor was wonderful. I'll make this again and again. Thanks for posting!!

target.recipe_text:
roasted kielbasa   potatoes

another recipe from mom. these are good and easy to throw together.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. mix all ingredients in a large bowl
3. pour into a 9x13" baking pan
4. cook in oven , covered with foil for approximately 1 hour
5. you can stir after 1 / 2 hour of cooking
target.review: This was so delicious and easy, I didn't want to cook since I worked a long day so I looked for something simple my son would enjoy. We had all these ingridents on hand; just added a little garlic powder and Johnny's to the batch before baking. I did have to increase the cook time. Served with some Pillsbury Cinnamon Rolls and a hard boiled egg. Definetly on hand for late night dinners from now on.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast
