5. top sandwich with lettuce
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Best egg salad sandwich on Zaar - I have either tried the others, or did not have all the ingredients asked for. This is simple enough to make with items that are always in my fridge. I saw another reviewer had added chopped celery, so I did that, and was quite pleased. I like relish so I tried that after tasting it first without the relish - and found that it's not bad, either way. I like the crispiness of the celery combined with the softness of the eggs.  Added recipe #51649 and about 1 teaspoon leftover powdered sugar from another recipe I made off Zaar (#88812).  Don't like mustard, but this was  the right amount to make it taste good.  Awesome!

target.recipe_text:
my nana s curried sausages

have had this since i was wee.  it is a great meal on a wintery night. (or any other night)

1. grill the sausages
2. slice and set aside
3. in a pot melt some butter and fry sliced onions
4. once cooked , add first measure of water
5. season to taste
6. mix together the remaining ingredients and add to the pot to thicken
7. add the sausages to heat through
8. serve with creamy mashed potato and seasonal vegetables
target.review: Fantastic had these for dinner last night very easy to put together would be an easy weeknight meal.  I boiled my sausages to as it was easier for me.  DH enjoyed these he love curry.  Made for Ed'n 9: MAKE MY RECIPE- Tag game in the Aust/NZ forum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy herb and garlic chicken over gnocchi

this is a very quick and easy recipe to throw together, it tastes great and makes for a wonderful after work dinner or great mid week meal when you want no fuss. you can make your own gnocchi if you prefer, but for quickness of this recipe i used fresh store bought gnocchi, you can find this in the fresh pasta section of most supermarkets. for those of you who have never eaten gnocchi before or do not know what it is, a quick explanation is basically italian dumplings, made from either potato, semolina or flour.

1. sprinkle combined garlic and parsley on both sides of all the breasts
2. heat some olive oil in a large frying pan and cook chicken , uncovered , about 20 minutes or until cooked through
3. meanwhile pour some water in a pan add a little olive oil and bring to the boil
4. while you are waiting for the water to boil , add a little oil to another saucepan , add garlic , cook , stirring , about 1 minute , add wine to pan , to deglaze , evaporate all liquid , add lemon juice and the stock , stir
5. pour cream in and bring to the boil
6. reduce heat to a simmer , simmer uncovered , about 5 min's until sauce thickens slightly
7. stir in oregano , keep warm over a low heat while you cook the gnocchi
8. once the water is boiling add gnocchi and cook as per packet instructions , mine was only 3 minutes
9. drain
10. while gnocchi is cooking remove breasts from pan , cut chicken into slices
11. to serve: divide gnocchi among serving plates , top with sliced chicken , drizzle with sauce
demonstrations.review:
this was a winner in my house.  Found out that DH will eat Gnocchi which is good something else he will eat.  He is a hard man to feed and he really like this slowy widening his tastes :)
thanks heaps.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger rice skillet

one dish meal with a taco twist.
from southern living magazine

1. cook first 3 ingredients in a large skillet over medium-high heat , stirring until beef crumbles and is no longer pink
2. drain
3. stir in tomato and green chiles and next 4 ingredients
4. cook , covered , over medium heat for 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and cook 15 more minutes
6. remove from heat
7. sprinkle lettuce and next 5 ingredients over hamburger mixture
8. stand tortilla chips around edge of skillet
9. serve with chips and salsa
demonstrations.review:
Wow,  This was fantastic.  I loved it.  I made it with corn chips not Tortilla chips as i was not sure what they were and tasty grated cheese as i don't think you can get mexican blend cheese in oz.  I did have to cook it for a bit longer and add more water as i did not have a lid that fitted the frypan i was using.
I will be making it again.  
I made this for PAC fall 2007

demonstrations.recipe_text:
calypso island coffee

a few cups of this and you'll be hearing the islands steel drums in your kitchen!

1. combine your frangelico , gourmet coffee and malibu rum
2. add chocolate and stir to melt
3. add sugar then top with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: This is a 10 * coffee. Yummo. Used the last of my Frangelico on this one will have to go and get more so i can have this wonderful after dinner drink again. I will be making this one again and again.  Made for JUNE/JULY Beverage Tag: How Does Your Garden Grow? Thanks Heaps

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat lemon chicken

i found this recipe in the jolly cook cookbook.  the chicken is coated in a flour mixture and baked instead of fried.  then serve with a delightful lemon sauce poured over the chicken.

1. heat oven to 450 degrees f
2. spray a baking sheet with nonstick cooking spray
3. cut each chicken breast in half
4. mix flour , baking soda and cayenne pepper in a plastic bag
5. combine egg whites and water in a medium bowl and mix well
6. add chicken a few pieces at a time and turn to coat on all sides
7. remove chicken from egg mixture and place in bag with flour
8. seal and shake to lightly coat each piece of chicken
9. place on baking sheet and bake uncovered for about 20-25 minutes or until chicken is cooked through
10. prepare sauce when chicken is almost done baking
11. heat all sauce ingredients in a small saucepan until it reaches a light boil , stirring occasionally
12. combine the cornstarch and cold water and mix well
13. gradually add cornstarch mixture to the sauce
14. cook , stirring constantly until thickened
15. additional cornstarch / water can be added if a thicker sauce is desired
16. cut each chicken breast digonally into about 5 or 6 slices
17. pour lemon sauce over chicken and serve
demonstrations.review:
This is a great recipe.  I asked my bf how many stars and he said more than 5 stars this is fantastic better than from the chinese takeaway.  So I was chuffed 
Thanks for the great recipe crafly lady 
made for CUPID'S CHOICE BEVY TAG feb 08

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best blondies ever

these are easy to bake and taste delicious!!

you can substitute flour and baking soda for self-raising flour .
and you can use white chocolate chips instead of butterscotch chips!

1. preheat oven to 350 f or 180c grease 16x16 inch pan
2. beat butter and sugar in bowl
3. add flour , soda , powder and salt then mix
4. press into pan then bake for about 20 minutes
5. cool , cut into square slabs and enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
These didn't work out for me.  I only made half a batch as i thought 16x16 inch pan is huge it wouldn't even fit in my oven.  Also the directions had ingredients missing.  it didn't tell me when to put in the eggs, vanilla and butterscotch chips.  
thanks  made for spring 09 pac.

target.recipe_text:
ground beef sukiyaki

this is one of dh's faves. i have cooked this many times for company and get raves. it looks like a lot of work, reading the recipe, but it is easy easy. we don't like water chestnuts or bamboo shoots, so i omit them. i have had this recipe forever, but it looks like i must have found it on an a.1. bottle or ad. i tried it with other steak sauces, but we didn't like it. the recipe says 8 servings, but the 2 of us finish it off with no trouble.

1. in large skillet , brown beef until crumbly
2. in small bowl , mix sugar , soy sauce , a-1 , and salt
3. set aside
4. drain mushrooms , reserving liquid
5. when meat is cooked , mix in vegetables
6. add sauce
7. simmer 3 minutes , or until vegetables are just tender crisp
8. combine cornstarch and reserved mushroom liquid
9. stir into sukiyaki
10. cook just until thickened
11. serve over rice
target.review: I made this last weekend and it makes plenty!  Really easy to make and very tasty!  I used Garlic A-1 - since we can't get enought garlic!  Didn't have any celery on hand, but used the chestnuts and bamboo shoots and it was really good!  Will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy red beans   rice with sausage

this recipe is a one dish meal. it's so easy to throw together and the cooking time just depends on the kind of rice you use. the flavor is great and this is easy to modify should you need to.

1. cut sausage into 1 / 2 inch pieces
2. lightly brown
3. add vegetables
4. simmer 5-7 minutes
5. add remaining ingredients and bring to a boil
6. reduce to simmer , cover with a tight fitting lid , and cook until rice is done
7. try one of the seasonings such as tony cachere's or emeril's cajun seasoning
8. sorry for any miscommunication
demonstrations.review: This was really good and easy to make on a busy weeknight!  I ended up using about 1 1/2 cups rice, then let it simmer for exactly 20 minutes and it was perfect!  Hubby loved it!  Says I HAVE to make it again!  Thanks for sharing it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry swirl cheesecake pie

i got this recipe off the back of a ready crust pie crust. it takes 5 minutes prep time and is fabulous! a great last minute company dessert to whip up! sure to impress!

1. beat cream cheese until fluffy
2. gradually beat in sweetened condensed milk , until smooth , add egg and 3 tablespoons lemon juice , mix well
3. pour half the batter into the crust
4. combine remaining 1 teaspoon lemon juice with preserves in a bowl
5. spoon half the preserves over batter
6. pour remaining batter on top
7. using a knife , swirl remaining preserves into a decorative pattern
8. bake at 300f for 55 minutes
9. cool
10. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: This was so quick to prepare and tasted fabulous!  I substituted lime juice for lemon and it tasted great!  If I start it right when I get home from work, then it's done and sufficiently chilled for me to have a piece that same evening!  Can't beat that!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate kahlua pound cake

very rich, decadent. a dessert worthy of a special occasion. i have been making this for many years, i got the original recipe from a duncan hines/puritan oil leaflet.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix all the ingredients and beat for 4 minutes
3. bake in a greased bundt pan fo 50 minutes
4. let cool for 10 minutes before icing
5. icing prep: heat the butter , sugar and milk
6. boil for 2 minutes stirring constantly
7. remove from heat and rapidly stir in chocolate chips , immediately pour over cake
demonstrations.review: I made this with Godiva cappuccino liqueur in place of the kahlua and bourbon - oh yum!!  I've made it for several parties and for work a couple of of times - it's easy to make and sooooo GOOD!  Thanks Maggie 0507!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german nudelsalat  noodle salad

posted by request - instructions, american equivalents to german products and measurements by heatherfeather. thank you so much!

1. mix ingredients for the dressing and mix well with cooked noodles
2. check the seasonings& adjust the flavor as needed after it chilled , and might even add a little extra remoulade or yogurt , if needed , tomorrow
3. it certainly does drink up the dressing quickly !
demonstrations.review: Made this for a family reunion - it was gone pretty quickly!  Next time I think I'll chill the salad and add the dressing right before I serve it - it really does soak it up!  It didn't really get dried out, but wasn't as moist as I wanted - but still really good!  Easy to make and makes a ton!  Perfect for a potluck!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory shrimp dip

this is so simple and easy to make for parties! they will think you spent hours!! it will be our little secret :) enjoy!

1. combine 1 / 2 the shrimp and the remaining ingredients in blender or electric mixer
2. blend until fluffy and smooth
3. coarsely chop remaining shrimp
4. fold into mixture
5. refrigerate
6. enjoy with chips or crackers !
demonstrations.review: So easy and so yummy!  I didn't pay enough attention to the recipe, so I didn't chop up the shrimp, but they were those little baby canned shrimp, so it wasn't that big a deal.  The group I made this for literally inhaled it!

target.recipe_text:
pan fried tofu with spicy peanut sauce

a tasty snack or appetizer. tofu cubes are very crispy outside, yet warm and soft inside. sort of like asian 

1. drain tofu
2. cut into bite-sized cubes
3. toss with cornstarch , coating the cubes
4. sprinkle a little salt and pepper
5. heat some oil
6. fry the tofu cubes in batches , making sure all sides are lightly browned
7. drain on paper towels , then sprinkle with salt and pepper if desired
8. sauce: heat the milk in small saucepan
9. add peanut butter , stirring well
10. add other seasonings , according to personal taste
11. if you use coconut milk , add 1 / 2 - 1 tsp of lime juice too - it will be great !
12. serve hot , as a snack or appetizer
13. sometimes i serve them with a sweet chinese dessert: green bean soup
target.review: Delicious peanut sauce, though it isn't very peanut-y.  More of a mild hot sauce.  This could be VERY hot if it wasn't for the milk base, so a great flavor!  I may add more peanut butter next time (I used smooth).  I was just throwing this together, but I had a fairly hard time coating the cubes with cornstarch, it seemed to clump.  I figured the moisture from the tofu would help it adhere, but I think it did the opposite.  Next time I will make sure to squeeze out more moisture and also pat it dry with paper towel.  Very tasty and healthy!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy chocolate pudding

this smooth, rich pudding, lower in fat than many recipes, has many variations. for chocolate almond, chocolate rum, or chocolate mint pudding, simply add either 1/4 tsp almond or rum extract, or 2 drops of peppermint extract along with the vanilla. yum!

1. in a medium saucepan , combine cornstarch , cocoa , and sugar
2. mix well
3. gradually add milk , stirring to dissolve cornstarch and cocoa
4. cook over medium heat , stirring , until mixture comes to a boil
5. continue to cook 2 to 3 minutes , stirring ,
6. remove from heat and stir in vanilla
7. spoon pudding into 4 custard cups
8. chill
demonstrations.review: This is delicious! I took a few suggestions from the other comments, so I made it exactly as it says (scaled down to 1 serving) but added a dash of cinnamon, a little extra splenda, and about 1/8 tsp of espresso powder.  It came out great, especially with the Cool Whip on top.  And it is surprising how mild the nutrition facts are, it seems so indulgent.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted red bell pepper pasta

in los angeles, my cousin made variations of this every single night and it is the best combination of flavors for a pasta that i have ever had! everyone i have made it for has begged me to make it again and again... but always use shredded parmesan! (great with french bread)

1. heat olive oil on medium to high heat in large skillet or wok
2. add mushrooms , onions and all seasonings and saute for 15 to 20 minutes
3. meanwhile , slice roasted red bell peppers as desired
4. add the peppers to onions and mushrooms and continue to saute for another 5 minutes
5. cook pasta and drain
6. toss contents of skillet in with pasta and the parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  I don't think I had 3 cups of mushrooms so I added broccoli and shelled edamame to the sauteeing onions and mushrooms.  I also added some minced garlic.  I thought I had penne, alas I had to use Elbows and cooked way too much pasta, so I didn't add all of it (I say that because 1 lb of elbows is a lot more than 1 lb of penne, so adjust accordingly).  Lots of leftovers!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ginger marinated tuna steaks

tuna steaks with asian flair.

1. in a small bowl , combine all ingredients except tuna
2. place tuna steaks in a plastic ziploc type bag
3. add marinade to bag and seal
4. set bag in a shallow pan
5. refrigerate for 30 minutes , turning bag occasionally to coat
6. lightly coat the grill rack with nonstick cooking spray
7. drain tuna and discard marinade
8. grill fish for 10 ro 12 minutes or until fish flakes with a fork , turning once
demonstrations.review: Just great! You can make this straight in a ziploc bag and save yourself washing the bowl. I added a little sriracha into the marinade for spice and refrigerated for about 1.5 hours. Pan fried for a few minutes and it's all done! Super simple and tasty. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deliciously spicy pumpkin bread

this is a recipe i've adapted over years and years until it was 'just right' (to my taste, anyway).

1. in large bowl , cream butter for 1 minute
2. add sugar and beat for 4 minutes longer or until light and fluffy
3. beat in eggs
4. in separate bowl , whisk together pumpkin , orange zest and juice
5. in third bowl , whisk together flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and spices
6. stir one-third of the flour mixture into the butter mixture
7. mix in half the pumpkin mixture
8. add another one-third flour mixture and remaining pumpkin mixture
9. sprinkle with remaining flour mixture , raisins and / or nuts
10. mix
11. spoon batter into greased 8- x 4- inch loaf pan
12. tap pan lightly on counter to remove air bubbles
13. bake in 350f oven for 55 to 60 minutes or until loaf is well risen and golden and tester inserted in center comes out clean
14. transfer pan to wire rack and let stand for 5 minutes
15. topping: remove loaf from pan , transfer to rack
16. brush butter over top of cake
17. combine sugar and cinnamon
18. sprinkle over cake
19. let cool completely
demonstrations.review: I made these as muffins and everyone loved them! I used pureed fresh pumpkin instead of the canned and pumpkin pie spice instead of all the other spices.  I didn't make the topping for it, but did stir in chocolate chips instead of raisins.  Made 12 muffins and baked for 30 minutes.  Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin bread pudding  low fat

a delicious autumn dessert. serve this either warm or cold with yogurt dessert sauce. this recipe comes from the new american diet cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. lightly oil a 2-quart casserole dish and set aside
3. crumble the bread by hand or food processor to make bread crumbs
4. combine the egg substitute , milk , pumpkin , brown sugar , cinnamon , spices and vanilla
5. fold in raisins and bread crumbs
6. pour mixture into prepared casserole and set dish in larger baking dish which has been partially filled with hot water
7. bake 1 hours or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Perfect! We halved the recipe, used fresh pumpkin puree, and a fluffy white, crusty bread.  Other than that, we followed the recipe exactly and I wouldn't change a thing! Topped it all off with some chopped pecans and cool whip!

target.recipe_text:
barley   rice pilaf from company s coming

this is an amazing recipe.  not only is it great as a side dish, it's terrific all on its own.  feel free to change up the vegetables.  because of my love for onions.....i tend to cut them into large chunks.   this makes a large amount, but i usually cut it in half.  freezes well too!  slightly different from others already posted.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. heat 1 tbsp of oil in a large frying pan on medium heat
3. add celery , onion and garlic and cook for 5 - 10 minutes or until the onion has softened to your liking -- or not :)
4. transfer to a 3 quart casserole dish
5. heat the remaining tablespoon of oil in the same frying pan , and add the barley and rice
6. heat and stir for about 5 minutes , or until the grains start to turn golden brown
7. add this to the onion mixture , along with the water , carrots , bouillon , parsley and pepper
8. stir well
9. bake , covered , for about 2 hours or until the barley is tender and liquid absorbed
target.review: This was a wonderful side dish!!! It was delicious and nice to know it's as healthy as it was tasty!! Will definitely be a keeper, that I will make over and over again. It did make too much for the two of us and I will half the recipe next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach melba ice cream pie

this is wonderful on a hot summer day.  make sure to allow time to refreeze.

1. heat oven to 325
2. lightly butter a 9-inch pie pan
3. put cookie crumbs , butter , sugar , cinnamon and nutmeg in medium bwl
4. toss with fork to moisten
5. press into pie pan
6. bake just until crust is set and golden , about 10 minutes
7. remove
8. cool on wire rack
9. strain peaches over bowl
10. reserve juice
11. coarsely chop peaches
12. put ice cream in large bowl
13. using wooden spoon , mix in drained peaches and 1 / 4 cup of the reserved juice
14. spoon into pie shell
15. lightly cover with plastic wrap
16. freeeze until firm
17. remove from freezer
18. spoon melted jam over top
19. arrange raspberries in concentric circles in decorative pattenr to cover top
20. return to freezer
21. freeze until firm , several hour , or up to one week
22. to serve , remover from freezer 15 minutes before slicing
23. cut with knife that has been dipped in hot water
demonstrations.review: This pie was really pretty and tasty. I usually hating reviews that change the original recipe so much, but this benefited from a few changes. My cookie crust was to dry, so I looked up how much butter most cookie pie crusts have and went with that , which is 6 Tbl. Turned out good. Also, no info. on how to melt jam, so put it in the microwave for 30 seconds, it thinned out to a good consistency to drizzle, as photo shows, Added frozen raspberries randomly. I'm going to make it again, but will use frozen peaches chopped up and some peach nectar if needed. for a more peachy flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stir fried shrimp in garlic sauce

this has a great garlic flavor and tastes delicious with or without the heaters!

1. in a small bowl , mix together chicken broth , vinegar , soy sauce , sesame oil , chile paste and sherry
2. set aside
3. in another small bowl or cup , stir together the tbsp of cornstarch with the 3 tbsp of water and set aside
4. heat the oil over medium-high heat in a wok
5. add ginger and garlic and sizzle briefly , then add vegetables and thai chilies
6. stir-fry vegetables for approximately 3 minutes , then add the shrimp
7. cook the shrimp 2 minutes or until it curls and turns opaque or pink
8. add the sauce mixture and cook 1 minute more
9. then stir in the thickener and stir-fry until mixture thickens , about 1 minute
10. serve with hot cooked rice
demonstrations.review: Delicious recipe!!!! My hubby and I were so very pleased. Took leftovers to his restaurant to share. I used bok choy, rainbow carrots, red bell pepper, fresh mushrooms, celery & green onions. Very pretty dish. I chose to serve it over spaghetti noodles, which I had stirred in sesame oil, soy sauce and black sesame seeds

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashion berry cobbler

very good served slightly warm with ice cream and recipe has been in family for over 100 years

1. cream butter and sugar together , then add milk on slow speed
2. sift dry ingredients together and add to wet a couple of tablespoon at a time , until smooth
3. batter should be very thick paste , turn out into greased 13 x 9 x 2 inch pan , put berries on top of batter , sprinkle with remaining 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , and pour 2 1 / 2 cups boiling water over top , dot with remaining 3 tbsp butter
4. bake at 425f for 30 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved this dessert. I read the reviews and also used less sugar and boiling water at the last step,on account I also use frozen berries. I thought it was strange putting the batter on the bottom. But what a fun surprise to keep peeking in and seeing the dough rise up through the fruit. It was delicious and fun to make. Can't wait to make another, and change up the fruit. I used 1 1/2 c raspberries and 1 1/2 blackberries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swiss  ham  potato soup

one of my most requested 

1. cook diced potatoes in saucepan with just enough water to cover
2. when tender , drain the liquid from the potatoes and save
3. set both aside while making roux
4. in large saucepan , melt margarine
5. saute the chopped green onions until tender
6. remove onion from pan and set aside
7. add flour to melted margarine and stir until incorporated
8. cook over medium heat until the roux begins to just turn a golden color
9. using a whisk , stir in 2 cups of milk and 1 cup of the saved potato liquid
10. whisk until smooth and no lumps are seen
11. bring just to a boil or until the soup thickens
12. add the diced ham , cooked onion and the swiss cheese
13. stir until cheese is melted
14. add salt& pepper to your preference
15. i usually add 1 tsp
16. salt and 1 / 2 tsp
17. pepper
18. stir well
19. if soup is too thick , you may add the final cup of milk
20. my bunch likes it thick
demonstrations.review: I was hesitant to try this only because Swiss cheese is not one of my favorite cheeses either, but do enjoy with a few things, ham being one of them so I gave it a whirl. I used baby Swiss and snuck in a piece of muenster. It is so delicious. Thank you for sharing this yummy soup!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick and creamy new england clam chowder

this is the best chowder i've ever had. i've had chowder at legal seafoods in boston, which i have to say is good, but mine is better! if you like thick chowder, you'll love this one!!

1. add bacon to sauce pan and cook on medium low heat until crispy
2. add onion and cook until translucent
3. add clam juice from both cans
4. add potatoes
5. cook and cover until potatoes are fork tender , about 15-20 minutes
6. stir occasionally so potatoes won't stick
7. add clams , soup , cream , milk , and dill weed
8. stir together
9. add butter and let melt into the chowder
10. cook for about 30-45 minutes or until thickened
11. stir occasionally
demonstrations.review: The best clam chowder recipe, that I have tried yet, and I have tried so many that I have been disappointed with. This is a keeper and I will make it over and over again. I followed a few of the other reviewers comments and added some diced celery, which I cooked with the bacon. I also prefer half & half instead of heavy cream. I left the dill out, but that is a matter of preference. Oops forgot I added a bottle of clam juice

target.recipe_text:
walnut chicken

this recipe was found on the net and posted by request. original recipe was from helen chen's "peking cuisine". you can also use shrimp in place of chicken.

1. add marinade ingredients to chicken and mix well
2. marinate for 10 minutes
3. while marinating chicken mix together the sauce ingredients
4. set aside
5. heat wok on high with the oil
6. add the garlic and stir for a few seconds
7. add the chicken and cook to 80% done
8. reduce heat to medium and add the sauce , giving it a good stir
9. cook for 1 minute
10. add the walnuts and sesame oil
11. cook for 1 minute more
12. remove from heat and serve with rice and veggies
target.review: This tasted just like what you would eat in a Chinese restaurant!  Very nice!  The only change I made was to marinate the chicken for 30 min instead of 10 min (at room temp) to make sure the chicken would be tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef kurmah  curried beef

this is a malay curry and it is really good as it can be frozen.

1. heat half the oil in a pan add steak in batches and brown all over , remove from pan
2. heat remaining oil in the same pan add spring onions , garlic and ginger and cook until spring onions are soft
3. add the coriander , cumin , star anise , cinnamon , cloves , cardamom and lemon grass cooking and stirring for about 3 minutes
4. return the meat to the pan add coconut milk and chili and simmer covered for about 1 to 1 / 2 hours until meat is tender
5. add the nuts and stir until heated through
6. discard cinnamon , cardamom before serving
demonstrations.review: This tasted pretty close to the real thing (we live in Singapore).  I used dried (flakes) coriander instead of ground.  I simmered the beef for about 2 hrs, and discarded afterwards the cinnamon and star anise, but not the cardamom.  My only suggestions are that you add a bit of sea salt or fine salt to enhance the taste, reduce the powdered almonds to 30g because the sauce becomes a bit too thick, and you can use chili flakes instead of the red chili.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef with mustard glaze

i cut this out of my newspaper years ago and prefer it to many others i have tried over the years.

1. rinse corned beef cut in cold water , place in a large , heavy pot and add cold water to cover
2. add peppercorns , bay leaves , onion studded with 4 cloves , garlic , carrot and celery
3. bring to a boil over medium-high heat and skim off any foam that rises to the surface
4. reduce heat to low , cover pot and barely simmer until the beef is tender , about three hours
5. while beef cooks , turn it over every 30 minutes
6. let meat cool in cooking water about 15 min
7. preheat oven to 350 degrees and transfer drained beef to a shallow roasting pan , fat side up
8. whisk together the mustards in a small , heavy saucepan
9. stir in remaining glaze ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes , stirring constantly
10. spread glaze evenly over top of brisket
11. bake in center of the oven , basting every 15 minutes , until heated through and beef has a deep , rich color , about 20 to 30 minutes
12. let meat rest for about 10 minutes
13. slice it across the grain and serve
demonstrations.review: I thought this recipe was great!  It's just what I have been looking for because I want to cook the corned beef by itself without potatoes.  The meat is very tender and tasty.  And the glaze is not overpowering.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
deep dish apple pie with its own crust

avoid having to make the pie crust with this fantastic tasting apple pie. serve warm with a big scoop of vanilla ice cream. heaven!

1. fill a 9" pie pan 3 / 4 full of peeled apple slices
2. combine sugar and cinnamon and sprinkle over apples
3. combine the rest of the ingredients and pour over apples
4. keep topping 2" from edge of pan
5. bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe twice.  The 2nd time around I used 5 red apples and a deep dish 9" pie pan, which made the pie taste more like an old-fashioned apple pie.  This recipe tastes much better than apple crisp/crumble.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna macaroni salad

as a teenager, my son loved this. he's grown now and still loves it. cook time is the chill time.

1. cook macaroni as directed on package
2. drain and rinse in cold water
3. combine macaroni , cheese , tuna , pickles and onion in large bowl
4. stir together salad dressing , salt , pepper and garlic
5. pour over macaroni mixture and toss
6. cover
7. chill at least 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I chose this recipe because my kids don't like red/green peppers and celery in their salad.  I also had to use one and a half cups leftover cooked chicken instead of the tuna.  But it tasted great!  The cubed cheddar cheese (I used 'tasty' cheddar) adds a nice contrast to the sweet gherkins.  Delicious and different!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate almond cake with chocolate almond cream cheese fr

a chocolate-y, decadent, rich cake with a silky, heavenly frosting all accented with a touch of almond. eat it and weep! adapted from a recipe by anne byrn out of her cake mix doctor book. soooo gooood!

1. oven@ 350 degrees
2. combine the cake ingredients and mix with a whisk
3. pour into 2 round 8 or 9-inch cake pans which have been lined with greased aluminum foil or parchment paper
4. bake for 28-30 minutes or until toothpick comes out clean when inserted
5. let cool in pans for 10 minutes before turning out
6. meanwhile combine the frosting ingredients and beat until fluffy with a hand-mixer
7. when cake layers are completely cool , frost the top part of the bottom layer
8. place second layer over the frosted layer
9. finish by frosting top layer and sides of cake
demonstrations.review: I used 2 eight inch pans and had a big crack in each cake layer by the time baking was finished.  Maybe the nine inch pans are more suitable.  The cake and frosting tasted nice, but given the choice and time, I would still prefer to make a homemade chocolate cake.

target.recipe_text:
barilla no boil lasagna

this is the best lasagna ever!! the noodles are so nice and thin and there is no preboiling!! i will never purchase any other lasagna other than barilla. i've been making this now for 3 years and everyone agrees--the recipe makes the very best! the instructions are right on the back of the lasagna box. i usually make multiple batches and freeze them. its a great housewarming or "new baby" meal for a friend!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. in bowl , combine beaten eggs , ricotta cheese and two cups of the mozzarella cheese and parmesan
3. if you choose not to use the parmesan , just add more mozzarella
4. set aside
5. in a 13x9x3 pan , spread 1 cup of sauce on bottom of pan
6. layer in the order , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , then 1 / 3 part of the ricotta cheese mixture , half the browned meat , 1 cup mozzarella cheese , and 1 cup of spaghetti sauce
7. next layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , 1 / 3 part of the ricotta cheese mixture , and 1 1 / 2 cups sauce
8. next layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , remaining ricotta mixture and remained meat , 1 cup of sauce
9. for top layer , 4 uncooked lasagna noodles , remaining sauce , and remaining 1 cup mozzarella
10. bake covered with foil for 50-60 minutes
11. uncover and continue cooking until all the cheese is melted on the top
12. let stand 15 minutes before serving
13. if you are using a 13x9x2 pan---just make 3 layers to avoid boiling over
target.review: This recipe was quick & easy.  I've tried cooking the noodles in the past and everything always came out watery.  I used my homemade sauce that I hade made earlier in the week for spaghetti.  Got rave reviews, even my Italian husband approved of the cooking method!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Sorry I'm late @ reviewing this recipe.  I've made this roast @ least 10 times w/ perfect results each time.  If people would just leave the ingredients alone, maybe they would have great results too! It's so easy to do & very tasty too.  This recipe is definitely one that I will use again & again. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever black eyed peas

a southern classic! in most southern homes, black-eyed peas are always served on new year's day for good luck. i usually cook these early on new year's eve day. that way, if we have guests over for a party that night, i can use part of this basic recipe to make "texas caviar" which is a fantastic salsa/dip to eat with tortilla chips. (that recipe follows)

1. sort and wash peas
2. place in a large dutch oven
3. add remaining ingredients and bring to a boil
4. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 1- 1 1 / 2 hours , or until peas are tender
demonstrations.review: Very tasty recipe & simple, simple, simple. Didn't have much time to cook so I bought my onion & ham & garlic chopped up & came home & threw it all in a pot. Say goodbye to canned black eyed peas because from now on I will be preparing these fresh.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized chicken wings

nan

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. place chicken in a 9x13-inch baking dish
3. mix the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper and pour over the chicken
4. bake at 375f for one hour or until sauce is caramelized
demonstrations.review: My family was hesitant to try this recipe as we have another wing recipe that has proven tried & true in our household.  I went ahead & tried it since I was intrigued by all the reviews & boy was I glad I did!  They were quite simple & tasty!  My husband & children raved about them.  I did try the pre-cook method to rid the wings of the excess fat however, I thought that they had lost some of their moisture.  Next time I will omit that recommendation.  Thanks again for a great & easy recipe, can't wait 'till football season rolls around again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: These chimichangas are awesome!!!  I had some cooked chicken in the freezer and decided to make these after I read the reviews, and I happened to have all the other ingredients too.  I took one to work and did not have time to warm it up but it didn't matter, they're great cold too!  I will definitely make these again and freeze them.  They're easy to make and, if you're having company over, you can prepare them to the point of just before baking them and  then just slip them in the oven when you're ready.  Great tasting & healthy too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
demonstrations.review: I can't remember if I have rated these yet, so here I go.  Made these for my in-laws in the muffin-a-month gift I gave them.  I made me a batch as I was curious to know how they tasted before I gave them out.  These were wonderful!!  They tasted like mini apple pies, I especially liked the apple chunks.  Thanks.

target.recipe_text:
zero fat soup

this is a delicious way to lose weight! there are three variations so you never have to get tired of the same old thing! adopted from "moosewood restaraunt new classics" cookbook. enjoy!

1. heat the broth in a soup pot
2. add the first seven vegetables one at a time
3. stir in the tomatoes , soy sauce , vinegar , basil , oregano , dill , thyme , and pepper
4. simmer for 15 or 20 minutes , until the vegetables are tender
5. add salt to taste
6. enjoy !
7. variation 1:
8. for mexican zero soup , add zucchini and minced chiles and replace the herbs with cumin , coriander , and cilantro
9. use lime juice instead of vinegar
10. variation 2:
11. for hungarian zero soup , add mushrooms and replace the basil , oregano , and thyme with paprika , marjoram , and more dill
12. top with nofat sour cream
13. variation 3:
14. for asian zero soup , replace the cabbage with bok choy and add straw mushrooms
15. replace the herbs with grated fresh ginger root and minced scallions
16. top with mung bean sprouts
17. to freeze: prepare soup as directed
18. allow to cool and place in freezer containers or bags
19. freeze
20. to serve: thaw in fridge and reheat on stovetop until hot
target.review: I'm not looking to lose weight.  I just had a half-head of cabbage in the fridge and DH wanted soup.  I substituted 4 cups water and 3 chicken bullion cubes for the vegetable broth, and 3 cups of V-8 juice for the diced tomatoes.  Since this was a "clean the fridge day", I just used what veggies I had on hand.  Great flavor and very nice for lunch.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked bean soup

this is from one of the moosewood cookbooks. i made a few changes to fit my own tastes.

1. in a large soup pot on medium-high heat , saute the onion in the olive oil until translucent and starting to caramelize , about 8-10 minutes
2. add the carrot and chili powder and continue to cook , stirring frequently , about 3 minutes
3. add garlic and stir for 1-2 minutes more or until carrots are tender
4. stir in the mustard , water , tomatoes , beans , vinegar , molasses and soy sauce
5. bring to a boil then lower heat and simmer for about 15 minutes
6. add salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I had started steps 1-3 on the stove, then I put everything into my crockpot for about 6 hrs on low.  It worked out perfectly and the taste was so delicious and filling.  I love bean soups and this will now be put at the top of my list.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vine ripened tomato  sweet onion and basil salad

make sure that the tomatoes are fresh vine-ripened tomatoes--they make all the difference in the world.  a delicious and quick summer salad using fresh ingredients.  for the garlic infused olive oil, i used the olive oil from juenessa's recipe #221637.

1. thinly slice the tomatoes and layer on individual salad plates , slightly overlapping
2. top with onion rings and basil
3. in a small dish , blend the olive oil and vinegar together , pour over the salad
4. sprinkle the cheese over all and add freshly ground sea salt and pepper to taste
5. allow to rest 10 to 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: YUMMY!  This was great with yellow hierloom tomatoes.  I used garlic flavored dipping oil from the store and forgot the goat cheese, but it was really great without it.  This will be my favorite late summer salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with dill sauce

another adopted recipe!  cook time does not include marinating time.

1. trim excess fat from chicken
2. place each piece between 2 sheets of waxed paper
3. flatten to 1 / 4" thickness , using a meat mallet or rolling pin
4. place chicken in 13x9x2" baking dish
5. combine next 5 ingredients in a small bowl
6. pour over chicken
7. cover and refrigerate 2 hours
8. remove chicken from marinade , discarding marinade
9. coat a grill with cooking spray
10. grill chicken 6" over med coals 8 minutes , turning once
11. arrange chicken on a serving platter
12. garnish with lime wedges
13. serve with 1 1 / 2 t dill sauce per serving
14. dill sauce: combine all ingredients in blender
15. process till smooth
demonstrations.review: This wonderful light dish is one that I chose for PAC Spring '06.  DH and I found the chicken easy to cut and very moist, but I could see how it could overcook very quickly so keep an eye on it when you are grilling.  I thought the sauce needed about 1/4 tsp of salt but could definately do without. I will be making this again and the sauce many times as we both thought it would go well with fish or as a sauce on gyros instead of tzatziki since I hate cucumbers.  Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato salad served with cottage cheese

i make this all the time to eat at work and my co-workers love it.  very flavorful.

1. cut tomatoes in half and gently squeeze , scooping out pulp and seeds
2. dice
3. mince green onions and chop cilantro medium fine
4. add onions , basil , cilantro , vinegar , oil and garlic powder to tomatoes and toss
5. add salt and pepper to taste
6. store in fridge until ready to use
7. serve with 2 scoops low fat cottage cheese and gently mix
demonstrations.review: I really loved this salad.  It was like a creamy bruchetta topping.  Even DH ate some with his dinner and really enjoyed it.  Thanks for a great dish.  This might be a standard lunch for me when the tomatoes get ripe in the garden!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy oatmeal fruit bars

delicious & chewy granola-like bars with protein

1. directions , oven at 350 degrees , have a baking pan ready
2. mix the dry ingredients together , add the oil and apple sauce and mix
3. separate about 2 cups of the mixture
4. put the mixture into a pan or two - we used 1 14"x12" pan
5. you can grease the sides of the pan , but it isn't necessary on the bottom
6. you want to pack the mixture down and have it be about 1 / 4 inch thick
7. spread on the preserves and then crumble the remaining dry mixture on the top
8. bake at 350 degrees for 25-30 minutes
9. let cool 10+ minutes and enjoy
10. oats & whole wheat are good for fiber , the soy adds some protein , and the apple sauce is a good partial substitute for oil / butter , keeping it pretty moist
demonstrations.review: I followed Neneldae's lead and added only 1 can of sliced peaches (drained).  The flavor was very good, but they stuck to the pan and didn't really hold together like I had hoped for a portable breakfast.  Sorry.

target.recipe_text:
herb pull aparts

                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                

1. grease a fluted tube bundt pan
2. combine cheese , herbs and garlic
3. divide thawed dough into 24 pieces
4. if using rolls , they are ready to use once thawed
5. dip each piece in butter and roll in cheese / herb mixture to coat
6. place coated pieces of dough evenly in pan
7. let rise until double in size
8. bake in a preheated 350f oven for 30-40 minutes or until well browned and top of bread sound hollow when tapped
9. remove from pan immediately to cool on wire rack
target.review: Made this for my b-day a few days ago and I was very impressed. The only thing I changed was to use my own bread dough instead of the frozen loaf, but I know the frozen dough would have been good too. This recipe is REALLY good and went over very well with everyone at the party. I will definitely be making this again. BTW, I made this is a bundt pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s danish potato salad

a easy-to-make inexpensive potato salad. the homemade dressing for this is really good and i feel what makes it so good, and works equally well with macaroni salad. this is my mom's recipe, and her mom made it before her. i use about 6 hard-boiled eggs because i like my potato salad with more eggs. the prep and cook time is only a estimate, as i've never timed how long it takes to make this.
if you use mayo instead of miracle whip i'd suggest starting with only 1 t. sugar and adding more to taste as mayo is sweeter than miracle whip.
and of course please feel free to adapt this recipe ingredient-wise to your familie's preferences.

1. combine first 6 ingredients and bring to a boil
2. gradually beat in well-beaten eggs
3. cook , stirring constantly until slightly thickened
4. remove from heat and add salad dressing
5. mix well and pour over potato , egg , celery , onion and relish
6. add more salt and pepper if desired
7. refrigerate until well-chilled and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Made this yesterday for a New Years supper that I served for my whole family earlier tonight. Everyone loved it and went back for more. This made a lot and my mom cannot wait to dig into the leftovers. So easy to make. I used 5 hardboiled eggs and garnished with paprika. This has become a staple. THANK YOU!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple krispie cookies

perfect for those after school or late night snacks.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. in large bowl , mix all ingredients well
3. roll into 1-inch balls
4. place 2 in apart on lightly sprayed cooking sheet
5. bake for 10-12 minutes
6. cool for 1 minute
7. remove and cool completely
demonstrations.review: Made these a while back to give as Christmas gifts and am only getting around to reviewing now. This is an extremely simple yet totally awesome recipe. JUST DONT EAT THEM RIGHT AWAY! I gave my mom a cookie to sample when they were fresh out of the oven and her comment was that the cookies were "so-so". However, that night my mom samples another and declared that they were delicious. Much tastier and crispier than fresh out of the oven. Im sure the people on my Xmas list will be thrilled to be receiving these little gems. Thanks for a great, quick recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple caribbean jerk chicken

i like jerk chicken but often don't have all the exotic ingredients. this simplifies the mix by using dry italian dressing. yummy on the grill!

1. mix all ingredients except chicken in bowl
2. pour over chicken
3. cover and marinate 1 hour or over night in fridge
4. grill it !
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Made this 2 days ago in the oven instead of on the grill. They came out perfect. My mom doesnt really like spicy food but she liked these...she said they were flavourful but not burning hot. I used about 12 chicken thighs and it took awhile to cook but it came out great. Smelled awesome. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean pork strips

quick and simple dinner for those busy weeknights that we all know and love! serve over steamed rice for a tasty meal.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. add all ingredients to ziplock bag , shake to mix , and marinate pork for 5 min , or up to 3 hours
3. spray 9x13 baking dish with cooking spray , then place pork in dish , pouring marinade over pork
4. bake 30-35 minutes
5. cut pork into thin slices before serving
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight for my mom for supper. All I can say is AWESOME. I had a bit more pork than what was called for but it still came out EXCELLENT! Added a bit more garlic and let marinate for about 4 hours or so so it was extremely tender. It did take a bit longer to cook than the recipe stated but that is probably due to my oven. Covered for a bit to speed up cooking, next time I think I will cut the pork into smaller pieces. Served this with Shanghai Noodles (also on this site) House smelled unbelievable. Not often my mom is floored by a recipe but all she could say was MMM KEEPER!!..lol. (even my dad, who hates Asian food raved about this). Thank you so much for an amazing recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 step peanut butter chocolate chip bars

this is a kraft recipe - i have not made it but it sounds so simple and good i thought i would post it. it is in their latest free recipe magazine.

1. heat oven to 325f
2. mix together the peanut butter sugar & egg , mix well
3. spread in a small baking pan , sprinkle with chocolate chunks
4. bake for 20 minutes cut into 8 bars
demonstrations.review: Bergy, you really need to try this recipe. They are sooo yummy. Much better than even a Reese, IMO. Made exactly as is, except for using peanut butter sweetened with Splenda, and they still came out great. Would not change a thing.

target.recipe_text:
master brine recipe for meats

soak for 48 hours before using-it will help produce the juicyyyyyy-est meat you have ever made!

1. bring all ingredients to a boil in a large saucepan , reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes
2. allow to cool completely before using
3. large heavy duty sealable plastic bags work the best
target.review: This recipe made my buffalo hanger steaks absolutely delicious. I marinated them for only about 8 hours, but since they were thin, it worked really well.  Not only were they very tender, but the taste was wonderful.  Thanks,Diana.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
arni youvetsi  lamb and orzo

this is a traditional 'sunday lunch' dish.  the orzo (a kind of pasta that is shaped like large grains of rice) cooks in the liquid released by the lamb and tomato and becomes very tasty.  many make it with a cut of beef suitable for roasting, cut into large pieces, or even with chicken pieces.

1. preaheat oven to 375f
2. wash and pat dry the leg of lamb
3. in a large baking pan , rub lamb with the lemon juice and olive oil over
4. season generously with salt , pepper , oregano and thyme
5. pour in wine , water , tomato puree , minced onion , garlic and cinnamon around meat
6. give the sauce a stir and roast , turning meat over occasionally when you see a crust forming for 2 to 3 hours
7. in a large saucepan , bring plenty of water to the boil , salt generously and boil the orzo pasta for 8 minutes
8. remove and drain - retain a cup of the cooking water
9. add the pasta to the lamb casserole and give everything a stir to distribute orzo throughout the pan
10. increase heat to 400f and continue to bake another 15-20 minutes , or until pasta is fully cooked and has absorbed most of the liquid in the pan
11. if the pasta is too dry , stir in enough of the pasta cooking water you've retained to keep it saucy
12. have lots of freshly-grated parmesan or kefalotiri cheese to sprinkle over pasta at table
demonstrations.review: Evelyn, I made this yesterday, which happened to be Greek Easter.  It was absolutely delicious, and I didn't change the receipe at all.  The only problem was that I couldn't stop eating the orzo -- it was so yummy.  I served it with asparagus and a Sicilian blood orange salad with mint.  My Italian family had a great Greek Easter!  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken ii

nan

1. preheat oven to 450
2. combine all dry ingredients in a plastic bag
3. wash your chicken and shake off excess water
4. drop in bag and shake each piece
5. place in a metal pan skin side down and put in preheated oven
6. turn pieces over after about 20 minutes
7. continue baking until crisp and browned
demonstrations.review: Just wanted to tell you I've used your recipe constantly since the first time I tried it.  I've also given it to my sisters, and it's a mainstay during the week for them, too.  We have convection ovens now, and the chicken comes even crispier than it did in the regular oven.  Bless you!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
little fruitcake bites

these little beauties are great to mix between your other christmas cookies on a platter. they freeze well too. put them in a tin with a tight fitting lid. great for gifts. put a dab of marzipan on top or decorate with a wee holly leaf etc.

1. pour the rum over the raisins , cover with plastic wrap and marinate them for several hours or overnight heat oven to 300 degrees f
2. cream butter and sugar , add eggs one at a time beat after each addition
3. in another bowl mix your dry ingredients
4. stir the dry mixture into the butter& sugar
5. stir in raisins / rum and milk
6. stir in the fruit& nuts
7. line miniature muffin tins with fancy christmas paper liners or plain ones
8. fill 3 / 4 full with the batter
9. bake 10-15 minutes or until the tops spring back when lightly touched
demonstrations.review: Made these on Saturday for a cookie party on Sunday, and they were really easy.  Instead of the green cherries, I added chopped apricots, chopped pineapple, and some dried cherries, which I also soaked in the rum.  Yummy!!  Everybody loved them.  The rum makes them so good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cauliflower bisque

i saw this recipe in bon appetit, it sounds like a soup i had recently, and couldn't believe it was cauliflower

1. combine chicken broth , water and bring to simmer
2. add saffron to pan , remove from heat , steep for 20 minutes
3. in pot heat butter , add onions , cauliflower , salt and pepper , stir to coat , add saffron broth , simmer for 20 minutes , covered in blender in batches , or with immersion blender puree all , add 3 / 4 c half and half
demonstrations.review: This soup was really good, and you're right -- it doesn't taste like cauliflower!  The saffron makes it a beautiful color, too.  I used milk instead of cream, because I'm on a diet, as usual.  It worked well, and I'll certainly make the soup again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sandra s key lime pie

i saw this in the food section of the cincinnati enquirer october 30 2002 pg e3. by chef sandra wilson. i really like key lime pie and until this recipe have never found one that satisfied me.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. beat softened cream cheese until creamy
3. add sweetened condensed milk and beat to incorporate
4. add egg yolks and beat well
5. add lime juice and beat till combined
6. pour mixture into pie crust and spread with spatula until evenly distributed
7. place on cookie sheet and then into the oven and bake for 10 min
8. until the filling begins to set
9. remove from oven and allow to cool on rack at room temp
10. then place in the refrigerator for at least an hour
11. two works better
12. cut into 8 slices and serve with a generous helping of whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I made two of these pies this week-end and took them to a graduation barbecue party.  They were gone in no time!  I used regular pie crust instead of graham cracker, just becuase I like it more.  The pie is absolutely wonderful, and I'll certainly make it again.

target.recipe_text:
peanut butter blossoms

my mom made these cookies all the time when i was little, now i like to make them for my kids.

1. combine shortening , sugars , egg , vanilla and peanut butter
2. add dry ingredients and milk
3. shape dough into small balls , then roll in sugar
4. place on an ungreased cookie sheet
5. bake 10 minutes at 350
6. place a kiss in middle of each cookie pressing until the edges crack
target.review:
These are evil. We had company over for dinner and ate the entire batch.

Our only substitution was using egg beaters rather than eggs. When you do this, it is safe to eat the raw cookie dough!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
disappearing sweet potato muffins

these are really good and a great way to get some good stuff into my kids, they eat them like candy! i didn't like the recipes with cooked/mashed sweet potatoes, so when i found this one, i was so excited. these smell absolutely wonderful when they are cooking too! we usually leave out the nuts, but put in the raisins

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease muffin tins to hold 12 muffins
3. whisk together brown sugar , oil , vanilla and eggs in a small bowl
4. mix together the flour , baking powder , spices , salt , and grated sweet potatoes in a large bowl
5. make a well in the center , and pour in the egg mixture
6. stir the egg mixture , gradually incorporating it with the flour mixture
7. stir in the raisins and walnuts
8. spoon the batter into the tins
9. i like to fill each tin to the rim to make a large cap
10. bake the muffins for 25 to 30 minutes or until a toothpick inserted into the middle comes out clean
11. take the muffins out of the oven and run a paring knife carefully around each muffin , then invert the pan , and knock one edge against your work surface to release the muffins
12. serve the muffins right away
demonstrations.review:
Nice for using up some giant sweet potato from the garden! Sometimes I have roasted sweet potato on hand, but this is nice and quick if you don't have any precooked on hand.

I used only 1/2 c sugar, and I tossed in some chocolate chips (a handful--maybe half a cup) instead of nuts and raisins. My daughter who hates sweet potatoes liked them.

Thanks for sharing this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elizabeth s chocolate zucchini cake

i got this recepe originally from my friend elizabeth who had a huge garden and plenty of zucchini.   it is a moist, lovely cake that i like plain with no icing or frosting, though elizabeth would use an orange or lemon glaze . she would also use whole wheat pastry flour.  i have also used bittersweet chocolate with great results. sour cream or yogurt can be substituted for the buttermilk.

1. melt chocolate , oil and butter at low heat
2. mix together in seperate bowl sugar , eggs , vanilla and dairy choice
3. in another bowl sift together flour , cocoa , soda , baking powder and salt
4. mix all ingredients alternating wet and dry
5. finally add zucchini
6. bake in greased and floured bundt pan at 350 degrees f
7. for 40-60 minutes or until straw comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Wow! This is the best chocolate cake I have EVER had! Period.<br/><br/>I used Ghirardelli semisweet baking chocolate. I subbed half of the zucchini for yellow squash because we had loads of it in t he garden (did that with other recipes, too, and they come out the same). The squash/zucchini really adds to the moistness. I made it as a bundt cake, unfrosted, and it took 50 minutes to cook in my oven.<br/><br/>I will say, this isn't a healthy cake--the amount of butter, sugar, and white flour pretty much cancels out the squash, but it is an incredible dessert--better than chocolate cake without squash, by far.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot salsa chicken

quick, healthy and delicious. just pop the four ingredients into the crock-pot in the morning and you'll have a great-tasting meal for dinner. this would also be great for larger gatherings.

1. place first four ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low 6-8 hours
3. 30-60 minutes prior to serving , remove chicken , shred and return to crock pot
4. to serve , use chicken mixture as filling inside tortillas
5. add desired condiments
demonstrations.review:
I really enjoyed this dish. 

A couple of comments on other reviews, though....

I only used 16 oz of salsa based on other reviews, but I found I would have preferred it a bit saucier. Next time, I may not go with 32 oz, but will probably try a 24 oz jar. 

Also, I had to cook this while at work, so it was more like 10.5 hours in the crockpot. The chicken was still fine. I don't know if that might have made it less saucy, though. Corn and beans did NOT overcook in that period of time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cookie dough hamantashen  parve

this recipe came from my synagogue's women's league cookbook.  after i made this recipe i knew i had a winner when my children begged for them at every meal.

1. beat eggs well
2. add oil and sugar , beating well
3. beat in vanilla , baking powder , and salt
4. gradually add flour
5. chill dough
6. may be chilled overnight but let it sit out a while so it is not so cold - the dough will be easier to work with
7. roll dough onto floured board
8. cut into 3 inch rounds
9. place a heaping teaspoonful of filling
10. i used solo poppyseed filling , solo apricot filling , seedless raspberry preserves , and chocolate chips - they were all yummy
11. take a little water and wet the outside area of the circle
12. draw up sides to form a triangle and pinch closed
13. place on parchment lined cookie sheets
14. bake at 350 degrees for 7-10 minutes or until brown
demonstrations.review: Very easy dough to work and pinched together better than other recipes I've tried. I used 375 oven, and that helped them from running for me. I do have to say, for flavor, I like hamantashen that use butter, rather than oil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini basil muffins

from just hungry - they adapted it from bernard clayton's new complete book of breads,

1. preheat the oven to 200c / 425f
2. grease muffin tins
3. combine the eggs , milk and oil in a large bowl
4. combine the flour , sugar , salt and baking powder in another bowl and add to the liquid mixture in batches , stirring to blend
5. don't overblend !
6. add the zucchini and basil and stir to blend
7. fill each muffin cup about 1 / 2 full
8. sprinkle the top with the cheese
9. bake for about 20-25 minutes for regular size muffins , 15-20 minutes for the mini muffins , until the tops are golden brown and puffy
10. serve while still warm
demonstrations.review: Finally, a savory muffin recipe! These were delicious. I followed the recipe exactly, except I substituted yellow summer squash for zucchini since I have an abundance from the garden right now. I used the basil and thyme version since I have more basil than parsley. The only thing I would change is I would reduce the amount of salt. I like salty food, but these were slightly too salty. Next time, I will use 50% less since the parmesan is salty.

target.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
target.review: So good!I doubled the recipe,added walnuts to half, and added nothing to the other half.These are so good and really don't need anything else added but it would be fun for kids to "personalize" theirs.Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no flour no sugar pancakes

great taste with no flour or sugar! i made this one up one morning while craving pancakes, but wanting to something healthy. i eat them plain- no butter or syrup!

1. mix oatmeal with yogurt and set aside
2. mash banana and chop the walnuts
3. mix all ingredients together
4. cook as you would other pancakes
5. sprinkle with more cinnamon if desired , or top with applesauce
demonstrations.review: These didn't turn out so well for me.They fell apart when I tried to turn them and the oatmeal wasn't cooked enough so it was tough.But I served them in bowls topped with warm applesauce and my kids ate them anyway:)Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious low carb cornbread

this is my very favorite low carb recipe! it's so easy to prepare, and it's done in only 2 minutes in the microwave. the best part is that it only amounts to 1 carb per slice!!! there isn't a trace of corn in the recipe, but try it; it really does taste like cornbread!

1. in a small bowl , mix wet ingredients , then work in the dry ingredients
2. pour into a greased microwave-safe container
3. microwave for 2 minutes at power level 8
4. cut into 8 slices , about 1 carb per slice
5. serve with butter
demonstrations.review: I have made this twice now and I still can't believe it!Not quite cornbread but I definately get that bread "fix".Quick and easy.I found that if I use 1tbsp butter and 1/8 tsp salt it's perfect for me.Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet potato and black bean burrito

sweet potatoes add an unexpected creaminess to the filling in these burritos. serve the burritos on a bed of rice, if you like, with plenty of salsa. enjoy!

1. preheat the oven to 350
2. place the sweet potatoes in a medium saucepan with the salt and water to cover
3. cover and bring to a boil , then simmer until tender , about 10 minutes
4. drain and set aside
5. while the sweet potatoes are cooking , warm the oil in a medium skillet or saucepan and add the onions , garlic , and chile
6. cover and cook on medium-low heat , stirring occasionally , until the onions are tender , about 7 minutes
7. add the cumin and coriander and cook for 2 to 3 minutes longer , stirring frequently
8. remove from the heat and set aside
9. in a food processor , combine the black beans , cilantro , lemon juice , salt , and cooked sweet potatoes and puree until smooth
10. transfer the sweet potato mixture to a large mixing bowl and mix in the cooked onions and spices
11. lightly oil a large baking dish
12. spoon about 2 / 3 to 3 / 4 cup of the filling in the center of each tortilla , roll it up , and place it , seam side down , in the baking dish
13. cover tightly with foil and bake for about 30 minutes , until piping hot
14. serve topped with salsa
demonstrations.review: Nice change!Omitted cilantro because I didn't have it on hand but still very good.I did mix by hand to keep texture and served it in wheat tortillas with cheese and sour cream.I will make this for my family again.Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
truly low carb hot cereal

this recipe was in a free booklet that i picked up at my local health food store.  credit is given to karen rysavy, and it apparently beats keto's version hands down.  i have never tried that brand, but i have to say i like this. because it contains flaxmeal, i keep the mixture in the fridge, and just add some dried cranberries to the portion i am cooking. i make mine in a tall sided bowl in the microwave for about 2 1/2 minutes, but microwaves vary, so watch closely to prevent boil overs.  the nutritional analysis with the recipe indicates 7g carbs, 4g fiber, 9g protein, 10g fat, 150 calories per serving

1. combine all ingredients
2. mix can be stored for later use
3. i store mine in the fridge
4. to prepare one serving , simply place 1 / 4 cup of the mix in a very tall , microwavable bowl , or use a saucepan on the stovetop
5. add 1 / 2 cup of water
6. bring to a boil , stirring , and continue to boil and stir for at least two minutes , to thicken
demonstrations.review: At first the texture was a little strange but now I just love it. It's a great change from eggs for a low-carb breakfast. Quick, easy, and yummy. I double the recipe because I eat it almost every day:)Thanks so much Sweet Bamboo!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
high protein no guilt skinny cheesecake

this is really good if you are trying to lose fat and maintain muscle.

for whole recipe:
calories: 820 / fat: 30g - 33% / carbs: 22g - 9% / protein: 112g - 57%

1. preheat oven to 375 deg f
2. put the cottage cheese , eggs , sour cream , whey powder , splenda , lemon rind an juice , and vanilla extract in a blender , and blend until very smooth
3. pour mixed into a sprayed pie pan
4. place the cake on the top rack of the oven and place a flat pan of water on the bottom rack
5. bake for 30-40 minutes
6. cook , then chill well before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a great idea and a pretty good "cheesecake".I used stevia and agave nectar for sweetening and used 1/4 c ff sour cream and 1/4 c ff plain yogurt.The lemon was very nice but I think I may use a little less potein powder next time as that is definately the dominant flavor.I baked it for 30 min. at which time the edges were puffed and browned and the center was set.I'm looking forward to making this again.Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
special day lemon bars

i originally got this recipe from "barefoot contessa" on food network. i wrote down all the ingredients as i was watching and made them to take to a family gathering. they were a huge hit, even with the people who don't normally like lemon bars. when i finally got the official recipe from "the barefoot contessa cookbook," copyright 1999, i realized i hadn't made them exactly like they were supposed to be made. however, they're so well loved by my family now, i just keep making them my way.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. for the crust , cream the butter and sugar until light in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment
3. combine the flour and salt and , with the mixer on low , add to the butter until just mixed
4. dump the dough onto a well-floured surface and gather into a ball
5. flatten the dough with floured hands and press it into a 9 x 13 x 2" baking sheet , building up a 1 / 2" edge on all sides
6. chill
7. bake the crust for 15 to 20 minutes , until very lightly browned
8. let cool on a wire rack , leaving the oven on
9. for the filling , whisk together the eggs , sugar , lemon juice , and flour , and pour into the crust
10. bake for 30 to 35 minutes more , until the filling is set
11. let cool to room temperature
12. cut into triangles and dust with confectioners' sugar
target.review: THIS is the lemon bar recipe I'll make from now on!! Tall, rich yummies with plenty of creamy lemon filling, and a flavorful, buttery crust. Everyone at work and at home loved them. I'm not very adept at baking bars in metal pans, so I use glass baking dishes, and have eliminated "chiseling" the bars out. (If you don't have a problem with metal pans, by all means use them). I found Mandarin's method of making them so easy, I don't care to know what the original recipe says. The Best!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon apricot bars

lemon bars with the added yummyness of apricot preserves!

1. for the crust: mix flour and confectioners' sugar in a bowl
2. cut in the butter until crumbly
3. preheat oven to 350
4. press the crumb mixture over the bottom of a 9x9-inch baking pan
5. bake for 30 minutes , let stand until cool
6. reduce oven temperature to 325
7. for the filling: spread the apricot preserves over the bottom of the crust
8. beat the eggs in a mixer bowl until blended
9. add sugar , lemon juice , lemon peel , flour , baking powder and salt
10. beat until blended
11. pour over the prepared layers
12. bake for 35 minutes
13. let stand until cool
14. sprinkle with confectioners' sugar to taste
15. cut into bars
demonstrations.review:
These were really tasty! The family loved them. The lemon-apricot combination is one I had never thought of. I used a food processor to make the crust. 
My personal history with lemon bars is this: they look great, until I have to remove them from the pan. The 9-inch pan became a quest---I went to 8 stores here before I found one, and it was metal. I would have preferred glass. Anyway, I lined the pan with parchment paper, because the instructions on the pan said not to use metal utensils. Only the corners of the bars stuck a little, but I was able to get the whole thing out in one piece. I would recommend refrigerating the bars before cutting them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana nut bread

this is an incredibly moist and tender banana nut bread.  the addition of the instant banana pudding gives it an extra banana "kick". i find baking it at a lower temperature avoids burning the edges.  my dh likes it for breakfast served under two eggs over easy.

1. preheat oven to 300
2. grease two 9 x 5 loaf pans
3. cream butter and sugar well
4. add buttermilk , eggs and vanilla and mix well
5. add instant pudding , salt , baking powder , baking soda , and cinnamon , mixing well
6. slowly add flour , one cup at a time , until well mixed
7. peel bananas , mash and add to mixture
8. add pecans and mix until blended
9. pour batter into prepared pans and bake for 1 hour and 10 minutes or until toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review: Very tasty, moist bread! I think that the only change I'll make the next time I prepare this is to leave out the cinnamon---this is NOT a criticism, just personal preference. I actually love cinnamon, I just prefer banana bread without it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple banana bread

this recipe is now back to my original posting as i posted it at recipezaar many years ago. recently i noticed that somehow  the name got changed as did some of the ingredients. in 2005 i wrote that this is a moist light bread/cake with just a hint of cinnamon. keeep an eye on cooking times as too long and it will be drier. also leave in tin for about 5 mins before turning out onto a rack to cool completely.  slices can be served as a dessert topped with custard and whipped cream, or cold and buttered. 

1. preheat oven to 350 deg f
2. cream butter and sugars , and beat in eggs
3. stir in sour cream , bananas and vanilla
4. in separate bowl , combine flour , baking powder , soda and cinnamon
5. gradually add to butter mixture
6. gently stir in apples and nuts
7. spoon into greased bread pan and bake 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I've had this recipe since March, 2000. This is a delicious bread! I doubled the recipe and made two 9x5 loaves, and the only change I made in the ingredients was to use pecans (which I had on hand) instead of walnuts. It is great for breakfast, lightly toasted with a little butter. Great for tea, gifts!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil soup with andouille sausage

from giuseppe's italian cafe, williamsburg, va.

1. combine both stocks and lentils in a large pot
2. over high heat , bring to a boil
3. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes
4. in a skillet , over medium heat , add fennel seeds
5. saute until light golden brown , about 2 minutes
6. remove seeds from skillet
7. heat oil in same skillet over medium heat
8. add celery , carrot , and onion
9. saute until onion is translucent and celery and carrot are tender , about 5-10 minutes
10. add toasted fennel seeds , sauteen vegetables , sausage , thyme and creole seasoning to soup
11. cover and simmer until lentils are very tender , stirring occasionally , about 45 minutes
12. season soup to taste with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!! Everyone enjoyed this soup. The only addition I made was to add a little lemon juice. I used fat-free broths, and a little less thyme. The Andouille sausage I bought was a bit challenging to remove the casings from---good thing it was going to be chopped anyway---lol. This is the best lentil soup recipe I've ever tried, and it is the one I'll use from now on!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cake with frosting

this cake is very popular with the younger crowd. my grandaughter especially likes this one.

1. combine cake mix , jello , and eggs
2. mix well
3. add oil , water , and 1 / 2 the strawberries
4. beat on med for 2 minutes
5. pour into greased 12x9 pan
6. bake at 350 for 30 minutes
7. cool
