8. frosting: combine powdered sugar , butter and remaining strawberries
9. mix well
10. spread on cooled cake
demonstrations.review:
I wasn't quite sure what to expect with the ingredients listed, but this cake was a huge hit with the family, and it is delicious! 
I did substitute half the oil with unsweetened applesauce (I might try 3/4ths next time), and because I intended to serve the cake from the baking dish, I only made half the frosting recipe---which was still an ample amount. 
This recipe is very easy, and is good for when you are short on time---which I was yesterday. I used an 8x12-inch baking dish, and baked the cake about 10 minutes longer than directed. I must live in a cooking-utensil-challenged area (lol), because in addition to my fruitless search for a 7x11-in. pan, I also cannot locate a 9x12-inch pan.
Yes, this cake is sweet---but aren't desserts supposed to be?

target.recipe_text:
spicy soybean cookies

interesting, very interesting

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. combine brown sugar , oil , prune baby food , egg , applesauce and vanilla in large mixing bowl
3. beat well with electric mixer , add soybeans and beat again
4. in medium mixing bowl , sift the flour , baking powder , cinnamon , nutmeg , cloves and ginger
5. stir into the soybean mixture
6. stir oats into the dough
7. drop by rounded teaspoon onto nonstick baking sheet
8. bake for 10 minutes or until firm and lightly golden
9. do not over bake
target.review:
What an intresting Cookie! More like a small soft cake really. However, the flavor is subtle and unique, having many diffrent undertones of earthyness, contributing to a nice pleasant taste with a soft chew to it, not overly sweet either, which was pleasant. 
However, I omited the cloves and ginger and reduced the amount of nutmeg used, and instead used chinese five spice powder.
No one would suspect that the secret ingredients was Soybeans (Which I had a 1/4c leftover on hand, hence I made these cookies) and prune baby food!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
polenta fig cake

this simple recipe is from bon appetit 5/05

1. preheat oven to 375
2. grease an 8" cake pan
3. beat yolks and sugar in a large bowl
4. in a saucepan bring milk , grappa , and salt to a boil , remove from heat
5. gradually add milk to egg mixture
6. return everything to the saucepan , add corn meal and whisk until thickened and beginning to bubble
7. add figs , raisins , nuts and fennel seeds to mixture , pour into the cake pan
8. bake 40 minutes until set and edges pull away from pan
9. cool 20 minutes in the pan , invert onto a plate , serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: A very diffrent taste and texture. It was dense and moist, with a nice sweetness (you could tell that it came from more than just sugar), and the fenel and pine nuts really hit it home! I will make this again, possible for Thanksgiving.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey oatmeal chewy bars

quick to mix and quicker to disapear.  i like to slightly underbake these for a more softer bar.  dont over bake or you will have rocks! for a really flavorful bar, toast the nuts and coconut in the oven while preheating...watch closely it will burn quickly.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cream butter , honey and sugar until light and fluffy
3. add egg and vanilla
4. mix together dry ingedients
5. slowly add to creamed mixture
6. stir in oatmeal , coconut and nuts
7. spread into greased 13x9 pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes in 350 degree oven
9. cool and cut into bars
10. store airtight with a piece of fresh bread to keep them soft
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe. It had a nice flavor and were soft with a nice texture (I underbaked them a little) However, I didn't have any coconut on hand so I used rasins instead, but the flavor was still great. I will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian banana chai bread

never tasted it, don't know what it's like, but sounds interesting. not as nice as the easiest (non-machine) white bread in the world. i've tasted that, its gorgeous, as is the chef.

1. in a medium bowl mix together flour , baking powder , and salt
2. in a separate bowl mix sugar , cream cheese , and eggs until light and fluffy
3. mix mashed bananas and chai into cream cheese mixture
4. add flour mixture and mix until smooth
5. pour mixture into a greased 9x5 inch loaf pan
6. bake in a preheated 350 degree f oven for 60 minutes
7. cool on rack
8. remove from pan after 10 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I found the bread to be rather dense, but good. However I did make the fallowing changes:

Instead of cream cheese I used fatfree yogurt, and instead of 1/4c of chia tea mixed, I added 1/2tsp (each) of ginger,pumpkin pie spice,  cardimon,  cloves,  allspice and left out the liquied. 
The cooking time was about an hour and some.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple krispie cookies

perfect for those after school or late night snacks.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. in large bowl , mix all ingredients well
3. roll into 1-inch balls
4. place 2 in apart on lightly sprayed cooking sheet
5. bake for 10-12 minutes
6. cool for 1 minute
7. remove and cool completely
demonstrations.review: A great and easy cookie recipe. I made these a few times, and decided to replace 2/3 of the butter with peanut butter, and OH MY the flavor has a more earth tone to it but they are so good! Though, you do have to press down the dough when you do that, else you end up with little hemispheres of cookies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yeast crisps

these crisp cookies are from a 1990 betty crocker recipe booklet. it's suggested that, while you can eat them plain, you can also try putting a small dab of jam, jelly or preserves on top.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water in large bowl
2. stir in remaining ingredients except sugar coating until smooth
3. cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour
4. to make sugar coating , mix 1 / 4 cup white sugar with one of the following: 3 tsp ground cinnamon
5. 2 tsp ground nutmeg
6. 2 tsp pumpkin pie spice
7. 1 tsp ground cardamom
8. 1 / 2 tsp almond extract
9. 1 / 2 tsp anise flavouring
10. 1 / 2 tsp rum extract
11. 1 / 2 tsp maple flavouring
12. preheat oven to 375f degrees
13. shape dough into one-inch balls
14. place on ungreased cookie sheet and flatten each ball with a glass dipped into sugar coating
15. bake 10 to 12 minutes or until edges are light brown
16. immediately remove from cookie sheet
17. cool
demonstrations.review: I found the flavor to be bland and uninspiring, I tried several diffrent verations of the sugar coating, all failed to depart any real flavor to the crisps. I suppose, though, you could use it as a complement to something very very sweet,

target.recipe_text:
baklava muffins

i love baklava and this is a delightful treat that brings the same flavors through.    from how to be a  domestic goddess by nigella lawson.

1. preheat oven to 400f degrees
2. mix all the filling ingredients together in a small bowl , set aside
3. in a large bowl , mix together the flour , baking powder , baking soda and sugar
4. mix the egg , melted butter and buttermilk
5. make a well in the dry ingredients and add gently mix in the wet ingredients
6. fill 12 miffin cups 1 / 3 full , add a scant tablespoon of filling , cover with more muffin mixture until 2 / 3 full
7. sprinkle any remaining filling on top of the muffins
8. bake for 15 minutes
9. put the muffins onto a rack to cool and drizzle with honey
target.review: These were a hit! The only substitution I used was the milk/lemon juice mixture in place of buttermilk. Worked fine! I made sure to spray the tins well (no cups) after reading some of the other reviews, and they did not stick. The texture is obviously much diffrent than traditional baklava, but "baklava" in a breakfast muffin is a brilliant idea!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
succulent prawns for the barbie

i love prawns. this is one of the yummiest prawn dishes that i have had. it combines two fantastic cooking elements, prawns and the bbq. i think they go hand in hand.

1. combine butter , oil , herbs , lemon juice , garlic , shallots , salt and pepper in a mixing bowl
2. mix in shrimp
3. marinate at room temperature 1 hour
4. stirring occasionally
5. prepare barbecue on medium heat
6. thread prawns on narrow skewers
7. grill until just opaque , about 2 minutes per side
8. arrange cups of letuce on a platter and then place the skewers on the platter
9. garnish with lemon and serve
demonstrations.review: I used the marinade from this recipe for scallops; I skewered them on bamboo and grilled them. They were the best scallops I've ever had - I'll definitely try this with prawns or shrimp as well. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seafood pumpkin curry   nigella lawson

i got this recipe from nigella bites- the show. loved it from the very first time i made it. the good thing about this recipe is that it also has a vegetarian version so no one misses out on the taste.

1. heat oil
2. skim the cream from the top of the can of the coconut cream and add to the oil
3. add the curry paste and whisk well until blended
4. add the rest of the juice from the can of coconut cream
5. snip the lime leaves with scissors and add to the above
6. bruise the lemon grass and add
7. add the fish stock , fish sauce , sugar
8. add the pumpkin cubes , cover and cook until tender
9. now add in fish pieces and the shrimp
10. cook some more until fish is almost cooked
11. add the bok choy and cook until the bok choy is wilted
12. add lime juice , salt and turn off heat
13. garnish with cilantro
14. serve with fragrant jasmine rice
demonstrations.review:
Terrific recipe, and a great way to use those small pumpkins I always buy around Halloween for display, but are too small to carve as jack-o-lanterns. I made this for a dinner visit from my sister and her two year old daughter, who gobbled it up and asked for more! My sister left with the recipe, and plans to share it with friends, so I'd say it was a hit. 

I made the vegetarain version, since I had vegetable broth and chickpeas, and made a couple of substitutions - I used the zest of a lemon for the lemongrass, and since I didn't have any bok choy, I threw in some frozen peas. I also omitted the lime leaves, just because I didn't have them (if I can find some, I'll use them next time). 

My neice called the pumpkin chuncks "potatoes," and I may try this with potatoes instead of the pumpkin when freah pumpkin isn't available. 

An excellent vegetable curry recipe - thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smothered chicken with creamy mushroom gravy

a nice quick entree after a hectic day at work. from bon appetit magazine. i saute the chicken longer than the time specified to make sure it's cooked through, or pound the breasts thinner.

1. blend flour , 1 / 2 teaspoon thyme and allspice in small bowl
2. set aside 1 tablespoon of flour mixture
3. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper , then with enough of remaining flour mixture to coat
4. melt butter in heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
5. add chicken to skillet
6. saute until brown , about 4 minutes per side
7. transfer chicken to plate
8. add mushrooms , onion , and remaining 1 teaspoon thyme to skillet
9. saute until mushrooms are brown , about 5 minutes
10. mix in reserved 1 tablespoon flour mixture
11. cook 1 minute
12. add cream and broth and bring to boil , stirring occasionally
13. return chicken and any collected juices to skillet
14. reduce heat to medium-low
15. simmer uncovered until chicken is cooked through and gravy thickens slightly , about 5 minutes
16. season with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe! Very homey. Much better than pouring a can of cream of mushroom soup on chicken, and not much more time consuming if you use pre-sliced mushrooms. I tried it with whole milk instead of the cream, but I will use cream next time, as I would have preferred a creamier sauce. It's still very good with the milk substitution if there's no cream handy. I also used boneless chicken thighs instead of breasts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pheasant

posted in response to a request. this was my grandmother's recipe for pheasant. we had/have a lot of hunters in the family and this was the best recipe for pheasant. i'm guessing on the serving size for 3 pheasants.

1. saute pheasants in butter 10 minutes
2. remove from skillet and saute mushrooms in butter remaining in skillet 10 minutes return pheasant to skillet
3. add wine , lemon juice , onions , salt and pepper
4. cover and simmer 1 hour or until tender
demonstrations.review: A friend recently gave us a few pheasants from his freezer - I'd never prepared it before, and this was the recipe I chose after browsing the pheasant recipes on 'zaar. This turned out amazingly good!! I followed it to the letter, except that I reduced it for one bird, which was enough for two adults and a five-year-old. I also used sliced portobello mushroom caps.  We have two pheasants left, and I plan to prepare this recipe again this weekend for a birthday dinner. HIGHLY recommended, thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sully s salisbury steak

delicious and easy i love being able to use stuff already in the house to make dinner.  i threw this together this evening and it was a winner.  served it with corn on the cob and smashed new potatoes.

1. mix first four ingredients together
2. add 2 / 3 package of the soup mix to the meat mixture and stir together by hand
3. make 4 or 5 small patties a little larger than a palm of your hand
4. i pan fried mine for about 2 minutes per side in nonstick skillet and then placed in casserole dish
5. i cooked the sliced onions till carmelized and set to the side
6. in the same pan i poured 1 1 / 2 cups of the water in and brought to boil
7. in measuring cup i added the package of gravy mix and the other 1 / 3 package of soup mix with the other 1 / 2 cup water
8. once water boiling add gravy soup mixture cook til thickened
9. once gravy is thick pour over patties and baked in the oven for 45 minutes on 350
10. plate and put 1 / 4 of cooked onion on patty
11. serve with sides and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Love this! Something different to do with ground beef that has an old TV Dinner nostalgia (for me), but is much better. I used half a package of soup mix in the meat mixture only, which was plenty, and used broth thickened with a little corn starch dissolved in water instead of the brown gravy mix.

target.recipe_text:
candy cane marshmallows

making for my friends for the holidays...

1. coat an 8-inch square pan with spray , line the bottom with parchment paper
2. coat parchment with spray and set pan aside
3. put sugar , corn syrup and 3 / 4 cup water in small saucepan
4. cook over medium heat , stirring , until sugar is dissolved
5. stop stirring , let mix come to a boil
6. raise heat to medium high
7. cook until mix registers 260 degrees on a candy thermometer
8. sprinkle gelatin over 3 / 4 cup water , let stand 5 minutes
9. set bowl over pan of simmering water , whisking constantly until dissolved
10. stir in peppermint extract after removed from heat
11. beat egg whites until stiff peaks form
12. whisk gelatin into sugar mix
13. add egg
14. mix on high until very thick , about 12-15 minutes
15. pour into lined pan and swirl with red food coloring
16. let stand overnight and cut into squares
target.review: This is actually pretty easy if you get everything organized before you start - even if you have hardly any experience with desserts/candies like me.  =]  The coloring is tough, I've gotta figure that part out still.  Based on a comment on the Martha Stewart site where this recipe is from, I rolled them in powdered sugar after I cut them so they wouldn't stick together.  And for cutting, kitchen shears worked a thousand times better than a knife.  I'm going to make some green ones, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger skillet supper

this is something new that our family tried that i got from a magazine. we were surprised that we would all like it so much! it doesn't take very much time at all so it is great when time is limited.

1. in a skillet , cook beef until no longer pink
2. drain
3. add noodles with contents of seasoning packet and water
4. bring to a boil
5. cook for 3 minutes or until noodles are tender
6. add the veggies and cook until tender , about 3 minutes as well
7. makes about 4 servings
8. here is another way to do it: cook the beef as stated previously
9. during this time , heat up a saucepan of water to cook the ramen noodles in
10. rather than just using 1 packet , use 2 packets of the beef flavor ramen noodles
11. when cooking the noodles , cook them without the flavoring
12. during this time , add the veggies to the meat and continue to cook
13. as the veggies become cooked , add the two packets of flavoring to the beef-veggie mixture
14. the ramen noodles don't take long to cook , so be sure to watch them
15. when they are done , drain them , and add them to the beef-veggie mixture
16. the completed dish will have more flavor , and more noodles for the noodle lovers ! enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I made this with the two packages of ramen, and I did add more than 2 cups of veggies (I didn't measure) so I added some low-sodium beef bullion powder to make up for it.  It was still really bland.  But it's so incredibly fast and easy that I think it's worth playing around with (onions, garlic, maybe even tomatoes?) in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
how scallops are supposed to be made

scallops don't need sauces or breading to be perfect. this method is fast, easy, healthy, and most of all, delicious! i love these scallops with some couscous or a simple pasta with olive oil, parmesan, and basil/oregano. enjoy!

1. preheat a large skillet over med-high to high heat
2. add oil
3. pat down scallops with a paper towel to remove excess moisture
4. sprinkle salt and pepper over one side of the scallops
5. place scallops on the hot skillet
6. do not touch , move , or tinker with the scallops at all
7. sprinkle salt and pepper over the other side of the scallops
8. cook scallops 3 to 5 minutes on each side or until caramel in color
9. squeeze the lemon juice over the pan
demonstrations.review: I had never eaten scallops that I could remember, but people seem to love them, so I wanted to give it a shot.  I followed your instructions and they were FANTASTIC!  (3-4 minutes on each side for what I think would be medium-sized sea scallops.)  If they weren't so darn expensive I'd be making these all the time.  =]  My husband was really impressed... and I couldn't believe how easy it was.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fsd   oatmeal cookies

fsd = fat smash diet.  from the fatsmashforum.com recipes forum, posted by mush.

1. mix and pat onto cookie sheet
2. bake at 350 for 9 minutes for chewy cookie
3. for crisp cookie , turn off oven and leave in for about 5 more minutes
demonstrations.review: I needed to use up some oatmeal and over-ripe bananas and this was perfect for that.  I used (real) brown sugar instead of splenda (I'm not on any particular diet).  I did add some unsweetened applesauce, but I wish there was a suggested amount in the recipe.  These are not incredibly sweet, which makes them a good snack or breakfast cookie instead of a dessert.  I would make these again if I found myself with mushy bananas!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry orange relish

wonderful for thanksgiving or christmas to serve with your turkey! this is another one of my mother-in-law's recipes that my husband must have for the holidays!

1. wash and drain cranberries
2. wash and quarter one orange and remove any seeds
3. place everything in a food processor and chop
4. add sugar
5. refrigerate overnight
demonstrations.review: Found this recipe when I rediscovered my "Joy of Cooking" book and had to see if someone had posted it here.  JoC says to refrigerate for two days up to two weeks before serving, so I waited 4 days, and it's fantastic.  It's really good mixed with plain yogurt!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black soybean hummus

discovering black soybeans (low in carbs, high in fiber) was been a major find for my lowcarb menus!  this hummus is seriously tasty, lower-carb or not.

1. combine all ingredients , except the green onions , in a food processor to create a thick puree
2. garnish with green onions
3. information on black soybeans available at the eden foods website , black soybeans are good for those eating lowcarb because they are lower in carbohydrates and high in fiber
demonstrations.review: Love this recipe - great creamy texture, and just the right amount of garlic and cumin!  I used black soybeans I had cooked from dried, and since they had no added salt I needed to add 1/4 to 1/2 tsp at the end.  I used full-fat greek yogurt instead of the sour cream, and was out of lemon juice so I used 2 tbsp rice vinegar and 1 tbsp water.  It might be a little too much onion for my taste but I think a lot of people would like it this way.

target.recipe_text:
mama vaun s meatloaf

you can do it better than his mother meatloaf.

1. ok , i don't measure , i only cook
2. review the recipe closely and you can figure how much of what for yourself
3. first step , make your self a little drink , light up a cigarette , turn on the radio , drink 1 / 3 of drink before food prep
4. roast garlic , onion& pepper
5. cool
6. chop up small
7. mix everything together
8. mold , cover and place in fridge for 2 hours
9. bake 300f degrees until done 1 1 / 4-3 / 4 hours
10. cover for half of the cooking time
11. problems in paradise
12. send your loved one to work with a meatloaf sandwich on potato bread w / a little mayo , remember the extras
13. candy bar , napkins , fruit juice , fruit , carrot sticks , chips , love
14. prepare as if she / he paid $8
15. 50 for it
16. works like a charm
target.review: Used about 2 lbs of ground beef and nearly a pound of chicken livers. Omitted the onion and did not roast the garlic. Added some ketchup and a bit of pomegranate juice. Delish. Even my picky eater ate this. Thank you so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuscan chicken stew

the original recipe comes from one of my favorite italian cookbooks. adapted to my own tastes and availability of ingredients, this comforting stew packs lots of flavor and can easily be thrown together for a mid-week meal. i usually serve mine with a nice green salad on the side.

1. heat the oil in a non-stick skillet until hot , not smoking
2. saute the chicken in the oil until brown
3. remove chicken from the pan and reserve
4. add the onions and peppers to the pan and cook 3 to 5 minutes until soft but not browned
5. add minced garlic
6. carefully drain tomatoes reserving liquid in a cup or bowl
7. mash the tomatoes into a thick paste more concentrated than tomato sauce but not as thick as tomato paste
8. add chicken , tomatoes , wine and oregano to the onions and peppers
9. simmer 30 minutes , until chicken is cooked through
10. if the pan becomes dry , add a little of the reserved tomato liquid
11. do so sparingly
12. add cannelloni beans to the pan , and simmer another 5 minutes until hot
13. garnish with sprigs of oregano
demonstrations.review: This was a nice start, but to my taste needed a lot more oomph. By the time I was done, I doubled the salt, garlic, and oregano and had added spinach and kidney beans. With parmesan cheese on top, it was quite nice. Thank you for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken tagine tajine with olives and lemon

from cooking light magazine, an easy way to prepare a dish like the traditional moroccan stew.
this is great served with couscous.

1. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in a large dutch oven over high heat
3. add chicken , cook 3 minutes on each side or until browned
4. remove chicken from pan
5. add onion and garlic to pan , cook 30 seconds , stirring constantly
6. add chicken , broth , olives , cinnamon , and ginger
7. bring to boil
8. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 45 minutes
9. turn chick over
10. cook , uncovered 15 minutes
11. remove chicken from pan with a slotted spoon
12. add lemon rind , juice , cilantro , and parsley to pan and cook for 30 seconds , stirring constantly
13. spoon sauce over chicken to serve
demonstrations.review: Fantastic recipe. This was absolutely delicious, lowfat and easy. Like the previous reviewer, I opted for more broth--about 1/2 cup--and I was happy I did so because it was so delicious. The light lemony flavor was delicious and not overpowering. A keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian style savory baked tofu

this was absolutely delicious! it will make a tofu lover out of you yet (i hope!). i let my tofu sit overnight in the marinade, and then baked it, and i thought it turned out great. as i describe below, be sure to really "press" the excess liquid out of your tofu to ensure that it absorbs the marinade. don't be afraid to put something really heavy on it to draw out the moisture. cast iron pan works great!  source: sunday moosewood cookbook

1. for best results , tofu should be "pressed" in order to remove excess liquid and absorb the flavors of the marinade
2. press tofu block between two plates , weighted down with a cast iron pan , large bowl of water , or heavy cans , for about 30 minutes
3. halfway through , you may dump the plate of water and flip the tofu block
4. to make marinade , simply whisk together the ingredients in a bowl
5. after tofu is pressed , cut the block into small cubes or triangles
6. place pieces of tofu into baking dish , and cover with the marinade
7. the tofu can sit overnight in the marinade , or can be prepared right away
8. preheat oven to 375 degrees
9. bake tofu about 35-45 minutes , or until all the liquid is absorbed
10. tofu can be eaten by itself , or added to stir-frys , salads , soups or sandwiches
demonstrations.review: Wonderful recipe and very flavorful. Even my picky 5 y.o. ate it. I discovered late that I didn't have sesame oil so I used peanut oil--which was very tasty too. I marinated it overnight. Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rosemary white beans

from tom douglas's book, and i love it. how can something so simple taste so wonderful.

1. cover the beans with cold water and soak overnight in the refrigerator
2. they will double in size so use a lot of water
3. heat the bacon in a large pot over medium heat , until the fat is rendered and the bacon is crisp , about 8-10 minutes
4. add the onions and cook 8-10 minutes until soft
5. add the garlic and cook 1 minute
6. then add the chicken stock and water til simmering
7. drain beans of their water and add to pot
8. cook on medium heat until soft , about 1 1 / 2 hours
9. there will be just enough liquid in the pot so it is frothy-- if necessary turn up the heat to reduce the liquid
10. stir in the rosemary and butter , and season to taste before serving
demonstrations.review: Wow. Incredibly simple. Indescribably good. Why aren't more recipes like this?!  Like some of the other readers I had to pour off some of the cooking water and will adjust next time. This is a real keeper. I will be making this often. Thank you, Gay.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna and sweet potato  kumera  patties

a quick n easy week night meal! 
recipe source - australian good taste mag.
yummy cold too, a nice addition to a picnic basket or lunchbox.

1. steam the kumera in the microwave until tender
2. drain and refresh under cold running water
3. transfer to a large bowl
4. use a potato masher or fork to mash the sweet potato until coarsely mashed
5. add the tuna , egg , parsley and breadcrumbs , and stir until well combined
6. season with salt and pepper
7. divide the tuna mixture into 8 equal portions
8. use wet hands to shape portions into 8cm patties
9. heat oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat
10. add the patties and cook for 3-4 minutes each side or until golden brown
11. remove from heat
12. divide among serving plates and season with salt and pepper
13. serve with lemon wedges , fries and a garden salad
demonstrations.review: These get a 5 star rating from me because my very picky 6 yo loved them. (He eats neither tuna nor veggies.) For my taste, they probably could have used a bit more kick. Still they were a nice and different way to serve tuna. I served them on buns. Next time I will do it with fries instead, as suggested.

target.recipe_text:
pineapple rice

this is a sweet rice dish that can beserved as a side dish, either hot or cold. it is also a great dessert if served with cream.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees
2. boil rice
3. place 1 / 3 of rice in bottom of buttered baking dish
4. cover with half of the pineapple , half the brown sugar , and half of the butter
5. repeat with next 1 / 3 of rice and second half of pineapple , brown sugar and butter
6. cover with last 1 / 3 of rice and pour over pineapple juice
7. bake covered for 30 minutes
target.review: I made this as a side dish to my Kilbasa Apple Kabobs.  It was good but a little disappointing.  It was sweet but there wasn't much flavor.  I drained canned chunky pineapple and poured the juice over the top. I will make it again but add some salt and maybe a bit of ground ginger or soy sauce.  My husband liked it but said it would be better as a dessert.  The kids loved it.  Thanx for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean  corn  and salsa dip  weight watchers

i got this from my daughter.  she had it with the baked tostito scoops.  it was delicious.  you can eat a whole cup and 15 scoops for 4 points, and one cup is a lot.  do you ever go to a gathering and there is nothing for you to eat if you are on weight watchers?  well now you can and you will enjoy it.  it can also be used for a condiment.  note:  i tried and tried to put in the tostito scoops in the ingredients and it wouldn't allow me, but you will need these for a dip.

1. rinse and drain beans
2. add frozen corn
3. add can of tomatoes and the salsa
4. mix well
5. serve with the scoops
demonstrations.review: Very easy to prepare and very tasty! My hubby gobbled it up quickly and when I told him it was weight watchers he didn't believe me!!! A definite keeper!! Thanx for sharing :) UPDATE: I just made this again but instead of using plain corn, I used Pictsweet Seasoned Corn & Black Beans with tomatoes, pepper and onions...WOW!! Awesome!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers beef stroganoff

8 points per serving - yummy beef stroganoff!

1. trim fat from steak
2. slice steak diagonally across grain into 1 / 4 inch wide strips
3. place a non-stick skillet over medium high heat until hot
4. add steak
5. cook 3 minutes
6. drain well
7. place skillet over medium-high heat until hot
8. return steak to skillet
9. add mushrooms , onion , and garlic
10. saute 2 minutes
11. add beef broth and next 5 ingredients
12. bring to boil
13. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 50 minutes or until meat is tender
14. remove from heat
15. stir in sour cream
16. spoon over noodles
17. sprinkle with parsley
18. serving size approximately 1 1 / 4 cup steak mixture and 1 / 2 cup noodles
demonstrations.review: This was very tasty and easy to make.  My husband could not believe it was weight watchers.  I used pre-sliced beef for stir fry and that saved some time.  I also used a bit of flour as others stated and it helped until I added the sour cream.  For some reason the sauce then became quite thin again but it was still very tasty.  Next time I may add a bit of cornstarch.  I served it over whole wheat egg noodes and there weere no leftovers!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
teriyaki sticky chicken   ww 4 points

a winning recipe from ww!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a small bowl , combine the ketchup , brown sugar , vinegar , teriyaki sauce and mustard
3. spray and 8x8 inch baking dish with non-stick cooking spray
4. place 1 / 2 of the sauce into the bottom of the baking dish
5. place the chicken breasts on top of the sauce and cover the chicken with the remaining sauce
6. bake uncovered for 40 minutes , or until the chicken is done and the sauce has thickened
7. divide any sauce that is in the dish evenly over each piece of chicken
8. serve with rice for additional points
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  I doubled the sauce because my husband needs to pour some over his rice.  When preparing the sauce I felt like the vinegar was a bit overpowering so I added a few dashes of dried ginger and wow....it was perfect!!  Will be making this one again.  My kids were fighting over the last piece of chicken!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato and  artichoke chicken breasts

very easy topping to your basic chicken breast - found this in woman's day magazine :)

1. mix flour , salt and pepper in gallon-size plastic food bag
2. add chicken , close bag and shake to coat
3. heat oil in large non-stick skillet
4. add chicken and , turning once , cook 8 - 10 minutes or until golden and barely pink in center
5. remove to a serving platter and cover to keep warm
6. in pan , add diced tomatoes , artichoke hearts and balsamic vinegar
7. bring to a simmer , cook 3 minutes to blend flavors
8. spoon on chicken , sprinkle with parmesan cheese and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good.  My family enjoyed it.  I wasn't sure if I should drain the artichokes or not, so I did, but reserved the juice.  I added some back during cooking.  I also set the chicken back on top to absorb some flavor of the sauce and to insure they were cooked all the way through.  We are HUGE fans of balsamic vinegar but found that it overpowered this dish, so I would definately suggest using half the amount.  I will make it again using the suggestion of adding fresh basil and less balsamic.  Thanx for a new dish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw asparagus pesto

after learning how good asparagus is for the body and how well it helps the kidneys. i thought this recipe was an excellent one. it is not cooked so the the asparagus is full of vitamin a, folic acid. did you know that asparagus has the largest percentage of rda of folic acid then any other food source!! so eat up. this is excellent served as a dip or a spread. this recipe came from one of my favorite magazines: organic gardening

1. put everything in a food processor
2. slowly add the olive oil
3. serve cold
demonstrations.review: I had 25 guests for Easter and not one person liked it.  I ended up throwing it away.  The taste combo was awful.  I even tried adding a bit of fresh basil as others suggested but it did not help.  Sorry.  At first I thought it was just me, but I asked everyone to try it with either fresh vegies or crackers and they all gave it a thumbs down.

target.recipe_text:
vanilla scented granola

great snack for everyone, or the for kids lunches or even as an after school treat! serve for breakfast with yogurt and fruit or over ice cream for dessert. watch your time in the oven because sometimes it cooks a little quickly. this recipe came from bon appetit, march of 2002.
a few baking tips i have learned from making this recipe often: i use a jelly roll pan so the granola will have maximum exposure while cooking.  also, if you do like your granola to clump, do not stir while baking.  allow to cool in pan for about 10 minutes or so, then run a spatula between granola and the pan to loosen.  you will have so many clumps you will have to break them with your hands ; )

1. position rack to middle of oven and preheat to 300
2. lightly spray large baking sheet with nonstick spray
3. mix next 5 ingredients in large bowl
4. combine oil , honey and sugar in small saucepan
5. bring to simmer over medium heat
6. remove from heat
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour hot liquid over oat mixture
9. stir well
10. using hands , toss mixture until thoroughly mixed
11. spread granola on prepared baking sheet
12. bake until golden brown , stirring occasionaly , about 30 minutes
13. transfer sheet to rack
14. cool granola completely
15. makes about 8 cups
target.review: I figured that I should finally leave a review since I make this ALL THE TIME!  This stuff is delicious.  I like the fact that it's simple.  We eat it more as cereal than anything.  I use pecans instead of walnuts, and sometimes I don't have vanilla, so I add just a little bit of maple flavoring, and it's still wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and pasta in white wine garlic sauce

this is simple and a crowd pleaser! intense combination of flavors that will have them back for seconds!

1. cut chicken breasts into bite-sized pieces
2. combine chicken in large skillet with water , olive oil , mushrooms , onion , garlic , and spices
3. cook until onion is tender
4. add tomatoes , wine , salt and pepper to taste
5. reduce heat , cover , and simmer about 15 minutes while preparing pasta , stirring occasionally
6. drain pasta al dente , place into serving dish and toss with olive oil
7. pour chicken mixture over pasta
8. serve with fresh salad and garlic toast
9. i am very generous with my spices when i make this dish and usually add more than the recipe calls for , but it is quite delicious as written
demonstrations.review: DELISH!  I was very pleased with this recipe.  Just enough spice, and very creamy.  I didn't have any heavy whipping cream, so I used milk, and little bit of melted butter and corn starch to thicken it up, and it came out delicious!  My 3 boys ate it up, which is not all too common!  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and garlic drop biscuits

these are very similar to red lobster's cheddar bay biscuits but a lot better than the recipes that start with bisquick, in my opinion. the kids adore them.

1. combine flour , salt , baking powder , cream of tartar , sugar and 1 / 8- 1 / 4 teaspoons garlic powder in a mixing bowl
2. cut in shortening using a pastry blender
3. mix milk and then cheese into mixture with a wooden spoon
4. drop by large spoonfuls onto greased baking sheet
5. bake at 425f for 10-12 minutes
6. mix melted butter and 1 / 8 teaspoons garlic powder together and brush on warm biscuits as soon as you remove them from the oven
demonstrations.review: Fabulous!  These were very delicious!  I don't use shortening, so I just substituted the same amount of butter for the shortening.  They turned out very soft, moist, and perfect!  My family of 5 devoured them.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I thought this was absolutely delicious.  I added chicken from this recipe:  http://www.food.com/recipe/cooks-illustrated-grilled-chicken-kabobs-420125 and it complemented perfectly with the salad.  The dressing was delicious as well.  I just can't wait to make it again!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s italian melt in your mouth meatballs

cooking the meatballs in simmering pasta sauce  will not only add so much extra flavor to the sauce the meatballs will be melt-in-your-mouth tender, you may of course oven-bake the meatballs for about 25 minutes,  --- don't be afraid to add in more parmesan cheese and a little more milk, there is no need to measure exactly, this recipe is pretty much foolproof, leftover cooked meatballs make a wonderful pizza topping just slice thinly and freeze until ready to use ----- these also make wonderful juicy burgers shaped into patties-- for more of my tried and true recipes check out my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com

1. mix all ingredients together in a large bowl
2. shape into small meatballs
3. drop the meatballs into simmering pasta sauce , do not stir for at least 20 minutes or you will risk breaking the meatballs
4. continue cooking in the simmering sauce for another 20 minutes
5. after the 40 minutes cooking time continue cooking your sauce with the meatballs in for as long as desired
demonstrations.review: Very good!  We thought these were very tasty.  The only thing I didn't like was that it made the spaghetti sauce a little greasy when I cooked them in the sauce.  Next time, I will probably try to bake them for a while first, and then put them in the sauce.  But, all in all, we really liked them, and will make them again!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli   cheese soup

a great soup, one of the deli classics.

1. saute onion and celery in butter in saucepan over medium heat until tender
2. add flour , and salt and pepper , cooking and stirring until mixture is smooth and bubbly
3. add broth and milk , stirring constantly until mixture comes to a boil and begins to thicken
4. add cooked broccoli , stirring until all is heated through
5. remove from heat and stir in cheese until melted and smooth
demonstrations.review: DEEEEElicious!!!  I am very happy to find a recipe for this soup that doesn't require processed cheese and buying special items like whipping cream, and being able to use ingredients I have at home (milk, cheddar cheese, etc.).  It tastes wonderful, and I will definitely make this again (and again, and again!)  Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
sweet salsa dump chicken   oamc

the theory is you dump this in a bag and freeze to pull out later. there are many variations which i will post separately but it's amazingly easy to make these up and have a different 

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the baggie is completely closed
6. place the bag on a refrigerator shelf to thaw
7. preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
target.review: I halved the recipe for DH and myself. We loved it! Made lots of sauce for the rice and was super simple. Made up an extra batch and stuck it in the freezer for another night. Made my own taco seasoning using Kittencal's recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
demonstrations.review: These cookies were quick to make up, but are far from my favourite. I used half white half brown sugar and half Skippy (the in-laws bought it, I usually get the 'just peanuts' kind) and half 'just peanuts' peanut butter. The batter was fine and they cooked up fine; hubby likes them but I prefer my own recipe. These were, believe it or not, not salty-tasting enough. Very easy and quick, though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oma s chocolate pudding

this is my mom's recipe.  she created it many years ago and it is still a favourite to this day.  we eat it while it is still warm.  this is the only way i will eat pudding now.  my sons just go nuts for this!  custard powder may be in the british import section or in with the pudding mixes and such in the grocery store.

1. scald the milk
2. in a bowl , beat the eggs
3. add the sugar , the cocoa and the custard powder
4. when milk is scalded , add one cup of it to the egg mixture slowly
5. then add the egg mixture back into the scalded milk slowly
6. cook until boiling
7. stir constantly
demonstrations.review: This makes an ENORMOUS batch! I scaled it down to "2" servings. I used soy milk instead of dairy milk (I heated it to almost boiling instead of 'scalding' the milk). It was a little lumpy but maybe next time I'll beat the egg a little longer. Also, DH and I like dark chocolate, so I will be doubling the amount of cocoa. But overall very creamy and thick... I ate what wouldn't fit into the tupperware warm and it was delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chocolate frosting icing

a wonderful frosting i have used for years made in very little time with perfect results and 100% better than any canned, this frosting is so good you will find yourself eating a fair amount of it before even using it to frost with! --- choose the amount of cocoa powder you desire for either a light, medium or dark frosting, and make certain to sift the cocoa powder and the confectioners sugar before using for the recipe--- this frosting *freezes* very well so double the recipe and freeze one batch for next time --- *note* for an ultra creamy fluffy milk chocolate frosting add in 1 to 1-1/2 cups thawed cool whip topping at the end of mixing the frosting and beat on low speed until blended ------- also see my recipe#80118 ---- recipe#282040 --- recipe#90142

1. cream the butter in a small bowl
2. blend in the cocoa powder , vanilla , confectioners sugar , alternately with the cream
3. beat with an electric mixer , until the desired texture is achieved
demonstrations.review: YUM! Used Earth Balance spread and soy milk as dairy-free subs... I put a little more than 3/4c cocoa in this because DH and I like dark chocolate. Nice consistency and great flavour! I also added a tiny pinch of salt... Delicious on my scratch chocolate cake!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy honey oatmeal cookies

these are easy to make! and healthy for you too (small amount of butter & sugar), but still so very sweet and wholesome. the cookies are chewy and go great with any other add-ins (raisins, cranberries, chocolate chips, etc.) courtesy of foodnetwork.com

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a cookie sheet with nonstick cooking spray
3. using a mixer with the paddle attachment , mix together the butter , brown sugar , honey , egg and water thoroughly
4. sift together the dry ingredients then stir in the oats
5. add the dry ingredients to the wet and mix
6. add any additional ingredients you've chosen
7. drop by heaping teaspoonfuls onto the cookie sheet
8. bake 12 to 15 minutes
9. cool on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Used coconut oil instead of butter and a gluten free flour mix. Added 1/2tsp of cinnamon and they turned out so great I almost ate the whole pan! My oven runs a little cool so I had to bake for closer to 13-14min (1tbsp sized cookies). Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review: NO FAIL and ALWAYS delicious! I use soy milk, cut the sugar a bit and use just over a half cup of boiling water. I have also made cupcakes and baked for about 20 minutes. They rose and were moist and didn't stick to the paper. My go-to cake recipe. I use Kittencal's Chocolate Icing to frost. I will never go back to boxed!

target.recipe_text:
jalapeno black bean dip

here's a dip you can make to suit your heat sensor--make it super hot, hot, or mild; it's still delicious and satisfying with your choice of chips.

1. mix all ingredients , but just 1 cup of shredded cheese
2. transfer to oven-proof dish and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese
3. bake uncovered at 350 degrees f for 15 minutes or until bubbly
4. serve with your choice of chips
5. enjoy with a cold drink
target.review:
I made this for our 
Chrismas party and printed out the recipe for three people during the party!  Everybody loved it.  I used a mexican cheese blend because that was what I had, and added enough jalapenos to make it have some zing.  I will make this often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed tomatoes

this recipe from southern living 1981 makes a wonderful side dish.  it's even more delicious using fresh tomatoes from the garden.

1. preheat the oven to 375 degrees
2. cut the tomatoes in quarters
3. reserve the juice that accumulates when you cut them
4. in a large bowl , combine the tomatoes , accumulated juice , 1 c stuffing mix , onion , sugar , salt , oregano and rosemary
5. mix well and pour in a greased 1 quart casserole
6. sprinkle the remaining 1 / 4 stuffing mix on top of the tomatoes and dot with butter
7. bake at 375 for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is great.  I have made it twice, and the butter on the top is an important part of the recipe.  The second time I added corn and black beaans.  It makes a great side dish, and with additions it can become a main dish.  Great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy sweet potato bake

this is a must at your holiday dinner table, it has just the right balance of sweet and spicy --- cooking time will vary depending on the size you cut the sweet potatoes you will love these!

1. in a resealable plastic bag toss the cubed sweet potatoes with melted butter or oil
2. add the rest of ingredients
3. toss well to coat
4. transfer to a greased baking dish
5. bake uncovered at 400 degrees for about 22-25 minutes , or until sweet potatoes are tender but not too soft
6. delicious !
demonstrations.review: I loved these sweet potatoes. Mine ended up kind of soft, probably because I cooked them too long. The flavor combination was great. I used 1/4 tsp cayenne and 1 tsp chili powder and they were just the right amount of spicy. I only used 1 1/2 tsp of seasoning salt. I will make these often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry oatmeal breakfast cake

got this one from my mom. i haven't tried it yet but will this summer. posted for safe-keeping. from gooseberry patch hometown favorites.

1. add the flour , oats , baking powder , salt , egg , sugar , 3 / 4 cup milk , and oil to a mixing bowl
2. stir to mix
3. fold in the blueberries
4. spread batter into lightly greased 8x8 inch baking pan
5. bake in a 400 oven for 20-25 minutes or until pick comes out clean
6. in a small bowl , mix together the powdered sugar , almond extract , and 3 teaspoons milk
7. pour / drizzle over warm cake
8. serve
demonstrations.review: Great coffee cake.  I didn't have enough blueberries so I used frozen cranberries.  It needed to bake about 40 - 45 minutes because of the frozen berries.  I also added a crumb topping (oatmeal, brown sugar, butter and cinnamon).  The 3/4 cup of sugar was perfect with the tart cranberries.  Made a great Sunday morning breakfast served with fresh fruit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion brie appetizer

guests will think you spent hours preparing these appetizers. they are very pleasing to the eye and the taste of brie, caramelized onions and caraway is delicious. prep time is approximate and includes the 15 minute chill time.

1. in a large skillet , cook the onions , butter , brown sugar and vinegar over medium-low heat until onions are golden brown , stirring frequently
2. remove with a slotted spoon and cool to room temperature
3. on a lightly floured surface , roll puff pastry into an 11x8 inch rectangle
4. spread brie over pastry
5. cover with the onions
6. sprinkle with caraway seeds
7. roll up one long side to the middle of the dough
8. roll up the other side so the two rolls meet in the center
9. using a serrated knife , cut into 1 / 2 inch slices
10. place on parchment paper-lined baking sheets
11. flatten to 1 / 4 inch thickness
12. refrigerate for 15 minutes
13. in a small bowl , beat egg and water
14. brush over slices
15. bake at 375f for 12-14 minutes , or until puffed and golden brown
demonstrations.review: These are incredible.  Easy to make and look great.  I doubled the recipe and stacked the cookie sheets in the fridge until I baked them.  I baked them through out the evening so we had some hot from the oven all night. They were a big hit.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese tortellini pesto pasta salad

this is most definately my favorite pasta salad in the world! i have been making it for years, but never wrote it down....well...thanks to recipezaar i'm learning to "measure", lol!!!! very happy to share! this recipe is for a small crowd. if making just for your family, omit the rotini, and add only as much of the rest of the ingredients (about half) that you'd like. don't worry, it's really simple and easy!

1. cook pastas , set aside to drain and cool a bit
2. in large bowl or punch bowl , add rest of ingredients , folding gently til well mixed
3. gently fold in pastas well
4. adjust seasoning to taste , meaning , add more salt , parmesan , etc
5. , til you like it
6. serve immediately , or refrigerate
7. if you make this say a day ahead of time , you'll need to "refresh" this
8. just add a bit more olive oil , salt and parmesan before serving
9. this salad is best , though , room temp , or even slightly warm
demonstrations.review: Not that this recipe needs another 5 star review.... This is an excelent pasta salad.  I made it as the recipe was written and it was wonderful.  As other reviewers commented you can chage it up to suit what you like and have on hand.  Sun dried tomatoes, cucumber, feta, etc. I did not add the olive oil when I made the  salad, but stirred it in later, right before I served it.  It was excellent the next day too.  Great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
thai grilled chicken thighs

this is my first recipe - please be kind! my kids love it and when i take it to a bbq everyone wants the recipe. it is a variation on one i found in epicurious a while ago. it is very easy and very yummy!!

1. combine all ingredients except chicken in a bowl
2. mix thoroughly
3. add chicken and leave to marinate at least one hour , preferably longer
4. grill chicken on the bbq , hotplate or in the griller until golden brown and cooked through
5. ususlly you would expect 12 thigh fillets to feed 4 to 6 people- in my family the kids eat 4 each so this recipe serves 3
target.review: I had to make it a couple of times to see if this recipe would work for me.  The first time, it didn't turn out so great, so the second time, I poked holes in the chicken and marinated it overnight.  It turned out much better that way, but it still didn't seem to work so great on breasts.  It was excellent on thighs.  Next time, I'll try cutting the breasts or pounding them to make them a bit thinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: This seemed to turn out well, even though I forgot to put the half and half in.  Hubby said it was good, and he's pretty picky.  The sauce was really delicious.  I will try to make it again with the half-and-half to see what that does for it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
angel hair pasta with simple garlic   basil

i adore angel hair pasta, and such a fine pasta doesn't always need a big sauce.  serve with some kind of cheese or "cheez" if you wish, sprinkled on top. my children like it with sliced olives.  there are many versions of this simple recipe, this one i adapted from www.cookingnook.com.  this would probably be good for 4 as a side dish or 4 for lunch with a salad.

1. bring a large pot of salted water to boil over high heat
2. meanwhile , heat the olive oil up a large saute pan over medium heat
3. once warm add the garlic and cook until it just begins to brown -- too long or too high and the garlic will burn
4. remove the pan from the heat and deglaze by pouring in the wine
5. return the pan to the heat and cook for a few minutes
6. the wine should reduce by about half
7. add in lemon juice , chopped tomato , and sea salt to taste
8. stir once or twice then remove the pan from the heat again and set it aside to wait for the pasta
9. add the pasta to the boiling water and cook until desired tenderness , following package directions
10. drain , then add the cooked pasta to the pan with the garlic & tomato mixture , along with the basil and some freshly ground pepper
11. toss well ,
12. generally they say 2 ounces of pasta is one serving , but for larger appetites this might not be enough
demonstrations.review: A very quick and simple recipe for pasta.  I used it as a side with breaded chicken. I forgot the lemon juice, though, and I had some Italian dressing mix that I threw in there for some extra flavor.  Also, I didn't have any white wine so I just used chicken broth.  This recipe is versatile enough to accommodate whatever you have in your pantry :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker hoisin beef stew

with an overnight marinade and all day cooking, this warm and hearty stew is an aromatic welcome after a long day. serve over hot rice with a side of steamed edamame or sauteed snow peas.

1. the night before , whisk together the broth , hoisin , hot sauce , garlic and ginger
2. add the beef , onions , carrots and celery
3. toss to coat well
4. cover and refrigerate overnight
5. in the morning , transfer meat mixture into the slow cooker
6. cover and cook on a low setting 6-8 hours
demonstrations.review: This was pretty good - a good recipe for a no fuss meal.  I didn't have any veggies on hand, so I made just the meat - that's probably where I went wrong.  Next time, I'll try with onions, maybe green peppers, and eggplant?  Can't wait to try again with veggies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for chicken marsala

a must have for anyone that loves italian food. this is a extremely easy recipe and it is great for dinner parties or a romantic dinner with your honey. try it and let me know what you think! i buy pre-sliced mushrooms and pre-made broth and it really cuts down the time you spend preping.

1. place chicken breasts between two pieces of plastic wrap
2. with a meat tenderizing mallet , pound chicken breast until they are 1 / 4 inch thick
3. dredge breasts in flour until all sides are coated
4. heat olive oil in a large skillet or frying pan
5. cook breasts until almost done , about 3-4 minutes on each side
6. remove from pan being sure to keep warm
7. deglaze pan with marsala wine , making sure to scrape bottom of pan to loosen all browned bits that may be stuck on
8. add broth , mushrooms and garlic
9. cook on medium / high for 10 minutes or until reduced by half
10. add breasts back to pan and cook for another 10 minutes
11. serve over angel hair pasta
demonstrations.review:
I thought it was pretty good, and my hubby liked it too, which is saying a lot. However, my picky daughter didn't care for it. And the plain pasta noodles I made to eat with it didn't do it for her either. Any ideas on how to kick up some pasta noodles without clashing with the chicken?

Oh, and I didn't use mushrooms because my family doesn't care for mushrooms. I just substituted onions for the mushrooms in the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage and sauerkraut pot

when i was a kid, i hated kraut. my mom popped it straight out of the can. then i learned that i could make kraut that i could actually like. come try some of my kraut. you'll like kraut too!

1. heat margarine in large pot over medium heat
2. add onions and saute until they are tender
3. add sauerkraut , apple juice , water , caraway seed , salt , pepper , and brown sugar , mixing all ingredients thoroughly
4. bring pot mixture to a boil
5. then reduce heat , cover , and simmer for 30 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. add smoked sausage pieces to pot , and cook for 30-45 minutes more , simmering , and stirring occasionally , until sauerkraut is tender
demonstrations.review:
So easy and so yummy. It does take an hour, but it's pretty easy - most of the time is just waiting. This recipe is definitely a keeper for me :)

Oh, like another reviewer said, I skipped the brown sugar because I know my hubby doesn't like his food too sweet.

target.recipe_text:
football lovers stew

when the weather turns nippy, warm up your insides with this stew. very good. found this on a calendar years ago. potatoes can be a substitution for turnips. this also can be made in a crock pot, add all ingredients cover and cook on low for 6- 8 hours.
note: the beef base is a concentrated beef stock made by superior touch. its in same location as bouillon cubes and i find it to have better flavor and not as salty.

1. in large kettle or heavy stock pot , saute bacon until golden brown
2. remove and set aside
3. combine flour , salt and pepper
4. dredge meat in flour mixture and brown meat over high heat a few pieces at a time in bacon drippings and olive oil , remove and set aside
5. add olive oil and saute onion until golden brown adding garlic at last minute
6. add orange juice , wine , tomato puree , bouillon beef base , nutmeg , bay leaves and salt and pepper to taste stir to deglaze bottom of pan
7. return bacon and browned meat to kettle , stir to combine and bring to a boil stirring occasionally , cover and reduce heat and simmer for 2 -3 hours
8. add turnips , carrots and mushrooms , cover and simmer another 1 hour or until vegetables are tender , stirring occasionally
9. remove bay leaves and sprinkle with parsley
10. serve with noodles if desired
target.review: OK, I must be doing something wrong because my review didn't show up.  I made this exactly as written - including using the better than bullion base.  I have trouble rating because I'm not a fan of wine in my cooking, but I wanted to be true to the recipe so I used it.  I wasn't wild over the taste (probably because of the wine)  but my DS and DD both liked the taste,   I will say it was a very hearty stew and perfect to warm you up on a cold day.  Made in honor of Papa D for the Papa D Cook-a-thon.  We'll miss you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy microwave blueberry mug cake

this recipe is something i came up with as a quick fix to my sweet tooth one lazy weekend afternoon.  so yummy and quick!

1. take a coffee mug and add the flour , splenda , brown sugar and baking powder
2. mix the ingredients together
3. add the milk and stir
4. continue adding more milk and stirring until it looks like cake batter
5. add a handful of blueberries and stir them inches
6. place mug in the microwave
7. microwave on high for 2-3 minutes , depending on your microwave's wattage
8. i sometimes microwave for 1
9. 5 minutes and cake comes out with a nice sauce
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Warning - use a large mug!  I used a regular mug.  I was afraid I wouldn't be able to mix it well, so I mixed the dry ingredients in a ziplock bag, then added it and the milk in parts.  It rose above the mug a good 3 inches, but didn't make a mess.  I made it exactly as written and cooked for 1.5 min.  Next time I'll cut down on the baking poser a bit, and add some vanilla & cinnamon since it was a tad plain.    Thanks for a quick snack - just what I needed, from thought to mouth in 5 minutes.  Thanks Galleguita!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy grill marinade

this is an all-purpose marinade used at the black dog restaurant in martha's vineyard. i love it on chicken but you could also use it over meat, vegetables or fish. if using it on white fish, omit the red wine vinegar. it's great for grilling.

1. mix all of the ingredients together and marinate your grilling choice in a large glass container
2. cover and put in the refrigerator
3. the longer you marinate , the deeper the flavors
4. i usually marinate overnight
5. have fun grilling !
demonstrations.review: We marinaded flank steak for about 10 hours.  I think it would be a better marinade for something lighter such as chicken or veggies, the acidity and the steak were good, but I think it would make the veggies pop.  Made for ZWT8 trip to Australia/New Zealand.  Thanks LIG!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy fruit salad

never fails to please.  update:  9/2/12--please note buzymomof3's (chef #949568) suggestion of using wondra (or perhaps recipe #438574).  thanks, buzymomof3!

1. combine all sauce ingredients in small saucepan
2. stirring to combine
3. bring to boil
4. cook about 3 to 5 minutes until thickened
5. cool to room temperature
6. pour over fruit in bowl
7. stir gently
demonstrations.review:
Update!! If you're in the USA, instead of 3 Tbs cornstarch, USE 3 Tbs of WONDER (gravy) flour - small blue can in flour section. Thickens perfectly.My lemons were a bit more tart this time, came out almost like a lemon curd. Delicious, but I'm putting it over ice cream tonight!

Nice light and lemony. But mine got too thick to pour over fruit. Still ate it because the taste was good, but would definitely cut back on the cornstarch next time. Thanks gailanng! Made for ZWT8, trip to Australia/New Zealand.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toffee malted cookies

another toh favorite!

1. in a large mixing bowl , cream the butter and sugars
2. add eggs , one at a time beating well after each addition
3. add pudding mix and vanilla
4. combine the flour , oats , baking soda and salt
5. add to creamed mixture
6. fold in the malted milk balls and the toffee bits
7. drop by rounded teaspoonfuls 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheets
8. bake at 350f for 12-15 minutes or until golden brown
9. cool for 2 minutes before removing to a wire rack
demonstrations.review: Wow - fantastic! They are great cookies, very rich tasting and surprisingly soft, even the next day.  I used skor chippets which are tiny, so I think a half a cup would have been fine.  Next time I'm going to increase the malted milk balls, I didn't have quite a cup's worth.  I chopped them each into 4-6 pieces which seemed to work fine (my ulu was perfect for this).   I used my silpat sheet which was great, because some of the toffee bled out and would have been a bugger-bear to clean from a pan. I did put a dozen balls in the freezer, and am going to see how they cook from there next, that way I can always have some ready.  Coffee B, I don't know how to thank you,  these will definitely be made often in our house.  Thanks!!   ***********Update 7-27-12 ***** I froze 12 of the raw cookie balls.  I took them out last night, let them thaw for a while and then baked.  Came out fantastic!  Great to have on hand for the unexpected guest.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
torrijas  spanish french toast

i found this on reciperewards.com. depends on the bread how many slices you'll get.

1. beat the eggs , milk and cinnamon together
2. dip both sides of the slices of bread in the egg mixture and fry in a heavy skillet over moderate heat until browned on both sides
3. dust liberally with powdered sugar and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Fantastic.  I love cinnamon and this had a good flavor.  I never thought of it before, but the day old bread really does make a better french toast!  I didn't think to take a picture before I put the powdered sugar on - I was too busy wanting to eat it because it smelled and looked so good.  Made for PRMR.

target.recipe_text:
egg filling for sushi

this makes a thick omelette which works very well in sushi. i like to use it in my sushi along with spring onions and mayo

1. in a bowl beat all ingredients together
2. heat a non stick or lightly oiled pan on a medium heat
3. i normally use a small frying pan to give me a 1 / 4 inch thick omelette
4. cook until golden on both sides
5. allow to cool and slice into 1 / 2 inch thick slices
target.review:
Yum!
I made this omelette and wrapped it with cucumber and rice to make sushi.  The sweetness in the egg really helped me with eating as I am suffering from morning sickness.  I was able to eat two rolls all on my own! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elvis presley s favorite whipping cream pound cake

this recipe appeared in our local newspaper about 20 years ago. the recipe comes from an old lady who was a dear friend of elvis. she made this cake for him every christmas and on special occasions. she made the paper promise to keep her name anonymous for fear that people would deluge her tupelo mississippi home with requests by fans to make her cakes for them.

1. butter and flour a 10 inch tube or bundt pan
2. thoroughly cream together sugar and butter
3. add eggs 1 at a time , beating well after each addition
4. mix in half the flour , then the whipping cream , then the other half of the flour
5. add vanilla
6. pour into prepared pan
7. set in cold oven and turn heat to 350f
8. bake 1 hour to 70 minutes , until a sharp knife inserted in cake turns out clean
9. cool in pan 5 minutes
10. remove from pan and cool thoroughly
11. wrapped well , this cake will keep for several days
demonstrations.review: The cake was very soft and rich in buttery taste.  But it was too sweet eventhough I only put 2 cups of sugar.  I would put even less if I make it next time.  It took me hour and a half to bake.  I would also add some almond extract to enhance the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
korean kimchee

my dad got this recipe from a korean lady when he was in korea about 28 years ago.my mom makes it really really hot by adding more pepper but i like it with less.

1. chop or slice cabbage into bite size pieces
2. put in a large bowl
3. add salt to about 2 cups water
4. stir to dissolve
5. pour over cabbage
6. add more water--enough to cover all cabbage and let stand overnight and all the next day
7. drain & rinse cabbage
8. add about 1 cup water the garlic and pepper flakes
9. let stand 2 more days then put in the fridge to chill and then eat
demonstrations.review: The kim chee came out pretty good.  It has the smell and taste of kim chee that I had at Korean restaurants.  Basically it is good recipe but I think it was too salty for me and my husband.  We're gonna make it again soon and this time we're gonna use less salt.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil and brown rice soup

healthful and hearty.  a good soup to make a lot of and have as a stand-by in the freezer for a quick, nutritious meal.

1. combine broth , 3 cups water , lentils , rice , tomatoes with reserved juice , carrots , onion , celery , herbs and sausage and bring to boil
2. simmer , covered , stirring occasionally , 45-55 minutes , or until lentils and rice are tender
3. stir in parsley and vinegar and season to taste
4. freezer
5. just defrost in microwave , reheat well and serve
demonstrations.review: Loved this so much!  It was easy and fast to make. I didn't feel like having any rice so eliminated the brown rice but it was still very yummy.  I made half of the serving size and no problems at all.  I got basil and pesto smoked chicken sausages from Trader Joe's.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous greek salad

be prepared for the best greek salad on the planet! --- plan ahead the dressing needs at least 2 or more hours to blend the flavors, i sometimes add in 1/4 cup parmesan cheese to the dressing for a more cheesy dressing, all amounts may be adjusted to taste ----  to marinade the salad allow to sit at room temperature before serving, see bottom of instructions --- you will find this and many more of my recipes posted here http://kittencalskitchen.com/2009/04/13/kittens-famous-greek-salad/  ---also see my recipe #359292

1. for the dressing
2. in a processor or use a wire whisk process / whisk the olive oil with lemon juice , 2 teaspoons dried oregano , garlic , dried , basil , red wine vinegar , salt and sugar until smooth
3. season with black pepper
4. chill in fridge for a couple of hours before using to blend flavors
5. place the salad ingredients in a large bowl
6. pour dressing over
7. toss to combine
8. if desired allow the salad to sit at room temperature for 20 minutes before serving , or you can refrigerate for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: This was really good.  I skipped parmesan cheese and dried basil since I didn't have any at home.  In replace of red wine vinegar I used a bit of white vinegar and balsamic vinegar.  The salad came out really good!!!  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy korean chicken

this was one of my favorite dishes growing up...mom would make it at least once a week. sometimes she would add potato cubes and fresh ginger, but this is the way we preferred it. i'm not sure what the proper name for it is, sorry! if boneless chicken is used, you can skip the first step, that is only done to discard extra fat from the skin.

1. boil wings in pot until blood no longer visible
2. drain
3. mix ingredients together and bring to boil
4. cover and let simmer over med heat for 15 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. cook until carrots reach desired tenderness
6. serve with sticky white rice
demonstrations.review: Yummy!!  The dish was easy and fast to cook.  However, I find it too salty for me so I added 2 tsp of sugar along with only 2 tbsp of kochujang only.  I even skipped the pepper flakes since I was kinda afraid that it will be too spicy for me.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
7 layer bean dip

this 7 layer bean dip is great for super bowl parties, work parties, other gatherings! pretty easy to make...you can use store bought guacamole if you can't find ripe avocados.

1. mix avocados , lemon juice , salt , and pepper
2. mix mayonnaise , sour cream , and taco seasoning mix
3. layer ingredients as follows
4. bottom layer: bean dip
5. second layer: avocado mixture
6. third layer: sour cream mixture
7. fourth layer: tomatoes
8. fifth layer: onions
9. sixth layer: olives
10. seventh layer: cheese
11. top with extra sour cream / olives / salsa , etc
12. if desired
13. serve with tortilla chips
14. this seems to be a little bit better if you can chill it for a few hours or over night to let the flavors intensify
target.review: This is the same recipe I've been making for many years.  Every time I make it it gets devoured instantly.  Absolutly the best. The only thing I do differently is to put the shredded cheese on right after the sour cream layer.  Then I layer on the tomatoes, olives, and onions.  I think it's prettier this way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins  healthy

you won't believe your taste buds once you get a piece of this muffin in your mouth.  these are so easy to make, and make a large size muffin.  these can be frozen also.  this recipe is courtesy of joanna lund.  each serving is only 186 calories as posted.  i have also substituted applesauce for the vegetable oil, and i use egg substitute.  in my oven it took closer to 25 minutes.  diabetic exchanges per serving:  1 starch, 1 fruit and 1 fat

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray 8 wells of a 12 hole muffin pan with butter-flavored cooking spray or line with paper liners
3. in a large bowl , combine flour , splenda , cocoa , baking powder and baking soda
4. in a small bowl , combine bananas , egg , oil / applesauce and sour cream
5. add banana mixture to flour mixture
6. mix gently to combine
7. fold in chocolate chips
8. evenly spoon batter into prepared muffin wells
9. bake for 20-25 minutes or until a tooth pick inserted in center comes out clean
10. place muffin pan on a wire rack and let set for 5 minutes
11. remove muffins from pan and continue cooling on wire rack
demonstrations.review: I've made these many times over the last several years and love them.  I do make a few changes based on a review on another site where I first got this recipe.  I reduce the splenda by 2 TBLS.  Increase cocoa by 2TBLS.  (This will add 40 calories.)  I also add 1 teaspoon coconut extract and 1 tsp butter extract.  These are wonderful and help me diet withought feeling deprived.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
