5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
demonstrations.review: Yummy.  I'll be making these again.  Instead of grilling the chicken, I cut it up, marinated a few minutes in fajita seasoning, and stir fryed.  I was surprised at how well all the flavors blended.  The sauce is the key I'm sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with black beans and rice

this is a variation of a cuban dish. the balsamic vinegar gives it an exceptional flavor!

1. in a large pan , heat olive oil and add red pepper flakes
2. add onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
3. increase heat , add chicken , stirring until cooked
4. lower heat to medium , add 1 tsp oregano , 1 tsp cumin , and simmer 1 minute
5. add black beans , pimentos , remaining spices , and balsamic vinegar
6. blend and simmer uncovered for 30 minutes , reseasoning if needed
7. while beans are simmering , bring broth to boil in a pan , add rice
8. lower heat to simmer , cover , and cook 20 minutes until rice is fluffy
9. serve bean mixture over rice
demonstrations.review: I liked this.  I really enjoy beans and rice. But I think I put too much chicken in and we like a little more spice.  Family wasn't thrilled so that's why I could only give it a three, but I liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
monterey jack chicken  bursting with flavor

served with your favorite mashed potatoes.... and this easy salsa topping, it tastes incredible..you will think you're in heaven!

1. at least one hour or even a day ahead of time , make the salsa topping
2. mix salsa ingredients in a small bowl , chill
3. in a 13x9" baking dish , place the chicken , and dot with butter
4. bake at 350 for 30-45 minutes , or until done
5. while chicken is cooking fry bacon and shred the cheeses
6. when chicken is fully cooked , remove from oven
7. turn oven up to 425f
8. spread the barbecue sauce on chicken , then the bacon and then add cheeses
9. place the baking dish , back into the hot oven or under the broiler for a few minutes until cheese is melted and bubbly , plate and top with the chilled salsa topping
demonstrations.review: I love eating this out at restaurants and have been making it at home for a long time.  But I've never tried this salsa before. The kids love monterey chicken but hate vegetables.  I thought the salsa really added to an already favorite dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburgers with brown gravy  total comfort food aka  meat cakes

these are sooooo great (and ez)! i grew up eating these about once a week and they are incredible with mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles and a veggie. while this recipe is basically my mom's, i have changed one thing...instead of using chopped onion in the burgers, i use an envelope of onion soup mix...it gives them the perfect flavor! this is now one of my family's favorite meals...try it and it will probably become one of your's, too. p.s. these burgers also work for grilling (without the gravy :).

1. combine ground beef , bread , soup mix , salt , pepper , ketchup , garlic powder , parsley and eggs in a large bowl until well mixed
2. prepare each burger with approx 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture and form into patties about 1 / 2 inch thick
3. heat a 12" skillet over med-high heat and fry burgers for about 5 minutes on each side , until they are almost done
4. remove burgers to a plate and discard all but about a tablespoon of drippings from skillet
5. lower heat under skillet and prepare brown gravy with water in a bowl or measuring cup
6. slowly pour into skillet , stirring constantly , scraping up any brown bits from the bottom
7. when gravy has thickened , place burgers back in the pan and cover
8. simmer for about 20 minutes , or until burgers are done
9. serve with mashed potatoes or egg noodles
10. yummy !
demonstrations.review: I'm really in the minority here, huh?  I did not find these easy to make.  I followed the directions exactly but the meat fell apart while cooking.  I used the two pounds of meat and it made so much I had to cook the meat patties in two batches in my skillet and still had about 1/3 of the mixture left, which I made a meatlof out of.  I cooked them longer than called for, but they still seemed a little less done than I would like.  And not nearly enough gravy. The overall flavor was good, but it's not a keeper for me.

target.recipe_text:
creamy tomato basil tortellini soup

a rich creamy tomato soup with some tortellini to fill your tummy.  serve with some hot garlic bread!  i just combined a few of my favorites from other recipes and added some parmesan it was a hit.  hope you enjoy it too!

1. coat soup pan with olive oil
2. add onion and garlic and saute till soft
3. add canned diced tomatoes , basil , tomato soup and two cans milk
4. stir till blended
5. add chicken broth and stir in tomato paste till blended
6. simmer for 20 minutes
7. add light cream and parmesan cheese
8. add tortellini and cook till tender
target.review:
This is great! Wife and even the kids loved it! I couldn't find fire roasted tomato's so I used a can of diced (regular) and a can of spicy (Brushetta type) and it had a really nice kick to it.

Restraunt quality soup for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sara s shepherds pie

i love making this. it's such a nice winter meal, and it's so easy and quick, and best of all..so economical!! growing up, mum made shepherds pie almost weekly.  over the years i have altered it, and this is the way my family enjoys it now.  we don't serve this with anything, except maybe a nice bread roll.

1. heat olive oil in a large saucepan
2. cook onions untiil tender , add beef and carrots
3. stir in gravy powder , garlic , pepper , and herbs
4. add enough water to just cover the meat mixture , stir , cover , and simmer until thickened , stirring occasionally
5. remove from heat , and set aside to cool
6. boil the potatoes until tender
7. drain , and mashe with butter and milk
8. using electric beaters , beat eggs into potato until creamy
9. pour the meat mixture into a casserole dish
10. top with mashed potatoes
11. you can spoon the potatoes on , or if you want a nicer presentation and you have the time , pipe on with a piping bag
12. top with grated cheese , and bake at 180c for around 30 minutes , or until cheese has melted and just started to brown
demonstrations.review:
Really enjoyed this and will make it again...I almost want it to turn cold cause it would be great comfort food. But I can wait til winter no problem.

Quite easy to make and very tasty...kids loved it too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq pork chops

can't remember where i got this recipe from but it is excellent !! it is sure to become a favorite of yours.

1. sauce: in pan combine water , vinegar , sugar , mustard , salt , pepper , and red pepper and onion
2. you can add a small amount of lemon juice if desired
3. bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer uncovered 20 minutes
4. stir in ketchup , worcestershire sauce , and liquid smoke and return to a boil
5. remove from heat
6. brown the chops on both sides and place in a casserole dish
7. pour the sauce over the chops
8. bake 350 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This is atleast a 4.5 star recipe. My Wife loved it and gave it a five. My 11 year old daughter gave it a 4 and my 13 yr. old son a 4 as well. A bit tangy for them. I can't help but think internetnut may be on to something with adding the brown sugar?

Will make this again. 

Thanks
Tapout

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom bacon burgers

nan

1. mix together first 8 ingredients in a bowl
2. shape mixture into 4 patties
3. grill over medium-high heat for 10-12 minutes or until done , turning once
4. just before taking off the grill , place cheese slice on each patty
5. serve on buns with lettuce , tomato , etc
demonstrations.review:
These were good burgers...I would have given a 4.5 if I could have. They were hard to handle and I fried them because I don't think they would have held together on the BBQ. I will try thme again and use a Burger rack to hold them if I have to and BBQ them...I'm sure that would help alot.

Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry swirl cheesecakes

these are divine! they are well worth the effort!  they were in a  desserts special, in a magazine, a couple of years ago.

1. preheat oven to 170c line a 12 hole muffic pan with paper cases
2. mix ground oreos and butter in a bowl
3. divide mixture among paper cases , pressing down well
4. bake for 5 minutes , then remove and cool
5. mash the raspberries to a pulp with the back of a fork
6. strain through a sieve into a bowl , pressing down well , then discard the seeds
7. stir in the icing sugar
8. place the cream cheese in the bowl of an electric mixer , beat until light and fluffy
9. add the castor sugar in a slow steady stream , beating until combined
10. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition , then beat in vanilla
11. pour cheese mixture over bases
12. place small drops of berry puree on top of cakes , and use a wooden skewer to carefully swirl through cheese mixture
13. baake for 10-15 minutes until just set
14. open oven door and allow cakes to cool completey in switchd off oven
demonstrations.review:
In a word...AWESOME! These are to die for! For some reason my kids think cream cheese is cheese...so they would not try them...until my Wife and I were going on about them. Then they proceeded to finish the rest! I think next time I'll tell em it has broccoli in it?

Thanks Sara

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my secret ingredient coleslaw

this is my own recipe for cole slaw. my secret ingredient gives it a little extra taste that everyone seems to like.

1. chop cabbage , carrots , onion and apple in food processor and transfer to large mixing bowl
2. add celery seed , sugar , vinegar and mayonnaise to bowl
3. salt and pepper to taste
4. stir until well blended
5. refrigerate until chilled and ready to serve
demonstrations.review:
Hey Chef #219653 Just because your Mother did it...doesn't mean everyone else in the world thought of it too!!!! 

I hadn't! and found this slaw to be GREAT! everyone said the apple made the slaw. 

Thanks again for what to me was a secret ingredient!!!

Tapout

target.recipe_text:
cream puff cake

a co-worker of mine brought this into work today and i had to share the recipe! it's like a giant eclair!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. in a large heavy suacepan , heat butter and water to boiling over medium-high heat
3. add flour and reduce heat to low
4. cook and stir until it forms a ball and pulls away from the sides of the pan
5. remove from heat and transfer to a large bowl
6. beat in eggs , one at a time , beating well after each egg
7. spread in bottom and up the sides of an ungreased 9x13 inch pan
8. bake at 400 degrees for 35 minutes
9. cool completely
10. to make the filling: in a large bowl , combine cream cheese and milk and beat until smooth
11. add pudding mix and beat until thickened
12. spread over cooled shell
13. top with whipped topping , and drizzle chocolate syrup over the top
target.review: "Wow," was the word of the night with this dessert!  I made it really quickly as my in-laws were coming to dinner.  Everyone loved it and between the six people eating it, there was not much left over.  It was fabulous and so easy to make.  I do have to agree with another reviewer who mentioned that creaming the cream cheese first a little at a time with the milk would make a difference.  I did not do that and I had a few chunks of cream cheese in the pudding mix.  It was still really good and I am looking for another reason to make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrots glazed with balsamic vinegar and butter

another great side to a roast. these are sweet/sour perfection. from bon appetit, december, 2000.

1. melt butter in heavy large pot over medium heat
2. add carrots and saut 5 minutes
3. cover and cook until carrots are crisp-tender , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
4. stir in sugar and vinegar
5. cook uncovered until carrots are tender and glazed , stirring frequently , about 12 minutes longer
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. add parsley or cilantro and toss to blend
8. transfer to bowl and serve
demonstrations.review: I just made 4 pounds of carrots this way for Thanksgiving dinner hoping there would be leftovers. I was wrong. Even the kids loved it. I did use splenda instead of sugar and I didn't really measure, but put in the amount that I would normally to take the tang out of the vinegar. Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s spinach parmesan rice bake

this is a wonderful easy side dish to chicken or meat and any leftovers freeze wonderful,  it may also be baked in a 10-inch deep-dish pie plate and cut into wedges, this may be doubled but i would still only use one package or spinach or maybe 1-1/2 packages adding in too much spinach will overpower all other ingredients,  prep time does not include cooking the rice --- for freezing prepare recipe as directed but do not bake, wrap pan in plastic wrap then tightly in foil and freeze, to serve thaw over night in refrigerator, remove wrapping bake at 350°f for 25-30 minutes or until hot.

1. set oven to 350f
2. generously grease a 11 x 7-inch baking dish
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients with a wooden spoon , mixing very well to combine
4. season with salt , pepper and cayenne to taste
5. transfer the mixture to the prepared baking dish then sprinkle with parmesan cheese
6. bake uncovered or covered for 25 minutes or until set
7. top with mozzarella cheese the last 5 minutes of baking
demonstrations.review: I was so hungry while I was making this that I am sure I would have eaten it no matter how it tasted.  It really was delish!  I added mushrooms to mine and sauteed them with the onions.  I did omit the butter and I did not use cream or even whole milk.  I used 1% and it worked just great.  I also put four eggs in instead of three.  I did use the brown rice as well and it was wonderful!  I am sure that if I used egg beaters and fat free cheese, it would still be just as good and really cut back on the fat and calories.  I know that this will be a big hit with my sister when we get together and make dishes that freeze.  I imagine it being a great dish if you were to add the chicken directly into it as well.  Thank you for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot ham and beans

this is cheap eating at it's best. really good for scraping by at the end of the month if your cash gets low. goes best with freshly baked corn muffins drizzled with honey.

1. sort beans and soak in enough water to cover overnight
2. or you may sort them and place in a saucepan with 2-inches of water to cover
3. bring them to a boil , boil for 3 minutes , then cover and remove from heat
4. allow to sit for one hour after boiling
5. whichever method you use , rinse and drain the beans before placing them in the crock pot
6. put the rinsed beans , garlic , onion , salt , pepper , parsley , cloves , ham or ham hocks into the crock pot along with 6 cups water or broth
7. cover crock , and cook on low for about 8 hours , or until beans are tender and creamy
8. skim any excess fat , if necessary , before serving
demonstrations.review: My husband's absolute favorite soup is ham and bean.  He said that this recipe tastes just like his grandmother's soup.  I hadn't expected it to be like soup, but it was.  I didn't mind that.  I suppose you could drain the liquid, but then what would you soak up with the cornbread?  It certainly was easy enough to make and we had plenty of leftovers.  Thanks for the quick, easy,and cheap recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jello cake

this is the moistest cake you will ever eat. i love it with strawberry jello and garnished with fresh strawberries. the cool whip makes such a pretty pure white and creamy frosting. it was my mom's favorite birthday cake. prep time is also chill time

1. prepare cake according to package instructions
2. allow to cool completely in pans
3. using a fork , poke holes all over the top of the cake through to the bottom
4. prepare jello according to package instructions except do not allow it to set yet
5. pour jello slowly over the entire surface of the cooled cakes
6. chill cakes until jello sets completely
7. to remove cakes from pans , set the pan in a dish of hot water for 1 minute
8. remove to a serving platter
9. frost with the cool whip
10. garnish with fruit pieces
11. keep any uneaten cake covered and chilled
demonstrations.review: Fantastic recipe!  I used yellow cake mix, strawberry jello, and applesauce in place of the oil.  I did let the jello sit for about 10 minutes on the counter before I poured it on top of the cake.  I topped it all off with cool whip. It was delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: I made two batches of these yesterday.  We ate an entire batch in the morning and I froze a batch in the afternoon.  I thawed a few this morning for my kids and then popped them in the toaster.  They were just as good as fresh out of the oven!  NO SYRUP NEEDED FOR US!  That's what makes it even better.  Without the sticky mess, they become portable for early morning rushes out the door.  I did notice on the first batch that when I mixed all of the ingredients together, the butter started to solidify again because the eggs and milk were so cold.  So, the second batch I made, I creamed the butter, sugar, and cinnamon befor adding the other ingredients.  Not only did it keep the butter soft, the cinnamon was incorporated more into the mixture instead of just floating on the top.  I did not have any vanilla, so unfortunately, I had to leave it out.  Had I had some, I would have definitely added it, but I didn't even miss the flavor as it was good enough on its own.  Thanks for a new family freezer recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
polish appetizer

this is a must at every holiday in our family. i suggest doubling the recipe...it always goes fast!

1. in a medium sauce pan , combine all ingredients except kielbasa
2. mix well , and cook over low heat until well balanced
3. cut kielbasa into bite size pieces
4. add kielbasa and heat thoroughly
5. make sure heat is low , and cook for at least an hour until the sauce cooks down
6. the longer it cooks , the better
target.review: This is the best!  When I first put everything together, I wasn't so sure, but after combining everything, I let it set on low in the crockpot.  After about two hours, it smelled and tasted so good!  My husband eats the leftovers (if there are any) with breakfast until it is gone.  I have used apricot preserves and pineapple jam, and also the peach jam from recipe#11488, and they all have turned out great.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cracker barrel green beans

this is the only way i can eat canned green beans!

1. in a 2-quart saucepan over medium heat , cook bacon until lightly brown but not crisp
2. when bacon has browned , add green beans
3. add salt , sugar and pepper and mix well
4. place onion on top of green beans
5. cover saucepan with a lid and bring to a light boil
6. turn heat down to low and simmer beans for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were very good, not exactly like cracker barrel, but close.  I drained the beans, and replaced the liquid with chicken broth, that was the only change I made.  Edited to say that these were excellent, but only after they sat for two days in the refrigerator.  They must be made ahead of time and left to sit, and then they are the best ever.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bleu cheese crab dip   oamc

this dip is excellent...it can be made ahead or eaten right away. great to pull out and take on the journey to relatives or friends. serve with potato chips. cook time is freezer time

1. mix together in order of ingredients
2. split the ingredients into two servable crocks
3. freeze
4. allow to thaw about 4-5 hours serve in a dish with crock in middle surrounded by potato chips
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I make crab dip similar to this without the bleu cheese, and wanted to try this b/c I love blue cheese.  To be honest, I really didn't taste the blue cheese in it, it tasted almost like my regular dip, which is very good.  I did add a little sour cream, so maybe that cut down on the flavor of the cheese.  But, still, it was a very good dip!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummiest ever baked mac and cheese

a friend brought a big pan of this to a potluck and i had to have the recipe to make for my family.  it is so yummy and creamy that it's hard to stop eating.  we like it as a main dish with a salad, but you could serve it as a scrumptious side dish.  these are directions for the full batch which will serve a crowd.  it halves easily.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. cook pasta according to pasta directions just until done - you don't want it mushy , because it will absorb a little of the cheesy liquid in the oven
3. combine soup , evaporated milk , butter , salt , and pepper in a large microwaveable bowl
4. cover with plastic wrap , leaving a small vent , and cook for 6-7 minutes until the butter is melted and the mixture is warm-to-hot throughout
5. in a large baking dish , spread 1 / 3 of the cooked noodles
6. top with 1 / 3 of the sauce
7. sprinkle with 1 / 3 of the cheddar
8. repeat layers twice , ending with the cheese
9. bake for 40-45 minutes
10. when it comes out of the oven , sprinkle with a little dried parsley if desired
11. this gives it visual interest , and you can also pretend it's healthier
12. let stand for 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This is best mac & cheese recipe I had ever made.  I don't like the ones that are all cheddar cheese, and am usually stuck making a velveeta recipe, but never really loved that either.  This is now the only mac & cheese I will make!  It cooked up very casserole like, but still very gooey & cheesy - it was just great!  I made half a recipe, and cut the butter and shredded cheese back a bit (maybe 3 T butter & 2 cups shredded cheese).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry bran breakfast treats

mini treats with the flavor of fresh blueberries and loaded with fiber. a wonderful way to begin your morning! adapted from a weight loss websites email newsletter.

prep tip: color, not size, tells you which blueberries are the ripest. look for berries that are deep purple to blue-black.
serving tip: spread the warm halves of each muffin with a little mashed, ripe banana instead of butter.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit and lightly spray a nonstick miniature muffin pan with cooking oil spray
2. in a medium bowl , combine bran , flour , flaxseed , baking soda , cinnamon , salt and set this aside
3. in another medium bowl using a hand mixer or blender , combine the milk , honey , banana , egg , olive oil , and vanilla extract until smooth
4. make a well in the center of the dry ingredients
5. pour in one-third of the liquid mixture and stir until smooth
6. slowly add remaining liquid mixture and stir until combined
7. add blueberries and stir again , do not over mix
8. carefully spoon 2 tablespoons of batter into each muffin cup
9. bake approximately 8 minutes , or until the tops spring back when pressed gently , do not overbake
10. place pan on a wire rack and cool 10 minutes before removing muffins from cups
demonstrations.review: I love these, not too sweet, but very good for you.  I made it with an extra banana and walnuts instead of the blueberries, and it was fine.  I have also used the blueberries as well, and liked it too.  I am also trying it with chopped peaches instead of blueberries tonight!  I also suggest to fill the mini muffin tins full, as they do not rise much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel apple dessert squares

it is apple picking season here in maine and this is an awsome recipe for apples. the caramel forms while it bakes. this comes from the bisquick web site.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. mix bisquick and granulated sugar in medium bowl
3. stir in milk until blended
4. pour into ungreased square pan , 9x9x2 inches
5. top with apples
6. sprinkle with lemon juice
7. mix brown sugar and cinnamon
8. sprinkle over apples
9. pour boiling water over apples
10. bake 50 to 60 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
11. serve warm with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: This was just ok for me.  I usually really like bisquick recipes, but I guess what I didn't like was the flavor the topping made.  I expected it to be really caramel like, but it was just barely so, and a bit runny, and there wasn't enough gooey stuff to the amount of cake when it was finished.  It wasn't terrible, but I probably wouldn't try it again.

target.recipe_text:
cap n crunch french toast

i saw this prepared on diners, drive-ins, and dives, and they only shared ingredients, not amounts.  after searching many french toast recipes, this is what my kids and i arrived at.  you'll never search for another french toast recipe after this.

1. pour cap'n crunch into a gallon-size ziplock bag and crush to a course meal -- make sure there are a few good size pieces in the mix
2. pour into a 9x13 pan in order to dredge properly
3. combine eggs , sugar , cream , vanilla , and spices in a large bowl
4. it will have the consistency of custard
5. soak each slice of texas toast in wet ingredients , 30 seconds each side
6. be sure the edges are moist , too
7. dredge in cap'n crunch , lightly press onto each side , and around the crust
8. place on parchment paper until all slices are coated
9. heat 2 tbs
10. butter in large skillet , then gently place slices in pan
11. two at a time
12. cook three minutes per side
13. place on parchment covered baking pan in a warm oven
target.review: This can be delicious and not that sweet.  Try crushing the cereal (I actually use Special K Vanilla Almond) and after dipping the bread (please don't soak) in the eggs mixture and cereal, Bake it in the oven (325-350) for about 10 minutes.  This is what puffs up the bread and cooks the inside so it doesn't come out gooey or undone.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kate s basic crepes

this is my foolproof method for crepes.  there are step-by-step photos in the french forum to go with it.  use oil for savory crepes, sweet butter for dessert crepes.  depending on your taste and the weather (humidity affects the batter), use anywhere from 6 - 8 eggs.  and check out the crepes! cookbook for dozens of crepe fillings and recipes posted here on 'zaar.

1. first , combine the flour , eggs , salt and oil in a large bowl so you have plenty of room to whisk and combine these ingredients well
2. then add about a quarter of the milk and mix till smooth
3. when it is smooth , add the balance of the milk all at once and mix gently until you have achieved a homogenous batter --no lumps
4. then let the batter sit at room temperature for at least half an hour -- now your batter is ready
5. heat your skillet or , if you are lucky enough to have one , your crepe pan , add oil or butter or a combination of both--just enough to give the pan's surface a sheen , and add just enough batter to make a very thin veil across the pan
6. then , using a spatula , carefully turn your crepe once it begins to brown around the edges and cook it on the other side
7. when it is lightly browned on both sides , remove it from the pan and lay it on a warm plate
8. repeat the process , stacking your crepes one on top of the other
demonstrations.review: Where do I start?!  These were wonderful and fun to make.  I really felt like I learned a great new technique I made these. I only needed 6 egges, batter was terrific and I let it sit out while I made the fillings I was going to use (about 30-45 minutes).   I goofed on the first one (I was using a cast iron skillet, too heavy for me to work with for these).  Once I got the pan right, the crepes came out terrific.  I waited for my pan to be good and hot, brushed it quickly with oil, poured in some batter (really thin) then turned the pan around to spread the batter thin.  Flipping it was easy as long as you waited until the edges were brown.  I used these three ways (1. "Kate's Easy Crepes Suzette", 2. "Delice Lorraine", and 3. Nutella, whipped cream and sliced strawberries) The first two are recipes on Zaar the third is almost assuredly on Zaar, but it was easy enough to not need a recipe.  What an outstanding treat for family and guests.  Thank you!!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with spicy honey orange glaze

nan

1. in small bowl , combine honey with juice concentrate , orange zest , garlic , salt and red pepper flakes
2. rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry
3. season lightly with salt
4. in large non-stick skillet , heat margarine and oil over medium-high heat
5. add chicken and cook about 4 minutes , until seared
6. turn chicken , cook another 4 minutes until just cooked through
7. pour honey mixture over chicken and cook , turning chicken to coat as sauce begins to thicken , about 2 min
8. serve chicken breasts with honey-orange glaze spooned over the top
demonstrations.review: I rate this 5 stars and so does my family.  I have tried it twice now and both times received rave reviews.  Thank you for posting this one, although now my husband doesn't think we ever need to order Chinese food again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
benihana hibachi meat

this is a copycat of the benihana hibachi steak, shrimp, chicken or scallops served at the restaurant. feel free to mix and match. choose other benihana copycat dishes and have a benihana night in.

1. mix all marinade ingredients in a bowl
2. marinate meat in the sauce for 30 min or longer
3. heat a frying pan or flat grill on high heat and stir-fry the meat until desired doneness a few minutes at most
demonstrations.review: I made this with chicken and it was just so so.  It was fine and I paired it with rice.  My family is used to a little more....spice or flavor.  I'd probably add some red chile flakes or ginger garlic paste to add a little more zing to it.  Overall, it was alright, but probably won't be requested by my team again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flank steak churrasco with chimichurri rojo

churrasco is  south american style skewers.  i got this from cuisine at home magazine.  i haven't tried this yet, but sounded good!!

1. slice the steak against the grain at 45 degree angle into 1 / 4"-thick strips
2. in a large bowl whisk together remaining ingredients
3. preheat grill to medium
4. toss meat slices into the chimichurri to coat
5. thread 4-5 strips onto each of 4 metal skewers
6. fold each strip accordion-style , then spear through the center with the skewer
7. spread strips down length of the skewer
8. grill skewers , covered , for 3 minutes
9. turn , baste with remaining chimichurri , and grill , covered , for 3 more minutes
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic and actually made for a memorable breakfast.  I had and extra pound of flank steak and wanted to use it in a breakfast dish and found this marinade.  I cut very thin strips of the flank steak and let it sit for 15 minutes in the marinade and prepared it in a cast iron skillet.  While it cooked (just a few minutes) I toasted cheddar-garlic bread and fried eggs.  To serve, I buttered the bread placed an egg on top and topped it all with the prepared flank steak and little sauce that formed while cooking.  Rave reviews from the family, this one is a keeper!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pot stickers  chinese dumplings

i found this recipe somewhere online and made a few variations. it tastes just like something you would get in the restaurants.

1. mix first 10 ingredients in a bowl
2. take a wonton wrapper and place 1 heaping teaspoon of filling in center
3. moisten edges with water , fold over and press to seal edges
4. add 3 tablespoons of peanut oil to a large skillet and saute until the bottoms are golden brown
5. when golden brown , add 1 / 2 cup chicken broth , cover pan and simmer 8 minutes
6. remove from pan
7. reserve broth in a separate bowl and repeat process until all potstickers are cooked
8. keep warm on a plate covered
demonstrations.review: These are excellent! I followed the recipe exactly and they turned out flavorful and perfectly cooked. My family loved them! I also made the soy ginger sauce Evie referred to and it was the perfect finish!!! Thanks for posting, it satisfied a craving!  Update:  I used the extra prepared filling to make breakfast sausage patties the following morning also to rave reviews :)

target.recipe_text:
red lobster pina colada dipping sauce

recipe by chef micheal laduke - senior director of culinary development at red lobster. came from red lobster's website. the recipe is no longer on the site, but it's a good thing i posted it here. enjoy!

1. combine sour cream and coco lopez in a mixing bowl , and mix together gently
2. do not use an electric mixer or over mix by hand as it will cause the sour cream to break down and make sauce too thin
3. drain crushed pineapple
4. fold crushed pineapple into cream mixture
5. finish with juice from one lemon
6. cover and store refrigerated
target.review: Just like Red Lobsters!! Fantastic sauce. We served it with Recipe #93688. Make sure you use Coco Lopez Cream of Coconut. It comes in a can. It isn't a pina colada drink mixer that comes in a bottle. It is much thicker than what comes in the bottle. Try to mix the sauce up ahead of time. The sour cream flavor isn't as pronounced after a little while.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked ziti with fire roasted tomatoes

this is a recipe from muir glen organic tomatoes, but i know hunt's has a fire roasted diced tomato product out too. my dh loves this--he requests it about once a month!

1. heat oven to 375
2. spray 2 quart rectangular glass baking dish
3. in a 10 inch non stick skillet , cook beef , onion and garlic over medium heat , stirring frequently , until cooked
4. add zucchini , cook 2 minutes
5. stir in tomato sauce , diced tomatoes , oregano , salt and pepper
6. heat to boiling
7. toss with pasta
8. spread in dish
9. cover with foil
10. bake 20 minutes
11. sprinkle with cheese
12. bake uncovered , about 5 minutes or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: This was a nice change from my usual Italian dishes. My husband and I really enjoyed the addition of the zucchini...the kids, not so much. ;) The only change I made was to use a full pound of ground beef and dried oregano. Next time, I plan on using only 8 oz. of tomato sauce and not drain the tomatoes. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef in guinness

i make this for my in laws whenever they come to stay. perhaps it will suit your own finicky relatives! serve with mashed or boiled potatoes, and pickled beets if you have them.

1. season flour with salt and pepper in shallow bowl or pan
2. coat beef pieces with flour mixture
3. heat oil in saucepan and fry meat and onions until lightly browned
4. add carrots to pan
5. pour in guinness , and season to taste
6. bring to boil , then cover and simmer 1 hour 30 minutes or until meat is tender and gravy is thick and rich
demonstrations.review: I made this for my Guinness loving Dad without much hope of liking it myself. I was surprised though because it was extremely tasty! I used stew meat and it cooked up extremely tender. I did have to add some flour water at the end to thicken up the gravy but that could be just personal preference of how we like our gravy. As suggested, I served with boiled new red potatoes and pickled beets. Dad and DH put there potatoes in a bowl with the meat and ate it like a stew. Mom and I ate them separately. Also made Guinness Beer Bread  #55355 which rounded out the meal nicely. Thanks for a great recipe Ppaperdoll!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon orange butter

from the foodcourt column, weekend.

1. combine everything in a blender or mixer
2. process until smooth
3. store refrigerated for upto 1 week or frozen for upto 2 months
4. serve on warm bread toast slices for a quick snack or brunch
demonstrations.review: I was in the mood for orange-cinnamon rolls but I didn't have the time to make them. I decided to try this recipe to see if it would satisfy the craving. Very easy to make and lovely on toast. It is even better the second day, as the flavors have blended more. Next time I will cut back on the orange a bit and increase the cinnamon so it is the more predominant flavor, but that is personal preference. This would make a fantastic addition to a brunch buffet as it makes ordinary toast something special. Thanks, Char, for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange chocolate chip muffins

what a great excuse for chocolate in the morning. this recipe came from a king arthur flour catalog long ago - i get rave reviews everytime i make them. so, go ahead, have chocolate for breakfast!

1. in medium mixing bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and chocolate chips
2. in a small mixing bowl , whisk together milk , vegetable oil , egg , and orange oil or peel until light
3. add wet ingredients to dry and stir together for 20 seconds , or only until ingredients are just moist
4. if you see lumps , it is ok to leave them
5. lightly grease cups of 12-cup muffin pan and fill each 2 / 3 full w / batter
6. sprinkle 1 / 2 teaspoon sugar over each for a crunchy , sugary crust
7. bake in preheated 400 f oven for 18 to 20 mins
demonstrations.review: A delicious gourmet-type muffin! The only 'fault' I can find with them is they are just a tad bit crumbly but the taste makes up for that. ;) I prepared them exactly as written except I used muffin papers. We were going to be eating them over a few days and muffins seem to stay moister longer when baked in papers, I think at least. I didn't measure my zest, I just used my microplane zester and added the zest of a whole medium-sized orange. These are definitely going into the "make again" file! Thanks for posting the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry orange bread

a wonderful recipie for blueberries. adapted from "blueberry thrills" by katherine knapp aho.

1. grease well , two 1 1 / 2 quart casseroles or two 9x5" loaf pans
2. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt and baking soda
3. in a medium bowl , beat the eggs with a fork and add orange juice , butter or margarine and orange peel
4. stir egg mixture into the flour until the flour is just moistened
5. do not over mix
6. dredge the blueberries in a small amount of flour , add to the mixture , gently stirring them into the batter
7. pour into baking dishes
8. bake in a preheated oven set at 375 for 50 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
9. remove loaves from baking dishes and cool on wire racks or serve immediately as desired
10. best served the day made
demonstrations.review: A heavy, dense bread...a little dry...but good with coffee especially. Despite the orange juice and zest, the orange flavor isn't very strong. The batter is very stiff and hard to mix but it baked up very nice. If I made it again, I'd cut the flour back to 4 cups and see if that lightened it up any.

target.recipe_text:
apple everything cake

i first found this on international recipes online, and it sparked my interest because it's supposedly from new york (new york does have great apples). it's a very simple cake, and doesn't have any cinnamon in it, so it's become my daughter nomi's favorite.

1. grease and flour a large fluted cake pan
2. preheat oven to 325 degrees f
3. beat oil , milk , extract and sugar till well combined
4. beat in eggs to combine
5. sift dry ingredients together and beat into to wet mixture and combine well
6. stir in fruits and nuts
7. turn batter into pan and bake until tested done with wooden toothpick- about 60 to 75 minutes
8. cool in pan 15 minutes and remove to rack to cool well
9. wrap overnight before slicing for best flavor
10. dust with sugar / cocoa
11. freezes well
target.review:
Was a nice moist cake, unfortunately the cherries I had planned to use had turned to vinegar so I just added some extra nuts and such.
Was nice with tea/coffee after (one of!) the festive meals during the last few days of Rosh hashana
Thanks and a happy new year!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey and cheese rolls

a delicious greek dessert that is sure to impress. simple to make and so different!

1. mix feta , anthotiro , honey , egg yolk and cinnamon until a thick pulp is created
2. cut the filo crust in stripes of 12 cm wide each
3. baste with melted butter and place on the bottom of each stripe a portion of the mixture
4. then roll each stripe like rolling a cigar
5. baste the surface of each roll with melted butter and bake in preheated oven in 160 - 170 c until golden
6. garnish with honey and grated nuts
demonstrations.review:
Thank you
I made this desert for a milk meal on the festival of Rosh hashana (the Jewish new year) was a huge success. I used ricotta and something called Toborg which i discovered,which is a bland crumbly white cheese (similar to what is called cna'an in Israel)
I put about 1 large tablespoon of filling at the bottom part of strip and after first roll I presed the sides down with my thumb to stick the sides down, then it is easy to roll. Another thing- the filling was enough for exactry double (got 12 rolls)
Thank you very much1 delicious

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spring mix salad with pomegranate  honey dressing and toasted p

this is a pretty recipe.  the pomegranate is a beautiful tropical fruit with seeds that are crunchy and help give texture to the whole salad experience.  you can change the dressing to your liking, but make sure you use a ratio of 1:3 acid to fat.

1. sort through the spring mix salad greens and clean out any leaves that are not completely fresh
2. mix all ingredients except pomegranate seeds and nuts in a jar or the container of a blender
3. whirl until smooth
4. place in refrigerator until needed
5. just before service , drizzle salad with dressing and arrange on a plate with pomegranate seeds and ground pistachios sprinkled all over
demonstrations.review:
ThoughtI'd give you a review :)
I made this for Rosh hashana festival meal (Jewish new year) as pomegranate is one of the ffrits used to symbolise the new year being full of sweetnes.
The salad was very good. I added 1 tablespoon pomegranate juice to the dressing.
Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken ii

nan

1. preheat oven to 450
2. combine all dry ingredients in a plastic bag
3. wash your chicken and shake off excess water
4. drop in bag and shake each piece
5. place in a metal pan skin side down and put in preheated oven
6. turn pieces over after about 20 minutes
7. continue baking until crisp and browned
demonstrations.review:
Sorry to spoil the good reveiws, I made this to the t but it wasn't a big hit, it wasn't too dry, the seasoning was good, but it was just felt too heavy to us. Maybe we are just not used to "fried chicken" (we never eat it) or substitutes.
Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
extremely healthy fiber packed zucchini carrot cranberry bars

this is a recipe i came up with myself after getting sick of on the run meals and i wanted to make something that would keep well during the day and energize me--while also giving me the fiber, veggies, and nutrition i need. a bar for quick snack to tide you over or even a few "bars" for a meal replacement. 
obviously i like being healthy, so if you like the bread bar sweeter then use 3/4 cup of both brown and white sugar. this is good served warm with a slice of fat free cream cheese, cottage cheese, or even honey.

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a cake pan with nonstick cooking spray
3. mix together milk with lemon juice
4. set aside for 5 minutes
5. beat egg well , then add brown sugar , sugar , oil and beat together again
6. add in vanilla , zucchini , carrots , cranberries and the milk and lemon mixture
7. mix together well
8. put the flour , cinnamon , baking soda , salt and nuts if you added any in another bowl
9. mix them together
10. add the dry mixture with the wet mixture , mix together until just combined
11. spoon the mixture into the oiled pan and sprinkle some cinnamon sugar mixture onto the top if desired
12. bake for about 35-40 minutes or until wooden stick inserted into the middle comes out clean and the bars are not sticky in the middle
13. turn off the oven but don't open the oven or take the pan out , just leave it in there for 5 minutes if you like the outside crispy
14. don't overbake , they become really dry and hard
demonstrations.review: I won't repeat what previous reveiwers wrote (cake not bars,OK taste, ommited PB etc) I just want to add an important note- these must be kept in the fridge as they have the milk in them ,I had to throw the whole lot out today even th'o were baked fresh just 3 days ago and kept in an airtight box (  I live in a warm climate) beware :) otherwise, thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage for those who dislike cabbage

this is so much nicer than plain steamed or boiled cabbage. try it on the cabbage haters in your family and see if it converts them.

1. in a large skillet , heat butter and oil over medium heat
2. add cabbage , garlic and brown sugar to pan
3. saut until the cabbage is limp , about 5 minutes or so
4. reduce heat to medium-low and stir in vinegar
5. cook , stirring very often , for approximately 20 minutes
6. taste and if cabbage is too crunchy for you , continue to cook for a few more minutes
7. add salt and pepper to taste and serve
demonstrations.review:
this was ok nothing out of the ordinary to be honets, noone would even taste it except for me, and I ifnished it off with ease-added a tbsp of caraway seeds to the finished dish-was a nice addition
Thanks

target.recipe_text:
french dip roast beef for the crock pot

this is one of the best recipes i've come up with for beef roast. the cheapest cuts come out tasting like you slaved over a stove all day long. you can add potatoes and carrots to the recipe if you like, or shred it and serve it as a french dip sandwich with the au jus juice from the crock pot on the side. if you are watching your sodium, use the lite soy sauce and it will taste just as delicious.

1. place roast in a 5-quart slow cooker
2. combine soy sauce and next 6 ingredients
3. pour over roast
4. add water to slow cooker until roast is almost covered
5. cook , covered , on low for 7 hours or until very tender
6. remove roast , reserving broth
7. you may shred roast with a fork and serve on sandwich rolls with the broth on the side for dipping
target.review: I don't even like roast that much, but loved this.  My DH said this was one of his favorite meals in my repitoire.  I didn't have rosemary or thyme and it came out great.  I also had to cook this on high due to lack of time, and it was wonderful.  We'll make this again.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fat free  sugar free   cholesterol free banana bread

this banana bread is very good and very healthy! it does tend to come out a bit dense for my own personal taste, but considering all the substitutions i've made to the conventional recipes, it's fantastic! enjoy!

1. mix all ingredients together either by hand or with an electric mixer , if you have one
2. spray loaf pan with pam non-stick spray , then pour batter into pan
3. bake for no more than 45 minutes at 300 degrees
4. test for doneness with a toothpick at 35 minutes , then every 5 minutes thereafter
5. remember to subtract 10 minutes of baking time when using a glass pan !
demonstrations.review: I made this for me (watching my weight) and my diabetic uncle.  It was awesome!  I doubled the recipe and make a loaf and 12 muffins.  The muffins cooked quickly, but the loaf took longer than the recipe states, just keep watching it like she suggested. Thank you for the recipe Jen O.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my favorite roll out sugar cookies

nan

1. cream sugar and margarine
2. add egg and flavorings and mix well
3. stir dry ingredients
4. mix into sugar and margarine mixture
5. refrigerate 2 to 3 hours
6. heat oven to 375f
7. roll out 3 / 16-inch thick
8. bake 7-8 minutes until delicately brown
9. let cool
10. icing for roll out sugar cookies: 2 cups powdered sugar , milk and 1 / 2 tsp vanilla
11. icing for roll out sugar cookies: in a mixing bowl , sift powdered sugar
12. gradually add milk , stirring continuously until mixture is the consistency of a thin glaze
13. add vanilla
14. blend well
15. food coloring may be added , if desired
demonstrations.review: My 5 year old couldn't stop hugging me when I made these cookies for Santa and for him!  These cookies are light and tender yet weighty enough to hold a good shape.  I also rolled these into balls and sprinkled them with colored sugar and they worked well that way also.  They are a bit whiter in color than most sugar cookies, so be careful not to overbake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
company chicken pasta salad

this is a delicious treat to serve your guests.  another entry in the rsc winter 2005 contest.  serve on your prettiest plates with hot garlic bread for a really special lunch!  cook time is chill time.

1. cook the pasta in a large pot of boiling salted water until al dente
2. drain
3. run under cool water to chill and drain again
4. in a medium bowl , combine the chicken , celery , apricots , raisins , cooked pasta , salt and white pepper , mixing well
5. in another bowl , combine the mayonnaise , curry powder , cumin , coriander , rice vinegar and sugar
6. whisking ingredients together
7. toss this dressing with the chicken mixture
8. cover bowl and chill for at least 2 hours before serving
9. serve on chilled plates , sprinkling with the toasted cashews
demonstrations.review: Great recipe!  I followed the recipe, except I cooked the chicken in the crockpot, so my chicken was more shredded than diced.  Also, being frugal I used a bag of dried mixed fruit, which included the raisins and apricots, instead of buying 2 bags of dried fruit.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic machine french bread

this is my winner with tammiev and our friends. this recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. i think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.

1. add to the bread pan in the order yours needs
2. for mine it is water first
3. then i add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top
4. this will run well on the normal , rapid , and delay start cycles
demonstrations.review: This is so simple, yet so good.  It provides a great french bread that is light and crispy.  Better than store bought and this recipe gave me 2 loaves.  I rolled it out, slightly, on a Silpat.  I twisted it until it was long and thin.  I cut it in half to make 2 loaves. I cut slits in the tops and let in rise again. My 2.00 bread machine purchase at a garage sale, has really paid off.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic cheese rolls for bread machine

i've been making this recipe for several years but i don't remember where i found it.  it's very good with italian dishes.

1. place first 7 ingredients in bread pan and select dough cycle
2. when cycle is finished , turn dough onto a floured countertop or cutting board
3. gently roll and stretch dough into a 24 inch rope
4. grease two 8 inch pie pans or one 13x9 pan
5. with a sharp knife , divide dough into 24 pieces
6. shape into balls
7. place into prepared pans
8. in small bowl , combine butter and garlic
9. pour over rolls
10. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
11. cover and let rise for 30-45 minutes until doubled
12. bake at 375 for 10-15 minutes until golden brown
13. remove from oven , cut apart , and serve warm
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe, but when the dough cycle was finished, I rolled the dough and made bread sticks.  I rolled the dough into a rectangle, added the butter, cheese, etc. and then let it rise a bit.  The result was large puffy breadsticks that everyone enjoyed.  Thanks

target.recipe_text:
excellent pulled pork

okay so here it is and it is fabulous,.  i know it's long and it's not a fast meal, but i promise it's well worth the trouble.  i can't tell you how important it is to me that people like what i cook, and this has gotten the best reaction to date.  i hope you agree--please let me know :d

1. mix dry rub ingredients
2. rub all over pork
3. cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour or overnight
4. preheat oven to 300f
5. place pork in a roasting pan and roast for 6 hours or until it falls apart
6. while pork is roasting , make bbq sauce: simmer for 10 minutes and remove from heat til ready to use
7. when pork is done , take it out of the oven and place on a platter and let it rest for 10 minutes
8. while it's resting , de-glaze the pan over medium heat with 3 / 4 cup water , scraping up all the good stuff from the pan
9. reduce by half and combine to bbq sauce
10. pull pork apart with forks and then put in a large pot or bowl and add bbq sauce
11. mix well and serve
12. if you like coleslaw , put it on the roll and top with bbq pork
target.review: Hey, I finally got around to making this, it was really good and simple! It was a little more tangy than I like for pulled pork, so I added a little bit of worcestershire sauce for some smokey flavor. I will make this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato cucumber salad

easy to make, healthy, and rather tasty

1. sprinkle salt over cucumber
2. toss gently and let stand 30 minutes
3. drain cucumber slices and press dry between paper towels
4. combine cucumber , green pepper , onions& tomatoes
5. combine vinegar and next 6 ingredients in a jar
6. shake vigorously
7. drizzle over vegetables
8. toss gently
demonstrations.review:
I made this last night and really got into it. I'm not a big salad person but I love tomatos, onions and cucumbers so this hit the spot. 

I left out the green pepper and used grape tomatoes cut in half instead, but I think what really brings this dish together is the dressing. It fringes on the acidic side, but the cucumbers I think really contrast the dressing and just taste fantasic.

It's definitely a keeper and I plan on using the dressing on my bruschetta. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma s soft sugar cookies

not sweet. great with coffee or tea. more like biscuits and not chewy-crunchy!

1. beat together eggs , oil , vanilla and sugar
2. add flour , baking powder and salt and mix well
3. drop by heaping teaspoon approx 3" apart on an ungreased cookie sheet
4. flatten with bottom of glass moistened with water and dipped in sugar
5. bake at 400f for 6-10 minutes or just until lightly golden
demonstrations.review: I've never made cookies before and didn't have vegetable oil so I substituted pure olive oil, the cookies still came out great, but I think using the wrong oil dried them out a little bit. Still very good and easy to make, will make them again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
louisiana sausage jambalaya

oh boy, is this one good! it's a simple, but very authentic louisiana jambalaya recipe given to me by a friend who grew up in new orleans! nice and spicy!

1. melt butter in large pot over medium-high heat
2. add the onions , green onions , bell pepper , garlic , serrano chile , bay leaves , creole seasoning , cayenne pepper and thyme
3. cover and cook until vegetables are tender , stirring occasionally , about 15 minutes
4. add sausage , broth , tomatoes and rice
5. bring mixture to simmer
6. reduce heat to low , cover and cook until rice is very tender , stirring occasionally , about 30 minutes to 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful! I changed it up a little bit and used spicy italian sausage and some leftover chicken breasts for the meat. I also used fresh red chili peppers instead of serranos. It came out great though, this will definitely be made again, thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken san remo

this is an incredibly, delicious chicken dish. i have make it twice, once using regular fresh spinach and once with the fresh baby spinach and i highly recommend using the baby. you're gonna love this!!!!

1. chicken: heat oil in skillet
2. mix flour , salt& pepper
3. light beat egg& water
4. dredge each chicken piece in flour , then dip each side of chicken in egg wash
5. place in pan in single layer& saute to a golden brown , turning once
6. about 2 min
7. per side
8. transfer to a baking pan just large enough to hold the chicken in a single layer
9. tent with foil to keep warm
10. preheat broiler sauce: wipe out the skillet& add oil over med heat add shallots& spinach
11. saute until spinach is completely wilted
12. stir in chick broth , wine and cream
13. bring to boil& cook 12 minutes until reduced by half season with cayenne& salt remove foil& spoon sauce over chick breasts
14. divide the mozzarella over the tops of each piece of chick
15. broil chicken 4 to 5 inches from the heat 2 to 3 minutes or until cheese bubbles& is light golden brown
demonstrations.review:
Nice for something different. I really like the chicken itself, but the sauce seemed to fall a little flat for my tastes. Everyone I have made this for though has loved it.

I recommend doubling the sauce (not the spinach though) and cooking it up with linguine and adding some garlic to the recipe for some extra flavor.

I can't stress enough making sure you let the sauce cook down to a thicker consistancy, the thicker the sauce, the better.

Overall it was a very savory dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s parmesan garlic bread or garlic toast

for a nice change substitute finely shredded white cheddar cheese for the parmesan cheese and fresh chopped chives for the parsley and also you could add in 1/4 cup mayo in with the butter mixture :)

1. set oven to 375f
2. for garlic bread
3. cut slices down the length of the bread about 1-inch intervals without cutting all the way through
4. in a bowl , combine the softened butter with garlic , parsley and parmesan cheese
5. mix well to combine
6. spread the butter / garlic mixture between bread slices , and then on the top of the loaf
7. wrap the bread in heavy-duty foil leaving the top partially uncovered
8. bake until heated through
9. for garlic toast
10. slice the bread into slices , then spread the garlic butter mixture over the top of each slice of bread , then sprinkle more parmesan cheese over the top of each slice or you can sprinkle shredded cheddar cheese on top in place of the parmesan
11. place onto a baking sheet and bake until lightly toasted to desired doneness
12. serve warm
13. to make ahead: combine all ingredients store covered in refrigerator for up to 3 days or freeze in a covered container ----- this bread can be made without the addition of the parmesan cheese if desired , but of course it's better with the cheese !
demonstrations.review: Incredible. I really dont have much more to say than that. I made this with my goulash (which everyone raves about, its a favorite of everyone I cook for), and this bread stole the show. I've never gotten so many complements on something so simple and easy to make. So thank you, your recipe is perfect!

target.recipe_text:
french onion chicken pot pies

a recipe i found in pillsbury pot pies and casseroles.  i haven't tried it yet but it sounded very good for a cool fall night.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray 8 ramekins or custard cups with cooking spray
3. place ramekins on a large cookie sheet with sides
4. in a 12-inch nonstick skillet , melt 2 tbls
5. of butter over medium-high heat
6. add chicken , cook about 10 minutes , stirring occasionally , until no longer pink in center
7. remove chicken from skillet
8. discard chicken juices
9. melt remaining 2 tbls
10. butter in skillet
11. add onions and mushrooms
12. cook and stir about 8 minutes or until golden brown
13. sprinkle flour over vegetables
14. cook and stir 1 minute
15. stir in water , sherry and soup mix
16. heat to boiling
17. boil about 3 minutes , stirring occasionally , until slightly thickened
18. spoon chicken into ramekins
19. spoon onion mixture over chicken
20. sprinkle with pepper
21. separate dough into 8 biscuits
22. place 1 biscuit in each ramekin
23. bake about 20 minutes or until biscuits are golden
24. carefully remove from oven
25. sprinkle 3 tbls
26. cheese over each biscuit
27. bake 4-5 minutes longer or until cheese is melted
target.review: This came out wonderful.  I cut the recipe in half, because it's only me and my wife, and it made three ramekins.  My wife got the extra, but only because I'm a softy.  I also didn't use Gruyere - Instead, I used a Mexican blend that I had handy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: The name says it all.  I read all of the reviews, and some said bake, some said use the skillet.  I did it both ways. 6 minutes browning, 10 minutes sauteing, 20 minutes in the oven, all in the same oven-proof skillet.  I used low sodium Soy sauce, and instead of dry ginger and garlic salt, I minced 1/2 tsp. of fresh ginger and two garlic cloves, thus reducing sodium and keeping my doctor happy.  The taste was to die for, but the lower sodium was to live for.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cubed steak paprika

i found this one in the better homes & gardens new cookbook.  super delicious!

1. in a 12-inch skillet melt butter over medium-high heat until butter sizzles
2. add steaks
3. reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 to 8 minutes or until done , turning once
4. remove meat , reserving drippings in skillet
5. for sauce , cook mushrooms , onion , garlic , paprika , and pepper in reserved drippings in skillet until mushrooms are tender
6. stir in broth
7. stir together sour cream and flour , stir into skillet
8. cook and stir over medium heat until thickened and bubbly
9. cook and stir 1 minute more
10. return steaks to skillet with sauce
11. heat through
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! at step 4, I cooked the onions, garlic and spices first, in order to soften the onions, then added the mushrooms.  I had to add butter several times during the cooking - I guess the butcher cubed a very lean cut, and the spices absorbed the juices.  It came out great! you can really taste the paprika!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed burger patties

we make our burger patties from scratch rather than buying the pre-made supermarket variety, as they're too salty for me. this recipe ramps up the flavour by trading the salt for a variety of either fresh or dried herbs instead. these are good on turkish breadrolls or ciabatta rolls with salad of your choice.

1. freeze the butter
2. separate out the beef in a mixing bowl so it's grainy
3. combine all herbs in a second bowl
4. grate the frozen butter into the beef
5. mix in herbs , and combine all ingredients loosely
6. shape mixture into 4 large round pattiess 1cm thick
7. make a depression in the centre of each
8. grill patties 7-10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe is one that proves that "low salt diet" does not mean "bland": or :"tasteless".  The butter keeps the inside of the patty moist, and the herbs make it yummy!  I did make a change, though.  I used a pound of ground beef (about 450 grams) to make my 4 patties, instead of 300 g, and scaled the other ingredients to match.  Thanks, Jenny!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy beef tips

an easy beef tip recipe

1. combine the beef
2. spoon into a 9x13 baking dish
3. bake , uncovered at 300
4. server or egg noodles or rice
demonstrations.review: really good basic recipe.  I added 10 thin slices of bell pepper and three cloves of chopped garlic,  I used 8 oz of fresh mushrooms (quartered) instead of a jar. I braised the beef before putting it into the crock pot and cooked it 8 hours on low.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallops in garlic cream sauce

i didn't really get this recipe from anyone, it's just (for as long as i can remember) one of the basic ways that i have always prepared scallops.  it's easy, quick to prepare and the sauce really complements the scallops.  i've prepared this with and without the wine (on those rare occasions when i happened to be out of my favorite white wine), and it is just as delicious either way.  that's why i listed that ingredient as optional.

1. melt butter in a pan over medium-low heat
2. add the garlic , parsley , scallions , wine , salt and pepper
3. cover
4. simmer 10 minutes
5. add the scallops
6. simmer for another 5 minutes
7. remove cover
8. stir in the cream
9. continuing heating , but do not boil , stirring constantly until sauce begins to thicken
10. serve immediately while scallops are hot
11. spoon excess sauce from pan and drizzle it over the scallops
demonstrations.review: Wow! This was excellent! I added a little bit of lemon juice (about a tablespoon's worth) The sauce was a bit soupy, so I thickened it a bit with some cornstarch.  The taste was wonderful.  I served it with Spinach and Garlic mashed potatoes for side dishes.

target.recipe_text:
cinnamon muffins

muffins are good anytime of the day.

1. mix flour , sugar , baking powder , salt , nutmeg and allspice
2. add egg , milk and butter
3. stir into dry ingredients until moistened
4. spoon into greased or paper-lined muffin cups
5. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes or until done
6. for topping combine sugar and cinnamon
7. brush top of warm muffin in butter and dip top of muffin into sugar / cinnamon mixture
target.review: Very good muffins.  I substituted some of the butter for apple sauce, and couldn't tell the difference.  I also added about 1/4 C of cinnamon chips.  Yum!  I made large muffins, and came up with 9.  Pretty light and fluffy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ohh  sweet granola

my boss said 

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the oats , nuts , coconut , brown sugar , cinnamon and salt
3. add the oil , honey and water
4. toss until well combined
5. spread the mixture evenly on a cookie sheet
6. bake for 40 minutes or until lightly browned , stirring every 10 minutes to keep the mixture from sticking
7. let it cool
8. then stir in the fruit or chocolate chips
9. store in an air tight container
demonstrations.review: Oh Wow!  This is really good stuff.  It has just come out of the oven, and I can't even wait to let it cool before sampling it.  YUMMY!!  I can't wait until it cools and i can add crasins and chocolate chips.  Although, it is great without them!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheeseburger mini muffins

you can enjoy the delicious taste of a cheeseburger without having to resort to fast food. these little appetizers are the perfect 'finger food' and can be frozen after baking. (cook time reflected is for two batches; add 15 minutes for each additional batch)

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. in a skillet , cook beef and onion over medium heat until meat is no longer pink
3. drain
4. in a mixing bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking powder and salt
5. in another bowl combine ketchup , milk , butter , eggs and mustard
6. stir into the dry ingredients just until moistened
7. fold in the beef mixture and shredded cheese
8. fill greased miniature muffin cups three-fourths full
9. bake for 15-18 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center of a muffin comes out clean
10. cool for 5 minutes before removing from pan to wire rack
11. refrigerate leftovers
demonstrations.review: Very good apetizer recipe.  I made these ahead of time, and froze them.  When my parents were in town, I pulled them out one evening and we enjoyed them.  They froze great and it was wonderful to have something at a moments notice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy granola bars

i "borrowed" this recipe from the kitchen at my college because i fell in love with these bars. they are so much better than store-bought, and you can add or subtract ingredients as you wish. they make a perfect on-the-go snack; a much healthier alternative to chips or cookies, especially for kids (great for lunch boxes!)

1. preheat oven to 350 and lightly grease or spray 9 x 13 pan
2. in large bowl , beat brown sugar , sugar , and butter until light and fluffy
3. blend in honey , vanilla and egg
4. in separate bowl , combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda , and salt
5. add flour mixture gradually to sugar mixture and beat until combined
6. by hand , stir in almonds , chocolate chips and oats until well mixed
7. press mixture firmly in bottom of greased pan , and bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes , or until light golden brown
8. cool and cut into squares
demonstrations.review: Very good bars!  I did a little tweaking, but mostly just with add-ins.  I only used the 1/4C butter, used half whole wheat flour, half white flour.  Added about 1/4 C. wheat germ, 1/4C. flax seen, couple spoonfuls of oat bran. Only used 1 C. of rolled oats, since I added so many other things.  Left out the almonds and only added 1/2 C. mini chocolate chips.  I baked these in two 8x8 pans, and added crasins to one of the pans.  they baked for about 17 minutes in my oven.  These are so good, I can't seem to stop eating them!  My hope is to get these into the freezer for lunches.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cheesy chicken

almost too easy, the chicken cooks in a creamy, cheesy sauce that is delicious over noodles. this freezes well, too

1. place chicken breasts in the crock pot
2. mix the undiluted soups together with the garlic powder and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours , until chicken is tender
4. serve with the delicious sauce over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very yummy.  I only used one can of chicken soup and one can of cheese soup.  We served it over rotini noodles.  My picky boys ate it up, and the leftovers were great for lunch the next day.  Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix chocolate cookies

here is a real easy one.  just use a chocolate cake mix.  i add a hand full of chocolate chips to get a double chocolaute fix.

1. in a bowl , stir cake mix , butter and milk until well combined
2. break egg into mixing bowl and mix well
3. bake in 350 f oven for 12 - 15 minutes
4. enjoy --
demonstrations.review: I made these cookies because I needed a chocolate fix and we got new neighbors in across the street from us and I wanted to bring them some.  The first batch in the oven didn't spread out or anything.  They looked the same coming out of the oven, as they did when I mounded them onto the cookie sheets.  They looked kind of like chocolate rocks.  Not very pretty.  The second batch to go into the oven, I gently pushed them together a bit more, and flattened them.  They looked nicer.  We ate the "rocks", and boy were they yummy!  I did add a handful of chocolate chunks, although they really didn't need it.  I will bring the "prettier" cookies to the neighbors this afternoon.

target.recipe_text:
potato spinach soup

nan

1. melt butter in a pan
2. add onions and celery
3. cover and cook until tender - about 15 minutes
4. stir occasionally
5. blend in flour , and add potatoes , water and salt
6. stir constantly until boiling
7. simmer 30 minutes
8. add spinach cook 2 minutes
9. then add cream
10. top with grated cheese if desired
target.review: I had some left over spinach I didnt want to waste so I tried out this soup. I found it lovely, but a bit bland so just at the end of cooking, I added the zest of one lemon and the juice as well. I also added mushrooms and garlic to help spice it up. It really brightened it up and was very lovely. I will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai grilled chicken thighs

this is my first recipe - please be kind! my kids love it and when i take it to a bbq everyone wants the recipe. it is a variation on one i found in epicurious a while ago. it is very easy and very yummy!!

1. combine all ingredients except chicken in a bowl
2. mix thoroughly
3. add chicken and leave to marinate at least one hour , preferably longer
4. grill chicken on the bbq , hotplate or in the griller until golden brown and cooked through
5. ususlly you would expect 12 thigh fillets to feed 4 to 6 people- in my family the kids eat 4 each so this recipe serves 3
demonstrations.review: Wonderful! My family really enjoyed these. I actually found a jar of purred ginger, garlic and chili all in one. I used 2 tsp and was just enough spice. Very good. My DH said that this would be a great marinade for ribs so I will try that some time, but I think he is right, this is too good for just chicken!! Great recipe.. thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review:
With so many great reviews how can you go wrong? I almost didnt post mine but I had to.

I made this last night for my mom who was visiting, my DH and my son. I used chicken thighs because that is what I had on hand and wow did the chicken fly off the plate!! They were so moist inside and a slight crunchy coating, not too crisp and not soggy. I got rave reviews and this will now be a keeper for sure.

Keep up the great postings Kittencal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted peanuts

make your own!  i was surprised not to find this recipe on here - it's very easy and tastes better than store bought canned.  i clipped this recipe from some newspaper.  if you like really sweet then try sprinkling with sugar. do not use margarine - they will burn or get too  dark.  photos taken by me on 2/26/06.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. place peanuts in a bowl
3. heat butter and honey together , in microwave or on stove top , stirring well
4. toss with peanuts
5. spread peanuts on a cookie sheet and bake at 350f for 5 to 10 minutes
6. after the 1st 5 minutes check them & stir every 1 or 2 minutes until peanuts are golden brown - the glaze will thicken and darken
7. remove , stir while cooling for 5 - 10 minutes until they no longer stick together
8. sprinkle with salt or mix it in with the honey & butter mixture
9. you can also toss with sugar
10. i saw these at a chinese restaurant covered with powdered sugar - yummy !
11. these taste great while they're warm !
demonstrations.review: I tried this tonight when I had a craving for honey roasted peanuts but didnt want to truck myself out to the store. I was shocked to see that there were so few recipes posted!! I loved them and I know I will use this again! I followed the instructions very closely, spraying my pay with non stick cooking spray. When they were quite cool but not cold and still slightly sticky, I lined a deep bowl with waxed paper for the nuts to totally cool and used the paper to "break up" any chunks. This will be made again and again and I think next time I will add some other types of nuts and maybe some cyenne pepper for an extra kick. Great recipe and so easy to make!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate chocolate brownie muffins

this recipe goes back to when my son was small and that is quite a while back,  and i still make them, these are moist and rich no need for an electric mixer for this recipe it's all mixed with a wooden spoon, i have even added in chopped walnuts or mini chocolate chips, my recipe #89207 works great with these :)

1. set oven to 350f
2. line 12 muffin tins with paper liners
3. in a medium bowl combine cocoa and baking powder
4. mix to combine
5. add in boiling water
6. mix well with a wooden spoon to combine
7. add in the melted butter and vanilla
8. mix well
9. add in the sugar , mix well with a wooden spoon
10. stir in eggs with a wooden spoon
11. mix until combined
12. mix the flour with salt
13. add in the chocolate mixture
14. mix well to combine
15. add / mix in mini chocolate chips or walnuts
16. using an ice cream scoop fill each of the muffin tins almost to the top
17. bake for 25-30 minutes or until muffins are done , don't over bake !
18. cool , drizzle glaze over or frost with buttercream frosting
demonstrations.review: I was stressing over what to bring to an "adult foozeball" tourny. I decided to make some fun "kid food" and found this recipe. I added a little more sugar (about 1/4c more) and the batter was great, not overly sweet for those with lesser sweet tooths. I played around and made mini brownies. On some I sprinkled icing sugar, some I left plain and the rest I dipped in white chocolate. Wow my son was CRAZY for them and the adults loved them too. This one is a keeper and I will do it agian.
