2. in a oven safe dish , combine all the above ingredients and bake in a heated oven at 350f for 45 minutes
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very good!  These are almost like a meal in themselves.  My wife, who will rarely eat any type of beans, went back for a second helping!  I added a couple of minced cloves of garlic and cooked them for about 1 1/2 hrs. to thicken them more.  I wonder what they would taste like if ground pork was used instead of beef???  THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy parmesan potatoes

quick, easy and addictive. great with steaks...never any leftovers, which is good, since i don't think it would reheat very well.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. scrub potatoes and cut w / skin on
3. spray cookie sheet w / cooking spray
4. place single layer on cookie sheet
5. spoon melted butter over each slice
6. sprinkle garlic powder , salt and black pepper evenly
7. cover with parmesan
8. bake for approx 20-30 minutes , remove when cheese is browned and potatoes crispy
demonstrations.review: Good, but not great!  I had made a similar recipe several years ago with the same taste results.  The best are served in some of the eating establishments in the upper eastern U.S. as appetizers. Most of us who have tasted them agree, it's the type Parmesan cheese these places use. Not just your average, run of the mill Parmesan that is available at most local grocery stores.  Sorry, but I guess once you have tasted the original ones, your spoiled!!!

target.recipe_text:
applesauce  crock pot

this smells great while it's cooking and is really nice served warm with roast pork. i found this recipe in the sunset crockery cookbook.

1. spread apple slices in a 3-quart or larger slow-cooker
2. sprinkle with sugar
3. insert cinnamon stick down between apples
4. drizzle with lemon juice
5. cover and cook on low until apples form a thick sauce , about 6 1 / 2 to 8 hours
6. remove and discard cinnamon stick
7. sprinkle with nutmeg
8. serve warm or at room temperature
target.review: Fantastic! The cinnamon stick was perfect. It was pretty sweet so if you prefer a less sweet applesauce than I would certainly reduce the sugar to 1/2 of what is called for, but my husband and I personally liked the sweetness so I cook the recipe as it is. I am making it for the second time in the last few days!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with prosciutto in a lemon cream sauce

my mom found this recipe years ago, and since then it has been a favorite among my own family and with anyone who got my mom to give up the recipe :) ... so flavorful, you too will not only enjoy this but never truly be able to get enough of it!

1. melt butter
2. add shallots and saut until translucent
3. add broth
4. simmer over medium-hi heat until reduced to 1 / 4 cup
5. add cream , lemon peel , orange peel , and cayenne
6. simmer until sauce thickens slightly
7. add peas
8. simmer until heated through
9. stir in mint and lemon juice
10. meanwhile , cook pasta
11. cut up prosciutto into bite-size pieces and add at end to mixture
12. mix cream sauce with pasta
13. sprinkle fresh parmesan on top
demonstrations.review: This turned out great, but didn't have the flavor I was expecting. In the future I would substitute capers for the peas, and I think it would fare better. The cayenne pepper adds suprising flavor, and is the perfect amount for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy oven fries

i like this recipe because it uses no oil, making it the most guilt-free french fries recipe that i know of.  it has been scaled down for 1-2 people.  try adding ground red pepper if you like your fries spicy.

1. combine the beaten egg white , paprika , garlic powder , salt & pepper in a small bowl and mix well
2. cut the potato into 1 / 2" spears
3. toss the potatoes with the coating mixture
4. line a cookie sheet with non-stick foil and coat with cooking spray
5. arrange the potato spears in a single layer on the cookie sheet
6. spray the potatoes with a light layer of cooking spray
7. dust with additional salt or paprika if desired
8. bake at 400 degrees for 30 minute
demonstrations.review: These were exactly as described! I LOVE french fries, but try not to eat them too often. I added fresh garlic (chopped) on top of the fries before I cooked them. Some of the garlic burned on the pan- but even THAT smelled good! It definately had a lot of flavor! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded chicken cutlets with lemon basil sauce

this is best served with mashed potatoes, and corn because the sauce is delicious on all 3!its important if you have the regular boneless chicken breast, to slice it into cutlets. you might want to double the sauce recipe if you like a lot sauce over your meal

1. rinse cutlets and pat dry
2. season cutlets with complete seasoning on both sides
3. set aside
4. mix eggs and milk and put breading in separate plate
5. put cutlets into milk mixture and bread them so they are fully coated
6. heat up canola oil or you can use butter in a skillet on medium heat
7. put cutlets in the skillet and let them start cooking
8. in a small pot , mix the 4 tbs butter , lemon , salt , and basil until completed melted , then keep on low setting
9. when chicken is golden brown , remove and pour an adequate amount of lemon-basil sauce over them
10. like i said , when i make this at my family's request i always serve mashed potatoes and corn because the sauce is perfect for all three
11. you can always double the sauce recipe if you serve the same sauce over everything , not only does it taste great-- it looks pretty
demonstrations.review: We loved this recipe. I actually baked my chicken, instead of frying it, and it turned out perfectly. I baked it at 350 until it was done, and then served the sauce as suggested. I was impressed by the flavor- thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal  cookies

this is a family favorite--moist and chewy.
this is an old recipe ,and the trick to getting a moist cookie, is to take them from the oven when the middle does not look done.
this recipe was on a quaker oats box years ago.

1. cream oleo and sugars
2. add eggs and beat well with the vanilla
3. mix together the flour , salt , soda , and cinnamon
4. add to the creamed mixture
5. stir in the hot water , oats , and raisins
6. mix well
7. place heaping tablespoonful batter on a greased cookie sheet
8. bake at 350 degrees until almost done
9. take out and cool on cookie sheet for 1 minute , then cool on a rack
demonstrations.review: I loved this recipe. I cut the sugar in half, and soaked the raisins in brandy for about four hours. I had to refrigerate the dough, as it was a little sticky. They turned out great, even with the reduced sugar. My boyfriend loved them too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
herbed turkey breast

we had this tonight and it was so good! i used the boneless, sliced turkey breasts and cooked on high in the crockpot for 4 hours. very tasty!

1. place turkey in crockpot
2. combine remaining ingredients in a bowl and mix well
3. brush over turkey
4. cover and cook on low for 8-10 hours or high for 4-5 hours in crockpot
5. you can cook this in the oven if you prefer
demonstrations.review: Made this on Thanksgiving day for my fiance and I and we loved it. It had perfect taste and was eaten, with the hopes that there was more. I baked it in the oven for twenty minutes, and it turned out perfectly. Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
korean vegetable beef stir fry

a mildly spicy stir-fry.  serve over hot rice.  as suggested by several reviewers, the sauce can be doubled.  just double the  marinade ingredients and the water and cornstarch.

1. slice beef across the grain into bite-size strips
2. combine green onions , soy sauce , garlic , sesame oil , sesame seed , red pepper flakes , sugar and pepper
3. add meat and marinate 30 minutes at room temperature
4. drain meat , reserving marinade
5. dissolve cornstarch in water and add to reserved marinade , mixing well
6. preheat wok or large skillet over high heat
7. add 1 tablespoon oil , then add carrots and stir fry 3 minutes
8. add broccoli and cauliflower slices and stir-fry 2 minutes
9. remove vegetables and keep warm
10. add remaining oil to pan
11. add half the beef to hot pan and stir-fry 2-3 minutes
12. remove beef and stir-fry remaining meat
13. return all meat to pan
14. stir marinade a little and pour into skillet or wok
15. cook and stir until thickened and bubbly
16. stir in the vegies
17. cover and cook 1 minute
18. serve over hot rice
target.review:
YUM! Very good and spice can be adjusted for taste. (We inevitably added more red pepper as crazy Koreans!). Two tips:
1) We decreased the amt of sesame oil as we used the DARK asian kind (about half). 
2) I par-steamed the broccoli before adding it to the stirfry so the other veggies would remain crisp. 
3) I doubled the sauce to cover the veggies more, and it was great over rice/noodles!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the sweetest blueberry muffins

very tasty and sweet.

1. heat oven to 375
2. grease 18 regular-size muffin cups
3. in bowl , mix butter until creamy
4. add sugar and beat until pale and fluffy
5. add eggs one at a time , beating after each
6. beat in vanilla , baking powder and salt
7. with spoon , fold in half of flour then half of milk into batter
8. repeat
9. fold in blueberries
10. spoon into muffin cups and sprinkle topping onto each muffin
11. bake 15 to 20 minutes , until golden brown and springy to touch
demonstrations.review: I made these non-dairy by using vegan margarine and soy milk. I also halved the recipe and only used 1c frozen blueberries. They were great! My nursing son is highly dairy allergic so I haven't had much experience with dairy-free, so I was hesitant. However, they tasted delicious and no one I served them to could tell I didn't use dairy, even my family who loves butter :) Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with spicy honey orange glaze

nan

1. in small bowl , combine honey with juice concentrate , orange zest , garlic , salt and red pepper flakes
2. rinse chicken with cold water and pat dry
3. season lightly with salt
4. in large non-stick skillet , heat margarine and oil over medium-high heat
5. add chicken and cook about 4 minutes , until seared
6. turn chicken , cook another 4 minutes until just cooked through
7. pour honey mixture over chicken and cook , turning chicken to coat as sauce begins to thicken , about 2 min
8. serve chicken breasts with honey-orange glaze spooned over the top
demonstrations.review: Great recipe, DH is raving about it now and wanted me to immediately post a review :). I didn't think it would be spicy enough (we're Korean!), so I added 1 tbs gochujang (Korean chili paste), and upped it to 1tbsp gochugaru (Korean chili pepper flakes). I also doubled the sauce so we could eat it with the rice and some spinach. It's pretty yummy, we ate it all even though we planned for leftovers! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super healthy hummus

taken off a website, don't have the reference. an excellent hummus, the only one i make anymore. you really need a blender or food processor to get the consistency right. 1/4 cup = 1 point ww.

1. combine everything in blender or food processor and process until smooth
2. the blender gives the best result
3. if you need more liquid to make a nice consistency , add a bit more yogurt
4. chill
5. serve with pitas or as a veggie dip
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe! Very versatile. I was out of regular plain yogurt so I used 1/8c sour cream and 1/8c low fat plain greek yogurt. I also added red pepper flakes and doubled the salt. I did add an extra garlic clove, as per my preference. Thanks for giving me a great base hummus (minus tahini!) that is easy to play around with!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect orange julius clone

this is as close as you will ever get to the real thing, it's a real refresher in the morning when you need a wake-me-up boost, you may add in sugar to taste if desired.

1. place all ingredients except for the ice cubes into a blender
2. add the ice cubes one by one until smooth
3. serve immediately-- enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I don't use a whole can of the concentrate, I just use one cup of the reconstituted juice, but if you like a stronger taste, this is good too! It's my favorite orange julius recipe out there. I also use a bit more ice, but my ice maker makes quite small ice cubes. Yum....perfect for summer!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever  and most versatile  muffins

these are wonderful for just throwing in your favorite ingredients---i don't need any other muffin recipes. editing to add, based on a recent review: be sure not to overmix muffins; if you do, they will be tough. they should still be lumpy when you are finished mixing them.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. stir together the flour , baking powder , salt and sugar in a large bowl
3. make a well in the center
4. in a small bowl or 2-cup measuring cup , beat egg with a fork
5. stir in milk and oil
6. pour all at once into the well in the flour mixture
7. mix quickly and lightly with a fork until moistened , but do not beat
8. the batter will be lumpy
9. do not overmix
10. this will create tough / heavy muffins
11. pour the batter into paper lined muffin pan cups
12. variations: blueberry muffins: add 1 cup fresh blueberries
13. raisin muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped raisins
14. date muffins: add 1 cup finely chopped dates
15. cheese muffins: fold in 1 cup grated sharp yellow cheese
16. bacon muffins: fold 1 / 4 cup crisp cooked bacon , broken into bits
17. bake for 25 minutes , or until golden
demonstrations.review: Delicious, quick muffins! I usually make cranberry or banana muffins, for cranberry I take about half a cup or more (preference) of craisins rehydrated, and add. For banana I add two mashed bananas and decrease the milk to 3/4 cup. I also always use soy milk because of a dairy allergy and love using the Very Vanilla kind in the fruit muffins. Yum! Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
sweet and sour cranberry chicken

great flavor!  easy to prepare. good for potlucks....just keep warm in a crockpot.  serve over hot cooked rice.

1. in a 13" x 9" baking dish , place chicken pieces
2. in a small bowl , mix together catalina salad dressing , whole-berry cranberry sauce , onion soup mix and brown sugar until smooth
3. pour evenly over chicken pieces
4. cover and bake at 350 for about 30-40 minutes
5. serve over hot cooked rice
target.review: This was delicious. I made it a day ahead and reheated when I got home from work...I'm sure this enhanced the flavor even more. I did use a low fat Catalina dressing, which didn't seem to affect the outcome. This is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken marsala

i got this recipe off of the back of a bag of frozen chicken breasts. it was really easy, but tasted very "gourmet". i know you will enjoy it as much as we did. the original recipe called for a 8 oz. can of tomato sauce, but i used the bigger can to make it more saucy.

1. in plastic bag , combine flour , salt , and pepper
2. add chicken
3. shake to coat
4. heat oil over medium heat and add chicken
5. cook until no longer pink in center
6. remove and set chicken aside
7. in the same skillet add garlic and mushrooms
8. cook 2-3 minutes
9. stir in tomatoes , tomato sauce , wine , and basil
10. reduce heat to low and simmer for 5 minutes
11. return chicken to skillet and simmer for an additional 5 minutes
12. serve over hot linguine
demonstrations.review: This was a nice variation on the traditional chicken marsala. I used chicken cutlets, and added 1 T. butter to my pan when cooking the mushrooms because my pan was too dry. I also let the chicken simmer a little longer than 5 min. to make sure it was cooked through. The dish had great flavor. I'll definitely be making this on again...and again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crescent roll casserole

too easy to be so good. when i made this my picky daughter said on a scale of 1 to 10 it was a 40. i have revised the spices after reading the reviews. if you do not have italian seasoning available you can use 1/4 tsp oregano, 1/4 tsp basil, 1/4 tsp thyme, & 1/4 tsp marjoram.

1. brown beef until no longer pink then drain excess grease
2. add the tomato sauce , olive oil , spices , & 2 tablespoons of parmesan cheese to the beef
3. simmer on medium heat for 5 minutes
4. remove from heat & stir in the sour cream
5. preheat the oven to 375f lightly spray an 8x8 baking dish
6. pull the crescent rolls apart but leave them in rectangle shape
7. lay 2 of the rectangles in the bottom of the pan , side by side
8. gently spread out to fit the bottom of the pan
9. cover the crescent rolls with 4 slices of provolone cheese
10. next add the beef mixture & then 4 more slices of cheese
11. take the remaining 2 rectangles on top of the last layer of cheese
12. lightly brush the melted butter over the crescent rolls & sprinkle the remaining parmesan cheese on top
13. bake for 25 minutes or until lightly brown
demonstrations.review: What a nice, simple, easy to put together casserole! I made it exactly as written and it was great...I saw no need to make any changes to it. 3 of us cleaned out that dish with no problem whatsoever. This will definitely be placed on the "make again" list. Thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot  chicken swiss bake

this recipe was gotten "somewhere" off the internet and tweaked by me :). i've made this many times and it's one of those i always have the ingredients on hand, it's simple and everyone i've ever served it to loves it. make a salad or some green beans in the microwave and dinner is served!

1. place chicken breasts in crock pot and sprinkle with salt and pepper
2. cover with swiss cheese
3. empty soups into bowl , but keep one of the soup cans
4. fill the empty soup can 3 / 4 full with the port wine and add milk for the last 1 / 4 to make one full can and add this to your soup mixture in the bowl
5. mix well and pour on top of swiss cheese
6. top with dry stuffing
7. slice butter into pats and place on top of stuffing
8. cover and let cook on low 4-6 hours
demonstrations.review:
When I put my boneless breast in the crockpot they still had some ice crystals on them and I was afraid it would skew the cooking time, but 6 hours was perfect. 
The chicken cut with a fork easily. I would make this again in a heartbeat. I've already passed it along to a couple friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered greek dip

from better homes and gardens magazine... may 2008 issue

1. in medium mixing bowl , beat cream cheese , lemon juice , italian seasoning , and garlic with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth and combined
2. spread cream cheese mixture into a deep 9-inch pie plate or shallow serving dish
3. evenly spread hummus on cream cheese layer
4. top with cucumber , tomato , olives , feta cheese , and green onions
5. cover and refrigerate 2 to 24 hours
6. serve with pita chips
demonstrations.review: I love this dip. It is so fresh tasting and a nice change from the Mexican layered dips. I used the Sabra brand hummus because it's the creamiest I could find. I agree with the previous review, it is a really festive-looking holiday dip. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tri tip roast    delicious

a tri-tip is also called a triangle roast. it's a very lean cut of meat that does not contain much fat. if you do not see it, ask for it. do not over cook this cut of meat. do not cook it more than medium. note: there are 24 hours of inactive prep time in refrigerator.

1. combine all ingredients , except garlic and rosemary , and blend well
2. place roast in an oven-proof baking dish
3. cover roast with the marinade and place in the refrigerator for 24 hours , turning and basting a few times , ending with the fat side down
4. preheat oven to 425 degrees
5. sprinkle the garlic powder and crushed rosemary over the top of the roast
6. puncture the roast with a fork all over the top , and bake for 30-40 minutes , or until a meat thermometer reads 135 degrees for medium-rare
7. remove from oven and allow to rest about 5 to 10 minutes
8. carve against the grain and serve , using the juices as a gravy
demonstrations.review: This was absolutely delicious. It had the best flavor. I was a little suspect of the time, but I decided to follow the directions and if it didn't work I'd make the adjustment the next time. The meat came out perfect! This recipe is a keeper. Thanks, Alan.

target.recipe_text:
zucchini cake

top this with cream cheese frosting for a special treat.

1. mix dry ingredients
2. combine oil and eggs with vanilla
3. add to dry ingredients , mix well
4. add zucchini , stir until combined well
5. fold in walnuts
6. place in greased 13x9 baking pan
7. bake at 350 for 40 minutes , or until pick comes out clean
target.review: This cake is great!  You wouldn't think that a cake with zucchini in it would taste so good, but it does!  We have an abundance of zucchini to use up, so I made this, along with the cream cheese frosting.  The recipe is very easy to follow - the hardest part is just shredding the zucchini if you don't have a food processor.  I hope everyone will give this recipe a shot!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome cheese dip in bread bowl

i served this recipe at a holiday party. it was the first appetizer to disappear, and was one of the easiest to prepare.  with all that pork bacon, cheese, and a bread bowl - where else to put this recipe but the midwestern u.s. states.

1. hollow out top of bread for the"bowl"
2. save removed bread for other use
3. mix together the cheese and other ingredients
4. fill bread bowl
5. bake at 350 for 40 minutes , until hot and bubbly
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This dip was great!  Everyone at our party loved it.  I left out the onion and used 1/2 tsp onion powder.  I also used bacos instead of bacon. The only problem I notices was as I baked the dip, the bread got very hard.  I used pumpernickel, so I don't know if that was the reason or not. Other than that, this was really good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boboli pizza crust clone

tasty "premade" pizza crust.

1. add all ingredients to breadmaker in order listed by your manufacturer
2. set breadmaker on dough setting
3. when cycle is done , form two crusts on pizza pans , sprinkle with parmesan cheese , cover and let rise again
4. bake 5-10 minutes at 450 f until light brown
5. cool
6. wrap tightly in foil and freeze
demonstrations.review: My husband has declared this his new favorite pizza crust!  It was very easy to make.  After forming the crust, we let it rise for an hour, then baked it for 7 minutes at 450.   We immediately topped it and baked for 7 more minutes, and it turned out great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with sausage  tomatoes  and cream

delicious and satisfying... i don't remember where this recipe comes from, but it's a pleaser! easily doubled.  also, works well with gf pasta and sausage

1. heat oil in a heavy skillet over medium heat
2. add sausage and crushed red pepper
3. cook until sausage is no longer pink , stirring frequently , about 7 minutes
4. add onion and garlic to skillet and cook until onion is tender and sausage is light brown , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
5. add tomatoes , cream , and salt
6. simmer until mixture thickens slightly , about 4 minutes
7. cook pasta in large pot of boiling water
8. drain
9. bring sauce to a simmer
10. add pasta to sauce and cook until pasta is heated through and sauce thickens , stirring occasionally , about 2 minutes
11. divide pasta between plates
12. sprinkle with parsley
13. serve , passing parmesan separately
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved this recipe!  I used two cans of tomatoes and a cup of cream and served the sauce over 16 oz penne pasta.  It made enough for four people that way.  I think next time I may add spinach also.  This recipe will definately be served next time I have company!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest ever pizza dough

this is so easy to make -- no long rising times and all in one bowl! and, if you don't feel like pizza, try just brushing the dough with olive oil, and topping with olives, parmesan cheese and rosemary to make foccacia bread. i have also topped it with a mixture of oil, finely chopped fresh herbs (parsley, basil, oregano) and garlic paste.

1. throw all ingredients into a bowl and mix together with a food processor or by hand
2. the dough will be fairly sticky but don't add any more flour
3. instead scrape it into an oiled bowl , cover with a cloth and leave to rise for 30 minutes or until doubled in size
4. i like to let my dough rise in an ever-so-slightly warmed oven or in an airing cupboard
5. when dough is finished rising , pre-heat oven to 400 f degrees
6. turn onto a floured surface and work in a bit more flour until the dough loses its stickiness -- you shouldn't need too much -- then roll out to desired size , keeping the dough about 1 / 2 inch thick
7. leave to rise for about 10 minutes , before topping with your favourite ingredients
8. put on a baking sheet sprinkled with flour or cornmeal and bake for 10-15 minutes in a very hot oven until lightly browned
9. our standard is 230-240 c in a fan oven for 10 minutes on a top shelf
demonstrations.review: This was an excellent pizza dough recipe!  It was easy, and the dough baked up chewy on the outside while still tender on the inside.  I baked mine 20 minutes on a pizza stone sprinkled with cornmeal.  Also, I mixed the water and yeast together first, then added the other ingredients to avoid any problems with it not rising.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice and lentil casserole

this is a great meal that we eat here often in the winter time. with some dark bread and maybe a salad it is a really hearty meal, though we have been known to eat just this for dinner. the recipe is adapted from amy dacyczyn's "the complete tightwad gazette"

1. preheat the oven to 300 degrees
2. mix all ingredients except the cheese in a baking dish
3. cover with foil and bake for 1 hour 10 minutes
4. then remove the foil , add the cheese , and bake for an additional 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: I was really surprised by how good this recipe was.  My two children (3 & 2) gobbled it up.  It looks like it's not going to make that much, but once the lentils and rice absorb the liquid, it fed our family of four with one lunch for the next day.

target.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine bananas , oil and egg
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in chocolate chips
5. fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full
6. bake at 350 deg f for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done
target.review:
I don't know what went wrong but when I cooked these I could see all the sugar granules - I don't understand why this happened, it was thoroughly mixed. Maybe I wasn't suppose to use granulated sugar?

I agree with everyone that the flavours were lovely, and I also only used a small amount of choc chips and it was still really chocolatey.

Thanks for the recipe, I might try it again but with a finer sugar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken breasts with rosemary

this is so easy to make and can be served over pasta, rice, etc.

1. pat chicken dry and season lightly with salt& pepper
2. dip chicken in flour and shake of excess
3. heat butter and cook chicken 4-6 minutes per side or until no longer pink in the center and lightly browned
4. remove from pan
5. discard any fat from the pan
6. return pan to heat
7. add chicken stock and rosemary
8. cook 2 minutes
9. add cream and mustard
10. bring to a boil
11. cook 4-5 minutes until slightly thickened
12. season to taste with salt and pepper
13. return chicken to pan
14. coat with sauce and heat thoroughly
demonstrations.review: Wonderful dish. Fast to prepare and delicious. I don't cook chicken usually because it never turns out well for me. This one exceeded expectations. I was nervous as I had a teenage guest for dinner and I'm not a confident cook. I have to thank you for this easy and tasty recipe. Not only did the teenager say it was fantastic, my husband said I'm cooking chicken from now on in. I confess I made one change to the recipe - I crumbled part of a vegetable stock cube into the flour, and I also used fresh rosemary but otherwise I stuck to it word for word. Thank you for an excellent recipe, it's given me a bit more confidence to cook chicken more often :o)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy banana muffins

nan

1. mash bananas , add sugar and the slightly beaten egg
2. stir in melted butter
3. stir in dry ingredients
4. spoon into medium size muffin pan
5. bake 20 minutes at 350f degrees - 375f degrees
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much for this recipe. I am trying my hand at baking now that I have given birth and these turned out perfect - they were moist, light and easy - seriously easy to make. I couldn't believe I actually made them :) I whipped up a cream cheese, powedered sugar and small flecks of chocolate as a topping - my husband and I devoured them. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried lamb stew

this rich, homemade stew is delectable.

1. mix flour , salt and pepper in bag
2. add lamb and shake to coat
3. in dutch oven , melt butter
4. add lamb and any flour left in the bag
5. brown over med heat
6. add potatoes , carrots , onion , green pepper , apple , tomatoes and water
7. heat to boiling
8. add curry powder , boullion , cinnamon and cloves
9. reduce heat
10. cover and simmer for 1-1 / 2 hours , until vegetables and meat are tender
11. remove cloves
demonstrations.review: Gorgeous! My husband loved this recipe so much his comments were ' This is so good, I can't believe you cooked it' - Charming but I'm glad I've finally could something he likes. I appreciate you taking the time to post the recipe. I didn't put cloves in it as we had none at the time and it still tasted amazing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamies chilli con carne

i was given 'happy days with the naked chef' and found that i enjoy jamies style, he can be relied on for sensible recipes that work.
i decided to try his chilli con carne for my son and husband one weekend when the girls were away.  good comfort food, served over rice, dh found this spicy while i thought it could be pepped up a little more (sometimes i surprise myself!!)....  adjust for your own taste!  jamie recommends chuck steak, minced, but i used ground beef that i had in the freezer.  i don't think the sun-dried tomatoes are traditional, but they are a nice touch!    this dish is ideal for make-ahead, and definitely tastes even better the next day!

1. in a large pot , fry onions and garlic in a little olive oil until soft
2. add chilli powder , fresh chilli , cumin and a little seasoning
3. then add the meat and continue to cook , stirring , until it has browned
4. process the sun-dried tomatoes in your food processor , with a little oil from the jar , enough to loosen into a paste
5. add these to the beef with the tomatoes , cinnamon stick , and the water
6. check the seasoning , and add more if you prefer
7. bring to the boil , cover , turn the heat down and simmer for about 1 and a half hours
8. add the kidney beans about 1 / 2 an hour before serving , they are already cooked and only need to be warmed through
9. serving suggestions , steamed rice , crusty bread , a tossed salad , some guacamole or / and sour cream / yoghurt
demonstrations.review: Second time of cooking this dish, fabulous everytime - it is afterall Jamlie Oliver!! Like reviewer Noo I motted the sundried tomatoes, and used sundried tomato paste instead just because we do not have dried tomatoes. This is a superb dish and yes load it up with cheese on top at the end, so tasty, a firm family favourite in our household now. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brazos river stew

great stew recipe i found in a wonderful cookbook called tastes and tales from texas.  nothing warms you up better on a cold and dreary evening.

1. fry bacon in a dutch oven or large stew pot
2. remove bacon and drain on paper towel
3. add stew meat to pan and sear
4. lower heat and add tomatoes , beef broth , water celery , onion , garlic , worcestershire sauce and chili powder
5. cover and simmer 2 hours
6. remove 1 / 4 cup broth from stew , cool , and mix with flour
7. add flour mixture to stew
8. salt and pepper as needed
9. add carrots and potatoes and cook 30 minutes
10. add corn and bacon
11. cook another 5 minutes
demonstrations.review: Wanted to make stew so went for this one. My husband really enjoyed it but me not so much - it tasted a bit too much of worcestershire sauce for my liking but as my husband says Worcestershire Sauce is used a lot in Texan food (?) no idea if he is right since we are not from the US. He loved the stew which is great, thanks for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
braised brussels sprouts with vinegar and dill

nan

1. trim sprouts
2. halved if desired
3. in large pot of boiling salted water , cook brussels sprouts for 8 minutes if whole , 6 minutes if halved , or until barely tender
4. drain , refresh under cold running water and drain again
5. in well-greased 13x9-inch casserole , combine sprouts , dill , vinegar , and salt and pepper to taste
6. mix well
7. bake , covered , in 350f oven for 10 minutes
8. uncover and bake for 5 minutes longer
target.review: This was excellent.  Wonderful flavor.  Perfect texture.  I cut the recipe in half but otherwise followed it exactly (using the option to cut the sprouts in half).  I was also fortunate enough to have fresh brussels sprouts from the farmers market.  The wine vinegar I have is probably not the best.  It would probably be even better with a better quality vinegar.  I might even try it with balsamic....

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sesame bok choy

i just love bok choy.  this is a great bok choy side dish.

1. wash bok choy
2. cut stems and tops into about 1-inch pieces
3. in a large bowl , combine last 7 ingredients and mix well
4. add bok choy to the dressing and toss to coat
5. place in a hot wok or large pan and stir-fry over med-high heat for about 8 minutes or until desired tenderness is reached
demonstrations.review: This was great.  I added some mushrooms that I browned a bit beforehand.  Also, I put the bok choy ends in first and cooked them (along with the sauce and the mushrooms) for about 5 minutes before adding the leafy part.  I cooked with the lid on to soften the bok choy ends, which created a lot of liquid, so I took it off in the end and thickened it up with cornstarch.  Very tasty and easy.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy vegan chili

this is a quick, extremely healthy vegan version of traditional chili. you can't even tell the difference! it came from the website for physicians committee for responsible medicine originally, but i tweaked a little to make it even healthier.

1. pour the boiling water over the tvp and let stand until softened
2. braise the onion , bell peppers and garlic in water until onion is clear , then add remaining ingredients , including tvp
3. simmer for at least 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good.  I did not have the TVP on hand and so I just left that out.  I also did not add the jalapeno but perhaps I should have.  I felt that it could have used a little more spice and a little more zip.  I will definitely make this again and just play around a bit with the spices.  Very glad that there are left overs available for the rest of the week.  Thanks Moody!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean and tortilla bake

great quick and healthy dinner.

1. preheat oven to 350 f
2. spray a large skillet with cooking spray
3. add garlic , onions , tomato , green onion , cumin , and chili powder
4. cook on medium heat until onion is tender
5. add tomato sauce and cook 5 minutes more
6. stir in beans , cilantro , salt and pepper
7. spray a 9 inch square baking dish with cooking spray
8. layer 4 tortillas , 1 / 3 cheese , and 1 / 3 of the bean mixture
9. repeat 2 more times
10. top with reserved 2 tablespoons of cheese
11. bake 20 minutes , covered , then 10 minutes uncovered or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: This was very good.  I doubled everything except the tortillas (I used handmade tortillas) and then baked it in a 9x12 glass dish.  The bottom tortillas were very chewy.  I think that next time I will put sauce on the bottom first and then the tortillas.  I served plain yogurt and chunky salsa with it, which were great additions.  Excellent recipe.  We will be enjoying this again and I'm very glad there are leftovers to enjoy tomorrow.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tofu stroganoff

this delicious vegetarian version of stroganoff comes from one of my favorite cookbooks: the vegetarian meat and potatoes cookbook. it was also suggested that cooked green beans can be added to this at the end with the tofu to add some additional color, flavor and texture. hope you enjoy this dish as much as i do!

1. heat 1 tbsp oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. add tofu and cook until golden brown on all sides , stirring occasionally , about 7 minutes
3. remove tofu from skillet with slotted spoon and set aside
4. add remaining 1 tbsp oil to skillet and cook onion until softened , about 5 minutes
5. next , add sliced mushrooms and cook until they begin to release their juices , about 1-2 minutes
6. stir in paprika and flour and coat onions and mushroom
7. be sure to cook for about 1 minute , stirring constantly , in order to remove the raw taste from the flour
8. add tomato paste and wine and stir until paprika and flour are well blended into the liquid
9. add vegetable stock and bring entire mixture to a boil
10. reduce heat to low , add salt and pepper to taste , and simmer for about 20 minutes
11. remove from the heat and whisk in sour cream
12. be sure its blended well
13. add tofu back to skillet and simmer for about 5 more minutes over low heat until heated through
14. serve over hot noodles , and top with additional sour cream if desired
demonstrations.review: I really liked this, although I'm not sure that I would make it again.  Nothing wrong with it.  It's very good, but it didn't completely wow me.  I believe that it could use a little more zing.  Not sure what it needs.  Maybe I will try again afterall and see if I can tweak it a little, because I like the basic recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
frijoles negros  cuban black beans

ay caramba, these are good!

1. fry the onion and pepper in a little oil
2. add the garlic and saute a little
3. introduce a little of the bean liquid until all previous ingredients are soft
4. add the beans with the remaining liquid
5. add spices and simmer about 30 minutes
6. add the vinegar just before serving
7. these are quite good when served over a bed of rice seasoned with just lime
demonstrations.review: These were excellent.  I cooked my own beans (with a few spices) and then made according to the recipe.  We ate this for dinner one night and then I had the rest over the next couple of days rolled into handmade corn tortillas.  I used to buy canned Cuban Black Beans occasionally, but no more.  Thanks Carol!

target.recipe_text:
easy low fat oven fried catfish

the catfish has a nice crunchy coating, just as good as pan-fried without all the greasiness! i like to serve this with southern dishes like baked sweet potatoes and collard greens.

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. heavily spray a large non-stick baking pan with non-stick cooking spray
3. pour egg substitute in large shallow bowl
4. sprinkle with some emeril's essence
5. also some salt and pepper , if you prefer
6. place fish coating on a large plate
7. add some essence to this also , if you wish
8. rinse fish fillets
9. squeeze lemon wedges over fish
10. sprinkle with essence , salt and pepper on both side of fish
11. dip in coating
12. dip fish in egg substitute , then again in fish coating , and place on baking sheet
13. bake at 450f for approximately 10-15 minutes , until bottom of fish starts to brown
14. turn fish , and bake about 5-8 minutes more , until fish is browned and crisp
15. serve
target.review:
This turned out to be a very easy to make and enjoyable dish. I used an actual egg as opposed to the egg substitute only as I didn't have any on hand. 

My wife enjoyed this recipe a lot as we always like a good "fried catfish" dinner. She said that this one was a "smiley face" success. 

It is now added to our list of favorites. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot beef barbecue

this is the first thing i made in my new crock pot. i borrowed a lot of this recipe from vincy bramblett's easy beef bbq.

1. cook the roast on low , covered with the bottle of beer
2. in the morning , drain the liquid out of the crock pot and shred the beef
3. combine the other ingredients and pour over the beef
4. keep the crock pot on low heat until ready to serve
5. if you need to add liquid , add a little bit of water
demonstrations.review: Yes indeed a very simple, easy and very delightful. The barbeque sauce we used was "Danny's Baldheaded" which we found many years ago at our local Publix Supermarket and has become our one and only sauce so far. I forgot the hot sauce but it didn't matter as the beef was very tender and on a fresh, french bread burger bun.... mmm, mmm, good stuff! Thanks for the recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy baked basa

basa, is a member of the catfish family, farm-raised in fresh water. the flavor of the basa is milder and more delicate than other carfish; when cooked it does not give off a 

1. combine the first six ingredients in mixing bowl
2. dip fillets first in lemon juice , then in almond mixture to coat throughly
3. place on baking sheet
4. bake at 400 degrees , 15-20 minutes , or until fish is cooked through
5. garnish with parsley , serve with lemon wedges and your favorite tarter sauce
demonstrations.review:
Very pleasant recipe. Enjoyed the lightness of the fish and the crust. I cooked it a tad too long as my wife does not like undercooked fish, but the tartar sauce on the side corrected for this. I would probably increase the amount of the almond mixture to get a little more breading. The breading mixture had very good flavor. I used a mortar and pestal to grind the almonds. Next time I'd use a food processor or a plastic zip bag and mallet to get a finer grind. 

Overall a very wonderful dish that I will add to my cookbook and pass on to freinds and family. We just had this and a good green salad on the side for a very light, pleasantly filling late night dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flattened cornish game hens with garlic citrus marinade

a delicious entree that is easy enough for a weekday dinner, yet pretty enough for a dinner party. serve with stir-fried summer squash, a salad and french bread. the recipe comes from bon appetit.

1. prepare bbq
2. combine olive oil , chopped thyme , garlic , lemon peel , lime peel , honey , salt , and pepper in a baking dish and stir marinade to blend well
3. place hens on work surface and cover with plastic wrap and pound gently with mallet to flatten slightly
4. place hen halves in marinade in dish , using fingers , rub both sides of hens with marinade
5. let marinate 20 minutes at room temperature
6. grill hen halves until just cooked through and skin is lightly charred , brushing with remaining marinade , about 12 minutes per side
7. arrange hen on plates and garnish lemon wedges , lime wedges , and fresh thyme sprigs
demonstrations.review:
This was a very easy recipe to make and sounds great. Although the end results for us was not so great. I grilled them on the grill for a little longer than the recommended time but should have allowed another 20 minutes or so. The lemon and lime marinade/basting sauce over was very overpowering for us on the outside of the hens and for some reason the meat was very bland. My wife commented that other than the strong lemon & lime flavor she would have thought I had poached the hens due to the lack of flavor in the meat. 

They looked wonderful from the start to the finish. They presented well... maybe less citrus and more honey? May try again with some alterations to the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick mediterranean chicken thighs

clipped from my local newspaper, posted until i can try. with only 6 ingredients, plus salt and pepper, this delicious and easy meal is on the table in only 30 minutes. serve with a salad and a side of pasta or crusty bread for a balanced dinner. i'm sure boneless skinless chicken breasts would be good too, but would probably take longer to cook.

1. season both sides of the chicken thighs with salt and pepper
2. in a large nonstick skillet with a lid , heat the oil over high heat
3. add the chicken thighs and cook until well browned , about 2 minutes per side
4. add the tomatoes , orange juice , garlic and capers
5. bring the mixture to a simmer , then reduce heat to low , cover the pan and cook for 8 minutes
6. uncover the pan and continue cooking , turning the thighs once , until the chicken is no longer pink in the middle and the sauce has thickened , about 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Outstanding is all I can say! I too clipped this from our local newspaper a couple of years ago and stuck it in my file of recipes to try. The other day while weeding through the file I came across this and thought I'd give it a whirl. My wife and I just loved it. A very unique flavor and filling with a side salad and bread to sop up the sauce as the recipe stated

demonstrations.recipe_text:
catfish in wine with broiled scallion butter sauce

this catfish entree is elegant and easy to prepare. i serve it with noodle casserole with four italian cheeses, sauteed fresh vegetables, and a wedge of iceberg lettuce with homemade 1000 dressing.

1. heat the oven to 350 degrees
2. in a baking pan , place the catfish filets , pour the wine over them , then salt and pepper
3. bake , covered for 20 minutes and remove from oven
4. turn on the broiler
5. mix together the sauce ingredients , and top each filet with 1 / 4 of the mixture
6. sprinkle on paprika
7. broil until the topping is golden brown
demonstrations.review:
Mmmm, mmmm, mmmm GOOD STUFF! 

What a wonderful recipe! I made this the other night after looking over several recipes in an attempt to find a different twist for one of our favorite fish... Catfish. What a pleasant surprise. 

My wife especially enjoyed it. She said it was one of, if not the best variations to catfish that I had come across. 

The combination of butter and mayonnaise makes for a very rich yet light touch.... 
I followed the recipe as written and it now resides in my seafood cookbook and will be sharing it with other family members. 

Thank you for a great recipe. OUTSTANDING!

target.recipe_text:
easy butterhorn rolls

delicious buttery rolls! no kneading needed, let rise overnight. so light and scrumptious! (from allrecipes.com)

1. combine 1 cup butter and milk in a small saucepan
2. heat until butter is melted
3. set aside to cool
4. dissolve yeast and 1 teaspoon sugar in the warm water
5. in a large bowl , beat the eggs , 1 / 2 cup sugar , and salt together
6. add the milk mixture and the yeast mixture in the egg mixture , stirring to blend
7. add the flour and baking powder
8. stir until no dry patches remain
9. the dough will be wet and sticky
10. cover and refrigerate overnight
11. divide dough into four parts , and roll each part into 1 / 2 inch thick circles on a floured surface
12. spread surface with the melted butter
13. cut each circle like a pie into 8 or 12 triangles , and roll up from larger to small end
14. place rolls point side down on a baking sheet , and allow to rise until doubled preheat oven to 400 degrees f
15. bake rolls for 8 to 10 minutes in the preheated oven , or until golden brown
target.review: I've made these countless times, and every time they're perfect. The first day the dough is basically a batter, but as long as it sits overnight in the fridge, its perfectly dough-like the next day. They're so butter-y and flavorful. I never use any other recipe :) Thank you Hannah:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 minute wacky vegan microwave chocolate cake for one

you absolutely will not believe how fast you can make the most decadent, moist, one-serving chocolate cake without eggs or milk. this is a variation of the famous wacky cake or crazy cake. it's sooo good! you stir all the ingredients and microwave it in a coffee cup. try it. seriously.

1. stir together all the dry ingredients in a large coffee cup
2. add wet ingredients and mix well with a fork
3. microwave on 50% power for 3 minutes
4. i always have my cup on the rotating plate
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wow!! I've tried a few other microwave cake recipes and they were all rubbery and tasted like flour. This one is awesome! Like dreamling_13 I used a full tablespoon of cocoa. So good. Cant wait to try it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
savory sweet potato fries

sweet potato fries are a favorite in our house and are so satisfying they could almost be a meal on their own. this is a savory version of our favorite fries. we enjoy dipping ours in barbecue sauce!

1. preheat oven to 450 degrees
2. wash the potatoes with cool water and pat dry
3. no need to peel them but you can pull of the little "stems"
4. cut the potatoes into fry-size pieces
5. if you don't have a fancy gadget for this , i suggest enlisting your husband to do this because sweet potatoes are hard to cut !
6. place all the fries in a gallon size ziploc bag along with the oil
7. seal the bag and toss to coat
8. open the bag and add in the seasonings
9. toss again until all the fries are evenly coated
10. spread the fries out on two baking sheets
11. this gives them enough room to get crispy
12. if they're too crowded , they just get steamed and soggy
13. bake the fries in the oven for 15 minutes and then turn the fries using a pair of tongs or a spatula
14. bake for another 15 minutes
15. fries should be slightly crisp
16. some black on the edges is okay , since it's pretty tasty , just not too much !
demonstrations.review:
Oh. My. Gosh.

WOW! These are so amazing. The cinnamon and rosemary are wonderful together, and the thyme, pepper, and garlic all marry beautifully. I couldn't help myself though. I had to add a dash of cumin :) I will make these very often! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic bchamel sauce with lots of flavour

this recipe comes from the wonderful book "mon premier dîner végétarien" by alice hart, which i was gifted for my bday a couple of weeks ago.
it is a bit more involved than your usual béchamel, but so worth it. the taste is outstanding and really makes gratins and pasta shine.

1. in a saucepan combine milk , onion , peppercorns and laurel leaf
2. bring to a boil , then take off the heat and let steep for 20 minutes
3. strain milk through a sieve
4. if using this sauce in my pasta gratin recipe , keep the onion , if not discard onion with the laurel leaf and peppercorns
5. in a second saucepan melt the butter over medium heat
6. add the flour and whisk in using a wire whisk
7. let colour for 1 minute whisking continuously
8. slowly add the 1 / 3 of the milk whisking it in so that no lumps form
9. when sauce looks thickened , add another 1 / 3 of the milk
10. keep whisking and finally add the last third
11. bring to a boil and let simmer for 15 minutes
12. season with salt and pepper to taste and a good pinch of nutmeg
13. if you dont use the sauce right away , cover it so that the milk doesnt form a skin on top
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I made it the same way Boomette did, and it was perfect. Just make sure that you use a large container, and keep an eye on it to prevent boil overs. :) I'll make this again for sure. :) Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sun dried tomato and parsley dip

a very yummy, summery fresh dip that goes great with crudites or crackers.

1. in a tall bowl combine all the ingredients
2. blend together using a hand-held blender
3. alternatively you could also use a food processor or blender
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe! A little thick, so next time I might add some milk, or use whipped cream cheese. And me being the garlic lover I am, I used uh.....5 cloves of garlic. Yeah, maybe a little too much :D Hahahahaha I'll make it again for sure though. Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pf chang s spicy green beans

copycat pf channg's. have you ever try popular szechuan spicy green beans like pf chang's, this stir fried green beans with fiery chili sauce and garlic won’t let you down.

1. rinse and trim green beans , set aside
2. mix sauces in a bowl well
3. pour water in wok , heat over high heat until bubbling , boil green bean for 3-5 minutes until crispy tender
4. remove and drain
5. heat cooking oil hot in wok over high heat , stir in ginger and garlic until aromatic , combine green bean , stir constantly until beans are soft about 2-3 minutes
6. combine sauce mixture , stir around until the sauce is thicken and glazes the bean
7. transfer and serve spicy green bean with cooked rice
demonstrations.review: These we're the most AMAZING green beans EVER! However, the reason I give only 4 stars, is because, the recipe calls for 2 full tablespoons of chili flakes. I only used about 1 1/2 teaspoons and it was still quite spicy. Other than that, they were perfect. I would eat them everyday if I could :) Thanks Tina!

target.recipe_text:
the ultimate chicken and dumplings

this is my ultimate comfort food.  while time consuming to make, the taste is out of this world.  i have always hated the bisquick type drop dumplings, so when i found this recipe, i was ticked pink!

1. in a large pot , add the chicken , 1 quart of water , onion , celery , garlic and peppercorns
2. stew the chicken until completely cooked
3. remove chicken from the broth and cool
4. remove skin and bones
5. cut the chicken into bite sized chunks or shred
6. remove 1 - 2 cups broth to use in dumplings
7. allow to cool
8. to the remaining broth , add the rest of the water , salt , pepper , bouillon cubes and shredded / cubed chicken and heat to simmering
9. to make dumplings: mix together dry ingredients
10. mix egg with one cup of broth and add slowly to the dry ingredients
11. use as much broth as needed to make a stiff dough
12. knead the dough on floured board , roll very thin
13. cut into 1-inch squares with a pizza cutter
14. drop in simmering broth
15. cover and cook 20 minutes
16. enjoy
17. if freezing , i will freeze the dumplings , still uncooked , separately from the soup
18. when time to reheat it , just bring dumplings back to room temperature , reheat the soup to boiling and drop in the dumplings
19. very tasty !
target.review: Made this tonite. Very, Very nice. But made it Weight Watchers Sytle with chicken breast, added a bit of pumpkin in for colour.And just added the bouillon stock to the flour mix for the dumplings Will be making this again. Thank you for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
poached chicken

i do about 12 breasts at a time and freeze for sandwiches or wraps or i use it for stirfry's.

1. place chicken in a large saucepan
2. add water and remaining ingredients , and bring to a boil
3. reduce heat , and simmer , uncovered , for 5 minutes or until chicken is done
4. remove from heat , let stand , uncovered , 20 minutes
5. place chicken and poaching liquid in a large bowl
6. cover and chill , or , put just the chicken in freezer bags and freeze for another time
demonstrations.review: This was great. I didn't have breasts so I used 6 skinned thighs.I used stock instead of water and wine. When cooked, it was nice a juicy. Saved the stock and shredded 4 of the thighs, added a little bit of soy sauce,green beans, black pepper and thickened it all with corn flour. Put it all into a dish covered it with frozen puff pastry. YUM!! Thank you for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kang jyd taohu  thai tofu soup

this recipe is not vegetarian. this recipe is from the kitchen of a local thai restaurant near my home town.

1. combine the pork , garlic , and salt in a small bowl and mix until well blended
2. set aside
3. bring the chicken stock to a boil in a large saucepan over medium heat
4. using a small teaspoon , drop small bits of the pork mixture into the soup and bring the mixture back to a boil again
5. add the tofu , bok choy , and season with the fish sauce , sugar and pepper
6. simmer uncovered for 5 minutes before removing from heat
7. serve hot , garnished with the green onions and cilantro leaves
demonstrations.review:
This was very nice and so easy to make. I didn't add tofu( personal choice) added some mushroom to bulk it up, and a little grated carrot, for color, I too, added pepper to the meat. Very healthy and filling .
Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curry flavored rice mix

once you do the prep, divide into 3 airtight containers, for here it is only 20 mins to the table whenever you need it. i have three-seasoned rice mix recipes see which one you like best. look for the other two chicken flavored and onion flavored rice mix.

1. combine all ingredients and mix until evenly distributed
2. store in a cool dry place
3. use within 6 months
4. cooking directions: for 8 servings
5. boil 3 cups water in a covered pan
6. add 1 1 / 3 cups of rice mix
7. stir
8. cover and simmer for 20 minutes or until liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: This was lovely. I made it with fresh onion, garlic etc as I didn't have instant minced garlic on hand.Making more today and freezing it in serving sizes. This is going to mix in well with my weightwatchers programme. Thank you so much for posting your mixes. will try them all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian pork and noodle soup

from betty crocker simple winter meals.

1. spray 3-quart saucepan with cooking spray
2. heat over medium-high heat
3. add pork , garlic and gingerroot
4. stir-fry 3 to 5 minutes or until pork is brown
5. stir in broth , water and soy sauce
6. heat to boiling
7. reduce heat
8. simmer uncovered 5 minutes
9. stir in noodles , carrot and bell pepper
10. simmer uncovered about 10 minutes or until noodles are tender
11. stir in spinach
12. cook until heated through
demonstrations.review: Yum...... as the others I redid the veges a little, and used mushrooms, bokchoy, just veges I had to use before they went too manky in the fridge. Used rinsed rice noodles because that's what i had. Very nice, will make again. Thank you for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek potatoes  oven roasted and delicious

these potatoes are a staple in our home. whether accompanying roast lamb or chicken, or just on their own, we have them a couple of times a week. they are delicious and the ones that get overly-brown in the pan and stick a bit are mine!  clean up is a little tricky with this recipe, unless you line your pans with foil, but i find that just filling the pan up with hot, sudsy water and forgetting for an hour (something i apparently have no problem doing ;-)) helps a lot.

1. preheat oven to 420f a reviewer has suggested spraying the baking pan with pam - that sounds like a great idea !
2. put all the ingredients into a baking pan large enough to hold them
3. season generously with sea salt and black pepper
4. make sure your hands are very clean and put them in the pan and give everything a toss to distribute
5. the garlic will drop into the water / oil solution but its flavour will permeate the potatoes , and this way , it won't burn
6. bake for 40 minutes
7. when a nice golden-brown crust has formed on the potatoes , give them a stir to bring the white underside up , season lightly with a bit more sea salt and pepper and just a light sprinkling of oregano
8. add 1 / 2 cup more water if pan appears to be getting dry , and pop back into oven to brown other side of potatoes
9. this will take about another 40 minutes
10. do not be afraid of overcooking the potatoes- they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: This turned out very nice,  Left out the water and only added 1 tlbsp of oil, I put mixture into a ziplock bag and put in zuchini,mushrooms,cauliflower  left it for about 1 hour then cooked them in a George forman grill, very healthy and went well with my weight watchers programme. Thanks for posting

target.recipe_text:
chicken in peanut curry

this is a favorite family recipe we received from a good friend. one batch is never enough! the recipe is so versatile that you can add tofu, mushrooms, or any other vegetables to your liking!

1. in a medium sauce pan heat coconut milk , curry paste , peanut butter , sugar , and fish sauce until they come to a very small boil
2. set aside and cool adding cornstarch to thicken
3. while the sauce is cooling , stir fry 1 chopped onion and 1 t minced garlic
4. cut up chicken into small pieces and stir fry with the onion and garlic until chicken is cooked through
5. combine the garlic , onion and chicken with the sauce and heat
6. spoon the chicken peanut curry over rice and enjoy
target.review: This is a keeper!  It's not spicy at all, but you could easily turn up the heat if you'd like.  I didn't have cornstarch but it came out perfect.  It's VERY good & will definately be used many more times!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick cherry cobbler

i found this recipe in the betty crocker "good and easy" cookbook and it's become a family favorite. the almond and cherry combination is wonderful. it's such a fast recipe, using ingredients that are easily kept on hand.
update 2/16/09:  thanks to several reviews pointing out that the recipe needs to be served a la mode, i am modifying the original recipe to the way i've been making it myself for years now.  i've always had ice cream in step  8 as a serving option (have now added it to the ingredient list) & i've always used a full teaspoon of almond extract in the mix because we prefer the stronger flavor.  thanks to everyone for taking the time to review.  *tink

1. mix pie filling & almond extract in ungreased 8x8x2" square baking dish
2. place in cold oven
3. heat oven to 400 degrees
4. mix bisquick , 1 tbl sugar , milk & butter with fork until a soft dough forms
5. drop six spoonfuls onto warm filling
6. it's not meant to be a top crust , just 6 individual biscuits with filling showing inbetween
7. sprinkle with additional sugar
8. bake 18-20 minutes or until topping is lightly browned
9. serve with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: I really like this.  I didn't use any extract and was way too stuffed to try it hot.  It was worth the wait and is very good cold!  I also put it all straight into a hot oven, and it came out wonderful.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy ranch chicken

my kids love this recipe. it's flavorful and yet easy to make. i place baked potatoes in oven at the same time. then use the rest of the dry ranch to make topping for the potatoes or salad.

1. mix ranch dressing , salt , pepper and dry bread crumbs in 1 quart storage bag
2. beat 2 eggs in bowl
3. rinse and dredge chicken through egg then place in bag and shake until completely covered
4. place in buttered 13x9-inch glass baking dish
5. place a pat of butter on top of chicken
6. cook at 375f for 1 hour
7. omit eggs and dredge through dressing and then trough dry bread crumbs or crackers
8. also can put crackers in dry bread crumbs to make crispier coating
9. time may vary depending on the size of the breasts
demonstrations.review: This was good.  I doubled the recipe (2 cups bread crumbs & a whole packet of ranch mix) the kick of the ranch flavor was hard to detect.  I added about a tablespoon of parmsean cheese to the mix, and I think that helped.  The chicken was perfectly cooked & juicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy yam casserole

my boss' wife always makes these for the annual christmas party. they are to die for. better than the kind made with marshmallows imho. thanks, holly! note: this recipe can be doubled and placed in one large 9x13 dish but the baking thime also needs to be doubled. added to omac (thanks to the freezer tag game) see freezing and cooking directions at the bottom of instructions.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. whip together "yam" ingredients and pour into a 9x13 glass baking dish
3. mix "topping" ingredients until it resembles coarse crumbs and drop over top of yam mixture
4. bake for 30 minutes
5. to freeze: assemble casserole as directed up to the point of baking
6. cover well with foil
7. label and freeze
8. to serve: thaw in fridge , uncover and bake as directed
demonstrations.review: I forgot to rate this the first time I tried it months ago.  It was so sweet and absolutely delicious.  I made it again for Easter, and didn't make the real topping (which is excellent), just used a sprinkling of chopped pecans.  It's REALLY sweet and an excellent side dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oh so yummy chocolate gooey layered dessert

the title speaks for itself. all i can say is mmmmmm...mmmmmmmm. a typically southern recipe.

1. first layer: mix well
2. press into 9x13 inch pan
3. bake at 350 for 15 to 20 minutes
4. cool
5. second layer: beat the cream cheese and sugar together
6. fold in cool whip and spread on crust
7. third layer: beat milk and pudding mixes slowly
8. spread over second layer
9. fourth layer: top with remaining cool whip
10. decorate with chopped nuts , shaved chocolate or cherries
11. chill 24 hours
demonstrations.review: I screwed this up and I can't figure out how, as I followed the directions exactly.  The bottom crust never set, so when I spread the next layer on it broke apart completely.  So I mixed the first and second layer together, and added the 3rd & 4th layers as the recipe states.  It was SO rich (so much so that nobody could get down more than a few bites) but all in all it was chocolately and pretty tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
any fruit fast fat free cobbler

this fabulous dessert is 3 ww points a serving and can be made with fresh, canned, or frozen fruit. it is adapted from a recipe in the 

1. combine all of the ingredients except the fruit in a bowl
2. pour it into an 8x8 pan coated with cooking spray
3. add the fruit right on top
4. the crust will come up over the fruit and cover it
5. bake in a 350 degree oven for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  I used thawed frozen blueberries.  I'm in Europe where we have vanilla powder rather than vanilla extract so I added some of that along with the baking powder.  It's awesome and perfectly sweet!  I used whole milk so my verision isn't 100% fat free but a good healthy dessert.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
british steak and ale pie

great stick to your ribs meal for those cold winter nights. serve with mashed potatoes, carrots, mushy peas and lashings of gravy. my own recipe enjoy.

1. fry beef until browned
2. transfer to a large pan , add onions and mushrooms , beef stock , beer and salt and pepper
3. simmer for 1 hour until tender and the sauce thickened
4. add beef mixture to a large oven proofed dish
5. roll out puff pastry and place on the top of the beef mixture ensuring no gaps
6. brush milk with a pastry brush
7. bake in a preheated medium oven for 30 to 40 minutes until risen and brown
8. serve
target.review: We lived in Britain for 4 years and we loved the steak and ale pies!  I struggled with handling the pastry crusts, but that was just me being clumsy.  I thought the gravy was a bit runny so I thickened it up a bit.  I should have used a darker ale than what I had on hand, but this was still very flavorful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo and peanut butter brownie cupcakes

i found this while searching the web and decided to try it today. my youngest son told me it was the best he ever had and my brother went so far as to say it was oreogasmic...so i'll let you decide. it is best to spay the cupcake liners so the brownies don't stick.

1. preheat oven to 350f degrees and line a 12 muffin cup baker with paper liners
2. prepare brownie mix according to package directions
3. for each cupcake cup spread 1 / 2 teaspoon of peanut butter over each oreo cookie and stack them on top of each other
4. place oreo stacks into the cupcake lined muffin cups
5. spoon 2 tablespoons of brownie batter over each stacked oreos and let it run down the sides of the cookies
6. if you have left over brownie batter , bake separately in a separate baker or muffin tin
7. bake cookies and brownies for 18 to 20 minutes , until brownies are cooked through
8. let cool completely then serve
9. makes 12 servings
demonstrations.review: My sister-in-law made these for her husband's birthday and they disappeared!  I had to use mint Oreos and Nutella because my daughter has a peanut allergy, but they're still awesome!  Thanks for posting the step-by-step instructions!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk doughnuts donuts

i got this recipe when i was a teenager and have been making it ever since. anytime my nephews and nieces spend the night, they request these. they take some time but they sure are worth it!

1. dissolve yeast in warm water in a large bowl
2. let stand 5 minutes
3. add buttermilk , shortening , sugar and 1 1 / 2 cup flour , baking powder and salt
4. mix well
5. add enough remaining flour to make a soft dough
6. turn dough onto a floured surface and knead several times
7. roll dough to 1 / 2 inch thick and cut with a 2 1 / 2 inch doughnut cutter
8. place doughnuts on lightly floured surface , cover and let rise 45 minutes or until double in bulk
9. heat 2-3 inches of oil to 375f
10. drop in 4 or 5 doughnuts at a time
11. cook about 2 minutes or until lightly golden in color , turning once
12. drain well on paper towels
13. combine 2 1 / 2 cups powdered sugar with 1 / 4 cup milk , stir until smooth
14. dip each doughnut in glaze while still warm
15. allow excess glaze to drip off
16. cool on wire rack or serve warm
demonstrations.review: These were such a hit!  I made some for my son's birthday breakfast and they disappeared!  My husband says they're better than Krispy Kreme (but then again, there is no Krispy Kreme where we live, so his memory may be a little fuzzy)!  :D  Definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef tips on rice   pressure cooker

a pressure cooker makes this much faster.

1. place first five ingredients in a zip top bag and shake well to distribute
2. add the beef cubes to the bag and shake until all are well covered
3. in a pressure cooker , brown the meat in the vegetable oil over medium heat
4. once the meat is browned , add the onions and the garlic to the the cooker and saute the onions while deglazing the pan
5. once the onions turn translucent add the can of beef consomm and stir to combine
6. place the lid on the cooker and bring to pressure over medium heat
7. cook 25 minutes and remove from heat
8. once the pressure subsides open the lid and simmer until the proper consistency
9. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: So delicious!  I had packages of sirloin tip steak (round steak, or cube steak....they all of the same texture to me!) and I had no idea how I'd ever use them up.  I recently got a pressure cooker at a charity auction and have been searching for recipes to use - this one is definitely a winner!  The meat was so incredibly tender - I've never had cube steak come out this delicious!  I served it with mashed potatoes and I should have doubled the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
prize winning marinade for beef

i combined my sister-in-law's marinade recipe with my friend's barbecue cooking method. i then submitted this recipe into to a radio station as part of a contest and i ended up winning the grand prize of a jenairre stove! it's so versatile that it works both with cheap cuts of beef and expensive too. i won't cook beef roast any other way. enjoy!

1. using a food processor , crush peppercorns until fine
2. add garlic to processor and crush
3. add soy sauce , worcestershire sauce and lemon juice and blend
4. pour mixture into giant zip lock freezer bag and add the meat to be marinated
5. seal bag
6. refrigerate for 48 hours
7. reserve the marinade for later use
8. barbecue the meat as you would normally however , i prefer to cook the meat very very slowly using an indirect cooking method--only one side of the barbecue is lit and turned down to low
9. the meat is placed on the one side of the barbecue which is off , over a pan of water , which sits on the barbecue rocks
10. relax while your dinner cooks
11. put marinade on the stove and bring to a boil
12. add just enough marinade to some sour cream , to make a sauce to drizzle over the cooked meat
13. sit back and enjoy the compliments
demonstrations.review: Such a wonderful marinade!  I wrapped the roast in foil and cooked it in the crock-pot on low with potatoes and zucchini (wrapped separately in foil packets).  Wrapped the potatoes in foil and put them on the bottom of the crock-pot, then placed the wrapped roast on top of the potatoes so that it would cook in low, indirect heat.  Tucked the foil packets of zucchini in beside it.  Wow - my new favorite crock-pot dinner.  This will be a frequent menu item!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave chocolate snack cake

this is sooo easy and really quite yummmy. it is also nice for small families, because it only makes a small cake.  the recipe originally came from taste of home and they used a 700 watt oven to test the recipe. mine is a 900 watt and you just have to adjust the time a bit to accomodate your microwave the first time you make it.

1. combine flour , sugar , cocoa powder , salt
2. stir in oil , cold water , vinegar , and vanilla until blended well
3. pour into an ungreased 8" microwave safe square baking pan
4. microwave on high for about 6-8 minutes , turning the dish every 2 minutes , or until a toothpick tests clean when inserted near the center
5. for sauce:in a 1 quart microwave safe bowl , combine sugar , cornstarch , and cocoa powder until combined well
6. stir in water and a dash of salt
7. microwave on high for 2-3 minutes , stirring occasionally , or until the mixture comes to a boil
8. once it hit the boiling point , cook another 1 minute more
9. stir in butter and vanilla and mix well
10. slice cake into squares and serve the warm sauce over the still warm cake
11. i like to add some sprinkles , shredded coconut , or chopped nuts on top too
demonstrations.review: My in-laws gave me a microwave to replace mine that had konked out and I used this recipe to make a 'thank you' cake (since it was made in my present!).  ;)  My kids (ages 8 & 9) actually did most of the work, which shows how easy it is.  All of the chocoholics in the family loved it.  Super easy and fast!  I baked it for 5 1/2 minutes in the 1100 Watt microwave, in case that's helpful to anyone!

target.recipe_text:
tess  any fruit crumble

i've been looking for the perfect crumble recipe for a long time and my friend tess had it! i've made this different times with peaches, apples, plums, and rhubarb/strawberry but really any fruit or berries will do. it is easy to change the serving size or make more fruity or more crumbly as long as the crumble ingredients remain equal parts.

1. mix fruit wiht 1 t flour , 1 t sugar and the cinnamon
2. crumble together flour , brown sugar , butter and oatmeal
3. butter a 9x9 pan and pour in fruit
4. top with crumble and bake at 350 degrees until browned and bubbly
target.review: Fantastic tasting fruit crumble and so easy to make. I used peaches, plums, and nectarines for my fruit and the combination was very good. Added a little more cinnamon since I love the flavor and we enjoyed for an early morning treat. Will make this again using apples and then blueberries. Made and reviewed for ZWT8 - 2012.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery cabbage casserole

nice vegetarian recipe

1. put cabbage into 1 1 / 2 quart casserole and pour rice over top
2. poke with fork several places to allow a bit of rice into the cabbage
3. sprinkle salt and pepper over rice
4. pour water over all
5. cover and bake in 350f oven for 1 hour
6. remove from oven
7. heat margarine in small fry pan
8. and saute onion until golden
9. add this to cabbage
10. stir to combine
demonstrations.review: I wanted to really like this cabbage casserole but I am sorry it didnt work to well for me. I used packaged cole slaw mix that included carrots and red cabbage. After an hour the rice was still not cooked so I put it back in the oven for a bit longer. After adding the onion it needed a little something so I added more salt, garlic powder, and some celery seed. That helped but it still was on the bland side. I think if chicken or vegetable broth was used instead of water that would increase the flavor. Maybe some other seasonings to boost the cabbage flavor too. Made and reviewed for Spring Spectacular 2008.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
souper chicken

got a crowd coming over? this can serve a lot of people. very simple and versatile. one of my favourites.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. mix soups and wine
3. pour over chicken
4. cover and bake for 2 1 / 2 hours
5. thicken sauce with cornstarch and water if you want gravy
6. if you want stew , add some onions , carrots , frozen peas etc
7. 30 minutes before it is done
demonstrations.review: This is an wonderful canned soup chicken recipe! I used a can of french onion soup, chicken broth instead of white wine, and 4 skinless boneless chicken breasts. I browned the chicken in my electric skillet, added the soups, and cooked slowly for about 1 1/2 hours. The chicken was moist, the gravy from the soup was tasty, and no other seasonings were needed! Thank you Tebo, this is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern living granny smith apple pie

this is the most amazing apple pie i have ever made and it is super easy!  the filling comes out moist and gooey and has the perfect blend of spices.  perfect for a cool fall evening!  (this is a southern living recipe)

1. unroll and stack 2 pie crusts
2. gently roll or press together
3. fit pastry into a 9 inch deep-dish pie plate
4. toss together apples and lemon juice in a large bowl
5. combine brown sugar , granulated sugar , and next 3 ingredients
6. sprinkle over apple mixture and toss to coat
7. spoon into prepared pie crust
8. unroll and place remaining pie crust over filling
9. fold edges under , and crimp
10. cut slits in top for steam to escape
11. bake at 450 degrees for 15 minutes
12. reduce temperature to 350 degrees , and bake for 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: I am not the best pie maker but this one was very easy and tasted great. For the pie crust I bought two boxes so I had three crusts to work with. Left them on the counter to come to room temperature than pressed two crusts together to layer the bottom of the pie pan. Baked according to the directions but my apples were still crunchy. I think I could have left the pie in another 15 or 20 minutes. Everyone enjoyed the pie and I will make it again! Thank you Megan for posting the recipe. Made and reviewed for Spring 2009 Pick A Chef.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blushing harvest crisp

a great recipe to have on hand for fall with the fresh apples and cranberries.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray an 8 inch square baking pan with cooking spray
3. in a large bowl , combine apples , cranberries and 1 / 2 t
4. pumpkin pie spice
5. toss to mix
