demonstrations.review: This was my first time trying tuna burgers, but I have the feeling it won't be my last! I reduced the recipe to serve 1, using half a can of tuna, 1 tablespoon bread crumbs, just an egg white, etc. I had it as suggested, on a bun with lettuce and mayonnaise. The only change I made was to omit the cayenne pepper. It was an excellent light dinner! The burger was tasty and moist, and also looked attractive with the flecks of orange (carrot) and green (green onions and parsley). Very quick and easy to make. I will definitely be keeping this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa apple salad

here's a great healthy grain salad!

1. pour the quinoa into a fine strainer and rinse it well under cold water
2. in a 2 quart saucepan combine the quinoa and 2 cups of water
3. bring to a boil over high heat , reduce heat to low and cover , simmering for 15 minutes
4. remove from heat
5. in a wide shallow bowl combine vinegar , apple juice concentrate , allspice , pepper and garlic
6. add the quinoa and stir occasionally until cooled , around 10 minutes
7. core the apple and chop it into 1 / 4 inch cubes
8. mix the apple , carrot , onion and mint with the quinoa mixture
9. line a serving platter with the lettuce and mount the quinoa salad on top
demonstrations.review: This was quite tasty -- I enjoyed it. Fresh and summery. When I make this again the only thing I'll do differently will be to reduce the vinegar (I found it a bit too tangy for my taste). Thanks for a good quinoa recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spiced  shake  n  bake  pita chips

my dad loves these! and he loves regular, unhealthy potato chips, so i'm more than happy to make these for him. we both like things spicy. i suggest serving with laura divine's low fat hummus (40517). adjust spices to your taste - they are just estimates anyway - i do spices by the senses - feel, smell, and look. can be easily doubled, tripled, etc - just need to do the oven steps a couple more times to account for the extra chips. optional equipment: spray bottle filled with water

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. halve the pita breads and cut into shapes of choice and size preference with either cookie cutters or a pizza wheel
3. place in a bag
4. in a very small bowl , mix together spices
5. spritz water in bag and shake contents
6. repeat until bread is moist
7. add spices and shake until evenly coated
8. place pita pieces evenly on a prepped cookie sheet
9. place in oven for an estimated 10 minutes or until to desired crispness or color
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I am dipping these into salsa as I type... Excellent low-fat snack! The only change I made was to use some basil, oregano and parsley instead of the Italian seasoning. Wasn't sure what was meant by "prepped cookie sheet", so I just sprayed my cookie sheet with Pam. They only took about 7-8 minutes before they were done. Next time (and there WILL be a next time!) I will cut down on the cayenne pepper or else use chili powder instead, because my mouth is on fire! Really great recipe, thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best dog gone pancakes ever

there is no mistake about the amount of baking powder. this is a very light and fluffy recipe for pancakes.

1. mix oil , egg and milk
2. sift in dry ingredients
3. add 2 tbsp oil
4. fry on hot griddle
demonstrations.review: These pancakes are indeed light and fluffy, which made a nice change for us since we normally have the thin type of pancakes. Just one comment though: there's no way on earth this recipe serves 8. I only got 8 large pancakes, and I would normally serve more than 1 pancake per person! I could have made them a bit smaller and made 10-12 pancakes maybe. I'd say this recipe makes 4 servings (or serves 2-3 hungry people!). Good pancakes though.

target.recipe_text:
sarah s tilapia

ok, here it is! my first recipe post to the site, this recipe was given to me by my mom, i have no idea where she got it, but it is just awesome, simple to make, and it is the only fish my picky, picky 11 year old daughter will eat, she loves it! she actually begs me to make it. update: after reading the reviews, i just want to emphasize the importance of using panko breadcrumbs in this recipe. it makes a huge difference! i also have never baked this fish, so cannot predict the results. for those who have commented that the breading isn't sticking well, i have found that this happens to me as well, when i have used too much of the mustard/mayo combo. a thin coating is best! i hope you all enjoy this recipe, and thanks for taking the time to review it!

1. heat oil in large non-stick skillet over med
2. heat
3. combine mayo and mustard in small dish
4. combine next 4 ingred
5. on a plate and mix well
6. brush thin coating of mustard mayo combo on to both sides of each fish fillet
7. press each coated fillet into panko crumb mixture , coating well
8. press more crumbs into any bare areas
9. saute fillets in hot oil until lightly browned , turn and saute other side until lightly browned and fish is opaque
10. serve with lemon wedges
target.review: This was super simple and just plain good.  I'm not a fan of tilapia normally and wanted something to dress it up.  This mustard/mayo coating did the trick.     And my toddlers had seconds!  I used breadcrumbs and dried parsley.  I threw in some dried dill, too.  The pan-frying seemed like too much trouble, so I baked mine in a 400-degree oven for 15 minutes on a foil-lined pan.  They came out perfect with no pan to wash!  We'll have this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple cinnamon overnight oatmeal

easy, easy, easy...t hat's what this is. put ingredients in crock pot the night before. upon serving, add more brown sugar to taste.

1. mix together the apples , cinnamon and brown sugar in bottom of crock pot
2. sprinkle oats over apples , then pour in water and salt
3. do not stir !
4. cook on low for 8-9 hours
demonstrations.review: This was so easy to do!  A few minutes prep the night before and we woke up to a hot breakfast.  We like ours sweeter so added more brown sugar after serving.  I halved the recipe to serve 2 adults and 2 toddlers, and I added raisins.  I'm going to be making this a lot now with different fruit.  I love being able to have hot oatmeal all ready to go on busy mornings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops with rosemary vinegar sauce

this elegant dish is simple and delicious! the sauce is to die for! this recipe came from bon appetit.

1. sprinkle pork on both sides with 3 / 4 teaspoon rosemary , salt and pepper
2. coat with flour and shake off excess
3. heat oil in heavy large skillet over medium-high heat
4. add garlic and saute until it begins to color , about 2 minutes
5. using slotted spoon , discard garlic
6. add pork to skillet and saute until brown and cooked through , about 7 minutes per side
7. using tongs , transfer pork to plate
8. tent with foil to keep warm
9. add chicken broth , white wine , whipping cream , vinegar and remaining 1 / 4 teaspoon rosemary to skillet
10. boil until sauce thickens enough to coat back of spoon , stirring often , about 10 minutes
11. season to taste with salt and pepper
12. pour any collected pork juiced from plate into skillet
13. spoon sauce over pork and serve
demonstrations.review: Delicious, different, and easy, too.  I've made it several times now, with both fresh and dried rosemary and the red wine vinegar.  I use whole milk instead of heavy cream, and of course it separates, but still tastes great and is more convenient.  This is a regular in our house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sage and rosemary pork chops

these are nicely seasoned and cooked on a contact grill or they could be done on an outside.  i serve these with potatoes, veggies and fresh baked bread.

1. heat contact grill for 5 minutes
2. wash chops and pat dry
3. in a small container , thoroughly mix the seasonings together
4. drizzle half the oil over the chops , sprinkle with half the seasoning mix
5. turn chops over and repeat with oil and remaining seasoning mix
6. place on heated grill and cook until meat thermometer inserted in center reads 160 degrees
7. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Really simple but SUPERB!  I've made these twice; once on a charcoal grill and once on the George Foreman contact grill.  They were great both times.  The second time I just poured the olive oil and herbs into the same freezer bag that I defrosted the chops in to season them.  Easier and less messy.  We had these with roasted potato chunks with fresh rosemary and a tossed salad with olives and a vinagrette to maintain the Italian theme.  Simple & fantastic dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
skillet sirloin

i think this is my husband's most requested steak supper. and it's ok with me, because it is so easy to do, and tastes super!

1. cut steak into 4 pieces
2. heat lg skillet
3. brown steaks in oil for 5 minutes a side
4. remove and keep warm
5. add onion and mushrooms
6. saute for 3 minutes
7. add remaining ingredients , bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer for 2 minutes
9. serve steak with sauce spooned over
demonstrations.review: This is so, so good.  And so easy!  I steamed some broccoli and made some microwave "baked" potatoes while I cooked the steak, and had a really impressive steak dinner on the table in 20 minutes.  Now THAT'S a lifesaver on weeknights.  The sauce really makes this special.  The only change I made was to deglaze the pan with a little red wine and substitute fresh garlic for the garlic powder and canned mushrooms for fresh.  Now that I've found this, we're going to have it often.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy wheat bran   flax meal muffins

this is a new recipe i just tried and i like it but i like wholesome muffins! it's really simple and bakes quickly. the wheat bran can be substituted with any highfiber bran cereal (as long as you grind it up in a food processor!)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix wheat bran , milk , and lemon juice together
3. let it sit while preparing the next step
4. in a separate bowl , beat the egg until fluffy
5. then beat in your sweetener of choice , honey , applesauce , ground flax , vanilla extract , baking soda , baking powder , salt , and cinnamon
6. add the wet ingredients to the bran mixture
7. stir well
8. add whole wheat flour to mixture
9. spoon the mixture into muffin cups till about 2 / 3 full
10. sprinkle the muffins with rolled oats
11. bake for about 20 minutes
12. do the toothpick trick !
demonstrations.review: These were yummy!  I used a scant 1/2 teaspoon of liquid stevia for the sweetener and apple cider vinegar for the lemon juice.  Wonderful hearty flavor.  The texture was a little coarser, but then they ARE bran, and I think bran muffins are maybe supposed to be.  I think I'll add a little canola or walnut oil next time to make them a touch lighter in texture.  But really, they're pretty darn good as is!  And they're so nutritious--they're whole grain, have Omega-3s from the flax, fat free, and nearly sugar free--you can make these all the time and feel great serving them to the family.  I plan to.  Oh, and I should mention that they were devoured by the small crowd, too: ages 4, 6, and 8.  Terrific with warm apple butter.  Thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
rosemary thyme marinade

with the end of the holiday season, i'm ready to return to more normal eating habits.  breaking out my little george foreman and looking for ways to prepare chicken, fish and vegetables.  came across this on another site and thought it would work well with poultry or zucchini or potatoes.

1. mix all ingredients together in a small bowl or resealable bag
2. the orginal recipe did not include marinating times but i would suggest at least 2 hours for chicken , preferably overnight
3. since fish tends to cook in marinades , 30 minutes should do
4. for vegetables , firmer vegetables can go longer but something like zucchini or yellow squash might be ready in 20-30 minutes
target.review:
I used this last night when making chicken...I omitted the thyme and used doubled the rosemary...I also used a little extra lemon juice and no water.  Next time I will marinade overnight!

Thanks for the great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mix   match kabobs

great for when you need something to tide you over. you can pick your favorite meat and cheese...i like turkey and cheddar.

1. skewer 1 cheese cube , 1 pickle cube , and 1 meat cube with a toothpick
2. repeat with remaining cheese , pickles and meat
3. serve with honey mustard dressing for dipping
demonstrations.review: YUM!  I used smoked ham.  I didn't have the pickles so I used a pineapple chunk instead and mixed some cream cheese with the honey mustard.  It was absolutely delicious and the kids thought it was neat to eat off of a stick!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
demonstrations.review:
Boy, how I hate to give this another 5 stars, haha!  I am pretty new at cooking and this was my very first ham.  I was a little scared because it wasn't my mothers traditional pineapple juice marinade, but I tried it anyway.  I swear, they should make a candle that smells like this ham slow baking in the oven!  It is wonderful.  I made a 7 lb. ham for our family just to piece on throughout the week...and I am on my second plate right now.  I may have overcooked mine a little, but that was just a first-timers mistake!  LOVE IT!!!!!  Oh, the only change I made...
I basted every 15 minutes and 10 before taking it out of the oven I used about 1/4 cup brown sugar and crumbled it over the top.  I put it back in the oven uncovered to get that burnt sugar taste...
AMAZING!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
7 layer bean dip

this 7 layer bean dip is great for super bowl parties, work parties, other gatherings! pretty easy to make...you can use store bought guacamole if you can't find ripe avocados.

1. mix avocados , lemon juice , salt , and pepper
2. mix mayonnaise , sour cream , and taco seasoning mix
3. layer ingredients as follows
4. bottom layer: bean dip
5. second layer: avocado mixture
6. third layer: sour cream mixture
7. fourth layer: tomatoes
8. fifth layer: onions
9. sixth layer: olives
10. seventh layer: cheese
11. top with extra sour cream / olives / salsa , etc
12. if desired
13. serve with tortilla chips
14. this seems to be a little bit better if you can chill it for a few hours or over night to let the flavors intensify
demonstrations.review: soooo good!  It took me a while longer to get it all put together becuase I had to eat all the avocado mixture that was left in the bowl!  I love the cool sour cream layer!  This is great!  I left off the olives and am garnishing with jalepenos!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
island pork tenderloin

a delicious meal that i saw on another web site; a quick meal for the entire family. i adjusted a couple of things.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. stir together salt , pepper , chili powder , cumin and cinnamon
3. coat the pork with the spice rub
4. heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a 12 inch skillet , over relatively high heat , and brown pork , turning every 30 seconds for 4 minutes
5. stir together brown sugar , garlic , and tabasco and pat onto top of the tenderloin
6. place pork in roasting pan and cook for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This was very good...family really liked it!  I actually made a pineapple stuffing to go with this...it sounded like it would go good and it did!  And the biggest perk is that I used a 3 pound tenderloin so today I made some really yummy bbq shredded pork.  The spices really made that work!  I will definitely use this again because it made two totally different but great meals!
I am so happy you reminded me to try this!

Linz

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review:
This recipe was very good.  I made a 3 lb. roast and cooked it for three hours.  I used the recipe exactly.  When the roast was finished, I boiled the gravy with a little flour to thicken and served over mashed baby red potatoes.  It was very good.  I am not used to the flavor; I would prefer a different recipe but this really was great!
Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
guy s green bean casserole

variation on guy's food network thanksgiving greenbean casserole.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. blanche green beans and add to ice bath , dry
3. butter 13x9 baking dish
4. cook bacon , remove and drain on towel
5. using leftover bacon fat , add olive oil and on medium high heat , add onions , then red peppers then mushrooms w / salt and pepper , set aside
6. for the roux:
7. over medium sauce pan , melt butter first , then add flour and vigorously stir with wooden spoon until well combined
8. add cup milk , stir to combine and bring to simmer , then add final cup milk and simmer until thickened like gravy
9. add seasonings , green beans , vegetables into roux and pour into pan
10. top with bread crumbs , bacon
11. bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes
12. add fried onions and cook for five more minutes
13. optional: replace roux with 1 can of campbell's cream of mushroom soup and 1 can milk
target.review: I have made this twice now.  Both times for Thanksgiving.  The second time I was making it I wondered why I was doing this again, since it is quite time consuming.  When I tasted it I knew it was worth the extra time.  So much better than the traditional green bean casserole using canned beans and soup.  I did make several changes. I added 1/2 tsp cayenne pepper to the vegetables.  Used panko bread crumbs, but reduced amount to 1 cup.  I also added some shredded parmesan to the bread crumbs for topping.  My family has asked that this be added to our Thanksgiving menu.  Not great for leftovers, I did not think it reheated well.  I do think it is worth the extra effort.  Very tasty dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best creole cajun seasoning mix

move over emeril!... you will never purchase creole or cajun seasoning again once you taste this one --- i have searched for the longest time to find the best seasoning blend, this is it! --- four tablespoons of seasoned salt will not be overly-salty if you prefer a more salty taste then add in some white salt --- this makes a fair amount of seasoning, just store in a tightly-sealed glass jar in the refrigerator to use in ground beef recipes, soups, or stews, homemade pasta sauce recipes, or use it to season roasts, chickens, pork, beef,  i use it on just about everything! if you like extreme spice then increase the cayenne up to 4-5 teaspoons. this makes a great gift for a spice-lover!

1. mix all ingredients in a glass jar
2. store in the refrigerator to keep the spices fresh
3. shake the jar before using
demonstrations.review: Love this seasoning mix.  Originally made it for Creamy Cajun Chicken Pasta (also delicious).  We loved it so much we use it to season all kinds of dishes.  Great on meat and veggies.  There will be a jar of this seasoning mix in our refrigerator from now on.  Thanks for another great recipe Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken avocado cheese bake

taken from taste of home magazine ---  delicious crispy breaded chicken topped off with avocados and cheese, this is a delicious recipe and worth making! :)

1. using a meat mallet , or the bottom of a small heavy saucepan , flatten the chicken breast halves to 1 / 4-inch thickness
2. in a bowl , combine the cornstarch , cumin , garlic powder , salt and pepper
3. dredge the chicken in the cornstarch mixture , then in the egg mixture , then in the cornmeal
4. heat the butter in a skillet over medium heat , and brown the chicken lightly on both sides
5. place the chicken in a shallow baking dish , and top with the avocado slices
6. top with the grated cheese
7. bake in a 350 degree oven for 15 minutes , or until the chicken is done , and the cheese has melted
8. serve with a dollop of sour cream and chopped green onions-- delicious !
demonstrations.review: Followed the recipe as written.  We were very pleased with the results.  Quick and easy to put together too.  This is really flavorful, moist chicken.  The spices and the cornmeal make for a great crust.  We did top with some sriracha sauce for heat.  Very good dinner.  Will definetly make again.  Thanks Kittencal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I have made this twice now.  Once with chicken, the next time with shrimp.  Was great both times.  Added red pepper and mushrooms.  Best recipe I have found from this site so far.  Thanks Lorac for such a wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese cinnamon crescents

these are so yummy.  would be perfect for breakfast or brunch or anytime!  i just made a batch late this evening.  a parent brought these in for a teacher's luncheon and everyone loved them.

1. roll out one can of crescent rolls in bottom of 9x13 pan
2. i sprayed pan with cooking spray
3. cream together: 2 8oz
4. cream cheese
5. 1 cup sugar
6. 1 teaspoon vanilla
7. spread this mixture over crescent rolls
8. lay second tube of crescent rolls over mixture
9. melt 1 / 2 cup butter , mix in 3 / 4 cup sugar ,
10. 1 teaspoon cinnamon , and pour over top
11. bake at 350 for 30-35 minutes
demonstrations.review: Made for Christmas morning.  What a hit with the entire family. Based on other reviews I decreased sugar in both the filling and the topping by 1/4 cup.  Used brown sugar for the topping.  This recipe is so delicious.  I'm sure we will try this again with some of the variations/additions others have posted.  Thank you Aunt Paula.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal toffee crunch cookies

from hershey's kitchen recipes... these rock!

1. heat oven 375f
2. lightly grease cookie sheet
3. beat butter , eggs , brown sugar , and vanilla in large bowl until well blended , add flour , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
4. beat until blended
5. stir in oats , toffee bits and coconut , if desired , with spoon
6. drop dough by rounded teaspoons about 2 inches apart on cookie sheet
7. bake 8-10 minutes or until edges are lightly browned
8. cool 1 minute
9. remove to wire rack
10. cool completely
demonstrations.review: Your are right Starlight, these do rock.  Great recipe.  Followed recipe exactly and they turned out fantastic.  The whole family loved these cookies.  My neice requested these for her birthday and my Mom asked for the recipe.  That is a true compliment.  Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
the best chicken tortilla soup

i'm in love with this soup!! a very good friend of mine made this for me recently and i fell in love. i'm very picky about my tortilla soup and this by far the best ever. she makes hers in the crock pot and i have to agree, that it's easy and tastes just wonderful!! whatever you do, do not skip the garnishes! they are the icing on the cake! update april 2010:  obviously i've made this so many times i never even look at the recipe anymore!  but i wanted to add some variations that i play around with that are great.  like many reviewers black beans and corn are great additions.  sometimes i add them to the leftovers (if there are any :-) so that is feels like something new the next day!  i have also made it several times with shredded pork which turns it into a pork carnitas type of soup.  if you like it on the spicy and smoke side buy a can of chipotle peppers in adobo sauce and mince up one or two and add it.  and lastly, a little swizzle of half and half or heavy cream just minutes before serving makes it a creamy tortilla soup that is wonderful and it is also a good way to tone down the heat if it got away from you...

1. throw everything except the garnishes in your crock pot and let it cook on high for 5-6 hours
2. dress with garnishes and give it a squeeze of lime and you're good to go !
3. enjoy !
4. if you are not using a crock pot , saute the garlic and onion in 2 tablespoons olive oil before adding the remaining ingredients
5. simmer for at least an hour so that the flavors mix together
target.review: I'm allergic to tomatoes, but my DH loved it. Insted of anaheim chilies and 3-4 tomatoes, I used 2 cans of rotel. I also used chipotle bouillon. This was my first time making tortilla soup and I will definately make it again with this recipe. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever pumpkin pie

southern living. always served for thanksgiving dinner.

1. combine pumpkin and remaining ingredients in a large bowl
2. beat at medium speed with an electric mixer 2 minutes
3. pour into prepared piecrust
4. bake at 425 degrees for 15 minutes
5. reduce heat to 350 degrees
6. bake 50 additional minutes or until a knife inserted in center comes out clean
7. cool on a wire rack
demonstrations.review: This was great. I made the recipe exactly as printed, but for some reason it was running over the edge of my 9 inch pie shell which made a little mess but the taste was worth it. I'm going to make another one for the holidays but maybe cut down the pumpkin and sweetened condensed milk about 1/4 cup each so it doesn't overflow. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel pull aparts

yummy breakfast or brunch addition

1. grease a bundt pan
2. cut the rolls in half and roll in each in dry pudding mix
3. arrange in pan alternately with nuts
4. be sure to stack evenly as possible
5. sprinkle remaining pudding mix over the top
6. combine the brown sugar and butter together and heat until the butter is melted and syrup is formed
7. make sure it is stirred well
8. pour the syrup over the rolls
9. cover with greased plastic wrap let rise until double in size or even with top of bundt pan
10. remove wrap and bake at 350 deg
11. f 30-35 minutes
12. cover with foil the last 15 minutes of baking
13. immediately invert onto a serving platter
demonstrations.review: I did not have a bundt pan so I used a 8x8 casserole dish. Worked fine. And instead of butter and sugar I used caramel ice cream topping. I only put nuts on half since my Hubby doesn't like them. Very yummy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
great balls of fire

this is a great way to light up a party. sausage balls with a little zip. big hit.

1. mix all ingredients thoroughly
2. roll tablespoonful of mixture into balls
3. place on cookie sheet and bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes
4. turn balls over and bake 10 minutes more or until done
demonstrations.review: OMG! I used pepper jack cheese instead of monterey because of the reviews and my mouth was on fire. Maybe I'll try again with the milder monterey cheese. I used hot sausage and jalapenos also. I normally like spicy food but this was too much for me and my DH.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious crab cakes

you may use imitation crab in place of the fresh crabmeat due to cost reasons,  i have made these using imitation and it was still wonderful --- i have listed a honey-mustard sauce on the bottom to serve with the crab cakes if desired but these are just as good served alone! --- plan ahead there is a 1 hour freezing time.

1. in a bowl combine all ingredients except the breadcrumbs and vegetable oil
2. mix until well mixed
3. form into 3-oz cakes / patties
4. roll each cake / patty into the bread crumbs
5. place the cakes in the freezer for 1 hour to set
6. remove from freezer , and saute on medium heat until each cake is golden brown and heated through
7. for the honey-mustard sauce
8. combine 1 cup mayonnaise with 1 / 2 teaspoon mustard powder , 2 tablespoons honey and pinch cayenne peper
9. mix and chill until ready to use
demonstrations.review: This was very good. I used 1 tsp red pepper flakes instead of 1/4 cup red bell pepper. And I accidently mixed the bread crumbs into the mixture but that didn't affect the outcome any. Next time I'm not going to put them in the freezer because the outside of the cake was very browned while the inside was cold and I only had them about 1/2 inch thick. Overall very good recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french onion beef au jus

this is a fabulous recipe for an open faced french onion beef au jus sandwich. this is truly a knife-and-fork sandwich. i have made this countless times, and have no idea where i got the original recipe, or why i have never posted it here. it can be made in the oven, or crockpot. i have made it both ways, depending on how much time i have, and really notice no difference. one little tip i can share, is when you are toasting your bread in the oven, slice a small sliver off the bottom (round side) of the bread to make a flatter surface, that way when you pile on the beef, onion, and cheese the sandwich won't tip over when you put it back in the oven to melt the cheese. (it keeps it from being top-heavy).

1. slice onions in 1 / 4 inch slices , lightly brown onion slices in butter
2. combine soy sauce , onion soup mix , garlic , onions , coffee , and 4 cups water
3. place roast in 4-quart casserole or dutch oven
4. add soy sauce mixture and onions
5. cover tightly and bake 2 1 / 2 hours in a 325 degree f oven or until beef is tender
6. remove roast and allow to rest 20 minutes before carving
7. keep broth hot
8. slice roast thinly across grain
9. return slices to liquid
10. slice french rolls lengthwise , butter and toast bread in 375 degree oven
11. to serve , place hot beef slices , and onions on top of bread , sprinkle with grated cheese and broil until cheese is melted
12. serve open-face with meat juices poured over each sandwich or closed with a bowl of broth like french dip sandwich
13. slow cooker directions: place onions in 4 1 / 2 to 5 1 / 2 quart slow cooker and top with beef roast
14. combine soy sauce , garlic , onion soup mix and 3 cups of water: omit butter
15. pour over roast and cook on high for 5 hours or low for 8 hours
16. finish preparation as above
demonstrations.review:
This tasted great! I didn't have any swiss cheese but I will definately get some for next time.
Instead of 4 cups of water and 1 cup of strong coffee, I just used 3 cups of regular coffee. I didn't use browning sauce and I used rolls instead of french bread. Will make again.

target.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin with balsamic cranberry sauce

nan

1. preheat oven to 450f
2. melt 1 / 2 tablespoon butter in heavy large ovenproof skillet over medium-high heat
3. sprinkle pork with salt and pepper
4. sear pork on all sides , about 2 minutes
5. place skillet with pork in oven
6. roast pork until thermometer inserted into center registers 155f , about 10 minutes
7. meanwhile , melt remaining 1 tablespoon butter in heavy medium skillet over medium-high heat
8. add onion and rosemary
9. saut until onion softens , about 3 minutes
10. add broth , cranberry sauce and vinegar and whisk until cranberry sauce melts , about 2 minutes
11. transfer pork to work surface
12. scrape any juices from large skillet into cranberry mixture
13. boil until sauce has reduced enough to coat spoon thickly , about 6 minutes
14. season with salt and pepper
15. slice pork and serve with sauce
target.review: This recipe is a family favorite.  I use it for easy entertaining as does my daughter-in-law.  Great substitute for T-day turkey for two.  Goes well with stuffing and other Thanksgiving sides.  I always double the sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braised lamb shanks with fresh rosemary

a wonderful blend of flavors- perfumes the whole house. perfect for company, since it can be made the day before. everyone raves about it! i've doubled and tripled the recipe with success. it's from a 1998 bon appetit and recipe #50881 that i've posted goes well with this--spoon some of the veggies and sauce over the polenta. wonderful !!

1. sprinkle lamb with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in heavy , large pot over medium-high heat
3. working in batches , add lamb to pot and cook until brown on all sides , about 8 minutes
4. transfer to bowl
5. remove all but about 2 tablespoons of oil from pan
6. add onions , carrots , and garlic to pot and saut till golden , about 10 minute
7. stir in all remaining ingredients
8. return lamb to pot , pressing down to submerge
9. bring liquid to boil , reduce heat to medium low , and cover
10. simmer until meat is tender , about 2 hours
11. uncover pot
12. simmer till meat is very tender , about 30 minutes
13. transfer lamb to platter
14. tent with foil
15. boil juices in pot till thickened , about 15 minutes
16. season with salt and pepper and spoon over lamb
demonstrations.review: So glad I chose this recipe for some lamb shanks that had been hanging out in the freezer long enough.  Pretty much followed directions...didn't use quite the whole bottle of wine and used a combination of fresh and dried herbs.  Toward the end of cooking, I put the lamb shanks in a low oven while I increased the heat and reduced the sauce.  Great taste!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera broccoli cheese soup

a very good broccoli cheese soup. served with crusty bread.

1. saut onion in butter
2. set aside
3. cook melted butter and flour using a whisk over medium heat for 3-5 minutes or until you see a noticeable golden brown color in your pan
4. slowly add in the chicken stock and whisk again to combine
5. simmer contents covered for 20 minutes on medium heat
6. add the broccoli , carrots and the sauteed onions , into the pot
7. stir , add the milk and half & half
8. cook covered over low heat 20-25 minutes but do not bring to a boil
9. this may cause the milk to curdle
10. add salt , pepper & nutmeg
11. continue to cook the soup on low heat and slowly add the grated cheese a handful at a time and stir to avoid clumps
12. once all the cheese has been added is melted , remove from heat , and serve immediately
13. suggestion: serve with crusty bread or in a breadbowl
14. refrigerate leftovers after they have cooled and store in a airtight container up to 5 days in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Even though I cut back by using 1% milk and 4 oz. cheese, it was a flavorful and satisfying soup. Thought it was very like Panera's even with the adjustments. If you look at the nutrition info on their website, you'll find my version comes closer.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review: This has become my go to shrimp recipe.  I dredge the shrimp lightly in flour and saute in a separate pan.  Then I add them to a pan in which I've heated the olive oil, pepper flakes and minced garlic. Then proceed as posted. Can't bear leaving the garlic behimd.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
our favorite wheat bread

this bread is the best bread i've ever eaten, hands down! i have a neighbor who always tells me when he does me a favor that this is what he wants as "payment"! really good fresh from the oven along with "aunt gin's vegetable soup" recipe #91938.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. combine butter , molasses , honey , and salt
3. mix well
4. add yeast mixture
5. gradually add flour
6. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
7. place in greased bowl and let rise until double
8. punch down
9. let dough rest a few minutes
10. shape into 2 loaves
11. place in greased bread pans
12. let rise about 1 hour
13. bake at 375 for 35-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: Have made this twice using a stand mixer.  The first time I substituted olive oil for butter and had good but slightly greasy results.  Yesterday I followed the recipe exactly and the loaves had a better texture, but not quite as tasty.  Maybe I'll use both fats on the next batch.  Very good, easy bread.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
decked out water

i admit, this is kind of a weird "recipe", but it's very attractive and different -- also refreshing.  if you have a nice clear pitcher, give it a try!

1. cut two thin lengthwise slices from cucumber , reserve remaining for another use
2. stir together cucumber slices , 12 cups water and next 5 ingredients in a pitcher , cover and chill for 1 hour
3. pour over ice in glasses before serving
4. individual glasses can be garnished with sprigs of parsley or cilantro
demonstrations.review: Love this stuff!  Cranberries haven't been available since I started making it, but will throw them in when I can.  I don't like plain water or sweet drinks...this is perfect for me. I get two days from the fruit and veggies.

target.recipe_text:
low carb low fat turkey stuffed bell peppers  italian style

i love stuffed peppers and was craving them on my low carb diet. i fooled around a bit and came up with these. i promise, they're so flavorful that you won't even miss the rice. enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. on stovetop in a medium skillet or saucepan , saut mushroom , onion , celery and garlic in olive oil until veggies are soft
3. remove from heat
4. meanwhile , in a medium mixing bowl , combine ground turkey , egg , garlic powder , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
5. add saut veggie mixture to turkey mixture
6. mix well
7. stuff peppers with turkey / veggie mix and place in an ungreased shallow casserole dish
8. in a small bowl , combine undrained tomatoes and tomato sauce
9. pour over peppers to cover
10. sprinkle with parmesan cheese and italian seasonings
11. cover with aluminum foil and bake for 50 minutes
12. uncover , sprinkle with mozzarella and bake for an additional 10 minutes or until cheese is bubbly and browned
target.review: I tried these last night.  I followed the recipe exactly, except I used low sodium tomato sauce.  I found it took longer to bake, probably because of the oven.  I will definitely make these again, but will probably omit the egg -- I thought it made the turkey filling seem tough.  I will also try them in the crockpot next time.  That is how I have always cooked stuffed peppers, and I want to try this recipe that way too.  Somehow, in my opinion, the peppers always seem to taste sweeter and are more tender in the crockpot.  Will definitely make this one again, but I may try a few of the "tweaks" I mentioned.  Good flavor!  Thanks for sharing your creation!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked italian round steak

don't know what i would do without my crockpot. savory tender beef over hot noodles. my family gave it the thumbs up.

1. trim all fat from meat
2. cut steak into 1-inch pieces put meat into a 4-quart slow cooker
3. add in carrots , celery , mushrooms , green onions , undrained tomatoes , beef broth , wine , tapioca , italian seasoning , salt , pepper , and bay leaf
4. cover and cook on low for 9-10 hours
5. season to taste with salt and pepper
6. discard bay leaf
7. serve over hot cooked noodles
demonstrations.review: Very easy to prepare with ingredients I usually have on hand.  We didn't care for this too much.  I'm thinking it could have been the bay leaf.  I've never been a real fan of it, and we typically like dishes with italian seasoning.  I'll probably try this one again in the future and leave the bay leaf out and see if that makes a difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken vindaloo

for the vegetarian version: use your favorite veggies, omit the cinnamon stick. this is my sister's recipe (thank you najla! xoxo), she made it on the stove top. it's really yummy!!

1. puree first 10 ingredients in a blender
2. pour into the crock pot , add tomato sauce , cinnamon stick and onion and mix well
3. add chicken and turn to cover
4. cook on low for 5 hours
5. sprinkle with chopped parsley before serving
6. serve with rice or rolls , enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make.  I liked it, but BF told me not to make this one again.  I would have rated it a 4, but he said 1. Because we were split on whether we liked it, that's why I'm giving it only a 3.  Normally, he's very open to new things, but he definitely did not like this recipe.  I thought it was easy to make, and I would make it again for myself.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy sloppy joes

this sloppy joe recipe is tasty, filling, and packed with veggies! it's a slightly tweaked cooking light recipe.

1. combine ketchup and next 8 ingredients , set aside
2. heat oil in dutch oven over medium-high heat
3. add mushrooms and next 7 ingredients
4. saute 5 minutes until meat is browned , stirring to crumble
5. stir in ketchup mixture
6. bring to a boil
7. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 20 minutes , stirring occasionally
8. serve on toasted hamburger buns
demonstrations.review: I tried this over the weekend.  It was very easy to make, and it smelled great while it was simmering.  The only adjustment I made was that I used 16 oz of ground turkey breast rather than 8 oz of ground turkey and 8 oz of ground round.  We liked it and will definitely make this one again.  I liked the fact that there was quite a few veggies in it -- and BF didn't even know it!  (He thinks veggies are nonsense.)  Next time I may add more hot sauce or some other seasoning for a little more spice(BF likes spicy food and this wasn't quite spicy enough for him).  We'll definitely be making this one again.  Thanks for sharing your healthy, veggie-packed recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amazing chicken tortilla soup

this recipe has been a huge hit with everyone who has ever tried it. we make it almost weekly, and the leftovers are eaten immediately. it is also very healthy! it is a little spicy, so if you don't have too much of a tolerance for spicy foods, you may choose to leave out the seeds of the jalapeño. if you love spicy, like we do, extra cayenne pepper adds even more zing. enjoy!

1. saut onion , garlic , jalapeo and green pepper with olive oil in a large pot until soft
2. add all the rest of the ingredients to the large pot and bring to a boil
3. after about 15 minutes , remove the chicken breasts and shred
4. return shredded chicken to the pot and simmer an additional 45 minutes
5. serve , topped with crushed tortilla chips if desired
demonstrations.review: Amazing, awesome, outstanding, incredibly good -- I'm not sure what else to say.  Tried this last night.  BF wasn't too sure about it but thought it smelled good.  He ate two huge bowls of it last night and took another large container to work today for his lunch.  I didn't have a regular onion, but I did have some green onions, so I used those.  Also, for the chicken broth, diced tomatoes and tomato sauce, I used the lowest sodium content I could find.  Even with these substitutions, we thought it was AWESOME!  We'll definitely be making this again and again and again -- Thanks for sharing your outstanding recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
better than chicken and dumplings

this dish is baked in a 9x13 casserole, and the dumplings sort of make themselves. it is easy and delicious.
it appeared in a local community paper some time ago.

1. combine the first 6 ingredients and bring to a boil
2. reduce heat to simmer
3. cook until chicken is done
4. remove from broth and cool
5. you will use 2 c of this broth in the preparation !
6. remove from bones if needed
7. saute the vegetables , except peas in a little butter or oil , until soft
8. melt the 1 / 4 cup butter and pour into the 9x13 dish , to grease the bottom
9. cut or tear the chicken into pieces and place on top of the melted butter
10. mix flour and milk
11. pour over chicken
12. mix soup , 2 cups of the broth , the sauteed vegetables and peas
13. pour over the top
14. do not stir !
15. bake at 400 degrees for 30-35 minute or until top is brown
16. to make this realy fast use rotisserie chicken and canned broth !
demonstrations.review: Nothing left!  My family likes chicken and dumplings, but our traditional recipe is quite a bit of work.  So when I saw this one, I had to give it a try.  When the entire pan was gone, I realized I'd hit on a winner.  (The taste and texture somewhat reminded us of a recipe my parents had tried from a Bob Evans restaurant.) The recipe didn't print out very well -- my printer was having problems -- and the first three steps didn't print at all, so I had to guess at the method in those steps.  My guessing was a little off but it worked out well.  We'll DEFINITELY have this one again!  Thanks for sharing this easy and delicious recipe!

target.recipe_text:
oven fried zucchini sticks

i love these.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. spray a cookie sheet with cooking spray
3. place bread crumbs , cheeses , garlic powder , oregano , basil , parsley in ziploc bag
4. shake well to combine
5. set aside
6. cut each zucchini lengthwise into 8 pieces
7. cut each piece in half horizontally
8. beat egg and milk in a shallow bowl
9. dip each piece of zucchini in egg mixture then bread crumb mixture
10. repeat until all of the sticks are coated
11. place them on prepared cookie sheet
12. bake for 10-15 minutes or until brown and tender
13. serve with warm spaghetti sauce or ranch dressing
target.review: Tasty (and semi-healthy) snack.  I made them with spaghetti one night as an appetizer.  They were definately not WOW for me, but they were very good and will probably make again sometime in the future.  Would probably be awesome fried...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
great aunt fannie old traditional potato soup

this is an old german recipe my great-aunt use to make. every one in the family loved it.

1. cook potatoes , onions , celery and carrots in the water until tender
2. meanwhile , in other pan melt butter and blend in flour
3. gradually add milk and cook , stirring constantly until thickened
4. add to soup
5. add evaporated milk
6. season to taste with salt and pepper
7. garnish bowls with paprika
demonstrations.review: This recipe was just ok for me.  I am used to a creamy, mashed potato type of potato soup.  This was more runny than I am used to...and I prefer sour cream and half & half...this recipe calls for evap. milk which was different.  It was good, but not great for me...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger steak with gravy

quick, easy and delicious comfort food dish. makes lots of gravy and wonderful served with garlic mashed potatoes.

1. combine all hamburger ingredients except flour
2. shape into patties and dredge in flour
3. brown patties in oil in heated skillet over medium high heat
4. remove from skillet
5. combine all gravy ingredients in a bowl , mixing well with a whisk
6. pour into skillet , stirring constantly until thickened
7. taste and adjust salt and pepper
8. can also add a little more seasoned salt
9. place patties into gravy and turn to coat
10. cover , reduce heat and simmer for 15 minutes or until done
demonstrations.review: Love...I use Beefy Onion instead of the onion.  Whip up some homeade mashed potatos, and veggies...it's amazing.  Also, I just use the other envelope in the package and make gravy as directed on box.  My husband LOVES this stuff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef mexican casserole  um gala

i grew up with my mother cooking this and loved it everytime. she got it from my aunt. and i'm not sure why it's called "um gala" but i think it's because someone after taking a bite, said, "ummmm good or maybe ummm golly this is good!" this was one of my mom's favorites to take to pot lucks and she made it for me when i would visit from college. i made it last night and my 8 year old daughter loved it and my dh couldn't stop talking about it. (if you want more meat add more meat. and if 1/2 cup of ro-tel tomatoes makes it too spicy (like for kids) then substitute some of it with regular canned diced tomatoes. or if you like it really spicy add more. also, to save time, use bagged tortilla chips.)

1. saute hamburger meat , onion and green pepper
2. drain if there is excessive grease
3. mix the soups , garlic salt , tomatoes and cheez whiz and heat in a separate pan until cheese is melted and mixture is well mixed
4. cut the tortillas into fourths
5. layer ingredients alternately in a greased casserole dish in this order: tortilla chips , meat mixture and soup mixture
6. end with the soup mixture last
7. you should have about 2 layers
8. bake at 325 degrees in pre-heated oven for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This tasted good, I only put 4 stars though simply because it was not the best Mexican Casserole I've eaten.  It tasted alot like a beef enchilada w/alot of cheese except it was in a casserole form.  It was definately nothing out of this world for me...but was good and def. edible.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
miss daisy s deviled eggs

these are the best deviled eggs i have ever tried. i usually have to double this recipe because they are gone almost as soon as i put them out.

1. cut eggs in half lengthwise , remove yolks , and reserve whites
2. mash yolks until smooth
3. combine yolks , mayo , worcestershire sauce , mustard , salt , pepper , and mix until smooth
4. stir in onion , and pickle relish
5. spoon mixture into center of egg whites
6. sprinkle tops with paprika
demonstrations.review: The absolute BEST Deviled Eggs I've ever eaten!  They are perfect!  I did not change one thing!!!  This is the recipe I will use from now on,,,received LOTS of compliments on how delicious they were!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moist poppy seed bundt cake

my cousin gave me this recipe a couple of years ago when i was getting married. i am not sure where she got it from. it is sooooo moist and delicious! no need to make an icing or glaze, sugar coating makes it just sweet enough. yum! my husband loves this cake. he eats a quarter of it at a time!!!

1. mix all ingredients together with an electric mixer , except eggs
2. mix in egg , one at a time
3. after all eggs are added , continue to mix for about another minute
4. spray bundt pan with pam , then sprinke sugar around pan
5. make sure you coat the entire pan with the sugar
6. bake at 350 for 45 minutes
7. i have made it as directed and added a package of instant lemon pudding mix to it for lemon poppy seed cake
8. it is good served with fresh fruit salad
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  This is the best stuff-we could literally eat the entire cake if calories did not exist! ha!  My husband likes to warm a slice up in the morning for breakfast!  But makes a great gift to give someone.  Tasted exactly how my mom makes it!  Thank you,,,will add this to my favorites!

target.recipe_text:
italian chicken in a skillet

pasta and chicken with an italian flavor.

1. cut chicken into bite sized pieces
2. in lg skillet , brown chicken in oil
3. add onion and peppers , cook for 5 minutes
4. add broth , tomatoes , and spices
5. cook 2 minutes
6. add pasta , reduce heat and simmer , covered , for 10 min or until pasta is done
target.review: Pretty easy to put together, but my pasta wasn't done in the time specified, (I used the shells) so I cooked longer and that seemed to dry it out. Maybe it needs more broth or tomatoes. We ate it fine, but it was just OK for us.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey   rice

my family was tired of the usual chicken & rice dish that i make so i came up with this one dish meal that's easy to throw together. they like this more than the chicken & rice.

if you like more rice you can increase it by another 1/2 cup.  you could even experiment using other vegetables i.e., frozen corn niblets, peas, green beans, etc.

1. sprinkle the seasoned salt and fennel seed over the ground turkey
2. mix well
3. spray large skillet with vegetable spray and place turkey mixture in pan
4. over medium-high heat cook and stir turkey until browned
5. drain well
6. while the turkey is draining add the vegetables to the hot pan and saute for about 5 minutes
7. add the turkey back into the pan and mix
8. sprinkle rice over mixture and pour in chicken broth
9. when broth comes to a boil reduce heat , cover and simmer for approx 20-30 minutes , stirring occasionally until liquid is absorbed
10. when the rice is cooked if there is still too much liquid in the pan remove cover , increase the heat and continue cooking until all liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at using ground turkey, so I chose my recipe carefully.  I added more rice, more like 3/4 cup (that was all I had) and added I tsp. extra chicken bullion and 1 cup water.  I was afraid of it being bland, so I added several shakes of red pepper flakes, probably too much as it was a little hot, but that was my fault.  I think the flavor would have been just great without it.  We enjoyed it a lot. Thanks!  I won't be afraid of ground turkey anymore.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ice cream cake with vanilla wafers

a friend at church made this and i had to have the recipe. this is so simple and yet so yummy! my kids request this for b-days! i hope you like it as much as we do.

1. grease 13x9 pan
2. crush vanilla wafers , mix with melted butter
3. press cookie crumbs in greased pan
4. melt chocolate chips and combine evap
5. milk and salt
6. pour over crust , freeze until firm
7. spread softened ice cream over chocolate layer , top with remaining cookie crumbs
8. freeze until firm
demonstrations.review: I had trouble with my chocolate layer firming up, it took closer to 1 hour instead of the 20 minutes stated in the recipe.  In the meantime my ice cream was softening and softening and softening.  I finally just spooned it over the slightly solid chocolate layer and froze for 7-8 hours. It was good but not quite like an ice cream cake for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chops that will make you eat til you pop

these have to be, hands down, the best meal i have ever made in a crock pot. i borrowed a friend's crock pot one weekend and made this for my honey. low and behold, i got a crock pot for my next birthday along with a request for this recipe to be the first thing i made. i really wish i know where i got the recipe from because i would love to give credit for it. i beg of you, do yourself a favor and try this. you will not regret it. let me know what you think!!

1. salt and pepper pork chops if desired
2. add all ingredients except water and cornstarch to the crock pot
3. cook on low for 5 1 / 2 hours
4. mix cornstarch and water together and stir into crock pot
5. cook 30 minutes more
6. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This was an easy meal.   The pork chops were tender, and the sauce was good, but I wouldn't say over the top.  My DH said 3 stars and I would say 3.5 for ease of preparation. I probably will make again.  Sauce was runny, maybe needs more cornstarch?

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mahi mahi

my husband and i are not big fish fans but our 5 yr old daughter loves fish so i wanted to make some. i couldn't find a recipe i liked so i made this one up. everyone has loved it whenever i have made it, even us non-fish lovers. tasted great and not fishy and really easy to make as well.

1. use a pan large enough to lay all of the filets inches
2. cover bottom with a thin layer of olive oil
3. stir in butter and cook over medium to low heat until butter is melted
4. stir in onions and shallots
5. cook until they are soft
6. using a garlic press add in the garlic cloves
7. stir in sour cream
8. mix together and cook until sour cream is melted inches
9. spread all ingredients evenly in pan and lay the filets over this
10. squeeze half of the lemon over filets and sprinkle with salt and pepper
11. let cook until that side is done , about 5 minutes
12. turn filets over , squeeze other half of lemon and sprinkle with salt and pepper
13. turn off heat and cover pan
14. leave in pan until done cooking , about another 5 - 7 minutes
15. you can leave them in pan until you are ready to serve to keep warm
16. turning off the heat before they are done cooking helps make sure that they don't get over cooked
demonstrations.review: I have made this twice now and I'm telling you it is fabulous! My favorite way to cook mahi mahi. It is so easy and I am amazed at the flavor with such simple ingredients.  I will be using this recipe from now on. Thank you so much for sharing your recipe, Estradagirl

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww chicken enchiladas

this is my variation of a real diet buster; swiss enchiladas by pierre dance. our family loved pierre's recipe so much, that when we started ww, we just had to make a low fat recipe. enjoy.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix chicken , chilies and salsa in a small bowl
3. mix the salt and cream in a large shallow dish
4. heat the oil in a frying pan over med-high heat
5. fry the tortillas one at a time for a few seconds til they start to blister and turn soft
6. immediately dip each one in the cream mixture
7. put a large dollop of the chicken mixture on each tortilla and roll it up
8. place in an ungreased baking pan
9. flap side down
10. pour remaining cream over roll enchiladas
11. sprinkle cheese over top
12. bake uncovered for 20 minutes , or till heated through
demonstrations.review: Loved the flavor of these enchiladas!  My only complaint was the sauce was too runny--like milk, but maybe it was because I had to use flour tortillas?  I will definately try this again with the fried corn tortillas.

target.recipe_text:
grand ma ma s deviled eggs  no mayo

this recipe is unique in that it doesn't have mayonnaise, if you are one that is expecting a "creamy" mayo type deviled egg, this recipe may not be for you!!  for me the melted butter gives these eggs a unique and added flavor.  
 
adapted from gooseberry patch newsletter.  

*cooking time varies based on your method of boiling eggs, so that is a broad estimate!!!

1. halve eggs and arrange egg whites on a serving platter
2. in a bowl , mash yolks well with a fork
3. add remaining ingredients except paprika
4. mix well
5. spoon mixture into a plastic zipping bag and squeeze down into the corner of the bag
6. snip off the corner and pipe mixture into whites
7. sprinkle with paprika
target.review: These were delicious!  I've been craving something creamy and we don't have any mayo in the house, so I whipped these up.  They hit the spot!  This will also be a great substitute for taking deviled eggs out to picnics - no need to worry about the mayo going bad.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese almond coffee cake

an adopted recipe, i have made this ahead when having company over for and easy breakfast.  original intro: a great moist coffee cake.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. spray a 9 x 13 cake pan
3. cream butter , sugar and cream cheese very well until smooth
4. add eggs , one at a time , scraping down as needed add vanilla and mix inches
5. sift together dry ingredients and add alternately with milk
6. stir in cherries
7. spread into cake pan , smooth top mix topping ingredients together
8. sprinkle almonds then topping over batter
9. press lightly
10. bake until tests done
demonstrations.review: Excellent coffee cake!  I am usually not a huge fan of coffee cake, but this was wonderful.  I didn't have almond extract, and so omitted it, as well as dried fruit; and I also used salted butter, but it turned out wonderful.  I also took the advice of others and doubled the topping.  So moist and fluffy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seared rainbow chard with leeks

epicurious. i love greens!

1. cut stems from chard , then cut stems crosswise into 1 / 4-inch-thick slices
2. stack chard leaves and roll into cylinders
3. cut cylinders crosswise to make 1-inch-thick strips of leaves
4. heat butter and oil in a 12-inch heavy skillet over moderately high heat until foam subsides , then saut chard stems and leeks with sea salt and pepper to taste , stirring occasionally , until slightly soft , 3 to 5 minutes
5. add chard leaves and continue to saut , stirring frequently , until wilted
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  I have rainbow chard and beet greens growing in my garden.  I picked them fresh and served this recipe for dinner.  Followed exactly as printed, only adding some fresh grated black pepper.  Delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sloppy lentils

a vegetarian version of sloppy joes

1. heal the oil in a skillet over medium heat
2. add in the onion and bell pepper
3. cover , and cook about 5 minutes , until softened
4. add in chili powder , stirring to coat
5. transfer mixture to a slow cooker
6. add in the lentils , tomatoes , water , tamari , mustard , brown sugar , salt , and pepper
7. stir to combine
8. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
9. serve sloppy-joe style on warmed buns
demonstrations.review: This was very good!  I made only a few changes - I added a little bit of liquid smoke, cider vinegar and blackstrap molasses to the mix.  I also substituted agave nectar for the sugar. The only thing I would do differently is add another can of tomatoes, but we like our sloppy joes tomato-y to begin with.  We'll definitely be making this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cottage cheese roast  vegetarian meatloaf

great vegetarian comfort food! don't be fooled by the ingredients; the flavor is very much like meatloaf. kitchen alchemy at its finest!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a loaf pan
3. in a large bowl , combine cottage cheese , eggs , vegetable oil , soup mix , walnuts , cereal and onion
4. spoon into prepared pan
5. bake for 60 to 70 minutes
6. let the 'roast' rest for 5 to 10 minutes
7. turn out onto serving platter
demonstrations.review: I didn't have onion soup mix, so I added a few of my own seasonings - salt, dried peppers, garlic powder, seaweed flakes, and some dry mustard.  I also topped the loaf with marinara sauce, drained the cottage cheese as was suggested, and omitted the oil.  It turned out fantastic!  I can't believe there was no meat in there whatsoever!  And my husband, the picky one, told me this was a keeper.  Fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the woodward veggie burger

this is from paul newman's cookbook, and was named after joanne woodward. lovely, healthy, delicious! prep time does not include cooking rice.

1. in a frying pan , saute onions and garlic in the olive oil
2. when onions are translucent , add the basil and mix well
3. add the mixture to the cooked rice
4. lightly toast nuts in frying pan and allow to cool
5. in a blender or food processor , grind all the nuts and sunflower seeds until coarsely ground
6. add to the rice mixture with the tamari sauce and tahini
7. shape into patties
8. to cook , brown in a nonstick pan on medium heat in olive oil
9. veggyburgers should be served in pita bread or burger buns with your favorite accompianments
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was excellent!  I'll definitely be making this again,and often.  Followed the recipe as stated, only adding some liquid smoke.  Instead of making burgers, I put it all into a baking dish and sprinkled the top with bread crumbs and a little bit of grated Parmesan cheese, and cooked for about 10 minutes at 350.  Fabulous, and so healthy for you, too. Thank you so much for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
thunderbird roast

omg this is the best roast i have ever made in a crockpot! the apple juice makes this gravy divine! 

1. crockpot instructions: place chuck roast , onion soup mix , brown gravy mix , and apple juice into a crockpot and cook on low for 5 to 8 hours
2. oven instructions: mix together the apple juice , onion soup mix , and brown gravy mix in a casserole dish
3. add chuck roast , and cook covered for 2 1 / 2 to 3 hours in a 325 degree oven
target.review: This is my kind of recipe! Set it and forget it!  At the end I took out the roast beef and mixed about 2 tablespoons of cornstarch with about 1/4 cup of gravy and poured it back in to thicken it a little.  Thanks for the keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy shepherd s pie

got this off of rachael ray's 30 minute meals. it pretty much follows her recipe. quick and excellent! the more gravy you make, the thinner your pie will be -- but we liked a lot extra gravy for the potatoes!

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. peel and dice potatoes and cook in boiling salted water until tender
3. in a large skillet , brown beef , onions and garlic
4. drain fat if necessary
5. add carrots , salt and pepper
6. in small pan whisk butter and flour together to make a roux
7. add beef broth and cook until thickened
8. add the gravy to the beef mixture
9. transfer to a greased casserole dish
10. when potatoes are tender , drain and mash with butter , sour cream , milk , salt and pepper
11. spread potatoes on top of beef mixture and bake until potatoes are golden on top , 15-20 minutes
demonstrations.review: My hubby loved it...I thought it was good but would probably have given it 4 stars.  Thanks for "modifying" Rachel's recipe.  I looked her's up and sort of took a little from each of you.  I added peas and a little worcester sauce.  Great tip on the canned carrots.  There is no way this meal could be made in 30 minutes!  I saw the episode where she made this and was planning on making it.  It took me more like 40 minutes before I put it in the oven.  I don't know how she does it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ruth s chris steak house creamed spinach

love their steaks, and i love their version of this classic side dish to a thick, juicy steak. sometimes i cheat and use 2 10 ounce packages of frozen, chopped spinach which i thaw and drain.

1. melt 4 tablespoons butter in heavy medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add flour and stir until light golden , about 7 minutes
3. stir in onion , bay leaf and clove
4. gradually whisk in milk
5. whisk until mixture boils and thickens , about 10 minutes
6. reduce heat to low and simmer 5 minutes longer , whisking frequently
7. remove bay leaf and whole clove
8. cook spinach in large pot of boiling water just until wilted and tender , about 2 minutes
9. drain
10. transfer spinach to bowl filled with ice water to cool
11. drain well
12. roll up spinach in kitchen towl and squeeze out as much liquid as possible
13. transfer spinach to processor and finely chop
14. add spinach to warm sauce , simmer over low heat until spinach is heated through , stirring often , about 5 minutes
15. stir in remaining 2 tablespoons of butter
16. season to taste with salt and pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: Ohhh this is so good.  I can'timagine using another recipe for creamed spinach again.  I used the 10 oz packs of frozen chopped spinach and it came out great.  Even used lower fat milk and I don't think you could tell the difference....if you like creamed spinach...this is the recipe for you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange cinnamon chicken

a wonderful chicken dish for the crockpot, and the smell is absolutely heavenly!

1. heat butter in a large skillet , and brown chicken
2. remove chicken to the crockpot as they brown
3. combine all other ingredients , except flour , in skillet
4. mix well and pour over chicken
5. cover pot , turn on low and cook 4-6 hours , or until chicken is tender
6. remove one cup of sauce from pot and combine with flour , mixing well
7. return flour mixture to the pot
8. turn pot on high and cook and additional 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was excellent.  I used boneless skinless chicken breasts cut in thirds.  I also had a sweet potato in the house so cut that up and tossed that in as well.  It made an excellent sauce which I served with rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy spinach and beef casserole

finally, a way to get even your pickiest eaters to eat their spinach! this is a filling and quick casserole that can easily be made low fat if you use ground turkey and low-fat cheese. serve with a green salad and some french bread and dinner is served!

1. in a large wok or frying pan heat oil and cook onion and garlic in a small amount of oil until transparent
2. add spinach and cook until wilted
3. set aside
4. brown ground beef and season with garlic salt , salt and pepper to taste
5. set aside
6. combine cooked pasta , spinach , ground beef , cheese and soup
7. add salt and pepper to taste
8. place in a large baking dish , cover in a layer of shredded cheese
9. cover with tin foil and place in a 350f oven for 30 minutes
10. uncover and place back in oven for another 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I really had my doubts but had to try it after reading all the reviews.  I used 8oz of pasta/low fat cream of mushroom, 2 C's lowfat chedder.  I think I might try green beans instead of spinach next time.  My test was asking my husband if he would eat it again...and he said yes.  We both kept going back for more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barb s gumbo

this is my recipe for gumbo. i have made it with shrimp or chicken. we like it either way. you can make it as spicy as you like . we do not care for it to spicy or hot.

1. add oil to skillet , heat over medium heat add the flour , to make a roux
2. this may take about 15 minutes
3. stir in onion , celery , bell pepper , garlic , and black pepper
4. cook over medium heat about 3 minutes or till vegetables are crisp tender
5. gradually stir in chicken broth , tomatoes , salt , worcestershire sauce , pepper sauce , corn , okra , basil , thyme , cumin and bay leaf
6. bring to boiling point
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer for 20 to 30 minutes
9. add shrimp during the last 5 minutes
10. serve over rice
11. this can also be made with chicken , if using chicken
12. use chicken breast cut in chunks add during the last 20 to 30 minute cooking time
13. smoked sausage is also good added with the chicken
14. i have added a can of crabmeat to the shrimp version
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I'm going to do what I hate most about reviews. Say how much I love it and then how much I changed It.  I didn't change much.  I wanted to make a bigger quantity so I did half cup ea oil and flour and 4 cups chicken stock.  I left out thyme and basil.   Added thinly sliced turkey sausage (kind that looks like andouille) when adding veggies (no green peppers).  Later added some cooked cut up chicken breast and before serving added shrimp and cooked <br/>another 20 - 30 min.  It was soo good..   Will make again.

target.recipe_text:
home style mexican rice

i've tried a lot of mexican rice recipes over the years, and this is my current favorite.  this can also be made into a gift mix.

1. combine water , bouillon granules , onions and all spices in a 2 quart pot
2. bring to a boil and add rice
3. reduce heat to low , cover and cook until rice is tender and water is absorbed , about 20-25 minutes
4. remove from heat , stir in cilantro and serve
target.review: I liked this, but had a few problems. I used twice as much of each spice but still thought it was a little bland and needed more flavor, However, I didn't have any dried onions on hand and used onion powder, so that may make a difference next time. I also used chicken broth instead of water and bouillon; this too might have created less flavor than the recipe as written. My rice never soaked up all the liquid, but was a good texture at the end of the recommended cooking time. Next time I will follow the recipe as written and see if I get more flavorful results. I specifically picked this recipe because it was just flavored rice - no chunky tomatoes or any other veggies (very picky husband with texture issues), and will use it again until I get it right for my family's taste buds. Thanks so much for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best banana bread

this is one of the recipes i am known for. super moist and super yummy. i have tried many over the years and always come back to this. i often give it as a gift around the holidays. just may be the last banana bread recipe you ever try! can also make 3 mini-loaves

1. cream butter and sugar
2. mash bananas and add by hand to creamed mixture
3. by hand add eggs , vanilla , baking soda , flour and salt
4. gently stir in buttermilk and chocolate chips
5. pour into a greased loaf pan
6. bake at 350f for 1 1 / 4 hour or until it tests done with a toothpick
7. i find that coarsely mashing bananas is best and make sure they are over ripe for best flavor
8. i also find that doing the majority of the mixing by hand makes for better texture in the end
9. even though the recipe says it makes 1 loaf , i usually use 2 loaf pans or 3 mini loaf pans because it seems to yield a moister bread
10. just adjust baking time down
11. if you do not have buttermilk you can put 1 teaspoons vinegar into a 1 / 2 cup measuring cup and fill to top with milk
12. let rest 5 minutes before adding to recipe
13. this freezes well
demonstrations.review: I made muffins using this recipe and enjoyed them very much. I had three large bananas that were definitely black and ready for bread-making. I cut back to 1/2 cup butter, 1 cup sugar, and used half unbleached flour and half whole wheat flour. I had to use sour milk because I didn't have any buttermilk on hand - I look forward to making this again with buttermilk. I did not use chocolate chips, I added chopped walnuts to mine. The result was an excellent moist and soft muffin with nice banana flavor that goes very well with my coffee addiction. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coca cola pork roast

there are lots of cola/meat recipes on this site, this one is a little different. i found this in a crockpot cookbook that my folks gave me for christmas. i tweaked it a bit, but still--great stuff!

1. rub the roast with salt and pepper then place it in the crockpot
2. add soup mix and coke
3. cook on low 8 hours or high for 4
4. before serving dump liquid from crockpot into a pot
5. skim fat
6. to the remaining juices add salt and pepper to taste and a dash of kitchen bouquet
7. bring mixture to a boil
8. remove a cup of the liquid and add corn starch to thicken
9. add corn starch mixture to the rest of the juices
10. cook until it reaches desired consistency
11. wonderful gravy !
demonstrations.review: I have made this several times and I'm amazed that every time it comes out so well since it's so simple. DH is not crazy about the gravy but he is not much of a gravy fan in general. My daughter and I liket he gravy, and I served this once when my parents came to dinner and they enjoyed both the roast and the gravy as well. Often I will take the leftover meat (we're a family of 3, so a 3lb roast will feed us 2-3 meals with leftovers), shred it, and mix it with my favorite BBQ sauce (Jack Daniels Honey Smokehouse) for some really lip-smacking sandwiches. It just doesn't get easier and tastier than this! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mary poppins  no bake cookies

as mary poppins would say, these are practically perfect in every way!! they have more chocolate and less sugar/butter than most no-bake cookies. brown sugar adds depth of flavor, while extra vanilla and a pinch of salt liven it up. besides, they are quick and easy, and everyone loves them! i think you could reduce the sugar even more, but they're great as written. try them with extra dark (dutch process) cocoa powder...mmmm.

1. combine all ingredients but quick oats in large saucepan
2. melt and bring to boil , and let boil for 1-2 minutes
3. add oats and stir to combine
4. drop onto sprayed or lined cookie sheets , and let cool
5. keep refrigerated in an air-tight container
demonstrations.review: I give this 5 stars because it's very easy, delicious and  flexible - even though I didn't quite have the ingredients needed on hand, this cookie turned out excellent! I used regular peanut butter because I didn't have natural, and I only had about 3/4 cup of dark brown sugar, so I used that and about 1/2 cup of white sugar to compensate. I had dutch cocoa, but was slightly short of the 1/3 cup needed. My cookies were still very chocolate-y. I also added 1 tbsp of brewed coffee to help emphasize the chocolate flavor. Because I cut back on the overall sugar, they were definitely not as sweet as the usual no bake cookie, but that was my plan (I think regular no bake cookies are waaaay too sweet). My result was a moderately sweet, very deep chocolate no bake cookie. I will definitely be using this recipe again. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
