demonstrations.recipe_text:
amish macaroni salad

i really love amish macaroni salad, and this is my favorite recipe for it. amish macaroni salad is somewhat on the sweet side, so if you don't mind your salads sweet, i think you'll like it too. it's even better the next day, so if you can, let it sit overnight. i got the recipe from a berk's county website a while back. note: it does make a lot of salad, so if you wanted a smaller amount, it halves easily. just use the 3 eggs chopped up and just garnish with paprika. time does not including cooking the macaroni.

1. cook macaroni as directed on package
2. drain& cool
3. in a bowl , whisk together the dressing ingredients so they are well-combined and smooth
4. in a large bowl , gently combine the macaroni , celery , carrots , onions , and remaining eggs
5. fold the dressing gently into the macaroni salad mixture
6. place into your serving bowl and garnish with the reserved slice egg and paprika
7. let sit overnight for the best results
demonstrations.review: I wish I could give this more stars but perhaps it was the Miracle Whip that didn't give me the wow factor. I will try this again with Hellmann's mayonnaise and less onions since most of the family members didn't like them in the salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salad with pudding

i get compliments on this fruit salad wherever i take it. it is super easy to make and a great dish to bring to a potluck or family party. kids love it too. everyone asks "what's in the sauce"? the secret ingredient is the vanilla pudding mix.

1. in a large bowl , combine peaches , pineapples , and vanilla pudding mix
2. this includes the juices from the cans
3. mix well until pudding is dissolved
4. stir in strawberries , banana , blueberries , grapes , and sugar if desired
5. chill
demonstrations.review: absolutely incredible!!! I didn't have vanilla pudding mix so used instant banana cream pudding mix and it was wonderful. I made one batch and next time will have to double batch it since there was none leftover!!! I fed my one year old nephew some out of a cup and he kept wanting to drink the juices after taking a small bite of the fruit!!! This is a definite keeper and has received high reviews on magicalholidayhome.com as I used it as part of our summer test it taste it rate it recipes!!! Thank you again for sharing this wonderful recipe with us!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy blue cheese hamburgers burgers

if you are a lover of blue cheese then you will love these burgers! they are at their best when cooked on the grill --- yield is only estimated depending on the size of your burgers you should get 6 good size burgers -- you may add in about 3 tablespoon finely grated raw potato for even more juiciness but no more than 3 tablespoons ---plan ahead the patties must be refrigerated for 24 hours to develop the flavors --- also see my recipe#208583

1. mix all the ingredients together
2. shape into 6 balls
3. cover and refrigerate for up to 24 hours to blend the flavors
4. grill or cook as desired until cooked through
5. serve with your favorite condiments
demonstrations.review: This is another great recipe Kittencal. There was too much blue cheese for my liking (which is surprising) but other wise the family members who ate them enjoyed them!!! Thanks again for sharing this recipe!!

target.recipe_text:
low fat double chocolate chip cookies

these came from a pillsbury healthy baking cookbook.  they make a small batch, so double if you're serving them to more than a couple of people.  also, the dough can get a little dry near the end sometimes.  adding a little bit of milk or chocolate liqueur will help loosen it up nicely.

1. heat oven to 375
2. in large bowl , combine brown sugar and margarine until light and fluffy
3. add vanilla and egg white
4. blend well
5. add dry ingredients
6. mix well
7. mix in chips
8. drop by teaspoonfuls 2-inches apart onto ungreased cookie sheets
9. bake for 8-9 minutes
10. cool 1 minute before removing from cookie sheet
target.review: I just had to review these again. I made these a 2nd time today and they were so good. I ended up using 6 tbsp cocoa instead of 3. Made them so chocolatey. Also used low fat spread to reduce the fat content a bit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna cheese pie

this is from more lean and luscious.  leftovers of this pie freeze nicely and can be reheated in a toater oven or microwave for a quick, delicious lunch.  we love it so much we make two and freeze one.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. arrange flaked tuna evenly in a 9 inch pie pan that has been sprayed with a nonstick cooking spray
3. in a blender , combine half of the parmesan with remaining ingredients
4. blend until smooth
5. pour mixture over tuna
6. top with remaining parmesan
7. bake , uncovered , 30 minutes , until set and lightly browned
8. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was yummy! I used 1 chicken stock cube instead of the bouillon powder because I didn't have any. I think next time I make it I will mix the tuna into the cheese mixture, just to make it more like a quiche. I only cut it into 4 serves. It also took about 15 minutes longer to cook but that is probably my oven!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real homemade soft pretzels

these are just like the ones you get at the fair! most recipes leave out the very important step of boiling before baking. you must do this to achieve the right results. *prep time includes rising time.

1. in large bowl , stir yeast , sugar and warm water
2. let rest til yeast is dissolved and is a little foamy
3. stir in 1 cup flour
4. then rest of flour mixed with the 1 tbl salt
5. knead on lightly floured surface til smooth
6. place in oiled bowl , rolling around til all oiled
7. cover and let rise till doubled in size
8. remove and knead again just a little bit , gently
9. cut into 16 pcs
10. , roll each pc
11. into 14" ropes , shape into pretzels and place on greased cookie sheet
12. cover and let rise 15 minutes
13. drop each , one or 2 at a time into a small pot of boiling water , boiling each 1 minute , and replace back onto greased cookie sheet
14. brush each with eggwash , sprinkle with coarse salt
15. bake in preheated 450 oven for 12-15 minutes ! this is the best recipe to make real soft pretzels !
demonstrations.review: Very good! This was my first attempt at making a yeast recipe and I was so proud of myself when they worked! Not quite as good as the ones you buy at the mall but close. I will now attempt to make bagels! I added poppy seeds on top. I should have taken a photo as they looked so pretty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lower fat cinnamon swirl quick bread

this is an easy and delicious cinnamon swirl bread. my family loves it...it's hard to keep on the shelf for long!   this is lower fat because my recipe substitutes applesauce for most of the oil, but you cannot tell..it makes it better i think.  we also don't make the glaze all the time- and love the bread even without it!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine 1 / 2 cup sugar and cinnamon
3. set aside
4. combine flour , baking soda , salt , and remaining 1 cup of sugar
5. in a separate bowl , combine buttermilk , egg , applesauce , and oil
6. stir into dry ingredients just until combined
7. grease the bottom only of a 9-in
8. x 5-in
9. x 3-in
10. loaf pan
11. pour half of the batter into pan
12. sprinkle with half of the cinnamon-sugar mix
13. carefully spread with remaining batter and sprinkle with remaining cinnamon-sugar
14. swirl knife through batter
15. bake at 350 for 45-50 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near the center comes out clean
16. cool in pan 10 minutes before removing to a wire rack to cool completely
17. if desired , combine glaze ingredients
18. drizzle over bread
demonstrations.review: This was okay for a low fat bread but I somehow forgot the applesauce when making it. I didn't use a large enough loaf pan and the mixture went all over the oven!!! Will try again and post review with results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no fat cinnamon apple squares

from the web, don't remember the site, fantastic and 3.5 ww points per serving

1. preheat oven to 350 lightly grease a 9 x 13 pan and set aside
2. beat egg whites 30 seconds with electric mixer
3. add next four ingredients and beat 1 more minute
4. stir in applesauce and fold apples into batter
5. combine remaining dry ingredients in a separate bowl and add to batter
6. spoon mixture into prepared pan and bake 50-60 minutes or until center springs back when gently pressed
demonstrations.review: This is our favourite dessert! Yummy served hot with cream. Better that apple pie and no fat! Does take longer than stated to cook, usually the whole hour, or it is mushy in the middle. Only serves 8 for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick soft breadsticks

our family likes these breadsticks because they are soft and chewy. i like to make them when i am in a hurry because they rise quickly.

1. make dough using your favorite method- bread machine , mixer or by hand
2. roll out into a 10x12 inch rectangle
3. cut into strips about 3 / 4 inch wide
4. give each strip a twist and place on a greased cookie sheet
5. let rise for at least 20 minutes or more if you have time
6. bake at 375 for 10-15 minutes
7. brush with butter and sprinkle with garlic salt and parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: These were great! I halved the reciped and got 8 breadsticks. Instead of rolling out the dough and cutting it up I just cut it into 8 pieces and rolled them with my hands into sausage shapes. I let them rise for about 30 mins in the oven on low with the door open(it is too cold here at the moment) I rolled them in cornmeal and sprinkled poppy seeds on top. Can't wait to try them with cinnamon sugar next time!

target.recipe_text:
rosanne s chicken spaetzle soup

there's nothing like homemade chicken soup! great comfort food.

1. in a large kettle , combine 1 cup water , water off of chicken , onion , celery and carrots
2. bring to a soft boil and cook until carrots are tender
3. add chicken , salt , pepper and broth
4. simmer on low
5. start making spaetzle
6. in a separate saucepan combine 4 cups water
7. bring to a boil
8. in a mixing bowl combine eggs , flour , 1 / 2 cup water salt and baking powder
9. beat well
10. drop small teaspoons of batter into boiling water , cook until spaetzle floats on top of water
11. scoop spaetzle out with a slotted spoon and add to soup
12. simmer soup on low for 30 minutes to flavor through
13. enjoy !
target.review: So yummy!  I considered making noodles from scratch, but I was raised German...and spaetzle is easier and tastier!  I made this as my very first attempt at soup last year and I'm making it again this year.  This recipe also segued into making a years worth of chicken stock.  Never going back to store-bought again!  Thanks for the terrific recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey stuffed yellow   red bell peppers

really good-a lighter version of the beef stuffed ones.

1. preheat to 375
2. cut peppers lengthwise and seed
3. place cut side up on a baking sheet-you can lightly steam them if you want to
4. heat oil in skillet over medium high
5. add onion and garlic and saut for 5 minutes
6. stir a few times
7. add meat , stirring often for 5 minutes
8. add tomatoes and rice and cook for 5 more minutes
9. remove from heat , add herbs and salt and pepper , stir in cheddar
10. fill peppers
11. combine breadcrumbs , parmesan and toss with melted butter-mix well
12. top peppers and bake for 30-40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was really tasty!!  I don't like ground meat, so I made them vegetarian, with some green onion (I should have used peas too) and some fresh cherry tomatoes.  I also added scrambled 2 eggs in with the rice and cooked the rice in homemade chicken stock.  My dad LOVES stuffed peppers, so when the parents come to visit, this will be on the menu.  I may try these with shredded chicken or turkey next time.  Thanks for the yummy recipe!!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
total delight

this pretty, refreshing drink is so good, you won't believe it. you can always add a shot of your favourite  vodka to it.  personally i love it mixed with ginger wine or sparkling wine.

1. peel and core the pears
2. put the prepared pears , raspberries , blackberries , pear juice , honey and candied ginger into a blender and process until smooth
3. pour the berry mixture nto a chilled glass and garnish with a lime slice , sit back , take off your shoes and enjoy
demonstrations.review: We had some really good high-end pears to use up and made this drink for Christmas with friends...it was an incredibly fun day...this drink was really tasty and added to the festive feeling.  Couldn't find candied ginger, so used some dry spice and added banana's to one batch...and yes, we added vodka...lots of it!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven roast beef

this roast can be made in a kitchen oven or at an outdoor camp site in a dutch oven. the recipe will make a very tender roast with its own gravy. leftovers may be kept in the gravy for several days.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees fahrenheit
2. rub the dry soup mix on the meat , place in a covered roasting pan
3. add mushroom soup and water or beer
4. bake covered for 1 hour per pound of meat
5. if the cut of meat is very dense with little fat , remove one half hour before reaching total cooking time , slice and return to finish
demonstrations.review: It had been YEARS since I'd had a oven-baked roast.  I have always made mine in the crockpot.  IT WAS DELICIOUS...absolutely delectable.  It also reaffirms my believe that cooking with alcohol makes everything better!  I made a small 2 lbs roast and threw in some whole red potatoes and onions I needed to use.  Next time, I will throw those in the oven a little early.  They were a little underdone for me and I the roast was just perfect, so I wouldn't want it cooked any longer.  Thanks for the great recipe!  I do the onion soup and a coke in the crockpot all the time, but I'll have to switch to beer!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and chip casserole

this recipe was passed to me by a friend.  it is simple to make and taste wonderful. it is just as wonderful right out of the oven or as a leftover.
my family all love it.


1. melt butter over medium heat , add chicken and onions
2. cook chicken until it is just cooked through
3. set aside
4. in bowl mix , add undiluted cream of chicken soup , broth , and rotel
5. in oven casserole dish crush 1 / 2 bag of chips , layer on bottom of dish
6. layer half of chicken and onions over chips
7. pour half of soup mixture over chicken
8. layer 2 cups of shredded cheese over chicken
9. repeat last 4 steps
10. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great and so easy and great for leftovers!  Because I didn't have tomatoes (and don't really like them anyhow) I used a drained can of corn.  I also added some leeks I needed to use in with the onion and chicken. We didn't have chips, but some tortillas we really needed to use up, so I cut those in strips and used those instead...turned out very yummy and very fast!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shredded beef for tacos or burritos

we love tacos around here, so this is a favorite.  i have used the meat to make burritos and enchiladas too.  this recipe also works well with pork.  the house smells so good when it is cooking!  leftovers freeze great too.

1. place onion in slow cooker and top with beef roast
2. in a small bowl , whisk together remaining ingredients and pour over beef roast
3. cook on low for about 8 hours
4. remove roast from slow cooker , reserving juice
5. use 2 forks to shred meat
6. mix in enough of the reserved juice until it is the desired consistency
7. use as filling to tacos , burritos , enchiladas , quesadillas , or nachos
demonstrations.review: My boyfriend is a HUGE fan of Mexican food, which I'd never really cooked before, but wanted to make for his birthday.  I made this for his family and our friends and it was a HIT!  By far a favorite over the shredded chicken.    I don't like a lot of spice and I was afraid a whole jalapeno would be too much, but it added just a hint of spice.  Very delicious and easy recipe.

target.recipe_text:
chicken legs grilled

generously seasoned crisp legs.
be sure to visit the grilling forum http://www.recipezaar.com/bb/viewforum.zsp?f=42 for any help!

1. mix all marinade ingredients in a zip lock bag add chicken
2. chill and marinade for 4 hours
3. grill chicken on a well oiled grill until well browned on all sides , turning once , 30 to 40 minutes
4. fyi
5. all grills are different temperatures
6. take advantage of indirect heat --
7. if the chicken browns quickly finish over indirect heat
8. all grills have hot spots so watch and be sure to move the chicken to spots on the grill so not to burn and completely cook the chicken
9. as the time of the year makes grilling quicker or slower
10. so take care and watch and enjoy you food as it grills
11. be sure to visit the grilling forum for any help !
target.review: A winner! Although I might have left the chicken on a bit longer (30 minutes on indirect heat), it still came out tasting and looking great. Based on comments made by reviewers, I made a few substitutions (honey for sugar, onion salt for seasoning salt, garlic for garlic powder) and additions (a bit of sesame oil and chili flakes). I also chilled the chicken in the marinade for 8 hours. Thanks Rita.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
decked out burgers

this is an easy way to make ordinary burger taste exceptionally good.

1. in a bowl , combine the cheese , mushrooms , mayo , and bacon
2. cover and refrigerate
3. in another bowl , combine onion , salt , peppers garlic powder and pepper sauce
4. add ground beef and mix well
5. shape into 6 thick patties
6. grill , covered over medium-hot heat for 4-5 minutes on each side
7. spoon cheese mixture on top of each burger
8. grill until cheese begins to melt
9. serve on warm hamburger buns with lettuce and tomato if desired
demonstrations.review: Wow! Hamburgers do not get much better than this. I used fresh mushrooms, as well as garlic salt instead of powder. But most of all, I complemented this tasty offering with Marie's Homemade Hamburger Buns (recipe #80413). A match made in burger heaven!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
demonstrations.review: Wow! This was a beautiful dish. Apart from cutting down on the butter a bit and using Panko instead of bread crumbs, I did not change a thing. We eat salmon once a week, so I'm always looking for new recipes. This just went to the top of the list. Thank you for that Tiger Jo.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal bread  bread machine bread maker

i love this recipe.  the oats give it a really good taste, and i use wheat flour for some wheat taste.  if you don't enjoy wheat flour, you can use all white flour and it is still delicious.  i use my bread maker to make the dough, then form it into a loaf.  you don't have to use a bread machine, i've done it by hand; the machine just makes it quicker with kids in the kitchen under my feet.
preparation time includes the bread machine dough cycle, mine is about one hour.

1. put ingredient in bread maker in the order listed above
2. set to dough cycle
3. check to see if a good ball is forming
4. if needed add a teaspoon of water or flour at a time to get a good dough ball
5. at the end of the dough cycle , form a loaf and put in lightly sprayed bread pan
6. cover , and let raise for about 45 minutes to an hour
7. bake at 350 for 45-50 minutes , depending on your oven
8. after removing from oven , lightly spread melted butter on the top crust with pastry brush
demonstrations.review: One of the best breads I've ever made in a bread machine. I followed the recipe, except that I used two teaspoons of bread machine yeast, and I only cooked the bread for 30 minutes in the oven at 350. It came out perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon baked cod

great baked cod recipe.

1. if fish fillets are large , cut into serving pieces
2. mix butter and lemon juice
3. in another bowl , mix flour , salt and white pepper
4. dip fish into butter mixture
5. coat fish with flour mixture
6. place fish in ungreased square baking dish , 8x8x2 inches
7. pour remaining butter mixture over fish
8. sprinkle with paprika
9. cook uncovered in 350 degree oven until fish flakes easily with fork , 25-30 minutes
10. garnish with parsley sprigs and lemon slices if desired
demonstrations.review: What a treat! I made a few adjustments based on the comments I read: bread crumbs instead of flour, half the butter, and slivered almonds on top. It came out perfect after 25 minutes. I might cut the butter a bit more next time and replace it with a bit of olive oil. But bottom line, this is a keeper. Thank you so much for this wonderful recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Thank you so much for this Marie. As I was preparing to try out Just Cher's Decked-Out Burgers for the first time (I encourage everyone to try them also), I decided to go all the way with your homemade buns. Eureka! Used AP flour, and substituted one cup of whole wheat for one of white. They came out perfectly.

target.recipe_text:
basic machine french bread

this is my winner with tammiev and our friends. this recipe is for a 2 pound loaf and has never failed me. i think it is the lack of oil and sugar that they like in this one.

1. add to the bread pan in the order yours needs
2. for mine it is water first
3. then i add half the flour and the salt followed by the rest of the flour and the yeast on top
4. this will run well on the normal , rapid , and delay start cycles
target.review: I can't believe I haven't rated this yet!  I've been making it for years and it's the best.  Especially since every other bread I try to make never turns out.  The first time I made it my husband didn't believe I made it myself.  I believe his exact words were, "Yeah, right!"  I follow the recommendations of Miss Diggy and bake it in the oven.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s chinese chicken balls with sweet and sour sauce

don't bother ordering chinese chicken balls make these at home they are just as good if not even better and the sweet and sour sauce is the same as what is served at your chinese restaurant!-- these are a great weekend snack or can be served as appetizers, if you want some extra flavor to you chicken batter feel free to add in some garlic or onion powder or spices of choice --- this makes a large amount so you may want to reduce the chicken ball batter amount by half (using 4 chicken breasts) --- note: the sauce recipe is one you may have to make a few times before you get the consistancy and sweetness to your liking, 1 cup white sugar and 1/2 cup lightly packed brown will give you a sweet sauce you may reduce the white sugar amount by a few tablespoons

1. to make the sweet and sour sauce sauce
2. in a saucepan combine the first 5 ingredients until combined
3. in a cup or bowl whisk the cold water or pineapple juice with cornstarch until smooth and well blended , then whisk vigorously into the ketchup mixture
4. bring to a boil stirring or whisking constantly over medium-high heat until bubbly
5. reduce the heat to medium-low and continue simmering and mixing until thickened remove from heat and allow to sit at room temperature while making the chicken balls or you may cool to room temperature then refrigerate until ready to use
6. to make the chicken balls: in a large bowl combine flour , cornstarch , baking powder , baking soda , garlic powder
7. add in water and sesame oil
8. whisk vigorously until smooth
9. add in chicken pieces
10. using clean handsand mix until well coated
11. heat oil in a deep-fryer or dutch oven to 375 degrees
12. carefully dip the battered chicken pieces in hot oil and fry until golden brown
13. remove to a paper towel
14. sprinkle with seasoning salt immediately after frying if desired
15. serve immediately with sweet and sour sauce
16. delicious !
demonstrations.review: These were great!  My husband always complains about sweet and sour chicken and this kept his mouth too full to talk.  This recipe makes a lot.  It was nice to have left-overs, though.  The sauce was great, too.  I prefer it to store-bought sweet and sour sauce.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: Holy Tamoly!!  I served this to my 4 picky kids and they ate it!  It was the first time I made meatloaf that was edible.  I don't even like meatloaf and I just ate about half of the leftovers.  I think next time I will up the ginger and maybe the salt and pepper.  Thanks so much for this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked balsamic chicken

love balsamic vinegar, hope you enjoy this chicken. note; i have found that it's better with boneless, skinless  chicken breast or  boneless, skinless thighs. baking time may be less due to size.

1. preheat oven 400 degrees
2. arrange the chicken bone side down in a 9-by-13 inch glass or ceramic baking dish
3. pour the vinegar over them and sprinkle evenly with the oil , oregano , salt and pepper
4. bake the chicken 20 minutes and baste with the vinegar juices
5. bake 20 minutes more or until juices run clear
6. serve chicken with juices spooned over them
demonstrations.review: I can't believe I haven't rated this yet!  I have made it half a dozen times and am pleased every time with how easy it is and how wonderful it tastes.  I love that I can decide to make this an hour before dinner and end up with something super tasty.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of applebee s oriental chicken salad by todd wilbur

this recipe is from www.topsecretrecipes.com. this actually tastes like the salad from applebees. it is a bit of work, but worth every second!!

1. preheat oil in deep fryer or deep pan over medium heat
2. you want the temperature of the oil to be around 350 degrees
3. blend together all ingredients for dressing in a small bowl with an electric mixer
4. put dressing in refrigerator to chill while you prepare the salad
5. in a small , shallow bowl beat egg , add milk , and mix well
6. in another bowl , combine flour with corn flake crumbs , salt and pepper
7. cut chicken breast into 4 or 5 long strips
8. dip each strip of chicken first into egg mixture then into the flour mixture , coating each piece completely
9. fry each chicken finger for 5 minutes or until coating has darkened to brown
10. prepare salad by tossing the chopped romaine with the chopped red cabbage , napa cabbage , and carrots
11. sprinkle sliced green onion on top of the lettuce
12. sprinkle almonds over the salad , then the chow mein noodles
13. cut the chicken into small bite-size chunks
14. place the chicken onto the salad forming a pile in the middle
15. serve with salad dressing drizzled over it or on the side
demonstrations.review:
Thank You!  Thank You!  Thank You!!
This is oh, so good.  I actually had made a different oriental dressing and it was so awful that I was looking for another recipe to fix it with.  So good!  Thanks again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork tenderloin w  balsamic marinade

this is an incredibly tasty way prepare a pork tenderloin. i could not get over how delicious it was. even my young kids like it. the amount of chili powder is deceiving, i thought it would be very spicy and it was not.
absolutely perfect for company!  serve with buttered noodles, baked apple sauce and you're good to go! enjoy.
note: 6-8 hour marination time required

1. trim and rinse pork as needed
2. place in a ziplock bag or dish with a tight seal
3. whisk together all ingredients until thoroughly blended
4. pour marinade over pork
5. marinate in refrigerator at least 8 hours or overnight , turning occasionally
6. heat grill to medium high
7. grill pork until center is pale pink , about 15-17 minutes or to desired doneness
8. let rest for 5 minutes , slice & serve immediately
9. may need to adjust cooking time + / - depending on the size & thickness or the tenderloin
10. the chili powder does not add the heat you may expect
11. not sure why , but it won't be spicy as one might anticipate
demonstrations.review: This marinade was very tasty.  I marinated for 24 hours and then used Perfect Pork Tenderloin Recipe #63828 to cook it.  It was so tender  my 9 month old ate it with just his 2 teeth.  Very good and company worthy!

target.recipe_text:
sirloin tips in wine

this is a wonderful way to use sirloin. it really tastes wonderful, and it's easy to make. prep time includes 1 hour marinating.

1. remove fat and fiber from meat
2. cut into bite-size pieces
3. sprinkle with meat tenderizer at least one hour before cooking
4. in a large frying pan , brown meat on all sides
5. mix all other ingredients together in a bowl and pour over beef
6. put lid on pan and simmer for 1 hour
7. do not remove lid until done
target.review: Yhis was good. I did make some changes I used about a cup less in water and still it still had alot of liquid. So I took a box of Pillsbury brown gravy powder and 1 tablesppon of flour and mixed it in. This thicken it up also added  8oz of fresh mushrooms.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon   egg casserole

another one from the penzey's spices catalog. a great way to use that stale bread. i like to add a diced, sauteed onion to this.

1. grease a 9x13 glass baking dish and set aside
2. fry the bacon , drain on paper toweling , cut into 1 inch pieces
3. cube the bread into 3 / 4 inch pieces and set aside
4. in a large bowl , beat the eggs
5. add the milk , mustard powder , salt , and blend well
6. stir in the bacon , cheese , and bread cubes
7. stir well to combine
8. pour the mixture into the baking dish , cover with plastic wrap , and refrigerate overnight
9. preheat oven to 350f and bake for one hour
demonstrations.review: Made this today. I did not have any bacon in the house so I took some Ham and Turkey lunch meat. I had a 6oz package. I made it according to directions. But I did put it in and 8 by 8 pan and baked it at 350 for about 35 minutes and then I topped it with a little more cheese. Thank you for shaing. It was really good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy rice pudding

i like this recipe because it is easy, quick (compared to other rice pudding recipes), and uses ingredients you probably always have around the house...and it's good!

1. bring water and rice to a boil
2. reduce heat to low , cover , and simmer 14 min
3. all water should be absorbed
4. heat oven to 325 degrees
5. beat eggs in ungreased 1 1 / 2 quart casserole dish
6. stir in sugar , raisins , milk , salt , and spice
7. stir in rice
8. bake uncovered 45 minutes
9. stirring occasionally
10. remove from oven and stir well
11. it will still be pretty wet
12. let set for 15 minutes to thicken
13. serve warm or chilled
demonstrations.review: Made this and it is so easy to make and wonderful. I doubled the recipe and cooked it for 15 minutes longer. Also did not add any Raisins. And then added more Cinnamon after it got out of the oven. Thanks for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple glaze for baked ham

posted at the request of my sister. glazing a ham while cooking is wonderful but the first person to the platter usually makes off the the glazed ends and the rest of the people get a "glazed rim". the solution in our house is to make lots of glaze and pour it over each slice!

1. place all ingredients in a small saucepan including the juice / syrup from the pineapple
2. turn heat on to medium and stir constantly to prevent burning
3. continue to heat until mixture thickens and comes to a boil
4. allow mixture to boil for approximately 1 minute
5. if mixture refuses to thicken , add more cornstarch- a little at a time
6. pour finished sauce into a serving bowl , complete with a ladle , and let your guests pour it over baked sliced ham
demonstrations.review: T%his was so good on the ham. I knew my family so I ended up doubleing the recipe. What I did was put some foil in the pan put the ham in covered it with eh glaze and then tented the ham with more foil. The Glaze baked in to the han it was so wonderful and it made for easy clean up. Thanks for sharing the recipe will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard salad dressing

better than the restaurants. adjust ingredient amounts to your taste.

1. whisk together or use blender to mix all ingredients
2. allow flavors to blend in refrigerator
3. keep chilled
demonstrations.review: Grilled some boneless chicken then topped it with Mushrooms and Bacon and a shredded cheese. Then coved it with the Honey Mustard. This Honey Mustard is a keeper. Only thing I omitted was the soy sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic buttercream frosting

a classic frosting used in my family for generations.

1. place butter , shortening , milk , vanilla , salt and one pound of sugar in large bowl
2. beat at low speed until combined
3. gradually add the other pound of sugar
4. stop and scrape sides
5. beat on high until mixture is light and fluffy
6. keep covered with plastic wrap to prevent crusting
7. chocolate buttercream: for each pound of sugar used in the butter cream , allow 2 / 3 cup unsweetened cocoa , 3 tablespoons butter and 0
8. 125 teaspoon salt
demonstrations.review: Had a boxed cake mis in the house nothing to frost it with found this.. It is really good. I am not sure how much powdered sugar I added as I just dumped until it was to the point I wanted it. I know I did not add the full bag. I am thinking about 1.5 pound. Thanks for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot potatoes

nan

1. lightly grease crock-pot
2. in small bowl , combine onion , garlic , salt and pepper
3. layer 1 / 4 of sliced potatoes in bottom of crock-pot
4. sprinkle with 1 / 4 seasonings
5. layer with 1 / 3 cream cheese cubes
6. continue layering process , ending with layer of potatoes then sprinkle with seasonings
7. cover and cook on high 3 to 4 hours
8. in last hour of cooking , stir potatoes to distribute cream cheese
9. serve when potatoes are tender
10. time saving
11. mixture should be cooked on low 6 to 8 hours or on high 2 hours or until potatoes are tender
12. substitute 32 oz
13. frozen hash browns for potatoes and prepare as directed
14. cook on low 4 to 6 hours or on high 2 hours
target.review: I just gave 2 stars the last time I tried these, and all I can say is I must have done something wrong, because these were fantastic!!!!!!!!  I lovedddddd them!  And they will become a regular in my household.  Yumm-o!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bean  n bacon

this is an old recipe that i have had since the 70's. it is off one of those mail order recipe cards. (before the internet). you can cook the bacon in a microwave oven. (this wasn't around either). because it is served cold it makes a great summer side dish. enjoy!

1. combine beans , onions , salad oil , 1 / 4 cup vinegar , 1 / 2 tsp salt and the pepper
2. toss lightly
3. cover and chill
4. just before serving , drain bean mixture and toss with bacon
demonstrations.review: This was good.  I omitted the onions because my boys don't like raw onions.  This was easy to throw together but think I might like it warmed up better than cold.  Thanks for a great recipe.  Made for I Recommend Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
turkey or chicken sopa

nan

1. melt butter in saucepan , then add onions
2. cook until tender
3. add green chilies , taco sauce , three soups , and turkey or chicken
4. place a layer of tortillas on bottom of 2-inch deep casserole dish
5. place alternate layers of soup mixture , tortillas and cheese on top
6. repeat for 3 layers , making sure top layer is cheese
7. bake at 350f for 30 minutes to one hour , or until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: Totally fantastic!  Quick to put together, and even my picky kids ate it!  I just used miscellaneous cheeses I had on hand, as well as used a can of chicken broth instead of the consumme.  Used salsa rather than taco sauce.  Great week night meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango   white chocolate cheesecake  no bake

in australian tables magazine november 2007.  looks absolutely delicious and if i wasn't diabetic would give it a go and the dh doesn't like mangoes so i can't see me making it at this point in time.  cooking time is chilling time.

1. place biscuits in a food processor and pulse until fine crumbs form
2. add melted butter and pulse to combine
3. press into a base of a 20cm springform pan
4. chill for 15 minutes , until base is firm
5. meanswhile , using an electric mixer , beat cream cheese and sugar together until smooth and creamy
6. fold through chocolate and whipped cream
7. whisk gelatine with hot water until dissolved
8. stir 1 / 4 cup of cream cheese mixture into gelatine , return to cream cheese mixture and mix well
9. pour cheesecake over biscuit base
10. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight
11. arrange mango slices over top and cut cheesecake into wedges to serve
demonstrations.review: This is SOOOOO yummy!  I didn't get a chance for a picture because it was devoured!  I will admit the that gram/cup etc. ratio was hard to figure out alot of googlin' but I figured it out.  The conversion button here isn't working yet or sumthing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
1 2 3 banana split ice cream cake

this cake comes out so moist and dense, you won't believe it!  the combinations are endless, just use your imagination.  thanks for the recipe mrs. kathleen!

1. cream together sherbet , bananas , and eggs
2. mix in the cake mix and beat for approximately two minutes
3. pour batter into bundt pan sprayed with nonstick cooking spray
4. bake at 350f for 45-60 minutes until toothpick comes clean when inserted
5. other great combinations include:
6. spice cake mix and butter pecan ice cream
7. chocolate cake mix and cookies & cream ice cream
8. vanilla cake mix and orange sherbet
demonstrations.review: This cake was quite a surprise!!!  The ingredients are so different, I wondered if the sherbet was going to work.  I will say that at first I thought that I had forgotten to write down all the ingredients!  I think these would be phenomenal in a cupcake, and I can't wait to try out the other flavors!  Made for Bargain Basement Tag.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rita s chili

very good homemade chili!

1. first chop and brown the chuck steak and set aside
2. second brown the sausage and set aside
3. next , saute the onion and garlic with seasonings
4. then add to the mixture the steak and sausage along with the tomatoes and simmer for 1 hour
5. finally add in the drained beans and water and cook for 30 more minutes
demonstrations.review: Super Fantastic!!!!  This is an insanely chunky chili and I absolutely loved it, as did the DH and kiddos.  I accidentally put 2 Tbsp of paprika, and the smokiness turned out great...instead of 1 cup of water I put in a can of beef broth.  Thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
target.review: You did it!!!! You designed a homemade spaghetti sauce that I really like!!! I've tried several others and hated them ALL!  I'm a stay-at-home dad with a baby, so I take any nap times and put dinner together. So, I put this together unheated and left it in the refrigerator for a few hours before putting it on the stove. I added a 32. oz can of crushed tomatoes, so I adjusted the spices and added extra brown sugar. It was AWESOME! The brown sugar is really what made it, in my opinion! I'll never use another recipe again for spaghetti sauce. Yum! Thank you so much for posting this!!<br/><br/>Edit: I make this recipe every week on "spaghetti night". I never look back at the recipe or measure anymore. I just eyeball it, and it always comes out perfect. The only change I consistently make is using hot sauce instead of crushed red pepper. Whenever I use red pepper, somebody ends up with a seed on their tongue and isn't a happy camper. haha. Thanks again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave chocolate mug brownie

this makes a delicious brownie for one in about a minute. 60 seconds makes a molten center brownie. 75 seconds make a uniformly done brownie. be careful not to overcook.

1. in a coffee mug , add water / milk , melted butter / oil , a dash of salt and vanilla extract
2. whisk well
3. add cocoa powder , whisk well
4. add sugar , whisk well
5. add flour , whisk well
6. microwave for 60 seconds
7. center should be slightly molten
8. careful not to overcook
9. enjoy with a spoon
10. careful , brownie will be hot
demonstrations.review: After making it as written and it being way too sweet for me, I decided I'd cut the sugar in HALF. Wow, was this rich! I was stuffed after eating it and could barely finish (oh, but I tried!). It was yummy. I also added chocolate chips to it before microwaving because it made it even more chocolaty and molten.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brussels sprouts in garlic butter

this is a recipe from joy of cooking... totally changed my mind about brussels sprouts! it's imperative that you use fresh sprouts, the texture would be way off with the frozen ones.

1. melt butter and olive oil in a medium skillet until butter is foamy
2. reduce heat to medium , add smashed garlic and cook until lightly browned
3. remove garlic and discard
4. add sprouts cut side down , cover , and cook without stirring on medium-low heat 10-15 minutes or until tender when pierced with a knife
5. the cut side of the sprouts should get nice and browned , with a nutty , buttery flavor enhanced by garlic
6. top with freshly grated parmesan and salt& pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: Brussels sprouts are the pregnancy craving of the day. I added garlic powder (yeah yeah I know) to the oil and butter instead of fresh garlic because I didn't have time to watch it and make sure I didn't burn it as I was chasing after my 12 month old. Even with the garlic powder and me letting it sit on medium-high heat for a good 5 minutes before remembering to cover it and turn it down, it didn't over-brown, and it is delicious!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: I made a gluten free version of this many months ago for a family get-together, simply substituting gf flour blend for the all purpose flour, and they  loved it... My mother requested I make it for a party she was throwing last night, so I quadrupled the recipe and made it almost exactly as written (I made the gravy with pan drippings used in a roux, then the chicken broth, in a pan and put that over the chops in the slow cooker). I didn't taste it because I have celiac, but everyone RAVED about it. The pork chops were the first thing to run out at the party, with people requesting them for the next party, too. It does work wonderfully when made gluten-free, too. My kids (1, 2 & 3) gave it two thumbs up.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oat pancakes  wheat free

these pancakes are made with oatmeal ground to a flour.  no wheat flour.  i serve these with soy protein sausage links (boca brand) and a little pure maple syrup or blue agave nectar (a low-glycemic syrup).

1. put oats in a blender or food processor and blend about one minute , or until ground to a flour consistency
2. combine oat flour , salt , baking powder and cinnamon in a large mixing bowl
3. mix well
4. combine egg , milk and vanilla in a small bowl and mix well
5. stir liquid mixture into dry mixture
6. mix until just moist
7. allow to rest 5 minutes
8. heat a nonstick large skillet or gridle over medium heat
9. when hot , pour 1 / 4 cup batter for each pancake
10. cook until bubbles form on surface of pancake
11. turn over and cook until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: I double this recipe for my 4 kids, so it doesn't make a lot. Skip the cinnamon and put the entire batter into my blender, blend it well, then let it sit while my griddle is heating up so it can thicken and soften up. I add chocolate chips to the tops of them while they cook of sometimes add a tiny bit of sugar/syrup instead. This also works well as waffles, just add 3-4 tablespoons of butter. We don't put extra syrup on them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lasagna   cheese   soup

hearty, cheesy and just plain good!!  the crusty croutons with stringy cheese along with tomatoes and beef is "to die for".  a wonderful entree for soup night! very popular!  easy to prepare! note:  add 1 cup of water to allow for noodles to cook in soup.

1. in large 5 quart saucepan , brown ground beef and onion
2. drain
3. stir in chicken broth , diced tomatoes , tomato sauce , italian seasoning , worcestershire sauce , garlic powder , brown sugar , salt and black pepper
4. bring to a boil and turn back to simmer on low heat for 30 minutes
5. add broken lasagna noodles and simmer until noodles are tender for approximately 20 minutes
6. stir in parmesan cheese
7. ladle soup into bowls and top with croutons
8. sprinkle with mozarella cheese and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: I actually took this recipe and threw it into the crock pot for 6 hours and then added the noodles for the last 30 minutes. I also used rotini because I didn't have lasagna noodles. I never measure my spices and throw in whatever I feel like, and I use oregano/basil/parsley cos I never have Italian Seasoning on hand. THIS WAS DELICIOUS, THOUGH! It was so good. This one will definitely be a staple in my household, and I'll definitely keep using the slow cooker just because I don't have the time or energy to stand over the stove for 50-60 minutes (I've got an 11 month old and one on the way). Thanks so much for this!!! Even my mom had two big bowls, and she NEVER eats a lot!

target.recipe_text:
italian lentil and barley soup

this is a surprisingly filling, vegetarian, crock pot soup. it is very good, and easy to prepare the night before, or chop the veggies in advance and turn it on before you leave for work in the morning. goes great with a crusty bread.

1. sort through lentils to remove debris and shriveled beans , then rinse
2. add lentils to crock pot , along with barley , carrots , celery , onion , garlic , dried herbs and bay leaf
3. pour in broth , water , and tomatoes
4. cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 14 hours , or on high heat for 5 to 6 hours
5. discard bay leaf and just before serving stir in parsley and vinegar
6. lentils aren't like dried beans
7. they don't require soaking and cook pretty quickly when you do it right
8. when you buy your lentils , go somewhere that has a decent turnover so your lentils haven't been sitting on the shelf for years
9. also , don't add any additional salt to the soup while it is cooking , and don't add lentils to already boiling water as either one can make lentils tough
target.review: This is a good base recipe, but I had to tweak it a little to suit my tastes. I added some destemmed kale to the slowcooker about 45 minutes before it was supposed to be done for some added nutrition. I've tried stirring in pesto, and that flavored it a little. I also tried adding balsamic vinegar, which adds a nice flavor, but is not what I am expecting from a soup. It's missing something, but maybe it'll taste better tomorrow.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: Wow, this soup is fantastic and really hits the spot on a cold fall (almost winter) night. I made 1.5x everything except the cream cheese (for which I just used an 8-oz block of neufchatel cheese) and added a chopped carrot, chopped celery, and 1 Tbsp of minced garlic. Tossed everything (except the cream cheese) into the slowcooker on low for 6 hours and stirred in the cream cheese before blending everything. I might never look for another potato soup recipe again...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tortellini tomato spinach soup

really healthy soup, good to use when there's no time to spend in the kitchen!

1. in a soup pot , heat olive oil over medium high heat
2. saute the onion and garlic , stirring often until onions are translucent , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. add broth and tomatoes , turn heat up to high , and bring to a boil
4. add the tortellini and cook according to package instructions
5. when tortellini is almost done , add spinach and taste , adjusting seasonings with salt and pepper
6. serve immediately
7. garnish each serving with a sprinkling of parmesan
demonstrations.review: Quick and easy. I used no salt added diced tomatoes, and the soup was a little on the acidic side... but I think if I use Italian style tomatoes next time, it'll turn out fantastic. Adding 4 cups of low-sodium broth and using a 10-oz package of cheese tortellini yielded six 1.5-cup servings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheat n  eat vietnamese chicken soup

sometimes you just don't have all day to make vietnamese soup! you can have this made and in your hands in 15 minutes!

1. soak noodles in very hot tap water
2. while noodles are soaking , cut chicken into thin julienne strips
3. heat oil in deep skillet over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. garlic , ginger , and pepper flakes
6. cook , stirring for 1 minute
7. then add broth and fish sauce and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat to medium and simmer until chicken is done , about 8 minutes
9. drain noodles and cut into short pieces , about 1-1 1 / 2 inches long
10. arrange noodles in bottom of bowls
11. ladle soup over the top and sprinkle with cilantro , onion , and basil
12. serve with"tuong ot sriracha" , or chile paste , if desired
demonstrations.review:
I made this with tofu and enjoyed it very much! It doesn't taste anything like what my mom made for me growing up, but it kept my craving for Vietnamese food at bay. This is not meant to taste anything like pho, as the spices are noticeably missing, and cellophane noodles (usually made of mung bean) are not the same as the rice vermicelli noodles used in pho.

In any case, I will be making this recipe again and again. Thank you so much for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best banana bread

you'll never need another banana bread recipe ever again!

1. remove odd pots and pans from oven
2. preheat oven to 350 / 180
3. cream together butter and sugar
4. add eggs and crushed bananas
5. combine well
6. sift together flour , soda and salt
7. add to creamed mixture
8. add vanilla
9. mix just until combined
10. do not overmix
11. pour into greased and floured loaf pan
12. bake at 350 / 180 for 55 minutes
13. keeps well , refrigerated
demonstrations.review: If this isn't the best banana bread ever, it certainly comes close. The bread comes out of the oven nice and crispy on the outside but moist on the inside. I added some dark chocolate morsels to the batter. The recipe is simple and comes together quickly. This will be my go-to from now on, whenever I have some browning bananas.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: The bf and I both loved this. I used a 3-lb sirloin and my sauce packets were 0.6 oz for the gravy and Italian dressing, 1 oz for the ranch. I tossed in some sliced onions, diced carrots, and potatoes. I didn't think this was too salty at all, although the veggies may have helped. This recipe is definitely a keeper. THANK YOU!!!

target.recipe_text:
best seller caramel corn

when i used to regularly do christmas craft shows, i always sold this packaged up in christmas tins; it was a big seller for me. my sil always hoped it wouldn't sell well, though, so she could eat what didn't sell! based on a bonnie stern recipe.

1. when i make this recipe , it's the only time i haul out my hot-air popcorn popper
2. use 1 / 3 cup popcorn to achieve the 8 cups of popped corn
3. preheat oven to 275f
4. have ready a jelly roll pan
5. place popped corn in a very large bowl
6. in a large , heavy saucepan over high heat , combine the sugar , butter and corn syrup and bring to a boil
7. let boil for two minutes , stirring continuously
8. remove from heat
9. add baking soda and vanilla to sugar mixture and combine well
10. pour this mixture over popped corn and combine , then spread mixture out onto jelly roll pan
11. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes , stirring well every 10 minutes
12. let cool before eating
target.review: Yum! Yum! Yum!  I baked it on the aluminum slide foil so nothing stuck to it & it made for an easy clean-up.  I also added some almonds.  It coated 1 bag  of microwave popcorn (which is supposed to yield 7 cups).  Buttery, salty, sweet... how can you go wrong? ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai noodles with spicy peanut sauce

this is a recipe that i've tweeked and adjusted to yield a warm noodle side-dish. it can also stand alone as a main dish. it's quick and easy and full of flavor! i serve it with chicken satay. leftovers are yummy hot or cold.

1. cook pasta in a large pot of salted water according to package directions
2. drain and return to pot
3. add 2 tbsp sesame oil and toss to coat
4. set aside
5. heat remaining 2 tbsp sesame oil in heavy pot over medium-high heat
6. add green onions , carrots , stir-fry veggies , garlic and ginger
7. saute until vegetables soften , about 4 minutes
8. add honey , peanut butter , soy sauce , vinegar and chili-garlic sauce and mix well
9. simmer sauce 2 minutes
10. pour sauce over pasta and toss well
11. transfer to platter and serve warm
12. garnish with additional green onions , if desired
13. yields 8 side dish servings or 4 main dish servings
14. chili-garlicsauce can be increased or decreased depending on how spicy you like your dish
15. as written , this recipe has some heat , but is still edible for my toddler son
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight with fresh veggies (red peppers, broccoli, zucchini) and it was fantastic. Also, I found out I was out of sesame oil so I had to sub peanut oil and it was still great but I'm sure that the seame oil would have added another depth of flavour.  This will go into our rotation.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
naan  indian flat bread

these are easy to make and taste just wonderful! prep time does not include 2 hours that you will need to set the dough aside. i cook these one at a time which will add up to about 60-80 mins total for cooking time!

1. sift the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt together into a nice sized bowl
2. stir in the beaten egg , yogurt and 2 tablespoons of the butter / ghee
3. gradually stir in enough milk to make a soft dough
4. knead dough very well
5. lightly grease bowl and cover the dough with a damp cloth and place in a warm place for 2 hours
6. preheat your oven to 400 degrees
7. knead dough on a floured surface for 2 or 3 minutes until smooth
8. divide into 8 pieces
9. roll each piece into a ball , and then into ovals about 6 to 8 inches long
10. grease a baking sheet with oil and brush both the sides of the rolled out naan with oil
11. sprinkle one side with poppy seeds if you wish to use them
12. place the naan on a baking sheet
13. bake for 6 to 10 minutes until puffy and lightly golden brown
14. the bread puffs slightly , and will lightly brown on the sides
15. you can enjoy these naan's plain or with your favorite indian dish , such as a curry dish !
demonstrations.review: I have made these several times and they are fabulous for homemade donairs or even for flatbread pizzas.  I have discovered that I prefer cooking the naan on a smoking hot cast iron grill pan rather than baking in the oven. This way you get it browned without making it too crispy.  I also brush with a mixture of melted  unsalted butter, minced garlic, chopped fresh parsley & sea salt before grilling.  Yum!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan grilled pork chops

these chops are so easy and very tender. it's based on a recipe in the mama dip's kitchen cookbook. be sure to follow the important steps of letting the chops rest with the salt and seasoning before cooking, then browning the sides slowly, followed by a covered "rest".  mama dip is a traditional southern u.s. cook, chef, restauranteur and cookbook author.

1. sprinkle the salt , thyme and pepper on the pork chops
2. let sit on counter top for 30 minutes
3. place oil in large cast iron skillet and heat until medium hot
4. place chops in the pan , placing them so they don't touch each other
5. cook each side slowly until nice and golden brown on each side
6. this will take about 4 minutes per side
7. cover the pan with a tight fitting lid
8. turn off the heat , and let the chops sit for about 8- 10 minutes , depending on thickness of chops
9. after removing chops , you can de-glaze the pan with a little water , wine or broth and a touch of butter and serve as a sauce
demonstrations.review: I'll admit I was a little skeptical of the technique but these were the most tender porkchops I have ever cooked.  Delish!  I also subbed Montreal steak spice & a little garlic powder for the spices.  After cooking,I deglazed the pan with some onions & chicken stock to make a sauce to pour over the chops.  This is my new favourite pork chop recipe! Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
make ahead garlic mashed potatoes

this is a wonderful recipe i found in a betty crocker magazine. it is a great comfort food with the added make ahead benefit. it is great with any roast or poultry dish.

1. place potatoes and garlic in medium saucepan with enough water to cover
2. cover and heat to boiling , reduce heat and simmer until tender
3. drain and shake potatoes to dry over low heat
4. mash potatoes and garlic in pan until lump free
5. heat rest of ingredients stirring over low heat until butter melts
6. reserve 1 / 4 c of mixture
7. add rest of milk mix in small amounts stirring after each addition until light and fluffy
8. grease a 2 quart casserole and spoon in potatoes
9. cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours
10. heat oven to 350
11. pour reserved milk mixture over potatoes and bake uncovered 40-45 minutes or until hot
12. stir before serving
demonstrations.review: I have never attempted making mashed potatoes ahead of time so I thought I would give it a try really not expecting them to be as good as made to order. I was wrong! These were terrific.  I used half & half instead of whipping cream but otherwise followed the recipe.  They get five stars because they taste wonderful and the for the ease of preparation.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy dinner party marinated mushrooms

i don't cook in my microwave very often, but here's a good recipe for making tasty mushrooms for the buffet table or dinner party.  sometimes shortcuts really are helpful!  :)

1. combine wine , vinegar , sugar , garlic , green onion , red pepper and red pepper flakes in 8 cup microwaveable casserole
2. cover
3. microwave on high for 3 minutes or until mixture is simmering
4. add mushrooms
5. cover
6. microwave at high 6 minutes or until mushrooms are tender but not mushy
7. stir partway through cooking
8. stir in salt , oregano and pepper
9. let stand , covered , for 30 minutes
10. transfer to covered jar or container
11. refrigerate up to 1 week
12. lower powered machines might take a couple of minutes longer , higher will take about what is specified above
demonstrations.review: These were awesome.  I am making my second batch today.  Like another reviewer suggested, I can see trying this with other veggies such as asparagus, carrots & pearl onions.  I didn't have white wine vinegar so I used rice wine which seemed to be a good substitute.  This would be a great addition to a tapas / antipasta platter.

target.recipe_text:
ez baked frito pie

this is great for times when you don't want to cook, but still want a hot meal. my dad has always made it, and over the years i have tweaked his recipe a bit. it is very easy to make, takes very little time, and the leftovers are great. it is a meal in itself, though i sometimes enjoy it with a couple of warm flour tortillas.

1. pre-heat oven to 350 degrees heat the canned chili and any optional ingredients on the stove
2. spread a thin layer of fritos along the bottom of an 8x8 or 9x9 baking dish
3. pour about half of the heated chili evenly over the bottom layer of fritos
4. completely cover the chili layer with a thicker layer of fritos
5. sprinkle about half the shredded cheese atop the fritos
6. pour the remainder of the chili atop the frito / cheese layer
7. completely cover the top chili layer with another thick layer of fritos , then sprinkle on the remaining cheese
8. bake in 350 oven for about 25-30 minutes , or until bubbly around edges and top cheese is melted
9. allow to cool for about 5 minutes before serving
target.review: This isn't something I would usually make.  I had never eaten canned chili before, and didn't trust it, but I had inherited a can (with turkey) from my mother who was cleaning out her pantry to adapt to a low-sodium diet.  I  was determined to make use of it even though everyone grimaced at the thought of canned chili with turkey.  What a surprise!  My kids and SO demolished it within minutes.  I couldn't believe how good it was.  I baked it in a deep dish pie plate and added green onions and a few jalapenos.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajunized oriental pork chops

yummy yummy yummy! i will absolutely gorge myself on these. which is why the servings are for 3 but there are only 2 of us.

1. use salt and cayenne to coat chops
2. heat oil in a large skillet
3. add chops and brown slowly
4. add wine , bell pepper , onion and garlic
5. cover and simmer for 25-30 minutes
6. remove pork chops
7. add soy sauce and reserved pineapple juice
8. stir and allow to simmer for 10 minutes
9. add pineapple chunks and pork chops
10. bring to a boil , turn off heat
11. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: my bf likes pineapples so i'll attempt this again, but it lacked oomph and the peppers and onions were overdone.  i used tony's and sesame oil, but otherwise followed the recipe.  next time i'll add the veggies later and perhaps some chili oil.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingered fish

inspired by a recipe from cooking light, this is a simple but full flavored dish. the original calls for flounder but works well with sole and other mild fishes. really surprised this isn't in the 'zaar collection already as it is one of our favorites.

1. using a damp cheesecloth or your hand , squeeze grated ginger over a small bowl gathering the ginger juice
2. combine 2 tablespoons ginger juice , soy sauce , sherry , lemon juice , and sugar or sugar substitute in a large food storage bag or bowl
3. add fish , turning or gently shaking to coat
4. marinate in refrigerator 20 minutes , turning fish occasionally
5. remove fish from marinade
6. discard marinade
7. place fish on broiler pan coated with cooking spray and broil 3 minutes
8. brush oil over fish , and broil an additional minute or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
9. place fish on individual serving plates , and drizzle remaining tablespoon ginger juice over fish
10. garnish with scallions
demonstrations.review: i used tilapia fillets and i didn't have any fresh ginger on hand so i used crystallized ginger slices instead and omitted the sugar, letting it soften a bit in the lemon juice and soy sauce before chopping it.  i have a spacemaker oven that doesn't have a broil option, so i let it bake for 10 minutes at 450 degrees, brushing on the sesame oil after 5 minutes.  i served it with steamed broccoli and jasmine rice.  for me, the green onions made the dish.  my bf raved about it and asked that i make it again.  thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked arroz con pollo

the original recipe was longer and used chicken pieces, but this is my quick and easy version! i hope you enjoy, it is packed with flavor!

1. saute veggies in oil
2. add broth , tomatoes and bay leaf
3. bring to a boil
4. spread rice in a 9x13 casserole pan
5. pour hot liquid over all , stir well
6. add chicken , mix
7. bake at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: arroz con pollo is one of my favorite dishes, but i have a hard time getting the rice perfect and had doubts as to whether or not baking would work.  estÃ¡ delicioso!  i used red bell peppers and added green peas.  muchas gracias!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh strawberry yogurt cake

this super moist cake weeps pink tears down its tender slices. amazing!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. grease and flour a 10 inch bundt pan
3. sift together the 2 cups of flour , baking soda and salt
4. mix in the lemon zest and set aside
5. with an electric mixer , cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
6. beat in the eggs one at a time , then stir in 1 tb
7. lemon juice
8. alternate beating in the flour mixture and the yogurt , mixing just until incorporated
9. toss the strawberries with the remaining cup of flour
10. gently mix them into the batter
11. pour the batter into the bundt pan
12. bake in the preheated oven for 60 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean
13. allow to cool 10 minutes in the pan , then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely
14. once cooled whisk together the remaining 2 tb
15. of lemon juice and the powdered sugar
16. drizzle over the top of the cake
demonstrations.review: i imagine this being served at Suri Cruise's tea parties.  i used strawberry yogurt and added a teaspoon of  almond extract.  don't skip the lemon glaze, though you could.  the cake has the consistency of a sweet, moist muffin.  a huge hit.  thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review: raves all around.  served in with  #110043 Spinach Saute With Brown Butter & Garlic adding red bell  peppers and onions and served it over angel hair pasta.  i used the jarred chopped garlic i always have on hand and didn't remove it.

target.recipe_text:
szechuan green beans

these are great. the recipe was originally from one of the moosewood cookbooks with a bit of tweaking. they recommend "follow the cooking method exactly, as it is critical to the success of this dish. both the wok and the oil should be hot, and the beans should cook quickly over high heat. they will attain an indescribable texture, both crunchy and very tender at the same time. also, try to hang in there with the full quantity of garlic. the intense cooking heat will take the edge off it, leaving behind just the right amount of flavor." enjoy!

1. place a medium-large wok or heavy deep skillet over medium high heat
2. after a minute , add the oil
3. wait a minute or so , and add the green beans
4. turn the heat to high and stir fry for about 5 minutes , or until the beans are well seared
5. add the garlic , salt , and ginger
6. stir-fry for several more minutes , then remove from heat
7. serve hot , warm , or at room temperature
target.review:
I made these about a month ago (sorry for the delay in posting I'm just catching up).
I simply adore these, I too changed the red pepper flakes to 1 heaping tsp as I love them spicy.
I'm so glad to finally find this recipe, so Ã«asy to make!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean garlic shrimp   olive garden copycat

this is a copycat recipe dedicated to rise.

1. heat olive oil in pan over medium heat
2. add red pepper flakes and garlic , cook for 1 minute
3. add shrimp , stir and cook until done
4. top with cheese
5. the second recipe is the same with 2 variations: add in just enough alfredo sauce to lightly coat the mixture and chunks of roasted garlic
6. serve over fettucini noodles
demonstrations.review:
*Popping a breath mint here *LOL As you know I just HAD to add more garlic, but darlin' this was without a doubt fantastic!
Since I made my own Mother's Day dinner, I chose what we'd be having! 
Mmmmmmm, I made the first variation and added some green onion I served it with some Yai-Yai's garlic bread and a small spinach salad with bleu cheese crumbles. Great dinner if I say so myself...thanks darlin'! Guess this means when I make the alfredo version I can review again?! ;D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chipotle lime marinated grilled pork chops or tenderloin

recipe from package of pork chops.prep time does not include marinating time. you can alternately use dried chipotle, just rehydrate in hot water for about 15 mins and then chop.
i actually like this better as a marinade for pork tenderloin.

1. place chops in large self-sealing plastic bag
2. combine remaining ingredients in a small bowl and pour over chops
3. seal bag and refrigerate for up to 24 hours
4. remove chops from marinade
5. grill over medium-hot coals for a totoal of 12-15 mins , turning half-wayt thru , or until done
demonstrations.review: In 1 word FANTASTIC! Just the kind of recipe I was looking for, simple easy and ever so tasty. I had wondferul thick boneless porkchops that I had planned on stuffing but after seeing the marinade I knew it wouldn't be necessary. I only marinaded for a little over an hour but next time I'll try for 24 as for a richer taste. I did use a fork and poked holes in the chops on all 4 sides to allow the marinade to enter. I used a can of chipotle sauce instead of the chilis in sauce and I added 1 tsp of oil and grilled them turning every 5 minutes pouring a little of the marinade on top each time. Served this with grilled corn on the cob along with a cold Italian pasta salad. Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot dorito dip

nan

1. brown and drain beef
2. reduce heat and add remaining ingredients
3. simmer until velveeta is melted , stirring occasionally
4. serve hot with doritos
demonstrations.review:
Like the others I make this with the "hot" Rotel.
also, I melt te cheese and other ingredients in a crockpot and just put the crockpot out so the dip stays nice and hot the entire time! "Great football food"!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate coated party mix

good christmas snack to have for guest and parties, recipe came from a family friend.

1. mix cereal and pretzels in a large bowl
2. melt white chocolate in the microwave
3. stir the chocolate until it starts to coat the cereal and pretzels mixture
4. pour m&m's into mixture and mix until blended well
5. do not over mix
6. line baking sheet or cake pan with wax paper
7. spread mixture in pan
8. let mixture harden , then break apart and serve
demonstrations.review: I'm a white chocolate JUNKIE. It is truly the only candy that I adore! This was the perfect recipe for the holidays. I used the white choc chips (not disks) and I did not put in M&M's but I did add some walnuts (by request). Thanks for this easy change from the usual mixture.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken   broccoli bake supreme

this is a dish that has been in my family for as many years as i care to remember. very rich & elegant. we serve it over rice with a crisp green salad.

1. defrost frozen broccoli throughly
2. in a large skillet sautee chicken breasts and garlic& mushrooms in chicken broth and white wine about 4 minutes each side or until no longer pink
3. in a large bowl mix together sour cream , cream of chicken soup , mayonaise& spices
4. in a casserole dish layer thawed broccoli and then chicken& mushrooms
5. bake at 350 for 35 minutes until mixture bubbles
6. remove and sprinkle cheddar cheese and return to back 10-15 minutes more until cheese slightly browns
demonstrations.review: This was great Cher! So easy to make and so tasty. As you know I didn't have curry powder so I decided not to try and substitue so I left that out but the taste was great! I had to sneak in the white wine as SO hates wine *LOL (what they don't know and all that)! Everyone loved it, I should have doubled the recipe! Thanks again!

target.recipe_text:
greek lamb casserole

this was printed in our local paper several months ago.  it is also one of those i clipped to make and then misplaced.  it sounds so wonderful.  i know if i post it, i want loose it.

1. heat the oil in a nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. add the onion and garlic
3. cook stirring frequently until onion is soft , about 5 minutes
4. add the eggplant and water
5. cook stirring frequently until eggplant is tender , about 5 minutes
6. add the cubed lamb and cook until longer pink , about 3 minutes
7. stir in the tomatoes , 1 / 2 cup of mint , 1 / 2 cup of dill , salt and bring to a boil
8. reduce heat to simmer , cover and cook 20 minutes or until lamb is tender
9. while the lamb mixture is cooking , cook orzo according to package directions , drain
10. preheat oven to 350 degrees
11. in a small bowl , combine the yogurt , flour and egg whites
12. stir the drained orzo into lamb mixture , spoon mixture into an 11 x 7 inch baking dish
13. cover and bake 10 minutes
14. uncover spoon yogurt mixture on top , return to oven and bake until casserole is bubbly , about 20 minutes
