1. slice hot dogs into long strips lengthwise
2. boil strips in water until they curl , and look like worms
3. toss hot strips with ketchup to make them look even grosser !
4. serve on buns
demonstrations.review: This got rave reviews at our Halloween party tonight.  I was serving adults so instead of ketchup, I put the worms in the crock pot with a jar of grape jelly and a jar of chili sauce... everyone loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jo mama s world famous spaghetti

my kids will give up a steak dinner for this spaghetti. it is a recipe i have been perfecting for years and it is so good (if i may humbly say) that my kids are disappointed when they eat spaghetti anywhere else but home! in fact they tell me i should open a restaurant and serve only this spaghetti and garlic bread. in response to requests, i have posted the recipe for recipe #28559 that uses approximately 1/2 of the sauce from this 
recipe. have spaghetti one night and lasagna later!  thanks to all of you who have tried my recipe and have written a review.  i read and appreciate every one of them!  chef note:  after i posted this recipe i remembered a funny incident--my dear husband usually has a nice bottle of wine handy so when i make a batch of spaghetti i just help myself to a splash of it. on one occasion, there wasn't a bottle opened, but there was a bottle sitting on the counter so i got out the corkscrew and helped myself. for some reason, the spaghetti that night was the best ever. my husband asked what wine i put in it and i showed him the bottle. he nearly fell off the chair. i had opened a rather expensive bottle he had bought to give his boss. goes to show you--don't use a wine for cooking you wouldn't drink. you get the best results from a good wine!

1. in large , heavy stockpot , brown italian sausage , breaking up as you stir
2. add onions and continue to cook , stirring occasionally until onions are softened
3. add garlic , tomatoes , tomato paste , tomato sauce and water
4. add basil , parsley , brown sugar , salt , crushed red pepper , and black pepper
5. stir well and barely bring to a boil
6. stir in red wine
7. simmer on low , stirring frequently for at least an hour
8. a longer simmer makes for a better sauce , just be careful not to let it burn !
9. cook spaghetti according to package directions
10. spoon sauce over drained spaghetti noodles and sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I used 1 lb 96% lean ground beef and 1 lb turkey italian sausage.  I think I will try it next time with crushed tomatoes instead of the diced... I'm not really a fan of tomato chunks.  The taste was awesome and it was very easy to make.  I served it on angel hair nests and topped with fresh grated parmesan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review:
This is just about the easiest thing on the planet to make, and it's sooooo good. I was making it for a friend who had just had sugery and was having trouble swallowing. I left out the pepper because I was afraid that would irritate his throat, but it was amazing. He loved it, and so did I. I used lowfat cream cheese. Upadte: I made this again and doubled the recipe using 8 oz lowfat cream cheese and 8 oz fat free. Then I added about 1/2 lb of chopped turkey kielbasa... heavenly...
UPDATE: Lately I have been making this using homemade vegetable stock instead of store-bought chicken broth. I add chicken bouillon to the broth, and then since the bouillon already has salt in it, I don't add the seasoned salt, but I give a good couple shakes of garlic powder, onion powder and paprika.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cherry pie

this is called best cherry pie because it is a blue ribbon winner at the county fair in vicksburg, ms (according to the cookbook 

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. drain cherries , reserving 1 / 2 cup juice
3. combine sugar , cornstarch and salt
4. combine cherry juice , food coloring , almond extract and lemon juice
5. add to dry ingredients , mixing well
6. add cherries and mix well again
7. add butter and let stand for 15 minutes
8. pour cherry mixture into pie crust and finish top with lattice work pie crust
9. bake for 50 to 55 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was terrific, though for some reason it was quite runny.  I was surprised because some reviewers said that they wanted more liquid in it.  I didn't add more, and it was still runny.  Maybe I didn't drain the cherries well enough.  But that didn't stop the people at work from devouring it in about 10 seconds. One guy said it was the best cherry pie he'd ever had... (but I already knew that ;-)

target.recipe_text:
pan fried tilapia

another very simple recipe...and a healthy one as well.

1. warm up olive oil in a 10" or 12" skillet
2. mix the corn meal and old bay seasoning thoroughly , then spread out on a platter
3. coat tilapia fillets lightly , but thoroughly with corn meal and old bay mixture
4. lay coated fillets in hot olive oil and cook until golden on the bottom , then turn fillets over and repeat
5. do not overcook the fish--it's easy to do
6. while fillets are cooking , combine miracle whip , sweet relish , and lemon juice and stir until well blended , then serve with the fish
7. it's quick , easy , and doesn't require a lot of cleanup
8. steamed carrots or broccoli and some form of potatoes go well with this
target.review:
The taste was very good and extremely easy to make.
Adaptations:
*Add more Old Bay. My husband and I agreed that we could barely taste it.
*Make less seasoning. I threw over 3/4 of it away. I buy Tilapia individually frozen from Sam's club, therefore they may be smaller, but I still had to needlessly waste alot of the seasoning

**Great side dishes: I made steamed brocolli and Taboule (wheat salad). I purchased the boxed kind (brand is Near East) You can find it in the health section of your grocery OR in the dry boxed goods section. I diced up a red pepper. Taboule is high in fiber and compliments the main dish visually, it is very tasty, and easy to make.
 FYI: directions on the Taboule box say to chill it for an hour or over night. I put it in the freezer while I pan fried the fish. It came out just good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chocolate chip sour cream banana bread

do not let this banana bread's long name fool you! very easy to make, and wonderful bread is the result.

1. cream the butter , sugar and vanilla together
2. then add the eggs and mix
3. then put in the dry ingredients and mix well
4. add the bananas and sour cream and mix
5. then add in the chocolate chips and pour into 3 greased loaf pans
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour , or until a toothpick that has been inserted into the center comes out clean
demonstrations.review:
Moist, taste chocolatey/banana and smelled great while baking!...I did a healthier spin on it and it turned out just as wonderful!!...
I cut the recipe to one loaf and here are my changes:
-REPLACED 7/8 cup white flour WITH 1/4 cup whole wheat flour/1/4 cup brown rice flour/
slightly less than a 1/4 cup whole grain pastry flour

-REPLACED sugar WITH splenda (kind that measure cup for cup)

-added 1/4 tsp dough enhancer (makes whole grain loaves lighter)

Dough enhancer can be found at a health food store and whole grain flours can be found in the health food dept. or baking aisle of regular grocery store.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with apricot and almonds

another easy dish for a midweek supper!  one of my daughter's favourite chicken dishes.  also good for an informal dinner party.

1. heat the oil , saut the chili , ginger , garlic , onions , allspice , cinnamon and turmeric until golden brown
2. add chicken portions and brown on all sides
3. stir in tomatoes with their juice , add the salt and apricots , cover and simmer for 15 minutes
4. sprinkle with almonds to serve
demonstrations.review: I also double the sauce (tomatoes, apricots, and spices) with 1/2 cup water for 30 minutes. It tasted great! Additionally 1 tbsp of sugar was added because I wanted to accentuate the sweetness of the apricots. Definitely an interesting mix of flavors!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon spinach bake

based on a recipe from family circle, this is easy , healthy, and quick to prepare.

1. put spinach , onion , garlic , butter and 3 tbsp water in micro , in a pie plate , cover w / plastic wrap and cook 3 minutes on high
2. drain
3. heat oven to 350
4. grease a 1 1 / 2 quart au gratin dish with cooking spray
5. mix spinach with rice , salt , pepper
6. in a small bowl , mix sour cream , egg , mustard , 2 tbsp parmesan , salt , pepper
7. reserve 2 tbsp of sauce , and mix in the rest with the spinach and rice
8. transfer to au gratin dish
9. place salmon over spinach mixture , add sauce over salmon , sprinkle with cheese , bake for 25-30 minutes
10. let stand 5 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this for my 1 year old twins and they absolutely loved it!....it was their first time eating salmon. :)....I did however omit the garlic onions and mustard...for now :)... I also used Kamut vegetable noodles (higher in iron) and mixed the salmon in the dish instead of placing on top....still turned out great...my husband wants me to make it for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian turkey sausage and peppers with bow tie pasta

i just threw this together one night with ingredients i had on hand. we loved the flavor and it's now a favorite after work meal.

1. saute onion , peppers and pepper flakes in olive oil until onions start to brown
2. add garlic , salt , pepper , basil and oregano
3. set aside
4. prick sausage links with a fork
5. saute in skillet with a little olive oil over medium heat until brown
6. add wine vinegar and canned tomatoes
7. add the sauted vegetable mixture
8. cover and simmer for 20 minutes
9. meanwhile cook pasta al dente
10. add cooked pasta to sausage and pepper mixture
11. stir and serve
demonstrations.review: Excellent! Quick and Easy to make and tasted great!...wonderful meal for working moms...I used penne instead of bowtie and I used red pepper, 1/2 yellow, and 1 green...was also a beautiful looking dish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review:
I made this recipe for my 4 year old's playdates. I made some changes to make a slightly healthier version  and it turned out great!...Changes I made:

1 1/2 cups whole wheat pastry flour and 1/2 cup all purpose flour

3/4 cup sugar and 3/4 splenda

1/2 cup of tub margarine

Thank you Thank you for an easy to make kid friendly recipe!

target.recipe_text:
garlic  herb  orzo and rice pliaf

garlic and fresh herbs flavor this orzo/rice combination pilaf. vegetable broth may be used for chicken broth.

1. in a large nonstick skillet heat oil over medium-high
2. add garlic and cook for 1 minute , being careful not to burn
3. add orzo and rice
4. cook 4-6 minutes longer or until lightly browned
5. stir in broth and water
6. bring to a boil
7. reduce heat
8. cover and simmer for 15-20 minutes , until rice is tender and liquid is absorbed
9. stir in the onions , basil , parsley and salt
10. serve
11. sprinkle some grated parmesan on top if desired
target.review: Really nice pilaf .  Fresh herbs and garlic and youn can't go wrong.  this recipe will be saved to use for entertaining.  I too used vegetable stock instead of the chicekn stock.  Great vegetarian dish.  Made for your win  for Wildcard weekend Football Pool

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shirley s date nut pinwheels   christmas

my mom used to make these every christmas for us when i was growing up, and they bring back special memories for me, especially around the holidays. we have been eating these for 50 years!  these are my all time favorite cookies :)  they make a lot of cookies, and the amount really depends on how thick you actually roll the dough, and how thin or thick you cut the cookies.  the cooking time is for each batch of cookies, and the prep time does not include time to chill dough.

1. date filling:
2. combine dates , sugar and water in a pan and cook until thick
3. add nuts to mixture , mix , and let cool
4. set aside
5. cookie dough:
6. cream shortening and add brown sugar gradually
7. add eggs , and beat well
8. add to the other ingredients , and mix
9. divide into 2 parts , and make 2 round balls
10. chill for 1 hr
11. , or until ready to bake
12. preheat oven to 375
13. make 4 balls from the 2 lg
14. balls of dough
15. roll out dough to 1 / 4" thick , and spread date mixture all over the top to the edge of the dough
16. roll into logs
17. cut into slices 1 / 4" thick , and place on greased cookie sheet
18. bake in 375 oven for 10-12 minutes
19. cool on cookie racks and store in a plastic container with lid , or a cookie tin
demonstrations.review: My Mom always made these each year for her holiday cookie tray.  Now that she is gone I make them .  This year I could not find her recipe. I decided on this recipe and I was not disappointed .  Just like Mom's. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stuffed reuben mushrooms

these are awesome! i made them for a christmas party and they were a big hit! everyone devoured them!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. brush mushrooms or wipe clean with a damp cloth
3. remove stems from mushrooms and discard
4. fold and fit 1 slice of corned beef inside mushroom cap
5. top with 1 teaspoons sauerkraut , 1 / 2 teaspoon salad dressing and approximately 1 teaspoon cheese
6. place on an ungreased sheet pan
7. sprinkle with chives
8. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes or until thoroughly heated
demonstrations.review: I made 3 times the recipe for our tailgate party.  I did take the suggestion of the other review and dried kraut on a paper towel.  I did change the reicpe to make the filling adhere together better- I added 4 oz of cream cheese.  Made for 2009 Football pool week 4

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sauteed swiss chard with bacon

here's an easy, quick and savory recipe for swiss chard from zany, excellent chef anne burrell. it's one of my favorites! chard is one of the super leafy greens packed with minerals and vitamins as well as a healthy dose of fiber. it tastes a lot like spinach with a slightly stronger taste, depending on the cooking method. use regular olive oil, not virgin, for best flavor. reduce the amount of bacon if desired.

1. coat a large saute pan lightly with olive oil and add the diced bacon , garlic , and crushed red pepper
2. bring the pan to medium-high heat
3. when the garlic has turned a lovely golden brown , remove from the pan and discard
4. at this point the bacon should start to become brown and crispy
5. add the swiss chard stems and the stock and cook until the stock has mostly evaporated
6. add the swiss chard leaves and saute until they are wilted
7. season with salt and serve
demonstrations.review:
Yummy!!
Just like my grandmother use to make when we were young.  she was always pushing vegetables on us.  My grandfather always had a great garden, so we had so many fresh vegetables to choose from. 
Thanks for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy never fail breaded chicken

this is the most simple chicken recipe i've ever made. my mom came up with it and i tweaked it a tiny bit and we eat it at least 3 times a month. i honestly don't see how anyone could dislike this chicken. i recommend serving it with homemade mashed potatoes!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. melt 2 t butter and pour into shallow baking dish
3. melt remaining 4 t butter in small bowl
4. dip chicken in butter and then dredge in bread crumbs
5. place coated chicken into baking dish
6. sprinkle cheese on top of chicken
7. cooking times vary according to the thickness of the chicken and your individual oven , so start checking for doneness after about 25 minutes
8. it takes about 35-40 in my oven
9. chicken is done when juices run clear and you can easily cut it with a fork
demonstrations.review: My neighbor's little girl is always asking me to cook up something good.   I let her help me make this recipe so that she could take it on a picnic with her Gram.  She want to suprise everyone. They all loved it and so did I.  Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy maple baked salmon

a nice canadian way to cook a nice canadian fish.

1. in a small saucepan cook first 7 ingredients till boiling
2. reduce heat and simmer till reduced to about 1 / 2 cup
3. season salmon with salt & pepper
4. brush sauce on salmon and bake skin side down for 10 minutes in a 350 oven
5. brush again and continue to bake for another 10 minute
6. brush again and bake for final 10 minute
7. do not turn fish
demonstrations.review: I was child sitting for my new neighbor last week end. Her oldest (6) loves salmon.  I made this for her. She has such sophisticated taste for a small child that it is a pleasure to cook for her.  she said this was a 5 star recipe.  I personally do not like salmon so I had cod. Thanks

target.recipe_text:
emeril lagasse s pumpkin cheesecake

emeril suggest that if you buy and extra pumpkin and puree it you will have the most fantastic cheesecake for the holidays. sounds amazing!

1. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine the graham cracker crumbs , pecans , brown sugar , and 1 / 2 teaspoon of the cinnamon in a bowl
3. pour in the melted butter and stir well to blend
4. press the mixture evenly into the bottom and 1 inch up the sides of a 9-inch springform pan
5. combine the cream cheese , sugar , cornstarch , vanilla , the remaining 1 / 2 teaspoon of cinnamon , and the nutmeg in the bowl of an electric mixer
6. beat until fluffy
7. add the eggs and yolks , beating on low speed until just blended
8. fold in the cream and pumpkin pure
9. pour the batter into the crust-lined pan , and place on a baking sheet
10. bake until the center is nearly set , about 1 hour to 1 hour and 10 minutes
11. remove from the oven and cool for 15 minutes
12. carefully run a small , sharp knife between the cake and the sides of the pan
13. release the sides of the pan and cool at room temperature for 30 minutes
14. cover the cheesecake tightly with aluminum foil or plastic wrap , and chill in the refrigerator at least 4 hours , or up to 8 hours , before serving
target.review: This dessert was my Thanksgiving contribution, and everyone loved it.  I used the gingersnaps like Jessica suggested, upped the spices like "Got Twins" suggested.  Good results.  Some at the party felt I should make these and sell them.  Yep, a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
doubletree chocolate chip cookies

not quite like the hotel's recipe, but close enough.

1. grind oats in a food processor or blender until fine
2. combine the ground oats with the flour , baking soda , salt and cinnamon in a medium bowl
3. cream together the butter , sugars , vanilla , and lemon juice in another medium bowl with an electric mixer
4. add the eggs and mix until smooth
5. stir the dry mixture into the wet mixture and blend well
6. add the chocolate chips and nuts to the dough and mix by hand until ingredients are well blended
7. for the best results , chill the dough overnight in the refrigerator before baking the cookies
8. spoon rounded 1 / 4 cup portions onto an ungreased cookie sheet
9. place the scoops about 2 inches apart
10. bake in a 350 f oven for 16-18 minutes or until cookies are light brown and soft in the middle
11. store in a sealed container when cool to keep soft
demonstrations.review: I liked it enough to send it to my Christmas gift list.  Everyone that received them loved them. When I made a second batch, I substituted one large banana for the two eggs, (for a vegetarian friend) and everyone that ate them still loved them, including the fellow that said he didn't like oats.  The cinnamon was to subtle for me, so the second time I used 1/2 teaspoon.  Easy to make with great results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: Followed recipe & they turned out fine. I found the sweetness a little off-putting for my burger, but it worked well with ham. I think next time I'll cut back on the sugar like Jean T. did. Also I didn't grease the baking sheet, but used parchment paper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut eggnog  non alcoholic

haven't tried this yet, but it sounds yummm

1. simmer the 3 "milks"
2. mix 1 cup into eggs , mix back into pan
3. stir over low heat , 5 minutes , to thicken
4. strain
5. chill
6. add nutmeg , if desired
demonstrations.review: I was wondering how this would work.  Whenever I put coconut milk into the fridge, it would lump up.  As good as (non-hydrogenated)  coconut oil is for you, it does start to solidify at 75 degrees or so.  Anyway, this is delicious, but there may be some soft lumps in the mixture after chilling.  I stirred them up to blend the milks together better, but it's good.  It was good when I thinned it with a little coconut rum later, too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
top secret recipes version of doubletree hotel chocolate chip co

from even more top secret recipes by todd wilbur. i am a huge chocolate chip cookie fan and this is one of the best chocolate chip cookies!  the recipe says to chill the dough overnight before baking - this chilling time is not included in the prep/cook time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grind oats in a food processor or blender until fine
3. combine the ground oats with the flour , baking soda , salt and cinnamon in a medium bowl
4. cream together the butter , sugars , vanilla , and lemon juice in another medium bowl with an electric mixer
5. add the eggs and mix until smooth
6. stir the dry mixture into the wet mixture and blend well
7. add the chocolate chips and nuts to the dough and mix by hand until ingredients are well-incorporated
8. spoon rounded 1 / 4-cup portions onto an ungreased cookie sheet
9. place the scoops about 2 inches apart
10. you don't need to press the dough flat
11. bake for 16-18 minutes or until cookies are light brown and soft in the middle
12. store in a sealed container when cool to keep soft
13. for the best results , chill the dough overnight in the refrigerator before baking the cookies
demonstrations.review: I liked it enough to send it to my Christmas gift list last year. Everyone that received them loved them. When I made another batch, I substituted one large banana for the two eggs, (for a vegetarian friend) and everyone that ate them still loved them, including the fellow that said he didn't like oats. The cinnamon was too subtle for me, so the second time I used 1/2 teaspoon. Easy to make with great results.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kimchi fried rice  kimchi bok eum bap

the name says it all.  a great way to use up left over rice.  don't feel limited to the listed ingredients; mushrooms, a bit of meat, a scrambled egg etc... are all great in this dish.  this recipe makes one really generous serving or two side dish servings.  multiplies easily.

1. heat oil in wok or good-sized frying pan
2. add kim chi and garlic
3. stir-fry until kim chi is translucent
4. be careful: it will really spatter when it hits the oil !
5. add rice , green onions , fish cake or meat , mushrooms
6. stir-fry until well mixed and heated through
7. remove from heat
8. add in sesame seeds , soy sauce , salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This was good.  I liked the serving, since I live alone.  Didn't have a Korean fish cake, but I discovered crumbled bacon tastes good.  I also discovered 2 tblspns of oil (in a wok) works, too.  What on earth makes the total carbs 158.9 grams??  The measurements exclude the kim chee & the fish cakes.  What's left, the rice?

target.recipe_text:
crouton egg casserole

this comes from the "bon appetot cookbook"-not a typo!  it's a book that was created by preschoolers' parents. it makes for a perfect for brunch.

1. cook bacon until crisp and drain on paper towels
2. set aside
3. in the bottom of a 10 x 6 x 1 3 / 4 inch baking dish , combine croutons and cheese
4. in a bowl , combine eggs , milk , salt , onion powder and pepper
5. mix until blended
6. pour egg mixture over the cheese and croutons
7. crumble the bacon and sprinkle on top of the casserole
8. bake in a preheated 325 degree oven for about 1 hour or until eggs are set
9. cool slightly before serving
target.review: Enjoyed this dish, gives the notion of having bacon and eggs a whole new twist.  It's a keeper in my books.  Instead of trying to combine the croutons and cheese (the cheese just falls to the bottom anyway), layer the croutons on bottom and sprinkle cheese over them.  I halved my 1%milk with rice milk, added some diced onion and 1 tsp onion powder, and omitted the salt.  I happened to check it after 45 minutes and it was pretty much done, so I just left it another minute or two. Good quality croutons (or homemade) are essential. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecue chicken basil calzones  oamc

this recipe can be easily doubled. this freezes wonderfully and makes a great meal/snack to have on hand. you can also make these and eat them hot out of the oven.   
this recipe was created for ready, set, cook! #6

1. for the dough: combine flour , baking powder , sugar and basil
2. add milk powder to water and stir until dissolved , add to dry mixture
3. add eggs and melted butter and mix well
4. set aside while making the filling
5. for the filling: cook onions in butter over medium heat until onions are tender
6. add chicken and mushroom pieces and cook 2 minutes
7. remove from heat and stir in barbecue sauce and cheese
8. divide dough into 4 pieces and roll out into 8 inch circles
9. place 3 / 4 cup - 1 cup of filling in each circle
10. fold dough in half and seal edges tightly
11. bake at 350f for 15-20 minutes or until top begins to brown slightly
12. for oamc: cool and freeze at this point
13. defrost in the oven or microwave before serving
14. serve warm with extra barbecue sauce to dip if desired
demonstrations.review: Enjoyed these -- what I would call 'fun food'.  The dough was easy to work with,very buttery though!, and it made four large size calzones.  The filling was good but I have to reconsider the BBQ sauce..perhaps blending it with some tomato sauce would be more to my liking..I cut back the amount to 1 1/2 cups which was still too much and I did have filling left over;  maybe I'll start with 1 cup next time and see how that goes.  I guarantee there will be  a next time..and a time after that and..you get the picture!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot hot fudge sundae cake

this is a nice fudgie cake for dessert. the cake can stand while you are whipping up a quick main course eg a grill and salad.

1. spray inside of 2- 3 1 / 2 quart crock with cooking spray
2. mix flour , sugar , 2 tbs cocoa , baking powder and salt in medium bowl
3. stir in milk , oil and vanilla until smooth
4. stir in nuts
5. spread batter evenly in slow cooker
6. mix brown sugar and 1 / 4 cup cocoa in small bowl
7. stir in hot water until smooth
8. pour evenly over batter in crock
9. cover and cook on high 2- 2 1 / 2 hours or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
10. turn off crock
11. let cake stand uncovered 30- 40 minutes to cool slightly before serving
12. spoon warm cake into dessert dishes
13. spoon sauce over top
14. 6 servings
demonstrations.review: Outstanding! Perfection in just 2 hours of no fuss free time after an easy prep. I used pecans and half milk, half yogurt. We had company staying and I made it 2 days in a row because it went over so well.  I won't be without this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with tomato  avocado  and shrimp

this features an "uncooked" sauce, but the pasta will warm it a bit.  sauce the pasta as soon as it is cooked and serve it immediately.

1. combine all ingredients except pasta in a large bowl
2. toss with the olive oil
3. salt and pepper to taste
4. set aside let rest at room temperature until you fix the pasta
5. when pasta is ready , toss with the sauce and serve immediately
6. serve with your favorite wine
demonstrations.review: Easy. Love the 'uncooked' aspect of the dish, and found this to be a great hot weather meal. It's a salad, really, pleasantly cool and cooling. The basil heightens the flavour of the dish, brings it together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
becky s quick   easy special stove top tuna casserole

a quick, easy one pan meal that won't heat up the kitchen on those hot summer days! kid friendly, if you omit the capers and use the lemon juice option vs. the wine. we like ours topped with parmesan cheese at the table. hope you enjoy.

1. cook egg noodles in boiling salted water til al dente , drain
2. return noodles to the pan
3. stir in the soup , onion , peas , drained tuna , milk , wine or lemon juice , and the pepper
4. heat over medium-low heat , stirring occasionally , until thoroughly hot
5. reduce heat to low and stir in the capers , cheese and the chopped eggs , if using
6. continue to stir until cheese is melted and mixture is hot and bubbly
7. serve topped with grated parmesan cheese , if desired
demonstrations.review: Wunnerful, wunnerful comfort food, not reserved for summer only. This turned into a two pan preparation, as I prepared the pasta (used fusilli) then added milk, 1 egg, and cheddar cheese, and then the can of mushroom soup.  In the other, a large skillet, I sauteed 1/2 cup diced onion plus 1 tbsp dried onion, 1 celery stalk diced, and then added 2 cups each baby spinach and baby bok choy, which I chopped. Added some white wine, 1 cup peas, pepper, capers, and sauteed till greens were wilted.  Added this to the pasta pot and combined.  Sprinkled some parmesan cheese on top.  This was so good I know I'll make it again.  Wunnerful, or have I said that already.  Thanks for your posting, BecR

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked butternut squash stuffed with apples and sausage

this is the ultimate comfort food, as we turn the corner into fall and cooler weather. it's simple and fills the house with great smells and the tummy with a nourishing, delicious meal. enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. lightly oil baking dish
3. half squash lengthwise and remove seeds
4. arrange squash cut side up on the baking dish
5. brush lightly with oil and cover with foil
6. bake until almost tender , 30-40 minutes
7. keep the oven on
8. meanwhile , crumble the sausage into a skillet and cook over medium heat until no longer pink
9. add apple
10. cook , stirring until crisp-tender
11. let cool slightly
12. scoop out the squash , leaving 3 / 8 inch thick shells
13. lightly mix the squash pulp into the sausage mixture breaking up squash as little as possible
14. mix the butter , brown sugar , pecans , sage , salt and pepper
15. pile the stuffing into the squash halves
16. dot with bits of butter and brown sugar
17. bake uncovered until piping hot and brown and crusty on top , 20-25 minutes
18. let cool for several minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I'm adding this to my Great Recipes list.  It was amazing!  I used regular beef sausage, unpeeled apples and omitted the pecans (only because I didn't have any in the house).  I dotted the tops with the mix of brown sugar, butter, sage, and salt and pepper, which did away with the second round of butter and brown sugar.  The other great thing about this recipe is that I prepared the whole thing in the morning and it kept in the fridge till suppertime when all I had to do was pop it in the oven. A BIG thank you, chef Jan Marie!

target.recipe_text:
they could be sliders  if eaten with eyes closed    white castle

a slightly "mock" rendition of white castles sliders, but we think only better. great "kid" sized burgers or even better for "adult" sized snacks! note: since posting this recipe i have found out that pepperidge farm no longer makes the small rolls in the pans so therefore use your own disgression on which rolls are available to you but i do suggest that you use a small size like a dinner roll in order to get the full "white castle" affect!

1. brown ground beef , and drain
2. stir in cheese , soup and onion , til cheese melts
3. cut buns in half
4. spread burger mixture on buns
5. wrap in foil
6. bake 350 for 15-20 minutes
7. open from foil and top each with pickle slice
8. serve immediately , with eyes closed
target.review: Everybody loved these. I wasn't sure if I was supposed to individually wrap these in foil, so I put them all on a foil lined cookie sheet and covered them with a sheet of foil and baked. Turned out perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kelly s cheese potato casserole

i know there are a lot of these, but i do make them a little different. everyone always asks what i put in them! so here's how i make them. enjoy!!

1. in large bowl combine well everything but the potatoes , crackers and butter
2. fold in potatoes well
3. pour into 13x9 glass baking dish
4. smooth top even and flat
5. mix crackers and butter and evenly sprinkle over the top
6. bake in 350 oven for 45 minutes
7. let set 5-10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: These were soooo good! I have made alot of different cheesy hashbrown casseroles and this one is the best by far. I doubled the recipe and made 2 pans for Easter. Everyone loved them and came back for seconds! I also left out the celery and rosemary, but I bet it is very good that way too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers broccoli cheese soup   2 pts per cup

i got this recipe from someone at my weight watchers meeting. i don't know where the original recipe came from. it's very low points and i can eat it every day without getting tired of it.

1. mix chicken broth , frozen broccoli and tomatoes and chilies together
2. simmer for 25 minutes or until veggies are tender
3. cube velveeta and put into soup pot
4. simmer just until cheese is melted
5. this recipe freezes and refrigerates well
6. i make a large recipe at the beginning of the week and use it to snack on when i'm in danger of breaking my diet
7. i can have a large bowl and some crusty bread with it and still be under 5 points
demonstrations.review: Made this tonight to start off our New Year's diet. Super good. My husband, I, and 3 of our children ranging from ages 12 to 3 gobbled this up and said it was the best soup.;) I added two Tbls. cornstarch and sprinkled with garlic powder, onion powder, and pepper also added 12 oz. reduced fat Velveeta. I also pureed one of my bags of broccoli,but left the other one as whole florets. We will be making this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel apple cheesecake bars with streusel topping recipe

paula's home cooking, episode: winter warmers. these were enjoyed by all! many different layers of taste.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a medium bowl , combine flour and brown sugar
3. cut in butter with a pastry blender or two forks until mixture is crumbly
4. press evenly into a 13 by 9 by 2-inch baking pan lined with heavy-duty aluminum foil
5. bake 15 minutes or until lightly browned
6. in a large bowl , beat cream cheese with 1 / 2 cup sugar with an electric mixer at medium speed until smooth
7. then add eggs , one at a time , and vanilla
8. stir to combine
9. pour over warm crust
10. in a small bowl , stir together the chopped apples , 2 tablespoons sugar , cinnamon , and nutmeg
11. spoon evenly over cream cheese mixture
12. sprinkle evenly with streusel topping
13. bake 30 minutes , or until filling is set
14. drizzle with caramel topping
15. make strusel topping:
16. in a small bowl , combine all ingredients
demonstrations.review: Cant.Stop.Eating.These.  They are amazing! Halved the recipe and they turned out great. These would be awesome for a Thanksgiving dessert. I thought these would be very time consuming considering all the different layers but I had these babies together in no time. In the picture I took they were almost gone, there was a ton more. I cut them into squares and then diagonal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butterscotch haystacks

tasty treats good for any occasion, these haystacks are mounded with a mixture of peanut butter, butterscotch chips, marshmallows and chow mein noodles. to enjoy in a snap, make them the microwave way.

1. microwave morsels in large , microwave-safe bowl on medium-high power for 1 minute
2. stir
3. microwave at additional 10- to 20-second intervals , stirring until smooth
4. stir in peanut butter until well-blended
5. add chow mein noodles and marshmallows
6. toss until coated
7. drop by rounded tablespoon onto prepared baking sheets
8. refrigerate until ready to serve
9. double boiler method: melt morsels over hot water
10. stir until smooth
11. remove from heat
12. stir in peanut butter
13. transfer to large bowl
14. add chow mein noodles and marshmallows
15. proceed as above
demonstrations.review: This is one of my favorite recipes of all times!!! My daughter had to make a snack for her class that started with the letter N, so we used this recipe and made nests, we filled them with speckled jelly beans. They look adorable!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s juicy hamburger burger

we all have our different tastes for burgers i like mine flavorful and juicy this recipe will give you the best of both! see the bottom of the recipe for tips on even more extra juicy burgers! --- making a indentation in the middle of the uncooked burger will prevent the burgers from puffing up into meatballs shapes while cooking and keeps them flat --- do not add any salt into the burger mixture as the dry onion soup already has a lot of salt content, you can sprinkle some on towards the end of cooking if needed, if desired you may add in 3-4 tablespoons of your favorite barbecue sauce to the ground beef mixture

1. in a bowl crumble the ground beef with clean hands
2. add in the dry soup mix , egg , garlic , breadcrumbs or crushed soda cracker crumbs , worcestershire sauce , black pepper and hot sauce
3. using clean hands mix until combined , add in more breadcrumbs or cracker crumbs if needed to just hold the mixture together
4. divide the ground beef into 6 equal patties
5. using your large finger or the back of a small spoon make a shallow dent into the center of each patty
6. place the patties onto a large plate or a small cookie sheet
7. cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate for a minimum of 6 hours or up to 24 hours to blend flavors
8. grill or pan fry the burgers as desired until cooked through
9. serve burgers in toasted buns with choice of condiments
demonstrations.review: I used to despise homemade hamburgers. Not anymore. I knew I could count on this recipe to change my mind. My husband said they were of restaurant quality. Topped them with pepperjack cheese and the usual toppings. Soooo good! I will always come back to this recipe when looking to make perfect burgers. Thanks again for another wonderful recipe!

target.recipe_text:
it s a gouda   hot ham sandwich

it doesn't get better than this!  ham and gouda with a hint of sweet and a dash of spice.  created for rsc no. 11.

1. if using a strong onion or shallot , peel and soak in ice water
2. preheat oven to 425 degrees
3. slice roll almost in half and lay open on a baking sheet
4. combine mustard , honey and cayenne in small bowl , then spread on both halves of roll
5. layer ham across both halves of roll , spread preserves over ham
6. dice shallot and sprinkle over preserves , then top with cheese
7. place in hot oven until cheese melts , about 3-4 minutes
8. fold to close sandwich before serving
9. enjoy warm or wrap tightly to serve later
target.review: Congradulations.  I tried to make this in time, but I couldn't find any raspberry preserves.  Made it.  My only problem was it was too sweet for our taste.  Next time I'll leave out the honey in the mustard.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheese and molasses beans

this recipe is posted in response to a request. it's from the marlboro country cookbook. i haven't tried it yet.
note to world tour participants.  this is a typical ranch/chuckwagon/cowboy type recipe - common in the southwestern region of the u.s.

1. fry bacon in large skillet
2. pour off fat , return 3 tbsp fat to skillet
3. fry onion and garlic in fat until tender
4. add pork and beans , brown sugar to taste , molasses and steak sauce
5. stir to mix
6. simmer 30- 45 minutes
7. crumble bacon
8. add cheese to beans just before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe if your going to a picnic or pot luck.  It would even be good for an everyday meal if you have kids.  To me it was too sweet for just a nightly meal.  Next time I'll cut down on the brown sugar.  No kids in this house.  The flavors worked well together.  I'll cook it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer  n bbq braised country style pork ribs

this recipe comes originally from the 

1. brown the pork in a lightly sprayed skillet on all sides
2. place the ribs in an oven proof pan and scatter the onions all around them
3. pour in the beer and seal with a lid or tin foil
4. bake at 375f until the pork is tender 1 1 / 2- 2 hours
5. pour out the beer
6. slather the pork with the bbq sauce and bake uncovered for 1 more hour or until the meat is brown and the sauce is thick
7. enjoy
demonstrations.review: I loved this.  My only problem with the recipe was the cooking times.  In order to keep this from burning, I had to turn the oven down to 300 degrees.  Very good flavor, but you have to keep a close eye on it while it's cooking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
demonstrations.review: This came out better than expected.  I made a gravy instead of extra sauce.  The run-off of juices in the gravy complemented the meal well.  Once a month we cook, what we call a TV dinner.  Pick a frozen dinner and look at the picture and go home and cook it.  Meatloaf was the choice.  I'm glad we picked that one.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy sausage casserole

this is a very easy casserole dish and is a change from ground beef. it's excellent with fresh rolls and a salad.

1. cook crumbled sausage in fry pan
2. add peppers , onion
3. remove seeds from zucchini do not peel
4. add to sausage and peppers
5. saute til vegetables are tender and sausage is cooked
6. put cooked noodles in a large casserole
7. add tomato sauce , tomatoes and sausage mixture
8. add spices and crushed garlic clove and combine all ingredients to coat the noodles with the sauce and sausage
9. sprinkle cheese on top
10. cook uncovered for about 30 minutes at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: To me this dish had no taste.  If it wasn't for the sausage, witch I make it wouldn't of had any flavor.  The first thing I would do is remove the basil and oregano.  Change it to 3 teaspoons of Italian seasoning. Use two or more garlic cloves.  Otherwise the cooking method is sound and works.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern living pinto beans

this has been my pinto bean recipe for the past many, many years. tried and true! time does not include soaking for dried beans.

1. place beans in a large dutch oven , and add water to cover
2. bring to a boil , and cook , uncovered , 30 minutes
3. drain
4. add ham hock , tomatoes , broth , and next 10 ingredients to dutch oven with beans
5. cook 55 minutes or until beans are tender
6. serve over rice with southwestern cornbreadin a cast iron skillet
7. dried pinto beans may be substituted for fresh
8. however , wash and sort beans
9. then soak overnight in water to cover
demonstrations.review: I was looking for something even a non-pinto bean person would eat.  I still didn't find it , but this is the best recipe I have cooked.  The only difference was I added water at the end and had to cook for about 20 minutes longer.  I wanted the pot liquer for sopping with biscuits.  Otherwise, made exactly as written.

target.recipe_text:
perfect  chocolate frosting

this is now one of my favorite chocolate frostings. i got it from "the chocolate cake mix doctor" by anne byrn. i have made a few changes to the recipe. actually, i didn't have the 1 cup of semisweet chocolate chips that the original recipe called for. lennie came to the rescue (thanks!) by figuring out the appropriate amount of semisweet squares to use, which i did have on hand. now i always make it with the squares instead of the chips. this frosting is very thick, creamy, and fudgy. i usually bake two 9-inch layers, cut them into four layers, and slather this frosting on each and every layer and all over the top and sides--because i like a little cake with my frosting :) another thanks goes out to leeannr for making me post this recipe. now she loves it as much as i do.

1. place a large bowl , filled halfway with ice , in the sink
2. in a medium size pot over medium low heat , melt chocolate , cream , and butter
3. stirring constantly , cook the mixture until all of the butter and chocolate melts and thickens
4. cook for 5-6 minutes
5. do not let boil
6. remove pot from heat
7. whisk in the sifted confectioners' sugar until mixture becomes smooth , then put the pot on top of the bowl of ice
8. beat with an electric mixer on low speed for 4-5 minutes until frosting becomes smooth , thick , and fudgy
9. remove from ice
10. spread onto cooled cake layers
11. the frosting will thicken as it sets up
12. if the frosting gets too hard to spread , put back on low heat and stir constantly until you get the spreading consistency desired
13. i have been adding 1 tbs
14. of light corn syrup to the initial heavy cream and chocolate mixture to add more glossiness to the frosting
target.review: I made this for my 3 year old's birthday cake (Something Special Birthday Cake #89883). I have never had so many compliments! I didn't bother to sift the sugar, and I think I probably beat it on too high a speed but it turned out wonderfully!  I also added the corn syrup.  So decadent! I think this will become a standard in my kitchen.  Thanks taylortwo!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan chicken casserole

came up with this easy recipe when looking for something just a little bit different.  smells divine while cooking, tasty and comes together quickly. although i used macaroni noodles, any kind of pasta you like can be used. enjoy!  *tip - to easily cut up boneless chicken, partially freeze it first and use a sharp smooth (non-serrated) knife.*

1. cook pasta , drain
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees
3. heat butter and olive oil together gently over medium heat
4. while noodles are cooking , mix bread crumbs , italian seasoning , and parmesan cheese in a large ziplock bag or bowl with tight-fitting lid
5. place diced chicken in the bag or bowl and shake vigorously , coating chicken with bread mixture
6. cook chicken in butter / oil mixture until cooked through , and browned on all sides
7. layer baking dish with noodles , 1 / 2 sauce , 1 / 2 shredded cheese , chicken , remaining sauce , remaining cheese
8. bake 30 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I used a lot more sauce (I had some frozen marinara) and thighs instead of breasts and panko instead of breadcrumbs. I also added ricotta mixed with cheese, egg and spinach and assembled it much like a lasagna. I ate it again for lunch today and it's even better! Thanks for the inspiration to make the most of what I had on hand!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy oven baked barbecued chicken

really this is such an easy recipe i wasn't going to even bother posting it, i have been making this for years and when you can't barbecue outside this is the next best thing! --- sweet baby ray's bbq sauce works really well or use your own favorite, i most always use my recipe#232433 and prepare the sauce a day ahead --- i did not list the amounts for the seasoned salt and garlic powder as i never measure but probably use about 2 teaspoons each for all the chicken pieces, i usually use about 2 cups sauce but a little more or less is fine -- boneless, skinless chicken breasts work well also but cooking time will need to be reduced, you will *love* this!

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a jelly-roll pan
3. pat chicken dry using paper towels , then place skin-side down on the jelly-roll pan
4. season the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder and black pepper
5. turn skin-side up and season again
6. cover the pan with foil and bake for 45 minutes
7. remove from oven and carefully drain all fat from the pan
8. pour the barbecue sauce over the chicken turning the pieces over to coat with the sauce
9. return to oven uncovered and bake for about 30 minutes more or until if cooked through
demonstrations.review: Another go-to recipe from Kittencal! I was craving BBQ chicken and didn't feel like grilling but really dislike the soggy, rubbery oven baked BBQ I've made in the past.  No more!  The rack is brilliant as is the rest of the process.  Thank you for another keeper!  My kids gobbled it up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
family favorite oatmeal pancakes

this recipe was from an old church cookbook and is a favorite breakfast treat in our family-kids and dad!

1. pour milk over oats and let stand 2-5 minutes
2. beat in eggs , oil , then remaining ingredients
3. mixture will be thin
4. fry on hot griddle
5. serve with honey butter , or favorite topping
demonstrations.review:
I soak the oats for a bit longer (more like 10 minutes) and use 1 cup of flour. I also add a dash of cinnamon and vanilla.  YUM!  My 3 year old son asks me to make them every morning.  Thanks for a new favorite recipe for OUR family!

edit: after making these at least 2 times a week for the past several months (my 1 year old is now the one who demands peecocks every morning) I now use 1/2 c. oat flour and 1/2 c. whole wheat flour, a dash of oat bran and walnut oil.  I've also used rice milk with great success.  Wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken nuggets

easy chicken nuggets that my kids like. they dip theirs in ketchup. i like them dipped in marinara sauce or honey mustard.

1. add the first 5 ingredients to a zip-top plastic bag
2. shake to combine
3. cut chicken into 1-inch pieces
4. dip the chicken pieces into the melted butter , then add a few at a time into the breadcrumb mixture
5. shake to coat
6. place on a lightly greased baking sheet
7. bake at 400 for 20 minutes or until tender
demonstrations.review: I used boneless skinless thighs because that's what I had on hand. I also cooked them for 20, turned and cooked for 5 more and these nuggets were perfectly seasoned and crispy!  I also like to use panko instead of the breadcrumbs. My 4-year old said they were awesome! My 18-month old refused them but he's not a meat kinda guy so his vote doesn't count! Thanks for the quick and easy recipe that I'm sure will become a standby in our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: I made this with bone-in thighs and removed them to reduce the sauce and it took longer than I expected, maybe because I doubled the sauce, but since it said to be patient it turned out beautifully. My husband was amazed at how well it turned out, he'd chided me for not searing the thighs before adding the sauce.  Glad I saw it in the top ten or I might have forgotten it!  Even my picky 15 month old ate it.  That's saying something, he usually refuses to eat chicken and he couldn't get this in his mouth fast enough! I served this with brown rice and broccoli

target.recipe_text:
grammie bea s  chocolate fudge

this is an "out of this world" old fashioned recipe that my gram always made when i was growing up, and she always brought it out when company came, and that was often!

it is one of my 3 favorite fudge recipes, and it is delicious!!! i am posting the other 2 also.  this fudge is different than most fudges, not the soft creamy kind... has a different texture and taste...  all i know, is it's one that will have you back in the dish searching for more, till it's gone :)

1. stir first 4 ingredients together in a heavy cast iron pan
2. bring to a boil
3. boil briskly until mixture forms a soft ball in a glass of cold water
4. take off stove
5. stir in marshmallow , walnuts and vanilla
6. you can also add a heaping t
7. of peanut butter too !
8. pour in well greased 9x13" pan , and let cool
9. cut into 2" squares , and refrigerate if desired
10. store in airtight container
target.review: People at work raved about the fudge I made and brought in to snack on.  This fudge is amazing!  Make sure you get it to the right temperature and it will come out just the way it is supposed to.  Also, make sure you let the fudge completely cool before cutting.  I am making some more next week for my families cookie trays.  They are going to be very happy with this choice!  Thanks for sharing your recipe Linda!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s chinese duck sauce

i use this on crab rangoon, chicken fingers, spare ribs, egg rolls, marinated chicken wings, beef teriyaki, chicken teriyaki, and of course rice.

1. combined all ingredients in a med-sized pan , and bring to a boil
2. turn the heat down , and simmer uncovered until all the fruit is very soft , about 30 mins
3. , or longer
4. when room temperature , mix well
5. put in a container , and store in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This sauce was so good with our Recipe #72124.  I used both plums and apples.  This is so much better than the orange stuff you get in many Chinese restaurants, that I can't even begin to tell you!  This is something I will keep as a staple, because it is so versatile and it is really delicious!  I drizzled it on our Fried Rice too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grandma vi s green jello salad

served at my grandma's house for every holiday occasion as long as i can remember. you wouldn't know there is cabbage in this unless you saw the ingredient list! tastes like fruit and whipped cream!

1. drain juice from can of crushed pineapple into a measuring cup
2. add enough pineapple juice to make 2 cups
3. bring the 2 cups of juice to a boil
4. remove from heat and dissolve completely 2 pkgs
5. of lime jello in the juice , stir , stir , stir
6. add all the cream cheese pieces using a gravy whip to blend
7. add 6 ice cubes and pineapple , stir until ice dissolves
8. put in the freezer until cool and syrup-like
9. fold in chopped nuts , cabbage , and cool whip
10. refrigerate several hours
demonstrations.review: Made as a test run for our annual halloween party.  The kids loved it even with the cabbage.  I added in some shredded carrots to make it even more festive for the occasion.  We will be using this one.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic italian meatballs

meatball recipes are often challenged by chefs who claim, "mine are the best!" even though my meatballs are the best, i will make no such claim. try them for yourself! this meatball recipe was given to me by my father who got it from a little old lady from italy that he knew. it's amazing that she gave up her recipe to him, but i sure am glad she did!

1. mix all ingredients in a large bowl by hand
2. use your bare hands for best results
3. roll meatballs to about the size of a golf ball
4. drop raw meatballs into large pot of sauce
5. simmer for about 3 hours
demonstrations.review: I made these to test run to use in a recipe for bloody eye balls for our annual halloween party.  Very good meatballs, that I think everyone will enjoy.  I know my kids loved them.  We will be using this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jhal frezi chicken  easy and delicious

this is an easy and delicious pakistani/indian recipe that is wonderful with any kind of pakistani/indian or middle eastern bread (chapati, naan, roti, pita, and if you just can't find/make any, then even soft tortillas) or basmati rice. "jhal frezi" means "dry fry" so there is not a lot of sauce when this is finished. you can find most spices in the spice section at your grocery store but you can get more for the same prices at an indian/middle eastern market.

1. heat the oil in a medium or large skillet over med-high heat
2. add the onions and saut 2 minutes , add garlic and saut 2 more minutes
3. add the chicken , ground turmeric , chili powder and salt
4. fry for 5 minutes constantly stirring everything
5. add the can of tomatoes , bring to boil , cover and simmer on med-low to low heat for 10 minutes
6. add ground cumin , curry powder , ground coriander ginger , and the optional green chilies , stir , cover again and simmer for another 10 minutes
7. remove cover , raise heat to to medium to evaporate some of the excess liquid , 7-8 minutes
8. add the butter / ghee , and cilantro , simmer on low 5-7 minutes and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I made this and had jasmine rice on the side, and my family and I woofed it down in no time!  Slightly hot and spicy, it was just right for us!  I served with some naan.  I vouch for this one... It's good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linda s mexican veggie pizza

i always make these for pot lucks, or when i need an appetizer for a special occasion... they are a big hit, and i always make them for the holidays to munch on before dinner!  you can also omit the taco seasoning mix and salsa and use 1 pkg. seven seas ranch dip mixed in with the cream cheese instead, to make just a regular veggie pizza.  it is also very good!

1. preheat oven to 375
2. roll out crescent rolls onto a lg
3. non-stick baking sheet
4. stretch and flatten to form a single rectangular shape on the baking sheet
5. bake 11-13 minutes in the preheated oven , or until golden brown
6. allow to cool
7. place cream cheese in a med
8. bowl
9. mix cream cheese with taco seasoning mix and taco sauce
10. adjust the amount of taco seasoning mix , to taste
11. spread the mixture over the cooled crust
12. arrange carrots , bell peppers , broccoli , onion and black olives on top
13. press down with hands
14. chill in the refrigerator approximately 1 hours
15. cut into bite-size squares to serve
demonstrations.review: I made a half batch as a test run for an appetizer for our annual halloween party.  The kids couldn't leave them alone, and it looked so pretty with all the colors of fall (green broccoli, red, orange and yellow peppers, carrots). Just what I was looking for.

target.recipe_text:
spicy asian cucumber salad

i received this via email update from america's test kitchen. i'm looking forward to employing some of our bumper cucumber crop on this.

1. bring vinegar and sugar to boil in saucepan over medium-high heat
2. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until mixture reduces by half , 5 to 6 minutes
3. transfer to medium bowl and cool to room temperature
4. whisk in lime juice , ginger , chile , and sesame oil
5. toss in cucumbers , scallions , and basil
6. season with salt and pepper , and let sit for 10 minutes or up to 1 hour
7. serve
target.review: Perfect for the Thai Turkey dish as a side.  It's just the two of us so I used 1 cucumber and cut the marinade in half just like JanuaryBride.  I also substitued lemon juice since I didn't have lime and it was very good.  I didn't have fresh or whole dried red chilli peppers so I used red pepper flakes for the heat.  I will keep this recipe on hand and make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
morrocan chicken with couscous

posted for zwt6.

1. in a large bowl , combine the flour , paprika , salt , and pepper
2. add the chicken and mix so that all sides are well covered
3. in a large , heavy pot , heat the olive oil over medium-low heat
4. add the chicken in batches and cook , turning occasionally , until brown on all sides , about 10 minutes
5. add the sweet potato or yam , onion , garlic , bay leaf , cumin , cardamom , cinnamon , saffron , raisins , dried apricots , and chicken broth
6. bring to a boil , then reduce the heat to medium-low
7. cover and simmer for 1 hour , or until chicken is tender and the potatoes are very soft
8. taste and adjust the seasoning if necessary
9. uncover , add the couscous and mint , and stir
10. reduce the heat to low
11. cover again and simmer for another 5 minutes
12. turn off the heat and allow the pot to sit , covered , for 10 minutes
13. uncover and , using tongs or a big fork , fluff everything in the pot
14. put the lid back on and let sit for another 3 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was very good and my first attempt at a Morrocan dish.  Husby thought it was "okay" but my two dinner guests raved about the complex flavors.  I used a little extra chicken stock (4 cups) so that I could use the whole box of stock and used just a little (1/4 cup) extra couscous and it was very good.  Be careful not to use too much couscous as it will soak up all the sauce and be dry.  Also use new dried spices as it will add to the flavor!  YUM

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: The dry bread crumbs made the topping taste stale - maybe fresh would be better.  I followed exactly and it was just okay - I have a parmesan chicken recipe that uses fresh and it crisped up better without getting mushy on the bottom.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallion sesame turkey burger

i found this in some random cookbook.  one of the best turkey burgers ever.  full of flavor.  make an extra for lunch the next day, reheats beautifully.

1. mix togeter , gently
2. the turkey , sesame seeds , soy , scallions , cilantro , garlic , sesame oil , 1 teaspoon of salt , and bread crumbs
3. form into patties
4. i usually mix all this together and make patties in the morning and leave in the refrigerator till i'm ready for them
5. sometimes that is the next day
6. brush with a little oil before grilling if desired
7. grill on the george foreman , in a grill pan
8. if you're using the outside grill increase the breadcrumbs a bit to insure they don't fall apart
demonstrations.review: YUM YUM YUM.  I made exactly as written and then grilled and basted with a honey haberno glaze I had on hand.  So flavorful and juicy.  This combination works so well that I wouldn't change a thing.  I can't wait to have the leftover burger for lunch!    SO GOOD!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy burrito casserole

satisfy your craving for something different tonight. it's good and fairly easy. this is stuff i usually have on hand too.

1. brown ground meat / turkey & onion
2. drain
3. add taco seasoning and stir in refried beans
4. mix soup and sour cream in a separate bowl
5. spread 1 / 2 sour cream mixture in the bottom of a casserole dish
6. tear up 3 tortillas and spread over sour cream mixture
7. put 1 / 2 the meat bean mixture over that
8. add a layer of cheese
9. you could put some hot sauce on this now
10. repeat the layers
11. sprinkle cheese over the top and bake , uncovered , at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a hit at the Mexican themed Super Bowl party.  I followed pretty closely except for adding about 1/2 lb. of chorizo to the ground beef when browning and I used 8 oz. of sour cream instead of just the four.  As other people have said you can play around with adding/substituing and using lowfat substitutions.  It's a great recipe and I will be making it again - EASY too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown rice  baked

brown rice is so much better for you than white rice. it has more nutrients and about 3 times more fiber than white rice does. 
i never really cared for brown rice until i tasted this one. you can do as many variations as you like with it. add your favorite herbs, spices or veggies to it. make it vegetarian by using veggie cubes instead of chicken. the rice turns out perfectly fluffy and delicious. the aroma that fills your house while it's baking is wonderful and it's hard to wait until it's done to sneak a taste. as it bakes the bay leaves will rise to the top so they can be easily 'fished' out of the casserole before serving. i like to top the finished rice with freshly chopped cilantro and a twist of black pepper. for a nice crunch you can add chopped water chestnuts.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. heat heavy skillet until hot
3. add oil and then add uncooked brown rice
4. stir rice in oil until golden brown , stirring constantly
5. in the meantime heat water and add bay leaves , bouillon cubes , poultry seasoning , black pepper , minced onion flakes , parsley , oregano , basil and pepper flakes
6. bring to a boil
7. when rice is golden and ready , pour rice into a covered 2 quart casserole dish
8. add the boiling liquid on top of the rice
9. careful ! it will sputter
10. cover casserole with aluminum foil and the cover for the casserole dish
11. bake for 1 hour
12. remove from oven and let sit covered for 15 minutes
13. fluff with fork before serving
demonstrations.review: Perfect texture and flavor.  I used 1 tbsp. olive oil to brown the rice.  Also used vegetable broth instead of water/bouillon.  Other than that followed directions exactly and it was light, fluffy and flavorful besides being easy to prepare.  Will do again, OFTEN!

target.recipe_text:
italian tortellini soup

i can't remember where i got this recipe but it is irresistible.  my dh loves this.  it is meaty and stick to your ribs delicious.  enjoy!

1. remove sausage casing
2. in dutch over brown sausage
3. remove sausage
4. reserve 1 tbsp drippings
5. saute onions and garlic in drippings until onions are tender
6. add broth and next 7 ingredients , and add sausage
7. bring to boil , reduce heat and simmer uncovered 30 minutes
8. skim fat from soup and stir in zucchini and remaining ingredients , except parmesan cheese
9. simmer covered an additional 35-40 minutes until tortellini is tender
10. serve topped with parmesan cheese
11. if you prefer to use fresh tortellini , simmer 20-35 minutes until tender
target.review: i saw this in a gooseberry patch cookbook, the only difference was using a 16 oz can of diced tomatoes instead of the 4 med tomatoes.  we absolutely love this.  i use the dried cheese tortelllini in the macaroni isle.  i also made this with ground beef instead of the sausage, also ground chicken and also chunks of chicken breast with chicken broth.  great anyway i make it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
devil bites

these little bites are so good that you swear that the devil is tempting you from the diet, but they are low fat little delights that my whole family loves!

1. heat oven to 375
2. in a large bowl , beat brown sugar and margarine until light and fluffy
3. add vanilla and egg white
4. mix well
5. add flour , cocoa , baking soda and salt
6. blend well
7. stir in chips
8. drop by teaspoonfuls on to ungreased cookie sheet
9. shape gently into balls with your fingers
10. bake at 375 for 8-9 minutes
11. cool 1 minute on sheet and then transfer to let cool
demonstrations.review: we loved these!  my son was skeptical about the chocolate with the butterscotch chips, but it turned out to be a great combination.  i do want to try these with other chips, but it will be hard as we loved the butterscotch so much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek style turkey burgers

the best turkey burgers i have ever tried .... i freeze left-overs, and heat in the microwave later ...

1. combine all the ingredients in a large bowl
2. form into 4 patties , then grill
3. i have served this on regular burger buns with tomatoes and mayo , and on pita with tahini , tomatoes and lettuce
demonstrations.review: these are my absolute new favorite.  very flavorful indeed.  i make the recipe as is and only add the olives to half as my husband won't eat them.  He doesn't care for  turkey burgers, but loves these.  Thank you so much for the recipe.  I mix them up and freeze two patties for another day.  I thaw before cooking.  I usually do these on a grill pan on the stove.  Delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
7 vegetable chicken stew with dumplings

a delicious meal on a cold evening. you can also use skinless boneless chicken thighs if you prefer dark meat. i sometimes add mushrooms too, making it an 8-veg stew!

1. in a large pot , combine chicken , all veg except peas , stock and spices
2. bring to a boil over high heat
3. reduce heat to medium-low and simmer , covered , for 20 minutes
4. stir in peas
5. meanwhile , in a food processor or by hand , make dumplings: combine flour , parsley , butter , baking powder and salt until mixture is in coarse crumbs
6. stir in milk , then drop by tablespoonfuls onto the hot stew
7. you should have about 6 mounds
8. cover pot and simmer-- don't boil hard and don't lift the lid-- for 15 minutes or until dumplings have risen
demonstrations.review: this was absolutely delicious!  very filling too.  i didn't think it would be enough for us, so i doubled the recipe.  i really didn't need to.  i had half left over and my husband and son had third helpings.  try this and enjoy! (my son didn't believe he ate rutabaga.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry cream cupcakes

i got this recipe from giada de laurentiis' show everyday italian.  they are so easy to make, but very aesthetically pleasing as well.  the whipped cream is a light and refreshing touch to the cupcake.

1. line 18 muffin cups with muffin papers
2. preheat the oven to 350 degrees f
3. using an electric mixer , beat the cake mix , water , egg whites , melted butter , almond extract , and vanilla extract in a large bowl for 2 minutes , or until the batter is well blended
4. using about 1 / 3 cup of batter for each cupcake , spoon the batter into the prepared muffin cups
5. bake the cupcakes until they are very pale golden on top , about 15 minutes
6. cool the cupcakes completely on a cooling rack
7. using a fork , coarsely mash 1 1 / 2 containers of raspberries in a medium bowl
8. beat the cream and 1 / 3 cup of powdered sugar in a large bowl until firm peaks form
9. fold the mashed raspberries into the whipped cream
10. remove the muffin papers from the cupcakes and cut the tops off of each cupcake
11. spoon the raspberry whipped cream atop the cupcake bottoms
12. place the cupcake tops on the cupcakes
13. dust with more powdered sugar and serve with the remaining berries
demonstrations.review: this is the most delicious cake.  i made this and my son started eating it without frosting.  i now follow this for all my white cakes.  i made a white cake for our strawberry social and everyone wanted to eat my cake even without strawberries.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken with garlic and rosemary

a simple chicken dish ideal for a family supper,serve it with a simple green salad and steamed baby potatoes

1. wipe chicken with damp cloth and place in casserole dish
2. mix oil , lemon juice , stock powder and seasoning together and drizzle over chicken
3. add lemon slices , garlic cloves and rosemary
4. roast in a preheated 200c oven for about 35 minutes
5. you will need to shake the pan from time to time during the cooking process to prevent sticking
demonstrations.review: My son chose this for Sunday dinner.  Everyone loved it.  I did not have the chicken stock powder either, and it was fine without it.  I will make this again, and next time i will try it with the chicken stock powder to see the difference.

target.recipe_text:
rumbled eggs

the beauty of rumbled eggs is that they cook practically on their own, and it's very hard to ruin them by overcooking.

1. put a saucepan of boiling water over a low heat
2. put the butter in a bowl and stand it in the saucepan to melt , while you beat together the eggs , salt , pepper and water
3. when the butter is hot and clear , pour in the egg mixture and stir twice
4. they can then be left over the gently simmering water while you set the table
5. give them an occasional stir as you pass by to prevent the eggs at the bottom from sticking
6. as soon as the eggs are the consistency of clotted cream remove the saucepan from the heat and the eggs will keep hot over the hot water until they are needed
7. serve on buttered toast
target.review: I just had to try this recipe simply because it looked so odd!  DH and I had for a late breakfast on a Sunday morning...FANTASTIC!  Served on buttered toast and it was just awesome!  Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut joys

we always made these for our christmas cookie plates. they are similar to the popular mounds candy but the unsweetened chocolate gives it a bit more kick. you'll want to use real butter and not margarine or chefs spread and the quantity of candies you get will depend on how large you make them.

1. in large saucepan melt one stick of butter
2. add sugar and coconut to butter mixing until well blended
3. form balls of dough appx 1-2 teaspoons making thumbprint wells into middle of balls
4. melt unsweetened chocolate in microwave safe bowl appx 1-2 minutes stirring occasionally
5. pour melted chocolate into wells
6. chill until chocolate is firm
demonstrations.review: These are the BEST at Christmas!  My mom has made these for the past 25 years or so and they go fast!  Instead of using the unsweetened chocolate squares, I use the premelted unsweetened chocolate and snip a corner of it off.  Less cleanup (which I like!)!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
great pumpkin dessert

this is a quick cooking magazine recipe that i have used over and over for treat days at work.

1. mix pumpkin , milk , eggs and sugar
2. add spice
3. transfer to a greased 9 x 13 baking dish
4. sprinkle with dry cake mix and drizzle with melted butter
5. top with walnuts
6. bake at 350 for 1 hour or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
7. serve with ice cream or whipped cream
