3. add flour , salt , cinnamon and soda and mix well
4. blend in egg-raisin mixture , oatmeal , and chopped nuts
5. dough will be stiff
6. drop by heaping teaspoons onto ungreased cookie sheet , or roll into balls and flatten slightly
7. bake at 350 degrees for 10 to 12 minutes or until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: Merrie, Merrie, Merrie,  this recipe is dangerous and should come with a warning!  It is indeed, the best oatmeal cookie recipe ever!  I doubled it, used about a third less sugar (I was almost out of brown) and added 1/8 teaspoon of nutmeg.  They were killer.  I am ashamed to admit that I ate 3 Ziploc bags full and had to give the rest away so that I wouldn't continue to binge.  I have never had a cookie that is so addictive.  I'm afraid to make more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken parmigiana

nan

1. cut whole chicken breasts into halves
2. in bowl , beat egg , salt , and pepper
3. dip chicken into egg then coat with crumbs
4. in large skillet , saute chicken in butter or margarine
5. arrange chicken and eggplant in crock pot with eggplant on bottom
6. pour pizza sauce over chicken
7. cover and cook on low 6 to 8 hours
8. add mozzarella cheese 15 minutes before serving
9. top with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: This dish is wonderful!   Followed exact recipe.  Very easy.  I will use a larger eggplant next time.<br/>I used Prego Traditional sauce.  Absolutely delicious! You can't go wrong with this, everybody loved it.  I will be cooking this for many years to come.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers chicken stroganoff for the crock pot   4 points

this is one of the many recipes that i wrote down while attending my weight watchers meetings.  very easy to throw together in the morning and have a wonderful meal when you get home from work.  the original recipe calls for 98% fat-free cream of mushroom soup but i prefer the chicken.  either one can be used interchangeably.

1. place the frozen chicken in the bottom of a crockpot
2. mix the other ingredients together in a separate bowl and pour it over the chicken
3. cover and cook on low for 7 hours
demonstrations.review: Winner, Winner, Chicken Dinner! <br/> Just wonderful.<br/> Made according to recipe and while cooking, I read a few reviews that said "Uh oh, salty!" So, I popped the lid and tasted after about 4 hours of cooking, sure enough, a bit salty.  I peeled a small potato, cut into 3 pieces and tossed it into the pot in what was now "gravy".  3 hours later, pulled out the potato slices and threw in some raw mushroom slices just to heat.  Served on plain white rice. Not salty and very tasty.   Nice entree.  I will make again.  <br/>Great dish for pot luck.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic batter waffles

this hearty waffle recipe comes from an issue of parent's magazine. ive made it every week for years and it comes out great every time. i double it and freeze the leftover waffles and reheat in toaster oven.

1. mix all dry ingredients together using a large whisk
2. mix the wet ingredients together
3. gently combine but don't overmix
4. cook as your waffle maker directs
5. sprinkle with powdered sugar
6. cover with toasted nuts , bananas , and real maple syrup
7. pour on log cabin and michele's maple cream syrup for my husband !
demonstrations.review: Just made these today.  Delicious, family loved them.  These had a rise similar to Belgian waffles without the extra beating of the egg whites.  Light and fluffy.   I made the full recipe and freeze the leftovers in bags of two.  Easy to reheat in the toaster.  A keeper for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potsie s creamed chicken and biscuits casserole

this is a wonderful and simple to prepare comfort food using things you probably already have around. kids love it- but so do adults. at least, in this home. try it. it is one of my quick and easy favorites. this is my first submitted recipe... be kind.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease the bottom and sides of an 11x7 inch baking dish or 10 inch quiche dish
3. chop the onion
4. heat butter in a small nonstick skillet and saute until tender
5. combine cooked onion , soup , chicken , milk , pimiento , and mayo in a bowl and then turn into the prepared baking dish
6. bake for 15 minutes and remove from oven
7. sprinkle 1 cup of the cheese over the baked mixture
8. arrange biscuits decoratively in a single layer and sprinkle remaining 1 / 2 cup cheese over them
9. return casserole to oven and bake until biscuits are golden brown and sauce is bubbly , usually about 20 minutes longer
10. the last time i made this i used a 1 / 4 cup of fat free mayo and 1 / 4 cup of sour cream
11. i think it was delicious ! also -- i took the suggestion of adding a cup of cooked green peas
12. what a terrific idea ! i loved it ! i think i might add two cups next time
13. thanks to you all for making my humble recipe and leaving your suggestions
14. you greatly improved a recipe i was already proud of
15. thanks so much
demonstrations.review: We loved it but it is very rich.  Wonderful basic recipe that begs to be "played with".  As other reviewers have stated, there's lots of possibility for variation and I will be trying some of them.  It is so great to get the input from so many creative cooks.

target.recipe_text:
yes  virginia there is a great meatloaf

absolutely delicious meatloaf and sauce! those who claim they don't believe there can be such a thing as a great meatloaf will love this. based on a meatloaf given to me by a dear friend, virginia strehl, memphis, and leesburg, fla. nita holleman, 2000

1. meatloaf: combine meat loaf ingredients and place into a loaf baking dish
2. smooth out top
3. sauce: combine sauce ingredients and pour on top and sides of meatloaf
4. bake at 350f about 1 hour to 1 hour 15 minutes or until done
5. enjoy !
6. the addition of 1 or 2 teaspoons of kitchen bouquet makes this recipe very good
7. recipe should be"plump" from the addition of the milk or half & half
8. it should not be runny
9. a second batch of sauce served hot is good to serve with the meatloaf
10. nita's
11. it is wise to have some fat added to the deer -- especially to ground deer
12. maybe 25 % fat , , otherwise your results will be poor
13. i don't know about some of the other game meat some are using
14. please consult an expert
15. the recipe is delicious as it stands ! enjoy ! nita holleman
target.review:
I had 30 pounds of ground beef 
and made meat loaves in 9 pound batches ( & one 3 pound batch)
I x6 all ingredients (for 9 lb batches) EXCEPT
I used water instead of milk due to allergies. The sauce I found 1 batch for a 1 1/2 pound loaf as written in the receipt was enough to cover 
3 ,3 pound loaves. 
Cooked all  the loaves , cooled and sliced in three inch slices , froze on cookie sheets and when frozen packed in gallon zip lock bags  for quick meals.
Freezes very well.
Did eat one three pound loaf same day cooked and left overs made wonderful cold meat loaf 
sandwiches.  The left over meat loaf also is great crumbled and used with recipes for ground beef
 adds  a wonderful flavor to beef and rice etc.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dark chocolate cake

while it takes slightly longer to prepare this recipe than a box mix, the resulting moist, delicious cake makes it very worth the little extra time. i consider this 'perfect' chocolate cake. this cake is excellent with  both with recipe #261024 and recipe #208959 (the dark flavor version). (i use recipe #95416 when i'm decorating the cake.) i love how the leftovers are still moist even a day or two later. (i store my loosely covered with plastic wrap.)
my father adores this cake with recipe #261024 on it. for his birthday, father's day etc. i make him cupcakes with the icing on them and individually wrap them. he keeps them in his freezer for when he wants "a piece of cake". he claims they are as good as when they are fresh. 
(even though it isn't where i got the recipe from so i can't vouch for it, reviewers have said it is the recipe on the hershey's cocoa can. i would recommend using their special dark cocoa if possible.)

1. heat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour two 9 inch round baking pans or one 13x9 inch pan
3. in large mixer bowl , stir together dry ingredients
4. add eggs , milk , oil , and vanilla
5. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
6. stir in boiling water by hand
7. i usually use between 2 / 3 & 3 / 4 cups
8. the cake is still very moist but it doesn't seem to "fall" as much as it cools
9. this might have to do with our high humidity or brand of flour or other factors so i don't know if it will work for everyone
10. pour into prepared pan
11. bake 30 to 35 minutes for round 9-inch pans , 35 to 40 minutes for rectangular pan or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
12. because they have a tendency to overflow if you fill them more than 2 / 3 full , i usually get about 27-28 cupcakes per batch
13. bake for approximately 18-20 minutes
14. cool 10 minutes
15. remove from pan to wire racks
16. please
17. chocolate drink mixes that you add to milk or water to drink will not work in this recipe
demonstrations.review:
Made this for my son's birthday...SOOO easy!
My husband wanted me to use a box mix and I argued it was cheaper and as fast to make home made.He was amazed at how fast this came together and the taste was fantastic! Best of all it was so economical.
It took me less than 10 minutes to get it mixed and in the oven, including  the pans preparing pans!
The flavor was moist and a nicely  rich  chocolaty flavor and rose very nicely. I choose to use a whipped vanilla frosting with milk chocolate shavings on top.
Was a hit with everyone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
outback steakhouse copycat bread  gluten free

close your eyes and this is pretty much the real thing! and you thought you'd never be able to eat outback's bread again! this copy cat recipe is based off of recipe #25456 and converted to a gluten free version. i recommend eating within 1 week. i used two mini loaf pans and one regular sized loaf pan only because i don't have more minis. (you can add food coloring to get the dark color too, but i figured i'd just keep it natural and close my eyes!) nutritional information (including flours, etc): 123 cal, 2.3 fat, 1 sat fat, 22 carbs, 1.8g fiber, 7g sugar, 3g protein. (slightly over 2 points a slice with ww)

1. whisk together dry ingredients in a medium bowl
2. mix together the wet ingredients in a mixer , then slowly add the dry while leaving the mix on low
3. then mix on high for 4 minutes
4. grease and flour two loaf pans
5. using a spatula , distribute the dough between the two pans
6. loosely cover with plastic wrap and let rise in a warm moist place for 90 minutes
7. loaves should just about double in height
8. bake at 350 degrees for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review:
A gluten free bread worth eating! I used unsweetened Almond milk in place of dairy milk. I too used potato starch instead of the sorghum flour and canola oil in place of butter. Popped it in my Zojirushi bread maker on quick bread and with it's 3 risings 
the texture was close to "regular"bread . I think next time I might try it with a bit less instant coffee though. When in the bread maker I was tempted to add more flours, because it was like cake batter not at all like "regular" breads in a nice tight ball.  I was surprised how it all came together and tasted wonderful. Now I can have sandwiches again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flour tortilla recipe

recipe for making flour tortillas from thibeault's table.  credit to ann from the gardenweb internet addy as the majority of this receipe comes from her post: http:// ths.gardenweb.com/ forums/ load/recipex/ msg0611460316237.html?7 
i like this easy recipe for tortillas that uses staples usually on hand.  i am battling cancer and cannot eat yeast or sugar, so tortillas are a great alternative to bread!

1. sift the flour , salt & baking powder into a large mixing bowl
2. into the dry ingredients cut in the shortening , or add oil if you are using this option , & mix with your finger
3. add the milk or water , working the liquid into the dough until a sticky ball forms
4. wrap in plastic and let rest for at least 30 minutes
5. divide the dough into 8-10 balls or 6-8 balls for larger ones , cover them again with the damp cloth
6. lightly dust a counter or pastry board w / flour & roll out each ball of dough into a circle or oval approximately 1 / 4" thick
7. if you want nicely rounded tortillas , trim off any ragged edges & discard
8. don't roll the dough out more than once or the tortillas will be tough
9. heat a dry griddle or heavy skillet over high heat for 5 minutes
10. cook the tortillas 30 seconds on each side or until the dough looks dry & slightly wrinkled & a few brown spots form on both surfaces
11. do not over cook or they will be hard
12. butter and roll up and wrap in damp tea towel to keep warm as you cook the other tortillas
13. serve warm
14. ~~
demonstrations.review:
Simple recipe and besides the 30 minute rest time for the dough , it was very quick to make. the tortillas were the best I've ever eaten and my husband agreed!
I made them a bit thicker than recommended in the recipe and it was like a flat bread. When warm spread butter and cinnamon sugar on so delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburgers with brown gravy  total comfort food aka  meat cakes

these are sooooo great (and ez)! i grew up eating these about once a week and they are incredible with mashed potatoes or buttered egg noodles and a veggie. while this recipe is basically my mom's, i have changed one thing...instead of using chopped onion in the burgers, i use an envelope of onion soup mix...it gives them the perfect flavor! this is now one of my family's favorite meals...try it and it will probably become one of your's, too. p.s. these burgers also work for grilling (without the gravy :).

1. combine ground beef , bread , soup mix , salt , pepper , ketchup , garlic powder , parsley and eggs in a large bowl until well mixed
2. prepare each burger with approx 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture and form into patties about 1 / 2 inch thick
3. heat a 12" skillet over med-high heat and fry burgers for about 5 minutes on each side , until they are almost done
4. remove burgers to a plate and discard all but about a tablespoon of drippings from skillet
5. lower heat under skillet and prepare brown gravy with water in a bowl or measuring cup
6. slowly pour into skillet , stirring constantly , scraping up any brown bits from the bottom
7. when gravy has thickened , place burgers back in the pan and cover
8. simmer for about 20 minutes , or until burgers are done
9. serve with mashed potatoes or egg noodles
10. yummy !
demonstrations.review:
I made these into large  meatballs and left out the gravy. I used homemade oatmeal bread(heartier bread)
These were great, moist and tender.
Family was asking for more!
Froze so perfectly too. Can take from freezer and pop in microwave for a few minutes and they were moist and tender, just like fresh.
Never had that happen before!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the italian buffalo

this is so easy and healthy that it's a regular at our house, though sometimes we use gr. turkey or beef too. thanks to my friend tabatha who had us over for dinner and introduced me to this recipe.

1. brown buffalo , drain grease and set aside
2. in large saucepan , saute onion and garlic in olive oil until tender
3. add buffalo , tomatoes , spinach , basil and oregano
4. heat through , mixing thoroughly
5. add salt and pepper
6. serve over rice or pasta
7. or cover a pizza crust with tomato paste , top with this and mozz
8. cheese , and bake
9. mmm
demonstrations.review:
This is very good!

 I used fresh tomatoes and fresh oregano, otherwise I followed recipe.
Wonderful flavor that lends it self easily to pizza, pasta, rice, taco's .I could easily go on.
Will be making this often!

target.recipe_text:
incredibly delicious cheese garlic bread spread

easy, cheesy, savory spread to transform regular bread into a taste sensation! goes awesome with pasta dishes or beside a fresh salad.

1. microwave margarine in medium glass bowl for about 40 seconds or until its melted
2. mix in all ingredients , using a fork
3. spread the mixture over bread
4. place on baking sheet and bake for about 10 minutes at 450 , until the top is golden brown
5. easy !
target.review: I made spaghetti for dinner tonight and decided to try out this bread...wow! sure am glad I did! It's so easy to prepare, spreads well and is very very tasty.  Excellent recipe, SarahFish...thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mom s chocolate cake

i can't believe i'm sharing this family recipe. it's the signature jansen family recipe and no family gathering is complete without it. i'm submitting it for a request for recipes and ideas for a sleep-over/birthday party event. it's from my mom, it's old, i have no idea where it came from. no need to drag out the mix-master for this, just a bowl and a pot is all you need.

1. combine sugar and flour in a large bowl
2. boil 1 / 4 c cocoa , water , 1 / 2 lb butter in a medium sized sauce pan
3. pour chocolate mixture over flour and sugar mixture and stir well
4. add buttermilk , beaten eggs soda and vanilla
5. pour into a jelly roll pan , bake at 400 for 20 minutes
6. while cake is baking , make frosting
7. combine frosting ingredients , except for confectioners sugar , in the same sauce pan used for chocolate mixture above
8. boil , then add confectioners sugar
9. pour over hot cake , sprinkle with nuts , and let set for an hour or two
10. serve and watch the smiles and requests for the recipe
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness, Jude...this is the exact cake my mom used to bake for special occasions! It's also the very first thing I learned to bake when I was just a little girl(pre-teen). Thanks for posting this fabulous recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review:
Excellent! I used a 3 lb rump roast and didn't deviate from the recipe. Well..maybe I did, but just a little. I added baby carrots and potatoes when I started the roast. Perhaps the next time I prepare this yummy roast I'll toss in a bell pepper and/or an onion. Thanks for sharing such a great recipe!
...txgammi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  geraldine s ground beef casserole

this recipe came from a local church fund raising cook book. mrs. geraldine is a good friend of the family. she reminds me so much of mrs. clause, that i can't help but smile every time i think of her. this recipe freezes well. do not bake before freezing. just put it together, freeze it, thaw it and cook.

1. brown meat in large skillet or dutch oven
2. add onions , pepper and celery and simmer for 15 minutes
3. add tomatoes and tomato sauce , mushrooms , brown sugar and worcestershire sauce
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. cook in skillet for 1 hour
6. place cooked pasta in bottom of large casserole dish
7. spoon mushroom soup over pasta
8. pour sauce over the soup and top with cheese
9. bake in 350f oven for 30-45 minutes
10. can sizes do not have to be exact , just as long as they are within a close range , everything will work out
demonstrations.review:
Excellent, Jellyqueen! I cooked down some fresh tomatoes for a few mins and added them instead of using canned. I also added a bit of garlic and used elbow macaroni since I was out of angel hair pasta and spaghetti (it's raining and I didn't want to go to the store). Yummy! This recipe is a keeper and will be made again. Thank you for sharing it, and please extend my thanks to Mrs. Geraldine.
...txgammi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaica cake

my mom clipped this out of some magazine eons ago and it was one of the first things i ever learned to bake as a girl. it is still a trusted stand-by for unexpected guests or when i just want something easy and sweet. no mixer and no frosting needed! great when you first bake it, even better the next day. i usually use 2 bananas, but sometimes use 3 if i want a strong banana flavor.

1. mix together the sugar , vegetable oil , pecans , flour and bananas
2. stir in the eggs , pineapple , vanilla , baking soda , cinnamon and salt
3. mix well but try not to mash the bananas
4. pour into a 9x13 inch pan and bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 60 minutes , or until cake tests done
5. can also use a tube or bundt pan , but you'll need to lightly grease and flour those
demonstrations.review:
Delicious cake, Kat...I made this cake the night before Memorial Day so we would have it for the cookout. (You had said it was good, but even better the next day) I loved being able to just mix the ingredients together with my trusty wooden spoon instead of getting out the mixer. It smelled wonderful while baking, turned out beautifully and sooo moist! I had SUCH a hard time staying out of it! It reminded me of my mom's fresh apple cake (which is marvelous) but yet was different. Thanks for sharing a terrific cake recipe!
...txgammi

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried potatoes   onions

this is a comfort food recipe from my youth. and a excellent side dish.

1. in 12 inch covered skillet add enough oil to cover bottom about 1 / 4 inch thick
2. add sliced potatoes and quartered onions
3. add salt and pepper to taste
4. cover and cook over medium heat , stirring occasionally till potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: I've been making these potatoes for 30 yrs and they are sooo good! I've never fried them in Canola though, having also used Crisco. Will certainly try that next time. They're also delicious fried in bacon grease.

target.recipe_text:
madagascar chicken

a very different way to spice up the same old chicken! plus a name that may unspire kids to get excited about the recipe! i found this recipe while searching the web. minor changes have been made to make this even better! note: one pound shelled and deveined shrimp can be added to or substituted for the chicken.

1. grate the lemon rind , removing the yellow only and leaving the bitter pith on the fruit
2. reserve rind
3. cut chicken into bite sized pieces and squeeze the juice of the lemon over the meat
4. allow if to marinate for 30 minutes
5. drain and season with salt and pepper to taste
6. in a hot skillet with a little oil or cooking spray , brown chicken over medium heat leaving chicken only partially cooked
7. remove chicken and discard any oil , leaving just a light film or spray pan again
8. add onions and cook until slightly browned
9. add bell pepper and garlic and saute for 3 minutes
10. reduce heat to simmer , add coconut milk , ginger , cayenne powder , and grated lemon rind
11. return chicken to pan , cover and simmer 30 min or until in thick stew consistency
12. if mixture is too thin simmer with lid removed until desired consistency is reached
13. serve over a bed of steamed white rice
target.review: This was good and easy to prepare. The cayenne pepper and ginger give it some heat- so might want to take it easy if you only like mild spice. I used lite coconut milk to cut down on calories. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
avocado salad with cumin lime mayo  dressing

delish! adapted from everyday with racheal ray magazine!

1. in a glass or woodenbowl , whisk together olive oil , mayonnaise , lime juice , honey and cumin
2. season with salt and pepper
3. in a large bowl , combine the lettuce with the dressing
4. top with the avocado pieces
5. serve and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yummy! We loved this. We are cilantro fans, so I threw all ingredients, including cilantro into a mini food processor. I forgot the honey until the very end and am not convinced the dressing needs it. May go without the honey next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheddar spinach and  mushroom pie with puff pastry crust

this is a perfect luncheon dish! you will need a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate, i used fresh sliced mushrooms in place of canned that i sauteed firstly when i made this, and i also added in a small chopped red bell pepper but that is optional. if you use more than 1 cup sauteed fresh mushrooms i suggest to use a 10-inch pie plate instead of 9-inch and roll the puff pastry out a little larger.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. prepare a 9-inch glass pie plate
3. roll out the puff pastry sheet to an 11-inch square , then transfer to prepared pie plate
4. trim edges
5. in a bowl beat the cream cheese until smooth
6. add in the half and half and eggs
7. beat until combined
8. squeeze out any moisture in the thawed spinach well using you hands before adding inches
9. add in all remaining ingredients
10. mix with a wooden spoon to combine
11. pour into puff pastry crust
12. sprinkle with about 1 / 2 cup grated parmesan cheese
13. bake for about 25 minutes , or until the filling is set
14. cool for 10 minutes before slicing and serving
demonstrations.review: Fabulous! We loved this recipe. The only changes I made were: small white onion chopped and sauteed instead of green onion (personal preference). I sauteed a clove of minced garlic with the onion. Will make again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned corn and potato chowder

this really is old fashioned! it comes from 

1. combine , in a large pot , all ingredients except milk and flour / water
2. cook until potatoes are fork tender
3. add milk and flour / water , stirring well
4. bring to a boil and allow to cook for 10 minutes
5. serve with chopped green onion and shredded cheese as a garnish
demonstrations.review: Great for a cold winter day! We really enjoyed this. I made a few small modifications. I sauteed the onion and about 1 clove of minced garlic in the butter before adding other ingredients. I did this in the soup pan. The soup was a little thin for my taste, so I added 1/2 tsp of corn starch and then the texture was perfect. I finished with some nutmeg and topped with shredded cheese and bacon pieces.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy tuna casserole  low fat

cooked chicken breast may be used in place of the tuna, if desired add in 1 cup low-fat grated cheddar cheese to the soup mixture, this is only optional --- for weight watcher's program 1 serving = 7 points :)

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease an 11 x 7 or 13 x 9-inch baking dish with cooking spray
3. boil the pasta in a large pot of boiling water until al dente
4. drain then transfer to a large bowl
5. add in onion and tuna
6. toss to combine
7. in a saucepan heat soup with milk until smooth
8. stir in mushrooms mayonnaise , mrs dash seasoning , garlic powder and black pepper until combined
9. pour into the bowl and toss to combine
10. transfer mixture to prepared baking dish
11. bake for about 30 minutes
12. remove from oven then sprinkle with cheddar cheese , return to oven for 2-4 minutes to melt the cheese
demonstrations.review: Great & easy. I used fresh sliced and sauteed mushrooms. I thought about sauteing the onions with the mushrooms and then changed my mind. Glad I did- as the slight crunch of the onions was nice! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy v 8 pot  roast

don't worry if your not a spicy food lover, we don't find it spicy at all-

1. in a large dutch oven brown the roast on all sides in oil
2. remove roast and drain off excess oil
3. in a bowl combine the garlic , v-8 , water , horseradish and the worcestershire sauce
4. replace the roast in the dutch oven and pour the combined ingredients over the roast
5. bake , covered 325' for 2-2 1 / 2 hours or until very tender
6. transfer the roast to a warm platter , cover with foil to retain heat
7. for the gravy measure cooking juices
8. skim away the fat
9. if necessary add enough water to measure 1-1 / 2c
10. return juices to dutch oven , combine the remaining 2 tablespoons water and the cornstarch , stir into the juices
11. cook and stir over medium heat until bubbly
12. cook stirring constantly for 1 minute
13. serve gravy with the roast
demonstrations.review: This was great- thanks LeezaH4! I followed the other reviewer's recommendation and used my crockpot. I browned the roast first and then cooked it on low in the crockpot (with first 7 ingredients) for 8.5 hours. I added some veggies for a 1 dish meal- chopped onion, 1/2 green pepper, 4 carrots (cut in 1 inch pieces) and 6-7 new potatoes. When it finished cooking, I added the cornstarch in the crockpot and put on high for 15 minutes. i will make this one again! And we agreed that this was not spicy.

target.recipe_text:
sweet and spicy ground turkey stir fry

i put this together for a light meal when i noticed that we had too big a collection of half-bags of frozen vegetables and little containers of leftover cooked veggies. the kind and quantity of the vegetables can vary according to what you have -- you just need to end up with between 2 and 3 lbs. some people prefer a more generous amount of thickened sauce on their stir-fry dishes. with a diabetic in the house, i skip that part but i've included the directions if you want it.

1. brown ground turkey in a little oil over medium-high heat
2. drain any excess grease leaving just enough to accomplish the stir-frying process
3. add garlic , onion , coriander , and a tbs of the soy sauce
4. stir well
5. begin adding the vegetables starting with long-cooking veggies like carrots and broccoli , and working towards the quick-cooking greens but not adding those just yet
6. just before adding the greens -- right after adding the beans or snap peas -- add the remaining soy sauce , the sugar , the sherry , and the red pepper flakes
7. stir well so that sugar dissolves and pepper flakes are well distributed
8. add the greens and complete the cooking
9. make the optional sauce if desired by whisking the cornstarch into the chicken stock
10. pour into pan just before the greens are done and cook , stirring constantly , until the sauce has simmered for about one minute
11. serve over rice , ramen noodle , or other preferred , asian starch
target.review: This was good. We didn't think it was spicy at all, so we'll add something to it next time. Maybe more red pepper flakes. We did add a chopped red bell pepper this time. The dish is really low-calorie, so we'll probably make this whenever we need to get back into the diet habit. It involves a LOT of chopping, so I'm thinking about chopping mass quantities of vegetables during the weekend and storing them in the refrigerator so that we can grab what we need during the week and quickly throw this together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled salmon with creamy tarragon sauce

i'm trying to incoporate more fish into my diet, and this one looks quick and easy sounds wonderful! from the current issue of 

1. brush salmon on both sides with oil
2. coat grill rack with nonstick cooking spray before starting the grill
3. place salmon , skin side down , on grill rack
4. grill , covered , over medium heat for 20-25 minutes or until fish flakes easily with a fork
5. for sauce , combine the remaining ingredients in a small bowl
6. serve with the salmon
demonstrations.review: Delicious! We had to use plain Greek yogurt thinned with skim milk because, strangely, we couldn't find any regular plain yogurt at the grocery store. We made the sauce for 4, but had only 2 servings of fish, so we used the rest of the sauce as a veggie dip. It was great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean scampi

who does not like scampi.  you have had scampi the usual method, with loads of garlic and extra virgin olive oil... now have scampi my med-way, and you won't go back.... have plenty of baguette to soak up all the sauce... so good, you will be sorry when it is all gone.   winning recipe entry, rsc#7.

1. in a large skillet or deep fast fry pan , melt butter
2. be careful it does not burn
3. saute the garlic
4. when golden in color , remove from heat and set aside for later use
5. add onions , saute until just softened
6. remove from heat and set aside for later use
7. add plum tomatoes with their juice
8. lemon juice , white wine
9. bring to a boil
10. add onion and garlic which you had set aside
11. add roasted red bell peppers
12. turn down heat and allow liquid to reduce
13. add fresh herbs
14. add shrimp and steam until pink
15. add capers and olives
16. allowing them to warm through
17. turn out onto a warm platter or serving bowl -- garnish with lemon wedges , and serve while hot
18. serves 4 - 6 comfortably
19. cook time - approximately 45 minutes , including peeling and chopping
demonstrations.review: Seriously - this took me FOUR hours to make from start to finish. I have never been so irritated with a recipe in my entire life. I don't know how anyone could possible prep this in 20 minutes (as it's listed). It was good, but certainly not great. That is 4 hours of my life I will never get back. I would highly recommend against making this. If you decide to make it, use canned tomatoes, bottled roasted peppers, ez-peel shrimp, and bottled minced garlic. Thank God that I got lucky with the olives - when I opened the jar, I was surprised to find that they were already pitted. I never want to see this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian stallion  bloody mary italia

this yummy italian style mary is sure to engage your guests in great conversations. take a pitcher of  this festive drink to a holiday party and you’re sure to be the star! you can cut the zucchini with mini-cookie cutters into star shapes and triangles for a festive stallion. add to a pretty toothpick and a couple of olives, and you have a party in a glass. if you want a spicier stallion, use spicy v-8 juice. this recipe is for six servings; for single serving, use the second set of instructions.

1. for 6 drinks:
2. pour vodka , tomato juice , worchestershire , and pesto into a large pitcher
3. stir in chili powder , cumin , and pepper
4. cut zucchini in thin strips or using a decorative mini-cookie cutter , make fun shapes
5. using a slice of lemon , wet the rim of each glass
6. dip the glass into salt , making sure the rim has salt all around
7. add ice to glasses
8. pour mixture into each glass , add olives and thin zucchini spear for stirring or use zucchini shapes and olives on a toothpick
9. set on the edge of each glass
10. add a straw
11. for one drink:
12. 1 oz vodka
13. 5 oz tomato
14. dash of each spice
15. 1 / 2 t pesto and worchestershire
16. mix in glass and serve
demonstrations.review: Very tasty. Rather than rubbing a lemon along the rim of the glass, I just put a squirt of fresh lemon juice in the glass. We didn't bother rimming the glass with salt and I'm really glad we didn't! Even without added salt, the drink is very salty, but it really is very very good. We will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
speedy ziti with zesty chicken

nan

1. prepare pasta according to package directions
2. while pasta is cooking , warm the butter or margarine over medium heat in a large skillet
3. add the onion and cook for 3 minutes
4. stir in the dijon mustard and flour
5. very gradually whisk in the chicken broth
6. bring the broth to a boil and stir in the lemon juice , peas and parsley
7. when pasta is done , drain it well
8. toss pasta and cooked chicken with sauce , season with salt and pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: We had leftover cooked chicken, so I decided to try this recipe to get rid of it. It was good. It wasn't fabulous enough that I would plan to make it again in the absence of a need to get rid of cooked chicken, but it was good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jewels   pasta

beautiful red beets contrast with the pasta in this unusual way of using fresh beets. i found this recipe on a vitamin website.

1. boil beets in their skins for about 45 minutes
2. while beets are cooking , cook linguine in boiling water until done
3. drain linguine , reserving about 1 cup of the liquid
4. rinse beets well under cold running water and slide the skins off
5. chop beets into 1 / 2-inch cubes
6. heat olive oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet and add onions
7. cook onions until tender , and lightly browned
8. add chopped beets and salt to the onions
9. transfer the pasta into the skillet with the beets and onions
10. stir until the pasta and the beets are well combined
11. top with the crumbled feta cheese and the freshly ground pepper
demonstrations.review: We felt that the beet flavor totally masked the flavor of the feta. This really tasted like cooked beets over pasta, which it was. To the extent that I like beets, it was good. I just think it needs something else to add complexity and make it taste like more than diced beets over pasta ... I'm just not sure what that something else is!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
target.review: I think I seasoned my chicken too well because I found it to be really salty.  I love salt so for me to say it was salty I know it had too much for the others.  But I ate it the next day and it was fine, not too salty at all.  what the heck?  The chicken had a great flavor and was so tender.  Will make again but will sub low sodium for the soups and less salt on my chicken.  I'm new to crock pot cooking so I'm sure any complaints or faults are operator error and not the recipe!  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Tried this one for a pot luck with 40 something people, it was hardly touched. It was too "plain" for them.  I liked it and added more seasonings to it to give it a little more kick.  Will try some different things in it next time and see if I get a better result.  It was a great way to use up the 2 chicken breasts that I had defrosted.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: I wasn't real thrilled with this recipe at first.  I used a 4# rump roast and it stayed tough for 8 hrs of cooking.  But after 10 hrs it was falling apart!  I poured the gravy/juices in a pot, cooked it down a bit, added a little cornstarch, and added a can of beef consomme.  That did the trick, it was wonderful on rolls for hot roast beef sandwiches that evening, with lots of gravy.  I will try a chuck roast next time, most crock pot recipes call for that one.  Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: I think this would have been better had I not used frozen broccoli and only one bag of it.  My skillet used was the wrong one for this dish, next time will use my nonstick pan.  I did eat it though and found it had a great flavor. thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cook down home pork chops and gravy

i don't even like pork, but was tricked into tasting this dish when i was told it was chicken. wow! the meat was sooo tender and juicy; so tender in fact, that it was literally falling apart! it was like nothing i'd ever tasted before! definitely not like my mother's hard, crusty pork chops! lol! this recipes goes hand in hand w/ some mashed potatoes. just pour the leftover gravy on the taters' and enjoy!

1. combine 1st four ingredients in a shallow dish
2. dredge chops in flour mixture and set aside
3. combine what is left of the flour mixture w / the chicken broth and pour into your crock pot
4. pour oil into a large skillet and cook the chops in hot oil until browned on both sides
5. place chops in crock pot and cook covered on high for about 2 to 5 hours or until tender
6. serve w / hot rice and / or mashed potatoes
7. ++if the gravy becomes too thick just add a little water
8. if you accidentally add too much water then add a little more flour
9. season w / salt and pepper too your taste
demonstrations.review: These were some great chops.  Tried many crock pot recipes this weekend, this was one of the keepers for sure.  I wilted an onion in the pan after removing chops, added a tiny bit of water to get all the good brown stuff also, and put this in the crock pot also.  Was great and sooooo moist.  It was nice to find a recipe that didn't require cream of something soup for the crock pot, husband hates that type of stuff.  Thank you for sharing this great chop recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raspberry filled almond shortbread with almond glaze

nan

1. in a medium mixing bowl
2. cream butter and sugar
3. mix in the almond extract
4. gradually mix in flour until the dough forms a ball
5. cover and refrigerate for an hour for easier handling
6. preheat oven to 350 degrees
7. roll into 1 1 / 2 inch balls and place on a ungreased cookie sheet
8. using a wooden spoon handle make and indention in the middle of the ball
9. fill with the raspberry jam
10. bake at 350 degrees for 14-18 minutes depending on your oven
11. add aditional raspberry jam if desired
12. remove and place on wire racks for cooling
13. mix the glaze ingredients
14. using a butter knife letting the glaze run off the butter knife , zig zag the mixture across the cookies creating a continuing z
demonstrations.review: these cookies are the biggest hit with certain relatives of mine for family dinners.  I love almond and raspberry!  I try to only make these for a gathering because I will eat the entire batch myself if left alone with them!  thanks for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
ashley s pecan squares

delicious, classic pecan squares, a favorite.

1. combine flour and powdered sugar in a medium bowl
2. cut in butter with a pastry blender until crumbly
3. press mixture evenly into a greased 13x9 inch pan
4. bake at 350 for 15 minutes
5. combine condensed milk and remaining 4 ingredients
6. pour over crust
7. bake at 350 for 25 minutes or until golden
8. cool
9. cut into squares
target.review:
Very easy, very good results!  I had difficultly finding Almond brickle chips so I used Heath toffee brickle piece instead. Had I thought of it sooner, I would have also included slivered Almonds with the pecans.
These pecan squares are very rich (sweet) a little goes a long way.
this would make an excellent food gift for Christmas presents.
BDavis Hudson, FL

demonstrations.recipe_text:
somen noodle salad with ginger cilantro dressing

a copycat recipe of a trader joe's pre-made salad i have tried to duplicate. all ingredient amounts are estimated.
best results when salad is allowed to marinate. feel free, as i have to play around with the ingredients. for a vegan version, substitute agave nectar for the honey.

1. toast the peanuts and coconut and let cool
2. cook somen noodles according to package directions
3. drain , rinse under cool water and set aside
4. meanwhile grate the carrots and add the diced bell pepper into a serving bowl
5. prepare the dressing by mixing the ingredients well in a blender and then toss together with the vegetables and cooked somen noodles
6. refrigerate at least 3 hours
7. stir together the peanuts and coconut
8. serve salad with toppings on the side
9. garnish with
10. cilantro sprigs and lime wedges if desired
demonstrations.review:
This was excellent - it was served as a side dish with baked chicken.
Once mixed together, I stored it in a large zip lock bag in the frig.  Give it a quick couple of squeezes when ready to eat - you're good to go.  A good idea for transporting to work potlucks or covered dishes.
Easy to store in the frig.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast pork  char shu  chinese

this recipoe came from my mother-in-laws highschool cookbook from molokai. my whole family likes this one!

1. stir together sauce ingredients adding only 1 minced garlic clove
2. place roast in crockpot
3. slice remaining garlic cloves and tuck into roast pour sauce over roast and cook 6-8 hrs
4. turn roast over half way through cooking
5. serving suggestions
6. serve with rice and ramen salad or coconut carrot salad
demonstrations.review:
This was ok - I left out the salt and used a Low Sodium Soy sauce, becasue I'm not big on salt.
The garlic gave it a good flavor throughout,though. Might be better cooked in the oven, than the crock pot - it did tend to be rather dry - but was certainly tender.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa dip

this dip is rich and creamy. dip is good with pumpernickel party bread, a pumpernickel bread bowl, wheat thins, wheat crackers.

1. mix all ingredients together in a 2 qt bowl
2. microwave on high for 4 minutes , stirring after 2 minutes
3. place in refrigerator to chill
demonstrations.review:
I took this to a work function. I doubled the recipe, serving it in a Rye Bread bowl with Pumpernickel cocktail toast surrounding it, and a Pumpernickel Bread bowl with Rye Bread surrounding it.  First the oooohs and Ahhhhs were for the presentation, but once the tasting began -  the real praises started.
I had a least 3 people ask for the recipe - one guy ask me I was the one that made that "rockin" dip...
What else is there to say... it's simple to make, easy to transport (I put it in a large Zip Lock bag and then simply cut a large corner out after I got to work and squeezed the dip into the bread bowls - no fuss - no muss!
BDavis - Hudson, FL

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ukranian peasant borscht

my grandmother always made this borscht in the fall and winter. she never made anything by recipe so this is my version. the kids and neighbors love it and always ask when i'm going to make it again. or tell me i should have made a bigger pot.

1. in a large dutch oven or stock pot , brown bacon and render fat
2. add beef and brown
3. cut the onion , carrot and celery in half cross-wise and add to pot with beef
4. also add beets whole with skin , shredded cabbage and water
5. add pepper corns and bay leaves
6. bring to boil , then turn heat to medium low , cover and simmer 1 1 / 2 hours
7. after an hour of cooking start boiling potatoes whole in a separate pot until soft
8. when soup is ready turn off heat , with a slotted spoon remove the celery carrot and beets
9. discard celery and carrots or use for something else
10. leave beets on a separate plate or bowl until cool enough to handle
11. peel and grate beets back into the soup pot
12. add grated carrot
13. bring soup back to boil
14. add vinegar and lemon juice
15. cook 5 minutes longer
16. to serve place a boiled potato in bowl and ladle soup on top
17. add a dollop of sour cream to each bowl
18. enjoy
demonstrations.review:
An excellent example of how looks (and prejudice)can limit our horizons...
I've never bought "real" beets before - much less with hugh leaves and roots still attached, or carrots with their long flowing leaves still attached - I hate cooked cabbage - to be quite honest I was given this recipe by a friend as a challenge. I was not very excited about it, but my pride forced me to give the whole adventure a try. Mostly because it was so far out of my element (guess I'm picky - don't really care for most vegetables outside of the usual cucumbers, lettuce, tomato - you get the picture )
So... this was like throwing stuff into a garbage can that was a soup pot. It had a pungent aroma (to me at least) while cooking.  I did everything I was supposed to do to it - then let it sit overnight in the frig, because I just couldn't make myself eat it -after making it.  The color didn't bother me nearly as bad as trying to fish all the stuff out of the "borscht" that was suppose to come out.
 I was certain this was so vile it would kill me - Boy - was I ever wrong.  
This was wonderful... I'm still stunned... AMAZING - just simply amazing. The description was right - I should have made a bigger pot! I could have never guess a more different outcome.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker london broil

this is such an easy recipe. it's one of our family favourites.

1. place meat in the bottom of the slow cooker
2. if necessary , slice meat to make it fit
3. in a medium bowl , mix together mushroom and tomato soup
4. pour mixture over beef
5. sprinkle dry onion soup mix over top
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review: I found this to be rather salty - and the meat rather dry. Next time I'd probably use a can of French Onion Soup in place of the dry Onion soup mix, and a more marbled meat, such as a chuck roast in place of the London Broil that I used.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate chip date nut squares

got this from my mother-in-law. if she had told me ahead of time there were dates in this i may never have tried it. mmmmm good
secret: must be prepared day ahead.

1. in medium bowl mix 1 1 / 2 c boiling water and 1 1 / 2 tsp baking soda with the dates
2. set aside to cool
3. beat together margarine , 1 c sugar and eggs in large bowl
4. to this add vanilla extract and date mixture
5. add flour , 3 / 4 tsp baking soda and salt
6. pour into greased and floured 13x9 pan
7. sprinkle 1 / 4 c sugar , nuts and chocolate morsels on top
8. bake @ 325 degrees 45 minutes
9. the difficult part: set aside until the next day to eat
target.review: This is my recipe of the year, and it met with serious competition.  I sent a few squares over to my Mom's and she was on the phone within minutes to ask for the recipe.  I couldn't wait a whole day to try it, so perhaps we should make two - one for today, and the other for tomorrow when they are even better!  This will definitely be a regular in our cookie jar, so thank you, Chicopee, for posting the recipe, and thank you, too, to your Mother-in-law for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft  spicy  heavenly ginger cookies

i found the original recipe for these cookies on allrecipes.com, and modified it to be vegan, as well as by changing the spices slightly. they are truly delicious cookies, and very easy to make.

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy
2. stir in the molasses
3. mix the water and baking soda and stir
4. sift together the flour , salt , and dry spices
5. add gradually to the sugar-margarine mixture
6. gradually stir the sifted ingredients , along with the ginger and raisins , into the molasses mixture
7. shape dough into walnut sized balls , and roll them in the remaining 2 tablespoons of sugar
8. place the cookies 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet , and flatten slightly
9. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: A delicious cookie.  Since I am on a diet, I have managed to resist these (failing only 3 times), and will be taking the tub to my Dad this morning.  He loves ginger and I know he will enjoy these. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate eclair dessert

who would have thought something so easy could be so delicious!

1. mix together vanilla pudding mix and milk
2. fold in whipped topping
3. line 9 x 13 pan with one layer of graham crackers
4. put half of the pudding mixture over the graham crackers
5. place a second layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
6. put the remaining pudding mixture over the graham crackers
7. place a third layer of graham crackers over the pudding mixture
8. heat the tub of frosting in the microwave for 30 seconds to soften
9. spread frosting on the top of the last layer of graham crackers
10. cover with plastic wrap and let set a couple hours or overnight in the refrigerator
11. cut in squares
demonstrations.review: My HUSBAND loved this dessert, and that is saying something.  He seldom ventures further than ice cream and chocolate sauce, so his even trying it is amazing.  The rest of us loved it too, but then we are a lot easier to please.  Thanks, Marianne, for sharing this really good recipe.  Highly recommended.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese mum s chicken

we have a japanese girl, tomoko, living with us, and tonight she and i cooked a japanese dinner for us and her friends. she phoned her mum,toshiko, in japan for this, as it's her favourite recipe, and i wanted to share it here. it's simple and so good, and tomoko, who is only 16, did such a good job of cooking this, then translating the recipe to english for me.

*the liquid will thicken to a glaze if you are patient. it just takes a bit of time. if you feel your chicken is cooked (and going to overcook) remove it before going on to reduce the liquid. same thing, if you must use breast meat, remove it (so it doesn't dry out) and continue reducing the liquid . if you do it this way rather than thickening with cornstarch you will get a richer glaze and not need to add stock or broth instead of the water. it just takes patience. and note: a glaze is sticky and coats the meat, this is not a sauce.

1. place all the ingredients in a saucepan over a high heat
2. bring to the boil , then reduce to a simmer for about 20 minutes
3. remove any scum that rises to the surface
4. increase the heat , turning the drumsticks frequently in the liquid , and cook until the liquid has reduced to a sticky glaze
5. arrange the chicken on a serving platter , remove the garlic clove and chili from the liquid , and spoon the glaze over
demonstrations.review: This turned out so tasty.  I was a little wary, and warned my guinea pig (husband) that it was a new recipe.  We were very pleasantly surprised.  My son claimed the last piece and is going to experiment with reducing the sauce/glaze, and then pouring it over barbecued chicken pieces.  I fancy trying it for oven-baked wings.  I will post any results when we try our variations, but can sincerely assure any timid cook (like me) that this is delicious and well worth trying.  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
our canada meatballs  not your average meatballs

my sil gave me this recipe from the latest issue of our canada magazine. a little time consuming but well worth it. i am sure you will agree there is not another meatball quite like it.

1. in a bowl , combine egg and soup mix
2. crumble beef into mixture and mix well
3. divide into 36 portions
4. set aside
5. in a bowl , combine the flour and milk until smooth
6. add cheese and bacon
7. mix well
8. shape cheese mixture into 36 balls
9. shape one beef portion around each cheese ball
10. in a shallow bowl , beat the eggs
11. place cracker crumbs in another bowl
12. dip meatballs into egg , then coat with crumbs
13. in a large skillet cook meatballs in oil for about 15 minutes , turning to brown on all sides , or until the meat is no longer pink and coating is brown
14. cook and prep time is aproximate
demonstrations.review: These were really good.  I haven't had much luck with meatballs, so was delighted with the result.  I used a no-name-brand cheese cracker and loved the coating.  I think I may prefer these cold, so leave some over (if you can) to try that way.  Thanks, Shirl.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thick chocolate pudding

this is the perfect chocolate pudding. it has a rich chocolate flavor, great texture and is not high in fat. i can't count the number of times i have made this. i hope you enjoy it as much as we do.

1. in a 2-qt
2. microwave-safe bowl , combine the first four ingredients
3. stir in milk until smooth
4. microwave , uncovered on high for 3 minutes
5. stir
6. microwave 4-6 minutes longer or until thickened , stirring after each minute
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour into individual serving dishes
9. cool
10. refrigerate
11. garnish with whipped topping if desired
demonstrations.review: My favourite cold weather treat, and the first thing I make when I ditch the diet!  We serve it with warmed syrup (not maple, but a cane sugar syrup - or golden syrup - found in Australia, South Africa, etc.)  My recipe should probably look like yours, but I have made it with dashes of this and heaps of that for years.  Give it a try.

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin cream cheese layer pie

a family favorite for years.  rich, creamy and a good blend of flavors!  this pie sets up well and provides a pretty slice.  a great pie to impress guests.

1. mix cream cheese , sugar , egg and vanilla well
2. pour into uncooked pie crust
3. place in refrigerator to chill and thicken for approximately 30 to 45 minutes
4. in a separate bowl mix pumpkin , sugar , eggs , cinnamon , nutmeg , salt and milk
5. pour on top of chilled cream cheese layer
6. in a small bowl combine pecans , butter and brown sugar
7. set aside
8. bake in a 350 degree oven for 45 minutes
9. edge of pie may be covered with a foil protector for one-half of baking time to prevent crust from getting too brown
10. carefully remove from oven and sprinkle pecan mixture around in a circle on top of pie
11. place back in oven for approximately 10 to 15 minutes
12. remove from oven and allow to cool slightly
13. chill in refrigerator for approximately 3 to 4 hours before cutting into serving pieces
target.review: This pumpkin pie was AWESOME! I loved the cream cheese layer and the pumpkin layer, and they were great together!  I did vary the crust.  I had some leftover brownies that I did not want to throw away so I made them into crumbs and made a brownie crumb crust for the pie.  It got rave reviews from my guests and my DH and I both enjoyed it too!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yelllow squash casserole

this is a wonderful side dish. even if you think you don't like squash you will like this. good to take to a pot luck dinner!

1. line 8x8 baking dish with half of pepperidge farm dressing
2. cook squash , carrots and onion in just enough water to cover until tender
3. drain well
4. mix sour cream and soup and add drained veggies
5. pour on top of dressing and top with more dressing
6. bake at 350 degrees for 1 / 2 hour
demonstrations.review: This is a great squash casserole recipe.  I asked DH to try it, and he replied "you know I don't like squash casserole but I will try it."  He truly did like it.  I, too, used a larger baking pan, used cream of chicken soup and topped it with crushed cheese crackers.  It was a great hit.  Thanks for posting a new family favorite recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
overnight french toast casserole

great make-ahead breakfast casserole.

1. melt margarine in a 9 x 13 baking pan
2. put 6 slices of bread in bottom of pan
3. in a bowl mix 1 cup brown sugar with 1 tsp cinnamon
4. sprinkle 1 / 2 of this sugar mixture over bread
5. add another layer of 6 slices of bread
6. in a bowl , whisk eggs with milk until well blended
7. pour over bread layers
8. sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture
9. cover and refrigerate overnight
10. bake covered at 350f 30 minutes
11. uncover and continue baking 15 minutes or until set and browned
demonstrations.review: Love this recipe!  I assembled it last night and cooked it this morning for a Christmas Eve brunch.  Everyone raved about it and ate it up!! Some used syrup and some ate it without syrup.  Everyone loved it!  Thanks for posting this keeper recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger or sandwich buns or hot dog buns

what a hamburger bun should be. substantial enough to handle a big burger with lots of toppings and yet have an excellent flavor all of its own. this is more like the kind of bun you'd get with a gourmet hamburger in a restaurant. if you are looking for one like grocery store buns, light and fluffy, these aren't what you are looking for.  (and yes, it really does call for 1 cup of oil)

1. dissolve yeast in water with a pinch of sugar
2. mix in with other ingredients
3. knead for 10 minutes on a floured surface
4. let rise until doubled in bulk
5. punch down and let rise again
6. punch down and form into bun shapes
7. make them on the small side as they do raise a little more when you bake them
8. let rise until double
9. bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes
10. let cool until just warm to the touch
11. place in a sealed bag to soften crust
12. makes 16-20 hamburger rolls
13. double wrap and freeze any remaining ones
demonstrations.review: I just made these buns/rolls for the second time.  My DH says it is the best roll recipe that I've ever tried, so I would give more stars if I could!  I put the ingredients in my bread machine on "dough" setting and let it do the work of the kneading, then flattened them, cut with a glass dipped in flour, let them rise, baked and they were GREAT!  We ate some as sandwich buns and more as dinner rolls.  Thanks so much for this great keeper recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my mil s coleslaw

my mil gave me the 'ingredients only'...........she never measured anything. after several attempts, i got it right. i made her proud. i prefer to chop the veggies rather than grate (like kfc's cole slaw - which this tastes like). servings are approximate.

1. in a food processor , chop cabbage , carrots , peppers and onion
2. chop them one-at-a-time-- not all together
3. put into a large bowl and add remaining ingredients
4. mix well
5. best prepared the day before you plan to serve to allow flavors to blend and juice to form
demonstrations.review: I made this for DH and my Mom tonight and they both loved it.  DH said it was the best cole slaw that I have ever made.  I did use Splenda instead of sugar, and used cider vinegar, but all else is as written.  I will be making this again! thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon patties

yum!

1. empty 1 can salmon with juice into a large bowl and remove bones
2. add 2 eggs
3. add lemon juice
4. stir well
5. add onion , pepper , crackers
6. stir
7. form into 5 - 6 patties 3 / 4 to 1" thick
8. set aside
9. let set 5 minutes
10. in large frying pan heat 1 / 2 inch cooking oilto medium high temperature when oil is hot , place patties in pan and cook 4 - 5 minutes per side
11. make sure they cook all the way through
12. serve with more lemon juice
demonstrations.review: I have made salmon patties from many different recipes, looking for one that I really liked, and THIS IS IT!!  It is my favorite, and so simple.  The saltines are what makes a great improvement in taste over other recipes.  Thanks, Cheri, for posting a winner (and so simple)

target.recipe_text:
grilled mexican chicken salad

we have a fun little restaurant that is only open for lunch. they specialize in different varieties of salads.  this is one of my favorites! i use  recipe #123526 for the chicken breasts.

1. grill chicken breasts on grill , on low heat till centers are no longer pink
2. in a large bowl put in lettuce , black beans , corn , onions , olives , avocados , cheese , and cooled chicken
3. toss and set aside
4. mix dressing w / taco seasoning , set aside till time to serve
5. when ready to serve , toss w / cheese and dressing until all ingredients are incorporated and serve
6. time does not include cooking time
target.review: This is a wonderful, easy salad.  Most ingredients I always have on hand anyway.  I'll admit, most ingredients I didn't measure since I made just 2 servings; our version too was very filling. I substituted sour cream for the ranch dressing & taco seasoning & avacado (I made it at the last minute and didn't have these), and it gave a nice texture and flavor.  The suggested marinade was delicious too!  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and spinach quiche

a filling, hearty quiche. i usually make this for supper but would be good for breakfast, brunch, or lunch.

1. evenly sprinkle 1 / 4 cup cheese onto the bottom of the pastry shell
2. set aside
3. in a mixing bowl , add the chicken , 1 / 2 cup spinach , onion , and remaining cheese
4. stir to combine
5. spoon mixture into pastry shell
6. spread evenly
7. in a bowl , add the eggs , milk , mayonnaise , salt and pepper
8. whisk to combine
9. pour over the chicken / spinach mixture
10. bake at 350 for 40-45 minutes or until knife comes out clean
11. let rest for 15 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: I love the taste of the chicken in this dish!  Next time I'll be sure to whisk the mayo mixture more thoroughly.  I too had to cook this about 10 min longer than listed.  I rated it 4 stars since the flavor is so very rich.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome fajita marinade

we use this all the time . works well with beef or chicken. i also use it to marinate chicken breasts for salads and other uses.

1. mix all well , pour in gallon ziplock bag and meat of your choice
2. marinade in fridge overnite or at least 4 hours
3. grill just till done
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I substitute lemon juice for the lime (for lacking of planning).  I marinated mine for about 30 min (again, for lack of planning), giving our grilled chicken nice, though mild flavor.  Next time I'll marinate it as suggested, and perhaps add more black pepper for a bit more zing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
six sisters  slow cooker honey sesame chicken

i found this on the six sisters' blog and had to try it. i can never get the sauce to thicken in the crock pot so i put the juices in a separate pan, add the cornstarch and cook it on the stove but i posted as it was written.

1. season both sides of chicken with lightly with salt and pepper , put into crock pot
2. in a small bowl , combine honey , soy sauce , onion , ketchup , oil , garlic and pepper flakes
3. pour over chicken
4. cook on low for 3-4 hours or on high 1 1 / 2 2 1 / 2 hours , or just until chicken is cooked through
5. remove chicken from crock pot , leave sauce
6. dissolve 4 teaspoons of cornstarch in 6 tablespoons of water and pour into crock pot
7. stir to combine with sauce
8. replace lid and cook sauce on high for ten more minutes or until slightly thickened
9. cut chicken into bite size pieces , then return to pot and toss with sauce before serving
10. sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve over rice or noodles
11. you can also sprinkle more red pepper flakes on top if you want more heat
demonstrations.review: "I could eat this anytime!" says my husband. (He's pretty "moody" with his food interests.)  I cooked it on high for 3 hr, and it came out a good texture; it was slightly like a pulled pork, but not much.  The flavor was excellent!  I used 1/2t salt, 1/4t pepper, and 4 lb chicken breasts.  Next time I'll use 25% more liquid for that volume of meat so none of the meat dries out.  I served it over rice, garnishing it with cooked broccoli and carrots, and slivered almonds (though sesame seeds would have been better, I'm sure).  mmm...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin pecan bread  bread machine

from bh&g.

1. add the ingredients to the bread machine according to the manufacturer's directions
2. select the basic white bread cycle
3. makes 16 servings
demonstrations.review: Wonderful basic recipe!  It was a bit bland on its own.  The second time we made it, we doubled the sugar and salt, and added 1c chocolate chips.  I made the dough in the bread machine and baked it in a braid in the oven (340F for 43 min).  To distribute the choc chips evenly, I divided the dough into 3 even snakes, then pressed/kneaded in 1/3 of the choc chips to each snake.  Amazing!  Too bad my bread machine isn't big enough for a larger loaf.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rigatoni  d   maggiano s

maggiano's rigatoni "d"
  

my spin on maggiano's best pasta dish! totally heavenly! also...for anyone doing low carb-substitute low-carb pasta & you've got a meal that makes you swear you're cheating!!!

(the sauce is thin-but if you've noticed, it's thin at maggiano's too! if you like it thicker, just lower the heat and let the sauce reduce some more)

also-if you want to use a rotisserie chicken, you can...it turns out quite well if you are pressed for time.)

1. heat oil
2. caramelize onions
3. saute mushrooms with balsamic vinegar
4. add onions to the mushrooms
5. season with salt and pepper
6. add garlic
7. add chicken
8. add chicken stock , marsala , and white wine
9. cook until reduced by half
10. add cream and bring to a boil
11. turn down heat and simmer to skim away any impurities
12. cook rigatoni al dente
13. add drained rigatoni to chicken mixture in pan and finish with basil-parsley mix , parmesan cheese , garlic butter , and salt and pepper
14. add more marsala for flavor as needed
15. place in pasta bowl and garnish with parmesan shavings and chopped parsley
demonstrations.review: I think Maggiano's original recipe and this recipe are way too rich and too many carbs (hence the 3 stars), so I just added extra onions, a head of broccoli, and a red pepper to mine.  I'll add even more veggies next time.  Even though I omitted the garlic butter and the wine (didn't have either), the flavor was still amazing!

target.recipe_text:
classic saffron rice

this is easy, simple and wonderful.  the original recipe which was printed in the spring 2005 penzeys catalog, calls for long-grain rice; however, i liked it much better with basmati. also, the original recipe called for minced onion but i found it worked very well with dried onion.  i indicated that the butter is optional, because i did not add it.

1. rinse the rice well , drain
2. in a medium size saucepan , add the rinsed rice and remaining ingredients
3. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat
4. simmer for 15 to 20 minutes or until stock is absorbed and rice is tender
5. fluff with fork and serve
target.review: This recipe is simple and quick and makes a great accompaniment for curries, etc.  I served it with Crockpot Chicken Vindaloo.  I, too, couldn't put dried onions in with my gold, I mean, saffron (Can you believe the price?).  I sauteed 1/4 of an onion in the butter and then added everything else.  It came out perfectly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple poached eggs

a simple, quick, delicious breakfast for any day of the week. this recipe is for 1 person but you can adjust the quantity depending on how many people you are feeding, etc.

1. bring your pot of water to a boil
2. crack your egg open into a small bowl
3. once your water has boiled , turn it down to a simmer
4. gently transfer your egg into the simmering water
5. cook the egg for 3 minutes
6. gently remove the egg from the water with a slotted spoon and place on buttered toast or eat as is
7. sprinkle with salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: This is a great, basic recipe to keep in mind for a quick, balanced breakfast.  When I was in Scotland, we stayed in a bed and breakfast where a two-egg version of this was ordered daily by a young, newly married man.  The innkeeper referred to it as a "Marilyn Monroe"!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: Who knew that you could bake a chimichanga?  I expected to lose a lot of flavor and texture without the deep-fry but this works very well.  As a Texan, I require good Tex-mex and this did not disappoint.  I used some fresh cilantro and a four cheese Mexican combo.  I tried the olive oil baste that someone else suggested.  It worked fine.  The filling possibilities are endless and could include a wide variety of meat/bean/cheese/sauce combinations.  I'll need to find a good ranchera sauce recipe to top this off.  Thanks for something new to add to the repertoire.  DH almost always orders chimichangas at restaurants.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
finally  delicious sprouted gluten free egg free bread

i never thought that i would find a delicious not only gluten free but egg free bread too!!! soaking the grains makes it much easier to digest and is the nutrients are unlocked and multiplied giving you ten times more absorbable vitamins and nutrients from those grains! and it doesn´t crumble, fall apart, or mush! it actually rose and is sliceable and sooo yummy! please try out this recipe, i am so excited!! 
this recipe was adapted from www.anniebbond.com

1. 1
2. preheat oven to 350f
3. 2
4. drain and rinse soaked grains and seeds
5. 3
6. place all ingredients in high speed blender and puree
7. 4
8. pour into medium loaf pan lined with parchment paper
9. if desired sprinkle sesame seeds or any type of seed or nut ontop
10. 5
11. bake for one hour
12. if top begins to get too brown , cover with foil
13. 6
14. let cool 20-30 min and enjoy with almond butter , agave , honey , pesto sauce -- its deeelicious !
demonstrations.review: I would consider this more soaked than sprouted, with the exception of maybe the quinoa, however, it was really good with some vegan butter. I also want to try it with hummus. I didn't have any coconut flour, so I doubled the rice (brown) rice flour and it worked. It's definitely a different flavor and texture than wheat bread but way healthier than most gluten free breads you will get at the store. It's really easy, also. It just takes some thinking ahead to soak your grains.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery cut out christmas cookies

these are delicious. the cream cheese in the cookie dough really adds a softness, and makes the cookies taste really flaky and rich. they're a great addition to one's christmas cookie recipes.

1. combine the first five ingredients in a large mixing bowl
2. beat at about medium speed until well combined and creamy , about 3-4 minutes
3. gradually add flour , and beat until well mixed , about 2-3 minutes more
4. divide dough in half , and wrap each on in plastic wrap
5. refrigerate until firm , at least two hours
6. preheat oven to 375
7. roll out dough half on a lightly floured surface to about 1 / 4" thick
8. keep the other half in the fridge until ready to use
9. cut out the shapes your prefer , using a 2 1 / 2 inch cookie cutter
10. place 1" apart onto ungreased cookie sheets
11. if i'm making christmas cookie shapes , i sprinkle the cookies with red , green , or multi-colored sugars before baking
12. bake for 7-9 minutes or until edges are just slightly browned
13. these cookies may also be baked plain , and decorated with icings after they are cooled
demonstrations.review: Easiest cookie dough I've ever worked with including several on RecipeZaar that say they are the best.  I used Kittencal's icing that hardens and they are perfect.  I love a lemony cookie and added the zest of one lemon.  Two would have been even better IMHO.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
double chocolate banana muffins

nan

1. in a large bowl , combine the first six ingredients
2. in a small bowl , combine bananas , oil and egg
3. stir into dry ingredients just until moistened
4. fold in chocolate chips
5. fill greased or paper lined muffin cups three fourths full
6. bake at 350 deg f for 20-25 minutes or until muffins test done
demonstrations.review: These are really great muffins.  I made them for a brunch with the girlfriends, and the next time we were having a get together I asked if they wanted a different kind of muffin or the chocolate ones and the vote was unanimous for these wonderful muffins.  You won't be sorry!

target.recipe_text:
hot german potato salad

this was passed down from my great-great-grand mother who came from germany in the 1800's.

1. dice and fry bacon
2. in a small bowl , add eggs , salt , mustard , sugar , vinegar and cayenne pepper
3. beat well and pour into hot pan with bacon and bacon grease stirring till thickened
4. add diced cooked potatoes and sliced onion
5. serve hot
target.review: This recipe has the perfect flavor for GPS, however, the sauce dried out rather quickly. I'm accustomed to a sauce that stays "wet" even after 2-3 days of refrigeration. I think what your recipe is missing is some water added to the sauce. You may also want to advise people to do the final mixing in a room-temperature bowl to prevent the egg in the sauce from cooking when it hits the hot pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
