demonstrations.review: I'm sorry, but these were nasty. I know how to make a roux, etc., and the sauce seemed promising when I put it in the oven. But when the dish came out, the sauce got "funny" after only a couple minutes. I refrigerated leftovers and heated some up for lunch today and -- disgusting, couldn't even eat it. The sauce itself needs to have cheese melted in to give it a better consistency; I will not be making these again. Sorry.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: I made these a long time ago and they were just not that good. For all the ingredients, these came out bland and pretty gross looking. There was just way too much work put into these for something that was nearly flavorless.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter oatmeal no bake cookies

(no wheat / no egg) cookies in five minutes!  no wheat or egg so these are great for wheat or egg free diets.  a friend gave me the original recipe that called for white sugar and they were great that way.  i tried it with brown sugar and that is the only way i'll fix them now!  totally a new level.  only takes 10 minutes total to prepare these.

1. mix together the first three ingredients
2. set aside
3. stir together sugar , milk , and butter in medium saucepan
4. cook over medium heat stirring occasionally - full boil for one minute
5. immediately pour over oatmeal mixture and stir thoroughly but rapidly
6. spoon cookie size scoops onto waxed paper or plastic wrap and let set until firm
demonstrations.review: These smell and taste great but I could not get them to set (and yes, I boiled the mixture for at least one minute). I let them cool for over an hour, then put them in an oven at 325 for 8 minutes. Still goopy. I've wasted half a can of oatmeal. Quite disappointed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chex mix

this is essentially the recipe on a box of chex, adjusted to my taste.  i like extra seasoning, a kick from hot sauce, and a few other adjustments.  i also leave out the bagel chips; they just don't seem very chex mix-y to me.

1. preheat oven to 250f
2. in ungreased large roasting pan , melt butter in oven
3. stir in seasonings
4. gradually stir in remaining ingredients until evenly coated
5. bake one hour , stirring every 15 minutes
6. spread on paper towels to cool , about 15 minutes
7. store in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: Oh man. I've got this in the oven right now and it smells heavenly. I had to use 9 C of Crispix cuz we don't have Chex in Canada. I used waffle pretzels and whole cashews. Instead of Pickapepper sauce I used Louisiana brand hot sauce, and for seasoning salt I used Slap Ya Mama (local to SE Louisiana, where I'm from). I can already tell this is going to be phenomenal. Thanks for this!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushrooms paprikash with egg noodles

creamy flavorful yumminess! this is a very rich dish. be generous with the tomato paste and paprika.

1. in a frying pan , melt butter over medium heat
2. add onion and cook until golden
3. add garlic and mushrooms and cook until liquid is mostly evaporated
4. add tomato paste , paprika and salt
5. simmer until blended and heated through
6. remove from heat and stir in sour cream
7. meanwhile cook pasta until tender
8. drain noodles and toss with mushrooms
9. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Oh my, what a GREAT base recipe!! This is perfect as-is. No, it's not spicy or "complex" but it is COMFORT FOOD... First time I made this as directed, but had to use canned shrooms as that's all I had on hand (next time: definitely doing fresh). Tonight I am making this with 1lb of Polish sausage I must use, in place of the mushrooms. This is classic Eastern European food and finally, I find a recipe with the right proportions. Stol laj!

target.recipe_text:
mama s bar b que  barbecue  chicken

this was a favorite dish my mother always cooked for my family.  she shared this dish at church suppers and reunions...now this generation enjoys it.  a good mix of flavors!

1. brown chicken pieces slowly in salad oil and remove from skillet
2. in same skillet cook onion and celery just until tender , but not browned
3. add remaining ingredients and simmer for 5 minutes
4. place chicken in baking pan and pour sauce over all pieces
5. bake uncovered in 325 degree oven for approximately 1 hour
6. baste with sauce after 30 minutes and just before serving
target.review: After 35 reviews of mainly OMG so great - I expected a lot more. This was ok at best. It tasted like a sweet and sour sauce, not BBQ sauce...and it wasn't all that flavorful. I would probably have gotten a better result using a commercial BBQ sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef tamale casserole

an easy alternative to tamales. i like to make it in my large oval casserole dish and round it up like a giant tamale.  i also substitute a small can of diced green chilies for the bell pepper when i didn't have any on hand and discovered i prefer it.  muy bueno.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. make the cornmeal layer by mixing yellow cornmeal , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt and 4 cups water in a saucepan
3. over medium heat , bring mixture to a boil
4. reduce heat and then cook , stirring , until thickened
5. in a large skillet , cook beef , onion , bell pepper and garlic until meat is longer pink and vegetables are tender
6. stir in seasonings , tomatoes , beans and corn and simmer for about 5 minutes
7. spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with non-stick spray
8. spoon in meat mixture
9. spread cornmeal mixture over and then sprinkle with cheese
10. bake , uncovered , until bubbly and cheese is melted , about 30 minutes
11. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This wasn't a success for me. I followed the recipe exactly, but thought that the cornmeal would harden while baking. It was just  mush on top with the cheese on top of that. The hamburg mix was good, but the overall texture wasn't.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blender quiche   or whatever you have in your kitchen leftover

the great part is you can use whatever leftovers (well...almost) you have on hand. this dish can be served hot or cold. freezes very well! use any cheese of your choice.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. generously grease a 9 inch pie pan
3. spread shredded cheese across bottom of pie pan
4. cover cheese with meat and vegetables
5. in a blender , combine eggs , baking mix , salt , garlic powder , onions , parsley , and milk
6. blend until smooth , then add olive oil
7. blend until combined , then pour mixture over meat and vegetable layer
8. sprinkle with paprika
9. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes
10. cool 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was ok. I used leftover ham and zucchini and pepper. I used Bisquick because I wasn't sure what "baking mix" was and that might have been the problem. It didn't have the consistency of quiche it was more like something you would get off the back of a bisquick package. If you like those things, I think you'll like this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy slow cooker chicken dinner

serve with a green salad, bread and wine, such as, pinot noir or zinfandel for a perfect meal. cook time is 5 to 9 hours.

1. place chicken , carrots and potatoes in slow cooker
2. combine remaining ingredients in a bowl and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on high about 5 hours or on low for about 9 hours , until chicken leg and thigh come off easily when pulled
demonstrations.review: I made this with a 6 pound chicken and added the carrots and potatoes and cooked it on high for alittle over 5 hours. It turned out alright...but not half as good as just roasting a chicken. I used chicken broth for the liquid and the potatoes and carrots took on that taste. Maybe it would have been better with wine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
manicotti cum laude

my college-student son always asks for this meal whenever he is home. top grades always go to this effort in the kitchen!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. in a large skillet , over medium heat , brown sausage , drain fat
3. add onion and garlic , cooking till onion is slightly transparent
4. stir in tomatoes , tomato paste , basil , sugar , salt and pepper
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat and simmer , uncovered , 15 minutes
7. in a medium bowl , comine cheeses and egg
8. mix well
9. store , covered , in refrigerator while manicotti noodles are cooking
10. cook manicotti as directed on package
11. drain
12. stuff manicotti shells with cheese mixture
13. spread half of the tomato based sauce on bottom of a greased 13 x 9" baking dish
14. place stuffed manicotti over sauce
15. spoon remaining sauce over manicotti
16. cover& bake 35 minutes or until hot and bubbly
17. remove from oven , top with remaining 1 cup mozarella cheese
18. bake 5 minutes longer
demonstrations.review: This was great! I did make the sauce and added some red wine to it. I substituted Mont. Jack cheese because I didn't have Provolone. I don't know if this made a big difference or not, but we certainly liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish beef stew with guinness stout

hearty beef stew for the irish-minded

1. heat a 6 quart stove top casserole or oven proof pot and add the oil and the bay leaves
2. cook the bay leaves for a moment and then add the meat
3. brown the meat on both sides on high heat
4. add the onion and cook for a few minutes until it is clear
5. reduce the heat to low and add the garlic , thyme , rosemary and flour and stir until smooth
6. add the beef stock and stout
7. simmer , stirring until the stew thickens a bit
8. add the remaining ingredients and cover
9. place the pot in the oven at 275 f: for about 2 hours , stirring a couple of times
10. check for the salt and pepper before serving
demonstrations.review: Very good. I also added potatoes and about a cup of Guinness. At the end I also added some water and flour to thicken it more. I especially like the taste of the rosemary in this dish. I'll make this again.

target.recipe_text:
emaw s goulash

as some of you know i have been attempting to record my mother's recipes for all eternity.  this has been one of my all time comfort meals all my life.  some of the ingredients would change depending on how much $$ we had at the time.  feel free to add any seasoning you might like.

1. prepare elbow macaroni according to directions on package till al dente
2. save a little of the pasta water in case you need it later to loosen the sauce
3. brown meat in a large skillet , drain the fat and add the onion and bell pepper half way through cooking
4. drain any ramaining fat when onion and pepper is done and add garlic , stir it about
5. add the meat mixture to the cooked macaroni , add the canned tomatoes , corn and sauce
6. mix all this together and add seasoning to taste
7. you may need to add some of the pasta water to loosen the sauce if it is too dry
8. this is really good the next day too
target.review: I love this recipe. I always try to keep these ingredients on hand as staples since they can be used in so many different recipes. I did follow Sarah Chana's advice and put the noodles in and added three cups of water which I used to rinse out the cans. It saved a pot and I let everything start cooking while I browned the meat (I used Ground Turkey). I also added Chili Power and it was a nice addition as well as also adding a can of Rotel. It is a very versatile and forgiving recipe that is sure to please. Thank-you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ice cream cone cannoli

clipped this recipe from sunday's coupon section. from sorrento.

1. with a woodwn spoon , mix ricotta , sugar , vanilla , and orange rind until smooth
2. add chips and stir until evenly blended
3. cover and refrigerate for one hour
4. spoon mixture into ice cream cones
5. add sprinkes and serve
demonstrations.review: These are the bomb!!! We made them for our desert on a camping trip for a Italian Night theme meal. They were devoured in minutes. So very easy and I made the filling during the day when I was bored. Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new mexico style chili chicken casserole

this is an easy to make tasty dish that i clipped from my local newspaper. i especially like that it can be prepared a day ahead.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. coat a 9x13 dish with cooking spray
3. in a large pan , combine broth , chilies , onion , sour cream , salt , cumin , pepper , soup and garlic
4. mix well
5. bring to a boil , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat
7. spread 1 cup mixture in the dish
8. arrange 6 tortillas over soup mixture and top with 1 cup chicken and 1 / 2 cup cheese
9. repeat layers , ending with cheese
10. spread remaining soup mixture over cheese
11. bake 30 minutes or until bubbly
12. when ready to serve , bake 1 hour
13. uncover and bake 30 minutes more or until bubbly
demonstrations.review: Super easy and yummy. I got a little confused on the cooking times,  (Line 10 if not refrigerated and only Line 12 if refrigerated) but it came out good. Agree with Dazy tastes like Sour Cream Chicken Enchiladas, but way easier. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken breasts

mmmmmm--this is so good and so creamy.  you will enjoy this dish.

1. butter a 13x9-inch baking dish and arrange breasts in dish
2. top with cheese slices
3. mix soup and apple juice together till well combined
4. spoon evenly over chicken breasts
5. sprinkle stuffing mix over soup
6. drizzle butter over crumbs
7. bake at 350 for 50 minutes to an hour , or till chicken is tender
demonstrations.review: This was a very easy recipe that was tasty as well. I followed the advice of some other reviewers and doubled the Apple Juice. The gravy was still the right consistency there was just more of it for the rice. This is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cube steaks au poivre

this is just plain good. i cannot remember where i had found this recipe, but i thank whoever came up with this!!!

1. sprinkle steaks with salt and pepper to taste
2. in a large skillet , melt butter and cook steaks 2 at a time on medium-high heat until browned on both sides , about 4 minutes for each set of steaks
3. reserve drippings in pan
4. arrange steaks on a platter and keep warm
5. into pan drippings , over medium high heat , add remaining ingredients
6. stirring often to losen brown bits on bottom of skillet , heat until warm
7. pour over steaks and serve
demonstrations.review: I wish I could give more stars. Man this was good. Super easy too. I doubled the sauce (less the pepper) and then added a touch of Cornstarch at the end to thicken. I served this with Stuffing. Thanks. It was Super Yum.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oriental mini meatloaves with honey garlic sauce

a yummy variation on traditional meatloaf. i have also made this mixture into meatballs as well.

1. meatloaves-combine all ingredients in a large bowl
2. mix lightly but throughly to blend
3. divide into 12 muffin cups
4. bake at 350 degrees for 30-35 minutes
5. or remove from pan and serve with honey garlic sauce immediately
6. sauce-combine ingredients in a sauce pan
7. cook and stir on low heat until hot and bubbly
8. serve with rice or oriental noodles
demonstrations.review: Thanks for an easy tasty recipe. I made a double batch and I am glad I did. They turned out great and I froze part of them. I followed the recipe, except that I put the Onion and the Water Chestnuts in the food processor and that made it super quick. I also used reduced Sodium Soy Sauce. Also I only had Bouillon Cubes so I just crumbled them up and it worked the same. Oh and I love making them in the muffin tins, I used disposable ones. Thanks again.

target.recipe_text:
southwest rice salad

this healthy salad has lots of taste and eye appeal. add more or less jalapenos to suit your own heat preference. most people like it this way and i serve some hot sauce on the side for the heat lovers.

1. in a large bowl , combine the rice , beans , corn and onions
2. toss to mix
3. in a food processor , blend remaining ingredients , except the cilantro and tomatoes , until the peppers are finely minced
4. pour the dressing over the rice mixture and mix well
5. garnish with the cilantro and chopped tomatoes
6. this salad can be made 1-2 days in advance and served either cold or room temperature
target.review: Overall I think this dish is great and a good way to jazz up the regular sidedish dilemma. I did change a few things as we do not have a taste for hot or spicy foods. I omitted the jalapeno all together and used 4 cloves of garlic instead. I also used vegie oil to replace canola, and 1 teaspoon of curry as I did not have cumin. I used frozen yellow corn thawed in microwave 2 minutes. I do think that the next time I will use Orzo instead of rice. I do not like the instant and I thought the Hanmi rice in the cooker stuck together a bit much for my liking. Orzo all the way next time. Other than the few diffrence's mentioned followed the recipe and it was  a hit! Thanks!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
napa dave s mexican chicken soup

a delightful combination of ingredients and easy to make as well. and if you are feeling under the weather, this will cure what ails you (just ask your mother!)

1. in a large saucepan heat the oil and saute the onion , garlic and bell pepper until soft and fragrant
2. add the chicken broth and bring to a boil
3. now add the lime juice , chicken and rice and wait for the mixture to boil again
4. throw the tomatoes and cilantro and turn off the heat
5. season with the salt and pepper and serve
6. i like to cut corn tortillas into thin strips with scissors and spray with pam
7. i then bake in a hot oven for about 15 minutes until well toasted and sprinkle on top of the soup to serve !
demonstrations.review: Thanks! This was what I was looking for ! I did make a few changes. I used egg noodles about 2 handfulls to sub for the rice. I used half the cilantro, I used half onion and half the lime juice added a small shake of adobe and yum yum!!!! thanks so much!!!! went great with melted cheese and sour cram nachos!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and chinese broccoli miso stir fry

this was a healthy throw together meal, which resulted from me wanting to use up some miso i haven't been able to use quickly enough.  this is a easy fast recipe, and some of the prep work like chicken and broccoli chopping can be done while cooking.

1. stir fry garlic and onions in oil until they are slightly cooked
2. add chicken meat and cook until mostly cooked
3. add chinese broccoli cut into bite size pieces along with miso and cook about 2 minutes more
4. add soy , water and cornstarch and bring to a boil
5. check seasoning once chicken has cooked through , and add salt as desired
6. garnish with green onions and parsley
7. serve with rice
demonstrations.review:
This was a GREAT recipe! My husband thought I bought it from a resturaunt. HAHA! I substituted miso for  1 and half teaspoon of ground ginger and extra soy. I omitted the sweet onion all together and added extra green onions.. using 5 in all. I also put a beef bullion cube in my half cup of hot water it dissolved about halfway. I threw out the half bullion cube that didn't dissolve and used the partial bullion water for the recipe.
It was really good I plan on using it OFTEN!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken and chip casserole

this recipe was passed to me by a friend.  it is simple to make and taste wonderful. it is just as wonderful right out of the oven or as a leftover.
my family all love it.


1. melt butter over medium heat , add chicken and onions
2. cook chicken until it is just cooked through
3. set aside
4. in bowl mix , add undiluted cream of chicken soup , broth , and rotel
5. in oven casserole dish crush 1 / 2 bag of chips , layer on bottom of dish
6. layer half of chicken and onions over chips
7. pour half of soup mixture over chicken
8. layer 2 cups of shredded cheese over chicken
9. repeat last 4 steps
10. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
This was GREAT!! and super easy. I changed a few things according to what I had in my cabinets.
I use 2 chicken breast chopped and I sauted them in some butter with onions then in a different bowl I combined can of corn can of black beans washed and drained, can of chicken broth, can of cream of celery(substitued for the cream of chicken) I cut up fresh tomatoes (sub for the can of rotelle) put crushed tortilla chips on bottom of bakeware then chicken and onions, then my soup mixture sprinkled some chedder cheese on top and then more crushed tortilla chips and viola! baked and then served over warm egg noodles... WAS A HIT!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amanda s cheese pound cake

my daughter amanda found this recipe in a old church cookbook, that i have had for years. its the kind of cake that you want to stick your face in the pan and never come up for air.

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. cream butter , cream cheese and sugar together
3. add eggs one at a time
4. add vanilla and then flour slowly
5. pour into a bundt pan or tube pan
6. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours
7. important: do not try and rush by cooking faster in a hotter oven
demonstrations.review: this is a definite keeper!! My husband had an almost 40 bday. He dosent like sweet cakes so i made this one. He loved it! eats it for breakfast with coffee. Its really an anytime cake. Thanks so much. I will make this often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef   corn noodle casserole

easy and delicious.  you would not think the ingredients would go together, but they are very good together.

1. brown beef in butter in iron skillet and add onion
2. brown slightly & pour off some of the grease
3. add tomatoes and noodles
4. cook until noodles are tender , adding some water if necessary
5. add corn & olives
6. turn into a 13x9-inch greased casserole
7. sprinkle with cheese
8. bake at 350 degrees , 40 minutes
demonstrations.review:
I am only giving this 5 stars because I put my own twist on it and it was FANTASTIC!
 I used a pc. of chuck roast sliced thin. chopped 1 oinion and sauted' the 2 together on low in a tblspn. of butter. After the meat was cooked I added a can of condensed tomato soup and 1 cup of frozen corn and let it simmer for about 20 minutes. Then added garlic and the black olives (from a can). I boiled some egg noodles seperatly and then tossed the 2 pots together in a oven dish. Added some salt and pepper and a dash of garlic powder for more flavor, we like garlic! and sprinkled some mild chedder over and it rocked!!!!!!400 degrees for 10 minutes  to all blend together and YUM! Thanks for the recipe!!!! great base for MANY twists! :)-Shelly

target.recipe_text:
chili sauce for hot dogs and burgers

easy to make, and a must have stuffed in the bun with dogs or burgers. any left overs can be frozen. i freeze in half cup freezer-proof containers, just reheat in the microwave to serve with burgers and hot dogs, also wonderful on top of french fries, then topped with shredded cheddar cheese yum!!  this chili sauce is even better if made a day or even days ahead of using. also the recipe may be cut in half for a smaller amount. all ingredients may be adjusted to suit taste.

1. in a saucepan , saut the onions and garlic until soft
2. add in ground beef , and saut until browned
3. add in all remaining ingredients and vinegar
4. bring to a boil , stirring occasionally , boil for 5 minutes
5. add in bread crumbs and vinegar
6. mix to combine
7. simmer for about 2 hours , stirring occasionally
target.review: DH loves cheese fries so I followed Kittencal's suggestion and topped crinkle cut fries with this chili sauce. I used about 1/8 teaspoon cayenne pepper and omitted the tabasco sauce for our taste. I did freeze some for the next time we have hot dogs on the grill which I hope will be soon as this was a great chili sauce! Topped my chili fries with a sprinkle of green onions, loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
teriyaki pork chops

it doesn't get any easier than this!! from the busy mom's slow cooker cookbook.

1. spray inside of slow cooker with cooking spray
2. combine teriyaki sauce , brown sugar and garlic in small bowl and mix well
3. place pork chops in cooker
4. pour mixture over top
5. cover and cook on low heat 7-8 hours
demonstrations.review: These are wonderful pork chops! I doubled the recipe and used a family pack of 8 boneless thick cut pork chops. So easy to make with a great flavor. I also served these with mashed potatoes and Kittencal's recipe #200043. Made and reviewed for my Pick A Chef adopted baby.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon crunch

from company's coming's "most loved treats".  i am intrigued by these bars as they contain soda crackers!  will let you know when i try them out!

1. bottom layer: combine all 6 ingredients in medium bowl until crumbly
2. reserve 1 cup for topping
3. press remaining crumb mixture firmly in ungreased 9x9 inch pan
4. bake in 350f oven for 15 minutes
5. remove from oven
6. lemon filling: beat eggs in heavy medium saucepan
7. add remaining 3 ingredients
8. heat and stir on medium until thickened
9. spread evenly over crumb layer in pan
10. sprinkle reserved crumb mixture over top
11. bake for about 20 minutes until golden brown
12. let stand in pan or wire rack until cool
13. cut into 36 squares
demonstrations.review: We really liked the texture and taste of the saltine crust and topping. With the lemon filling this reminds me of a moist coconut macaroon type cookie. For the bottom layer I only used 1/4 cup of sugar since the coconut was pretty sweet on it's own. When making the filling I followed the previous reviewers suggestions and added 3/4 cup of sugar and I used 4 tablespoons of lemon. The lemon flavor was not quite where I wanted it, I like the tartness, so next time I would add a bit more. I did whisk the filling mixture the whole time it was cooking and also for the bottom layer, I used unsalted saltines. This is a sweet treat and I think the sugar can be adjusted to personal taste. Thank you Redsie for a unique and tasty dessert!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cherry bomb chicken

this is with cherry preserves, from penzey's spices.  they had it in their recipes for 4th of july.  even my picky dh, who doesn't like fruit in his main dish, likes this.  prep. time includes marinating time.

1. in small saucepan , mix soy sauce , preserves , garlic and mustard
2. stir over med heat just until preserves are melted and mix is well blended
3. season to taste with hot pepper sauce
4. cool
5. arrange chicken in single layer in baking dish just large enough to hold pieces
6. pour sauce over all and turn to coat evenly
7. cover and refrigerate at least 2 hours or up to 1 day
8. lift chicken from marinade , collecting remaining marinade in small bowl
9. grill chicken over med coals until done , about 25 min , turning frequently and basting with additional marinade
10. garnish with green onions
demonstrations.review: DH grilled drumsticks that I had marinated overnight. He basted the chicken while grilling and I am sorry to say this didnt have the flavor that I was hoping for with all the five star reviews. There was more of a soy sauce asian flavor, the cherry and dijon flavors really did not come thru. I did not add the hot pepper sauce or green onions before serving. The chicken drumsticks were moist and tender and I will try this again baking it in the oven and basting so hopefully I will get the results the other reviewes did.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious lemon pound cake

this is a simple yet elegant dessert.  great served alone or with fresh blueberries.   to simplify the preparation i use a food processor or blender.    if using the creaming method be sure all ingredients are at room temperature. recipes courtesy of cook's illustrated . . . my favorite food magazine!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease 9 x 5-inch loaf pan with butter
3. dust pan with cake flour
4. mix together flour , baking powder and salt
5. melt butter , whisk thoroughly to reincorporate any separated milk solids
6. in food processor or blender , process sugar and lemon zest until combined
7. add lemon juice , eggs and vanilla , process until combined
8. with machine running , add melted butter through the feed tube in steady stream
9. transfer mixture to large bowl
10. sift flour mixture over eggs in three steps , whisking gently after each addition until just combined
11. pour batter into prepared pan
12. bake for 15 minutes at 350f
13. reduce oven temperature to 325f and continue to bake until deep golden brown and skewer in center comes out clean
14. cool in pan for 10 minutes
15. turn onto wire rack
16. while cake cooling bring sugar , lemon juice and zest to boil in small saucepan
17. stir occasionally to dissolve sugar
18. reduce heat to low and simmer until thickened slightly , about 2 minutes
19. with toothpick poke holes on all sides of cake
20. brush on lemon glaze
21. allow to cool at room temperature at least one hour before serving
demonstrations.review: This is a great pound cake and the lemon glaze, so good! I didnt have cake flour so I used all purpose and I think my pound cake was a bit heavier than described by other reviewers but still very good. A bit of lemon curd would also be tasty along side! Thank you Galley Wench for posting this recipe, a new favorite for us!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern style pork chops

a family favorite!  this recipe comes from my mother.  zesty, hardy and delicious!  everyone that has had it wants the recipe.  the best thing is that it is so simple.  i hope your family enjoys it as much as we do.

1. in a skillet , brown pork chops in 1-2 tb
2. vegetable oil , 2-3 minutes per side
3. do not cook through
4. place in a large dutch oven
5. mix together sauce ingredients
6. personally , i tend to double the sauce and put in more or less of the ingredients to your own taste
7. pour 1 / 2 of sauce over pork chops
8. add vegetables on top
9. pour remaining sauce over the vegetables
10. bake , covered , in a preheated 375 degree oven for 1 hour to 1 hour and 15 minutes , or until vegetables are tender
demonstrations.review: Easy meal to put together and very tasty. I did use 6 thin cut boneless pork chops and only one onion. The potatoes were russet's and I left the peel on them. For us the celery was a bit overwhelming but loved the green pepper. Next time I will decrease the celery and add another pepper. The sauce made this dish! I didnt add the cornstarch and next time I will double the sauce and use a larger baking dish. Baked for 1 hour and 15 minutes and served with crusty rolls.

target.recipe_text:
pork chop and stuffing casserole

delicious pork chops and stuffing,with yummy gravy. i got this recipe from home cooking magazine years ago from janice goff. everyone who makes this loves them,tasty and tender,too.

1. brown chops
2. remove and add water to the frying pan
3. place chops in a single layer in a baking dish
4. in a bowl , mix the vegetable packet from from the stove top mix with 1 cup very hot water and 1 / 2 stick melted butter
5. then add contents of crumb packet
6. mix well
7. for as many chops , make a ball of stuffing and place on top of each chop
8. put soup into skillet containing the drippings , mix and pour over the chops and stuffing
9. bake uncovered , 1 to 1 1 / 2 hours at 350 degrees
target.review: This was good! Very easy to make and tasted really good with mashed potatoes and green beans. I didn't use the whole soup/drippings mixture as DH doesn't like mushroom soup that much, but this still came out really good. The pork was juicy and tender and we will be making again. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq turkey meatloaf   5 ingredients

the secret to this tender, flavor-packed bbq meatloaf is the boxed cornbread stuffing mix!  beginning cooks will love the convenience, but so will any cook with a keen eye for a healthy, quick entree.  tip:  we eat one meatloaf for dinner, and i freeze the second one for another meal.

1. crumble ground turkey into large mixing bowl
2. if sausage is in links , remove casings and crumble sausage into bowl
3. add 1 cup dry stuffing mix , egg and 1 cup of the barbecue sauce
4. mix gently
5. divide in two
6. pat into two loaves in a greased / sprayed 9x13 pan
7. use remaining 1 / 4 cup bbq sauce to spoon over tops of loaves
8. bake uncovered at 350 degrees for one hour
9. option: this meatloaf could easily be made with lean ground beef and sausage , but it is so delicious with the lower-fat ingredients that you should give it a try !
demonstrations.review: This was amazing!! I will never go back to making meatloaf with greasy ground beef again. Surprisingly my meat (beef) and potatoes hubby and picky 'I don't like meatloaf' stepson both inhaled it, so this was a huge plus that they both loved it. I used KC Masterpiece original BBQ sauce and added a little extra to the mixture as it seemed a little dry. Thanks so much for a delicious, healthier version of a classic dish...this will definitely go into heavy rotation in our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
montreal rubbed chicken

i came up with this meal when i wanted something simple to put together, but packed with flavor.  this recipe is done in the oven, but can be also grilled.  i served it with a simple salad and crusty french bread.  roasted vegetables, rice pilaf and buttered noodles would also be great side dishes for this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. line a sheet pan with foil and spray lightly with nonstick cooking spray
3. coat chicken breasts with olive oil
4. in a bowl mix remaining ingredients
5. rub evenly over top and bottom of chicken breasts , and place on sheet pan
6. bake for 25-30 minutes or until chicken is lightly browned and done
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and so easy to make! I loved the sweetness of the brown sugar...what a fabulous taste!! I couldn't find the steak seasoning either, so I used the chicken seasoning and it tasted so darn good!! Thanks for posting such a delicious and easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s casserole

complete comfort food. great on a cold day.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray 2-3 quart casserole with non-stick cooking spray
3. cook noodles as directed on package
4. brown beef with garlic until cooked through
5. drain
6. add salt , sugar and tomato sauce and simmer for 5 minutes
7. combine sour cream , cream cheese and onion
8. layer 1 / 2 of the noodles then 1 / 2 of the meat mixture in casserole dish
9. spread with sour cream mixture
10. top with remaining noodles and the tomato sauce
11. bake for 30 minutes
12. sprinkle grated cheese on top and bake for another 5 minutes
13. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: DH said to give this 5 *'s and I agree! Very easy and yummy! I didn't have green onions so I sauteed a small yellow onion with the ground beef and garlic, and I did cover with foil while baking. I took the foil off and covered with 2 cups of  cheese as we both LOVE cheese! The sour cream/cream cheese mixture makes this so rich it's just heavenly! There's tons for leftovers...I brought some in to work to share and they all agreed...this is some kinda wonderful!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
philadelphia brownie cheesecake

recipe from philadelphia brand cream cheese.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. line 13x9-inch baking pan with foil , with the foil extending over the sides of the pan
3. spray with cooking spray
4. combine brownie mix , oil , water and 2 eggs
5. spread brownie batter into the prepared pan
6. bake 15 minutes or until the top of brownie is shiny and center is almost set
7. meanwhile , beat cream cheese , sugar and vanilla in a large bowl on medium speed until well blended
8. add sour cream and mix well
9. add the final 3 eggs , one at a time , mixing on low speed after each egg just until well blended
10. pour over partially baked brownie in the pan
11. bake 40 minutes or until center is almost set and let cool
12. refrigerate 4 hours or overnight
13. let stand at room temperature for 30 minutes before serving
14. lift cheesecake from pan , using foil handles
15. drizzle with chocolate and let stand until chocolate is firm
16. cut into 16 pieces
17. store leftovers in the refrigerator
demonstrations.review: These bars are richer than Donald Trump! Oh man these are so rich and so good!! Although the foil didn't work for me (the brownies stuck to the foil), and the chocolate drizzle didn't stay stuck to the top, and I think it was too humid down here for this to set up properly, these STILL rate a 5+!! What a yummy, yummy recipe! Thanks for sharing Nana Lee!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chop and corn stuffing bake

this is quick and easy . . . add a veggie and dinner's ready!

1. mix stuffing , soup , corn , onion and celery and spoon into a greased 9" pie plate
2. top with pork chops
3. mix sugar and mustard and spoon over chops
4. bake at 400 degrees for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was super easy to make, and I really liked the brown sugar/mustard glaze on the pork chops. I didn't care for the stuffing, but I think it was because of the onions because I don't like onions, but my DH really liked it. This was good and we will probably make again. Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
easy blintz souffle

this is an easy version of my regular homemade from scratch blintz souffle.

1. melt butter in an 9"x13" pan
2. place blintzes over butter in one layer
3. blend the other ingredients with the eggs and pour over the blintzes
4. bake 45 minutes at 350f or until the top starts to brown
5. the souffle can be served with powdered sugar , strawberries , or any other fruit
target.review: Very good! I alternated cheese/apple blintzes in the pan-- and liked the apple best. Very easy and tasty. I only used 1/2 stick butter, and it was fine. I like the fact that it can be breakfast or dessert. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple marinated chicken

the name says it all! the nutritional information will not be correct, as the marinade is discarded.

1. combine soy sauce , mayonnaise , vinegar and garlic in a large plastic food storage bag
2. add chicken and marinate 20 minutes , turning occasionally
3. broil chicken 7 minutes each side , or until cooked through
4. sprinkle with pepper
demonstrations.review: It was so good!! When chicken is on sale, I buy a bunch and freeze with the marinade. That way it marinates as is thaws, and all I have to do is turn on the grill when I get home from work. The chicken was juicy (we basted during grilling) and everyone liked it. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven barbecued hot dogs

kid pleaser!

1. poke each hotdog several times with a fork , and place in a 9 x 13 inch casserole dish
2. mix flour and water in a small bowl , stirring until smooth
3. add next 9 ingredients , stirring well and pour over hotdogs
4. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes
5. serve in warm buns
demonstrations.review: Good sauce. I used a 9in square pan. I'm afraid if I had used a 9 x 13, the sauce would have all dried up. Served in buns with shredded cheese on top. Next time, I might omit the flour/water-- the sauce was pretty thick at the end.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive chicken tenders  one taste and you re addicted

i found this recipe on a low-carb site, (dh is doing a low-carb diet). i modified it some and dh says the name is very appropriate. he craves this so i end up making it once or twice a week. good thing it is easy!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine all dry ingredients
3. line a shallow pan with foil
4. melt butter in a shallow dish
5. dip each piece in butter then roll in seasoning mixture and place in pan
6. bake for 20-30 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: The taste was ok- but the chicken was just soaked in grease. Is the 1/2 cup butter really needed or could it work to spray with cooking spray and then roll? Thank being said- the chicken did taste good. I think I'll experiment with either less butter to reduce the grease.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon snowflakes

this is an easy recipe that produces a tart and soft cookie. i believe that it was clipped from a taste of home magazine several years ago.

1. in a mixing bowl , combine cake mix , whipped topping and egg
2. beat with electric mixer on medium speed until well blended
3. batter will be very sticky -- and i can't even begin to tell you how sticky it is
4. :)
5. drop by teaspoonfuls into confectioner's sugar
6. roll lightly to coat
7. place on ungreased cookie sheets
8. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes or until lightly browned on edges
demonstrations.review: What a nice little cookie! Yes, takes a little longer than just a drop cookie, but it's worth it. I think this would also be good with chocolate cake mix--or any stronger flavored cake mix. Thank You for this addition to my keepers. I baked just 10 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin pie pudding

a light, delicious pudding that tastes just like pumpkin pie.

1. stir milk and instant pudding together until smooth
2. stir in pumpkin and pumpkin pie spice until smooth
3. serve , or chill and then serve
demonstrations.review: This was good. It definitely was better on day 2, so suggest to make ahead. It's nice to know it doesn't have a lot of calories and fat and yet still tastes like pumpkin pie. Thanks for this healty option.

target.recipe_text:
easy  n elegant chicken with lime butter

few ingredients, simple to make, yet chicken with lime butter never fails to impress. i have served this to children and adults, family and guests, and everyone has loved it. i found the recipe at a family owned store in valparaiso, indiana - which means i've had it for about 16 years. i was grocery shopping with friend of mine, who is now a missionary in a country i'd never heard of five years ago. we were looking for something new and different to feed her family and my dh, who were all back at her house. now her husband wouldn't eat anything green other than jello, and the closest he got to eating vegetables was the occasional baked bean. so he hemmed and hawed at this chicken sitting on his plate with little green flecks in it. when we finally convinced him that herbs aren't really considered to be vegetables, he finally relented and tasted. it passed the test and became one of his favorites -- and everyone else's as well. pair this with your favorite rice pilaf or buttered parsley potatoes, add a nice big tossed salad, and maybe some fresh rolls, and you've got a simple but sensational dinner.

1. sprinkle chicken with salt and pepper
2. spray large non-stick skillet with cooking spray , or lightly brush with oil
3. place on stove over medium heat , and add chicken
4. cook about 4 minutes or until lightly brown on the bottom
5. turn chicken , cover and reduce heat to low
6. cook about 10 minutes or until fork can be inserted in chicken easily
7. remove chicken to warmed serving dish
8. drain off pan juices and wipe pan
9. over low heat , add lime juice to pan and cook until juice begins to bubble
10. add butter , cut into chunks , and stir until butter becomes opaque and forms a thickened sauce
11. stir in chives and dill weed
12. spoon over chicken and serve immediately
target.review: DH and I both really enjoyed this dish.  It really did taste as if the preparation was more complicated than it was.  We used boneless/skinless chicken breast, but made the recipe exactly as written.  Don't think we'd make any changes, as this results in a lovely-tasting meal.  We'll be using this recipe often to make this great-tasting chicken to chill and slice for summertime main-dish salads.  Excellent recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
shrimp quesadillas with cajun remoulade

this recipe is very good and quite easy to make.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees
2. make cajun remoulade by mixing mayonnaise with 2 tbsp
3. cajun seasoning , worcester sauce , cayenne pepper , lemon juice , and tabasco
4. refrigerate for 30 minutes
5. meanwhile , heat 1 tbsp
6. olive oil in skillet over high heat , 2 minutes
7. toss shrimp with 1 tsp
8. of cajun seasoning and salt
9. cook for 3 minutes
10. transfer to large bowl
11. add chiles and cilantro to shrimp and mix
12. brush a large cookie sheet with olive oil
13. arrange 1 tortilla on cookie sheet
14. top with 1 / 2 of cheese and shrimp mixture
15. place another tortilla on top of that
16. brush lightly with olive oil
17. bake 8 minutes , until lightly browned
18. repeat with the remaining tortillas and mixture
19. cut quesadilla into wedges and serve with the remoulade
demonstrations.review: We doubled this recipe, as we had a pound of shrimp, and it was extremely tasty!  We had this with refried black beans and guacamole for a lighter, but extremely satisfying dinner.  The remoulade is unbelievably spicy!  We loved the mix of flavors, but would consider backing off of the spices just a bit as we expected the remoulade to provide a bit of a cooling effect, and the spices really heated it up instead.  We had leftovers, which were delicious as a light lunch the next day, too.  Winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean tuna

ratatouille tuna, this is delicious and low fat, low carb too

1. in a large skillet heat olive oil
2. add peppers , zucchini , eggplant , garlic , saute about 5-10 minutes until softened season with salt , pepper , red pepper
3. in a heavy pot add onion , top with tuna , add salt& pepper
4. pour sauteed vegetables over , add in olives and capers , cover
5. simmer over low heat20 minutes until tuna is cooked through
demonstrations.review: Five stars for sure, and my DH and I agreed that it deserves both stars and the moon!  What a spectacular, easy recipe!  I made it exactly as directed except I scaled back on the olives a bit (DH isn't too keen on them), and I only made two servings of tuna, but kept the rest of the recipe as is, since we love veggies, and almost ate all of them.  This recipe just sparkles - nice spice, a great melding of flavors with the vegetable mix, and the tuna was moist and flavorful.  It was incredibly easy, too, so is a weeknight contender, for sure.  I'm so glad I made this recipe - it was really delicious and I'll make it often - thanks, chia!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
everyday food lemon and olive chicken

a yummy-looking recipe from martha stewart's new everyday food magazine. i havent tried it, but if anyone does, let me know how it turns out. cook time includes prep time. 303 calories 15g of fat 34.3g protein 7g carbs per serving

1. sprinkle the chicken with 1 tsp
2. each salt and pepper
3. in a large skillet , heat 2 tbsp
4. of the olive oil over medium heat
5. in two batches , sear the chiken , skin side first , until golden brown , about 3 minutes on each side
6. transfer the chicken to a plate
7. cut the lemons in half lengthwise and then into thin slices crosswise
8. if the skillet is dry , add the remaining 1 tbsp
9. oil
10. add the onions and garlic and cook over medium heat until soft but not brown , about 3 minutes
11. stir in lemon slices , olives , stock , and 2 cups water
12. bring to a boil , reduce the heat , and simmer for 10 minutes
13. put the chicken on top of the vegetables , pour in any accumulated juices from the plate , sprinkle with thyme and crushed red pepper
14. cover and simmer until the chicken is just cooked through , about 15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Definitely 5-star!  DH, who isn't wild about olives, even liked this!  He enjoys the taste of olives, but won't eat 'em (hey, more for me!).  The taste was totally delicious.  I made this exactly as written, and it was truly piquant and memorable - I'd definitely make this for company (another dish to make for friends - yea!).  The only thing I'd do differently would be to trim all the peel and pith from the lemons, so they can be consumed with the chicken.  The lemon peel was a tad too bitter to eat, but this is a nit-pick.   The dish is easy and delicious - great recipe, Cookbook Carrie!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
key lime tarts

i found this recipe by paula deen on food network. a recipe for the key lime cooler cookies was provided by bliss. (thanks so much bliss).

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. fill 2 mini muffin tins with paper cups and spray with cooking spray
3. place 1 key lime cooler cookie in the bottom of the cup , flat side down
4. beat together cream cheese , egg , sugar , lime juice and zest until well mixed
5. fill the cups to the top
6. bake for 10 minutes
7. remove tarts to cool
8. when completely cool , top with whipped cream
demonstrations.review: I thought I'd already reviewed this, but I guess not.  I made this for Easter this year, and used Lime Meltaways #55471 from this site as the base cookie for the tarts. They were excellent.  I made the recipe as directed, and had no problems at all; didn't even have problems peeling off the paper shortly after the tarts had cooled.  Personally, I think that the whipped cream is gilding the lily - I preferred mine with a bit of powdered sugar dusted over.  Although the whipped cream does disguise any cracks in the top of the tart.  Very nice, not-too-sweet dessert for spring/summer.  Thanks, WVCarrie.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey roasted new potatoes

simple side that goes very well with all types of meat.

1. place potatoes in an oven safe baking dish
2. drizzle with olive oil , stirring potatoes to coat
3. add salt , pepper , sage , cajun seasoning and garlic powder being sure to sprinkle evenly
4. drizzle with honey
5. stir well to coat all potatoes
6. bake uncovered in a 375 oven for 40-50 minutes
7. serve
demonstrations.review: Very tasty recipe.  DH really, really loved this.  I followed the ingredients exactly, with the exception of using only 2 T of honey, but ended up dumping everything in a bowl to mix ingredients and coat the potatoes.  Next time, I'll cook them to be a little crispier.  However, the flavors were perfect together, and this is a lovely side dish for a lot of different meats.

target.recipe_text:
cream pasta sauce with zucchini

this is awesome pasta sauce! much different than alfredo-ish sauces, which i don't like. this one could be healthy, depending on which ingredients you use. i found the original version of this in a cookbook i received as a gift, but this is very different from that recipe.

1. melt butter in saucepan
2. cook minced garlic in butter for 3-4 minutes or until soft
3. stir in flour
4. cook for one minute , stirring constantly
5. add sour cream , milk , and lemon
6. cook until heated through
7. add zucchini , and cook just until bubbly
8. add to pasta
9. add parmesan and black pepper to taste
target.review: I was really excited about this recipe from the looks of the ingredients and the reviews.  But while I was cooking it...I was a bit frightened!  I did use FF sour cream and FF 1/2 & 1/2 (after DH requested that we eat 'lighter').  So then I threw in some serious red pepper flakes (1 1/2 Tbsp) and some serious black pepper.  It turned out so much better than I expected!!  I served it over whole grain penne and my husband grilled some lemon pepper chicken...VERY GOOD.  The consistency was EXCELLENT...not too thick but still stuck to the pasta. Also...so quick and EASY!  Will definitely keep this recipe around...maybe next time I will try sauteeing the zucchini before...but thought the whole dish was pretty great!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato and basil bruschetta

my first culinary 

1. whisk together chopped garlic , vinegar , salt , pepper , and basil
2. when combined slowly drizzle in oil
3. add tomatoes and let sit for 20 minutes at room temp
4. meanwhile back at the bat cave , toast the bread
5. this can be done either in the toaster or under the broiler
6. when the bread is toasted rub each piece , on one side , with the whole garlic pieces
7. place the bread on a cookie sheet and top with tomato mixture
8. sprinkle on a little cheese and broil till the cheese melts
9. serve immediately
10. the tomato mixture also makes a wonderful vinegrette for an an
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Ohhhhhhh...this was FABULOUS!!  So, so good!  Was having a craving for bruschetta and found this popular recipe...followed it exactly (except I did not put in the oven to melt cheese)...and it was absolutely perfect!!  Ate most of it for dinner (shared a little with the hubby) and barely have any leftover for lunch today!  So easy and so delicious!!  Thank you for a wonderful recipe...we will be making this again and again!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s salisbury steak

this is total comfort food at it's best, i have been making this for over 20 years and it is still one of my family's favorite meals, a must served with mashed potatoes or fries, this also will work great using pork chops, not the fast fry chops --- this ground beef amount should give you 7-8 fair-sized burgers but will depend on how large you make them, and will also work great using thicker cut pork chops, if desired you may use your own favorite recipe to season the hamburger --- you will need a large skillet for this recipe or your electric fry pan will work great, do not add in any salt to the soup mixture or the burgers the dry onion soup mix is salty enough, i also recommend using low-sodium mushroom soup --- also see my recipe#318998

1. in a bowl mix together all ingredients for the burgers
2. shape into desired size patties
3. heat 1-2 tablespoons butter in a large heavy skillet over medium-high heat
4. brown the burgers for about 4-5 minutes on each side (the burger will be browned on the outside they do not have to be fully cooked as they will cook more in the gravy
5. remove to a plate
6. add in onion and saute for about 3 minutes scraping up the browned bits with a wooden spoon while stirring
7. add in fresh garlic and canned mushrooms
8. cook stirring for 1-2 minutes
9. in a medium bowl , mix together cream of mushroom soup , 1 / 2 package dry onion soup mix , grated parmesan cheese , worcestershire sauce and black pepper
10. mix well to combine then add to the skillet and bring to a simmer over medium heat stirring
11. reduce heat to low and stir in the cream to thin out the gravy
12. place the burgers back then turn to coat with a spoon to coat the burgers with the soup mixture
13. simmer uncovered on low heat for 1 hour or even longer
14. serve with or over fries or mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: This was EXCELLENT!!  The flavor was very rich, but unbelieveable!!  I made the mistake of not stirring this often enough...so my gravy burned a little...fixed it with some half and half...but I will keep a better eye on the gravy next time.  Served this with mash potatoes and roasted green beans!!  My idea of perfect southern comfort food!  Thanks Kittencal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broccoli burritos

non-meat and non-bean based, if you don't like meat (or even if you do like meat) and you're looking for something different.

1. wrap tortillas tightly in aluminum foil
2. bake at 350 degrees f for 15 minutes
3. combine broccoli , cheese , tomato , jalapenos if you want , and onion
4. spoon mixture evenly in center of each tortilla
5. roll up each tortilla
6. place seam side down in a lightly greased 12x8 2-inch baking dish
7. top with tomato sauce or other tomato variant
8. cover dish , and bake at 350 degrees f
9. for 45 minutes
10. spread sour cream over top
11. garnish with parsley if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this for the first time last night.  I think the veggies need a little spicing up.  I added baked chicken breast (i know...so much for a vegetarian meal!).  I used 3 cans of tomato sauce and 1 can of diced tomatoes.  Next time I will use salsa.  I forgot to add jalapenos...so there was not a whole lot of spice.  The family loved that it was so healthy.  Also...next time I will add more cheese and put some on top too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bow ties with sausage  tomato  and cream

a very easy pasta dish for busy evenings. i like it served with crusty bread (to dip in the sauce) and a tossed salad. i have even doubled the recipe and served it to guest on a casual evening.

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. cook pasta in boiling water for 8 to 10 minutes , or until al dente
3. drain
4. heat oil in a large , deep skillet over medium heat
5. cook sausage and pepper flakes until sausage is heated and browning around the edges
6. stir in onion and garlic , and cook until onion is tender
7. stir in tomatoes , cream , and salt
8. simmer until mixture thickens , 8 to 10 minutes
9. stir cooked pasta into sauce , and heat through
10. sprinkle with parsley
demonstrations.review: This was good...but was missing something.  I agree with a previous reviewer that red pepper or some veggie would be a great addition!  This was very easy to put together and is great for a busy night.  Definitely will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan fried onion dip

from the barefoot contessa cookbook. this is great for parties. we have really enjoyed this recipe. great with chips or veggies!

1. cut the onions in half and then slice them into 1 / 8-inch thick half-rounds
2. heat the butter and oil in a large saute pan over medium heat
3. add the onions , cayenne , salt , and pepper and saute for 10 minutes
4. reduce the heat to medium-low and cook , stirring occasionally , for 20 more minutes until the onions are browned and caramelized
5. allow the onions to cool
6. place the cream cheese , sour cream and mayonnaise in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment and beat until smooth
7. add the onions and mix well
8. taste for seasonings
9. serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I was thinking this was going to be a little better based on all of the reviews.  It was very mayonaissey...and a little too sweet for my tastes.  A lot of my guests enjoyed it...so I will keep the recipe...but definitely not my favorite.

target.recipe_text:
baklava salmon  salmon with honey  butter  walnuts  and mustard

one of my friends deemed this "baklava salmon" and the name stuck. the salmon & mustard go well with the honey, butter, and walnuts. we usually serve this with rice and steamed carrots or broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. line shallow roasting pan with non-stick aluminum foil , or spray with non-stick pan spray
3. in small bowl , blend butter , mustard , and honey , set aside
4. in another bowl , mix together bread crumbs , nuts , and parsley
5. place salmon fillets on prepared pan , sprinkle with salt and pepper , and brush with honey-mustard mixture
6. sprinkle tops with crumb / nut mixture
7. if any remains , press into sides of salmon
8. bake salmon 12-15 minutes in preheated oven , or until it flakes easily with a fork
9. serve with lime or lemon wedge
target.review: Wow!  I don't think I have ever had better salmon.  I generally don't like salmon, as it has always been a bit too "fishy" for me.  This recipe balanced out that fishy flavor.  It was FANTASTIC.  I didn't change a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon chip apple cookies

this recipe is from hershey's. yummy! i also made a glaze for them with 1 cup powdered sugar and enough butterscotch schnapps to spread on the cookies.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. lightly grease cookie sheet
3. beat butter , brown sugar , egg , apple juice and vanilla in large bowl until creamy
4. stir together flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
5. add to butter mixture
6. beat until blended
7. stir in oats
8. add cinnamon chips , apple and raisins
9. stir until blended
10. drop by teaspoons onto prepared cookie sheet
11. bake 10 minutes or until edges are lightly browned
12. cool 1 minute
13. remove from cookie sheet to wire rack
14. cool completely
demonstrations.review: These were good.  I liked the texture.  I used a Jonagold apple, and it maintained it's shape and texture well.  Next time I make them, I will only use half a bag of cinnamon chips and cut back on the sugar.  The overall recipe was a little too sweet for me.  I also substituted milk for the apple juice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft  spicy  heavenly ginger cookies

i found the original recipe for these cookies on allrecipes.com, and modified it to be vegan, as well as by changing the spices slightly. they are truly delicious cookies, and very easy to make.

1. in a large bowl , cream together the margarine and 1 cup sugar until light and fluffy
2. stir in the molasses
3. mix the water and baking soda and stir
4. sift together the flour , salt , and dry spices
5. add gradually to the sugar-margarine mixture
6. gradually stir the sifted ingredients , along with the ginger and raisins , into the molasses mixture
7. shape dough into walnut sized balls , and roll them in the remaining 2 tablespoons of sugar
8. place the cookies 2 inches apart onto an ungreased cookie sheet , and flatten slightly
9. bake at 350f for 10-12 minutes
demonstrations.review: These were good, but I don't know if I'll make them again.  The spices were a little too much for my taste and I even left out the cloves and fresh ginger.  I also only used 1/2 cup of margarine.  They certainly were soft and chewy.  I did get great reviews from friends.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage potato lasagna

yes, this takes some effort but it is scrumptious. i think it is even better the next day.

1. in a large skillet , cook sausage and mushrooms over medium heat until meat is browned
2. drain and set aside
3. place potatoes in a saucepan
4. cover with water
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat
7. cover and cook for 5 minutes or until crisp-tender
8. drain and set aside
9. in a bowl , combine the spinach , cottage cheese , parmesan and egg
10. set aside
11. in a saucepan , saut onion and garlic in butter until tender
12. stir in flour , salt , pepper and the optional nutmeg until blended
13. gradually add milk
14. bring to a boil
15. cook and stir for 2 minutes
16. remove from heat
17. layer half the potatoes in a greased 11x7 inch casserole dish
18. top with half of the spinach mixture , sausage mixture , white sauce and mozzarella cheese
19. layer with remaining potatoes , spinach , sausage , and white sauce
20. cover and bake at 350f for 30-35 minutes or until potatoes are tender
21. sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella
22. bake , uncovered , 5 minutes more or until cheese is melted
23. let stand 15 minutes before cutting
demonstrations.review: Will definitely make this one again.  It made a lot, so I think I will be freezing some of it.  I used broccoli instead of spinach and it was still great.  I may make a little more of the ricotta chesse mixture next time to add, otherwise...yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best apple pie muffins ever

i got this  recipe from a friend.  i make these often and take them to many potlucks, office parties, the cottage, picnics, children's lunch and the list goes on. recipe from the cookbook "just the best."

1. cinnamon could be added to the batter
2. topping: in a small bowl toss together sugar , flour , butter and cinnamon until crumbly
3. set aside
4. muffins: in a large bowl whisk together brown sugar , oil , egg and vanilla until smooth
5. in a separate bowl , sift together flour , soda and salt
6. stir oil mixture into flour mixture alternately with buttermilk
7. fold in apples , mixing just until combined
8. spoon into greased muffin cups filling 3 / 4 full
9. sprinkle topping over evenly
10. bake at 350f for 25-30 minutes or until golden brown and tops spring back
demonstrations.review: I LOVED these!  I made them in mini muffin pans and used 1 1/4 cup self rising flour and 1 1/4 cup wheat flour and left our the baking soda.  I also substituded 1/2 cup oil for apple sauce and used 1/4 cup oil instead. They were chewy and moist.  I got many complements!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon mocha biscotti

delicious italian biscotti recipe that tastes like a cup of fresh cappuccino. great as a christmas gift too. just wrap a biscotto in cellophane and tie with a bow.

1. preheat oven to 325f on convection bake setting
2. combine butter , sugars and espresso or coffee granules in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. add vanilla and mix briefly
5. add flour , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix until well blended
6. fold in pecans , chocolate morsels and cinnamon chips
7. line a baking sheet with parchment paper
8. scoop dough out onto paper and form into a large rectangle , -inch thick
9. bake 25 minutes , or until firm
10. remove from oven and cool 10 minutes
11. use a serrated knife to cut the dough into -inch thick slices
12. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and return to the oven for 8 minutes
13. turn and bake 8 minutes more
14. remove from oven and cool completely on wire racks before storing in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: This is the best biscotti recipe  I have found.  They are wonderful.  I was a little worried that I overbaked them the second time around, as they were pretty dark in color.  I baked them for about 11 minutes on each side.  I may reduce that time when I make them in a few days (since I know they will all be gone before Christmas!) I also used wet hands to form the dough and made two loaves instead of one.  I got 22 biscotti plus the ends. FANTASTIC!!!!

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: I feel like I would change a couple things on this recipe and then it would be perfect! I would substitute part of the cream for milk...maybe 2 parts cream to 1 part milk. I used all cream and it even looked a little runny while it was cooking. Boy was I wrong! All the cream made it sooooo rich.  I wouldn't add salt as a lot of cajun seasonings already have a lot of salt.  I added a lot of fresh garlic, and I also added a can of artichokes at the very end which I cut into quarters.  Minus the thickness and saltiness, which I will adjust next time, this was the bomb!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
paula s cheese ball  by paula deen

this wonderful recipe was featured during paula's recent television appearance on oprah's show --- i made it recently but added in 2 scant teaspoons fresh minced garlic and tabasco, i also increased the nuts for the outside of the ball, this may be made up to 24 hours in advance, try this, you will love it! :)

1. place the cream cheese and milk in a bowl
2. beat until well combined
3. add in shredded cheese , onions , pimento and half of each , crumbled bacon and chopped pecans
4. mix to combine
5. season with salt and black pepper
6. transfer the mixture to a large piece of plastic wrap , then form into a ball
7. cover tightly and chill a minimum of 2 hours
8. in a pie plate mix together the remaining chopped pecans and bacon , then mix in the parsley and poppy seeds
9. unwrap the cheese ball then gently roll into the nut mixture
10. wrap again in a clean piece of plastic wrap and chill up to 24 hours
demonstrations.review: This was delicious! I made it twice over the holidays and everyone loved it.  The first time I used a grated 4 cheese blend because it's what I had on hand but it was just as good! I left out the poppyseeds because I didn't have them but followed the reciped otherwise. What a hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy chicken casserole

the water chestnuts and sliced almonds gives this dish a nice 

1. in a skillet , saute' the celery in butter until tender
2. remove from heat and add the next 8 ingredients
3. spoon into an ungreased 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish
4. combine melted butter& cornflakes
5. sprinkle on top
6. bake 350 degrees f for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I just finished eathing this and already had to comment becuz it was soooo good! I altered mine a little bit to lower the fat. I didn't use the butter, I used low fat cream of mushroom soup and light mayo. I added about 3/4 cup of mushrooms while I was sauteing the celery as well as some red chili flakes to give it a little spice.  I added some garlic powder and dry parsley as well.  For the topping, I used Baked Ruffles and ommitted the butter for the top too. I think my changes probably made this recipe quite a bit healthier but it still tasted sooooo good!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
saucy bacon roll ups

these are very easy to make for a buffett or appetizer party. i usually double this, because they go fast!  note:  the last time i made these, i fried the bacon after i cut it into thirds until it was almost done, cooled slightly on paper towels then wrapped around the water chestnuts and secured with toothpicks.  the sauce was a lot less greasy.  i cooked for about 5 minutes less.  enjoy!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. seperate bacon into slices
3. cut each slice in thirds
4. wrap each cut slice of bacon around a water chestnut
5. secure with a toothpick
6. place in a baking dish
7. in a bowl combine chili sauce , mayonnaise , and brown sugar
8. pour sauce over bacon roll ups and bake in the preheated oven for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have always made these without the chili sauce and they are a hit. I also always hand dipped each one in the sauce so my only complaint is that they are a bit tedious to make.  Next time I'll try just pouring the sauce over them and see how they come out.  I do recommend covering the dish with foil before baking them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
susan s vegas pasta    vegas baby  vegas

yes, silly name!  i ate at a little italian restaurant in the bellagio hotel on one of my many trips to vegas.  it was love at first bite!  i begged and begged the waiter to get me the recipe.  he even brought the chef out.  the chef wrote down the ingredients on a napkin but would not give me amounts nor preparation instructions.  i tweaked and tweaked and this is what i came up with.  funny thing is...i went back to that little restaurant after i came up with this version - ordered theirs again - and mine blew it out of the water!  hope you enjoy as well.  it's delicious!

1. cook pasta according to directions and drain
2. sauce - in a small saucepan , add 1 / 8 cup extra virgin olive oil and saute 5 cloves garlic , shallots and crushed red pepper until lightly golden and fragrant
3. add in tomato sauce and wine
4. simmer until flavors blend
5. add in half and half and heavy whipping cream and heat through
6. seafood - meanwhile , in a small saute' pan , add 1 / 8 cup extra virgin olive oil over medium high heat and add in the garlic until golden and fragrant
7. add the scallops and saute' until done
8. season with salt and pepper
9. mix seafood and sauce together and toss with pasta
10. serve hot with fresh parmesan cheese !
demonstrations.review: This was awesome. I made it w/ extra garlic but followed the recipe other than that.  I almost feel like the time it says it takes to make is too long and i'm not a fast cook! This was super tasty and so easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple fried rice from cooked  leftover  rice and chicken

a quick recipe to use up the leftover white rice.

1. put oil in a wok
2. add garlic
3. when it turns slightly brown , add eggs or vegetables , rice , chicken or vegetables , spring onions , salt , soy sauce , white pepper powder and sugar
4. mix well
5. add in raisins and pineapples
6. mix well
7. garnish with fried cashews and serve
demonstrations.review: This was so good.  I think it's probably the best fried rice i've ever had and my bf agreed.  I used diced celery and carrot for my veggies but used double the amount recommended.  I had to use chives instead of spring onions cuz it's all I had. I definitely recommend sauteing the veggies and then adding the egg and letting it cook before adding the rice and other ingrediants. I think the small amount of sugar and the flavor of the white pepper totally balance out this dish.  I left out the raisins but threw in the cashews and let them cook w/ the dish for a couple minutes instead of just sprinkling them on top.  This was devoured!!

target.recipe_text:
slow cooked shoulder of lamb with roasted veggies

this is a jamie oliver recipe that we make often. i have also used butterflied leg of lamb successfully.

1. preheat oven to 200c
2. rub leg with oil , salt and pepper
3. put into roasting tray
4. using a sharp knife make small incisions all over the lamb and poke rosemary leaves and quartered garlic cloves inches
5. add rest of garlic cloves , onions , carrots , celery , leeks and fresh tomatoes to the tray
6. tuck remaining herbs under the meat
7. pour tinned tomatoes over the top , followed by the wine
8. cover tray tightly with double layer of foil
9. put into oven , turning down temperature to 170c
10. cook 3
11. 5 to 4 hours
target.review:
Haven't made any lamb in a long time and this came out really great. Didn't follow the recipe exactly, but used the general ideas.

My changes.
Browned the lamb in olive oil on top of the stove first.
Didn't do step 4 - making incisions. Instead spread chopped garlic and rosemary springs on top of roast.
Added the other ingredients and brought to a boil. Then covered and placed in a 300 oven.
Also, used mushrooms instead of carrots

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican tomato lime soup

my family loves this soup. very refreshing and good tex-mex flavor. good served with polenta. adapted from a moosewood recipe.

1. in a big pot , over low heat , saute the garlic and cumin in hot oil for 1 minute
2. add in the tomato juice , fresh tomatoes , lime juice , and cilantro
3. stir to combine
4. let simmer for several minutes
5. add hot sauce , salt , and pepper to taste
6. to serve , put broken up tortilla chips in shallow soup bowls
7. add soup and top with monterey jack cheese
demonstrations.review: I make a very similar recipe, but I use V-8 juice to give it a little more kick.  Also, I add in a can of corn and sometimes one of beans.  It's good with or without the cheese.  As others have said - a homemade taste that takes little time to prepare.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parslied mushroom patties

tasty vegetarian patties, serve in a toasted bun or pita bread, with melted cheese if desired, or as a side dish. (this is an old one, i think from better homes and gardens)

1. in a large mixing bowl , combine eggs , mushrooms , flour , bread crumbs , onion , jalepeno , if using , parsley and pepper
2. mix well
3. in a 10 inch , nonstick , frypan , heat oil over medium high heat
4. using 1 / 3 cup mixture for each patty , shape mixture into 3 1 / 2 inch patties
5. using a spatula , place 4 patties at a time into hot oil in frypan
6. cook 3 to 4 minutes per side till brown
7. remove from frypan
8. drain on paper towels
9. keep warm in oven
10. cook and drain remaining patties
demonstrations.review: Can I give this 6 stars?  This was great.  The one big change I made was to replace the flour & bread crumbs with ground almonds for DH on a low carb diet.  The batter was a little wet, but it worked really well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple cinnamon liqueur

this is amazing.  a really nice amber color and a mellow, almost apple cider like taste.

1. in a quart jar , add apple , cinnamon sticks , 1 cup sugar , and vodka
2. seal jar tightly , and place in a dry , dark place for about 2 weeks
3. after two weeks , strain the liquid using a double layer of cheese cloth
4. gently squeeze the apples , getting as much juice from them as possible
5. in a fresh quart jar , add the second cup of sugar , the glycerin , water to top and the strained liquid
6. seal and store again in a dark place until sugar is dissolved
7. once the sugar has all dissolved , bottle the resulting liqueur in a fresh bottle and let age for roughly 3 months
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at making liqueur and it came out great. I used 2 cups of honey instead of sugar and water.   Also, didn't let it age as long as suggested because I planned to give them away and hadn't started early enough.  After only 3 weeks of aging (post straining) it already tasted nice and mellow, but maybe it will improve with more time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm artichoke dip

nan

1. preheat oven to 325
2. drain and chop artichoke hearts
3. combine mayo , sour cream , and parmesan cheese
4. mix together artichoke hearts with mayo mixture in an oven safe glass pie dish add garlic to taste
5. bake for 25 minutes
6. serve with crackers or pita bread
demonstrations.review: This was great!  Brought it to an election eve party & everyone loved it.  I used full fat sour creme and real mayonnaise but replaced half of each with Z trim fat replacer gel.  It still tasted rich, but cut the calories by about 40%.  I don't know if it was because of my replacement, but I thought it need to bake about 10 min longer than instructed.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
versatile layered polenta

this is a wonderful way to get the flavors of a lasagna with a fun twist by using polenta instead of noodles. this recipe is great by itself but can also be used as a base for any number of your favorite lasagna recipes. just add the lasagna fillings you usually use (vegetables, meat, squash, etc) between the layers.

1. for the polenta:
2. boil the milk and water together
3. whisk in the cornmeal and salt
4. turn down the heat and stir constantly until the polenta is suspended in the water and no longer settles to the bottom of the pot
5. it's done in about 15 minutes , but is supposedly even better if you cook it for about an hour - i wouldn't know , i'm always too impatient :)
6. take of the stove and stir in the butter or olive oil and 1 / 2 cup parmesan cheese
7. for the lasagna:
8. in a 9x9 baking dish , ladle in 1 / 3 of the polenta
9. spread 1 cup tomato sauce over top of the polenta
10. arrange half of the mozzarella on top of that and sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup of parmesan
11. ladle over half of the remaining polenta and spread the left-over sauce and cheeses on top
12. ladle over the last of the polenta and allow the lasagna to sit for about 30 minutes before baking to let the polenta set
13. bake in a 350 degree oven until hot and bubbling , about 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a lot of work, but it came out great and looked very impressive.  Instead of the directions here, I used the procedure in microwave polenta http://www.food.com/recipe/microwave-polenta-3503  to make the initial polenta.  Also added some sauteed mushrooms as one of the layers because I love mushrooms.

target.recipe_text:
the best snickerdoodles i have ever eaten
