"this must be one of the best cookies i have ever eaten." yep, that's what my mother said the first time i ever made this cookie. it is a great cookie recipe, and not difficult to make at all. i tripled the recipe and took it to school to sell... i sold all of them with in an 80 minute time span to only 4 people. they are good cookies, i can't resist them whenever i make them. and they turn out so nice whenever you bake them, it's hard to make an ugly snickerdoodle. lol. enjoy. (prep time is estimated)

1. in a large bowl , cream butter and sugars at high speed
2. add egg , vanilla , and beat until smooth
3. in another bowl , combine flour , salt , baking soda , and cream of tartar
4. pour dry ingredients into the wet ingredients , mix well
5. preheat oven to 300 while you let dough rest 30-60 minutes in fridge
6. in a small bowl combine topping
7. take about 2 1 / 2 tablespoons of dough and roll it into a ball
8. roll this dough in the cinnamon / sugar mixture and press onto greased cookie sheet
9. bake cookies 10-12 minutes , no more
10. cookies may seem undercooked but will develop
11. don't roll your dough into too big of a ball
12. they may not turn out in that much time if you do that
13. it happened to me
14. lol
15. if the cookies don't turn out , please try again
16. it's a very good cookie , it's just all a matter of getting the cooking time right
target.review: These turned out great the 2nd time.  Haha it was my own fault the first batch didn't turn out.  I cooked them at a higher.  I am not quite sure what I did wrong.  I did have to bake the 2nd batch at 350 degrees for 15 minutes.  I know it says not to overcook them.  But they were quite undone still.  Ok after saying all that, this cookie tastes scrumptious.  I would recomend it to anyone.  Although I changed the temp and time in my own notes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green chile bites

this recipe captures the distinct flavor of mexico in a delicious appetizer. the golden brown pastry brims with the mild, fire-roasted flavor of diced green chiles and the smooth texture of cream cheese.

1. preheat oven to 400 f
2. grease baking sheet
3. separate dough into four 3 x 6-inch rectangles on cutting board
4. press seams closed
5. spread half block cream cheese onto each rectangle
6. top each rectangle with half can chiles
7. fold rectangles in half lengthwise
8. cut each into eight pieces
9. combine milk and egg in small bowl
10. combine breadcrumbs and seasoning mix in shallow dish
11. dip each bite into milk mixture
12. roll in breadcrumb mixture
13. place on prepared baking sheet
14. bake for 18 to 20 minutes or until golden brown
15. serve with salsa
demonstrations.review: These were really good.   I made them a day ahead into the 4 rolls, then the next day sliced them and put the breading on. Which was very easy with them cold.  I also added a little bit of the taco seasoning into the cream cheese.  They were good.  Mine did take longer to cook though, about 30 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime zingers

simple, fresh and delicious!  disappear quickly.

1. in large mixing bowl beat butter on high speed for 30 seconds
2. add sugar and beat until combined
3. beat in lime peel , lime juice and vanilla until combined
4. mix in flour until combined
5. add nuts and stir just until combined
6. divide dough in half
7. on lightly floured surface , roll each half of dough to 1 / 4 inch thickness
8. using 1-2 inch cookie cutters , cut out dough
9. place cutouts on ungreased cookie sheets
10. bake at 350 degrees for 8-10 minutes or until light brown around the edges
11. transfer to wire rack and cool completely
12. while cooling , beat all frosting ingredients together with mixer , until smooth
13. may tint with green food coloring if desired
14. adjust consistency with powedered sugar until spreadable
15. frost cooled cookies
16. store frosted cookies in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: This has just become my FAVORITE cookie.  I did not use the cream cheese frosting just the cookie recipe.  What a great tart cookie.  The only thing I did different is, I refrigerated the dough for about an hour before rolling it out.  What a beautiful beatuiful dough.  No problems what so ever.  I got exactly 24 cookies out of this recipe.  For those of you who love really tart recipes may I suggest just mixing some powder sugar and fresh lime juice.  It was an excelent icing on these.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
applesauce topped pork loin roast

really good recipe found in a magazine. makes a very sweet gravy.

1. in a small bowl combine applesauce , brown sugar , vinegar and ground cloves , set aside
2. cut slits in top of the loin roast and insert garlic strips into those slits
3. combine flour , salt , sugar , pepper and mustard , like a rub and rub over the roast
4. place roast on a rack in a shallow roasting pan
5. bake uncovered , at 350f until a thermometer reads 160 degrees
6. brush applesauce mixture over roast during the last 1 / 2 hour of baking
7. when thermometer reads done , remove the roast to a warm serving platter
8. to make gravy thicken broth in pan with cornstarch and water
demonstrations.review:
This roast was a big hit here. A great 5 star recipe.  I prepared it a little different, here is what I did.  I placed the applesauce mixture on the bottom of a slow-cooker, Roast on top of that, covered the roast with the mustard paste.  Cooked on low all day.  FABULOUS!!  Boy did it make the house smell good too.
P.S.  I left out the cloves and used garlic powder (all I had)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sirups kager  danish brown spice cookies

sirups kager, a danish spice cookie "as brown as a reindeer," was a humble but coveted christmas prize enjoyed by her grandfather in denmark, writes our contest winner, julie k. cook, of chicago.
holiday cookies that can be found in danish, denmark, dane, european, and scandinavian cuisines. the recipe is from food down under's website and included in zaar world tour 2005 swap.

1. in a medium mixing bowl , cream butter or margarine , sugar and corn syrup
2. when well combined , stir in cinnamon , cloves and baking soda mixture
3. slowly add flour and mix well after each addition until dough becomes stiff
4. cover dough with plastic wrap and refrigerate until firm , approximately one hour
5. this time is included in the preparation time
6. preheat oven to 400 degrees
7. on a floured surface , roll dough to 1 / 8-inch thickness
8. using a reindeer or desired shaped cookie cutter , cut shapes into dough
9. dough can also be rolled into logs about 1-inch in diameter and sliced crosswise into 1-inch-thick rounds
10. bake on ungreased cookie sheets until lightly browned , about 8 to 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: My husband especially loved these cookies (I would give them 5 stars myself).  They are so spicy and yummy.  We couldn't help eating them warm out of the oven so they were nice and soft.  These smell so heavenly when they are baking.  I was out of corn syrup so I substituted dark brown sugar with a couple of Tablespoons water.  Other than that I followed the recipe.  Wonderful Wonderful recipe.  Thank you for sharing Lauralie41

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gooey butter cookies

so easy to make and always a hit!

1. cream together cream cheese and butter
2. add egg and vanilla , then cake mix
3. refrigerate for at least 1 hour or until cookie dough is firm
4. roll in 1 inch balls , then roll in confectioner's sugar
5. preheat oven to 350
6. bake cookies on ungreased cookie sheet for 10-15 minutes or until cookies are slightly firm to touch
7. wait a minute or two before removing cookies to cooling racks
8. dust with confectioner's sugar
demonstrations.review: These cookies are definitely a 5 star recipe.... Everyone raved about them.  My mother in law especially loved them.  They are so pretty too.  Definite addition to the cookie tray.  Very very simple to make.  I used the butter recipe yellow cake mix.

target.recipe_text:
easy peanut butter balls

super easy and super yummy. it's served frozen, so it's a good treat on a hot summer's day!

1. in a medium bowl knead peanut butter , margarine , vanilla and sugar , with your hands , until smooth dough is formed
2. shape into half-inch balls , place on tray lined with wax paper and freeze for at least one hour
3. melt chocolate in the microwave
4. use 20-second zaps and mix in between each zap until smooth
5. insert a toothpick into each peanut butter ball and dip ball into melted chocolate
6. return to wax paper and refreeze
7. store in airtight container and serve from frozen
target.review: These were fabulous and they are addicting!!  You can't eat just one!  But the fact that you can freeze them is great.  I keep them in my freezer and only take out a few at a time. These are a must to make!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot peanut chicken

a simple crock pot recipe for tender chicken. serve over hot rice or noodles. update: do to the many comments about too little liquid, i have added an optional chicken broth.

1. combine all ingredients in a crock pot
2. mix well
3. cover and cook on low for 6-8 hours or until chicken is tender and thoroughly cooked
4. serve over hot rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: I wish I would have re-read the reviews before I finally made this.  I didn't double the sauce and it really needs to be doubled.  The chicken tasted delicious and was very tender, but there was not enough sauce to cover the noodles.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
regular white icing  add butter to make buttercream icing

i love this icing with the white cake recipe that i posted. this is not a thick icing like those you buy. this also came from my sister-in-law. we use this for lots of different baked goods that require icing.

1. mix powdered sugar and vanilla
2. add milk teaspoon by teaspoon until desired consistency
3. dash salt
4. trust me
5. do this as instructed , or you will have to keep adding sugar until you get a good consistency , and then you will end up with enough icing to cover surplus amout of cakes !
demonstrations.review: My 15 year old daughter made this icing for my cake on Mothers Day.  It was delicious.  She added the butter in the beginning of the recipie, whipping it until it was creamy, then she put in the sugar and added the milk slowly like the recipe indicated. It was really creamy and buttery tasting!!  We will be making this again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean guy s general tso s chicken

this is an adoptee.  i have made it many many times and want to be able to help people out when they make it!  one of the best i've ever had.  takes some time, but oh so worth it.   good eats ;-)

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly blend the 1 / 2 cup of cornstarch and the eggs
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. if the mixture is too thick , add some vegetable oil to separate the pieces
4. in a small bowl , prepare the sauce mixture by combining the 2 tsp cornstarch with the wine , vinegar , sugar and soy sauce
5. first-stage frying: heat 1-2 inches of peanut oil in a wok to medium-high heat
6. fry the chicken in small batches , just long enough to cook the chicken through
7. remove the chicken to absorbent paper and allow to stand
8. second-stage frying: leave a tablespoon or two of the oil in the wok
9. add the pepper pods to the oil and stir-fry briefly , awakening the aroma but not burning them
10. return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the pieces are crispy brown
11. the general's favorite sauce: add the sauce-mixture to the wok , tossing over the heat until the sauce caramelizes into a glaze
12. serve immediately
13. serves 4 , along with steamed broccoli and rice
demonstrations.review: I have a MSG and a Gluten/Wheat allergy and havent had General Tso's for over 4 years.  I was so excited when I saw this recipe!  We had to change it a little because we didn't have all the ingredients on hand and because I wasn't sure if some of them had Gluten in them or not.  We used Apple Cider Vinegar instead of the Rice Vinegar. And we didn't have the Rice Wine on hand so we left it out.  We had to use Red Pepper flakes because we didn't have the peppers, and we just had to guess how much to use.(In between 1/4 and 1/2 tsp.) The first time I made it I used Chicken Thighs and the second time I used breasts.  It is much better with the Thighs.  It fries up Crispier and has more flavor. We bought the Chili peppers at the store and the Rice Vinegar, so we will be ready the next time we make this, but it was great with the substitutes too.  Thanks for a great and easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ham and cheese macaroni

good use for left-over ham; kid favorite.

1. cook macaroni in a large saucepan according to package directions
2. drain and return macaroni to saucepan
3. add butter and stir until melted
4. stir in remaining ingredients except paprika
5. pour into a lightly greased 2-quart shallow cassserole
6. sprinkle paprika lightly over top
7. bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: I just made this last night and it went over great!  I wonder if those that thought it was bland didn't use a good brand of cheese. (They are not all created equal!) Or if they didn't use the amount of fresh parsley it called for.  I would definately make this again.  The only change we made was to add more noodles.  One cup just didn't seem like enough for a family of four with two teenage children. (But we had a small amount of left overs so one cup might have been enough.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best browned beef stew ever

i originally found this recipe at recipe goldmine but have added and subtracted after trial and error. the original recipe called for a 10 oz pkg of frozen peas to be added during the last 15 minutes of cooking. i usually add a little rosemary and cayenne. can add the spices you wish. this is very good!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a large ziploc bag
2. heat oil over medium heat in a large dutch oven
3. place meat in bag with the flour and shake until well coated
4. shake off meat pieces and add them to the oil and stir until slightly browned , add remaining flour from the bag and the finely chopped onion
5. stir until well browned
6. add finely chopped carrot and next 4 ingredients
7. cover and cook over low heat for 1 1 / 2 hours
8. add diced potatoes , carrots , and onions , cook for another 45 minutes or until potatoes are tender
demonstrations.review: My Family Loved this Recipe! We have made this twice. We changed it a little to make it easier for us.  We browned the flour covered meat and then put it in a crock pot, we left out the finely chopped carrots, but added the rest including carrot chunks into the crock pot. The first time  I had home-made beef broth in the freezer that I added. The second time we were out of broth, so I just put in water.  It came out just delicicious!  It must have somthing to do with being in the crock-pot all day.  This a great dish to come home from work to!

target.recipe_text:
downunder cheese puffs

these are not popovers and have nothing to do with bread. these are very quick snacks that you can whip up during commercial breaks when you are watching tv and you feel like something cheesy. vary the taste with different types of cheeses.

1. beat the egg in the milk
2. mix together with the flour , baking powder , salt and grated cheese
3. put large teaspoonfuls on a cold greased tray
4. bake for 10 minutes in a hot oven 400 degrees fahrenheit
target.review: WOW these were awsome!  I put more salt, garlic powder, and I mixed up the cheese with some swiss, colby-jack, and a fiesta blend, just because i didn't have two cups of any of them.  They reminded me a lot of red lobster's biscuts.  Thanks for the recipe it was awsome!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade pie crust

a nice all purpose pie crust. when i need a crust for a cobbler, i change it to self rising flour because i like lots of crust in my cobblers.

1. put flour into a mixing bowl with the butter
2. using a pastry cutter , cut the butter into the flour
3. add salt and water
4. mix until dough is formed
5. roll out on flat surface
6. bake at 375 degrees until brown
7. prick crust prior to baking for non filled baked pies
demonstrations.review: I have never made a pie crust that actually stood up, but this one was fantastic!  It was so buttery and flaky!  I used butter flavored crisco as well and used it with recipe #56 Buttermilk Pie and it was divine!  thanks so much for this yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy and super easy crock pot oatmeal

tip for oatmeal: make it in the crock pot overnight! it comes out very creamy from the slow cooking, and i love being able to get up and have that hot steamy bowl right away without having to do anything at all. you do have to clean up the crock pot, but you can make a large quantity and refrigerate the leftovers to be heated in the microwave for the next several days. i use two cups of oatmeal at a time, which is enough for four breakfasts (for me, anyway; probably more for people who don't have huge bowls like i do).

1. put the oats and the water , along with anything else you want to add to the mix in the crock pot , turn on to low , and go to bed thinking about what a great breakfast you're going to have !
2. i scoop it out of the crock pot and eat it with maple syrup , or blueberry syrup , or pourable fruit , and soy milk--yum !
3. to reheat leftovers , i usually add a little water , and stir it a couple of times while microwaving until it's hot
4. you can add other flavorings as you like , such as dried fruits , other sweet spices , diced apples , etc
5. i usually put raisins on after it's cooked because i like them chewy
6. i've been meaning to try dried cranberries
demonstrations.review: This was an ok recipe.  I always use milk when I make oatmeal so it tasted really plain and watery made with water.  It was also really slimy and goopy so I had to add a lot of whipping cream to it to give it a smoother texture.  We ate it all, but it wasn't nearly as good as it is when made with milk which is unfortunate because it was so easy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s slow cooker vegetarian chili

this is a rich, satisfying meal that freezes well. great on a cold winter day. serve it with tortillas, cornbread, french breadand/or rice! enjoy!

1. in a saucepan , saute the onion , bell pepper , zucchini , and celery for about 5 minutes
2. in a slow cooker , combine black bean soup , kidney beans , garbanzo beans , baked beans , tomatoes , corn , onion , bell pepper , zucchini , jalapeno , chilies , and celery
3. season with garlic , chili powder , cumin , parsley , oregano , basil
4. cook for about 6 hours on low
5. serve with tortillas , cornbread , rice , or french bread
6. enjoy !
7. this freezes well !
8. leftovers are good on top of nachos !
demonstrations.review: I can only think of one word that can describe this chili...WOW.  My very picky husband even liked it.  My kidlets who normally wont even eat chili cleaned their bowls!  I am completly sold!  I put some colby-jack shredded cheese on top while it was hot, and then put sour cream on mine (rest of the family doesn't do sour cream)  I served it with garlic toast instead of PB sandwiches and it was FABULOUS!  Thanks so much for this recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tsr version of outback ranch dressing by todd wilbur

from www.topsecretrecipes.com. this is my all time favorite ranch dressing and i found it at outback. each packet of the dressing mix hold approximately 3 tablespoons worth of mix so you can triple the recipe, or make it 3 separate times. this recipe goes great with cheese fries! (prep time is chill time, but isn't necessary)

1. mix all of the ingredients in a medium bowl
2. chill at least 1 / 2 hour before serving which is the key step to maximize flavor
3. edit 4 / 15 / 2007: if you prefer a spicy , kicked up version of outback ranch dressing , substitute cayenne pepper for the paprika - your spicy preferring taste buds will thank you
demonstrations.review: FANTASTIC RECIPE!!!  I am SOO extremely picky when it comes to my ranch and have tried every store bought kind I could find and none of them measure up to my standards.  I LOVE LOVE LOVE this recipe!!  It will be our ranch recipe from now on!   THANK YOU SO MUCH for posting this recipe!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  geraldine s ground beef casserole

this recipe came from a local church fund raising cook book. mrs. geraldine is a good friend of the family. she reminds me so much of mrs. clause, that i can't help but smile every time i think of her. this recipe freezes well. do not bake before freezing. just put it together, freeze it, thaw it and cook.

1. brown meat in large skillet or dutch oven
2. add onions , pepper and celery and simmer for 15 minutes
3. add tomatoes and tomato sauce , mushrooms , brown sugar and worcestershire sauce
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. cook in skillet for 1 hour
6. place cooked pasta in bottom of large casserole dish
7. spoon mushroom soup over pasta
8. pour sauce over the soup and top with cheese
9. bake in 350f oven for 30-45 minutes
10. can sizes do not have to be exact , just as long as they are within a close range , everything will work out
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe!  My husband didn't care much for it, but he is extremely picky and he doesn't like mushrooms, so just knowing the soup was in it turned him off to it lol.  I thought it was wonderful, thank you for sharing!

target.recipe_text:
baked pecan french toast

the chore of making french toast on a weekday morning is standing over the stove when you're short on time. by assembling breakfast the night before, then letting the french toast bake instead of fry, you've got more time to get organized for the new day.

1. place the eggs , milk , sugar , nutmeg or cinnamon and vanilla in a medium mixing bowl and whisk to combine
2. mist the bottom of a 12 by 8-inch glass casserole with vegetable oil spray or brush with melted butter
3. place the bread slices in a single layer in the pan
4. pour the egg mixture over the bread , distributing it evenly
5. turn the bread slices once
6. cover the pan with plastic wrap and place in the refrigerator overnight
7. the next morning , preheat the oven to 425 degrees
8. remove the pan from the refrigerator and remove the plastic wrap
9. sprinkle the bread slices with pecans and drizzle with melted butter
10. bake for 20 to 25 minutes , or until bread slices puff up and pecans are deep brown but not burned
11. serve warm with maple syrup
12. instead of a cup of milk , use 2 / 3 cup orange juice and 1 / 3 cup of the milk
13. you can vary this further by adding a little grated orange zest with the pecans before baking
target.review: This was delicious. I sliced the bread and let it dry out a bit for a few hours by setting on a wire rack before assembling. Got rave reviews from my brunch guests. Will certainly be keeping this recipe handy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the bomb burgers

awsome burgers if i do say so myself!

1. in a bowl combine beef , bread crumbs , green onions , coriander , hoisin sauce , garlic , ginger and egg
2. mix well
3. make 5 burgers
4. poke a hole thru the middle
5. in a small bowl mix together water , hoisin , and sesame oil
6. place burgers on a hot grill and brush the top with the previous mixture
7. flip after 7 min or so and baste the other side
8. serve with condiments of choice
demonstrations.review: These were really good. I added salt and pepper based on some of the comments. I was a little unsure of poking the hole through the burger so I just basted both sides of the burger with the sauce. Very yummy. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry dumplings

i haven't tried these yet but they sound so good!

1. in a saucepan , combine 1 / 3 cup sugar and the water
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes
4. stir in vanilla extract
5. in a medium mixing bowl , sift together flour , the 2 tablespoons sugar , the baking powder , and salt
6. cut in butter with pastry blender or fork until mixture is crumbly
7. add milk and stir just until dry ingredients are moistened
8. place strawberries in a 1 1 / 2-quart casserole dish
9. pour hot sugar mixture over strawberries
10. immediately drop dough evenly in 8 to 10 spoonfuls over strawberries
11. sprinkle dumplings with the remaining 1 tablespoon of sugar
12. bake at 450 for 25 to 30 minutes , or until dumplings are lightly browned
13. serve hot with whipped topping or ice cream , if desired
demonstrations.review: This was delicious and very easy to make. I think next time I'll reduce the amount of sugar in the syrup and add some more sugar to the dumpling dough. The strawberries in the sauce seemed really sweet and the dough not sweet enough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon mocha biscotti

delicious italian biscotti recipe that tastes like a cup of fresh cappuccino. great as a christmas gift too. just wrap a biscotto in cellophane and tie with a bow.

1. preheat oven to 325f on convection bake setting
2. combine butter , sugars and espresso or coffee granules in a large bowl and beat with an electric mixer until light and fluffy
3. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
4. add vanilla and mix briefly
5. add flour , baking powder , salt and cinnamon and mix until well blended
6. fold in pecans , chocolate morsels and cinnamon chips
7. line a baking sheet with parchment paper
8. scoop dough out onto paper and form into a large rectangle , -inch thick
9. bake 25 minutes , or until firm
10. remove from oven and cool 10 minutes
11. use a serrated knife to cut the dough into -inch thick slices
12. place on a parchment-lined baking sheet and return to the oven for 8 minutes
13. turn and bake 8 minutes more
14. remove from oven and cool completely on wire racks before storing in an airtight container
demonstrations.review: These are delicious. It was my first time making biscotti. I couldn't find the cinnamon baking chips anywhere so I had to omit. I also omitted the pecans and increased the amount of chocolate chips. I couldn't quite get the shape right but they still tasted delicious. Many thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy chickpea   rosemary soup

we love chickpeas so this recipe from chef april bloomfield of the spotted pig "gastro-pub" in manhattan soon became one of our favorites.

1. in a large saucepan , heat the oil over medium heat and add garlic , rosemary and red pepper flakes
2. cook , stirring constantly , until the garlic starts to brown , about 1 minute
3. add chickpeas and cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
4. add chicken broth and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer 30 minutes
6. let cool slightly
7. transfer soup to a blender
8. cover loosely , and puree until just smooth
9. return to the saucepan and stir in lemon juice and sea salt to taste
10. serve , garnished with a fresh rosemary sprig , or an additional drizzling of olive oil
demonstrations.review: This is a great soup. Its nice and thick and tasty. I added a bit more red pepper than called for to spice it up a bit more. The aroma when the garlic, rosemary, and red pepper flakes get going is a delight. I used a stick blender so clean-up was super easy as well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy chicken tagine with apricots  rosemary  and ginger

from the book tagine: spicy stews from morocco.

this tagine is both fruity and spicy, though not too hot. the ginger and rosemary give a wonderful aroma!  it can be made with chicken pieces, (i use boneless skinless breasts) pheasant or duck.  serves well with a buttery couscous and a leafy salad.

1. heat oil and butter in a tagine or heavy-based casserole dish
2. stir in ginger , onion , chopped rosemary , and chilies and saut until the onion begins to soften
3. stir in halved rosemary sprigs and the cinnamon sticks
4. add chicken and brown on both sides
5. toss in the apricots and honey
6. stir in plum tomatoes with their juice
7. add a little water if necessary to ensure there is enough to cover the base of the tagine and submerge the apricots
8. bring liquid to a boil , then reduce heat to low
9. cover with a lid and cook gently for 35 - 40 minutes
10. season to taste with salt and pepper
11. sprinkle shredded basil over chicken
12. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Great easy and flavorful recipe. This was the first dish I made in my tagine and I really loved it. The flavors married together so well. The  only thing I did differently was use a can of diced tomatoes instead of the plum/whole tomatoes. Impressive dish. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
cajun chex mix

if you like a little spice in your snacks this recipe is for you. i make this year around for camping and snacking but especially at christmas for gift giving.

1. melt butter in medium saucepan
2. add everything but cereals , pretzels , cheerios and nuts to butter
3. heat to just below boiling
4. mix together cereals , pretzels and nuts in large roasting pan
5. pour butter mixture over gradually mixing all together
6. bake@ 300 degrees for 45 minutes stirring every 15 minutes
7. cool and store in plastic bags
8. this freezes well
target.review: This was a good base recipe for me, but I prefer something with more spice to it.  The spices together I found nice, but just not spicy enough, so I upped the Tabasco to 3 teaspoons, the Worcestershire sauce to 4 tablespoons and about 1 teaspoon of red cayenne pepper and I still didn't find it very hot or spicy.  But I am definitley going to keep this recipe as a base and just adjust the spices according to my tastes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick chocolate cake

this is so fast & easy to prepare. another winner from robin miller.  i prefer to ice mine, she just dusted with powdered sugar. either way, this is a moist, delicious cake that is ready so fast...i don't even let it cool first if i am just using powdered sugar.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine dry ingredients in large bowl
3. in a large measuring bowl , mix the wet ingredients together except boiling water
4. stir the two mixtures together , then add boiling water
5. beat together until smooth
6. pour batter into greased 9 x13" baking pan and bake for 25 minutes
7. allow to cool if planning to use icing
demonstrations.review: Yum, yum, yum!  I loved this cake, I'd give it 10 stars if it was possible.  It was so moist and the texture was literally like silk!  Like with most recipes, I made some slight modifications; I used egg whites instead of whole eggs, applesauce in place of oil, and I soured skim milk with vinegar.  To the boiling water I added just a little bit of instant coffee (1/2-3/4 tsp) because I find it usually helps bring out the flavour of the chocolate.  I iced this cake, but it is so moist that I think next time I will try without.  Tanks for the wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iceland dip

this is a great dip for kids.

1. mix
2. chill
3. serve with fruit slices
demonstrations.review: I loved this dip!!  I tried it with apples and it is delicious!  I will be making it a lot now when I am eating fruit.  I used plain fat free yogurt as that is what I had in the house at the time, but I am going to look for thick yogurt and try it with that.  I can't wait to make it again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
danish banana cake

my children did not like banana bread and i found that recipe in a small magazine, i tried it. they love it so much that when i make it i cannot keep it for long. it is very tasty. it is now the only banana cake i make.

1. cake: grease a mold 9 x 13 , beat together the butter and sugar
2. add the eggs and beat
3. add vanilla and the mashed bananas
4. in another bowl mix the flour , baking powder and baking soda
5. alterning with the sour cream add the dry ingredients to the first part
6. pour into the mold and add on top the cinnamon , brown sugar , chipits and nuts
7. cook 50 to 60 minutes at 350 degree f
demonstrations.review: I really liked this, however, I will probably cut down on the chocolate and cinnamon on top and add an extra banana next time as I found the banana flavour was lost a little bit.  Other than that I thought it was a great cake;  moist and not too sweet.  Also I used yogurt in place of sour cream since that was all I had and it didn't seem to have any negative affect on the cake!  Thanks for the wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almond fudge banana cake

so glad i adopted this recipe.  i finally tried it and my family all said yum!

1. mash bananas and set aside
2. beat sugar and margarine until light and fluffy
3. beat in eggs , liqueur and vanilla
4. combine dry ingredients
5. stir in almonds
6. add to sugar mixture alternately with bananas
7. beat well
8. pour batter into greased 10-inch bundt pan
9. bake in preheated 350f oven 45 to 50 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out almost clean and cake pulls away from side of pan
10. cool 10 minutes
11. remove cake from pan to wire rack to cool completely
12. drizzle glaze over top and down side of cake
13. make 16-20 servings
demonstrations.review: Absolutely delicious.  I used 4 egg whites and 1 whole egg, added one extra banana and cut down on the butter a little bit because of it, used 2/3 cup of Amaretto and omitted the almonds because I didn't have any on hand.  Even with my substitutions the cake still came out so moist and perfect!  To make a glaze I boiled 1/4 cup sugar and 1/8 water with some almond extraxt and then poured it over the hot cake; it gave it a nice crispy, sugary glaze on top.  The only change I'll make next time is to let it sit for a day before serving because I found the almond flvouring really came through when I had a piece a day later instead of the day it was made.  I think this will definitely become a family favourite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best seller caramel corn

when i used to regularly do christmas craft shows, i always sold this packaged up in christmas tins; it was a big seller for me. my sil always hoped it wouldn't sell well, though, so she could eat what didn't sell! based on a bonnie stern recipe.

1. when i make this recipe , it's the only time i haul out my hot-air popcorn popper
2. use 1 / 3 cup popcorn to achieve the 8 cups of popped corn
3. preheat oven to 275f
4. have ready a jelly roll pan
5. place popped corn in a very large bowl
6. in a large , heavy saucepan over high heat , combine the sugar , butter and corn syrup and bring to a boil
7. let boil for two minutes , stirring continuously
8. remove from heat
9. add baking soda and vanilla to sugar mixture and combine well
10. pour this mixture over popped corn and combine , then spread mixture out onto jelly roll pan
11. bake in preheated oven for 40 minutes , stirring well every 10 minutes
12. let cool before eating
demonstrations.review: This was great!  It it way better than any store bought caramel popcorn I have ever had.  After reading reviews I decreased the heat in my oven to 225 since my oven runs hot and only left it in the oven for about 25 minutes, stirring it about 4 times in that time.  Also I used 10 cups of popped popcorn and probably next time will use more since it is still pretty heavily coated.  All in all this is delicious and I will be making it often I'm sure!

target.recipe_text:
beef fondue with dipping sauces

this is our traditional new years eve dish that i have been making for years. i also serve it with salsa and mango chutney, cornichons, boiled new potatoes.

1. layer onions , beef , onions , drizzle with oil , refrigerate overnight
2. heat oil to bubbly , keep hot over sterno , dip beef in oil until cooked to your liking
3. for horseradish sauce , mix all ingredients , refrigerate
4. for garlic butter , mix all ingredients , refrigerate
5. for bernaise sauce: combine vinegar , water and pepper in double boiler
6. add egg yolks , stir constantly
7. slowly add butter , stirring as it thickens
8. add lemon juice , tarragon , salt& pepper- if sauce is too thick add a drop of water
target.review:
Love it!  This is a traditional special occasion meal for us too...Christmas or New Years Eve, Valentines Day, Anniversary.  A great way to relax over dinner!

The sauces were great. We always served clarified butter, but LOVE the garlic butter here.  If I might add one more of our super easy favorites, mix sour cream and A-1 sauce (about 2 parts to 1).  Creamy with just the right amount of seasoning to perk up the steak chunks!

I like to serve Steak Fondue with a Baked Potato and a big salad.

I'm always suprised how many people have never had fondue. Suprise someone by planning this fun and yummy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled tilapia with thai coconut  curry sauce

this dish is loaded with flavor and makes a lovely, colorful presentation. you'll want to serve with plenty of rice to absorb the wonderful sauce. (noted added 11/05/07: i like to credit original recipe sources when known, but wasn't sure about this one when i submitted the recipe. fortunately, a reviewer pointed out that the recipe came from cooking light, so i searched their site--indeed, it was originally published in their september 2002 issue. thanks to the reviewer for bringing this to my attention, and thanks to cooking light for developing the recipe! :) )

1. preheat broiler
2. heat 1 / 2 teaspoon oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
3. add ginger and garlic
4. cook 1 minute
5. add peppers and onions
6. cook 1 minute
7. stir in curry powder , curry paste , and cumin
8. cook 1 minute
9. add soy sauce , sugar , 1 / 4 teaspoon salt , and coconut milk
10. bring to a simmer
11. remove from heat and stir in cilantro
12. brush fish with remaining 1 / 2 teaspoon oil and 1 / 4 teaspoon salt and place on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
13. broil 7 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
14. serve fish with sauce , rice , and lime wedges
demonstrations.review: When I've seen it on a menu, I always thought fish and curry seemed like a not to appealing combination. This recipe rocks!! I'm not a huge white fish lover, so hard to find recipes that I will make again. The fish was tender inside and crispy exterior and the sauce is killer.  Served with sauteed spinach, basmati rice and naan.  Only changes were I made were squeezed 2 of the limes over fish before brushing on oil. Also used a bit of EVOO mixed with sesame oil to brush on fish...wanted to get a nice crisp on top.  DELISH -- thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best blasted rapid roast whole chicken

blasting with high heat will shrink the skin and seal in all the juices to create an extremely moist and tender chicken with lovely crispy skin - and it will be on your table in about an hour. this method will also work with a larger chicken, but cooking time will need to be increased. you may adjust all seasonings to taste. if you are not a lemon lover, then you may omit the lemon juice. you really can use whatever seasoning that you like for this. i like to use seasoned salt. make certain to use a fork and poke holes all over in the lemon, then place it into the cavity of the chicken. roast roast as stated. the chicken with be moist and have a faint lemon flavor. for more of my tried-and-true recipes, visit my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com.

1. rinse the chicken inside and out well under cold water , then pat dry using a paper towel
2. in a small bowl mix the lemon juice with oil and melted butter until blended , then rub all over the chicken
3. using clean hands rub the inside and outside of the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder , black pepper and cayenne
4. place the lemon / s inside the cavity
5. place the chicken into a baking dish
6. using cotton string tie the legs together tightly
7. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 6 hours
8. set oven to 450 degrees f
9. roast the chicken at 450 degrees for 20 minutes , then reduce the heat to 400 degrees and continue roasting for about 40 minutes
10. cover with foil and let sit for 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: Yum!  Made 2 chickens side by side in my roaster pan.  Followed directions but put 1/2 lemon in each chicken with the onion. Have done this for years and it helps make the JUCIEST meat (even good if you're not a big lemon fan!)  Thanks for a great way to cook a chicken quickly, and let us enjoy crispy skin and juicy, tasty chicken!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon with muenster cheese and dill

we eat a lot of salmon in our household as my father is a commercial fisherman in alaska.  i prepare salmon numerous ways, but this is always my favorite way to make salmon when i have company.  even people who say, "i don't care for fish, i'll have a small piece," usually end up having heaping seconds.  enjoy and please don’t use farmed fish for this recipe aka...atlantic salmon.   it’s bad for you and it doesn’t taste nearly as good.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. in baking dish , place salmon skin side down
3. cover with wine , butter and juice of 1 lemon
4. spread mustard evenly on top
5. cover with foil and bake in 400 degree oven for 8-10 minutes
6. remove foil and cover with cheese and dill
7. return to oven just long enough to melt the cheese
demonstrations.review: YUM!!  I used Dill Havarti for the cheese, since I had it here, omtted the fresh dill (would have used it in the summer when I have it in the garden) and reduced butter to 1/4 cup. Cooked perfectly, great taste. One of my new favorite salmon preparations!  Thanks ~

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan broiled flounder

this easy and delicious recipe is a classic!

1. place fillets in a single layer on a lightly greased or pan sprayed , shallow oven-to-table type broiler pan
2. brush with lemon juice
3. in a small bowl , combine remaining ingredients to make the cheese topping mixture
4. set aside
5. broil fillets 4 to 6 minutes or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
6. remove fillets from oven
7. spread with parmesan topping
8. broil an additional 30 seconds or until cheese is lightly browned and bubbly
9. garnish with lemon twists and parsley , if desired
10. since the flounder in the recipe is not marinated , if the fish comes out mushy i suspect the results are the from overcooking
11. either the fish was left under the broiler for too long , the temperature of the broiler is too high , or the rack on which the the pan placed under the broiler is too close to the heat
demonstrations.review:
This tasted good -- but .. sorry to say... it really wasn't my favorite preparation.
I think if I were to try it again -- I'd put the butter on the fish before broiling...and not in the mayo/parm mixture.  With the butter mixed in, the whole cheese topping kind of just 'melted' off the fish and I ended up with most of it on the pan. Have had similar preparation without the butter, that stayed on the fish and made a nice creamy, cheesy topping.
Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review:
This was really easy, and really good!  Only had about 15 minutes to marinate, but it was fine. The salmon had good flavor and was very tender.

I didn't have any orange juice, but did have (go figure!) some Sake (japanese white wine), so I used that.

target.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped chicken  oamc

this is another great way to make something great ahead of time to thaw as needed or eat right now with little effort!

1. flatten chicken to 1 / 2" thickness
2. spread 3 tablespoons cream cheese over each chicken piece
3. dot with butter and sprinkle with salt
4. roll up
5. wrap each with a bacon strip
6. place , seam side down , in a greased pan
7. bake , uncovered , at 400f for 35-40 minutes or until juices run clear
8. broil 6 inches from the heat for 5 minutes or until bacon is crisp
9. if you are making these ahead for future use , freeze these uncooked on a cookie sheet in your freezer
10. when solid , wrap and put in a ziplock bag or vacuum seal desired quantities
11. to cook from frozen state , thaw before cooking and follow directions above
target.review: This is a great OAMC recipe. So easy and delish! The only thing I changed was that I had some fresh parsley in the fridge so I sprinkled some chopped on top of the cream cheese. With some broccoli and no starch, this is a low cal meal...looking forward to cooking up the next 7 breasts I made.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon wrapped jalapeno poppers

these bacon-wrapped jalapeno poppers are unbelievably good! you'll love them!

1. cut stems off of peppers and cut them all in half longways
2. remove seeds from peppers
3. fill each pepper with cream cheese and sprinkle cheddar cheese on top
4. wrap 1 / 2 slice of bacon around each pepper half
5. place on baking sheets and place in 450 degree oven for 10 to 15 minutes or until bacon is fully cooked
6. remove and serve when cooled
7. enjoy !
8. i always freeze them after they are made for about 20 minutes to a hour before putting them in the oven or on the grill
9. doing this will keep the cheese from melting out as much
demonstrations.review: Yummy! The only thing I did differently was instead of shredding cheddar, I made long slices and placed it on top of the cream cheese so it wouldn't escape. I didn't precook the bacon or even place the poppers on a rack to cook, I just placed them straight on a lined baking sheet and it was great, the bacon grease just ran to the corner of the baking sheet. Next time I will leave some seeds/ribs on the jalapenos for more spice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini lasagna  lasagne    low carb

great for anyone going low carb or who has so many zucchini, they don't know what to do!! :) we found the sauce to be very mild. i think it would be better with twice as much garlic. i boiled my zucchini slices for about 3 minutes so they were partially cooked. i wanted to make sure they were soft in the finished dish or i knew the kids wouldn't eat them. ;) the cottage cheese provides a slightly tangy note. i think we would have preferred ricotta, but that is personal taste. i use my 11x7 baking dish and got 6 pieces the size of what you see in my photos. both of the guys ate two so it fed 4 of us, and i double the meat. adjust the recipe accordingly for your family.

1. cook zucchini until tender , drain and set aside
2. fry meat and onions until meat is brown and onions are tender
3. drain fat
4. add next 8 ingredients and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer , uncovered 10 minutes or until reduced to 2 cups
7. in small bowl slightly beat egg
8. add cottage cheese , half of shredded cheese and flour
9. in baking-roasting pan arrange half of the meat mixture
10. top with half of the zucchini and all the cottage cheese mixture
11. top with remaining meat and zucchini
12. bake uncovered at 375 degrees f for 30 minutes
13. sprinkle with remaining cheese
14. bake 10 minutes longer
15. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was a good recipe. I grilled my sliced zucchini before concocting my lasagne. I used ground turkey, doubled the meat, and the cheese mixture as well as the herbs and garlic. Next time I make this, I think I will add an onion bechamel as the top layer to add to the richness. Thanks for a good base recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best apple cake

this is my dh favorite cake, i have tried many apple cakes over the years and this is a winner!! so moist and dense, with a caramel taste, cannot say enough, just try it and see.

1. in a large bowl combine flour , sugar , soda and salt
2. make a well in the center and set aside
3. in a medium bowl combine eggs , oil , apple juice and vanilla
4. stir in apples and nuts
5. add the egg mixture to dry ingredients , just until moistened
6. spread batter in a greased and floured 9 x 13-inch pan
7. bake at 350f for 45-50 minutes
8. in a small saucepan combine the brown sugar , butter and cream
9. cook and stir till bubbly and all of the sugar is dissolved
10. cool slightly
11. drizzle warm sauce over cake , when it has cooled for 5 minutes , so it can seep into the cake , keeping it moist
demonstrations.review: My boyfriend loves any cake with a sauce to drizzle over it, like sticky toffee pudding. I tried this one afternoon and we tried it for an afternoon tea snack. Not only did he love it, but it was really easy to make, and all I had all the ingredients in my kitchen except for the apples which was really helpful. You gotta love any recipe that can make something out of things you already have!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
absolute best ever lasagna

my family's favorite. this is a very meaty lasagna. we prefer it with cottage cheese, but you can easily substitute ricotta.

1. brown ground meat , onion and garlic
2. add salt , pepper , parsley , oregano , basil , chopped tomatoes with juice
3. stirring until well mixed
4. cover and simmer 1 hour
5. cook lasagna noodles according to package directions
6. drain and set aside
7. spray a 13 x 9" baking pan with cooking spray
8. combine riccota cheese , eggs , pepper , 2 tablespoons parsley , parmesan cheese and 1 / 2 1lb of mozzarella cheese
9. in a lasagna pan , layer noodles , meat sauce , and cheese mixture
10. repeat
11. top off with layer of noodles
12. sprinkle evenly with remaining mozzarella cheese
13. make sure to cover noodles completely
14. bake at 375f for 40-60 minutes , or until cheese mixture is thoroughly melted
15. (i cover w / foil for about 40 minutes , then uncover for 15-20 minutes
16. let sit for 15-20 minutes before cutting and serving
demonstrations.review: Perhaps I had my expectations too high, but I thought this was okay-not as mind-blowing as the other reviews. I followed the recipe to a tee and although good, I certainly have had much better. Giving a recipe 5 stars means perfection...and I am afraid to say I didn't go for seconds.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s scalloped potato and ground beef casserole

sliced potatoes in a delicious creamy sauce on the bottom then topped with a ground beef mixture --- instead of layering the potatoes you can just mix them with the sauce in a large bowl transfer to the baking dish then top with the ground beef mixture either way is fine but the potatoes will cook a little faster if mixed with the sauce --- feel free to throw in some cooked chopped green beans, mushrooms, corn niblets to the ground beef mixture or whatever you wish, i also like sprinkle some grated cheddar cheese over the potato mixture before topping with the ground beef and then again after the casserole has been cooked, this casserole is very versatile and you don't have to worry about the exact amounts --- to save time you may cook the ground beef mixture a day ahead and refrigerate, all ingredients may be reduced to half if desired to yield 4-6 and baked in a smaller baking dish--- note some of the reviewers are stating that the potatoes are taking a long time to cook so you may want to pop them in the microwave first just to soften slightly,

1. in a skillet cook the ground beef with onion , bell pepper and chili flakes until no longer pink
2. drain fat over a colander
3. return to pan and add in garlic , season salt and black pepper
4. cook stirring with a wooden spoon until the meat is lightly browned set aside
5. for the sauce
6. in a medium bowl mix together the undiluted soup with onion , milk , sour cream , parmesan cheese , garlic powder , seasoned salt and black pepper to taste
7. mix well to combine
8. in a greased 13 x 9-inch baking dish or a large oval casserole dish , alternately layer the sliced potatoes on bottom of the baking dish , then soup mixture then the ground beef mixture on top
9. since this is a large casserole i strongly suggest to place the baking dish on a jelly-roll sheet in case of any spills
10. bake covered with foil for about 1 hour at 350 degrees f
11. uncover and continue baking for another 20-30 minutes or until the potatoes are tender
12. remove from oven then sprinkle with grated cheddar cheese
13. return to oven for 4-5 minutes or until the cheese has melted
demonstrations.review: I had really high expectations coming from Kitten & all the great reviews, unfortunately, it is not a keeper recipe for me, just personal preference. I kept all the recipe ingredients/method 100% true to the recipe too....sorry to be a party pooper!

target.recipe_text:
cherry crisp   from scratch

there are many crisp recipes on the site, but i didn't find one quite like this one. there are no cans of cherry pie filling here. yes, you too can make a cherry crisp from scratch, using real cherries! you could use this filling for many other things like ice cream topping, or toast-tites on the campfire! yummy!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. in a large bowl , gently toss first 5 ingredients together
3. place in a greased casserole dish or 8 inch square pan
4. in another bowl , mix the rest of the ingredients , using a pastry blender or fork
5. the mixture should resemble course crumbs
6. spread mixture over pie filling
7. bake for 30 minutes or until brown
8. serve warm with vanilla ice cream
9. you can substitute canned cherry pie for the homemade cherry filling if you want to , but why ?
target.review: We picked 25 pounds of Queen Anne and Bing cherries at an orchard yesterday.  We enjoyed this recipe today.  I tripled the recipe and baked it in a 9x13. I used the crisp topping (only doubled, not tripled) from Recipe #82925 since I didn't have any granola on hand.  It was an excellent dessert that I will make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
another   sommer  smoothie

okay, it's not summertime yet, even where i live in az, it's still cool.  but i love smoothies and love finding new ways of making them.  because of my ibs i have to use non-dairy products but pureeing and blending of fruit is a bit easier on my digestion (as long as i don't quaff the smoothie on an empty stomach), but you may not need to worry about that *grin^.  so i just started throwing things into the blender and please be advised all ingredient amounts are estimated, as i didn't measure them at all (except for the yogurt).  feel free to substitute with the real deal if you don't have to worry about it.  my sliced bananas were from a small bunch of organic bananas that i sliced and froze on a cookie sheet lined with foil, then put in a bag when completely frozen.  the other frozen fruit was pre-packaged from the grocery freezer section.  i poured this into a 20 oz plastic bottle to take with me to class on the bus ride and it filled it to about 3/4 from the top.  this makes 1 large serving or 2 standard size servings (i'm guessing).  this would be great for breakfast, snack, or dessert.

1. place frozen banana slices , frozen mixed berries , and frozen whole strawberries in blender with the unsweetened soy milk
2. blend , blend , blend , stopping to scrape sides occasionally
3. blend until no more large chunks remain and mixture is smooth , but thick like soft-serve ice cream consistency
4. add more milk if needed , but try to keep it thick
5. add vanilla and blend a few seconds more
6. add apple juice , cinnamon , and honey
7. blend some more
8. add in the 6 oz container of yogurt
9. blend some more
10. keep blending until everything is smooth but still thick
11. serve immediately or refrigerate or freeze and partially thaw for drinking later
12. mine is in the fridge right now and is still fairly thick , creamy , and drinkable
13. i just shake my container a couple times
14. i don't think i'll have enough left over for tomorrow , lol
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
This has a good blend of fruit.  I use raw milk rather than soy, and kefir in place of yogurt.  One of my children is lactose intolerant and can not have yogurt or pasteurized milk.
We have smoothies every single day for a snack, and this is a good addition to our recipes.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
real homemade nacho cheese sauce

found this recipe on "how to cook like your grandmother" blog.
no velvetta(yuk) no processed cheese.  real cheese real ingredients.  serve hot as it will set when cool.

1. melt the butter in a heavy bottom sauce pan
2. stir in the corn starch
3. add the milk
4. add cream cheese stir until it's melted and smooth
5. add the cheddar and stir until it is well melted
6. add the monterey jack and stir again
7. stir in hot sauce and paprika
8. enjoy over tortilla chips or veggies
demonstrations.review: Made as written, I got a gloopy, thick, oily, unappetizing mess.  However, I poured off the cheese oil and slowly added cream and the texture improved greatly.  I probably added 1 full cup, though I didn't measure.  I also added salt, home canned jalapenos and more hot sauce.  As a base, this recipe is good, but it was still missing something flavorwise.  I'll be comparing other recipes and added/subtracting till it's just right!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
texas homemade bbq sauce for canning or oamc

ok, in texas we do not cook with sauce! it is only used as a condiment to top anything we want or to dip things in. there have been so many arguments started over whose is best- but we all know mama's is best! this makes a bucket load so use the tool to change the number of servings or freeze, can or give away the rest. 

"samantha in uk states that this is not safe to can as it has butter in it. i have never had a problem but please be aware of that info. if you are concerned please try substituting with butterbuds / molly mcbutter type butter substitute or do not can. freezing is another option as well "


if you do decide to can this use a boiling water bath, process half-pints and pints for 20 minutes at 0-1000 feet in elevation, 25 minutes for more elevation.

1. saute onion in butter until clear
2. add garlic and saut for 1 minute
3. add all other ingredients and simmer for at least 30 minutes
4. i throw the lemons in after i have squeezed the juice out and remove before serving
5. taste and adjust seasoning as desired
6. can be frozen , canned or stored in refrigerator for 6 months
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent sauce. I have put up 12 pints and will make more as needed throughout the summer.  I omitted the butter, since I was planning on canning it, and just added the onions to the mix with everything else.  I didn't worry about chopping the peppers too fine; I just took my immersion blender to the sauce after the simmering.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
venison  goetta

goetta is often compared to scrapple or breakfast sausage. i found this recipe in a wild game cook book.

1. combine venison , hot water and onion in a large skillet
2. strip bay leaf from vein and finely crumble into skillet
3. simmer until meat is no longer pink and onion is tender
4. add pepper , oatmeal and salt
5. stir quickly and cook for 3 minutes
6. remove from heat and season with onion powder , thyme , sage , nutmeg and crushed red pepper
7. spoon meat mixture into loaf pan sprayed with vegetable oil spray
8. let stand until firm
9. remove from pan , cut loaf in half and wrap each half in plastic wrap
10. freeze one and refrigerate the other
11. to use , slice meat 1 / 4-inch thick , coat gently with flour and pan fry in small amount of butter or vegetable oil until broned on each side
12. serve with eggs and toast for breakfast
13. you can add more crushed red pepper flakes to taste
demonstrations.review: I was gifted with 9 pounds of venison burger.  I searched for good recipes and found this one.  It was the first time my eight children had ever tasted venison.  They loved it!  I made a 1.5x recipe, since the meat was portioned into 1 1/2 pound packages.  I served it scooped, since I was too impatient to let it stand and 'age' overnight.  Paired alongside scrambled eggs with cheese and homemade buttermilk biscuits, it was a satisfying meal we will repeat.  I have plenty left over to make the sausage rolls for the freezer.  Thanks for the great recipe and a good experience with venison for my children!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground turkey   rice

my family was tired of the usual chicken & rice dish that i make so i came up with this one dish meal that's easy to throw together. they like this more than the chicken & rice.

if you like more rice you can increase it by another 1/2 cup.  you could even experiment using other vegetables i.e., frozen corn niblets, peas, green beans, etc.

1. sprinkle the seasoned salt and fennel seed over the ground turkey
2. mix well
3. spray large skillet with vegetable spray and place turkey mixture in pan
4. over medium-high heat cook and stir turkey until browned
5. drain well
6. while the turkey is draining add the vegetables to the hot pan and saute for about 5 minutes
7. add the turkey back into the pan and mix
8. sprinkle rice over mixture and pour in chicken broth
9. when broth comes to a boil reduce heat , cover and simmer for approx 20-30 minutes , stirring occasionally until liquid is absorbed
10. when the rice is cooked if there is still too much liquid in the pan remove cover , increase the heat and continue cooking until all liquid is absorbed
demonstrations.review: I tripled this recipe to serve as a main dish for my family of ten.  Everyone agreed I could have 4x or 5x'ed it.  It tasted great.  Changes: I used two pounds of ground turkey, 1 tsp of a homemade seasoned salt, no fennel, omitted the green peppers and onion, added other veggies.  It came out perfect for us!

target.recipe_text:
chardonnay spinach turkey burgers

easy twist on a burger.  i love this recipe. great moist flavor and served with, feta cheese and of course ... fresh tomato and my tarragon mayo.

1. bacon -- saute the bacon in a non stick pan on medium heat until crispy , add the onion and garlic and cook just a minute until soft
2. to a large bowl , add the turkey , bacon mixture , , eggs chardonnay , parsley , scallions , spinach and mix well but do not over mix
3. it will only make the burgers tough
4. form the patties -- and cover and freeze for 15-30 minutes
5. this just helps them to stay together once grilled
6. make the aioli -- mix the mayonnaise , red pepper and tarragon
7. grill away ! just grill in a saute pan , grill pan or outside -- which ever you have
8. make sure to add the cheese and melt to get nice and gooey
9. for the burger -- i like to toast the bun , that is up to you and then slather with the mayo , add the lettuce and tomato and that is all it needs
10. now you can add mustard or other condiments but i don't think anything else is needed with this burger
11. make ahead and freeze and make the next week
target.review: This was fabulous. I used a 1.25 pound package of turkey which yielded 5 burgers. Still I used the entire box of spinach and the full amount of bacon. I only used a splash of chardonnay since I didn't use the full amount of meat which was perfect. So decadent. I served this with the mayo that was a real cinch to throw together along with romaine lettuce leaves, ripe tomatoes, and extra raw onion for the adults. I had feta but it was easy to put cheddar on the other burgers for my family whom aren't nearly as adventurous as I am.  My husband had 3! I only know this because I had planned to take one to work with me for lunch today but there wasn't any leftover when I went to the fridge. Very good and easy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kmart sub s   a blast from the past

i had an awful craving hit me for one of these wonderful k-mart sub's and had to have one! i searched high and low and finally found a woman on a message board that used to work the deli counter in the late 80's at a k-mart in dayton, ohio. this was one of the same stores that my mom would take me as a kid to get one of these wonderful sub's and a frozen coke! i used to stand in front of the counter and watch them make these sub's and remembered all but one of the ingredients. make sure that you wrap your sub's and allow them to sit for 30 minutes before serving or they are not the same. this allows the bread, meat and veggies to show some love to one another.

1. slice all of your veg
2. dill pickle , tomato , lettuce and onion
3. layout your meats in a stack and slice them half
4. slice your cheese in half
5. open the rolls without breaking the hinge of the bread
6. squirt on the mustard in a v shape pattern across both the top and bottom bun
7. top bun: place 4-6 pickle slivers on the top bun
8. bottom bun: 4 salami halves
9. 2 bologna halves
10. 2 cheese slices
11. 2 ham halves
12. 4 tomato slices
13. shredded lettuce
14. 4-8 pepper rings
15. carefully close the sandwich and wrap it in foil or plastic wrap and allow to sit either at room temperature or in the refrigerator , for 30 minutes
16. unwrap and serve !
17. i cannot locate it on the west coast , but mom says she still buys it in the deli back in ohio
18. if you can find it , use it ! the stuff is addicting
demonstrations.review: It does not get more nostalgic than this!  I can not believe that I purchased processed cheese or bologna but I did and I have no regrets.  I made these last night, wrapped them up, and stuck them in the fridge. I just sunk my teeth into this gem an I am in love.....right down to the soggy lettuce!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crispy cornflake potatoes

one of our favorite ways to make potatoes and you generally have the ingredients on hand. it's out of a church cookbook by suzanne sachs

1. pre heat oven to 400f
2. cut potatoes into 4 wedges
3. dip them in the melted butter and sprinkle with salt
4. roll in crumbs and place on greased baking sheet
5. bake for 40 minutes
6. serve hot
demonstrations.review: This got mixed reviews at my table.  My husband loved them, I thought they were okay, and my son wouldn't eat them.  It may be a texture thing since we have never eaten potatoes quite like this before.  I think some extra spices in this would go a long way if I were to make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
butter baked apples

this is a recipe that i came up with.  my friend love it.

1. peel , core , and cut apples in half , and place in slow cooker
2. drizzle with melted butter , and lemon juice
3. sprinkle with sugar , cinnamon , and nutmeg
4. cover & cook on low for 3 hours , or on high for about 2 hours
5. it can be served with vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: This wasn't quite what I had expected so perhaps I did something incorrectly but it seems so straight forward so maybe it is just a matter of expectation.  This turned out more like an applesauce for me which isn't what I was expecting at all.  I had envisioned something more like a baked apple even if this was done in a slow cooker.  Also I used a tarter apple and this was a mistake.  The recipe didn't call for enough sugar for a tart apple which is fine, just wish I had known that going into it.  I did not serve over ice cream as I did not have any but I do imagine that would have helped the situation quite a bit.  Thank you for posting and I will be trying again and updating my review.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grenadian spice cake

i used a tube or bundt pan and served it with a spiced whipped cream.
i also added a bit more lime zest.
make sure to test for doneness at around 50 minutes depending on what pan you use.
just want to add a note.
this is a dense cake .
the flour is sifted into the measuring cup for each cup and not measured first then sifted.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease a 9x5 inch loaf pan
3. sift together the flour , baking powder and salt , set aside
4. in a medium bowl , cream together the sugar and butter
5. beat in the eggs one at a time , then stir in the lime zest , nutmeg , cinnamon and allspice
6. add the dry ingredients alternately with the milk , stirring after each addition
7. pour batter into the prepared pan
8. bake for 75 to 90 minutes in the preheated oven , until a toothpick inserted comes out clean
9. cool in the pan for 10 minutes before turning out onto a rack to cool completely
demonstrations.review: My cake turned out dry and dense and not what I was expecting.  I used a bundt pan and checked it at 50 minutes and it was done.  When the cake came out of the oven it wasn't as fluffy as I expected it would have been and upon cooling it dropped.  My baking powder is active and I double checked the ingredients but something didn't go as planned.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
annas apple ginger pecan tart

this is from anna olsen and the splenda site.

1. for crust , beat butter and cream cheese until smooth
2. add flour and stir until dough comes together
3. shape into a disk , wrap and chill for 2 hours , until firm
4. preheat oven to 375 f
5. on a lightly floured surface , roll out dough to 1 / 4-inch thick and line an 8-inch , removable-bottom fluted tart pan
6. freeze while preparing filling
7. for filling , whisk butter and the splenda brown sugar blend
8. add eggs , one at a time , whisking after each addition
9. stir in ginger , cinnamon , vanilla and salt
10. place chilled tart shell on a baking tray and arrange apples and pecans in shell
11. gently pour filling over apples and pecans
12. bake for 40 to 50 minutes , until edges of pastry are browned and filling no longer jiggles when pan is moved
13. let tart cool for an hour before slicing
14. serve warm , room temperature or chilled
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  For a crust novice I was frustrated but I powered through and got out the flour :)  and it turned out really good!  I used regular brown sugar and walnuts (personal preference) and was very happy.  This may find a space on my Thanksgiving table this year!

target.recipe_text:
taco chicken nuggets

this is always one of the first things to disappear during parties! (if you use the egg substitute and no butter it won't be as crispy, but will be low fat.)

1. heat oven to 375
2. mix crumbs , taco seasonings and butter
3. dip nuggets into egg , then into crumbs , coating evenly
4. place on an ungreased cookie sheet and bake 10-15 minutes til chicken is done and coating is crisp
5. serve with picante sauce for dipping
target.review: So Easy and quick. Instead of adding butter to the crumbs I just put a thin coat on the cookie sheet instead. I got carried away and made extra bread crumbs so thin sliced a couple potatoes , coated them also and cooked right on the same cookie sheet with the chicken. Both were a big hit. Thanks for sharing this great recipe Junebug!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bow tie lemon chicken

i have found that you can use this as a main dish or a side dish it good both warm and cold. i added a cook time but that is mainly for the cooking of the chicken. enjoy

1. cook pasta according to directions
2. meanwhile , sprinkle chicken with lemon pepper
3. in a large non-stick skillet , stir fry chicken with garlic in oil until chicken juices run clear
4. remove and keep warm
5. add broth , peas , carrots , cream cheese and lemon juice to the skillet
6. cook and stir until cheese melts
7. drain pasta
8. add pasta , chicken , salt to vegetable mixture
9. heat through
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner last night and the family loved it. I really liked that the vegis were in the dish so made it an easy one dish meal and they added alot of color too. The cream cheese really made for a tasty sauce and a change from a regular cheese sauces. Will be making this alot in the future I am sure. Thank you for sharing this with us Kim1 !!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sheila s orange sauce

this is a nice sauce to serve with roast pork....a change from applesauce. it's on an old food covered recipe card.....no idea where it came from.

1. combine all and cook until thick and clear
2. remove cloves and serve
3. cooking time is approximate
demonstrations.review: Great recipe !  Very good with roast duck. I find the amount of cloves to be more of a personal taste amount. I only throw in a few to enhance the orange just a bit. Very quick and easy to make. Thanks for sharing this recipe with us!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome sesame chicken

people love this sesame chicken. it tastes as close to the restaurant version as i think you can get. it is from about.com i found this a couple of years ago on that site, and bf requests it a tleast 2-3 times a month. it really is great, and although there are a lot of ingredients, it's basically simple to prepare.

1. cut the chicken into small , approximately 1-inch cubes
2. add the marinade ingredients and marinate the chicken for at least 20 minutes
3. while the chicken is marinating , prepare the sauce
4. mix together all of the sauce ingredients except for the green onion
5. pour them into a small pot and bring to a boil
6. turn the heat down to a low and keep warm while you are deep-frying the chicken
7. heat oil for deep-frying
8. when the oil is ready , add the marinated chicken a few pieces at a time , sliding them into oil carefully , and not to overcrowd
9. deepfry until golden brown
10. remove the cooked chicken pieces from the oil and drain on paper towels
11. repeat with the remainder of the chicken
12. just before you are finished deep-frying , bring the sauce back up to a boil
13. mix in the green onion
14. place the chicken on a large platter and pour sauce over
15. sprinkle with the sesame seeds
16. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This is definantly 5 star ! My husband and step kids here in the UK love it and my own grown children in the USA have me make it now whenever I am home for a visit! Its easy and delicious!! Thanks for sharing this recipe with us !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top scalloped potatoes

great any time, particularly good on a campout on the camp stove, we have even done over an open fire, in a cast iron pot, a little ash never hurt.
(the amount of salt has been corrected to 1 teaspoon, sorry it was a typo)

1. combine potatoes with onion , salt and milk in heavy frypan
2. simmer covered for 30 to 40 minutes or until potatoes are tender
3. sprinkle cheese , cayenne and crumbs over top
4. continue cooking uncovered for 15 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe for when your oven is already in use and you need a stove top potato recipe! I went with GinnyP's idea for 1 cup cream and 1/2 cup milk and I always put extra cheese in anything that calls for cheese but otherwise did it all according to the recipe. Very good! Thanks for sharing this recipe with us Derf!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 layer vanilla chocolate raspberry bars

i love recipes like this! the vanilla chips are creamy and combine well with the raspberry! it is just perfect for any occasion! 8)

1. heat oven to 350
2. in large mixing bowl , combine sugar , butter , salt and vanilla extract
3. beat at medium speed , scraping bowl often and then reduce speed to low
4. beat , adding in flour 1 cup at a time , scraping bowl often , until mixture is crumbly
5. set aside 1 cup of mixture
6. add eggs to remaining crumb mixture in the bowl
7. beat until mixture forms dough
8. evenly press into ungreased 13x9-inch pan
9. bake 30 minutes or until lightly browned
10. slather preserves over the hot , partially baked bars
11. sprinkle vanilla chips over and add reserved crumb mixture
12. baking for additional 20-25 minutes or until topping is lightly browned
13. allow to cool thoroughly before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review: This recipe is wonderful! Its perfect for a quick desert that looks like you spent alot more time making than you actually did. The vanilla chips make it more than just a desert bar. I have not had anyone try this that didnt love it. Thanks Ocean~Ivy!!

target.recipe_text:
banana brunch cake

i use this recipe a lot with over ripened bananas.  i got it out of an electric cooperative newsletter years ago.  if i have overripened bananas, i stick them skin and all in the freezer.  when i want to make this, i take them out and defrost them in the microwave.
(per reviewers suggestions, i have doubled the topping ingredients)

1. heat oven to 350 and grease 13x9 pan
2. combine bisquick , 3 / 4 cup brown sugar , and cinnamon
3. add bananas , milk , egg , and oil
4. mix well
5. spread into prepared pan
6. combine nuts , 1 / 2 cup brown sugar , and butter
7. sprinkle evenly over batter
8. bake 30 minutes or until golden brown and toothpick stuck in center comes out clean
9. cool and enjoy !
target.review: WOW! I made this recipe for Mothers Day Brunch yesterday and let me tell you it was sooo good.  Everyone raved about it.  It is very simple to make with ingredients I always have on hand.  I used pecans in my topping and it was yummy indeed.  I am making again this weekend for my father-in-law.  Thanks for the keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy one bowl vanilla cupcakes

this recipe goes back over 20 years, i like the simplicity of this recipe and for a one bowl cupcake they are pretty darn good, 1-1/2 teaspoons almond extract may be used in place of the vanilla, using butter in place of shortening will alter the texture it is best to only use shortening --- if you don't have paper liners grease the tins generously or see my recipe#78579

1. set oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , mix together the flour with sugar , baking powder and salt until combined
3. add in the shortening cream or milk , vanilla and eggs
4. beat on medium speed of an electric mixer scraping the bowl constantly until just blended
5. pour into paper-lined regular size muffin tins filling under just three-quarters full
6. bake for 20-22 minutes or until the cupcakes test done
7. immediately remove from pans
8. cool completely before frosting
demonstrations.review: I made these this past weekend and I must say they were very good.  My daughter loved them.  I have to say, as with most home made cakes they do taste better the next day.  I also frosted them with chocolate butter cream frosting, very very good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade gnocchi

i have not tried this recipe yet, but i intend to soon. according to the article, that came with the recipe in this morning's local newspaper, these gnocchi are light as a feather. the recipe comes from a former fine dining establishment in our area that we used to go to very often and the food was outstanding! i am guessing at the prep and cook times.

1. boil potato and mash
2. combine potato with eggs and salt and whip until fluffy
3. add ricotta cheese , butter , romano cheese and flour
4. knead until smooth
5. shape into 1 / 2" rolls and cut into 1" lengths
6. make impression with thumb in each piece , then lightly dust with flour
7. drop into boiling salted water and cook only until they rise to the surface
8. drain and serve with tomato sauce and grated cheese
demonstrations.review: These were PERFECT.  The texture and taste were just like at my favorite Italian Cafe.  This does make a lot of dough and I was not prepared to freeze it so I cut the recipe in half.  I made mine with a garlic alfredo sauce and served it with Fillet Mignon. Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
