demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: WOW! For the amount of effort involved, this recipe really delivers over the top flavor! I doubled the pasta and chicken, but the sauce was plenty using 2 cups of cream. I also added a large fresh chopped tomato and more green onions. I will definitely be using this recipe over and over again. Thanks for posting it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mushroom   nut pate

found this recipe years ago, and don't even remember where it came from. i've tweaked this endlessly, adding parmesan cheese, different nuts, combinations of mushrooms, and different seasonings. if you like mushrooms and nuts, you'll like this. the recipe even looks like a pate - very similar color and texture. we especially like it hot, but it's still very good cold (put on a cracker, top with some cheese and roasted red pepper and broil - yum) or at room temperature. great year-round, and especially at parties.

1. spread nuts in shallow pan and toast in oven until lightly browned
2. melt butter or margarine in large frying pan / skilled on medium heat
3. add onions , garlic , mushrooms , salt , thyme , and pepper
4. cook , stirring occasionally , 'til onion is soft and most of the juices have evaporated
5. in food processor , whirl nuts to form paste
6. add oil and whirl until creamy
7. add mushroom mixture and whirl until smooth
8. can be served hot , cold , or even at room temperature with fresh bread or your favorite crackers
demonstrations.review: Delicious and simple.  I used Baby Bella mushrooms, and will experiment with others.  I also used walnuts, and was very happy with that.  I do think I may try the ideas mentioned by others - adding parmigiana, and maybe also Madeira.  I will use this recipe time and again, I am sure.

target.recipe_text:
grilled t bone steaks

this is an excellent marinade for any steak.  the flavor is just wonderful.  our t-bones came out perfect.  very tender with a wonderful flavor. the original recipe is from toh with some changes to suit our taste. prep time does not include the time it takes to marinate the steaks.

1. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the first 11 ingredients
2. add steaks
3. seal the bag and turn to coat
4. refrigerate overnight , turning as often as you can
5. drain and discard marinade
6. grill steaks , over high heat for about 5 minutes on each side or until meat reaches desired doneness
target.review: What a awesome recipe. Made this for Father's Day. You know when you have a good steak when they melt in your mouth and the family puts the steak sauce down, due to "these are so good without any steak sauce"! The flavor speaks for itself. Thanks for the posting. This is Top of the list in marinades!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever baked beans  crock pot

these are a hit at my house for even those that aren't fans of baked beans.  i think it's the bacon that adds the x-tra somethin somethin.  or maybe the french fried onions.  this can also be done in the oven and so reduce the baking time to 1 1/2 hrs.

1. fry bacon until it's almost done
2. mix all ingredients together using only 3 / 4 of the can of french fried onions
3. cut up the bacon into bite size pieces
4. add bacon
5. place crock pot on low for 6 hours
6. 1 / 2 hours before it's done place remaining onions on top
demonstrations.review: These are now our family baked beans! We made these for Fathers Day Cook Out. These are the best beans I have ever ate. These are 5***** plus 5 more stars! I baked my bacon in the oven and this was quick and easy. My mom who is 73 years old could not believe how good this recipe is! Thanks for Posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best brown sugar turkey brine

this brine is enough for up to a 20-pound whole turkey and will produce the most juiciest and delicious bird you will ever have, with this brine you will taste only the turkey not any extra herbs or flavorings that are added in to some brines  ---  i use my food-safe picnic cooler to brine my turkey in it works quite well, you might want to purchase one if you plan on brining your turkey on a regular basis, and you will once you have tried this method just make certain to purchase one that is food-safe --- you may omit the garlic but i strongly suggest to add it --- you must use only kosher salt not regular table salt --- if desired after brining continue with my recipe#199612

1. in a large bucket or container mix together the warm water with brown sugar and salt
2. stir until no kosher salt and sugar granules remain in the water
3. add in worcestershire sauce , peppercorns , and garlic
4. stir until the worcestershire sauce is combined
5. cool the water until almost room temperature
6. wash the turkey inside and out with cold water , then place in the brine
7. place in refrigerator for 24 hours ,
8. remove the turkey from the brine and rinse the turkey thoroughly under cold running water
9. pat dry with paper towels then cover and refrigerate if not preparing right away or continue with my turkey recipe
demonstrations.review: This is the 2nd year our family has brined our turkey. Was not happy with last years recipe, so I searched for a new brine. This was amazing. We brined our turkey at least 30 hours. It was great. Prepared the turkey in a roaster oven. Thank you for this recipe. I will use this again next year.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe I make often. It truly has an exceptional taste. I would give this 20 stars if I could. I actually make a whole casserole dish of this on Sunday Evening and then make individual lunches for the following week. This freezes well and taste wonderful. This paired with a vegetable is an inexpensive lunch and good for you. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cheesy hash browns and kielbasa soup  crock pot

when my mom first gave me this recipe, i was pretty skeptical - but it became an instant favorite in our house!! i like it because it is fast and simple to make, inexpensive, and reheats very well. i'll post the ingredients for the original version and offer the healthier alternatives at the end of the recipe.

1. in crock pot , combine hash browns , kielbasa , broth and onions
2. stir well and cook on low 6-8 hours
3. 30 minutes before serving , cut cheese into cubes and stir into soup
4. cover and cook on high 30 minutes or until cheese is melted
5. we like this soup pretty thick , but if you prefer a thinner soup now is a good time to add some extra broth or milk
6. wait until after the cheese has melted to add extra liquid so you can be sure of the consistency
7. serve hot with crusty bread !
8. to make this recipe a lot healthier , use turkey kielbasa , fat free / low sodium chicken broth , and light velveeta
9. i routinely use these substitutions and the soup still turns out fantastic ! if i have the time , i do like to remove the casings from the turkey kielbasa as i think they tend to get a little chewy when cooked all day
10. just split them carefully with a knife and peel away the casings before chopping
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I crocked this while at work. Wonderful flavor with the Kielbasa. Easy preparation. I added more chickenbroth for our taste. Very addictive! Could not have just 1 bowl. Yum Yum!! This is a keeper and I will be taking this to work for a pitch in where I know it will be well received. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini shrimp cocktail appetizers

from kraftfoods(dot)com website.  i made these for a party and i've had so many people request the recipe.  kraft calls for using finely chopped onions but i skipped that just to make it an even faster appetizer to get on the table.

1. spread each cracker with 1 tsp of the cream cheese spread
2. top evenly with the cocktail sauce and one shrimp
3. sprinkle some of the finely chopped onions on top
demonstrations.review: Great Presentation and Great Taste. I made these for  a St. Francis University,  Fort Wayne, Indiana) tail gate party. I used the Ritz Club Crackers. Making these again for office pitch in. Thank you for posting this recipe. I used the cream cheese with chives. This is a Keeper. Happy Holidays!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous caesar salad

i developed this dressing years ago, and i can honestly say that you won't be able to keep your spoon out of the fridge for a taste, it is *that* good! --- although i do think the dressing is better with the anchovy it can certainly be made without them. in a pinch i have even substituted buttermilk for the half and half cream, just use about the same amount --- this dressing gets stronger with refrigeration time so a small amount of fresh garlic goes a long way! ---- usually one recipe without doubling is perfect for one large romaine lettuce, if you are serving a large crowd of people you might want to double -- salad dressing will not work for this use *only* mayonnaise, i find hellman's brand mayonnaise works the best and for the  perfect companion to this salad see my recipe#125034-------------lower-fat option use reduced fat mayonnaise and fat-free half and half or low-fat milk --- also see my recipe#66596

1. in a small 2-cup mini food processor , process / mince the anchovy fillets and garlic together until finely minced
2. add in the remaining ingredients , and process for 30 seconds , or more until well mixed
3. adjust seasonings to taste
4. thin with buttermilk for a thinner consistency if desired
5. store in fridge , covered in a glass container for 3 or more hours before using
6. toss desired amount of dressing with romaine lettuce and croutons
7. sprinkle with more grated parmesan cheese if desired
target.review: I love a really good Caesar salad so, when I came across this one, I had to try it.  I followed the recipe exactly w/one exception; I used Romano instead of parm (personal preference).  Try this with Kittencal's Garlic Croutons and you will never buy bottled dressing or a box of croutons again.  Thanks, Kittencal for another winner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best garlic pizza dough for the bread machine

i sometimes add in some dried herbs like oregano or basil it really adds tons of extra flavor, this recipes makes a lovely soft chewy crust and i don't think you will searching any further once you try this dough, it also makes great calzones :)

1. place all ingredients into the pan in order , or according to your manfacturer's directions
2. press the dough cycle and start
3. check the dough after about 4-5 minutes of kneading to see is more water or flour is needed to create a soft semi-sticky dough
4. when the machine signals the end of the cycle , remove the dough and knead gently into a tight ball on a lightly floured surface
5. cover and let rest for 20 minutes
6. stretch into desired size for your pizza pan
demonstrations.review: This can also be made in a KA mixer.  I combined the water with the yeast and sugar to proof.  I then added to the yeast mixture the oil and powdered milk to dissolve.  The mixture was then added to the dry ingredients and kneaded with the dough hook for about 5 min.  The texture of the dough was pizza-perfect.  The use of bread flour makes all the difference.  Like some of the other reviewers, I too added dried herbs to the dough, it gave it that something extra missing from other pizza dough recipes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review:
So simple yet so unbelieveably scrumptious.  
The first time I made them I followed the recipe precisely with walnuts, white choc. chips & semi-sweet as the add-ins.  Last night playing around with the batter, I added 1t of instant coffee to the batter to enhance the flavor.  Also, I used dark 100% cocoa.  In a word-delicious.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon bun french toast

this just might be the best french toast you will ever have! this tastes like a giant sticky cinnamon bun. i used texas toast in place of egg bread for this and it worked well. you can use half and half in place of whipping cream. this recipe serves 2 people double or triple the recipe to serve more. although i have not tried it as yet, if you plan on doubling the recipe, i would guess you could use half maple syrup and half pancake syrup due to cost factor.  when i doubled the recipe, i used 2 cups of maple syrup, 1 cup whipping cream and 1 cup half and half.

1. in a saucepan bring the maple syrup , 1 tablespoon butter and 1 teaspoon cinnamon to a boil
2. boil for 2 minutes
3. in a bowl whisk eggs , whipping cream , vanilla , 3 tablespoons maple syrup mixture and the remaining 1 teaspoon cinnamon
4. place the bread slices in a large baking dish
5. pour the egg mixture over bread slices
6. turn to coat
7. pierce bread in several places with a fork
8. let stand for 5 minutes
9. melt butter in a skillet over medium heat
10. add bread and cook until brown
11. add in more butter to skillet , and turn bread over
12. cook until brown
13. transfer to plates and serve with more syrup of sprinkle with confectioners sugar
demonstrations.review: Amazing!  This is my new standard french toast recipe.  I prepared this the quick way by dipping my favorite Pepperidge Farm Soft White into the batter and frying in butter.  I did not have any maple syrup on-hand so, I substituted regular butter-flavored pancake syrup.  Also, to get the full flavor of this recipe you must, must, must use the best quality cinnamon you can find; it makes all the difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrabba s chicken bryan

i got this copycat recipe from algy's recipe exchange.

1. saute garlic and onion in 2 tbls
2. butter in a large skillet over medium heat until tender
3. stir wine and lemon juice into skillet , increase heat to medium high , and simmer to reduce by half
4. reduce heat to low and stir in cold butter , one slice at a time
5. stir in tomatoes , basil , kosher salt , and white pepper
6. remove from heat
7. set aside
8. brush chicken breasts with olive oil and sprinkle with salt and black pepper
9. grill chicken over hot coals 15-20 minutes , or until cooked through
10. a couple of minutes before chicken is done , place equal amounts of cheese on each breast spoon prepared sun-dried tomato sauce over chicken
demonstrations.review: This was a pleasure not only for my taste buds, but my nose as well; my mouth and the mouths of my guests were watering the entire time the topping simmered on the stove.  Unbelieveable flavor, the lemon juice and white wine really paired harmoniously with the sundried tomatoes and goat cheese.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
demonstrations.review: Easy and delicious.  I seasoned the chicken with my go-to spice blend and sauteed in butter, to impart more flavor.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe as written.  Served with Spanish Rice, Smashed Pintos w/ Cheese and a salad.  This dish also freezes very well.

target.recipe_text:
new red potato salad

we can't wait for those lucious little new red potatoes to be ready in our garden so we can fix this great potato salad!!

1. bring a large pot of water to a boil
2. drop in the new potatoes and reduce to low
3. cover and cook for 20 min , or until potatoes are done
4. dice potatoes into a lg bowl
5. add onion
6. mix all remaining ingredients in sm bowl
7. pour over the potatoes and mix well
8. best if refrigerated for 1-2 hours
target.review:
This is so amazingly good! I did omit the vinegar and used celery instead of the seeds & it turned out great.I found this reciepe last week and have made it twice as everyone loves it!
Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breaded breast of chicken  chicken cutlets

very simple chicken recipe, but one my family is quite fond of. they love when there are leftovers, so they can make sandwiches!

1. pound chicken to flatten
2. sprinkle salt and pepper on each
3. dip into beaten eggs and then coat with bread crumbs
4. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium heat
5. saute garlic until golden and then discard
6. place chicken in skillet and brown on both sides , cooking about 5 minutes on each side , or until chicken is fork tender
7. cooking time will vary depending on how thick your chicken is
demonstrations.review: Boy was this good! I followed the directions exactly except I added some panko crumbs (japanese bread crumbs)to the italian bread crumbs for an extra crispy crunch. Our grandson,who is 7, couldn't eat enough and niether could we for that matter. Will use this one over and over. A great change form regular ol' chicken breast's! :) Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
demonstrations.review:
This dish rocks! The only thing I changed was to add thinly sliced onion and freash mushrooms to the top of the sauce before I added the bread crumbs. Next time I think I will add some capers also.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chimichurri

this too easy sauce, of argentine origin, makes your steak taste like it was just dragged through the garden! great on rare, chargrilled, flank steak.

1. pulse parsley in processor to chop
2. add remaining ingredients and blend
3. separate sauce into equal parts
demonstrations.review:
This is the best chimichurri I have ever had!My boss whi is from argentina served it at a bbq and didn't follow a recipe so it was very hard for me to reproduce,ahhh but now I can.We use it on ribs,steak,bratwurst and alot more.I have made many copies for our friends as they all love it.
Many thanks Chef Blade!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish taco sauce

to save time, i oven-bake breaded or battered frozen fish (but if we had a deep fryer, i'd probably use it). i slice cabbage very thin, it works better for the tacos than shredded cabbage. add your favorite tortillas, and you have an easy, crunchy, and great tasting meal. prep time is just for making the sauce.

1. blend mayo and sour cream together
2. blend in lime juice , then capers , cumin , oregano , dill , and cayenne
3. it can be served immediately or can be made ahead
4. i assemble my tacos by putting 1-2 fish fingers , add a sprinkle of cabbage , a drizzle of sauce , then roll up
demonstrations.review:
This is so good! I have been looking for a good sauce for fish taco's and this is it! I did omit the cumin & cayanne and followed the rest to a "T". Wonderful, I will use this one often.
Thanks TigerJo

demonstrations.recipe_text:
microwave poached eggs

i have been poaching eggs in the microwave for many years.  for me this is the best way to prepare poached eggs for 2.  it is quick, easy and almost foolproof.  please make sure you use a toothpick to pierce the yolk before cooking or it will explode!

1. add the water and white vinegar to a 6 ounce custard cup
2. break egg into cup , pierce egg yolk with toothpick , and cover dish loosely with plastic wrap
3. place in microwave and cook for 1 minute or until desired doneness
4. you may need to experiment with cooking times based on the wattage of your microwave and taste preference
5. immediately remove egg from hot water with a slotted spoon as it will continue to cook
6. serve with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: This is a wonderful way to poach eggs! My microwave is a 1350 watt so I had to loose a couple of eggs before I got it. (power at 6 for 60 seconds)But we have chickens so loosing a couple of eggs is no big deal.This is the only way to go from now on...Thank you!

target.recipe_text:
whole wheat peanut butter oatmeal cookies

i love these cookies.  they are crunchy and chewy and creamy and warm and good.  i have been known to let the kids have them for breakfast when i want to sleep in on a saturday morning.  but that is a secret, so don't tell anyone. ;-)

1. in a large bow combine the softened margarine and peanut butter
2. i measure the peanut butter by packing it tightly into a metal measuring cup
3. then i scrape it out with my fingers
4. add the sugar or sucanat and the egg to the bowl
5. mix it up really good until it is smooth , fluffy and glossy
6. i do this with a wire whisk
7. you could use a big spoon if you prefer
8. add the vanilla and stir it in a little
9. add the salt , baking soda , oatmeal , and flour
10. stir it all up really well
11. you need a spoon to stir in the dry ingredients
12. a whisk just won't work for this part because the batter is so thick
13. drop the dough by spoonfuls onto an ungreased cookie sheet
14. these cookies don't spread very well so flatten the cookies with a fork or the flat bottom of a cup which has been dipped into flour
15. bake at 350f for about 12 minutes
16. half a cup of chocolate chips may be added to the batter if desired
target.review: I was looking for a cookie that wouldn't be "so bad" to give to my one year old. These were so easy! So tasty! I didn't quite have enough oats, but they still turned out really good. All I heard from my daughter was num num num. Thanks for posting this recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft snickerdoodle cookies

these snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. they are so fast to put together too! i actually got it from an old recipe that my great grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. grandma always knows best!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix softened butter , 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl
3. combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt in a separate bowl
4. blend dry ingredients into butter mixture
5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I lost my snickerdoodle recipe, tried another and it was miserable...came here, which I should have anyway since I get so many good recipes from this site. I think these are better than the recipe I lost! Soooo delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony salmon patties

enjoy.        

1. combine the first nine ingredients
2. mix well
3. spoon into eight greased muffin cups , using 1 / 4 cup in each
4. bake at 350 for 45 minutes or until browned
5. meanwhile , melt butter in a saucepan
6. stir in the flour to form a smooth paste
7. gradually stir in milk
8. bring to a boil over medium heat , stirring constantly
9. cook for 2 minutes or until thickened
10. remove from the heat
11. stir in lemon juice , salt and cayenne
12. serve over patties
demonstrations.review: I had a playgroup scheduled for the local playground with just snacks, but weather changed our plans and we had to take it indoors. So, it was the night before and I wanted to make a lunch item but couldn't run to the store for anything. This recipe was great. I love that I could make several patties without frying! The patties pretty much tasted like the ones I make and fry, but the sauce was awesome! I added more lemon juice as I love lemon. I kind of wish I'd added a little less cayenne, however...it was super tasty but a little spicy for my personal taste. Husband loved it and didn't think it was spicy at all. I put the sauce in a bowl and everyone spooned it to use as dip for the patties. Much loved!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic biscotti

this isn't anything fancy, just a basic biscotti.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spread almonds on a baking sheet and toast them in oven until lightly golden
3. let cool
4. coarsely chop half the nuts
5. butter 2 large baking sheets
6. mix flour , sugar , salt and baking soda
7. beat in eggs , then whole and chopped nuts
8. mix to obtain a firm dough
9. knead briefly , then divide dough into 2 pieces
10. on a floured work surface , roll each piece under your hands into a cylinder 15 inches long and about 1 1 / 2 inches in diameter
11. place 2 rolls , well separated , on each baking sheet and bake 15 to 20 minutes , until very lightly browned and firm to the touch
12. with a spatula , carefully transfer the rolls to a cutting board and slice each onediagonally into cookies about 1 / 2-inch thick
13. set wire racks on the baking sheets and lay out the biscotti on them
14. return them to the oven for 20 to 30 minutes , or until very firm and crisp
15. cool on the racks , then transfer them to a tin for long keeping
demonstrations.review: I had a hard time with the dough, I couldn't get all the dry ingredients to incorporate, but mostly. I added 1 tsp of vanilla. After slicing I sprinkled with cinnamon sugar before baking again. These are a bit harder than other recipes I've made, but are very good. Next time I will probably add a touch of milk to the dough.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach cheese squares

i found this in my mother's collection of recipe clippings, from the 1960's. the only change i made was to reduce the salt to one-half teaspoon. you could probably substitute frozen chopped spinach to save time. i think these taste great at room temperature.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. melt butter in a 9 x 13 pan
3. either melt butter in microwave and then pour into pan , or place baking pan with butter into oven for a minute or two
4. then remove from oven and
5. beat eggs
6. mix flour into beaten eggs
7. stir in milk , salt and baking powder
8. add cheese and spinach , mixing well
9. add onion and seasonings , stirring thoroughly
10. spread into baking pan and bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes
11. cool 30 minutes before serving
12. cut 6 across and 9 down for the perfect sized finger-food appetizer
demonstrations.review: I made this for a baby shower brunch and thought it was pretty good, but was missing something. I think next time I will try the pepper jack as I think that will probably make this perfect. Very easy, thanks for posting this keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot sour cream salsa chicken

easy dinner recipe

1. spray the crockpot with cooking spray
2. add the chicken breasts
3. sprinkle withtaco seasoning
4. top with salsa
5. cook on low for 6-8 hours
6. when ready to serve , remove the chicken from the pot
7. place about 2 t cornstarch in a small amount of water
8. stir well
9. stir the cornstarch mixture into salsa sauce
10. stir in 1 / 4 cup of sour cream
11. serve
demonstrations.review: Tasted really good, but even with the cornstarch and sour cream, it turned out more of a soupy mixture rather than the sauce I was hoping for. I'll make it again, for sure, but will have to do some tweaking to make the sauce thicker

target.recipe_text:
caramel bread pudding

as my son says, it is like eating french toast for dessert. :) it is very much like french toast with a lovely caramel sauce on it. we all like it warm best. make sure you use a 2-quart dish. trust me, it will boil over in your stove in a 1 1/2-quart one. oops! and don't worry, it will fall a little bit as it cools.

1. place bread in greased 2-qt
2. baking dish
3. combine water and brown sugar
4. pour over bread
5. combine remaining ingredients
6. pour over bread
7. bake at 350 degrees f for 50-60 minutes or until knife inserted in center comes out clean
8. serve warm or cold
target.review: First of all, thank you for this recipe.  It was just what I was looking for: easy, ingredients I had on hand and fast (no need to soak overnight). <br/><br/>The good:  In addition to the three points above, the flavor was great!  I used old cinnamon raisin bread that was sitting around and 1 can of evaporated milk + 1/2 cup whole milk for extra richness. I also doubled the vanilla and cinnamon additions.<br/><br/>The bad (and the reason this doesn't get 5 stars): The water was a mistake. Either I had not quite enough bread or the water was just too much, but I did get that "scrambled egg" texture. I baked in convection oven, 350, for a full hour to try and mitigate, it did firm up a bit without burning. Next time I will decrease the water, eliminate it altogether or substitute with 1/2 cup heavy cream. ( I would have given 3 stars for this texture, but really, I should have known it was too much liquid when I was pouring over the custard).<br/><br/>Will definitely make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
demonstrations.review: With over 800 reviews,  I doubt mine will make much of a differnce, but here goes: Really good! Best banana bread ever, even with allergy subs: GF Flour, Applesauce (eggs), Coconut oil (butter) and soymilk (milk).  I doubted the recipe  for not adding cinnamon, vanilla or nutmeg but it was SO GOOD without them! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coconut custard pie  tammy s blend pie

a family recipe i've made for years for dozens of people. only one hasnt liked it sofar. coconut floats to the top and crisps, while pie makes its own very good crust. serve while warm, it will fall apart if cut hot. (oh, and use flaked/shredded sweet coconut in the bag)

1. melt butter then add all ingredients into mixing bowl
2. mix well
3. pour into greased 10" pie plate
4. bake 40 minutes@ 350f degrees
5. pie makes its own crust !
demonstrations.review: This is a fantastic pie! The custard is perfect and the coconut goes perfectly with it. I made it with the exact ingredients listed. Instead of melting the butter though, I did as one reviewer suggested and just cubed the cold butter. Everything went into the blender then into the pie dish. It could not be any easier! Also, I have a convection oven and baked at 350 for 40 minutes, then took it out to cool and rest for 20 minutes. Color, texture, taste all winners! The first time I made it, I had to make 2 in the same day because the first just didn't last long enough for everyone to have some. Thanks for sharing this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic fried catfish

from southern living magazine, 1982. excellent!

1. combine first 5 ingredients in a large shallow dish
2. sprinkle fish with 1 / 4 teaspoon salt
3. dredge in cornmeal mixture , coating evenly
4. pour oil to a depth of 1 1 / 2 inches into a deep cast-iron skillet
5. heat to 350 degrees
6. fry fish , in batches , 5 to 6 minutes or until golden
7. drain on paper towels
demonstrations.review: This was just the recipe I wanted! I was looking for a crispy catfish that didn't require seven pans of coating but still had crunch. I was determined to make it as easy as possible, so I skipped soaking in milk as some reviewers recommended. It turned out perfect. Very crispy exterior and moist, flaky interior. I had about 2lbs of fish so I doubled the recipe. Since I didn't have garlic powder I used some minced garlic from a jar (about 1tsp) on the fish before coating. I cut the fish into small chunks, similar to the picture and did a test batch. It wasn't spicy enough so I added 2Tablespoons of red pepper to the cornmeal mixture and used another 2 Tablespoons to rub over the naked fish, then shook them in a zipper bag to coat. Everyone loved it, this is going in the rotation. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the clockmaker s caramel coated popcorn  a haunted recipe

in 1921, a german born clockmaker quit his well respected job to open a popcorn stand in chicago’s wicker park district. the clockmaker’s typical fare was freshly popped popcorn drizzled with warm butter and sprinkled with salt; but his favorite, and most beloved popcorn, was his caramel coated popcorn. the recipe he used to make it was given to him from his only true love, who tragically died four years earlier during world war i. the tattered and torn recipe, which was scribbled on the inside of an old playbill, was carefully framed and sealed in an exquisite frame. the clockmaker faithfully took the framed recipe with him everywhere he went.  

by the summer of 1924, the clockmaker’s caramel coated popcorn had captivated the entire city’s attention; everyone was frantically lining up at his busy stand to buy the sweet, sticky confection. a few months later, just as the clockmaker was preparing to close his stand for the day, a small fire ignited near the stove. the clockmaker instinctively ran out to call for help. when he returned, just seconds later, he remembered leaving the framed recipe hanging on the wall. the clockmaker quickly ran into the burning stand to retrieve the recipe, but he never made it out.

when the fire inspectors went into the charred ruins to investigate the accident, they found the clockmaker’s frame lying in a pile of smoking debris. the frame was in pristine condition; not a dent, nor a blemish, could be seen on it. however, the recipe was gone.  

the recipe for the clockmaker’s caramel popcorn recently surfaced and is beginning to circulate around the globe. unfortunately, many people think the recipe is haunted because it is believed that if your clock stops running after making the recipe it’s because the clockmaker has paid you a visit in hopes of reclaiming his long, lost recipe.

note:  this recipe, as written, results in a sticky, chewy caramel popcorn.  if you prefer a crunchier caramel popcorn, bake it in the oven at 250 degrees for 1 hour, stirring every 15 minutes.

1. in a large pot , heat the margarine , brown sugar , karo syrup , and salt together over medium heat
2. while stirring , bring mixture to a boil and allow to boil for five minutes
3. remove from heat
4. add baking soda and vanilla
5. mix well
6. pour over freshly popped popcorn
7. stir until the popcorn is well coated
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Perfect caramel!  I halved the recipe and put some in the oven to see the difference. Still waiting.  In the meantime, the 'gooey' version is actually a very good consistency and tastes fantastic!  *update* The kids prefered the oven batch, especially when it comes to braces; came out crisp and crunchy after 30 min at 250 and one stir. Thanks for sharing.  I'll probably use this caramel for other things too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oyster stuffing

classic oyster stuffing for thanksgiving. enough for a 14 to 15 pound turkey.

1. preheat oven to 400f and toast the bread until golden brown on the middle rack
2. turn into a large bowl
3. meanwhile heat butter until melted and foam subsides
4. add onions and celery and cook about 5 minutes until tender
5. remove from heat and stir in the spices
6. stir in the bread cubes , and drained oysters and toss well , until the stuffing is moist , but not packed together
7. stir in the stock and eggs
8. put in bird while moist , remoisten and adjust spices as necessary
9. if cooked in a casserole dish at 350f until heated through with a crust on the outsides , 25 to 40 minutes
10. oyster juice may be used in place of some of the stock
demonstrations.review: This came out great.  I used jar oysters, so I chopped them beforehand.  Also I used a combination of water and leftover oyster juice because I didn't have any stock.  It looked very moist, so I skipped the eggs.  Doubled the recipe and baked in a 9x13 pan.  Everyone loved it!

target.recipe_text:
quick tomato basil pasta with fresh mozzarella

look for fresh mini mozzarella balls in the gourmet cheese section of your supermarket. this is an easy meal to prepare, and a delicious one ot eat!!
campanelle can also be used for the pasta.

1. bring 4 quarts water to boil in large pot
2. meanwhile , heat 2 tablespoons oil , garlic , and pepper flakes in medium saucepan over medium heat until fragrant but not brown , about 2 minutes
3. stir in crushed and diced tomatoes , bring to simmer , and cook until slightly thickened , 15-20 minutes
4. stir in 3 tablespoons basil , sugar and 1 / 2 teaspoons salt
5. add 1 tablespoons salt and pasta to boiling water
6. cook until al dente
7. reserve 1 / 4 cup cooking water , drain pasta , and transfer back to pot
8. stir in sauce and remaining tablespoons oil , and cook over medium heat until heated through , about 1 minute
9. stir in mozzarella and season with salt
10. serve , sprinkling with remaining 2 tablespoons basil and parmesan
target.review: This is a delicious pasta meal - I used fresh tomatoes instead of canned and it was incredible!  The mozzarella balls that I got at Costco were already marinated but I still added the fresh basil to the tomatoes.  I heated the oil then added two whole cloves of garlic with the red pepper flakes but removed the garlic bevore adding the tomatoes. Will definitely prepare this again, we didn't really require a meat with this but grilled chicken, tuna or shrimp would be wonderful.  I used a thick spaghetti noodle ( pici like) instead of the fusilli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best easy blueberry crumb muffins

we love this recipe for blueberry muffins, they are perfect, tender and full of berries! i usually do 1/2 all purpose flour 1/2 white whole wheat. subsititute any milk (dairy or non) in this recipe and it works fine. *** i edited to change the mistake- it should be baking powder in step 2, not soda :)

1. preheat oven to 400
2. combine sugar , flour , salt , baking soda and whisk to combine
3. combine oil and eggs in a 2 cup measuring cup
4. fill the rest with milk to 2 cups and whisk
5. stir wet into dry ingredients
6. fold in blueberries gently
7. fill 18 muffin cups just about full
8. sprinkle with crumb topping over tops and bake 20-25 minutes
9. crumb topping:
10. using a fork combine all ingredients until small crumbs form
demonstrations.review: These muffins did not turn out very well - I tried the tip from Jane about the whole wheat and regular flours - the recipe stated baking powder in the ingredients and baking soda in the directions - I went with the baking powder - maybe that's the reason these flopped; nevertheless, I feel sure I won't attempt this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
risotto with asparagus rice cooker 2008

this is from wolfgang puck and his rice cooker manual.

1. so rice needed for this recipe is 1 1 / 2 cups in a regular measuring cup
2. measure out the rice and rinse with cold water well
3. add thefirst 7 ingredients together in the rice cooker
4. close lid and press cook lever down
5. when the rice cooker switches to warm , add the grated fresh parmesan cheese
6. stir in well
7. serve
demonstrations.review: This was just pretty good...really tasted more like a rice dish than actual delicious, creamy risotto. I did like the ease of putting everything in the rice cooker as opposed to standing at the stove stirring and stirring.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice cooker rice pilaf

my husband loves this rice pilaf. everytime i make rice he requests it. hopefull you'll like it too! it takes a little extra preparation than a rice mix, but i think it's well worth it. you can also use wild rice, instead of white rice, but you'll need to add more liquid and it will take longer to cook.

1. in a small frying pan over medium heat , sautee the onion and garlic until onion is translucent
2. the garlic will cause the onion to scorch a bit , don't worry , it gives it flavor
3. add the rice , sauted onion and garlic , almonds , mushrooms , and chicken broth to a 4 cup capacity or larger rice cooker
4. stir briefly to distribute ingredients
5. set to cook
6. when done , let sit for 10 minutes
7. stir and enjoy !
8. depending on your rice cooker , the bottom may get brown
9. i like it , it gives it some extra zip !
demonstrations.review: This is a fabulous rice dish! I didn't have mushrooms - no big loss but feel sure it's a smidge better to include.  After the onion and garlic were sauteed, I put the rice in the pan with the two ingredients for a minute or so then added all to my rice cooker with at least 2 1/2 cups of chicken broth - delicious!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
why i joined zaar carrot cake

on october 2, 2001, i discovered the recipezaar web site. i immediately joined so i could post a request for a recipe i had lost. in less than an hour, i had a reply: this recipe. unfortunately, i never posted it into the database -- until now. my mistake. this cake was the reason i joined, and the friendly response i received was the reason i stayed!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease and flour a 9x13 inch pan
3. mix flour , baking soda , baking powder , salt and cinnamon
4. make a well in the center and add sugar , oil , eggs and vanilla
5. mix with wooden spoon until smooth
6. stir in carrots , coconut , walnuts and pineapple
7. pour into 9x13 inch pan and bake for about 45 minutes
8. don't panic , the centre will sink a little
9. allow to cool
10. when cool , ice the cake
11. you can certainly use your favourite cream cheese frosting to ice this cake , but the one i've included is highly recommended
12. to make the frosting: cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
13. add the icing sugar and beat until creamy
demonstrations.review: Yes, this is an excellent cake - I made it per the directions but used pecans instead of walnuts  and used my pound cake pan. I added a smidge of vanilla extract to the icing recipe as well as using the lowfat cream cheese - so, so good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
helen s rockville shrimp pie

this recipe from st. michael's church in charleston, sc originated with a sea islands gullah cook.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. saut onion , bell pepper , and celery in butter
3. process tomatoes and crumbled bread in your blender
4. in a bowl add sauted vegetables to the processed tomato-bread mixture
5. stir in 1 1 / 2 cups grated cheese , shrimp , and all of the seasonings
6. pour the mixture into a greased 1 1 / 2 quart casserole dish and top with the 1 / 2 cup grated cheese
7. bake in oven for 30 minutes or until bubbling
8. serves 8
demonstrations.review: This is absolutely delicious!  I live in Charleston and have never had a shrimp pie this good! I left out the celery because I didn't have any and used Progresso bread crumbs (1/2 plain & 1/2 Italian) which added some lovely spices to this mix.  Will absolutely prepare this yummy pie again! Thanks for the great receipt!

target.recipe_text:
should be illegal oven bbq ribs

after not being able to find restaurant ribs that satified my hot sweet appetite, i carefully attempted various combinations of flavors until i found one that i and my family thought was perfect. hope you enjoy them too.

1. place all ingredients together in large roasting pan
2. cut ribs apart for easier serving
3. mix together making sure to coat all ribs with this semi-dry paste
4. spread ribs out evenly on bottom of pan
5. cover lightly with foil
6. bake at 375 degrees for approximately 1 hour
7. turning or stirring occasionally
8. you can use broiler for these ribs , just watch more closely , and adjust cooking time
9. these ribs are also great finished on the grill for a few minutes on each side
target.review: Not that this needs another 5-star review, but after I received an "oh my God these are the best ribs ever" compliment last night; I knew I had to share it. I used the 3 hour crockpot method and finished the ribs on the grill for 10 minutes. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick chile relleno casserole

my mother has been making this recipe for years. its quick and easy and comes close to the original. i am not a big fan of the "chile". i have substitued chopped green chiles and shredded the jack cheese - which i actually prefer - but either way, this is a tasty one!

1. remove seeds and pith from green chiles
2. cut the jack cheese into large slices and divide evenly between the chiles , folding or tucking the cheese inside
3. butter a 1 1 / 2-quart casserole dish and arrange the chiles side by side on the bottom
4. with an electric mixer , beat eggs until thick and foamy
5. add milk , flour and baking powder and beat until smooth
6. pour egg mixture over the chiles and sprinkle with the cheddar cheese
7. bake , uncovered , in a 375f oven for about 30 minutes or until casserole is puffed and appears set when gently shaken
8. just before casserole is ready , heat marinara sauce to pour over individual servings if so desired
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent recipe.  I was suprised that the flavor of the chiles permeated the entire dish.  I stuffed the peppers with Chihuahua cheese and topped with a Mexican cheese blend.  Will definitely make this again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled vietnamese chicken

this chicken is just full of flavor.  scoring the breast or thigh before marinating allows the marinade to penetrate the meat better and faster.  i found this recipe in cooking pleasures magazine and we just loved it.  another plus is a short marinading time that does not compromise the flavor at all.  longer would only make it better.

1. heat grill
2. place all the ingredients except the chicken in a shallow glass baking dish and stir them together
3. make shallow slits across the chicken breast , going a little deeper in the thick end
4. make shallow slits long ways , resulting in a slight diamond pattern in the meat
5. put the chicken in the marinade and make sure some gets in the slits
6. this only needs to marinade for 10 or 15 minutes to pick up the flavor , i believe this is because of the slits
7. place on grill and cook for 8 to 10 minutes , until no longer pink
8. turn once during cooking
demonstrations.review: I think I have a favorite new chicken recipe and this is it!  I used 1 t black pepper and 1 t red pepper flakes and marinated for 2 hours.  The result was a moist, extremely flavorful breast.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome baked ham

i love this recipe because it is so easy and it calls for hardly any ingredients, and i always have these ingredients in my pantry. this recipe came from a good friend's mother, who was always asked to bake the ham for get-togethers and family dinners. now i get those requests. people who ordinarily aren't too fond of ham rave over this one. after i carve, i spoon a little of the glaze over the meat in the platter - yummmm!

1. in a medium size mixing bowl , mix yellow mustard and brown sugar until you have a thick"paste"
2. take all wrappers off of ham and trim away excess fat
3. line baking pan with aluminum foil
4. place ham on foil and spread brown sugar / mustard paste on top
5. fold and seal foil
6. do not open again until ham is done
7. bake at 350 for 4 hours
8. let set for about 1 hr then carve
9. one of the best tasting hams you will ever have !
demonstrations.review: This was the BEST ham I have eaten in a long time.  I did not seal the foil well enough so it leaked into the pan.  Nonetheless, the mess in my baking pan was worth it - I will use this recipe whenever I bake a ham.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sweet and tangy flank steak  oamc or make ahead

this recipe is from super suppers, the franchise that allows families to prepare meals ahead of time in their central kitchen. they do the prep, you do the assembly for  quick dinners from the freezer. i love flank steak and this sweet/spicy combination appealed to me.   the addition of pepper is mine and the way i like this dish.

1. mix together all ingredients except steak together in a bowl
2. fold steak into thirds , placing outer edges towards the center
3. place steak into a resealable freezer bag
4. add marinade and squish around so that all of the steak surface is covered
5. place into a second bag , seal and label
6. freeze steak for up to 2 month
7. to prepare , remove 2 days ahead and defrost in the fridge
8. to prepare , pre-heat grill or broiler
9. remove steak from bag and pour sauce into a small sauce pan
10. bring sauce to a boil and simmer for 5 minutes
11. grill or broil steak for 5 minutes per side or until steak reaches 135 degrees
12. remove steak from heat and allow to rest for 5 minutes before slicing
13. to serve , thinly slice steak across the grain and spoon a bit of sauce on top
demonstrations.review: This recipe truly takes flank steak to a whole new dimension for me.  I included the chili pepper flakes, marinated it overnight and then broiled it.  The result was a moist and delicious steak.  I cannot wait to eat the leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian barbecue chicken

this a cooking light recipe that i have been using again and again and again since the beginning of the summer - the chicken once marinated is very moist and tasty.  and the leftover chicken is wonderful in a salad the next day!

1. combine first 6 ingredients in a large ziploc plastic bag , add chicken
2. seal and marinate in refrigerator for 4 hours or overnight , turning ocacsionnally
3. prepare grill
4. remove chicken from bag , reserving marinade
5. place marinade in a small saucepan
6. bring to a boil , cook 1 minute
7. place chicken on grill rack coated with cooking spray
8. grill 20 minutes or until done , turning and basting frequently with cooked marinade
9. garnish with lime wedges and green onion tops , if desired
demonstrations.review: Wow!  This was delicious.  I followed the recipe exactly, using hot curry powder and my George Foreman grill.  The complexity of flavors was amazing.  I will definitely use this recipe again and again.

target.recipe_text:
my grandma s chocolate pies

my grandma didn't measure anything so this is as close as i could get. i never said it was a healthy recipe. it can be made without the evaporated milk and using low fat or skim milk and using margarine instead of butter but please use real vanilla and a good quality cocoa. you might have to adjust the cornstarch or cocoa depending on how thick or chocolaty you like your pies. i make 2 of these pies for every church covered dish meal and never get to bring a slice home. oh yes...you can cook the filling in a large double boiler to avoid scorching it, it just takes longer.

1. stir together sugar , cornstarch , salt and cocoa in a heavy 3 quart boiler
2. beat egg yolks with milk and stir into dry ingredients
3. add butter that has been cut into small cubes and cook over medium heat , stirring constantly until mixture thickens and just begins to "bubble"
4. you must stir constantly or this filling will scorch
5. remove from heat and stir in vanilla and pour into baked pie shells and let cool some
6. make a meringue from the 6 egg whites , cream of tarter and sugar
7. spread on top of pies and brown in the oven at 325f
8. remove pies from oven when meringue is nicely brown
9. let cool at least 30 minutes before you attempt to cut these pies
10. let the kids or dear hubby have the pot and stirring spoon to lick clean
target.review:
A fabulous creamy and rich chocolate filling!  Instead of filling two pies I ended up filling to the brim my restaurant style pie pan and having a bit left over to eat as pudding!  Yummy.  
I left off the meringue for I am the only one in this household that will eat it and I didn't want my hips to reap the benefits of me eating the pie by myself!...lol......If I had put the meringue on this gorgeous pie I know it would be fit for the centerfold of any cooking magazine!  Thank you for sharing your Granma's recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
orange crescent swirls

these simple little orange rolls begin with refrigerated crescent dough. quick to make but sure to make a good impression early in the morning! from the foote creek bed & breakfast in aberdeen, south dakota where speedy but impressive food is a must first thing each day. ;o) if you are living in warmer climates, it may help to place the dough in the freezer for a few minutes before slicing.

1. heat oven to 375f spray 12 x 1 / 2 inch pizza pan with nonstick cooking spray
2. in small saucepan , combine brown sugar , margarine , orange peel and juice
3. mix well
4. cook and stir over med heat until bubbly
5. set aside
6. remove dough from each can but do not unroll
7. leave as a log / roll
8. cut each roll into 12 slices
9. arrange slices evenly in prepared pan
10. spoon brown sugar mixture evenly over rolls
11. bake at 375 for 13-15 min or until golden brown
12. remove rolls from pan with spatula
13. serve warm
demonstrations.review: I am not a huge lover of crescent rolls but thought I would try them on the kids.  Very easy and quick to make with a big impression.  I used the reduced fat crescent rolls  (not that it made much difference for I ended up eating half the pan)and they cooked up beautifully!  The pan we used was a 12"X8" pan with sides.  If the glaze sticks the cooled rolls to the pan I found that one can just pop the pan back into a warm oven for a few minutes and the moist, glazed rolls are good to go!Yummy ......... I can see this comfort treat being made a bunch of times once the cooler weather hits.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot roast beef

so easy, and the meat is so tender.

1. place potatoes , carrots and onions in crock pot
2. mix salt , pepper , celery seed , parsley and basil
3. sprinkle over vegetables
4. place roast on top of vegetables
5. pour beef broth over roast
6. cover and cook on low for 10 hours
demonstrations.review: I followed the recipe to a tee and was I ever rewarded with a scrumptious meal that night!  The roast was sliced and I drizzled a bit of the crockpot juices over it.  The kids turned up their noses at the brown tinted potatoes and carrots so I cooked some rice, mashed the veggies up in the juices and drizzled that over the rice.  The munchkins kept saying, "Oh Mom, this rice is so good!"  (ha ha- and mom scores!  lol)  The seasoning were not overpowering and I have to say that the fresh basil mixed in with the meat was excellent.  The meat was so tender and could be cut with a fork.  I was so happy to have a healthy, comfort meal on such a cold night.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast mess

i watched my brother in law skip make something close to this and it looked good, when i tried it my kids loved it, and wanted it again!!

1. in a large frying pan cook sausage until brown
2. drain fat
3. add the onion , pepper strips , potatoes and seasoning salt
4. cook approximately 10 minutes , or until vegetables are tender
5. while vegetables are cooking , preheat broiler
6. add eggs and cook until set
7. sprinkle cheese on top and put under broiler until cheese is melted and slightly browned
demonstrations.review: A perfect 5 stars for this one!  Most of the precooking and chopping can be done ahead of time for a quick but fabulous breakfast.  I like a sprinkle of parmesan cheese over the top as well.  I may try with ham next time.  Thank you Jeffie for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana nut pineapple bread

esy yummy banana nut bread recipe,with pineapple! yumm! 8)

1. preheat oven to 350 , & lightly grease& flour 2 8-inch loaf pans
2. in large bowl , combine flour , sugar , baking soda , cinnamon& the salt
3. stir in walnuts
4. in separate bowl , mix eggs , oil , banana , vanilla& pineapple until well combined
5. add wet ingredients to dry ingredients , stir just until moistened
6. pour equal amounts into pans
7. bake about 50 to 55 minutes or until toothpick in center comes out clean
8. cool for 10 minutes on racks
9. remove from pans and continue cooling
demonstrations.review: A definte must for banana bread lovers that are looking for a little pizzazz!  The pineapple flavor never overpowered the banana flavor. It was a combination made to work!  I used macadamia nuts in place of walnuts .....yyuuuummmmm!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mexican horchata

i haven't made this, but it does sound interesting.

1. place the rice in a bowl with enough hot water to cover
2. let the rice sit overnight
3. next day , remove the water
4. place 1 / 2 cup of rice , and 2 cups milk in a blender
5. blend until rice is all ground up
6. mix in 1 / 4 cup sugar ,
7. 1 / 2 teaspoons vanilla ,
8. 1 / 4 teaspoons cinnamon
9. do the same with the other half of the ingredients
10. strain through cheesecloth
11. serve over ice
demonstrations.review: I only made this because I had the few simple ingredients in my cupboard.  I was wrong to be so ho-hum about this drink.  It ended up being quite tasty!  I served it over ice but I definitely will be making this one again when our cold Maine weather hits.  Only I'll be warming it up.  A nice light drink that reminds of a hot tea (chai) that I get once in a while from Dunkin' Donuts.

target.recipe_text:
bev s spaghetti sauce

this is a recipe i have developed over a number of years. this is the only spaghetti sauce my family will request! very easy to make. i hope your family enjoys it as much as mine does!

1. brown the ground beef , onion and garlic in olive oil with bay leaves , oregano , basil , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
2. add tomato paste , tomato sauce and diced tomatoes
3. stir well and bring to a simmer over medium heat
4. cover and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
5. use sauce to top your cooked spaghetti
6. top with sauteed mushroom
7. pass the parmesan
target.review: We make your recipe all the time. We love to double it and freeze in portions for many quick meals,,Thank you so much!!<br/>ps I do switch up the meat ,,made with ground beef is excellent! Also with mild Italian sausage its wonderful too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker beef short ribs

you won't believe how good these ribs are!!! i think we could have these every other night with no complaints! they're yummy!!!!

1. put flour , salt and pepper in a bag
2. add ribs and shake to coat
3. brown ribs in butter in a lg skillet
4. put in slow cooker
5. in same skillet , combine remaining ingredients
6. bring to a boil , stirring
7. pour over ribs
8. cover and cook on low for 9 hours
demonstrations.review: Just sneaked a sample- dinners in approx an hour- I've put the crock pot on high lid off to reduce liquid + skimmed off as much fat as possible. Just before dinner I will make a cornstarch slurry and thicken sauce. Making mashed spuds..OMG Excited as the sample was juicy tender nom nom nom. Thank you so much!!! My first time ever making beef short ribs- they were bone in...Not my last with this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepsi pork roast

this recipe sounds strange and tastes wonderful. we have experimented with other brands of soda, but none worked as well. you can also cook potatoes and carrots with the roast for a complete meal.

1. place roast in crock pot
2. mix soup mix with soup
3. add cola to soup mixture and pour over roast
4. cook on high for 4-5 hours
5. when done , remove roast and thicken juices with cornstarch for wonderful gravy
demonstrations.review: I used Pepsi Max because I'm a diabetic, Me and the family loved it!! Definite make again and again recipe.Pork was tender, very juicy. I also used whole pkg Garlic onion soup mix and sliced yellow onion.<br/>I did not make the gravy. This is no negative to the recipe..I used a pork shoulder and it was fatty. Most of it rendered down into the gravy..Trying to keep fat down I made a pkg of pork gravy on the side. And sadly discarded the crock pot gravy (I'm thinking had I made this the day before I wanted it, I could have cooled and refrigerated to remove fat next day) But no time for that when hungry family wants to at NOW! lol..Enjoyed the simplicity. Thank you a Whole Bunch! I WILL MAKE THIS ALL THE TIME!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very berry muffins

the original recipe used frozen raspberries, but i had a berry mix of raspberries, cherries, blueberries, and blackberries on my hands.  the result was very tasty!  i made these for a light brunch on thanksgiving day.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease 12 muffin cups
3. for crumb topping , combine 1 / 4 cup flour and brown sugar in a small bowl
4. cut in 2 tablespoons butter until mixture is crumbly
5. set aside 1 / 4 cup flour
6. combine 1 3 / 4 cups flour , granulated sugar , baking powder , baking soda , salt and lemon peel in a medium bowl
7. combine milk , melted butter and egg
8. mix well
9. toss berries with 1 / 4 cup flour until coated
10. add berries to muffin mixture
11. spoon batter into muffin tins until 3 / 4 full
12. sprinkle with crumb topping
13. bake for 25-30 minutes or until toothpick inserted comes out clean
14. cool in pan for 2 minutes then remove to wire rack
15. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review:
Thank you for a wonderful recipe, I made a couple changes, I doubled these muffins and it worked great. (I like to freeze for the work week.) I did not double the sugar,,white or brown, the mixed frozen berries are sweet enough. Last change - the 4 1/2 cups of flour I subbed 1/2 cup with ground flax ..extra nutrition added a nutty flavor, OH..I didn't have lemon peel so I added lemon extract.
Thank you so much!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade hamburger buns  bread machine

you will never want to buy hamburger buns again after trying this recipe. easy to do using a bread machine and so awesome! you can also top rolls with sesame seeds after brushing with melted butter.

1. place all ingredients , except butter , in pan of bread machine according to manufacturer's directions
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is complete , turn out onto floured surface
4. cut dough in half and roll each half out to a 1" thick circle
5. cut each half into six 3 1 / 2" rounds with inverted glass as a cutter
6. place on greased baking sheet far apart and brush with melted butter
7. cover and let rise until doubled , about one hour
8. bake at 350 for 9 minutes
9. some reviewers baked these anywhere from 12 to 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have made this every night this week(its Thursday), using my black and Decker machine..everyone wants them. I made this with water as my daughter is lactose intolerant and cannot have milk. I did make them once with milk and I find it a lighter bun when water is used..I cut dough in half and then the half in half till I got 8 . Then I formed them into smooth balls. Let rise in a slight warm turned off oven for 30 min..baked for 20..checking on them..tap bottom sounds hollow..Done!<br/>This is a keeper..thank you<br/>ingred went in as follows<br/>water<br/>yeast<br/>sugar<br/>flour<br/>salt <br/>butter<br/>egg<br/><br/>dough setting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s best tomato soup canning recipe

my mennonite mother's 'famous' tomato soup - hard to beat! perfect anytime of the year! enjoy!

here's what i purchased (for you to use as a baseline reference): - to yield 75 quarts of soup - 3 bushels of tomatoes, 6 lbs. butter, 5 lbs. sugar, 3 bunches celery, 5 lbs. flour. hope that helps! (recipe below is for 8-10 quarts)

(i make lots, and then frequently give this as a gift for a new mother, a hostess gift (when invited to dinner), a get-well meal, etc..) super quick - easy to make, and can easily add garlic bread and a salad and dessert for a quick meal to bless someone. enjoy!

1. chop onion& celery
2. place in large kettle w / just enough water to keep them from burning
3. while this simmers , cut tomatoes
4. add to kettle& cook until tender
5. place this all through victorio strainer
6. return to kettle
7. add sugar& salt
8. cream butter and flour together& mix thoroughly with two cups of cold juice , until dissolved , to avoid lumps of flour in the juice
9. add butter / flour mixture to warmed tomato juice
10. stir well
11. heat just until hot
12. just prior to boiling , turn off the burner
13. ladle into jars& close securely with lids
14. return to canner & process 20-30 minutes
15. remove from canner & allow to set until sealed to serve , mix equal parts tomato concentrate to milk , and add 1 / 2 t
16. of baking soda per pint as it cooks
demonstrations.review:
I can not say enough about this recipe except that I will not make any other, this has all the things that I love in a tomato soup... I made a couple changes
1.I used 3 very large tins from Costco of tomato sauce (tomato's are very $ here right now)
2.Splenda in exchange for sugar
3.I added no salt..didn't need it
4. Sauce is so thick I didn't need the flour
5. pressure canned 10lb for 30min
Thank you WJKing, Thank you for passing this recipe along to my family.

target.recipe_text:
low fat spinach and artichoke dip

i love spinach and artichoke dip, but hate the fat... i came up with this fast and easy recipe that tastes great, is easy to put together, low in fat but big on taste! flavored with roasted red peppers and parmesan cheese, no yicky mayo here! makes enough for a large crowd. can be made in the microwave for even faster preparation. also delicious served cold. note: recipe can be made with fat-free marinade artichokes, i usually buy two small jars, adds a little extra zing!  ww points = 1/serving

1. preheat oven to 375f and lightly spritz a shallow baking dish with cooking spray
2. using food processor , mix light cream cheese , sour cream and artichoke hearts by pulsing until even consistency
3. add roasted bell pepper and parmesan cheese and pulse until creamy
4. to bake dip: place mixture into prepared baking dish
5. add spinach and stir until combined
6. bake for 25 minutes , stirring half way through
7. dip is done when browned and bubbly around the edges
8. to keep warm , lower temperature in oven to 250f and stir every 10 minutes until dip is served
9. for microwave directions: place mixture into microwave safe dish , add spinach and stir until combined
10. cover with plastic wrap , leaving room for steam to escape
11. microwave on high for 7 minutes or until dip is hot and boiling on the sides - microwaves vary , check often
12. mix well before serving
target.review: I made this last night and it was SO good! Four people nearly polished it off by themselves--and no one even knew it was low-fat. It was great with veggies, bread, and pretzels, delicious hot or cold, and ridiculously easy to make. (One note: When I was mixing everything together, I was worried it was too liquidy. That was not the case at all--it sets as it cooks--so don't worry as you're making it!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mock mashed potatoes cauliflower

this is a great substitute for the real thing if you are on a low carb diet like atkins. good way to get your veggies too,even if you don't like cauliflower.

1. steam or microwave cauliflower until very soft
2. put cauliflower in blender or food processor with butter and sour cream
3. process or blend until creamy like mashed potatoes
4. add seasonings to taste and serve immediately
5. grated cheese or minced chives make a nice topping
demonstrations.review: Great, simple recipe! Make no mistaking: if you hate the taste of cauliflower, this is still, well, cauliflower. But for those of us who can "fool" our brains into thinking we're getting decadent carbs simply through texture, this is divine! I make mine with low-fat sour cream, only 1/2 tbsp. of butter, salt, pepper, and rosemary. But, then again, I like cauliflower to start with!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mini meatballs in cranberry sauce

these cute little meatballs go very quickly at holiday gatherings.

1. in a large bowl , combine the ground meat , bread crumbs , parsley , eggs , garlic , onion powder , basil and pepper
2. mix well but do not overwork or meat will become tough when cooked
3. form into small balls the size of a walnut or smaller
4. place meatballs in a slow oven of 300 degrees f and bake for 25 minutes
5. in the meantime , in a crock pot set at 325 degrees f , mix together the cranberry sauce add remaining sauce ingredients
6. when meatballs are baked , transfer them to the crock pot and stir into the sauce
7. cook in crock pot for 1 hour
8. lower heat to keep warm for serving
demonstrations.review: Although I didn't love these, my guests and husband certainly did! Here's my big caveat on the recipe: 1 1/2 cups of ketchup makes the sauce WAY too ketchup-y! To correct the "error" once I'd already added in the ketchup, I added some cayenne pepper (that gave an extra kick that was good) and also some cranberry relish I had in the fridge. In future, I'd definitely do chili sauce instead of ketchup. Otherwise, the meatballs themselves were delicious and I think I'll make them on their own--or into a meatloaf--another night this week!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low fat zucchini bread

you can barely taste the hidden zucchini in this recipe, which makes it a perfect way to get kids to eat their vegetables. it is moist, sweet, and flavorful- not to mention easy to make! use it for breakfast, dessert, accessory to a meal, or a snack.

1. mix together all ingredients
2. pour into 3 loaf pans
3. bake at 350 for about 60 minutes
demonstrations.review: Fantastic recipe! My dad gave me a HUGE zucchini from his garden (I've made 2 loaves and 24 muffins, and it's barely halfway done!). My modifications (any ingredients not mentioned I left as were): 1 1/2 c. sugar, 3 c. zucchini, 1/8 c. oil, 2 small snack packs of applesauce, 1 1/2 tbsp. vanilla. Next time, I'm going to experiment with adding some orange rind for a citrus flavor. One additional note: when I made the 2 loaves, it cooked for 45 min. When I made 24 muffins, it only took 25 min. Thank you--great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken and wild rice soup

i found this recipe in a crock pot recipe box i recently purchased.  it is easy to make and easier to eat!  especially great for a quick meal on a cold, winter day.

1. do not use quick cooking or instant rice
2. combine broth , chicken , water , celery , carrots , rice and enclosed seasoning packet , onion , pepper and parsley flakes in a 4 to 7 quart crock pot slow cooker
3. mix well
4. cover
5. cook on low for 6 to 7 hours , or on high 4 to 5 hours , or until chicken is tender
6. stir in vinegar , if desired
demonstrations.review: I was looking for a good crock pot soup that would use up the remaining chicken left from our roast chicken last week. I found this recipe and was really pleased--though I did make some additions/changes. Not being a fan of celery but wanting something green, I substituted spinach (I added it only in the last 30 minutes). Though my chicken was already cooked, I put it in at the start to add flavor to the broth. However, I did hold off on the wild rice until 3 hours in (I was cooking on low). I also added salt, 3 cloves of garlic, and the juice of 2 lemons (lemons added in the last 30 minutes, too). I'm giving it 5 stars because it was a great launching pad for me to figure out how to make a tasty, healthy, slow cooker soup!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini orange bread

a variation on zucchini bread.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease and flour bottoms only of two 8x4 or 9x5 loaf pans
3. in large bowl , beat eggs until thick and lemon-coloured
4. gradually beat in sugar
5. add oil , orange juice and zucchini
6. stir in remaining bread ingredients
7. mix well
8. pour batter into prepared pans
9. bake at 350f degrees for 45-55 minutes or until cake tester inserted in centre comes out clean
10. cool 10 minutes
11. remove from pans
12. cool slightly on a rack
13. in small bowl , blend glaze ingredients
14. spread over warm loaves
15. cool completely on wire rack
16. wrap tightly and store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: Like some others, I skipped the glaze (for travel purposes) and used OJ concentrate (2/3 c., as a replacement for the OJ) because that's all I had. It was delicious as a breakfast bread and the perfect thing to bring as a hostess gift--no one had to worry about cooking in the morning!

target.recipe_text:
grilled chicken pesto panini

if you have an electric panini maker then use it for this, if not you need two skillets, one heavy cast iron skillet or similar for the top to weigh down the panini. this makes a perfect lunch or light dinner.  plan ahead the chicken needs to marinade for 1 hour before cooking....this works with a george foreman grill, just make certain to hold down on the top lid firmly while cooking to ensure toasting the bread, or maybe you are lucky enough to own a panini maker, then you will not need the heavy skillet for the top. double the recipe if desired. you will love this!

1. pound the chicken fillets until thin between two pieces of waxed paper , then marinate in oil , garlic , pepper and italian seasoning for about 1-1 / 2 hours
2. heat a grill pan or saut pan
3. season the breasts with salt and pepper
4. cook the chicken on medium heat for about 5 minutes per side , or until golden and cooked through
5. remove from pan and place on a plate or board
6. top each fillet with some of the roasted peppers and a slice of cheese
7. spread both sides of the bread with pesto sauce
8. place chicken inside the bread and form to a sandwich
9. brush both sides of the outside of bread with olive oil
10. heat a grill pan or a 10-inch skillet on medium high heat
11. place the panini in the pan
12. weigh the panini down with another heavy skillet and then top with a heavy can cook for about 3 minutes , or until bread is toasted
13. turn the panini , and weigh it down again with a heavy skillet and a can on top , and toast for another 3 minutes
14. remove from pan and cut in half
target.review:
This was a really tasty treat.  I used garlic flavored ciabatta bread and served some sliced Romano tomatoes & avocado.  It's fantastic (and quick) with the roasted chicken found at the grocery store! 
Thanks again for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
christina s killer dip

this is my sister's dip. she got the recipe while backpacking in europe a few years ago. she is now forced to make it at every party she has. people smell it cooking and stand drooling by the oven until it comes out! (many have not been able to wait for the cooling part and burned their mouths to get to it first).  you might have to make 2 portions.

**note: please check the sodium content before you choose a ranch dressing mix, because it will affect the flavor! some people have complained it is "too salty". please also make sure you are using only a 1 ounce packet; there are other sizes from various manufacturers. too much mix throws off the balance of flavors. my sister and i always use the hidden valley ranch original and we do not have any problems with it :)

you can also substitute half the sour cream for prepared ranch dressing and skip the dry mix. it will come out a bit wetter.

1. defrost the spinach
2. place it in a colander and press it until as much moisture as possible is removed
3. mix all ingredients , and blend well
4. put it in a shallow baking dish in the oven for 20 minutes at 350f
5. remove from oven
6. while still hot top it with remaining cheese , heat in oven again for 5 minutes
7. remove and cool below lava stage and serve
8. goes well with tortilla chips
demonstrations.review: I made this for a friend's Super Bowl party last night.  Took the advice of Shae and used Pepper Jack.  It was great and super easy to make!  There was a lot left over however. (Probably due to the fact there was SO much food there)  I'd definately make this again!  Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best albondigas soup

this albondigas soup recipe was given to me from my mother-in-law. it's definitely one my favorite soups. honestly, it's better than most restaurants that i've tried.

1. make the meatballs first: combine everything and mix thoroughly
2. form meatballs and roll between your palms
3. you should make around 20 to 24 meatballs , set aside
4. combine chicken broth , onion , celery , tomatoes and their liquid , cumin , oregano and cilantro leaves in a large pot
5. bring to boil , and reduce heat and simmer for 10 minutes
6. drop meatballs in the soup
7. return to simmer and cook another 10 minutes
8. add zucchini and cook 10 minutes
9. season with salt and pepper , to taste
10. you could top the soup with cooked rice , or just by itself
demonstrations.review:
