I didn't quite follow this recipe exactly, but everyone loved it and asked for more.

I used frozen Italian meatballs, I was out of onion and celery, I added baby carrots, fresh tomatoes instead of canned, garlic salt & red pepper flakes instead of regular salt & pepper.  I topped with 2 cups of white rice & served with warm tortillas.

I'll definitely make this again.  Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scrambled egg muffins

i got this recipe from a magazine. it's very easy to make and is great for any meal. kids love them.

1. brown sausage
2. drain well
3. preheat oven to 350
4. in a bowl , beat eggs , then add onion , green peppers , salt , pepper and garlic powder
5. stir in sausage and cheese
6. spoon 1 / 3 cupfuls into greased muffin cups
7. bake at 350 for 20-25 minutes or until a knife inserted comes out clean
demonstrations.review:
What a great idea!  This recipe is pretty much only limited to your own imagination.  I used basic omelet ingredients & everyone loved them!

I added mushroom, cheddar cheese, chopped tomato, cooked spinach and bacon bits with a pinch of pepper to our eggs. 

Thanks for sharing!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
iced coffee  dunkin donuts

i have tried to make iced coffee before but it never tasted like my favorite from dunkin donuts! i finally realized they were added as much milk as they were coffee, and extra sugar. often, later in the day, after the coffee in the carafe is not so hot, i make these as a refreshing drink. you can also add a tablespoon or so of flavored creamer, like amaretto, hazelnut, etc. for some variety.

1. put sugar in a large glass
2. drop in ice cubes
3. pour coffee over ice and add milk
4. stir until sugar is melted
5. that's it !
demonstrations.review:
Thanks for posting!  
Note:
Instead of double brewing, you can add twice the coffee  (I add 4 scoops instead of 2 for one cup).  Like a previous poster commented, otherwise it will get watered down with the milk and ice. =)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tater tot breakfast bake

got this off the back of a bag of frozen tater tots. sounds good. putting it here for save keeping

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. beat together eggs , milk , salt , mustard and pepper
3. grease a 9x13 baking dish
4. layer bacon , egg mixture and cheese
5. arrange tater tots on top
6. bake for 40 minutes or until eggs are set and tater tots are golden brown
demonstrations.review:
This is a good recipe to mix ahead of time and pop it in the oven when getting ready for the day.  Next time I will add more bacon and layer it on TOP of the cheese so there is bacon in every bite.  I did not add the salt and it was plenty flavor-full. 
Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
pan seared rib eye steak with smoked paprika rub

i picked up a kosher ribeye steak at trader joe's last week and pan-seared it using the technique that's become my hands-down favorite: alton brown's pan searing method. it turned out so perfectly-- tender and pink on the inside with a brown, spice-laden crust on the outside. the simple smoked paprika spice rub gave it a sweet, barbecued flavor. this is such an easy way to cook up a smoky, juicy ribeye steak without firing up the grill.

1. bring the steak to room temperature
2. mix all spices and oil into a thick paste
3. rub spice rub mixture onto both sides of the steak
4. optional: if you have the time , wrap the steak with plastic wrap and allow to sit for 15 minutes or longer at room temperature
5. put a 10 to 12-inch cast iron skillet in the oven , and heat oven to 500 degrees
6. when the oven thermometer indicates that it has reached 500 degrees , remove the pan from the oven
7. transfer quickly to a stovetop burner on high heat
8. immediately place the steak in the middle of the pan
9. cook for 30 seconds without moving
10. flip with tongs and cook for 30 seconds on the second side
11. quickly remove the pan from the heat and place into the oven
12. cook for two minutes on each side for a medium rare steak , or three minutes on each side for a medium steak
13. transfer steak to a wooden cutting board and make a loose tent of aluminum foil over it
14. allow it to rest for a few minutes before serving
target.review: Fabulous! We loved this so much, this will be frequently enjoyed in our home. I had to go to a cooking specialty shop to get the sweet paprika & it was a little pricey, but well worth it having eaten this steak. I will see the end of that little tin of spice for sure with this recipe! My husband grills his steaks and LOVES them...he LOVED this too, so that is a true compliment. I made one 1 lb. steak and I even messed up and bought a sirloin instead of a ribeye, even so it was tender, juicy and delicious! I rubbed the steak and wrapped it in saran wrap for about 1 1/2 hours before cooking it. I have pan seared steak before in my iron skillet, but have never enjoyed it so much. The method here really does something special. Thanks so much What's Cooking. **UPDATE**2/10- we had this again...except we seared it in the iron skillet as directed and then we grilled it and it was still fabulous!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fusion avocado

had this in texas a couple of years ago! my sil kathie turned me on to it!
sushi without the fish, nori, and trouble of making it! ok she just had the soy but darn the pickeled ginger is so good! this is so quick and easy!!!!! it'll satisfy that i want sushi need!  i myself can eat one a day!

1. take a spoon between the meat and skin to loosen
2. pour 1 / 2 teaspoon soy sauce over each half of avocado
3. scoop out with a spoon and enjoy !
4. using optional wasabi or ginger to taste is a great healthy option !
demonstrations.review: This is FABULOUS!  I love just plain avocados and I have had your recipe saved and in the back of my mind forever.  Anyway, I just cut an avocado for my toddler and decided to eat the other half myself, so I finally decided to try this.  I can't believe I waited to long.  So very simple and just amazingly good.  I sliced my avocado inside the skin and then poured it in.  I think this would be a lovley side to a sushi dinner or any oriental dinner.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
my family s favorite sloppy joes  pizza joes

i've tried many recipes, this is the best. i once 'dec-tupled' (10x) this recipe to sell sandwiches at a craft fair at my church. people were waiting in line to buy leftovers. freezes well, goes up to the lake or camping well and is a hit on halloween...it's no-fail. easy to double, triple, etc. i've been making joes this way for over 20 years.
***03-08-09, i just reinvented this recipe tonight when i went to make it for dinner and found i didn't have an 8-oz. can of tomato sauce (shame on me).  the family was upset with me when i subbed an 8-oz. can of pizza sauce and told them to suck it up and call them 'pizza joes' and then served them up with shredded mozzarella cheese on the toasted buns, top and bottom.  they loved it.  i left out the bbq sauce in this preparation and just used a 1/2 cup ketchup.  pizza joes are good to go!

1. in a large skillet , brown ground beef , celery and onion
2. drain the fat , who needs it ?
3. stir in remaining ingredients , simmer covered , 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
4. if joes appear too'loose' , leave cover off and let moisture evaporate
5. cook until it's the consistency you like for serving on toasted buns , with french fries and cole slaw
demonstrations.review: These were great & in the running against our regular sloppy joes.  I used celery salt instead of celery and dried onion flakes, so I did no chopping!  They were saucier than our regular and we really liked that.  I missed the pickle relish, so next time I will add that in.  Thanks, this just might be our new favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot barbecued bbq ribs

so easy but very delicious. they just fall off the bone. broiling them first keeps them from being greasy. from the rival crock-pot cookbook.

1. cut ribs into serving portions
2. i usually do two ribs together
3. sprinkle both sides with salt and pepper
4. place ribs on a broiler pan and broil 12 minutes per side or until browned
5. i like mine a bit 'crisp'
6. drain if necessary
7. place sliced onion in crock pot
8. place rib sections on top of onions
9. pour a little barabecue sauce over each section as you place them in the crock pot and the rest of the bottle over all the ribs
10. cover and cook on low for about 8 hours
demonstrations.review: I made these yesturday morning and they were ready at about 6 hours.  I turned them off in the middle of the day and turned them back on for an hour before dinner.  Used only one rack of ribs layered with onions, crushed red pepper and cattlemans barbeque sauce.  Wow- so easy and so good.  My husband said that they were the best ribs he has ever had.  Now, that is high praise because we are talking about a man with a smoker and his own 'secret' rib marinade.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
just cucumber slices

this is a simple recipe to have as a refreshing side dish. it's especially good for picnics, bar-b-ques, potlucks and buffets. if you like your slices on the tart side cut back on the sugar a little bit. please note it will need to be chilled at least 3 hours.

1. in a bowl toss together the cucumbers , onion , if using , and dill
2. combine sugar , vinegar , water and salt and bring to a boil
3. pour over cucumbers
4. stir to coat
5. cover and refrigerate 3 hours or overnight
demonstrations.review: These cucumbers are so easy and so tastey!  I would have used splenda, but was out, so used the real thing.  I will definately make them again.  They remind me of the cucumber salad served at a Japanese steak house here.  Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious tuna mushroom noodle casserole

this recipe goes back years, it is a family favorite that i still make to this day, and i have also make it using cooked chicken or cooked turkey in place of the tuna, is a easy basic casserole, but it has tons of flavor!

1. set oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch casserole dish
3. in a skillet saute the onion , celery , green bell peppers and garlic in butter for about 3 minutes
4. add in flour and cook for 1 minute
5. remove from the heat and slowly add in the milk
6. return to the heat and whisk until thickened and the sauce comes to a boil , then season with salt and pepper
7. add in mushrooms , cheddar cheese and tuna
8. mix to combine , then add in the cooked egg noodles
9. transfer to a baking dish
10. sprinkle with bread crumbs then parmesan cheese if using , then drizzle with melted butter
11. bake for about 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: By far my favorite tuna noodle casserole recipe! I used green onions and didn't have celery, but added two cloves of garlic. I used peas instead of mushrooms and only had 2% milk which worked great! I topped with a little more cheese and crushed seasoned croutons. I made a 12oz bag of egg noodles but added only about 8oz of them and it was perfectly creamy... loved it! My youngest child says she wants leftovers for breakfast:)

target.recipe_text:
tastes like apple pie apple squares

from my favourite church cookbook, where all the recipes are tried and true!  **like most of the reviews state, if you don't want to fight with the pastry to make it fit a cookie sheet - make 1.5x the dough recipe or use a smaller pan.

1. mix flour and salt and cut in shortening
2. add egg and milk mixture and mix till it forms a ball
3. divide dough in half
4. roll first half in 17 x 12 inch rectangle
5. place in cookie sheet and bring pastry up sides
6. cover pastry with apples and sprinkle with sugar and cinnamon
7. roll out second half of dough and place on top of apples
8. moisten edges with milk and pinch together
9. beat egg white until stiff and brush on crust
10. bake at 400f for 1 hour
11. mix glaze ingredients together and brush on crust
12. this square freezes beautifully
target.review: Loved this recipe.   Cuts beautifully.  Used a 10x15 pan. I used butter for the shortening and it worked perfect.  Needed a tad more crust,  so next time I will do 3 cups of flour and 3/4 cups of milk.    Used a simple egg wash, which browned beautifully.  I did not put the glaze on and it didn't need it at all.  I use a convection oven  at 375 degrees.  Looks just like an apple pie but square, but better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream cheese coffeecake

this coffeecake is well worth the time it takes to make it. this is by far my most requested recipe. it is hard to just eat one piece.  enjoy!

1. batter: cream butter and sugar
2. add eggs and beat well
3. mix flour , baking powder and salt
4. gradually add to creamed mixture
5. batter will be thick
6. set aside
7. filling: cream all ingredients for the filling together and set aside
8. topping: combine sugar and flour
9. cut in butter until crumbly and set aside
10. to assemble: spread half of the batter in bottom of greased and floured 9 x 13 inch pan
11. batter is thick so it doesn't have to cover the entire bottom of pan , just spread around the best you can
12. spread filling over batter
13. spoon remaining batter on top and sprinkle with topping
14. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minute cut into squares and serve warm or cool
15. keep refrigerated
demonstrations.review: This is the same as #67856.  I have made it many times and it is delish.  The only change I make is I use one package of cream cheese instead of two.   It's just enough to make it the moistest coffeecake the you have ever eaten.  I make it in a 9X13 pan.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttermilk doughnut coffeecake

from the best of sunset low-fat cook book.  baked in a ring mold this coffeecake even looks like a big doughnut!  serve with a tangy orange syrup, recipe included.

1. sift together the first five ingredients in a large bowl
2. in a small bowl beat the next four ingredients until well blended
3. add the egg mixture to the flour mixture and stir just until evenly moistened
4. batter will be stiff
5. spread batter evenly in an oiled 4-cup metal ring mold and bake in a 375 oven until browned , about 20 minutes
6. meanwhile: prepare orange syrup by combining the juice and sugar and bringing to a boil over med-hi heat until reduced to 1 1 / 2 cups
7. back at the ranch:
8. remove cake from oven and while still in the pan use a long skewer to pierce holes all the way through to the bottom of the pan at 1 / 2-inch intervals
9. immediately spoon the orange syrup onto cake , letting it soak completely between additions
10. let stand for about 15 minutes then invert cake onto a platter
11. sift powdered sugar onto cake
demonstrations.review: This is not what I expected.  It made a very small cake and despite 2tsps of baking powder and 1/2 tsp of baking soda it didn't rise very much.  It almost looked like bread or scone texture when it came out of the oven.  The orange sauce, althoughy good,  didn't soak in very well, even with the holes.  The texture of the cake was ok.  It appeared that it would be much harder,  but on tasting it , it was a good texture, just not too attractive.  I love trying new coffeecake recipes, but I have so many that are better, that I probably won't make it again.  My son said was just ok. Sorry

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal shortbread

i cut this from the winnipeg free press food section on february 25, 2004 and decided to post it here for safe keeping! i plan to try this soon! cook time does not include the 1 hour chill time for the dough.

1. cream butter and sugar , add vanilla and beat until fluffy
2. blend flour , baking soda , and rolled oats and then add to butter mixture
3. mix well
4. chill dough for 1 hour
5. roll dough into balls and flatten with a fork
6. bake on ungreased cookie sheet at 350 dgrees for 13 to 15 minutes until lightly browned
demonstrations.review: This cookie is tasty, crispy and one of my favorites.   I was looking for something without a ton of sugar in it.   I made these with 1/4 cup of splenda brown sugar, and 1/4 cup of regular brown sugar.  I chilled my dough for 1 hour,  which is necessary.   I baked the full 15 min.   These were crazy good and kept for a week very well.... if they last that long.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pennsylvania dutch crumb cake

this is the moistest crumb cake i have ever tried. it's my mother-in-law's recipe, and i just can't get enough of this, and i usually don't like crumb cake.

1. sift flour , baking power , salt , sugar and soda
2. cut in butter until mixture has the consistency of course meal or small peas
3. reserve about 1 1 / 2 cups of this mixture
4. combine the eggs , milk and extracts and stire into the remainder of the dry blend
5. pour into 2 well-buttered 10-inch pie pans
6. brush the top of the dough w / butter and sprinkle with the reserved crumb mixture
7. bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes or until cake is done
demonstrations.review: I pulled this recipe off this site in 2004 and have been making it ever since.   It's an excellent  moist cake that goes great with coffee or tea.    I also make it in a 9x13 pan and bake for 40 min at 350.   I add a cup of chopped pecans to the topping.   It's a family favorite.  Thanks Lee

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter sheet cake with peanut butter frosting

attention all peanut-butter lovers, i urge you not to pass this one up, this is a wonderful moist cake with delicious peanut butter frosting :) servings are only estimated depending on the the size of the slices.

1. set oven to 350f
2. line the bottom of a 10 x 15-inch jellyroll pan with parchment paper
3. in a large bowl stir together flour , sugars , baking soda , salt and cinnamon
4. in a saucepan combine water with 3 / 4 cup butter
5. bring to a boil
6. remove from heat then stir in peanut butter and oil
7. mix until completely blended , then add / stir into the flour mixture until combined
8. in a bowl mix together eggs with buttermilk and vanilla until completely combined , then stir into the peanut butter / flour mixture until combined
9. spread the batter into prepared pan
10. bake for 18-25 minutes or until cake tests done
11. cool cake in pan completely
12. for the frosting
13. in a large bowl beat butter with peanut butter and vanilla until light and fluffy
14. beat in the whipping cream until combined
15. add in 1 / 2 cup confectioners sugar to start then beat in the remaining confectioners sugar adding in more if necessary to achieve desired consistency
16. spread over cooled cake
demonstrations.review: I have made this 3 times now.   Every time is just as good.  It has become a favorite at birthday time.   Frosting is excellent, and a must.  I serve it with chocolate ice  cream,  and it is a huge hit.  I adjusted the recipe for a 12x17 inch pan.  For that size it bakes for only 22 min. at 350 in a convection oven

target.recipe_text:
aloo gobi   potato and cauliflower curry

my youngest sons most requested side dish when we eat curry. he loves the left-overs hot or cold too.

1. boil the potatoes in their skins and allow to cool
2. peel the potatoes and cut them into 2 inch squares
3. blanch the cauliflower in boiling water for 2 minutes-do not over boil the cauliflower as it should still be firm after cooking
4. cut into small florets
5. heat the oil over medium heat in a wide frypan
6. add the mustard seeds and as soon as they begin popping , add the cumin and fenugreek seeds and then the red chillies
7. add the onion and the green chilli , stir and fry until the onions are golden brown-8-10 minutes
8. add the cauliflower , reduce the heat to low , cover the pan and cook for 6-8 minutes
9. add the potatoes , dried spices and salt
10. stir gently until all the ingredients are mixed thoroughly
11. cover the pan and cook til the potatoes are heated through-6-8 minutes
12. stir in the coriander leaves and remove from the heat
target.review: Another winner. Made as written, but needed a little water. Was suitable for a main for the vegetarians and a great side dish for the rest of us. will be making the next time a curry is on the menu. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard microwave salmon

tasty, healthy and quick.  prep time 5 minutes and cook time 4 minutes...can't beat that!  i serve with rice and steamed broccoli.

1. place salmon steaks in microwave-safe dish
2. in a separate bowl , mix together remaining ingredients
3. drizzle mustard glaze evenly over salmon
4. microwave on high for 4 minutes
5. remove from oven and allow to stand for 2 minutes before serving
6. makes 2 servings
demonstrations.review:
Fabulous recipe - thank you. Have made this two nights running and have tweaked it slightly. 1.5 minutes is perfect for one piece of salmon - covered with baking paper cause it can make a mess. I subbed thyme for dill - personal preference - also instead of mixing mustard and honey - I smeared the salmon in mustard, added dill then drizzled honey over. Also tonight - I subbed dill with dried chilli's - delicious!
Thank you - could not be quicker or easier - this is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable pasta sauce  crock pot

this sauces simmers all day to blend the flavours. dinner can be on the table in no time after a hard day's work. there are so many chunky vegetables in this that the meat lovers won't even miss the meat :) this sauce makes a lot but freezes well. created for ready, set, cook! winter 2005.

1. combine tomatoes , spinach , carrot , onion , mushrooms , celery , water , butter , and milk powder in a blender and blend well
2. pour into a crock pot and add seasonings , tomato paste , and cheese
3. cook on low for 8 hours or high for 5 hours
4. serve over your favourite pasta
demonstrations.review: We also added too much spinich and left out the blending. During the day various people added there own touch, extra tomato paste, red wine, chilli's etc. When serving we stirred in lite sour cream which neutralised any acidity. Lovely.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef satay

makes me think of bali! prep time doesn't include marinating time.

1. remove all fat from meat
2. cut meat into strips approx 2 1 / 2 cm thick , then cut each strip into 5mm pieces
3. mix remaining ingredients marinade ingredients together
4. add meat
5. mix well
6. let stand overnight or for several hours
7. drain marinade from meat
8. reserve marinade for sauce
9. thread meat on bamboo skewers
10. put under hot grill
11. grill until golden brown and cooked through
12. turn skewers frequently , brushing with extra oil
13. serve with sate sauce
14. sate sauce: heat butter in pan
15. add peeled and finely-chopped onion
16. saute gently until onion is golden brown
17. add remaining ingredients
18. mix well
19. add reserved marinade
20. stir until combined
21. bring to boil
22. boil uncovered 5 minutes or until sauce is thick
23. serve hot or cold
24. serves 6
demonstrations.review:
Thank you for a great recipe!!
I divided the marinade into 2 parts, using 1/2 for beef and the rest for chicken. Both were cubed and served with toothpicks at a party. The plates emptied very quickly. This is easy and a recipe I will be making again soon.
Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq hinty minty lamb chops

superb combination of flavors! lamb is a heavenly meat once you acquire a taste for it. serve lamb with fresh peas, baby carrots and new potatoes mmmmmmmmm

1. combine all the marinade ingredients and mix well
2. place chops in a large zip lock bag
3. pour marinade into the bag with the chops , seal bag
4. place in refrigerator for 2-3 hours , turn several times to coat the chops
5. heat bbq to medium high
6. have heat 5" from the chops
7. sear chops for 5 minutes
8. turn heat down to medium low and cook for a further 12 minutes , brush with the marinade
9. adjust this time to suit how you like your chops
10. garnish with mint leaves& serve
demonstrations.review:
Cooked this for my parents - using a rack of lamb and baking on the BBQ - needed extra liquid for the baking but they loved the flavour - and it turned out moist and tender.
Thanks for a great recipe Bergy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
florentine slice

taste sensation!

1. melt butter and sugar in a large saucepan
2. remove from heat and add almonds , raisins and cherries
3. sift flour and baking powder into the saucepan and mix until combined
4. spread into a greased 20cm square shallow tin
5. bake at 180c degrees for 25 minutes or until golden and cooked
6. melt chocolate in microwave or over hot water
7. drizzle over slice while still warm
8. cut into sqaures or fingers while warm
demonstrations.review: Thanks Evie. I did not get to try this myself but it smelled really good (It was in the back of the car all day - very tempting) Gave them to a supplier and my order was filled and the car was loaded for me - the florentine slice MUST be good to get that service. THanks again will be bribing with it again soon!!!!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot country ribs

nan

1. place the ribs in a crock pot
2. combine remaining ingredients and pour over ribs
3. cook on low for 7- 9 hours or until done
target.review: The meat was so tender and moist, it just fell apart, fork tender.  Although it may have been a little too sweet for us.  I will try the other person's suggestion and add some tabasco I think next time and will also try fresh garlic in it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tasty collard greens

would be equally as good with turnip or mustard greens or even kale.  *i do the cooking of the smoked turkey leg a day ahead, refrigerate and then skin the congealed fat off the top of the broth.  this is our favorite method of cooking greens.

1. heat oil in a large pot over medium heat
2. saute garlic until light brown
3. add turkey leg and chicken broth , cover and simmer until turkey leg is tender
4. remove turkey leg and cool slightly so comfortable to remove and chop meat and return turkey meat to pot
5. add collard greens and turn heat up to medium-high and let the greens cook down for about 45 minutes , stirring occasionally
6. reduce the heat and season with salt , pepper and red pepper flakes
7. continue to cook until greens are tender - about 45 to 60 minutes
8. drain greens and reserve liquid to reheat leftovers
9. i often freeze some of the liquid and use with frozen greens at another time
demonstrations.review: These were SOOO good!  The only difference is that I used 10 cups chicken stock, 2 smoked turkey legs and I chopped up onion to brown with the garlic.  I also added some hot sauce and put a bay leaf in it as well.  I don't drain the liquid, I like to drink it.  The "pot liquer" is GREAT to sip out of a mug on a cold day and is so healthy full of vitamins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heidi s fried cheese sandwich

my first culinary 'experience'. i must have been about 7, reading heidi. this recipe was in the edition i was reading and i had to run to the kitchen and try it out immediately. mom watched. still fantastic!  expect something like a savoury-cheesey french toast.

1. butter the bread generously and layer the cheese between the two pieces
2. beat the egg with the milk in a container large enough to contain the sandwich and season lightly
3. allow the sandwich to absorb the egg / milk mixture- turn over 1 / 2 way through so the other side absorbs some too
4. this should take about 10-15 minutes so as much of the custard is absorbed as possible
5. drop a tablespoonful of butter into a skillet , on medium heat
6. when it bubbles and smells very fragrant , add the sandwich and fry on both sides till a lovely dark-golden-brown and the cheese is all gooey and melted
7. put it on your best plate , pour yourself a big glass of milk , get out a fork and knife and enjoy
demonstrations.review: I LOVED this sandwich.  I used hearty thick white bread and Boar's head baby swiss cheese.  i forgot to season the custard mixture but it didn't make a difference.  I had this wish a cup of tomato soup and it was DELICIOUS!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s favorite

i was raised by a single mother who never had a lot of time to cook. she would make this 

1. begin boiling noodles in water with 1tbsp cooking oil and 1tsp of italian seasoning
2. brown all hamburger meat in skillet over medium-high heat
3. when noodles are almost done , begin to saute mushrooms in skillet with butter , garlic , salt , & pepper to taste
4. when hamburger meat , noodles , and mushrooms are fully cooked , mix together in a medium-sized bowl
5. add shredded cheddar cheese to taste
6. when cheese is melted , serve
demonstrations.review: My daughter made this tonight....very good!  The kids LOVED it...the only things she did differently was to add chopped onion with the ground beef and a can of diced tomatoes (the seasoned kind) and a bit more cheddar cheese....it was tasty.   What a wonderful meal to quickly make on a soccer, baseball, karate night!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled cauliflower

i actually won a cash prize in our local paper for this recipe. my husband and i will eat the whole thing ourselves - make several if you're having guests. if someone you love doesn't care for cauliflower, this may be the ticket!

1. remove stem& leaves from cauliflower
2. wash& pat dry
3. spread the butter over the cauliflower
4. sprinkle with seasoned salt& cheese
5. wrap head of cauliflower in heavy duty aluminum foil
6. grill over medium heat about 40 minutes or until desired tenderness
demonstrations.review: This was a great side dish to our grilled steaks!  I used olivio in place of the butter, added some pepper and garlic.  We will be making this one often.  SO was worried because he said he didnt like cauliflower.....he does now!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest tastiest barbecue country style ribs  slow cooker

i threw this together one morning before going out for the day. it was super easy because only three ingredients are needed! not only did the house smell heavenly when we came home, but dinner was ready and it was awesome!

1. place all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on low for 6 to 8 hours
3. meat starts to fall off the bones-- be careful of the small ones in the juices !
demonstrations.review: Super tender ribs!  The meat fell apart, and had great flavor.  We prefer ribs on the grill, but we dont always have time.  This hit the spot when I was short on time because of work and sports, and and was craving ribs.

target.recipe_text:
chicken with sumac jujeh al sammak

middle eastern (arabian) grilled chicken. simple but delicious!

1. place the chicken pieces in a dish
2. mix the remaining ingredients together , pour over chicken
3. marinate for several hours or overnight
4. grill or barbecue , turning 3 or 4 times and basting frequently with the marinade until the chicken is browned
target.review: This is awesome. I love Middle Eastern food and this has a really authentic taste. Very easy to prepare, and good with any cut of chicken; I have used breast fillets, drumsticks and thighs and they are all yummy. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pears poached in spiced wine

"i love the rich garnet color that the pears take on after they've been poached in this fragrant spiced wine syrup," writes laura frankel in "jewish cooking for all seasons." for the wine to use in poaching, frankel suggests a kosher merlot by baron herzog.

1. heat wine , sugar , water , peppercorns , bay leaves , rosemary , thyme , cinnamon , vanilla bean and lemon zest to a boil in a large saucepan over high heat
2. meanwhile , remove the pear cores with a melon baller
3. add pears to saucepan
4. reduce heat to a simmer
5. poach the pears until tender enough for a knife to pierce them without resistance , at least 20 minutes , longer if the pears are less ripe
6. let pears cool in the poaching liquid , about 15 minutes
7. place the pears on a serving platter
8. strain the poaching liquid through a sieve into a large saucepan
9. discard the solids
10. heat the liquid to a boil
11. reduce heat to low
12. cook until reduced to a thick syrup , about 45 minutes
13. let cool slightly
14. serve the pears drizzled with the warm syrup
demonstrations.review: These were really yummy! I never thought of putting rosemary and thyme in with pears to poach, but it worked wonderfully. Before I've only ever poached pears in white wine, this was my first time with red, and they turned out beautifully. The flesh was silky and the little puddle of syrup in the bottom of the bowl blended really well with a nice dollop of low-fat Greek style yoghurt. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry dumplings

i haven't tried these yet but they sound so good!

1. in a saucepan , combine 1 / 3 cup sugar and the water
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer for 5 minutes
4. stir in vanilla extract
5. in a medium mixing bowl , sift together flour , the 2 tablespoons sugar , the baking powder , and salt
6. cut in butter with pastry blender or fork until mixture is crumbly
7. add milk and stir just until dry ingredients are moistened
8. place strawberries in a 1 1 / 2-quart casserole dish
9. pour hot sugar mixture over strawberries
10. immediately drop dough evenly in 8 to 10 spoonfuls over strawberries
11. sprinkle dumplings with the remaining 1 tablespoon of sugar
12. bake at 450 for 25 to 30 minutes , or until dumplings are lightly browned
13. serve hot with whipped topping or ice cream , if desired
demonstrations.review:
This was wonderful! I changed the sugar around a bit, thanks to comments in other reviews; I only used 1/3 cup of sugar overall, and took 3 tbs out of this to put in the dumplings. The rest went in the syrup, and then a little bit extra over the top before it went in the oven.
Very, very yummy - thank you. :-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review:
This was really easy, and very yummy. Like another reviewer, I used fresh ginger and garlic, and then I baked it in the oven on 170C for about 30 minutes. The salmon was lovely and tender with a good flavour.
The only reason that this recipe doesn't get 5 stars from me is that I think one third of a cup of soy sauce is far too much and dominates the other flavours. I used only half of this and think it could have done with less than that.
Great recipe Mirj, and thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon with tomatoes

this savoury dish is very popular in andalusia, spain. you can use red pepper flakes (to your taste) in place of the hot pepper and any firm whitefish can be a substitute for the salmon. great with rice and a green vegetable.

1. in a medium sized frying pan , heat oil and saute onions , garlic& peppers over medium heat for about 10 minutes
2. add remaining ingredients , bring to a boil , then lower heat& simmer for 5 minutes
3. place the fish into a greased medium sized casserole dish
4. pour the tomato mixture over the fish& bake , uncovered , in a preheated 350f oven for 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is great, and so very easy. Who would have thought that salmon steaks and cumin would complement each other so well?! Even my 'non fish liking' husband likes this one. I have already made this several times and it will most definitely be made again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wacky chocolate orange cake with orange frosting

when i first saw this recipe (on the label of a white vinegar bottle - where else?), i thought 

1. ---- the cake ----
2. preheat oven to 350 fahrenheit
3. sift together flour , sugar , baking soda and salt into an 8" x 8" baking pan
4. make 3 holes in the dry ingredients
5. place oil in the first hole , vinegar in the second hole , and vanilla in the third hole
6. pour orange juice over everything and mix well
7. spread batter evenly in the pan and bake in dish that the batter was mixed in
8. bake 30 minutes or until center is firm
9. allow to cool
10. refrigerate leftovers
11. ---- the frosting ----
12. combine gelatin , orange juice , and cold water in small saucepan
13. let stand until thick
14. place over low heat , stirring constantly , just until gelatin dissolves
15. remove from heat and cool , but do not allow to set
16. whip cream , sugar and vanilla until slightly thickened
17. while beating slowly , gradually add gelatin to whipped cream mixture
18. whip at high speed until stiff
19. spread thickly on the cake
demonstrations.review: Very yummy! I left off the icing, being too lazy, and used wholemeal flour to make the cake a bit healthier. This was really easy and the best part for me is that it didn't require any beating - which is always annoying when you want to make a cake quickly. Thanks for the new cake recipe!

target.recipe_text:
hamburger helper style beef with noodles

this is my quick and easy weeknight dinner when we are in a hurry. (vegit is available at health food stores)

1. cook noodles according to package , drain and set aside
2. combine mushroom soup and bouillon in medium bowl and whisk till smooth , set aside
3. brown beef and onion in nonstick fry pan till meat well cooked , drain if necessary
4. add soup mixture to meat& onion , heat till bubbling , then add noodles
5. reduce heat and simmer 10-15 minutes or until liquid absorbed by noodles
6. serve with a crisp salad or a green vegetable
target.review: This is really good! It's been a long time since I've had anything like this because hubby is particular about ingreds in processed foods, so this is good from scratch. I used Mrs Dash Table Blend and used a soup can of water instead of bouillon.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger stew

i love this stew because it is so easy to throw together,and it goes great with a hot pan of cornbread. i suggest sweet cornbread (recipe #83625).
this recipe was my great grandma's and my grandma taught it to me. it was hard for me to put this in recipe format because it is all in my head. you can adjust some of the ingredients to suit your family.

1. brown hamburger , garlic , salt , black pepper , and oregano in a dutch oven over medium heat
2. drain
3. return meat to pot
4. add worcestershire sauce , potatoes , onions , carrots , tomatoes , green beans , corn , peas and tomato sauce
5. stir to combine
6. over medium-high heat bring to a slight boil
7. reduce heat to low
8. cover
9. continue simmering stew , stirring occasionally for 30 minutes
10. this stew can easily be tweaked to your family's tastes
11. i have added cabbage , okra , zucchini and various spices
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe yesterday and we enjoyed it. I will put less black pepper in next time. DH used hot pepper sauce on his. Also I added some basil and used sliced baby carrots (didn't have canned), and used 2 cloves of garlic minced. Very good!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs  shirley s goulash

this goulash was made everytime our church would go to the homeless shelter in detroit.  the ladies from our church would get together the day before and get all the food ready.  we would go to mrs. shirley's home and she would just whip up this goulash.  i usually do not like goulash but hers was just so good that you couldn't help but love it.  it is a simple as can be.  she would always cook it for hours while we prepared other foods for the shelter.  you could smell it coming together and mmmmm  smells so good!!

1. brown ground beef , green pepper , onion , and celery
2. drain
3. place ground beef mixture into a large cooking pot and add tomtoes
4. when it comes to a good rolling boil add macaroni and cook another 15-20 minutes
5. shirley would actually cook her goulash for a good 3-4 hours before adding the macaroni and then refrigerate overnight
6. she said it helped get the flavor of all the ingredients to blend
demonstrations.review: I made this for hubby and me and took some over to my mom too. Very nice. I used Kamut rotini pasta. I used a 28 oz can diced tomatoes and a 14 oz can diced tomatoes and a yellow pepper. I also added 1 1/4 cups extra water as it cooked. Good reheated. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken avocado date sandwich

i've been trying to add more protein to my "almost vegetarian" diet. this sandwich was inspired by an avocado!

1. mash the avocado , date , jalapeno pepper and mayonnaise in a food processor to chunky paste
2. roast the chicken slices gently on both sides in a small skillet
3. toast the bread and layer the avocado-date spread on a slice and add chopped scallions to top
4. layer the chicken and the toast
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Very good. I didn't use the dates or the jalapeno pepper. But I bought some fresh dates to snack on. We got a whole BBQ chicken at the store deli and used slices of that. Hubby & I both liked this! Thank you

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quick and healthy vegetable beef soup  low carb and ww friendly

easy, quick and good for you soup.  this recipe is actually from a ww website; but for my low carb diet i added some lean ground beef and made some other adaptions.  if you are on ww, skip the beef and it's 0 points per serving.  if you are watching your sodium intake, use low sodium broth and no added salt tomatoes.

1. in a medium to large pot , heat 1 / 2 tsp olive oil
2. brown ground beef , onion and garlic
3. add broth , tomatoes , veggies and seasonings
4. bring to a boil
5. simmer , cover and cook on low for 15 minutes to 30 minutes
6. discard bay leaf , serve
demonstrations.review: I had a 28 oz can diced tomatoes and a 4-cup container of chicken broth on hand so I used those. I didn't have zucchini. It took about one hr. for cabbage to be cooked. Very Good. Both DH and I liked it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
two step truffles

these will be the easiest truffles you've ever made and they are sooo yummy!  they are a tradition at my house for christmas and we coat them in pink-tinted white chocolate for my daughter's birthday.  you can shape them like eggs for easter and dip them in dyed white chocolate or roll them in colored sugar.  you can add different flavorings, different coatings, substitute milk, dark or white chocolate... the variations are endless.  no matter how you finish these, they will taste great!  the original recipe came from one of the chocolate companies several years ago but i can't remember which one.

1. place chopped chocolate in a bowl
2. slowly bring cream to a boil in a small saucepan
3. pour over chocolate
4. let stand 1 minute
5. stir until smooth
6. cover and chill
7. using a melon baller , scoop into 2 teaspoon sized balls
8. smooth them out a little by hand
9. serve as is or roll or dip in your choice of coatings
10. try not to eat too many of these while you're making them or there won't be any left for the party ! we have lots of fun rolling these in all different things and sampling the results as we go
11. the kids have a ball doing this
12. i usually set up 6 or 8 little bowls of things in advance
13. i always make a double batch that way my family can enjoy taste testing and i still have enough for the party !
demonstrations.review: DH said they taste like they were professionally made. Rolled some in toasted coconut, some in ground walnuts and a few in sifted cocoa powder. I would prefer the walnuts not so fine next time. We're saving half for when our nephew visits from NB tomorrow. Thank you.

target.recipe_text:
off the cob  freezer corn

this recipe allows you the fresh taste of sweet corn-on-the cob all year long. i've been making it for years and will today make it with olathe corn i picked up at the market for 10 ears for $1. it stacks neatly in your freezer and is ready in a jiffy.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. shuck ears of corn
3. rinse to remove silks
4. place on paper towels to drain
5. using an angel food cake pan and electric knife , stand each ear on tube part of pan and cut corn off cob
6. your cuttings will fall neatly into the pan
7. as the cake pan fills , empty into large roaster pan
8. season with salt and pepper to your taste
9. cube butter and distribute onto corn in roaster pan
10. pour half and half throughout corn
11. roast for 1 hour , stirring gently every 15 minutes
12. allow to cool for half an hour
13. label freezer bags with contents , quantity and date
14. ladle into bags at portions suitable for your personal use
15. stack neatly in freezer for later use
target.review: My FIL gave me a bunch of corn (not very sweet) so I wanted to make some of this freezer corn to use in corn chowder recipes this winter.  This method is terrific.  I was able to cut a cob every 30 seconds with the electric knife.  Very neat & clean.  My BIL and FIL who freeze a lot of corn each year, will be switching to this technique.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
silky vanilla butter frosting

this is not your usual butter-cream made with powdered sugar. butter is beaten into a flour-thickened base to make an exquisitely light and creamy frosting. not overly sweet like those made with powdered sugar, but sweet enough to be the perfect compliment for a cake. make sure the base is completely cooled before beating in the butter. i added in 15 minutes cooling time, but it will vary depending on conditions.

1. in 2-quart saucepan , thoroughly combine sugar and flour
2. with wire whisk , gradually stir in milk until smooth
3. cook over medium-high heat , stirring frequently , until mixture has thickened and boils
4. reduce heat to low
5. cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat and cool completely
7. in medium bowl , with mixer at medium speed , beat butter until light and fluffy
8. gradually beat in milk mixture
9. beat in vanilla
demonstrations.review: I cooked the flour/sugar/milk mixture thoroughly but still detected a floury taste.  Added an additional 1/3 cup of powdered sugar after tasting the final product.  I guess we like it a little sweeter but I also don't care for the "hurt your teeth" gritty sweet versions.  I'll keep looking for a vanilla frosting that will be my standard.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with mushroom garlic sauce

this recipe is for garlic lovers.it is a quick easy meal when you are rushed and want some comfort food

1. in a skillet melt 2 tbsp butter
2. add garlic , allow to brown , then add mushrooms , basil , salt& pepper
3. cook until the mushrooms are just tender
4. add remaining butter and olive oil
5. stir and remove from heat
6. when pasta is cooked reheat the sauce add parsley
7. mix with pasta and enjoy
demonstrations.review: We really enjoyed this simple dish.  I added some leftover grilled asparagus (still firm to the bite) and the sweetness and green color pop was a nice addition.  Peas and broccoli would also work, I think.  I might also try sautéing onions with the garlic next time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheddar spinach and  mushroom pie with puff pastry crust

this is a perfect luncheon dish! you will need a 9-inch deep-dish pie plate, i used fresh sliced mushrooms in place of canned that i sauteed firstly when i made this, and i also added in a small chopped red bell pepper but that is optional. if you use more than 1 cup sauteed fresh mushrooms i suggest to use a 10-inch pie plate instead of 9-inch and roll the puff pastry out a little larger.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. prepare a 9-inch glass pie plate
3. roll out the puff pastry sheet to an 11-inch square , then transfer to prepared pie plate
4. trim edges
5. in a bowl beat the cream cheese until smooth
6. add in the half and half and eggs
7. beat until combined
8. squeeze out any moisture in the thawed spinach well using you hands before adding inches
9. add in all remaining ingredients
10. mix with a wooden spoon to combine
11. pour into puff pastry crust
12. sprinkle with about 1 / 2 cup grated parmesan cheese
13. bake for about 25 minutes , or until the filling is set
14. cool for 10 minutes before slicing and serving
demonstrations.review:
Excellent.  Made for my parents and sister along with my family.  Everyone raved.  The first time we made this was based on a search for some miscellaneous ingredients I needed to use up.  I'm glad we stumbled on this one.
I used sauteed fresh mushrooms and would highly recommend the effort to do that vs. canned.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ziploc bag omelet  eggs in a hurry

eggs-in-a-bag, this has got to be the easiest and tastiest way i've ever found to prepare breakfast, or even just a snack. each person prepares their own with the particular omelet ingredients that they prefer. recipe is for each serving.

1. mix all ingredients well , in a sandwich size zip-lock plastic bag and seal
2. drop bag into a pot of boiling water
3. boil for 13-15 minutes
4. remove and enjoy
demonstrations.review: Works great!  I need to remember to use this when we have company.  I'm a little leary about boiling plastic for 15 minutes though.  I know it doesn't melt, but the latest "chemicals leaching out of plastic and into foods when heated" scare makes me a little hesitant to do this again.  I can't find anything conclusive on this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best cream of broccoli soup

this recipe is thick and flavorful. simple, delicious, and quick to make. hope that you enjoy it as much as my family does. i have added chicken to this soup, very good

1. melt 2 tablespoons butter in medium sized stock pot , and saut onion , garlic and celery until tender
2. add broccoli and broth
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes
4. pure soup or mash with potato masher
5. return to heat
6. in small saucepan , over medium heat melt 3 tablespoons butter , stir in flour and add milk
7. stir until thick and bubbly , add to soup
8. add cheese
9. stir until melted
10. season with pepper and serve
demonstrations.review: The first time I made this it was going to be my standard.  The last time, we weren't impressed.  I must  have done something wrong so I'm writing this review to remind myself to try again and follow the recipe carefully.  It was bland tasting on round 2.

target.recipe_text:
easy marinated pork chops

nothing could be simpler than this recipe, and it's great because you can start marinating it the night before, or in the morning, and then all you have to do at dinnertime is take the pork chops out of the bag and grill them. note:  the time listed does not include the time for marinating.

1. in a large resealable plastic bag , combine the first eight ingredients
2. add the pork chops
3. seal bag and turn to coat
4. refrigerate for 8 hours or overnight
5. drain and discard marinade
6. grill pork chops , covered , over medium heat for 4-5 minutes on each side , or until they reach 160 degrees f
7. serve
target.review: These were very tasty.  Next time I'll probably add a bit more salt.  I broiled mine in the oven instead of grilling.  They probably would have tasted better on the grill but the husband couldn't be bothered. *roll eyes*

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizzeria pizza sauce

this quick and easy sauce tastes like that which you would find at your neighborhood pizzeria! i found the original recipe on the internet, but adapted it to my families taste.

1. in a medium saucepan , saut garlic in oil until golden
2. add tomato paste , water , sugar , oregano , basil , cheese and wine
3. season with salt and pepper , to taste
4. simmer for 10 minutes over medium low heat
demonstrations.review: That is the BEST sauce I've ever tasted. My husband and kids absolutely LOVED it. I hardly ever get compliments anymore but this one had my family asking for me!  Thank you so much for posting it. Homemade pizza is finally good at our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
enchilada sauce

this is a very easy, quick enchilada sauce to use instead of the canned variety. we prefer to eat freshly made foods without alot of preservatives. this has a wonderful flavor.

1. heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
2. add the garlic and saute for 1 to 2 minutes
3. add onion , oregano , chili powder , basil , ground black pepper , salt , cumin , parsley , salsa and tomato sauce
4. mix together and then stir in the water
5. bring to a boil , reduce heat to low and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes
6. use in place of canned enchilada sauce
demonstrations.review: It was my first try making enchiladas!  This was really easy and really yummy!  Next time I'll double it because I dipped my tortilla's in it to soften before I filled them and by the time they were rolled and in the pan, there was just barely enough left to pour over the top.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili  real texas chili

there are many cities that claim to be the birthplace of chili, but it was born on the cattle trails of texas. this will be a big surprise for a lot of you, but real texas chili does not have beans or chunks of tomato. i say that to say this; if you want to experience what early cowboys of texas experienced then follow this recipe. oh yeah, don't freak out by the amount of chili powder. if you like your chili hot and spicy leave as is, if you like it spicy omit the cayenne.

1. the sausage used for this recipe is pork country style like jimmy dean or owens roll etcetera
2. brown meat and onion together in a large 12 inch skillet and drain well
3. for even lower fat rinse meat with hot water , drain and place back in skillet
4. add remaining ingredients into a mixing bowl then stir in 8 ounces of water mixing well , now blend well in with meat and onion mixture
5. simmer 30 minutes
6. you can simmer for hours if you want , just stir every 30 minutes
7. chow down
8. this is great by itself or to make nachos , top cheese enchiladas , frito pie , quite good rolled in a flour tortilla with cheddar etc --
demonstrations.review: This chili was AWESOME!!!  I couldn't find mexican oregano in my area but I just used a little bit of regular oregano. I was also out of Cayenne pepper and it just wasn't quite hot enough so I used some Franks Cayenne Pepper sauce in my bowl.  This is now our staple chili recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jambalaya for the crock pot

try this for your next crock pot adventure. wonderful flavor!

1. cut chicken into 1 inch pieces
2. put all ingredients in crock pot
3. cover
4. cook on low for 8 hours
5. add shrimp the last 20 minutes of cooking
6. stir in rice before serving
demonstrations.review: This was really good!  I wanted to put some andouille sausage in it but our meat counter didn't have any.  I half cooked some Jimmy Dean Hot sausage and put that in. I think it would have tasted better with andouille.  I didn't use any shrimp. No one else likes it but me.  Other than that, I stayed to the recipe, very tasty!  I had to freeze some!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s moist cheddar garlic oven fried chicken breast

this is for serious garlic lovers. the chicken bakes out so moist and tender! grated cheese may be sprinkled on top of the breast the last 5 minutes of cooking if desired but that is optional. double all ingredients for more than four breasts and adjust the amount of garlic to suit taste. for the coating amount you might be able to get away with 5 or maybe 6 very small chicken breasts, but i would suggest to increase the amount slightly --- to take this dish to yet another level, about 10 minutes before the cooking time is finished, drizzle the top of the chicken with a little pasta sauce, then sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top. return to oven for about 10 minutes until the chicken is completely cooked and sauce is hot and cheese has melted. for a lemon-garlic flavor add in 3 tablespoons lemon juice to the melted butter/garlic mixture ---  *note* for a healthier alternative smart balance butter blend may be used in place of the melted butter --- you will love this chicken!
visit my food blog, www.kittencalskitchen.com, for more of my recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. butter an 11 x 7-inch pan
3. in a bowl , combine melted butter with fresh minced garlic , 1 teaspoon garlic powder and salt
4. in another bowl , combine the dry breadcrumbs with 1 / 2 cup finely grated cheddar cheese , parmesan cheese 1 teaspoon garlic powder and coarse ground black pepper
5. dip chicken in butter mixture
6. then in crumb mixture
7. place in prepared pan and bake uncovered for 35-45 minutes or until cooked through , larger breasts may take more time
8. top with shredded cheddar or mozzarella the last 5 minutes of cooking (this is only optional
demonstrations.review: This just didn't go over well at my house.  I think it was too soggy or something.  The flavor was good but the breading just didn't stay on. I wish I'd had a rack to try cooking it on so it didn't have to sit it its own juice.

target.recipe_text:
my favorite peanut butter pie

i have always loved peanut butter pie- this one is especially decadent and delicious!

1. mix peanut butter and confectioners sugar together until crumbly
2. put in bottom of pie shell
3. mix flour , sugar , salt , milk , and egg yolks together in sauce pan
4. bring to rolling boil
5. stir frequently to prevent sticking
6. when mixture has thickened , remove from heat
7. pour cooked mixture over peanut butter mixture in pie shell and let cool
8. spread cool whip on top of pie and sprinkle with reserved peanut butter and sugar mixture
target.review:
i had this and then lost it.  THANKS so much for posting this. I sometimes put beaten eggs whites on top then crumbled peaanut butter on top and brow it nicely.    thanks again

            Ladies of the Lake.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old widow walker s ziploc omelettes

mrs. walker was my sunday school teacher and we used to do this in the church kitchen, occasionally. this is my first memory of cooking that i cherish to this day. she keeps her age a closely guarded secret but is rumoured to be 115+ years old and perhaps, immortal. she has out lived three husbands and four children. she is still sharp as the bowie knife she carries in her purse. i don't know why she carries a bowie knife in her purse- but she always has. i asked her about it years ago and she said, "you would be surprised how often it comes in handy, honey." i suppose it does, mrs. walker. god bless you. btw- she is thrilled that i want to pass this on to another generation of schoolchildren. she was surprised that i remembered doing this with her over 35 years ago and was touched. when asked how to do it- she rattled off the instructions faster than i could write!

i've eaten this bag-n-boil recipe for 40+ years with no toxicity what-so-ever, obviously. if it was toxic... i would be in too poor of health to type.

google the topic for yourself and make your own judgment. the danger is greatly exaggerated.

1. have children write their name on a quart-size ziploc freezer bag with permanent marker
2. crack 2 eggs into the bag shake to combine them
3. put out a variety of ingredients such as: cheeses , ham , bacon , onion , green pepper , tomato , hash browns , etc
4. each child adds prepared ingredients of choice to their bag and shake
5. make sure to get the air out of the bag and zip it up
6. place the bags into rolling , boiling water for exactly 13 minutes
7. you can usually cook 6-8 omelettes in a large pot
8. for more , make another pot of boiling water
9. open the bags and the omelette will roll out easily
10. be prepared for children to squeal with delight at their first meal they have cooked
11. a lifetime memory has just been served
12. this of course , depends on your situation and how carnivorous the kiddies are
13. i've tried to guestimate for five servings
demonstrations.review: Perfect for families with different tastse!  Made this for breakfast for 6 people.  Each had different items, each turned out wonderful.  We checked at 11 minutes but was still runny, so 13 minutes was perfect for us. The easiest omelet breakfast I have ever made, and they looked and tasted great!  A new favorite for both cook and family!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review:
These turned out so much like the real thing!  Even for as novice as my skills in the kitchen are, these were so easy and so rewarding.
I figured out that if you cut into a long strip strip, then turned it up on its side, (so the peanut butter was against a flat surface) it didn't squish out the peanut butter.  
So good!  My DH says 10 stars!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
braciola  braciole  with tomato and wine sauce

i cut this recipe out of the newspaper years ago. it is terrific, and i have never seen this recipe anywhere else.

1. place steaks between waxed paper or plastic wrap- pound until very thin
2. cut steaks into serving size pieces , or you can roll the whole thing and tie with string combine garlic , crumbs , egg , bacon , 1 1 / 2 tsp oregano , cheese , parsley flakes , 1 / 2 tsp salt 1 / 8 teaspoons pepper , 1 tbs
3. olive oil
4. spoon equal amounts of this mixture on steaks
5. roll steak and tie with string , or secure with toothpicks
6. heat oil in skillet and brown rolls
7. transfer to oven proof casserole
8. add tomatoes , onion powder , 1 tsp oregano , 1 / 2 tsp salt , 1 / 8 tsp black pepper
9. simmer , covered for 1 1 / 2 hours
10. add water if necessary- add wine and cook another 10 minute
11. serve with pasta
12. yummmmmmyyyyyyyy !
demonstrations.review: this is my great grandmas recipe    the only thing different  i do is after  you brown the roll you simmer in your sauce for 1 or 2 hours.  this really brings all the flavors together.   thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingersnap pot roast

mmm!  cookies... one for the roast, one for me, one for the roast, two for me...

1. trim fat from roast
2. cut if necessary to fit crock-pot
3. in large skillet brown roast on all sides in hot oil
4. in a small bowl combine water , gingersnaps , vinegar , bouillon , and red pepper
5. in crock-pot , place potatoes , carrots or parsnips , and bay leaf
6. place meat on top of vegetables
7. pour gingersnap mixture over meat
8. cover
9. cook on low-heat setting for 10-12 hours or high-heat setting for 5-6 hours
demonstrations.review:
This was so good on this cold December day!  So easy to make, smelled great while cooking, and very tasty and filling.  
The only thing I did differently was to add 4 potatoes, and 1 stalk celery.
The first time my kids ate sweet potatoe and loved it!  Thank you for posting this fantastic recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix extender

a simple way to make a bigger and better cake mix. makes a 13x9 pan come out very high and moist.

1. mix all together
2. add to your already mixed cake mix batter
3. bake per directions but may need and additional 5-10 minutes longer to become done
demonstrations.review: this is simply a GREAT idea !! THANKS SO MUCH FOR SHARING WITH US  this worked great for all kinds of cakes even my from scratch ones. they were very moist and tender. now we can all bake those killer cakes you pay a small fortune for at the bakery.

target.recipe_text:
stuffed jalapeno pita bites

these delicious appetizers were a hit at our easter sunday potluck brunch. i was pleased to find the recipe was in one of our local cook books 'a taste of heaven' and surprisingly a recipe i had been thinking of trying. delicious, easy and a crowd pleaser! i find putting them on a cookie sheet and heating through in a 350 oven  make for a marvelous hot appetizer.  also excellent at room temperature.

1. cook bacon , cool and crumble
2. cut mini pitas in half with scissors
3. in bowl microwave margarine and onions until soft - about 2 minutes
4. add cream cheese and blend with mixer until creamy , fold in crumbled bacon , tomato and peppers and stuff into pitas
5. this also makes a terrific dip
target.review: Yummy! I did make one change and that was using leftover ham instead of the bacon. I am not a tomato fan but I found that the tomatoes really tasted great. I also threw it in the oven for about 5 minutes at 350. It made the pita nice and crispy. Next time I would add another minute. Thanks for posting :)  Made for PAC 2010

demonstrations.recipe_text:
panera s cream cheese potato soup

this is my favorite recipe for potato soup.  it's a copycat of the one they use to serve at the st. louis bread company (panera).  the recipe originally called for shredding your potatoes, but i never could get them to cook that way. i know they should cook faster, but i never could get it to work.

1. combine broth , potatoes , and spices
2. boil on medium heat until potatoes are tender
3. smash a few of the potatoes to release their starch for thickening
4. reduce to low heat
5. add cream cheese
6. heat , stirring frequently , until cheese melts
demonstrations.review: I thought this was great. I used onion flakes and a combination of bakers and red potatoes. In the end I had to wisk the top of the soup to get the cream cheese to melt but it was worth it. Will make this again, thanks for posting :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dirty  cajun  rice

this is a recipe i developed by trying to duplicate a rice dish from a restaurant. it ended up being very simple and quick. it came very close to the original. some folks even say it's better.

1. cook rice
2. while rice is cooking , chop onions into 1 / 4" pieces separating the bottoms from the tops
3. saut the bottoms along with the loose sausage until cooked thoroughly , about 15-20 minutes
4. then add 1 / 2 bouillon cube and 1 / 4 cup water and mix thoroughly
5. turn off heat
6. add onion tops and toss so that residual heat will take the bite out of the onions
7. mix rice with meat mixture and serve
8. the cajun seasoning is also to taste
9. do not add salt , as the bouillon and cajun seasoning take care of the saltiness
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe! I like how it all came together. Even with all the seasonings I did find the rice a bit bland so next time I might cook the rice in the water with the bouillon powder and some more seasonings. Thank you so much for posting :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy pasta salad

this is a delicious, summery pasta salad that's incredibly easy to make! i often get requests for it at family gatherings. i usually use fat-free italian dressing and light mayonnaise and it still tastes fantastic. feel free to throw in some peppers and other veggies too!

1. bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil
2. add pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes or until al dente
3. drain and pour pasta into a large dish
4. stir in the celery and tomatoes
5. in a separate bowl , whisk together the salad dressing and mayonnaise , then pour this mixture over the salad and toss again , to coat
6. cover and chill until ready to serve
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Really good. I did change the celery for cucumber and the Italian dressing for ranch and it turned out well. I didn't use all of the dressing/mayo. I'll make this again with more veggies.

Thanks for sharing :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
simple cucumber slices

got this recipe from a website that does just vegetables.  with a few tweaks, i made it mine.  hope you enjoy, also!

1. in a bowl with a lid , combine cucumbers , onions and dill
2. in a saucepan , combine sugar , vinegar , water and salt
3. bring to a boil
4. pour over cucumber mixture
5. cover and chill at least 3 hours , but better overnight
demonstrations.review: Tasty! Made as directed except for one exception, I couldn't find any apple cider vinegar so I used white vinegar. It still tasted good. Next time I will make it with the vinegar called for. Thanks for posting :) Made for PAC 2010

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamsicle freeze

exactly like the orange julius in the mall, without the stomach curdling mixture of acidic orange juice and milk/ice cream.... i also included variations including different fruit, like peaches & cream, strawberries & cream, etc. i tried for years to figure out this recipe, beginning at around age 12! i finally got it one day at age 25 and now my 11 year old daughter whips them up for herself and friends after school or for breakfast.

1. add all ingredients into blender and blend on high until no ice chunks are left
2. makes about tall glasses
3. i don't recommend replacing the powdered creamer with milk , as the acid in the orange juice will curdle the milk !
4. powdered milk may be used in emergency !
5. strawberries& cream version: replace orange juice with strawberries
6. peaches& cream: replace orange juice with canned or fresh peaches
7. add vodka for a tasty , refreshing cocktail on a hot summer evening !
8. be creative !
9. there are so many ways to change this recipe to make the most delicious frozen drink that kids & adults will love !
demonstrations.review:
This was too sweet for my taste so next I'll use half the amount of sugar. Besides it being too sweet the flavour is really really good. I think frozen strawberries or a banana would also be really good in here. 
 Most smoothy recipes have milk, ice cream, or yogurt as base ingredient and I like how this doesn't. 
Thanks for the recipe!----------- Update: This is one of my most favourite recipes!! I add less sugar and sometimes replace some of the ice cubes with frozen raspberries. I also don't add as much water. Sometimes I don't even measure, just throw the whole this into the blender (or if I am making just one, into the magic bullet). Since I have reduced the amount of sugar I haven't really found any other smoothy that is healthier or better tasting then this!!!

target.recipe_text:
copycat olive garden minestrone soup by todd wilbur

from http://www.topsecretrecipes.com it's finally here! what everyone's been waiting for! just in time for winter, this soup is sure to warm your soul with it's savory flavor and wonderful aroma. i've asked many an olive garden waiter for this recipe, but none gave it to me in detail. one waiter told me the secret ingredient was to add a little red wine to the stock, but i'll leave that up to you to try.

1. heat three tablespoons of olive oil over medium heat in a large soup pot
2. saute onion , celery , garlic , green beans , and zucchini in the oil for 5 minutes or until onions begin to turn translucent
3. add vegetable broth to pot , plus drained tomatoes , beans , carrot , hot water , and spices
4. bring soup to a boil , then reduce heat and allow to simmer for 20 minutes
5. add spinach leaves and pasta and cook for an additional 20 minutes or until desired consistency
6. makes about eight 1 1 / 2 cup servings
target.review: This recipe is great and is an excellent meal to make for company. You can visit while it is simmering and many compliments are paid when it is done! It however needs a few tweaks. I fully agree it needs red wine. I use whatever kind I have on hand. I add 1/4 a cup to 1/2 a cup depending on how strong the wine is. DO NOT DRAIN THE TOMATOES! I add an extra 1/4 a cup of tomato sauce or V8 juice to get more flavor in the broth. I always use fresh ingredients and so the thyme, oregano, and basil were fresh and minced and that really jazzed it up,. Finally, I felt there was not enough broth (it%u2019s easy to go overboard with the vegetables). To fix this, on the side in a separate saucepan, I mixed 3 cups of vegetable broth, 2  1/2 cups hot water, and 1/4 a cup of tomato sauce/V8 juice to a boil then added 1/4 a cup of red wine and brought it to a boil again then let it simmer alongside the soup. You can just not do this part separately and just add it to the soup but I did it this way so I could store some broth separately for leftovers. That way, the liquid that is lost in the refrigerator can be restored. When I serve, I mix this in with the soup and it doesn't taste any different.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
olive garden copycat zuppa toscana

this is a clone of the olive garden zuppa toscana. tried and true, approved by former olive garden chefs.

1. chop or slice uncooked sausage into small pieces and cook until browned and meat is ground in bottom of your soup pan over med-high heat
2. add onions , garlic , salt , pepper , and red pepper flakes to sausage and cook until onions are clear and aromatics of the seasonings blend together
3. reduce heat back to medium and place , potatoes , in the pot
4. and slowly add the chicken stock and water and stir
5. cook on medium heat until potatoes are done and stir occasionally
6. once potatoes are done , add flour or cornstarch and simmer for another 15 minutes
7. reduce heat to lowest setting and sprinkle in your kale and cooked bacon and slowly pour cream while stirring
8. check for taste and then serve
demonstrations.review: Love, love, love this recipe. I make it whenever I can without burning myself out on it. Instead of  using italian sausage links, I use ground italian sausage and brown it in a skillet. Afterwards I pat it down with paper towels so there is no grease (not a big grease fan). I also add the kale in with the sausage so it is cooked through without being too done and add twice the bacon (we do love bacon). Sooo good. I am salivating just thinking of it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef barley stew soup

this is a winter staple here, especially when my college kids come home

1. heat oil in large soup pot
2. add beef to flour mixture , add to oil , brown on all sides in batches , remove add onion& celery , saute til soft , add mushrooms , carrots , beef
3. add 8 cups of liquid , spices , bring to boil and simmer for 45 minutes
4. add barley and potatoes simmer for 45 minutes
5. add peas cook til heated through
6. thicken for stew as mentioned above
demonstrations.review: I was really disappointed in this recipe because it was so highly rated. I hate to be one of the people who disparage a possibly good recipe but it was a miss with my family. It turned out way too thick and the barley was way undercooked. It was not unusually flavorful enough to really turn the tide of negative reactions to it and the leftovers sat in a lump on the bottom of my refrigerator. I tried to be optimistic and eat it but it was gluey at that point. I hope other people had better luck than me...we just did not prefer it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon cream cheese frosting

today is labor day, and where we are in new jersey, the rain is coming down in sheets:( not the best way to bid farewell to summer; but we moved the party indoors:) my sister, sister-in-law, future sister-in-law, and mother are all gathered around the computer, posting lots of recipes, eating (of course!), and enjoying the inevitable "girl talk." all of our men are out on a "food run," and the kids are napping (yay!). but anyway, my sister came over with lemon cupcakes frosted with this sensational frosting (she had to wrap the platter in foil so her husband couldn't grab any away without her knowing!); and the girls are doing quite a job on them now! and don't worry, we've seized control and hid the cupcakes from the men:)!

1. in a large bowl , cream together all ingredients until thick , smooth , and spreadable
2. use immediately
3. store frosted goods covered in the refrigerator
4. bring to room temperature before serving
demonstrations.review: So good! I was making my dad a citrus cake for Father's Day. I used this for the frosting but added some orange zest and orange juice. It was super tasty and just the right combo of cream cheese and citrus tanginess!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter cup cookies  tarts

i first saw these at a bake sale and was so impressed. you bake a ball of dough in a mini-muffin tin, bake, and press a reese's peanut butter cup into it after you take it out of oven. you are left with a picture-perfect tart, receiving "oohs and aahs" and "how did you do it?" you could even use the refrigerated sugar/peanut butter cookie dough too.

1. cream peanut butter , butter , sugar and brown sugar until fluffy
2. add egg , vanilla , flour , baking soda and salt' mix well
3. roll into 1-inch balls and place in miniature muffin tins or in mini cupcake wrappers)
4. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f
5. when tins are removed from oven , immediately press 1 peanut butter cup into the center of the cookie
6. allow to cool completely before removing cookies from the tin
demonstrations.review: This is a definite 10 star cookie for me! I did it exactly like it said and they turned out great. I added reeses pieces on the top and they looked professional! I also use the dough for plain ol' peanut butter cookies. The cookies turned out great and stayed soft for days (not that they were around for very long).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sirloin steak casserole

this is similar enough to swiss steak to be comforting, but different enough not to be boring. i often substitute freshly minced garlic for the garlic powder. serve with mashed potatoes and a green vegetable; i prefer green beans with this.

1. preheat oven to 325f degrees
2. in a small dish , combine flour , salt , pepper and dry mustard
3. transfer to a plastic bag
4. cut steak into strips , larger than for stir fry , and place in a large bowl
5. pour just enough of the red wine onto meat to moisten
6. reserve remaining wine
7. in a large skillet over medium-high heat , heat oil
8. shake steak strips in flour mixture , then brown floured meat in hot oil
9. place browned strips in a large casserole dish
10. you may need more oil to brown all your beef
11. when done , pour any meat juice / red wine left in bowl steak was in onto browned meat
12. add remaining ingredients , including reserved red wine , to casserole and stir to combine
13. cover tightly and bake for 1-1 / 2 to 2 hours , or until steak is tender
demonstrations.review: So so so good! I served it with chunky garlic mashed potatoes and  it was perfect. Only thing I would do differently is cook the meat longer, like four hours, so it is very tender. I would definitely recommend!

target.recipe_text:
carrots and ham in gingered chicken broth pasta sauce

a flavourful pasta sauce. perfect for using up leftover ham.

1. in a large skillet or saucepan on medium heat , heat the oil with the garlic and onion
2. when the onion and garlic sizzle , add the ham and saut about 1 minute
3. add the broth , raise the heat , and bring to a simmer
4. stir in carrots and ginger
5. when broth returns to a boil , stir in parsley
6. pour over cooked pasta , preferably spaghetti , linguine , or fettuccine
target.review: Really, really awesome.  Not nearly as salty as I thought it would be; used low-sodium canned broth, of course.  Also used probably a 1/4 cup ginger (hey, I like ginger & I cut up too much anyway) & spiral pasta & it still turned out marvelous.  Thank you SO much for posting this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts
