I substituted buttermilk and almond milk for the sour cream and milk, added more vanilla, used a box of pistachio pudding mix plus a few drops of green food color, and baked it in a Bundt pan for 60 minutes. Even with all the substitutions, it still came out lovely. Thanks for such a versatile recipe.

target.recipe_text:
low carb lemon mousse

i had a guest on a low carb diet and she gave me this recipe. it's really lemony and delicious. there was a slight aspartime aftertaste, but for those trying to cut back on the carbs it's a great dessert! prep time includes chilling.

1. melt butter in a medium saucepan over low heat
2. remove from heat and whisk in yolks one at a time
3. beat in lemon juice , zest and 4 packets sugar substitute
4. chill
5. beat egg whites and extract with 1 packet sugar substitute
6. fold into the chilled egg yolk mixture
7. beat cream with vanilla extract and fold into the mixture
8. fold into the chilled egg yolk mixture
9. spoon into 8 serving cups and chill for at least 2 hours before serving
target.review:
I liked this. I wasted the first batch because I had the butter too hot and all the yolks cooked. My fault.
So I tried again and had the butter just warm. I made some for the fridge and the other I put in paper cups and froze. They taste like ice cream (put a squirt of canned whipped cream on it for more sweetness). It made a lot. Liked it frozen much more. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bean salad   for weight watching people

nan

1. rinse and drain beans , and add drained corn
2. add chopped veggies , and chopped cilantro , and just a bit of lime juice
3. toss with salsa
demonstrations.review: This was so good! I made it with the celery, and it was the best, so crisp. I ate my fill on Sunday and then on Monday and Tuesday ate it in a warmed tortilla with alittle cheese. I can't get over how good this was!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the  bombdiggity  chicken

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium-high heat
3. add chicken breasts , and saute 4 mins on each side , until browned
4. place browned chicken breasts in a 9x13 inch baking dish
5. make sure to use teriyaki basting sauce ! regular teriyaki sauce is too thin !
6. brush on teriyaki sauce , then spoon on salad dressing
7. spread drained mushrooms over chicken
8. sprinkle with cheese , green onions and bacon bits
9. bake for 25-35 mins , or until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I did this differently, always looking for a shortcut. I browned 6 breasts the laid them in a single layer in the crockpot, put a cup of Teriyaki marinade (couldn't find basting sauce at the store) and then put on the layer of ranch. Cooked about 3 hours on low and in the final 10 minutes covered the top with cheddar cheese. Hmmmmm, it was so delicious and tasted like a meal you would get at a bistro. I can't wait until next time when I will add the onions and mushrooms I just didn't have at the time.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mike s fav wine and ginger crock pot roast

this is soooo good. everyone will love it.  the crock pot makes a wonderful blend of all these flavors.  i served this over rice and the onions that cook with the roast make a great side dish.  your kitchen or in our case, our patio will (& did) smell wonderful.  in arizona, in the summertime you don't want to add any extra heat inside the house so i put the crock pot on the patio.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium high heat and brown roast on all sides
2. in the bottom of your crock pot , place the sliced onions first , then the browned roast
3. mix the remaining ingredients in a bowl and pour over roast , cover and cook on low for 6 to 8 hours or until meat is fork tender and falls apart easily
4. pour the cooking juices into a sauce pan and simmer on the stove until reduced , about 10 minutes
5. serve sauce over the top of the roast
demonstrations.review: Oh my goodness, this was good. I used 5 good sized pork chops instead of roast. Browned them and followed the same directions. The chops were tender with super flavor and this does make a superb gravy! Thank you so much for an excellent recipe. P.S. the carpet cleaning man was driven crazy with the aroma!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb  pancakes

this sounds a little strange, but it makes the best low carb pancakes i've ever eaten! if you're doing atkins or south beach these will become a regular on your breakfast menu....

1. crush pork rinds and set aside
2. beat eggs and then fold in cream , splenda , cinnamon , and vanilla flavoring
3. add crushed pork rinds and let the mixture sit for 5 minutes
4. meanwhile heat skillet with butter or oil and then fry mixture pancake style
5. serve with low carb pancake syrup
6. only 6 net carbs for the entire batch !
demonstrations.review: My 16 year old on the Atkins diet loves these! I had made pancakes the day before with the Atkins baking mix and we couldn't stomach them. Horrible. SO I told her to try these and she said very good. Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
low carb four layer delight

this is a luscious dessert i invented when i was trying to come up with a low carb dessert for my weight loss support group.

1. layer the toasted pecans in the bottom of a glass jelly roll pan , reserving enough to make 1 t of chopped nuts for topping
2. whip all ingredients for 2nd layer with a mixer until fluffy
3. drop in mounds on top of pecans and carefully spread to cover pecans
4. sprinkle graham cracker crumbs over 2nd layer
5. don't use more than 1 t
6. follow same directions as the 2nd layer for the 4th layer , using , of course , the chocolate fudge pudding instead of the white chocolate
7. drop in mounds over the graham cracker crumb layer
8. spread very carefully , taking care not to mix the layers
9. garnish with whipped cream , chopped toasted pecans and a sprinkling of graham cracker crumbs
10. refrigerate
demonstrations.review:
Fabulous! A low carb version of the Southern delicacy, Chocolate Delight. I used a little crushed walnuts (toasting is a must), vanilla
sugar free fat free instead of white choc (used instant). In place of the graham cracker I put 2 T. unsweetened coconut. Wow this is great. Thank you !

target.recipe_text:
mom s orange curry chicken

i can remember deciding this was my favorite chicken when we lived in florida -- when i was three or four! it's still my favorite. the curry gives the chicken a wonderful color and adds an exotic flavor to the sweet orange-honey-mustard sauce. i always serve with white rice. 6 ww pts per serving; rice is 3 pts for 3/4 cup.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees f
2. rinse and remove skin from chicken pieces and dry thoroughly
3. sprinkle chicken with curry powder to cover and a little salt on both sides and rub into meat
4. arrange chicken in baking dish sprayed with cooking spray , "skin"-side down
5. combine orange juice , honey and mustard in saucepan
6. simmer for 5 minutes
7. pour over chicken and bake for 30 minutes
8. turn chicken and continue baking another 20-30 minutes or until richly browned
9. remove chicken to heated serving dish
10. add orange cartwheels to sauce and heat on stove 1 minute , scraping bottom of pan
11. pour sauce over chicken and serve
target.review: Excellent chicken recipe!  Sweet and tangy, tastes like a zippy honey mustard with fresh oranges.  We loved this.  I served it with some couscous. I had no idea how good this would smell while reducing and cooking - just like my favorite L'Occitane honey perfume! Thank you quantumgirl, I will make this again soon!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf  hey virginia  mine is better

ha-ha, i do love the "meatloaf: yes virginia, there is a great meatloaf" recipe, however i believe mine is just a hint better.  you be the judge.  i made this for my husband’s birthday- party of 15, and everyone raved over it- so, hey everyone- give it a shot, i would love some feedback.  i use dried onion as opposed to fresh because i didn't like the bite of fresh onion, it's much more subtle yet still flavorful to use dried... you be the judge though- use 1 small fresh yellow onion chopped if you like. by the way- some of you may be wondering- this is not a 'sweet meat'... it may be confusing with all the brown sugar and sweetened condensed milk- but i assure you- this is not sweet- if you want to- just omit the savory sauce and make it on the side to use as a dipping sauce the first time around... i'm highly confident in this recipe.

1. preheat oven to 325
2. mix all ingredients thoroughly in mixing bowl and pat into a 9" round pie plate and pat flat
3. mix the "savory sauce" in a separate bowl and spoon over the meatloaf
4. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes
5. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yes, Virginia, vegetarians can make this recipe too!! I made this vegetarian style by substituting mock ground beef crumbles and it worked beautifully. What an amazing meatloaf. I was a bit reluctant at first about adding sweetened condensed milk but it made for a great finished product. I think that the savory sauce is the key to balancing out the sweet flavour. I tried a little without the savory sauce and it was slightly sweet, but still very good. And the savory sauce has a nice taste all on its own: I used the leftovers as a dip with seasoned french fries. Brilliant.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
almond cream cheese pound cake

this cake comes from one of my favorite cookbooks, *the cake mix doctor*.  it is a keeper of a cake recipe

1. bring cream cheese to room temperature
2. place all ingredients in large mixing bowl
3. mix with electric mixer on low for one minute until all combined
4. mix at medium for two minutes
5. batter should look uniform and thick
6. bake in a greased and floured 10 inch tube pan at 350f for about 45 minutes or until cake springs back when touched
7. serve alone or with berries and sweetened whipped cream
8. the cake is rich on its own
demonstrations.review:
Have to agree with all of the previous reviewers, this is great.

I am always incredibly skeptical of these "cake mix doctor" recipes, most of them taste awful, like artificially flavored cake mix, but this one was truly the exception.  You cannot tell that this is made with a mix.  It is beautifully light and fluffy- but not too "eggy".  Will make again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
colette s european salad

this salad is like no other. i 

1. in a non-stick frying pan , toast the walnuts on low heat , stirring occasionally set aside
2. in a large bowl , rinse and drain salad mix and refrigerate
3. just before serving , drain salad mix again to make sure it is completely dry
4. toss all ingredients together and serve
demonstrations.review: Wow! This is an amazing salad, wouldn't change a thing!  I made this at a family dinner and EVERYONE had seconds, and I'm sure that they would have gone for more...if there was any left!  P.S. My mom bought Marzetti's Poppyseed Dressing by mistake and it was fine, so if you can't find the Brianna's (which I would have preferred because I'm a big fan) it should all work out well.  Thanks for sharing your wonderful salad recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
warm and creamy swiss cheese dip with caraway

this is wonderful with chunks of rye bread for dipping! keep warm in a small crock pot for dips, or a fondue pot. heaven! you'll want to double this!

1. in small bowl , toss cheese and flour
2. in small saucepan , heat buttermilk and cider
3. add cheese and caraway seeds
4. stir til melted
5. keep warm while serving
6. serve with chunks of rye bread for dipping
demonstrations.review: This was a very good recipe for Swiss cheese fondue.  I thoroughly enjoyed this.  I also was able to make this without any difficulty unlike the previous reviewer (that was a rather nasty review, don't you think?) - my fondue was smooth and creamy.  Here is how I achieved this: I whisked the cider and milk together over medium heat, then whisked in the flour until the mixture thickened.  Then, I gradually mixed in the swiss cheese, stirring until it was melted and smooth.  I used a whisk to do this and I made sure to stir it constantly over medium heat.  It is important that you do not allow the mixture to boil, otherwise the milk will curdle.  By the way, I'm not sure what Wildflour means by "apple cider", I wasn't sure if she intended me to use the alcoholic or non-alcoholic version in this recipe.  I used the alcoholic version and it was great, it did not dominate the taste at all.  I really liked this fondue and will make again! Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
new england soup factory s spicy chickpea and butternut soup

when we lived in boston, we loved to get soup from the new england soup factory, known for their hearty and unusual combinations. this is one of their recipes. although it's a 'cream' soup, since the base is coconut milk it remains vegan. the coconut is perhaps not what you're used to seeing with chickpeas and butternut but it really adds a sweet richness and fullness.

1. heat olive oil and garlic in a large heavy stockpot
2. saut 1-2 minutes
3. add onions , carrots and celery
4. saut 10-15 minutes
5. add squash , canned tomatoes , stock , tomato juice , soy sauce , lime juice , chickpeas , ginger and coriander
6. bring to a boil
7. cook until all the vegetables are tender , approx 30 minutes
8. add coconut milk , flaked coconut , coconut extract and cilantro , warm through
demonstrations.review: This was tasty. I only used 1/2 the amount of broth called for - 4 quarts (16 cups!!!!) is A LOT of broth! Mine was chunky and substantial, and I definitely preferred it that way. At the end of cooking, I used a potato masher to lightly mash the soup together, which resulted in a thick and slightly chunky soup - not completely smooth, yet not brothy either.  Very good!  The coconut is a nice addition, but I think that I will skip the flaked stuff next time because it (in my opinion) adds a grainy consistency.

target.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
target.review: WOW this is SO good.  We made this two nights in a row!  My BF ate three pieces of fish!  The only thing is that I reduced the butter and the mayo a bit the second time around and I left out the onions because I didn't have any.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amy sedaris s vanilla cupcakes

amy sedaris, so i hear, sells her cupcakes in new york city bakeries. i found this recipe for amy's cupcakes on the web, but i don't remember where. 
this was my first time making cupcakes from scratch and i have to say, i was quite proud of the results. i gave them away to friends and family, and everyone loved them.

march 2, 2011 hi, guys! it was several years ago that i found and posted this recipe. since then, amy sedaris has published a cookbook which contains her recipe for vanilla cupcakes. it's not the same as this one. :(  like i said before, i don't remember where i found this recipe, but i remember that the person who posted it was very certain about it being amy sedaris's recipe.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl , cream together butter and sugar
3. add in the eggs , two teaspoons vanilla , salt and baking powder
4. add flour and milk in batches , starting and ending with flour
5. stir until batter is smooth and satiny
6. fill paper-lined muffin tins with batter
7. bake at 375 for 18- 20 minutes
8. for frosting , whip together the box of confectioners' sugar , half-and-half , and one teaspoon vanilla until smooth and fluffy
9. allow cupcakes to cool about 45 minutes and frost
10. hint i added about one extra teaspoon of vanilla to the batter
11. this recipe didn't specify , but i used all-purpose flour
12. to the frosting , i added a bit more half-and-half to reach a thinner consistency
demonstrations.review: I am convinced Marna D. had some ingredient issues.  I have never before made cupcakes, I am an inexperienced baker so I followed the directions ALMOST perfect.  I didnt have milk so I ended up using fat free evaporated nilk cup for cup and it worked just fine.  These are AMAZING!  They came out perfect (well I burned the first ones - oops!).  No problems getting them out of the pan or out of the cup.  This will be my go-to cupcake recipe.  Even the ones I overcooked were good, I kept that batch for us at home and it did not stop us from eating them!  I used store bought frosting due to lack of time and ingredients.  Delicious!  Thank you!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
granny s slow cooker vegetarian chili

this is a rich, satisfying meal that freezes well. great on a cold winter day. serve it with tortillas, cornbread, french breadand/or rice! enjoy!

1. in a saucepan , saute the onion , bell pepper , zucchini , and celery for about 5 minutes
2. in a slow cooker , combine black bean soup , kidney beans , garbanzo beans , baked beans , tomatoes , corn , onion , bell pepper , zucchini , jalapeno , chilies , and celery
3. season with garlic , chili powder , cumin , parsley , oregano , basil
4. cook for about 6 hours on low
5. serve with tortillas , cornbread , rice , or french bread
6. enjoy !
7. this freezes well !
8. leftovers are good on top of nachos !
demonstrations.review:
This is a really great recipe!  My fine tuning;  1)2 Jalapenos and 3 banana peppers, sliced.  2)replaced baked beans with seasoned chili beans.  3)added 2 additional tbsp of chili powder.  4) did not add the cillantro.  5)  used a head of garlic and instead of mincing left it in huge chunks/whole cloves.  6) omitted celery, replaced with broccoli.  7)added boca crumbles!
Thank you so much, this really turned out fantastic...we gobbled this up and will be making it often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fruit salsa and cinnamon chips

this is really easy to make and is great as an appetizer or snack!

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly mix kiwis , golden delicious apples , raspberries , strawberries , white sugar , brown sugar and fruit preserves
2. cover and chill in the refrigerator at least 15 minutes
3. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
4. coat one side of each flour tortilla with butter flavored cooking spray
5. cut into wedges and arrange in a single layer on a large baking sheet
6. sprinkle wedges with desired amount of cinnamon sugar
7. spray again with cooking spray
8. bake in the preheated oven 8 to 10 minutes
9. repeat with any remaining tortilla wedges
10. allow to cool approximately 15 minutes
11. serve with chilled fruit and spice mixture
demonstrations.review: YUM wow this is a great recipe, i added a small can of mandarin oranges and used sugar free strawberry preserves.  This was delicious, everyone was asking for the recipe!  I cheated and bought pre-made sugar/cinnamon baked pita chips from the organic section due to lack of time and it was still a hit!  Thank you so much!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
silky vanilla butter frosting

this is not your usual butter-cream made with powdered sugar. butter is beaten into a flour-thickened base to make an exquisitely light and creamy frosting. not overly sweet like those made with powdered sugar, but sweet enough to be the perfect compliment for a cake. make sure the base is completely cooled before beating in the butter. i added in 15 minutes cooling time, but it will vary depending on conditions.

1. in 2-quart saucepan , thoroughly combine sugar and flour
2. with wire whisk , gradually stir in milk until smooth
3. cook over medium-high heat , stirring frequently , until mixture has thickened and boils
4. reduce heat to low
5. cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat and cool completely
7. in medium bowl , with mixer at medium speed , beat butter until light and fluffy
8. gradually beat in milk mixture
9. beat in vanilla
demonstrations.review: I really liked this!  I make a sweet vanilla cupcake and this less sweet frosting with some cinnamon added was the perfect compliment!  I love the fact that it's not incredibly sweet.  Everyone is begging me to make this again.  i used my mixer and really made sure i beat the butter for a long time and also cooked the flour/millk mixture for the right amount of time.  There was no flour aftertaste and for me the frosting was a great consistency.  All you have to do is beat a little longer if you want it fluffier!  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft batch chocolate chip cookies

a soft & chewy cookie. one of my favorites

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs together until creamy
3. add the remaining ingredients and blend well
4. bake until lightly browned
5. store in an air tight container
demonstrations.review: This was my first crack at making cookies from scratch.  Everyone said they were really good but I felt that they were missing something.  i did use an organic granulated sugar and I soon realized that for some reason it wasn't as sweet as the regular granulated sugar.  That being said, I will be making these again with the correct ingredients!  They definitely stayed chewy and moist...I have some leftover dough in the fridge and i can't keep my DH out of it!  Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
softest ever bread machine bread

my sister gave me this recipe soon after i brought home my bread machine. it's a staple in our house. soft and fluffy and great for sandwiches or just to eat fresh out of the oven!
update 3/25/2005 - i made this using the dough cycle of my bread maker today but baked it in the oven and it turned out perfectly! i baked it at 350°f for 25-30 minutes.

1. place the water , sugar and yeast in the pan of the bread machine
2. let the yeast dissolve and foam for 10 minutes
3. add the oil , flour and salt to the yeast
4. select basic or white bread setting , and press start
5. you can also use the dough cycle of your bread maker and then place in a greased loaf pan
6. punch down and let rise again and then bake at 350 for 25-30 minutes or until done
target.review: Made this bread tonight after realizing I didn't have any to make my daughter's lunch. Used the dough cycle of bread machine and baked in the oven. This is awesome! I don't think I will ever buy bread again. So soft it melts in your mouth.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wacky cake

this is mom's favorite chocolate cake. easy to make and has a little different twist. also has no eggs or dairy products. pick your favorite frosting for the top--mom likes 7-minute the best.

1. sift together and make 3 holes in dry ingredients
2. in first hole , pour vegetable oil
3. in second hole , pour vinegar
4. in third hole , pour vanilla
5. pour cold water over all
6. mix well with fork or whisk , but do not beat
7. bake in greased 8 x 8 pan for about 35 minutes at 350 deg f
demonstrations.review: My girls and I just made this for breakfast! Tried to think of it as muffins..he he. My daughter has now declared today wacky day/backwards day and insists that we have a breakfast meal for dinner. Thanks for a fun and yummy recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken pan pie

i got this recipe several years ago from a church cookbook and i have made it so many times. my family loves it. it can be made up and refrigerated over night, then just pop it in the oven the next day. serve with a salad and your meal is complete.

1. boil chicken until tender
2. debone and cut into small pieces
3. reserve 2 cups of broth
4. put chicken in a 9x13 pan
5. in saucepan , bring 2 cups broth and 10 1 / 2 can cream of chicken soup to a boil
6. drain 16 ounce can of veg-all vegatables and pour over chicken
7. pour broth mixture over vegetables
8. in a bowl combine flour , salt , pepper , buttermilk and margarine
9. mix thoroughly with spoon to form batter
10. spread batter on top
11. bake at 425 for 30 minutes
12. for oamc: bake as directed above , then wrap , seal and label
demonstrations.review: Made this last night using a store bought Rotissorie chicken and canned broth. Simple and tastey! This would make a great meal for a sick friend or a someone with a new baby (like myself!). Not spicey yet very tastey and filling. Reminds me of chicken and dumplings.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
authentic chinese pork chow mein

no need to order in chow mein when you can make it yourself, this is just as good if not even better than any chinese restaurant or take-out -- if you prefer more flavor then add in more soy sauce --- if desired after the pork is finished browning you may add in fresh minced garlic and stir for 2 minutes, this is only optional --- you will love this!

1. cut meat into thin strips
2. combine 2 tbsp cornstarch with sugar , blend in 1 tbsp soy sauce and 2 tbsp oil
3. mix to blend
4. pour over pork strips
5. toss well to coat , marinade in mixture for 20 minutes
6. in a wok or large saute pan heat 2 tablespoons shortening
7. brown the meat lightly on all sides in hot shortening
8. add remaining 4 tbsp soy sauce and 1-1 / 2 cups water
9. simmer , covered on low heat for 45 minutes
10. add in the celery and onions
11. simmer for 15 minutes more
12. in a small bowl , blend in remaining cornstarch with 1 / 4 cup water
13. stir into meat mixture
14. add molasses , water chestnuts , bean sprouts and mushrooms
15. heat thoroughly
16. season with salt and pepper
17. garnish with chopped green onions and toasted almonds
demonstrations.review: This was great. I've been craving chinese food but haven't been able to eat it since I'm having to avoid salt at the moment. Used low sodium soy sauce and this was definitely a treat.  Used fresh mushrooms. It did take a little longer to prepare than I had hoped but it may have been the juggeling of 3 small children while cooking that did us in. Served over rice. Highly recommend this!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
casserole with black eyed peas

this is a delicious casserole and it's so easy to make. i've put it in the crockpot for 4 hours on low instead of baking it, and that works great, too, especially if you're taking it to a pot-luck.  southwestern u.s. is where you'll find this great recipe.

1. brown meat
2. combine all ingredients in 13x9x2 casserole
3. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes
4. serve
demonstrations.review: My husband and I loved this which is why I'm rating it a 5. Would even be good on tortillas with salsa. The kids didn't care for it but they just aren't used to eating casseroles. The only change I made was adding some butter after it baked. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq pork chops

can't remember where i got this recipe from but it is excellent !! it is sure to become a favorite of yours.

1. sauce: in pan combine water , vinegar , sugar , mustard , salt , pepper , and red pepper and onion
2. you can add a small amount of lemon juice if desired
3. bring to a boil , then reduce heat and simmer uncovered 20 minutes
4. stir in ketchup , worcestershire sauce , and liquid smoke and return to a boil
5. remove from heat
6. brown the chops on both sides and place in a casserole dish
7. pour the sauce over the chops
8. bake 350 25-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: We absolutely loved these. I finished cooking pork chops in skillet instead of baking. I also didn't add the red peppers or onions since kids won't eat them. Made a really nice sweet BBQ sauce. I'm sure it would be great with the onions and red peppers too. I would recommend doubling the sauce. Served with rice and fresh green beans. Thanks for an easy, great tasting recipe!

target.recipe_text:
hearty cabbage soup

a thick and hearty cabbage/potato soup which is just perfect for those cold winter nights.

1. melt butter in saucepan over medium heat
2. add onion , celery , cabbage , salt , and pepper
3. partly cover and cook for 10 minutes over a low heat
4. add potatoes , chicken stock , and dill
5. bring to a boil while stirring periodically
6. boil , partly covered , for 20 minutes
7. mix the flour with the sour cream in a bowl
8. add 1 / 2 cup of the hot soup stock to bowl , mix well , and pour into soup
9. mix well and serve
target.review:
I followed the recipe almost exactly; I just used dried dill instead of fresh. 

This soup is a perfect winter soup. I needed something use up the cabbage I had bought at the farmer's market, and this fit the bill. Preparation was easy, and the cooking time was just enough for me to clean the dishes and straighten up the kitchen.

I served it with dark pumpernickle bread with butter. I almost thought I'd like the soup to be richer when served as a main dish, but I quickly forgot that idea as I enjoyed the hearty warmth.

I would say the recipe makes somewhat more than four main dish servings, but the soup heats up wonderfully the next day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
la madeleine s tomato basil soup

nan

1. combine tomatoes , juice / and or stock in saucepan
2. simmer 30 minutes
3. puree , along with the basil leaves , in small batches , in blender , food processor
4. return to saucepan and add cream and butter , while stirring , over low heat
5. garnish with basil leaves and serve with your favorite bread
6. excerpted from an article by beverly bundy of the fort worth star-telegram around may 20
7. 1994
8. she wrote , "once a year , in january i run a column of our most requested recipes -- this year , that column included the recipe for la madeleine's popular tomato basil soup
9. i continue to get at least 10 calls a week asking for the recipe
10. so here it is , once again -- "
demonstrations.review:
I really wanted to make some tomato soup from scratch because of the high amount of sugar that is in Campbell's canned stuff, but I did not like this recipe all that much. I used mostly tomato juice, but if I did make it again, I think I might use more chicken stock.

Eating it right after I made it, I did not like it very much. It was almost too rich, perhaps.  I served it a couple of days later in bread bowls, and I enjoyed it much better then.

My immersion mixer was perfect to puree the soup right in the pan, and it was not difficult to prepare.

I think I will look for another tomato soup recipe before I try this one again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moroccan chickpea and vegetable stew with couscous

this is delicious stew. very flavorful from the spices, but not too spicy, just right. there is no meat in it, and you most likely won't miss it, as the chickpeas are very "meaty" themselves. but i don't see why you couldn't add some meat if you really wanted to. it also goes from prep to table in about 30 minutes, great for weeknight dinners. from cooking light.

1. heat the oil in a large skillet on medium high heat
2. add the zucchini , onion , carrot and garlic
3. saute 5 minutes
4. stir in the broth , and the next 9 ingredients , and bring to a boil
5. cover , reduce the heat , and simmer for 8 minutes or until tender
6. stir occasionally
7. while the stew simmers , bring the 1 1 / 2 cups water to a boil , stir in couscous , and remove from heat
8. cover and let stand for 5 minutes
9. serve stew over couscous
demonstrations.review: I really wanted to like this, but it ended up being un-exciting.  I left out the raisins due to personal preference, and I used an entire can of chicken broth, and I upped the spices slightly to compensate, but it maybe wasn't enough.  The end product had a lovely texture and fragrance, but served over couscous, it just didn't have the spicy flavor I'd expected.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
szechuan green beans with ground pork

this is a bit spicy so you may want to decrease the pepper flakes and add more at the end for taste. i made this for a pot-luck chinese dinner that is why the serving size is for 8. can be cut in half. delicious over chinese white rice.

1. steam beans 5 minutes
2. combine the first 4 ingredients in a medium bowl
3. heat oil in a large non-stick skillet over med high heat
4. saute pork mixture until pork loses it's pink color - stirring to a crumble
5. add steamed green beans and garlic - saute for 3-5 minutes more
6. combine hoisin sauce , sugar , pepper flakes and soy sauce in a small bowl - stirring with a whisk to incorporate ingredients
7. pour mixture into pan with pork and green beans
8. cook another 3-5 minutes or until heated through , stirring frequently
9. serve over hot rice - enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I used a entire bag of frozen whole green beans, and it came out great.  That amount of red pepper flakes leaves your lips just slightly tingling, so if you're more of a mild-type person, I'd use half the amount of flakes and then allow those eating to spice to taste if desired. Will be making this again, maybe next time with broccoli.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
balsamic tomato couscous

we had a potluck to attend where we had been asked to bring a side dish.  i was craving couscous though i knew few (if any) of my friends would be willing to try it.  never mind, i moved forward!  this is a slight adaptation of one i found in one of my favorite cookbooks "500 almost fat free pasta recipes."  and truth be told, i brought very little home and got asked for the recipe!

1. in a medium pan , bring the broth to a boil
2. when it is boiling add the basil and garlic and stir
3. then add the couscous , cover the pan , and remove it from the heat
4. let sit 5-10 minutes
5. chop the tomatoes
6. in a small bowl mix the balsamic vinegar , the oil , and the pepper
7. add the tomatoes
8. when the couscous is ready add the tomato mixture and mix well
9. serve hot or cold
demonstrations.review: I liked it as a cold salad, but it wasn't really a very intresting dish. The flavors, however, were nicely balanced; though I watered down a can of chicken broth to make the two cups, and so it maybe needed some bullion added for an 'oomph' of flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the secret to perfect gyoza n pot stickers

i learned this on a japanese show where they investigated why regular housewives' gyoza was so yucko compared to professional masters' gyozas. let me share the secret with you....:d

1. first combine the meat and the seasonings
2. mix it with your hands
3. this is important
4. then add in the rest of the vegetables
5. mix it very very well with your hands till it changes texture and cannot fall apart
6. place a teaspoonful of filling in a wrapper and put water along the edge of the wrapper
7. make a semicircle , gathering the front side of the wrapper and sealing the top
8. put the gyozas into a pan and fill the pan with boiling water
9. the water must come up to half the height of the gyozas and no higher or lower
10. cover and let boil / steam for 3 minutes exactly
11. open the lid and drain off excess water
12. add vegetable oil and let it fry for only 1 and a half minutes
13. no longer , no shorter
14. remove and serve :d
demonstrations.review:
Hmm, lovely, wonderfully tasty recipe, but I do know why they are called 'potstickers' now!!!!  As soon as I drained the water and put the dumplings back on the heat, they glued themselves to the bottom of my regular skillet.  I don't own nonstick cookware, so that isn't an option.  Perhaps if I dump the gyoza into a colander, add oil to the pan to coat, and then drop in the dumplings again?

In any case, I'll have a chance to try something again. I doubled the recipe, made and cooked about 20, and then I made the rest and frozen them. So... now I have to figure out how to get from frozen to cooked.

Oh, and simple sauce to accompany the gyoza: 2 parts soy sauce to one part rice vingear with sesame oil or hot chili oil to taste.

target.recipe_text:
taco bell quesadillas

i used to love these when i was younger, i could eat two in one sitting! i haven't had fast food in a year or two, but these taste like i remember taco bell's quesadillas tasting. i hope you enjoy it as much as i do.

1. combine sauce ingredients and stir until smooth
2. grill chicken in vegetable oil and cut into thin slices
3. preheat skillet over medium heat
4. one at a time , lay tortilla into hot skillet and sprinkle with 1 / 4 cup of each shredded cheese and 1 / 2 cheese slice on one side of the tortilla
5. arrange about 1 / 4 cup chicken slices over tortilla on the same half covered with cheese
6. on the empty side , spread about one tablespoon of sauce
7. fold over , and press gently with spatula
8. cook until cheese is melted and slice each into 4 pieces
target.review:
Loved it, the sauce was amazing! I used low fat mayo, wheat tortillas, 2% cheddar and American cheeses, and a cooked store-bought rotisserie chicken that I sort of shredded. 
It was easy to put together and even my picky children ate them! Thank you, we'll be making these often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned linguine with white clam sauce

this recipe is easy and takes less than 20 minutes. it's one of my weekend favorites and has been a family tradition for years.

1. in a 5 qt pot , heat water to a boil and cook pasta until al dente
2. while the pasta is cooking , melt butter and olive oil in pan
3. sautee onion and garlic , and add crushed red pepper flakes
4. add lemon juice , oregano , basil , and old bay seasoning , stir for one minute add clams with juice
5. simmer for 5 minutes
6. drain pasta and place in large bowl
7. cover pasta with clam sauce , stir well and top with parsley and parmesan cheese
8. serve with warm crusty bread and chilled white wine
demonstrations.review: Wow! I grew up around the Chesapeake Bay and never even thought of adding Old Bay seasoning, and it really does make a delicious difference in this recipe. The measurements were in perfect proportion and the taste was just incredible. We sopped up  the leftover sauce in garlic bread and it was heaven! Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ramen noodle egg foo yung

i can't believe i like this dish as much as i do. i was surprised. this is a variation of a rather bland scrambled egg mix that i found on the net but turning it onto an egg foo yung is really special.  add your own favorite things but this is a good start. if you add water chestnuts, ham, shrimp, pork, whatever- then you will have to adjust the cooking time. this is a basic recipe-  make it your own. but an easy recipe to amend- as soon as the egg is set- then it is done! i really love this and it is so good for a family on a budget or a bachelor short on time. if you want a terrific egg foo yung sauce then try this one recipe#45270 .

1. cook ramen noodles according to package instructions for 3 minutes blah blah and drain well in a colander
2. if you don't know how to cook ramen noodles you are too stupid to cook
3. call dominos and have them deliver you a pizza
4. whisk eggs , onions , the seasoning packet , sesame oil , soy sauce , and baking powder with a fork in a small bowl and toss in the cooked ramen noodles
5. heat butter on med high heat in an 8 inch nonstick skillet
6. throw the ramen noodle / egg mixture in the skillet and cook it
7. i reiterate if you don't know to to cook ramen noodles call dominos because you are obviously , stupid
8. :(
9. flip the patty over and cook the other side until the egg is set , about two more minutes
10. flip over again and cook about 1 minute more
11. serve with soy sauce if you wish or an egg foo yung sauce
demonstrations.review: What a delicious disaster! I doubled the recipe and added shrimp but cooked it all at once.  Next time, I will do it in smaller batches. Enjoyed by all, especially our noodle-loving five year old. Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
joshua s favorite tilapia with jasmine rice

this is my very own creation, i whipped this up one day quite by accident. i call this joshua's favorite tilapia, because my husband (like me) could eat this 7 nights a week if we could. this is the easiest way to cook tilapia, and if you are watching those calories then you need not worry this is extremely low fat, oh and did i mention to die for !!! this recipe is simple with few ingredients, but has the potential to add what ever you want. i like it as is !

1. pour your dressing straight from the bottle into the pan , i usually make sure the bottom is covered but not too much , i gave approximate measures here
2. place the fillets on top of the dressing in the pan
3. sprinkle with all 4 seasonings
4. i usually just sprinkle a generous amount on each filet
5. don't leave out the cumin it is a wonderful addition to the fish
6. saute the fillets on med-low heat approximate 4-5 minutes each side until fish flakes easy with a fork
7. while the fish is slowly cooking , cook the rice , using 2 1 / 2 cups water and 1 cup rice , with butter , bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes on low
8. serve the fillet on top of the jasmine rice
9. i will usually add more s&p and cumin according to my taste
demonstrations.review: I usually pan fry my tilapia with a few of the same spices as in your recipe, but cooking it in the dressing gave it so much more flavor. I loved the addition of the cumin, and since it was a bit too spicy for our tastes, I will cut back on the amount of Old Bay (but not by too much!). Served with brown rice and roasted asparagus #50847. Enjoyed by all, thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
awesome shredded beef  burritos or tacos  crock pot

this recipe is so easy and the shredded beef makes fantastic filling for burritos or tacos. i buy can of enchilada sauce to smother the burritos with and then top with shredded lettuce, tomatoes, onions, sour cream, shredded cheese and of course my own homemade salsa recipe #239651. my father declares them "better than restaurant burritos".

1. place roast in crock pot
2. sprinkle with taco seasoning , salt and pepper
3. top with diced tomatoes
4. cook on low 8-10 hours
5. remove beef from crock pot and shred with two forks
6. return beef to crock pot for 30 minutes or so
7. serve rolled in flour tortillas with your favorite toppings or in taco shells with your favorite toppings
demonstrations.review: True to its name, this made the most awesome tacos!  I used a 2 pound boneless beef chuck (which worked well because all I had was a 10 oz. jar of Rotel), placed that on top of sliced onions, and rubbed the spices onto both sides of the beef.  It was perfectly cooked and seasoned and not too spicy. No more ground beef tacos for this family.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fish tacos and cilantro coleslaw  20 minutes max

this is one of my best-kept secrets recipe for serving a healthy, easy and really flavorful dinner in about 20 minutes.

1. bake fish fillets according to package directions
2. wrap the tortillas in aluminum foil and place them in the oven to heat
3. or heat them at the last minute in a microwave in plastic wrap
4. shred or chop the cabbage
5. in a medium bowl , combine the cabbage with all the remaining ingredients
6. cut each hot fish fillet into 6-8 pieces , then pile into a hot tortilla with lots of slaw
demonstrations.review:
I've never had fish tacos before and admit that I'm not a big fan of cilantro, but these are so amazing (and super easy) that I've made them twice this week! 
I prepared the slaw in the morning, added a bit of lime zest, used taco-sized tortillas and the "crunchy" battered filets. The second time I used regular battered filets, and the crunchy ones are definitely better.  
Many thanks for a great keeper!

target.recipe_text:
mexican flaming cheese

absolutely scrumptious! definitely not low fat and it looks like ****, but it tastes great. i sometimes make mine in the crockpot when asked to bring it to a party and it works just as well. enjoy!

1. brown the ground beef and drain
2. add remaining ingredients and cook until cheese is melted
3. pour into a casserole dish and bake at 400 degrees for 15 minutes
4. serve with flour tortillas
target.review: I couldnt believe when I stumbled on this recipe because I have only had this a one mexican restaurant and usually no one has ever heard of it.  It was extremely close to our favorite authentic mexican restaurant.  I used chihuahua and monteray jack cheeses which were excellent but NOT cheap.  We have always had this as an appetizer and this made a healthy 9x13 pan which was way to much, so next time I will make like a quarter recipe. Overall very very good so glad I finally found a recipe for one of my favorites!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops in gravy

nan

1. in a bowl , beat egg and water
2. dip pork chops in egg mixture
3. coat with bread crumbs
4. in a large skillet , brown chops in oil
5. transfer to greased 9x13 baking dish
6. mix the soups together and pour over then sprinkle with cheese
7. cover and bake at 325 for 1 1 / 2 hours or until tender
demonstrations.review: This was awesome! I was shocked at what a delicious impressive gravey this made. I served with mashed potatoes and mixed veggies. What a hit!  It is definately the ultimate in comfort food and my new prok chop recipe!!!EXCELLENT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Well after reading all the reviews I had to try this and see what all the hype was about and yup! It was awesome!!!! I used vension roasts (3 small ones, about 3.75lbs) I used a full cup of water and half of the ranch like recommended. I threw some chunks of onion on top, let it cook on low for 9 hours and it was sensational. I thinken the juice with cornstarch for an outstanding gravy. I served with homemade coleslaw, cresent rolls, carrots and potatoes. What a hit. It was the perfect meal. The most incredible part is it doesnt get any easier than this. My number one roast recipe. Thanks yooper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best green bean casserole  i promise

this is a family recipe, ususally a big hit at thanksgiving dinners. i have not found one person who did not like it. the ritz mix on top add the perfect seasoning and crunch to the recipe

1. in a 9x11 casserole dish , drain and put both cans beans on bottom , then drained corn on top of beans in separate bowl , mix sour cream and cream of celery soup together , spread mixture over top of corn , then add the cheese on the top
2. melt butter in small bowl and add crushed ritz , stir until butter is all soaked up
3. sprinkle ritz topping over casserole then bake uncovered for 40 minutes at 350 degrees
demonstrations.review: This was very good except the directions were unclear on what kind of cheese, bake uncovered or covered and what size casserole to use. I made two casseroles one with parmesan and mozarella cheese and one with just parmesan.  They were both good but my family still prefers the traditional green beans casserole but a nice change.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pepper steak with rice

i first had this for dinner at the house of a good friend and it was delicious! that was at least 10 or more years ago and i still make it for my family and company, too.

1. method: while rice is cooking , pound meat to 1 / 4" thickness
2. sprinkle meat with paprika and allow to stand while preparing other ingredients
3. using a large skillet , brown meat in butter
4. add garlic and broth and simmer covered for 30 minutes
5. stir in onions and green peppers
6. cover and cook 5 minutes more
7. blend cornstarch , water and soy sauce
8. stir into meat mixture
9. cook , stirring until clear and thickened- about 2 minutes
10. add tomatoes and stir gently
11. serve over fluffy rice
demonstrations.review: This is awesome!  The sauce is absolutly perfect. I omitted the tomatoes and peppers and used a 16 0z. bag of frozen stir fry veggies added the last 20 minutes of cook time.  Very easy and my significant other said its a keeper and the only response I ever get out of him is "its fine."  Will be a permanent recipe in our house! Thanks for the great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato kielbasa skillet

a very hearty, tasty supper. this is very easy to make and a real pleaser.

1. in dutch oven , brown potatoes , kielbasa , onion and peppers in oil
2. add seasonings and water
3. bring to a boil
4. cover tightly and cook for 20 minutes on low , stirring occasionally
5. uncover and put cheese on top
6. simmer until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I made this but maybe I did something wrong because I couldnt understand the water after you browned everything in a pan, it just drowned everything and was very watery, I followed the directions exactly.  After I drained it it was good but I just didnt understand what the water was for.  It was still good though. Thanks!

target.recipe_text:
banana banana bread

why compromise the banana flavor? my banana bread is moist and delicious with loads of banana flavor! ultimate comfort food, and it's wonderful toasted!! (make sure to use bananas with a lot of black on them for the best flavor! the blacker the bananas, the stronger the banana flavor of the bread.)

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly grease 9 x 5 loaf pan
3. in large bowl , combine flour , soda and salt
4. in separate bowl , cream together butter and brown sugar
5. stir in eggs and mashed bananas until well blended
6. stir banana mixture into flour mixture
7. stir just to moisten
8. pour batter into prepared loaf pan
9. bake in preheated oven for 60-65 minutes until a toothpick inserted into center of loaf comes out clean
10. let bread cool in pan for 10 minutes , then turn out onto a wire rack
target.review: If I were rating this recipe on taste alone it would get 5 stars for sure but it just isn't a bread recipe.  The ratios don't make a bread...just too much moisture.  I think burning the outside to get the inside done is a dead give away.  Maybe with a few alterations this one could be amazing though.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
finally found four bean salad

i lost this recipe and i found it just this morning, while going through a bunch of old papers. i'm so happy! i'm posting it immediately so it won't get lost again! i got this from a former co-worker, who had it at a potluck and liked it so much she got the recipe, and brought me a copy since she knew how much i loved to cook. i changed it up a bit, making big changes to the dressing and adding a bit to the actual salad components. this is a little on the sweet side, admittedly, but the sugar can be cut back to suit tastes. this is my favourite and i'm so glad i found it!

1. drain a 19-oz tin of chick peas , rinse well , then drain again
2. place in a large mixing bowl
3. drain a 14-oz tin of green beans and a 14-oz tin of wax beans well and then add to bowl
4. drain a 19-oz tin of red kidney beans , rinse well then drain again
5. add to bowl
6. dice up a coloured bell pepper and add to beans
7. peel a small red onion and slice into very thin strips and add to bowl
8. lastly , add about 1 / 2 cup of chopped fresh flatleaf parsley
9. now make dressing: in a separate bowl , whisk together the vinegars , oil , sugar , minced fresh garlic , worcestershire , and salt and pepper
10. pour dressing over salad ingredients and toss
11. cover and refrigerate overnight , stirring occasionally
12. when ready , spoon bean salad into a serving bowl using a slotted spoon , to drain off most of the dressing before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this today and it was a big hit.  The only change was that I only put 1 1/2 tbs. of sugar oh and I didn't have balsamic vinegar so I used a little rice wine vinegar.  It still turned out very good.  Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
trout amandine

we catch a lot of trout here, and this is a great way to fix it!

1. sprinkle salt and pepper in the cavities of the trout
2. in shallow bowl , mix eggs and half and half
3. dip trout in egg mixture , then roll in flour
4. in small skillet , saute the almonds in 2 t butter until light brown
5. add lemon juice and tarragon
6. remove from heat
7. keep warm
8. in large skillet , on med heat , combine oil and remaining butter
9. fry the trout for 8 minutes , turn and fry another 8 minutes
10. place trout on serving platter
11. top with almond mixture
demonstrations.review: I made this ages ago and just got around to rating it.  I don't eat fish so I'm rating based on the husband and guests.  EVERYONE asked for the recipe.  I didn't make any changes.  This one is a real gem.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
secretly delicious spinach pie

the tortilla adds a delicious crunchy shell and it smells so good while it is cooking. i actually made up this recipe from items in my kitchen and couldn't believe how wonderful it tasted! it is now a hit in my family and so easy to make. please rate and give feedback.  


update: since i first made this five years ago, we still enjoy this at least once a month. i have found that i can alternate the ingredients to use up items i have in the fridge. i have used mushrooms, sauteed onions, cherry tomatoes and even feta cheese instead of cheddar cheese. and it always comes out fantastic. i have also found that there are times i need to use more or less eggs depending on the ingredients. also, a glass pie pan is so much better than a metal as it toasts the tortilla just right. such an easy recipe with gourmet taste!

1. mix the first six ingredients in a bowl
2. set aside
3. lay the flour tortilla in a glass pie dish , press gently - does not need to lay perfectly flat against dish
4. i don't spray it prior and have never had any issues with it sticking
5. especially when made using a glass pie pan
6. sprinkle only 1 / 2 cup cheese on tortilla
7. sprinkle remaining cheese and the spinach onto tortilla in layers , and press gently
8. i don't chop or tear the spinach but you might opt to do this
9. pour egg mixture evenly over spinach , be careful not to pour any outside of tortilla as this causes it to stick to pan
10. bake in oven at 365 degrees for 35 to 45 minutes
11. insert fork in center and it should come out clean
12. use sharp knife to cut into pie slices and serve hot
13. other options: instead of garlic , you can use 1 / 4 cup onions
14. for added flavor , serve with homemade salsa
demonstrations.review: Fabulous!!!  Both of my kids ate it.  My oldest isn't usually a fan of Spinach so this was a surprise.  I put this together at the last minute so I didn't use roasted garlic.  I subbed a bit of garlic powder.  I used the recommended 5 eggs.  Probably only 1 1/2 cups of spinach as that was all I had on hand.  For the cheese I used a 1/2 cup of shredded cheddar then 2 sliced of colbyjack and 1/4 cup mozzarella.  It cooked in exactly 30 minutes.  Thank you for posting.  This will be one I come back to often.  The prep work was so very easy and quick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: I tried this using a basic homemade white bread and it worked perfectly.  I only had enough bread to make four thick slices so I halved the recipe.      To save time, I made them as whole French toast pieces.  The kids gobbled them up so I had none left to freeze.  I'll be trying this again soon.  Thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian lemon ice

it was very hot and humid here today, so i made some italian lemon ices to help cool off :) i have included both versions because most people have a definite preference for either the "water ices", or the creamier "roman style" ices. one of my fondest summer memories as a child, was when my grandmother would "slip" me a dime, so i could go down to the neighborhood italian bakery and buy a cup of lemon ices....yum!

1. water ices
2. melt sugar in hot water , add lemon juice and rind
3. let mixture stand for 5 minutes
4. strain , place mixture in a freezing tray and freeze , stirring frequently , until it reaches a mushy consistency
5. if you have an electric ice cream machine , pour mixture into machine and freeze according to manufacturer's directions
6. roman style
7. combine sugar and water in saucepan , heat until sugar melts
8. add lemon juice
9. strain mixture through a very fine sieve
10. freeze until mushy , stirring frequently
11. beat egg white until stiff
12. remove ice mixture from freezer when mushy
13. add stiffly beaten egg white and 1 / 4 cup sugar and mix well
14. add rum and mix
15. return to freezer and continue to freeze to ices consistency , stirring often
16. if you have an electric ice cream machine , pour mixture into machine and freeze according to manufacturer's directions
17. add beaten egg white and sugar according to manufacturer's instructions as you would if you were adding additional ingredients to your ice cream
demonstrations.review: I'm a huge fan of this recipe.  I make it for my kids all the time and somehow forgot to rate it.  It does take a long time to set so do it a day ahead. If you forget to stir it during the freezing process you can easily set it out for a while then stir it and return to the fridge. Thanks for posting this one.  It's in my ace in the hole file.  :)

target.recipe_text:
greek oven fries

guilt-free fries! by all means try the malt vinegar, other vinegars won't be the same. very easy.

1. cut each potato lengthwise into 8 wedges
2. place in bowl , cover with cold water and let sit for 30 minutes
3. drain
4. pat dry with paper towels
5. toss with oil and place skinside down on greased baking sheet
6. combine oregano , salt and pepper and sprinkle over potatoes
7. bake in preheated oven at 400 for 45-50 minutes or until they are browned and tender
8. remove and sprinkle immediately with malt vinegar and serve
target.review: Very nice crispy fries!These were delicious.Along with the olive oil I also added 1/2 tsp of Watkins Black Pepper Grapeseed Oil.Very nice.I also added 1/2 tsp onion powder.I did not have malt vinegar so I used white.They were fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
homemade pie crust

a nice all purpose pie crust. when i need a crust for a cobbler, i change it to self rising flour because i like lots of crust in my cobblers.

1. put flour into a mixing bowl with the butter
2. using a pastry cutter , cut the butter into the flour
3. add salt and water
4. mix until dough is formed
5. roll out on flat surface
6. bake at 375 degrees until brown
7. prick crust prior to baking for non filled baked pies
demonstrations.review: I always have trouble with pie crusts.But this one turned out perfect.I would always just use butter but I tried using shortening this time and I think that's what made the difference.But this recipe is great,very simple to make and a great end result.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wholesome homemade honey whole wheat bread

this is the most awesome wheat bread i have ever eaten. it is worth the extra effort and because this recipe makes 4 loaves, you can freeze them and have enough for awhile :) rising time included in prep.

1. dissolve yeast in warm water
2. in a large bowl , combine butter , molasses , honey and salt and mix well
3. add yeast mixture and then gradually add flours
4. turn onto floured surface and knead until smooth
5. place in buttered bowl and let rise until double
6. punch down and let rest for a few minutes
7. divide dough into 4 parts and shape into loaves
8. place in greased pans and let rise for about an hour
9. bake at 375 for 35 to 40 minutes
demonstrations.review: This bread is sooo delicious!I couldn't wait to have some this morning for my breakfast.I used the 6 cups of whole wheat flour but it was more like 5 cups of white to get the bread to a smooth consistency.Very tasty,a keeper for sure!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fresh strawberry yogurt cake

this super moist cake weeps pink tears down its tender slices. amazing!

1. preheat oven to 325
2. grease and flour a 10 inch bundt pan
3. sift together the 2 cups of flour , baking soda and salt
4. mix in the lemon zest and set aside
5. with an electric mixer , cream together the butter and sugar until light and fluffy
6. beat in the eggs one at a time , then stir in 1 tb
7. lemon juice
8. alternate beating in the flour mixture and the yogurt , mixing just until incorporated
9. toss the strawberries with the remaining cup of flour
10. gently mix them into the batter
11. pour the batter into the bundt pan
12. bake in the preheated oven for 60 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cake comes out clean
13. allow to cool 10 minutes in the pan , then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely
14. once cooled whisk together the remaining 2 tb
15. of lemon juice and the powdered sugar
16. drizzle over the top of the cake
demonstrations.review: Delicious tasty cake!I used low fat organic strawberry yogurt for mine and it turned out great so the yogurt doesn't have to be a thick greek,it works well with a thinner one also.An easy fresh tasting cake..

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potatoes supreme

this is delicious and easy to make. we use it for holidays, but could easily be part of dinner rotation. can use real potatoes, or frozen shredded or obrien potatoes.

1. boil potatoes til slightly tender
2. coarsely grate
3. toss all ingredients to mix
4. place in greased , shallow 1 1 / 2 qt baking dish
5. bake 350 for 30 minutes or til hot , bubbly , and slightly browned
demonstrations.review: This is very delicious and so quick and easy to make.I used the flat kind of hash browns since that's all I had on hand.I just cooked them for about 10 to soften them up then I just cut them into small pieces.It worked great.Great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super creamy and cheesy mac and cheese

i always make a big batch of this because my husband and i both love this and always want more.

1. cook the macaroni and set aside
2. in a pot , melt the butter and mix in salt and pepper
3. slowly add in the flour , stirring continuously
4. gradually add the milk and stir the mixture until smooth
5. add the cheese on a low heat and melt into the mixture
6. once the mixture is at your desired consistency , mix in the drained macaroni
demonstrations.review: I wasn't in the mood for baked mac and cheese so I decided to try this one.I love the creaminess of this recipe.I cut the ingredients down to 4 servings and cut out the salt.I also added garlic powder,onion flakes and yellow mustard.A great,fast meal.

target.recipe_text:
low fat broccoli  rice and cheese casserole

nan

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. spray a 9x13-inch baking dish with buttered flavored cooking spray
3. set aside
4. spray a medium skillet with butter flavored spray
5. saute celery and onion over medium heat until onion is clear
6. transfer onion and celery to a large mixing bowl
7. add soups and cheese
8. stir until well blended
9. add remaining ingredients and pour into prepared pan
10. bake uncovered 35-40 minutes or until bubbly and golden brown
target.review: This will be my new broccoli rice casserole from now on.  So easy and the family went wild for it. I couldn't find low-fat American cheese so I used 2% Velveeta.  Instead of transfering everything to a bowl after cooking the celery and onion, I just put everything in the same skillet and let the cheese melt in there over low heat.  That way I got the cheese to melt and had one less bowl to wash. :) Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon with sweet and spicy rub

this is from the show healthy appetite with ellie krieger.

1. coat your grill or a grill pan with cooking spray and preheat over medium heat
2. while the grill is heating , combine the brown sugar , chili powder , cumin , salt , and pepper
3. brush each salmon fillet with 1 / 2 teaspoon of the oil , then rub each fillet with about 1 / 2 tablespoon of the spice mixture
4. grill the salmon , flesh side down , until charred , 4 to 5 minutes
5. flip the salmon and cook another 5 to 6 minutes for medium doneness
6. for well done fish , cook an additional 1 to 2 minutes
7. remove to a platter and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Wonderful!  I doubled the recipe and added a 1/4 teaspoon of cayenne pepper.  Loved the sweet/hot taste.  Even my teenagers commented on how good it was!  Thanks so much!  This recipe is a new family favorite!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy  ranch broccoli and cheese

a yummy new way to serve broccoli.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. place cream cheese , milk and ranch dressing mix in a food processor or blender and process until smooth
3. place broccoli in a 9 inch baking dish , add cream cheese mixture and stir
4. top with cheddar cheese and bake 25 minutes or until cheese has melted
demonstrations.review:
This was SO GOOD!  My whole family loved it!!  All my kids kept coming back for second.......and hello....it's BROCCOLI!!  LOL!
I doubled the recipe to fit in my 9x13 pan and used 6 heads of broccoli with all the stems removed.  I only used the flowerettes.  It was perfect!  I can't wait to try it as a main dish with the chicken and pasta!  Thanks so much for a new favorite side dish that is really easy to prepare and very yummy!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jamaican jerk nachos

we love this dish because it's simple to prepare but full of flavor!

1. boil chicken until done then chop into small pieces
2. mix 3 tbs of jamaican jerk rub in to the chicken
3. take seeds out of bell peppers and chop into small pieces
4. add juice of 1 lemon to bell peppers
5. layer 1 bag of doritos on large baking pan and spread the chicken mixture of it and then add cheese to your own preference
6. pop into 400 degree oven until cheese melt
7. before you serve add the bell peppers to the top
8. you can also add sour cream , guacamole , or salsa
demonstrations.review: Jerk nachos are fantastic!  Great idea Chef Wedemeyer!   We used a rotisserie chicken and added the jerk spice.  We usually just use hamburger with taco seasoning but this is so much better. This is a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooked korean beef

this is based on a recipe i saw in chatelaine magazine.  it is hands-down the best slow cooker recipe ever!  it's great served over mashed potatoes, but my favourite way to serve it is in kaiser buns, with the yummy shredded beef piled high on top.  i put out toppings like arugula or lettuce, horseradish, mayonnaise, and sliced dill pickles, and let people fix their own bun the way they like it.  make sure to drizzle some of the wonderful sauce on each bun too, and also some of the onions too.  sooooo good!

1. stir all ingredients but meat together in the bowl of a slow cooker
2. remove string from roast
3. cut roast in half
4. place meat in the soy mixture and turn to coat
5. cover and cook until beef is fork-tender , 5-6 hours on high or 8-10 hours on low
6. remove beef from slow cooker and shred with a knife and fork , then return it to the sauce
7. pile onto mashed potatoes , or buns with toppings
8. dee-licious !
demonstrations.review: This was really great!  We had it over mashed potatoes with kimchi  and a eggroll on the side.  I know it sounds weird but it was SO GOOD!  I cook alot of Korean food and this has most of the same seasonings as Bulgoki but tastes totally different.  It also just fell apart in the pot because it was so tender.  Thanks for a yummy new recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked cinnamon donuts doughnuts

so simple!  easy to make and full of cinnamon flavor!  the topping goes on the donut before baking and offers a crusty sugar-cinnamon coating.  makes a great weekend breakfast or snack.  leftovers (if any) freeze well.

1. mix all 7 dry ingredients in a medium size bowl
2. in a smaller bowl , beat egg
3. mix egg with milk and melted butter
4. add vanilla
5. stir milk mixture into dry ingredients until just combined being careful not to overmix
6. pour into greased donut baking tin , filling approximately 3 / 4 full
7. mix cinnamon into brown sugar and sprinkle over donuts
8. drizzle or spoon melted butter over top of each donut
9. bake in a 350 degree oven for 17 minutes
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Wow!  So good!  Tastes like cinnamon toast except better!  I bought a donut pan in Estes Park, CO last week and picked this recipe to try first.  So glad I did, my kids LOVE them!  Now I wish I had bought two pans because I will be making these alot!  Thanks so much for the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
sinfully delish garlic mashed potatoes

sinful and yummy! a definite splurge but so worth it!

1. quarter the potatoes and put into a large pot of salted water
2. add the 8 cloves of peeled garlic
3. boil until tender
4. drain and add the sour cream , butter and cream cheese to the pot and mash with a potato masher , for best texture do not use a mixer
5. spread mixture into an oven proof casserole dish and garnish as desired
6. bake uncovered in a 325 degree oven for 15 minutes or until the top has browned to your satisfaction
7. for faster results , skip baking and place under broiler for a few minutes
target.review: To DIE for... I do not like mashed potatoes but my family loves them. I try to find a happy medium so that I can enjoy my meal as much as they do. This recipe does it. From a self professed mashed potato hater these are wonderful. I try to cook heart healthy in the house as my hubbies has high cholesterol. I substituted fat free plain yogurt for the sour cream and low fat cream cheese for the regularly cream cheese. I still used the butter as I prefer the taste but cut it to 1/4 cup. these potatoes were creamy and delicious. I have never not whipped my potatoes with a mixer. This recipe does NOT need to be whipped. They mashed beautifully. I barely got the dish to the table before the family started digging in. thanks for a marvelous recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwest tuna salad

i just love tuna! it's so fun to open a can and make a recipe up. this one turned out so flavorful and yummy... just popping with flavors. i also love a versatile recipe. you can enjoy this atop a bed of lettuce, rolled in lettuce leaves, in a wrap, in a sandwich or my favorite as a melt! i spread some of this on some whole grain sourdough and sprinkled some lowfat cheddar on it...stuck it in the broiler for a few minutes and wow! the tangy sourdough went really well with it. i can also imagine this with pasta added for a cold pasta salad or as a hot tuna casserole...yum!  i think i'll be making it every which way i can think of because the flavor is soooo delish! if you prefer a non-creamy salad just cut the mayo and sour cream and you might increase the lime juice and perhaps add a little bit of oil. if you want more heat add a jalapeno or two. enjoy yourself and make it how you'll like it.

1. mix salad ingredients together
2. mix dressing ingredients together
3. stir dressing into salad , mix well
4. this is great right away but if you let it sit in the refrigerator it will develop even more flavor
5. enjoy this how you'll like it
demonstrations.review: The best tuna salad my hubby says he has ver had. I omitted the sourcream and used fat free miracle whip. I think next time I may just add a little more lime juice and omitted the miracle whip all together (just for a more heart healthy choice). I used this as the filling for a simple sandwich on homemade multigrain bread. It was soooooo good. I could even eat it as a stand alone dish or on a bed of lettuce. This is a homerun recipe and is now our tuna salad of choice. It does not get any better than this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
incredibly delicious cheese garlic bread spread

easy, cheesy, savory spread to transform regular bread into a taste sensation! goes awesome with pasta dishes or beside a fresh salad.

1. microwave margarine in medium glass bowl for about 40 seconds or until its melted
2. mix in all ingredients , using a fork
3. spread the mixture over bread
4. place on baking sheet and bake for about 10 minutes at 450 , until the top is golden brown
5. easy !
demonstrations.review: this is the BEST garlic bread EVER!!! I have made it MANY times before but have forgotten to review it. If I could give it more than 5 stars I would. I am constantly getting requests for this bread. Everyone devours it. I will be making this for many years to come. For a little extra something something I add sun-dried tomatoes when I am so inclined. YUMMY YUMMY YUMMY a million times over.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked chicken and artichoke penne with sundried tomatoes

i found this recipe at http://onceamonthmom.com/ (a great site that helps you fill your freezer by creating monthly menus using seasonal recipes).  i haven't tried it yet...please review if you do!

1. in a large pot , cook pasta in salted , boiling water before al dente , according to package directions
2. drain and rinse with cold water to stop cooking process
3. while pasta cooks , combine artichokes in water , garlic , and parmesan
4. season to taste with salt and black pepper
5. add artichoke mixture , cooked chicken , and sliced sun-dried tomatoes to pasta , stirring to coat evenly
6. place pasta mixture in well-greased baking pan
7. top with mozzarella cheese
8. bake at 400f about 30 minutes or until heated through and cheese is melted
9. to freeze , follow directions above but do not bake
10. cover tightly with foil , label and freeze
11. when ready to serve , preheat oven to 400f bake , covered , until the center is hot , about 1 hour
12. remove foil
13. bake until cheese is golden , approximately 10-15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: I was looking for recipe to use up some of the jars I had in the fridge and this one fit the bill. I used this as a base and expanded on it greatly. I had oil packed sun-dried tomatoes and marinated artichoke hearts that I wanted to finish off. I used feta cheese instead of mozzarella on top (also something I needed to use up). I cooked the chicken in Roasted garlic and red pepper seasoning and some of the oil from the sun-dried tomatoes and baked it as directed. Haven't tried it yet but it smells marvelous. I will finish the review when we have had it for supper. Tried it and it was excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mussels in white wine and garlic

elegant seafood extravaganza

1. rinse and scrub mussels under cold water
2. using your fingers or paring knife , remove beards , and discard
3. in a large stockpot set over medium heat , combine wine , shallots , garlic , and salt
4. simmer 5 minutes
5. add mussels , cover , and increase heat to high
6. cook until all mussels are open , about 5 minutes
7. stir in herbs and butter
8. remove from heat
9. divide mussels and broth among four bowls
10. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: We have a local restaurant that is known for their fabulous mussels . Well let me tell you not any more. Everyone knows if you want reastaurant quality mussels you come to my house. These are marvelous. I use a cheap dry white cooking wine and they are still to die for. The first time I made them I ate two pounds on my own and used half a loaf of bread for the juice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reveillon tourtiere

i have discovered the tourtiere since coming to canada and i have tried several varities. this is my favorite and you might want to use a deep pie plate for it. chill time not included. i have not personaly made this but i have had it 3 times at a friends home and she passed the recipe to me.

1. in a large skillet , heat oil over medium high heat
2. cook pork , breaking up with spoon , for about 10 minutes or until no longer pink
3. drain fat
4. stir in stock , onions , garlic , mushrooms , celery , salt , cinnamon , pepper , savory , and cloves
5. bring to a boil
6. reduce heat to medium low
7. simmer for 35 to 45 minutes , or until 2 tablespoons liquid is left
8. stir in fresh bread crumbs and parsley
9. taste , and adjust the seasoning to your liking
10. cover , and refrigerate until cold
11. the filling can be stored for up to one day
12. roll out pastry to about 1 / 8 inch thickness , and fit to pie plate
13. spoon filling into shell
14. roll out top pastry
15. moisten rim of pie shell with water
16. cover with top pastry , pressing edges together to seal
17. trim and flute pastry edge
18. beat egg with water , and brush over the top pastry
19. cut steam vents in top
20. bake at 375 degrees f for 40 to 45 minutes , or until golden brown
21. allow to cool for about 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent tourtiere. I made it last Christmas for my friends from Quebec and they raved about it. In fact I think between the two of them They ate half of one and I sent them home with the second one I made. After the fact I received many requests for your marvelous recipe. It was a HUGE hit. Thank you so much. For my friends who were dearly missing their own friends and family clear across the country during the holiday seasons it added a little bit of home away from home and made the holidays just that little bit more enjoyable.

target.recipe_text:
america s test kitchen cheesy garlic bread

yummy, crusty, cheesy goodness from america's test kitchen.  garlicky, but not overpowering.  using a small cheese grater or zester to grate the garlic cloves will give a better texture.  better than store-bought!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. move rack to the 2nd from bottom space
3. saute garlic , 1 tablespoon butter , and water over low heat , 7 to 10 minutes
4. it forms a paste
5. combine hot garlic , 7 tablespoons butter , salt , and pepper in a bowl and spread on both halves of the bread
6. put the halves back together and wrap in foil
7. place on baking sheet and bake for 15 minutes
8. unwrap bread and place halves , buttered sides up , on baking sheet
9. bake until it begins to color , about 10 minutes
10. take out of oven and turn on the broiler
