11. sprinkle bread with cheese
12. place under the broiler until cheese has melted and bread is crispy , about 1 or 2 minutes
13. put on cutting board , cheesy side down
14. cut into pieces
15. serve
target.review: Wow!  This really has a strong garlic taste!  I liked the bread but unless you're a big garlic lover you might want to cut down on the cloves just a little.  Thanks for posting.  Made for Fall Pick-A-Chef 2012.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry squash

this tasty strawberry treat is from the best of cooking by arne kruger & annette wolter & it included a pineapple variation i have also noted. it was described as a "pre-dinner" drink, but works as an after school treat or dessert & might also be fun for a family of 4 to share ... as written for the kids for the 1st 2 portions & then adding 2 tbsp rum for the 2 adult portions. (time does not include 30 min for the strawberries to "sit" in the sugar) *enjoy*

1. halve strawberries & place in a bowl
2. sprinkle w / the sugar , stir to combine & leave for 30 min for juice to be extracted
3. using a blender or immersion blender , puree strawberries & juice created
4. add ice cream , milk , lemon & orange juice , lemon zest + confectioner's sugar & blend till well-mixed
5. pour into 4 glasses & add 1 ice cube to each glass
6. so i freeze the milk in a freezer container as my 1st prep step
7. using very cold milk w / ice crystals that often form means no ice cubes are needed when prep is done & you are ready to serve
8. variation: replace strawberries w / canned or fresh pineapple & use vanilla ice cream
demonstrations.review: I made the variation using vanilla ice cream and canned crushed pineapple.  I left out the confectioners sugar and didn't bother adding the ice cube at the end.  It makes a nice, refreshing snack and would be a great after-school treat.  Made for Football Pool 2012.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered salad

easy and yummy. if you don't like onions, go easy because the taste really comes out in this salad.

1. layer in order given
2. then frost with mixture
3. let meld overnight in frig , then , just before serving put cherry tomatoes and crumbled cooked bacon on it
demonstrations.review: This salad is a really good layered salad.  I cut the recipe in half but added some finely chopped celery and chopped my onion......also sprinkled some Parmesan on top.  I also made it with the 3 slices of bacon.......you can't go wrong with extra bacon!  Made for Bargain Basement Cooking tag game.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey soy chicken drumsticks

this is out of "the backyard barbecue cookbook" we don't really care for drumsticks so i used this on skinless chicken breasts. worked great. i have it marked "excellent!" in the book. you can add a little chili sauce if you prefer it hotter. hope you enjoy! cooking time does include 1 hour marinating.

1. combine the soy sauce , garlic , onion , pepper , honey and ginger wine or sherry in a small pan , stir over a low heat until the honey softens and the ingredients are thoroughly mixed
2. remove the skin from the drumsticks and score through the flesh at 3 / 4 inch intervals
3. pour the marinade over the prepared chicken and allow to marinate for 1 hour
4. remove the drumsticks from the marinade and barbecue over a preheated , oiled gill with the hood down for 20-25 minutes , turning occasionally until the chicken is tender and juices are clear
5. brush two or three times with the remaining marinade towards the end of cooking
demonstrations.review: Really delicious!  I don't have a grill so I browned the chicken on the stove then finished cooking them in a 350 oven for about 40 minutes.  Next time I think I will try cooking them only on the stove as another reviewer tried.  Made for Please Review My Recipe cooking games.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy rosemary potatoes

this recipe reminds me of some roasted potatoes we had at victoria station restaurant at the burswood resort and they were delicious.

1. preheat oven to 220c
2. line a baking tray with foil and then baking paper and spread potatoes on the tray in a single layer and scatter with rosemary leaves and ross with a decent slurp of olive oil until potatoes are thoroughly coated and cover loosely with foil and roast for 20 minutes
3. remove the foil , reduce the oven to 200c and cook for 35 to 40 minutes until golden brown
4. sprinkle with sea salt to serve
demonstrations.review: These were really crunchy potatoes.  I roasted mine starting at 425 degrees, then lowered the oven temp to 400 when I removed the aluminum foil.  I didn't have any rosemary so I sprinkled some creole seasoning on the potatoes before putting them in the oven.  My only complaint was you didn't say how big to cube the potatoes.  Mine were on the smaller side...maybe 1/2 an inch thick.  Made for Went to the Market cooking tag game.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek rotini salad

pasta salad with colorful veggies and feta!  i serve pepperonici peppers on the side.

1. cook the rotini according to the package directions
2. drain
3. rinse with cold water
4. drain well
5. combine the rotini and the next 9 ingredients in a large bowl
6. toss gently
7. combine olive oil , garlic , lemon juice , salt , pepper , and oregano in a jar
8. cover tightly and shake vigorously
9. pour the dressing over the rotini mixture
10. toss gently to combine
11. cover and chill thoroughly
demonstrations.review: I really liked the olives in this dish.  I decreased the amount to serve it just for 2 people.  Didn't have any cucumber but I added some shredded carrots and sliced mushrooms...the only thing I would change is that I would like more pasta in the salad.  Made for Rookie Recipe Tag game.

target.recipe_text:
snowy snack

this is a deliciously addictive holiday snack.  it combines sweet with salty, making it perfect for snacking.

1. melt the chocolate in a heavy saucepan on low heat or melt it in the microwave , stirring often
2. combine all the other ingredients in a large roasting pan
3. pour the melted chocolate over the ingredients in the roasting pan and stir to mix well
4. turn out on to wax paper and let it cool
target.review: We loved this; especially DH who couldn't remember what it was called so he kept renaming it.  He'd ask, "Where is that Snowflake Surprise?" or "Can I have some more Snowball Delight?"  I used red and green M&Ms for Christmas.  I bet this would be pretty using the pastel M&Ms at Easter.  Didn't have any pretzels, but we didn't miss them.  Thanks for posting!  Made for 1-2-3-4 Hit Wonders.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
special delivery chicken

from taste of home

1. in a bowl , combine the sour cream , soup and poppy seeds
2. stir in chicken
3. pour into a greased 11-in
4. x 7-in
5. x 2-in
6. baking dish
7. combine the cracker crumbs and butter
8. spinkle over top
9. bake , uncovered , at 350 for 25-30 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Can't get much easier or more delicious!  This a great make-ahead recipe.  Complete steps 1-3, put in the fridge, then when you're ready to cook it, top it with the buttered cracker crumbs.  Thanks for posting!  Made for My 3 Chefs for my "Get Over Your Canned Soup Phobia!" theme.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sausage pinwheels

for breakfast, brunch or a snack. you can slice them thinner if you prefer. can also be made with lean sausage meat.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. unroll crescent roll dough on a lightly floured surface
3. press seams and perforations together
4. roll into a 14-in
5. x 10-in
6. rectangle
7. spread sausage to within 1 / 2 inch of edges
8. sprinkle with chives and the cheese
9. carefully roll up from a long side , cut into 12 slices
10. place 1 inch apart on an ungreased baking tray
11. bake for 12-16 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Loved these!  My mother used to make something similar to these.  She made up her own dough, but using the crescent rolls is so much faster & easier.  DH asked, "You are going to make these again, aren't you?"  I found that slicing them without chilling them first was a little difficult, so I chilled them like you suggested and that made it much easier.  After I'd rolled them up, I remembered I forgotten the cheese, but they were still great.  DH loves cheddar cheese and is ready for me to make these again, next time remembering the cheese.  Thanks for a great breakfast idea!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek seasoned smothered chicken

this recipe comes from a restaurant that i worked at a few years ago. the cook told me how he makes it. i'm sure there are other versions of this but i love this one! no salt or additional spices are needed, the seasoning i used has plenty of flavor.
i don't really measure anything in this recipe, you pretty much put your preferences, but then there really isn't any measuring needed.
this meal is great with a salad and garlic bread. enjoy!

1. sprinkle cavender's seasoning on each piece of chicken , front and back
2. do not over season , as the flavor may be too strong , but adjust according to your tastes
3. slice mushrooms , peppers and onion
4. brown veggies in butter , to desired doneness , set aside
5. in skillet , heat oil and butter on medium heat and brown the chicken breasts coated with seasoning
6. cover and cook slowly until done
7. heat may have to be adjusted down to allow cooking all the way through without burning
8. when chicken is cooked , top each piece with the vegetable mixture
9. top each chicken piece with 1 or 2 slices of provolone cheese
10. heat on low until cheese is melted
demonstrations.review: I love just about anything with Greek seasoning, so I knew I would like this. Was going to shred the provolone, but at the last minute I couldn't find my grater, so I just tore the cheese into strips so the red bell peppers, onions, and mushrooms were visible. Thanks for posting! Made for My 3 Chefs (Around the World theme).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian inspired tuna cakes

found this recipe in "the metro st. louis guide to smart parenting" as a kid-friendly healthy recipe.  very simple and very tasty!  the sauce really makes the recipe!  the soy and panko give a nice twist to the familiar boring tuna cakes of yesteryear.  can be used as a main dish or as an appetizer.  note:  due to the concensus of reviewers, i have decreased the original 1/4 cup soy sauce to 1.5 tablespoons.

1. beat eggs and then combine with tuna , soy sauce , pepper , onion , panko and melted butter
2. form into patties and chill in refrigerator for 20 minues
3. in the meanwhile , make your dipping sauce
4. mix the mayo , garlic powder , lemon juice , lemon pepper and tabasco sauce
5. place dipping sauce in a sandwich size ziplock baggie
6. heat oil in large pan
7. cook tuna cakes for approx 4 minutes per side , or until golden brown , turning cakes only once to get good color
8. when browned on each side , remove and place on a paper towel to drain off excess oil
9. take baggie with the dipping sauce and barely snip off one of the corners of the baggie
10. drizzle the sauce over the top of each cake
demonstrations.review: These were ok, but the soy sauce was so overpowering.  Was out of ziplocs so I just brushed some of the sauce on the patties with a basting brush.  I did like the nutty flavor that came from cooking them in the sesame oil.  I'll probably try that next time I make my regular tuna patties.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
inside out bacon cheeseburgers

i made this for dinner tonight. i found it in kraft food & family magazine, and i'm glad i did.

1. preheat grill
2. mix meat and 2 tablespoons of the dressing
3. shape into 8 very thin , flat patties
4. mix remaining 1 tablespoons dressing and the bacon
5. spoon about 1 tablespoons of the bacon mixture onto the center of 4 burger patties
6. top each heap of bacon mixture with 2 cheese quarters
7. cover with second patty and pinch edges to seal
8. grill patties 7 to 9 minutes on each side , or till cooked through
9. place each burger on a bun and add your choice of condiments , lettuce , tomato , and onion
demonstrations.review: We really liked these!  Next time I make them I'll have to make a better attempt at sealing the edges.  I guess the beef shrank up while cooking.  I used smoky provolone for the cheese which added a wonderful smoky flavor.  Thanks for posting!  Made for 2008 All New Zaar Cookbooks Tag.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
target.review: This was a very flavorful meal!  Easy to prepare, I used thin cut chicken breasts so baked for 25 min and it came out great, even my super picky kids ate it.  I now have to come up with a way to make it taste this great while also making it healthier!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crunchy baked tilapia

i'm a real fan of tilapia with so many ways to fix it. here's another. delicious! excellent for those who do not like fish, but need the omegas.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. melt butter in shallow pie dish
3. set aside
4. in another shallow dish , mix cracker crumbs , seasoning and spices
5. dry fillets and dredge in butter
6. then , in crumb-seasonings mixture
7. place on oil-sprayed foil-lined baking sheet and distribute remaining crumbs on tops of fillets
8. drizzle remaining melted butter over crumbs
9. sprinkle each with grated cheese
10. bake for 15-20 minutes , until fish flakes easily and topping is golden
11. serve with chili sauceii-recipe #7161 , if desired
12. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: What a great and easy recipe!  I used only 3 tbsp butter and added extra parmesan b/c I love cheese and it was great.  Next time I'll add more seasonings to the crackers/breadcrumbs for a little more kick, or maybe season the fillets before adding the topping.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy parmesan orzo

from cooking light, this is a wonderful side or light main dish.  it is good even without the pine nuts if you don't have them on hand, also any herb will work for the basil, you just may need a little more or less depending on the herb.

1. heat butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat
2. add orzo and cook 3 minutes , stirring constantly
3. stir in broth and water
4. bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and simmer until liquid is absorbed , and orzo is done , about 15 minutes
6. remove from heat
7. stir in cheese , basil , salt and pepper
8. sprinkle with pine nuts
9. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Delicious!  I used only chicken broth so I omitted the salt and I used dried basil b/c it's all i had.  I loved this dish and will be making it regularly.  I think my picky toddler may even eat it.  THANKS!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy baked salmon

this recipe is so delicious, yet it takes less than 5 minutes to prepare.  it's a perfect dinner for a busy night!  for even more flavor, marinate for up to one hour.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees
2. mix together soy sauce , lemon juice , and spices
3. place salmon in a shallow baking dish , and pour liquid mixture over the filets
4. bake about 25 minutes or until salmon is flaky
demonstrations.review: I just made this and it was SUPER easy!  I am a novice who finds cooking fish a bit intimidating, so this was a great recipe for me to use.  My only qualm would be that it was a bit salty from all the soy sauce (but my husband thought it was perfect).  Next time i may reduce the soy sauce or use the low sodium kind.  I'll definitely make this again, thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatloaf barbecue style

this is our favorite meatloaf recipe. it's easy to make, moist and delicious!

1. mix together beef , crumbs , onion , egg , salt , pepper and 1 / 2 can tomato sauce
2. form into loaf and put into loaf pan
3. combine rest of tomato sauce , water , brown sugar , prepared mustard and worcestershire sauce
4. pour over loaf
5. bake in 350f oven for 1 hour and 15 minutes
6. makes 4-6 servings
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at making meatloaf and it was marvelous!  It was so moist I wasn't even sure I'd cooked it enough.  (I said I was a newbie!)  I used 1 lb. of beef, 1/4 onion b/c we're not huge onion fans, 1 T brown sugar, eggbeater, and italian bread crumbs.  It was delicious, thanks for the great and easy recipe, we'll be making this again soon when we're in the mood for some comfort food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
to die for crock pot roast

amazing flavor, and so simple! no salt needed here. in fact, you may wish to use half the ranch dressing mix to cut back on the saltiness. found this crock-pot pot roast recipe on of a website called www.recipegoldmine.com. it's all the rage there, so i thought i'd try it.

1. place beef roast in crock pot
2. mix the dried mixes together in a bowl and sprinkle over the roast
3. pour the water around the roast
4. cook on low for 7-9 hours
5. use onion soup mix instead of ranch
6. add one cup , of red wine
7. add potatoes , carrots , mushrooms , celery and onion 2-3 hours before end
demonstrations.review: Ok, I know this recipe doesn't NEED another review, but since I tried it based on so many reviews, I thought it best to add my results!  I used a 2 lb. top shoulder roast (not cheap!) and used the full amount of seasoning and cooked on low for 8 hrs.  I used a full cup of water and rubbed 1/2 the seasoing on the meat and put the rest over the veggies with the water.  Overall, the meal was really good.  My meat came out a litte bit dry, next time I'll cook it for 7 hours.  My veggies were very good, maybe a tiny bit salty, but we don't mind that too much. I'll definitely make this again, it was so easy, but I may make a few adjustments.

target.recipe_text:
costa rican tilapia

this recipe is from www.tastycooking.com.  authentic costa rican dish!

1. for the tilapia marinade , combine lime juice , 1 tablespoon olive oil , 2 tablespoons cilantro , 1 teaspoon garlic , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt , and sugar in a shallow dish
2. add tilapia and marinate 15 minutes , turning once
3. to prepare the bean and rice mixture , cook the rice according to package and keep warm while the tilapia is marinating
4. preheat oven to 400 degrees
5. in a large , skillet or saucepan , heat 2 tablespoons olive oil on medium heat
6. add remaining garlic and onions
7. saut until translucent , about 5 minutes , stirring
8. add 2 tablespoons cilantro , oranges , tomatoes , beans , oregano , 1 teaspoon salt , pepper , and cayenne
9. cook , uncovered , until hot , 7 to 8 minutes , stirring occasionally
10. transfer hot rice to a 9 by 13 inch baking dish
11. spoon the bean mixture on top of rice and gently blend
12. slightly overlap tilapia fillets on top and scrape marinade over fillets
13. bake 16 to 20 minutes
target.review: this was FANTASTIC! very unique, fresh, and healthy. my family LOVED it and only paused eating long enough to say "WOW this is DELICIOUS" every minute or so. i made it exactly as posted, no changes at all. thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby food pineapple coconut carrot cake

this incredibly moist carrot cake is brimming with yummies, like pineapple, coconut and walnuts! and the best thing about it is...no grating carrots...that's where the baby food thing comes into play!!! try it, you'll love it and never grate carrots again..at least not for cake :)

1. cake: preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a large mixing bowl , combine dry ingredients and mix well
3. add oil , eggs and baby food and mix on low speed until well combined
4. fold in pineapples , nuts and coconut
5. pour into 2- 9 inch greased and floured pans
6. bake for about 35 minutes or until center tests done
7. cool for 15 minutes on wire rack and then remove from pans
8. cool completely before filling and frosting
9. frosting: in a large bowl , beat cream cheese and butter until smooth
10. add vanilla and confectioner's sugar and beat until desired spreading consistency
11. frost cakes and sprinkle top with additional chopped walnuts and coconut , if desired
12. if you have any left , store in the refrigerator !
demonstrations.review: delicious!! omitted the coconut (didn't have any). my boyfriend was completely skeptical about the substitution of carrot baby food instead of real carrots, but when he tasted it he said "WOW! this is really good! it tastes like the normal stuff!" i cut the recipe in half and baked it in a 9x7 pan. also, i subbed applesauce for 1/3 of the oil. i used '1/3 less fat' cream cheese and no vanilla for the frosting and it was still fantastic!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jack daniel s flank steak

tasty marinated flank steak for grilling or broiling.

1. score the flank steak with a sharp knife , about 1 / 8-inch deep , in a diamond pattern
2. set aside
3. mash the garlic with the mustard
4. stir in the whiskey and oil
5. place steak in a zipper type plastic freezer bag
6. pour mixture over the steak and refrigerate overnight
7. set out at room temperature for 1 hour before cooking
8. remove steak from marinade , reserving marinade
9. grill , using charcoal or gas grill
10. cook over high heat 3 to 5 minutes per side
11. heat reserved marinade in small pan to a boil
12. slice the steak by cutting across the grain into 1 / 4-inch thick slices
13. serve with heated marinade as a sauce
demonstrations.review: tasted like jack daniel's... which shouldnt be surprising i suppose, but that's ALL it tasted like. my boyfriend asked me, "did you dump a bunch of alcohol in this marinade? because that's what it tastes like!" uh oh

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peanut butter chocolate chunk cookies

these are impossible to stop eating.

1. cream the butter and peanut butter together until fully incorporated
2. add the sugars and cream on medium speed
3. add the egg and vanilla and mix until completely incorporated
4. add the flour and baking soda , mix until no white remains , then add the chocolate and mix on low just until everything comes together
5. drop by teaspoonfuls onto parchment-lined baking sheets
6. bake at 350 for 9 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: i made a half batch of these and my boyfriend had consumed all of them within 2 hours of them coming out of the oven -- they were delicious! underbake them slightly for a perfectly chewy cookie. I cut the recipe in half and got 24 medium-sized cookies

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal and banana cookies

yummy!  hope you like these!

1. mix all but the chocolate and peanut butter chips
2. add in chocolate chips
3. bake at 350 for 12-15 minutes
demonstrations.review: Mm! tasty!!  i had a bunch of partial bags of chocolate chips left so i used 2 cups worth of a mix of dark chocolate, semisweet, and butterscotch.  i ground up the oats because my family doesn't like the oatmealy texture. also, i didn't have quite enough oats, so i made up the difference with walnuts powdered in the food processor with the oats. they turned out fantastic! soft and moist, but not at all squishy. thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black bottom banana bars

delicious and very moist. even better the second day.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and sugar
2. add egg and vanilla
3. beat until thoroughly combined
4. blend in the bananas
5. combine the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt
6. add to creamed mixture and mix well
7. divide batter in half
8. add cocoa to half
9. spread into a greased 13-in x 9-in pan
10. spoon remaining batter on top and swirl with a knife
11. bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes or until the bars test done
12. cool
demonstrations.review: MARVELOUS!! soft and moist and just delicious. sifted the dry ingredients together (out of habit) and used half light brown sugar (also habit). followed other reviewers' suggestion to add chocolate chips to the bottom layer. i used a 10x10 pan. when spreading the batter out it seemed REALLY thin, almost didn't cover the bottom of the pan, but it baked up thick and beautiful! will definitely make again... in fact, i'm going out tomorrow to buy some bananas to leave on my counter for OOPS too long until i'm forced to make this again ;)

target.recipe_text:
crock pot creamy italian chicken

nan

1. place the chicken breast halves in the crock pot
2. combine the italian dressing mix and water until smooth
3. pour over top of chicken
4. cover and cook on low for 3 hours
5. combine the cream cheese and soup until smooth and blended
6. stir in mushroom pieces
7. pour soup mixture over chicken
8. cook 1 hour more or until chicken is cooked through
9. serve over hot cooked rice or pasta
target.review: I have friends that are very picky eaters and EVERYONE loves this dish! I cooked it on low for 6 hours before adding the sauce...the chicken melts in your mouth! I always double the sauce because it is SO good and everyone wants more!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried eggplant  aubergine

this recipe appeared in "cooking light" magazine. this is a non-traditional way to prepare eggplant, but it really cuts the calories.

1. combine first 2 ingredients , stir well
2. spread evenly over both sides of eggplant slices
3. combine breadcrumbs , cheese , and italian seasoning in a shallow bowl
4. dredge eggplant in breadcrumbs mixture
5. place eggplant on a baking sheet coated with cooking spray
6. bake@ 425 degrees for 12 minutes
7. turn eggplant over
8. and bake an additional 12 minutes or until golden
demonstrations.review: This is seriously my favorite recipe I've found on this site so far! TASTES DEEP FRIED, BUT IS HEALTHY! My fiance and I are obsessed. I didn't even think I liked eggplant very much until today. My breading was really crispy, maybe because I mixed some panko cumbs in with the bread crumbs...and I ran out of breadcrumbs at the end so some got coated with crushed croutons, which were equally delicious. LOVE IT LOVE IT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
halibut florentine

i hate fish! but this is so good!  my mom made this for us and it is deelish - the fish is very mild and not fishy at all, i love spinach and the cheese, yum - next to "yummy chicken" i would have to say honestly that this is now one of my favorites!

1. melt butter in sauce pan
2. add flour
3. add milk and stir until thick to make a white sauce
4. add 1 / 4 cup of the parmesan cheese and stir until melted
5. add salt and pepper to sauce to taste
6. place spinach in bottom of casserole dish
7. top with fish fillet
8. cover with white sauce
9. combine mozzarella , 1 / 4 cup of parmesan , cheddar cheese , bread crumbs and old bay seasoning
10. sprinkle over top of sauce
11. bake at 350f for 20-30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I did not like the cream sauce...there was not nearly enough and it was too bland, I'd use half&half or heavy whipping cream next time. The crust was okay but not spectacular with the halibut. The best part, to me, was the spinach, except the spinach under the fish didn't cook in the cream sauce so that part was very bland.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
joshua s favorite tilapia with jasmine rice

this is my very own creation, i whipped this up one day quite by accident. i call this joshua's favorite tilapia, because my husband (like me) could eat this 7 nights a week if we could. this is the easiest way to cook tilapia, and if you are watching those calories then you need not worry this is extremely low fat, oh and did i mention to die for !!! this recipe is simple with few ingredients, but has the potential to add what ever you want. i like it as is !

1. pour your dressing straight from the bottle into the pan , i usually make sure the bottom is covered but not too much , i gave approximate measures here
2. place the fillets on top of the dressing in the pan
3. sprinkle with all 4 seasonings
4. i usually just sprinkle a generous amount on each filet
5. don't leave out the cumin it is a wonderful addition to the fish
6. saute the fillets on med-low heat approximate 4-5 minutes each side until fish flakes easy with a fork
7. while the fish is slowly cooking , cook the rice , using 2 1 / 2 cups water and 1 cup rice , with butter , bring to a boil and simmer 15 minutes on low
8. serve the fillet on top of the jasmine rice
9. i will usually add more s&p and cumin according to my taste
demonstrations.review: Very good recipe! but the seasoning didn't stay on the fish that well, so I  had to scoop the sauce onto the fish at the end. I used Basa, which was just as delicious as tilapia! Italian dressing was a great idea :o)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mama s supper club tilapia parmesan

you asked for it. here it is. thanks so much to mama's supper club. wish we could all go there.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in buttered 13-by-9-inch baking dish or jellyroll pan , lay fillets in single layer
3. do not stack fillets
4. brush top with juice
5. in bowl combine cheese , butter , mayonnaise , onions and seasonings
6. mix well with fork
7. bake fish in preheated oven 10 to 20 minutes or until fish just starts to flake
8. spread with cheese mixture and bake until golden brown , about 5 minutes
9. baking time will depend on the thickness of the fish you use
10. watch fish closely so that it does not overcook
11. makes 4 servings
12. broil 3 to 4 minutes or until almost done
13. add cheese and broil another 2 to 3 minutes or until browned
14. thank you mama's supper club in wisconsin
demonstrations.review: I would suggest using less butter; there was butter-soup under the fish when it was done! But the actual topping was fantastic and delicious! I made this over Orange Roughy and Scallions- both were great

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: I read some reviews that said they made it in a crock-pot and it turned out great, so I tried it too...but it turned out so liquidy that I doubled the meat and it still turned out looking like a soup. I wonder if more liquid might have evaporated better  on the stove? I will try that next time. Flavor was fine but I expected the beer, coffee, and cocoa flavors to come through a bit more. I couldn't notice them at all.

target.recipe_text:
corn on the cob

when you add milk to the liquid in which you cook corn on the cob, it keeps the kernels from becoming bitter.

1. place the water , milk , butter , sugar , salt , and red pepper flakes in a large , heavy pot and bring to a rolling boil over high heat
2. add the corn , reduce the heat to a simmer , cover , and cook until tender , about 5 to 8 minutes
3. remove the pot from the heat and let stand until needed
4. drain and serve hot , either plain or with the condiments of your choosing , such as oil , butter or maple syrup
target.review: This was great!  This would work good with corn that isn't so fresh and may have lost some of it's sweetness.  I usually roast my corn on the grill, but my husband wasn't here to help me with it so I wanted a way to cook them on the stovetop.  I left the butter out of the water and served it with the corn.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken papadoris

this is an excellent light curry dish to be served over cooked rice. i developed this recipe in palm springs, ca and it has been a big success with everyone who has tried it. the recipe name is very original as i named it after some friends of mine. her name was "doris" and i called her husband "papa". therefore, "chicken papadoris". you can also use chicken drumettes, wings or thighs.

1. remove all fat from chicken breasts and discard
2. cut chicken breasts into bite size pieces
3. in a large frying pan , melt butter , add onion and garlic and saute' until onions are translucent
4. add chicken pieces , cover and fry until cooked through and have turned white , about 6 minutes , stirring occasionally
5. stir in pine nuts , soy sauce , paprika , coconut milk , cumin and curry powder
6. cover and continue cooking for about 5 more minutes , stirring occasionally
7. in a cup , mix together tapioca starch and water until dissolved
8. near the end of cooking the chicken and while sauce is bubbling , add cornstarch mixture , small amounts at a time , stirring constantly until the sauce thickens
9. use only enough tapioca mixture so that the sauce has the consistency of gravy
10. adjust seasonings to taste
demonstrations.review: This was great!  Curries have always intimidated me because I didn't know how spicy they were, etc.  But this one is perfect for a beginner like me! So easy to make and very good too!  If you like it hot, you'll want to spice it up, but if not, it is perfect!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pumpkin upside down cake

very rich, but a nice change from pumpkin pie.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine eggs , pumpkin , evaporated milk , cinnamon , ginger , nutmeg , salt& sugar until well combined , and pour into an ungreased 13x9 baking dish
3. sprinkle dry cake mix on top of pumpkin mixture , drizzle with butter
4. bake 30 minutes
5. sprinkle nuts on top& bake for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is amazing -- a family favorite in the fall.  I do not usually use many mixes in my kitchen, but cake mixes are not easy to replace because of their speed and simplicity.  They add a wonderful flavor to this.  Try it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
very berry coffee cake

simple to make and a good way to use up leftover sour cream as it only calls for 3 tablespoons of it. you can mix and match berries or use all one kind too. recipe courtesey killahevlin bed and breakfast front royal, virginia

1. spread solid shortening on bottom and sides of a 9-inch square pan
2. position oven rack in center of oven and preheat to 350 degrees
3. sift together flour , baking powder and salt
4. set aside
5. cream butter and sugar with electric mixer
6. add eggs one at a time and beat until fluffy
7. add vanilla and sour cream and mix well
8. alternately , add flour mixture and milk to batter , beginning and ending with flour
9. spread half the batter into the prepared pan and smooth the top
10. spread berries on top of batter
11. cover berries with remaining batter and spread the top evenly with a spatula
12. for crumb topping: combine all ingredients and pinch them with finger
13. spread on top of cake and bake for 30 to 35 minutes or longer if glass pan- or until a toothpick comes out clean and cake is golden brown
14. cool cake completely on wire rack
15. refrigerate overnight and cut into squares
16. serve at room temperature
demonstrations.review: I made this for my husband and his coworkers for breakfast.  I did not have a 9-inch square, so I used a 9-inch round.  Because of the pan difference I did not have enough batter to layer properly, so I placed the batter on bottom, then the berries, then a double batch of the crumb topping.  I used frozen (defrosted and drained) mixed berries.  This recipe produced amazing results and I will be making this often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: This is an absolutely amazing recipe.  My husband actually argued with a co-worker over who's wife made the best meatloaf -- turns out it was the same recipe!  I've never enjoyed meatloaf but actually crave this.  Wouldn't change a thing, except my family loves ginger so we add a little more.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vanilla butter icing

this is my favourite icing. you can make it in vanilla or chocolate flavours.

1. place icing sugar and butter in a bowl and add boiling water slowly , stop when it is the consistency you want
2. stir until it spreadable and add vanilla essence
3. ices a 20cm cake
4. add 1 / 4 cup cocoa powder for a chocolate version
demonstrations.review: This is such a nice simple icing, exaclty what I was looking for.  I used it to ice a vanilla cake.  One warning:  wait until the cake cools to frost!  I know this, as I decorate many cakes.  This one, however, was just for my family, so I thought the only thing that might happen would be the icing might melt a little and drip.  Oops!  The butter separated and floated on top.  Luckily, it was just us eating and still tasted great, just wanted to make sure everyone else knows never to frost a warm cake!!

target.recipe_text:
stir fry bok choy

greens are feel good food! this combination of flavors works every time.

1. get wok hot
2. add olive oil , onion , ginger , garlic , salt and red pepper flakes , saute for a few minutes
3. add chicken broth and lemon juice
4. add bok choy and stir on high till done
target.review: Love this recipe - The chili flakes and lemon juice give this recipe a super flavor burst. I had some left over carrots in the fridge so threw them in with the bok chok. I only stir fried the Bok Choy for about 2 minutes, still had some crunch but hot through  ad the greens wilted. Thanks Brewster for a recipe that goes in with my favorite veggies

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pico de gallo garlic burgers

if you love a good burger, this should do the trick!

1. using your hands , squeeze excess liquid from pico de gallo
2. mix all ingredients together
3. i use my hands as it tends to blend the ingredients better
4. form into burgers
5. cook and enjoy with your favorite condiments
6. i grill the buns for added taste
7. i also love to make my own fresh french frys and when i pull them out of the deep fryer i sprinkle them with tony cachera's cajun seasoning
8. you can use store brand pico de gallo , i however make my own but also love the recipes that are on zaar
9. i couldn't narrow it down to one recipe to refer you to , so please do a search for your choice of recipe
10. i admit , i have fallen in love with yai-yai's garlic sauce , it is a very strong wonderful sauce
11. you can use fresh micned garlic as well
12. as i love garlic , if i used fresh i would probably use 2 to 3 cloves at least
demonstrations.review: Great Burger! I made sure to squeeze some of the juice from the Pico de Gallo - you are right the burgers are moist but I had no trouble flipping them in the pan.  I recommend that you have a solid surface to cook these on. I did "Oven Fries on a baking stone" and used Tony Chachera's exra spicey seasoning..  Couldn't find Yai-yai garlic sauce but found another great one "Joseph's Garlic sauce" by JoAnn and I used" Pico de gallo Sauce" by Polly Salama.  Great combination - Thank-you Rise it's a winner

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggs with crab meat

this is an old madame wong recipe that i tried for the first time last night.  it came out like a great big, loose, egg fu yung, or 'egg stew' and was total comfort food on a cold night.  i changed a couple of things (added more egg and scallion and less oil) but this is pretty close to the original recipe.  i think this recipe could really be played around with...i plan on trying it with small, cooked shrimp and, perhaps, adding some chopped spinach for more color and nutrition.  one thing for sure, don't omit or substitute the fresh ginger!!  the ginger is what made this so special for us.  a non-stick wok is very useful for this recipe.

1. combine crab meat , eggs and stock
2. add soy sauce and beat lightly with a fork
3. heat 1 t
4. of oil in wok over medium-low heat
5. stir-fry ginger and scallion for one minute , remove and set aside
6. heat 2 t
7. of oil in wok over medium-high heat
8. add crab meat and egg mixture and stir-fry very gently
9. when mixture starts to set , add ginger and scallion
10. cook for about 2 more minutes then thicken with dissolved cornstarch
11. stir in the vinegar and serve hot over steamed rice
demonstrations.review: The flavor is wonderful - the ginger comes through beautifully.  I only used 3 tbsp of chicken stock and no corn starch - Sprayed the pan with "No Oil" Cut the recipe to 3 eggs but followed all the ingredients except the stock - Gorgeous flavor loaded omelet  Thankd Hey Jude for a lovely dinner

demonstrations.recipe_text:
barbecued chicken thighs au vin

nan

1. put chicken thighs in a freezer bag
2. in a saucepan , heat oil and butter
3. add shallots and garlic , cook over medium heat for 5 minutes or until softened
4. add jelly , wine , stock , orange rind , mustard and ginger
5. heat until the jelly has just melted
6. remove from heat and cool to lukewarm
7. pour marinade over chicken , close bag and refrigerate for at least 3 hours
8. drain marinade into a saucepan and bring to a boil
9. reduce heat and simmer 5 minutes
10. use as a basting sauce during barbecuing
11. turn the barbecue to medium heat
12. put chicken thighs on the grate , skin side up , and grill for 20 minutes
13. brush occasionally with marinade
14. turn thighs and cook another 10 - 20 minutes or until a meat thermometer inserted in the thickest part reads 180f
15. brush occasionally with marinade
demonstrations.review: Dancer you continue to amaze me. This recipe is so easy to make and so good I did not know what"blackuce heat" meant but just put it back on the stove and simmered it for 5 minutes. I used skinless boneless breast but followed your recipe (cooking time was shorter).Great blend of flavors that complimented each other perfectly.  Thanks Dancer for another great recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ground beef stuffed green bell peppers with cheese

we had these not too long ago and we both decided that they needed a little more seasoning. we put a little hot pepper sauce on them and they were much better. i would probably include 2 teaspoons in the meat mix the next time that i make them.

1. cut off the tops of green peppers
2. discard seeds and membranes
3. chop enough of the tops to make 1 / 4 cup , set aside
4. cook the whole green peppers , uncovered in boiling water for about 5 minutes
5. invert to drain well
6. sprinkle insides of the peppers lightly with salt
7. in a skillet cook ground beef , onion and 1 / 4 cup chopped pepper till meat is browned and vegetables are tender
8. drain off excess fat
9. add drained tomatoes , salt , worcestershire , and a dash of pepper
10. in a separate pot put water bring to boil add rice cook until rice is soft
11. if needed add more water
12. add rice to beef mixture
13. stir in cheese
14. stuff peppers with meat mixture
15. place in a 10x6x2 baking dish
16. bake , covered in a 350 degree oven for 30 minutes
17. in the last 5 minutes add any remaining cheese to the top of the peppers
demonstrations.review:
Very tasty recipe.  I did add 1 tsp of hot sauce (I do like spice).
 I cut the peppers long ways - they cook faster and I  did not pre cook them.  25 minutes in 375 oven and they were perfect - still had some crunch to the peppers and totally hot through. Used Lite Havarti cheese.  Thanks for a very enjoyable recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
norwegian betasuppe

zwt6 - scandinavia

1. combine peas , ham , onion , thyme and water in a large dutch oven and simmer for 1 1 / 2 to 2 hours
2. add potatoes , rutabaga , celery root , leek and salt
3. and cook for another 30 to 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: We loved this soup. Yes it does make a large potful. I have 4 double servings in the freezer and we had it for lunch today. Come  Winter we will be enjoying it. The store where I did my produce shopping did not have celeric. I was in a hurry and did not have time to shop around - I used celery and it worked. It may not be the prettiest color (no split pea soup is) but it sure makes up for it in flavor.

target.recipe_text:
stuffed green bell pepper soup

nan

1. in 6-quart saucepan or dutch oven , brown beef
2. drain
3. add remaining ingredients
4. bring to boil
5. reduce heat
6. cover and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes or until tender
7. makes about 16 servings
target.review: As others have said, I also add a diced onion, use a combo of Spicy V8 and a bottle of chili sauce instead of the tomato sauce and brown sugar.  I prefer using Better than Bullion (beef) instead of cubes, skip adding extra salt and brown rice instead of white.  I'm a green pepper lover, so 3-4 jumbo ones aren't too many for me.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the original cabbage soup diet

i got this out of the national enquirer in 1995-1996 when the soup diet originally came out. i don't remember the rules of the diet other than you could eat as much of this as you wanted.

1. place all in large stock pot and bring to a boil
2. simmer for 1 hour
3. refrigerate all leftovers
demonstrations.review: I switched his up a bit and roasted 2 green and red bell peppers, a container of diced mushrooms and 2 large onions and 2 cloves of garlic (finely chopped) with some salt and pepper in a 425 degree oven for 20 minutes.  Then I combined 2 cans of Muir Glen fire roasted crushed tomatoes with the remaining ingredients in a large stock pot to warm through before adding the roasted veggies and Spicy V8 (love my spicy stuff) and simmered for the time stated.  I squeezed the lemon juice at the end of the cooking time and ate 2 huge bowls.  Yummy!  I think the balsamic vinegar and lemon are such a great addition to the original recipe.  Thanks for posting this "oldie, but goodie."

demonstrations.recipe_text:
da best  chicago style italian beef

tender, garlicky and full of oregano 'n stuff! start this one a day ahead; the beef slices need an overnight stay in da gravy to be at their best. and please don't overcook the roast! as it rests right out of the oven and as it's reheated it'll stop mooing! serve on crusty italian sandwich rolls; add sauteed peppers if you like, but too much more and it starts looking like a philly steak 'n cheese, a whole other beast. prep time includes overnight marinating.

1. preheat oven to 325f
2. sprinkle the roast with garlic powder , oregano and pepper , then cook roast , uncovered , in a shallow roasting pan , about 30 minutes per pound
3. roast will be very rare-- don't overcook it !
4. let cool slightly , then thinly slice
5. add to the roast's pan drippings: the boiling water , bouillon cubes , oregano , thyme , pepper , tabasco sauce , garlic and worcestershire sauce
6. simmer for 20 minutes , scraping up the browned bits
7. taste for salt and add some if you wish
8. add the sliced beef
9. cover and marinate in da gravy overnight
10. reheat the next day and serve in crusty italian sandwich rolls
demonstrations.review: This was "Da Bomb!"  I used a 2.5 lb rump roast, but made the amount of gravy listed in the recipe.  I cooked the roast for 60 minutes, took it out and let it rest for 20 minutes while I made Da gravy.  The next day (after marinating), I put everything in the crockpot to reheat.  Served on toasted ciabatta rolls with grilled onions and melted provolone cheese.  YUM!  Great recipe!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
boston market dill potato wedges

from copykat.com (http://www.copykat.com)

1. wash potatoes well and boil until soft , drain well on paper towels
2. melt 1 stick of butter , in large frying pan saut garlic for a couple of moments , and then add potatoes and the rest of the seasonings
3. pan-fry the potatoes until they are lightly brown
demonstrations.review: Boston Market's potatoes are not "browned."  When I make my version, I just melt butter and garlic salt together while the potatoes are boiling.  When the potatoes are done, slice them into wedges and pour the melted butter/garlic salt over the potatoes.  Add salt, pepper and dried dill (yeah in the little container) to the mixture to taste.  My husband has told me that the way I make them is just like Boston Market, only better.  Gotta love him!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable quiche cups  sbd

these are a breakfast option in the south beach diet (phase 1). they can be eaten hot or cold and can also be frozen. these make a handy and healthy snack to take to work too.

1. heat oven to 350f
2. line a 12 cup muffin pan with foil baking cups , spray the cups with cooking spray
3. thaw and drain spinach , wring it out well by hand
4. mix the spinach , egg whites or substitute , cheese , peppers , onions , hot pepper sauce and salt in a bowl
5. fill the foil cups with the mixture
6. bake at 350f or 20 minutes , testing so that a knife inserted in the middle comes out clean
7. remove from cups to serve
demonstrations.review: As written, it's an OK recipe.  Here are my "modifications."  First, I use an entire 15 oz container of Egg Beaters, saute the onions and peppers until softened and put in an 8x8 baking pan sprayed with nonstick spray.  Instead of shredded cheddar cheese I put swiss cheese slices to cover the top and top with cracked black pepper.  Bake at 350 degrees for approximately 20-30 minutes or until "egg" mixture is set.  Cut into 6 slices.  The amount of extra egg substitute is minimal extra calories and makes them sooooo much yummier.  In the morning I nuke them in the microwave and put them on a whole wheat english muffin with a slice of tomato.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy roasted vegetables

super easy roasted vegetables for summer barbecuing... can be used in lasagna, pasta salads, etc...

1. mix chopped vegetables and dressing in large bowl
2. allow to marinate for 2 hours , stirring to distribute dressing frequently
3. place in hot bags , heavy foil , or release foil , in medium sized packets
4. grill over medium bbq or roast in oven at 350 for approximately 30 minutes , until tender-crisp
5. enjoy as they are , or use in pasta salads , sandwiches , or other recipes calling for grilled veggies
demonstrations.review: This is very similar to a SBD recipe for roasted veggies.  I also add 2 cloves of finely diced garlic cloves and extra virgin olive oil (instead of the bottled salad dressing) and a few shakes of red pepper flakes before roasting.  I freeze in them in 4 containers.  Then I can add chicken, beef, fish or add them to whatever I'm making that needs roasted veggies.  I can add pasta with peanut sauce to make Pad Thai, make veggie soup or a veggie lasagne with pasta, ricotta cheese and bake it.  The list goes on and on.  Great  basic recipe....the possibilities are endless!!!

target.recipe_text:
shrimp   chicken with rice

this is the first recipe i ever came up with.

1. cook rice in water with chicken bouillon for 20 minutes or until done
2. put on the side
3. cut chicken breast into thumb size pieces
4. put flour and spices into small bowl
5. you can change amounts or types of spices to your taste
6. mix the flour and spices together
7. heat oil in skillet
8. put chicken pieces in flour and dredge them till covered
9. put into heated oil in skillet
10. cook chicken till no longer pink in color
11. add frozen salad shrimp
12. these should be the ones that come 100 to a pound
13. you can add more if you really like shrimp
14. add soy sauce or braggs liquid aminos to the skillet
15. the flour , water from the shrimp and soy sauce form a thin sauce
16. cook down till shrimp are hot and sauce is thin
17. put rice on plate
18. add chicken and shrimp mixture
19. mix so the sauce is stirred well into the rice
target.review: This was delicious. Shrimp and chicken, couldn't be better together. I did everything as you stated except I added onion with the chicken and used brown rice. It was full of flavor and this will definately go on my list of repeats. Cooking the rice in the bouillon really sets the flavor. Thanks Barb, we really enjoyed this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
speedy white chicken enchiladas

this is a quick and simple chicken enchilada recipe.  don't remember where the original came from, as i have tweaked it over the years into this recipe.

1. mix soup and sour cream and set aside
2. heat butter in medium saucepan
3. add onions and chili powder and cook until onions are tender
4. add the canned chicken and chilis and 3 tablespoons of the sauce mixture
5. spread 1 / 2 cup of the soup mixture into a 9x13 pan
6. spoon mixture into tortillas , roll up , and place on top of the soup mixture
7. spread remaining sauce mixture on top , and cover with cheese
8. bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes -- or until cheese is bubbly and browning
9. suggestion: one can use chopped / shredded leftover chicken rather than canned chicken
10. suggestion: serve with salsa and chips for a great meal !
11. suggestion: this is a very forgiving dish
12. i have added black olives , used less chicken , doubled the sauce mixture , upped the spice factor , etc
13. you can easily tweak this recipe to your liking
demonstrations.review: This was a quick and tasty dinner. I bought a package of cooked chicken strips that Tyson puts out so this was super fast to make. I used Rotel tomatoes since I didn't have any chilies left. I cut this recipe in half and it was perfect for the 3 of us. Thanks for nice fast delicious meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish hamburgers  malda flaskbiffar

this recipe is different from my other swedish burger recipe in that it is made and served with fried onions and cream gravy over mashed potatoes.  kind of like meatballs only in a bigger form!

1. soak bread crumbs and seasonings in water and cup cream for 10 minutes
2. add pork , egg and parsley
3. mix well until blended
4. shape into 8 round flat patties
5. melt half of margarine in large skillet
6. fry patties about 4-5 minutes on each side over medium heat
7. place on warm platter and keep warm
8. peel and thinly slice onions
9. saut in remaining margarine until soft and golden about 12-15 minutes
10. spoon onions over burgers and keep warm
11. pour 1 cup cream into frying pan
12. cook , stirring down the sides for about 4-5 minutes until it starts to thicken
13. season with salt and pepper
14. pour over burgers and serve immediately , preferably over mashed potatoes
demonstrations.review: Oh just lovely. The burgers tasted great and I would have never thought of this as a regular burger. I didn't have any cream so I improvised and used liquid coffee creamer and worked great. We had the sauce over rice and that was quicker to fix and dinner was running kinda late. Thanks for a new burger recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
swedish turkey meatballs

this recipe is the most requested recipe in our household. it is the result of many attempts to get the right combination of seasonings for turkey instead of hamburger meatballs that still have that swedish meatball taste. we much prefer the taste to the original hamburger recipe.

1. combine the first ten ingredients and shape into 1 1 / 2" meatballs
2. in a large non-stick dutch oven , brown meatballs in 1 tbsp of butter , turning carefully every few minutes to brown all sides , maintaining meatball shape
3. add chicken broth and simmer for 15 minutes
4. add white sauce
5. stir , heat and serve over hot cooked egg noodles
demonstrations.review: These were great. I used Cream of Mush soup as my white sauce is kinda sad. I have never tried to cook them in chicken broth and I think that is what made them realllly stand out. I could eat them for a meal alone without putting them on noodles or rice.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach oatmeal

i have created one delicious oatmeal!  it sort of reminds me of the quaker peaches and cream oatmeal.  i still prefer this oatmeal however, which is healthier, to packaged any day.

1. cut up peach slices into small pieces
2. in a bowl add oats , water , and peaches with juice
3. microwave in 500watt microwave for 2 minutes , stir , microwave for another 2 minutes , stir , then microwave in 1 minute intervals until cooked
4. in a 1200watt microwave , microwave for 30 seconds , stir , microwave for another 30 seconds , stir , and then continue microwaving in 30 second intervals until cooked
5. once cooked , add cinnamon , butterscotch extract , and sweetener
demonstrations.review: Did you know this was great for dinner? I was left all by myself and I wanted something a little different and this was wonderful. Not only did I use peaches, but I had some canned cocktail fruit left over so I added it all. Very good. Great change from the usual oatmeal. Thank you for a tasty breakfast type dinner.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken pot au feu

recipe taken from the shape magazine.

1. preheat oven to 435 degrees
2. spray potatoes with olive oil spray
3. and season with salt and pepper
4. transfer potatoes to a baking sheet and roast 12 minutes
5. meanwhile , salt and pepper both sides of chicken
6. spray a large nonstick skillet with cooking spray and set over high heat
7. add chicken and sear 1 minute per side
8. add leek , carrots , mushrooms , garlic and herbs
9. cook 1 minute
10. add wine and simmer 1 minute , until liquid reduces to 1 / 4 cup
11. add broth and simmer 5 minutes
12. add chard to one side of pan and simmer 1 minute , until chicken is cooked through and greens are wilted
13. to serve , place chard in the bottom of 4 bowls
14. slice chicken into 5 pieces each and arrange atop chard
15. put potatoes and remaining vegetables around chicken and ladle remaining broth on top
demonstrations.review: I thought this was a really tasty dish. We cooked the chicken and carrot ahead of time like Toni suggested but the prep time was alot longer than I thought it would be. I thought the carrots were fine but everyone else wanted them a little bit softer. I also used spinach as that was the only thing I had on hand but I know that wouldn't have changed the flavor any. I really enjoyed this and it was quite different than what we  usually have. Will make again. Thanks for posting this.

target.recipe_text:
outrageously good broiled shrimp

i experienced the most wonderful broiled shrimp dinner at a local restaurant and created my version which is pretty darn close to their recipe. you will absolutely love these! prep time includes cleaning and butterflying shrimp.

1. butterfly shrimp and place on non-stick baking pan or line pan with aluminum foil for easier cleanup
2. brush shrimp with melted butter
3. sprinkle lightly with garlic salt
4. mix together bread crumbs , parmesan cheese and parsley
5. sprinkle lightly over shrimp
6. drizzle lightly with additional melted butter
7. broil until light brown
target.review: I would give this recipe 10 stars if I could. Amazing! Easy! Neat and Clean! I used panko and Parmigiano Reggiano, broiled them for four minutes and the taste was fabulous. This will be made over and over again at my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cheesy artichoke bread

i got this off a hellmann's coupon, i think. it is super duper easy & extremely good. i made this for the first time last week for friends,and they raved & raved. it's like artichoke dip already on the bread! i liked it a bit broiled on top.

1. mix mayo , garlic , cheese and chopped artichoke hearts well
2. spread on bread-- it makes enough to spread each side of the bread
3. bake at 375 for 20 minutes
4. slice& serve hot
demonstrations.review: This was a super tasty recipe as written. Once I make a recipe the way it is written, I try to healthy it up as much as possible. Here is what I did to this recipe and it still tasted fantastic.  I used vegenaise (or Hellmann's olive oil mayo) I only used 3/4 cup of parmesan cheese and then substituted 1 and 1/4 cup shredded Soy-Sation mozzarella style for the rest of the parmesan. (A lot fewer calories, no sat or trans fat, no cholesterol, and way less sodium) Then I finished the rest of the spread according to directions. I spread a real light layer of this mix onto the bread (just enough to help the spinach stick) and then stuck raw spinach leaves onto the bread. I coated the spinach leaves with the rest of the cheese mixture. I topped the bread with sliced cherry tomatoes and chopped black olives and baked as directed with the exception of broiling for the last few minutes. This was so yummy. Thank you for the idea.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
scallops on asparagus spears with wine reduction

this is a perfect light dish for spring or summer.  i used bay scallops and reduced the cooking time to 2 minutes per side.  an easy way to season the scallops is to put them in a plastic bag along with the coating mixture, and just shake the bag a few times.  if you need the old bay, dib's recipe #15562 is good.  this recipe's source is mccormick.

1. cook asparagus in boiling water in a large skillet 3 minutes or until crisp tender
2. drain on paper towels and set aside
3. keep warm
4. combine flour , old bay , and paprika in a shallow pan
5. stir to blend thoroughly
6. add scallops and coat with flour mixture
7. dry skillet with a paper towel , and place over medium-high heat until hot
8. add 2 tablespoons of butter
9. when butter is melted , add scallops and cook 4 minutes , turn and cook 4 minutes longer or until opaque in center
10. top asparagus with scallops and cover to keep warm
11. add wine and dill weed to pan residue
12. bring to a boil and cook 1-2 minutes or until liquid measures about 1 / 3 cup
13. remove from heat
14. stir in remaining 1 tablespoon butter and stir until completely melted
15. pour sauce evenly over scallops
16. garnish with lemon wedges , if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this recipe as is the first time and it was fantastic. The second time I made it, I added some Panko that I had ground to a powder, some grated parmesan and some turmeric to the flower/Old Bay mixture. I also used bay scallops and some tiger shrimp. PERFECT! This is so yummy. I absolutely love the sauce. Thank you so much for sharing the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
filet mignon with cherry balsamic reduction

while visiting los angeles, i found this recipe on a card that you can pick up at the local grocers.  this particular combination of meat and fruit had me intrigued so i brought it back for use at some later point.  filet mignon is pricey so this is certainly a special occasion food.  planning to serve it with roasted potatoes and maybe some nice asparagus.

1. heat olive oil in a small heavy metal or ceramic saucepan
2. add shallots and cook until they are soft and wilted , not browned
3. add garlic and stir for 30 seconds
4. add the wine , preserves , vinegar and cherries
5. increase the heat to bring the sauce to a light boil , stirring occasionally
6. let the sauce reduce to half the original amount
7. it should get thick and syrupy
8. when the sauce is almost done , preheat broiler
9. pat steaks dry and sprinkle salt and pepper on both sides of the steaks
10. broil to the desired level of doneness
11. for rare steaks: cook 2 1 / 2 minutes per side
12. for medium rare , cook 3 minutes per side
13. for medium , cook 3 1 / 2 minutes per side
14. for medium well , 4 minutes per side
15. to serve , serve steaks on a serving platter and sauce on the side
16. or you can spoon sauce over each steak served on individual plates
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic! I was afraid I was going to ruin my nice steaks, but the flavor was amazing. Great restaurant quality. I will use this at dinner parties to impress my friends. I used regular tenderloins and 1/3 cup dried cherries in place of the frozen. They soaked in the sauce and tasted wonderful. I will make this over and over. Thanks for the recipe Toni.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pasta with asparagus and balsamic reduction

my mother made this for a dinner party i loved it so much she gave me the recipe

1. bring water to boil cook pasta
2. mean while
3. place balsamic in a pan cook at med heat untill it reduces to a syrup
4. chopp asparagus in about 1 inch pices place in frying pan with red onion and a bit of the oil and a bit of water cover alow to stream untill asparagus changes dark green and onion is cooked
5. drain pasta
6. top with asparagus and red onion then drizzel balsamic over and top with lots of parm
7. add salt peper to taste
demonstrations.review: I was very surprised to find that I really liked this recipe a lot. I used 1/2 red onion and probably about 30 spears of asparagus because I like the veggies, but the recipe was great as is too. The reduction gave it a very nice flavor. (Just don't breath in through your nose over the stove top as you're boiling the reduction. That will clean out your sinuses.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
demonstrations.review: If you love chimies, you must try this. I like to top mine off with lettuce, tomatoes, and sour cream. There is just something about the hot and cold combination that I really like. As others have said, you will be so surprised how crunchy the tortillas turn out. I sprayed mine with butter flavored Pam and they turned out great. Thank you so much for this outstanding recipe.

target.recipe_text:
oven fried chicken chimichangas

a fast and healthier way to serve chimichangas than the traditional deep fried. these are very good, and you may dress them up to you own preference. i like to serve with green chile sauce sometimes instead of the picante sauce.

1. mix chicken , picante sauce or salsa , cumin , oregano , cheese and onions
2. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture in the center of each tortilla
3. fold opposite sides over filling
4. roll up from bottom and place seam-side down on a baking sheet
5. brush with melted margarine
6. bake at 400f for 25 minutes or until golden
7. garnish with additional cheese and green onion and serve salsa on the side
target.review: This was great!  I too did my own thing with it.  I added mexicorn, black beans, cilantro and a chipolte pepper.  Brushed with olive oil it was so crunchy.....served with a fresh salsa I made and sour cream.  Can't wait to make again and again YUMMY!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken wings with thai sweet   hot chili glaze

this came across my email today from a grilling website.  think it sounds delightful and easy too...so i am posting it for the zaar world tour to asia. give it a try!

1. make the glaze , in a small bowl , whisk the sauces , sesame oil and ginger together
2. trim excess skin from the edges of the wings
3. lightly brush or spray with the oil , and season with salt and pepper to taste
4. grill the chicken wings over direct medium heat until the skin begins to crisp , about 10 minutes , turning once or twice
5. brush the wings with the glaze and continue to grill until the meat is no longer pink at the bone , 8 to 10 minutes , turning and brushing with the glaze 2 or 3 times
6. serve warm
demonstrations.review: TRY THESE WINGS! These were really good!  I think I can stop going to my fav wing joint now!  I did toss some chopped garlic in and used hot chili paste (2 tablespoons caus I like it HOT)  I'm going to use this on chicken breast too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
thai chicken fried rice with basil   kao pad krapao

another delicious way to enjoy fried rice, fragrant with the heady aroma of basil!

1. in a wok or large skillet , stir-fry garlic in oil until golden
2. then add chilies and chicken and stir-fry until chicken is cooked
3. add rice , sugar , fish sauce , and soy sauce , and stir-fry , mixing gently
4. when well mixed , add shallots , basil leaves and cilantro
5. cook another minute or so , and serve
6. if you desire , serve with lime wedges , chile sauce , fish sauce , or soy sauce at the table
demonstrations.review: This was so good I almost finished the whole wok full! I did change it up a little. I used shrimp that I stir fried in chili sauce, added some peas carrots ginger and egg. Instead of shallots I had green onions on hand. And at the end I add just a little sesame oil and toasted sesame seeds on top. YUMMY!!! No more take out for me!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baja black beans  corn and rice

a south of the border blend of textures and flavors. serve hot as a main dish or a side dish with grilled meat or chicken.

1. cook brown rice
2. in a medium bowl , combine black beans , corn , tomatoes , onion , cilantro , jalapeno , lime juice , oil , salt , pepper and hot sauce
3. to serve , place a scoop of hot rice in a bowl or on a plate , top with a generous scoop of the black bean mixture
4. stir together before eating
demonstrations.review: This was pretty dam* good!  I did add extra spices and next time I think I will add avacado and maybe some mango!  It went really well on top of the enchiladas I made.  My son who is a hater of veggies LOVED it!  I will be making this again and again. Thanks Barb!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potato salad with chipotle peppers a man s salad

warning warning !! this tex mex salad is very spicy !!!  use your best judgment in how much chipotle peppers you use. taste as you add just don't dump them all in. each pepper has it's own heat level. yes us girls love it too! ;)

1. mix first 7 ingredients together
2. toss in remaining ingredients except 1 tablespoon bacon and salt and pepper
3. mix well
4. taste to see if you need to add salt and pepper
5. i myself like lots of pepper
6. top with bacon bits
7. chill& serve
demonstrations.review: I must say when I saw this recipe I couldn't figure out how these ingredients would go together.  Boy am I glad I tried it!  If I could rate it 10 stars I would.  I used low fat mayo, more chipolte (I like it hot!) no bacon, and I added some adobo spice, cumin and cayenne pepper.  I also added green chilis I had leftover in the fridge.  This is the last potato salad recipe I need.  Thanks alot Rita!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
batter dipped deep fried cauliflower

great appetizer or snack.  the breading is not too heavy.  the only time i've seen guys eat cauliflower during a football game is when it's this recipe.

1. preheat fryer oil to 375
2. place the beaten eggs , milk and salt in a shallow bowl
3. in a separate shallow bowl , mix together flour , cheese , garlic powder , thyme , oregano , paprika , cayenne , and pepper
4. place flowerets into egg mixture and toss to coat well
5. remove and place into flour mixture and toss to coat well
6. fry in batches for 4 - 6 minutes or until golden brown
7. drain on paper towels and lightly salt
8. serve w / dipping sauces such as marinara , ranch or blue cheese
demonstrations.review: I've made fried cauliflower before with the dry mixes in the store...boy does this blow those away!  Never again will I buy those.  I did change it up a little since I like things pretty spicy.  I added cayenne pepper drops to the egg mixture and used a ton of garlic and onion powders and put some Pampered Chef "Chipolte Rub" in the flour mix.  I also increased the parm & romano cheese blend to about 1/4 cup. I used cheddar cheese soup made with 1/2 a can of milk  to dip this in.  I had to pry myself away!  Thanks for a great recipe!!!

target.recipe_text:
almost heaven

this is a super cake, its both easy and fast to make.  great for large get- togethers!

1. mix the cake according to the package directions
2. bake cake in a 9 x 13 inch pan
3. while hot poke with skewer or chopstick and pour pineapple with the juice over the cake
4. mix the pudding , milk and cream cheese , beatnig until smooth
5. spread over pineapple layer
6. spread whipped topping over top
7. sprinkle with the nuts
8. refrigerate
target.review: I followed the directions exactly, and the cake came out very moist.  However, it lacked much flavor.  Perhaps using a different flavor of pudding mix would help? (I notice another reviewer suggested adding another flavor as well.)  I would only use 1/2 C chopped pecans instead of the full cup, as it seemed to be a bit much.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lisa s swirled chocolate chip cookies

this is a chocolate chip cookie recipe that my friend delynn's best friend gave to us. this is the recipe i use for normal chocolate chip cookies, but i've recently been making them with nestlé's new white & milk chocolate swirled chips. this is a yummy soft and delicious cookie!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix butter , granulated sugar , brown sugar , vanilla and eggs in a large bowl
3. stir in the flour , baking soda and salt
4. stir in 2 cups of swirled chocolate chips
5. drop dough by rounded measuring tablespoons , about 2-inches apart , onto ungreased cookie sheet
6. place the several of the reserved swirled chocolate chips on top of each cookie
7. bake 9 to 12 minutes or until light brown
8. cool slightly
9. remove from cookie sheet
10. cool on wire rack
demonstrations.review: This is the best chocolate chip cookie recipe I have ever tried!  It is the only one I will be using from now on.  I did not use the swirled chips in the first batch, just semi-sweet chips.  But I do plan to try the swirled chips in the future.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana quesadillas

these are delicious dessert quesadillas! an emeril recipe from his episode on tortillas. my young nephew loves these, but we did too! i serve drizzled with store-bought caramel sauce or chocolate sauce. this makes 10 servings, so you may want to scale down the recipe.

1. in the bowl of an electric mixer , beat the cream cheese until smooth
2. add the sugar and bananas , continue to beat until smooth
3. spread 1 / 4 cup of the filling over half of each tortilla
4. fold the other half over the filling and press slightly
5. place on a large plate and cover with plastic wrap
6. refrigerate until the filling sets , about 30 minutes
7. in a large saute pan , over medium heat , melt 1 tablespoon of the butter
8. pan-fry the tortillas in batches , 3 at a time , until golden on each side , about 2 minutes per side
9. repeat the above process with the remaining butter and filled tortillas
10. to serve , slice each filled tortilla into thirds
11. arrange the slices in the center of each serving plate
12. spoon a 1 / 4 cup of the warm caramel sauce over each plate
13. peel the bananas and slice 1 / 4-inch thick
14. garnish each plate with the sliced bananas and whipped cream , if desired
demonstrations.review: Yummy!  We had these for breakfast and they were a huge hit!  I prepared them the night before, and covered with plastic wrap and refrigerated overnight.  The next morning just heat up some margarine in the pan and fry them up.  Great taste!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best deviled eggs

these have been a favorite for years, when i serve these at my get togethers or make them for socials and large events they are always the first to go and everyone wants the recipe, i suggest to use large, extra large or even jumbo eggs for this, i like to make the yolk filling a day ahead and refrigerate this will blend the flavors --- for a nice presentation place each egg half in a colored paper muffin liner --- all ingredient amounts may be adjusted to taste --- see my recipe#259573

1. slice the eggs in half lengthwise
2. remove the yolks , and set whites aside
3. in a small bowl , mush yolks well with a fork , leaving no small lumps
4. add next 10 ingredients mix well to combine
5. spoon or pipe egg yolk mixture evenly into the whites
6. sprinkle with paprika
7. cover tightly with plastic wrap
8. store in the refrigerator until ready to serve
demonstrations.review: We enjoyed these at our Easter Brunch.  I used the ziploc bag method which made refilling the eggs a snap!  This is definately a new twist on the old-fashioned deviled egg recipe!  The only problem was that I didnt make enough, 24 didn't last long at all.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blueberry banana pie

a quick and easy, no cook recipe. it makes two pies, but don't worry, this will go so fast you will definitely need two pies!  you can also use strawberry pie filling on this.

1. mix cream cheese and sugar well
2. blend in cool whip
3. slice bananas and divide evenly in the bottom of the pie shells
4. spread cream cheese mixture on top of the bananas
5. spread 1 / 2 can of filling over each pie
6. cover and chill at least 2 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Don't let this super simple recipe fool you, the taste far exceeds the difficulty! I used an 8oz container of Cool Whip, since the size was not specified in the recipe. Also, since I didn't have any blueberry pie filling on hand I substituted a can of blueberries in light syrup for a lighter dessert. This pie is creamy and yummy and oh so easy, it's a definite keeper for our family!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby pacifiers  shower favors

i saw this on an episode of 

1. unwrap all the lifesavers
2. take one lifesaver and apply a thin layer of frosting around the inner hole
3. grab a jellybean and place one of the short , round ends in it , so the length of the jellybean is coming out of the hole
