4. flip the lifesaver over
5. on the other side , take the frosting and make a slightly thicker layer of frosting around the inner hole / center , and place another lifesaver perpendicular attaching edge of 2nd lifesaver to center of 1st lifesaver with jellybean attached to it
6. place on flat surface and allow to dry
7. after drying for 3-4 hours , thread curling ribbon through the hole of the 2nd lifesaver and tie in a knot
demonstrations.review: I bought the Jelly Belly Smoothies jelly beans, and used all of the peachish colored ones for the nipples.  They looked almost identical to authentic pacifiers!  I made up a batch of Royal Icing instead of the tube kind, and they held together perfectly.  Thank you for posting the recipe here, at my favorite recipe search site!

target.recipe_text:
extra creamy fluffy white frosting

this is a really great fluffy white frosting --- for the best results use only whipping cream for this --- this may easily be doubled and also freezes well.

1. in a bowl using an electric mixer , beat together the shortening , salt , vanilla and half of the icing sugar
2. beat until very smooth
3. add in whipping cream
4. beat well
5. add in remaining icing sugar to desired texture
6. beat until fluffy and creamy
target.review: I really loved this frosting!  I was asked to make a cake at the last minute and didn't have time to do my normal crumb coat first.  I made this thin enough to spread easily but still pipe shapes from a bag.  It was very easy to work with.  I used half & half since that is what I had on hand.  The taste of this frosting is superb - just sweet enough but not too sweet.  I will definitely make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
no bake light and fruity pie

my family loved this recipe.
 i got it from as jell-o book,along time ago.

1. dissolve gelatin completely in water , stirring about 3 minute
2. add ice cubes and stir constantly until gelatin is thickened about 2-3 minute remove any unmelted ice
3. using wire whisk , blend in whip cream then whip until smooth , fold in fruit and chill , if necessary until mixture is mound
4. spoon into crust
5. chill 2 hours garnish with additional fruit , if desired
demonstrations.review: Excellent recipe for a quick and easy pie.  I used lemon jello and didn't use the full 2c of ice because I didn't want to dilute the lemon "tang" too much. Everyone loved it. I will use this recipe again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bordelaise sauce

i love this recipe.  i'm posting it as i make it - i add more beef broth (not a huge wine fan, so i prefer the beef taste).  however, if you prefer a stronger wine flavor, just use 8 oz of beef broth instead (that was the original recipe amount).  i also put more green onions, but that's just because i love them!  really easy to make, too!  oh, and complete guess on the servings and cook/prep time.

1. in a small saucepan , combine wine , shallot , thyme , and bay leaf
2. bring to a boil
3. reduce heat and simmer briskly , uncovered , for 5 minutes or until reduced by one-half
4. remove bay leaf and discard
5. combine beef broth and cornstarch
6. stir into wine mixture
7. cook and stir until thickened and bubbly , then cook and stir 1 to 2 minutes more
8. add butter , lemon juice , parsley , and pepper
9. reduce heat and simmer , covered , for 5 minutes
10. serve over roasted potatoes or whatever meat you choose
11. i typically serve with chicken
demonstrations.review: I have to agree with the previous reviewer - this sauce was bland.  I was hoping for a very rich sauce to go over our fillets, but once on the steak, we couldn't even taste the sauce.  Garlic would be a good addition to try, but I'm not sure it would be enough.  It was super simple, I followed directions to a T, but I wouldn't use as much cornstarch the next time either.  It was too thick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white velvet cutout cookies

this is in response to a request. the recipe is from the taste of home magazine. it is a cream cheese cutout cookie.  frost with recipe #48001.

1. in a mixing bowl , cream butter and cream cheese until light and fluffy
2. add sugar , egg yolks and vanilla: mix well
3. gradually add flour
4. cover and chill 2 hours or until firm
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. roll out on a lightly floured surface to 1 / 4-inch thickness
7. cut into 3-inch shapes
8. place 1 inch apart on greased baking sheets
9. bake for 10-12 minutes or until set
10. cool for 5 minutes
11. remove to wire racks to continue cooling
12. frost after completely cool with white velvet buttercream cookie frosting
demonstrations.review:
These cookies deserve more than 5 starts!  They were easy to make, rolled and cut nicely and tasted delicious!!!  I followed the directions exactly.  Cooking time was perfect (some shapes took 10 min, others took 12).  I baked these on one of those air insulated pans and they came out perfect.  I tried one batch on a nonstick pan with re-usable parchment and they browned (but still tasted delish!) so I made the rest on the insulated pan.  I will definitely make these again, I'm anxious to try them with the recommended frosting (I used royal icing so it would flow).  Thank you TT for the fabulous recipe.

(BTW, I made these for both boys Christmas parties in their classes.  My boys said everyone gobbled the cookies and wanted more.)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
french toast sticks   oamc

i got this basic recipe from another site but changed it a little for my family.  the original recipe called for orange juice as the liquid instead of milk.  i also added the vanilla as we think it gives it a nice flavor.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. cut each slice of bread into 3 pieces to make sticks
3. texas toast is a very thick sliced bread about 3 / 4" thick
4. you could substitute french bread if texas toast is not available
5. in a bowl , mix together melted butter , eggs , sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and milk
6. beat well
7. dip sticks into egg mixture and place on a cookie sheet that has been sprayed with cooking spray
8. if there is any dip left , you can drizzle it over the sticks
9. bake for 25 minutes on middle rack of oven
10. turn halfway through baking time
11. allow to cool
12. flash freeze on cookie sheet , remove and place in a ziploc bag
13. to reheat: place 3 sticks on a microwave-safe plate and heat on high for 1 minute until warm
14. serve with syrup
demonstrations.review: We used to buy the frozen french toast sticks at the grocery store -- not any more!  These are soo good that not all of them make it to the freezer after a batch is made.  I add more vanilla, and my kids just devour them.  Thank you for the recipe.  My kitchen smells yummy while these are baking.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer battered fish  for fish n chips

i love fried fish.. always have. when dining out, nine times out of ten, i will order fish n'chips. it's getting to be very hard to find a restaurant that serves good fish n'chips anymore..so i just had to learn to make them myself.

1. sift together flour , salt , and paprika
2. stir in enough beer to make batter so it is barely thick enough to coat a spoon
3. usually somewhere between one and two cans
4. set batter aside while you heat your deep-fryer or deep pan of oil to 375 degrees
5. use a candy thermometer if you need to
6. peanut oil is best but any vegetable oil will do
7. cut the cod fillets diagonally into 2 inch wide strips , and remove any pin bones from fish
8. lightly coat fish in flour and shake off excess
9. this will allow batter to stick to fish
10. when oil is heated , dip fish in batter , let excess drip off , then fry fillets 2 or 3 at a time until golden brown
11. drain on paper towels
12. serve with fries and tartar sauce
demonstrations.review: Very good!  I followed the recipe closely but not exact.  I only used 1 beer and didnt dredge.  Tasted excellent coming straight out of the fryer but didn't hold in the oven well - my fault, not Bethany's.  I will make this again and I will follow the directions exactly next time.  We used up the leftover batter for onion rings and this was also excellent.

target.recipe_text:
sunday dinner roast chicken

delicious and moist, this chicken makes a beautiful centerpiece on any dinner table, and is incredibly easy to prepare.

1. preheat oven to 300 degrees
2. clean chicken cavity and rinse thoroughly
3. place in a large roasting pan
4. place half of chopped onion inside the of the chicken , and other half around chicken as a bed
5. add chopped potatoes to the bed around the chicken
6. drizzle olive oil over chicken and vegetables
7. season entire dish with rosemary , onion powder , salt and pepper
8. rub herbs into the chicken , evenly coating and pushing some of it under the skin on the breast
9. bake chicken for approximately 2 hours
10. rub butter over skin of chicken and bake another few minutes or until chicken is done
target.review: This was excellent. I thought it would be too strong a taste with 2 tbsp rosemary, so I used 1 tbsp instead. It probably would have been even better using 2 as you suggest. I also added two whole garlic cloves inside the cavity with the onion. I will be making this again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spinach baked with three cheeses

another very easy and yummy side dish/first course, this can be put together in advance and refrigerated until ready to bake.

1. preheat oven to 350^f
2. butter an 11x7x2 inch baking dish
3. combine the first 7 ingredients in a large bowl and set aside
4. in a large pot , heat the oil over medium heat
5. add the spinach and saute about 3 minutes , until wilted and juices evaporate
6. drain well
7. arrange spinach over the bottom of the prepared dish
8. sprinkle with the cheese mixture and bake until heated through , about 20 minutes
9. preheat broiler and broil spinach dish until the cheese is golden brown on top , watching closely so not to burn , about 2 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very, very good. I blanched the spinach in water instead of sauteing it in olive oil. I used the whole egg (well beaten)as a result of not reading the recipe properly. Even so, this turned out great. Thanks for sharing a really easy to make and tasty recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s buttery apple cake

a family favorite!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. grease a 9 round baking dish with butter
3. in a large frying pan melt the butter
4. add the apples and fry until tender , 5-10 minutes , over medium to medium-high heat , moving the apples around to be sure they are all coated in the butter and watching them so that they do not burn
5. while apples are frying , in a bowl stir together flour , salt and baking powder and spices
6. in a separate bowl , whisk together sugar , 2 whole eggs , 1 egg yolk , vanilla extract and lemon zest until creamy and well mixed
7. stir apples with the melted butter into egg and sugar mixture and mix quickly so that the hot butter does not scramble the eggs
8. once apples are covered , add the flour mixture and mix to coat apples
9. spoon into 9" round buttered baking dish
10. bake 30-35 minutes or until cake forms a brown crust on top
11. let cool in pan for 5 minutes
12. invert , then flip back over , apple-side-up , and let cool completely before serving
demonstrations.review: I made this in the early morning. The plan was to serve it later, after dinner. The house smelled so good and it looked so scrumptious when it came out of the over, that it became breakfast! We ate half the cake in one sitting, with lots of coffee. Thanks for sharing a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker london broil

this is such an easy recipe. it's one of our family favourites.

1. place meat in the bottom of the slow cooker
2. if necessary , slice meat to make it fit
3. in a medium bowl , mix together mushroom and tomato soup
4. pour mixture over beef
5. sprinkle dry onion soup mix over top
6. cover and cook on low for 8 to 10 hours
demonstrations.review: Simply delicious! I made this with 2.5 lbs of london broil, all in one piece. I used 3/4 of the onion soup packet. I cooked it on the stove, in a dutch oven. I brought it to a boil, covered it and reduced the heat to simmer, for 3 hours. Then I added a sliced onion, two peeled and cubed potatoes and about 1 1/2 cups of baby carrots. I cooked it for an additional two hours, on simmer. I removed the meat, sliced it up and returned it to the pot. I served it with brown rice and some sauteed green beans. Thanks for a recipe that I will use again and again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
karythopita  walnut spice cake

a favorite any time, this greek dessert is also a christmas tradition for many families.

1. make the syrup: in a saucepan , add all syrup ingredients and bring to a boil , stirring well
2. reduce heat and allow to boil gently for 10 minutes
3. set aside to cool
4. beat egg whites , salt , and water to the firm peak stage
5. preheat oven to 340f
6. in a mixing bowl , beat the egg yolks , sugar , cinnamon , and ground cloves very well until creamy and smooth
7. in a separate bowl , mix the baking soda , baking powder , and flour , and stir in to the mixture
8. add grated orange peel and juice , brandy , breadcrumbs , and walnuts
9. finally , and carefully , fold in the beaten egg whites
10. lightly grease a 13x9 inch baking pan with butter , pour in the batter , and bake at 340f for 40 minutes
11. cake is done when a knife inserted into the middle comes out dry
12. spoon the cooled syrup evenly over the hot cake
13. sprinkle with walnuts mixed with a little cinnamon
14. allow to cool before serving
15. make sure the syrup is completely cooled before adding to cake
16. if necessary , refrigerate for a few minutes
demonstrations.review: Good cake. A little more effort than usual for a cake, but well worth it. I cut back on the cloves because of personal preference. I will be making this again. This is really good with a cup of hot tea. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: I spread the mayonnaise all over the 6 bone-in chicken thighs I used. I mixed the other ingredients together with 1 c panko bread crumbs and then covered the chicken pieces with the crumb mixture. I baked the chicken on a rack over the baking sheet, and all the oil from the mayonnaise and the chicken fat ran off. The chicken was very tender, moist and delicious. Thanks for sharing the recipe. It was a hit with all the family.

target.recipe_text:
how to make french fries

this is the beginner's step-by-step guide to making fried french fries. i thought there might be a few people out there who would like excrutiating detail, so here you go!

1. heat oil in large skillet on medium-high heat
2. scrub potatoes
3. peel them if you like
4. stand each potato on end , and slice in half
5. slice each half in half again
6. lay the quarters on top of each other , and cut into thin strips
7. if you can't get the quarters to lay together , just slice each one individually
8. no biggie
9. check to see if your oil is hot enough by dipping the end of one fry in it
10. if the oil bubbles up and makes noise , the oil is ready
11. put about a quarter of the fries in at a time
12. cook until they turn the color that you like
13. some people like soft fries , other crispy
14. go with what looks good to you
15. while the fries are cooking , get a plate and place about four paper towels on it
16. when the fries are done , put them on the paper towels to drain
17. put the skillet back on the heat , and let it heat back up
18. put the next batch of fries in the oil
19. salt the finished batch of fries
20. add more paper towels on top of the fries
21. eat and enjoy !
target.review: I liked the detailed instructions, great for new cooks. If you like a crunchier fry just cook until lightly brown..drain on paper towel and freeze. After they freeze, remove and fry again. Thanks Amanda

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mrs allen s date loaf

this was my playmate's mother's recipe oh how i loved this date loaf! (doris eppinger --neeallen). after school if we were lucky we'd get a slice. i hope it tastes as good now as it did 63 years ago.

1. heat oven to 350f , lightly grease a loaf pan
2. mix the dates , butter& boiling water , set aside& cool
3. when cooled mix in the beaten egg& sugar
4. mix the flour , baking soda& salt together
5. add dry ingredients to the batter
6. add nuts and vanilla , blend well
7. pour into the prepared loaf pan
8. bake in 350f oven for 50-60 minutes or until a wooden skewer comes out clean when inserted in the center
demonstrations.review: I made this bread a few days before Thanksgiving and it was perfect..the longer it sits the better it gets. I kept it in a ziplock bag and it got better every day. Very easy to make. I used brown sugar instead. Awesome..thanks for the recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
martha washington candy

paraffin wax (gulf wax) is a food-grade, indigestible wax used commonly in the past to seal jams/jellies.  these days, it's used to help chocolate to be easily handled.  if you'd prefer not to use that ingredient, substitute chocolate-flavored bark (confectioner's candy coating) for the chocolate/wax mixture.

1. cream butter , sweetened condensed milk and vanilla
2. add confectioner's sugar , mix well
3. add pecans , mix well
4. roll into 1 inch balls and put in freezer for 30 minutes
5. melt chocolate chips and paraffin in double boiler over low heat , until melted
6. dip ball into chocolate mixture , one piece at a time , holding with a tooth pick
7. drop on wax paper
8. store in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I've been making this same recipe for over 40 years. I split the basic fondant recipe into thirds. I make 1/3 with pecan pieces, 1/3 with maraschino cherries and the other 1/3 with orange zest. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baby ruth bars  no bake

i went looking for these on the net when i couldn't find one of my favorite candy bars locally. these are almost as good as the originals!

1. butter a 9" x 13" baking pan
2. heat sugars , syrup , and peanut butter in a heavy saucepan
3. mix until smooth
4. combine cornflakes , chocolate chips , and peanuts
5. pour peanut butter mixture over the cornflake mixture and mix well
6. press into the bottom of the prepared pan
7. allow to cool before cutting into bars
demonstrations.review:
I make candy for Christmas for about two weeks and love the no bake recipes. I saw this one and had to try it. 
I had to laugh while making it because I noticed mine getting way too thick right off the bat and remembered the lower rating against all the other good reviews. I removed it from heat and started with another pan, but added 2 tablespoons of butter first and then mixed what I had started into the new pan.I think I might know what happened to their batch. I know there is a big difference in peanut butter and this needs the really moist type. If your peanut butter is somewhat dry, melt one or two tablespoons of butter in pan before starting. Don't let the mixture come to a boil, just heat until melted,but remember this mixture will be thick.
I used 3/4 white and 1/4 cups of dark syrup. I added 1 1/2 cups of salted peanuts. With buttered hands I pressed the top down. I then melted chocolate bark and frosted the top of the 9 x 13. I let the chocolate set then cut into bars. I sent this to work with my husband and the phone rang off the hook all morning with people wanting the recipe.  This is also my new personal favorite of all the candy I make. 
Totally awesome recipe Mirj...Thanks soooo much for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate sheet cake

this is our favorite chocolate cake. it is rich and moist. note: if you don't have the buttermilk on hand, put about 1 teaspoon of vinegar into 1/2 cup milk and let it sit for 15-20 minutes. ***note: if you don't have the butter flavor crisco, just increase the 1/2 cup butter to 1 cup of butter and omit the crisco.  i've made it both ways and it is great either way.

1. cake: stir first four ingredients together
2. put butter , crisco and water in saucepan and bring to a rapid boil
3. pour over flour mixture
4. add eggs and buttermilk that have been mixed with baking soda
5. add vanilla and beat until well mixed
6. bake in a greased cake pan
7. bake at 350 for approximately 25 minutes
8. while cake is still hot , frost it
9. frosting: bring butter , cocoa and milk to a boil
10. add to powdered sugar
11. mix well
12. add vanilla and pecans
13. mix well
14. spread on hot cake
demonstrations.review:
I have been making this cake for over 40 years.
I make at least one cake a week and try to vary the types I make so family and friends won't get tired of the same thing. 
When we get chocolate hungry, this cake always comes to mind first. There is never any of this left!! I use a cookie sheet pan to bake it in. I don't add the cinnamon, simply because I don't like the after taste it leaves in the cake. I always use the full one cup of butter instead of 1/2 crisco, and sometimes add instant coffee granuals or black coffee for that old fashion taste of home.
Thanks for posting this all time great standard!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon blossoms  paula deen

these mini cupcakes are packed with lemon flavor.  a paula deen recipe.

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. spray miniature muffin tins with vegetable oil cooking spray
3. combine the cake mix , pudding mix , eggs and oil and blend well with an electric mixer until smooth , about 2 minutes
4. pour a small amount of batter , filling each muffin tin half way
5. bake for 12 minutes
6. turn out onto a tea towel
7. make the glaze while the cakes are baking
8. sift the sugar into a mixing bowl
9. add the lemon juice , zest , oil , and 3 tablespoons water
10. mix with a spoon until smooth
11. with fingers , dip the cupcakes into the glaze while they're still warm , covering as much of the cake as possible , or spoon the glaze over the warm cupcakes , turning them to completely coat
12. place on wire racks with waxed paper underneath to catch any drips
13. let the glaze set thoroughly , about 1 hour , before storing in containers with tight-fitting lids
demonstrations.review:
I couldn't tell you how many times I have made these and everyone loves them. I like making them with orange cake mix, using orange juice, my family is especially fond of the pineapple ones I make using pineapple cake mix and the juice from crushed pineapple. I always add the zest to the wonderful glaze..I think the oil in the galze is what sets this recipe apart!!
Thanks for posting.

target.recipe_text:
baked mustard chicken

something easy and delicious. you can serve it either hot or cold. goes great in chicken salad.

1. brush chicken with mustard and dredge in bread crumbs
2. place in a 13- x 9- x 2-inch baking dish
3. combine margarine , lemon juice , and wine
4. drizzle 1 tablespoon over each piece of chicken and pour remainder in dish
5. cover and bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
6. remove cover , sprinkle with paprika , and bake an additional 15 minutes
target.review:
Loved it!  Here are my variations, which I think are a little different from those already posted:

To avoid the slippery/soggy crust problem suffered by a recent poster, I omitted the butter, poured the lemon/wine mixture into the baking dish instead of over the chicken, breaded the chicken only on the top side and sprayed the breaded chicken pieces generously with olive oil to aid browning.  This worked great:  the chicken was both poached and browned!  I had no open bottle of wine, so used madeira, and my standby breading:  50/50 breadcrumbs and grated parmesan, with a little garlic.  These  flavors all worked great together and my whole family enjoyed the meal.  Finally, I think an hour is too long, the meat reached 165 in under 40 minutes in my oven.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red coconut chicken curry

this dish can be quite hot and spicy depending on the brand of curry paste used.  the variety in the pouch (instead of the jar or can) tend to be milder.  for those sensitive to spicy food, reduce the curry paste to 2 teaspoons.  in a pinch, use mild indian curry paste. serve over rice.
from canadian living magazine.

1. cut chicken into bite-size pieces
2. in a wok or large skillet , heat 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat , stir fry chicken in batches , until browned , about 3 minutes , transfer to plate , set aside
3. add remaining oil to wok , stir fry eggplant , onion , garlic , ginger and curry paste until onion is softened , about 3 minutes
4. pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil , reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes
5. reduce heat to simmer , add fish sauce , sugar , lime rind and lime juice , salt , peppers and chicken and any accumulated juices
6. cover and cook stirring occasionally until slightly thickened and peppers are tender , about 10 minutes
7. add basil and coriander , and serve
demonstrations.review: Oh my, this was good!  And I even forgot to add the basil and coriander at the end.  Other than that, I made it exactly as written, except that, having no fish sauce, I added a tiny sliver of indonesian shrimp paste (trassi) instead.Thanks, Daisygirl.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
babganoush hummus pasta  vegan

this is a rachel ray recipe that is actually vegan!  i was channel surfing, stopped on 30 minute meals, and could not wait to try this easy, hearty, healthy, delicious vegan meal.  try crumbling soy feta on top.  serve with a greek salad and warm pita bread.

1. heat a large pot of water to a boil , salt water and cook pasta to al dente
2. while water boils heat extra-virgin olive oil in a deep skillet over medium heat
3. add garlic and cook 1 to 2 minutes then add the eggplant and chick peas and stir to coat
4. season the chick peas and eggplant with cumin , coriander , red pepper flakes , salt and pepper , cover with lid and allow to cook for about 10 minutes
5. stir in lemon zest and continue to cook until eggplant has broken down , about another 5 to 10 minutes
6. remove the vegetables from the pan and place into a blender or food processor
7. add the vegetable stock and tahini paste and process until a sauce consistency
8. add the sauce back to the saucepan and heat over low heat until ready to serve
9. add a ladle of starchy cooking liquid to the sauce , drain pasta and toss pasta with chickpea-eggplant sauce 1 minute then top with parsley and pine nuts
10. place into a serving dish
demonstrations.review: My whole family enjoyed this dish, and I will definitely make it again.  It's a nice change of pace; I don't use Middle Eastern flavors very often, but they are so good!  Quick and easy prep, too.  I reduced the olive oil by half to cut the fat a bit and did not miss it.  The only negative is the appearance on the plate:  greenish tan sauce over tan pasta is not exactly a mouthwatering sight.  My advice is focus on the delicious smell and don't forget the parsley!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
maple orange chicken with acorn squash and sweet potatoes

from food tv show "quick fix meals with robin miller".  a slow cooker meal that has a lot of flavor and color.  a complete meal in one pot.

1. place squash and sweet potatoes and leeks in the slow cooker
2. season chicken all over with salt and black pepper and place on top of vegetables in slow cooker
3. in a medium bowl , combine orange marmalade and remaining ingredients
4. pour mixture over chicken and vegetables
5. cover and cook on low for 4 hours or on high for 2 hours
demonstrations.review: I made this pretty much as written, except that I braised the leeks and chicken in a bit of oil before putting them in the pot, for softer flavor and because I hate that pasty white look of poached chicken.  I used breast, not thighs, because that's what I had, and added them to the pot with 2 hours left to go.  Next time I'll use thighs; they are definitely better for slow cooking.  I'll also use butternut squash for ease of peeling:  no discernable flavor difference to me.  The sauce was great, I served with brown rice and it was a big hit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
15 minute pasta combo

just like the name implies, this meal is fast, easy and fresh tasting. it's perfect when you want a quick, delicious one-pot meal without heating up the oven on those hot summer days. just add a crisp green salad and a glass of iced tea and dinner is ready in no time.

1. cook spaghetti until tender
2. drain
3. in same pan , heat the italian salad dressing over medium heat
4. add cooked pasta
5. toss to coat well
6. add tomatoes , turkey and parmesan cheese
7. toss lightly and serve
demonstrations.review: This is a weeknight winner for sure.  I made the following changes: Used whole wheat pasta, used more pasta in proportion to the dressing (I used a whole 13.25 oz. box of Ronzoni Healthly Harvest rotini), used halved grape tomatoes unseeded, and added 8oz baby spinach at the end, mixed till just wilted for the color and extra vitamins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
healthy wheat berry and shrimp salad with thai vinaigrette

low fat, low calorie salad with interesting tastes. fish sauce, a table condiment from southeast asia, is made from salted fish and aromatics. quite pungent, it mellows wonderfully when combined with other ingredients. look for it in the asian aisle of most supermarkets. 3 pts per serving.

1. place the wheat berries in a medium pot , cover with 3 inches of water , and bring to a simmer over medium-high heat , stirring once or twice
2. cover , reduce heat to medium-low , and simmer until tender , about 50 minutes
3. drain and cool to room temperature
4. meanwhile , rinse out the cooking pot , fill halfway with water , and bring to a boil over high heat
5. add the shrimp , reduce the heat , and simmer until the shrimp are pink and firm , about 2 minutes
6. drain in a colander set in the sink and refresh under cool water
7. roughly chop the shrimp
8. to make the dressing , whisk the lime juice , fish sauce and brown sugar together in a small bowl until the sugar dissolves
9. toss the wheat berries , shrimp , cucumber , radishes , basil and mint in a salad bowl
10. pour the prepared dressing over the salad and toss to coat
11. if desired , cover and refrigerate for up to 3 days
12. points value per serving : 3
13. yields 4 servings
demonstrations.review: I've recently discovered wheat berries, and my family loves them so I prowl around frequently looking for different recipes.  This was a winner; it has a great combination of flavors, it's really healthy and it's easy to make! I did do some tweaking, for starters I doubled the recipe to feed my family of four (two teenage boys). We had some leftover, but not much.  To the dressing I added 2 Tablespoons of canola oil and at least that much honey (was out of brown sugar).  Without these, I thought the dressing tasted thin and sharp but with them it was balanced and still low fat.  And I used a pound of shrimp.  Thanks, Kasha, great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
rotel spicy skillet chicken

found this recipe in a magazine and it looked wonderful so i decided to try it and it's absolutely great.

1. in large skillet , cook chicken in hot oil until brown
2. add onion and garlic , saute until tender , about 5 minutes
3. add mushrooms and rotel tomatoes
4. reduce heat
5. cover and simmer 25 minutes , stirring occasionally until meat is done
6. sprinkle with cheese
7. replace cover and heat until cheese melts
8. serve over rice
target.review: This recipe was really good, but I also added some Adobo seasoning to the chicken while it was cooking, one yellow pepper and Monterrey Jack Cheese w/Jalapeno's instead of the Mozzarella. I did leave the mushrooms b/c my husband doesn't eat them. I will make this again! Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker chicken in sour cream sauce  crock pot

this is a family favorite. we like to serve this over noodles but i am sure rice would be yummy too. i have also made this in the oven and with boneless chicken breasts and shrimp.

1. combine the first four ingredients and rub over chicken
2. place chicken in crock pot
3. combine the soup , sour cream , broth and mushrooms
4. pour over chicken
5. cover and cook on low for 4-8 hours or until a meat thermometer reads 170
6. thicken the sauce if desired
demonstrations.review: This was good, I made a couple of changes though. I took the chicken out and removed it from the bone once it was finished cooking and placed it back in the crock pot. I used 2 cans of cream of mushroom soup in stead of the one. I omitted the mushrooms b/c my husband doesn't like them if he can see them. I also cooked egg noodles and mixed in with it along with frozen peas. Once it was finished kinda tasted like chicken stroganoff.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jolean s cheese potato   smoked sausage casserole

this was another one of our favorites in the 70's  very inexpensive and very easy to make.  just recently found this recipe hand-written by my mom, and the warm feelings flood back to me, because this was a true favorite in our house.  little did i know that she was on such a tight budget, yet made things like this that we all loved!!  note:  the meat that was used in this recipe always varied, according to whatever we had available at the time.

1. cut skinless smoked sausage in half , lengthwise , and then chop into 1 / 2 inch "half moon" cuts
2. cook in a frying pan for about 15 minutes , turning frequently to slightly brown
3. meanwhile , put cooked & diced potatoes in 2 quart casserole
4. add cooked meat and give it a gentle toss
5. mix all remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat until warm , melted and smooth
6. pour white / cheese sauce over potatoes and meat
7. sprinkle shredded sharp cheddar cheese on top , and then sprinkle paprika evenly over the top
8. bake in preheated 350f oven for 35-45 minutes
9. hot dogs , sliced into 1 / 2-inch slices or 1 / 2 lb
10. ham diced into 1 / 2-inch dices or 12 oz
11. can of spam diced into 1 / 2-inch dices , instead of the smoked sausage
demonstrations.review: This was very good! It was very easy to make and my whole family loved it. The only thing I changed was I only had 1/2 of a 1/2lb of velveeta so I added in some cream cheese also (awesome). I will be making this one again. Thanks

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoked sausage  green beans  and potatoes

simple, but very good. i think this may be a midwest, us kind of thing. super fast and easy too! we serve the potatoes to the side, with some butter on them. i don't recommend the low-fat varieties with this, they don't seem to boil well.

1. cut kielbasa into bite sized pieces
2. in large pot , combine all ingredients
3. add water to barely cover ingredients
4. cook over medium heat until potatoes are done
5. serve with a slotted spoon so the water can drain away , or drain the whole batch
demonstrations.review: This was wonderful. I did cook the green beans separate from the potatoes and the sausage because i don't like the way they taste straight from the can. I added them in once the potatoes were close to being done. Very good and quick meal on a cold winter day.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stroganoff

this recipe was used by both my mother and my mother-in-law. it's been a favorite of our families for years, and is both easy and delicious.

1. brown beef in large skillet
2. add onions and cook until onions are translucent
3. drain grease
4. stir in condensed soup , then garlic powder , salt , and pepper
5. allow to simmer until all other parts of meal are prepared
6. minutes before it's time to serve , stir in the sour cream completely and heat through
7. serve over egg noodles
demonstrations.review: Alright, I used leftover london broil from the night before. I cooked it with the onion and added fresh garlic. I used 1/2 c of sour cream and 4oz of cream cheese and about 1/3 cup of milk (i am guessing didn't really measure) along with the cream of mushroom soup. I added some worcestershire sauce, salt and pepper. This turned out wonderful and my husband loved it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mean guy s general tso s chicken

this is an adoptee.  i have made it many many times and want to be able to help people out when they make it!  one of the best i've ever had.  takes some time, but oh so worth it.   good eats ;-)

1. in a large bowl , thoroughly blend the 1 / 2 cup of cornstarch and the eggs
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. if the mixture is too thick , add some vegetable oil to separate the pieces
4. in a small bowl , prepare the sauce mixture by combining the 2 tsp cornstarch with the wine , vinegar , sugar and soy sauce
5. first-stage frying: heat 1-2 inches of peanut oil in a wok to medium-high heat
6. fry the chicken in small batches , just long enough to cook the chicken through
7. remove the chicken to absorbent paper and allow to stand
8. second-stage frying: leave a tablespoon or two of the oil in the wok
9. add the pepper pods to the oil and stir-fry briefly , awakening the aroma but not burning them
10. return the chicken to the wok and stir-fry until the pieces are crispy brown
11. the general's favorite sauce: add the sauce-mixture to the wok , tossing over the heat until the sauce caramelizes into a glaze
12. serve immediately
13. serves 4 , along with steamed broccoli and rice
demonstrations.review: My husband and I made this together last night. I am only giving a four star rating because we didn't use the sauce. We had never attempted General Tso's before and it really wasn't hard to do. We omitted the chili pods b/c we just didn't have any and used red pepper flake. We deep fried the chicken and we used a bottled General Tso's Stir Fry sauce I bought at Target (Archer Farms Brand...Also the best Teriyaki) we added chili oil to the final product it was awesome! Served with Fried rice and Spring Rolls. Perfect at home Chinese meal.

target.recipe_text:
grilled salmon steak

this is so good. the salmon doesn't taste fishy.  i got this recipe in new brunswick.

1. mix all ingredients
2. place 4 salmon steaks in a shallow pan and pour the marinate over
3. marinate 30 minutes or 1 hour in refrigerator , turning once
4. place fish on grill 4 inches from heat
5. grill 5 to 7 minutes on each side or until fish flakes easily when tested with a fork and pulls away from the central bone
6. baste with marinate during cooking
target.review: I didn't have time to marinate this for long enough so the flavour was great but I believe it would even have been better had I marinated it for the full time suggested. I took a photo and the reason that my salmon appears to be blushing is that I grabbed red onions instead of white ones so the colour of the sauce is somewhat pinkish. I used boned, filleted salmon steaks and mostly followed the recipe to the letter, but instead of turning these over during the cooking time, I placed them in a small,  shallow, metal baking tray, put it as close to the pre-heated grill/broiler (in the oven) as I dared and cooked it without turning  for 12 minutes. It was completely cooked and we really liked the flavours... DH says a smidge more tabasco next time please... and there will be many more next times for this recipe at our dinner table believe me :) The flavours were there but subtle, it was salmon with a hint of a little extra... no it didn't smell fishy either, and the only negative I could really find was that I just wish my piece of salmon had been a little bigger LOL. Please see my rating system: an excellent 5 stars. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pina coladas

using the coconut sorbet instead of the traditional coconut cream decreases the fat to just 1g per serving.  don't let the 4 hours scare you away.  it's just the time spent freezing the pineapple juice in an ice cube tray.  make the cubes ahead of time and you can enjoy this in minutes.

1. freeze pineapple juice in ice cube trays for 4 hours , or until solid
2. in a blender , add the frozen pineapple juice , 1 cup ice cubes , coconut sorbet , run and lime juice
3. blend until smooth
4. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Don't tell DH, but the only place to get coconut sorbet was the local  specialty Italian Ijs shop so I nipped in and got a few small scoops... (I normally don't like strong coconut flavour much and DH adores it, but in this case the pineapple and rum and lime balance things out very well indeed, much to my surprise) Therefore don't skimp on the pineapple and lime.  I also used fresh pineapple because I had it to hand, and the juice attachment on my new blender does the job nicely. (less processed sugar than in commercially juice) and easy as well.  I don't have dark rum so used white rum instead. Please see my Rating System: 4 wonderful stars for my very first Pina colada... very nice indeed. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic and sapphires sauted brussels sprouts  try this

adopted from recipe zaar.  i noticed that there was no garlic added to the recipe, so i've updated to include the garlic.  this is very very good.

1. over medium heat , saut the garlic in the butter for about a minute then add the brussels sprouts and saute until wilted , about 7 minutes
2. we like to cook until they get a bit brown which took about 10 minutes
3. add salt and pepper to taste
4. add cream and serve
5. feel free to adjust proportions to suit your taste !
demonstrations.review: Oohhh... lovely indeed! DH and I demolished these! In fact I made these ages ago, and have made them multiple times from a printout of the recipe I'd made, and only discovered that I'd forgotten to review it when I misplaced the printout. Luckily the photo with the recipe number was still in my computer. This was SO easy to make and wonderfully tasty. Please see my rating system: an excellent 5 stars for dressed up sprouts that are all out to impress and do !

demonstrations.recipe_text:
marinierte toamten   marinated tomatoes

this is a great recipe, very refreshing.

1. slice tomatoes and put in serving bowl
2. combine remaining ingredients and pour over tomatoes
3. toss lightly
4. chill for at least 1 hour before serving
demonstrations.review: We liked this too.. tasty and refreshing and very very edible ;) I had a huge plate... sadly I think that our watery dutch glasshouse tomatoes let it down a little (not the fault of the recipe of course), I will have to look for some organic ones to make this again with. I am going to be writing this into my handwritten family cookbook and making it often as it definiately a wonderful dish for a hot summer's day. Please see my rating system, a wonderful 4 stars ! Thanks :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast parsnips with soy  honey and orange

parsnips are at their best near christmas and there are so many wonderful things you can do with them.

1. preheat oven to 200c / 400f
2. pour oil into a roasting pan and put in oven to heat
3. add parsnips to hot oil , season if desired and roast for 20 minutes
4. mix honey , soy , juice and zest
5. add to parsnips and toss to coat
6. return to oven for another 10 minutes until caramelised
7. serve with and remaining juices poured over
demonstrations.review:
Our opinions were divided on this recipe, but firstly a small note about the orange: my SiL and BiL have just returned from Greece where they signed on the dotted line to own the wee holiday home that they have been holidaying in every year for approx 18 years...  and this orange came straight from a tree in their new Greek garden: it was seedless, sweet and juicy.
Dh isn't fond of fruit in meals, and LOVED parsnips this way! said he would eat oranges far more often if they were like this! ... I love fruit in meals but found the orange overpowering, so personal taste and preferences are obviously very subjective. Please see my rating system: By myself I would have given this a 3 and DH would have given it a 5 so we have opted for the middle road and you have a great 4 star recipe that DH had already requested that I make again. With oranges aplenty both in the supermarket and from a family greek garden, I definiatly will be making this for him often in the future. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rachel s apricot fudge biscuit slice  unbaked

this comes from my very good friend rachel and is very easy to make.  be warned though that it is very tempting to eat the lot all on ones own....lol

1. crush the biscuits and mix with the chopped apricots
2. in a pot melt the condensed milk , butter and brown sugar together
3. mix with the biscuits & apricots
4. press into a greased sponge roll / slice tin
5. refrigerate and cut when cold
demonstrations.review: Jo, this recipe is totally identical to one given to me by a New Zealand friend... her only difference is the optional adding of chocolate chips at the end once the main mix has cooled just slightly, which  I did since I had some, (choc chips are hard to get here in the Netherlands, I only have them occasionally). These are a favourite in my DH's family and since everyone is coming around for my son's 2nd Birthday party tomorrow I made this becuase I know it will please the crowds. I line my dish with plastic wrap and then press the mixture in, once it's been in the fridge and firm, all you have to do is to cut it down the middle first and gently ease it out on both ends.. peel off the plastic wrap and cut it easily into squares on a cutting board. Great recipe, definiate crowd pleaser and one I make over and over and over, both with the choc chips if I have them, and without :) Thanks !!!

target.recipe_text:
blueberry coffee cake muffins

from ina garten (the barefoot contessa family style cookbook).

1. preheat the oven to 350f
2. place 16 paper liners in muffin pans
3. in the bowl of an electric mixer fitted with the paddle attachment , cream the butter and sugar until light and fluffy , about 5 minutes
4. with the mixer on low speed , add the eggs one at a time , then add the vanilla , sour cream , and milk
5. in a separate bowl , sift together the flour , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
6. with the mixer on low speed add the flour mixture to the batter and beat until just mixed
7. fold in the blueberries with a spatula and be sure the batter is completely mixed
8. scoop the batter into the prepared muffin pans , filling each cup just over the top , and bake for 25 to 30 minutes , until the muffins are lightly browned on top and a cake tester comes out clean
target.review: At first I ate one of these right out of the oven and wasn't crazy over them, but I ate one when completely cooled and I think these are one of the best blueberry muffins, I have had.  I shared them with people at work and baked a batch for the 4th of July and everyone liked these.  It's a keeper.  Ina Garten has some really great recipes. I've tried a few already.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate orange fudge

this is so easy and yet it is probably the best fudge i've ever had. i usually omit the pecans. my niece used this recipe, substituting 3-4 drops peppermint extract for the orange zest, and earned a blue ribbon at the county fair. even my 12-16 year old 4h girls had no problems making it. note: make sure you use fresh orange zest. dried will make the fudge bitter. also make sure you don't get any of the bitter white part of the rind when you are zesting your orange.

1. line a 8x8x2-inch baking pan with lightly buttered waxed paper or aluminum foil
2. set aside
3. melt chocolate chips with condensed milk in the top of a double boiler or in a bowl in the microwave
4. stir until smooth
5. remove from heat and stir in pecans and grated orange peel
6. spread in prepared dish and chill until firm
7. carefully remove fudge from pan using the edges of the foil
8. cut into squares
9. store covered in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: although, this candy had a great orange flavor, we didn't care for this.  It's not what I consider fudge. My husband thought it was more on the chewy side.  I also don't care to keep my fudges refrigerated.  When I took it out of the refrigerator, the chocolate melted on our fingers.  Sorry, I was really hoping to love this, seeing how it is so easy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
symphony  brownies

a 

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees , or 325 degrees for glass baking dish
2. lightly grease the bottom only of an 11 x 7 inch baking pan
3. set aside
4. in a large mixing bowl prepare brownie mix according to directions on the package , using 2 eggs , 1 / 4 cup water and 1 / 2 cup oil
5. stir until smooth
6. spread half the batter evenly into prepared pan
7. unwrap candy bars and place them on top of the batter
8. top with remaining brownie batter
9. bake 40 minutes or until a toothpick inserted near center comes out with only a few moist crumbs clinging to it
10. remove pan from oven and let cool on wire rack before cutting into squares or other shapes
demonstrations.review:
I just made these earlier this evening.  I used duncan hines chewy brownie mix and 3 symphony bars.  Also, I used a 13x9 inch pan
and baked for 30 minutes.  I put foil in the bottom of the pan and lightly greased.  Omg!  these are so delicious.  I saw Paula Deen make these and had to try them.  This is definitely a keeper!  To my suprise my DH really liked these too.  I will be making these again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
patti labelle s macaroni and cheese

got this off of the "good morning america" website after i saw her cook this on the show. this is the best macaroni and cheese i have ever tasted!!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. lightly butter a deep 2 1 / 2 quart baking dish
3. fill a large pot with water and bring to a rapid boil
4. add macaroni and the 1 tb oil
5. cook for 7 minutes , or until somewhat tender
6. drain well , and return to the pot
7. meanwhile , in a small saucepan , melt 8 tb of the butter
8. stir into macaroni
9. in a large bowl , combine all of the shredded cheeses
10. to the macaroni , add 1 1 / 2 cups of shredded cheeses , half and half , the cubed cheese and the eggs , and the seasoned salt and pepper
11. transfer to the prepared casserole dish , and top with remaining 1 / 2 cup shredded cheese
12. dot with remaining 1 tb of the butter
13. bake for 30-35 minutes or until the edges are golden brown and bubbly
14. serve hot
15. serves 8
demonstrations.review: I made this one for thanksgiving and christmas last year.  I have had alot of m&c and this is my fave so far.  I believe I did add a little more cheese.  I didn't want to waste what was left.  It's awesome.  Love it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s traditional italian cookies

these cookies are a staple in my family. they are so simple, yet so incredibly wonderful. this recipe has been passed down from my great-grandmother. i've listed here the original recipe from my nonna and great aunt, as it was given to my mother. it can easily be cut in half, or in fourths. obviously the full recipe makes alot of cookies!! my mom has been known to actually make the full batch, especially for christmas. besides the traditional "knot" shape, the cookie dough can be rolled out and cut with cookie cutters. pumpkins, autumn leaves, christmas trees, stars, and easter eggs are but a few of the shapes we like to make these in. i hope you enjoy them as much as my family does. (prep time includes dough resting time, and cooking time includes glaze drying time)

1. for cookie dough: cream butter & sugar
2. beat in eggs , baking powder , extracts and 3 cups of flour
3. add remaining flour until a stiff dough forms
4. chill dough for at least an hour to make it easier to work with
5. at this point you can form the dough into knots or roll out the dough and use cutters
6. bake for 10-12 minutes at 375
7. for glaze: i put about 2 cups of powdered sugar in a bowl , add the extract and a little milk
8. then i mix and add more milk until it gets to a smooth consistency- i don't like it too runny
9. should be like the consistency of a thick alfredo sauce
10. once cookies are cooled , dip the tops of each one into the glaze , or drizzle glaze over the cookies , and allow to dry completely
11. can be topped with colored sugar or sprinkles , your choice
demonstrations.review:
I have been using this recipe for the past 2 or 3 christmases.  I did cut the recipe in half and still had enough to feed an army.
 I love this cookie. I also used almond and anise extract. Not everyone likes anise, but I make alot of cookies and this one is for me!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot triple chocolate mess

a good dessert for the chocoholic!

1. spray crock pot with non-stick spray
2. mix all ingredients and place in crock pot
3. cook on low for 5-6 hours
4. try not to lift the lid
5. serve with ice cream
demonstrations.review: I am so sorry, but my dh and I did not like this.  I only cooked it about 3 hours and it smelled burnt.  I served it with vanilla ice cream and we both felt it was too spongy tasting.  It looked very good, however it's just not to our tasting.

target.recipe_text:
strawberry rhubarb crumble

since strawberries and rhubarb are a typical pair, a new twist is added to this crumble...an appealing topping of oats, sugar and pecans.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
2. butter the bottom and sides of a 10-inch deep-dish pie pan
3. prepare the filling: combine the strawberries , rhubarb , and lemon juice in a large bowl
4. mix together sugar and cornstarch in a small bowl
5. add to the strawberry mixture
6. toss gently to coat all over
7. spoon into the prepared pie pan
8. prepare the topping: place the oats , flour , dark-brown sugar , chopped pecans , cinnamon and butter in a food processor
9. pulse with on-and-off motion until the butter is the size of peas
10. do not over-process
11. sprinkle the crumb topping evenly over the fruit in the pan
12. bake in 375 degree oven until the crumb topping is golden brown , about 35 minutes
13. cover the dish loosely with aluminum foil
14. bake for additional 10 minutes or until heated through and bubbly
15. serve warm with vanilla ice cream , if desired
target.review: This was excellent!  The whole family enjoyed it and there were compliments all around - it won't even make it 48 hours here!  I went ahead and ground up the topping more than called for because I have one child who hates nuts unless they're hidden.  Definitely a keeper - thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
blond zucchini brownies

my neighbor makes these. i love them. she was kind enough to pass the recipe along to me so i'm sharing it with all of you. i hope you enjoy them!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. use the hot water to melt the margarine
3. add brown sugar & beat well
4. cool
5. add egg and vanilla beat well
6. mix dry ingredients together and add to sugar mixture
7. stir in zucchini & nuts
8. pour mixture into greased & floured 9 x 9 inch pan , spinkle with butterscotch chips and bake 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: OMG - these were SO good!  Wonderful flavor - I fully expect these to be gone within 24 hours once my kids taste them!  I used white chocolate chips since we don't buy butterscotch and I think that may have brought these over the top.  I'd already had shredded zucchini, so I used that rather than the chunks.  Just amazing - definitely a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
guacamole with sour cream

my guacamole is very free-form, but here are the basics:  figure about 1/2 large avocado per person. i don't care whether i'm using haas or regular avocados - some people do. pick ones that give to mild pressure but are not mushy. if you can't find any that are ripe, get hard ones and keep them in a paper bag for a couple of days until they ripen.

1. cut the avocado in half , scoop out the flesh with a spoon
2. mash 3 / 4 of it well and chop the remaining 1 / 4 coarsely
3. mix it into the mashed portion
4. mix all remaining ingredients together
5. serve immediately , or cover with plastic wrap , pressing wrap firmly to surface of guacamole and refrigerate up to 4 hours before serving
demonstrations.review: Didn't make this exactly as written - free-form and all.  It seemed to be a little bland as we made it, but as the avocados we had (the great big huge ones) pretty tasteless, so that probably didn't help.  Next time we'll use a different kind.  I don't care for black olives, so skipped that - but might use green next time.  We used some fresh pico de gallo that we'd made, which was nice.  Also will definitely use some extra garlic.  The sour cream adds a different dimension to it - great for a spread on BLTs or for homemade chips.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken or turkey  stock

i now have my crock-pot 6 months. because i don't need it as a time saver i have not used as much as i thought i would. but, it is great to make good chicken stock and i use it for that purpose a lot. i let the crock-pot do this during the night. my crock-pot is 3 liter/quart so a small one, adjust the ingredients to the size pot you are using and use your own judgement. i find it handy to freeze some of the stock in ice-cube bags for sauces.
if you do not have all the ingredients on the list...it does not matter, you also do not have to follow the amounts exactly,  be creative and add other veg or more of the same, or what you have in the fridge and think is suitable for making this recipe, just let it cook slowly to get a great rich stock. have fun with this and enjoy the result!

1. preheat the crock-pot on high
2. try breaking up the bones as small as possible , place with all the other ingredients in the crock-pot
3. cover with as much boiling water your crock-pot can take , i can add approx 6 cups of water
4. switch to low and cook for 12 or up to 24 hours
5. strain , cool , skim of the fat , use the stock or freeze
6. if there is any meat on the bones , remove it and use for the soup or other dishes , it will be also good for a ragout
7. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Yum!  So much better than the salty broth we normally have!  This was my first time making chicken stock - loved the simplicity of throwing everything into the crock and letting it go all day. Next time I'll plan on letting it go longer than 12 hours and see whether the flavor is enhanced.  I had everything on hand but the leek, but I don't know that it would have made much difference. Used all 10  cups on a homemade chicken noodle soup - the kids were all excited that we'd made our own stock and ate heartily. Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
intensely chocolate cocoa brownies

a rich brownie that is mixed in a sauce pan on the stove. easy, dense and soooooo good!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. melt butter in sauce pan
3. when melted remove from heat
4. add cocoa and stir well
5. add sugar , eggs and vanilla
6. mix until shiny and smooth
7. add flour , baking powder and salt
8. mix well
9. add choc chips or walnuts if desired
10. pour into an 8 inch or 9 inch pan
11. bake for 15-20 miutes
12. do not over bake
13. look for edges slightly pulling away from pan
14. cool and cut
15. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These were insanely good and easy! Used maybe a half cup of chocolate chips with it and everyone in the family thanked me for making them and told me how great they were!  Real test will be with the chocoholics I'm feeding a pan to tomorrow.  Definitely a keeper and will be my standard "go to" recipe for brownies!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s beef stew  pressure cooker

i grew up with this recipe and now i make it for my family...my picky hubby and kids gobble it right up...and it can be made so quickly in the pressure cooker.  to make an easy beef soup, omit the potatoes, add more water and a few boullions and serve with egg noodles or rice.

1. cut the roast into chunks , about 1 inch
2. heat oil in bottom of pressure cooker until hot and add the meat all at once (do not turn for at least 1 minute - you really want to let the meat sear - this gives the stew such yummy flavor
3. stir the meat , letting it brown on all sides
4. add the chopped garlic , stir for 1 minute , then add the onions , carrots , celery , potatoes , salt , pepper , parsley , water and optional beef bouillon
5. lock the pressure cooker lid in place and bring to high pressure over high heat
6. cook 15 minutes
7. cool pot immediately and serve
8. enjoy !
9. optional ingredients - you can add some chopped tomatoes if you'd like before cooking , or after bringing it to pressure , you can throw in some canned mushrooms or frozen peas and heat thoroughly
demonstrations.review: This was a HUGE hit even with my picky eaters!  Not a drop was left by the time we were done.  We used frozen egg noodles in place of potatoes and they turned out just fine. My husband said he thought it needed something, but couldn't quite place it, so I'm sure we'll play around with adding some other type of seasoning to see if we can make it just a bit better.  Definitely a keeper!

target.recipe_text:
chicken  rice  and spices bake

i got this recipe from my friend kasey a long time ago (i have adjusted the spices to my taste) and it is very easy--even for those that just can't seem to get basmati rice to cook "just right". so long as you cover the baking dish tightly with foil, it will not fail! i brought this to a pot-luck at work one day and ever since this dish was always requested by everyone at all of our potlucks.***i am cutting the salt to around half since there are quite a few reviews saying it is too salty. i don't measure the spices when i cook so i think i guessed the amount wrong.***
*** the cinnamon amount should be 1/2 tsp to 3/4 tsp only, not 2 teaspoons.  i have tried changing it twice now and get email confirmation that the changes have been approved but it still says 2 tsp of cinnamon.

1. preheat oven to 375f and grease a 9x13-inch baking dish
2. bring water to boiling and add chicken bouillon cubes , lower heat and simmer till dissolved--keep it hot
3. sprinkle chicken with half the spices
4. heat the olive oil in a large skillet on med-high to high heat and fry the chicken till both sides are brown , lower heat to medium and remove the chicken to a plate
5. in that same skillet saut the onions for 2 minutes , then add the garlic and remaining spices and saut another 2 minutes , then turn off the burner
6. add the rice and stir for about 30 seconds to 1 minute , till well coated
7. spread rice in the baking dish and place the chicken thighs over the rice
8. gently pour in the chicken stock and cover tightly with foil
9. bake for 40-45 minutes
target.review: I made this dish again last night and it turned out even better than the first time!  I used both chicken breasts and thighs - they both turned out great.  I used almost double the spices (about 1tsp of everything for the chicken plus the same for the rice). The curry powder I used is Nirmal Spicy Curry Powder.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chili   football soup

this recipe comes from the blue owl restaurant and bakery in historic kimmswick, mo. my daughter named it "football soup" because we always make it when we have a crowd over watching the game after church! incredibly easy, freezes beautifully, and my bean hating husband even loves it. i add an extra can of green chilies for more flavor. you can make it without the chicken for a cheaper meatless meal, and you can make it without the monterey jack cheese for a low-fat, less thickened soup (but the cheese adds a lot of flavor!)

1. heat oil in large pot over medium high heat
2. add onions and saute until translucent , about 10 minutes
3. stir in garlic , then chilies , cumin , oregano , and cayenne and saute 2 minutes
4. add undrained beans and stock and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat and add chicken and cheese to chili and stir until cheese melts
6. season to taste with salt and pepper and ladle into bowls
7. for freezing: pour soup into a rigid container , label and freeze
8. to reheat , thaw in refridgerator overnight or simply put frozen soup into a large pot and gently heat , with lid on and stirring often , till heated through
demonstrations.review: My fiance loved it!  It will be a permanent dish in our house.  I added twice as much red pepper and I seasoned the chicken with salt/pepper/chili powder/oregano & boiled in chicken broth (low sodium/no fat).   All I need now is a bigger pot.  Thanks for making me look like a great cook ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramel apple brownie dessert

whoa! this dessert is packed with all of your favorites! fudgey brownies, caramel, crisp apples, peanuts and reese's peanut butter cups! this is a to-die-for dessert that will turn even the pickiest eaters into little pigs!

1. combine brownie mix with the oil , water , and eggs
2. pour into a greased 13x9 inch pan and bake for 25-35 minutes or until cake tester comes out clean
3. cool completely
4. combine softened cream cheese with 1 / 4 cup of the caramel dessert topping
5. spread cream cheese / caramel mixture over cooled brownies
6. sprinkle chopped apples , peanut butter cups , and peanuts over the cream cheese / caramel mixture
7. drizzle remaining caramel dessert topping over the dessert
8. slice into squares
9. refridgerate left-overs
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to make and very yummy!  Everyone loved it.  It was good for a couple of days afterwards too if you keep it in the fridge.  I would have added more peanut butter cups, especially because when you're cutting them up you want to eat them right away :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red coconut chicken curry

this dish can be quite hot and spicy depending on the brand of curry paste used.  the variety in the pouch (instead of the jar or can) tend to be milder.  for those sensitive to spicy food, reduce the curry paste to 2 teaspoons.  in a pinch, use mild indian curry paste. serve over rice.
from canadian living magazine.

1. cut chicken into bite-size pieces
2. in a wok or large skillet , heat 1 tablespoon of oil over high heat , stir fry chicken in batches , until browned , about 3 minutes , transfer to plate , set aside
3. add remaining oil to wok , stir fry eggplant , onion , garlic , ginger and curry paste until onion is softened , about 3 minutes
4. pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil , reduce heat to medium and cook for 5 minutes
5. reduce heat to simmer , add fish sauce , sugar , lime rind and lime juice , salt , peppers and chicken and any accumulated juices
6. cover and cook stirring occasionally until slightly thickened and peppers are tender , about 10 minutes
7. add basil and coriander , and serve
demonstrations.review: WOW!  So glad I found this recipe.  I hunted high and low for the perfect recipe, and this is IT!  My curry tasted better than the restaurants'.  My husband and I don't like eggplant, so I subbed in green beans chopped in half and it was perfect.  I also subbed one red bell pepper and one green instead of 2 green and used 3 large chicken breasts cut into pieces instead of thighs.  One thing I was a little afraid of at first was the fish sauce because I really dislike seafood, but the fish sauce adds no fish flavor :)  I used the rind of one lime because I didn't have lime leaves and that turned out great.  I would also like to mention where I got my curry paste because this is very important.  I bought the curry paste on Amazon.com through a company called TastePadThai.  I got red/green/yellow curry paste in a set.  It was amazing and I can't wait to try the other colors.  I used half a can for this recipe.  Thank you for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili blanco

a football weekend/cold weather family favorite.

1. heat oil in large saucepan over medium-high heat
2. add onion and cook until tender
3. mix in garlic , jalapeo , green chile peppers , cumin , oregano , and cayenne
4. continue to cook and stir until mixture is tender
5. mix in chicken broth , chicken and white beans
6. simmer 15-20 minutes , stirring occasionally
7. remove from heat , stir in cheese until melted
8. serve warm with tortilla chips and salad
9. we put tortilla chips in bottom of serving bowl , add the chili
10. good eating !
demonstrations.review: I've been using this recipe for at least a year now.  It is one of our go-to meals.  REALLY good.  I follow the instructions pretty exactly and add a little extra red pepper for some heat.  It's fun to eat it with tortilla chips too :)  Thank you for this recipe!  I will be making it for the rest of my life :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey peanut butter cookies

an easy, sweet peanut butter cookie with a hint of a crunch. topping is strictly optional

1. preheat your oven to 350
2. coat a baking sheet with melted butter or oil
3. sift the flour into a large bowl and stir in the oats , the baking powder , and the salt in a pan , over medium heat , mix together the butter , sugar , peanut butter , and honey until melted
4. add the contents of the pan to the flour mixture and stir to combine
5. form teaspoonfuls of mixture into balls and place on baking sheets , allowing room for spreading
6. flatten or "squish" the dough balls lightly with a fork
7. bake for ten minutes or until golden in color
8. cool on baking sheet before removing from sheet
9. ---topping---
10. stir together the powdered sugar , butter , and water until smooth
11. dip tops of cookies into the topping
12. allow topping to set
demonstrations.review: I didn't like them at all.  They tasted like honey, and only honey.  I couldn't even taste the peanutbutter.  I didn't like the texture of the oats either.  Other people liked them though, this is just my opinion. I think you need to like honey a lot to appreciate these cookies.

target.recipe_text:
ww 0 point weight watchers cabbage soup

you can eat as much of this 0-point weight watchers cabbage soup as you like. it's so good for you.

1. spray pot with non stick cooking spray saute onions carrots and garlic for 5 minutes
2. add broth , tomato paste , cabbage , green beans , basil , oregano and salt & pepper to taste
3. simmer for a about 5-10 minutes until all vegetables are tender then add the zucchini and simmer for another 5 or so minutes
4. i have tried different variations
5. leaving out green beans
6. adding chopped green onions in addition to the yellow onion
7. all very good
8. you can customize it a bit
target.review:
My friend and I really liked this soup!  I doubled the recipe so I'd have enough for my lunches all week.  The only thing I'd change is to simmer everything for 10 minutes more than the directions say. The carrots were a bit too hard for my liking.  Also, maybe next time I'll add a little Rotel to give it a kick!
Thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian lentil and barley soup

this is a surprisingly filling, vegetarian, crock pot soup. it is very good, and easy to prepare the night before, or chop the veggies in advance and turn it on before you leave for work in the morning. goes great with a crusty bread.

1. sort through lentils to remove debris and shriveled beans , then rinse
2. add lentils to crock pot , along with barley , carrots , celery , onion , garlic , dried herbs and bay leaf
3. pour in broth , water , and tomatoes
4. cover and cook on low heat for 12 to 14 hours , or on high heat for 5 to 6 hours
5. discard bay leaf and just before serving stir in parsley and vinegar
6. lentils aren't like dried beans
7. they don't require soaking and cook pretty quickly when you do it right
8. when you buy your lentils , go somewhere that has a decent turnover so your lentils haven't been sitting on the shelf for years
9. also , don't add any additional salt to the soup while it is cooking , and don't add lentils to already boiling water as either one can make lentils tough
demonstrations.review: Well, I didn't know what to expect since I had never eaten lentils before.  Since it had such a high rating I thought I'd give it a try but after trying it and trying it all week in leftovers for lunch I have decided that I really don't like it that much.  I do have to admit that I didn't add the parsley or the vinegar but I'm not sure how much difference it would have made.  I did have to turn it from low to high after 13 hours because the lentils were so hard still.  I left it that way for at least 1&1/2 hours and I still don't know if the lentils were supposed to be the texture they turned out to be.  If I do try it again I will double all the spices and add a good amount of salt.  Thanks anyways :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review:
Well these cookies turned out so awesome, even though I made a ton of substitutions.  I put in 2 eggs instead of one, chocolate chips since I didn't have white chocolate, raisins since I didn't have dried cranberries, and I added a bit more salt and almost 1 whole tsp. of baking soda.  Anyways, I don't know if you can even still consider this the same recipe, but I really liked it and so did everyone who tried them!
Thanks so much!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
best ever banana cake with cream cheese frosting

this is one of (if not) the best banana cake i have ever tasted! i thought the oven temp of 275° sounded a little low, but this cake baked up (and rose) beautifully in my oven at this temp after pretty much exactly one hour. i do not know if the little "freezer trick" to this recipe is what ensured its moistness or not, but i did it, and it was exceptionally moist & delicious. would be interesting to see if it still came out as great if this step was skipped. all i know is that i followed this recipe exactly as stated (except that i had no buttermilk, so i subbed with a mix of lemon juice & milk) and i got exceptional results. so moist and yummy...a dense cake, similar in texture to a carrot cake... i personally would not call this frosted banana bread :o)  depending on the amount of frosting you like you can decide whether to half the recipe or not. i used the full recipe and had some leftover. i sprinkled on the chopped walnuts and threw this baby in the fridge and cut it the next day...to die for! i really liked it slightly chilled, but great at room temp too! it got better each day it sat, i always make this cake at least the day before i need or want it.  i was extremely pleased with this cake and will be making it over & over again!! so glad i came across this one!! (on another website).


(* * just to update the recipe, (based on some of the reviews), the baking time may vary based on individual ovens. it was right on for my oven, but some others have stated it has taken 1 hour 10 minutes, 1 hour 20 minutes, and my sister just informed me that it took 1 hour 30 minutes in her oven!!!!!)

1. preheat oven to 275f
2. grease and flour a 9 x 13 pan
3. in a small bowl , mix mashed banana with the lemon juice
4. set aside
5. in a medium bowl , mix flour , baking soda and salt
6. set aside
7. in a large bowl , cream 3 / 4 cup butter and 2 1 / 8 cups sugar until light and fluffy
8. beat in eggs , one at a time , then stir in 2 tsp vanilla
9. beat in the flour mixture alternately with the buttermilk
10. stir in banana mixture
11. pour batter into prepared pan and bake in preheated oven for one hour or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean
12. remove from oven and place directly into the freezer for 45 minutes
13. this will make the cake very moist
14. for the frosting , cream the butter and cream cheese until smooth
15. beat in 1 teaspoon vanilla
16. add icing sugar and beat on low speed until combined , then on high speed until frosting is smooth
17. spread on cooled cake
18. sprinkle chopped walnuts over top of the frosting , if desired
demonstrations.review: Wow!  Totally awesome!  The only thing is, I was making it for a potluck and no one wanted to wait the 45 minutes for it to be put in the freezer.  They devoured the whole thing hot out of the oven, none the less.  The other reason why I didn't put it in was because I baked it in pyrex.  Would that have cracked the glass if it went directly from the oven to the freezer?  Anyways, just something to consider if you're going to bake this cake.  But really, totally worth the effort!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
addictive chicken tenders  one taste and you re addicted

i found this recipe on a low-carb site, (dh is doing a low-carb diet). i modified it some and dh says the name is very appropriate. he craves this so i end up making it once or twice a week. good thing it is easy!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. combine all dry ingredients
3. line a shallow pan with foil
4. melt butter in a shallow dish
5. dip each piece in butter then roll in seasoning mixture and place in pan
6. bake for 20-30 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: Pretty good but I did make some adjustments because I didn't have the right stuff on hand.  I sub. 2 tbsp. parsley with italian seasoning and the oregano with garlic powder.  Unlike the other reviews, I had a lot of the mixture leftover.  It was a bit too salty for my taste.  Next time I'd cut the salt and add something spicy to the mixture.  Thanks, Nane, for the easy recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This was extraordinarily easy to make and I even had time to get a good workout in before my guests came over!  I used Pace Chipotle Salsa and it gave the whole dish a nice mesquite taste.  My guests absolutely loved it and so did I!

target.recipe_text:
caramel pecan sticky bun cookies

the title says it all! the recipe will be requested often. from pillbury's the complete book of baking. prep time includes 1 hour chilling time.

1. in large bowl , beat 1 cup margarine and sugar until light and fluffy
2. add 1 / 2 cup corn syrup and egg yolks
3. blend well
4. stir in flour
5. mix well
6. cover with plastic wrap
7. refrigerate 1 hour for easier handling
