3. add 1 heaping tablespoonful of sweet potato to the center of each biscuit
4. fold in half and crimp the edges to seal
5. lay in pan appx
6. 8 per side
7. you can overlap them
8. combine butter , sugars , cinnamon , and water in a saucepan and bring to a boil
9. pour over biscuits
10. they may float , but they will settle
11. bake@ 350f , uncovered , 35-45 minutes until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I made this for Thanksgiving and got rave reviews from my guests along with several requests for the recipe.  So delicious and sweet it could easily have been used as a dessert.  We had leftovers which were just as delicious reheated.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cranberry barbecue chicken   crock pot

this is a variation of an old favorite, cranberry chicken...adding the barbecue sauce adds a little zest!

1. combine all ingredients in a slow cooker
2. cover and bake on high for 4 hours or on low for 6-8 hours
3. before serving , you may want to pull the meat out and thicken the sauce with flour or corn starch
demonstrations.review:
Easy and tasty, but I agree with Peggy - you really need to serve this with rice or pasta.
I was in a rush at dinner time and just served it with vegetable -- since the sauce is not super thick, we had a hard time enjoying the sauce.
Rice or pasta would be perfect.

target.recipe_text:
red snapper with lemon butter

nan

1. roll the fish lightly in flour mixed with salt and pepper
2. heat oil in skillet
3. cook fish until brown on both sides
4. remove fish to platter and keep warm
5. to skillet add butter and lemon
6. allow to simmer 1 minute
7. pour over the fish
8. sprinkle with parsley
target.review: So good!! The fish cooked up perfectly. We did one fish fillet with the flour coating and one without. We definitely preferred the one with, but both were good and the one without sticks with my Paleo diet, especially since I used Kerrygold butter. :) Picture is of the fish without the coating, yummy!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kale   potato hash

from eating well magazine, this can be served as a side dish with a steak or pork chops or set a poached egg on top for a hearty breakfast or brunch.

a 1- to 1 1/2-pound bunch of kale yields 16 to 24 cups of chopped leaves.when preparing kale for this hash, remove the tough ribs, chop or tear the kale as directed, then wash it--allowing some water to cling to the leaves. the moisture helps steam the kale during the first stages of cooking.

fresh, partially cooked, shredded potatoes for hash browns can be found in the refrigerated produce section and sometimes in the dairy section of most supermarkets. alternatively, boil potatoes until they can just be pierced with a fork but are not completely tender. let cool slightly, then shred.

1. place kale in a large microwave-safe bowl , cover and microwave until wilted , about 3 minutes
2. drain , cool slightly , and finely chop
3. meanwhile , mix horseradish , shallot , pepper and salt in a large bowl
4. add the chopped kale and potatoes
5. stir to combine
6. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
7. add the kale mixture , spread into an even layer and cook , stirring every 3 to 4 minutes and returning the mixture to an even layer , until the potatoes begin to turn golden brown and crisp , 12 to 15 minutes total
demonstrations.review: Loved the horseradish in this which I was kind of skeptical about in the first place. Don't get me wrong I love horseradish, but in breakfast food? Worked so well!! Didn't have shallots (darn!) so I used onions. Served with an over-easy egg on top for the perfect breakfast :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal  cookies

this is a family favorite--moist and chewy.
this is an old recipe ,and the trick to getting a moist cookie, is to take them from the oven when the middle does not look done.
this recipe was on a quaker oats box years ago.

1. cream oleo and sugars
2. add eggs and beat well with the vanilla
3. mix together the flour , salt , soda , and cinnamon
4. add to the creamed mixture
5. stir in the hot water , oats , and raisins
6. mix well
7. place heaping tablespoonful batter on a greased cookie sheet
8. bake at 350 degrees until almost done
9. take out and cool on cookie sheet for 1 minute , then cool on a rack
demonstrations.review: Oleo is butter. These spread for me more than I wanted for some reason and the edges kept on getting dark as well. They taste great but no ideal for a bake sale as they were so fragile to hold up in a bake sale with being delicate.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
japanese style marinated mushroom salad

a japanese-style salad which can be served as a side dish with any grilled or bbqd meat dish.  i found this recipe in the october 2005 issue of the australian magazine 'super food ideas', and i have posted it for the 2005 zaar world tour.  the "cooking times" below do not include the 3 hours refrigeration time.

1. make marinated mushrooms: place soy , mirin , peanut oil , sesame oil , garlic and ginger in a glass or ceramic bowl , and stir until well-combined
2. add mushrooms and turn to coat
3. cover and refrigerate for 3 hours
4. place asian greens , cucumber , capsicum and marinated mushrooms in a large bowl
5. toss to combine
6. serve as an accompaniment to lamb , beef or chicken
demonstrations.review: I only marinated my mushrooms for about an hour and half, but they were so flavorful and so good! When I went to get my cucumber it was spoiled :( so I used some radishes instead, which were a great substitute IMO! YUM!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey mustard mozzarella chicken

got this recipe from allrecipes.com that is sounded good.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees f
2. place the chicken breast halves in a baking dish , and drizzle evenly with honey and mustard
3. sprinkle with lemon pepper
4. bake chicken 25 minutes in the preheated oven
5. top each breast half with 2 bacon slice halves , and sprinkle evenly with cheese
6. continue baking 10 minutes , or until chicken juices run clear , bacon is crisp , and cheese is bubbly
demonstrations.review: This recipe is delicious, but I had to deduct the star, because 10 minutes is not anywhere near long enough to get that bacon cooked.  I precooked my bacon until crisp then added it to the chicken, topped with cheese and baked the 10 minutes.  Perfect!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
peach oatmeal

i have created one delicious oatmeal!  it sort of reminds me of the quaker peaches and cream oatmeal.  i still prefer this oatmeal however, which is healthier, to packaged any day.

1. cut up peach slices into small pieces
2. in a bowl add oats , water , and peaches with juice
3. microwave in 500watt microwave for 2 minutes , stir , microwave for another 2 minutes , stir , then microwave in 1 minute intervals until cooked
4. in a 1200watt microwave , microwave for 30 seconds , stir , microwave for another 30 seconds , stir , and then continue microwaving in 30 second intervals until cooked
5. once cooked , add cinnamon , butterscotch extract , and sweetener
demonstrations.review: This was SO GOOD! For preference I used milk instead of water. Also used a fresh peach and coated the pieces in sugar and let them sit for a minute before adding them in. Used the honey and probably added a little bit more than called for :) Can't wait to make for the kids!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot swedish cabbage rolls  the best

my husband has tried many different recipes for cabbage rolls and swears these are the best he has ever had.

1. immerse cabbage leaves in large kettle of boiling water for about 3 minutes or until limp
2. drain
3. combine egg , 1 / 4 cup of sauce , onion , salt , pepper , beef , and cooked rice
4. place about 1 / 4 cup meat mixture in center of each leaf
5. fold in sides and roll ends over meat
6. place in slow-cooking pot
7. combine tomato sauce with brown sugar , lemon juice and worcestershire sauce
8. pour over cabbage rolls
9. cover and cook on low 7-9 hours
target.review: My husband really enjoys these.  I do too.  I do make a few minor adjustments however.  Sometimes I use ground turkey instead of beef...there isn't much of a difference in flavor.  I also use instant rice instead of cooked rice for convenience and I add more sauce and a little extra water to compensate for the rice. My mom used to make these for me as a kid and it brings back nice memories whenever I make them.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free oreo cookies

what's your favorite way to eat an oreo cookie? some of us celiac's may have forgotten our favourite way ... or tried really hard to forget oreo cookies even exsisted. well forget no more, you will never have another craving for an oreo cookie. these taste exactly like the real wheat containing oreo cookie. split these cookies apart and lick the frosting from each side, or dip them in milk, they are so similar! slip these cookies into your children's lunches for a real treat.  they won't feel different from the other kids eating these, infact the other children will definetly be envious of them for once! note: if you have a cookie stamp, press onto sliced cookies before baking to give a more authentic look to the cookies.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a medium bowl , whisk together the flour mix , xanthan gum , egg replacer , cocoa , baking powder , baking soda , and salt
3. set aside
4. in the bowl of the mixer , cream the margarine and sugar until light
5. add the egg and vanilla and beat well
6. add the dry ingredients in 3 additions
7. if the dough becomes too stiff , add the milk as needed
8. shape the dough into two 10"x1-1 / 2" rolls
9. wrap in foil and chill
10. chill for about 15-20 minutes
11. cut into 1 / 8" slices , if you have a cookie stamp , you can at this point press in onto the sliced cookies before baking
12. bake these cookies on an ungreased cookie sheet for 10 minutes
13. let cool for only a few minutes before removing from the cookie sheet
14. cool thoroughly on a rack
15. for the filling , combine confectioners' sugar , shortening , vanilla and hot water
demonstrations.review:
I want to update my review.  We have made these several times now.  Recently I had to stop eating corn and dairy because my 4 month old infant is sensitive to them and I am nursing.  So...for the cornstarch I substituted equal parts tapioca flour and arrowroot.  I used Spectrum shortening in place of butter, and almond milk in place of milk.  Worked out just fine.  You will need to add a bit more milk than listed if you do this however.  
Another thing I discovered...I was going to use my cookie press for these but the dough was too thick HOWEVER...I did find that you good put a mishapen log of doughin the cookie press and press the dough down toward to die and then just remove the whole log.  What you end up with is a perfectly round dough log and better looking cookies...more uniform.  I sliced them up and put a piece of parchment over each cookie and then presed the bottom of a juice glass over the top to flatten them out a bit.  They look much nicer this way:)

My 3 year old helped make these with me. They were really easy. His comments about the dough.. "That looks like mud mommy. It's really good". They ARE really good. The only thing I will change next time is to double the filling. We ran out before filling all the cookies.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
grilled pineapple and banana with honey

quick easy healthy dessert.

1. melt butter with honey
2. add rum and mixed spice
3. place pineapple and banana onto oven tray
4. brush with honey mixture
5. grill for 3-4 minutes , turning once , until golden brown
6. serve with thick cream or ice cream
demonstrations.review: Mmmmmm...I wanted to grill some bananas with dinner tonight so I used this as reference.  I didn't actually measure anything and I wasn't sure what mixed spice was.  I used pumpkin pie spice.  I also used rum liquer instead of regular rum.  I think they sell that here...we bought it in Jamaica on vacation.  Anyway, the bananas were delicious.  I just served it as a side the the fish we were eating tonight.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flounder stuffed with arugula and sun dried tomatoes

this is a healthy dish using a potato to hold the arugula and sundried tomatoes together in the flouder roll topped with pine nuts. cooking time depends on how thick th flounder is. you can also lay the flounder down next to each other, fill and roll up together in one roll, baking time may be a bit longer for this.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. in small saucepan , bring 2 cups of water to a boil over medium heat
3. add potato , garlic and salt and cook until potato is tender , about 10 minutes
4. with slotted spoon , transfer potato and garlic to medium bowl
5. add 2 tablespoons of cooking liquid and mash with a fork or potato masher
6. stir in parmesan , pepper , nutmeg and a pinch of salt
7. stir in arugula and sundried tomatoes
8. lay flounder fillets on a work surface with skinned-side up
9. sprinkle 2 tsp of lemon juice evenly over fish
10. spoon arugula or spinach mixture onto fillets and roll up
11. butter a baking pan
12. place flounder rolls in buttered pan seam-side down
13. sprinkle flounder with remaining 2 tsp lemon juice , olive oil , paprika and pine nuts
14. bake 20 minutes , or until fish is cooked through
demonstrations.review: This was easy to make, but we didn't like it very much.  The potato made for an odd and a bit tasteless combo.  Neither my husband nor I finished our dinner and to fill me up the rest of the way I ate a PB&J and he had a bowl of Cheerios.  This was also an expensive recipe so I was disappointed.  I follwed the instructions to a "t", but no good for me.  I gave it two stars considering it is a very healthy dish at least.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chewy granola bars vegan  gluten free  egg free  dairy free

i have modified recipe #20184 to fit into our allergen free diet. everyone loves these!! these are free of milk, egg, gluten, corn, soy and so on!! 

sorry about missing changing the directions. i have been tweaking the recipe. everything should be correct now. 

you will have to read labels to be sure that the items you buy are allergen free. this recipe is quite forgiving but using regular rice flour helps them to stick together.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. oil 9x13 baking pan
3. in large bowl , beat sugar and shortening until light and fluffy
4. add honey , egg replace and vanilla
5. beat until smooth
6. in medium bowl , combine flour , gar gum , salt and baking soda
7. blend
8. add flour mixture to sugar mixture
9. mix until well combined
10. by hand mix in chocolate chips , nuts , rice cereal and oats
11. press firmly into pan
12. bake for 20 minutes , until brown
demonstrations.review: These are really good.  They are a bit more cakey than I wanted though so the second time I made them, I decreased the rice flour and increased the oats and crispy rice.  I also decreased the sugar to 1/2 cup.  Oh...and I have only ever made them with currants and almonds rather than the chocolate chips.  One thing that is a bit confusing however is the inconsistencies between the recipe and the directions.  Maybe Silly Goose can fix it.  I almost didn't make them because I was concerned I was using the wrong ingredients.  For instance it mentions using rice milk in the directions but not the recipe.  I did not use rice milk.  It mentions baking pwder int he recipe and baking soda in the directions.  Anyway....it might be easier for a reluctant cook to make this recipe if the recipe and directions used the same language and ingredients.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gluten free pizza crust

from carol fenster's "special diet solutions".

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. in medium bowl using regular beaters , blend all ingredients on low speed
3. beat on high speed for 3 minutes
4. dough will resemble soft bread dough
5. put mixture on lightly greased 12-inch pizza pan or 11 x 7-inch pan
6. liberally sprinkle rice flour on dough , then press dough into pan , continuing to sprinkle with flour to prevent sticking to hands
7. make edges slightly thicker to hold toppings
8. bake pizza crust for 10 minutes
9. remove from oven
10. spread pizza crust with your favorite sauce and toppings
11. bake another 20 to 25 minutes or until top is nicely browned
demonstrations.review:
I get rave reviews from gf people as well as non gfer's.  I do have a little trick for making this perfect though.  Once I get the dough on the well greased and well floured foil, I put the foil directly onto a preheated grill over medium heat.  I cook for 5 minutes and then flip the dough over so it is directly on the grill and I peel off the foil and discard it.  I cook the dough another 2 minutes and remove.  Then I put on my topping and return to the grill.  If the dough starts to get overdone, I remove the pizza from the grill and pop it under the broiler in my oven for a couple of minutes to get the cheese nice and bubbly.  This cooking method makes a big difference.  
I have also doubled or tripled the recipe to make several crusts at once and then I freeze the crust to make an impromtu pizza later.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot waikiki chicken

quick week night meal

1. dump all in crock pot cook on high for 1 hour
2. cook on low for 7 hours
3. serve over rice
4. enjoy
target.review: Good concept, I didn't like that everything turns the same color in the crockpot..and it was a bit too much sugar.  Next time, I will add pineapple later in the cooking so it keeps some color and stays crunchier and not soft. I will also reduce sugar and add more veggies.  A recipe worth trying again, though the first go round wasn't a success. thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brown sugar meatloaf

i use chili sauce or salsa instead of ketchup to give a nice contrast to the sweetness of the brown sugar.  a lighter version can be made using splenda brown sugar blend, skim milk, and egg beaters. got this one from the allrecipes website. it's one of their most popular recipes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. lightly grease a 5x9 inch loaf pan
3. press the brown sugar in the bottom of the prepared loaf pan and spread the ketchup over the sugar
4. in a mixing bowl , mix thoroughly all remaining ingredients and shape into a loaf
5. place on top of the ketchup
6. bake in preheated oven for 1 hour or until juices are clear
demonstrations.review: I loved this. I made a few changes, used bread crumbs, turkey meat, and threw in some garlic, and a bit of worstershire sauce and no ginger (didn't have it on hand) I double the recipe to make 2 loaves...it turned out fantastic. thanks!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked blue cheese chicken

excellent! if you like blue cheese you will love this dish. i make it often for just the family or dinner parties and everyone always comments on how good it is. i like to serve this chicken with baked potatoes or a rice dish and a green salad. enjoy!

1. mix together the blue cheese , sour cream and garlic
2. set aside
3. lightly salt chicken breasts
4. dredge each one in the flour , dip in the beaten egg , then roll in the bread crumbs
5. place the butter& oil in a non-stick skillet and heat over medium-high heat
6. brown chicken breasts on both sides then place in a lightly greased baking dish
7. pour the blue cheese mixture over the breasts
8. cover and bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 45-60 mins or until chicken is tender
demonstrations.review:
I made this with fat free sour cream, I also substituted bread crumbs for crunched up crackers since I had no BC. Served over pasta, with broccoli, rolls and fruit salad. Nice meal.
I am rating this so high because my family loved it. my kids ate it! (wow) and my husband said this was one to make again. The chicken was super moist, I actually cut it with the side of my fork.  thanks for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot thai chicken

my sister gave me a slightly different version of this recipe- it called for hot salsa and a tablespoon of lime juice. my kids find it too spicy with the hot salsa, and the lime salsa saves the lime juice step. this makes its own delicious sauce.

1. mix all in crock pot
2. cook on low for 6 hours
3. serve over rice
demonstrations.review: This was a different type of meal to make in a crock pot and very good.  I added a little more lime and also about 1/4 cup of coconut at the end of the cooking time.  The chicken was so tender it fell apart.  I put this over Jasmine rice. Very good!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chicken fajita skillet

this is from menus4moms.  i think it sounds pretty good; plus easy, quick and done in one pan!  another perk: the macaroni goes in uncooked.

1. cook chicken with chili powder and salt in a non-stick or pam sprayed fry pan until cooked through
2. add broth and bring to a boil
3. stir in macaroni and cover , reducing heat to medium-low
4. simmer 5 minutes and add peppers and onions and velveeta cubes
5. cook until cheese is melted , stirring frequently
demonstrations.review: I was making chicken fajitas and didn't have tortillas, so I quick checked recipezaar and found this recipe.  I had cooked the chicken with fajita seasoning,one sliced green pepper and dry onion so I just threw in the noodles, broth and a package of shredded sharp cheddar, simmered and it was great!  My kids loved it too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan baked chicken

nan

1. mix all dry ingredients in medium-sized bowl
2. melt butter in microwave
3. dip chicken in butter and then coat in dry mix
4. place on large baking pan sprayed with pam and bake for 20 minutes at 400 degrees
demonstrations.review:
Great easy meal.  I made this with pasta, broccoli and I made the Creamy Parmesan sauce # 132351 to go over it all. 
I pounded the chicken down, followed instruction in breading it, then I baked it on 350 (instead of 400) for longer (about 45 minutes)...so I was able to scoot out of the house to get my daughter from her girls scout meeting :)  It was nice to have dinner cooking while I was out!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot teriyaki steak

this steak comes out very tender and i love the sauce. i serve over rice.

1. combine all ingredients and pour over steak
2. cook on low 4 to 6 hours in crock pot
3. serve over rice
target.review: This didn't taste much like teriyaki even with the addition of brown sugar as suggested by others. Even using light soy sauce it was too salty for us. But I did like the method of slow cooking since it made the meat nice and tender. I'll likely use this method again but use a different sauce.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mango chicken pita sandwiches

a simple recipe for a summer meal! enjoy :)

1. combine the first 5 ingredients
2. layer pita halves evenly with chicken , mango churney , and slaw mixture
3. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: A nice combination of flavors here, it made a very tasty light lunch. I made this with cold leftover chicken and assembled just before serving to avoid sogginess.  This was easy to make, would definitely make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pound cake with a caramel glaze

this is a delicious cake!  the caramel glaze is the perfect finishing touch.

1. preheat the oven to 325f
2. mix the flour , baking powder , baking soda and salt together
3. cream the butter and shortening together , then beat in the brown and white sugars gradually , beating constantly for 5 to 7 minutes
4. add the eggs one at a time , beating until the hellow dissappears
5. add the flour mixture alternately with the milk , beating at low speed until blended after each addition , beginning and ending with the flour mixture
6. stir in the banana , pecans and vanilla
7. pour into a greased and floured 10 inch tube pan
8. bake for 65 minutes or until a woodenpick inserted in the center comes out clean
9. cool on a wire rack for 10 minutes before removing from the pan to cool completely on a wire rack
10. to make the glaze , bring the butter , brown sugar , white sugar and cream to a boil in a heavy saucepan over high heat , stirring frequently
11. boil for 1 minute , without stirring
12. remove from the heat
13. stir in the vanilla
14. cool until slightly thickened , then drizzle over the cooled cake
demonstrations.review: The combination of the banana with the caramel was great.  This took much longer than stated in the recipe to bake though.  The glaze was too much, so I reserved some & poured it over each slice to serve.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic turkey and rice soup

a nice basic soup, simple to make and an especially good use of your left over turkey meat!i like to serve it piping hot with different flavored crackers (like sociables or ritz or any type of vegetable flavoured crackers)

1. in a dutch oven , on medium heat , saute the garlic and onion in oil until tender
2. add broth , rice , celery and carrot
3. cover and simmer 15 minute
4. add peas , nutmeg , sage and salt & pepper to taste
5. simmer on low 10 minutes
6. add the turkey and heat through
demonstrations.review: This soup was a good way to use up Christmas leftovers & enjoy a warm soup on a cold day.  I added an extra cup of liquid as there didn't seem to be enough for our tastes and I also added a bay leaf for some extra flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pizza spaghetti pie

wow...pizza and spaghetti in the same dish? how much better can a meal get??

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. combine beef , bread crumbs , onion , salt , pepper and evaporated milk
3. press firmly onto bottom and sides of a 9" pie plate
4. bake 35-40 minutes
5. spoon off drippings
6. combine warm spaghetti noodles with egg , parmesan cheese and butter
7. spread in baked meat shell
8. top with pizza sauce , then mozzarella cheese , then green pepper rings
9. bake an additional 10 minutes
10. let stand 5 minutes before cutting into wedges
demonstrations.review: I made this the other night in order to clear out the fridge. I was pleasantly surprised at how good it was since I was a little sceptical going in. I added some dried basil & oregano & used 1 whole, small onion to the meat layer to give it some extra flavor, used whole wheat spaghetti & added some mushrooms in place of the green pepper. Very family friendly, versatile & easy to prepare.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate  chocolate  chocolate  bundt cake with chocolate glaze

need i say more...chocolate! decadently rich and moist. add a scoop of vanilla ice cream and you're in heaven.

1. cake: preheat oven to 350
2. grease and flour bundt pan , set aside
3. in large mixing bowl , combine cake mix , pudding mix and chocolate chips
4. in another bowl , combine water , eggs , and vanilla mixing well
5. add egg mixture to dry mixture and mix with spoon until just blended
6. pour into prepared pan
7. bake for 50 to 55 minutes or until cake tests done when wooden pick in center comes out clean
8. cool 15 to 20 minutes before removing cake from pan
9. when completely cool , drizzle cake with chocolate glaze
10. chocolate glaze: combine all ingredients in bowl
11. mix with spoon until smooth
demonstrations.review: We generally make cakes from scratch, but I happened to have all the ingredients in the house so I thought I'd give it a try. Everyone loved it! I followed the suggestion of others and used some instant coffee in the glaze to bring out the chocolate flavor even more.

target.recipe_text:
baked frittata for one

if you want to use the tomato, look for a roma plum tomato at the grocery store; it's perfect. this is a great lunch or supper for one person, and the recipe easily doubles too.

1. use vegetables you like
2. use the kind of cheese you like
3. and if you don't have leftover boiled potatoes , don't sweat it
4. the dish will just be a little less hearty
5. preheat oven to 350f degrees
6. spray a pie plate with pam
7. beat eggs in a fairly large bowl
8. meanwhile , heat butter in a skillet and saute the veggies of your choice along with the garlic
9. when tender , scrape into the beaten eggs
10. add the parsley , cheese and seasonings and stir
11. pour into prepared pie plate and bake for 20-25 minutes until set
12. let stand for two minutes , then cut into wedges and enjoy
target.review: This is a great recipe on the basic making of a frittata! I had never made one before, so this recipe was perfect on teaching me the basics! The first time I used this, I used a pie plate, but the second time I used a little round cake pan, and it came out just as great! DON'T forget to grease a pie plate WELL if you're using one. This recipe is so perfect, it's the same baking time pretty much for however many eggs you add! Thanks for teaching me to finally bake one of these things! No more basic omelets for this gal!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate lovers deluxe fudgy brownies

rich and chocolaty, these brownies satisfy even the most hardcore chocolate lover. these are always the first thing to sell out at a bake sale! great with a glass of cold milk.  enjoy!

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease an 8 square baking pan with non-stick cooking spray
3. in medium bowl stir together butter , sugar , eggs and vanilla
4. add flour , cocoa and salt stirring just until blended
5. mix in half of the walnuts , if desired
6. spread mixture and sprinkle with remaining walnuts
7. bake about 30 minutes , until top appears dry and center is set
8. cool brownies in pan on wire rack
9. to wrap , cut brownies into squares
10. bake in 350 degrees oven stirring occasionally , about 10 minutes or until lightly browned
11. remove from oven and cool completely
12. my dh has also added chocolate chips to the batter with wonderful results !
demonstrations.review: Mmmm mmm MMM!!! This is the BEST brownie recipe I have ever made y'all! It was quick to do! The only thing I had an issue with was that mine took 35 minutes to be ready, but i did use "I can't believe it's not butter" so maybe that had something to do with it! These brownies have a slightly crunchy top, and a chewy DELICIOUS center! I will be for sure making this one again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish omelet

a great way to use up leftover boiled, baked or mashed potatoes. i love omelets and separately whipping the egg whites makes this light and fluffy despite the inclusion of potatoes.  in case you're wondering about taste - imagine a cross between a knish and a souffle.  other herbs or grated onions might be good variations.

1. separate the eggs and beat the yolks
2. add , the mashed potato to the yolks , mixing thoroughly
3. add the lemon juice , chives , and salt and pepper
4. whisk the egg whites until stiff
5. fold the egg whites into the potato mixture
6. melt the butter in a nonstick skillet or omelette pan over low-medium heat
7. cook the omelet until golden , then run under the broiler to finish and puff the omelet
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Yuck. This is probably the worst omelet I have ever made. Whisking the egg whites until stiff? My hand is still sore, and it didn't happen. I suggest all of you use a mixer for that. Takes 3-5 minutes to cook? I don't know what super oven and pan y'all use but that wasn't the case for me. It gets 2 stars because I like the basic idea of this. but i will be changing almost everything else about this recipe. Very bland!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
meatball sub casserole

wonderful take on the italian meatball sandwich. taken from "quick cooking" magazine.

1. preheat oven to 400
2. in a bowl , combine onions , bread crumbs and parmesan cheese
3. add beef and mix well
4. shape into 1-inch balls
5. place on a rack
6. in a shallow baking pan , bake for 15-20 minutes or until no longer pink
7. reduce oven temperature to 350
8. meanwhile , arrange bread in a single layer in an ungreased 13x9x2" baking dish
9. combine cream cheese , mayo , italian seasoning and pepper
10. spread over the bread
11. sprinkle with 1 / 2 cup mozzarella
12. combine sauce , water and garlic
13. add meatballs
14. pour over cheese mixture
15. sprinkle with remaining mozzarella
16. bake , uncovered at 350 for 30 minutes or until heated through
demonstrations.review: Mmm Mmm MM! This recipe was very good! It tasted just like a meatball sub sandwich from subway! The only thing i would have done differently is more meatballs for sure, and maybe using a different bread for the base to have more bread layer! I was a little skeptical of the meatball recipe, I thought for sure they wouldn't turn out, but it was simple and they came out GREAT! I'll definitely be using that meatball mix for all my meatball dishes! Y'all if you haven't made this dish yet, TRY IT!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southwestern stuffed bell peppers

simple preparation & delicious taste! use a mixture of red, green, yellow & orange peppers for a colourful presentation. recipe #2642 instead of store-bought taco seasoning mix--it makes this dish even better!

1. combine beef , onion , seasoning mix and egg in a large bowl
2. add rice and mix well
3. cut peppers in half lengthwise
4. remove seeds and membrane
5. spread tomatoes on the bottom of an ovenproof 12 x 9 inch baking dish
6. the liquid from the tomatoes will reduce during cooking so if you like lots of sauce , add about a cup of water
7. this also helps make the peppers softer
8. place peppers , cut side up , on top of the tomatoes
9. spoon beef mixture into peppers , mounding as necessary
10. top each pepper with salsa
11. bake in preheated 375f oven for 40-45 minutes or until beef is cooked thoroughly and peppers are soft
12. cover each pepper with cheese and return to oven , under the broiler , until the cheese melts- less than a minute , so watch carefully !
13. serve with sour cream and additional salsa
demonstrations.review: This recipe was good... In certain aspects. It is a very quick and easy recipe to prepare, and looks very fancy when it's all done! I love the premise of this, but I really didn't like the Mexican flavor of it all. The taco mix ruined it in my opinion. Also, I wanted the peppers softer so I added extra water like recommended, and still i made a mess on my self trying to cut it fast right off the bat, the pepper was still not easy to cut. They looked fancy and cute after, and are very filling, but I will be changing most of the flavor premise in this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the sweetest blueberry muffins

very tasty and sweet.

1. heat oven to 375
2. grease 18 regular-size muffin cups
3. in bowl , mix butter until creamy
4. add sugar and beat until pale and fluffy
5. add eggs one at a time , beating after each
6. beat in vanilla , baking powder and salt
7. with spoon , fold in half of flour then half of milk into batter
8. repeat
9. fold in blueberries
10. spoon into muffin cups and sprinkle topping onto each muffin
11. bake 15 to 20 minutes , until golden brown and springy to touch
demonstrations.review: These muffins were easy and DELICIOUS to make! I overfilled my muffin cups(can't help myself) And they baked up the perfect amount and didn't look funky at all! I used fresh blueberries because I don't about y'all, but I can't stand that blue/grey color that frozen blueberries give off after baked! These were even better the next day, as they got that nice soft sticky top! I will for sure be using this recipe many more times!

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s ranch potato salad or macaroni salad

i have made this many times over the years for large gatherings, everyone loves it and i am always asked for the recipe --- the dressing is wonderful with potatoes or cooked pasta,  you may of coarse double the amounts to feed more people --- all ingredients may be adjusted to suit taste, throw in some cooked ham or bacon if desired, plan ahead this salad must chill for at least 3 or more hours before serving, the longer chilling time the better! --- if making the potato salad and prefer a creamier salad then double the dressing amount

1. in a large bowl , combine the cooked cubed potatoes or cooked pasta with peas
2. celery , green onions , cheddar cheese and chopped eggs
3. toss to combine
4. in a small bowl , combine relish , mayo , ranch salad dressing and mustard and garlic powder mix well then add to macaroni mixture
5. toss to coat then season with salt and pepper
6. add in chopped yum yum pickles if using
7. mix to combine
8. season with more salt and black pepper to taste
9. cover and refrigerate for 3 or more hours to blend flavors
10. delicious !
target.review: Made this recipe using potatoes, it was great, even better the next day! So as many have recommended prepare in advance and allow to sit in the fridge- if possible over night. Thanks for sharing another great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hidden valley ranch sausage stars

these are easy to make you can do the wonton wraps the day or so ahead and have the sausage mixture made in advance then just 5 minutes before serving you fill the wraps and pop them in the oven. for a lighter exterior i prefer to use spring roll wraps. use your regular pork breakfast sausage. if you wish use italian sausage or bratwurst

1. heat oven to 350 degrees f
2. combine drained cooked sausage meat with the cheeses , salad dressing , olives and red pepper
3. lightly oil mini muffin tins and press a wrap in each tine so there are 4 wings sticking out
4. brush with oil bake 5 minutes until golden , remove wraps from pan , place on a baking sheet
5. fill wraps with the sausage , cheese mixture
6. bake for 5 minutes or until the cheese is bubbly& brown
demonstrations.review: Love it. May try to add a little moisture to the wonton wraps next time, they were not very flexible, which made it hard to get into the mini cups without breaking. Otherwise easy and wonderful recipe...

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot beef stew

this is a great crock-pot recipe for beef stew.

1. place meat in crock pot
2. mix flour , salt , pepper and pour over meat
3. stir to coat meat with flour
4. add remaining ingredients and stir to mix well
5. cover and cook on low for 10-12 hours or high for 4-6 hours
6. stir stew thoroughly before serving
demonstrations.review: Wonderful, I have tried to make beef stew in the past and it was always horrible. This is exactly the way it should be, I did add a small bag of frozen crinkle cut carrots. This is a keeper. Thanks so much Ellen for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cream cheese bars

i was looking for something to do with a strawberry cake mix that i had hanging around.  i found these in a cookbook, quick fixes with cake mixes.  as the into says "if you like cheescake or pastries with cheese filling, you'll really like these..."

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees and spray a 9 x 13 inch baking pan with vegetable spray or non-stick cooking spray
2. in a large bowl , combine the cake mix , butter and 1 egg
3. mix well
4. press the mixture into bottom prepared pan
5. in a medium bowl , beat cream cheese with remaining eggs and sugar until mixture is smooth and well blended
6. pour the mixture over cake mix batter and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until light brown on top
7. cool , cut into bars and enjoy
demonstrations.review: This is my first "not" five star post. I have to say this is not a keeper. The strawberry layer is just a thick not-so-right cake. The top layer tasted like an extremely thin version of cheesecake. Alone these two layers would be terrible and together they are not much better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
eggnog cookies

"what a delectable treat for eggnog lovers everywhere! these cookies have a wonderful spicy aroma and are great tasting. the fragrance of nutmeg and cinnamon will infuse your home with holiday spirit as you bake these cookies. they make delicious gifts and are a welcome addition to cookie exchanges. "

1. preheat oven to 300f
2. combine flour , baking powder , cinnamon and nutmeg
3. cream sugar and butter until light
4. add eggnog , vanilla , and egg yolks
5. beat at medium speed with mixer until smooth
6. add flour mixture and beat at low speed until just combined
7. do not overmix
8. drop by teaspoonfuls onto ungreased cookie sheet 1 inch apart
9. sprinkle lightly with nutmeg
10. bake 20 to 23 minutes until bottoms turn light brown
demonstrations.review: Added these cookies to my christmas baking. They were alright. Gave it four stars because one of my sons liked them because they tasted like egg nog and he loves egg nog. I did not like these cookies at all compared to all of the other yummy treats we made and they were the last to go. The consistancy of the cookie is not appetizing and the flavor is nothing to write home about. Don't think we will make again especially with all the great cookie recipes we have found on Zaar!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy enchiladas  beef or chicken

these easy enchiladas are my husband's favorite recipe of mine. because of the many different options, it is very versatile.

1. if using chicken , boil chicken in water
2. then rinse and shred with fork
3. add onion and garlic
4. if using ground beef , brown with onion and garlic , drain
5. add next 7 ingredients
6. in another skillet , heat oil
7. add tortillas , one at a time , for 10 seconds on each side
8. drain on paper towel
9. in 10x13 baking pan , pour just enough enchilada sauce in the bottom to coat the bottom of the pan
10. fill each tortilla with a spoonful of meat mixture
11. cheese , onions , and / or olives can be put inside each enchilada at this time , if desired
12. roll tortilla and place seam side down in pan
13. continue with remaining tortillas
14. pour remaining enchilada sauce over tortillas and top with cheese
15. at this time , pan may be refrigerated for several hours or overnight
16. bake in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes
17. top with sour cream
18. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I made the chicken enchiladas using my crock pot I put chicken, spices and sauce in for 6 hours on low. Took a couple of forks and shredded in minutes. Followed the rest of the instructions and voila, yummy! Oh, also used flour tortillas, fajita sized, not a fan of corn tortillas. Great recipe! Will make this many times, it's a keeper.

target.recipe_text:
brandied rabbit in mustard sauce

nan

1. wipe meat pieces and trim off any fat
2. heat olive oil and butter or margarine in large skillet until bubbly
3. add meat pieces and saute on all sides until browned
4. while browning , press whole cloves into onion chunks
5. add chunks to skillet in between meat pieces
6. add bouquet garni
7. sprinkle with salt
8. generously'slosh' brandy over top
9. cover
10. cook over medium to low heat about 30 minutes or until meat is cooked through
11. remove meat pieces from pan and keep warm
12. discard onion chunks , cloves and bouquet garni
13. increase heat to medium high
14. add cream and mustard
15. cook , stirring constantly until slightly thickened
16. return meat to pan and coat on all sides with sauce
17. serve at once
target.review: First things first:  the gravy is to die for!  My husband having taken charge, made some "secret" changes but I know the major one was using bacon fat along with olive oil.  We ate the yummy onion chunks and strained the gravy before serving.  It is an elegant dish, which we served with pasta.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
southern fried oysters

my dad loves to have a good old southern fish/seafood fry. this is the recipe he uses for fried oysters.

1. in a mixing bowl , add the first 3 ingredients
2. stir to combine
3. in another bowl , combine the egg and milk
4. whisk to combine
5. dip oysters in egg mixture , then dredge in flour mixture
6. add oil to 2-3 inch depth in a cast-iron dutch oven
7. heat to 375 degrees
8. fry oysters in oil until golden , turning once
9. drain on paper towels and serve immediately
demonstrations.review: Our family considers fried oysters a very special treat.  This is an easy, fast, wonderful recipe.  I would add either "Old Bay" or Tony Cachere's seasoning, but we thoroughly enjoyed it as written.  As I don't use self-rising flour, I just added a bit of baking powder and baking soda to the flour and corn meal.  I am sure there are conventions for the correct quantities, but my slap-dash method worked fine.   Thanks, "Rather be Swimming'".

demonstrations.recipe_text:
salmon fillets with fresh tomatoes

nan

1. heat oven to 450 degrees
2. cut 4 square pieces of parchment paper or foil
3. and coat each with cooking spray
4. in medium bowl , combine the garlic , tomatoes , onions , oil , lemon rind , dill , parsley and capers
5. season with the salt and pepper
6. mix well
7. place each fillet on the prepared parchment paper or foil
8. top with equal amounts of tomato mixture
9. for each packet , bring 2 opposite edges of paper or foil together over the top of the fish and fold over several times
10. twist each of the open ends to close the packet and make a tight seal
11. place the packages on a baking sheet
12. bake for 10 minutes for every 1 inch of thickness of fish , or until the center portion of the fish flakes easily when tested with a fork
demonstrations.review: THE most delicious salmon recipe I have ever sunk my teeth into.  The blend of flavors is tantalizing; just perfect. The topping does mask the flavor of the salmon considerably but that works for us.  The fresh tomatoes and herbs from our garden most certainly made a great recipe even better.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
osso bucco for two

this is really good for a romantic dinner for two on a snowy night.

1. 4 hours before cooking or the night before rub the french dry rub into the shanks , both sides
2. in a large dutch oven over medium high heat add the oil and sear the shanks on both sides
3. reduce heat to medium and add the carrots , celery , and onions and cook , as is , for 5 minutes
4. now add the tomatoes , broth , wine and pepper and fresh herbs
5. bring to a boil , cover and reduce to a simmer for 30 minutes
6. when done remove shanks to individual plates along with the vegetables and over high heat quickly reduce the liquid
7. pour this over top
8. i serve this with a cesar salad , garlic bread and roasted potatoes
9. don't forget the wine !
demonstrations.review:
The French Dry Rub sets this osso bucco way above other osso bucco recipes I've made.  Did make some changes, tho.  I used 8 shanks, 2 carrots, only about a cup of red wine and did not add the fresh rosemary/thyme (tho I had them handy) during cooking.  I didn't want to risk overpowering the great flavor of the rub.

After browning the shanks, I removed them and sauteed the veggies quite a while till caramelized. After all was put together, I very-slow cooked it - several hours - then took out the shanks, defatted the liquid and thickened it with a flour/water mix.  Removing the meat for a while tends to firm it up, which I like.  Makes lots of gravy and I am plotting to incorporate the leftover as an experimental soup-base.  Thanks, Diana!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
linzer torte cookies

these cookies i got off of allrecipes. they are delicious! you can make any kind of nut flour and they still taste amazing. to make nut flour, toast nuts and allow to cool. place in food processor and pulse until fine grounds.

1. 1
2. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
3. 2
4. in a medium bowl , cream together the butter and sugar
5. beat in the egg and lemon peel
6. in another bowl , stir together the flour , nut flour , cinnamon and cloves
7. gradually stir the dry ingredients into the creamed mixture
8. the dough will be stiff , so you may need to knead it by hand to get it to come together
9. 3
10. roll the dough out to 1 / 8 inch thickness and cut into rounds using a cookie cutter
11. place cookies onto a cookie sheet spaced 2 inches apart
12. count your rounds and use a small cookie cutter to cut the center out of half of the cookies
13. this can be done while the other half of the cookies bakes
14. bake for 10 to 12 minutes in the preheated oven , until firm and lightly browned at the edges
15. allow cookies to cool completely
16. spread jam on the tops of the solid cookies and top with the cookies that have shapes cut out
demonstrations.review:
What a find! These cookies are so much like our family's traditional Christmas Linzer Torte, which is a beast to make. There are so many advantages to having it all in cookie form, but I won't enumerate them here.

So, taking from our recipe, I added 1 -2 T. rum, and about 1 T cocoa powder. Hazelnuts are THE nut to use if you possibly can. I chilled the dough overnight and found it very easy to handle.. Everything else is the same. Regarding the jam filling: melt the jam and put just enough on bottom cookies to cause them to stick together, else it could be runny.

Thank you, Baking Girl!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
squid stewed with tomatoes  white wine and black olives

this recipe is from french food at home chef laura calder.

1. slice the squid cross-wise into rings , like onion rings
2. heat two tablespoons of olive oil in a saut pan and fry the squid , tossing occasionally , for 5 minutes
3. remove the squid , and set aside
4. add another tablespoon of olive oil to the pan and saut the onions until soft , but not coloured
5. add the tomatoes , garlic , and pepperoncino , and cook 10 minutes
6. return the squid to the pan , and add the wine , bay leaf , thyme , and saffron
7. season with salt and pepper
8. cover , and simmer until the squid is tender , 40 minutes
9. remove the hot pepper and the bay leaf
10. stir in the olives and lemon zest and continue to cook uncovered to reduce the juices , 10 minutes
11. the dish should be quite sloppy , but not like a soup
12. squirt in some lemon juice
13. taste , and adjust the seasonings
14. transfer to a warm serving bowl , scatter over the parsley , and serve with crusty bread
demonstrations.review: This is an acceptable dish.  As I began cooking according to the directions, I realized there was no provision for when to add the olives, zest and lemon juice.  Also, the reference to pepperoncini threw me off, but I am sure that meant the red pepper.

target.recipe_text:
garlic spinach with white beans

warm comfort food.  fast & easy.  very healthy and yummy.

1. heat a large skillet
2. add oil
3. saut garlic 1 minute
4. add all the spinach
5. lower heat to med and cover
6. cook just long enough to wilt spinach
7. add beans & stock and heat through
8. serve
target.review:
Thanks for this recipe!, I actually use it as a beginning of a new recipe, so instead of a side dish, became a vegetarian main dish... I follow the instructions, except the chicken stock, but then add more veggies (mushrooms and zuchinni) to cook together with the spinach and then add pine nuts and a bit of feta cheese, then i add some barbecue sauce and a pinch of thyme.

MMmmm... now i need to look for something crunchy to serve it with, hehe...

thanks again, blessings

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fungus gravy

nan

1. melt the butter in a small saucepan
2. add the onion and mushrooms and fry gently until they are very well browned
3. dissolve the stock cube in the hot water and add to the saucepan
4. add the blended cornflour or bisto and heat , stirring constantly , until thickened and smooth
demonstrations.review:
Wow!!!, absolutly delicious!, thanks a lot for such wonderful recipe!...I was tipped about this wonder in one of the reviews of SaraFish's Really Good Vegetarian Meatloaf (really!) [#33921]
Is amazing!.Alredy in my favs.Greets :D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
greek tempeh pitas

this is by far my favourite way of eating tempeh.  i am craving it right now! you can make it vegan by using vegan tzatziki.

1. slice tempeh medium thin
2. marinate in olive oil , soy sauce , crushed garlic , dried oregano and lemon juice
3. after 1 hour saute in frying pan until crispy
4. meanwhile mix diced tomatoes , cucumber , onion , garlic , balsamic vinegar and a drizzle of oil in a small bowl
5. heat pita on each side in frying pan
6. to assemble , place pita on a plate , lay tempeh over pita , spoon on tomato and cucumber mixture and top with tzatziki
7. i eat mine with a knife and fork , but my husband prefers to fold his in half and eat with his hands
8. either way , this is my favourite tempeh dish !
demonstrations.review:
FAN-TAS-TIC!!! We just had this as brunch and we totally loved it!!, is certainly a keeper and well, i didn't make tzatziki but a yogurt dressing and i didn't have oregano so i marinated with thyme... this is the second time in my life that i make something with tempeh so i just don't know how to cook it until crisp, but the flavors were amazing!
Thanks a lot for the wonderful recipe

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy pizza dough for bread machine

this is basically an amalgam of several basic bread recipes, simplified and adapted for use as a pizza crust. the bread machine just makes it easier. makes a 10-14" inch pie.

1. add ingredients to pan in order listed , set bread machine on"dough" and walk away
2. after the cycle is completed , lightly coat dough ball in flour and roll or slap out to desired size
3. top with desired sauce , cheeses , meats and / or veggies and bake at 450 until cheese is golden brown
4. will make a 9-10" pizza of average thickness , or a 13-14" thin crust pizza
5. for best results , bake on a preheated baking stone sprinkled with corn meal
6. i've used 3 / 4 cup flat beer and 1 / 4 water with excellent results
7. a teaspoon of semolina may be added as well -- it provides a nice crunchiness to the dough when baked
8. corn meal can be substituted for the semolina
demonstrations.review: I've made it today and it turned out great, it was my first attempt on making pizza at home and ended up making 2 pizzas with the dough, one thinner than the other, I coated it with the corn meal and i didn't add the herbs to the mix, but it was nice and fluffy,i have it already in my cookbook :),tnx 4 sharing it

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cinnamon sugar bread  bread machine

this bread is just so good, more like a coffee cake than a bread. i didn't have bread flour, so used regular unbleached, all-purpose flour and took it out about 3 minutes before the beeper because i like a less-crispy crust. well, what a treat. major keeper. not only would i make it again, i think it would make some of the most awesome cinnamon roll dough, and i'm definitely going to try that very soon.  i would also suggest using this bread to make cinnamon toast deluxe, recipe #93128.  a definite cinnamon extravaganza, and a wonderful treat, especially for those of you who are looking for a stronger cinnamon flavor.

  

1. place ingredients in the bread machine pan in the order suggested by the manufacturer
2. bake using the sweet bread setting if your machine has it
3. if not , use white bread setting
4. when the bread is done , remove from the machine and let sit on a rack for 10 minutes before removing from the pan
5. if it sticks , just loosen the sides with a pliable , plastic spatula and it should slip out easily
6. this makes a 1 1 / 2 pound loaf that rose really nicely
7. i did check the dough about 5 , 10 minutes into the kneading cycle
8. if you squeeze a good amount of the dough between your thumb and fingers and it seems a bit moist , and some dough sticks to your fingers , it should be just right
9. if not , adjust with water or flour accordingly
demonstrations.review: Fantastic, everything: the texture, the flavor, the consistance, the smell of it while baking. My bf loves it too. Is the first bread i make in the Sweet bread option and was really good, is already in my cookbook...btw,i did add more sugar, as i read could be sweeter, thanks for sharing such wonder!:)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn dog casserole

originally from 

1. in skillet , saute celery in butter for 5 min
2. add onions
3. saute 5 min
4. place in a large bowl
5. set aside
6. cut hot dogs lengthwise into 1 / 4s , then cut into 1 / 3s
7. in the same skillet , saute hot dogs for 5 min
8. or until lightly browned
9. add to vegetables
10. set aside 1 cup
11. in a large bowl , combine eggs , milk , sage and pepper
12. add the remaining hot dog mixture
13. stir in corn bread mixes
14. add 1 1 / 2 cup cheese
15. spread into a shallow 3 quart baking dish
16. top with reserved hot dog mixture and remaining cheese
17. bake , uncovered , at 400 degrees for 30 min
18. or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Was very nice, i made it today and my bf and me liked it very much. I love corndogs but as they usually have to be fried and i try to not do it, when i found this recipe was very glad that was baked instead. I made some variations though, I used polenta meal with baking powder and all-purpouse flour, instead of the cornbread mix. It's already in my favorites and i will make it more, but i guess will use something else like mushrooms instead of celery :).Tnx 4 sharing

target.recipe_text:
herbed pork tenderloin

this special pork is tender and juicy and seasoned just right.

1. mix the first 11 ingredients
2. rub over the pork
3. put on a rack in a shallow roasting pan
4. bake , uncovered , at 400 for 45 minutes
5. remove from oven , cover with foil and let set for 10 minutes
6. slice into servings
target.review: WONDERFUL!!!!   I didn't have any thyme so I used a little more basil, rubbed it all on, crowded the two tenderloins together and cooked for 40 minutes.  My husband and son raved about it!  So moist and tender -- I'm so glad I didn't give up on pork tenderloin -- this was the best!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
twinkie banana cream pudding dessert

this a very easy recipe. everyone loves it.  tastes cool and creamy on a warm day and doesn't heat up the kitchen!

1. split twinkies lengthwise and lay in 9x13 pan
2. prepare instant pudding with 1 1 / 2 cups milk
3. lay sliced bananas over twinkies in pan and pour pudding over bananas
4. prepare 2 envelopes of dream whip as per package directions and spread this over the top of pudding
5. chill in refrigerator until set
demonstrations.review:
This was good but the twinkies never softened up enough.  Sometimes the twinkie spongecake is overly done, so this could have been the problem.  The sponge cake cups (used for strawberry shortcake), sliced in half, would be an excellent substitution.  

Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dunkley s famous macaroni salad

for large gatherings, i think this salad would go over great! this is one of the best tasting macaroni salads i have ever had! i know there are a lot of ingredients, but don't skimp.  the flavor sensation is absolutely incredible!! i saw this on food network's 'calling all cooks', and got the recipe from the website. this recipe serves about 25 people.
note:  the original recipe calls for 1-2 tbsps. garlic salt, and that's the way i entered the recipe.  if you are salt sensitive, i suggest you use less.  you can always add more.

1. bring 2 quarts of water to a boil
2. add macaroni and cook until it is al dente , approximately 7-9 minutes
3. do not overcook the pasta or it will fall apart when the salad is tossed together
4. rinse macaroni until cool
5. drain well and let it dry out slightly
6. place pasta in a large bowl
7. carefully fold in celery , onion , cheddar , swiss cheese , parmesan , dill pickles , salami , and black olives
8. refrigerate the mixture , covered , overnight
9. mix the garlic salt , minced garlic , white pepper , black pepper , cayenne pepper , dry mustard and celery salt together
10. add to the salad
11. fold in pimentos
12. mix 1 cup of mayonnaise and horseradish
13. fold into the salad
14. refrigerate for another 30 minutes to 1 hour before serving
demonstrations.review:
Huge, Huge hit!!!  After two bites, people were asking for the recipe!  I heard repeatedly that this was the best pasta salad they had ever eaten.

Notes:  Didn't add as much onion -- 3/4 cup of each (red and white).  Did not add dill pickles.  Had chopped more than a cup of each of the cheeses and salami, so just threw it all in.  Used more mayo and more horseradish -- just a personal preference -- gave it a creamier texture and a little more kick. 

Thanks for a wonderful recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot spinach and artichoke dip  lower than normal fat

made with lower fat ingredients. thicker texture (not runny). dip freezes well. if you haven't tried this type of dip yet, you don't know what you're missing! cook time is for microwave.

1. drain any liquid that may be sitting on top of the sour cream
2. mix everything together well
3. bake it at 350 degrees , stirring once or twice , until heated through
4. if lazy , hungry , or just plain impatient , use the microwave
5. this mix freezes well
6. there is no need to bake before freezing
7. you may want to freeze this recipe in four 2-cup containers
8. serve with tortilla chips or pita
demonstrations.review: This was by far the best spinach and artichoke dip we have tried!  My kids were complaining when I said I was trying a new dip for pre-Christmas dinner.  However, they were soon raving about how great it was!  I used low-fat cream cheese and low-fat sour cream.  This makes a lot!  I will be making and freezing it for my daughter's baby shower.  Great recipe.  Thanks Kat!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan crusted turkey cutlets

a nice quick weeknight dinner.

1. combine bread crumbs , parmesan cheese , sage , salt and pepper
2. dip each cutlet into the eggs and then into the bread crumb mixture
3. in a large nonstick skillet , heat oil over moderately high heat
4. add as many cutlets as will fit and cook until done
5. keep warm while cooking the other cutlets
6. remove all from pan and add to the pan the juice of 1 lemon , deglaze the pan for a couple of minutes and then pour juices over cutlets
demonstrations.review: This is definitely delicious!  The sage gives it such a wonderful flavor and frying in just a little canola gives the outside such a nice crispy coating.  It doesn't take long to cook -- browned and in the oven on low to keep warm until the rest are done.  I didn't like the taste of the lemon pan juices, so I served them without.  I put a bottle of Bullseye BBQ Sauce on the table thinking they might want a sauce.  I was wrong!!  My son, "Mr. Picky Eater," went back for seconds, finishing off the last two cutlets!  I call that a complete success!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious corn muffins

these delicious corn muffins were served at kenny roger's restaurant. i found the recipe on "top secret recipes". i love to serve them with bbq. they are so good it is almost like eating a dessert.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. mix butter , sugar , honey , eggs , and salt into a large bowl
3. add flour , cornmeal , and baking powder and blend thoroughly
4. add milk while mixing
5. add corn to mixture and work into mixture
6. do not mash corn , the whole kernel is baked into the muffin
7. fill a muffin pan with 12 paper / foil muffin cups and fill 2 / 3 full with batter
8. bake for 20-25 minutes until muffins are light brown
demonstrations.review: I was really expecting "corn" muffins and should have realized that with more flour than cornmeal that they would not be.  These were just ok,  something seemed to be missing.  The texture was not what you would expect from a corn muffin.

target.recipe_text:
stupendous london broil

so easy! so delicious! an experiment i tried once, and the family has asked for it again and again. to feed more people, buy a larger cut of london broil.

1. heat a large , heavy saute pan over medium high heat
2. when hot , add oil and swirl pan to cover bottom of pan completely
3. salt and pepper one side of the london broil
4. place seasoned side down in the prepared pan
5. salt and pepper the remaining side and add a splatter screen to the pan
6. for medium-rare , saute meat for three minutes on the first side
7. turn and saute for three and a half minutes on the other side
8. for more well-done meat , saute four minutes per side
9. using tongs , transfer meat to a heated plate and place in very low-heat oven
10. return pan to burner and while stirring , add the green onions , garlic and mushrooms
11. stir just until onions start to wilt
12. pour in wine and add bouillon paste
13. stir up any browned bits and boil until liquid decreases by half
14. when sauce has reduced , slice meat on the bias into thin strips and serve with sauce
target.review: Stupendous indeed!! The only thing I changed was I used a container of Knorr Homestyle concentrated beef stock and that was only because I didn't have any beef bouillon paste and I used Vermouth because I didn't have white wine.  Otherwise, I followed the recipe exactly. Wonderful flavor and meat was tender! Will definitely be making this again!! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy cherry cobbler   from gooseberry patch

enjoy this recipe from 101 homestyle favorites cookbook.

i haven't tried it yet but i wanted it here for safekeeping!

1. in a saucepan over medium heat , cook cherries with their juice until boiling
2. remove from heat
3. in a medium bowl , mix flour , one cup sugar , milk , baking powder and salt
4. spread butter in a 2-quart casserole dish or in 4 to 6 one-cup ramekins
5. pour flour mixture over butter
6. add cherries
7. do not stir
8. sprinkle remaining sugar over top
9. bake at 400 degrees for 20 to 30 minutes
10. serve warm , garnished as desired
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! Easy & delicious! I didn't need to go through the cooking process and sprinkling the sugar on top at the end because I used a 21 oz. can of Cherry Pie Filling. I have also made this with Strawberry Pie Filling. My hubby LOVED it! Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nestle toll house chocolate chip pan cookie

this recipe was in my paper recently and i made them for my co-workers. divine! i looked & looked and was surprised i couldn't find it already on zaar.

1. preheat oven to 375 grease a 15x10-inch jelly roll pan
2. combine flour , baking soda and salt in small bowl
3. beat butter , both sugars and vanilla in large mixer bowl
4. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each
5. gradually beat flour mixture into butter mixture
6. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
7. spread into prepared pan
8. bake 20-25 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I just made this tonight and was so pleased with the results and so was my hubby! I did use a 9 x 13 pan as suggested by the many reviews but I do think I will try it in the larger jelly roll pan next time. I had to bake mine for 30 minutes but I'm sure it is because of my oven. They turned out golden brown on the top and soft and chewy on the inside. Served warm with vanilla ice cream. WONDERFUL!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corned beef dinner   crock pot

very nice aroma to come home to and a wonderful taste. satisfying

1. trim brisket of all visible fat , cut to fit 4 qt or larger crockpot , if necessary
2. place onion , celery , potatoes and carrots in bottom of crockpot , lay brisket on top
3. whisk together bouillon , bay leaf , garlic , worcestershire sauce and dry mustard
4. pour over brisket , cover pot
5. cook on low setting for 8 to 10 hours , adding cabbage wedges and caraway seed for the last hour of cooking
6. to serve , discard cooking liquid , slice meat onto hot serving plates , accompany with the cooked potatoes , carrots , celery , cabbage wedges and your favourite mustard
demonstrations.review: Absolutely wonderful! I had to cut this recipe to half because there's no way a whole recipe would ever fit in my 5 quart crockpot! I used canned low sodium, low fat beef broth instead of the beef bouillion, omitted the celery (since we don't like celery) and used 2 cloves of garlic because we love garlic. I kept everything else the same. I took it over to my mother's & plugged it in to cook while we were running around all day & boy, the wonderful smell when we walked in! The taste was even better! My mother had 3 helpings & my husband just ooh'd & aah'd through the whole thing. GREAT recipe that I'll definitely make again. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
breakfast casserole supreme

this is a wonderful almost do ahead breakfast. great for company or christmas morning.

1. melt margarine and place in the bottom of 9" by 13" baking pan
2. spread potatoes in bottom of the pan
3. sprinkle chopped vegetables over potatoes
4. add salt and pepper to taste
5. sprinkle meat over potatoes and vegetables
6. pour beaten eggs over potatoes
7. bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes
8. remove from oven and sprinkle cheese evenly over top
9. bake another 5-10 minutes or until cheese is hot and bubbly
10. remove from oven and let set for approximately 5 minutes
11. cut into 2
12. 5"-3" squares and serve with a spatula
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was WONDERFUL! I used smoked ham. Instead of the chopped tomatoes, I used a can of diced tomatoes with green chilies (drained), a 4 cheese blend instead of the straight cheddar and omitted the green peppers just because I didn't have any. I did the overnight thing and it turned out perfect. The tomatoes with green chilies gave it a nice kick. It's just Hubby and me, so I was able to freeze part in individual baggies for convenient, microwave breakfasts throughout the week for both of us. Thanks so much for sharing. I can't wait to try it again with sausage and bacon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
world s best butter cookies

i tested 8 different butter cookie recipes, looking for the "perfect" butter cookie. it had to be buttery, a little crumbly (like shortbread), and not too sweet. this is the winner. i think these are the worlds best butter cookie, courtesy of chef alice medrich.

1. beat the butter , sugar , salt and vanilla together until smooth and creamy
2. mix in the egg yolk until well incorporated , scraping down the sides of the bowl at least once
3. add the flour and mix just until incorporated
4. scrape onto a lightly floured board and knead a few times , just until the dough smooths out
5. turn onto a sheet of plastic wrap and roll into a log , wrap up and refrigerate for several hours or freeze
6. before baking , preheat the oven to 325f
7. line your baking sheets with parchment
8. slice the dough into slices about 1 / 8" thick and place them on the sheets about an inch apart
9. bake until just beginning to turn golden around the edges , about 16-18 minutes
10. you could roll the dough out and cut shapes
11. you could slice them even thinner and sandwich them with chocolate or jam or lemon curd
12. you could make them and then dip them half into chocolate
13. you could just make them and eat them , which is my favorite
14. whatever you do , they will be delicious
demonstrations.review: These are AWESOME!! PERFECT!! I rolled dough into logs wrapped in plastic wrap, refrigerated them overnight and just sliced and baked them the next day. Wonderful! This will definitely be THE Butter Cookie recipe in my box. Thanks!!

target.recipe_text:
asparagus with thyme

love asparagus and this one is very good!! from cooking light.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. rub the cut sides of the garlic over a 13 x 9 inch baking dish , place garlic in dish
3. snap off tough ends of asparagus
4. add asparagus to dish , drizzle with oil
5. sprinkle asparagus with thyme and salt and fresh ground pepper to taste
6. toss gently and bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes , stirring once
target.review: Good flavor, but 20 minutes was way too long. I bought fresh picked asparagus from the farmer's market this morning. The 20 minute cooking time left it mushy. I'll try again and cut the cooking time by at least 5 minutes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chili maple glazed dump chicken oamc

i love dump recipes and this one is an easy 4 ingredient one!

1. for immediate cooking: pre-heat oven to 350f place all ingredients into a large baking dish , turn chicken to coat
2. bake until chicken juices run clear
3. for freezing: place all ingredients into a 1 gallon freezer bag
4. lay flat in freezer
5. to thaw and cook: take the bag out of the freezer the night before , make sure the bag is sealed completely
6. for the oven: preheat the oven to 350f empty the contents of the bag into a large baking dish and bake until the juices run clear
7. for the crockpot: cook on low for 6-8 hours or on high for 4-6 or until done
8. on the grill: cook over medium heat until juices run clear
demonstrations.review: I love finding recipes that can be made with ingredients usually on hand.  The family liked this, but we felt it could use a little more zip to the flavor.  It is getting added to the rotation, but next time I'll increase the amount of chili powder and maybe add some red pepper flakes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon chicken alfredo fettuccine

very rich and tasty meal, but also easy because it uses ready-made ingredients. it's not a fussy meal for busy night. my favorite alfredo sauce has also added mushrooms in it for extra flavor that goes great together with bacon. time for prep and cooking is quesstimated.

1. cook fettuccine according to package directions
2. meanwhile , in a large skillet cook bacon over medium heat until crisp
3. remove from pan using a slotted spoon
4. set in on paper towels to soak up the grease and drain the skillet reserving 3 tablespoons of drippings
5. season the chicken with salt and pepper
6. cook chicken in the bacon drippings over medium high heat until juices run clear
7. drain fettuccine , stir into skillet with the chicken
8. add the alfredo sauce , spinach , italian seasoning , and bacon
9. cook and stir occasionally until heated through
10. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: Very easy to make.  My 12 yr old son picked this out as one of the recipes he wanted me to use to teach him how to cook.  It used some basic cooking skills but nothing fancy.  We made this exactly as the recipe read with no changes. The whole family loved it.  My son wanted me to add to make sure you only cook the noodles al dente. Squishy noodles are gross.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beer can duck

a variation on beer can chicken. i did this with a can of iced tea rather than beer but i don't think it makes that big a difference (my beer can chicken does not taste like beer and this duck did not taste like tea - the flavors come from the rub). remember roasting duck is not like roasting chicken. the skin of a duck is massively fatty and the meat is dark meat. you need a lot of cooking time and you want the fat to drip out. piercing the outer layer of skin and long roasting time will accomplish this and will leave you with a crispy delicious skin.

1. salt the duck and place it uncovered in the refrigerator overnight to dry out
2. preheat oven to 425
3. pierce the duck skin with a sharp knife in mul
4. make sure not to pierce through to the meat
5. piercing at an angle will help to ensure you only go through skin and fat
6. combine ingredients for the rub and rub over the entire duck
7. open the can , empty half and pierce 2-3 extra holes in the top
8. optionally you can make extra rub and add to the can
9. plug the duck neck opening with a small lime or shallot or spud
10. stand the can in a relatively deep drip pan with a bit of water in the pan and lower the duck onto the can shoving it into the backside as far up as it goes
11. place in oven and roast for one hour at 425 , then one hour at 375 , and then one hour at 325
12. remove from oven and carefully separate can from bird then carve and serve
13. you will have a huge amount of rendered duck fat in the pan which you can refrigerate or freeze and save for future use
demonstrations.review:
I had never prepared duck before, but my daughter loves it and I was tired of paying $25/plate for it when we went out to dinner.

My only suggestion is to cut down the cooking time by 15-30 minutes.  I had a 5.5 lb duckling and it came out a little dry.  

The flavor was excellent. I used a dark beer and put about a tbs of the rub in it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nutty rice salad

refreshing and delicious!  unique blend of flavours.  taken from cottage life's summer weekend cookbook.  great with steak!  be sure to advise guest of peanuts as they're not obvious in presentation.

1. salad: in a small saucepan , bring water and rice to a boil
2. reduce heat to low
3. cover and cook 20 minutes or until done
4. meanwhile , cut asparagus into 1 / 2" sections and blanch
5. chop red pepper , green onion , peanuts and parsley
6. zest and section orange
7. mix all ingredients together including orange zest , but not orange slices
8. refrigerate
9. dressing: whisk ingredients together and spoon over servings of rice salad as desired
10. serve with orange sections
11. time to make includes prep and cook times
demonstrations.review:
I needed a quick side dish to go along with Pork Chops Bambara (#112557). I had almost all of the ingredients except the  asparagus spears and lemon juice. I took a creative liberty and substituted lime juice and left out the  asparagus spears.

It still was great and went well with the Chops.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious apricot glazed pork roast  crock pot

wonderful taste! a tender, succulent roast from the crock pot is the answer to your dinner dreams. put on to cook before leaving for work and it's ready to eat when you get home!

1. mix broth , preserves , onion and mustard in slow cooker
2. add pork and turn to coat
3. cover and cook on low 8-9 hours or until done
4. is good served with steamed broccoli and carrots , baked potato and warm dinner rolls
demonstrations.review: Recipe was very easy, but following the recipe as written gives you a lot of very runny sauce. I should have followed the advise of other reviewers. It didn' have a lot of flavor and the the meat did not absorb as much of the "sauce" as we would have liked. I'll try it again put not add the broth and maybe add it some other seasoning to give it more pep.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot breakfast apple cobbler

this makes a great breakfast or dessert for 2. put it on before bed and its ready in the morning and the house smells like apples.

1. place apples in slow cooker and mix in remaining ingredients
2. cover and cook on low 7 to 9 hours or on high 2 to 3 hours
3. serve with milk
target.review:
This was delicious but several other cooks scared me about it burning or ruining my crock pot so this is what I did:
1)  I made it just after dinner and left it unplugged until I went to bed so it only cooked for 8 hours.
2)  I put in 1/2 cup of water and it was a little soupy at the bottom but as left overs the water was completely absorbed.  I would go less - even 1/4 cup of water.
3)  I didn't understand the need to pour melted butter over the top so I just put in two tablespoons of butter on top - less effort on my part.
Comment:  This makes way more than 2 servings.  My two daughters and I each had a serving and there were at least 2 servings left over.  So that makes 4-6 servings in my book.  Definitely a keeper.  No worries on the crock pot if you  follow the directions and stack the foods.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerly molasses christmas banana bread

this is a quick, warmly-spiced banana bread that i invented for christmas 2010.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix butter , oil , bananas , sugar , molasses , and egg until smooth
3. sprinkle baking soda & spices over mixture , mix lightly
4. add flour , stir until combined
5. add raisins , stir
6. pour into buttered bread pan
7. sprinkle top with kosher salt
8. bake for one hour
9. remove from pan and cool on rack
