demonstrations.review: I'm sorry but this bread disappointed me; it did smell good cooking in the oven though.  The ingredients intrigued me, particularly the molasses and the bananas.  The batter was dense and the resulting bread was dense and dry.  The cooking time is off as several have noted the edges being burnt.  I followed the directions exactly, except I combined all the dry ingredients and sifted them together (Like all recipes call for.).  I would do two things.  First, I used a 9" pan, I would use a 8" pan and pull it out after 45-50 minutes at 350F.  The author says he invented this bread.  I should have known the outcome was going to be disappointing as the recipe only calls for 2 tablespoons of butter and one tablespoon of oil.  Most other recipes call for more moisture in the form of butter, oil or apple sauce.  The other thing that surprises me is that the resulting bread is not sweet at all.  I think this is a result of all the allspice used.  This is only one loaf and it calls for a full teaspoon of allspice.  I will look for another recipe like this which calls for more wet ingredients.  One final thought: what is the smell of Christmas?  I always thought it was the smell of pine??

demonstrations.recipe_text:
back of    that   bag choc  chip cookies   toll house

you know which chocolate chip bag i am talking about! i didn't see any recipes posted yet that matched this recipe from the "house of toll" so i thought i'd go ahead and post it. here you go!

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. in a small bowl , combine flour , baking soda , and salt
3. set aside
4. in a large bowl , beat butter , granulated sugar , brown sugar , and vanilla extract until creamy
5. add eggs , one at a time , beating well after each addition
6. gradually beat in flour mixture to the butter mixture
7. stir in chocolate chips and nuts
8. drop by rounded tablespoon onto ungreased cookie sheet
9. bake for 9-11 minutes , or until golden brown
10. allow to cool on the baking sheet for 2 minutes , then transfer the cookies to wire racks to cool completely
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: This is simply the best chocolate chip cookie recipe there is.  I have tried others and they don't compare.  By the way, I use generic brand chocolate chips and they come out just as delicious.  I don't think the recipe can be beat (just like the pumpkin pie recipe on the libby's pumpkin can label).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
top secret recipes version of wendy s chili by todd wilbur

originally from top secret recipes by todd wilbur http://www.topsecretrecipes.com

1. brown the ground beef in a skillet over medium heat
2. drain off the fat
3. using a fork , crumble the cooked beef into pea-size pieces
4. in a large pot , combine the beef plus all the remaining ingredients , and bring to a simmer over low heat
5. cook , stirring every 15 minutes , for 2 to 3 hours
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved this.  I must have put a bit more tomatoes and sauce in this as I did not have the exact cans specified.  It produced a chili on the soupy side so we decided to serve it Cincinnati style: on spaghetti with cheddar cheese on top.  Very good for this!  This makes a lot of chili.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fisherman s wharf stew

this is a great chunky stew that is made in the crock-pot. slightly adapted from a pillsbury recipe.

1. in a 4-quart crock pot , add the oil , onion , and garlic
2. stir to mix well
3. add in the carrots , tomatoes , bell pepper , fennel seed , bay leaf , wine , and clam juice
4. stir to mix
5. cover and cook on low for 8-9 hours
6. 20 minutes before ready to serve , add the cod , shrimp , sugar , basil , salt , pepper , and hot sauce
7. stir to mix
8. cook on high for 15-20 minutes or until fish flakes
9. take out bay leaf and add parsley
10. stir and serve
demonstrations.review: I've cooked this dish several times.  I followed the directions except where it called for fresh parsley (using dried instead and putting that in with the fish).  This dish was easy to make and was delicious every time.  It is so rich but yet there's no milk in the recipe.  The hot sauce gives it that extra kick.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
libby s famous pumpkin pie

well, after looking for this recipe on here and not having any luck, i decided to find it and post it. in my opinion, this is the best pumpkin pie. make your own graham cracker crust or buy an already prepared one.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees fahrenheit
2. mix sugar , salt , cinnamon , ginger , and cloves in small bowl
3. beat eggs in large bowl
4. stir in pumpkin and sugar-spice mixture
5. gradually stir in evaporated milk
6. pour mixture into pie shell
7. bake at 425 degrees fahrenheit for 15 minutes
8. reduce temperature to 350 degrees fahrenheit
9. bake for 40 to 50 minutes or until knife inserted near center comes out clean
10. cool on wire rack for 2 hours
11. serve immediately or refrigerate
12. top with whipped cream before serving for best results !
13. do not overcook
14. overcooking leads to pie cracking in the middle
15. try to bake the day you will serve the pie
16. cooking in advance can make the crust soggy
17. if you have to bake a day before serving , pop the pie in the oven for 5 to 10 minutes and it should bring the crust back to life !
demonstrations.review:
Yes, yes, yes.
This is it; this is better than my mother's!  I have made quite a few pumpkin pies and this recipe is the best.  It makes just the right amount and is very light and tasty.  With the whipped cream, it's even more delicious.  Best when just cool enough to slice!

I substituted generic brand pumpkin and used the pumpkin spice mix.  Thanks for the tip on the spices.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s potato kugel

this is mostly served as a side dish with pot roast and gravy, i have even made this for sunday brunch and served it with eggs! --- to save time the potatos may be grated and kept refrigerated covered completely in cold water for up to 3 days ---i like to also add in some cayenne pepper for a little heat --- for a lighter fluffier textured kugel add in another egg with 1 teaspoon baking powder --- for passover subsitute matzo meal for the flour.

1. set oven to 400 degrees f (
2. grease a 13 x 9-inch baking pan , then pour about 3 tablespoons oil into bottom of the baking dish
3. squeeze out excess moisture from the shredded potatoes with hands , and place into a large bowl , then add in chopped onion
4. add in remaining ingredients with 3 tablespoons remaining oil
5. mix well to combine
6. adjust the salt and pepper if needed
7. the next step is only optional it will speed up cooking time and create a crispy bottom and sides
8. place the baking dish with the oil in the oven and heat the oil for about 6-8 minutes
9. carefully spread the potato mixture in the baking dish
10. this step is only optional otherwise just pour the potato mixture into the oiled cold baking dish
11. bake uncovered for about 1-1 / 4 hours , or until nicely browned on top
target.review: Mmm, eating the leftovers right now.  This is so yummy, definitely the best potato kugel I've made.  I halved the recipe, and I tried to do the optional oil step but I wasn't paying close attention and missed where you say not to use olive oil.  I used olive oil, and nothing happened, even though I left it in the oven for way longer than I intended to.  It was still delicious! Thanks for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
never fail tuna patties  salmon works too

i've made these for so long that i'm not sure of the recipe origin. they never fail, are easy to make & always good. they also work well & impress as a starter if served with crisp veggies, tartar sauce or a light mayo sauce thinned-with-milk & flavored with lime juice, dill & chives. makes 4 patties of entree size or 6-8 of starter size. *edited to add* -- my spec thx to chef jillaz for reviewing this recipe for the freezer tag game in the oamc forum & for the info she provided. pls see note #2 at the end of prep steps for this info. :-)

1. combine 1st 5 ingredients in a mixing bowl
2. add corn flakes til you no longer see any liquid in the mixture , but more is usually better
3. divide into 4 equal portions on a cutting board
4. shape patties & flatten to 3 / 4 in thickness
5. use spatula to transfer carefully to non-stick skillet & saute over med-low heat in olive oil til golden brown & crisp on both sides
6. i use crushed corn flakes or pepperide farm dressing mix
7. i don't care for the mushy texture of the end-product or the difficulty holding the patties together when potato is used
8. place patties in a freezer bag w / layers of parchment paper in between
9. seal , label & freeze
10. to serve ~ thaw in fridge or microwave & cook as directed
11. ~~ cooked patties can also be frozen wrapped in plastic wrap & placed in a freezer bag
12. thaw in fridge or microwave & reheat on stovetop or in oven
demonstrations.review:
Yum!  Easy and yummy.  My husband and I both really enjoyed these.  I used bread crumbs instead of corn flakes.  Thank you!

FYI - I have made these a million times - and they come out just as good with only one egg. :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect chocolate brownies

this is the best brownie recipe i've ever used and i've used several!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease a 9x13" pan
3. melt shortening in a large saucepan over low heat , then stir in cocoa
4. remove from heat
5. mix in sugar and vanilla then mix in eggs one at a time
6. stir in remaining ingredients then stir in nuts
7. bake for 30 minutes
8. cool completely , before cutting into 2x2" squares
9. i have read all the great reviews and learned from them , thank you all
10. now i line my pan with buttered alumunin foil or parchment paper
11. this works very well
demonstrations.review: My guests all LOVED these and so did I.  A few guests snuck away with some wrapped in napkins! lol! Thanks for a great and easy recipe.  I used dark chocolate chips and crushed almonds instead of walnuts or pecans and olive oil for shortning.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy polenta with parmesan and mozzarella

i love polenta with stew, sausages, salmon,etc. this is easy and in expensive to prepare.

1. in a large saucepan over high heat , combine milk and cornmeal , whisking until mixture boils
2. reduce heat to medium and simmer , whisking frequently until mixture thickens , about 15 minutes
3. add rosemary and cheeses
4. whisk until cheese is melted
5. season to taste
demonstrations.review: Just what I was looking for.  Thanks so much, really delicious!  I used dried thyme instead of rosemary and it was really good.  I threw some eggs into the leftovers and made little polenta cakes.  I will definitely use this recipe again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
quinoa stir fry with spinach   walnuts

found this in prevention magazine, this is easy, healthy and most importantly...very tasty.  you can substitute any cheese for the parmigiano-reggiano cheese. i recommend a strong hard cheese, but i have used all kinds and they all work.  when i’m in a rush, i leave out the walnut pieces.  a great side dish or when i am really lazy, add some cooked chicken for a great meal.

1. place quinoa in small bowl , add water to cover , and swish to rinse
2. pour into mesh strainer and drain well
3. heat oil in medium skillet
4. add quinoa
5. toast , stirring , over medium heat until golden add garlic and cook for 1 minute
6. add salt and 2 cups of water
7. heat to boil
8. cover and cook over medium-low heat until water is absorbed , about 15 minutes
9. spread walnuts in small skillet and stir over medium-low heat until toasted , about 5 minutes
10. set aside
11. when quinoa is cooked , add spinach and tomatoes to skillet
12. stir fry over medium heat until spinach is almost wilted and tomatoes are warmed , about 1 minute
13. stir in walnuts and cheese
14. garnish with basil
15. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Ok. I'm trying to not be so liberal with my 5 star ratings, but this is the best quinoa that i've ever had, and I've made LOTS and LOTS of quinoa.  This is just filled with delicious flavour.  Yum!  I left out the cheese and I added some finely chopped mushrooms to the mix as well.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chickpea burgers

good for that day in the week when you don't want to eat meat.

1. peel and mash the boiled potato with the chickpeas
2. combine with onion , garlic , oregano , parsley , coriander , salt and pepper
3. add the egg and mix well
4. shape into burgers and dust with flour
5. fry in olive oil until nicely brown on both sides
6. serve with lemon or lime slices
demonstrations.review: Pretty good.  Kinda.. bland.  I put them between bread and topped with lettuce, tomatoes, sprouts, mushrooms. Filled me up!  Very easy to make, thanks! :)  Okay I felt like I needed to add another star becuase my husband LOVED these.  He was really impressed! :)

target.recipe_text:
chow gai laan  jade green broccoli

adapted from a chinese cookbook by jim lee that was published around 1970. this is one of my all-time favorite cookbooks; i was introduced to it by friends who were chinese students i knew at university of virginia. the gai laan which the chinese eat is not actually broccoli, but broccoli is a good substitute which works well in america, where most of us don't have access to gai laan.

1. mix together sugar through soy sauce plus 1 / 2 cup water and put aside
2. heat oil in a skillet or wok over medium heat and add the garlic
3. when garlic is golden brown , add the broccoli
4. turn the heat up and stir-fry 2 minutes
5. add sherry , cover quickly and cook 2 minutes
6. lift cover& add the soy sauce mixture
7. when sauce thickens , remove and serve
target.review: We LOVED this!  Even DS, who hates broccoli, said this was "pretty good" to him.  I don't think I used a full two pounds, but DH and I were fighting over who was gonna get the last of it in the pan.  HAHA.  I won.  I didn't have any rice wine, so steamed with water  instead and it worked perfectly.  Thanks for a tasty tasty way to have broccoli!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana pudding cake

instead of making banana bread to use up those ripe bananas, why not try this instead?

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease a bundt pan and set aside
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients and beat with your electric mixer for 3 minutes
4. pour into prepared pan and bake for 50-55 minutes , or until a tester comes out clean
5. cool for 15 minutes before removing from pan
6. if desired , combine 1 cup of sifted icing sugar with a little milk and drizzle this over the cake
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and moist.  I used vanilla pudding instead, because that's what I had on hand.  I prefer it chilled...but the rest of the family loves it either way.  Thanks for a great way to use the bananas up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: 10 STARS!!!  Both DH and DS raved!  DS abhors broccoli, but he was sneaking the broccoli off of our plates and asking if there was more!  Both he and DH asked for it again this week.  Super easy too.  The only change I made was to not use the water on the beef.  Instead I laid the beef out on my cutting board, sprinkled it with cornstarch (only 1TBSP) and garlic powder.  I tossed it around to cover it all.  Next time I'm going to add water chestnuts and red peppers.  YUM!  Thanks for a definate keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken cream cheese enchiladas

this is a creamy enchalada recipe that is mildly spiced. no scotch bonnets or even jalapenos here. it's quick to make and great for a week night or lazy weekend.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. de-bone chicken , and shred chicken into small pieces , if you dont have a rotisserie chicken
3. in a large skillet , combine chicken , cream cheese cubes , sour cream , chilies , chopped onion , seasonings , and 3 / 4 cup cheddar cheese
4. heat until the cheeses are completely melted
5. coat baking pan with cooking spray
6. scoop a heaping spoonful of chicken mixture onto tortilla , roll and place into pan with seam side down , repeat until all of the filling is used
7. pour enchilada sauce over the rolled tortillas
8. sprinkle remaining cheese on top of enchiladas and bake at 350 uncovered for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: My Father-in-Law asked me to give this 10 stars!  Very tasty and rich.  I used full sized flour tortillas, 1/2 of a rotisserie chicken, mild green chiles and Hatch green enchilada sauce (my mother-in-law doesn't do anything spicy!).  I've already put this recipe into the rotation folder.  So yummy and quick and easy for a weeknight.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s sit sandwich  aka squishy sorta muffuletta

from my family recipe box, mom loves this sandwich! "this sandwich is a 'smashing success'... in more ways than one. it's a great traveler." you must admit, it is pretty amusing. :) from the family recipe box, dated 3/1/85.  the sandwich keeps well, chilled, and is good for taking along on picnics and camping trips.

1. cut loaf of bread in half horizontally and hollow out the soft bread from both halves , leaving a shell about 3 / 4-inch thick
2. reserve soft bread for another use
3. in small bowl , combine artichoke liquid with mayonnaise and spread onto bread shells
4. in bottom half , layer ingredients at least three times until mounded high , beginning and ending with tomatoes
5. place top half of bread over mound of ingredients
6. wrap entire loaf tightly with plastic wrap
7. this must be assembled at least 2 hours before serving , but can be assembled up to 8 hours before serving
8. refrigerate
9. before serving , place sandwich on a hard surface and sit on it ! this smashes the ingredients together and makes it easier to serve
10. do not omit this step , strange as it seems , as this step is what makes the sandwich delicious
11. slice the loaf into wedges or slices to serve
12. also , regarding the artichoke juice mixture: you can add only half of it to the mayo , if you like - how much of the spread you're going to need depends on the size of loaf you've gotten
13. yum !
demonstrations.review: Oh my!  How did I not remember to rate this??  This is to DIE for!  DH and DS ask for this often.  I think DS just gets a kick out of Mom letting him bounce around on dinner!  The only thing I do differently, I add the olives and the chopped up artichokes to the mayo mixture....YUM YUM!  Thanks for a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
moo shu beef lettuce cups   4 points

i made this recently and even my 9 year old daughter loved it!  she has requested it again since then.  this is a great recipe for weight watchers, core or points.  it equals 4 points per serving, 2 lettuce cups per serving.

1. brown ground beef , onion , ginger and garlic in a skillet on medium heat
2. break meat up as it cooks
3. when beef is browned , add bok choy , pepper , mushrooms and soy sauce and cook until bok choy is wilted , about 3-5 minutes
4. clean and dry bibb lettuce leaves
5. when beef mixture is done , spoon 1 / 2 cup of beef mixture into each lettuce leaf
6. yields 2 filled leaves per serving
7. serve with extra soy sauce if desired
demonstrations.review: Loved it!  I had gotten the recipe off of the WW website and was just coming to post it here.  To quote DH's words... "Hon, feel free to make this any time you want to!"  Even the picky 10 year old loved it.  Served with rice for a filling, yummy 8 pt meal!

target.recipe_text:
asian noodles  my sister s recipe

we are staying in my sister's home right now although she's not here. she left the sauce, noodles and recipe for this dish for us along with brief instructions to go out and buy some meat and bits to go in it to make a quick meal. it's really delicious. i have converted the mls to teaspoons for the metrically challenged ;-) use half the sauce, the rest keeps well in the fridge til next time.

1. sauce:
2. mix all ingredients , set aside
3. you'll need half-the remainder stores well in the fridge
4. noodles:
5. in a bowl , pour boiling water over the hokkien noodles , broccoli and shredded snow peas
6. allow to stand for 3 minutes , drain
7. heat a wok as high as possible , add the oil and stir fry the pork slices and garlic until fragrant
8. add the noodles , broccoli and snow peas and toss for a few minutes
9. add the chili paste and half the sauce and toss a couple more minutes , then add the beaten egg continuing to toss
10. lastly add the bean shoots and chives , toss briefly and serve
target.review:
made this to the recipe, it was wonderful! Samantha and I fed it to the 3 kids, (3, 5 and 8) and they fiddled around with chopsticks for a while, then opted for a fork, because they loved it!
It isnt "out of the box" but it is a damn good feed, easy to make and healthy! saving the "HALF" IT A BIT WeiRD :) but I used it over fish the next night, great! highly recomened, made for Aussie swap April 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken adobo

this recipe is based on one from atkins, the complete cookbook. the intro to the recipe reads, "the tangy vinegar marinade called adobo reflect the spanish influence on the cuisine of the philippines. islanders enjoy adobo-seasoned pork, too." allow an hour for the chicken to marinate in the refrigerator.

1. in a large glass baking dish , mix together the vinegar , garlic , bay leaf , peppercorns , and soy sauce
2. add the chicken and toss to coat
3. cover and marinate for 1 hour in the refrigerator
4. transfer chicken and its marinade to a large saucepan
5. add water and bring to a boil
6. cover , reduce heat to low , and simmer 20 minutes
7. using tongs , transfer chicken to a plate to cool
8. boil cooking liquid about 10 minutes , or until reduced to 1 cup
9. allow sauce to cool
10. strain into a small saucepan
11. skim off fat and reheat
12. pat chicken dry with paper towels
13. in a large skillet , heat oil over high heat until quite hot
14. brown chicken in batches , about 2 minutes per side
15. transfer to a deep platter and pour hot sauce over chicken
16. if desired , garnish with cilantro
demonstrations.review:
I didnt like this much, but Hubby did. I found it a little too salty for me, though I thought that the chicken itself, cold, without the sauce was very nice. I think the skin  absorbed too much of the soy.
BUT, the recipe was easy to follow, and turned out well.
thanks mersaydees

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry cream cheese dream pie

a nice, fresh summer pie - or anytime you have fresh strawberries available to you!  lovely pie to take to gatherings- especially things such as 4th of july,etc.

1. blend cream cheese and milk together
2. spread on bottom of pie crust
3. cut up 1 cup prepared berries and simmer with 1 / 2 cup water for a few minutes
4. mix sugar and cornstarch and lemon juice with 1 / 4 cup water and add to cooked berries , stirring until thick and clear
5. add a few drops food color
6. cool
7. place rest of whole berries on cream cheese and pour mixture over this
8. chill until ready to serve , at least 30 minutes
9. to serve , this can be topped with cool whip , fresh whipping cream with a touch of rum or brandy would be lovely as well --
demonstrations.review:
excellent! came together well, very easy to make. made my own crust, and the cream cheese was very soft, so I didnt add the milk.
The strawberries I had were a little tart, so I sprinkled the fresh ones with a little sugar. 
For the Aussies, a quart of strawberries is about 2 punnets :)
would recommend this recipe!
2009 Aug Aussie swap

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cabbage filled pastries

filled pastries are a popular item all over eastern europe. these are a vegetarian version filled with cabbage.

1. heat oil in a large nonstick skillet over medium heat
2. add onion , and cabbage
3. sprinkle with brown sugar , lemon juice , dill weed , salt and pepper
4. cook , strirring frequently , about 8 minutes or until tender
5. stir constantly toward the end of coooking time to keep vegatables from sticking
6. remove from heat and let cool 5 to 10 minutes
7. preheat oven to 400 degrees
8. have an ungreased baking sheet ready
9. separate biscuits and place them between two sheets of wax paper several inches apart
10. with a rolling pin , roll biscuits into 4 to 5 inch circles
11. carefully remove the top sheet of wax paper
12. using a heaping tablespoonful of filling , place slightly off-center on each circle
13. carefully fold biscuits over , making a half-circle and stretching dough gently over the filling
14. crimp the edges together with a fork
15. place pastries on baking sheet
16. bake 8-10 minutes until golden brown
17. serve hot or at room temperature
demonstrations.review:
it was wonderfull! I ate way too much! I have been trying to duplicate a piroshki recipe I had in Sydney, so I made half as directed, and to the other half I added cooked bacon and rice noodles.
It was "ok" but the original recipe was wonderful!
we dont have "refrigerator biscuits" here, so I made up a pillsbury recipe I got from another site.
would recommend this one!

made for aussie recipe sway, june 2012

demonstrations.recipe_text:
filet mignon with whiskey cream sauce

for those that must sauce their filet but are not willing to sacrifice their good wine, this recipe is amazing.  i would venture to say that it will meet, if not rival, your favorite restaurant's offerings.

my recipe calls for cracked black pepper, but i also like to use coarsely chopped peppercorns as an alternative.  additionally, substituting toasted fennel seeds for the rosemary works very well.  cooking time is approximate.

1. bring filets to room temperature
2. on a plate combine the pepper and rosemary
3. salt both sides of filets , then press one side into pepper mixture to form a crust
4. in a very hot , heavy skillet add a little olive oil and butter
5. sear filets until desired doneness is reached
6. remove to cutting board to rest for 5 to 10 minutes
7. for the sauce , combine broth and pepper
8. reduce to half
9. add whiskey , cream and mustard
10. reduce to desired amount
11. remove from heat and swirl in butter
12. allow to cool slightly to thicken
13. serve steaks whole or slice thinly and top with sauce
demonstrations.review:
This is very close to the one I was about to submit:)
If I may add a footnote, I always melt butter and mix in some mustard, then brush this on to thick bread, (crust removed) and put in the oven for 20 mins, turning once. Sit the steak on the crouton, and pour the sauce over.
Because I HATE cold steak, I usually add a little butter and flour to the pan, helps the thickening process. 
This is truly an elegant dinner party recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
t d  f   hot bread dip

this is a must try recipe....i've been making it years and have nothing but rave reviews. i recommend everyone give this a go and if you dont love it you can hunt me down and beat me with a stick...lol

1. cut a thin slice from top of bread loaf , set slice aside
2. using a gentle sawing motion , cut vertically to , but not through , bottom of the loaf , 1 / 2 inch from the edge
3. lift out center of loaf
4. tear into 1-inch cubes , and set aside
5. cut ham , spring onion , jalapeno and capsicum into very small dice
6. mix cream cheese , sour cream and tasty cheese in bowl , add other ingredients and mix well
7. place mixture into the cavity of the bread and replace top of loaf
8. wrap in foil and cook in moderate oven for about 1 hour
9. before serving give the dip a little stir to ensure even distribution of cheese
10. serve with reserved bread chunks that have been toasted in oven
11. once these have been consumed everyone just tears open the bread bowl
12. also good with corn chips
demonstrations.review:
made this for my nephews engagement party, and followed the recipe almost to a T, (jalapeno are not common here) I added a teaspoon of my home made chili sauce.
turned out very well, also you can make the mixture the day before :)

target.recipe_text:
creamy cajun chicken pasta

n'awlin's style of chicken with an updated alfredo sauce.

1. place chicken and cajun seasoning in a bowl and toss to coat
2. in a large skillet over medium heat , saut chicken in butter or margarine until chicken is tender , about 5 to 7 minutes
3. reduce heat add green onion , heavy cream , tomatoes , basil , salt , garlic powder , black pepper and heat through
4. pour over hot linguine and toss with parmesan cheese
target.review: Great recipe! Takes very similar to Pasta Weesie at Carrabba's. I added sliced baby bella's and used 1/4 of a yellow onion (didnt have the green onion). Next time I would like to try with half the chicken and add some shrimp. Thanks for posting...great meal!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian sausage pie

this pie makes a lovely light supper dish. it takes very little time to put together and bake. serve it with your favorite salad. this recipe is adapted from a cookbook by the sons of italy florida foundation.

1. place pie shell in oven during the pre-heating time for about 5- 10 minutes in order to firm the bottom some
2. don't overcook !
3. remove casing from the sausage and crumble
4. saut sausage and onions
5. drain well and spoon into prepared pie shell
6. blend eggs , milk , cheese , salt and pepper
7. pour over sausage mixture
8. bake at 350 degrees f
9. for 35 minutes , or until custard sets and tests clean with a knife
10. allow to cool slightly
11. cut into 8 wedges and serve
demonstrations.review: Great recipe! I used heavy cream instead of the milk. Definitely not low fat, but ohhhh sooo good! I made a couple of alterations...added some garlic and Italian seasonings with the onions and sausage, but that's it. For the pie crust, I used Pillsbury refrigerated pie dough. My husband told me that he is eating the leftovers for breakfast tomorrow! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coca cola pork roast

there are lots of cola/meat recipes on this site, this one is a little different. i found this in a crockpot cookbook that my folks gave me for christmas. i tweaked it a bit, but still--great stuff!

1. rub the roast with salt and pepper then place it in the crockpot
2. add soup mix and coke
3. cook on low 8 hours or high for 4
4. before serving dump liquid from crockpot into a pot
5. skim fat
6. to the remaining juices add salt and pepper to taste and a dash of kitchen bouquet
7. bring mixture to a boil
8. remove a cup of the liquid and add corn starch to thicken
9. add corn starch mixture to the rest of the juices
10. cook until it reaches desired consistency
11. wonderful gravy !
demonstrations.review: This was great! I decided to chop up some onions and add to the slow cooker as one reviewer suggested. I also substituted the onion mix for beefy onion mix (all that I had on hand). After 8 hours, I took the roast out and added the corn starch to the sauce (I did not add the Kitchen Bouquet). I shredded the pork and added it back to the pot to marinate for another 30 minutes. Served this "burrito" style in some warm tortillas and rice. YUMMY!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
portuguese paella

i love the blend of flavors in this dish.  this is a hearty one dish meal. the secret spice is the saffron.  saffron is expensive, but you must add it or the taste of authentic paella is lost.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. sprinkle chicken with rosemary , 1 / 2 teaspoon salt , and black pepper
3. heat oil in a large oven proof nonstick skillet or paella pan over medium-high heat
4. add chicken
5. cook for 3 minutes on each side or until lightly browned
6. remove chicken from pan
7. cover and keep warm
8. add chourice and cook until lightly browned
9. add onion and bell pepper
10. cook for 7 minutes , stirring constantly
11. add rice , tomato , paprika , saffron and garlic
12. cook for 1 minute stirring constantly
13. return chicken to pan
14. add broth and 1 / 4 teaspoon of salt
15. bring to boil
16. wrap handle of pan with foil , cover pan
17. bake at 400f for 10 minutes
18. stir in shrimp , asparagus , and peas
19. cover and bake an additional 5 minutes or until shrimp are no longer translucent
demonstrations.review: Yummy Yummy Yummy! This is my first time cooking paella and it was a total success. I used 2 spicy chorizo links instead of the 1 link suggested. I also used Vigo yellow rice with saffron so I didn't need to buy the threads. The rice took a little longer to cook, but just stay patient! My husband took the leftovers to work the next day and all of his colleagues wanted the recipe! Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
yummy crunchy apple pie

great pie!

1. use foil on bottom of oven rather than a cookie sheet under pie pan
2. prepare pastry for single-crust pie
3. place in pie plate and trim and crimp the edge
4. refrigerate 30 minute loosely covered with plastic wrap
5. in a large mixing bowl , stir together the sugar , flour , cinnamon , nutmeg , allspice , and salt
6. add apple slices and gently toss until they are coated well
7. transfer mixture to pie
8. for crumb topping: stir together brown sugar , flour , and oats
9. using a pastry blender , cut in the butter until topping resembles coarse crumbs
10. sprinkle over apple mixture in pie
11. to prevent over-browning while baking , cover edge of pie with foil
12. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for 25 minutes
13. remove foil and bake 25 to 30 minutes more , or until top is golden
14. remove from oven
15. cool on wire rack about an hour and serve !
demonstrations.review: This recipe certainly doesn't need another review, but I just couldn't resist! This was AMAZING!!! Probably the best apple pie I have ever tasted. I used a frozen pie crust, about 6-7 small/medium Granny Smith apples (cut thick and peeled), and walnuts instead of pecans. Everything else the same.  It came out perfect...thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked arroz con pollo

the original recipe was longer and used chicken pieces, but this is my quick and easy version! i hope you enjoy, it is packed with flavor!

1. saute veggies in oil
2. add broth , tomatoes and bay leaf
3. bring to a boil
4. spread rice in a 9x13 casserole pan
5. pour hot liquid over all , stir well
6. add chicken , mix
7. bake at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: Thanks for a wonderful and easy recipe! I ended up using an entire large pouch (16 ounces) of Vigo yellow rice and shredded a rotisserie chicken that I bought from my grocery store. The rice was perfectly cooked in an hour. I would recommend spraying your 9 x 12 dish with cooking spray before putting all of the goodies in...I can see how it could be a nightmare to clean if you didn't. Thanks again for a yummy and easy recipe!

target.recipe_text:
bean   banana cookies

i haven't tried these yet, i'm posting as a request. the recipe comes from a cookbook called "wholly frijoles! - the whole bean cookbook" by shayne fisher. note the yield amount was estimated!

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. cream together sugar , eggs , butter and vanilla
3. add beans and banana and beat until fluffy
4. add baking soda , flour and oats
5. blend until smooth
6. stir in chocolate chips
7. drop by tablespoonfuls onto a baking sheet
8. bake for 15-20 minutes or until golden
9. ~
10. ~
target.review: I have made this recipe. and they are very easy..the dough is a little bland in tase..I would add a tsp of cinnamon..made about 48 cookies...added just a bit of walnuts, and more chipits.. But as far as rating the initial recipe, its not too bad, so I will give it a five star, becasue of the protien and nutrients..easiness, and no trouble with baking size and texture is all fine.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
couscous salad with dried cherries

from the cherry institute.  you can substitute almonds for the pine nuts or leave the nuts out.  use water or vegetable broth for a meatless dish.  a very nice take on the north african classic--and quite simple.

1. bring water or broth to a boil in a medium saucepan
2. stir in couscous
3. remove from heat
4. let stand , covered , 5 minutes
5. fluff with a fork
6. let cool 10 minutes , uncovered
7. put cooked couscous , dried cherries , carrots , cucumber , green onions and pine nuts in a large bowl
8. mix well
9. combine vinegar , olive oil and mustard in a small container
10. mix well
11. pour over couscous mixture
12. stir to coat all ingredients
13. season with salt and pepper , if desired
14. serve chilled or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Made this to take on our outing to the park picnic, went over really well. At  room temperature it does impart more flavour, and I did add a little zucchini to it also, and shredded the carrots as to me that was simplier and then those bits were not so hard.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion rolls  bread machine

these are easy with the help of your bread machine and taste way better than the store bought rolls. directions are given for a 1 1/2 lb. machine. note: in my photo the rolls are pictured with "recipe #287863", which is delicious!

6/20/10 note: many reviewers have noted the dough seems sticky. i always watch my machine as it starts to knead the dough and if it is looking sticky at the time, add more flour then. 

however, i am changing the recipe from 3 cups flour to 3 1/4 cups flour today so definitely don't add additional flour unless the dough looks too moist.

1. in a small skillet over medium heat , melt the butter
2. add onion
3. saute onion about 10 minutes until tender , but not browned
4. remove pan from heat and allow onion to cool slightly
5. reserve 1 / 4 cup of the onion mixture
6. set aside
7. place remaining onion mixture and dough ingredients in bread pan , select the dough setting , and press start
8. when dough cycle is complete , turn dough onto a floured countertop or cutting board
9. gently roll and stretch dough into a 12-inch rope
10. with a sharp knife , divide dough into 10 pieces
11. grease a large baking sheet
12. roll each piece of dough into a ball and then flatten slightly
13. place rolls on prepared sheet
14. in a small bowl , beat together remaining egg and 1 / 2 teaspoon salt
15. brush egg mixture over each roll
16. spread approximately 1 teaspoon of reserved onion mixture on each roll
17. let rise in warm oven 30 to 45 minutes until doubled
18. preheat oven to 375f bake rolls 20 minutes until they are golden and onion is brown , but not burnt
19. remove from oven and cool on racks
demonstrations.review: I chopped one small onion and it was one cup, so I used all that into my bread, didnt save any for the tops. I also used all milk instead of the water since I didn't have powdered milk in the house. Made 8 large hamburger buns with the recipe, they were very good in texture, but could still use more onion, if you want to call them onion rolls. I will make again for hamburgers and sloppy joe recipes. I think they also will make a good roasted pork sandwich.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork mushroom casserole

this recipe is one of my favorites for using pork chops. the meal turns out to be very tasty and tender. i got this many years ago from nova 
scotia, where i am originally from.

1. season chops with pepper and paprika
2. saute chops at low temperature in butter
3. season with salt after chops are brown
4. transfer chops to baking dish or casserole
5. combine celery , onions , parsley , soup mushrooms and water
6. pour over chops
7. cook covered in 180 c or 350 f oven for 30 minutes
8. turn chops over and cook for another 30 minutes or until done and the meat is no longer pink
9. serve with rice or noodles
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I was going to make chicken for supper, so I did. I followed this recipe using fresh mushrooms, and chicken, then followed exactly as written instructions.   Lightly browned chicken breast first and continued on. Cooking time was one hour total. Even though I did not use pork I am giving this five stars as the recipe and ingredients worked out all well together. Also using the chicken added more liquid which in the end had a thinner and richer sauce for my noodles.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vinegar cookies

wonder how these taste..found the recipe in an old cookbook..the recipe does not call for eggs...?

1. cream margarine and sugar
2. mix in flour , soda and vinegar
3. shape dough into small balls
4. place on greased cookie sheet and flatten with a fork or small wooden mallet
5. bake 8-10 minutes at 350
demonstrations.review:
I made these with solid  margarine  as stated. Baked ten minutes at 350, until golden on bottom and just barely starting to get golden on upper edges.  These are like a crispy yet top layer chewy sugar cookie.  Very good plain.  I am going to put powdered sugar on all sides (dredging ) on some and place in a container to see how that is too. No there is no vinegar or soda taste.

All in all this is a fast good cookie..  I recommend everyone giving this one a try for this Christmas cookie tray.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
luscious california burger

full flavor and satisfying.  each ingredient alone is delicious but together the tastes are fabulous.  you won't soon forget it.  the name says it all.
this recipe comes to you from the lucious luggage ladies, zaar world tour 3.

1. cook bacon as desired
2. separate burger into 4 patties
3. grill sirloin burger until done
4. when just about done place a slice of american cheese on each burger
5. meanwhile , roast on the bbq slices of red pepper
6. rinse all vegetables and slice into rounds
7. choose your condiments
8. build your burger !
9. salt and pepper to taste
10. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Plain and simple that is what I love.  I chose this burger for the ZWT3 because its toppings are of choice and been allergic to avocados I just left it out of my layers. But I did make a sauce of mayo, ketchup, mustard and jalapenos. Layers then consisted of charred red peppers, romaine lettuce,  onion cheese bacon and then sauce. 

 Great nice tasting burger today for our family outing.

target.recipe_text:
rye bread sausage snacks

these are great for get togethers and make great appetizers!

1. mix and melt all ingredients together
2. top rye bread with mixture
3. bake at 350 for 10-15 minutes
target.review: My girlfriend makes a similar snack that I was trying to duplicate.  I searched and found these--after making them I realized this isn't the same recipe but it is just as good.  I didn't change anything.  I mix the hamburger and sausage raw and then fry and drain with hot water.  I used reduced fat cheese and don't think there was any noticeable difference.  Also, I made them a day ahead and have some left over that I am going to freeze for another day.  Thank you for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mashed potatoes with cream cheese

i was surprised i couldn't find this recipe here. it is the only mashed potato recipe i use for the holidays,as it is even better made a day ahead. not only is it delicious, but it's one less pot to wash when you want to enjoy your company. this also makes a nice potluck dish.

1. peel and cut the potatoes into large cubes and boil in salted water until tender
2. meanwhile , beat the cream cheese , then stir in the sour cream , milk and spices
3. drain and mash the potatoes in the pot , then stir in the cream cheese mixture
4. spoon into a casserole dish or a 9x13 pan
5. you may cover it and refrigerate for 24 hours , or proceed to baking right away
6. bake covered with foil at 350 for 45 min's
7. increase the time if the dish has been chilled
demonstrations.review: I made this tonight.  We LOOOOVED them!  I will be making them again.  We didn't use all of the potatoes so we are freezing half and also have enough for lunch tomorrow.  I followed the recipe exactly.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baja black beans  corn and rice

a south of the border blend of textures and flavors. serve hot as a main dish or a side dish with grilled meat or chicken.

1. cook brown rice
2. in a medium bowl , combine black beans , corn , tomatoes , onion , cilantro , jalapeno , lime juice , oil , salt , pepper and hot sauce
3. to serve , place a scoop of hot rice in a bowl or on a plate , top with a generous scoop of the black bean mixture
4. stir together before eating
demonstrations.review: Another 5 star review.  Thank you so much for posting this Barb Gertz.  I recently decided to try a vegan diet and tonight I just couldn't decide what to have for dinner.  I almost gave up and ate wrong.  Then I stumbled upon food.com and this was the first recipe I found.  I made it exactly as posted except I used canned tomatoes (winter) and doubled it.  I am looking forward to the leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken ala king

this is one of my families favorites.  a great comfort food.

1. in saucepan melt butter
2. stir in flour , salt and pepper
3. add milk and chicken broth at once
4. whisk until thick and bubbly
5. stir in chicken , pimento and mushrooms
6. heat through
7. pour over toast points
demonstrations.review: Thank you for the recipe.  This is really good and really easy.  I grill enough chicken for the ala king and also for my fussy son's to eat plain.  I have made it more than once and will continue to make it over and over.  Great and simple!  Gina

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork stir fry

tasty stir fry! you can add your favourite vegetables to it make your way.i experimented until i came up with this result.this is great as is for 2 or serve with rice for 4.

1. combine cornstarch , soya sauce , vinegar , honey and garlic together
2. add sliced pork and marinate a few hours:this can be done on the morning
3. refrigerate
4. remove meat from marinade
5. heat wok or large frypan on high
6. add oil , ginger and pork
7. stir fry until golden brown
8. remove meat
9. add onion , celery , pepper , mushrooms and broccoli
10. stir fry for 2-3 minutes
11. add chicken broth , marinade , pork and beansprouts
12. stir on high until vegetables are tender crisp
13. recipe can be easily doubled
demonstrations.review: This was my first attempt at making stir-fry.  My husband and I loved it.  It was easy.  I had to omit a few things because I didn't have everything on hand.  I didn't use the gingerroot, celery, pepper, or mushrooms.  It still was really good with a lot of flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
strawberry shortcake trifle

looks elegant,tastes awesome, and easy to make. the perfect dessert for company.

1. break the angel food cake into small pieces
2. cook the glaze following package directions , stir in the sliced strawberries , set aside
3. beat the softened cream cheese with the sugar , then fold in the cool whip
4. place half the cake pieces into the bottom of a large trifle bowl
5. spoon 1 / 2 the cream cheese mixture over the cake
6. place 1 / 2 the strawberry mixture over the cream cheese , then repeat all three layers
7. garnish with cool whip and whole berries , chill for several hours
demonstrations.review: I made this for my bunko party.  It was very good.  I used a 9x11 pan.  I also made my own glaze.  It was easy and tastes so much better.  It wasn't as red but I didn't care about that.  It was still a beautiful tasty dessert.

target.recipe_text:
greek garlic bread

another terrific one from my mil! great with anything from the grill.

1. preheat oven to 350
2. slice the loaf of french bread horizontally through the middle so that you have two"boats"
3. place bread on jelly roll pan , or in other large casserole dish , cut sides up
4. combine all ingredients , including garlic salt and seasoned salt to taste
5. with spatula , spread each half of the french bread with the mixture
6. bake for 15 minutes
target.review: I have to disagree with another reviewer and say this was indeed heavenly! I followed the recipe to a t and we all loved it, this is a real treat that will go with anything you serve. This will be enjoyed many times in my home. I am thinking if you added some chopped cooked chicken breast before you bake this you would have a great meal in one. Oh I am sorry, I DID add red pepper flakes but I add those to everything.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy oyster sauce chicken

do not season the chicken with any regular salt or onion salt as the oyster sauce already has plenty of sodium in it,  you may need to add in more sugar to suit your taste, start with 1/2 cup and add in more, if you like spicy then add in some cayenne pepper, serve with cooked rice --- this is very good!

1. set oven to 400f
2. lightly grease a 13 x 9-inch baking dish
3. pat the chicken dry with paper towels
4. season both sides of each piece of chicken with a small amount of onion powder , then pace the chicken into the baking dish facing skin side up
5. bake uncovered for 25 minutes
6. meanwhile in a bowl combine the oyster sauce with garlic , 1 / 2 cup sugar and water
7. after the chicken has cooked for 25 minutes remove from oven and spoon off any fat that has accumulated in the bottom of the dish
8. pour the oyster sauce over the chicken and turn the chicken to coat with the sauce
9. return the chicken to the oven and bake for another 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was great! I used 4 leg quarters and followed the recipe a using a little less than half a cup of sugar, we love oyster sauce. Watch your chicken, the garlic bits on the top began to burn a little. I served this with sticky rice and broccoli and we all loved dinner. I did add lots of cayenne too!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easiest broccoli rice casserole

i got this recipe from someone i worked with 20 years ago...her name was ruth and she was such a sweetheart!  lost track of her when i left ohio and moved to indiana...anyway, this is so easy that my kids can help me make this and they love it...

1. mix all ingredients except shredded cheddar cheese in a 2 quart casserole dish
2. bake in a preheated 350 degree oven for 35-40 minutes
3. take out and stir
4. sprinkle shredded cheese on top and bake for an additional 10 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Yes this recipe is outstanding to me and my family.
It is simple and so so good! I also doubled the recipe and can't wait for lunch to have some more, I think everything gets even better the next day so I am very much looking foreward to this.
I thought I had an onion but I didn't so omited that, otherwise followed the recipe exactly and it was a definate crowd pleaser in this home.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy french bread  extra large

easy french bread using the breadmaker to mix and the oven to bake.  the bread machine is a great invention, but i find the bread tastes better when it bakes in the oven.  prepare at least 3 hours before serving.  to make a regular sized loaf, change the number of servings to 1/2 a loaf.

1. place ingredients in bread machine as shown
2. set for dough
3. form into loaf on floured board - do not punch down
4. placed on greased cookie sheet and allow to rise 1 hour
5. bake 30-35 minutes in preheated oven at 350 degrees f
demonstrations.review:
I am new to ABM dough cycle and this recipe was suggested to me, I am so glad!
I made this yesterday and wow did it turn out good! I used garlic salt in place of the salt and added Italian herbs and it is really good! and it  [b]looks[/b] like a beautiful loaf of french bread, the texture is light and fluffy with a crisp crust. I put a pan of water on the bottom shelf of my oven, someone suggested that, I don't know what it did if anything but I did it. I read the pack of yeast and proofed it for 10 minutes before I added it to the bread machine,used half bread flour and half white (I am picking up hints here and there) and baked for 30 minutes at 350 when it came out of the oven I brushed the top with melted butter. It was marvelous as bread and butter and it is fantastic as toast as Claudia said!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
rice uruguayan

my adopted recipe that comes from uruguay. instead of regular ground beef i used ground round to cut down on the fat. this recipe can also be made using some of your favorite seasonings.

1. in large non-stick skillet , saute onion and garlic in olive oil
2. add ground round and brown well
3. add rice , carrots , parsley , beef or vegetable broth , and pepper
4. stir well and bring to boil , stirring occasionally
5. lower heat and simmer for 20 minutes
6. add potatoes and continue cooking until potatoes are tender or approximately one hour
demonstrations.review: This was our lunch today and it was very good. I was afraid it would be slightly bland so I added more garlic and some cayenne. I did cover the last 10 minutes because my rice did not seem to be doing much and it was perfectly cooked. This will be wonderful with fried eggs in the morning. Thank you Lauralie41!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttery bread machine rolls

these golden, fluffy, butterfy rolls are great hot from the oven. the dough is very easy to shape. this recipe is from a quick cooking magazine

1. in bread machine pan , put all ingredients in order suggested by manufacturer
2. select dough setting
3. when cycle is completed , turn dough onto a lightly floured surface
4. divide dough into 24 portions
5. shape dough into balls
6. place in a greased 13 inch by 9 inch baking pan
7. cover and let rise in a warm place for 30-45 minutes
8. bake at 350 degrees for 13-16 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: I used yeast!!! and the crazy thing is it was easy AND it worked! I, Robyn a yeastaphobe made Recipe #65340 and they turned out just like rolls should! I have not been this excited since I don't even know when! I have had a bread machine for years and have never once used the dough cycle because I thought it would be really hard to do anything with the dough but it was so easy! and dough is so theraputic! I am going to make some sort of bread again today, a monster has been created! thanks shapeweaver for urging me and jean for a super easy intro into the bread world! I followed the advice of a few reviewers and disolved the sugar in the milk that I warmed in the micro for 1 min 20 seconds, then added the yeast and let it sit for 15 minutes, I let them rise almost 2 hours then I baked at 350 for 17 minutes and brushed with butter when I took them out of the oven, next time and that may be today, I plan on adding some garlic, herbs and maybe some parmesan cheese. A last burst of excitement, if I can do it anyone can! I am just thrilled!

target.recipe_text:
absolutely the best gluten free peanut butter cookies

not just for the celiacs! i was skeptical, since the last recipe i tried was gritty, heavy and nasty.  these are light, rich and absolutely perfect.  i actually like these better than "regular" peanut butter cookies, and from a big fat momma, that's saying something!  adapted from catherine's recipe.

1. preheat oven to 375
2. make sure you have beaters that can handle thick batter
3. in a medium bowl , cream margarine and sugars
4. beat in egg and peanut butter
5. in a separate bowl , mix flours and baking soda evenly
6. add in two parts to wet ingredients , beating on med-high speed until thoroughly blended
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls , and place 2 inches apart onto ungreased baking sheet
8. you can press them with a fork if desired , but not necessary
9. bake 8-10 minutes
10. let cool 5 minutes before removing from baking sheet
target.review: My customers loved these cookies.  I did substitute the garbanzo flour with rice flour and I added 1/2 teaspoon of vanilla extract as I do with my regular peanut butter cookies. The next time I will make them vegan by replacing the egg with an egg replacement.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
brownie caramel cheesecake

it is very rich, and worth the time and calories

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. grease the bottom of a 9 inch springform pan
3. in a small bowl , mix together brownie mix , 1 egg and water
4. spread into the greased pan
5. bake for 25 minutes
6. melt the caramels with the evaporated milk over low heat in a heavy saucepan
7. stir often , and heat until mixture has a smooth consistency
8. reserve 1 / 3 cup of this caramel mixture , and pour the remainder over the warm , baked brownie crust
9. in a large bowl , beat the cream cheese , sugar and vanilla with an electric mixer until smooth
10. add eggs one at a time , beating well after each addition
11. pour cream cheese mixture over caramel mixture
12. bake cheesecake for 40 minutes
13. chill in pan
14. when cake is thoroughly chilled , loosen by running a knife around the edge , and then remove the rim of the pan
15. heat reserved caramel mixture , and spoon over cheesecake
16. drizzle with the chocolate topping
demonstrations.review: One of the very best cheesecakes. I did make my brownies from scratch. This was really good and easy. I also make my caramel from scratch too. I melted chocolate in butter to top it and let it harden in the fridge. Then served. My customers love this one and they roll their eyes when I don't have it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sugar free cinnamon nut balls

these cookies are so easy to make, it's hard to believe they are sugar-free. the aroma in the air while baking is heavenly. these cookies are like a cinnamon roll and sugar cookie rolled into one.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. sift together flour , baking powder and salt
3. beat margarine , sugar replacement , egg and vanilla until creamy
4. add flour mixture , stirring to mix completely
5. refrigerate for 1 hour
6. shape level tablespoons of cookie dough into balls and roll each one in mixture of cinnamon and walnuts
7. place on ungreased cookie sheet 2 inch apart
8. bake at 375f for 12 to 15 minutes
9. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I had a small taste of these and they taste pretty good.  But the real test came in when my diabetic father who hates sugar free desserts requested a third helping.  I do use Xylitol sugar replacement.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kentucky butter cake

this is a favorite of our family. my mother-in-law has made it for years.

1. to make batter: in a large beater bowl cream the butter
2. gradually add the sugar
3. creaming until light and fluffy
4. add the eggs all at once and beat at high until thick and creamy--at least 5 minutes
5. add milk and blend thoroughly
6. stir and let sit for 5 minutes
7. in a small bowl combine flour , salt , powder and soda
8. add to batter all at once and beat for at least 10 minutes
9. batter will be very thick and creamy
10. stir in vanilla
11. generously grease 10" inch bundt pan
12. turn batter into pan
13. bake at 325f for 55-60 minutes until top springs back when touched lightly in center
14. meanwhile prepare the butter sauce by combining the sugars , hot water and butter and stirring over low heat until butter is melted
15. do not boil !
16. remove from heat and add vanilla
17. let cake sit on a rack for 5 minutes after baking
18. poke deep holes all over cake with a long skewer
19. pour warm butter sauce slowly over cake and letting it soak into holes and down between sides of cake and pan
20. cool completely before removing from pan
21. if desired sprinkle with icing sugar before serving
demonstrations.review: This is an excellent cake.  I make this cake to sell at my local farmers market.  I do turn the glaze into a rum glaze by adding three to four tablespoons to the glaze after I remove it from the stove.  I let the glaze soak in and then I turn the cake over, remake the glaze and add about a 1/2 a cup of powder sugar to the glaze and pour it on top of the cake.  This is a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate toffee candy cookies  saltine candy

this simple candy shows up at all of my family gatherings .this recipe is quick and easy. the saltines may sound like a strange addition to something sweet, but i have never known anyone who made this recipe just once!

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees
2. cover cookie sheet with a single layer of saltines
3. boil butter , sugar , and vanilla for one minute
4. pour evenly over saltines
5. if needed , gently spread to make even
6. bake for 7 minutes
7. while toffee is still hot and bubbly , pour chocolate chips evenly on top of candy
8. when the chocolate chips begin to melt , gently spread chocolate over toffee
9. freeze for one hour
10. break into pieces and enjoy !
11. i have sprinkled nuts and / or drizzled white chocolate over the top of this candy to make it even better , but the basic recipe is outstanding as well
12. you can also change the type of chocolate that you use in the chips
13. white chocolate chips and milk chocolate both work , but make the candy incredibly sweet
demonstrations.review: MAKE THIS COOKIE, EVERYONE!!!! This is the absolute best cookie ever known to mankind. Do not let the cracker fool you, you won't even know that it is there. My customers crave this one.  I do dribble melted white chocolate on top to give it a beautiful finish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegan lemon cake

nan

1. mix dry ingredients
2. finely grate lemon peel and stir it inches
3. squeeze the lemon's juice into a small bowl , mix it with the powdered sugar , and set it aside
4. beat margarine and brown sugar and add egg replacer
5. add flour mixture and milk to margarine mixture
6. add vanilla
7. pour into greased loaf pan and bake for 1 hour at 350f
8. let cool for at least 20 minutes
9. invert onto a serving plate and drizzle with glaze
demonstrations.review: I made this cake gluten and vegan by substituting the flour for a rice flour, potato starch and tapioca starch and guar gum.  As soon as I took the cake out of the oven I poked holes in the cake and poured a lemon juice and sugar glaze over the cake and allowed it to soak in.  The cake is small if you make it into a bunt cake.

target.recipe_text:
pasta with garlic and oil  aglio e olio

easy and so good, if you love garlic then you love this pasta dish! adjust the garlic to taste, i use 4 tablespoons for this recipe, you might want to reduce that a bit. increase the dried red pepper flakes for more heat!

1. bring about 5 quarts of water to a boil with 3 teaspoons salt
2. add in the spaghetti and cook only until firm-tender
3. drain but reserve 1 / 2 cup pasta water
4. start this when you are boiling the pasta
5. heat about 4 tablespoons olive oil over medium-low heat in a skillet
6. add in 3 tablespoons garlic and about 1 / 2 teaspoon salt with black pepper to taste
7. saute stirring often until the garlic is light brown remove from heat and stir in the remaining 1 tablespoon minced garlic , crushed red pepper flakes , parsley , lemon juice and about 2 tablespoons of pasta cooking water
8. mix to combine
9. transfer the drained pasta to a large serving bowl
10. toss with remaining 3 tablespoons olive oil and the remaining reserved cooking water
11. add in the garlic mixture
12. toss well to combine
13. season with more black pepper and salt to taste if desired
14. serve immediately with grated parmesan cheese
15. delicious !
target.review: 3.5 stars. It's a good recipe considering it is "pasta from nothing." Basically, you can make it from thin air and I really wasn't expecting this to be anything special. I added some dried crushed basil and more lemon juice. I was thinking this would be a watery mess, but it all incorporated quite nicely. I only cooked my garlic for about 3 mins. I think if I cooked it for the full 6 mins, I would have had burned garlic. I'd serve this as a side dish as it doesn't really have anything nutritious in it. It has a similar mouth feel of a cream sauce. It's good for what it is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot kimchi pickle   quick

so simple so deeelisious!! as a side with any thing. (from canadian living mag.)

1. in a bowl , toss the cucumber with the salt
2. let stand for 15 minutes
3. drain
4. add the vinegar , sugar , sesame oil , garlic , hot pepper flakes and cayenne pepper
5. toss to combine
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: Thank you for this recipe! It was very quick and easy to make. I had all the ingredients at home. It does have a very nice kick to it. I ate these alone but I think it would be great along with a meal. This recipe can be easy doubled as the amount in the recipe didn't make a lot or maybe they were just that good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spaghetti alla carbonara

great pasta dish.

1. cook the pasta following the instructions on the package
2. meanwhile , heat the oil in a frying pan and saute the onion and bacon for 5 minutes , until softened
3. stir in the garlic and saute for 2 minutes , stirring
4. beat the eggs in a bowl , then stir in the cream and season with salt and pepper
5. grate the parmesan cheese and stir it into the cream mixture
6. stir the cream mixture into onion and bacon and cook over low heat for a few minutes , stirring constantly until heated through
7. season to taste
8. drain the pasta thoroughly and put into a large serving bowl
9. pour on the sauce and toss to coat
10. serve
demonstrations.review: I made this today for lunch. I didn't have any bacon so I used ham instead. It still came out great. Instead of heating the egg mixture with the onions and bacon, I added the onions and bacon to the egg mixture. I was afraid of getting scrambled eggs. I then transfered the hot, drained pasta into a pot and added the egg mixture and let it simmer for about 5 minutes mixing it the whole time as I wanted to make sure the eggs weren't still raw. Next time, I'll try it with bacon and maybe add some fresh herbs as this was good but felt like it was missing a little something.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chunk macadamia cookies

chock full o' chunks!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. cream butter and sugars together until light and fluffy
3. beat in the eggs and vanilla
4. mix together the flour , baking soda , and salt
5. add gradually to the butter mixture
6. fold in the macadamias and chocolate
7. drop by heaping tablespoonfuls onto greased baking sheets
8. bake at 350 for 10-12 minutes or until undersides are lightly golden
9. cool slightly before removing from cookie sheets
demonstrations.review: These are delicious but they are a bit too sweet and really greasy. I also think the cooking time is a bit off. I made some cookies and half the batch burned at 10 minutes, I would check these after 8 minutes (maybe just bake these at a lower temp) or else make large cookies. My cookies also were very dark, some of the cookies got this caramelly ooze that tasted really good, like toffee. I don't know if I would remake this recipe, the greasiness of this recipe really puts me off, I would not remake this recipe as is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spanakopita triangles

greek spinach and feta appetizer triangles

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. heat vegetable oil in a large saucepan over medium heat
3. slowly cook and stir onions until softened
4. mix in spinach , dill and flour
5. cook approximately 10 minutes , or until most of the moisture has been absorbed
6. remove from heat
7. mix in feta cheese , eggs , salt and pepper
8. lay phyllo dough flat and brush with butter
9. place a small amount of spinach mixture onto each piece of dough
10. fold phyllo into triangles around the mixture
11. brush with butter
12. place filled phyllo dough triangles on a large baking sheet
13. bake in the preheated oven 45 minutes to 1 hour , or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was very delicious. Basically, I just used the filling in this nrecipe and used Sara Moulton's phyllo dough recipe. I made a few changes to the recipe, I used 2 tsp of dried dill, subbed part of the onions for green onions (used one small onion and a med onion and 1 c of gree onions) and I added a tsp of oregano. I think next time I make this, I will use fresh baby spinach as I've made spanakopita before and I think fresh spinach tastes better, also I saw another recipe that added lemon juice and cumin. I also will add less oil next time as 1/2 c of oil was too much for sauteing the onions.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
potatoes in spicy cheese sauce   papa a la huancaina

this famous peruvian dish papa a la huancaína was posted by marian blazes.  i have posted it here for use in the zwt-7 world tour of south/central america. 

this is a dish of sliced potatoes covered in a spicy cheese sauce that is typically served cold, as a first course or as a lunch dish. it is delicious made with yellow or white potatoes. 

the sauce for the dish is called salsa a la huancaina and is made with aji amarillo peppers.  the spiciness can be adjusted by using less or more yellow chile peppers. (your preference) if you would rather not have it spicy, you may use some tumeric powder instead for flavor.

1. for the sauce - remove seeds from yellow chile peppers and chop into 1 inch pieces
2. saut the onion , garlic , and chile peppers in the oil until onion is softened , about 3-5 minutes
3. if using the tumeric option , add it now
4. once onion is softened remove from heat and let cool
5. place the onion-chile mixture in a food processor or blender , add the evaporated milk and blend
6. next add the cheese and crackers and blend until smooth
7. the sauce should be fairly thick
8. if necessary thicken you can thicken the sauce with more saltines or thin the sauce with more
9. season with salt and pepper to taste and serve at room temperature or chilled
10. for the potatoe dish - heat a large pot of salted water to boiling and add the potatoes
11. boil the potatoes until tender , drain and let cool
12. slice the potatoes and place on top of the lettuce leaves
13. then pour the huancana sauce over the potatoes and garnish with slices of hard-boiled egg and black olive halves
demonstrations.review: This recipe is okay, but not quite what I was looking for. It's missing something. It is very easy to make though and is worth trying. I've eaten many papas a la huancaina though and this sauce while good doesn't quite do it for me.

target.recipe_text:
kittencal s easy and delicious ranch parmesan chicken

there are plenty versions of this recipe, this is mine and can be on your table in less that an hour, my family loves this chicken! --- the ranch dressing is the secret it holds in all the flavor and moistness while the chicken is baking and also adds flavor, i find that hidden valley ranch dressing works the best but kraft or any other brand will do, i sometimes top the baked chicken with mozzarella cheese or cheddar, but that is optional --- although i have only made this using breasts i imagine that chicken pieces could be used although you would have to increase the breadcrumb mixture slightly, you can marinate the chicken breast in the ranch dressing for a few hours in the fridge, although you will need more than 1 cup of dressing if you are marinating .... *note* to avoid a soggy bottom crust, place the chicken breasts onto a flat rack on top the baking sheet, also it is important not to bake the chicken in a small baking pan, if you do not have a rack bake on a large baking sheet so any juices in the pan will spread out and not accumulate under the chicken causing a soggy bottom ---------------
for low-fat option: use low-fat ranch dressing and omit the melted butter on top or use a healthy butter alternative such as smart balance 50/50 blend.

1. set oven to 400 degrees
2. in a shallow bowl mix together the dry breadcrumbs with parmesan cheese , seasoned salt , black pepper and garlic powder
3. dip the chicken into the ranch dressing to coat both sides
4. coat in the breadcrumb mixture
5. place in a single layer onto a greased baking sheet or line with non-stick foil
6. lightly drizzle the melted butter over each breast
7. if desired you can sprinkle black pepper over the chicken pieces
8. bake uncovered for about 30-35 minutes or until the chicken is cooked)
target.review: Had another really awesome meal tonight thanks to Kittencal!  Used Panko, and this was super crunchy!  I also marinated the chicken in the ranch for about an hour and a half, Dont know if it made a difference, but it was SO flavorful!  YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gyro loaf with tsatziki sauce

i confess, my husband is a gyro junkie. i had never had the ethereal pleasure of a gyro until he introduced me to the wickedly intoxicating greek concoction a few years ago. the trouble you ask? we were low-carbers for about two years running and it was not cost-effective to make special trips out for a couple of paper-thin slices of meat and some sauce. i developed this recipe out of pure desperation by combining several different recipes (found online) and then adding some of my own ideas and spice.

1. mix loaf ingredients together and shape into a freeform loaf in a baking pan
2. bake at 375f for about 1 hour 15 minutes
3. once loaf has cooled to room temperature or has chilled in the refrigerator , slice it as thin as possible
4. serve it warm or at room temperature
5. can be served in pitas , flatbreads or tortillas with lettuce , tomato , black olives , feta cheese and tsatziki sauce or as a main course with a greek salad , pasta salad or potato salad
demonstrations.review: I made the tzatsiki sauce and I'm in love.  I doubled the amount of dill because I couldn't get fresh, but the parsley gave it that fresh taste.  Also I used greek yogurt, AMAZING.  I don't have to go to my favorite greek place anymore.   I can make it myself and its better!!  =D

demonstrations.recipe_text:
string cheese pizza roll ups

i made these for our super bowl party and they were so easy and a fun twist to pizza...........and who doesn't like pizza?

1. unroll crescent rolls into individual triangles - should be 8 of them
2. sprinkle each triangle with garlic salt and italian seasoning
3. lay 4 slices of pepperoni on each triangle
4. place a 1 / 2 piece of string cheese on top of the pepperoni and roll them up
5. sprinkle with a little more garlic salt and italian seasoning
6. bake according to the directions on the crescent roll package or until they are browned
7. when you are ready to eat , dip them in pizza sauce
8. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I don't eat pepperoni, so I tried it without...pretty blah.  Hubby loved them with the pepperoni, Easy to make, so I will be making them for him again!  Maybe I will find something fun to stuff in mine =]

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best chicken stock broth  crock pot option

plan ahead this method takes 2 days to create the best most richest flavorful stock, far better and cheaper than any canned broth, once you try this you will never purchase cans of broth again! --- this can be done either on a stove top or in a crock pot but start the stock firstly on the stove top then transfer to a crock pot --- the same method may be used for turkey stock use the carcass and leftover legs, thigh and wing bones from your roasted turkey in place of the chicken pieces, also save your carcass and bones from roasted chickens and freeze them to throw in the pot, roasted bones will produce a richer golden colored stock but uncooked chicken works just as well --- i freeze the cooled cooked broth in 2 or 4-cup plastic freezer containers and store in the freezer until ready to use, you may do a quick defrost in the microwave when needed --- yield depends on size of pot and how much water is used, use this broth to make the best tasting chicken soup, don't remove the skins from onions they add color and taste to the stock adding in another onion won't hurt :)

1. place the chicken pieces and / or carcass in an extra large stock pot , along with all remaining ingredients
2. fill with cold water to cover ingredients , and up to almost three quarters of the stock pot
3. place on stove element
4. cover and bring to a full boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer and remove any fat or scum that is floating on top of the water
7. at this point you can transfer to a crockpot
8. simmer covered with a lid on low heat for about 4-5 hours for stove top
9. adjust salt to suit taste
10. after the 5-6 hours of simmering time turn off heat and allow the pot to sit until room temperature with all ingredients still in the pot , do not remove bones or veggies
11. transfer the pot to the fridge and chill overnight
12. the following day: remove the pot from the fridge
13. remove any fat that has gathered on top
14. heat again until just to a liquid
15. remove all chicken pieces and strain in a large strainer , if desired you may strain again in a cheesecloth , but it is not necessary
16. let cool completely and freeze in containers
demonstrations.review: Oh man is this great!!  Mine is dark, and rich.  I will never buy canned broth again!  It was so simple, I used one chicken carcass that I had stored in my freezer just for this, and one whole rotissere chicken.  everything else was the same.  Oh, and I have been saving my mushroom stems for a while too, so I threw those in.  Amazing yet again Kitten =]

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s garlic croutons

you will never purchase store bought croutons again after making these! make a double batch and store in the fridge or freeze them, use in salads or soups, for easier slicing make certain to use stale bread, or place your bread in the fridge overnight, for extreme garlic flavor use fresh finely minced garlic and increase to 2 tablespoons, to infuse the flavor into the butter allow the melted butter/garlic mixture to sit for 30 minutes or more at room temperature before brushing on the bread

1. set oven to 325f
2. lighly grease a large baking sheet
3. place the butter , garlic powder or fresh minced garlic and salt or seasoned salt in a microwave-safe bowl and microwave until melted
4. mix in the dried parsley
5. if you are using fresh garlic allow the melted butter mixture to sit at room temperature for 30 minutes to infuse the garlic flavor into the butter
6. brush both sides of the bread slices liberally with the melted butter mixture using a pastry brush
7. using a serrated knife slice into small cubes or desired sizes
8. place the bread cubes onto the baking sheet
9. bake for 25 minutes , or until desired crispness
10. let cool and store in a covered container in the fridge or freeze
demonstrations.review: SO amazing.  I used fresh garlic and let it sit like you said, and used sourdough bread.  Oh man, I could snack on these ALL day!  They didn't take quite as long to cook for me as it stated in the recipe, more like about 15 or so min.  Made with Kittencals caeser salad, and man, I will have these 2 recipes in my fridge/pantry at all times =]

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s famous caesar salad
