I halfed the cherry tomatoes but left out the cheese (didn't want it soggy) as well as the pepperoni (don't eat meat) but it was fantastic.  Making it again this weekend for a BBQ.  Thanks so much for sharing.

target.recipe_text:
eggless  milkless  butterless spice cake

i found this recipe in the newspaper twenty years ago. i was impressed by the author's stories about life in the homefront during wwii so i decided to try this recipe. it was very good even without the allspice.

1. stir together flour , cornstarch , baking soda , spices and salt
2. cream sugar , oil , lemon juice and vanilla
3. add flour mixture to sugar mixture , a little at a time , alternating with up to 1 cup of water
4. mix briskly with fork until thoroughly blended
5. pour into lightly greased and floured 8 or 9 inch square pan and bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes or until cake tests done
6. let cool in pan
target.review:
I read all the reviews before I made this and I knew I had choosen a great one! 

Like a few others said before these were quite done they looked like they would fall but then ended up perfect! I will base when these are done by their tops in the future!

I poured the recipe into 3 mini loaf tins to use as Christmas gifts. DH and I ate one to make sure we liked what we were giving people and it was AWESOME!

I have about 15 more tins to make and this will be PERFECT! We are a young family with limited funds and this is a great way to stretch a dollar! THANK YOU!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
perfect pasta salad

this is an absolutely incredible recipe. every time i've made it i've had to double it and it is still gone in nothing flat. people will beg you for the recipe

1. mix together dressing first and set aside until sugar is dissolved completely
2. cook pasta according to box directions and rinse under cold water until cool
3. slice the sliced pepperoni circles in half and separate slices
4. mix together with pasta and chopped items , except the provolone cheese
5. pour dressing over it all and mix well
6. chill well
7. add provolone cheese to salad before serving , otherwise it gets soggy
8. you may have to add extra red wine vinegar or olive oil to get it to the desired consistency
9. some people like it moist , others on the drier side
10. this is guaranteed not to last long before it is completely devoured !
11. enjoy !
demonstrations.review:
Very good! Thank you for the recipe!

I used store brand noodles, vinegar, and olive oil with fantastic results!

Only change I made (besides brand names) was that I used cubed pepper jack cheese instead of provolone. 

I also decreased the sugar to 2tablespoons instead of 1/4 cup. 

Thanks again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  shrimp and andouille jambalaya

a cajun classic, meal in one pot! have the hot sauce ready to splash on. serve with some crusty french bread, a nice crisp salad, and some of your favorite wine. :)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , brown chicken in hot oil on both sides
3. remove and drain
4. add andouille , onion , celery , bell pepper , thyme , oregano , paprika , salt , and cayenne pepper to the pan , cooking and stirring for about 5 minutes until onions are tender
5. add rice , tomatoes with juice , and broth
6. bring to a boil
7. place rice mixture in a baking dish or oven-proof casserole
8. top with chicken
9. cover and bake at 350 degrees f for 40-45 minutes or until rice and chicken are done and tender
10. stir in shrimp , parsley , and green onions
11. cover and cook 5-8 minutes longer or until shrimp curl and turn bright pink and serve
demonstrations.review: Pretty good. I think it's missing some flavor. I needed to add more liquid as well. I also would double the tomato. That would probably be enough extra liquid. My husband and I really like spicy stuff. It's a great recipe and very versatile. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streamlined chimichangas

this is a great tasting recipe and so easy that even my daughter doesn't complain when i ask her to make it.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. brown meat with onion and garlic
3. drain , but do not rinse
4. stir in picante sauce , cumin , oregano and salt
5. simmer 5 minutes or until most of the liquid has evaporated
6. brush one side of the tortillas with butter
7. on unbuttered side spoon heaping 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture into center
8. fold 2 sides over filling , fold ends down
9. place seam side down in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish
10. bake for 13 minutes or until golden brown
11. to serve , top with sour cream , guacamole and additional picante sauce
demonstrations.review:
Great recipe! Delicious, easy, and inexpensive! A young/new cook could easily do this. Great one to teach older kids how to cook too! I used 1 cup Newman's Own medium salsa instead of the 3/4cup picante (the salsa isn't as liquidy). We might make them spicier next time for personal preference. We have two young children, one is super picky (age 4). The picky kid put up with them (which is saying a lot). My son (age 2) gobbled them right down.

This will be thrown into our rotation, thank you!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s best blasted rapid roast whole chicken

blasting with high heat will shrink the skin and seal in all the juices to create an extremely moist and tender chicken with lovely crispy skin - and it will be on your table in about an hour. this method will also work with a larger chicken, but cooking time will need to be increased. you may adjust all seasonings to taste. if you are not a lemon lover, then you may omit the lemon juice. you really can use whatever seasoning that you like for this. i like to use seasoned salt. make certain to use a fork and poke holes all over in the lemon, then place it into the cavity of the chicken. roast roast as stated. the chicken with be moist and have a faint lemon flavor. for more of my tried-and-true recipes, visit my food blog at www.kittencalskitchen.com.

1. rinse the chicken inside and out well under cold water , then pat dry using a paper towel
2. in a small bowl mix the lemon juice with oil and melted butter until blended , then rub all over the chicken
3. using clean hands rub the inside and outside of the chicken with seasoned salt , garlic powder , black pepper and cayenne
4. place the lemon / s inside the cavity
5. place the chicken into a baking dish
6. using cotton string tie the legs together tightly
7. at this point you may cover and refrigerate for up to 6 hours
8. set oven to 450 degrees f
9. roast the chicken at 450 degrees for 20 minutes , then reduce the heat to 400 degrees and continue roasting for about 40 minutes
10. cover with foil and let sit for 15 minutes before slicing
demonstrations.review: I've made this a few times and I was surprised I haven't rated it yet! We always love Kittencal's recipes and this is a big hit! The flavor is amazing. It's always nice and juicy; never dry. And SO EASY. Not to mention I rarely have time to spend hours preparing a meal so I love the quick prep and cook time on this! Thanks again!!! Really....this is so easy...a caveman could do it ;)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
split pea soup  crock pot    dairy free

very little prep, just layer in crock pot/slow cooker, leave it for the day and a filling, delicious soup will be ready for dinner.

this recipe is a very versatile base split pea soup.  for a vegan option, omit the meat. i have made this recipe using ham, ham hock, and bacon. i have used veggie broth, chicken broth and water... each tasting different but yummy! i have reduced the salt but have not adjusted the recipe as written. this soup is even better the next day, it freezes well. this tends to be a thicker soup (especially once it has cooled) so adjust liquid after cooking to desired thickness.

1. layer ingredients in crockpot
2. pour in water , so don't stir
3. cover and cook on high 4-5 hours or on low for 8-10 hours
4. remove bay leaf
5. serve with some nice crusty bread or buns
demonstrations.review: Very good soup! I made this when my in-laws visited (6 adults) and they all enjoyed the soup! A few things to note for people concerned about the thickness of the soup. After the peas are soft enough to your liking, turn off crock pot, leave open about 15-20mins. Soup will thicken upon standing. If you keep cooking the coup after the peas are soft the soup will darken. There are a few comments about the soup being dark, this is because it was over cooked. Only changes I made was using an extra carrot and stalk of celery. Next time I will use a couple more carrots per personal taste (we love carrots in our soup!). Thank you for a great recipe!

target.recipe_text:
italian pepper and sausage dinner

it seems like i make this with my eyes closed already. the family loves it as well as guests. you can make as much as you want and if you are lucky to have leftovers, it's better the second time around. enjoy!

1. in a large , skillet brown the sausage until it is cooked through
2. drain the fat and drain the sausage on paper towels
3. in the same pan heat your olive oil add and saut the peppers , and onions , until the onion is translucent , then add the garlic and saut gently but do not brown your garlic
4. this will make the dish bitter
5. the vegetables should be tender
6. stir in the tomatoes , spices , romano cheese and sausage
7. cover the pan and simmer all over a medium-low heat for 8-10 minute
8. if your mixture seems too thick you can add a little water or red wine
9. while the meat mixture is cooking , the pasta can be prepared as per directions
10. you do not want to overcook your pasta
11. you want a little firmness to your noodles
12. when you are ready to serve use a large platter
13. the noodles first , then spoon the meat mixture over
14. mix slightly
15. sprinkle with the parigiano-reggiano and place your fresh basil leaves atop
16. this goes well with a full bodied red wine , a green salad with italian oil and vinegar dressing , and most of all a good hard crusted peasant bread
target.review: I've made this once with sausage, and my boyfriend raved about it. I'm not a huge sausage fan, so the second time I replaced it with grilled chicken--it was still spectacular. The boyfriend still loved it too. Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baja fried fish tacos  a san diego surfers delight

wow! do we love these fish tacos, and there are so many variations.  this is one of my favorites and most authentic. or, think fresh grilled mahi-mahi slipped inside a thick warm corn tortilla and topped with thinly sliced cabbage, drizzled with lime juice and a splash of creme fresh. yummy!

1. in a bowl , whisk beer , flour and salt , blending well
2. rinse fish and pat dry
3. cut into six oblong pieces
4. in a deep skillet , heat about one inch of oil to 360f
5. coat fish pieces in beer batter and drain briefly
6. slide coated fish into oil
7. turn when golden about one ot two minutes
8. cook another one or two minutes on the other side and remove from oil with a slotted spoon and drain on paper towels
9. mix mayonnaise with a little water to thin , and add the mined garlic
10. to assemble the taco , add one piece of fish to each soft corn tortilla
11. give the fish a squeeze of lime juice
12. top with shredded cabbage , salsa and dressing
demonstrations.review: Yum! Very good; I made a few adjustments because-let's be honest-that's how we all cook. I used about 2 tablespoons of mayo for the dressing, and instead of using water I used lime juice...and four garlic cloves. So, although nothing like the original, I loved it--ate the cabbage salad by itself the next day for lunch! Good recipe to be sure.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini lasagna  lasagne    low carb

great for anyone going low carb or who has so many zucchini, they don't know what to do!! :) we found the sauce to be very mild. i think it would be better with twice as much garlic. i boiled my zucchini slices for about 3 minutes so they were partially cooked. i wanted to make sure they were soft in the finished dish or i knew the kids wouldn't eat them. ;) the cottage cheese provides a slightly tangy note. i think we would have preferred ricotta, but that is personal taste. i use my 11x7 baking dish and got 6 pieces the size of what you see in my photos. both of the guys ate two so it fed 4 of us, and i double the meat. adjust the recipe accordingly for your family.

1. cook zucchini until tender , drain and set aside
2. fry meat and onions until meat is brown and onions are tender
3. drain fat
4. add next 8 ingredients and bring to a boil
5. reduce heat
6. simmer , uncovered 10 minutes or until reduced to 2 cups
7. in small bowl slightly beat egg
8. add cottage cheese , half of shredded cheese and flour
9. in baking-roasting pan arrange half of the meat mixture
10. top with half of the zucchini and all the cottage cheese mixture
11. top with remaining meat and zucchini
12. bake uncovered at 375 degrees f for 30 minutes
13. sprinkle with remaining cheese
14. bake 10 minutes longer
15. let stand 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review: This was great and easy to make; a good one to make ahead of time. I put it in the fridge in the afternoon so all I had to do was pop it in the oven in the evening. I assume the cottage cheese was probably suggested to keep this a low-fat meal, but I used fat-free ricotta to keep my calories down and still get the Italian taste of ricotta. I also doubled the meat portions--because my boyfriend is a meat head...and we love us some meat.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
layered chicken and artichoke casserole

this comes from the "heart and soul: cookbook from memphis.my whole family love this one. good with plain buttered pasta and a green salad on the side.

1. cook spinach according to the directions , drain , squeezing out excess liquid
2. stir in water chestnuts
3. set mixture aside
4. preheat oven to 350
5. in a 12" skillet , arrange chicken breasts and add 1 / 2 cup of the sherry and the bay leaf
6. bring to boil and cover and reduce heat , allowing to simmer until no longer pink , about 20 mins
7. drain and set chicken aside
8. in the same skillet , melt the butter and saute the mushrooms , green onions and garlic over med heat for 5 mins , until tender , set aside
9. in a med bowl , stir together mayonnaise , 1 / 2 cup of the parmesan cheese , sour cream and remaining sherry
10. to assemble , spread spinach mixture evenly in the bottom of a 13 by 9 by 2 inch baking dish
11. top with chicken breasts , artichokes , and mushroom onion mixture
12. spread the mayonnaise mixture over the top and sprinkle with thr remaining parmesan cheese
13. bake for 30 mins or until heated through
demonstrations.review: This was so good; naturally, I quadrupled the garlic and parm, which made it even more delicious! My boyfriend gave me a new compliment after every bite, "This is the best thing I've ever eaten," "You amaze me more everyday," "I want to marry you." Okay, not that far, but it was a delicious meal nonetheless.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cuban spiced pork chops

this is the perfect recipe for those who love the flavors of a classic cuban pork roast but are cooking in small quantities. typical of cuban fare, these are full of tropical flavors but not spicy. the garlic and lime pair beautifully in a fragrant marinade.  though you can marinade as briefly as an hour, for best results let the pork soak up to 6-8 hours. (don't marinade overnight as the citrus cooks the pork over longer periods). serve these with my almost fried plantains  #134349 for a delightful healthy meal.

1. trim excess fat from pork chops
2. use a knife to cut shallow cross-hatch marks over both surfacesof the chops
3. mix all remaining ingredients together in a resealable bag or non-reactive container
4. add the chops and place in the refrigerator
5. marinate at least an hour
6. grill or broil at 500 degrees fahrenheit 8-10 minutes , turning once half way
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe. Good way to impress your boyfriend. I forgot the cumin at the store and replaced with mustard powder--it was unique and probably nothing like the original recipe, but still very flavorful. Marinated for probably 2 hours. I made 3 chops and added a little extra of each ingredient and it was great. I broiled for 10 minutes and found it raw inside, so I baked for an additional 20 minutes and it still maintained it's juicy-goodness. Served with home-style mashed potatoes and a salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mediterranean spinach turkey wrap

this is a good for lunch. you can make pinweels out of these and serve them as a finger food for parties.

1. chop up olives
2. combine cream cheese , feta cheese , olives and oregano in bowl and mix
3. evenly spread the mixture over entire tortilla
4. place turkey over the cream cheese mixture on half of each tortilla
5. place spinach leaves on top of turkey
6. to assemble just start with the side that is topped with the turkey and roll up tightly
7. wrap each sandwich with saran wrap
8. refrigerate wraps at least 1 hour
9. before serving , unwrap , and trim of ends of each roll
10. cut wraps into 3 sections
11. cut each section on a slight diagonal into half
12. wraps can be made a day ahead
13. enjoy
demonstrations.review: This was a very tasty wrap, but the feta and cream cheese mix was a little too overpowering for me. Next time, I think I might try adding some cottage cheese or something else to give it it's bulk, but still seem light. I can see this being an ideal appetizer cut into mini pin-wheels as suggested, but sitting down for an entire wrap--the flavors were just too heavy for me.

target.recipe_text:
mbaazi wa nazi  pigeon peas in coconut milk

mbaazi wa nazi (pigeon peas with coconut) are the swahili way to prepare this popular tropical pulse. the pigeon pea is evidently native to africa or asia. in egypt, the cultivation of pigeon peas began before 2000 b.c. today pigeon peas are widely cultivated in all tropical and semi-tropical regions the world over, and are especially popular in india and the caribbean.

1. in a large pot , combine pigeon peas and just enough water to cover
2. bring to a boil , reduce heat , cover , and simmer until the peas begin to become tender and most of the water is absorbed
3. stir in 1 1 / 2c coconut milk
4. continue to simmer over low heat
5. add more water as necessary to prevent the peas from becoming dry
6. while peas are simmering: heat a few tablespoons of oil in a skillet
7. add the curry powder to the oil and stir for a minute
8. fry the onion and chile pepper until they are tender
9. combine the peas and onion-chile mixture
10. continue to simmer until peas are tender enough to eat
11. add the remaining coconut milk and simmer on the lowest possible heat for five to ten minutes , stirring occasionally
12. serve "swahili style" with chapati , rice , or "up-country style" with ugali
target.review: This was really yummy and my first experience with pigeon peas!  I used a can of pigeon peas and didn't have a jalapeno so I used a pinch of cayenne. I also used garam masala instead of curry powder.  It was very quick and easy as well as healthy and delish!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
amy s cajun shrimp florentine

this is really yummy with chicken too!  prep time includes marinating time (you don't have to marinate...it's just better this way).

1. combine shrimp with olive oil and cajun seasoning
2. let marinate several hours if possible
3. in heavy dutch oven , melt butter over medium heat
4. saute shrimp until pink , about 3-4 minutes
5. remove shrimp and set aside
6. add flour and cook a few minutes , whisking continually
7. gradually add milk or cream , whisking until smooth
8. add onions , garlic , nutmeg , spinach , salt and pepper
9. let simmer until thickened
10. add cheese and basil
11. add shrimp back into pot
12. stir to combine
13. add most of sauce to cooked pasta and toss well to combine
14. top pasta with remaining sauce
15. top with tomato
16. garnish with additional cheese and basil if desired
demonstrations.review: Don't be fooled by the lack of reviews -- this recipe is AMAZING!!  I made it exactly as it's written  (I used Tony Chachere's for the cajun seasoning and salt/pepper) and it was extremely de-lish!!  This will definitely be a permanent recipe for dinner parties for us!  Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
african spinach and peanut butter stew

found online at www.fooddownunder.com, while looking for economical 'african' recipes.    
tasty and nutritious, a vegetarian main dish or a good side dish.  you could easily add garlic, cooking it with the onions, add some mushrooms, adding with the tomatoes,  and i think some chilli, fresh, powdered or flaked,  would also add a bit of spice to this very versatile dish!

1. slice the onions and fry in oil until soft
2. peel the tomatoes in boiling water
3. slice and add to the onions
4. wash , trim and chop the spinach coarsely
5. add to the stew and cook , covered , over a medium heat for 5 minutes , stirring to prevent sticking
6. thin the peanut butter with hot water to make a smooth paste
7. add to the stew
8. season with salt and pepper and cook for another 5 - 10 minutes , stirring and adding water if necessary to prevent sticking
9. serve over steamed rice , polenta , or mashed potatoes , in fact , you could eat it with anything , really !
demonstrations.review: I love this dish!  I also found it first on the downunder website but then lost it and needed it again and found it here (thank you!).  I use canned tomatoes and serve it over quinoa.  It is SO good - I always want to eat a ton of it!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate garbanzo bean cake

i actually saw this mentioned on a weight watchers board and found the recipe online. i didn't find it on recipezarr, so i thought i would add it. my friend calls it chocolate f*rt cake! it is different and one way to get some fiber in your diet. i am sure you could play around with an egg substitute and splenda.

1. puree in food processor till smooth the beans and eggs
2. add the baking powder and sugar , pulse till smooth
3. in a microwave safe bowl , melt the chocolate chips , stirring often till smooth
4. add to food processor , pulse till smooth
5. pour into a greased and floured 9 inch cake pan
6. bake at 350 degrees for about 40 minutes
7. dust with sugar if you like
8. i could not find a 19oz can of beans , so i used about 2 cups
9. i also added a splash of vanilla flavoring
10. i also 'floured" my pan with dark cocoa
demonstrations.review: Wow! When I read this recipe I just had to make it because I couldn't believe that it has Garbanzo beans in it.  Man is it good!  My girlfriend thought I was kidding that it has beans in it - she asked me at least 4-5 times if I was kidding.  It really is a delicious chocolate flavor and pretty easy to whip up!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemony lentils and spinach

this satisfying blend of healthy ingredients is refreshingly reminiscent of lemony mediterranean dishes. it can be served hot, room temp or cool.

1. bring water & lentils to a boil in a large heavy pot
2. reduce heat , cover & simmer 20 minutes
3. meanwhile , saute the onion in a large pot in oil
4. stir in garlic , cilantro , and spinach and saut 5 minutes , stirring frequently
5. add potatoes and lentils with cooking liquid to cover
6. season with salt and pepper
7. bring to boil , reduce heat to simmer
8. cook 20 minutes
9. stir in lemon juice
10. serve immediately or when cooled or chilled as desired
demonstrations.review: I LOVE this dish!! I've made it twice and I love the earthy taste of the lentils complemented by the fresh lemony zest.  I forgot to put the cilantro....didn't matter - it was still SO YUMMY!! Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green kale with raisins   toasted pine nuts

nice combination of kale, raisins & pine nuts. i sometimes add a hint of cinnamon. loaded with iron.

1. to toast the pine nuts place them on a cookie sheet in a 325f oven for about 5 minutes , be careful they burn easily
2. bring water to boil in a skillet with a tight fitting lid , add kale and cook for approximately 5 minutes of until the kale is just tender , drain& set aside
3. rinse out the skillet , dry , add olive oil and heat over medium heat , add garlic and saute for 30 seconds , add raisins and stir for about 30 seconds
4. the raisins should be glossy and slightly puffed
5. add kale , stir , season and saute until heated through
6. garnish with the pine nuts and serve
demonstrations.review: Best way to eat kale - for sure! I did use a pinch of cinnamon and only 2 garlic cloves which I boiled with the kale, then mashed. Otherwise, exactly as written.  My first experience with Kale - I expected a strong (bitter) flavor and it's actually pretty mild - I think kids would eat this!

target.recipe_text:
smoked salmon terrine

a very impressive dish for summer parties and gatherings! prep time doesn't include chilling time.

1. line a 900g loaf tin or 1
2. 4litre terrine dish with plastic wrap
3. beat the butter until very soft
4. dice the anchovies , and beat into the butter with the lemon zest and juice
5. mix in the dill , season with salt and pepper and set aside at room temperature
6. line the loaf tin or dish with salmon slices , making sure there is an over-hang of about 5cm around the sides
7. cover the bottom with more smoked salmon , then smear over a thin layer of butter
8. cover the butter with a layer of salmon
9. continue until the tin is full , finishing with a layer of salmon
10. fold the over-hanging salmon over the layered salmon
11. place another loaf tin weighted down with a couple of small tins or another terrine dish on top
12. this will help press the layers together
13. refrigerate for several hours or preferably overnight
14. serve thin slices alongside a green salad accompanied with brown bread or bruscetta type bread
target.review: I love this recipe. Its great in the hot weather. The only thing I lrft out was the anchovies as I am not a great lover of them.  I took it to a luncheon. Lots of requests for the recipe.My first try at a Terrine and it was a smash.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
seafood cream cheese quiche

this is a very delicious seafood quiche, i have made this quite often for a luncheons, everyone just loves it. this recipe make 2, 8-inch pies, just divide all ingredients evenly between the two pie shells. if my memory serves me right, i believe the original recipe called for one large deep-dish, 10-inch pie plate, but i prefer to make it into two, 8-inch pies.

1. set oven to 425f degrees
2. in a saute pan , melt the butter , and saute the onion and the celery , until soft
3. add in the shrimp , cook until the shrimp are pink in colour
4. set aside
5. divide the cream cheese in half , and cut the cream cheese into 1 / 4 inch pieces
6. sprinkle evenly into the bottom of the two pie crusts
7. top with the sauteed shrimp / onion mixture
8. top with the grated swiss cheese
9. mix together the milk and eggs
10. divide evenly between the two pie crusts
11. bake for 10 minutes at 425f degrees
12. reduce the temperature to 350f degrees , bake for 30 minutes more
demonstrations.review:
This is a delicious quiche. I made it the same as the recipe and I also made it with two dishes and used Bacon in one and tinned crab in the other.
I had compliments on all three.I served these with crusty bread and a salad.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nanna s christmas cake

as the name suggests, this is the grandmother of all cakes. the cake has excellent keeping qualities. you can frost the cake or i like to decorate the top with blanched almond kernels and glace cherries. if you intend to keep the cake, it may tend to dry out. just pour some sweet sherry or brandy over the top surface and it will help to regain the moisture.

1. on the first day
2. finely chop fruit and soak overnight in the alcohol , parisenne essence , orange juice and rind
3. on the second day
4. pre heat oven to 160 degrees celsius
5. cream butter and sugar
6. add eggs one at a time , mix well and set aside
7. sift flour , bicarbonate soda , nutmeg , baking powder and mix through the fruit mixture
8. add the almonds and creamed mixture
9. line a 20cm x 7cm square tin with two layers of brown paper , one layer being greaseproof paper
10. bake at 160 degrees celsius for 30 minutes , then reduce the oven to 120 degrees celsius and cook for a further 150 minutes or until a skewer comes out clean
11. let cake cool in tin and then remove from tin and place on a cooling rack
demonstrations.review:
This Christmas Cake was outstanding. I did pour Brandy on it afterwards and my friends said they had to drink the cake it was so moist. This is identical to a cake my Grandmother in the UK  always made. Bought back emories and I will keep this recipe for next time I make a rich cake.
Thank you for sharing Peter.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon curd and berry  trifle

tyler florence's recipe, this looks wonderful.

1. to make the lemon curd: bring a pot of water to a simmer over medium-low heat
2. combine the egg yolks , sugar , lemon juice , and zest in a metal or glass heat-resistant bowl and whisk until smooth
3. set the bowl over the simmering water , without letting the bottom touch , and continue to whisk
4. keep working-out that arm and whisk it vigorously for a good 10 minutes , until the curd has doubled in volume and is very thick and yellow
5. don't let it boil
6. remove the bowl from heat and whisk in the butter , a couple of chunks at a time , until melted
7. refrigerate until the custard is cold and firm
8. to build the trifle: put the berries in a mixing bowl and toss them together so they are evenly distributed
9. fold the whipped cream into the chilled lemon curd to lighten it up into a mousse
10. line a glass trifle bowl with pieces of pound cake to fit
11. drizzle or brush the cake with the lemoncello , spoon a layer of the lemon curd over the cake , and then a layer of mixed berries
12. repeat the layers until the ingredients are used up , the last layer looks best if it's the berries
demonstrations.review: I thought this was fantastic. Very rich and very hard to stop eating.  I am having to start more excercises but I will definately be making this again and again. Love the Lemon flavour so much. Thanks for a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fontina gruyere white cheddar mac and cheese

adapted from a food and wine article.

1. in a large pot of boiling salted water , cook the macaroni until barely al dente , about 6 minutes
2. drain
3. return to the pot
4. heat the oil in a large saucepan
5. add the onion and cook over moderately high heat until softened , about 5 minutes
6. add the milk and bring to a simmer
7. meanwhile , preheat the oven to 350f melt 6 tablespoons of the butter in another large saucepan
8. add the flour and cook over moderate heat , stirring constantly , until lightly golden , about 5 minutes
9. remove from the heat
10. gradually whisk the simmering milk into the flour and butter mixture until smooth
11. bring the sauce to a simmer and cook over low heat , whisking , until thick and bubbling , about 7 minutes
12. stir in the mustard , worcestershire sauce , salt and pepper
13. add the cheeses and cook over low heat , stirring , just until melted
14. fold in the macaroni until coated with sauce
15. spread the macaroni in a 3-quart baking dish
16. bake for about 25 minutes , or until lightly golden and bubbling
demonstrations.review: I decided to try this recipe instead of my usual one. The Gruyere which is one of my favorite cheeses was a winner in this recipe. I gives it a zing. Because I was cooking for company I decided not to use the skim milk but used whole milk mixed with half and half. More calories but everyone raved about this dish. Thanks for sharing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy chile rellenos casserole

a tasty casserole that is great for brunch for a light dinner :)

1. set oven to 325f
2. grease a 9 x 13-inch casserole dish
3. split chiles lengthwise , and spread in a single layer in bottom of prepared baking dish
4. combine the cheddar cheese with the monterey jack cheese
5. toss to mix
6. sprinkle half of the mixed cheeses and all of the green onions over the chiles
7. in a bowl , beat together the eggs , milk , flour and salt until smooth
8. pour over chiles and cheese
9. bake for 50 minutes , or until done
10. meanwhile , mix salsa with remaining 1-1 / 2 cups cheese
11. sprinkle over casserole , and return to oven for 10 minutes
12. let stand for 10 minutes before serving
demonstrations.review:
This is a great recipe. I was reluctant to try it as my other half is not a chili lover.  This was mild and delicious.  I am so glad I decided to try it. Its easy to make and heats up very well if you have left overs.
Thanks Kittencal you always have the best recipes.

target.recipe_text:
turkey brine

for a juicier and tastier turkey, brine before cooking! if your turkey or chicken is kosher do not brine since it has already been salted. brining isn't just for poultry but also lean cuts of meat and even fish and shrimp. but you must adjust time to their size. example; a whole trout takes only 20 minutes and the same with shrimp, a whole chicken takes about 4 hours, a cut up chicken about 2hrs. may add honey or maple surup, may replace some of the water with something like apple cider or coffee. let loose your creativity. yes, you have to plan ahead but for little effort the results are worth it!

1. combine 2 quarts of water in a 6 quart pot with salt and sugar , over high heat until dissolved
2. if wanted , add other seasonings at this time
3. let come back to room temperature
4. you will need 2 gallon turkey size oven roasting bags
5. place one roasting bag inside the other , roll down the edges of the bags to help them stay open
6. put bags in a heavy roasting pan that will hold turkey
7. place turkey breast side down , with legs facing you in the inner bag
8. some help from another person at this point would be of help , they can hold the bags open for you as you pour the cooled brine into the cavity and over the turkey
9. gather the inner bag as tightly as possible and secure with a twist tie
10. secure outer bag with twist tie
11. refrigerate in the roasting pan for 12-18 hours
12. remove from bags , rinse very well , pat dry with paper towels
13. it's now ready for your favorite recipe
target.review: This really did turn out perfect.  I did it overnight and I doubled the recipe because I had a 26 pound turkey.  I did inject it with cajun butter, but the meat was just perfect.  It was moist and VERY juicy.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
soft snickerdoodle cookies

these snickerdoodle cookies are so delicious, and they have the best texture. they are so fast to put together too! i actually got it from an old recipe that my great grandma had clipped out of a newspaper. grandma always knows best!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. mix softened butter , 1 1 / 2 cups sugar , 1tps of vanilla extract and eggs thoroughly in a large bowl
3. combine flour , cream of tartar , baking soda and salt in a separate bowl
4. blend dry ingredients into butter mixture
5. chill dough , and chill an ungreased cookie sheet for about 10-15 minutes in the fridge
6. meanwhile , mix 3 tablespoons sugar , and 3 teaspoons cinnamon in a small bowl
7. scoop 1 inch globs of dough into the sugar / cinnamon mixture
8. coat by gently rolling balls of dough in the sugar mixture
9. place on chilled ungreased cookie sheet , and bake 10 minutes
10. remove from pan immediately
demonstrations.review: I know this is just adding to the pile of accolades, but these cookies are fantastic.  I took a double batch of these cookies to work among several other cookie trays, and these were gone within an hour.  I don't know how they ate that many cookies, but they did.  Very easy recipe, does make a difference to keep the dough chilled.  Will make over and over and over and over again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
died   went to pimento cheese heaven  pimiento

a true southern delicacy! i didn't know i even liked pimento cheese! this stuff is addictive... so addictive i am having a lock installed on my refrigerator (not to keep me out - but in case the neighbors find out!). i have picked at pimento cheese spreads at parties and potlucks but never have the desire to make my own... and then i was asked if i would make a batch for a friend...this is a cross between her mom's recipe and my creativity. great on celery sticks, crackers, bread... even straight out of the bowl! even picky four year olds liked it!

1. using a hand held mixer , beat cream cheese until soft
2. add the remaining ingredients and beat until creamy and combined
3. cover and refrigerate for about an hour
demonstrations.review: OMGOODNESS, this is the stuff that every southern gurl lives for.  I use to go to a  friend's  house as a child and her MIMI  would make something similar to this and we would sit on the back porch eating pimento cheese with crackers as a snack with a mason jar of ice tea.  This stuff is just plum good!  Thanks for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken  gravy and stuffing

nan

1. season chicken breasts with salt and pepper and place chicken breasts in crock pot
2. pour chicken broth over breasts
3. put one slice of swiss cheese on each breast
4. combine both cans of soup and milk
5. cover chicken breasts with soup mixture
6. sprinkle stuffing mix over all
7. drizzle melted butter on top
8. cook on low for 6 hours or high for 3
demonstrations.review: This was about as tasty as it gets!  We all really liked it.  Our one very tiny, VERY TINY, complaint that there wasn't enough stuffing.  I think I will add more than the 2 cups next time to see if that helps.  Swiss cheese gave it just a great flavor.  I can't wait to make it again.  It's a keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oatmeal cottage cheese pancakes

these are wonderful and are almost too healthy to be true. lots of calcium, protein, fiber, etc. i usually eat them without any topping and just keep popping them in my mouth! yum. but a good jam will do them nicely as well.

1. blend all ingredients in blender
2. spray skillet with cooking spray and cook just like"silver dollar" pancakes , a few small ones at a time
3. top with your favorite pancake topping !
demonstrations.review: Really liked this! I did the recipe to the letter the first time and found that it was alittle bland, so next time I put in two over ripe bananas, used 2 whole eggs, splenda and cinnamin. My kids and I gobbled these up like crazy. I make some on Sunday now so that I can eat these for breakfast. I keep some in the fridge and freeze the rest of them. Works really well.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
elvis  favorite sweet potato casserole

this is from my "recipes from graceland" cookbook that i got this summer. this is typical elvis.

1. cook sweet potatoes , peel and mash
2. in a large mixing bowl , blend sweet potatoes , brown sugar , cinnamon , vanilla and a pinch of salt
3. stir in eggs and milk
4. pour into a square baking dish
5. bake at 375f for 35 minutes
6. remove from oven
7. top with pecans and marshmallows and return to oven for 5 minutes or until marshmallows are puffed and browned
demonstrations.review:
This is my sweet potato must have at the holidays now.  All of my 
in-laws agreed this was the best.  They are my "testers".  I did add just a little bit more brown sugar, but I sincerely think that it would have been fine without it.  Husband's idea. It was just an absolutely fantastic recipe.  I knew that Elvis had great taste!

target.recipe_text:
impossible peanut butter cookies

these are the quickest, simplest peanut butter cookies that you will ever make and they taste great!

1. mix peanut butter , sugar , and egg together until smooth
2. drop by teaspoon onto cookie sheet two inches apart
3. if desired , roll in extra sugar before placing on cookie sheet
4. press with fork
5. press again in opposite direction
6. bake 10 to 12 minutes at 350 degrees fahrenheit
7. do not brown
8. do not over bake
target.review: i loved these...everytime i have made peanut butter cookies,they have not turned out well...Peanut Butter Cookie recipes have been hit or miss with me and i havent found one that i liked until now.this is a great recipe,along with being simple..they taste great!!! I do agree not to let them get brown,they crumble when they get too dark.Great recipe,thanks for sharing!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops yum yum

i copied this from the orlando sentinel months ago and just now found it. we eat pork chops at least once a week and this is our favorite.

1. brown chops on both sides
2. place in greased casserole dish
3. mix all remaining ingredients and pour over pork chops
4. bake , uncovered , at 350 for one hour
demonstrations.review: I made this for my Fiance,myself and our two kids....My kids are very picky eaters but my son really liked this - it was a total hit!!! I definately plan on making this again sometime soon.Its different,it has a very unique flavor.Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
whatever floats your boat  brownies

these are absolutely the chewiest, moistest, fudgiest brownies ever! i have tried adding so many different things to the batter, and they always comes out great.  they are also great without any add-ins! but by varying the add-ins, you can make different brownies every week (or day!!) super easy prep! so, add "whatever floats your boat" and you will not believe how yummy they come out :) oh, and the recipe doubles just fine--use a 9 x 13 inch pan instead and add a few more minutes of baking!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. grease an 8 inch square pan or line with foil
3. in a medium bowl combine melted butter and cocoa and stir until cocoa is dissolved
4. add sugar and mix well
5. add eggs one at a time and stir until well combined
6. stir in vanilla , flour and salt until you no longer see any flour
7. fold in "whatever floats your boat" !
8. spread in pan and bake for approximately 25 minutes
9. do not over-bake -- your brownies will come out dry
10. adjust time / temp accordingly for your oven
11. if you do the knife / toothpick test , it should come out with moist crumbs , not clean
12. cool completely before cutting into squares
13. for vegetarian omit the marshmallows
14. for double recipe , bake in 9x12 pan and add 5 minutes to baking time
demonstrations.review: these were awesome! I dont like using box mixes at all and searched for the perfect homemade recipe for a long time...I have it now!!! i added chocolate chips to mine...great recipe.Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: I have to agree with all the other reviews...these are awesome and the crumb topping is delicious.I plan on making these again in the near future.Best part is,they dont take long to prepare or bake...wonderful recipe and thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: these are wicked good!!! easy to make and taste great.I let mine set for about 15 mins in the fridge and took them back out and cut them while the chocolate was still soft and creamy.I put them back in the fridge for another 10-15 mins to let them finish setting.I had no problems getting mine out of the pan.Thanks for sharing!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cheesy chicken

almost too easy, the chicken cooks in a creamy, cheesy sauce that is delicious over noodles. this freezes well, too

1. place chicken breasts in the crock pot
2. mix the undiluted soups together with the garlic powder and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours , until chicken is tender
4. serve with the delicious sauce over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: I made this for dinner on a 95 degree day...definately didnt want to turn my oven on.This is absolutely delish!!!!! I used a little more chicken b/c my fiance is a big eater...i did everything exactly as the recipe called for it It had great flavor.Next time I think I am going to use 2 cans of cheddar cheese soup and 1 can of cream of chicken soup,I am a cheese lover...this was a wonderful recipe,thanks for sharing.I plan on making this again really soon!!

target.recipe_text:
black and red fiesta beans with rice

this is low fat with tons of flavor and fiber.  a quick, easy weeknight meal.  serve with corn chips and a green salad.  from quick fix meals with robin miller on foodnetwork.com.

1. cook rice according to package directions
2. meanwhile , combine remaining ingredients in a large saucepan and set pan over medium-high heat
3. bring to a simmer
4. fold in rice and season to taste with salt and black pepper
target.review: Pretty good recipe.  I just used regular brown rice, not instant.  The flavor was alright but when I reheated the leftovers I ended up adding some of the salsa I had leftover in the jar because the flavor was slightly lacking for my taste.  But overall pretty good.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn maque choux  fried corn

i had no idea this dish even had a name until i grew up. we had it any time we had fried chicken, which was often. i love this dish - to me it is comfort food.

1. in the skillet , heat the butter over medium low heat until melted
2. add the onion and saute until wilted but not brown
3. add the bell peppers and the corn and stir to coat everything with butter , sprinkle with some salt , pepper , and cayenne , and continue cooking over med-low heat , stirring frequently , until all liquid completely evaporates , the vegetables start to take on a slight caramalization and the whole room smells really , really good
4. taste , adjust the seasonings if you need to , and serve
5. however , if you don't have one , you can use another skillet- just know that it would be much better cooked in a cast iron skillet
demonstrations.review: I tried this several weeks ago and just remembered to review it.  It was very tasty and quite spicy, but that may have been due to my being a bit generous with the spices. Regardless of how spicy it was (I do love spicy food!), I loved the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lentil and brown rice soup

healthful and hearty.  a good soup to make a lot of and have as a stand-by in the freezer for a quick, nutritious meal.

1. combine broth , 3 cups water , lentils , rice , tomatoes with reserved juice , carrots , onion , celery , herbs and sausage and bring to boil
2. simmer , covered , stirring occasionally , 45-55 minutes , or until lentils and rice are tender
3. stir in parsley and vinegar and season to taste
4. freezer
5. just defrost in microwave , reheat well and serve
demonstrations.review: A good soup.  I did make a few changes, mainly just due to what I had available and to use up some frozen vegetables.  No celery and only used 4 cups of vegetable broth and used water for the rest.  Added some frozen peas and corn that needed used up.  Also, as others have said, with the existing directions it is very thick.  I ended up adding an additional 3 cups of water to thin it out for my preference.<br/><br/>It makes a larger batch than I anticipated. I'm single and cook only for myself and I ended up freezing about half the batch because I know there is no way I could finish the entire thing before I got tired of eating the same thing over and over or before it went bad.  But freezing is fine, I have soup for next week or the week after

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb coated potato halves

when baking potatoes, i used to cut them in half, brush with butter, then salt & pepper before baking them, cut side up. here's a dressed up version of that!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in shallow pan , combine bread crumbs , paprika , salt & pepper
3. brush sliced side of potato halves with butter , before dipping each into crumb mixture to coat
4. place in 13"x9" baking dish & cover
5. bake for 60 minutes , or until tender
demonstrations.review: Really good, I wasn't sure if I should add something to it after cooking (sour cream or anything) but after trying it straight out of the oven I decided it was just perfect plain.  The spices add a very nice flavor.  Tasty way of making baked potatoes.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
basic trustworthy meatloaf

i have been making meatloaf for years and years, always the same way with minor variations, but always with saltine cracker crumbs as the binder. recently, i tried oats. well! quick-cooking oats (not instant) make a surprisingly good substitute for either cracker crumbs or bread crumbs in a meatloaf. i have also made this meatloaf without any garlic, and it's just as good. make sure the onions are chopped up fairly small; the texture of the meatloaf is best that way. also, don't use extra-lean ground beef as you risk having a dry meatloaf rather than a moist one. leftovers make a wonderful cold sandwich!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. lightly grease a 9x5 loaf pan and set aside
3. in a large bowl , combine all ingredients except for optional barbecue sauce
4. pack into prepared loaf pan , and spread barbecue sauce over top
5. bake until cooked through , at least one hour
6. drain off fat in pan , let rest for 5 minutes , then cut into slices and serve
demonstrations.review: First let me say I made several changes.  I used a meatloaf mix (grd. beef, veal, and pork), I added some green pepper, sauted the onion, garlic, and gr. pepper.  Unfortunately I had to omit the Worcestershire sauce, I thought I had some, but I don't.  However, it turned out really moist and delicious.  Thanks for the recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toad  in  the  hole ii

found this in a 1970's oscar mayer cookbook.

1. preheat oven to 400 degrees f
2. place sausages in an 8x8 square pan or baking dish
3. bake 20 minutes
4. combine other ingredients and beat well
5. remove sausages from oven and pour off all but 2 tablespoons drippings
6. arrange links around pan and pour batter over them
7. bake 30 minutes longer or until batter has risen to top of the pan and is golden
8. cut into squares and serve immediately with dijon mustard
demonstrations.review: I made this with some fresh pork linguisa sausage from Whole Foods.  When I removed them after the initial 20 minute bake there wasn't nearly 2 tablespoons of grease and I was afraid it the batter might stick, but no problems at all!  The cooked batter barely stuck at all.  Very nice dish!

target.recipe_text:
lemon mint barley salad

adapted from cooking light

1. combine 1 / 4 teaspoon salt and water in a medium saucepan
2. bring to a boil
3. stir in barley
4. cover , reduce heat , and simmer 30 minutes or until liquid is absorbed
5. remove from heat
6. cover and let stand 5 minutes
7. spoon barley into a large bowl
8. cool slightly
9. add mint , tomato , green onions , capers , and olives
10. stir well to combine
11. combine remaining 1 / 4 teaspoon salt , 2 tablespoons lemon juice , red pepper and oil , stirring well with a whisk
12. drizzle over barley mixture
13. toss gently to coat
target.review: chia, I made this salad last night and it tastes great. I used whole wheat couscous rather than barley (thought I had some but couldn't find it!). I also didn't have any tomatoes and felt that canned wouldn't work well for this fresh recipe so I went without, instead adding an extra tbsp of lemon juice. It's a really nice salad. I love the combination of lemon and mint, which work well with the remaining ingredients. Little bursts of heat from the red pepper flakes really complete the dish. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
reeses squares   5 ingredients   no bake  reese s

these bars are extremely rich and not for people with a fear of chocolate and peanut butter (if those people actually exist)!!! very easy no bake 5 ingredient recipe!

1. combine graham crumbs , sugar and peanut butter and mix well
2. blend in melted butter until well combined
3. press mixture evenly into a 9 x 13 inch pan
4. melt chocolate chips in microwave or in double boiler
5. spread over peanut butter mixture
6. chill until just set and cut into bars (these are very hard to cut if the chocolate gets "rock hard"
demonstrations.review: I'm hardly blazing a trail here with 223 ratings submitted before this one.  Still!  These suckers are excellent, and I don't care who knows it.  I used about 150 g of graham crackers (1 package of 10 sheets of crackers), and that was perfect.  I also went with 360 g of confectioners' sugar, which should be about 3 c according to the package. Perfect replica of Reese's Peanut Butter Cups. My 9-year-old says they're like the mini ones as opposed to the bigger ones.  *shrug*  I found that a 10"x15" pan was perfect, and no need for extra chocolate (although I'm sure that wouldn't hurt!).  48 bars are what I got.  Thanks so much for posting these.  I'll be sharing this recipe far and wide.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoked sausage supreme

it's a different from the everyday at home pasta. very colorful. great dish to serve to company.

1. cook pasta according to package instructions and drain
2. slice the smoked sausage and cook in the microwave for 2-3 minutes
3. drain off grease and set aside
4. in a large frying pan , heat the olive oil over medium-high heat
5. add in the onions and cook till translucent
6. add in the all of the peppers and continue to cook till just tender
7. cut heat down to medium
8. add in the saugage , garlic , basil and capers
9. cook another 2-3 minutes
10. in a large bowl , combine the pasta and the sausage / pepper mixture
11. top with grated cheese
12. serve with a ceasar salad , hot bread and a good red wine !
13. great in the summer when peppers are not as expensive !
demonstrations.review: This was a very good way to use smoked sausage. I really liked the peppers and garlic in this, a nice complement to the salty sausage. I reduced the capers to about 1 tbsp (can't really imagine using a half cup of them), and threw in 10 oz of sliced mushrooms because I had them on hand.  I did feel like something was missing... I think next time I'd use more fresh basil (recipe didn't say how much), and I think some fresh oregano would be nice too. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crumb topped banana muffins

these are so good. we love the topping.

1. in a large bowl , mix the flour , baking soda , baking powder , and salt
2. mix bananas , sugar , egg and melted butter
3. stir into dry mixture until thoroughly combined , then stop mixing
4. fill muffin cups 3 / 4 full
5. combine brown sugar , flour , and cinnamon topping ingredients
6. cut in cold butter until crumbly
7. sprinkle over muffins
8. bake at 375 degrees fahrenheit for about 20 minutes , until muffins test done
9. cool in pan for 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: Delicious! I didn't make the crumb topping but the muffin itself was wonderful: sweet and moist with a nice high dome. I actually preheated the oven to 425 and turned the temp down to 375 when I put the muffins into the oven to encourage a nice rise. Thanks for posting this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
classic flax bread

from http://www.cancernutritioninfo.com.

1. set aside 1 cup flour
2. mix remaining flour , flax seed , sugar , salt , and yeast in a large bowl
3. heat water , milk , and oil until hot to the touch but do not boil
4. stir milk mixture into dry mixture
5. mix in enough reserved flour to make a soft dough that does not stick to the bowl
6. turn out onto floured board and knead until smooth and elastic , about 8 minutes
7. cover dough and let rest 10 minutes
8. divide dough in 1 / 2 and shape into loaves
9. place into 2 greased loaf pans
10. cover and let rise in a warm place until dough has doubled in volume
11. bake in a preheated oven at 400f for 30-35 minutes
12. remove from pans and cool on wire racks
demonstrations.review: kburie, this bread is delicious. I used ground golden flax seeds, and took some liberties with the ingredients (types of flours, including some gluten, and upping the oil). Just had a hunk with nothing on it, fresh from the oven. Yum. This will make great toast and sandwiches.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sesame salmon fillet

a tangy honey-mustard sauce.  green onions and sesame seeds dress up this salmon for a delightful meal.

1. place the salmon in a shallow dish
2. combine vinegar , soy sauce , honey , oil , mustard , and ginger
3. pour over salmon
4. cover and refrigerate for 1 hour , turning once after 30 minutes
5. drain and discard marinade
6. broil the salmon or grill , covered , over medium high heat for 15 to 20 minutes or until the fish flakes easily with a fork
7. sprinkle with sesame seeds and onions
demonstrations.review: Fabulous marinade for a salmon filet.  We really enjoyed this.  I used walnut oil, fresh grated ginger, and brown mustard.  And now I'm bummed because looking at the ingredient list, I realize that I forgot to add the honey!  I think that would have made an already wonderful dish even better, and I won't forget it next time.  I prepared this in the morning before work and let it marinade all day before grilling it at dinnertime.  Served it over Asian cole slaw and couscous.  Thanks for posting, CD.

target.recipe_text:
crock pot chicken with black beans   cream cheese

i love this crock-pot chicken recipe for two reasons: one, my family loves it and two, it is so easy to make! i got this recipe from my sister. she has two children of her own, and they love it too! it's also the best leftovers in the world -- if there are any!

1. take 4-5 frozen , yes , frozen , boneless chicken breasts put into crock pot
2. add 1 can of black beans , drained , 1 jar of salsa , 1 can of corn drained
3. keep in crock pot on high for about 4-5 hours or until chicken is cooked
4. add 1 package of cream cheese and let sit for about 1 / 2 hour
5. all done and enjoy !
target.review: easy to make... used a jar of spicy hot salsa, frozen corn and a 19 oz can of beans, along with the frozen chicken... went i went to stir the cream cheese in, the chicken shredded nicely... no extra "juice" at all... in fact it was quite thick... we put it into whole wheat wraps with some lettuce... YUM!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
harvest pumpkin apple bread

all the flavors of autumn combined into one scrumptious bread. this tastes great with coffee or tea! i make this using egg beaters and unsweetened applesauce in place of half the oil to make it healthier. prep time includes cooling time.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour two 9 x 5-inch loaf pans
3. combine flour , cinnamon , baking soda and salt in large bowl
4. combine sugar , pumpkin , eggs , vegetable oil and apple juice in large mixer bowl
5. beat until just blended
6. add pumpkin mixture to flour mixture
7. stir just until moistened
8. fold in apples
9. spoon batter into prepared loaf pans
10. bake for 65 to 70 minutes or until wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean
11. cool in pans on wire racks for 10 minutes
12. remove to wire racks to cool completely
13. to make using three 8 x 4-inch loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 60 to 65 minutes
14. to make using five or six 5 x 3-inch mini-loaf pans: prepare as above and bake for 55 to 60 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was a great recipe, though I did follow some of the other reviewers advice and changed it some.... I used only 2 cups of sugar, and I substituted all of the oil for applesauce. Since I had cinnamon flavored applesauce, I omitted it from the recipe and added 1 teaspoon of ground nutmeg instead. I made 8 mini loaves and 6 extra large muffins, and after 35 minutes they came out perfectly! A big hit at my "apple & pumpkin" themed play date with my son!! Thanks for the keeper!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tuna and sweet potato  kumera  patties

a quick n easy week night meal! 
recipe source - australian good taste mag.
yummy cold too, a nice addition to a picnic basket or lunchbox.

1. steam the kumera in the microwave until tender
2. drain and refresh under cold running water
3. transfer to a large bowl
4. use a potato masher or fork to mash the sweet potato until coarsely mashed
5. add the tuna , egg , parsley and breadcrumbs , and stir until well combined
6. season with salt and pepper
7. divide the tuna mixture into 8 equal portions
8. use wet hands to shape portions into 8cm patties
9. heat oil in a large non-stick frying pan over medium-high heat
10. add the patties and cook for 3-4 minutes each side or until golden brown
11. remove from heat
12. divide among serving plates and season with salt and pepper
13. serve with lemon wedges , fries and a garden salad
demonstrations.review: Found this recipe while looking for something my 15 month old would eat (he LOVES sweet potato!) and DH ate 2, saying it was better than those salmon patties I have made in the past. Thanks Stardustannie for a recipe both my men enjoyed!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fried brussels sprouts

i've only eaten brussel sprouts steamed, until i found this recipe. this is from my mom's 500 low-carb recipes' cookbook by dana carpender. i added the lemon juice.
this recipe has lots of possibilities!

1. remove brown outer leaves of brussel sprouts
2. cut the brussel sprouts in half
3. it's your choice to cut in half or leave whole
4. in sauce pan , heat olive oil over medium heat
5. add the brussel sprouts and fry , stirring occasionally , until very dark brown , almost charred , but not burnt
6. the last minute of cooking , add the garlic and stir in to combine
7. be careful not to burn the garlic !
8. season to taste with salt , white pepper and lemon juice if using
9. serve warm
demonstrations.review: Honestly, I HATE brussel sprouts. I only bought some because my husband insisted he had a craving. Not wanting to boil them, I found this recipe... OMG!!! I actually ate them, and LIKED it!!!!! I would give this 10 stars if I could. Way to go, Cookgirl!! WOO HOO!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy and tasty barbecue chicken sandwiches in the crock pot

this is almost too easy to be called a recipe, but i had to share it anyway. i came up with it one night when i wanted a nice meal but wasn't feeling too motivated. i love crock-pot cooking!

1. remove all visible fat from the chicken and toss it in the crock pot
2. place the onion slices on top of the chicken
3. pour the barbecue sauce over top
4. you may not need the entire jar , just enough to cover the chicken
5. cook it on low for 8 hours or until the chicken is nice and tender
6. shred the chicken with a fork and knife
7. scoop the mixture onto the bottom buns and top it with the top buns
8. or , if you're like my dad , you might prefer leaving the breasts whole and eating it that way
9. voila !
10. an easy weeknight meal that doesn't heat up your kitchen in the summertime !
11. i love this with potato chips and a carrot and raisin salad
demonstrations.review: This was awesome!!! I used Pamela's suggestion and made Bobbie's sauce (Bobbie-Q Sauce (Barbecue)) and ending up omitting the onion since i didn't have any in the house. I was able to leave it in the crock all day... told hubby to open the lid 1/2 hour before I got home and just enough of the sauce evaporated, so the shredding chicken was thick with sauce. Incredible!!!! We had it on whole wheat tortillas with a sprinkling of shredded cheese. MMMMMMMMMMM!!!!!!! Thanks Kree!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
banana oatmeal bread

i love bananas and oatmeal, so when i saw this in the september 2004 issue of cooking light, i just knew i had to make it! i wasn't at all disappointed. the oatmeal makes it hearty and somewhat chewy, while the bananas and buttermilk make it sweet and moist - yet it is not as sweet or sticky-moist as some other banana breads i've had. this makes a smaller loaf than some recipes. i made 2 mini-loaves instead of one large one, and they were done in 30-35 minutes.  edited to mention- since i posted this recipe, i've made it several times.  it has become the banana bread recipe for this household, and when i give it as gifts it never fails to receive compliments.  it is extremely versatile also.  i have made it with yogurt in place of buttermilk, walnut oil for the vegetable oil, and i have cut back the sugar and added cinnamon as a couple reviewers suggested.  this last time i made an eggless version by substituting 2 tablespoons ground flax seed + 6 tablespoons water for the eggs.  (i think next time i will try a vegan version by also replacing the buttermilk with soymilk.)  every time it has turned out perfect!

1. preheat oven to 350f and spray a 8 x 4 inch loaf pan with cooking spray
2. combine dry ingredients together in a large bowl
3. combine banana , buttermilk , oil , vanilla , and eggs in a small bowl or measuring cup
4. pour wet ingredients into the dry ingredients and stir gently just until the dry ingredients are moistened
5. spoon batter into the prepared pan and bake for 55 minutes , or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
6. cool on a wire rack , in the pan , for about 15 minutes
7. remove the bread from the pan after 15 minutes and cool thoroughly on the rack
demonstrations.review: I used this recipe to make 6 jumbo muffins. I also made some substitutions, using plain yogurt instead of the buttermilk and I used applesauce instead of the oil. The muffins were a little dense but VERY moist and flavourful! My son and husband loved these!!

target.recipe_text:
oven cooked bacon with black pepper and brown sugar

nice and smokey, spicy and easy clean up. if you like it sweet try some brown sugar sprinkled on it too.

1. line a cookie sheet with parchment paper
2. preheat oven to 400 degrees fahrenheit
3. lay bacon on paper
4. sprinkle bacon generously with optional black pepper , chiptole pepper and brown sugar
5. bake 10 minutes then drain fat from pan
6. bake 5 more minutes or until it's as crisp as you like
target.review: This is a wonderful recipe so much easier than frying--much less mess!  So nice to be able to work on the other breakfast dishes and let the bacon pretty much take care of itself.  And I like how the slices come out straight and not all curled up like when I fry in a pan.  The parchment paper makes clean up a snap.  Thanks so much for sharing this wonderful time saver.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bev s sauteed yellow squash

this is the way i have been serving summer squash to my family to years. it is so easy and tastes great. i hope you enjoy it too!

1. melt butter in large skillet
2. add onion and cook just till tender
3. add yellow squash and continue cooking over medium heat , stirring until squash begins to soften
4. cover and continue cooking over low heat until nice and tender
5. i add lots of salt and pepper
demonstrations.review: I never liked squash and so never even tried to cook it before I tried Bev's recipe. Squash seemed too intimidating to cook and since I didn't care for them I didn't try very hard. But my son and husband love squash and when I saw this recipe I decided to give it a try. What do you know? Now I like squash as much as they do! This is a great recipe to start with and wonderful just the way it is, although I like to soak 5 minutes in buttermilk first. And sometimes I use a little bacon grease to cook them in and use the bacon for a topping. Optional items I sometimes add are paprika, garlic powder, sugar, lemon pepper, or Paula Deen's House Seasong. Not all of these additions at once, of course, just one or two for variation, but usually always Paula Deen's House Seasoning. Thanks, Bev!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crispy stuffing coated chicken breasts

only five ingredients are used for a tasty and quick main-dish recipe.

1. heat oven to 375 degrees
2. spray 13x9-inch glass baking dish with cooking spray
3. place stuffing crumbs in resealable food storage plastic bag
4. seal bag and coarsely crush with rolling pin
5. in shallow bowl or pie plate , mix stuffing crumbs and butter
6. in another shallow bowl , beat egg and half-and-half with fork until well mixed
7. dip chicken into beaten egg , then coat with stuffing mixture
8. place in baking dish
9. bake 30-40 minutes or until juice of chicken is clear when center of thickest part is cut
demonstrations.review: This had a very good flavor.  I agree that this would be great with mashed potatoes and gravy.  a little cranberry sauce might be good too.  I used only 4 chicken breasts but doubled the stuffing and butter because we love stuffing.  And I used 1% milk instead of half-and-half.  Very tasty!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
stove top coated baked pork chops

this is a great recipe that works well every time!

1. place stuffing mix in a bowl
2. lightly salt and pepper chops
3. dust with flour , dip chops in egg and coat with stuffing mix place chops in a baking dish with about 3 or 4 tablespoons of melted butter or olive oil
4. bake at 425f for about 40 minutes , turning once
5. voila !
demonstrations.review: My son said these were the bomb!  They were crispy, yet moist inside.  Very tasty.  I used the olive oil and it worked very well.  Very nice to be able to get it in the oven and get the sides together without having to watch the pork chops every few minutes.  Thanks for sharing this great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven bbq pork chops

this is an easy go-to recipe that has been around for a long time. it is a nice one for those days when you want a bbq flavour but don't feel like digging the bbq out of the snow. serve it up with some fluffy rice and a tossed salad.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit
2. place the chops in a shallow baking pan
3. mix all the rest of the ingredients to create the sauce
4. pour the sauce over the chops
5. bake for 11 / 2 hours
6. enjoy !
demonstrations.review: These were tasty and I love that the recipe called for things I already have in my kitchen.  They did smell heavenly cooking.  I was a little unsure of adding the water.  I had 8 pork chops so I doubled the sauce to make sure that I would have some to use over the meat.  I don't think that was necessary.  Or, maybe I could have doubled everything except for the extra cup of water.  It made a LOT of sauce so think next time I will not double it.  Pretty good and a nice, easy dish to put together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
corn casserole  paula deen

corn casserole recipe courtesy paula deen 

i have had this at a pot-luck lunch at work and it is fabulous!!! i wanted the recipe to put in my cookbook so i decided to list it on here...enjoy!!

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. in a large bowl , stir together the 2 cans of corn , corn muffin mix , sour cream , and melted butter
3. pour into a greased casserole dish
4. bake for 45 minutes , or until golden brown
5. remove from oven and top with cheddar
6. return to oven for 5 to 10 minutes , or until cheese is melted
7. let stand for at least 5 minutes and then serve warm
demonstrations.review: Made this exactly and it was delicious, although I kept thinking that all that butter may not be necessary.  After reading the reviews I think I may agree that I could have added another can of whole kernel corn.  And maybe the cheese would have been even better mixed right in or reduced if putting on top as directed.  Think I'll add an egg next time as suggested by several reviews.  But, I will be making it again!  Mmmm, good.

target.recipe_text:
chicken with sun dried tomato dressing

this is a quick and easy meal to make. i have cooked chicken with sun-dried tomato and oregano dressing for some time, but found a recipe in chatelaine with the dried seasonings added. original recipe called for 4 cloves of garlic, but i found that  a bit much.  i would only use 4 cloves if they were small.  wonderful flavor. serve this with steamed green beans and rice pilaf.

1. using sharp knife , make 2 or 3 slashes in each piece of chicken
2. place chicken in a large plastic bag , then pour dressing overtop chicken
3. sprinkle with garlic , italian seasoning , salt and pepper
4. seal bag and shake or massage bag to mix spices and evenly coat chicken
5. refrigerate chicken in the bag with marinade at least 1 hour when ready to cook , heat barbeque to medium heat
6. remove chicken from marinade and pour remaining marinade into a small bowl
7. barbeque with lid closed 10 minutes
8. brush tops of chicken with remaining marinade , then turn chicken
9. turn chicken occasionally , while grilling 20 to 30 minutes
10. before serving sprinkle with basil
11. can be done in the oven at 350 degrees for approximately
12. 40-45 min depending on size of chicken pieces
target.review: This was pretty good and easy to make.  We grilled on the charcoal grill, but next time I will bake to taste the true flavor a little better.  I couldn't find the salad dressing mentioned, so I used Ken's Steakhouse Sun-dried Tomato Vinaigrette.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
coffee brined chicken breasts

try this for really moist chicken on the grill. prep time doesn't reflect brining time. this is from fine cooking.

1. combine the brine ingredients , except coffee in a saucepan , heat until sugar and salt dissolve pour into a large bowl , stir in coffee , refrigerate until cool
2. add chicken and use a small plate to keep it submerged 2-3 hours
3. heat grill to high
4. remove chicken from brine , blot with paper towels , and brush with oil or butter on both sides grill 4-8 minutes , moving halfway to create grill marks
5. turn over and grill 4-6 minutes more until done
demonstrations.review: I had a hard time getting the flavor from this since I used a charcoal grill.  The chicken was very moist and cooked very well.  The combination of the ingredients seemed weird (and smelled odd), but worked well together.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
impossible lasagna pie

nan

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. grease 10" pie plate
3. layer cottage cheese and parmesan cheese in plate
4. mix beef , herbs , tomato paste and mozarella cheese
5. spoon beef mixture on top
6. beat milk , eggs , salt and pepper in blender on high until smooth
7. pour into plate
8. bake at 400f for 30 to 35 minutes or unril knife inserted in center comes out clean
9. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese
demonstrations.review: I was really happy with the way this turned out.  I used as many low fat and fat free ingredients as I could and it turned out great.  My husband is usually not too keen on eggy (quiche-like) meals, but he really liked this.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
spicy sweet mustard chicken

this is a very low carb and low fat recipe.

1. blend oil , mustard , honey , curry and tarragon
2. arrange chicken in a 11 x 7 x 2 inch baking dish coated with nonstick cooking spray
3. pour sauce over chicken
4. bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes or until chicken is done
demonstrations.review: I guess I need to face the fact that I do not like curry.  It was way too strong for me, and I even doubled the amount of honey to dilute a bit.  If you like curry, you will probably like this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy mushroom chicken casserole

this makes a delicious sauce to serve over pasta or with rice. recipe found on the internet.

1. melt butter in a large saucepan over low heat , add packages of salad dressing and mix
2. stir in the soup and wine , then blend in cream cheese and stir until smooth
3. add mushrooms and heat through
4. add a thin layer of sauce in a greased casserole and place chicken breasts over sauce
5. pour rest of sauce over chicken and bake at 325 degrees for 1 hour
demonstrations.review: I halved the recipe, and it was good to me.  I even used low-fat or fat free ingredients.  I did not serve over rice or pasta, but served with sauted potatoes and steamed broccoli.  I thought the sauce was very tasty.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken with fresh tomato sauce

nan

1. heat the oil in a nonstick skillet
2. sprinkle both sides of the chicken with the rosemary and salt and add to the skillet
3. saute the chicken until browned and cooked through and remove to platter
4. then add the shallot and garlic to the same skillet
5. cook 2 minutes till softened , add the vinegar and stir to scrape up browned bits
6. cook till almost evaporated
7. stir in tomatoes and chicken broth , bring to a boil
8. reduce heat and simmer uncovered until the tomatoes just begin to soften , abouth 3 minutes
9. stir in basil , spoon sauce over chicken
demonstrations.review: Fantastic!  I actually baked my chicken instead of cooking it in a skillet.  I omitted the salt and shallot and used dried basil.  I could've eaten the sauce on anything.  I will definitely be making this again!

target.recipe_text:
easy chicken supreme  chicken with stuffing

i make this favorite recipe for my kids and am posting for a cookbook i'm making for them.

1. prepare stuffing as directed
2. best if stuffing is leftover or made 1 day in advance
3. spray an 8 x 8-inch pan or casserole dish with non-stick spray
4. place breasts in pan
5. place 1 slice of cheese over top of each breast
6. spread soup undiluted over top of cheese
7. layer stuffing over soup
8. bake at 350f for 1 hour until bubbly and stuffing is golden
target.review: This was more like 10 stars. Very easy to prepare. My whole family loved it. I too have a picky one in my family. I used cream of chicken soup since I didn't have cream of mushroom on hand. I also used mozzarella cheese instead of swiss for personal taste. I did cover the dish like suggested my others for the first 40 min and then uncoverd the last 20 min. the stuffing came out just right. I will definately be making this recipe again. Thanks for posting it.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger veggie mix up

my mom made this when i was a kid. i make it now when i want comfort food. it's definitely something you can make when you are in a hurry. it is so easy to do and it tastes really great. it's easy to make, easy to eat, and fun for kids. plus, there isn't a lot to clean up afterward. call it a semi-homemade dinner :) you could change it in many ways like using turkey burger or any veggie that will cook up fairly quickly in a skillet. enjoy!

1. brown the meat as you would for spaghetti
2. as the meat is browning , i usually add in a good amount of season salt and the garlic
3. once the meat is well cooked , add in the veggies
4. cook on a med-low heat for about 10 mins to make sure that all the meat is done and the veggies soak up the juices from the meat
