demonstrations.review: These were very nice cookies and look pretty in a jar although I will be putting the choc chips on top so the flour doesn't sift through the chips and be giving them out for christmas presents this year!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
onion parmesan roasted red potatoes

very easy, very little prep. i use to buy a product made by lipton, which came in a bottle and you poured it over your diced potatoes and baked/grilled the dish. they have since discontinued the product, so i have found this to be the next best thing.

1. combine all ingredients in a large plastic bag , seal and shake until well coated
2. empty bag into a 13x9 dish , cover and bake at 350 degrees for 35 minutes , stirring occasionally
3. uncover and bake 15 minutes longer or until potatoes are tender
4. i think they even taste better more browned and crispy , so you may want to turn up the temp after uncovering and cook them longer
5. you could also make this on the grill , covered in foil in an aluminum pan
6. grill for 1 hour , turning potatoes occasionally
demonstrations.review: These had a nice flavour although i couldnt get them to crisp up without burning the cheese i did find they had too much oil so i might just use cooking spray next time as the flavour made them nice anyway crisp or not.very easy to make

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pineapple upside down bundt cake

i love bundt cakes because they are so easy to serve. i found this recipe on a camping website and adapted it for use in the home kitchen instead of on the camp fire! it comes out great and it will be the easiest pineapple upside down cake you'll ever serve!

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. melt butter in bundt pan in oven
3. spray cooking spray on the parts of the pan that aren't covered by the melted butter
4. sprinkle brown sugar over melted butter
5. place maraschino cherries on top of sugar
6. spread crushed pineapple over all
7. mix cake ingredients according to the package directions regarding time and mixer speeds
8. pour cake mix over topping ingredients in pan
9. bake for 40 minutes , until golden brown
10. test for doneness , knife or toothpick inserted should come out clean
11. immediately invert onto serving platter and remove pan carefully so none of the topping stays in the pan
12. cool completely before serving
demonstrations.review: Excellent presentation and so easy to do! Looks like you've put heaps of effort into it but haven't. I used glace cherries for topping. I was a little confused about the cake directions I didn't know whether to do it as directed on cake mix or use cake mix and add your 3 eggs and juice. Turned out anyway. Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bacon mushroom chicken

very easy to put together, and the result is fabulous. make sure to serve mashed potatoes or rice along side of this, to mop up the great tasting sauce!

1. preheat oven to 350
2. pour melted butter into a 9x13-in baking dish
3. add chicken , skin side down , sprinkle with seasoning salt and garlic
4. turn chicken over , season and lay bacon strips on top
5. sprinkle with mushrooms
6. bake in the preheated oven for 45-60 minutes , or until chicken is no longer pink and juices run clear
7. remove chicken , bacon and mushrooms to a platter and keep warm
8. pour juices from baking dish into a small saucepan and whisk together with cream over low heat until thickened
9. pour sauce over chicken and serve warm
demonstrations.review: A superb tasting dish and so easy to make! The sauce is absolutely devine and goes well with all the flavours of the dish next time I will thicken the sauce with cornstarch as I like it thick but was great to mop up with mashed potato and corn while thin as well. i doubled the garlic and used herb seasoning salt. A definate keeper

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fabulous honey white bread   bread machine

this recipe makes a loaf of bread that is high rising, soft textured, slices well, and keeps well too. all the qualities we get in store bought bread but, warm and fresh out of the bread machine, at a fraction of the cost too. i make this recipe 3 to 4 times a week. you will love this!!!

1. place ingredients in bread pan in order specified by your manual
2. use the white bread and light crust setting
3. press start
4. your dough should be slightly tacky to the touch and soft when you press down on it , like playdoe when you first open it
5. if too dry add warm milk 1 teaspoon at a time
6. if too wet add white flour 1 tablespoon at a time
demonstrations.review: An excellent white bread.The slight honey flavour was more prominate the next day and kept well. It was a light airy bread which is the way I like it and rose well. A definate keeper.I also used plain flour and butter as this is what I had on hand

target.recipe_text:
hearty and delicious beefy chili  soup

i find that this soup works best with only the chili macaroni flavor hambuger helper. this is a hearty soup that should be served as a main meal, with recipe#105726 or crusty buns on the side! adust the chili powder and chili flakes to suit taste.

1. in a pot cook the macaroni from the hambuger helper package in boiling water until just al dente
2. drain and set aside
3. in a large pot cook the ground beef with onion , garlic and bell pepper until no longer pink
4. drain fat
5. add in chili powder , cumin , dryed chili flakes and jalapeno pepper cook stirring for about 3-4 minutes
6. add in broth powdered sauce mix from the hamburger helper and tomatoes with juice
7. cook uncovered over medium-low heat stirring occasionally for about 45 minutes
8. add in the cooked macaroni , undrained corn and olives , season with salt and pepper and simmer another 10 minutes or until heated through
9. ladle into bowls and dollup with sour cream if desired
target.review: This was delicious. It took a little over an hour from start to finish, so it's something you want to get started on early, but it was still a lot faster than most chili recipes. I drained most of the ingredients and added a can of beans to thicken it up. Great recipe, thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
summer rice salad with tomatoes and green beans

this is a recipe i altered aftering finding online - cooking light, i think. it's a great dish that can be eaten/served chilled or warm. the dish is great for summer parties or just something to add to an everyday dinner/lunch. add 1/4 cup of grated romano cheese after preparation of the dish for some added flavor!!!

1. steam white rice according to package directions
2. easiest is to buy frozen rice and steam in microwave
3. steam green beans
4. again , best to buy bagged beans and microwave for steaming according to directions on bag
5. cut cherry tomatoes into halves
6. chop 1 / 2 cup green onions
7. place chicken broth , olive oil , red wine vinegar , salt and pepper into pot above low heat for 3 minutes , stir constantly
8. add remaining ingredients and stir over low heat for 5 minutes
9. serve warm or place in refrigerator until chilled and serve
demonstrations.review: This was good. I was afraid at first that I wasn't going to like it, but the more I ate the better I thought it was. We had this warm along with some grilled steaks. I'll definitely make this again. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
sunshine chicken drumsticks

the perfect barbecued chicken

1. blend steak sauce , ketchup , and preserves in a small bowl with a wire whisk until smooth
2. marinate the chicken for an hour and brush the chicken with the sauce when placed on the grill
3. grill chicken over medium heat for 20 minutes or until no longer pink , turning and brushing with remaining sauce
demonstrations.review: I used Heinz 57 instead of A-1 because that's what I had on hand I also used boneless chicken breasts instead of drumsticks. I let it marinate for about 3 hours and then cooked them on a Foreman grill. This chicken was delicious and moist. It was even better the next day as a grilled chicken sandwich.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
3 cheese manicotti

years ago my grandmother ordered me these recipe cards in the mail that you file in a box that the company provides. i didn't much care for the recipes so we ended the subscription. there was one gem in the bunch, though. it remains a family favorite! (i don't remember the name of the company) i have adjusted the cooking times several times based on different ovens (military, moving, rental houses, unreliable ovens!) so you may need to watch it and cook it more or less based on your oven. it is not a very traditional recipe but it is quick with little mess! you can also make it ahead and just cook it when you are ready.

1. cook shells according to the package directions
2. rinse well in cool water and dry
3. while the pasta is cooking , mix together the cream cheese and 3 cups of mozzeralla cheese
4. stuff shells with cream cheese mixture put a thin layer of sauce on the bottom of a 13 by 9 baking dish
5. place manicotti in dish and cover with remaining sauce
6. sprinkle 1 cup of mozzarella over the top
7. cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes at 375
8. uncover , sprinkle with parmesan cheese , and bake for 15 minutes more
demonstrations.review: This was delicious. I made it as directed and the whole family loved it. The preparation is fairly easily and doesn't take very long. I think it took me 30 minutes to get it in the oven, and that's even with distractions from a 1 and a 3 year old. I will definitely make this again, but I think I will add ricotta in the mix too because I thought the shells could have been a little fuller.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hearty chicken   noodle casserole

this can be made in minutes. recipe is from campbell's.

1. stir soup , milk , black pepper , grated parmesan cheese , vegetables , chicken and noodles in 1 1 / 2 quart casserole
2. bake at 400 degrees for 25 minutes or until hot
3. stir
4. top with cheddar cheese
demonstrations.review: This was very easy to make. When I added the cheese at the end I also topped it with some bread crumbs and put it under the broiler for a minute to brown the top. Great one dish meal for busy weeknights.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia with white beans and spinach

the first time i had this was at houlihans.  they have since discontinued the dinner, so i was in search of a great recipe.  i found this on epicurious.com by doing a google search.  i love this recipe and would recommend to anyone who loves an elegant tilapia dish.  it's easy and impressive.  this recipe can be easily doubled for a dinner party.  i like to serve with crusty italian bread and sometimes i'll serve it with rice on the side, too.

1. preheat oven to 425 degrees f
2. pat fish dry , season with salt and pepper , then dust with flour
3. saute fillets in olive oil for one minute on each side
4. set aside in baking dish
5. add butter to pan and melt , then saute garlic
6. add chicken stock and wine , and bring to a boil
7. once boiling , add lemon juice and white beans
8. stir
9. top fish with white bean mixture and bake for 10-12 minutes
10. while fish and beans are baking , saute spinach in same pan until wilted
11. plate fish on spinach and serve with lemon slices
demonstrations.review: This dish was so delicious and very quick and easy. I accidentally bought frozen spinach instead of fresh but I thought it still turned out great. I also didn't use fresh lemons, but they would have made a nice presentation.I will definitely be making this again. Thanks for posting the recipe.

target.recipe_text:
toll house butterscotch chip cookies

these are my absolute favorite cookie. ever. i have licked many a beater after mixing these cookies up. they are of course from the back of the toll house package.

1. mix together the flour , salt and baking soda in a small bowl , set aside
2. cream the sugars and butter together , add the vanilla
3. add the eggs one at a time
4. slowly add the flour mixture
5. when completely mixed , add the butterscotch chips
6. drop by the spoonful onto an ungreased cookie sheet
7. bake 8-10 minutes at 375f degrees
target.review:
simple, delicious cookie. hard to go wrong with a nestle toll house recipe, though!
my 3 1/2 yr old and i made these and couldn't even wait for them to cool off before we dug in.
thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
toffee fondue

too great foods: fondue and toffee! this recipe is reprinted with permission from http://www.24hourmom.com

1. melt the butter in a bowl over a pan of hot water , and add all the other ingredients except the vanilla
2. stir until thick , then add the vanilla
3. place in a fondue pot to keep warm , and serve with pieces of fruit
demonstrations.review: 5 stars really do not do this fondue justice. i made it for a lingerie shower where we had 4 different kinds of dessert fondue. this was EVERYONE'S favorite. we had about 10 different kinds of dippers, but our favorite for the toffee fondue was coconut macaroons! i cannot even begin to descibe how sinfully delicious they were. this recipe will definitely be used again as soon as i find the opportunity!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken packets  oamc

another once a month meal that's sure to please. my little girl likes these because they pick up easily in her hands! *i revised this recipe based on several folks pointing out that i had made a mistake on the amount of cream cheese.  thank you so much for the input!

1. mix chicken , cream cheese , chives , milk , and salt in a medium bowl to make filling , and store in a 1 qt freezer bag
2. put crouton crumbs in another 1 qt bag , attach it to bag of chicken filling , and freeze
3. refrigerate crescent rolls
4. to prepare for serving , thaw chicken mixture
5. preheat oven to 350f
6. unroll crescent rolls
7. each tube will contain 4 rectangles of dough with a diagonal perforation
8. press dough along each perforation so the rectangle halves will not separate
9. place about 1 / 4 cup of the chicken mixture into the center of each rectangle
10. fold dough over the filling , and pinch the edges to seal tightly
11. dip each packet in melted margarine , and coat with crouton crumbs
12. place packets on a baking sheet
13. bake for 20 minutes or until golden brown
14. packets are good either hot or cold
demonstrations.review: oh wow. delicious! i simplified the recipe quite a bit by using chive and onion flavored cream cheese. i also cut the step w/the butter and bread crumbs after reading other people's reviews. i didn't feel like i was missing anything. i only used 3 ingredients- chicken, the flavored cream cheese, and reduced fat crescent rolls. a meal this simple will DEFINITELY be used in our house again!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
ww  2 points   caramel apple salad

ww recipe!

1. cut up apples into small pieces
2. add in all other ingredients and mix
3. chill for 1 hour
4. 2 points per serving
demonstrations.review:
OH. MY GOODNESS. This is amazing! I just got back on Weight Watchers (have to lose the rest of that baby weight from my second child!) and this is now my favorite weight watchers recipe for sweets! I used a 1 ounce (small) box of butterscotch pudding and it was plenty. I was going to have this for dessert after tonight's dinner, but after I tasted this, I ended up filling up on it and not eating any dinner! :)
This is definitely a keeper! Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
4 minute spicy garlic shrimp

recipe is originally from the food network courtesy of rachael ray, but i tweaked it to fit our tastes. very quick & easy shrimp recipe that's done on the stovetop. if your tastes desire spicy & garlic, then this recipe is just for you.

1. heat a large skillet over medium high heat
2. add olive oil , garlic , red pepper flakes , and shrimp
3. season with grill seasoning or salt & pepper
4. cook shrimp 3 minutes or until just pink
5. toss with lemon zest , juice , & chopped parsley
6. remove shrimp to a serving platter , leaving the garlic cloves in the pan
demonstrations.review:
yum! i didn't have parsley, but i didn't miss it. i had to make a second batch that was not so spicy for my 4 yr old son. he loves it! i, however, love the spice! served this over brown rice once and it was great. made it with lime juice the next time and served it on top of recipe #10808 and pasta. yum!
i have also used this same recipe with chicken instead of shrimp. it's a huge hit at our house!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
streamlined chimichangas

this is a great tasting recipe and so easy that even my daughter doesn't complain when i ask her to make it.

1. preheat oven to 475 degrees
2. brown meat with onion and garlic
3. drain , but do not rinse
4. stir in picante sauce , cumin , oregano and salt
5. simmer 5 minutes or until most of the liquid has evaporated
6. brush one side of the tortillas with butter
7. on unbuttered side spoon heaping 1 / 3 cup of meat mixture into center
8. fold 2 sides over filling , fold ends down
9. place seam side down in a 13 x 9 x 2-inch baking dish
10. bake for 13 minutes or until golden brown
11. to serve , top with sour cream , guacamole and additional picante sauce
demonstrations.review: YUM! I cooked these for 15 minutes and then carefully flipped them over using tongs and cooked them for 5 more minutes to help crisp up the underside. I added cheese to all of them and refried beans to half of them. I also used homemade salsa instead of Pace and I used olive oil instead of butter. DH LOVED them, which is saying something huge because he is super picky. DD loved them too but DS didn't care for them. He's 5, so his opinion doesn't really count too much when it comes to new food :) I will definitely be making these again!

target.recipe_text:
black beans  sausage and rice

my whole family enjoys this easy dish. i make it often with cornbread on the side.

1. in a large family skillet with lid , heat oil on medium heat
2. add onion , green onion and garlic
3. saut until soft
4. add sausage and creole seasoning
5. once sausage is slightly brown , add rotel and black beans
6. stir until just combined
7. pour chicken broth into measuring cup and add water to measure 2 cups
8. add 1-cup rice and broth , water mixture to skillet
9. stir until combined
10. bring to a boil , cover and reduce heat to a simmer
11. cook until rice is cooked through and mixture is thickened slightly
target.review: Great recipe- I used kielbasa and to keep the dish from getting gummy, I rinsed the rice several times before adding it in.  Thanks for a quick dinner idea that my son (who is allergic to eggs and milk) can have as well!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker split pea soup

this split pea soup is almost as easy as opening a can, and twice as yummy. hope you enjoy it!

1. mix all ingredients except ham in 5 qt slow cooker , then add ham
2. cover and cook on low heat 8 to 10 hrs or on high heat 6 to 7 hours until peas are tender remove ham from cooker
3. place on cutting board
4. pull meat from bones , using 2 forks
5. discard bones and skin
6. stir ham into soup
7. stir well before serving
demonstrations.review: Great recipe- I had not made this in the crock pot before but will be making split pea soup this way from now on!  Everyone loved it, including my picky eaters.  Simple and done when I get home- thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
white chocolate chip cranberry oatmeal cookies

i originally made these at the request of my old chorus director john kelleher, who also worked at seattle area starbucks (i think he'd had the combo in a cookie there, once). i was surprised but very pleased they came out so tasty! these days, these are pretty much the only cookies which are requested and i make on a fairly regular basis.

1. preheat oven to 375f
2. in a large bowl using an electric mixer combine the sugar , brown sugar and butter
3. mix well to cream together
4. add in egg and vanilla extract and mix until combined
5. add the cinnamon , baking soda , salt and flour and mix well
6. fold in the oatmeal , dried cranberries and white chocolate chips- making sure that all ingredients are uniformly distributed
7. roll dough into 1-inch balls and place 3 inches apart onto a greased cookie sheet and bake at 375 for 10-12 minutes , just until the edges are lightly golden
8. remove from oven and let cool for 2-3 minutes on the cookie sheet , then transfer cookies to cooling rack
demonstrations.review:
Wow!  I needed something different than the typical cookie, and these turned out great!  I am not a big fan of white chocolate and thought that they might be too sweet, but it works with the oatmeal and the tart cranberries.  
The dough was a little stiff but after making the 1" ball for each cookie I pressed them down gently- just a tad.

Great recipe-Thank you for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot cornbread dressing

this is absolutely the best dressing i have ever had and so simple to make.  put it in the crock pot and forget it.  hope you enjoy (update) i have also made this with rita's corn bread with jalapeno & cheddar cheese recipe #50379 and just left out the cheddar cheese and it turned out great)update:  i omitted the salt after susied's review. just add to your liking.  i have recently made this and added chopped up chicken to it and it's excellent.

1. lay your bread out on the counter the night before you prepare the dressing so that it will dry
2. crumble the breads
3. add all other ingredients except butter
4. salt to taste
5. pour into a sprayed crock pot
6. dot with butter
7. cover and cook on high for 2 hours or on low for 4 hours
demonstrations.review: I finally decided to try this recipe after seeing it several times.  Needless to say, it is wonderful to have dressing that is not dry, AND to be able to prepare it ahead of time.  I used regular cornbread, and would probably add a bit more onion next time (family preference).  Thank you for this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cake mix banana bread

i got this recipe off recipegoldmine and i love it.  it is my favorite "easy" banana bread.  the texture is awesome too!  sometimes i add chocolate chips or white

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. grease and flour 2 loaf pans or 1 large bundt pan
3. mix all ingredients together until well blended and pour into pan
4. bake for 30-35 minutes or until toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean
5. remove from oven to cooling rack for 10 minutes before removing from pan
6. cool completely on wire rack
demonstrations.review: This is a great recipe to have on hand.  I used it with the spice cake mix and about 4 bananas.  I also added about 1/4 cup of milk.  It was moist but still held it's shape enough to make a cake with (I wanted to incorporate bananas into the cake I was making for my son's monkey-themed b-day cake).  Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the ultimate strawberry shortcake

the perfect summer dessert. not your ordinary strawberry shortcake!

1. wash , stem , and cut strawberries in half
2. add sugar
3. toss to mix well
4. chill
5. beat cream cheese and powdered sugar well
6. fold in whipped topping and cake cubes
7. spread cake into an ungreased 13x9 dish
8. cover and chill for at least 2 hours
9. cut cake into squares
10. top with strawberries
demonstrations.review: What a great summertime dessert!  Had a request from everyone to make it again soon.  It's great because it can be made ahead of time and I can remember all of the ingredients when I go to the store- thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
crock pot collard greens and ham

an excellent choice as a side dish for fried catfish or pulled pork. also goes well with cornbread to soak up the juices which are called "pot likker". when you eat this kind of food, you know you are living!

1. remove any thick stems and tear or chop leaves into strips
2. cook bacon in a skillet until the fat renders and bacon becomes translucent
3. place bacon , with its drippings , into the bottom of the crock pot
4. add the greens , ham hock , salt , pepper , and water into crock pot
5. cover and cook on low for 6 hours or on high for 3 hours
6. remove ham hock , discard skin and shred meat , returning meat to crock pot
7. serve greens with minced onion , vinegar and tabasco , if desired
target.review: We got our greens though our Bountiful Baskets co-op. Having never cooked collard greens before, I went straight to my comfort zone: my crock pot. We loved this recipe! The only thing I did different was add an extra ham hock. Easy to make and the flavor was wonderful. My wife loved the vinegar and I went for the Siracha. As noted in other comments, the meat from the hock didn't go far. I may add some diced ham in the future. Also, I ended up with a lot of extra broth. You better believe I ladled it out, froze it, and used it in a chili verde recipe soon after. I'm a broth enthusiast, so I loved re purposing the flavor of this dish (dubbed "green pork broth") for another use.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carrots piedmontese

this can be done ahead and warmed in a microwave later. colourful and tangy.

1. cook carrots in boiling water 3 minutes then drain
2. return carrots to saucepan
3. add butter , onion , garlic and salt
4. cover , cook over low heat 10 minutes or until carrots are tender crisp
5. discard garlic
6. add vinegar
7. place in serving dish and sprinkle with chives
demonstrations.review: I used basalmic vinegar. My partner didn't mind this dish, but I very much disliked it. As soon as the carrots cooled the vinegar left an awful taste and to me made this inedible (and I usually love basalmic).

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot sauerkraut and pork shoulder roast

this is great!  i like to serve this with mashed potatoes.  it is also great with noodles,  spaetzle or boiled new potatoes.  if you have any leftovers, you can make open-faced pork sandwiches with the meat and sauerkraut.

1. place sauerkraut in a 3-1 / 2 to 4 quart crock pot
2. trim fat from meat
3. if need be , trim the meat to fit in crock pot
4. lightly sprinkle meat with salt and pepper
5. spread mustard over meat and place the meat on top of the sauerkraut
6. pour beer over the meat
7. cover and cook on low heat setting for 8 to 10 hours or on high for 4 to 5 hours
8. transfer meat to cutting board
9. cool slightly
10. slice meat , discarding fat , and serve
demonstrations.review: My wife and loved this! And it was sooo easy. Served it with twice baked potatoes with leeks. My pork was so tender, there was no slicing about it. We just shredded it and mixed it with the sauerkraut. It was wonderful over the potatoes. We are vinegary type people, so I served it with balsamic vinegar that we added to taste. I will definitely be making this again soon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bbq pulled pork  crock pot recipe

this is an easy recipe to make your own barbecue pulled pork in the crockpot.

1. i like to use a crockpot liner for this
2. take boston butt and place in crockpot
3. cover meat with brown sugar
4. i usually make it about 1 / 2 inch thick on top and stick some to the sides
5. pour worcestershire sauce over meat and down the sides until the bottom of the crockpot is just covered
6. cover and cook on low in crockpot for about 8 hours
7. when finished , shred with two forks , add some of the juice from the crockpot to the meat , then add as much bbq sauce as you would like
demonstrations.review: Loved how simple this recipe is. Turned out good, but plan on using less sugar next time (a bit sweet for our tastes). Also, didn't realize I should have drained juices and it was a bit fatty and oily since I just threw the bbq sauce in after cooking and called it done. My mistake, so I give this recipe 5 stars for the simplicity and yummyness!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
red skin potatoes with bacon and cheese

this is a great side dish with steak, chicken or burgers.  not for the those looking for low-fat recipes.  just so yummy like potato skins appetizers.

1. clean and cut potatoes into cubes
2. add potatoes and sliced butter to a microwave safe covered dish
3. microwave on high for 5 minutes and then stir to coat all potatoes
4. season with salt , pepper to taste
5. return to microwave and cook on high for another 5 minutes
6. stir and let rest for 5-10 minutes
7. check the potatoes to see if they are done , if not , add another 5 minutes and let rest again
8. add cheese , bacon and mix with potatoes and cook on high in microwave for 2 minutes or until melted
9. if you would like a crisper potatoes then put the dish in a 350 degree oven for 15 minutes rather than microwave for the last 2 minutes
10. serve with sour cream and sliced green onions
demonstrations.review: A big win here. We added slivered garlic and leeks because they're a staple in our household. UH-MAY-ZING. The wife garnished with ketchup and me with my sriracha. Leftovers were served with eggs the next day. Win x 2.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
raw asparagus pesto

after learning how good asparagus is for the body and how well it helps the kidneys. i thought this recipe was an excellent one. it is not cooked so the the asparagus is full of vitamin a, folic acid. did you know that asparagus has the largest percentage of rda of folic acid then any other food source!! so eat up. this is excellent served as a dip or a spread. this recipe came from one of my favorite magazines: organic gardening

1. put everything in a food processor
2. slowly add the olive oil
3. serve cold
demonstrations.review: We got a ton of asparagus in our Bountiful Basket last week, and this recipe was a great easy way to use some of it in a new way. We are garlic lovers in this house, therefore this recipe was WELL received. Glad I tried it out just before St. Patty's, this will be a great easy green side to bring to a get-together this weekend (good thing mistletoe isn't a part of this holiday... I still taste the garlic a day later). I am very intrigued by the flavor of raw asparagus (I had never tried it raw before this) and will keep trying this recipe with my own twists and ad-libs depending on what we've got at home. And I agree with Leslie, we are also feeling cleansed. ;)

target.recipe_text:
vermont country baked ham from governor howard dean  m d

i found this recipe while browsing the web looking for ideas for a dinner party. i was very impressed and everyone loved it!

1. simmer ham in cider for 2 hours
2. drain , skin ham , and cover it with paste made from maple sugar , mustard , cloves , and water
3. place in baking pan , pour cider over it , add raisins to pan , and bake 2-1 / 2 hours at 325 degrees
4. baste frequently
5. make thickened gravy of cider raisin drippings
target.review: I made this for a large gathering at Christmas and our families loved this ham. I had a 20 lb bone in ham and I used apple juice instead of cider and brown sugar instead of maple. I covered with the "paste" after the 2 hours, I did not drain and skin however. The ham was absolutely delicious. Thank you for posting

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oprah winfrey s deviled eggs

best i've ever had!!

1. hard boil eggs
2. cut each in half lengthwise
3. remove yolks and place in bowl with all other ingredients
4. mix well
5. spoon into egg whites and sprinkle with parsley & paprika
6. cover and refrigerate at least one hour or more
7. serve chilled
demonstrations.review: I tried these for a family gathering and they were very popular. I especially like the touch of Tabasco. My "regular" recipe includes dry mustard, and think I will add that next time to tweak them a bit.  Thanks so much for posting.  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tomato vegetable casserole

veggies are good for you! due to reviewers' comments, it is advisable to put more than a dash of salt and pepper in this casserole, whatever is to your liking.

1. preheat the oven to 400 degrees f
2. toss the potato , yam , bell pepper , carrots and 2 tablespoons of olive oil in a 13x9 baking dish to coat
3. sprinkle with salt and pepper to taste and toss until coated
4. spread vegetables evenly over the bottom of the pan
5. arrange the onion slices evenly over the vegetables
6. arrange the zucchini over the onions
7. drizzle with 2 tablespoons of olive oil
8. sprinkle with salt and pepper
9. arrange the tomato slices over the zucchini
10. stir the parmesan and bread crumbs in a small bowl to blend
11. sprinkle the mixture over the vegetables in the baking dish
12. drizzle with 1 tablespoon of olive oil
13. bake uncovered until the vegetables are tender and the topping is golden brown , about 40 minutes
14. garnish with fresh basil if desired
demonstrations.review: I made this or dinner yesterday and it was a hit. I prepared pretty much as directed except I used baby carrots instead of sliced, grape tomatoes instead of tomato slices. (what I had on hand) I also did not have fresh basil and added dried basil to the breadcrumbs I made from homemade bread.  Since my b/f and I are very fond of cheese, I added shredded mozzarela to the top the last 5 minutes of baking. Thanks so much for posting! :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
mom s  the best  lettuce pea salad

my mom has made this as long as i can remember. it is a crunchy, very tasty salad. it is a 

1. prepare this salad the day before you want to serve it
2. it just isn't as good made the morning of
3. after lettuce is throughly dried , tear into pieces in put in large bowl
4. on top of lettuce place the chopped green onion , celery , drained water chestnuts , and well drained , uncooked frozen peas
5. do not mix over the top of this , spread the hellman's mayo to edges of bowl sealing the salad in cover tightly and place in fridge until the next day
6. dice 2 cups cheddar cheese and place in a plastic bag and put in fridge to toss with salad the next day
7. just before serving , add the cubed cheese to the salad and mix all well
8. pour into nice serving bowl and enjoy !
9. guest may add pepper and salt when salad is served
demonstrations.review: Made this for Christmas and it was very good. I did leave out the water chestnuts as not everyone in my family care for them. It was very easy to put together and very popular.  Thanks so much for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cream of potato and vegetable soup

i made this potato soup for a family get-together and people were scraping the bottom of the pot. it is very good and easy to put together. i used milk to keep it more healthy, but i'm sure the half-and-half would make it even better.

1. melt margarine in large saucepan or dutch oven over medium heat
2. stir in onion
3. cook 2 to 3 minutes or until crisp-tender
4. add broth , potatoes , salt and pepper
5. cook 10 to 15 minutes or until potatoes are just tender , stirring occasionally
6. in small bowl , combine flour and half-and-half
7. mix well
8. stir into potato mixture
9. add frozen vegetables
10. cook uncovered for 8 to 10 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender and soup is throughly heated
demonstrations.review: This soup was simple and delicious. I doubled the recipe and used the frozen veggies I had on hand which happened to be Flavor Fiesta and Mediterranean Blend. I also added a little bit of Extra Spicy Mrs. Dash just to add a little zip and then served with shredded cheddar cheese. Thanks so much for posting this wonderful soup.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tater taco casserole

i'm not for sure where i got this from but it sure is good.

1. in a skillet cook beef and onion over medium heat until meat is no longer pink
2. drain
3. stir in taco seasoning and water
4. simmer uncovered for 5 minute add corn and soup
5. mix well
6. transfer to a greased 13x9 baking dish
7. arrange tater tots in a single layer over the top
8. bake uncovered at 350 for 30-35 minute or until potatoes are crispy and golden brown
demonstrations.review: What a great dish! Since my BF is a vegetarian, I used boca crumbles instead of hamburger, and didn't need to brown. He is also not fond of onions, so I left those out. I mixed all but the cheese and tots in a bowl, transferred to baking dish and then covered with cheese, tots, then more cheese. It was delicious, and I will be making this one again. Thanks so much for posting.

target.recipe_text:
sopa seca de tortilla

a rich and creamy mexican side dish - full of peppers, onions, cheese and corn tortillas. it will surprise you. the name means 

1. cut tortillas in strips about 3 inches long and 1 / 2 inch wide
2. in medium skillet heat 1 / 4 inch of oil
3. fry tortilla strips , a few at a time , about 10 seconds or just until limp
4. remove with slotted spoon
5. drain on paper toweling
6. pour off all but about 2 tablespoons oil from skillet
7. add green pepper strips , onion and garlic
8. cook till onion is tender
9. sprinkle vegetables with salt
10. in 1-1 / 2 quart casserole , combine tortilla strips , vegetables , and half of the cheese
11. pour whipping cream over all
12. cover and bake in 350-degree oven for 20 minutes
13. uncover
14. stir gently
15. sprinkle with remaining cheese
16. bake uncovered about 10 minutes more or until heated through
target.review: I was a little disappointed in this recipe.  It certainly is not difficult to do but I feel it really needs some help.  I found it a little bland.  I'm not too sure what I would do to perk it up but I doubt I will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
heavenly pie   lemon meringue reversed

this my grandma used to make for my dad! found the recipe once she passed away. it's yummmyyyyyyyyyyyyyyy!!!!!!

1. sift together 1 cup sugar and 1 / 4 teaspoon cream of tartar
2. in a large grease-free mixing bowl beat the egg whites at a slow steady speed
3. when they are foamy gradually add the cream of tartar and sugar mixture
4. when the meringue begins to form soft peaks , increase to a moderate beating speed
5. beat another 5 minutes , until the meringue is thick , but still glossy , and forms peaks when the beaters are lifted
6. line a well greased 9 or 10 inch pie pan with meringue mixture to form a pie crust
7. bake for 1 hour at 225 degrees
8. stir in 1 / 2 cup sugar to egg yolks with lemon juice and zest , cook in double boiler until very thick about 8-10 minutes
9. cool
10. combine 1 / 2 whipped cream with lemon egg mixture and fill meringue shell , chill 24 hours
11. cover with remaining whipped cream
12. serve away !
demonstrations.review: I've been wanting to make this for a very long time.  It certainly wasn't the prettiest dessert I have ever served.  The filling was very tasty.  Not too sure about the meringue shell.  I doubt I will make this again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buttered baby carrots and sweet peas

easy, quick to put together veggie side dish. goes well with any main course.

1. in a skillet , saute carrots in butter for 5 minutes
2. stir in remaining ingredients
3. cover and simmer for 10 minutes or until vegetables are done
demonstrations.review: This is a nice and different way to do carrots and peas.  I certainly wouldn't want to be using this recipe all the time but I definitely will make it again. I think I will add some basil next time. Just a very nice change!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
black pepper butter cookies

these are my absolute favorite cookies. a friend in college had received a huge tin of homemade cookies from her mother and a version of these cookies were inside, along with many other types of cookies. i had never heard of black pepper cookies before and loved the unique flavor-sweet & buttery, with a slight kick from the pepper. i searched for years to find the recipe and finally found it in a watkins spices cookbook several years ago. i make these every year for the holidays and everyone always wants to know the secret of my "vanilla flecked" butter cookies. update: eggs sizes seem to be shrinking, so depending upon the size of the eggs in your area, you may need to use an xl egg rather than a large. regarding the pepper: fresh ground will produce huge grains of pepper and make things far too peppery and savory tasting. please use finely ground pre-ground black pepper in this recipe, carefully measured using a measuring spoon and leveled off.

1. mix all ingredients together well using a heavy duty mixer
2. roll into 1 / 2 inch size balls-you will need three large ungreased cookie sheets , 16 balls per sheet
3. use the flat base of a drinking glass that has been dipped into sugar to flatten each dough ball on the cookie sheets
4. bake in a preheated 350 f oven for 8-11 minutes or until lighly browned on the edges- do not overbake
5. remove to wire racks to cool
demonstrations.review: I will start by apologizing for not using the correct amount of pepper.  I chickened out after having read some of the reviews.  These cookies are great and the next time I will use the 1 1/2 teaspoons.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
old fashioned spicy oatmeal raisin bars

tasty and good for an energy boost. goes nicely with a glass of milk. these soft, moist bars are a great snack and kids love 'em.

1. combine raisins with water , and simmer for 10 minutes
2. add oats and all other remaining ingredients
3. blend , then beat at medium speed for 1 minute
4. spread evenly in greased 13x9" pan , and bake at 350f until top springs back when touched lightly in the center
demonstrations.review: Just took these out of the oven a few minutes ago and they are great.  Just a wonderful, not sweet, treat.  I think they would be awfully good with ice cream. By the way, the house smells awfully good. Thanks for posting.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked squash and apple casserole

this is my favorite casserole! my mother brings it to thanksgiving dinner every year, and the whole family loves it.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. pare , seed , and cut squash into small slices
3. place squash and apple slices in oblong baking dish
4. blend rest of ingredients with fork , fingers , or pastry cutter until crumbly
5. distribute over squash and apple
6. cover and bake for 45-50 minutes
demonstrations.review: I really did not care for this recipe but it would be great for people who do not like squash. I am a squash lover and I felt this recipe camoflouged the great taste of this "misunderstood" vegetable.

target.recipe_text:
apple squash soup

what a delicious fall soup this is - fantastic for thanksgiving!!

1. heat oil over medium heat in a stock pot or a large pot
2. add onions and garlic and cook gently 2-3 minutes or until soft and fragrant
3. add squash , sweet potato and apples
4. stir to combine
5. add next 5 ingredients
6. bring to boil
7. reduce heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes or until squash is very tender
8. pure soup
9. return to low heat for 5 minutes to warm soup
10. stir in evaporated milk
11. taste and adjust seasoning if necessary
target.review: This soup was SO good. I am recently allergic to onion and garlic and have been convinced I couldn't find a good soup without those ingredients. Needless to say, I left them out of this recipe and it was still amazing! I did saute some chopped celery in the first step instead. I didn't have any thyme so I just left it out. I toasted the squash seeds with some olive oil and salt and garnished the soup with them. It was perfect. I didn't think my husband would like it, but he had 2 bowls!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish cream coffee fudge

fudge, coffee, irish cream. yeah!

1. in a microwave safe cup , cook irish cream on high 30 to 45 seconds until hot enough to dissolve the instant coffee
2. in a large pan or dutch oven , on medium heat , melt the butter , add sugar , evaporated milk , irish cream and coffee mixture , marshmallow creme , then mix well
3. bring to a full boil , stirring constantly , for 5 minutes
4. remove from heat and stir in vanilla chips until completely melted and mixed thoroughly
5. stir in the vanilla , then the hazelnuts until mixed well
6. pour into a greased 8-inch square pan and spread evenly
7. chill until just set but still easy to cut , cut into 1-inch squares
demonstrations.review: Wow is this delicious. This was my first attempt at making fudge so I was a little nervous, but if you stir it patiently, it will turn out great. It seems as if the lumps will never dissolve, but they will and you will get a perfectly smooth, sweet, flavorful fudge that is every bit as good if not better than what you'd spend a lot of money on in a fudge shop. I didn't have hazelnuts but used hazelnut flavored Irish Creme and added in about 1/2 a cup of toffee bits at the very end. I let it chill for only about 30 minutes before cutting it and that made it relatively easy to get out of the pan later. I received many compliments when I served this and one of my guests even asked to take some home. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
special green bean casserole

great for holiday dinners.

1. saute onion in butter
2. add flour , salt , sugar and pepper
3. mix in sour cream , beans and cheese
4. pour into 9x13 baking dish
5. top with cornflakes
6. bake at 400 degrees for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was tasty! I liked it better than the traditional green bean casserole with the canned soup (and I love that!) I'm allergic to onion, so I left that out and added sliced mushrooms which were the perfect addition. The Swiss cheese was a bit chewy as it doesn't melt as nicely as other cheeses but I don't think I'd change it because the flavor was excellent.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried salmon and rice slice

this is very very good, my aunty's recipe--we love this in my house. this may seem like a lot of ingredients, but it is too good to miss out on.

1. cook rice in boiling salted water for 12 minutes
2. drain
3. combine rice with butter , egg , salt and pepper
4. line a 18cm x 28cm dish with aluminium foil , bringing it above sides of dish
5. press mixture over base and sides of tin
6. arrange drained , flaked fish over rice base
7. sauce:
8. melt butter
9. add flour and curry powder , stir until smooth , cook 1 minute and then remove from heat
10. add milk gradually , stirring until smooth
11. add mayonnaise and return to heat
12. stir until sauce boils and thickens
13. add lemon juice and parsley
14. reduce heat , simmer 1 minute and then remove from heat
15. add beaten egg , cool slightly
16. pour mixture onto fish
17. sprinkle with grated cheese
18. bake in a moderate oven 25-35 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: This was really good. The curry flavor was perfect and it was so creamy. Great comfort food! It did take a bit of effort but I will definitely make it again. The only thing I changed was using plain yogurt instead of mayo because I'm allergic to soy. My husband and little ones loved it too! I might add a bit of cayenne pepper next time, but that's it. Thanks for posting!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
gingerly molasses christmas banana bread

this is a quick, warmly-spiced banana bread that i invented for christmas 2010.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees
2. mix butter , oil , bananas , sugar , molasses , and egg until smooth
3. sprinkle baking soda & spices over mixture , mix lightly
4. add flour , stir until combined
5. add raisins , stir
6. pour into buttered bread pan
7. sprinkle top with kosher salt
8. bake for one hour
9. remove from pan and cool on rack
demonstrations.review: This is so delicious. I made it just as written, except I doubled it to make one regular loaf and two small loaves and I used equal parts cinnamon and cloves because I didn't have any allspice. I barely finished my first slice when I got on here to review it because it it SO good. Definitely tastes like Christmas; tastes more like gingerbread than banana bread, which is just fine with me. I can't decide what I think about the salt on top so next time, I might try mixing it in like other reviewers suggested to see which way I like it better. I'm so excited to make more mini loaves to give people for Christmas. Thanks for posting!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
delicious chicken pot pie

this chicken pot pie recipe takes a little time, but it is well worth it!! this is an all-time favorite in our family. great on a cold winter day.

1. preheat oven to 400f
2. saute onion , celery , carrots and potatoes in margarine for 10 minutes
3. add flour to sauteed mixture , stirring well , cook one minute stirring constantly
4. combine broth and half and half
5. gradually stir into vegetable mixture
6. cook over medium heat stirring constantly until thickened and bubbly
7. stir in salt and pepper
8. add chicken and stir well
9. pour into shallow 2 quart casserole dish and top with pie shells
10. cut slits to allow steam to escape
11. bake for 40-50 minutes or until pastry is golden brown and filling is bubbly and cooked through
demonstrations.review: Another 5 star review...delicious! The only changes I made were omitting the onion (allergy) and doubling the recipe. The doubled recipe easily served 10 and everyone loved it. I might try adding a bottom crust next time, but it was great as is. I baked the chicken with olive oil, salt and pepper and cubed it. 4 lbs of chicken breasts gave me the 8 cups for the doubled recipe. Doing a homemade crust was definitely worth it-so light and flaky. It was a bit time consuming, but totally worth it. This will certainly be part of my regular rotation now.

target.recipe_text:
cottage cheese walnut dip

this was originally from another recipe , but i made so many variations that i decided it was mine! 
now instead of a pasta sauce this is a lovely fresh and easy dip. all ingredients should be room temperature , but chill just for a bit then stir before serving.

1. roughly chop basil , parsley and walnuts
2. combine cheese and yogurt
3. then add margarine , garlic and walnuts in a bowl
4. mix thoroughly
5. stir in basil , parsley and pepper
6. eat :)
target.review: After reading the previous review, and checking with Chef #258867, I cut the amount of parsley to 10g (assuming 100g to be a typo).  The result was a think and chunky salad - not really a dip, but nice on lettuce leaves or crackers.  I don't know what purpose the margarine served (I used butter), and the Parmesan was drowned out by all the fresh herbs, so I would suggest either omitting the butter and Parmesan or greatly increasing their quantity.  I would also chop everything finely, not roughly, to give the flavours a better chance of merging together.  In fact, I would recommend blending everything - I did this with the leftovers, using a hand blender, and the resultant dip was much nicer, with a lovely flavour, a delicate green colour, and a slight grittiness of pulverised walnuts.  Reviewed for Pick A Chef, Fall 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
dad s crock pot spaghetti sauce

hearty tomato, onion and garlic red sauce that is perfect with ground beef or meatballs and your favorite pasta!

1. combine all ingredients in crock pot
2. cook on high for 3-5 hours or low for 6-8 hours
3. serve over spaghetti or pasta of choice
demonstrations.review: A good basic spaghetti sauce, which is easy to prepare.  I hadn't tried putting parmesan actually into the spaghetti sauce before (rather than on top), and it smelt gorgeous while it was cooking  :-)  This is a good basic recipe, which I am sure I will use often, and which will be easy to modify.  I often add a splash of sherry and a dribble of balsamic vinegar to spaghetti sauce, and that worked well with this sauce, too, stirred in at the end.  Reviewed for Pick A Chef, Fall 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bourek  meat filled pastry

this is an algerian appetizer.  traditionally ground lamb is used for the filling but you can also try ground beef or turkey or even one time i did spinach and feta.  you can also adjust the seasonings.  i think phyllo dough is a pain to work with and was told to try it with an asian type wrapper.  i tried but it didn't come out as well.  you can fold the dough around it pretty much any way you want.  just do them all the same so they cook in the same amount of time.

1. melt the butter in a skillet over medium heat
2. add the lamb and stir-fry a minute
3. add the onion , parsley , salt , pepper and cinnamon and cook over medium low heat til lamb is cooked through
4. take one sheet of phyllo and fold both side to the center length-wise
5. sprinkle lightly with melted butter
6. place 2 heaping tablespoons of meat stuffing at one end of the phyllo
7. press it out til it is about 4 inches wide and 1 inch deep
8. roll the dough over and roll about 3 times
9. sprinkle a bit more butter on the end and dab with egg to seal
10. do this with the remaining meat mix and phyllo
11. bake in a buttered baking dish in 350 degree oven for 15 to 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Very good.  The whole family loved them.  I served them with Hajar's Wicked Sauce Tomatish!, my own Coriander/Cilantro Yoghurt (Very Easy Side Dish) and a mixed leaf salad.  We had two boureks each, as a main course.  I didn't use the egg to seal the packages shut, because if you just lay them on the tray seam-side down, you don't need to seal them.  I often make another version of this which has more spices, and I would have preferred more than 1/8 tsp cinnamon in this recipe because I couldn't taste it in the finished product - next time I'll increase the amount.  I have to say that nobody else felt that more cinnamon was needed, so this is obviously a matter of personal taste!  This is a great recipe - very easy to make, and a big hit with my family.  Thank you.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lemon chicken  oamc

delicious lemon chicken recipe that is easy to make and stores well.  from once-a-month cooking.

1. mix all of the spices and lemon juice in a 1-gallon bag , add chicken pieces , and freeze
2. to prepare , thaw bag of chicken , preheat oven to 450 degrees
3. arrange chicken skin-side down in an 8x8x2-inch bakind dish treated with nonstick spray
4. pour liquid over chicken
5. bake for 20 minutes
6. turn chicken over and baste
7. bake for an additional 15 to 20 minutes
8. prepare rice according to package directions
9. serve chicken over rice
demonstrations.review: Superb.  Deeply, intensely lemony.  I used cut up pieces of chicken breast fillets.  Very easy to prepare, and very easy to cook.  I feel inspired to stock up the freezer!  Reviewed for Pick A Chef, Fall 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
weight watchers tomato spinach slow cooker  0 point  s

when your low on points for the week or if you want something that will fill you up that won't count against your points, indulge yourself in this yummy soup.. 

btw- my 3. 5, and 7 year old loved this soup with some oyster crackers.. family pleaser!

1. place all ingredients in a slow cooker
2. cover and cook on high for 5 hours
3. remove bay leaves , stir and serve
4. yields about 1 cup per serving
5. i used whole baby carrots , and also included the top parts of the celery , i cheat with my garlic and buy it already minced from costco and my family loves garlic so i am sure i added more than what it calls for , i also added more spice on everything , including the red peppers
6. but after doing all of that , i still came out with a 0 point soup that tastes so good ! :)
demonstrations.review: Very good.  A lovely, light soup, full of flavour and goodness.  Great that it can be popped in the slow cooker, as well!  Next time, I will reduce the quantity of chilli flakes, since the children found the soup a little spicy.  Reviewed for Pick A Chef, Fall 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
smoked salmon egg salad

my own egg salad!

1. chop up the eggs finely
2. chop up the celery finely
3. chop up the green onion finely
4. chop up the salmon finely
5. mix all ingredients together !
demonstrations.review: I loved this.  The smoked salmon adds a subtle salty undernote, and the celery and scallion give it a tangy crunch.  I didn't have any dried chives, so I used fresh instead.  And I used full-fat mayonnaise.  A very luxurious salad, which would make a delicious sandwich filling.  Reviewed for Pick A Chef, Fall 2007.

target.recipe_text:
spinach and spaghetti casserole

i never liked spinach til i had to try this recipe at my sister-n-laws and from than on i made this casserole for special dinners i either attended or made for supper at home. its a favorite to many of my friends and family and i thought i would share with everyone here at recipezaar. hope you like it too!

1. preheat oven to 350'
2. cook spinach and drain well
3. cook angel hair spaghetti according to package and drain well
4. combine egg , sour cream , milk , parmesan cheese , chopped onion , salt , black pepper , and montery jack cheese in a large bowl
5. stir well to combine add cooked / drained spaghetti and spinach to mixture and mix well
6. grease lightly a casserole dish and spread mixture into dish
7. cover casserole dish and bake for 15 minutes than take out of oven and uncover and bake for 45 minutes longer in oven or until lightly browned
target.review: This casserole made a great meatless dinner for me and my husband.  It was a perfect way to eat more spinach.  I added a can of cream of celery soup and used pepper-jack cheese, it tasted wonderful.  Thanks for such a great recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kaitlin s delicious banana muffins

rich chocolatey, bananay, moist and wonderful. because there is little mess it is easy to whip up a batch.

1. beat margarine , sugar , eggs , vanilla and bananas together
2. add remaining ingredients
3. mix lightly
4. fill muffin pan 3 / 4 full
5. bake 25 mins 350 degree farenheit oven
demonstrations.review: I made these muffins awhile back when I was looking for a way to use up some bananas I had in the freezer.  They were easy to prepare and very little mess to whip up a batch just like you said.  The chocolate chips were a nice addition to the muffins.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
country ribs   crock pot

mouthwatering classic!!

1. place onion rings in bottom of a 3 1 / 2 quart
2. crock pot , place ribs on top of onions
3. make sure ribs are trimmed of all excess fat
4. in a small bowl , whisk together the remaining ingredients , reserve 1 cup for sauce , cover this reserved portion and refrigerate
5. pour remaining tomato mixture over ribs , cover pot
6. cook at high setting for 5 to 6 hours , drain ribs , discarding cooking liquid
7. in a small saucepan , simmer reserved sauce for 10 minutes , serve over cooked ribs on heated plates
demonstrations.review: These ribs came out very tender and I really loved the sauce.  I have been looking for recipes to use my crock pot and this was great.  The ribs made a very nice Sunday dinner and everyone enjoyed them alot.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
apple french toast casserole

here's another make-it-the-night-before breakfast casserole. you don't need syrup with this one. prep time does not include refrigerating overnight.

1. melt the butter in a large skillet and add apples
2. cook and stir for 5 minutes
3. add brown sugar , water , and cinnamon and continue to cook and stir for 10 minutes until apples are tender
4. spoon mixture into 13x9 baking dish
5. cover apples with bread slices , making sure to cover the entire surface
6. trim the bread to fit if you must
7. beat eggs until foamy , then beat in milk and vanilla
8. pour egg mixture over the bread slices
9. cover the dish with plastic wrap and refrigerate overnight
10. in the morning , remove the dish from the refrigerator and let it stand while oven is preheated to 375 f
11. bake uncovered for 35 minutes , or until bread is golden and firm
12. let sit 10 minutes before serving
13. to serve on a platter , run a knife around the edges of the casserole , place platter on top of casserole , and carefully flip
14. to serve individually , use a spatula to remove serving , place serving plate on top of serving and carefully flip so apple side is up
demonstrations.review: Everyone loved this casserole for breakfast this morning.  I loved the fact that I could make it last night and put it in the oven this morning when I got up.  This was very easy and very good.  I used french bread and it came out perfect.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
wonderful salsa

this is the best salsa recipe i've found so far and i've tried about a dozen. i got it from one of the local hospital cookbooks that are sold in my area. i changed it a bit and have been canning it for years. the reason i plant a garden is for this salsa. we would be lost without it. hope you like it as much as we do.  one of our members who is a food scientist took this salsa to work, tested the ph and found it measured under 4.0 (well within the safety limit for boiling water bath processing).

1. mix all together and bring to a slow boil for 10 minute
2. seal in jars and cook in hot water bath for 10 minute
3. this is a medium salsa
4. this is also a chunky salsa so if you want a smoother salsa cut your veggies into smaller pieces
5. yields 3-6 quarts or pints
demonstrations.review: The name says it all.  This was my first time canning anything and it came out great.  I did pressure can it because of some of the reviews I read.  I have made this recipe twice in the last couple of weeks because my family keeps requesting more, I love it too.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
10 minute pork lo mein

from betty crocker's kitchen to your table in a flash!

1. heat skillet or wok over med-high heat
2. add oil and rotate skillet to coat
3. add pork and stir fry 5 min or until no longer pink
4. gently break apart noodles
5. add to skillet along with water , seasoning packet , and remaining ingredients
6. heat to boiling
7. boil 3-4 minutes , stirring occasionally until noodles are softened
8. diet exchanges: 2 starch , 3 lean meat , 1 / 2 fat
demonstrations.review: I make this recipe all the time, it has become a favorite. It is so much of a favorite that I posted the same recipe before I saw it here already.  This is a very versatile recipe, sometimes I make it with chicken and chicken flavored noodles.  You can add any vegetables that you have on hand.  This is really good and quick to prepare,also it is not high calorie which is a plus to me.

target.recipe_text:
thanksgiving turkey brine

brining the turkey with this recipe makes a very moist turkey!  delicious!

1. combine all ingredients in a stock pot , bring mixture to a boil , lower heat and simmer for 15-20 minute allow brine to cool completely
2. rinse turkey under cook running water , inside and out
3. pat turkey dry with paper towels , then immerse turkey in cooled brine
4. turkey should be completely submerged in liquid
5. my pot wasn't big enough , so the
6. cover the pot and refrigerate for 8-10 hours or up to 24 hours
7. remove turkey , rinse , pat dry and roast as usual
target.review: This recipe is AWESOME.  This is the first time I ever brined a turkey.  The turkey came out so tender and moist.  The flavor was outstanding.  I will always use this recipe for my turkeys from now on.  I plan on trying it with chicken soon.  I would give this more stars if I could.  Thanks for creating a new Thanksgiving tradition in our home!  I won't even bother with all the other brine recipes I found...why mess with perfection!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
jiffy scalloped corn casserole

nan

1. beat eggs slightly
2. add sour cream , butter and corn
3. fold in dry jiffy corn mix
4. put in baking disk
5. sprinkle cheese on top
6. bake at 350 for 45-60 minutes
7. make sure center comes out clean
8. another rendition is to mix in the cheese-- this was very good since it spread the cheese throughout the corn
demonstrations.review: I thought of giving this recipe a 4 but I'm giving it a 5 because of the multiple requests for the recipe I received after serving it at Christmas.  It wasn't my favorite but everyone else seemed to love it.  I agree with other reviews, you can get away with half the butter.  I doubled the recipe and there simply was not a need for all that butter.  EXTREMELY easy to make.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roast crock pot chicken

whole chicken that actually browns in the crock pot. the secret is to place it on top of wadded balls of aluminum foil. tastes just like it came from the deli.

1. spray chicken with olive oil spray
2. sprinkle with seasoned salt
3. insert onion and garlic inside cavity of chicken
4. spray inside of crock pot with pam
5. roll wads of aluminum foil into balls and place in bottom of crock pot
6. put chicken back side down on top of aluminum balls
7. do not add water or any liquid
8. cover and cook on low for about 10 hours
9. skin will actually turn brown as in a deli roasted chicken
demonstrations.review: This was EXCELLENT and EASY!  I used Lawry's Seasoning Salt and black pepper to season.  The seasoning salt gave it a great brown color and wonderful taste.  The only disappointing thing is that the skin does not crisp, but having been cooked in a crock pot, I expected this.  The chicken turned out super moist and delicious.  This will become a staple in my house.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked stuffed pasta shells

these are just fantastic! this is one of dh's favorite things i make. great for family dinner or pot luck. this is really pretty easy to make and true italian comfort food!

1. in an 8 quart pot , bring water to a boil and cook shells for 8 minutes or until al dente
2. drain and cool immediately with cold water
3. drain and place open side down on paper towels
4. in a medium bowl , combine the rest of ingredients except the spaghetti sauce
5. reserve the 1 / 4 cup of mozzarella
6. place a thin layer of spaghetti sauce into the bottom of a 12 x 9 x 2 inch baking dish
7. preheat oven to 375 degrees fahrenheit
8. spoon the cheese mixture into each pasta shell and place open side up , in a single layer , in prepared pan
9. pour the rest of sauce over the stuffed shells
10. loosely cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes
11. during last 5 minutes of baking , remove foil and sprinkle remaining mozzarella cheese on top
12. bake 5 more minutes
13. garnish with fresh chopped basil
demonstrations.review: These turned out great.  Very simple recipe.  I made a pie plate full of these for my husband and I and another for my parents.  I even froze another 10 to be used at a later time.  My husband had 2nds...and 3rds! (not typical!)  I took the suggestion from another review and put the ricotta filling in a pastry bag for easy filling.  It made it so easy.  Great recipe!!  Will make often!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
easy crock pot stuffing  dressing

when i used to stuff the turkey with my dressing, there was never enough so i had to make some of it in a casserole dish too.  but that batch never came out the same, so i decided to adapt my recipe slightly and make it all together in the crock pot.  it came out great (lots of compliments) and i didn't have to bother with stuffing (and unstuffing) the bird.  in fact, i got to sleep in just a little longer because i didn't have to make the stuffing until after the bird was already in the oven (bonus).  you can also prepare it through step 3 in advance.  i make this recipe to go along with a 20 lb turkey, so if i make it right after the bird goes in the oven the timing is about perfect.

1. brown ground beef and drain grease
2. melt butter in saucepan and cook celery and onion until tender
3. combine stuffing cubes , ground beef and celery onion mixture in extra large bowl or roasting pan
4. add chicken broth and mix well
5. i like my stuffing pretty moist and the amount needed can vary depending on how dry the bread cubes are
6. i generally use about 5 cups , but adjust this to your liking
7. it will not dry out in the crock pot like it does in the oven , so make about as moist as you want it to be when it is done , then add about 1 / 4 cup more
8. you can always add a litte water later if it looks too dry , but it will be a bigger ordeal if it is too soupy for you
9. place stuffing in crock pot and place turkey neck and giblets on top to help flavor the stuffing
10. cook on medium-low for about 4 hours
11. remove turkey neck and giblets before serving
demonstrations.review: I used Bob Evan's sage sausage rather than ground chuck.  It worked out GREAT in the crock pot.  Brought it to work for a Thanksgiving lunch and it was the first thing to go.  Everyone loved it.  This is pretty much the recipe I make on a regular basis but I never put it in the crock pot.  Great idea and recipe.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: YUM!  It is taking all my willpower not to go get seconds!  It was fantastic.  The only changes I made was using steamed broccoli and I did omit the ginger based on personal preference.  My beef started to stick to the pan...and then stick a little more...i did use more than 1 Tbsp oil but I don't have a non-stick wok so I probably just didn't let it cook enough before messing with it.  I thought I had ruined it but it turned out fine.  I got this from the Top 100 Recipes of 2009.  I find that out of the very popular recipes, I either love 'em or hate 'em.  No question I loved this!  Served over brown rice.  Can't wait to have it for lunch tomorrow!!!

target.recipe_text:
pad thai with chicken and shrimp

please note: this calls for one 1/2 pound package of noodles. not one pound. not a pound and a half. i'm not sure how else to write it so that it's clearer. 

i think this is a great pad thai recipe - quick and easy. it's certainly a favourite in our house. i would suggest making a double batch of the sauce, so the dish is even more flavorful. for those with milder tastes, cut back on the red pepper flakes. the recipe as is has quite a bite to it. this isn't a "authentic" pad thai recipe, so if that's what you are looking for, then this may not be it.

1. place noodles in large bowl and cover with boiling water for about 10 minutes
2. drain
3. set aside
4. mix together fish sauce , ketchup , worcestershire , chili-garlic sauce and sugar
5. set aside
6. cut chicken into 1" cubes
7. peel and de-vein raw shrimp and chop coarsely
8. finely chop garlic
9. heat peanut oil in large frying pan or wok
10. add garlic , chicken , shrimp and red pepper flakes
11. stir until shrimp turns pink
12. add sauce mixture and stir for 3 more minutes
13. add beaten eggs and stir constantly for one minute
14. add drained rice noodles and toss until coated
15. stir in bean sprouts , onions and 1 / 2 cup cilantro
16. stir and toss for a minute or so , until heated
17. spoon out onto large serving platter
18. sprinkle with chopped peanuts and remaining cilantro
19. top with slices or wedges of lime , which will be used to squeeze over noodles upon serving
target.review: We loved this dish!  I did add more noodles, I used a 14 ounce box and did double the sauce as suggested.  It was wonderful!  I followed the directions as written (other than the noodles) would not change a thing.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pan seared veal chops with rosemary

this is a wonderful veal dish. it doesn't take very long to make.

1. rub the chops with 1 tbsp
2. oil , garlic , rosemary , salt and pepper and let sit on a plate for 15 minutes
3. heat a large cast iron skillet over medium high heat and add remaining oil
4. add chops to pan and cook until golden brown on one side , and flip
5. remove chops from pan to a baking dish , brown side down and roast at 375f
6. for 10 minutes
7. add wine and stock to cast iron pan and stir up brown bits from the bottom
8. serve chops with juice from pan
demonstrations.review: This was fantastic!  My husband says he never wants to order veal out again, and only wants it fixed like this!  It was so moist and juicy. Perfect timing for a touch of pink.  I did  use morel mushrooms in the broth and 2T of butter.  The rosemary was the perfect spice and loved it with the white wine! Thanks for sharing, I will serve this again for guest!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
liar   fatmouth bang bang shrimp

i've been trying to get this recipe right forever but i haven't been able to worm my way into the kitchen at bonefish grill just yet. they lie to me like the worst of ex-boyfriends. this is as close as i got, help me out here! it's a great recipe, just not quite the real deal. reviews totally welcome.

1. clean & devein shrimp
2. soak shrimp in buttermilk for 1 hour
3. chop head of lettuce by 1 / 8" lengths & chill
4. finely chop green onions
5. heat peanut oil at medium
6. combine cornstarch , cayenne , garlic powder & onion powder
7. combine mayonaisse , chili garlic sauce , sweet chili sauce , & lemon juice in large bowl
8. dredge shrimp in cornstarch mixture
9. fry in peanut oil for 2-3 minutes
10. remove & drain on paper towels
11. add shrimp to mayonaisse mix & toss to coat
12. serve over chilled bed of lettuce & sprinkle green onions on top
demonstrations.review: I made this last night and it was wonderful.  I used the seapack fozen breaded shrimp.  Everyone loved it and I would make it exactly the same next time.  It tasted very much like the real thing.  It was a party hit!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best chili you will ever taste

this is the best chili recipe i have ever tried. i'm not sure where the recipe originated, but it is amazing! sometimes, i don't bother adding all four cans of the kidney beans and it still turns out wonderful. once anyone tastes this chili, they will be begging for the recipe!! enjoy!

1. heat oil
2. cook onions , garlic and meat until brown
3. add tomatoes , beer , coffee , tomato paste and beef broth
4. add spices stir in 2 cans of kidney beans and peppers
5. reduce heat and simmer for 1 1 / 2 hours
6. add 2 remaining cans of kidney beans and simmer for another 30 minutes
demonstrations.review: This was very good, I am not sure why all the tough ratings. This had a nice combo of spicy and sweet which was great. I made minor changes due to ingredients on hand. I used only one can of beans, 1 can of tomato sauce and one paste instead of two paste, I used a large can of diced tomatoes, and 1 1/2 T of Sriracha instead of the Chili sauce. Would make again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
5 cup pecan pie

don't like too sweet pecan pie? you'll like this one then, it's mostly nuts with just enough filling to hold them together. nice change of pace and very decadent.  i saw a pecan pie at a local creole restaurant, in a suburb of washington dc,  that gave me the idea to develop this one.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. spread 1 / 2 cup of the pecans on a baking sheet and toast them in the oven for 8 to 10 minutes , until lightly browned and fragrant
3. let cool completely
4. place the roasted nuts in a food processor and process until smooth and buttery
5. add the flour and pulse until incorporated
6. scrape into a large bowl and set aside
7. heat the butter in a small saucepan over medium-high heat until it starts to foam and turns a light brown
8. remove from heat and set aside
9. add the brown sugar , corn syrup , eggs , vanilla , and browned butter to the nut paste and stir until well blended
10. fold in the remaining 5 cups pecans
11. pour the filling into the pre-baked pie shell
12. bake for 30 to 40 minutes , until the filling is slightly puffed and the crust is golden brown
13. transfer to a rack to cool
14. serve warm or at room temperature
demonstrations.review: Love this not too sweet pecan pie.  I must say I did not follow the recipe exactly as I mis-read the direction.  Instead of 1/2 C of Pecans toasted and processed, I used 1/2 of the Pecans!  But, it turned out great and was very tasty.  I had request for the recipe! Next time I will follow the direction, who knows maybe even better.  Love the flavor

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked scallops with mushrooms

a delightful scallop recipe, enhanced with cheese, wine and spices. the mushrooms also give the recipe another different taste.

1. preheat oven to 450
2. in a large heavy bottom frying pan , melt 1 / 4 cup of butter
3. add green pepper and onion and saut over medium heat for 3 minutes
4. add sliced mushrooms and cook for 3 minutes
5. add 2 tablespoons butter to pan and sprinkle in flour , salt and lemon pepper
6. mix well and cook on low heat for 3 more minutes , stirring constantly
7. remove from heat , add half and half cream , cheese , paprika and nutmeg and stir to mix
8. return to heat and on medium-high heat return to boiling , stirring constantly
9. reduce heat to low and cook until mixture is thick and smooth stirring frequently
10. remove from heat , stir in scallops and wine
11. spoon mixture into buttered scallop shells or buttered baking dishes , about 1 cup size
12. in a small bowl , mix together bread crumbs with italian seasoning mix and 2 tablespoons of melted butter
13. sprinkle bread crumb mixture over scallop mixture in each dish
14. bake in preheated 450f oven for 12 to 15 minutes or until bubbling and lightly browned on top
15. serve immediately
16. if scallops are large , cut into smaller chunks before adding to mixture
demonstrations.review: I made this as an appitizer, I served it in a large heated chaffing dish, with small shell dishes to ladel it into.  The flavor is wonderful.  I increased the scallops to 3 lbs.  I also used a mixture of bay scallops and sea scallops.  I would make this again!

target.recipe_text:
pumpkin zucchini bread

pumpkin adds a twist of fall to the ever popular zucchini bread. haven't tried this one yet but it looked like a winner so i thought i'd share it.

1. before beginning , preheat your oven to 350 f and grease and flour two loaf pans
2. mix eggs and sugar together , then stir in the pumpkin and butter
3. stir dry ingredients together and add to egg mixture
4. mix well
5. stir in the zucchini and nuts
6. divide into pans and bake 45 to 50 minutes or until the loaves test done
7. cool in pans ten minutes before removing to wire racks to cool completely
target.review: This was perfect! We loved it. A great combo. I used 1 cup bread flour because I ran out of regular flour. I also did not add the cloves- I didn;t have any. Also instead of walnuts, I added raisins. If I had another zucchini, I would make more today!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
caramelized baked chicken legs wings

delicious! yummy  caramelized legs, kids love these! so quick and easy and no marinating required. just prepare the sauce, pour over the chicken and pop in the oven!  i actually like this with wings better ;-)
 

very important to leave it in the oven until it has caramelized to avoid disappointment. 

thank you to everyone for their positive reviews!

try adding sambal oelek as chef  #27416 has suggested in his review. what a great idea ;-)

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees fahrenheit or 180 degrees celsius
2. place chicken in a 9x13 inch baking dish
3. mix together the oil , soy sauce , ketchup , honey , garlic , salt and pepper
