5. scrape the sides of the bowl and continue to beat on high speed for 3 minutes
6. by hand , stir in enough flour to make the dough stiff
7. knead until smooth which can take up to 10 minutes
8. place in a well greased bowl and turn the dough until it is lightly greased
9. cover and let rise for about 1 1 / 2 hours or until the dough has doubled in size
10. punch it down and chill for 2 hours
11. cut the dough in half
12. on a floured surface , roll the halves into 12 inch circle and about 1 / 8 inch thick
13. brush the surfaces of the dough with olive oil and add the toppings of your choice
14. cook at 425 for 25 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is our new favorite pizza crust recipe! I actually cut the dough in half after punching down, put each half in a sandwich bag then into the fridge. Very easy to put together, wonderful flavor and texture. We've used this recipe for breakfast and dessert pizzas as well and it's always perfect. We've also put it into a cake pan and bushed some olive oil on top then sprinkled it with cheese and herbs and ate it that way and with dipping oils and it's just delicious. Really the best pizza crust recipe I've ever tried, I love it!

target.recipe_text:
ham steak   whiskey sauce

an irish dish gammon.a nice sweet and salty dish.great for st. patty's day!alternate cooking method: fry ham in butter 3-4 minutes per side then remove ham add onions cooking till translucent, sprinkle with sugar and then with flour mix till blended in, add stock simmering for 5 minutes. add whiskey season with salt, pepper and dried parsley. top ham with sauce.

1. brush steaks with melted butter
2. trim and cut into fat to prevent curling , and grill for 7-8 minutes each side
3. --to make sauce , gently fry onions in remainder of butter until cooked
4. remove from heat cover with foil then whisk flour gradually into pan
5. add water or stock
6. return to heat
7. add brown sugar , dijon , and vinegar and bring to the boil
8. lower heat and simmer gently for about 3-5 minutes to cook flour
9. if sauce seems a little thick , add more water
10. add whiskey and season to taste
11. place ham steaks on a warmed serving platter and pour on sauce
target.review: Really good!  I wasn't expecting much, but was looking for some different Irish dish, and this one really suprised me and my wife.  The stock I used was beer and bullion.  I added some salt and pepper to taste.  Came out a tad salty but we liked it that way.  I probably added some garlic too as usual and I used maybe two shots of whiskey (JWR) near the end so it didn't cook out the alchohol bite I love.  Delish!  Side dishes were sauteed fresh spinach with mushroom, red onion, cream, country dijon, and garlic.  Also new baby red potatoes with fresh parsley and parmesan.  Enjoy with a nice stout. THANK YOU!  :)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey dijon mustard fish

moosewood restaurant says sweet and tangy, with a crunchy coating, these fillets make a mouthwatering main dish that delights the senses with aroma, tatse, and texture.

1. preheat oven to 375 degrees
2. rinse the fillets and pat dry
3. set aside
4. in a shallow bowl , whisk together the honey , mustard , and lemon juice
5. in a separate shallow bowl , combine the bread crumbs with the thyme and add a few shakes of salt and pepper
6. dip each fillet into the honey-mustard sauce and then dredge it in the bread crumb mixture to coat both sides evenly
7. place the fillets in a sprayed or lightly oiled baking pan and bake , uncovered , for 20-30 minutes , or until thoroughly hot and tender
demonstrations.review: Just OK.  Nothing special.  I thought the flavor would be bolder and crunchier.  Maybe add 4x the honey next time?  I used wild salmon and the wife liked it, but I thought it was just average.  Side dishes french greenbeens with dijon/ garlic/ onion and white rice with mushroom.  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
beef steaks with mushroom sauce

this is one of my old reliable recipes. i can always count on this to please everyone.

1. heat oil and 2 t butter in large skillet
2. add steaks and cook on med-hi for 6-7 minutes per side
3. remove from heat and keep warm
4. to pan add remaining butter and mushrooms , cook and stir 3 minutes
5. add onions , saute 1 minute
6. add flour , salt and pepper , cook and stir 2 minutes
7. add broth slowly , stir until smooth
8. boil 1 minute
9. serve steaks with sauce on the side
demonstrations.review: A very nice dish.  My wife liked it more than I did as she prefers mellow flavors.  I wanted more of a bite.  Next time I'll add merlot and capers to the sauce.  As you can imagine, a really nice piece of meat is the most important part.  I accompanied with new red potatoes and sweet pees.  Thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
honey ginger grilled salmon

super easy, sweet and spicy!

1. in a large self-closing plastic bag , combine first six ingredients
2. mix well
3. place salmon in bag and seal tightly
4. turn bag gently to distribute marinade
5. refrigerate 15 minutes or up to 30 minutes for stronger flavor
6. turn bag occasionally
7. lightly grease grill rack
8. preheat grill to medium heat
9. remove salmon from marinade
10. reserve the marinade
11. grill 12-15 minutes per inch of thickness or until fish flakes easily with a fork
12. brush with reserved marinade up until the last 5 minutes of cooking time
13. discard leftover marinade
demonstrations.review: Quite lame and a waste of good wild salmon.  Followed instructions and marinated for 30 mins prior to grilling.  I know baking in marinate would improve drastically and I should have done that rather than following instructions.  Flavors were bland even for my wife and we were quite disappointed.  Stick to foil baking and don't waste your time chilling in fridge as it makes little difference.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
pork chops with an oregano wine sauce

the sauce on these chops is so good i could eat it with a spoon!!! it's a great combination of flavors.

1. brown chops in oil for 10 minutes
2. add peppers and mushrooms , cook 5 minutes
3. add garlic , tomatoes and tomato sauce
4. stir and cook 3 minutes
5. add wine
6. add seasonings
7. cover and cook for 20-25 minutes
demonstrations.review: Outstanding recipe.  Turned out really well and was a hit with me and the wifey.  Flavors were perfectly balanced and unique.  My side dishes were risotto and broccoli sauted in cream with mushrooms, green onion, and parmesan.  THANK YOU!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bow ties alfredo with ham and peas  or broccoli

nan

1. bring large of lightly salted water to boiling
2. add pasta
3. cook 12 minutes or until firm but tender
4. add peas for last 3 minutes of cooking
5. reserve 1 / 2 cup of pasta cooking water
6. drain water
7. meanwhile , shake together flour and milk in jar with tight-fitting lid until blended
8. heat butter in saucepan over medium heat
9. add garlic , saute 1 minute
10. whisk in milk mixture
11. simmer 3 minutes
12. whisk in cream cheese , 2 tablespoons parmesan , salt and pepper
13. simmer , whisking , 2 minutes
14. remove from heat
15. toss together pasta , peas or broccoli , sauce and ham in large bowl
16. add 1 / 4 to 1 / 2 cup of reserved pasta water , tossing to make creamy sauce
17. top with remaining parmesan
18. serve hot
demonstrations.review: Decent pasta.  Bland enough for the wife and a good base for me to pep up.  I would use a very flavorful ham (smokey or southern) and tons of garlic.  The cream cheese worked but I prefer straight alfredo with cream.

target.recipe_text:
beef and rice casserole

this is a super-simple concoction of my mom's, and a family favorite. terrific with some green vegetables or a salad!

1. brown beef with onion and drain
2. add rice , soup , water , celery , peppers , salt and black pepper , mix well
3. place in greased two-quart casserole dish and bake , covered , for 1 hour and 15 minutes at 350 degrees f
4. serve and enjoy !
target.review: Great recipe!  My kids and I both ate it up.  It's a pretty quick and simple meal for any week night and it's pretty inexpensive.  I was a little surprised in how little it made so I'll probably add a little more rice next time but other than it was wonderful!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oreo balls

my sister's co-worker brought these to a party and they were quite a hit. i don't know where the recipe came from originally.

"bark" is an artificial chocolate or vanilla candy coating/confectioner's coating used to make a treat called almond bark and can be found at most grocery stores near the chocolate chips. 

you can use chocolate chips and white chocolate chips if you don't have almond bark, but i have found that almond bark melts better and is easier to work with.

1. using a blender or hand held mixer , mix oreos and cream cheese together
2. roll into walnut size balls
3. chill for an hour
4. melt approximately 3 / 4 package of white almond bark
5. stick a toothpick in an oreo ball and dip it in the melted white almond bark
6. allow to harden on wax paper
7. takes about 15 minute
8. while waiting , melt about 1 / 4 package of chocolate almond bark
9. when oreo balls are no longer sticky to the touch , decorate with drizzles of chocolate and white almond bark
10. i just use a sandwich bag with a tiny hole cut in one corner to drizzle the almond bark
demonstrations.review: I've already made these twice since Christmas at the request of my other half.  So simple to make and they turn out so pretty! The last time I did leave out a few cookies to make the mixture a little more moist and cake like.  I used the white almond bark and then regular milk chocolate chips to drizzle on top.  Turned out so pretty! Thanks for sharing

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crook s corner shrimp and grits

crook's corner is a restaurant in chapel hill, nc. this is a dish served at the restaurant and i found the recipe in the latest southern living magazine. i made this last night for dinner and my husband and i went nuts for it, it's the ultimate comfort food. don't let the long list of ingredients throw you off, this goes together quickly and easily.

1. bring first 4 ingredients to a boil in a medium saucepan
2. gradually whisk in grits
3. reduce heat and simmer , stirring occasionally , 10 minutes or until thickened
4. add cheddar cheese and next 4 ingredients
5. set aside but keep warm
6. cook bacon in a large skillet until crisp
7. remove bacon and drain on paper towels , reserve 1 tablespoon of drippings in skillet
8. crumble bacon and set aside
9. sprinkle shrimp with pepper and salt
10. dredge in flour
11. saute mushrooms in hot drippings in skillet 5 minutes , or until tender
12. add green onions and saute 2 minutes
13. add shrimp and garlic and saute 2 minutes or until shrimp are lightly brown
14. stir in chicken broth , lemon juice and hot sauce and cook 2 more minutes , stirring to loosen browned bits from skillet
15. divide grits into 4 large , shallow soup bowls
16. divide shrimp mixture into four servings and place on top of grits
17. top each serving with crumbled bacon and serve with lemon wedges
demonstrations.review: I was really disappointed in this recipe.  From the picture it looks like it has a red sauce and my turned out more like a brown gravy.  The only flavor it really even had was from the extra seasonings that I added and even still it was bland.  It wasn't at all what I was expecting!! I'm from Alabama and this is no southern cooking!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bread pudding in the microwave

i have no idea where i got this recipe, but it is handwritten in a small book where i saved recipes back in the mid-80s. i haven't made this in ages, but i do recall i used to make it a lot. i think i will make it again today! :-) ordinary sandwich bread works fine, or use a spiffier bread to make a spiffier pudding. serve with a vanilla custard sauce, whipped cream, or even ice cream.

1. spread bread cubes evenly in an 8-inch round glass pan
2. sprinkle with the sugar , salt , and raisins
3. place milk in a 4-cup glass measuring cup and add the butter
4. microwave on high for four minutes , until butter melts and milk is warm
5. rapidly , stir in eggs with a fork or small whisk and combine well
6. pour over bread
7. microwave on medium-high for 9 to 12 minutes
8. when cooked , centre may still be slightly soft , but does set up as pudding cools
9. serve warm or chilled
10. your preference
demonstrations.review: I have probably made this recipe 10 times already.  I love it! I love bread pudding and this is so easy since I usually have all the ingredients right on hand.  I've done it with italian break and plain white bread, both work extremely well.  The only thing I ever do different is that I add about a tsp of vanilla and cinnamon but sometimes reduce the milk to 1&1/2 cup but everything else is perfect. LOVE this recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bayou pasta with chicken   copycat chili s cajun chicken pasta

i got this recipe from a place that claimed it as a copycat of chilis cajun chicken pasta, so i had to try it, and was pleasantly surprised that it did taste a lot like it!

1. bring a pot of salted water to a boil
2. cook penne according to package directions
3. melt butter over medium heat
4. add flour
5. stir for 1 minute
6. add half-and-half
7. stir until thickened , 6 minutes
8. remove from heat
9. add parmesan , salt and pepper
10. cover
11. pound chicken to 1 / 2-inch thickness
12. rub cajun seasoning and cayenne evenly over chicken
13. warm oil in a nonstick skillet over medium-high heat
14. add chicken and cook , turning once , until no longer pink in center , 6-8 minutes
15. slice chicken
16. in a bowl , toss pasta with sauce
17. top with chicken and tomatoes and serve
demonstrations.review: I've cooked this twice now and it's pretty good.  It has a great taste and the tomato adds a ton of flavor.  My only problem is both times the sauce has been a little thicker than I like or remember of the actual chilis sauce.  Everything else is great though! Super easy to cook for anyone!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
utterly deadly southern pecan pie

the secret to this rich pie is cooking the sugar and corn syrup first. it is definitely not diet food!  i bake this pie for 45 minutes according to my oven but you may need to bake longer.

1. in saucepan boil sugar and corn syrup together for 2 to 3 minutes
2. set aside to cool slightly
3. in large bowl beat eggs lightly and very slowly pour the syrup mixture into the eggs , stirring constantly
4. at this point i like to strain the mixture to make sure it's smooth and lump free
5. stir in butter , vanilla , and pecans and pour into crust
6. bake in a 350f oven for about 45 to 60 minutes or until set
demonstrations.review: I fixed this for Thanksgiving and all we could say was WOW.  It was the first pecan pie I've ever done solo and it turned out perfect.  I think I ended up eating half of it myself because it was just that good!  We couldn't get enough.  Great recipe! Super Easy.  I even let my 4 year old in the kitchen to help. Thanks for posting!

target.recipe_text:
simply sour cream chicken enchiladas

easy to assemble, deliciously creamy and a great choice for once-a-month cooking. and there is no canned cream soup in my enchiladas -- hope you give them a try!

1. in a frying pan , cook chicken and onion together in oil over medium-high heat until chicken is just done
2. divide cooked chicken evenly between 8 tortillas
3. add 1 1 / 2 tablespoons cheese to each tortilla
4. roll enchiladas and place seam-side down in a 9x13" baking dish that has been lightly sprayed with no-stick cooking spray
5. melt butter in a medium saucepan
6. stir in flour to make a roux , stir and cook until bubbly , and gradually whisk in chicken broth then bring to boiling , stirring frequently
7. remove from heat
8. stir in sour cream and green chilies
9. pour sauce evenly over enchiladas
10. top with remaining 3 / 4 cup cheese and bake at 400 f for 20 minutes until cheese is melted and sauce near edges of baking dish is bubbly
target.review: Excellent Dish.  I made this tonight for the first time and was worried that the sauce would taste like flour....because I have made enchiladas that didn't turn out well in the past.  These were very good.  My husband added a little salsa to his....but other than that - followed the recipe exactly and was a big hit.  Thank you for a great meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hamburger noodle bake

this is almost like a lasagna. very good!

1. brown hamburger , onions , and spices until cooked
2. add tomato sauce and simmer 15 minutes
3. mix cream cheese and sour cream
4. in 2-quart casserole , put 1 / 3 noodles , 1 / 3 cream mix , 1 / 3 meat mix
5. repeat twice
6. sprinkle cheddar on top
7. bake at 350 for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review: Great Recipe.  I followed it exactly and used Mini Penne Pasta as my pasta of choice.  I did cook it a bit longer - maybe 40 minutes.  I wanted to go back for thirds, but decided to pack it away for leftovers.  Thanks for the easy, delicious recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
silky vanilla butter frosting

this is not your usual butter-cream made with powdered sugar. butter is beaten into a flour-thickened base to make an exquisitely light and creamy frosting. not overly sweet like those made with powdered sugar, but sweet enough to be the perfect compliment for a cake. make sure the base is completely cooled before beating in the butter. i added in 15 minutes cooling time, but it will vary depending on conditions.

1. in 2-quart saucepan , thoroughly combine sugar and flour
2. with wire whisk , gradually stir in milk until smooth
3. cook over medium-high heat , stirring frequently , until mixture has thickened and boils
4. reduce heat to low
5. cook 2 minutes , stirring constantly
6. remove from heat and cool completely
7. in medium bowl , with mixer at medium speed , beat butter until light and fluffy
8. gradually beat in milk mixture
9. beat in vanilla
demonstrations.review: While I was making this frosting I was skeptical.  I was afraid that it was going to taste like flour.  It turned out great.  I really like the lightness of it.  It is Buttercream without the sickening sweet taste.  I frosted angel food cupcakes with this...and my 5 year old daughter and I are thoroughly enjoying them.  Thanks for the great new frosting recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
creamy pink vodka sauce with penne

creamy,rich,and smooth vodka sauce. quick and easy! use a vodka that you like to drink, if you can't drink it you won't eat  this.

1. put the olive oil into the pan and add the onions and garlic
2. turn on the heat to medium-low and gently cook for a few minutes
3. add the red pepper flakes cook 1 minute add crushed tomatoes
4. raise the heat to medium and bring the mixture to a boil
5. add the vodka and a pinch of salt and pepper simmer uncovered for about 8 minutes over medium-low heat
6. add the cream and lower the heat , add drained pasta and toss in parsley
7. stir to coat well and grate a generous amount of parmesan into the pasta using our microplane grater
8. serve immediately sprinkled with more parmesan , and red pepper flakes
demonstrations.review: Great Recipe.  I followed it exactly....other than using Crushed Tomatoes w/Basil - did not realize I didn't have plain tomatoes until it was too late.  I also added some chicken from a Rotisserie chicken I bought at the store today.   I halved the recipe for just the 2 of us - and still had some leftovers.  Thanks for a great pasta recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
crock pot potato chowder

another of my aunt's recipes. great for those cold nights.

1. combine potatoes , onion , broth , and cream of chicken soup in crock pot
2. cover and cook on low 8-10 hours or until potatoes are tender
3. add cream cheese and blend
4. top with bacon and chives before serving
demonstrations.review: Excellent!!!  I have not made a lot of crockpot recipes and wanted to start with a recipe that was fairly simple.  Not only was it simple, it was Delicious.  I followed some of the previous reviews and mixed my cream cheese in a bowl with soup broth...then added back into cropckpot and cooked a bit longer.  Just finished dinner and already looking forward to leftovers.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
buffalo chicken wing dip

i first tried this buffalo chicken wing dip at my neighbor's picnic.  a friend of theirs brought it and we munched on it all night til it was gone!  i love this recipe for picnics, potlucks and tailgate parties.  it's a much less messy way of enjoying chicken wings.  my oldest son loves it.  you can make it as spicy hot as you want...or leave it mild.  it's best served warm, but you can also eat it cool.

1. preaheat oven top 350
2. in a large bowl , mix shredded chicken , celery and cheese
3. in a saucepan over med-low heat , combine cream cheese and salad dressing and stir until smooth
4. stir in bottle of hot sauce
5. pour heated mixture into bowl with chicken mixture
6. stir to mix well
7. pour into a 13" x 9" baking pan
8. bake uncovered for 40 minutes or until bubbly----make sure top doesn't get browned
9. let stand for 10 minutes
10. serve warm or cold-----tastes best warm--- with celery or other veggies and crackers
demonstrations.review: Great Appetizer!  I made it for a Tailgate party and it was delicious.  I used Bleu Cheese dressing (only) and no celery in the actual dip.  We used celery sticks for dipping.  I also only used half of bottle of Frank's Hot sauce - as I had some folks that didn't like spicy foods.  It still had plenty of spice for us.  Thanks for sharing the great recipe.

target.recipe_text:
baked steak burrito casserole

this is a great introduction recipe to mexican cooking. yummy steak in melted cheese rolled up in a tortilla, covered in sauce! it doesn't use exotic ingredients and it isn't spicey. this recipe was a winner in a bake off contest that i found on a web site. a good hearty recipe for pot lucks, family gatherings etc.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. set aside a 13x9 inch baking pan
3. melt butter in a large skillet over medium heat
4. stir in taco seasoning
5. add beef strips and cook until meat is browned and drain
6. microwave beans until warmed
7. warm tortillas in microwave about 30 seconds
8. spread beans onto tortillas , leaving a 1 / 4 inch border
9. top with beef , cheddar cheese and green onions
10. roll up tortillas and fold in sides and place seam side down in an ungreased baking pan
11. pour enchilada sauce over burritos in pan and sprinkle with mexican cheese blend
12. bake at 400 degrees for 12-15 minutes until burritos are heated and cheese is melted
target.review: We absolutely loved this meal!!! From the first bite, you had to close your eyes and think MMMmmmmm.  I did make some changes:  I used left over grilled steak (sirloin and rib eye) and white onion instead of green (Green onions would have tasted better, but I didn't have them).  From reading Sheri's comment, I'm not sure why she didn't like the flavor, unless she used a yucky taco seasoning mix or enchilada sauce--I used Taco Bell and Gebhardt, respectively.  I only made six burritos, stuffed full and filled the pan.  This is a keeper!!  and answer to left over steak!  The only bad thing I have to say about this meal is the amount of dirty dishes.  Since there are no vegetables in this meal, a side is needed--more dirty dishes.  Anyway a fresh garden tomato salad seasoned with sea salt and fresh ground pepper completed the meal.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
german style eiskaffee  iced coffee drink

in germany, there are charming areas outside many restaurants called a 

1. place ice cream scoop into a decorative wine goblet or tall clear drinking glass
2. add coffee to fill glass 1 / 2-3 / 4 full
3. completely cover with a mountain of sweetened whipped cream - the whipped cream should be plentiful and just start to peak over the top of the glass rim
4. sprinkle with freshly grated good quality chocolate
5. stick a wafer cookie into the whipped cream off to the side
6. serve with some sugar on the side , a long spoon , and a straw
demonstrations.review:
I served this beautiful drink to a group of ladies I really wanted to impress.  And was everyone amazed!  There were several non-coffee drinkers in the group, but after seeing how pretty the drink was, they changed their mind.  

I did make one change:  I used hazelnut flavored coffee with a hazelnut cookie.

This is a wonderful end to a great meal too.  It makes your guests feel special.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
italian beef patties with balsamic cream sauce

boston's north end is famous for it's italian markets, restaurants and saint's day weekend festivals and i miss it so much! i was thrilled to find "the north end italian cookbook" by marguerite buonopane.

1. in a medium bowl , mix together beef , cheese , egg yolks , salt and pepper and form into 6 patties
2. heat 2 tbls butter in a heavy skillet over medium high heat , brown patties on both sides , reduce heat to medium and cook until juices are pink
3. remove patties and cover with foil
4. add oil , 1 tbls butter and onion to the pan and cook over medium heat until onion is golden brown
5. add cream and vinegar and cook on low 2 minutes
6. pour sauce over patties and serve
demonstrations.review: My husbands favorite dish, which he asks for weekly.  The kids love it too, I just serve them the patty--they are not into onion gravy, no matter how good it is.  I love this recipe because it's fast and easy.  This meal is a people pleaser!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kielbasa with tomatoes and white beans

a polish-italian quick fix main dish!

1. heat oil or butter in a large skillet , add kielbasa and cook over medium high heat until lightly browned , remove with slotted spoon
2. reduce heat to medium , add onions and cook until transparent
3. reduce heat to low , add garlic and herbs and cook 1 minute
4. add kielbasa , tomatoes and white beans , bring to a boil , reduce heat and simmer 10 minutes
demonstrations.review: This is a really good recipe.  I didn't have navy beans (Discovered this when the onions and spices were already in the pan---eeeeek.)  In a pinch, I used kidney beans.  The dish was wonderful and the family ate every last bite.  Just think what the recipe would have tasted like, had I all the ingredients.  I can't wait to make it again, the right way.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
zucchini cakes my mom s recipe   wonderful summer side dish

wonder what to do with you're zucchini fresh out of the garden? here is a wonderful side dish passed down from my mom.

1. place shredded zucchini in colander
2. squeeze as much liquid out as possible
3. sprinkle zucchini with salt
4. set aside in large bowl
5. saute onion in butter , drain and add to zucchini
6. in seperate bowl mix eggs , flour and pepper
7. add wet mixture to zucchini , stir well
8. drop mixture into rounded teaspoons , into well oiled frying pan , flatten slightly , cook 4 minutes on each side
demonstrations.review: My son and I are not fans of zucchini, but my neighbor grows it and gives it to me because my daughter and husband like it.  Since I had it on hand, I searched for an easy recipe with ingredients already in the pantry.  My son and I loved this dish (This is a great compliment, because he hates veggies)!!  I still don't like zucchini, but will eat it as long as I use this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
slow cooker cheesy chicken

almost too easy, the chicken cooks in a creamy, cheesy sauce that is delicious over noodles. this freezes well, too

1. place chicken breasts in the crock pot
2. mix the undiluted soups together with the garlic powder and pour over chicken
3. cover and cook on low 6-8 hours , until chicken is tender
4. serve with the delicious sauce over rice or noodles
demonstrations.review: My family really ohhhhs and ahhhhs everytime I make this recipe.  I've served it over both noodles and rice, I can't decide which is best.  I have to also mention the ease of this recipe--just a five minute investment, and I smile inside all day because I know my family is going to love me for making this dish.  Thank you, thank you.

target.recipe_text:
banana cherry cordial  cocktail

i found this cocktail recipe on a website called the greecelogue.  this is one of my favorite ouzo discoveries, because it's is a tasty cocktail that i really enjoy sipping while i'm relaxing and have time to read a good book or unwind after a busy day. it's served in a cordial glass or small cocktail glass.

1. in a cocktail shaker , add the chilled jgermeister , banana liqueur , coconut rum and ouzo
2. shake a few times , just enough to mix ingredients
3. add ice to the shaker , then strain cocktail into a cocktail glass
4. carefully add the blue curacao to the cocktail glass
5. garnish with two cherries , and enjoy
target.review: The flavors I got from this were mostly the anise from the ouzo and the Jager.  I really couldn't taste the banana.  I'm not saying I didn't like i, cuz I did, and wow, it packs a punch! It certainly allowed me to unwind after a long day!!  Thanks NG for sharing!!  Made for ZWT6!!  Team SSaSSy!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
garlic pickled green beans

i love a good pickled green bean recipe and these beans are very good!

1. in a medium saucepan combine 1 teaspoons
2. of the salt with the vinegar , sugar , garlic , bay leaves , onions , peppercorns and dill seed
3. place the pan over moderate heat and bring liquid to a boil
4. reduce heat to low , cover the pan and simmer for 30 minutes
5. meanwhile , half fill another medium pan with water and bring to boil over moderate heat
6. add remaining salt and beans and cook for 3 to 5 minutes
7. remove the pan from heat and drain beans
8. place them upright in dry , clean jars
9. set aside
10. remove vinegar mixture from heat
11. strain the mixture over the beans up to the top of jars
12. seal , and boil in a hot water bath for 10 minutes store in a dark , cool place
demonstrations.review: Yeah!  My first pickling experience was a success.  The recipe was very easy to follow and the results were awesome.  Definatley a potent pickled bean.  I was able to properly pickle 3 pints, but there was a significant spillage incident, so I'm sure 4 would be more likely for others.  Oh well, I'm hoping to do this agian soon.  Thanks for the recipe Sharon!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
green beans with almonds

the beans can be cooked the day before wrapped in paper towel and finished just before serving.

1. clean and trim green beans
2. simmer in lightly salted water until just tender , about 10 minutes
3. drain and rinse in cold water to keep the color bright
4. set aside
5. put remaining ingredients in a saucepan over medium heat and cook for two minutes , stirring constantly
6. add green beans and almonds and stir briefly to coat
demonstrations.review: What a nice way to do green beans!  Easy too!  I kinda cheated and used those Almond Accents they sell in the produce aisle, garlic flavored.  They were perfect for this!  Made for Las Mistico Magicos Sirenas - ZWT 5.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chocolate chip zucchini cookies

these are realllllllllly yummy cookies. dont tell anyone there is zucchini in them... they'll never know! cook time is the amount of time it takes to cook each batch of cookies!

1. first you will want to preheat your oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray cookie sheets with cooking spray or line with parchment paper
3. next you want to cream your butter and sugar together in a large mixing bowl until light and fluffy
4. then you want to add the egg , flour , baking soda , cinnamon , and salt into the butter mixture , gradually
5. mix well
6. stir in the zucchini
7. fold in your walnuts , and chocolate chips
8. drop by teaspoonfuls with two inches between each cookie-- onto the cookie sheets
9. bake for 15 to 20 minutes , or until golden
10. do not over-bake , or you will not enjoy your cookies
11. let stand to cool for 2 to 3 minutes , then remove and place on wire racks to allow to cook completely
12. this recipe makes a lot but is easily halved to make 4 dozen instead of 8 !
13. we make these for christmas sometimes , and therefore make a lot to give away !
demonstrations.review: I was interested to know how these would taste with zucchini in them, they were great!!  You would never know.  Its gotta be one of the best ways to use up some of those garden zucchini.  I really like the hint of cinnamon too.  I did halve the recipe and they came out fine!  Thanks love!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
hot sandwich with meat and mushroom sauce

a recipe from the issue of november 2005 of coup de pouce.  it looks so good on the photo.  can't wait to see a photo of one of you ;)

1. in a large skillet , heat oil at medium-high heat
2. add mushrooms , bell pepper , onion and garlic
3. cook , stirring often , for about 5 minutes or until liquid of mushrooms have evaporated
4. add ground beef , chili seasoning , salt and pepper
5. cook , stirring , 2 to 3 minutes or until beef is not pink anymore
6. add tomatoes , tomato paste and sugar , bring to boil smashing the tomatoes with a potato-masher
7. reduce the heat and let simmer , uncovered , for about 12 minutes or until preparation has thicken
8. meanwhile , toast kaiser bread
9. put mushroom preparation on bottom of inferior kaiser
10. cover with swiss cheese and the top of the kaiser
demonstrations.review: Great sandwich!  Reminded me of a sloppy joe but with more.  I did have to adjust a few things just to use what we had.  I used baby bella mushrooms, half red pepper and half green pepper and instead of the stewed tomatoes I used petite diced tomatoes.  All in all, don't think I really changed the recipe much and we loved it!  I think this would even be good served over pasta or with tortilla chips.  Very hearty meal and perfect for today's rain.  For the buns I used California Jan's Recipe #296559.  Thanks Boomette!!!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asian steamed dumpling filling

this a really terrific filling for those asian steamed dumplings. the recipe was given to me by a good friend who is a chef at benihana. you can use ground pork, ground shrimp, or ground turkey with great success. i have posted the recipe using ground pork because that is the typical mixture most people are accustomed to... but shrimp is a great indulgence and ground turkey is what i usually use and i love it.

1. whisk all ingredients for the dipping sauce well and set aside
2. mix all of the meat mixture ingredients together and let it marinade for an hour or so for best flavor
3. place a scant tablespoon of filling in the center of a wrapper and fold and tuck
4. you know how it is done or look up a video tutorial on youtube
5. they aren't as pretty as the little cute parcels but it is a huge time saver for me
6. steam them for 9 minutes
7. if you have a chinese steamer- fine
8. you can use a vegetable steamer in a large sauce pan or i use my electric wok with the steamer attachment
9. spray the steamer rack with pam or vegetable and you will have no problem with them sticking
10. the serving size is subjective depending on whether you use little wonton wrappers or egg roll wrappers so don't pay any attention to that -- but i had to enter something
11. the recipe will feed four however you decide to make them unless you are a glutton like me and then the serving size is just for one with a little bit left over for a snack the next day :-)
12. ?
13. bon apetit in japanese !
demonstrations.review: I am just thrilled beyond words with this recipe!  Loved everything about it and I just can't believe I was able to make them myself.  I could do a little happy dance for this one.  I used my brand new bamboo steamer and just sprayed it with pam.  It does take a little time to make the dumplings but it really isn't that bad.  Keeper!!!!  Thanks Potscrubber!!  Made for the Babes of ZWT4.

target.recipe_text:
sesame soy dressing

this sweet-tart japanese style dressing is from the flying fish restaurant in beautiful carmel-by-the-sea, ca.  this dressing can also be used as a marinade for chicken, pork and beef.

1. place all ingredients in a glass jar and seal the lid tightly
2. shake the jar until the sugar has dissolved
3. the dressing can be refrigerated , covered , for up to 1 month
4. bring to room temperature before using
target.review: This is the BEST steak marinade I've ever used and that's saying a lot because I try marinades all the time.  Easy to make; tenderizes the meat nicely and has a terrific blend of sweet and soy.  Made for ZWT4 for the Crazy Cooks! (-:  Thanks.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
flaky pineapple bars

i clipped this out of a newpaper years ago.  the recipe is yellow with age.  these are so flaky and delicious.  hope you like them.

1. cut butter or margarine into flour with pastry blender or two knives
2. add sour cream and vanilla
3. mix well and refrigerate 2 hours
4. meanwhile , cook pineapple , sugar , and cornstarch over medium heat stirring constantly until thick and clear
5. preheat oven to 325 degrees
6. roll out half of the dough and place in the bottom of a jellyroll pan
7. add cooled filling and spread over dough
8. cover with remaining rolled out dough
9. bake at 325 degrees for 55 minutes or until golden brown
10. sprinkle with confectioners sugar
11. cut in 70 squares
12. refrigerate if not used within a short period of time
demonstrations.review: This recipe is OUTSTANDING!!! Granted, it takes a bit of work, but trust me when I say, "It's worth it!"  I didn't have a jelly roll pan so used the largest pan I had and the bars came out YUMMY and GORGEOUS!!! Thanks so much, Nanny Annie.  Please keep those recipes coming.  Made for PAC 2007.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked empanadas

a spanish-style appetizer.

1. heat oven to 400 degrees
2. cook sausage , onion , green pepper and garlic in 10-inch skillet over medium-high heat , stirring occasionally , until sausage is browned and onion is crisply tender
3. drain well
4. stir in tomato and oregano
5. set aside
6. roll 1 sheet puff pastry to 12-inch square
7. cut into 16 squares
8. place 1 rounded tablespoon filling in center of each square
9. fold opposite corners of squares together to form triangles
10. pinch edges of pastry together
11. crimp with fork to seal
12. place triangles onto lightly greased baking sheets
13. repeat with remaining pastry sheet and filling
14. bake for 15 to 20 minutes or until golden brown
demonstrations.review: These were spicy little parcels which we enjoyed for lunch yesterday.  I loved the filling but didn't think there was enough of it to do the pastry justice.  Will happily make again but will use double the filling.  (-;  Made for ZWT 5!  YUM

demonstrations.recipe_text:
asparagus  n  shrimp with angel hair

i got this recipe from cooking for 2. i double the recipe since there are 4 of us :) we really like this.

1. cook pasta according to package directions
2. meanwhile , sprinkle shrimp with salt and pepper flakes
3. heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large skillet or wok
4. stir-fry shrimp for 2-3 minutes or until pink
5. remove with a slotted spoon and keep warm
6. in the same skillet , stir-fry the asparagus , mushrooms , tomato , garlic and onion in remaining oil for 5 minutes or until vegetables are crisp-tender
7. add wine or broth , basil , oregano , parsley and thyme
8. return shrimp to the pan
9. drain pasta
10. add to shrimp mixture and toss gently
11. cook and stir for 1-2 minutes or until heated through
12. sprinkle with parmesan cheese
demonstrations.review: I liked this pasta...mainly because it had shrimp and asparagus in it.  I followed the recipe to the letter except in the end, I didn't have Parmesan cheese (like I thought I did) so had to do without.  Wish I had gone with the chicken broth now as the wine seemed to overpower the dish a bit for my taste. May try this again with the Parmesan.  Sorry, bmcnichol, wish I could give it a higher rating.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fizzy raspberry citrus ice tea

a refreshing "fizzy" for those hot summer days.

1. place tea bags , berries , orange , lemon and sugar in a heat-proof pitcher or bowl
2. pour boiling water over
3. let steep 10 to 15 minutes , then remove tea bags
4. let mixture cool to room temperature , then chill
5. you can either keep fruit in or strain it out , depending upon your preference
6. when ready to serve , fill a tall glass with ice
7. pour in tea mixture to fill half way
8. top off with club soda
demonstrations.review: Very refreshing...very fruity...very yummy! Made for ZWT3 - U.S. Beverage Challenge.  We don't get orange spice tea here in New Zealand so I mixed and matched spiced and fruit teas I could get and it came out just fine.  Thanks, Nick's Mom. (:

demonstrations.recipe_text:
curried sauteed chicken chunks with coconut milk

serve with white rice.

1. toss the chicken with the curry powder , salt to taste , chilie and lemongrass
2. place the oil in a medium skillet , turn the heat to medium-high
3. when hot , add chicken and cook stirring occasionally until it loses its raw color
4. add the coconut milk so that it isn't saucy and cooks off mostly and turn heat to medium
5. cook for another 2-3 minutes until cooked through , then stir in the fish sauce and nuts and cook for another 30 seconds
6. garnish with cilantro and serve
demonstrations.review: This was a yummy main for dinner tonight.  I would recommend draining any remaining oil after cooking chicken...and also not cooking the coconut sauce too long as we found it needed more "sauce" after adding the peanuts.  Also, for our tastes, I would use about half of the fish sauce called for as we found it quite salty.  Overall, the dish was very nice.  I had never used chicken thighs like this before and found the flavor and texture worked quite well (I usually only use breast meat for these types of dishes).  I would use half the peanuts next time as well...we found they overpowered the chicken a bit.  LOVED the cilantro as the herb of choice for the garnish...great fresh flavor.  Made for PAC 2008.

target.recipe_text:
pineapple upside down cake

this recipe is by far the best pineapple upside down cake that i've ever made.  it is also quick and easy.  the cake is very moist and rises much higher than the average recipe.  the combination of pineapple cake mix and pineapple juice isn't overwhelming either.  i've been meaning to edit this for ages, however it looks so much better if you use dark brown sugar.  also if you'd like more topping, use 3/4 cup butter with 1 1/2 cups dark brown sugar.

1. preheat oven to 325 degrees fahrenheit
2. melt butter in a 9x13 pan in oven
3. sprinkle brown sugar evenly over butter in pan
4. drain canned pineapple into a measuring cup
5. place pineapple slices evenly in pan , cutting the last two in half to cover pan
6. place the maraschino cherry halves in the center of the pineapple slices , cut side up
7. combine the rest of ingredients in a large mixing bowl on slow speed for 30 seconds
8. beat on medium speed for 2 minutes
9. pour batter into pan
10. bake for 45 to 55 minutes , or until a toothpick comes out clean
11. cool 5 minutes and turn cake out onto a serving platter , pineapple side up
target.review: Yep! It's that good. I went with the crushed pineapple, pecans and no "extra" topping. It isn't overly sweet and soooooo moist. I had DH flip the cake onto the serving tray and waited anxiously as he removed the pan. There wasn't even in topping stuck in the pan, it all stayed beautifully on the cake. Thank you. This is definitely a keeper.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
carthagenian flank steak

this recipe was adapted from a gourmet and international recipe website. the flavors sound wonderful and i will be making this soon. the african recipe can also be found in the zaar world tour 2005 swap.

1. combine all ingredients , except steak , in a jumbo ziplock bag that has been placed in a glass bowl for support
2. after scoring the flank steak place it in the bag
3. seal the bag and refrigerate at least 20 minutes or up to overnight
4. heat the grill or a grill pan on the stove
5. remove the flank steak from the bag and pat dry with paper towels
6. grill 4 to 5 minutes per side or until done to taste
7. let rest 5 to 10 minutes before carving before serving
demonstrations.review: I'm sorry.  It wasn't our favorite by any stretch.  There is something missing that would turn this from okay to amazing.  The turmeric made it a strange orange color that was unappealing. The marinade smelled like carne asada and maybe that is what I was expecting.  I also cooked it on a grill pan and it smelled delightful while grilling but just didn't meet expectations when served.  I will keep watching because I think with a small tweak it could be really good.  I am just not sure what that tweak is.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
the best easy beef and broccoli stir fry

i clipped this recipe from taste of home magazine several years ago and have found it to be the best-tasting easy beef and broccoli stir-fry. it is credited to ruth stahl. i often use charcoal chuck steak, which is very tender and lean. i also like that it doesn't call for any unusual ingredients.

1. in a bowl , combine 2 tablespoons cornstarch , 2 tablespoons water and garlic powder until smooth
2. add beef and toss
3. in a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat , stir-fry beef in 1 tablespoon oil until beef reaches desired doneness
4. remove and keep warm
5. stir-fry onion in remaining oil for 4-5 minutes until softened
6. add the broccoli and cook for 3 minutes until the broccoli is tender but still crisp
7. return beef to pan
8. combine soy sauce , brown sugar , ginger and remaining 1 tablespoon cornstarch and 1 / 2 cup water until smooth
9. add to the pan
10. cook and stir for 2 minutes
11. serve over rice and garnish with toasted sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: This doesn't need another review but it was that good. I've tried other recipes that said they were as good as a restaurant and found them to be lacking. This one was. My husband, whom does not like chinese food raved. I doubled the ingredients in step six, added 1 tbls of oyster sauce, 1 tsp red pepper flakes and 3 cloves of minced garlic and used it as a marinade. Then when I cooked the recipe I skipped step 6. It was amazing. One of those recipes I keep thinking about and wanting more of. I also left my chuck blade steak slightly frozen and sliced it extra thin. Just delicious. Thank you for really having a restaurant quality recipe and sharing it with all of us! Outstanding. Probably one of the best recipes I've pulled off 'zaar.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
irish omelet

a great way to use up leftover boiled, baked or mashed potatoes. i love omelets and separately whipping the egg whites makes this light and fluffy despite the inclusion of potatoes.  in case you're wondering about taste - imagine a cross between a knish and a souffle.  other herbs or grated onions might be good variations.

1. separate the eggs and beat the yolks
2. add , the mashed potato to the yolks , mixing thoroughly
3. add the lemon juice , chives , and salt and pepper
4. whisk the egg whites until stiff
5. fold the egg whites into the potato mixture
6. melt the butter in a nonstick skillet or omelette pan over low-medium heat
7. cook the omelet until golden , then run under the broiler to finish and puff the omelet
8. serve immediately
demonstrations.review: The technique made a REALLY light and fluffy omelet.  I used roasted garlic mashed potatoes and topped the omelet with goat cheese and some leftover carmelized onions.  It was wonderful!  The technique (beating the egg whites) will be used anytime I make an omelet.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fake rotisserie chicken

this is so easy to prepare - and it tastes so good!

1. spray large crockpot with non-stick spray
2. form six pieces of aluminum foil into balls the size of a golf-ball and place in the pot
3. rinse the chicken thoroughly inside and out
4. rub your favorite seasonings both inside and out
5. poke holes in the lemon and insert it in the cavity
6. insert the onion in the cavity
7. place the chicken on top of the foil
8. add nothing else
9. cover and cook on low for 8 hours
demonstrations.review: 10 stars for sure.  I throw the chicken in the crockpot on day one.  Pick the bones clean and use the leftover chicken for day two's meal and boil the carcass with veggies and herbs for a wonderful broth to use in something else.  I really feel like I "use" that chicken up.  Flavor, texture, ease and versatility make this a staple recipe in our home.  Thank you!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
morning glory carrot muffins

this is a good way to start your morning, get your day going, finish off the day, hey, this is just a good thing to eat any time.

1. preheat oven to 400f degrees
2. lightly spray 12 muffin cups or line with paper cups
3. stir flour together with baking powder , baking soda , salt , spices and sugar in a large mixing bowl
4. whisk egg in a medium-size bowl with buttermilk , oil and vanilla
5. stir in pineapple
6. pour into flour mixture and stir until just combined
7. stir in carrots and raisins
8. spoon batter into muffin cups
9. bake 15-17 minutes or until a toothpick comes out clean
demonstrations.review: I make something baked every Monday morning for my office.  This is the favorite and most requested item on the list.  Even the fussiest eaters request these muffins.  I add flaxseed to them but other than that...recipe is unchanged.  Thank you for helping me ensure my staff and faculty remain happy with me time after time.

target.recipe_text:
chocolate pudding french toast

this is actually a modified version of "delish"'s very vanilla french toast recipe #136751 - which is tasty in itself!  i simply changed one ingredient - chocolate pudding mix instead of vanilla. it is amazing! and a whole new recipe! it's not over-powering, but yummy. i served it with the buttermilk syrup recipe also part of # 136751 - fabulous!  enjoy!

1. combine all ingredients except bread
2. whisk until well blended
3. dunk bread in mixture , coating both sides
4. cook on griddle until done
5. serve with whip cream , strawberries and buttermilk syrup recipe #136751
target.review: Incredibly easy to make and to modify the recipe for 2 servings.  I discovered the hard way to NOT use a cast iron griddle!  Non-stick is your friend on this recipe.  I suggest syrup on the side in a bowl to dip in if you are more calorie-conscious (which I am).  Thanks for posting this recipe!  Its a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun garlic pork roast

a lovely cooking light recipe.

1. preheat oven to 350f
2. in a small bowl mix the oregano , garlic , black pepper , seasoned salt , chili powder , cumin and red pepper together
3. rub evenly over roast
4. place on a broiler pan coated with cooking spray
5. bake for 1 1 / 2 hours or until a thermometer register 155-160f
6. let stand 10 minute before slicing
demonstrations.review: Incredibly easy and tasty.  Pleasantly zingy without being overwhelming.  Since there's only my husband and me, I only used a 1 lb. roast, which was perfect.  I also added in some Cajun seasoning and substituted ground red cayenne pepper for the crushed red pepper flakes.  Hubby thought it was so good that it's "company food."  Great recipe!!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
super easy oven fried chicken

my sister is a big weight watchers follower and this is her recipe. i've used bone-in chicken pieces (legs, thighs,etc..)and it always turns out good.

1. heat oven to 400f
2. spray cookie sheet with cooking spray
3. pour buttermilk into shallow glass or plastic bowl
4. add chicken
5. turn to coat
6. let stand 5 minutes
7. meanwhile , in 2-quart resealable food-storage plastic bag , crush cereal with rolling pin
8. add bisquick mix or flour and dressing mix to cereal in bag
9. remove chicken from buttermilk
10. discard buttermilk
11. add chicken to cereal mixture
12. seal bag
13. shake to coat
14. place chicken on cookie sheet
15. spray with cooking spray
16. bake 45 to 50 minutes or until juice of chicken is clear when center of thickest part is cut
demonstrations.review: Oh my GOODNESS this was a great recipe.  The chicken came out juicy, and the ranch dressing mix in the coating gave it a really unexpected flavor.  Very easy to prepare, and (since it's just my husband and me) very easy to modify to fewer servings.  I will definitely be replacing my old oven chicken recipe with this one (sorry Mom!)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
cajun salmon fillets

this is almost the only way i eat salmon.  note: i find this dish spicier when baked than when grilled.  i use a frozen wild whole salmon fillet cut into about 6 pieces; feel free to use fresh salmon or whatever cut you like.  if using salmon steaks, i would brush the seasoning on both sides.

1. thaw salmon
2. cut salmon into desired number of pieces
3. place skin down on a large tray or baking sheet
4. combine oil and spices , spread on top of salmon fillet
5. grill on barbeque till done , about 15-20 minutes or bake in a 400f 15-20 minutes
6. remove skin prior to serving
demonstrations.review: Very tasty and easy to prepare for just 2 people!  I used frozen Schwan's Alaskan salmon fillets and they worked out really well; perfect size, skin already removed, easy to defrost.  Even though they weren't steaks I brushed the seaoning on both sides anyway, which just added to the flavor.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tilapia wraps

super easy and diet friendly, these saved me from food boredom on my low-carb, low-fat, low- calorie diet!  they also happen to be fabulous.

1. set oven to broil
2. empty taco seasoning into a bowl
3. dredge fish in seasoning on both sides
4. broil fish 11 minutes , turning once
5. heat 4 tortillas in the microwave under a moist paper towel
6. place 1 fish fillet in each tortilla
7. top each with 1 / 8 cup shredded cheese , 1 tbs
8. avocado , 1 tbs
9. salsa , and lettuce
10. wrap and enjoy !
demonstrations.review: I agree--these ARE fabulous and super easy!  My husband added fat-free sour cream and diced tomatoes to his, and declared this meal "a gamble that really paid off."  I learned tonight, though, that the "taco size" burritos are too small, so I'll have to go up a size next time.  Thanks for a great recipe!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
parmesan crusted tilapia

fast, easy and healthy! this recipe is for 2, but i have easily doubled it for more.  this bakes so quickly that i often make a bunch of these fillets and eat them leftover for lunches.

1. thaw and wash tilapia fillets if frozen
2. pat dry on paper towels
3. combine crumbs , parmesan , italian seasoning and garlic powder on a plate , mixing well
4. on a different plate , pour 1 tbsp lemon juice
5. working 1 at a time , place a fillet on the plate in the lemon juice , sprinkle with desired amount of kosher salt , black pepper , and garlic powder
6. turn the fillet over in the lemon juice and sprinkle seasoning on the other side
7. dredge fillet in the parmesan mixture patting it all over to coat
8. place in an oiled baking dish , repeat with remaining fillets
9. sprinkle a little lemon juice over fillets and drizzle or spray them lightly with olive oil
10. bake at 425f for about 20 minutes or until they easily flake with a fork and edges are browning
11. you can also bake these faster at 450f
demonstrations.review: Awesome!  Easy EASY to put together, not a long cook time, and extremely tasty.  My husband (who said, "YAY!" when I said I'd fix this again sometime) and I have have been looking for a way to get a little more fish into our diet, and this recipe is definitely getting added to my meal rotations.

target.recipe_text:
1 hour ham and bean soup

made this one up myself, from a mix of different recipes.  no need to wait for dry beans to soak. you get great homemade soup in about an hour!

1. heat vegetable oil in a soup pot
2. add carrots , celery and onion
3. saut for about 4 minutes , just until onion is beginning to soften
4. add ham , saut 2 minutes
5. add garlic , saut one more minute
6. add 3 cups stock , bring to a low boil for about 10 minutes , stirring once or twice
7. meanwhile , in a food processor , combine all but 1 / 2 of a can of beans , including juice , and the tomato sauce
8. process until smooth
9. add remaining stock to processor to thin mixture
10. process to combine
11. add mixture from processor into ham mixture
12. add remaining 1 / 2 can of beans , stir to blend , bring to a boil , lower heat , cover and simmer for 30 minutes
13. serve hot !
target.review: Love ham just for the soup! I actually didn't have tomato sauce so I mixed some diced tomatoes and a can a cream of potato soup to add the thickness to the soup.  Like others, also added another can of whole beans.  Good stuff, Kelly!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fettuccine with asparagus and smoke salmon

from hallmark magazine. i made some modifications to the recipe to make it slightly more healthful and less fat. enjoy!

1. in a large pot of boiling salted water , cook fettuccine according to package instructions
2. add asparagus for last 2 minutes of cooking time
3. drain , reserving 1 1 / 2 cups cooking water
4. return pasta and asparagus to pot
5. meanwhile , in large non-stick skillet , heat oil over medium heat
6. add leeks and cook until tender , 8 - 10 minutes
7. add reserved pasta water , cream cheese , tarragon , and chives , and stir until cream cheese is melted
8. pour over pasta , ad smoke salmon and toss until well combined
9. season with salt and pepper to taste
demonstrations.review: I found this dish tasty, but a little on the bland side.  However, having said that, I need to reveal that I used a fat-free cream cheese, so maybe that had something to do with the blandness.  I did use fresh chives from my garden, and plenty of leeks, too.  Maybe some salt-free lemon/pepper seasoning would spice this up a bit, or perhaps a smokier salmon.  Thanks, though, for the recipe, as I wouldn't have had any idea for dinner without it!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
bon appetit cranberry margaritas

great for holidays...or any days!

1. blend ingredients in blender until smooth
2. transfer to large glass measuring cup
3. pour half of margarita base into blender
4. add 3 1 / 2 cups ice cubes
5. blend until mixture is slushy
6. pour into salt-rimmed margarita glasses
7. garnish with fresh cranberries
8. repeat with remaining margarita base and 3 1 / 2 cups ice cubes
demonstrations.review: Upped the quantity to 12 servings and placed in a pitcher to chill. The jellied cranberry sauce really pumped up the flavor here. I'm a connoisseur of margaritas, and this one passed the muster!  Thank you, KathyP53.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
lime and honey glazed salmon with warm black bean and corn salad

we got this recipe from a rachael ray cookbook and thought it was great.

1. black bean corn salad
2. preheat medium to large skillet over medium heat with 2 tbsp of olive oil
3. add onions , garlic , red pepper flakes , cumin , salt and pepper
4. stir occasionally for 3 minutes
5. add bell pepper and corn and cook for an additional minute
6. add chicken stock and continue to cook for an additional 2 minutes
7. add black beans and cook until beans are just heated through
8. remove skillet from heat and add juice of 1 lime , cilantro and spinach
9. toss to wilt spinach
10. lime and honey glazed salmon
11. preheat a medium non-stick skillet over medium high heat with 2 tbsp of olive oil
12. in shallow dish combine: juice of 1 lime , honey , chilli powder , salt and pepper
13. add salmon fillets and toss to coat
14. add salmon to hot skillet and cook until done
15. serve salmon over bed of black bean corn salad
demonstrations.review: Made this with double the spinach and shredded the salmon, tossing it into the salad itself.  (you can then use the same amount for a larger number of people). Four couples thoroughly enjoyed this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
roasted beet salsa  or salad

oh goodness, this is a super way to eat beets! beets, roasted, diced with ginger, jalapeno, garlic, mint and cilantro. throw in a little lime juice and mmmmm..mmmmm!


adapted from chef2chef!

1. to roast beets:
2. preheat the oven to 375 degrees f
3. trim the tops off the beets and drizzle with the olive oil
4. season the beets with salt and pepper , wrap them in aluminum foil individually and roast until tender , about 40-60 minutes
5. when cool enough to handle , peel the beets
6. while the beets are roasting , place the shallot , jalapeno , ginger , garlic , mint , cilantro , lime juice and 6 tablespoons of olive oil in a small bowl and stir to combine
7. when the beets are done , carefully remove the foil
8. let cool , and then peel the beets by slipping the skins off with your fingers
9. dice the beets and add salsa mixture , stirring to combine
10. taste for seasoning
11. great served with fish or eaten alone as a salad !
demonstrations.review:
I'm the BFF that made the aforementioned salsa put over italian lettuce mix!  this was fabulous, and I am even less of a beet fan than my BFF:)
Thank you for posting, as I will continue to buy fresh beets at the farmer's market now!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
winter tomato and cucumber salad

this salad was intended to extract the maximum from off season tomatoes by coxing out the flavors that are only soluble in fat or alcohol. the dressing will start to breakdown after one hour. if you want a little more zip, try pepper vodka.

1. combine the liquids and spices in a glass or plastic container with a tight fitting lid
2. beat the mixture with a fork or a whisk until it starts to thicken
3. add the vegetables , put on the lid , and shake several times
4. allow the salad to rest in a refrigerator for at least 20 minutes , but no longer than one hour
demonstrations.review: This was a fabulous, easy recipe, and with winter-time, the ingredients are inexpensive and readily available.  The marinade performed perfectly in bringing out the flavors of the three ingredients.  Cudos, Brother!

target.recipe_text:
zesty chicken saut

in a recent cookbook swap, i received some stellar cookbooks from chef #22015.  this recipe is from one of them.  "cheap. fast. good!" by beverly mills and alicia ross.  what a wonderful book!  this recipe is now one of my favourites.  the chicken is perfectly spiced, in my opinion.  i love the ease of preparation! you may need to increase the spice mixture though (if you like it thick like i do!).  i made up a batch of the spices and when it was gone, i simply made up another half recipe of it.  worked out perfectly with no waste!

1. place the chili powder , garlic powder , onion powder , cumin , salt and allspice in a gallon-size zipper-top bag and seal the bag
2. shake the bag to combine the spices thoroughly
3. place the chicken breast halves , one at a time , between two sheets of waxed paper or plastic wrap and pound them with several whacks of a meat mallet or rolling pin so that they are an even 1 / 2 inch thick
4. peel off the paper
5. place the chicken pieces in the bag with the spices , seal it , and shake until the chicken is coated with the spice mixture
6. set the bag aside
7. heat the oil in an extra-deep 12 inch skillet over medium heat
8. add the chicken pieces and cook until lightly browned on the first side , 4 to 5 minutes
9. turn the chicken and cook until no longer pink in the center , another 4 to 5 minutes
10. transfer the chicken to a platter and serve
11. a salad would be great alongside
12. my family's favourite is deep browned potatoes and corn
target.review: My mouth is still dancing for joy! I used 1/2 tsp of chili powder, 1/2 tsp of Mrs. Dash's Chipotle seasoning & 1/2 tsp Mrs. Dash's lemon pepper and normal cumin & garlic. I used olive oil as it is healthier.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
light and hearty cajun chicken pasta

this is a quick, easy and delicious one-pot meal which is low in fat but high in taste. this makes a large serving when divided by four and could be enough for six, depending on the appetites.

1. cook the pasta in a large amount of boiling water until al dente
2. drain and set aside
3. sprinkle the chicken with 2 t of the cajun seasoning and mix until coated evenly
4. spray a large nonstick skillet with nonstick cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat
5. add the chicken to the hot pan and cook for 2 minutes without stirring
6. when the chicken is lightly browned on one side , stir it to cook the other side
7. cook for about 5 more minutes , or until no longer pink inside
8. remove from the pan and keep warm
9. spray the pan again with the nonstick cooking spray and add the olive oil
10. over medium-high heat , add the peppers , mushrooms and 2 of the green onions
11. cook for 3-4 minutes , stirring occasionally
12. stir in the lemon pepper , basil , garlic powder , remaining teaspoon of cajun seasoning and the salt
13. then add the half-and-half , bring to a boil and add the chicken
14. stir until coated and warm
15. add the pasta and toss to coat
16. garnish with remaining green onions
demonstrations.review: I replaced the half & half with soy milk. I keep Kosher, meaning no mixing milk & meat. This was still a creamy tasty meal.  I used whole wheat spaghetti, because that is what I had in the house. Either my Cajun seasoning has lost it's heat or the seasoning needs to be kicked up a notch, but that is just a personal preference of spicier food.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
vegetable pasta bake

a tasty, easy meal from kraft.

1. mix spaghetti sauce , pasta , vegetables and 1 / 2 cup of the parmesan cheese
2. spoon into 13x9-inch baking dish or 3-quart casserole
3. sprinkle with mozzarella cheese and remaining 1 / 4 cup parmesan cheese
4. bake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes
demonstrations.review:
Very basic. If you don't have a good sauce... it lacks a lot of flavor. I recommend My Mama Iuliucci's "Don't Skip a Step" Spaghetti Sauce


Read more: http://www.food.com/recipe/my-mama-iuliuccis-dont-skip-a-step-spaghetti-sauce-26947#ixzz1Rqk0EXmQ

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken or turkey meatballs  moroccan style

my husband's mom would make this for me while i was in morocco. after the first time i tried to figure out what she put in it to make them so good. mine were ok but not wonderful like hers. so the next time i was there i paid close attention when she made them.

1. mix parsley , onion , & spices with the ground chicken
2. make sure it is well blended so that the spices are evenly distributed throughout the mixture
3. make 1 inch balls flattened to about 1 / 2 inch thickness
4. optional: dip the balls into the flour until coated
5. pour enough oil to just cover the bottom of the frying pan , heat on medium heat
6. place the balls into the heated oil
7. turn frequently so they do not burn on the sides
8. cook until they are done all the way through
9. optional: to eat moroccan style , use pieces of a thick bread to break off chunks of meatball
10. pop into mouth & enjoy
demonstrations.review: I was in Heaven!!!! Growing up one of my best friends mother was from Morocco. These meatballs were a taste from the past. Absolutely to die for. I mixed them into "Moroccan Spaghetti (Very Low Fat and Healthy)" Recipe #301361

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chicken  broccoli  and lemon stir fry

from everyday food november 2003

1. in a large , shallow bowl , whisk together soy sauce , 3 tablespoons water , vinegar , honey , garlic , and crushed red pepper
2. pour half of the mixture into another bowl
3. reserve
4. place chicken in remaining mixture
5. marinate for 15 minutes
6. in a 12-inch nonstick skillet , heat 1 / 2 tablespoon oil over high heat
7. add half the chicken
8. cook , tossing often , until brown and cooked through , 2 to 3 minutes
9. transfer chicken to a plate
10. repeat with another 1 / 2 tablespoon oil and remaining chicken
11. wipe skillet with a paper towel
12. heat remaining tablespoon oil in skillet over medium-high heat
13. cook broccoli and lemon , tossing often , until broccoli is bright green , about 3 minutes
14. add 1 / 2 cup water
15. cook until broccoli is tender and lemon is translucent , about 6 minutes
16. add reserved marinade , cornstarch mixture , chicken , and any accumulated juices from plate
17. bring to a boil
18. cook , stirring until thickened , 1 minute
19. sprinkle with sesame seeds
demonstrations.review: This was very good! My friend gave me a bag of lemons from her tree... so I am going lemon crazy. that is what led me to this recipe. I added sliced red pepper and onion. I also substituted olive for canola oil.  Thank you for sharing, we will make it again.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
oven fried southern style cinnamon honey chicken

while watching foodtv, i saw a piece about amy ruth's restaurant in new york where the owner made fried chicken dipped in a honey cinnamon mixture. it looked so good i began searching on the web for a recipe which approximated it... and after much browsing of webpages i put together a recipe that i thought might taste something like it. i don't fry my chicken, so here's a baked version, tweaked to my own tastes.

1. preheat oven to 350 degrees f
2. spray a large roasting pan lightly with cooking spray
3. combine the flour with the salt , cinnamon , turmeric , black pepper , and a pinch nutmeg
4. coat the chicken pieces well with the flour mixture
5. beat together the egg and milk
6. dredge the flour-coated chicken pieces in the egg mixture , then into the breadcrumbs
7. arrange pieces skin side up in the sprayed roasting pan , making sure that the pieces are not touching each other to ensure they bake crispy
8. spray chicken pieces with oil spray or sprinkle with 2 tablespoons oil and place the chicken in the oven to bake
9. while the chicken is baking , in a saucepan over medium low heat combine the butter , honey , pinches of cinnamon , and lemon juice
10. after the chicken has baked for 25 minutes , pour the butter and honey mixture generously over the pieces
11. bake for an additional 15 minutes or until the juices run clear and the chicken is crisp and brown
demonstrations.review: This was amazing!!!! For some reason I did not have nutmeg in the house so I added ground cloves. Also I don't mix milk & meat so I used soy milk. A trick I learned from watching Rachel Rae is to mix the oil in with the bread crumbs before breading the chicken. It mean rather than oily chicken it is evenly spread throughout. I also used cayenne pepper in the flower & sauce. I will make this again. THX!!!!!

target.recipe_text:
denny s style french toast

i do not remember where i got this recipe, but my husband says it tastes just as good as what he had at denny's. i am just amazed at all of the great reviews on this recipe!! my family loves it, so i thought i would share it here and i'm so glad i did because it seems you all love it just as much!!! thanks to all of you who have tried it!

1. mix together the eggs , milk , flour , sugar , vanilla , salt& cinnamon
2. heat a large skillet , or griddle
3. when the skillet is hot , add 1 tablespoon butter
4. if the butter smokes , your pan is too hot
5. turn down the heat
6. dip each slice of bread into the batter for 30 seconds on each side
7. let some of the batter drip off , then put in skillet
8. cook each slice 1 1 / 2-2 minutes per side until each side is golden brown
9. add more butter , if necessary , to cook all of the slices
10. to serve , put on plate , dust with powdered sugar
11. serve with butter & hot syrup
target.review: I just finished making it for my 11 year old daughter's New Year's sleepover.  It was a hit with all the girls.  I made it with Hawaiian bread.  I got the one cold piece that was left when they were done, and it was delish.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
tahitian coconut bread

i got this recipe in hawaii at the polynesian center. they were giving samples away and it was delicious.
i haven't make it yet and the baking instructions are not very good (it doesn't mention a baking pan), but i will try it and see what happens.

1. combine coconut , sugar and water
2. blend flour and baking powder together
3. mix all ingredients to a doughy texture adding a little flour as needed so is not too sticky
4. wrap in aluminum foil and bake in oven at 350 for 1 hour to 1 1 / 2 hours
5. makes 5 loaves
demonstrations.review: We live on Oahu and have made this bread quite a few times.  Coconut are free!  I use the food processor to chop the coconut fine.  I have also updated the recipe to make it a wee bit healthier - white whole wheat flour and subbing Splenda for half the sugar.  I also add a teaspoon of vanilla and a 1/2 teaspoon of salt.  This is my go-to "welcome to Hawaii" bread when family and friends from the mainland come to visit.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
broiled parmesan tilapia  low carb

you'll love this fish recipe! i have also made this with other meaty fish fillets too, works well with basa fillets also!

1. set oven to broiler heat
2. grease a broiler pan , then line with foil and grease the foil slightly
3. in a small bowl mix together parmesan cheese , butter , mayo , lemon juice and garlic
4. add in all the remaining seasonings and salt if using
5. mix well and set aside
6. arrange the fillets in a single layer on the prepared pan
7. broil a few inches from the heat for about 2-3 minutes
8. turn the fish over and broil a couple minutes more
9. remove from oven and cover them with the parmesan mixture on the top side only
10. return to oven and broil for about 2 minutes more or until the topping is browned and the fish flakes easily
demonstrations.review: This is the recipe that makes my husband give me the look like, "What do you know, she actually can cook!"  ;-)  It is 1) yummy, 2) great for our low-carb diet, 3) cheap, and the most important for my skills 4) EASY.  Many thanks!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
chex muddy buddies

another popular name for this favorite mix is "puppy food". chow down; it's doggone good!

1. into large bowl , measure cereal
2. set aside
3. in 1-quart microwavable bowl , stir together chocolate chips , peanut butter and butter
4. microwave uncovered on high 1 minute
5. stir
6. microwave about 30 seconds longer or until mixture can be stirred smooth
7. stir in vanilla
8. pour mixture over cereal , stirring until evenly coated
9. pour into 2-gallon resealable food-storage plastic bag
10. add powdered sugar
11. seal bag
12. shake until well coated
13. spread on waxed paper to cool
14. store in airtight container in refrigerator
demonstrations.review: I halved the recipe because I knew we couldn't be trusted with it in the house.  What an easy dessert to enjoy while the kids finish homework.  I'm not really a cook, but I'm trying to move away from packaged, expensive snacks and treats.  This is a winner!

demonstrations.recipe_text:
fiber one crunchy fudge cookies

these taste like little crunchy brownie bites!! i made this exactly as the recipe stated, but i realized i had a box of brownie mix that was a couple ounces bigger than the recipe called for. i added another 1/3 cup water to compensate as the mix was pretty dry. i also baked them the full 12 minutes, which was fine for my oven. hope you like these somewhat healthy little chocolate cookies! from a box of fiber one cereal; calories 70, calories from fat 10, 1 gram fat

1. heat oven to 350f
2. spray cookie sheets with cooking spray
3. in large bowl , mix all ingredients with spoon
4. onto cookie sheets , drop dough by rounded tablespoonfuls 2 inches apart
5. bake 10 to 12 minutes until set
6. cool 2 minutes
7. remove from cookie sheets to cooling rack
8. cool completely
9. store in tightly covered container
10. freeze up to 2 months if desired
demonstrations.review: My family LOVES these cookies.  It's the taste of brownies with a great texture and the Fiber One makes them a much healthier treat.  Itâ€™s cookies you can feel good about, AND the kids will actually eat â€¦ what a concept!  ;-)

demonstrations.recipe_text:
nut encrusted mahi mahi

from one of the best chefs on the island, this recipe is quick, easy, low fat and gourmet. what could be better? wait until you taste it.

1. heat oven to 350 degrees
2. in a food processor , pulse nuts until coarsely chopped
3. add cornflakes and pulse both together until flakes are in small pieces but not broken down
4. add chopped parsley , salt and white pepper to the mixture and spread on a platter
5. roll the fish fillets in the cornflake breading and press it on the fish with your fingers to make it stick
6. spray the baking pan , lay the fish fillets inches
7. bake for 10 minutes
8. the fish should still be moist and delicate- not overcooked or dry
9. while the fish is baking , mix the honey , soy sauce , and dry mustard until thoroughly integrated
10. place the mahi mahi on a dinner plate with rice
11. pour a little honey soy glaze over the fish and drizzle a little around it on the plate
12. serve
demonstrations.review: This is a regular in our Hawaiian home.  My husband loves to spearfish here on Oahu, and we have fresh fish at least once a week.  Tonight itâ€™s uhu (parrot fish).  I get a big bag of mac nuts from Costco since I use this recipe so often.  The first time I made it, I had trouble getting the crust to stick, so I dunk the fish in Egg Beaters first.  The sauce is so simple, yet so perfect.  Thanks for the recipe!

target.recipe_text:
charlie s famous chicken salad with grapes

a really great guy i used to work with would make this and bring in to share. we all loved it so much and would beg for more! sounds strange with the grapes, but it's so good! allow time for salad to chill.

1. combine all ingredients
2. chill
3. serve with just about anything- crackers , chips , rolls , bread or bagel
target.review:
yes, this was really good.  Just from reading the reviews alone made me run down to the store to get the ingredients needed to make this salad, and it was well worth it. Thanks so much for sharing.   
s/n: I followed the recipe exactly as written except I used  used half pecans and half walnuts.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
melt in your mouth chicken breasts

the mayonnaise make these chicken breast very moist and tender--enjoy!

1. mix mayonnaise or yogurt , cheese and seasonings
2. spread mixture over chicken breast and place in baking dish
3. bake at 375f for 45 minutes
demonstrations.review: This recipe was very very delicious and truely unique, a big twist from the regular baked chicken breast I usually make. I used 1 teaspoon of salt instead of the 1 1/2 seasoning salt, to make sure it didn't come out to salty, and I was out of Pepper so I used a dash of Cilantro and Parsley, and also added sweet onions, and red and green peppers to the top of the chicken before baking it.... it came out beautiful.  Thanks so much for sharing this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
baked salsa chicken breast

nan

1. place chicken breast in a 2 quart baking dish that has been sprayed with cooking spray
2. combine the salsa , brown sugar , vinegar and mustard in a bowl
3. pour over chicken bake at 400 for 30 minutes
4. serve with rice or buttered noodles
demonstrations.review: This was very good, a quick last minute recipe.  I put on a pot of yellow rice and threw some sweet corn in it.  Yummy.  They went together perfectly.  I can't wait to make this again.  Thank you so much for this recipe.

demonstrations.recipe_text:
kittencal s scalloped potato and ground beef casserole
